-EX1hrPRBqNkVavtMllTCA.review_text: We had food from this "restaurant" delivered to our office for a luncheon.  Big mistake.  Several orders screwed up.  Fried chicken and waffles were tasteless.  Tomato soup too salty.  And they managed to even screw up salads.  Imagine that.  Avoid like the plague.
Had our Christmas party here this year.  The service was top notch, the food came out right on time, and the steak was HEAVENLY.  The sides were excellent.  Definitely worth the trip!

Went here on a lark, basically.  I had enough of C list luncheries and wanted something a bit better.  I ended up getting a Luke Burger and devoured it in moments.

The service was top notch.  My waiter, Richard, was always attentive and even made a glass of sweet tea for me! (Note: they serve only unsweet tea)  Earned him a 25% tip for that.

It will be a good bit before I try it again, as the average price for a meal is $16, but when I want treat myself to a delectable burger I'll come here.

This is one of the "retro" McDonald's and it's one of the better ones in New Orleans East.  The place is always clean, always busy, and the employees are friendly.  The orders also are filled quickly, always a plus especially in the mornings.

This location is inconsistent.  Sometimes it bats it out of the park, and then there are times that the batter must be blind because of the misses.

This location has a dual drive thru and that does cause some confusion when you get to the first window.  Don't bother coming here in the mornings, because the lines will be long (both inside and out) and the service inside is slow.

I am currently listing to port as I type this.  You'll have to forgive me, I had a Big Jack for lunch.

I was hesitant to try this place out, as I had heard wildly conflicting reviews about it.  But, it was my co-worker's "last day" luncheon and she wanted a burger.  So, we all trooped down there.

Word to the wise, either go really early (we had a twenty minute wait when we got there at 11:30) or go really late (it was half full at 12:45 p.m.)  

Our food was delicious.  The Big Jack was, well, big and tasty as all Hell.  The fries were hot.  My co-worker couldn't finish her BBQ burger and had to take it home.

One giant plus, our waitress was more than accommodating when it came to splitting up the check.  That's means a lot, since most places get snippy when you ask for separate checks.

All in all, try it out.  You won't be disappointed.

Used to love to eat here when I was in high school, but when I returned after a bit neither the food nor the service kept up.  The pizza's bland, greasy, and flavorless and the pricing for some of their offerings are off the wall expensive for what they offer in quality.  Avoid.

If you're looking for excellent food, HUGE portions, and quick turnaround then this is the place to eat when you're in the CBD.  The quality of the food is in direct proportion to the price.  You get what you pay for here!  I never turn down a request to go here for lunch.  

People who list a "con" about this place fills up fast really mean it's a "pro".  I find a place that is wall to wall busy indicative of a good place to eat.  If it's completely dead, it's usually a tell that the place sucks.  That's not the case here.

I hit this location intermittently, usually when I'm coming home from work on the weekends or when we close the office early. My usual is a Roadhouse Burger and a large order of the seasoned fries.  

I have no complaints about this store, the staff is always nice to me and I've never gotten a wrong order yet from here.  If you're in the area, and you want something other than the King or Mickey D's, try them out.

Ate here all of once and that was enough.

The place was far from busy, but our waitress was far from helpful.  Why attend a three person table when you can chat up the all male table catty corner to us?  The food was all right.

I notified corporate and nothing happened.  A place that doesn't even bother to respond to your concerns, but seems quite fine in throwing coupons your way to drum up business will NOT get it from me.  Avoid.  There are better places to eat.

A teeny, tiny hole in the wall that has some of the better food in the CBD.  Portions are plentiful and the service is down to earth and friendly.

Try them out!  You won't go wrong.

There's nothing better than hearing out of towners sitting next to you rave about their po boys.

Eaten here several times and have received awful service each time.  The food's acceptable, though not for the price.  Stretch your legs and check out what other eateries in the area have to offer.  This place is for people who don't know or don't care for other places to eat.

I went here for a change of pace.  It's a pleasant restaurant but overpriced for what you get.  The sweet potato fries are a welcome change, but unfortunately inconsistent in preparation and taste.

Try it once to see if you'll like it.  I've given it a chance and decided not to go back.
Love this place.  Food is delicious.  The service is prompt and the staff is always friendly.  Eat there when you're out by the Lakefront.  Can't go wrong.

I've eaten here several times, and the best I can say is it is mediocre.   The prices aren't worth the food you get, it's simple as that.  I love the ambiance of the place, though.  The place would be great if they married the ambiance with an improved food quality. 

Until that happens, there are other, actually better, Japanese restaurants in the nearby area to eat at.

Gah!  I hate finding new burger places in the CBD to try out, especially when it's one I'm going to become a regular at!

Dress It! is primarily a burger restaurant located in the Omni Royal Crescent.  The interior very swanky and pretty spacious. The menu's the novelty of the place.  You check off what you want, the toppings, the bun (or lack thereof) and the sides. Once you've finished compiling your culinary masterpiece, you hand off your order to the waitress and away you go.

I've noticed other reviews mentioning inconsistent service/food.  Well, I'm here to add my two Cardinal's Crowns.

I was seated promptly.  Ordered a medium well burger with bacon and onion rings.  Turnaround time from order placed to receiving order: less than ten minutes.  The burger was cooked to my specifications and the toppings were fresh.  The onion rings, while pricey, were a pleasant surprise.  Instead of the standard batter, they were battered in what appeared to be fish batter.  That left them crispy to the bite and debris wasn't falling all over the place.

My waitress, Jenny, was very nice and even gave me a to go cup for my sweet tea.  

To quote MacArthur, "I shall return..."

This is my second time eating here.  I had the A-Train (roast beef, grilled onions, pepper jack cheese on Italian bread) and a order of fries.  The sandwich was hot, the bread soft, but the meat was as dry as the Utah salt flats.  The fries were excellent, though, and they gave you nearly a wheelbarrow of them.

It's not Subway and that's a step up, but the dishes I've had from the place have not really wowed me.  I'll try again, but it's doubtful that I'd go here regularly.

This franchise isn't one of the better ones (BK is low on my fast food listing anyway).  The drive thru experience could be described as rushed, but polite, with the rushed being that my hash browns skittered all over the bag due to improper placement.  Crossoinwich was warm, but not hot.  Avoid.
Decent pizza.  A little slow on delivery to One Shell, but otherwise unremarkable.

This past weekend, after attending a company picnic at the Zoo, I convinced my family and mother in law to get some ice cream at the only DQ in the metro area.  The place is small (Hence the reason why they don't serve hamburgers, no space for grill), but it was packed with several girls little league teams enjoying ice cream after playing softball.

Watching the employees, it was obvious they were used to the crush of nearly constant customers.  One thing of note is the reason WHY I give this place five stars:

Ahead of me was a recently minted graduate from Tulane University, still wearing his gown from the ceremony.  He placed his order and was waiting to be cashed out.

The manager came over and asked him if he graduated.  The customer confirmed that he did.

The manager asked where he graduated from, the customer told him.

Then the manager comped his entire order.

THAT IS AWESOME!

Even though this place is located in my old neighborhood, I'll gladly take a trip out here for ice cream from Dairy Queen.

Goodbye, Subway(s) in the CBD.... HELLLLLLO, JIMMY JOHNS!

Ludicrous amount of seating.  Very clean.  Sandwiches?  BAMF! Done, here ya go! Have a nice day.  

CHEAPER THAN SUBWAY AND YOU GET MORE!

I have found my new favorite cold sub sandwich place!

If I wanted the Wal-Mart experience, I'd have gone to one.  The place was cluttered, messy, and half the checkout lines were closed.  Used to like this location when I lived in Metairie, but now you won't be able to drag me in here again.

Nothing to write home about, but better than the offerings in One Shell, and reasonably priced.  Also, if I want a caloric breakdown of menu items, I'll read the back of some packaged food.  Seriously, if you're counting calories then maybe you should make your own lunch, or make better choices of what's available, before categorically slamming a place because you're on a diet.

Service and speed, excellent.

Food quality, pretty good.

Prices? Absolutely not.

The food was really good, just not $16 good.

First time coming here and was optimistic. Too bad it didn't live up to it. 

I had the fried rice with chicken and a cucumber wrap roll. The rice looked delicious, but when I started to eat it, any possible flavor it could have had was OVERWHELMED BY PEPPER. That's all I could taste. 

The cucumber wrap roll was equally underwhelming. It looked beautiful, but tasted like mushed carrots. 

$30 for this? Pass, I'll find somewhere else to eat.
Used to be a good place to grab a bite to eat. But now they're way overpriced, their poboys are small and are nothing to write home about. Better places to eat here in NO, I assure you.

This was my first time trying Korean food, and I'm glad that I chose The Bop for my first foray. I got the Koko Bop, which was fried chicken with a custom orange sauce and white rice. Oh my God, the sauce was delicious! *Homer Simpson gurgle* 

Overall, I'm really glad we got a great new place to eat in the Capital One building. I will definitely be back for more!

Koz's Lakeview is dead. LONG LIVE KOZ'S LAKEVIEW! =o(

At least we still have Koz's in Harahan. =o)

Alas, I am full of sadness with my most recent excursion.  I went to Dress It to have a simple meal: a burger and onion rings.  Unfortunately, what greeted me was an unwelcome change.

The little mini menu checklists to mark off what you want on your burger? Gone. Replaced with a VERY truncated menu placard.  My beloved onion rings? Also gone.

So, I ordered a burger with lettuce, cheese, tomato, and pickle with an order of fries.  While the fries were good, they couldn't hold a candle to the onion rings missing from their menu.

As for the burger, they also changed how they were made.  My first bite gave me an overwhelming pepper taste.  I soon found out why, as they made the burger meat with finely chopped green pepper.  That's all I could taste.

After these two disappointments, I knocked off two stars, and probably won't be back.  The thrill is gone.
Tried it out today. It's okay, nothing to write home about. But! I really enjoyed the atmosphere and Sean, the bartender, is really great. I might try it again when I get a chance.
The place is always busy, loud. However, it has extremely delicious pizza and the turnaround time for your order is quick. Environmental foibles aside, it's a great place to get a pie on the cheap.

I have to echo the other reviewers of this place. At the time of my visit through drive through, the employees screwed up an order two cars ahead and had to sit there for at least five minutes while they fixed that. When I got up to the window, the two employees were just talking about the previous screw up and not really paying attention to me. I received my order and this is how it turned out:

I got a two chalupa meal and both of the chalupa shells were over cooked, leaving them brittle.  My crunchy taco hardly had any meat in it, same goes for the lettuce and cheese.  My drink had AN ice cube in it. One. Singular. That left it room temperature.  I'm never eating here again and corporate's going to hear about it.

A gas place of last resort.  Lots of panhandlers and homeless people hang out here, and the very last time I went they were completely out of gas.

Let that sit with you.  Out of gas.

Not going back.

This place gets a resounding "Meh" from me.  I've dined here several times and now I'll post my review.

Now, on the customer service side, I've never, ever had bad service here.  Unfortunately, the dish quality is definitely hit or miss.  On my first visit, I tried the jerk chicken, but wasn't wowed by it because it just didn't taste right to me.

Today, I tried the chicken western burrito, and again it just didn't taste right.  Then my brain told me why.

"They're probably using dark meat."

Of course they would, it's cheaper.  So, this is marked off my list as places to go for lunch.  Sorry, Juan.

I really enjoyed my initial visit to this restaurant.  I ordered snowcrab roll and cucumber roll, as well as a hibachi chicken lunch plate.  The sushi is rather on the expensive side, but overall the food was downright delicious.

One of the shabbiest Applebee's I've ever been to.  The floor was dirty, with napkins and discarded straw wrappers next to the booth. We were blessed with a HIGHLY INATTENTIVE waitress, whom I spent most of the time watching the back of her head while she watched TV.  Our appetizers came out lukewarm and the entrees weren't much better.

Paid bill, 10% tip, and NEVER AGAIN for this location.

-M7fUg7FrdGctKr5f_eMUQ.review_text: Really unfortunate experience here...had friends visiting from out of town and wanted to introduce them to the delicious mojo bowl. Waited 15-20 minutes and didn't even have a waiter come by the table. After reminding the hostess that we were still waiting for a server, 10 more minutes passed with nothing, so we left. For context, it was not crowded. This was the second time I've been to this establishment and they are 0 for 2 in the service department.

Absolutely some of the best Mexican grub on this side of town. As others have posted, the Oro Valley "branch"  lacks some of the nostalgia and atmosphere that the historic downtown location has, but maintains the excellent food. Recommend the Birria burro or the carne seca if you're looking for a ton of flavor and a drier meat. Price points are the only thing keeping el charro from getting five stars.

The food was authentic, delicious, and clearly home-made. The tortillas in the enchiladas were really tasty, and the chicken tortilla soup is a must. Unfortunately, this restaurant is truly a "diamond in the rough (neighborhood)", so I'd recommend a daylight visit to El Sur unless you have a concealed carry permit, black belt, or guard dog (half-kidding).

Utter service disaster. Called in a reservation for 3 at 8pm. Showed up and the table wasn't ready. Finally got seated at 8:45. Took 20 minutes for drinks. Food still wasn't served by 10pm, and when it came out the grouper was still cool in the center. Waitress gave us a free beer as compensation... Manager (if there even was one) never showed up to do so much as apologize. Shameful.

I come to Guadalajara Grill 4-5 times a year and it never disappoints. I usually go with a chimi but recently discovered the molcajete bowl. Similar to fajitas,  it came out in a sizzling stone bowl, with the carne/mariscos simmering in a tomato stew. Delicious and a huge meal. The lively decor, mariachi band, friendly service and extensive menu make this a great destination for out of town visitors and locals, young and old alike. Check it out!

Great experience to complete our trip to St. Pete-treasure island! Mango nut grouper was cooked to perfection, fresh, and delicious. My girlfriend went with the sirloin and shrimp skewers, which was also really good. If you're looking for a nice sit down atmosphere near the beach, this is the place to go. Prices are a bit high, which is the only thing keeping it from getting five stars.

Great location, price points, and most importantly...food! I had the two burrito combo with rice and beans. You can mix and match meats and I went with the al pastor and barbacoa. The former was very tasty, the latter was probably the best barbacoa I've had. The menu is priced like Nicos, and the tastes are on par with el Charro. What's not to love?

Highly recommend. Cheap, convenient, and food quality that far exceeds the price point. Sonoran hot dogs are tasty, and the Barria (sp?)and carne asada tacos were great. I haven't tried the corn tortillas, but the flour tortillas really made the tacos. Check this place out-puts the taco shop across the street to shame.

Great casual Japanese dining experience on Tucson's east side. Tons of menu options, polite and friendly staff, and a very comfortable and traditional feel inside the restaurant. Love the hand-written specials all over the walls. Can't find better raw fish in the desert. Try the Mahi Mahi Tempura for a new and delicious change of pace.

Wow, this place lived up to the high expectations. The snickerdoodle pancake was delicious (and also provided to us free-of-charge since it was our first visit), and there were lots of interesting breakfast options and combinations. The atmosphere is low-key and relaxed, but it is a pretty small restaurant so I'd expect a wait on any weekend like we experienced.

This place is awesome. Lots of local products used (Thunder Canyon Brewery Stout, Savaya Coffee, local raw honey), and they offer traditional flavors as well as some ecletic hybrids. Don't miss an opportunity to support a locally owned establishment that EASILY tops national competitors in flavor and quality.

This place is perfectly fine and nothing exceptional, but sports bar options on the northeast side are limited so we will likely be back. I would recommend the machaca benedict as a brunch entree, although 12 bucks is a bit steep for these parts. They have a pretty extensive beer selection, although price points are also north of what you'd expect in Tucson. The atmosphere is odd--I couldnt tell if they were going for upscale or dive--and they need to splurge for HD receivers on all of the TVs for football. All in all, its a solid B.

Good spot to watch sports, have a beer, and eat some unhealthy, but pretty tasty pub fare. The stuffed burger with green chilis and pepperjack was really good, and the tater tots are a nice change of pace. Service was fine on a pretty quiet weekend evening. It looks like this place is getting unfairly hammered on yelp based on negative experiences during the first few weeks of operation. If you are in the NE, its worth a shot.

Super comfortable atmosphere with unique drink options. They offer agave and whiskey flights, local beers, wines, and spirits. Didn't eat, but other patrons' food looked solid. Great option in downtown Tucson that supports local business. Check it out!
High quality food, great bloody mary, laid back atmosphere. Super impressive (and locally owned!)
Awesome pizza, great beer selection, sports on one of the many TVs, and a laid back atmosphere. Great place for grown-ups, and they also have a cool outdoor and indoor play area for the kids.

I can't speak to their food, but they proved incapable of processing a confirmed Grub Hub order. Grub Hub blamed Pita Jungle, I couldn't even get a hold of the restaurant. At the end of the day it doesn't really matter who is to blame. This partnership is a total mess. Good news is that Grub Hub has the courtesy of running my card immediately when the order was placed, and it will take 3-5 days to process a refund.

One of the business leads from Pita Jungle had the courtesy to personally reach out after a frustrating mix up with a Grub Hub order placed at their restauarant, was very apologetic, and helped make things right. Still work to do with Grub Hub, but a much appreciated gesture.

Very unpretentious and laid back atmosphere, with a great blend of higher end steaks with Mexican influence. Definitely recommend checking it and adding it to your list for date nights and special occasions!

Our waitress was generally disengaged aside from when she was trying to rush us out of the bay when our final game ended (this was after we extended multiple times and continued to order food and drinks). As soon as we started wrapping things up, she was suddenly present every 1-2 minutes to remind us that she left the check at the table, offer to-go boxes for food we were still eating, and warn us that a new group would be arriving at the bay in 5 minutes. I get that there was a wait list, but pushing out current customers who just spent hundreds of dollars is terrible business and disrespectful.

Really good beers and a dynamic selection. Friendly, laid back atmosphere. They have a cool program where customers can 'pay it forward' and buy a beer for a veteran who comes into the brewery at a later time. Highly recommend checking it out!

I don't understand the bad reviews. We have been here multiple times and it has always been a positive experience. Everything we tried was tasty, nice variety of sauces, good beer lineup, welcoming staff. Seems like a bunch of people writing negative reviews were frustrated by the prices. Don't go out for BBQ and get mad that it isn't priced like McDonalds. Others complained about "counter style". That's how literally every renowned BBQ joint in Texas, North Carolina, and Tennessee operates. We'll be back!

-WM58wLjtlHlR91xVfM1FQ.review_text:
Please please do NOT GO HERE! First the food was not good at all, had no flavor and the chicken was hardly tasty. Could not eat half of it. It tasted like the chicken was just fried and sauce poured over. I asked for Fried Rice and the Rice was just plain and not the typical Fried Rice and had no Eggs. Imagine Fried Rice with no Eggs?

The food was the least of my concern. Even though I was the only customer in the dining room, the wait staff did not care about what I witnessed at this place. First, there was a young man helping with the utensils and he went behind the bar area and I saw him blow his nose. He did NOT wash his hands. I was quite in disbelief. Then he proceeded to wrap the utensils and he dropped a spoon and picked it right back up and wrapped it. Imagine my shock!!! 

By this time I have had enough and I called the waitress and asked if this young man has a Food Handler's permit. Her response was he did NOT, but she was certified. At this point because of my volume, the young man said he used hand sanitizer after he blew his nose. I was again quite shocked because if you know anything about handling food, you know hand sanitizer will not replace warm water and soap. 

The owner was sitting in the restaurant eating a Jimmy John's sub sandwich and was not even supervising this young man. After my complaint, the owner apologized and gave a weak excuse saying the guy was new. I told him that the practices at his place is going to make people sick and I am concerned. 

Will never visit this place again!!!
The veggie burrito was AWSOME!!! The Mickey pancakes for the kids are a hit. Total hidden gem in Tucson and has the best breakfast :)

We ordered Wings from here as recently as yesterday 2/13/2014, the days before Valentine's. The wings were so good!! They haven't failed us yet. We also ordered their fries, regular fries and the Garlic Parmesan fries. Those house cut fries were huge and cooked to perfection. 

We called in our order over the phone and they got our order 100%. There were no mistakes. I love how they don't over season the Wings and let them speak for themselves. I eat & cook with low Sodium so it was perfect for us. This is a great place to get the best wings in town hands down. I look forward to trying their burger next.

This does Brunch food right! Their approach to food is artisanal, yet classy and planned. The menu is not extensive and it shouldn't be. Their offerings are gourmet food yet simple and hearty. 

I've had their Pork Belly Sandwich, Chef's Omelette, Cronut pastries are out of this world and the best in town, made by Pastry Chefs. I'm not much of a Cocktail drinker, but their Teas and Coffee are excellent. They source their loose-leaf Teas from Maya Teas, an Indian Tea provider.

Recently ate here and had the delicious tofu pie :) everything is great but when I asked for the ingredients I was disappointed to hear they use Margarine in there cooking and the pie also has it. It's a great vegan pie but I would definitely consider using something other than margarine as a ingredient. This is the only reason why I gave 3 stars and except this everything was great!!
Great Coffee and Desserts. The Key Lime Tart was the best!!! We really enjoyed the atmosphere and the star made us feel really comfortable.

Recently ate here and had the delicious Tofu Pie :) Everything is great!! But when I asked for the ingredients I was disappointed to hear they use Margarine as a ingredient. It's a great Vegan Pie, but I would definitely consider using something other than Margarine. This is the only reason why I gave 3 stars and except this everything was great!!

We really love this place! It's in like a warehouse part of town in Tucson. The size of this place is amazing! We thought they didn't serve food, but they have a great food menu. We ordered the Chicken Wings and a whole bunch of other items. The Chips & Salsa are to die for. 

I have not even mentioned the Beer yet. They have a great extensive collection of Arizona Brews and other top brands. We were there with a group of people for an after event party (about 20+ total). The wait staff was excellent and accommodated everyone very well. If you love Beer and great food served hot, then you will love this place!

This Taco Fish restaurant is awesome and amazing at what they do, which is to serve great Fish Tacos! We love coming here and look forward to it all the time, yes- all the time. The fish and Shrimp are fried to PERFECTION in the batter and the Corn Tortillas are fresh local hand made!

 The condiment bar is nice too, allowing t=you to take as much coleslaw, sauce, lime etc as you need. The Soups taste just like home made and fresh. It has that home-made taste to it. Meaning, they spent their time to develop the flavors and taste profile. Oh how I miss the place now that I live in Florida!

While I lived in Tucson, AZ I would look forward to having lunch here at Frank's. I even met Frank a few times.

I simply love the Cheesesteak sandwiches...they are as authentic as they get without being in Philly. They ship the Ambrosia Bread Rolls directly from Philadelphia. C'mon!

Tucson is blessed to have this Chef open his restaurant here. A James Beard award winning taken can only guarantee great food and attention to detail. I love his approach to Pizza! It is the best Pizza outside of New York...this is even gourmet Pizza.

We actually found this great Burger joint restaurant on Yelp while traveling with a group of people (8) through the Tampa area and we decided to drive through Saint Petersburg. The group was drawn to this place because of the Seasoned Fries they promoted and the many reviews.

When we got there we were greeted by a friendly server and our dress were taken with drinks. WOW! When the food came, they looked like works of art!. I've never seen food looked so good before. The Burgers were AWESOME and filling! I could've gotten more Fries, so I just ordered more...lol Oh my gosh, I plan to visit again when I'm in town.

My wife stopped in for Breakfast because we were craving for a nice Bagel Breakfast. I was impressed how the formulate their food compared to their competition. They crack real eggs and cook them fresh!! WOW! Other places heat up their frozen eggs and use pre-cooked products for their Sandwiches. 

Everything was tasty and the Coffee was great! Service was good too, the young man was very warm and inviting.

We were on vacation in St. Petersburg and we got a chance to visit this Tea place located in the Station House. What a beautiful interior! They hand pick their tea's from around the world and their collection of loose teas were impressive.

The Tea House also is part of a co-lab work space. A very impressive fusion of business's to workspace to create an environment for entrepreneur's to thrive.

Coming from Miami, I stopped while on vacation with my family and a cousin (June 2017). We had the last for Doubles, a Trinidadian and Tobago street food. Vegetarians and meat eaters alike enjoy this food. At first we didn't acknowledged by the shop keeper so we sat there till she finished her conversation with her two senior friends. I thought here we again, with our Caribbean shops who have no customer service.

Once she took our order, things got better; she opened up to us once she realized this was our first time at her place. We ordered 8 Doubles! Which took like nearly 20 minutes wait! What? A long time to wait. Mind you, it was about 3p in the afternoon, and no one was there except for the two senior ladies. So not sure what was the wait for; except for making them hand-made and artisanal. Giving them the benefit of the doubt.
 
We also ordered some Roti skins (1 Buss up Shot and 1 Dahl Phouri) to get an idea what they were working with. We took everything home and went in. The Doubles dough was a bit light in the color, meaning less Curry or Turmeric in it. Not a bad thing, just used to a more Yellow dough coming from Miami, with tons of Trini's and Trini shops around. Although, Tara's Roti Shop puts more sauces and filing than in Miami. This is not meant to be a comparison, just an observation. I'm sure Tara is from a region in Trinidad and Tobago where that's how they make their dough for their Doubles.

***I also asked for a Jamaican Beef Patty while I waited the 20 minutes for the Doubles. She forget it, at the end at check she remembered. Bro, I was so hungry I figured I would eat it in the car. Bro, she goes into her Refrigerator and pulls out a Patty to MICROWAVE and give to me. It was so damp and steaming hot; I wish I had never ordered that Patty.

The Roti skins were standard, meaning no surprises, they were good. I would would to visit again to try more of their dishes, like Chicken Roti, Curry Shrimp, and their Bakes! Yum.

This place is amazing! The ambiance, the look, the feel, the design, and spacious. I brought my family here after my cousin recommended this place to us while on vacation (June 2017). I'm sure glad we visited.

Upon arrival, there was a short wait, so we sat down. There is nothing blocking the views so the kitchen and the dining room is well visible. So we people watched for the 7 minutes we waited. Lol

I ordered their Breakfast Sandwich, the wife had their Quinoa dish with a fried Egg, and I ordered their Belgium Waffles. OMG that Waffle was perfect. I mean simply PERFECT. I ordered another Waffle and shared it with them. My Breakfast Egg Sandwich was a bit weak on the eggs though...

Service was excellent, space is clean, portion is adequate, and most importantly food taste great!

When I returned to Miami, I search for locations in my area and found a few in Ft. Lauderdale. Looking forward to it!

While on vacation in Tampa, FL., we stopped by here to try it out. Sometimes the best food offerings comes from little standalone joints like this. The advertised Gyros and Chicken Wings drew us in over other establishments on this restaurant ridden street.

Got in, ordered, and sat down to wait...15 min later the food came and they gave me the wrong Wing order. They did change it to correct it, once they realized they made the error. (It showed my version on the order on their screen...lol) So it was the Cook's fault.

The Gyro meat in the Gyro was cold. Why is the meat of the Gyro COLD? Blows my mind, that you shave the meat from the vertical rotisserie, char it on the grill to wake it up and serve it! Well that did not happen. So I ate it cold. No, I didn't go and complain, because we already shamed them once over the Chicken Wings. And you know....

I would not recommend this place, nor will I return. The only reason for the 2 stars is their Fries were actually half decent. We love Fries. lol

I was really looking forward to eating in an authentic Greek restaurant. I mean we are touring a Greek town, settled by Greek immigrants, selling Greek products. We happen to be in the area while on vacation, and our relative decided to take us to this area.

I ordered the Lamb Shanks with Rice and gravy. The shanks were just mediocre Ok, but not knock my socks off. The Rice was average but the gravy was tasteless. Other members of my party ordered non-Greek inspired food. I was surprised that there were so many American inspired dishes here: for example, my cousin had a grilled chicken with Bacon sandwich and Fries, What? My other cousin had a fried Fish Sandwich and Fries, What? Our guest friend had some Shrimp Linguini thing, What?

I know, you might say, well they have those for the "American Tourists"...well I say, "Are you a Greek restaurant or an American restaurant?"

The place was NOT busy at all, and I had to get up to find the server lady to get my check to pay so we could leave. Wow.

This location was a God sent. We went here nearly every morning for our coffee while visiting some relatives in Tampa. We ordered Americana Coffee and it was always on point. I had coupons everyday and they never made me feel out of place.

That's one of the techniques I use to gauge a place; to see if they still treat customers with dignity and respect when using coupons, or other vendor discounts. Great job guys!!

The seats recline, I mean really recline, eat real food while you watch your movie, sip on alcoholic drinks, and of course pop Popcorn into your mouth. You can do all these things in this movie theatre.

But beware, service is non-existant. Ok let me clarify, ALL the workers there are genuine people, really nice folks; so I'm NOT blaming them at all. There is no system; there is an odd Bar that divides the theatre into two halves.

We had 30 minutes to wait for our showing (The Mummy, Tom Cruise reboot - don't see it) and we needed all of the 30 minutes to get 2 popcorns, a Coffee, and a large Coke. Yes, 30 minutes. Other folks behind left when they say saw this. 

Why didn't we leave? Because we met up with a group of family members whose show started (Wonder Woman). SO we sat at the Bar and waited it out. Again, she was a sweetheart, running around practically doing everything - no system and only 1 worker in the front. The popcorn machine was oddly placed behind a partition wall which was semi-closed.

Then 1 of the guys attempts to bring us some appetizers that the folk a few rows below us ordered. I almost took it because I thought they were...and I got a salty look from the lady. Serves me right! Did I mentioned that the reclining chairs were awesome!?

This was a good experience getting Milk Tea at 8:00pm on a cool Philly Saturday night. We got the tea craving and decided to make a run here 4/7/2021.

A popular place with the young crowd, the place was busy, but the line went fast and soon it was our turn. The employees were young but very attentive. Not overly nice, subdued but seemed they had good work ethic. 

The interior was clean and their brand color scheme was mysterious and mesmerizing: black and yellow. We got our tea within 5 mins of ordering and it was delicious! The Boba was soft and texture was perfect. Definitely deserves 2nd visit.

A near whole in the wall, you will miss it if you blink while following the GPS. You will see a giant ATM machine within 3 steps of entering in. This means "Cash Only" and now electronic currency. 

We almost left but we heard this was voted the 2nd best Ramen shops in town. The dining room was empty, and we were sat down by a male worker working the front. 

The menu is short and simple. Very easy to choose. I chose the Black Pig Ramen and the broth was delicious. Get the extra meat and I got the extra noodles dry, on the side. Yum. Also, you must get the fried chicken and the sauce. You can thank me later.

We loved their Boba tea flavors! Many varieties and options. The boba itself was soft and not chewy. The Milk tea was awesome and not overly sweet. Weekends are extremely busy at night, be prepared for a line out the door!

The interior of the restaurant is very simple and pleasing. There is a lot of space for dining, because they are located on the corner. The 3 display desserts in the west facing window looks so delicious. 

However, we were not a fan of the flavors of the Red Bean in the desserts. I might have been an acquired taste.

-qTtg1D3RidRa4cTB-ftwg.review_text: Thank you for the wonderful Thanksgiving meal!  The best part of the day was no in-laws, but the second best part was our wonderful traditional meal at MB. Felt like home!

These holiday Cinnamon Chip Pancakes are  the bomb!  Seriously!  Unbelievably good. But three was simply my eyes bigger than my stomach. My wife chose the healthier option on avocado toast which is a good stan
Always my favorite healthy choice each day for lunch. No better juice bar anywhere. John and Vui have created a special choice for all of us. No sugar, all fresh.  Al good.
Not just THE best Vietnamese in town, some of the freshest and best food in town. Quick drop in, easy order, fantastic food!
Always good and consistent.  Great having the bar open to the outside now.  Was able to walk in and get bar seating tonight.  WIN!
Thank you for the wonderful Thanksgiving meal!  The best part of the day was no in-laws, but the second best part was our wonderful traditional meal at MB. Felt like home!

Back yet again.  Best brunch in town and an annual favorite for Mothers Day!  Our family knows exactly where we are headed every year. Book early though because of high demand.  Their staging is excellent though and they keep you moving just fine.

Exceptional service, timely/quick, food quality and freshness were great.  Great value too.  Good food, right price. Manager went out of his way to welcome us, check in with us and brought me a granola pancake at no charge to try it out.  Well done!
Has been hot and cold.  Praline bacon was part of what made this place unique.  Bring it back!

Open three years?!?  How have we kissed this place!!?  OMG. DEFINITELY A NEW FAVORITE. We've hit a lot of the new trendy places but damn this food is good.  Each dish we've had has been truly a masterpiece. And we just found out they have brunch in the Weekend's too!  We WILL be back.
Afraid the food quality is dropping.  Fried chicken was under cooked and meatballs over cooked.  But it's still a great place to get into, especially with a group and for social functions.

Much better experience.  Great neighborhood restaurant and bar.  11:30am on Saturday for brunch.  No wait, quick service, good food.  With so many choices around town these days it's nice to have quick access and good food.

We judge breakfast/brunch restaurants in Nashville by their grits and biscuits.  Honeysuckle got both right!  Two thumbs up.  I don't drink but if I did, I reckon this is where I'd come too with their Bloody Mary bar and extensive alcohol lists.  Our god was truly excellent and truly authentic southern.  Well done.
Great neighborhood restaurant and gathering place.  Excellent food, great cocktails, great service.  They even take the shrimp shells off the tails THANK GOD!   I hat when other places leave them on!
Fabulous food!  Creative and flavorful.  Such great choices and the recommendations are spot on.  VERY well organized and we felt very CV19 safe.  Well done!

02H49g16MdRoZKoX6IEoFA.review_text:
I come here almost every Saturday after the gym. Even though they're always packed, the service is fast. The staff are very nice. Majority of the entrées are really good. I normally get the Hai Nam chicken platter or their pho. My wife always gets there pork chop platter. The downside about the Hai Nam chicken is that they only give 4-5 pieces or like a quarter of a chicken. That's not much meat for someone who is close to 200 lbs (need to lose more weight but I'm bulking though).

The prices are cheap. Besides the little bit of Hai Nam chicken and rice platter,  portions for the other dishes (like the pork chop or grilled chicken platter) are good and similar to other pho restaurants in the area.

There are no issues with parking because it's in a plaza so there's a huge parking lot, shared with the Oregon supermarket next door.

The best Cambodian food in Philly.

The service is great.  Only one person, sometimes 2 if you're lucky, waiting on all the tables. The place is small so it's get packed quickly. If you have any questions about anything on the menu,  they will be glad to talk about the entrees.

Best bang for the buck. For the price you pay, there is a lot of food. My wife doesn't normally finish her food but it was so good, she ate all of her Cha Lok-Lak. My wife is Honduran and it was her first time at a Cambodian restaurant and she loved it. I had the Sach-Khoe Ang with Prah-Hok, my favorite. I like my steak medium rare so it was just right. If you guys never had Prah-Hok, you're missing out.

Parking isn't too bad. They don't have a parking lot. But it's in a residential area so you can park anywhere on 6th or on Morris.

Overall, great food but the place is small. If you get there close to their closing time, they'll most likely run out of the good entrees.

I came here for a birthday dinner. We had  a party of 25 people. I never been here before but I drove by it a lot. It's located near FDR Park and the Sports Complex. It's a good size restaurant and they have their own parking lot. If their parking lot is full, you can always park on the street.

Food was good. My wife and I ordered their sampler and mussels for appetizers. I liked the fried calamari and bacon wrapped shrimp the most. I had better crab cakes. My wife enjoyed the mussels. For our entrees, I had the filet trio and my wife got the Lobster Ravioli. The filet was great. One had a little bit of spice, the second one was sweet and the third one was cheesy. The flavors were just right. My wife loved the lobster ravioli.

Service was good. Our servers were friendly, attentive and nice. My water was always refilled without me asking.

I came here on a Sunday evening. We were a party of 7 with 2 babies. The service was good and all the employees were friendly. There's plenty of street parking.

The food in the buffet area were good. It's BYOB so that's a plus. We went a few doors down to grab some beer. The steaks that came out were a little salty. They have a small selection of cuts.

Best bang for the buck compared to other competitors in the area. For the cheap price, overall, the food was good. I would give them more stars if there were more selection of steaks and less on the salt.

This place is close to where I work so it's great for a quick lunch. Their lunch specials are great and cheap. The one I normally get is the one that everyone is raving about, their chicken and yellow rice. Reminds me of Boston Market but better. Some other stuff I tried were their saltado de pollo (chicken sandwich) and their grilled chicken salad. The sandwich and salad are also really good.

Staff are friendly. Service is good. On Fridays,  you wait a little long since they get really busy in the afternoon. They have their own parking lot so there's plenty of parking. 

Overall, great food and service.  If you have never been there before, I definitely recommend it.

I have been going to D & B for awhile now. The atmosphere is nice and it's a good place to hang out for a few beers or play pool. If you have kids, this place can be an option for them. There are games you can play, get tickets and trade the tickets in for items that they have in their shop. The price is a little high but my overall experience wasn't bad.

First off, this place is really spacious. They have a parking lot, which fills up pretty quickly, but there's plenty of parking on the side. Staff are friendly. Out of all their food selection, I like their tater tots, pizza and sliders the most. The upstairs is a game area. When the weather is nice, you can go out to their deck and hang out. In case you are interested...they do not have Heineken or Corona.

I would have to say this is one of my top 3 steakhouses. It felt like I was eating in a library because their decor consisted of bookshelves everywhere. Bathroom is unisex with multiple stalls. Before serving dinner, we were provided with a selection of knives from different countries. All I wanted was just a sharp knife that can get the work done lol, but this was a nice option.

I went here for a birthday dinner. I got the 28 day dry aged ribeye and my wife got the 16 oz. bone-in filet mignon. The ribeye was good and cooked to perfection. My wife said her filet mignon was the best she ever had. So I tried it and I thought it was really good. The filet mignon was rich in flavor, tender, and will definitely make you want more than a 16 oz.

Overall great experience and definitely would go again.

I always have a great experience when I go to this Starbucks. They know my name and the drink I normally get. The place stays clean and the staff are nice. Parking is terrible in the morning. The parking lot is shared with other businesses.
Great place for brunch. Huge portions. Huevos rancheros and eggs benedict are good. Street parking.
You have to try their square pizza. Good food. Fast delivery. I normally order using GrubHub.
Great Hawaiian pizza. A must try. The slices of their 16" pie is large. Everything else is just ok.
If you love Honduran food then you should definitely go eat here. I highly recommend their carne asada, tamales, or pupusa.
They have the best Phnom Penh noodle soup (aka Ka Tieu Phnom Penh). Very flavorful. A good amount of meat. Great staff. Fast service. Good food. Street parking.
Great place for smoothies and teas. I like their Cambo Fire Bomb because it has a spicy kick with mango and pineapple on a stick. Other good drinks are the Forbidden and Enlightenment.
Best spot for burritos in the area. Friendly staff and quick service.

When I go buy groceries at the Oriental Market, I would stop by here. You can park in the lot or street parking. Favorite entrees are the mussels, loc lak, steak and prahok. The sauce for the mussels is flavorful. Since the food is fresh, the wait is a little long but it's worth it.

If you want the best bang for your buck, this is your place. It might not have as many cuts as Fogo or Chima but the cuts still tasted good. You also have the option to pay for food by the pound. The location is BYOB so we brought our bottle of wine.

Ordered online in advance but the food always takes longer than usual. After waiting for a little over an hour, they still messed up the order. No sauces were added to my barbacoa and high protein bowls. I have ordered here in the past and they always got my orders wrong. I do not recommend this location.

This spot did not disappoint. Same great taste, just a different location. I used to drive to Kensington just for pho ga so I'm glad there is a South Philly location. They are usually packed. If you don't have time to wait, just order for takeout. It's the best pho ga in the Philly area. The portions are a good size. Food comes out fast. Glad that they also accept credit cards now too.
This is the worst Burger King. From the time of ordering to picking up the food at the window, it was 40 minutes. If you're in a rush, do not go to this location.

Best dining experience.

Customer service. Before we got to the door, security already had the doors opened for us. The front desk were able to get us in a private booth. One side was clear glass, where we were able to see the chefs cooking.

Staff. Everyone were friendly and very attentive. Our server was knowledgeable about the food and drinks. Always quickly refilled our water when it was low.

Food. I ordered the Australian wagyu filet which was delicious. Cut through like butter and was tender. My wife ordered Chilean sea bass with a crab cake. The crab cake was topped off with hollandaise sauce. The seafood were also good.

Dress code. The website states that business casual is good. Just as long as you do not wear any hats, excessively revealing clothing or workout attire.

Parking. We did valet and it was $31. Request your vehicle 5 minutes before you are done. They are fast.

Minimum spending. I know there is a $100 per person food and beverage minimum, but you will easily spend that on just beverages.

0650daOKAuufqymyOBe3cA.review_text: If you are in a hurry this place is not for you. Thanks to Yelp we found this awesome, laid back, extremely casual place. I loved the shrimp and grits. My husband enjoyed a huge steak sandwich and a beer. One son loved his wings and the other picky son wanted chicken fingers. Even though they were not on the menu the waiter said no problem and my son gobbled up his chicken and fresh cut fries. Free beignets. Yum! The place looks like an old house. The outside bar was a garage. Great place to sit outside with a large group. Look forward to coming back.
Awesome local place. We walked from Hilton. Very casual on the water.T

Great service. Great food. Great view. Live music. Indoor and outdoor sitting. Victoria treated me well on my birthday. I had the Mahi special. Awesome! Kid friendly inside. Loud and happy outside. Fun for everyone. Walked across the street to the pier to watch guys catch fish and enjoy the sunset. Beautiful day.

Great spot in downtown St. Petersburg. We ordered 2 appetizers and didn't need to order dinner. The portions were huge and yummy. The Irish nachos are awesome. Enough for many to share. Great waitress. Awesome cold draft beer. Enjoyed sitting outside watching people go by. Felt very safe. Walked back to hotel that night.
Best service I have ever had at a Walmart. Chris helped us with our list and took us around the store to find each item. Awesome.

This hotel is a great place to stay if you just want to hang at the beach. There is Jimmy B bar right by beach at end of hotel. Great drinks and food. Awesome live music. Beautiful beach. Nice breeze. You don't have to drive anywhere. Eat, drink and be merry. The hotel is nicely renovated. The rooms are comfy, clean and tastefully done. Great service at front desk. Richard and the ladies were Very helpful. Parking can be challenging but they check to make sure you are staying at the hotel before allowing you to park there. Overall great experience.
True Italian. Excellent food. Big portions. Great atmosphere. Quaint location. Smells wonderful when you walk in. Lots of fresh herbs.
Right on the water. Good food and drinks. Great atmosphere. You can watch the boats go by and the birds perch on the dock. Great for all ages. Extremely casual.

This place is awesome. Cheap cover to see excellent live bands in a quaint, Intimate setting. Food is good and reasonable. Wonderful wait staff. Rachel rocks. Brought my teenage kids and they loved it too. We saw Kaleigh Baker and Hannah Harber. Hannah opened the show but she can hold her on. Great band. Harmonized well. Kaleigh's range is crazy good. The bands were so awesome. I would have paid more than the $10 cover. Well worth it.
Enjoyed sitting outside on the patio. The food is excellent and the portions are huge. The bruschetta was yummy. The veal Parmesan was really good too. The happy hour wine was very nice.
Brand new remodeled Taco Bell. Clean and friendly. Great service and the food is priced right.

Took my son here for his 20th birthday. The service, atmosphere and food was great. My 20 year old son got sushi and my 16 year old son got flatbread so there is something for everyone. I enjoyed Sushi and we shared the awesome chocolate fries. They brought out a complimentary birthday dessert for my son that had ice cream and beignets with warm chocolate inside. WOW! Incredible! I DO RECOMMEND making reservations. We had reservations on a Saturday but it was an hour wait for others.

The food was good. The service was good. The entertainment was great. We sat upstairs and enjoy drinks and pizza and salad and live music by Aubryn. The atmosphere and general feel was very friendly and open.
Lots of flavors. Excellent ice cream. Great service. The girl was by herself with a crowd of people but she was pleasant and was working hard. We will be back.
I have been to three different Tupelo Honeys and they never disappoint. Love the food, service and atmosphere. Staff is wonderful.
Always great service, good food and excellent music with the best view, especially at sunset. We come here every time we are in St. Pete Beach. Love it!

06Yz-YYYa1U9PN37b6UniA.review_text:
Friendly staff and the best Cuban sandwich I have ever had.  One of my top stops when I come to Tampa Bay. 
The sauce they make adds a nice zing.  Very good value too.

The gumbo was very good.  The seafood was all fried and very fresh but not exceptional.  The only negative I can offer was serving the food in foam take out containers.  Place was clean and basic.  The staff was very friendly and gave very good service.  Not top of my list but I would go back.

Just got done with my meal.  Decent service from Breanna.  Fun and lively atmosphere. That is where the positive ends.  The clam chowder while hearty was bland and had a strange slick texture I couldn't get used to.  The ayce fish fry was also tasteless and plain.  Not what I would have expected from a busy local place.  More what I would have expected from a very cheap diner.  My most disappointing meal of the 6 months down here.

Stopped by last night with my friends based on other yelp reviews and am sure glad we did.  Nothing fancy atmosphere wise but the food was top of the scale and nice portions at a very reasonable price.  Very authentic.  The strawberry lemonade was homemade and delicious with bits of real strawberry to suck up. Service was spot on and very friendly. Don't pass this place up.

Stopped by tonight by a friend's recommendation and had a very good meal overall.  Typical fish shack atmosphere which I enjoy.  Good service. Drink was always full and never waited for my courses nor were they too fast.  The smoked fish spread was very nice.  Wasn't very impressed with the clam chowder.  Wasn't bad but have had numerous better.  Had the fisherman platter which was great.  Best fried oysters I ever had.  Every thing else was fresh and tasty.  Will be back for sure.

We were looking for something different tonight. Years ago we ate at a fabulous Peruvian restaurant when we were diving in Bonaire and it was so incredible. Best meal of the trip. I happened across this place and was going to be pleased if it was half as good. This was more of a fusion place but all I can say was the food and the service were outstanding. The ceviche mixto which we asked for spicy was a home run and our favorite. The fried mixed seafood was awesome because of the citrus marinated onions to give it a great flavor kick.  The seafood fried rice was very good and a huge portion. Maybe just a little too much sesame oil but would order again.  Our last dish was a very flavorful sliced beef dish over fries and had a nicely flavored spiced gravy. I might have pounded the beef to tenderize it a little. Atmosphere was very comfortable and what you would expect from a nice family owned restaurant.  Service was spot on. Never an empty glass and our server was there often to make sure we were happy. Also he gave great recommendations of what was special. When he was getting orders another server was seamlessly covering.  We will go back for sure and often. A good value too. Check it out for yourself.

Just got back from visiting this restaurant.  As a KCBS judge and pit master up north with lots of years and events under my belt I can say with all honesty this was probably the best BBQ I have had in a restaurant.  It was on par with some of the best I have had at a competition.  The ribs were visually appealing, perfectly rubbed, moist, incredibly tasty and cooked competition style with just a slight pull on the bone.  Tough to do at the end of the night near closing.  The brisket burnt ends were tasty, perfectly done and melt in your mouth with no bitterness.  The pulled pork was tasty, tender, and moist.  The bark was great from the pulled pork.   The brisket was moist, tender, tasty, and perfectly cooked.  My friend likes a little bark on the brisket which this did not have much of but hard to do and not over cook it.  The burnt ends however gave him that so he was very happy.  The baked beans were a 10.  I thought Sonny's had good beans but these were on another scale.  My friend said the cole slaw was very good but I did not personally try it.  The mac n cheese with jalapeno was also a great choice that I had to try.  The BBQ sauces were home made and all very, very good.  The place is small and the staff was great and all were super friendly.  I can tell you from experience most restaurants that compete and win awards either don't serve the same as they compete with or take as much care with what they serve in their restaurants. Not the case here and if it is then it would be something I want to experience.  LeeAnn is the head pit master and is as good as they come. If you want to experience competition level BBQ without having to become a judge then this is the place for you.  Tell them Forrest (Woody) sent you!

Was in the mood for trying a new restaurant and K-Pico did not disappoint in any way. Tried two appetizers. The cod fish and chicarron salmorejo arepas was really unique and delicious.  The sweet and sour chicken cracklings were tasty and well executed though really based on the chefs talents he exhibited on the dinner I had I would challenge him to do more than a out of bottle sauce.  The entree was a special item. I don't usually do those but it was amazing. It was a fresh whole fish that was deep fried whole. A seasoning crust that was perfect. The flesh was moist, flavorful and well presented with the fish wrapped around a fresh and unique tasting salad. On the other side a nice helping of buttery tasting coconut rice.  I hope this dish becomes a regular item. I was really impressed the chef came out several times to make sure I was happy. The service was spot on. Never once had an empty drink glass.  Had a nice pleasant conversation with the owner.  The prices were very reasonable for the quality and portions were good sized. Atmosphere was pleasant.  I wish this new restaurant well and can't wait to return.

Tried the place today and had a chopped pork sandwich, slaw and beans. Outdoor seating or take out. Had a nice portion of pork. Flavor of the pork was not bad but not a lot of smoke flavor or any unique or memorable flavor. Just ok in my book. Slaw was pretty good and the beans again were again just ok. The 2 sauces offered again were just ok. Nothing unique. Prices were reasonable and the counter staff very friendly.  I'm not saying don't go there. Far from it. Just don't expect anything to knock your socks off.

Stopped their on our first day in town. The menu on the website had so many interesting items we wanted to try. When we got there the real printed menu was very different.  After a little discussion we decided to stay. Waitress was Very understanding if we had decided to depart.Very glad we did stay. Had gumbo, fried seafood platter and several other dishes. The server who I don't remember her name but she's been there for 11 years treated us so well and took such good care of us since we decided to stay after the menu issue. The food was very,very good and we would return in a heartbeat. We did speak to the owner about the online menu issue but he has a good following and I don't think he grasped the importance of keeping his on line presence up to date. If it wasn't for the server's initial chat with us we probably would have left. The owner was a really nice gentleman who was fun to talk to. I guess he has a following because of his place being on diners, drive ins and dives. We were not aware of that nor would it have influenced our decision.  Go and enjoy! You won't be sorry. And I'll change to 5 stars when he fixes his online menus.

Moved down to Clearwater a year and a half ago from NY,  But also spent 5 weeks in FLA every year.  Was never able to find a decent pizza until a friend who were also from NY told me of this place.  It has the closest to authentic NY pie and Italian food I have been able to find down here.  The Sicilian pie is the best I have had but being fresh expect an hour for that so order ahead.  The soups are great and very good calamari for an app.  The wait staff are friendly and attentive and they always remember me and what we like as well as my name!  You wont be disappointed. Fairly extensive menu.  Nice, friendly atmosphere.  Decent parking in back.

Basic pizza joint but excellent pizza.  Lived in NY for over 38 years so had a lot of good pies in my years.  In general FL pizza is at best mediocre.  Tony's is one of the few exceptions.  As good as NY pizza.  Many claim that but very few deliver.

Tried the pizza there a few days ago and frankly wasn't impressed. It was mainly the crust that I didn't like. Didn't have the flavor I've grown used to after 38 years in NY. Was kind of flat tasting.  Wasn't the worst I've had down here by far but I'll stick with my two favorite places

OK,first off this review is based on being an experienced 20 year BBQ judge who has his preferences so understand up front I am critical.   I ordered the four meat sampler with my chosen choices being dark meat chicken quarter, pulled pork, St. Louis ribs and an unusual item being their Montreal corned beef.  Sides of potato salad and cole slaw.  My one big thing was the Q was done in Hickory (easy to tell) and they said some apple too.  My two least favorite woods but I will say they did a good job with it.  Not over smoked.  I'm an oak fan or more like an anything but hickory fan, sorry.  Having said that the chicken was a little over cooked and dry.  Dark meat chicken should never be dry.  Nice flavor however.  Pulled pork was good.  Hand pulled and some nice bark and nice rub flavor.  Ribs were over done and fall off the bone but if you like that, great.  Judges look for clean pull but not fall off.  Flavor was very good and a very nice flavor rub.  Not sauced which is also good.  Let the customer choose his sauce.  The two sauces were excellent and I would love the recipes.  The Ancho BBQ was tasty with a little vinegar tang.  The Memphis had some nice pepper notes.  I plan to do a tasting next time of all their sauces.  Will be worth the extra charge to try them.  The Montreal corned beef was really tasty.  Years ago I was told to try it if I ever got the chance when I was in Canada.  I can't vouch for authenticity but I can vouch for it being really good.  I have cooked close to 5000 lbs of regular corned beef in my life for my club and this was cooked perfectly.  The slaw while fresh and nice looking was just not my favorite flavor profile.  Not knocking it at all.  Just not for me,  The potato salad was good. 
Service on the porch was very good.  Didn't go inside so can't comment on the inside or bathrooms.  Lots of fans on the porch making the heat tolerable.  
While my gold standard for restaurant BBQ is LeAnn Whippens Deviled Pig in Tampa, that is a long drive.  So would I go back which in a nutshell is my key? Very much so.  Close to the house, above average BBQ, exceptional sauces, nice seating, very prompt efficient friendly staff.  I would bring friends here anytime and expect it would be a pleasant experience.

Took some friends and went back today for lunch.  Friend had wedge salad with pulled pork upgrade. She enjoyed it very much and a healthy portion of pulled pork. A little pricey though.  Tried the brisket chili and it was excellent. Even better than mine.  Baked beans were also first rate.  Tried spicy ancho sauce and was very good.  Also tried the cajun butter just to taste it . Not really for pork or beef but would be excellent for wings.  Somewhat similar to Frank's wing sauce but with an interesting flavor twist. Brandy gave great service. Never an empty drink.

Second review. Tried the Buffalo wings here and they were as good as the wings in NY.  Lived there for my whole career and believe me they are a food group of their own in NY like pizza. Real Buffalo style not like almost all others down here.  Frank's hot sauce and butter IS buffalo style. Everything else is hot wings.  Good but not buffalo.  Like their pizza it is as good as NY. Great service as always

Tried it for the first time last week.  Very pleased overall. Had a double bacon cheeseburger and it was very good.  Juicy and tasty.  Definitely would order again but also looking forward to the Philly cheesesteak.  Wasn't that fond of the onion rings but that was very much a personal taste thing with the coating that was used. 0xJwTzZuWOac7ufeTioeig.review_text: Best place to eat in Conshy and it's BYOB, so I bring a 6 pack every time I come. I've tried most things on the menu and haven't had anything I would rate less than 4/5. My favorite thing is the carnitas burrito with tomatillo sauce. The tacos are excellent and so is the alambre platter.

I was in search of a good BBQ place because the area is seriously lacking as far as BBQ. I was really relieved when I found this place. You can't really ask for better BBQ in the northeast. So far I've tried their brisket which was tender, ribs which were moist and fall off the bone good, and their rotisserie chicken which was moist and flavorful and surprisingly good for "just chicken" and could hold its own next to anything else on the menu.

The atmosphere is good, but a little small and I wish they served beer, but that's OK since its BYOB. I either bring a 6-pack of homebrew or there's a place you can buy beer from 2 doors down.

The thing that separates a great BBQ joint from an average BBQ place is the quality of the sides. Most BBQ places can serve good ribs, brisket and whatnot, but some of those same places will serve soggy coleslaw, dry cornbread, and bland baked beans. Barbacoa is not one of those places. All of the sides are delicious, especially the mac and cheese, although I'll admit the coleslaw could be slightly better. One time I went they had a weekly special of chili. The friendly staff let me substitute the chili as a side rather than buy a full dinner size serving. Anyway, the chili was some of THE BEST chili I've ever had and was as good as anything else on the menu. Hopefully they make it a permanent item on the menu.

This is a pretty good place. The wings were surprisingly good. I'm a bit critical of the wings I eat and don't really like to settle for dry or bland wings, but Flanigan's were moist and had well-balanced flavor. Also, their burgers and fries are really good and their fish and chips entree is excellent. Some of the other things on the menu can be hit or miss.

The only reason I subtracted a star is because the service can be shady depending on who you get and because they are never stocked as far as a lot of the beer on their menu. Whenever you order a craft beer off their menu, make sure you give the waiter a "back-up" beer because there's a 50/50 chance they won't have the beer you ordered.

This is a pretty good place. Their cheesesteaks and grinders are better than their pizzas. The cheesesteaks and grinders are always hot and fresh. Their pizza crust is not that good through and I think there's too much cheese and not enough sauce. The service here is very friendly and they treat you like family.

This place is pretty solid. I've been there a couple of times and it doesn't disappoint.

I had a chicken cheese steak triple play which is basically a chicken cheese steak with american cheese and a variety of fried peppers. The meat was OK. The thing that surprised me and kind of caught me off guard is the bread the chicken was in. The bread tasted very fresh and was soft as if it was just baked. It wasn't that re-heated or steamed bread type of fresh, but it was soft and fresh as if it had just been baked. I'm not sure if they bake thier own or order it from a bakery, but I'll be going back because of it.

I had a side of their sweet potato fries. The fries were just as good as the cheese steak. They were not that crispy, but they were sprinkled with powdered sugar which tasted great.

One thing I'll say is that I feel like this place's best characteristic is it's creativity. It doesn't have the best meat and cheese, but the variety of toppings and combinations make you want to try everything on their menu.

I never really take the time to review large franchises on yelp because you usually know what to expect when you walk into a subway. This place will be an exception to my usual practice.

I will never go back to this subway. It's pretty difficult to make a bad sandwich but they managed to do just that. I ordered a sammich and wanted sweet peppers on it. The guy scraped a few bits out of the bottom of the bin when it obviously needed to be refilled and just threw them on the sandwich. How could they be so lazy and cheap that they would put a few small chunks of sweet peppers and old stale, floppy green peppers on the sandwich when they needed to replenish the bin. I have a feeling that they would serve another 5 people with those scraps before they would replenish the bins.

On top of that, they supposedly aren't a "participating" subway so they did not accept my coupon. I wouldn't have minded that if they at least made me my sammich right.

I went here during the late afternoon on a weekend and I really liked the place. I've heard it gets crowded at night, so you might want to avoid it at night if you're not into the packed bar crowd. The best thing about this place is the atmosphere. It has really nice decor, with a ton of huge TVs with any soccer game that you want to watch playing. They have a unique set of brews on tap and the food I got was pretty good. I'll definitely be going back.

This place has great food for a decent price. Somehow it really does manage to have a picnic atmosphere even during the bitter cold of winter. The staff is very friendly, the burgers are juicy, but the pulled pork sandwich is a bit salty. 'nuff said.

This is a great place to go with a group of friends. They have really good prices on their beer and food, and the atmosphere is excellent although it can get really crowded on weekend nights. I like to go here around happy hour on weekends when you can still find a table and get a round in on the foosball table. Their sausages are tasty, and their pretzels are hot and fresh. I would highly suggest checking this place out.

This place is kind of strange. Apparently it's more of a breakfast diner during the morning/day, and kind of an Indian restaurant at night? Anyway, I've only been here in the morning for breakfast. Their food is slightly below average for breakfast food. That said, it's not bad since it's really hard to mess up scrambled eggs and pancakes. The reason I gave this place 3 stars is because the three times I've been here, they've messed up our orders every single time. Whenever my group's plates arrive to our table, we find ourselves swapping this and that, so that everyone gets what they ordered. Or sometimes we get completely wrong things and have to wait longer for our orders.

Ordering is confusing, the hours suck, it's kind of expensive for what you get($4 for one taco), and it's cash only. It's also the most authentic best tasting Mexican food in the city. If you like Mexican food at all, visiting this place is a no-brainer.

Service can be hit or miss, and the pizza can be really oily especially if you order one with meat. You can smell the oil as you walk by this place. But the crust is really good, the meatless pizzas are 5/5, and the beer menu is really good.

Went here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon and there was a 15 minute wait. Overall it wasn't worth it. I got the pastrami on rye and although it was well seasoned on the outside, the meat was dry inside, and there was way too much meat on the sandwich so it's like they were going for quantity over quality. With all of the great meats you can find in Philly throughout the Italian and Reading Terminal Market, this sandwich was kind of an insult to Philly's reputation, especially for the price and sub-par service. This was the first time I've ever felt completely ignored by a server at a restaurant which was really insulting. The server only made eye contact with myself twice throughout service. I always tip 20% regardless of service, but this waitress is making me reconsider that standard.

Up until coming here, I had been very "meh" towards cheesesteaks. They were good, but the best 3 roast pork I'd had were better than the best cheesesteak I previously had. That's all changed because Woodrow's is finally doing the cheesesteak justice. The other cheesesteak  places should be embarrased...compared to Woodrow's it's as if they aren't even trying and they're just getting by on the reputation of the Philly Cheesesteak rather than trying to make something that actually tastes good. After my first bite  of Woodrow's whiz whit, I thought wow, this is actually seasoned and isn't just bland rubbery beef covered in bland cheese whiz, who would've thought food could be seasoned??? Woodrow's cheesteak absolutely murders all other cheesesteaks, it's no comparison really. The beef is heavily seasoned, the cherry pepper mayo gives a nice kick, and the truffle cheese whiz actually tastes cheesy and flavorful instead of serving as a moist cover up to dry beef as seen on other cheesesteaks. This is not just the best cheesesteak I've had, it's some of the best food I've ever eaten.
Some of the best pizza you can get in the Philadelphia area. The beer and service can be hit or miss though. Definitely worth visiting overall...it's a cozy spot.

Filthy inside and health inspections repetitively reporting mouse droppings as recently as June 2017. I'd go elsewhere if your looking for a Chinese food fix.

This place have a cafeteria style. Reserved seating is only for 2hrs then after you will be moved to the bar

Our waiter was Kristinna P and she was the worst no one at my table wanted to leave a tip. She seldomly came to check on us my meal was very dry which was the fries soft shell crab sandwich and by time she came and asked if there was anything that I needed my food was cold. So I've heard so much good things about this place and have finally went. 

OMG it was a party in my mouth and tummy it was amazingly good. I highly recommend calling your order in ahead of time due to the wait is long. 

Price was reasonable 

I got the snow crab platter however the guy let me substitute the shrimp for clams. I was also able to intensify the spice. If you don't like spicy food advise you not to intensify the heat.

Was a little disappointed that I didn't receive any sausage with mine in which it came with it.

okay so I came to this location due to my daughter, cousin and I was in the area. The waiter was very nice and pleasant.
However when our drinks came out the glasses were dirty and there were objects floating in the beverages. informed waiter and she apologize and brought us out our drinks in to go cups as we asked. Then when my food came out it was not fresh and hot I didn't informed the waiter due to my food was the only one that was not hot.  probably will not return to this location due to I was not pleased with my food

First thing first they have changed they name to Redlands grill. They food was still amazing.

Went for a birthday luncheon and the waiter Vince was excellent.

The calamari was nice and tender fried to perfection
 
The shrimp was tender also with a nice little kick if you like spicy.

They macaroni and cheese is one of my favorite

I ordered the prime rib cooked medium flashed on the grill. OMG..... it was amazingly tender along with a side of the smash potatoes ummmm party in my tummy...

Dessert was a nice warm large slice of carrot cake

Came here for my friend birthday and the food was great.

Crab Cake La Cajun Caf: made-from-scratch blue lump & claw-meat crab cake, sautéed in butter and served with our rémoulade sauce

Creole Gumbo

Thus place is not your average day to day Americanized taste its good but different i had the curried chicken and waffles the syrup was too sweet for me and the sticky buns were awsome
