I've been to Wilko three times now, all under very different circumstances: a celebratory glass of wine with my best friend, dinner with a group of work colleagues after a conference, and a date with a handsome young man. After each experience, I was totally underwhelmed and left feeling like I'd paid too much (except the date, of course he paid.) 

The atmosphere is odd, with a deli-type counter combined with a couple grocery store-ish beverage refrigerators, Tuscan-looking furniture and menus, and exposed ceiling like an urban warehouse. The tables feel gigantic, and as a petite individual, I felt a bit like Alice in Wonderland during the "shrinking" phase. The corner view of University and Park, however, is a great people-watching location. 

The food is inconsistent in quality. The cheeses are expensive and  not very memorable. I had the mac and cheese for dinner and while I enjoyed the crisped onions on top, the $10 price was a bit ridiculous. My friend had a burger and thought the English muffin style bun was weird and difficult. Maybe they've changed that in the meantime, but the food was never good enough for me to have any inclination to return to Wilko and find out.

Several other reviewers have mentioned the shoddy service and I have to agree with that. The servers seem to be hippies who don't know anything about cheese, wine, or the menu. For such a small place, they take forever to get around to you, and when you first enter it's confusing as to where you're supposed to be (wait for a server? seat yourself?) They really need to put up a sign or something.

One full star has been deducted due to the restroom set-up, where you have to meander through the kitchen area to find the little room. It's awkward and kind of creepy. 

Next time someone invites me to this place, I'm afraid I'm going to have to make a different suggestion--like Pasco just down the street, which gives you the same touch of real class with much better service, food, and prices.

This place is consistently delicious. The pad thai is seriously yum, and the sesame chicken is wonderful. One thing I like about Chopstix (as a spicy food lover) is that if you ask for it extra-spicy, that's the way it arrives, without questioning you with "are you sure about that?" I'm always sure. The food here tastes fresh and healthy, and the portion sizes are very generous--I always end up with a full dinner of leftovers, more to enjoy later!

The atmosphere is relaxed, clean, and well-decorated, and the service is A+, friendly and non-intrusive. It makes me happy that the closest Asian restaurant to my house is also one of the better ones.

I visit this place about once a week with a couple of other tea-loving girlfriends. Upon entering this jewel of a tea shop, you immediately feel calm and relaxed. The decor is lovely and Eastern, and the tea is even better. Every variety of Chinese, Japanese, etc. teas can be found, along with yummy little sweets and snacks and some amazing green tea gelato. I was told on my most recent visit that even the large-crystal sugar is imported from China, so authenticity is a priority here.

The prices are on the high side, ranging from about $3 to $9 for a single pot of tea, but there are plenty of hot water refills and you can taste the absolute quality. From one pot I usually end up drinking -- gosh -- about seven cups!

A wonderful place to sit for a couple hours, unwind, tell secrets, or just enjoy the moment.

I'll start my review with what's great about the Hub: the ice cream. Flavors here are unique, fun, and totally delicious. There are classics like the salted caramel and turtle pie and there are seasonal varieties like pumpkin spice in the fall, and a good selection of sorbets as well. I loved the honey ginger and the blueberry port cheesecake. Ice cream at the Hub is the perfect balance of sweet, flavorful, and not "fake" tasting like anything you would buy in a store. I'll never go to Baskin Robbins for ice cream again as long as The Hub is around.

What's good about the Hub: the décor. No matter where you're sitting, there's something interesting to look at, like upside-down lamps, ropes scaling one wall, exposed brick, rows of colorful bottles behind the bar, and floor-to-ceiling glass windows overlooking Congress Street for some great people-watching. Another nice touch is the tables bent over the long sofa in the bar area, which easily solves the problem of where to put your drink while you're sitting.

What could be improved: the food. I've eaten here several times and was left feeling underwhelmed. Most recently I had the cheeseburger, which is something fairly basic that every restaurant should do decently. While the burger itself was tender and cooked just right, the bun was lackluster and rather spongy/tasteless. The side accessories were a leaf of lettuce, some raw onions, and two very stingy slices of tomato that didn't even cover half of the burger. I've had better cheeseburgers at certain Californian fast food joints. The other food item I've tried at the Hub is the mac and cheese, and it's nothing to write home about. I found it rather bland, more sauce-y than cheese-y. It wasn't terrible, but I didn't feel it was worth the price.

I'll definitely come back to the Hub, but only for the bar and especially for the ice cream. It's perfect for a little after-dinner treat, as long as you eat dinner elsewhere.

So this is a tentative four-star review. Umi Star has a lot of potential and I hope to see it fulfill its niche.

I had the Scottish Salmon roll, and I have to say it was utterly delicious. The fish was cut on the thick side and was of extremely good quality. The cucumber and dill sauce was a great British twist to the sushi idea, which I appreciated being something of an Anglophile. The only problem was there wasn't enough! I'm a small person with a generally small appetite, but only four pieces left me hungry. Make it six pieces of sushi and I'll be there every day.

Other reviewers have noted the prices as being somewhat high, which they are. The quality is worth it, but like I mentioned the portions need to be just a tad more generous. Otherwise I'm afraid cheap n' dirty Tucson will vote no on this promising new restaurant.

I've never had to write a review based on horrendous service/hospitality alone, but I've also never felt so humiliated as I did when I visited Wings Over Broadway for the first time the other night.

I was really looking forward to trying this place since people rave about how good the wings are and the great Tuesday night specials. I was coming from work so I arrived a few minutes after my party. The restaurant was half-empty when I arrived and there was no one waiting in line, so I went to my friends' table where their food had just arrived. That's when I was informed by the waitress that I couldn't sit down.

The manager came over and explained the policy of "no add-ons" to a table, and the waitress offered me one of the (many) empty tables, where I would be "allowed" to sit BY MYSELF, as if I was some kind of pariah. My friends were aghast and we explained that we'd never been to Wings before, and they would never have invited me if they'd known I wouldn't be allowed to join them.

I said I understood the policy for busy nights, and in the future we'd certainly abide by it, but since there was no one waiting for a table it couldn't hurt for me to sit down.

Then the owner came over and very rudely said, "Fine, you can sit down. But you have to pay full price for wings, no special for you." He and the manager were glaring at me, totally unsympathetic. I've never felt so insulted, and never before experienced this sort of treatment from a restaurant. It pretty much ruined my day.

To the owner of Wings: I was the nicely-dressed young lady that you turned away, and I'll be telling everyone I know how you made me feel and to avoid your establishment in the future.

As a consequence of its central downtown location, size, and general appeal, it seems that at least half of my nights out in Tucson start out or end up at Playground. The concept was cool from the start -- quirky decor, swingsets hanging from the ceiling, menus like school notebooks, astroturf on the patio -- and with the now-open roof deck, I can spend many happy social hours here.

The drinks are a little on the pricey side, but there's a good selection of beer on tap and the service is quick. I haven't tried the food since the menu was changed from the cute brown paper "lunch" style snacks, so I look forward to trying their menu items in the near future.

Another fun aspect of Playground is the constant entertainment (makes sense, given the name!) with old movies playing on the big projector on the patio, strange trippy images playing indoors, and oftentimes a DJ on the roof. When the weather is nice, there's nothing better than gathering a big group and hanging out on the large sofas on the patio, and if you run out of things to talk about, there's always great people- and tv-watching.

How can I not give 5 stars to Hotel Congress? This place is the essence of what's good about Tucson. Quirky, hip, historical, a little rough around the ages, a totally random mix of people that somehow ends up working. When in doubt about where to go, the Hotel Congress will have something for you.

The lobby/bar area is full of visual interest, with a cozy little bar area, the staircase with its wrought-iron railings, a couple of comfortable leather sofas with a giant Ouija board table between them. The bartenders here can make you any of the classics with skill. Next door in Tap Room, you can find good conversation with locals and visitors alike, along with some really excellent bar food. The outdoor patio is pleasant, spacious, and has trees. Club Congress, the venue for concerts and events, is likewise full of charm, with a fascinating ironwork thing surrounding the stage where there's always a new or old favorite band playing.

The delicious Cup Café is subject of its own review. Next up for me is to actually stay the night in one of the HC's haunted rooms. (Seeing a ghost will not change the star rating of this review.)

Sullivan's is at the top of my favorite-places-in-Tucson list for three big reasons:

1) The location. I've been to Sully's in other cities, but the one here has a great view of city+western mountains, and the patio is exceedingly pleasant in both summer and winter.

2) The happy hour. The crowd gets younger as it gets later, and there are always friendly regulars. The service can be slow (especially if it's crowded) but they really do try and are good about splitting checks. Drinks (wine for $5, martinis for $6) and food (every dish is $6) are a steal for the quality. Also, there's usually a band.

3) The Knockout. Drinkable, delicious, fresh pineapple infused vodka, perfect for Tucson nights.

Food can be hit and miss, but mostly hit. I love the bleu cheese chips, the gnocchi, and the burger is always a good choice. Go for the happy hour prices, though, otherwise I would say the bar food was overpriced.

In all, this is a classy, friendly place. As long as Sullivan's doesn't change their formula for success on Thursday nights, I'll be there.

There are some things I really like about Lindy's. The location is extremely convenient for when you're wandering around hungry on 4th Ave late at night. Some of the menu items are delicious for the price, comfort food like the famous Mac & Cheese burger (with Kraft!), tator tots, and the yummy Lindy's sauce.

I'm not brave or silly enough to try some the more outrageous burgers, but more power to those who do.

However, the cheese on the cheese fries tastes rather manufactured (some are into that, but not me) and for the love of all that's good, don't order the Hooligan punch, it tastes something unspeakably awful. But really, you should already have done your drinking elsewhere before (or after) eating at Lindy's!

Downtown Kitchen has some of the best food to be found in downtown Tucson. The decor is fun and off-kilter, the service is good and fast and friendly, and there's occasional live music to accompany the cocktails and the food. Oh my gosh, the food. 

I've only ever eaten at the bar -- having a full dinner here is something I'll do very soon -- but even the bar food is exemplary. The lamb's tongue taco is tremendous, never thought I'd say that about lamb OR tongue! And the Downtown burger is divine (I think its the foie gras that gives it that extra oomph) and served on a soft griddle-warmed bun. 

The other awesome thing about DK+C is the reverse happy hour (I believe it's Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays). I'm a night owl anyway, and I'll gladly wait until 10pm to get one of the best deals in the downtown area. 

The cocktails are made well, but for me the star of the bar is actually the non-alcoholic serrano chili soda. It has a sweetly subtle kick that's every bit as yummy as a cocktail.

A star for the lovely patio overlooking St. Phillip's Plaza and the sociable round bar area -- there's always a good option for sitting with a group, a friend, or a date.

A star for the shepherd's pie. If you come here hungry, I definitely recommend it.

A star for the beer selection. They have girl-friendly beers like pear cider and the white chocolate ale, among many others, which makes my life that little bit happier!

A star for the Moscow Mule cocktail, because you get to drink it out of a fun copper cup.

I'm glad Union has worked out many of its early identity issues, and it seems to be moving past "trendy" and settling into a nice niche. The service could be a little friendlier and faster, but overall it's a win.

I hate having to downgrade from two stars to one, but after my latest experience at Wilko, I must.

After several years of staying away, I decided to give Wilko another try with some friends that were meeting for happy hour. Big mistake.

A) There's no happy hour. No specials, not ever. And the cheapest drink on the menu is beer at $6. That would be fine if the food/drinks were something extraordinary (like they are at Scott & Co.) but they're not.

B) The burger is still tiny and served on an English muffin, but this time mine came out RAW. And I do mean red-raw, bit into it and discovered chewy uncooked ground beef. (I'd ordered it medium-well done). The server was totally unapologetic. The manager did send us out some fries while we waited for a new burger to be cooked, but I was really disturbed -- I'm still waiting to see if I get sick from swallowing a small bite of raw ground beef. Gross.

C) The service is as slow and unresponsive as ever. Servers at some restaurants bother you too much, asking if everything's "all right," but Wilko has the opposite problem. Took forever to order, get our food, and settle the bill.

The overall verdict is a downgrade, since Wilko has had plenty of time to iron out their early hiccups and (from reading other reviews) many issues with service, overpriced food, etc. I won't be coming back here for a third chance.

Diablo Burger is new (and yay for new restaurants in downtown Tucson!) and so this is just a first impression. If it were a date, I would only say yes to a second with a little extra convincing.

The idea of locally-sourced, healthy gourmet burgers is fantastic, and there were some big positives to the experience: I thought the fries were delicious and flavorful and herb-y without being overwhelming. I ordered the Diablo House burger medium, and it was cooked just right, accompanied by a generous spread of yummy pesto and a fried egg. The Diablo sauce was really good, too.

However, there are a few things to be aware of. The English muffin bun was WAY too tough on the outside -- every time I tried to take a bite of my sandwich, the burger and fillings slid out the back end. It was a messy, uncomfortable business. Also, the seating set-up is awkward, with every four-person table/bench fixed to the floor. We had a party of 5 (and later 6) and I ended up having to set slightly apart, at the table of the people next to us. They were nice, fortunately! 

The tables probably can't be fixed as easily as the English muffin, but for a $12 burger, I'd like to have it not fall apart. Still, Diablo Burger's philosophy is a good one, they have plenty of gluten-free options, and the fries were darned good. 

Til next time...

Whenever I want a casual-yet-classy atmosphere and a great happy hour, there's no question -- Armitage it is. I've never had a bad glass of wine or a bad meal here. The menu changes often enough to stay fresh and seasonal, but they keep the classics available: the spinach and artichoke dip and the ahi tuna sliders are standouts of deliciousness.

The service is friendly and non-obtrusive, the bartenders are cheerful, and I've noticed a lot of the same faces working here over the years, which to me speaks of a well-run establishment. The ambiance is chatty, relaxed, and with good seating options -- long tables for groups, regular tables, and some too-comfortable huge leather sofas.

Armitage is a wine bar, so the real test is in the wine list, which is stellar and reasonably priced. I've seen the same wines across the street at Fleming's for at least $2 more by the glass. Armitage always chooses a good New Zealand Marlborough region sauvignon blanc by the glass, which I love.

Sundays are a great time to go, as there's live music at 8 and happy hour starting from 4pm onwards... and before you know it, you've been sitting there drinking and talking and eating for hours on end. 

Highly recommended.

The Barrio is a Tucson institution for a reason -- despite its odd location just south of downtown, in the middle of warehouses and railroad tracks, and a little hard to find the first time. But cross the tracks and it's totally worth it! For happy hour or dinner, this place always has a crowd, but not too crowded, and there's a treat every time a train rumbles past.

The microbrew beer is delicious -- I'm a big fan of the Redcat Amber and the Tucson Blonde. My IPA-loving friends tell me that's good, too. The food is pretty standard pub fare, especially the excellent pretzels.

Also: BEST shuffleboard table in Tucson.

This five star review is entirely dedicated to the crab and chorizo pasta dish at Dante's Fire.

There's plenty of other good things to say about this place -- the dimly-lit, "nice dive bar" feel, the yummy cocktails, the fact that it has the name of Dante for this Divine Comedy fan -- but the deliciousness of the pasta overwhelmed even all these solid good marks.

Parpadella Diablo is the seriously the best pasta I've ever had, with hearty pieces of quality crab, perfectly spicy chorizo, and a tomato-based sauce with just enough cream to cut the heat to a pleasant burn. And the pasta itself is delicate, obviously house-made, and light enough that I actually ate the entire dish (and maybe licked the plate...) which is a first for me. 

Thank you, Dante's Fire, for giving me such a delectable taste experience and I look forward to meeting your pasta again very soon!

This is quickly becoming my go-to local place when I'm on the northwest side of Tucson. This town is crowded with sushi places as of late, but Sushi Cortaro keeps it simple with high quality, thickly-sliced nigiri (I always end up ordering "just one more salmon"). Their rolls are also not skimpy on the fish, which I appreciate.

The lunch specials here are excellent, as is the happy hour -- a true half-price list of many of the popular maki and nigiri. And the beer is $2, can't go wrong.

While this is not a fancy place, it's solid in quality for the price, and WAY better than driving twenty minutes for an iffy experience at Foothills Sushi Garden. Recommended.

What a classic. The Shelter never changes, and that's a good thing. High points of this place include:

The indoor smoking patio (heated in winter, air-conditioned in summer) -- I don't smoke, but several of my friends do and it's nice to be able to hang out with them without going outside.

The amazing cocktails -- especially the Caucasian and the Bloody Mary. The bartenders are also knowledgeable and will make you pretty much anything to your taste.

The decor -- I don't think it's changed since the 70s and it's such a throwback, full of vintage conversation pieces. Your eyes will never be bored, whether sitting at the bar or in one of the cozy booths.

Also, I spent the best New Year's Eve of my entire life here, with no cover charge, crowded and happy but not over-crowded, and the usual drink specials and excellent rock music.

In short, The Shelter is the ultimate dive bar with appeal for all.

The B-Line is consistent -- not outstanding but not terrible. Time for a pros and cons list!

The pros: the ambiance is nice, intimate, quiet, and classy, lending itself to good conversation. The crowd is more upscale and older than the rest of 4th Avenue. The food is good -- I've had the steak salad with avocado dressing (my favorite, healthy yet filling), the quesadilla, the fish tacos, all without complaints.

The cons: the menu is rather limited, especially the wine and beer list. Last time I was here, I only saw two wine options, a red and a white. The wait-in-line style of order and pay can create long backups. The food and drinks are also too expensive, especially for the European-bistro-sized portions. A cup of soup for $4.50 better be like liquid heaven, and it's not -- it's just soup.

There's talk about the desserts here but I don't have a sweet tooth myself so I can't speak for them. They look good in their little rotating case, though.

In all, not too bad. A better happy hour, better wine selection, or something more to distinguish itself would bring me back to the B Line for sure.

Sorry Sullivan's, but your Thursday happy hour has become a lot less happy. I remember $5 burgers and glasses of wine, but now everything is $7, including drinks. What also makes me sad is that the portion sizes have reduced drastically -- I used to share the delicious blue cheese chips with a friend or two and not be able to finish them, but now the portion is literally about half of what it used to be. Same with the burger and the tavern steak. It's still good, just not good value.

This is all probably an upper-management decision from higher up the chain than Tucson, but this former regular won't be going to Sullivan's on Thursday night as eagerly anymore.

Subway is Subway, so baseline expectations aren't that high, but this branch is really shoddy in terms of service. One star is deducted for the staff: unfriendly, unprofessional, the girl making my sandwich scratched /wiped her nose while wearing the food prep gloves which was gross, and despite the place being empty i.e. no rush, she forgot to ask if I wanted the sandwich toasted.

Another point deducted because of portion size. I asked for double meat, and she only gave me 50% of normal, and when I pointed this out, she said no that's double. I eat at Subway all the time and it was NOT double. I suspect it was because it was the last slice  in the container and she was too lazy to go open a new one.

Third star deducted because the register card reader didn't work at all and I had to try my card a bunch of times. I don't carry cash so if the card didn't work, what was I supposed to do? It was stressful, and I don't like stress when I'm hungry for a sandwich.

4B9kkFFDjgx7UbE82sQyng.review_text: This lunch was AWESOME!!! We had all you can eat at the bar and it was heavenly!!! I recommend this restaurant!!! I believe out sushi chefs name was kei but can't be for certain but he awesome!!! We told him our dislikes and gave him free reign and we enjoyed everything he made for us. My first time eating mussels and ahi tuna !!! I definitely will be returning! Staff was wonderful and atmosphere was peaceful!! Thank you !! Kopokellis!!!!!!

All I can say is yummy!! My favorite still is the lettuce wraps!! We had Mongolian beef and Singapore(?) street noodles and both were delicious!! Waitstaff were extremly attentive and friendly even it being lunch time. Can't wait to go again!!

Did take out and bf picked up so only based on food itself. 
Good!! First time having it and can't complain. Ordered Shanghai special fried rice, basil chicken with mild sauce and combo chow mein. 
All very good. Fried rice had a fishy ish smell I didn't care for but flavor was good. Basil chicken was excellent and chow mein was done perfectly. Will return again. Want to try their sushi.

Wonderful food and service!! Haley was one of the best waitresses I've ever had!! Can't remember everything we ordered but spinach artichoke dip was amazing!! Had a raspberry martini (or 3 lol) very good but recommend no sugar on rim. Bf has widow maker burger which was done perfectly and had wonderful flavor. I had prime rib with veggies and mashed potatoes and clam chowder. Potatoes and gravy were average but meat and veggies were cooked perfectly with excellent flavor! And clam chowder was extremely good as well. Strawberry cheese cake was to die for and chocolate lava cake too!! Will return for special occasion as it's a bit pricey
Top notch sushi chefs. Say at the bar and had fast service! Pink lady and twister were my favorites. Will be a return customer for sure!! Funky chicken was the best tho!!
Wonderful food. Large portions. Went for breakfast but really wanted lunch after watching and smelling the bbq!
It's ok. Kids like it. Salad bar is decent. Have gone a couple times now  and always part of the dining room has been closed off. In need of a update on the building. And a very thorough cleaning.

Great food but kinda small tables. Like the decor and multiple TVs for the sport channels. A bit on the speedy side but am cheap lol. But worth it. The draft root beer is so good! Steak and mashed potatoes are my favorite.
Best tri tip dip sandwich I've ever had! Meat is so tender. Love this little place! Will be the place to go for Virginia City trips! And no fries but potato salad was great!!!!!
It's ok for a simple meal. Milkshakes are wonderful. Is in need of a update and deep cleaning tho.
Great place! Food was great! Kids burger is very big for a kids meal! I loved the mixed vegetables and I could have mushrooms left out. Half chicken was moist and flavorful.

Absolutely delicious!! Small place but was busy when our party of 3 got there. Could sit at bar, regular table or bar table. Very friendly staff with one new girl who didn't have menu memorized yet. Mango island roll was by far the best. Please try it!!! But everything was delicious!

Nice adult arcade gaming!! We went to get away from kids and was perfect! Wide variety of games and lots of pinball (my fav). Nice to play old school games and have a drink or two! Will be a repeat customer!

I absolutely love the gyros!!! And the tatzikie (sp) sauce!! And they have the best French fries which was unexpected lol. Meat melts in your mouth! We are regulars for sure and recommend them to everyone!!! And the staff are so friendly and patient!!

I regret not taking more pictures of the decor! Beautifully decorated with amazing artwork. Kids and I plus a takeout order was $55. Food was good I had cashew chicken with fried rice and was delicious. Wontons were the bomb!! Liked the house salad with dressing! Will be a repeat customer for sure!

BBQ wings were good. Food took a while to get to us but also had a big order. Nice large tables and plenty of seating. Pizza and fries were very good. The building is in need of a thorough cleaning and updating and no ac or at least it felt like it. Will return but maybe just for takeout.

Went for boyfriends birthday dinner on a Sunday evening. Got seated fairly quickly. The free rolls with cinnamon butter are AMAZING!! The blooming onion was cooked perfectly and enjoyed the sauce that came with it. Took a bit for the food to arrive but they kept us stocked with rolls and we bunches on onion blossom. No complaints with the food, everyone enjoyed their order. Not a complaint but the two in our party didn't care too much for the brown gravy on their mashed potatoes. Plenty of tvs around the bar area to watch the various games. Some areas of the restaurant did have access to the TVs but we got a decent spot. They also offer free peanuts to munch on just about everywhere in the restaurant. Music was a bit loud but so was everyone else!

The food was delicious. The service really sucked tonight. We were being taken to be seated just to turn around twice. Then once we were seated we were ignored until a waiter came to take our order.  I had a box dinner from back of menu. Teriyaki chicken, California roll and tempura. Hubby had shrimp fried rice and crispy chicken. He received both his plates then I had to wait to get mine. Was awkward. Plenty of food for both. My only complaint about mine was they put the salad on the plate with the warm food so salad was warm and crunchy food got soggy soaking up the salad dressing. Was a disappointing experience. If we return I hope experience will be better.

The only complaint about this place in sparks is that it's small!! Otherwise wonderful food, absolutely amazing staff. Love their omelettes!! My go to for sure!  They are large and with the home fries and toast/pancakes it's definitely 2 meals. Writing this is making me want one!! The French toast and the waffles are delicious as well!! Highly recommend this place!! Are repeat customers!

Group of 9. Took awhile to be seated and wasn't that busy, half restaurant empty. Our server Jordan was amazing and is the reason I gave 3 stars instead of one. He took our drink and appetizer orders and we received drinks quickly. Took a bit for the appetizer to arrive. Mozzarella sticks were ok I guess, almost seemed microwaved. Artichoke dip was a little better but nothing to sing about. Took about 45 min to get our food during which Jordan was attentive but not overbearing as some servers can get. Kids were happy with their burger and pizza. Adults were ok with their food except me and the 8 oz steak I ordered. It was raw. I like rare steak but this didn't even have sear marks and was just raw so I sent it back. I requested a new steak since I had cut into the first one. I took it home and as it looked prettier it was still raw and not cooked properly. They were also out of mashed potatoes so I requested bacon Mac n cheese instead and that was good.

We went Christmas Day. Arrived in line about 4pm and got seated at 4:45, we actually thought we would be waiting longer. Staff were very nice and the place seemed to be as well taken care of on such a busy day. With that said, I was not impressed nor was the rest of the family. Before arriving, I was told this was one of the best buffets in Reno but I didn't see it that way, especially for the $45 per person. There didn't seem to be much of a variety of foods, even in each "section". I tried a little bit of most everything and to be honest nothing stood out except for the dessert bar. Dessert bar made it seem almost worth the wait and cost (almost). Plenty of variety!! And cotton candy and chocolate dipped rice crispy treats and strawberry's with your choice of white or (dark?) regular chocolate. 
If you like a lot of seafood then maybe this is the place for you. 
This place just reminded my family and I why we don't care for buffets.

Made a reservation for 5:30pm for our party of 7 with a birthday. Our party was 4 adults and 3 children. Was seated right away with 2 other couples so 11 people total at the table. We got situated and ordered drinks/meals no problem. The cook came out and started the meal and was nice. Young man but we forgot his name. Then went downhill from there. The only thing he got correct for our meals was the shrimp appetizer since everybody ordered shrimp. Other than kids and my bf everyone else didn't get what they ordered. And one of kids got extra food they shouldn't have. The fried rice ended up being over cooked and burned in some parts, my scallops were spotty some undercooked some just right and some over cooked. I had to ask for my lobster because he gave it all to others that didn't order it. The fillet minot was over cooked and chicken was so over done  those of us who received it couldn't eat it. Our birthday boy only got the fried rice, shrimp and veggies when he ordered the same meal I did with shrimp, chicken, lobster, scallops and fillet mignon. His gf got scallops and shouldn't have. 
This was a disappointing experience, especially since we were there over 2 hours. 
For one of the couples, not in our party, this was their first time to ichiban. The rest of us reassured them that this was not a normal occurrence and to try again another time. I doubt they will tho. I will try once more. 
I feel the cook may need a bit more guidance/training. 
We are hoping this was just a one-off occurrence and that the cook was just having an off night. But still am upset that what was supposed to be a good birthday dinner turned very sour.

Nice little place for small venues. Bar seems decent, but I've only had soda and water. They have a separate room for merchandise but very small. Biggest challenge is finding parking. Spirit Animal was very good, have become a new listener. Dorothy was ok, but guitarist Nick Perri was the show stealer!!

Food was delicious! Service kinda sucked. We had 3 different people serve us and one lady seemed like she hated being there. The other 2 were very pleasant. Service was timely. Chimimiechonga big and crispy with plenty of rice, beans and cheese. Kids quesadilla was good and enchiladas just as good. My favorite was the chips and salsa! Large amount and salsas tasted fresh. 
Will be repeat customer.

Have been craving pupusas for a long time and this establishment did not disappoint me!! They have the best horchata in town!! The fish taco was amazing!! Chips were average but the salsa bar was on point! Burrito was good according to bf. Wasn't a fan of the beans. 
Will definitely be back soon!! 
Small place. Bathroom in need of cleaning/fixing up. 1 star removed for that reason.

Did not eat here. Was planning on it but we waited over 15 minutes as it seemed busy but not a single person greeted us even though they walked by us multiple times. We tried to get their attention but was ignored. We understood we probably had to be put on a wait list but to not even be approached or respond to us was frustrating.

Average but Good donuts.  It was also afternoon so selection of donuts was limited. My favorite, apple fritter, was very large and almost a meal in itself. 
3 stars due to employee. Only seen one there and he seemed unhappy to serve/help us. It was our first time there so was asking questions which I guess wasn't helping his mood. 
I don't know if we will return.
Delicious food as always!!! Had flautas lunch special and it was delicious!! Perfect amount as was not hungry but not stuffed when meal was over. Flan is some of the best I've had!! Will be back!!

Very good burgers!! But zucchini fries top everything!! I could make a meal out of them!! 
Burgers always cooked to perfection and most have great flavor. 
Plenty of tv screens with various sports so you never miss a game.

My favorite stop for a quick and tasty breakfast  and or lunch . They have a wide variety of bagels, muffins, and some good espresso coffee  too. Bagel sandwiches are filling and tasty!! First time trying the pumpkin cheesecake muffin and it was amazing!!

4Z2lfaP3d3oOKmEfmc9PCw.review_text: This place is well loved by the locals. It's a taco truck They have great food, outdoor seating and an indoor seating area with A/C. I had the quesadilla with a taco and it was great! On the taco I had lengua, which is a nice option that they offer. The quesadilla is more like a large taco and delicious! Wife had the enchiladas. Combo orders came with a soda. Great food and friendly service. Try this place when in the area.

Delicious! We were in Tucson checking out the local university and this place came highly rated on Yelp. We were not disappointed. I had the Pulled Pork Sandwich (in picture), which was awesome! It came with the cooling coleslaw on the sweet hot meat on a Kaiser Brioche Bun. It came with a side of beer battered fries (small upcharge). Others in my party had some of the tacos and they loved theirs as well. I had a leftover one the next day and it was very good.
We had the fortune of finding this location when it was hosting the local Seahawk "12's" fan group watching the game vs. the Rams (Hawks won, of course). I spoke to a few of the 12's and they said they've been having Hawk parties there for over 10 years. I bought some of their merchandise to support them.
We ate outside in the covered area which was quite large and still socially distanced due to the pandemic. There is also a rooftop area that is in use during the warmer or more crowded months.
Our waitress said she was a Senior at the UofA and gave us some good tips on the area. She was very nice and attentive. Took our picture also. 
Overall, this place is very close to campus and is in a trendy, hip and fun area of Tucson. I highly recommend stopping here when in the area. Thanks for being open during the pandemic!

Messy and good!
We were at the next door Dunkin Donuts and my son noticed this place and had a hankering for some hot chicken so we stopped in here. He and I placed an order and took a sidewalk table while we waited for the food. It was prepared fresh and took about 15-20 minutes as promised.

My son had a 5 piece traditional wings order (Nashville Hot flavor) and I had an order of the Small Buffalo Fries with BBQ sauce. I had the Buffalo Fries upon the employee's recommendation as I've never been here before. She said they were popular. I ate every bite and was stuffed! Very messy and good. My son loved his as well. 

Thanks for being open during the pandemic guys!

We had a wonderful time here when in town visiting the U of A. 
We had the pleasure of having the owner and his brother as our hosts/servers. They were both delightful and super nice. You can tell they love what they do here. 
A friend recommended this place to us for some great Italian food and it was great.
We each had something different (see receipt) and everyone loved their dish. I had the Spaghetti Carbonara which was excellent! Very filling and sprinkled with pieces of lean pancetta. I had to eat the rest the next day as this was very satisfying. 
The owner took the time to speak to the people at the tables and even offered us some chilled homemade Limoncello at the end. It was pretty darned good. 
They offer a selection of Gelato at the front counter that looked very tempting but we were all too full to partake and promised we would return another day for that treat. 
Everyone here practiced social distancing due to the pandemic and there was available outdoor seating if desired. Give this place a try when in the area, you won't be sorry. I definitely will return here another day and will have the gelato then!
Thanks guys for staying open during the pandemic.

I love trying the different Nashville Hot Chicken places around the country. This place has great service with a one man show. Sam took my order, answered the phones, cooked, was my cashier and host.

It was hard to tell if it was open since I didn't see any "open" signs or lights on but you can sure tell it's open by the wonderful aroma of chicken as you walk up to the place. 

I ordered the Combo #1 which is 2 giant tenders served with bread and pickles. I substituted slaw for fries.  Based on a prior review regarding the heat, I ordered mine mild but would've ordered medium if I had to do it again. There was pretty much no heat to the mild version. Great flavor with the breading on the really large tenders, crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. Served with their dipping sauce which was tasty as well. 

I love to support local places so if you agree, give Crazy D's a try next time you're in Reno. Thanks Sam for your great service!

Having just arrived in Reno, I needed a quick beer and some lunch. I Yelped the area for cheap food and the Top Deck at the CalNeva came up. I walked about 3 blocks to get there and through the smelly VERY old casino up several escalators, around hidden corners, up some stairs, around more corners and finally found the Top Deck. For some reason, I thought it would be outside or have a view based on the name. 

Anyways, this place is everything it should be, from the staff, old booths, patrons, and the food. It is definitely old school but in a charming way. Everyone I dealt with was super nice and checked up on me often. I ordered the special "Tuna Melt with fries" (only $5.00!) and a Coors Light (big can, maybe 16 oz only $2.50). This meal also came with soup or salad. I had the salad. What a great deal!

My tuna melt was toasted nicely, lots of tuna and cheese oozy goodness. Fries were hot and average type. Beer was cold and salad good. There were a lot of other options I considered from their menu from breakfast items to steak & eggs or lobster to the Hangover Special (Intriguing - I almost got this one). 

If you want a great deal for some old school type food, give the Top Deck a try. Just plan for an extra 15 minutes to find the place once you enter the doors.

We wanted Mexican food and Yelped it and found Taqueria Juanito's to be one of the top rated ones in this area. We had a great quick meal with awesome service. 

The building is very distinctive looking having been painted a deep purple and a good sized eating area. You place your order at the counter and they give you a number and deliver your food to you after preparing it.

My daughter had a cheese quesadilla, my wife had the beef Barbacoa, and I had the burrito with the rice, beans, etc. The counter person was very friendly and helped describe the items and really had great charisma about him. We also had some Horchata and the Jamica (?) flavored drinks which were very tasty.

I recommend Taqueria Juanito's for any meals when in the area. They also serve breakfast.

There's a lot of choices for frozen treats in the Tucson area. We were dropping off our daughter for school and stayed for a few days. The Screamery was rated highly on Yelp so we stopped here. We each had 2 singles at $4.95 each. The very helpful and nice employee was able to give us 2 smaller scoops in it so we could try different flavors. I had the Whiskey Way (?) and Rough at Sea. My wife had the Coffee Toffee and Rough at Sea. 

While we were there a local news reporter and camera person came by and did a brief interview of the employee. I believe the topic was the outdoor seating options and effectiveness during Covid. 

We really loved our choices and highly recommend the Screamery. There were some very interesting flavor options so it was hard to choose. So glad we were able to get the 2 smaller scoops option. Give this place a try, you won't be sorry.

My first time trying Eegee's. They seem to be a local fast food chain that has been around for awhile. They seem to be known for their Slurpee-type drinks. We drove by one after flying in to town and needed dinner so we went here. 

The drive thru gal was super friendly and helpful and made recommendations for me after I told her it was my first time there. We had the 5 inch grinder, a couple orders of Ranch Bacon Fries and Cheesy Bacon Fries and a couple of Eegee drinks (which are basically Slurpees or Slushies). I can see how popular these drinks are with the high heat in Tucson. 

Overall, everything was pretty good. The sandwich was a bit messy to eat in the car and the Eegee drinks seemed super sweet. The fries were done well and were tasty. 

Thanks for being open during the pandemic and great job hiring your awesome drive through person.

This place is an institution in the right location next to UofA and a great place to try.

We saw the insane college crowd here on Saturday nights and heard the food was good so we went back the next day for lunch. I read that Illegal Pete's started in Colorado and they are spreading around the area. They picked a great location as they are right on the Ave and will get lots of business.

We had the Steak Bowl and the Pork Bowl for our meals. They are similar to Qdoba or Chipotle with the walk through order what you want style. This place is waaayyy better than those two places and really has the right vibe. 

We loved our food, employees were great (even the guy with the Green Bay Packers jersey - Go Hawks!), and great seating options. This place is worth a try when in the area. I will return one day. Thanks guys!

This is a great salad place. They have other items like sandwiches and mac n cheese but the stars of the show are the salads.

You can order what you want manually on a menu or just order one off their menu. They make the items right as you go down the line to pay. Fun to watch them prepping the food. 

I had the Cobb Salad and we all shared a side of Mac & Cheese. Both were super awesome and delicious! I loved the Mac & Cheese served hot in the cast iron skillet and it was very cheesy and tasty. My wife had the Brussels and Bacon Salad and my daughter had a custom salad. 

They lose a star for having a clogged toilet in the men's room. Nasty and very unappetizing, especially with only a single men's room. I told the staff and it took like 10 minutes for a dude to take care of it. Two other customers tried to use the men's bathroom before they fixed it. Sucks.

Everyone loved their food and I hope you guys open a location in the Seattle area soon. I will definitely visit!

We came here on our last night in Tucson with a group of about 11 people. We had just dropped off our kids for UofA and we had a last dinner together. 

The staff and food were wonderful. We all seemed to like our dishes and I tried a few of my tablemate's dishes. All were tasty and done well. I had the chicken pot pie which came with some bread and honey butter. Lots o' starchiness but good comfort food. 

The staff were the highlight as they were patient, friendly and helpful while serving our large group. I especially liked the bouncer guy who checked id's of the kids at our table. He had a great sense of humor. 

This is a good place to try when in the area. Nice atmosphere and a large variety of menu items.

When near the Sonoran Mountains, one must have a Sonoran Hot Dog! I haven't had one of these until now. I Yelped the best rated Sonoran Hot Dogs and El Sinaloense Hot Dog Cart was right up on top so we went there. It is a cart with a shaded seating area in a dusty abandoned lot with plenty of parking available. 

One man working the grill non stop with several coolers and drink dispensers on the side (self serve). The selections are pretty minimum which usually means they do that one thing right. In this case, the Sonoran Hot Dog. 

We each loved our dog and it appeared pretty authentic. Good place to try to support the small businesses and have some great local food.

Yummy smoothies here!

I am visiting this area and while charging my car, I walked around this outdoor mall and discovered Nekter. The idea of a cool refreshing and nutritious beverage sounded great so I had one. 

The nice young lady behind the counter recommended a Banana Berry Burst and I enjoyed this delightful treat. It was tasty and prepared just right. 

I've since seen some of their other locations around town but this is a great location for this sort of business and it seems popular. 

Great to try!

So delicious! When in the desert, a cool treat is a must and the HUB is a great choice. 

The line was long as there was only one person scooping and taking payments. It was worth the wait as the ice cream choices were unique and the tastes were great. The worker had a great attitude and that cannot be easy with the never-ending line. 

Great place to try for ice cream.

I found this place on Uber eats, I usually order Marinas until they can't read my request on uber order nor did they even care when I called so I tried Enzo. Pricing is great for children's meals as well! Large portions & fresh caprese which I appreciate. Try this west chase cuisine! I'm a fan 4sure

I order delivery from this location every week. It's always fresh & delish! The most reliable pizza place in the area thus far . I prefer their delivery opposed to uber eats delivery.

Plus it was their treat so I didn't want to be greedy :) we didn't make it to the dessert room since I could barely finish the courses. The ambiance was classy, quite sophisticated. Here's what I do know: they have crazy drink specials that are sure to get you wasted and on the dance floor for the rest of the night. That's where I'll be.

I went here for dinner for my friend's birthday a few weeks ago and loved it. I've been to Silk numerous times for Mo Money No Problems on Thursday nights, and ate here when it was a gritty late-night diner but this was my first time eating at the facelift version. It was sooo good. I don't know if it was the relaxed atmosphere of sitting outside in the beer garden, or if the food was really that delicious. We all decided to split a few appetizers. The baked mac and cheese with the garlicky crust and I seriously had a food orgasm while eating it.  I usually don't even order mac & cheese out, I'm more of a mom's homemade type of girl but I am so glad I did. 
I don't remember  what else we ate, but it was all bangin'. I'm definitely coming here for dinner again.
Tuscany is my jam. You can pretty much find me here getting my iced coffee refilled everyday in the summer. I've never had the food here, but it always looks good.

I came here with my dad on Father's day under the assumption that I liked the food here. I guess I was thinking about another place because I really did not enjoy it. The menu they have here is just  way too large so I felt overwhelmed with choices. Seriously, you guys don't need six pages of options. I decided on a noodle dish that was supposed to be filled with garlic and hot spices. I really like spicey dishes so I  was pretty excited for my food to come. But what I got just tasted weird. It had no garlic. It had no spice. It was just odd and there were tons of mushrooms (which I hate, and did not see listed in the description). I'm still convinced that my order was mixed up. On a good note, I had the samosas as an appetizer and they were surprisingly tasty. They just aren't reason enough to come back.

I LOVE TAMPOPO. I could pretty much go here whenever, except the hours are pretty weird. Do not come here at like 4pm. It will be closed. i would take away a star because of that, but I really just love the food too much. I always get the hot and spicy chicken rice bowl and I wish the bowl was never ending so I could eat it forever. My friend loves the spicy salmon rolls and gets those every time too. Tampopo is casual, fast and cheap. The 21st street location is small but the one by Jeweler's row is a lot bigger so you can pretty much sit anywhere. The food is just as good at that location. Mmm, I could go for some right now.

I came here for breakfast last Sunday with a co-worker since we were working an event at the Piazza. I used the bathroom here a few weeks ago when ?uestlove was DJ'ing and noticed how cute the place was and how good the food looked, so when we got hungry I immediately suggested we go here. The place wasn't packed but we decided to sit at the counter since we couldn't really dilly-dally. Service was very attentive and multiple waiters came often to refill our cups of coffee and waters and ask if we needed anything. They were also very friendly and suggested what was good on the menu. I ordered blueberry and banana pancakes with a side of bacon. I love when places give you a few strips of bacon and Darling's gave me like five. Very much appreciated. And the pancakes! They were HUGE! I could only eat one of the three and gave the rest to my friend. He ordered a chocolate chip waffle and scarfed it down in minutes. It looked delicious. When we got the bill, I was very pleased to see that it was pretty cheap, as breakfast should be.
I will definitely come back to try out the lunch menu. 
Oh! And this place is famous for their cheesecake. They had a wonderful looking display case of all the different varieties.

For the past week, I have seriously been craving a gelati from John's. And while yes, I could really go anywhere and get one I am holding out until I feel like walking the few blocks to get one. Becasue really, John's is the best. There' s none of that Dairy Queen or Rita's nonsense going on here, you can't add bits of candy to your water ice or make it into a "Blendini" (what the fuck is that, anyway?). John's is no muss no fuss just delicious home-made water ice. Anyone wanna walk over with me?

So...I worked here for three years during my high school days. And I hate that I know the goings on behind the scene. The bagels are sooo DELICIOUS and when they are fresh from the oven there is simply nothing better. But...this place has it's fair share of problems. The staff is usually incompetent (trust me, I'm pretty sure I lost a lot of brain cells working with some of them) and the manager will talk your head off, or flirt with you if you're female. But the main issue with the bagel place is that it is dirty. Like, extremely, extremely gross. In every nook and cranny there is mysterious gunk or crumbs, dirt and dust.  It was always such a constant battle...Do I pretend like I don't know what things look like behind the counter and just eat a warm and soft everything bagel toasted with BLT? (I'm not a cream cheese type of girl but last time I checked, we had something like 17 different varieties, sometimes a bit excessive as the honey-mustard flavor was always left untouched.) Even now I still get the cravings for a bagel sammy from here but I just can't do it.  I  wish management could get their shit together and just clean the joint. I mean, it's not that hard!!
And when they finally do, I'll be the first in line for the ridiculously cheap baker's dozen but I won't hold my breath.

I went to the original Cafe Spice in Olde City with my family for dinner one night. We were roaming the area and got hungry and since we all love Indian food we went there. It was honestly the best Indian food I have ever had. And this was like over five years ago. The only problem, Indian is not supposed to be expensive!!! I mean, the places by Penn are so much more reasonable, although they lack the luxurious ambience. 
But anyway, Cafe Spice Express is like the best of both worlds. I can get my delicious, most favorite foods in the entire world, Vegetable Samosas, and a side of garlic Naan (mm fresh from the oven and filled with flavorful bits of garlic...) for a reasonable price.
 I haven't ever had any of the entrees from here, but I am sure they are just as tasty. My favorite part of the Express is the location. After a day of roaming around or shopping with friends we can go to the food court at Liberty and all find something we like to eat. I will always, of course, choose Cafe Spice.

OH! Totally forgot-- Now Whole Foods carries Cafe Spice samosas to go! And I got some today and they were pretty tasty. Not as good as fresh from the restaurant but definitely an upgrade from the ones they were carrying before.

The first time I went to Continental I was probably around fourteen and had no idea who Stephen Starr was. I don't even remember why my friends and I decided to come here, but once our Starr cherry was popped, we were hooked. When everyone else our age was going to Applebee's and eating chicken fingers, we were coming here and other Starr joints thinking that we were the shit. 
For a while, this was my favorite restaurant and it was really just because of the atmosphere. Starr definitely knows how to decorate a joint and I remember being in awe of all the different features of Continental: the swing chairs, the pit seating area, the two way mirror in the bathroom etc etc etc! They were things I never thought would be in a restaurant. Of course, I was fourteen and up until then my dining experiences were the decisions of my parents, but I mean, the restaurant is still cool and classy.
Last summer was the first time I came here for drinks and I probably never will again. Continental attracts a certain crowd that my friend and I did not fit in with. My scene does not usually include post frat boys and high-powered execs. plus, the drinks are not cheap and the music was not good. I would've felt uncomfortable dancing anyway.
From now on, my trips to Conti remain solely for the food. I love the Continental House salad, sans feta, and the thai chicken lettuce bowl. I'm pretty sure they changed the menu last time I was there so I don't remember what else I like. The bite size desserts are forreal bangin' and I am a dessert fiend. 
The Continental is not for everyone, it definitely attracts a certain crowd. Unfortunately, I am not a part of that crowd.

I came here last week to meet up with my friend. I was pretty tipsy when I got there so my overall experience was pretty hazy. Neither of us ordered any food besides some chips and salsa and seriously it was the best salsa I have ever had, especially the salsa verde. Of course, it could have been just the alcohol telling me it was the best salsa but I really was enjoying myself eating the chips. My date wasn't as amused with the salsa which was fine, more for me!
This review is pretty bad, I know, but I'll definitely be coming back soon and actually eat the food.

GAY PIZZA! I did not know this was called 13th St Pizza...I didn't know this place even had a name. Whatever, that doesn't matter to me. This is the coolest and creepiest place ever.  Coolest because they are open late and have sooo many different types of pie. I stick with the classic and it never fails me. Creepy because of the location...13th street at 2am is not really my favorite place to be but it adds character and a little excitement. And where else in town can you buy a slice of pizza, a pack of condoms and chat it up with some of the most interesting people in town while waiting?? I'm gonna go with nowhere besides here.

I don't think I can express my love for TJ's enough. I am a pretty picky eater and I hate cooking. If I can find something delicious that will be ready in 15 minutes, I'm sold! And grocery shopping at Trader Joe's is the mecca of easy to prepare, cheap, delicious food. It's definitely more college budget friendly than it's main competitor, Whole Foods.  My favorite items are the Shu Mai, Gyoza, samosas, and other Indian entrees. The best thing about all of these is that they are not loaded with calories and fat and they actually fill you up. TJ's is definitely doing something right and I wish they had a location that was a little bit larger (the one on Market is just waaayyy too small and the store and parking lot are both always packed, just proving how much the city loves the store) and a little bit closer. Hopefully Trader Joe's will expand within the city,

The first time I went to Vesuvio it had just opened and was at the time just another run of the mill Italian restaurant in South Philly. My family and I came here with pretty average expectations. Since it was a really long time ago, I really only remember two things about it. The mashed potatoes were soo good and my sister ordered something in parchment paper and I thought it was weird. (I was like ten...?). 
Anyway, I hadn't given Vesuvio another thought until recently when my friend got a job as the doorman and told me I should visit him at work sometime. The place is seriously two blocks away so I took him up on his offer and came early one Saturday night with two of my girlfriends. We were going to a party later and thought this could be a good place to pregame. Wrong. When we got there it seemed like it was a good time- some good ol rock n roll playing in the background and tons of bike messangers (shh..I have a not so secret soft spot for them) Seriously, TONS. The three of us girls felt so out of place ( we were not only the only girls in the bar but the only ones without messanger bags, too). It seemed like we were crashing someone's private party. At least the bartenders were friendly. I ordered a vodka tonic and it was $7. I thought that was a bit steep, or maybe the places I usually go to always have cheaper drinks? Well regardless, after my first I switched to beer since my wallet these days is not exactly the thickest.
After our second round we were told that there is a dance floor upstairs and immediately needed to check it out. A ha! So that's where everyone was going off to! When we went up, there was a DJ spinning and people around, but no one was dancing. My friends and I looked at each other in confusion and then decided after our pints we were outta there.
I'm sure this place is a lot more fun later in the night and it seems to be getting a lot more attention these days so maybe I'll come back at a more appropriate time.

UPDATE: Shut down over the weekend because of serving minors.

My friends live next door to the Institute and that's really the only reason why we go here. We know the owner, the bartenders, the DJs, and the doorman so it's always comfortable and friendly. It's a very chill bar and whenever we go, we know that we will run into other friends or sit at one of the tables by the window and motion for other neighbors to come in and have a drink with us. It's a true locals bar and on nights when there's really nothing to do, we'll come here and  it's like having the whole bar to yourselves. The prices are right, the selection is good and they even have a whiskey bar upstairs which is also conveniently located next to the dance floor. Come out for Solid Good Times every Saturday!

If you are under 21 in this city and need a spot to drink, go to Oscar's as you are most likely to never get carded. 
Now, besides that, Oscar's is the epitome of  a dive bar. You can smoke inside, play your favorite songs on the jukebox (3 for a dollar), the beer is ridiculously cheap and served in ginormous glasses,  and eat greasy bar food. It's wonderful. The service is pretty good even though the place is always busy, no matter the day of the week. I've been here with three other people and I've also been here with thirteen others and somehow we always manage to get  a table and have a great time. It's the perfect place to pregame.

The cupcakes always have a decorative ring on the top that goes along with whatever holiday or season it is. My favorite is the halloween jack o lantern rings. I eat the cupcake in it's entirety, then lick the remaining icing off of the pumpkin and then stick it on my ring finger like I just got engaged. 
I used to look forward to any holiday or birthday celebration cause the cakes and pies would always come from here. And I knew that if I took the short walk with my mom, I'd get the cupcake and the ring.

I LOVE SUPERIOR MEATBALLS! And I am not a meatball girl by any means but these are seriously soooooo gooood. We always have a bag of them in the freezer and no spaghetti night at my house is complete without them. I like to have two in my bowl. They also make bangin' Marinara gravy- not too salty, and not too sweet, just the way I like it.

I came here for the first time last summer and I was afraid of falafel. I'll admit it, I was young and stupid. And while I still am probably both of those things, I can now safely say that I am a fan of Maoz. On my first visit I was disappointed to find that it was vegetarian as I like to have some chicken in my sandwiches, especially since at the time I was afraid of those mysterious falafel balls. So I just had a pita with hummus and some of the delicious fixins they have (although nothing can compare to my beloved and departed, Pita Pocket.  It came with fries which surprised and delighted me at the same time. The fres were exactly the way I like them, crispy, but not  burnt , and salty. i was completely satisfied with my first visit.
The second time however, I felt a little more brave and adventurous. Since I tried falafel at a few other places in the year it had been since my first visit, I went ahead and tried them here. I loved them. The falafel was definitely the missing link from my first trip and they added so much more to the sandwich. I couldn't finish it, I was so full! And I only ordered half! i left completely satisfied and I am in fact getting ready to go there for a late night bite!

I totally forgot to mention the staff here! I don't remember much about the employees the first time, but on my next visit they were hilarious! The two guys were really friendly and probably high, which just added to my dining experience. I think they were planning their weekend acid trips and while  typical customers may be offended to overhear this, I don't think anyone who frequents Maoz would mind.

Ehh...this place kinda sucks. The people who go here totally suck (I felt soo out of place. Next time I'll wear boat shoes and a cardigan) and the service is worse. Well actually, no. The service didn't seem bad for the other people having brunch this morning, but my friend and I were completely ignored. We were served our waters in plastic cups while everyone else in the place had normal glasses. I am not at a barbeque, give me a real cup. We waited for like 15 minutes to even get our menus, despite the place being pretty empty. When we finally got them there were only seven or eight things to choose from. Being the horribly picky eater I am,  I was stuck to choose between French Toast, Wings, or Nachos ( I hate eggs so was not a fan of the omelette heavy menu ).  Umm..well since I just woke up I guess I'll get have to get the French Toast. My friend got a Filet Mignon Cheesesteak (I don't really know why, but hey, his meal). 
We waited for a really long time to get our food and saw couples who came in after us already eating theirs, again we were completely ignored. I kept thinking, okay yes,  this place sucks but maybe the food is going to be great. Nope. It was just average. The French Toast could have been good but it was just way too sweet and I totally regret eating it now. The bread on my friend's cheesesteak was so hard he could barely bite into it. 
  After waiting for the check for what seemed to be forever, we finally added in our heads and left cash on the table. Yeah, we were in that much of a hurry to get out of there.
Needless to say I will never come back to Ten Stone. We should have just gone to the Oregon Diner with the rest of hungover Philadelphia.
Oh, and they were playing all Dave Matthews music. Vomit.

I like this place for one reason..it just needs some love. It's always emptyExcept for some old dude just lurking in a booth eating his pizza. There's always one of those! And he's always listening to our conversations. I love it. !The Spot is around the corner from my friends house and we like to hang out here sometimes when we wanna pig out and be really lame. 
Umm...chicken fingers are banging. I will always love the Spot. And it's called The Spot! Who doesn't love that?!

I'm not going to write about the food. It's pretty standard and it's good. I always order from here. 
What i do want to write about is the experience eating here. It's awesome because you will always have the place to yourself. Seriously, inside Rich City is a ghost town and it's a shame because the place is actually nice inside. It's not like going into No. 1 Chinese Food only a few blocks away (where my dad, for some reason, loves to get his take out) where the place is dirty and sticky. Rich City is a decent spot. 
I used to come here all the time with my friends and eat dinner inside. The service is friendly and quick, but they never rush you out the door.   Bonus points for the most random music selection ever. Celine Dion? Michael Jackson? Awesome and authentic background music!

I have two pieces of advice when it comes to the Jamaican Jerk Hut: 
1. Do not come with people who are starving and grumpy. They will become a huge annoyance to you and everyone else in your party if you come here.
 The thing about JJH is that the service is slooowww. It's no secret. You will be here for a very, very long time. You will feel ignored. You will be on the verge of tears by the time you order.  Bring a snack. Or eat before you come and then by the time your food has actually arrived you won't be tearing out your hair in hunger and confusion. Trust me, I've been there. 
2. Expect to spend a lot more money than you think. 
When I first walked by this place I thought it would be a great spot to host the birthday dinner of one of my friends. We could sit outside, listen to free live music and eat some good, cheap Jamaican food. The only true thing about that previous statement was the eating al fresco. Because there was music we had to pay an entertainment fee even though the band played for a very small portion of the time we were there (which was a pretty long time). There's also a corkage fee if you bring your own alcohol. Uhh...what? And the food...it ain't cheap. It was good though. I got the classic chicken curry and it was seriously phenomenal. And there was some spicy salad my friend ordered and that was bangin, too.

I wish I had known these things before I went, I would have enjoyed my time there soo much more. I'll probably go again but I definitely will eat something beforehand.

When you're hungry at 2AM and you happen to be in South Philly, or you have quick access to a car, bike, shoes, scooter...COME AND GET A WARM PRETZEL. They are delicious and you can pay for one with probably the amount of change you have in your pocket right now. I don't remember exactly how much they cost because well, I've never been here sober, which is so sad since I can practically spit on the factory from my house. 
There's another location in SP too where my sister and I went to after a house party and the guy just gave us the pretzels for free. It made my night. 
There is nothing bad to say about the Pretzel Co. And if you have something bad to say, you're just crazy.

This is another place that I will never understand the hype surrounding it. The food is good but  i don't know why it draws such insane crowds every weekend. I mean hello, there are other places in the city to get your brunch on. Stop coming here to my block and parking like jerks! 
Annnyyywaayyy, onto the food. This place declares itself as a "finer diner". It's fancy and it's kinda expensive, two things diners really shouldn't be. I like a diner where the waitress smacks her gum and calls me "hun".
But I do like the pancakes with the fresh blueberries and stawberries. The maple syrup is delicious, none of that Aunt Jemima "pancake syrup" nonsense. I like eating a shortstack of pancakes and not feeling like I'm going to die of fullness and regret. I never get those feelings when eating the pancakes at Sam's. 
Everything else to me is just kinda blah. People seem to love the ketchup here but in all of my experiences eating at Sam's I find that it really doesn't taste like anything. 
The Morning Glory really to me, just does not live up to the hype. I would not drive all the way from Jersey or the suburbs to wait half an hour to eat mediocre food. But hey, that's just me.

I met up with my friend and her boyfriend (third wheeling, I know) last Friday night for dinner downtown. And of course, it  was up to me to choose the restaurant. For the record- I hate making decisions. And especially when it comes to restaurants downtown since the only place that I can ever come up with is the consistently mediocre food from Marathon Grill. Bleh- no mood for settling for that tonight. Soo, I made a mental list of all the places we could go downtown and voila! I remembered how much my parents raved about La Viola and called information to reserve a table. Since it is BYOB, we stopped by the Wine and Spirits and picked up two bottles of vino. By the time we got to the restaurant, our table was ready for us.
One problem...this place is small. It's really just a rectangular room jam packed with tables, family style. Not only was I third wheeling this date, I was also the third wheel of the random couple sitting inches away from us at the same table. Talk about awkward. The girl on that date did not look pleased when we were seated, clearly ruining their romantic evening. Oh well. La Viola is so not the place to go for a quiet, intimate date. The place is way too loud I could barely hear what my friend was saying and we were practically sitting on top of each other. I don't like eating when I can even hear myself think. Another note: I felt really out of place. The other patrons were business executive types dressed up for a night on the town.  I described the restaurant later to my friend "like going out in Olde City, only with food". Not my scene, but what do I really expect on a Friday night at 16th and Locust?
Anyway on to the food. The menu is pretty limited, a few appetizers, some pasta dishes (a lot of which had seafood in them...disappointment), and some meat entrees as well. I opted for the orecchiette pasta with mushrooms, plum tomatoes, and sausage. There may have been one other ingredient but it was delicious, nonetheless. My friend ordered a pasta dish with salmon and her boyfriend got the veal. They enjoyed their meals as well. 
I just don't know if i will make a second trip to La Viola. The menu is too limited for my picky tastes and it was way too loud. If I do, I'll make sure to go on a nice night so I escape the noise and sit outside.

I finally got my water ice fix this weekend. Well actually, I kind of went twice, ssshh. The chocolate-cherry gelati was seriously orgasmic. Why did it take me until August to finally make it down there??! I will definitely be back a few more times while they are still open for the season. And if you haven't been, GO! I corrupted not one, but two Rita's fans this weekend.

This is my go to pizza place when I am in the Rittenhouse area. It's just consistently good pizza. I wouldn't say the best pizza in the world by any means, but if you are craving a slice this is the place to go. Lunchtime can get pretty hectic. I went in yesterday and some old man tried to school me and say I was in the wrong line. Hey buddy, why don't you worry about your own order, eh? I'm a regular. I know how the place works.

It's a well known fact that I am notoriously picky. And the 4 stars Im giving Audrey Claire is not because I love the food so much. The menu and I have a pretty rocky relationship. It wants me to like it but the things it's offering are just a little too weird for my taste buds. However, I have had really good food here, even if it wasn't the most exciting thing on the menu. The 4 stars is for the service and attractiveness of the waiters. Here's the story: My best friend's family lives around the corner from AC and they are Sunday night regulars  so I've been here on multiple occasions. One visit, a waiter (who wasn't even serving our table) noticed that I was the only one not indulging in any appetizers and he brought me over a bowl of Mushroom soup hoping that even the pickiest of eaters would try and like it. I tried my friends, but only because he  was cute. I then passed the soup over to my friend's dad and just waited for my pasta dish to come out. 
But seriously, how attentive and nice is that?!  A complimentary bowl of soup (and the food is not cheap here)? Where else in the city would that happen??
 Also it's BYO which is always nice.

Cake makes desserts. Bangin' delicious desserts. They also serve real food too and it's just as good as the baked goods. The french toast at Cake on a Sunday morning with a delicious hot cup of coffee makes me wish I lived in Chestnut Hill. 
The only reason why i know about this place is because my good friend/formerroommate has been working the counter for almost 4 years. On thursday nights, when they serve dinner, she would bring home a box of extra goodies after work. MMM what is better than a free cupcake? Or a ridiculously rich and decadent chocolate tart? Oh man, i miss those nights.

I have nothing negative to say about Wawa. And if you do, please don't even think of speaking to me. 
Here are my favorite Wawa staples:
MAC AND CHEESE. sorry, just had to get that out of the way early. 
Wawa ice cream.
Shortie Hoagies and the touch screen menu, in general.
I also love the smell of Wawa. What is that smell and why is it so inviting?

7-11...you ain't got shit on Wawa.

I don't feel like writing a crazy long review so I'll keep it straight and to the point. I had a dream about the chicken burrito I had there last night. I wish I was still asleep because it was so perfect- filling but not in that gross, instant stomach-ache way, and it made me wish I could eat the rest. I should have just taken it home to treat my drunken appetite, but I was clearly not thinking ahead. The jalapeno mac and cheese we ordered was also really good. I love coming to ECR.
I learned something when I visited Yogurino the other day. I do not like plain yogurt. With that said, I will not be back.

I was at the Piazza yesterday for the magazine's release party and saw a few of my friends at Swift Half. I went over, beer in hand and sat down with them. I realize that I am technically not allowed to walk around with a tall boy can in plain sight, but it was a party and no one seemed to mind. Except when I came over to say hello to a group sitting outside and put my can on the table. A waitress quickly walked by and picked it up with a blunt 'you can't have that here" and walked inside with it.
I know I was breaking the rules but come on, you could have just asked me to leave. 
i have had good experiences here, but that just made me a little sad.

I really like the Pope and I've been coming here at least once a week for the past month. Since my friend is a regular here our service is always friendly and attentive. We hadn't even been inside for a minute and already one of the bartenders made eye contact with my friend and quickly got our order.  Another bartender came by later and asked him why he wasn't drinking his usual brew. i like coming here with him because I know we'll be taken care of. Other reviewers have complained about surly service, but it's a locals bar in South Philly, come on what do you really expect? 
Also, they have delicious fries. That's all I've tried but I'm sure one of these days I'll order something and be just as satisfied. 
Aaannndd the jukebox has something for everyone. 
I really like it here.

I crave burritos on the reg. A few weeks ago, my mom and I ordered some from El Jarocho after doing a little neighborhood burrito web browsing. I ordered the food, which was a little difficult with a language barrier but they got the order just right, two chicken burritos, no sour cream or cheese. The burritos arrived within fifteen minutes and they were HUGE. Delicious, warm and home-made, just the way I like it. I loved the way the beans were mashed up inside, and the chicken was cut up in little pieces so I wouldn't have to worry about choking. The salsa verde, which I have recently discovered a love for, was fresh and tasty. Just enough zest. They give you extra lettuce and pico de gallo to add in, which I most certainly did.
We scarfed these bad boys probably a little too fast and got a little bit of  a stomachache, but it was well worth it. 
i even ordered another one yesterday and it was just as scrumptous.
