"i've been craving pad thai for two months. it's like I'm pregnant with a monk's baby" were the words of my friend when we were trying to figure out what to order for dinner. After hearing this statement there was no way I could deprive her of her beloved pad thai, but I ran into a dilemma. Where do I order it from? I'm not a huge fan of Thai food so I was clueless. She suggested we use Grubhub.com to find a place that delivers and OMG this site is amazing to find delivery in you area. Every cuisine and every place that delivers in your area! We chose Smile Cafe because of their expansive menu and location. Downside? The delivery charge was $7, which I thought was a little ridiculous. Well at least we won't have to tip the delivery man, right? Wrong! When her Pad Thai and my Rad Na was delivered the man gave me the evil eye when I asked for the cash back (our bill was $36 for two dishes, a little pricey for delivery in my opinion). He was really pissed that I asked for change from the $40 and told me that he only gets a dollar from the delivery charge. I felt so awkward and uncomfortable. Am I wrong to feel this way? But, hungry and annoyed I just let him keep it  and quickly closed the door. This food better be worth the hassle.
I was a little disappointed. My Rad Na came in two compartments, the vegetable, chicken and broth in one and the noodles in another. I would have liked them to be in the same container so the noodles could marinate and soak up all the juices. But I put it all in a bowl and tried to mix it around as much as I could. The chicken and broth were really good but the noodles were a little lackluster. They had a weird aftertaste and didn't absorb the broth well. I ended up just eating all of the ingredients from container one and left the noodles aside.
My friend was not upset with her Pad Thai at all and ate it all within minutes. She was definitely satisfied with her meal, but I was left still hungry and broke.
In my opinion, delivery should not be expensive. Twenty bucks for a dish that didn't wow me makes me pretty upset. And I'm not  a cheapskate by any means, I love to sit in a nice restaurant and just throw away my bills on delicious eats, but this was a rainy Friday chill-night. Smile Cafe delivery just  did not deliver.

When Im on campus, I don't spend real people money. I use Diamond Dollars. 
When I'm on campus, I don't eat campus cafeteria food. I go to Koja.

Koja started out as a Food Truck on Penn's campus and the kids loved it so much they turned it into a restaurant and then one came to Temple. I've been coming here since I was a freshman and even made it a Sunday night ritual "family" dinner when I still lived on campus. Almost three years later and I'm still coming back for more.

I love "the Line", you can pick your starch (either rice, soba noodles, or udon noodles, your meat (chicken, beef, shrimp, or tofu), and your spice (teriyaki, hot n spicy, or something a little sweeter? I always go for the hot n spicy chicken with soba noodles. 
When the food comes, you also get a little salad and a side of garlicky green beans. I think those are my favorite or maybe the vegetables mixed in with my noodles. The portions are huge but somehow I seem to finish it completely every time. I got all of my friends to become devoted fans of Koja as well.

Saxby's chumps Starbucks anyday.

1. They play awesome music. It's like they know exactly what I song I want to listen to every time I come in. One of the reasons why I decide to stick around and sit down to drink my coffee is to listen to their playlist.
2. They don't have ridiculously long lines like the TECH center Starbucks. I don't understand why people wait so long there when usually at Saxby's I can just walk right up and order.
3. I feel like the staff is just a lot cooler, like you have to audition to work here. Must be the reason why the music is so much cooler. 
4. They have good coffee, tons of different drinks (if you're into that whole candy bar flavored drink thing)
5. I like to take advantage of their outside seating and people watch on Liacouras.

I'm pretty sure that my friends and I kept Lucky's in business this weekend. After a long Halloween weekend full of dancing, drinking, and who knows what else, we certainly worked up late-night appetites. Thank goodness Lucky's is just around the corner from my friend's apartment and she has the number on speed dial. 
Thinking about those steamed dumplings I devoured while watching The Shining might give me a stomache now, but they were just the thing I needed. Opening up the fridge and seeing a half-eaten cheeseburger someone ordered could have given me an upchuck reflex at the time but i remember how clutch that food was at 3am. 
Yes that's right, Lucky's was still open. All we needed was someone to collect the left over drinking/cab money we all had (or didn't) and walk over to pick it up.
Thank you Lucky's for being a crucial part in our sobering-up process. 

P.S. I've had this food sober and for being a bulletproof window late night  Chinese food store, it's actually pretty tasty.

I love that this is located in a basement. I feel like I'm in a dungeon of sin full of drunken dancing fools I like to call my friends.
I am sad I'm missing Hurrah this month, but hey, there's always December.

I always forget that this place exists which is strange because the food is excellent and its ridiculously close to my house. I came here for brunch last week with a friend from high school who I haven't seen in years. The Fitzwater Cafe is situated smack dab in the middle between our two houses so we decided to meet there for our reunion meal. We met at noon on a Thursday afternoon and the place was oddly packed and were told we'd probably have to wait a little as everyone was just seated. An employee (I think) who was sitting to have his break overheard this and offered to give up his table to sit at the counter, which was awesome.
Since it was noon I wasn't sure to go the breakfast or lunch route and was debating between a Prosciutto sandwich and the French Toast. We all know my issues with brunch and having an egg infested menu but these two options sounded equally delicious. I chose the French Toast which came complete with fresh berries and about enough food to feed a village. Nathan devoured the Prosciutto sandwich and although I was envious I was getting wayy too full with my own meal to ask for a taste. I ate about half of mine, got a doggie bag and waddled home.

I live a block away and have always wanted a good bar to move into this space. Unfortunately, for one reason or another, they never work out and I won't be surprised if Bar One follows suit. 

The drink menu does not have prices. That should have been the biggest indicator. We ordered Kenzingers and Philly Pale Ales and the prices were absolutely ridiculous. Almost $7 for a single Kenzinger is unheard of, even in the most pretentious Center City bars, and this is South Philly. A shot of Jim Beam- $8. 

I'd rather walk a few blocks and go to literally any other bar then give this place my business again. 

Two stars go towards the half-way decent music and I can't deny that the food smelled pretty good. Can't imagine how overpriced that must be, though...

4wRC2RIspOc_Oxr-sAo7SA.review_text:
Narberth Pizza still makes very good pizza; ditto cheesesteaks.......chicken fingers were OK, but not great.

I do have an issue with their pricing, as their online menu doesn't match the restaurant pricing....my last visit was about $9 more than the online menu...they should either lose the online menu or keep it insync.

I ordered take-out from Wilson's Secret Sauce the other evening and it was great. I had chicken wings Fried with BBQ sauce....they were fantastic, I wish I had more...could be very happy with a double order of them and no entree.  For my main course I had the brisket plate. The beef was tasty and tender, served with BBQ sauce, had a side of baked beans and grilled carrots ( disappointed with carrots, no carmelization). Beans were very good. All in all a good experience..... little bit of a glitch when picking up, but they got it straightened out in a few extra minutes.

Tried out the Narberth Diner for breakfast today. The food was OK, nothing special.I ordered a ham omelet, it was very good.....can't say the same about the home fries. Also served with toast and coffee.

The place is not fancy, it looks like a typical dinner....the thing is it's new ,. doesn't look new. I will return as it is convenient, but will go elsewhere for an upgrade ( Nudy,'s Sabrina's, The Kettle or AWC.
Service was adequate, nothing more.

I have visited this Panera on many occasions, actually I am currently in the restaurant. I was planning to order something to eat until I witnessed one of the employees walk out of the men's room without washing his hands....decided on coffee instead. I will need to find a new coffee/fast food option.....never can be too careful.....aka "Poppy's Pizza" on Seinfeld show.

Minellas has always been a favorite restaurant for me for many years.....what happened to it. They always had really great burgers and fries, this visit not so much. Must have switched from fresh to frozen patties. Other guests were OK with hot turkey, but not sure if there is new management now, but overall we felt the quality has dropped. Hopefully they can get their MoJo back to where it used to be.

The Kettle has been a breakfast favorite since my first visit, however "stupidity" made our last visit not so great. We had a party of 4 but everyone had not all arrived. The restaurant was only half full with at least 6-7 empty tables for 4; 4 being the key. They wouldn't seat us (3 were there) until our 4th diner showed up. Keep in mind there was no one else waiting and all the tables were for 4. Maybe the owners have been watching the Seinfeld "soup Nazi" episode too often. Sometimes a little common sense may coming in handy to operate their business.

Made my first visit here this AM with friends for breakfast. The food was very good, the waitress was very attentive and made sure our coffee cups were always full. Unfortunately there was a big downside too. The place was pretty empty but it took at least 30 minutes for our food to be served, and my home fries, although very good were cold.... couldn't afford to wait for a warm up or replacement. Not sure if I will go back, as our experience confirms the yelp rating...will check back to see if they improve.

Went there to have coffee and a bagel while my car was being serviced nearby. Unfortunately it was a very cold day and they must have had the turned down. Bagel was fine, but coffee was watered down. Prices are a real ripoff, upcharge  of $1.50 for butter and $2.25 for cream cheese... didn't price the other menu items but most likely more of the same. They exist b/c there is little competition, too bad.

Love the food at Anthony's and they have remodeled the restaurant very nicely. Great place for dinner for the whole family. Pasta, pizza and sandwiches are all very good.

One complaint is that they recently decided to tell their customers how much to tip and actually added it to the check....one thing to list amounts and percentages at the bottom... another thing to total it in. Almost didn't catch it, and actually saw they overcharged for an item. I will decide my own tip, thank you!

Went back to the Pub for dinner last night. The Wild Mushroom Soup was fantastic as usual, wanted to lick the bowl I was disappointed with my Burger though, I have had much better ones there before...I also wish they had options for the fries, don't care for the dipped kind. Not sure if the burgers are still freshly made or frozen patties.... pretty sure the fries are.
Another member had the Cheese steak eggrolls and enjoyed them.

We had a family outing last night at Fellini's (Waterview) and everyone was talking about the Phillies signing Bryce Harper ---- how appropriate was it that as Fellini's struck out! Actually a strikeout is only three strikes ---- they got 4!

It took 1:15 minutes for everyone to get their food ----- almost every dinner was served COLD, along with a side of "microwaved" pasta (no Al'Dente here) ----- our waitress was pleasant but inexperienced (without any management guidance) ----- and the manager was extremely RUDE (WATTA DO YA WANT ME TO DO, IT'S SATURDAY NIGHT --- WE'RE BUSY) ...... MAYBE FIND A NEW MANAGER??? DUH.

WE WON'T BE GOING BACK ---- ALL OF US!! Too many better options.
We should have checked YELP first

Their salad size has shrunk, big-time, about 3/4 of the former size. We usually don't eat in as it is a dark and dingy location, we normally drive to another location for that. Chicken Noodle Soup was thin and watered down, not much on chicken or the noodles. Food is normally OK, but their prices always seem to creep up. They must spend a fortune on buying smaller bowls and take-out containers. We don't patronize them as we used too as there are better options.

Went to Mission BBQ KOP today for lunch with some friends....it was really good food, we all loved it. I had brisket and pulled pork which served Texas Style on Butcher's paper. Tried the KC style and Texas Twang sauces.
One friend enjoyed the sausage; another had beef ribs but wasn't a big fan.. Definitely worth a try.

Server was excellent, very attentive. The Insalata Mista chilled and crunchy, very good. We were both disappointed with our Entrees, as the food was way too salty - the Chef needs to get a second opinion on how much salt to use. We ordered the Lasagna Bolognese and the Eggplant Parmegiano.

We tried the Town Tap for a second time tonight, and once again we were disappointed....it won't happen again!

Started with the Pretzel Appetizer, it was OK but they need to lose the oil spray they put on it. Does nothing to improve it, just sloppy....ditto on the bun for the Buffalo Chicken sandwich. Buffalo sauce overwhelmed the chicken, just killed my taste buds. Blue Cheese was a liquid, never saw anything like that before. 

They need a new manager or chef, not sure what will help. It was empty at 5:30 on. Friday afternoon, wonder why

Anthony's has been a long time family favorite. We went there tonight to celebrate my Grandson's Birthday. Mostly everything was OK, but it has been better in the past. I ordered the Cheese Tortellini, the "gravy" was fantastic, but I could barely taste any cheese in the pasta...my wife had Chicken Marsala, and she said it has been better. I understand the restaurant has been thru hell and back during pandemic Draconic Closure rules, but hopefully better days are coming. We will be back, but will be looking for some improvement. Maybe the chef was having a bad night.

Disappointed with an old favorite Diner..... grilled chicken was OK; ditto Hot Turkey platter..... consistently have had better food there??? What happened?? Chicken noodle soup tasted like it came out of a can.

4xfnYMwSHPoPcX_qUORIOg.review_text: A block from the craziness of Bourbon Street is a small bar on Iberville with great music and a woman bartender who shakes a better Hurricane than Pat O'Brien's (she garnished them with black cherries.). If you stand or are lucky enough to get one of the limited seats, try during off-hours, it is worth the effort. This was our "go to" spot for drinks after several tiring days and before heading out for dinner. Don't miss it.

When we entertain at home, one of my favorite "go-to" recipes is Oysters Rockefeller; so I wanted to enjoy some from the place where they got their start. I was not disappointed. We started dining with the best Alligator Soup my wife ever tasted (one less alligator on the planet) and the Oysters, naturally. I continued with the Pompano Pontchartrain and it was delightful, however, my wife had what she called the most delicious Lamb Chops she ever ate. So combined with the Alligator Soup, she was in "culinary nirvana." We were a little tired so we had the Bread Pudding (they have a fancy name for it) and Mousse au Chocolate and called it a night, very happy with the results. Oh yes, the service was exquisite. Cannot forget that.

We only had drinks and appetizers at this great location because they were booked until very late in the evening. However, we thoroughly enjoyed our wine, bowl of Gumbo and Catfish Po'boy seated at the long tables near the bar and promise we will return next trip and that should increase our rating.

By far and away the best restaurant in NOLA. This time in, we celebrated Palm Sunday at the Jazz Brunch. Lovely. The room was festive, the service impeccable, and the music was hopping. Nevertheless, you go to Commander's for the food. Started with Bloody Marys to get the juices flowing. Our brunch began with Turtle Soup and the Commander's Creole Gumbo, the best Gumbo I had during our week visit, and I had Gumbo every night. We then feasted on the Cochon De Lait Eggs Benedict and the Louisiana Wild White Shrimp. Superb. Top that with two sides of Sugarcane and Black Pepper Bacon. However, the real flavorgasm came when we thoroughly consumed two orders of the Creole Bread Pudding Soufflé and that decadent sweet, creamy whiskey sauce. Out of this world. Can't remember having a better dessert, EVER!

We were wandering around the French Quarter during Jazz Fest and needed a quick drink so we stumbled upon Curio. We were looking for a place to eat but the menu did not appear as inviting as those from others establishments, however, we had drinks at the bar and chatted with a very friendly bartender.

On the third floor of the Ritz Carlton Hotel is a cozy but spacious, intimate cocktail lounge with some of the best music in the city. On many nights, Jeremy Davenport and his ensemble play some of the sweetest music you will hear in the city, a very distinctive sound, with many of the "Greatest Generation" singing along. They offer great service and a generous pour of Port and Chardonnay and we munched on the most delicious chips around. This is the perfect place to relax, unwind, and reminisce about the day gone by.

We were looking for a place with good, down home Louisiana cooking and found it at The Gumbo Shop. After scanning the menus at 3-4 places cruising the Bourbon Street area, we decided upon this venue because of their menu offerings and the great open-air courtyard in the back. We delighted with Rice and Beans, Jambalaya, Shrimp Creole, Catfish. Although our favorite was the Alligator Sausage, we were just in the mood for all of those things and Gumbo, of course. We ate a lot and were not disappointed. The service was excellent, the music great inside, and the bartender gave us a generous pour. Just what we needed after walking the city and taking in all of the music.

It started drizzling during Jazz Fest and Mahoney's was the closest place to grab a bite. Beer list was nice and I have not seen a fishbowl beer mug quite like the one I got since my college days. We had the Fried Onion Rings, Wings, Catfish Po'boys, and something else. The food was tasty but not memorable. One stellar point was the service we received from our server; it was excellent.

Everyone who visits New Orleans should be required to eat breakfast at Mother's at least once during their stay because the food is very good, the prices are better, and the service is priceless. My Bloody Mary was the "lightest" drink I had over a week's stay but the food portions made up for that, and the coffee was delicious. Worth the wait in line because the food was dependable and you get a lot of food for your money.

Our Uber driver recommended we try Mr. B's since we were staying in the area and were grateful for his tip. We started with the Oven Roasted Pork Belly which was phenomenal as well as the Duck Spring Rolls. We continued with the Wood Grilled Fish which was light and packed with flavor as well as the Pork Chops with Honey Ginger Sauce that were seasoned to perfection and were so tender you hardly needed the extra sharp knife placed by my place. Finished the meal sharing a slice of Pecan Pie and a glass of Port and that was an evening well spent. Happy we had the foresight to generously tip the Uber driver in advance for his on-target advice.

This is the place where many of our New Orleans-centric friends said we had to go for a Hurricane and Hand Grenade. Although it was packed with people, we found a little space to try their Hurricane, and although very good, we cannot say it was the best we had over the week.

Our choice for NOLA's best Muffaletta, this cramped yet comfortable setting tucked away in the Warehouse District is a "necessary stop" for everyone looking for unique New Orleans lunchtime cuisine. Their Muffaletta offering is stuffed with delicious meats and olive salad and is scrumptious. Combine that with an order or two or three of Mac and Cheese and a few bottles of local beer and you are set for the rest of the afternoon.

We went in for a highly recommended brunch and were immediately impressed with the casual, vibrant, open-air atmosphere featuring several garage doors that let in a lot of light when open Our recommendation is to start with a few refreshing Pineapple Mimosas because they are delicious and really hit the spot. We were seated right in front of a large, open kitchen where the food maestros conducted a wonderful culinary symphony. We started with a Smoked Trout Spread supported by a large basket of crisps. We then shared portions of a bountiful plate of Catfish and Chips, various Burgers, and two mountainous dishes of the tastiest Kale Salads we've ever had. The bad news is we did not have room for dessert, and we were Brunching. The good news is we will leave room for dessert when we return.

What started out as a food truck has morphed into three successful restaurants, our favorite being in the Gulch. And yes, it was worth the hour wait in a light drizzle underneath a large Biscuit Love umbrella. Question: What could possibly be better than a perfectly crafted Biscuit and Sausage Gravy? Answer: Add a slab of Fried Dark Meat Chicken in the middle of it. Accompany that with a side of seasoned Alma's Potatoes and a few Churros with a Chocolate Dipping Sauce and it was love at first bite. For a slightly lower caloric option, the eggs, bacon, and biscuit are a delight unto themselves. The coffee is great but the Cappuccino is outstanding. All in all, you can taste the love.

We watched a vignette about this shop on Food Channel and when we saw the sign a chip shot off Broadway, we were drawn in like a goo goo magnet. There really isn't that much inside other than different packages containing the three flavors of Goo Goo Combination Candies, but the Original, Peanut Butter, and Pecan make it a destination to buy sure-fire gifts to bring home.

An attractive, open cocktail area with the best seating and attention at the bar, Red's offers a sweet selection of perfectly purged Oysters at Happy Hour, making a few dozen affordable. The three sauces all rock. Once the barn doors open, a spacious dining room is revealed. We are excited about returning for dinner. One suggestion during Happy Hour though is that the wine by the glass was a little pricey so next time we will order beer.

We adored this cozy venue which offers excellent "wake me up" coffee. Although I asked for Blueberry Pancakes, I was told they were totally out of berries that day so I moved my attention to their well thought out Breakfast Burrito, and suggest that you ask for a small cup or two of their zesty salsa to accompany it. We also enjoyed an extremely creative Omelet crafted in a waffle maker, which was very appealing. Waffle Omelets, who knew? We also chose to sit on the comfortable couches with attached swinging trays rather than the tables, but feel the tables would be perfect for holding a business breakfast.

Probably some of the best music we heard on Broadway, particularly a rendition of Jimi Hendrix that was excellent. This is one place you absolutely cannot miss, especially if the windows are open, as the music can be heard blocks away.

We went in, had a beer, listened to some music, and went out. Just another of the iconic watering holes in an extremely competitive Broadway bar scene. Unfortunately, we must have stumbled in on a bad set. Time to find another bar to hit.

Now this is why we came to Nashville. This cavernous, multi-leveled, picnic table oriented barbecue joint was my favorite eatery in the city. Passionately prepared and presented authentic cuisine with great country music on a smack-dab up-front stage. You must walk by the ping-pong, darts and other games to order your food before sitting, and when situated, you're in for a fantastic time. Once you finally sink your teeth into the ribs, the chicken wings, the pulled pork, the brisket; oh heck, it is all packed with flavor. Each sauce is freshly made and special. Order beer by the pitcher and wine served in a jelly jar. What character. This place, and especially the Ribs, are simply kickass phenomenal.

Of all the bars we bounced in and out of on Broadway, we enjoyed the music at Old Red's the best. At this terrific two-tiered listening venue, we had the pleasure of listening to the Frank Ray Band and we were toe tapping, singing along, and having a totally good ol' time. So much so that we went home after they finished their set because they were the capstone of the evening.

If you told me the first restaurant we would enter upon arriving in Nashville was a British Pub, I tell you that your nickers must be in a twist. However, and with a strong recommendation, we ventured inside and were delighted with the bright, modern pub atmosphere included a Foosball table in a stadium-like setting. We quickly settled in with some Chardonnay, a few pints of Guinness and some Soft Pretzels with Pub Cheese. After quickly perusing the menu, I settled in on two old favorites: Sheppard's Pie or Bangers and Mash. When I asked our server which was better, she insisted that we order their famous Fish and Chips. Man, was that the right choice. First, it was the largest piece of fried Haddock I've ever seen, accompanied by a heaping pile of chips. Second, the flavor was outstanding, best I've had outside Portsmouth. Okay now, Foosball anyone?

I've been converted. At first, I thought that this old Landmark would not be worth the fee but after it was done, I would say it was worth every penny. No trip to Music City is complete without going on the walking tour around this storied music mecca; and if it is not crowded, you can see everything you need to see to get the entire flavor and history of this magnificent venue. One can only imagine watching Country History on that large stage, even sitting in one of its "rock hard" pews. I also now have a deep respect for Emmylou Harris, who helped save this musical shrine from destruction. (Google it!)

We were told that Margaritas were the pinnacle of good taste at Saint Anejo's so we tried both the Gold Coast and Natural Waters varieties. I must say those were the correct choices for our pallets. We then moved to some spicy Chips and Guacamole, although I preferred the tangy Salsa in a sidecar attached to the chip bowl. I quickly moved to three Catfish Tacos with some flavorfully spicy Rice and Black Beans and they made my mouth sing with joy. Our table also enjoyed the Mahi Mahi Tacos with Mexican Corn and that was an awesome combination - along with terrific music and with another Margarita, of course.

This joint is more than just the purple walls and famous murals. It is one of the mainstay's in the Nashville bar scene; Tootsie's is a cramped, loud, 4-story funhouse that offers some delicious Peanut Butter Whisky. Seriously! I won't soon forget the singer belting out "Don't Stop Believing" while standing on top of the bar. It is wonderful for an hour or two and then it was time to move on.

Attractive, upscale Sushi-driven restaurant that offers many food choices and a large Saki menu. I went with the Godzilla Roll and my favorite Ikura Sashimi placed inside a fine cucumber wrap that did not disappoint. The unquestionable star on the menu can be summed up in three words. Crispy Brussels Sprouts. I've never tasted anything like them and, coupled with a glass of bourbon, boast such a uniquely powerful flavor that this is clearly a restaurant we will frequent again and again.

Extremely open and airy industrial chic coffee bar guaranteed to jump-start your day. Or afternoon. They offer many delightful coffee options, although I went with a simple cup of Sumatra. It is definitely a youthful hangout to recharge.

I must say first that I am a pizza purist who believes pizza can only be found in New York with the "big 8" ingredients on top and should only be eaten folded in one hand. So the thought of pizzas named Kiamue Karma, Holy Shiitake, and Pacific Rim were not exactly choices that I would ever make. Pineapple, Avocado, Spinach, and Buffalo Chicken do NOT belong on top of a pizza. So we selected "Build Your Own Pizza" with Pepperoni and Sausage and I admit it was really was a treat, even if I had to eat it with a knife and fork (Yikes!) like NYC Mayor Bill DeBlasio. Additionally, the Small Salad is a misnomer as it is generous in stature and extremely flavorful. Normally, I would give this place a "3", but enhanced my rating to a "4" to honor this eye-opening experience.

54-9e0S8JkMC4OZDPIdHgw.review_text:
I was expecting more from this restaurant since I had read some good reviews on here.  

The interior left a lot to be desired... crumbs on tables, water in a large orange cooler you'd see at a construction site, flies.  An employee walked past me with a big, smelly bag of garbage as we waited for the food.

I shared a side tossed salad and the tandoori chicken meal, which came with naan, rice, a veggie side (I chose chickpeas), and a small salad.  The chicken, rice, and naan were really great, but the chickpeas, and all the vegetable sides, were just spiced goop in a gallon of oil.  The cucumbers in the salad were yellow and on the verge of spoiling, and the dressing selection included Wishbone products you'd find in a high school cafeteria.  I tried the light ranch dressing, and it tasted rancid.

The garlic heads are sprouting, the blueberries are molding, the greens are limp, and the tomatoes are flavorless.  The people who work at the deli are either cold and grunt at you or are unresponsive.  The aisles are poorly organized.  

And the cashiers? The first time I shopped here, I was shouted at for placing my basket on the conveyor belt.  One time a cashier gave me the stink eye for having the nerve to ask him if his line was open.  

Recently, I watched a cashier take out the garbage from beneath his register, and then reach for my strawberries to scan them.  I stopped him right there and asked him to wash his hands.  That was the last time I subjected myself to the "Fresh" Grocer.  I would rather trek a mile to Trader Joe's than pay for crappy produce and even worse customer service.  The employees act like working here is punishment.

I arrived slightly unnerved since Pita Pit was completely empty at 7PM on a Friday night, but I decided to go ahead and order since I had read good reviews on Yelp. I had a delicious whole wheat gyro pita with tzatziki, spinach, mushrooms, tomatoes, and sprouts.  I generally avoid ordering tomatoes at restaurants since they're usually bland and mealy, but Pita Pit's were perfectly ripe and flavorful.  The gyro meat was heated over a griddle, quite juicy, and well-seasoned.  The service was pleasant, which is a rarity in Philadelphia :p.  The portions are generous, but the price was a little steep without sides (~$7.50 including tax).  I'll buy a Yelp coupon for the next time I return, which will definitely be soon!

Supreme trumps Fresh Grocer by miles in produce and service.  I've found the freshest garlic, perfectly ripe papayas, local blueberries for $0.99, and a fantastic selection of yogurts.  They also have a dedicated area for vegetables closing in on their expiration dates; I've picked up trays holding 3 red bell peppers for $0.99 (great for romesco!).  I love their diverse fresh and packaged international foods selection, as well.  I've never purchased their meat before, so I can't vouch for the quality or taste, but they do have a large selection.  Unfortunately for this type 1 diabetic, they don't carry much in the way of sugar-free products, but they are helping me overcome my addiction to NSA Turkey Hill ice cream.

I've found the cashiers to be warm and friendly.  I've never had to wait in line for more than a couple of minutes, either.

For authentic Thai food, large portions, reasonable prices, and attentive service, come here.  I ordered the lemon grass soup with veggies and the Pattaya salad.  The broth was very flavorful and had some mild heat.  The vegetables surprisingly retained some crispness. The salad was decent.  The sweet coconut fried shrimp were addictive.  I knocked off a star because I had some crab shells in my salad and the lime-mayo dressing was a bit too acidic for my taste.

I came here for my birthday and decided to be daring and try 3 new foods: octopus, gingko nuts, and quail eggs.  The takoyaki (octopus balls), topped with bonito flakes and some Japanese sauces, were creamy, savory, and absolutely delicious.  The gingko nuts also had a creamy quality, but I found them somewhat flavorless.  The quail eggs were more tender than chicken eggs; when wrapped with bacon, they were a sinful treat.  The last item I ordered was the yakitori eggplant, and like the rest of the meal, it was tasty.  

The rest of my party also enjoyed their dishes: chicken cutlets, philly & sweet potato sushi rolls, chicken teriyaki, and the very generous "mini" udon soup.

The pricing for food is extremely reasonable, but the beer is kind of steep!  A bottle of Yuengling costs $5.  Next time I'll come during happy hour (5-7PM).

Wow, just wow!  I haven't had dim sum since I lived in Atlanta, and I really missed it.  For my birthday, my boyfriend and I went to Joy Tsin Lau on a weekday at 11:30 AM.  There were 3 carts going around with so many traditional dishes to choose from.  We ordered the lotus sticky rice, cha siu bao, scallion dumplings, pork dumplings, spare ribs, and the coconut jello.  One of the waiters generously gave us 3 quails as well!  We had such a good meal and great service.  Just thinking about the cha siu bao is making me salivate.

Went there last night and had perfect buffalo wings and a glass of dry champagne-like cider; my boyfriend had a flawlessly cooked medium rare NY strip and well-seasoned fries with a crispy exterior and soft potato-y interior.  Tapestry has a great and attentive staff, too.  I wish there was a late-night neighborhood gem like this in West Philly/University City.

I haven't had barbeque in several years, so I'm not sure how authentic it was, but the food was definitely delicious.  I ordered the pulled pork platter with sauteed okra and collard greens.  I really enjoyed their regular bbq sauce mixed with XXX.  I didn't care for the hot sauce or apple cider vinegar, which was oddly flavorless, and I didn't try the sweet bbq sauce with molasses and brown sugar.  The pork was savory and so juicy, it soaked my cornbread.  The okra was seasoned and cooked well- not slimy at all, and had some stewed tomatoes for sweetness.  I feared being served mushy collard greens, but these were pleasantly soft with a little chew and a lot of flavor.  Our waitress was very friendly and attentive.  This restaurant is highly recommended!

I rarely order delivery, but when I do it's always Spring.  Their portions are extremely generous, and their garlic sauce rocks.  I recommend the spare ribs, roast pork, diet chicken and broccoli, and tofu and veggie soup.  The only thing I've ordered and haven't liked is the hot and sour soup- it's neither hot nor sour.

I came here on a Saturday at 9pm with my boyfriend, and despite it being quite busy, it wasn't too noisy to have a conversation.  The interior design is gorgeous, and the restaurant is surprisingly large.  My boyfriend ordered the pepperoni pizza and happily downed it in 10 minutes.  I was able to sneak a bite, and I'm not sure if it was a lingering flavor from my beer (highly recommended saison Pretty Things' Jack D'or), but I thought the crust tasted mushroom-y.  I am a self-proclaimed chicken wing connoisseur, and City Tap's 10 spice wings were flavorful and the portion was generous, but they did not meet my crispiness standards.  Our server was pleasant and attentive.  Overall, the meal was pretty good, and I wouldn't hesitate to return when it's late in University City, I want a fantastic beer selection, and I don't feel like cooking.

Order the jerk chicken drumsticks.  Although you only get 4 for $8, their finely-crushed potato chip(?)-crust is like crack.  My boyfriend always gets a medium-rare burger.  The patty is cooked perfectly and the toppings are garden-fresh.  Although the chefs are usually on-point, I was disappointed by the arugula salad.  For $9, you get a small plate of arugula doused in lemon oil, 1/4 of a pear, and three thin slices of parmesan.  A sweet port gastrique is supposed to cut the tartness of the oil and the bitterness of the greens, but it just sticks to the plate.  I had to scrape it off with my fork, and then pull it off with my teeth.  I might not have a problem with this if I were at home in my jammies, but when I'm on a date, it's a bit embarrassing.  I like White Dog, but there are equally tasty and more affordable dining options for this broke grad student.

I hate writing negative reviews, and I hate sending food back even more, but the meal I was served was inedible and overpriced.  I ordered two sunny-side up eggs and a side of the maple turkey sausage.  I told the waitress I like runny yolks, and I was brought two barely-cooked eggs.  The whites were completely translucent!!  I cannot believe I had to ask for my whites to be cooked.  Aren't eggs the first protein a diner chef should learn to prepare?  I was brought eggs a second time, and still the whites were not cooked.  Nobody wants to eat food that is reminiscent of snot.  My dining partner had already eaten half her meal by this point.  By the time my third plate of eggs arrived, the meat I had planned on dipping into the yolks was cold.  The sausage tasted decent, but the portion was so tiny: 3 links the size of a kid's thumb for $2.59.  I think my disappointment in this meal was magnified because there are so many fantastic dining options at Reading Terminal.

Wow, I will be returning again and again!!  I had a whole crisp and juicy fried fish with a large and fresh side salad for only $12.  This could've been two meals, but I couldn't stop myself.  The waitress was kind and attentive.  My only qualm is that their tv was pretty loud.  It's cash only, but if you forget to bring some there's an ATM two doors down at Queen of Sheba.

I came here tonight with two friends, and we had a very good meal.  I had an authentic bowl of spicy and sour shrimp lemongrass soup.  Although it was a tad salty, I still thought it was fantastic: I salivate just thinking about it.  I also ordered Jim's Tofu, a dinner special consisting of crispy, deep-fried tofu over salad with a chile-fish sauce dressing.  Salivating again.

Both my dining partners had the red curry.  I was able to take a spoonful of the sauce, and it was very coconutty.  The portions are generous, as are the owners.  When we notified them of our friend's gluten sensitivity, they sincerely wanted to make sure that he'd have a tummy-friendly meal, and listed the ingredients of dishes he was considering.

This small convenience store has organic, gluten-free treats; fresh veggies; lots of cheeses; Greek yogurt; and tons of Asian goods at great prices.  I found a recipe for miso soup with poached eggs on kitchn.com, and was able to locate everything I needed at Fu Wah: powdered dashi stock, seaweed, refrigerated miso, tofu, and even cage-free eggs!  I also picked up hard-to-find kaffir lime leaves and frozen, processed lemongrass for only $0.99!  The employees are really helpful and kind, too.

I ordered a stir fry with Indonesian BBQ and lettuce, and they drowned my food in a salty, flavorless sauce! :( I tried my boyfriend's stir fry with the spicy garlic sauce, and his tasted a lot better. I don't expect to return soon since the prices are pretty high for the small portions, but if I do, I'd go with the spicy garlic.

Came in here this morning after fasting and then getting blood drawn at the Curtis Center. Delicious bacon, sausage, sunny-side up eggs, and unlimited coffee refills made me feel invincible. The waitress (Melanie?) was very friendly. I wish there was a Mrs. K's in West Philly! The only thing I wasn't too keen on was the seating situation: although I'm only 5'7", my legs are too long to sit comfortably underneath the shallow counter.

Came here last Sunday for the clams and a fantastic hefeweizen on tap. The food was amazing, and the atmosphere was romantic and charming. I also liked that not too many people were there, as I could actually have a conversation with my partner. I would give it 5 stars if the portions were larger. My $13 plate was really small.. probably around a dozen small clams at the most.

Ate here tonight with my partner. I had the arugula salad with grilled chicken. The lemon lager vinaigrette is delicious and definitely boozy tasting. Overall the salad was pretty good, but I thought it was one-note with the acidity from the pickled onions and the lemony dressing. The "poached apples" tasted like they were poached in vinegar, too. 

My partner had the roasted chicken with green beans, mashed potatoes, and gravy, and wow, it was so delicious. The chicken was shockingly tender and flavorful, and the potatoes were so buttery.

There was a gigantic table of at least 20 people, and we still got our food within a reasonable amount of time. The service was great and attentive as well.

I really wish I could join in the 4 & 5 star ratings, but I left feeling disappointed with what I had paid for. The house salad was delicious. I wish I had ordered a large! I wanted to drink that ginger dressing. The age dashi tofu's batter was really sticky; they should have been fried for longer. The spicy, sticky sauce it was sitting in made the tofu really hard to tear apart, and it made the batter have a glue-like consistency. Finally, the tuna tartare was slathered in this miso sauce that completely masked the flavor of the tuna. The avocado it was paired with was underripe as well.

The raves about Mo are true. I haven't felt good after a hair cut in a long time, especially after the last disaster which essentially left me with a different hair style on either side of my head. I told Mo I wanted to look normal and have one hair style; she spent a long time ensuring that the left side matched the right. It's a long trip to get here from West Philly, but it's worth it.

I think I've been spoiled by the fresh, thick, plentiful, and inexpensive sashimi at Zen in Northampton, Massachusetts, which made my visit to Uzu less than stellar. Although the fish here is fresh and tasty, the prices are quite for the tiny portions. I had sashimi, the mixed sashimi appetizer, the yakko tofu, and a house salad. I was barely sated after spending $30 on food alone. I even thought about eating the parsley garnishes! The service was subpar: at one point my partner and I were the only diners in the restaurant, and it was difficult getting our plates cleared. After two more couples arrived, it became harder to get any attention. I never got an offer for a soda refill or a glass of water.
Well-priced and fresh tasting sashimi, BYOB, attentive service, and less than a mile walk from my apartment? I've finally found my favorite Japanese restaurant in Philly.
One month later and my hair still looks great. Thanks again, Mo!

I dined here with two friends on Saturday, 2/15. I ordered the lobster bisque and the duck & pork sausages over a bed of kale and stoneground mustard. The lobster bisque was primarily cream - there was very little shellfish taste, and the broth was underseasoned and very thin. I would estimate that there was about 1 oz of lobster in my bowl. The sausages and kale really lacked flavor too, so they also required additional salt. I'm not one to typically add salt to restaurant dishes, but the food was so underseasoned. 

The service was also lacking. I asked questions about some dishes and the waiter just restated what the menu listed. When I asked for clarification, he seemed bothered by my questions. Overall, I was unimpressed and don't plan on returning.

5Dx195Sp4xN8VqYOr7I62w.review_text: Made reservations for my birthday and was sorely disappointed.  Food was just fine, not fabulous (but priced as if it was fabulous). We waited, even though we had a reservation.  It was freezing at our seat.  We asked the waiter to adjust the thermostat, but he said the manager wouldn't let him.  I contacted the manager after our visit, and she was barely apologetic and offered nothing in response to our bad experience.

This is the Cheers of Mount Airy. Excellent beers, ever changing. Friendly staff who remember you (well, we go regularly). Decent food. Actually pretty family friendly, despite being a bar. Love this place.
Our family's favorite dinner out. Love all the flatbreads (their name for pizza). The house salad is just delicious. Good house made brews. If we have room, we also love the house made ice cream.

Love the white sangria, free salsa, and vegetarian menu. Everything is delicious. Try the French fried yams. Margaritas are good, too. My father-in-law has celiac disease and loves their gluten-free menu. Do not be put off by the decor. The staff are all friendly and efficient, always. A favorite for my family!

Tried In Riva recently on a perfect summer evening. Sat at the outside bar while we waited for an outdoor table. The view of the river is divine. i felt I had escaped to Europe. The staff were friendly and helpful. Loved the appetizer that consisted of a spread in a mason jar with grilled bread. So delicious! We also tried three small plates of pasta; a sampler.

This is our current favorite dinner spot. Delicious, house-made, strong, real margaritas--expensive but good. I like the blood orange margarita. Creative street tacos. Amazing fajitas for two. Great guacamole. Good nachos. The plantains are great. Everything is tasty. Cute, current decor and amazing patio. The servers are friendly and attentive. You may need a reservation at busier times. We usually go on Friday evenings, but there are great happy hour deals Monday through Thursday.

I've seen some negative reviews on here, want to respond with my experience. We came once when it was extra, extra busy--with everyone arriving at the same time. We had poor service that night, but complained and haven't seen that server lately.  That was once. We eat here at least twice a month and service is always good. Every place has an off night. 

Also, it used to feel cold inside in the winter, but that has improved. We came on some frigid evenings recently and felt warm inside.

My kid loves this place and always requests it for her birthday dinner, so I am doomed to keep coming here. The place is always busy; families love it. I don't. People say the burgers are good, but I don't eat burgers.

The trolley outside, which serves ice cream in the warm months, is better. I would give that three stars. The guy who manages it is really friendly. The ice cream itself is good and much less expensive than Bredenbeck's, up the street. However, they don't always have all the flavors so listed, which is annoying and disappointing.

The rest of this review is for the diner itself. The kitchen can be really slow, so you can wait forever for a simple meal or even an appetizer that they are only heating up. In the past, I have had several omelets which came out with a huge section in the center completely uncooked and runny. This grosses me out. I've also had a vegetable quesadilla swimming in water.

Last night my family was there (on a Friday night) for my kid's birthday. We waited forever for our appetizer, the spinach artichoke dip, which we had ordered because we were hungry. It was obviously just reheated, and they weren't that busy yet, so the wait was confusing. It was just sufficient, not stellar. I won't order it again.

We then waited another eternity for our dinner. Our waitress told us it was coming soon at one point, but we waited at least ten more minutes after that. When the food finally came, it was piecemeal, so two of our party of four had food and two of us were still waiting several minutes. It is not cool to leave a very hungry kid waiting when other people at the table get their food.

The bathrooms are not very clean. It can be too cold in the original diner seating area. Most of the wait staff is friendly now, but that has not always been the case. 

On the positive side, they have a huge, fantastic beer selection, which is also available for take out. You can try a beer before committing to a whole case under the crazy Pennsylvania system. The milk shakes are also good, and the pancakes look nice and fluffy. I like the homemade potato chips that come with the sandwiches. They're much better than the fries, which are not good, in my opinion.

Overpriced. Great view if you can sit outside. Too cold inside--too much air conditioning. They've changed the drink menu and it's disappointing. We just had a terrible experience with the hosts. One told us, "We just have to clean off a couple of tables." She did not take our names or even direct us to where we could wait. She then sat a bunch of people who came in after us. She thought we wanted to sit outside, which we never said. When I complained, she said some of the people she sat before us were on a waiting list. Then why did she act like she was seating us immediately, and not take our name? When I asked this, she offered a lame, insincere apology. Our server was excellent, though. Jarred appetizers on grilled bread are fantastic. Pasta dishes are small and fine, but not amazing.

These are the most delicious cakes I have ever eaten. Even people who don't care for cake love the cakes here. I will never get a cake anywhere else. I especially recommend the chocolate cake (they call it mocha cake) with cream cheese icing and mocha mousse filling. Totally worth the extra money compared to anyplace else!

We ordered specially decorated birthday cakes for my daughter's parties and always been pleased.

Also a nice place for lunch. Fresh sandwiches and salads. Quite delicious. You can get a little cookie or other bakery treat for dessert. The cafe seating is cozy or you can sit outside on the sidewalk on a nice day.

This place is always busy, so I guess it's what people are looking for. We come here about once every three months. The food is fine--even good. I don't recall having a problem with the food. Nothing is stellar or amazing. Prices feel a little high for what it is, but I guess they style themselves as a classy place. We never have a reservation, and there is usually a wait, but we can usually find a seat in the bar area, where there are no reservations and seating is self-serve. The servers are friendly and usually attentive at the beginning of your visit. However, I have a big problem with their attention AFTER your food is served. The same thing happens every. single. time. Your food comes out, then your server comes over immediately, or maybe after you've had one bite. They ask whether you need anything else. You say no, because the food just came and you can't see anything missing. But then they disappear for a very long time. You can't see them anywhere. You need something--another drink, ketchup, a spoon, whatever. Where the hell are they? This happens in the dining room, too. Sometimes part of your meal gets stone cold while you wait for the thing you need. I have a kid and ice cream comes with the kids meal. She will be finished with her dinner, ready for ice cream, and it will be approaching bedtime, but our server is nowhere.  But what kid is going forego the ice cream because it is late? Not my kid! I was there last night and I asked for the ice cream at that just-got-the-food check-in. This helped, but it was still a longer wait than I would like before seeing my server again. This is another of those places I would just stop frequenting altogether if my kid didn't request it regularly. 

They used to have a house-made veggie burger that was pretty good, but this was eliminated from the menu.

I wanted to love this. A black-owned breakfast place. We need more of both (black-owned and breakfast) around here. The service was fine, seems like they've worked out some of the kinks from earlier reviews. We are used to breakfast places having a wait on a Sunday morning. The hostess was courteous and competent. The place is clean and fresh-looking. But no one in our family of three loved their meal. We waited a long time and it was "meh." Both my daughter and I got something on our plates that seemed suspiciously like store-bought-fake-cream-cheese-icing. You know, Betty Crocker. The home fries were salty and dry. We want natural, homemade breakfast. Also, my husband's meal and my side dish came out at least five minutes after the first two entrees. We will keep schlepping to Sabrina's and Honey's and Morning Glory. So disappointed.

Everything here was fine, but not spectacular. We had the Brussels sprouts appetizer, which was tasty, but the veggies in it were mushy. I would say overcooked. It was more like a filling for an entree (wrap, maybe?) than an appetizer. There are as a special Bavarian soft pretzel, which was good, but the cheese dip was bland and resembled velveeta. The sesame-crusted salmon salad was fresh and fine but not flavorful and honestly disappointing. The timing of our food coming out was awkward. The service was decent and the building was cool on the outside. The decor I nside was dark but I guess that's the vibe they're going for. Decent beer list and rotating drafts. I feel this may be an amazing experience if you're looking for a good bar, but there is tastier food to be had in the city.

We loved the old location and ate there 2-4 times per year.  Would have given 4 or 5 stars to those experiences. We loved the old place and experience . Tonight was our first visit to the new location but we won't be back. While our salads and appetizers were lovely and the complimentary bread was warm and fresh, all three entrees were disappointing. In particular, I ordered the mushroom pappardelle. I've had it a few times. The pasta is homemade. But tonight it seemed all the pasta stuck together AND didn't taste fresh. I considered sending it back, but it is exhausting to complain and I didn't know how to explain my complaint. My husband had the eggplant Parmesan. His side of pasta was tiny--insulting even. My daughter had the clams with linguini and she felt the clams in the shell (not all were fresh) tasted artificial or chemically. We also missed the familiar staff. Our waitress tonight was adequate, but we didn't get the warm feeling we got in Mount Airy. We love Mount Airy, so it's not the same in the suburbs--well, it could have been,if tonight hadn't been so disappointing!! PS the owner brought our salad and said he'd bring us more bread which we never got. Oh, well. We are moving on to other places to love.

Everything was delicious. Warm, attentive service. We had the special appetizer and special pasta, as well as spaghetti Nero. All were very good. Now that Bacio has moved (and was not particularly warm or tasty in new location) we will be at Moma more often. Several dessert choices all sounded delicious.
Everything is delicious. Chef Bobby and the staff are some of the nicest people ever. We especially like the roasted cauliflower and the mushroom pide.

5iyWHRIE-WM2hqc0-lWlLQ.review_text:
Went with my wife and kids to this new Italian restaurant.  Everything was hot and freshly made. 
Crispy calamari with fresh tomato sauce,  garlicky white pizza with ricotta stars, Fettuccini Alfredo,
Lasagna,  Veal Sorentino? Provolone,  fresh tomato sauce over gnocchi . Veal could have been pounded thinner or tenderized, but that aside,  all flavors were spot on. Took cannoli, chocolate cake,  tiramisu and pastry home for later.  We'll be back to try other menu items . Could be our Italian go-to if they keep up the quality .

This place is awesome.  I've never eaten there, but the take out is always consistently delicious. 
 I get #12 Pho (rare beef), shrimp and pork lotus salad, Apollo shrimp wrapped in springroll wrapper for the kids, shrimp paste on sugar cane, 
mixed grill sampler, some of the best tempura I've ever had,
PORK TACOS ARE TO DIE FOR !!! ( on special menu) .
I love turning my friends on to this place !

Great place !!  Friendly service.  Perfect for kids and adults.  Lots of choices. Mac and cheese dog for my kids and I usually get the Reuben dog with your choice of kraut or slaw. Onion rings, cheese fries,  tots. All hot and cooked to order.  Tasty shakes and fried Oreos are both winners for dessert.

Fun place for the family. We love the burgers and cheese fries. Better than average chicken fingers. Huge variety of soda flavors. Delicious milkshakes. 
50's music !!

We love supporting small businesses, especially when the food is so tasty !!!!  
These guys do it right. Delicious and fresh every time.  Short rib and goat cheese burrito and the pulled pork with pineapple habanero salsa are my favorites. Totally customizable. 
Choose to add bacon and chorizo and you won't be sorry.  
 CAN'T GET THOSE AT THE BIG CHAIN RESTAURANTS.

We got take out this time. My wife picked up dinner for the family Monday night.  She said every table was occupied and the place was jumping. They still managed to get our entire order correct including the last cannoli of the night :) 

This time we tried the garlic knots which were freshly made and accompanied by their tasty marinara. Simple and delicious. 

We also tried their homemade meatballs (2/side)
I wish we got more. They were a big hit with the kids.
They also loved the Fettuccini Alfredo, which was just as good as it was at the restaurant. 

We ordered their Sicilian style pizza with sausage and broccoli rabe.  Delicious,  yet thin and crispy.  I always thought Sicilian style meant thick doughy crust . 

I still give them 5 stars for their organization when very busy.  Cafe Sitaly is definitely the best Italian/pizza joint in our area.  

Next trip we'll have to try the stromboli and cheesesteaks .

Keep the good stuff coming.

Third trip to Cafe Sitaly was another success.
We've bumped into friends every time we've been there. Cannolis and tiramisu are sold out ! Two great signs that the good word is spreading about this place.

Cheesesteak stromboli was authentically rolled. Most local pizza shops fold a pizza in half and call it stromboli. This was tasty and beautifully open at each end. 

Copious amounts of clams atop the mound of linguine. 

Sides of sausage and meatballs bathed in homemade marinara . 

Blueberry lemon cheesecake was enjoyable. 


Sciarrino's, Riviera , Luigi's menus all in the trash.

Looks like I found my new go-to florist in Wilmington. 
They delivered a beautiful bouquet of 28 red roses to my wife at the restaurant where she works as Chef de Cuisine.  We couldn't be together on the day of our 14th Anniversary,  but She was showered with attention from staff members and customers alike. 
All commenting on the breathtaking arrangement. 
I run a small business and I understand the importance of personal and friendly customer service. These guys get it.
Well done Petal Pushers !!!!

So I tried Claymont Steaks tonight for dinner.
2 large cheese steaks Xtra cheese
1 small cheese steak 
Terrible Rolls
Cheese on roll not mixed in with meat
Meat sat on top overcooked and dry and completely UNSEASONED 

Still searching for good delivery in the Boothwyn/Wilmington area.

As you can see, I don't write too many reviews because I only write about the GREAT experiences and choose not to mention the others at all. 
That being said,  my wife and I got an Italian hoagie and a cheese steak wit tonight. 
After trying MANY other sandwich shops in the area,
Don's was by far the best  !!! 

Criteria : 

1st The Order, was called in and we got exactly what we asked for. Don't laugh people. Seldom is a phone order correctly executed. 

2nd  Size Matters !  The hoagie had so much ham on top, I thought they gave me the wrong sandwich. I lifted up the ham to find a well loaded Italian hoagie.
Plenty of meat, cheese and onions all lovingly chopped and mixed together on the cheese steak. 

3rd The bread had just the right amount of "chew".
Fresh !!!

4th Price/ Value These large sandwiches were $11 and change. Well worth it for the amount of food.

5th Delivery ????  No, sadly. But the food is worth the drive.

Let me start this review by explaining that my wife and I walked in with our 2 kids about half an hour before closing on Sunday afternoon.  We were the last customers of the day. 

Our server was helpful with menu suggestions considering it was our first visit.  
We ordered mac and cheese and chicken fingers for the kids. Shrimp and grits for my wife and homemade Biscuits and sausage gravy for me. And an order of cornbread to share. 
Our beverages arrived in a timely fashion. The coffee was exceptional. 
Warm toasted Cornbread was served in a metal pail lined with paper and pats of butter placed all throughout as if to help soften. Cornbread was Very flavorful and not too crumbly.

Everything else arrived a few minutes later. 
The mac and cheese looked good although I didn't try it.
I had to try the buttermilk dipped chicken fingers which turned out to be an entire chicken breast breaded, fried, and cut into strips.  Hot, crunchy, juicy and seasoned well. The dipping sauces were good. Bbq, Chipotle ranch . Hand cut fries were golden, crispy and seasoned. (Potatoes blanched "fried twice" to keep golden color). 
My wife's Shrimp and grits were surprisingly worthy with plenty of shrimp . Grits needed a touch of salt. 
My platter of  Biscuits and gravy was hot and definitely surpassed my expectations. 

We'll be back to try other breakfast items and several sandwiches sounded good.  Bugers, rueben, brisket sandwich etc.  

Check out the antique shop next door Fri-Sunday.

I've never been inside, but my wife has brought food home from this place 4 times and everything has been FANTASTIC! !!!!!   
Onion pakora, Samosa Chaat, chicken curry, chicken biryani all delicious, very reasonably priced, huge portions.
Best pizza, hoagie, cheesesteaks in the area.  The rolls are way better than most local pizza shops. Delivery can take a while, but that's probably because they're the best around.

Does anyone else know about Charlies Pizza ??
We own a business on Philly Pike and picked up a lg plain and a lg pepperoni mushroom to feed the crew. Everyone was impressed.  Tasty homemade dough and sauce.  
I'll be trying their wings, stromboli and cheese steaks in the near future.

Just got home from our first visit and everything was delicious.  We split 3 pizzas between 3 hungry adults and 2 children.  Margharita (plain) , Bianca ( white pie with garlic), Soppresotta  (spicy with red pepper flakes).  Dessert Nutella pizza was fun for the kids. I give 5 stars for quality, fresh ingredients and overall execution.  Still a little pricey. 
4 drinks, 3 pizzas, 1 small dessert pizza + 20% tip = $88

We tried Charlie's Pizza for a second time and after my first bite of pizza, I remembered why I liked it so much the first time.  Some pizza chain claims to have better ingredients, better pizza. But that's exactly what I think of when I eat Charlie's Pizza. Better dough, better cheese, deliciously garlicky tomato sauce.  We tried a Cheesesteak stromboli which  surpassed all expectations.  It was juicy and  cheesy with plenty of steak.  The best I've had in this area.  5 stars for quality and consistency.

Great for the whole family  !! We've been to Tom's twice and we walked away with the same great experience.  Scallion Pancakes are my kid's favourite.  As well as the meat buns, springrolls, soup dumplings. Steamed soup dumplings are better than pan fried (not much soup left inside) . My kids 12 and 8 didn't like the wonton soup because it was very different than your everyday wonton soup.  It contained homemade wontons with pickled vegetables and some kind of greens. I loved it. Hot and Sour soup was superb !!
Very affordable,  under $50 for 4 of us. 

We haven't tried any entrees yet and the giant  bowls of soup look enticing.  Yum !!!!

A good friend mentioned Aurea's a few weeks ago and I've been back twice in 2 weeks. My 8 year old daughter proclaimed that it's her new favorite.  I've gotten takeout on both occasions.   
The chips were fresh and salty enough to balance the mild salsa. The guacamole was delicious with large diced tomato and onion.  Got the Lengua (beef tongue) taco which has an unctuous short rib consistency that I will most certainly be revisiting on a burrito in the near future. They offer grilled chicken or pulled chicken for taco, burritos,  etc. My kids loved the grilled chicken quesadillas and the pulled chicken enchiladas (3 per order) with green sauce was tasty and satisfying.  The Chorizo is juicy and flavorful. I've had the Chorizo Torta, which is a sandwich. And the Chorizo Chalupitas (4 per order) are incredible  !! The dough is thick and has the texture of tamale dough.  I don't know if the Horchata is homemade,  but either way,  it's delicious. I hope to try their Pasole which hasn't been available the 2 times I've gotten takeout.  
Extremely happy overall,  great food,  reasonably priced.

I've been to Il Granaio 6 or 7 times.  A few times with a large group for Mother's Days and on several occasions with my friends and family.  They have never disappointed.  Try no to eat too much of the complimentary bread and White Bean Puree.  It's incredible,  but so is everything else.  My wife and I struggle to choose only 2 appetizers.  The Beets and Burrata are a perfect match with a sprinkling of pancetta and a drizzle of balsamic and extra virgin olive oil. The grilled octopus is always fresh and tender with just the right amount of char-grilled flavor accented with a spicy red pepper puree.  The ricotta and mascarpone app has plenty of basil served with grilled bread. I get the polenta with mushrooms and gorgonzola cream sauce every time.  It simply has no room for improvement.  The entrees are just as solid as the appetizers.  I usually get the Fettuccine Arigosta. Homemade pasta, perfectly cooked with copious amounts of lobster,  tomatoes and asparagus in a brandy truffled cream sauce.  The Spinach Gnocchi with braised Pork Cheeks is another favorite. 
Save room for dessert because the lemon cake and tiramisu are not to be missed.  Complimentary limoncello is a nice touch. 
Fresh food, consistently delicious.

I've been looking forward to trying this restaurant for a few years.  My wife and I own 2 small restaurants so we rarely get a chance to get out. 
A few months ago,  we went with our 2 children (9 & 13 years old) and our friend. 
The 5 of us were greeted and seated promptly as we were 15 minutes late for our reservation. Immediately I noticed that although the restaurant is small, the tables are not crammed so close together that you're part of someone else's conversation.  I also noticed the cool, funky, soulful background music that was loud enough to enjoy, but not too loud to talk over. 

Our server, Isaiah, was pleasant and quickly started chilling the wine that we brought. 
He was very comfortable discussing menu items including ingredients as well as preperation procedures. 
He wasn't shy discussing his favorites and was very helpful steering us in the right direction as far as ordering the right amount of food. 
A basket with 5 generous slices of warm sourdough arrived at our table accompanied by perfectly softened butter. It was heavenly. 
I told my wife before we ate anything else that the Chef could make a living just selling this bread. 
Our appetizers arrived in a timely fashion and we dove right in.

The Pork Belly was hot with a touch of crispness. Topped simply with a grapefruit supreme and crushed pistachios. We all liked this one a lot, even my friend who loves bacon, but not pork belly.  YUM !!

The Gnocco Fritto is Fried dough accompanied by an incredible homemade ricotta cheese and slices of prosciutto.  I made myself a little open faced sandwich and enjoyed how the flavors all played well together. 
All 5 of us devoured our portions as if we'd never eaten before. 

The Veal Tartare was My dish.
Everyone at the table including my 9 year old,  including my wife, who doesn't eat veal, including my friend,  who doesn't eat raw stuff tried it. They didn't dislike it,  but they graciously let me finish it and I graciously accepted.  Perfect balance of acid and fat in the Tartare.  Truffle was present, but not overwhelming.  I could eat those homemade crackers all day long. 

The Antipasti Board rounded out our 1st course.
My wife loves to order the meat and cheese board when she sees it on a menu and this one didn't disappoint.  

On to the  pasta course !!!!
We decided to try the small portion of all 5 and I can honestly say that we enjoyed them all. 

The gnocchi was lighter than air.
The cavatelli was hearty and toothsome. The kids tried escargot.  
The pappardelle with shreds of braised lamb and a hint of curry was popular with everyone at the table. 
The Mushroom Ravioli with Foie Gras knocked everybody's socks off.  My 9 year old daughter ate one and insisted on her own order of Mushroom Ravioli. 
Lastly, and probably my favorite if I could only choose one pasta dish, it would be the Bucatini with a delicious tomato sauce enhanced with smoky cheese and meat . Hearty, rich and smoky to the last bite. 

At the onset of our feast, we decided that 2 entrees would be plenty for the 5 of us to split, and everyone seemed most interested in the Braised Pork Shank. So we got 2,  even though we took most of the second one home. It was falling off the bone tender and just as flavorful. My son loved the polenta so much, he wanted to order a side to take home.

It was Father's Day and my Wife's Birthday, so we couldn't skip dessert.   Homemade Raspberry Rhubarb Sorbet and Cappuccino Semifreddo

Overall,  this place was a hit !! My friend who joined us for dinner has spent time living in Italy and was equally impressed with everything especially the homemade pasta. 
Since my wife and I are Chef's we try not to be overly critical yet we have certain expectations, especially for ambitious restaurants. This place filled up quickly and the kitchen seemed to keep pace efficiently.  The food arrived hot and seasoned properly, but nothing was "salty".  Offering homemade bread and pasta dishes along with imported ingredients is incredibly ambitious just not overly.
Remember to bring cash . Parking lot directly across cost $13 for 2hrs+ 

Photos to follow.

About 2 years ago, my cousin recommended Tom's DimSum in Media. My wife and I took our 7 and 12 year old kids and we loved every bite. It was cramped, hectic and the servers seemed confused, but delicious and worth returning. 

After a few dozen visits over the next year or so, we noticed that a new DimSum restaurant was opening 2 doors down from our favorite!! Turns out that the Chef and owners had a "split" and the Chef decided to open his own place 2 doors away from the original.  Whether you are familiar with the lawsuit or not doesn't matter.  

Tom's Dimsum Mania is more spacious, less noisy and the larger tables are big enough to accommodate many plates. 

The servers were attentive throughout the night and the kitchen efficiently pumped out hot fresh food on a Sunday night when the restaurant slowly filled up to 3/4 capacity.  

The original Tom's only offered hot tea and water. 
Tom's  dimsum Mania offers Mango, Strawberry, Papaya-Banana and Avovado Smoothies which are all on point, as well as homemade iced tea and canned sodas. 

The most important part of this comparison is the food. Considering that the Chef is the same, the recipes are exactly what we have been enjoying for the last few years, with a few additional items. 
The always delicious scallion pancakes are now available with cold beef or pork and pickled vegetable. Kinda like a scallion pancake sandwich. Mmmm  !!!
We also gobbled up the new Tom's Spicy Dumplings (3per)
Spring rolls were hot crispy little 2 biters (2 per)
We love the Hot and Sour Soup and the other soups are fresh and flavorful. 
And of course many, many steamed pork soup dumplings.  Consistently rich, unctuous broth soaked pork mini meatball wrapped perfectly in dumpling dough.  I dream about these tiny packages of heaven !!! 

I must tell you that we finished our meal and walked over to the original Tom's and there wasn't one customer in the entire restaurant.  Hmmm.

My wife and her family have been enjoying Mike food at Cafe Riviera for many years.  We were excited to hear about his newest endeavor Pizzeria Metro. 
We checked it out a few months ago and we weren't disappointed. 
Before I continue, I must explain that from '95-2002 I worked in 2 extremely busy kitchens that featured  a wood burning oven (my favorite station). So I was stoked to get seated close to the action.  
Ambitiously,  the only cooking source in the restaurant is that wood oven.  So that means all appetizers and pizzas are put together and wrangled by the same guy, who I found out later is the owner's son. 
The food bar was empty but looks like a great set up for interacting with customers and perhaps young aspiring chefs.  
We ordered cheesy tots , wings, mac and cheese,  White pizza and the special pizza with Brussels sprouts and  prosciutto and Caesar salad. 
Everything was tasty. I prefer oven Roasted wings to fried and these really hit the spot.  
Special pizza was my favorite. 
My only criticism is that I would eat all of the crust if it wasn't so dark. Maybe 20-30 seconds less cook time. 
We'll be back !!!!!

Family wanted Lobster Rolls so we tried Trolly Square Oyster House. 
Now, I'm prepared to spend some $$ on lobster rolls, but these were incredibly disappointing for $26 each. The amount of lobster was ok. The Texas toast they use  was ok.  There was so much onion chopped up and mixed in that it was like eating onion sandwiches couldn't taste the lobster at all. Inedible waste of $78 dollars.   The only reason I gave 2 stars is because the clam chowder was good and had plenty of clams.  My daughter's crab cake sandwich was pitiful.   Nothing special here.

I've written about Dim Sum Mania before, but not since Covid.  I just wanted to say that the online ordering system is great .  Our order has been correct every time. And yes, it's still just as delicious.  
We usually get Hot and Sour soup (the best in the area). Chicken on a stick, MANY Soup Dumplings, Tom's Spicy Dumplings,  plenty of Scallion Pancakes  (Original and Stuffed with Pork), Spicy Chilled Noodles . All on point and that dipping sauce is BOMB  !!

This place is great and I don't even drink.  My family of four get take out from 2SP at least twice a month.  We usually get the Foie Gras Burger with arugula and fig jam on brioche bun.  The Brussels Sprouts app is delicious.   Fried (not breaded) till almost crisp and tossed in a soy glaze. Served with an awesome Sriracha Mayo.  The loaded nachos are my kids favorite.  Pulled Pork Sandwich is very good too.  I'm  alcohol free, but their beer  selection is pretty strong as well. 
Sad they took scrapple fries off the menu.

My family and I have been enjoying the food from Harry's Savoy for years. We had our son's Bar Mitzvah  service and party at Harry's as well, which far exceeded our expectations.  
But I'm writing this review specifically about their Lobster Rolls. 
I had a hankering for Lobster Rolls on Easter Sunday and realized that Harry's was running a limited Easter menu which didn't include Lobster Rolls. 
So , we decided to try another restaurant that offered them and were severely let down. (See my other review).   
A few nights ago we ordered takeout from Harry's with Lobster Rolls, Crab cake salad, and Clam Chowder and everything was delicious !  
Most importantly,  the lobster was fresh and simply dressed with some mayo, lemon, celery.  Plenty of Lobster meat on every sandwich. The seasoned fries were perfect as well. 

The Clam Chowder is rich and creamy with lots of clams. 

Anyone who's had the Crab Cakes from Harry's would agree that they are hands down, THE BEST ! 
There's some "filler" , but just enough to hold the HUGE clusters of colossal crab together.  
Salad was fresh with my FAVORITE  Creamy Garlic Herb Dressing which is also great for dipping your fries in.
 
Chef Mike, Manager Judy and their  crew really made my night. 

But the most important thing about Harry's, or any other restaurant for that matter, is consistency. And 
Harry's Savoy nails it every time. 
I'll post photos next time.

If you're anywhere near this place, stop what you are doing and GO NOW !!! 

You can get a medium size with 2 different scoops.  
We tried....
Espresso/ Mint Chocolate Chip
Banana/ Strawberry 
Oreo / Nutella 
Peaches and Cream/ Cheese 

All deliciously rich and creamy top notch ice cream. 
We got a few popsicles for the freezer. Definitely be back soon. 
Very streamline ordering . Line moved quickly.  Gonna try the tacoria next door on our next visit.

I'm updating my review from a 4 star to a 5 star review.  Our last takeout order was perfectly executed as well as delicious. 
We loved the meatballs and the pizzas were excellent.  Got a Bianca with pepperoni,  Mushroom and Carmelized Onion,  South Philly Stromboli and the Wilmington Sandwich with prosciutto,  roasted red peppers... All delicious !!! Can't wait to get this for my staff on Tuesday for lunch !!

Officially our first dining out experience since Covid. Il Granaio gets it right every time !! Their small menu is a testament to the perfect execution. They handled our Father's Day party of 7 with ease. We got 3 courses and the timing was just right. We didn't feel rushed, yet we didn't wait for any of the food to arrive. The food was exceptional, hot and seasoned.
Ribeye special was on the mark. Pork Cheeks and Gnocchi are always my daughter's goto. Seafood Special with pasta was outstanding.  Stuffed Pork Chop and Veal Parm were on point. Don't miss the Polenta Appetizer,  or the Pulpo (Octopus). Desserts are just as consistent and delicious as the apps and entrees. Lemon Cake, Tiramisu,  Cheesecake  YUM !!

Did you ever get so excited after your 1st experience at a restaurant that you not only couldn't wait to go back, but also wanted to tell everyone you know about a new "hidden gem"? 
I've been thinking about trying this breakfast/lunch place Two Birds Cafe since they opened in 2019. I finally got to take my family today for brunch. All I can say is WOW, just WOW !!
The four of us split a slice of Crumb lovers cake and a cinnamon bun to start our meal.  They were both super fresh and delicious.  
Best cinnamon bun I've ever had !! Not overpowering cinnamon (like most ) and the Icing wasn't too sweet either.  AMAZING !!!
