 The Crumb Lovers Cake was served warm which gave it that "just out of the oven" vibe.
Very nice touch ! 
3 of us got the Classic Eggs Benedict. The eggs were perfectly poached, hollandaise was exceptional with a velvety consistency and lemony zing. So good, I asked for extra !!  I noticed that The "Canadian Bacon" was smokey and way better than average. I asked about the brand, they told me and I can't remember.  But it really elevated the entire dish. 
My wife got the Brisket Omelet which was beautifully cooked and loaded with shredded, super flavorful Brisket .
All of our platters came with potatoes that were enhanced with fresh herbs and perfectly seasoned.  
I forgot to ask what brand coffee they use, but it was noticeably fresh and hot.
Can't wait to go back and try the French Toast, Pancakes and the entire lunch menu. 
Everything was Eggsceptional not even eggsagerating  
Last but not least, the entire staff was friendly and efficient.  So glad to support this local family's small business. 
 Positively our new Sunday brunch go-to ! 
My only regret is that we forgot to take photos.  Maybe next time.

My 11 year old had been to Bubble Shack with my Mother in law a few weeks ago,  and she's been begging my wife and I to go back ever since.  
 We realized that they close at 5pm. so my daughter and I made a trip out to pickup dinner early. 
This tiny little spot in a strip of stores was clean, yet festively decorated.
The hand written menu boards were straightforward.  
 Neverending combinations of Teas (black,green, milk teas), flavors (syrups added to tea..Mango, Blueberry, Strawberry, Banana, Lychee etc. ) , Boba pearls, popping pearls and jellies.  
Today My daughter got  Strawberry Milk Tea with Strawberry popping pearls and lychee jellies.  
I got Iced Vietnamese Coffee for me and my son.
Both were on point.

Now for the food. The pork and veggies springrolls were crisp, fresh and tasty They were served with a homemade duck sauce. 
I got 2 small pork buns , for my kids who ate them before I had a chance to try them. So I guess they were good. 
I also ordered a few BBQ Pork Bahn Mi Sandwiches without jalapeños . 
They were perfect !! 
Fresh shredded carrots,  slice of cucumber, cilantro,  pork. I toasted them at home and added Sriracha to mine .
I love supporting small businesses and we'll definitely be back. 

From the awesome logo, I was convinced that this place must be a franchise.  
I chatted with the person who took my order and she informed me that they were just a small family business.  Hopefully,  they will expand their hours soon. By closing at 5, I feel like they are missing out on a dinner rush. My hunch is it's probably a staffing issue . 
I almost forgot to mention the drink fridge filled with interesting canned beverages such as lychee drink, coconut drink, sugar cane and a coffee drink. 
I grabbed 3 lychee 'cause it's my jawn.

2SP Stacked Nachos hit the spot every time. I get them to go with everything on the side .  Pulled Pork, Chorizo, queso, black beans, salsa fresca, Avocado Crema, fresh jalapeños.   I build them and pop them into the oven for 5-7 minutes. 
Aaaaaand perfection  !
Always fresh, seasoned well and always scrumptious.

5nbkwkrTYbQhubYahtFCxQ.review_text:
Never has a bad experience. Fresh guacamole made at your table with fresh tortilla chips and two side of salsa. Great dinner specials along with drink specials. There is a happy hour and I think lady's night on thursdays. Great out door dog friendly patio. Open in house seating and bar. Several tv's at the bar area.  Casual attire and good customer service. I really enjoy this place. 
Yummy yummy!!
Love the beer menu and out door seating area. Never had a issue with any of my food orders and love the bread pudding!! Must have. Very casual atmosphere and live music on the weekends.

Fast friendly service. Fresh bread and meats or sliced to order. I had the steak and cheese sub, so yummy! One of the best steak and cheese subs I have had ever. The steak and cheese is the sub they are known for.

Great restaurant. Not overly priced and very satisfying portions long with food. Customer service is worth the four stars so far. Outside seating area is dog friendly. Plenty of seating, tables are small so a three seater table is a tight fight. Fries where searved with two dipping sauces. They serve a spicy ketchup and a very yummy white sauce...didn't find out what it was but I 'recommend trying. Restaurant is worth trying

This is has to be one of their best locations. Exceptional service. A few years ago I requested donations for my daughters PTA fundraiser and was able speak to a supervisor with out a problem. 
Employees recognize public service workers with discounts or beverages.
Family owned and operated cafe. Delicious yogurts with a large selection of yummy treats to add to every yogurt. Also serving a light cafe style menu- salads,wraps,and sandwiches.
Friendly staff members. Baggers help you out to your vehicle & unload your groceries. I always want to tip very clean store.
2nd best location and a busy location as well. Clean store located near the FedX store.friendly staff. They were out of grill cheese sandwich so I was a little disappointed but good craft sodas

Very busy location during lunch and dinner hours. Casual attire with plenty of seating both indoor and out. Week day happy hours,burger specials during the week as well. Great diner idea after a long day. Yelpers receive a 50% appetizer coupon for check in. 

Near had a problem with customer service! Very friendly & helpful staff. Clean bathrooms also.

Great location. Open seating plan. Menus posted clearly over cashier station. This is there second location in the Tampa Bay area. I believe it's family owned and operated. Recipes are family recipes and very delicious. I ordered the ropa verda sandwich & was very pleased. They serve breakfast,lunch, and donner items. Sandwiches are served with chips or fries. The fries are very yummy.

Little Greek hosted a school spirtit family night at one of the Tampa locations. My daughter and I placed a take out order to show our support. While I was waiting for the food I checked in & received a first time drink on the house. Of course I cashed that in. The restaurant was busy from all the kids and their families & the size of the place as well. There were outside seating available but not much. Maybe three tables. 
Our order was fairly large & when it was time to collect & go home for supper. I asked the man if I had everything because I was surprised my whole order for into one bag. I was told everything was correct. Sounded good to me. So we left. 
When I got home & started to distribute meals to everyone I noticed I was missing food. I was not very happy with this finding so I called the restaurant. 
I do not remember the man's name who answered the phone but he was polite. I explained what happen to find & I return to correct the problem tells me he will deliver our order & gave me a free Greek salad. 
For this kind professional gesture I had to give them a 5 start review!

fun modern clean line decor. Has a tv with both booth and tables seating. Several yummy favors along with tons of toppings to choice from. Waffle Bowls and cones, fresh cookies, and fruits. Friendly staff, helpful and welcoming to customers.
Clean bathrooms. Lots of happy cows every where and you can buy a happy cow shirt or other items. Great location.

This is a small location on cross creek in new Tampa. The place is conveniently located next to the Mobil gas station in the small shopping mall. 
There are a few tables and booths to dine and there menu is fairly large. 
I have always had pizza from this location and nothing else but I am always satisfied with my service and product. 
Daily specials are offered for lunch and i think there are a few coupons circulating some where. 
The chicken Mediterranean pizza is wonderful. Plain cheese pizza is great to. The crust is crispy with a soft inside. It's stone baked and so yummy good. Sauce is satisfying not to tomatoey with just the right amount of spice. The order time is not long and all pies are made fresh to order. I can't say enough about this place so far. It's the too go stop for a great New York style pizza.

This is a outdoor pet friendly mall with a number of great restaurants and top named stores. Wiregrass mall offers and fresh farmers market very first Saturday of the month, junior and adult cooking classes @ William Sonoma's and a number of other events monthly. 
Mall is pet friendly and most restaurants in the mall are pet friendly as well. So you have a family pet friendly environment for every one to enjoy. There are pet clean up spots located threw out the mall area so you can keep things clean. 
I would recommend this place to everyone

I would say this place is a great casual first date location. Great drink menu and starter appetizers. Outside seating available with a full bar. Inside area with British decor, super cute. Clean bathrooms a plus. 
Menu options where spot on. I wanted to try a little bit of everything and had a hard time selecting. This is when your friend, date, coworker, family member will be of great assistance. I would recommend this location and decently venture back out that way.

Acai Bowls are not a disappointment. Another great casual, fun, no expectations first date location. This juice bar is located in a shopping mall that is in a residential area..little weird. Fresh ingredients used in all smoothies and acai bowls. No outside seating provided. Large indoor seating area. Great customer service. Nice place to try.
Always clean and friendly baristas. Experienced first Dirty Chai Latte and have been hooked since.

Homemade breads and pastries so delicious. I order the almond chocholate dipped crescent moon but can't finish one.. Cause I don't want it to end onr of my first Germany bakery visits when I moved down here to the bay area.

This place is now named Zio's but still owned by the same family. I have enjoyed this Italian delicatesa for many years. The cold subs are amazing and a full sub can easily feed two adults comfortably. Stuff bread is another great meal. The portions are large and pricing is great for the quality. They have italian cookies and a small grocery area.

6-0FuiHh5SBgnbK_YduupQ.review_text: Went here on a Friday night with three friends. Booking was easy and done only 15-30 minutes beforehand. Pleasant ambience: no annoying or loud music and the decor was understated. Jovial waitstaff. Grilled calamari was perfectly cooked. The mushroom appetizer had great freshness and earthiness. Veal chop was perfectly cooked, as was the gnocchi and lobster ravioli. Excellent prices. Will return for sure.

Very crowded on weekends and had difficulty seating us without reservations, which is hardly their fault. Serve is good but food is very overrated. Drums of heaven (stuffed chicken wings) were interesting, and packed with flavor and texture. Onion bhaji was light, crispy and seasoned perfectly. Most interesting thing I ate was dahi avocado chaat, which was delicious. Sorry to say the main courses were disappointing. Lamb biryani was hardly a biryani at all as the rice and lamb were cooked separately. The chicken tikka masala was totally forgettable, as was the lamb dakhsiki and fish kotmiri. All ingredients are very fresh but portions are paltry at these prices.

Solid, fresh, dependable. Not much more to say. Guac is extra, as you know, but is sort of uncalled for in a bowl anyway. Chicken, steak and carnitas are always perfectly seasoned. I've started to go for simplicity with just double rice, beans, lettuce and double meat, and honestly I prefer that to the mushy confusion of flavors you get when you order everything.

Awful experience here. I go to steakhouses to have steak cooked perfectly to my specifications. That's why I spend the money. It's not to stare at a robotic mouse head or to hear Taylor Swift blasting on the speakers. It's to eat. And this place, like all the other two-bit chain steakhouses, just doesn't get that. I guess it's my fault for going. I could have forgiven all the tacky shit -- after all, I did sign up for it when I walked in the door. But what I can't forgive is paying $25-30 for a ribeye that was not cooked to order. I asked for medium rare and they gave me a completely "black and blue" steak -- not cooked at all. It was amateur night. I told the waitress who seemed to have no idea what I was talking about, as she, like the chef, probably thinks that "medium rare" means an uncooked piece of meat. The manager came over and offered me a free desert. I wasn't interested. I will not be back.

Simple, no frills, to-the-point, and most importantly, delicious. Great place to stop in for lunch. They are quick and bring the food right to your table. The ingredients are fresh. You can't go wrong with any of the cheesesteaks here.

Decent diner. Not a bad place for your run-of-the-mill breakfast fare. You can't really go wrong with their eggs. However, I would really stick to that and not get too adventurous since they are capable of producing "slop," as another reviewer wrote. The salads are hardly fresh, the pasta is never al dente, and everything is always slathered in too much sauce.

Great place to go in a large group. Dan dan noodles are not dry at all and are full of spiciness and porkiness (two of my favorite things in the world). The fried fish is wonderful, as is the garlic chicken and cumin spiced lamb. I would recommend coming here in a large group so you can really sample the menu. Can't wait to go back.

I have been here two or three times and I'm never disappointed. The seafood is absolutely among the best in the area. I would come here for the oysters alone. I usually get the fish of the day, which has been branzino the last couple of times I went. I've also tried their dover sole which is equally delicious. And of course all their pasta is perfectly al dente and they don't drown it in sauce. I have to say they know what they are doing and that makes it worth the money. My only drawback is that it can sort of be disorganized at the front of the house. Last time I went they seated several people before me who had arrived later. But when I pointed it out to the hostess she was very gracious and that more than made up for it. I will definitely return.

Came here in a large group and went for one of the BBQ options with the food grilled right there on your table. It was a lot of fun, but nothing exceptional. Good vegetarian options as well. Slightly on the pricey side.
Probably the best pizza in an area which, let's face it, just doesn't have great pizza. I haven't tried the pasta. The chicken parm is great, and so are the cheesesteaks. The staff are very friendly.

One of my favorite restaurants in Philadelphia. I came here in a group of 4 during restaurant week and was just blown away. A very memorable evening. The appetizers were probably my favorite part of the meal, especially the escargot and fishermans style poached egg with taragon cream, which was so wonderfully simple and complex at the same time.The foie gras was solid, but a little boring. The main courses did not disappoint. I had the beef cheek bourginon, my friend had the duck confit with white beans. It was all spectacular. The wine list was solid too. The ambience was friendly and romantic, but not stuffy. Definitely the best bistrot style French food in Philly as far as I can tell.

Really solid place. Delivery is fast and reliable. Chicken shwarma is their star player -- perfectly seasoned and juicy, good to the last bite. Portions are generous and sides aren't bad either. The falafel is green, which shows that they are serious, know what they are doing, and aren't poseurs. The lamb kebab could be better seasoned and less overcooked, but whatever. You won't really get better around here for this price.

So much better than the overrated obnoxious El Vez across the street. I came here on a weekend for a friends birthday dinner. It was delicious. The mango guac was a good opener. My favorite was the slow roasted pork shoulder in banana leaves. What a sexy dish. The pork just broke loose and just exploded into a wonderful frenzied flavor dance in my mouth. The braised short rib with egg was great also (I'm an egg slut). Portions were generous and great to share. The zucchini and squash tacos were very inventive and fresh and lively.

Unfortunately I have to give this place only two stars. I have been here many times. Let me start with the buffet. It is hit or miss. They do occasionally have interesting dishes like keema peas and eggplant. But their chicken tikka masala is so watery. Their chicken korma is also extremely watered down and lacks any sort of korma cocunut scrumptuousness. I came here and tried the lamb biryani, which I use as a bench mark for quality. It was awful. After that I decided not to return. It is the more expensive of the two Indian buffet options in the immediate area, and honestly, not the better in my opinion.

What can I say about this place? I'm in love. If I could marry a restaurant in Center City this would be it. Humble, sweet, delicious, reliable, down-to-earth, direct, cheap but cheerful. No frills. No obnoxious hipster telling you "that will be 45 minutes" so you can eat some ridiculous skillet full of overcooked scrambled eggs and recklessly seasoned potatoes. You will never want to eat another dunkin donuts breakfast sandwich again after you see what they do here. The simpler you go here the better. The bacon and egg sandwich is two perfectly cooked over-medium eggs with bacon on wheat or white toast. What more do you need in life? And it's $3.15! Are you kidding? I am in love.

Absolutely delightful place. The proprietor is a very sweet Indian woman with a warm smile. The food is superb, easily the best Indian in the area. The lamb korma is rich, creamy, luscious, tender, and generously portioned. The chicken tikka masala is equally good. You can tell all the ingredients are fresh. The meat is cooked perfectly. It's a no-frills place. Much better than Indeblue in my opinion. It's my go-to Indian restaurant now.

Avoid at all costs. We went on Sunday night. There was a tapas tasting menu. It was horrendous. The dishes were half-assed and completely forgettable. One or two of them was a salad. I don't mind salad in a tapas menu but it has to be interesting, and this one wasn't. There were none of your classic tapas dishes offered, just thrown together crap. At those prices it was outrageous.

Unfortunately they ran out of lamb early in the evening but it was still a great experience. The halumi and hummus deserve their reputations. This place was full of wonderful surprises. All the meat dishes sang-- from the chicken shislik to the kofte to the lamb merguez. Definitely a great atmosphere, warm and cozy.

You can't go wrong here. Get the soup dumplings. They will fill you with warm crab and pork loveliness. Always pleasantly surprised when the bill comes. Not sure about the entrees but you can't go wrong sticking to the dim sum offerings.
I want to give this place 3stars because the staff can be obnoxious and it's so hard to get a reservation. But the food is heavenly. Excellent pizza and some of the best pasta in the area.

The only circumstance under which I would give one star is rude service. It takes away from everything. The server was short with me, refused to give any sort of recommendation, kept me waiting after I told him I was ready to order. The whole night he is ignoring me and then asks me later where I am studying, assuming I'm a student, perhaps because I carried a backpack in there with me. Last I checked, that is no crime. I told him I'm not a student, I'm a doctor at a local hospital, and he looked flabbergasted. But the point is that even if I'm a student I deserve more respect than I was shown.

I was hoping the food would save the day, make up for the abuse. It didn't. The octopus was completely underseasoned, perhaps even unseasoned. It had a very strange texture to it as well -- a slight crunch followed by a very chewy center. Octopus should be tender and this wasn't. The main dish was Bronzino, which again, lacked in both flavor and texture. Completely forgettable. For the first time ever I almost asked for my money back. By far my worst dining experience in Philadelphia. I won't return, and I hope you don't either.
Yuca fries are delicious, so is the fat pig, but the sauce tastes a little odd, almost synthetic. It's very pricey. I'll be back for sure. My friend got the shrimp taco and was not impressed.

This is a decent place and I'm glad it opened. I've been a few times now and each time I've left happy. Although it is quite expensive. The last time I got the ravioli which was quite oily and had a good flavor, though the texture was quite homogenous and the portion was skimpy. The time before that I got the meatloaf which was scrumptious. My friend got the fried chicken which was slightly dry. Overall, I'll be back, although there are restaurants in the area offering similar cuisine for less.

Delicious. I actually like that they don't take reservations. It filters out the uncommitted. It also gives you a few hours to work up an appetite. The menu was simple but perfectly executed. I loved the pork Milanese although I did feel the apple accompaniment was quite boring and too acidic. The lasagna was great too. I will definitely be back. This is a great romantic option in the area and it won't break you financially.

This is by far the most overrated establishment in Center City. I never tire of shaking my head in disgust and pity at the droves of clueless brunchers who insist on subjecting themselves to the elements for the greasy slop served up here. The dishes are horrendous and lack any thought. All the Benedict dishes follow a similar pattern: poached eggs,  a bread or pastry soaked in butter, an overseasoned overcooked piece of meat, and a wallop of creamy "sauce" that coagulates in front of your eyes. The prices are outlandish, especially the cocktails. Seating is a nightmare. You will leave feeling like someone shot you in the stomach.

I was expecting a lot more. I came here early evening on a Saturday. It is BYO which is good. We started with the cold appetizer sampler -- wouldn't have been my first choice but my girlfriend wanted it, so okay. I was very disappointed immediately by the solitary dolmades on the plate. The various dips were nothing special at all. The hummus was very lackluster, and to be honest I'm suspicious that it came from a large store bought tub. I followed with the roast lamb. Again, disappointing. It was well seasoned, sure, but so dry and overcooked, which is a sin with roast lamb. I am actually wondering if it was tossed into the microwave given that it came so fast and it was early in the evening. The server was quite nice but the food was disappointing so I wouldn't recommend.

I went back with a group of friends. The manager reached out to me after the above review. They were very conciliatory which shows they care about pleasing their customers. That alone gets points. The food was much better this time around as well. Best thing I had was the Philly cheesesteak spring rolls. They were just scrumptious. The tagliatelle bolognese was good but too much sauce for the amount of pasta and it wasn't perfectly al dente. Steak was great, so were the scallops.

I use this place a lot. Obviously it's overpriced, as everything is in Center City, but not outlandishly so. Definitely good if you're in a fix. The meat is completely unaffordable so I don't even go there, and forget about the cold cuts. But for produce and dairy it's not bad.

One of my favorite places to order out from in Philly. The lamb kebab is perfectly seasoned and cooked to perfect temperature. It drips with goodness and melts in your mouth and yes I am getting horny thinking about it. The chicken samosas are the neat crispy triangular kind, not the crumbling overstuffed monstrosities that Americans are used to. Portions are generous as well. Could not recommend more.

I've only been here once but I still close my eyes and fantasize about the massive pork chops that just tickle you all over. I wish they were a woman so I could date her. The portions are so generous and I love the way the pork leaves its kiss on the rice. The pork spring rolls are definitely good as well. This place is my new pork mistress.

Love this place and you will definitely get some here. It's a little hipster with the books and deep chairs but in an awesome non-obnoxious way that is a great change from the overblown beaux arts establishments wth their towering Corinthian columns. You feel like you're in some happening living room but it's just you and your date. Then the food comes and it makes you happy to be alive and have the money to afford this stuff. Will definitely keep this at the top of my list for special occasions in Philly

This place is like walking into the ambassadors ball. Very grand and actually a little grandiose. I guess there's a time and place for that. It's not cozy at all but makes an impression and of course I can't complain about the steak which is as perfect as it should be at those prices. I have been 3 or 4 times. There is a good wine list but for the love of god don't come here with an expensive date because you'll blow a mortgage payment

The brunch is a good change from the monotony of eggs Benedict that has conquered this city. The omelette is on point and I guess $15 is reasonable. It's a fun place to sit outside and slurp down oysters and people watch and make creepy faces at the rittenhouse yuppies and get drunk, so yeah I do like that aspect of it. It's cozy and you can get a steak or lamb chops at 11 pm which is not easy in this town. It's not the best French food in philly but more than serves its purpose - would give 4.5 stars if I could.

This is hands down the best Korean restaurant in the area (including Philly) and one of the best restaurants in the area period. The one reviewer who gave it 1 star is clearly an amateur; anyone who judges a Korean homecooking establishment on their miso soup should be expelled from Yelp. Also, who orders chicken bibimbap? The food here is truly special because it comes from the heart. This place is the vision of its owner and you taste it in every dish. The katsu, galbi, pork dolsot and jjingae are unmatched. The owners cuts no corners. She is back in the kitchen cooking all day and everything is homemade from scratch. So don't come here if you want to be in an out in 5 minutes. Every dish is fresh and the flavors are deep and soulful and will temakn in your heart long after you leave this place. If you are a the type of person who wants to come here on a work lunch break and order a miso soup then save yourself the time. But if you are someone who knows Korean food and appreciates its subtleties, then this is your ultimate destination. Cannot recommend it enough.

I grew up in London so this type of food has a special sentimental value for me. I was looking for a nostalgic fix, and got it, more or less.
The sausage roll was savory and satisfying, though a little buttery. Definitely a full course, not a snackable treat. The mince and onion pie with mash was probably my favorite. It warmed the cockles of my heart. I didn't get that tear-jerking jolt back to my childhood in Croydon, but it did strike some happy reminiscent notes. Drawback is that it's quite expensive; this type of food is supposed to be fuel for the working man, and at these prices it's sort of a bourgeoisie hipster curiosity, instead.

Great bar during the day if you just want a place to relax and have a cheap drink and watch the game. It's a nightmare on the weekends. The bouncers must literally be recruited from pirate ships and look like they spend most of the day sniffing glue. I'm not sure I've ever met a bouncer I like but here they are particularly reprehensible.

This place was unbelievably good. I understand the five star rating. I don't think I've ever had chicken so perfectly seasoned. This place does every little thing really well. I ended up scooping up rice and beans with my fingers and licking them dry.
One of the best sushi places in the neighborhood. The fish is fresh, prices are good and they deliver. Just a solid sushi restaurant with no frills.

Burgers are delicious. They have that famed crispy crunchy texture. My favorite is the smoke shack. Fridays are pretty decent as well. However it can be Mayham in there between all the bros and tourists. I try and avoid it at peak hours. Plus the seating is not comfortable. But I will return over and over because the burgers are that good.

Burgers are delicious. They have that famed crispy crunchy texture. My favorite is the smoke shack. Fridays are pretty decent as well. However it can be Mayham in there between all the bros and tourists. I try and avoid it at peak hours. Plus the seating is not comfortable. But I will return over and over because the burgers are that good.

Pretty solid place. The burgers are good, though not quite as craveable as Shake shack, and sometimes cooked a little more than I like - medium means I should see pink. You can get an egg on them though which obviously makes anything awesome. Even though the burgers aren't top tier ; this place makes up for it with comfy seating, super friendly staff and all around good vibes. And the milkshakes are awesome. And beer.

I have been here twice so my review is based on a composite of those two experiences. I first had the seafood mixed grill. The shrimp and scallops were quite good, and the portions are quite generous. Unfortunately the salmon was overcooked to my taste. The second time I got the rainbow trout which was also overcooked. The service was excellent on both occasions. I couldn't have asked for better there.
Definitely the best croissant in Philly hands down. Metropolitan does not compare. They have captured the essence of the croissant which is the most important test of skill of any baker.

This place is pretty good food but for the love of god do not order delivery from this place. I have spent the last three hours trying to get my order to no avail. They are completely hopeless. What's worse is that their phone number went straight to a busy signal every time I tried calling. Save the aggravation and get reliable delivery from one of the many other Indian restaurants in the area.

I had the chicken with eggplant and it was delicious. I could tell the ingredients were fresh. It had the perfect amount of heat. I think this is the best Chinese option in an area pretty thin on good Chinese food. I would highly recommend.

As an Egyptian and an American I can say that this isn't just some of the best middle eastern food in Philly, it's some of the best food PERIODT. 

I came in a large group and sat outside. Despite one reviewers comments, the safety precautions were excellent. Masks are worn at all times. This is a mom and pop establishment, not a Steven Starr chain. Please keep that in mind. 

Now onto the food. It is exceptional. The chicken kabob, chicken shawarma, lamb chops and kofte were beautifully seasoned. You can tell all the food here is cooked from the heart. It just has that special something. I'm biased, because it reminds me of my grandmothers cooking. The portions are as generous as the staff. At the end of the meal the owner came out and asked us if we would like hot black tea. He asked us like we were guests in his home, not just customers. It was a beautiful experience and I will be back again and again.
