For our meals, I had the hangar steak, served with mushrooms, mashed potatoes, and kale, and a side order of beets with orange zest and ricotta cheese. My husband had roasted leg of lamb and a side of "roasted mushrooms galore." We both enjoyed our meals, but again, not my all-time favorite, and the portions again seemed small, especially for the price.

Finally, for dessert, I had the "Petite Cookie Collection," which was a plate of four different mini cookies. And my husband had the raspberry and citrus mousse, which was amazing and very refreshing.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was really neat - you enter via this little courtyard, which is filled with Christmas lights and I'm sure in warmer weather is a really nice place to enjoy your meal. Inside, the building is an old hotel or bank or something, with crazy high ceilings. The decor includes birdhouses, gourds, and farm stuff. We were seated in a banquette in the bar area, where there were four tables along the window. In the wall on either end of the bench, there was a huge metal vent that was part of the original ventilation system of the building. The decorative grates are beautiful, but according to the manager (who apologized to the women on either side of me, but not me, I guess I didn't look cold enough), they do get "drafty." She did keep turning up the temperature on the thermostat, but I was freezing. Overall, it really was a lovely dinner, and I love that my husband surprised me with something he knew I'd like. But would I go back? I'd rather go back to GTC first.

I am not a major chocolate fan, but like most others here, I saw a LivingSocial deal for a half price tour and thought it sounded like a neat idea. I was already familiar with most of the stops on the tour, but figured we'd get some inside information on some of these shops and on the city in general. The day we picked was pouring rain. Our tour group was pretty large, with 15 people, consisting of visitors from the far suburbs and recent transplants to the area. Our tour guide, Jeff, was very! energetic! and excited! about chocolate! We first introduced ourselves and named our favorite type of chocolate, and learned a few facts about the history of chocolate in the region (though all the questions our tour guide asked, my husband and I were able to answer right away). Then we headed off on the tour.

The tour started at the Reading Terminal Market, where we each received a chocolate chip cookie at the 4th Street Cookie Company. I've eaten many a cookie from here, and we didn't learn anything about the company or the Reading Terminal. My husband chimed in that he was always impressed that every cookie he's had from here was warm, despite the fact that there were no warmers in the display (i.e., they're always fresh from the oven). The shop owner looked at him like he'd spoiled some great secret (they really do have warmers?!), and then agreed that yes, they are always pulling out fresh cookies. The second stop was also at Reading Terminal, the Pennsylvania General Store, where we each got a Wilbur Bud and literally a crumb of some kind of chocolate bark. We took a few minutes to browse before moving on.

The third stop was interesting to me because I wasn't aware of it: Marcie Blaine, a chocolate shop inside a boutique called Verde. They had a lot of unique flavors, many of which I would have loved to try, but instead we received small samples of yet another chocolate bark with nuts and pretzels. We ended up buying a couple additional pieces of chocolate to try (the Smoked Bacon one was amazing, but at $2 a piece, it better be!).

Next we went to Teuscher's, famous Swiss chocolate, inside the Bellevue. This was the most interesting stop, because the girl working there had a lot of information to share, but the shop was so small and it was so hot with all of us crowded in there, I could tell everyone was uncomfortable. She actually turned down the thermostat while she was talking, I bet she thought the chocolate would start to melt.

Our final stop was Capogiro gelato, where I have also been many times. We didn't really learn anything about Capogiro or gelato, but we did sample 4 chocolate flavors (everyone passing around a cup and taking a sample with a small spoon). Afterward, the guide accepted tips and everyone split up. Luckily, it had mostly stopped raining by this point, but we had a long, humid hike back to our car at the starting point. I know the route is subject to change, but it would be nice if it were at least planned to bring you back to where you began (there were two stops in the Reading Terminal, why not do one first and one last?).

As others have mentioned, I would definitely have been disappointed if I had paid full price, or had I really been a chocolate lover. It might have been fun if it was a group of friends (they apparently do a lot of bachelorette parties and similar events), because we probably would have enjoyed hanging out and shopping together. As it was, it was an awkward group of strangers who never really mingled and mostly tried to stay out of each others' way. Our guide did a good job, but we didn't really learn anything new. It seems from their web site that they hire mostly actors as tour guides, rather than experts on Philadelphia and/or chocolate. Having actual subject matter experts, rather than people who can follow the script, would probably make for a more interesting tour.

My husband and I took their Cheese 101 class a few months ago, but still hadn't gotten to the actual Tria restaurant, so we decided to come in for dinner to finally try it out! The restaurant is small and they don't take reservations, but we figured we wouldn't have any trouble getting a seat for an early dinner on a rainy Tuesday. Wrong! The place was packed and noisy. We added our names to a list and waited around in the vestibule for a little while before moving to a bar seat where drinks were ordered, and then finally getting a table. Luckily, this gave us plenty of time to examine the menu, so we knew exactly what we wanted to order.

We decided to get a bunch of small plates, and then of course a cheese board. For himself, my husband picked spicy crab-stuffed peppers and a lamb sausage with white beans, peppers, and mint-feta sauce. (I don't really do lamb or sausage, but tried the beans and peppers with the mint sauce, it was very good!) For myself, I chose roasted beets with feta and pistachio herbed ricotta bruschetta with lavender honey - both were awesome. And then I made a kind of last-minute decision and also ordered us the truffled egg toast with fontina fontal, just because it sounded interesting. It was amazing, and I'm seeing after the fact that just about every review here seems to rave about it, so good choice!

Then they brought out our cheeses, and at that point I was beginning to think maybe we'd made a bad decision in ordering so much food. If we go there again, I would probably do one fewer small plate and/or one fewer cheese. But we ended up with four cheeses, which they paired with four different condiments: a brie paired with a truffle paste, Reisling-Washed Sawmill Sleeper with Alagash-soaked cherries (this combo was especially amazing), a gouda with beet jelly,  and Montgomery's Cheddar with apricot honey. As we learned at Cheese 101, Tria's cheese prices are maybe a little high, but you get a much bigger portion than you do on most other cheese boards. So big that, for once, I did not finish all my cheese!

Overall, I was really impressed with the food and the service was great, but I took away one star for the ambiance - crowded and very loud (not just the people, but the music). I would go back, but make sure it's at a slow time of day.

I feel kind of bad about giving this place a less-than-stellar review because my husband had come here for drinks with friends and he was SO excited to go back for dinner with me. He was really thrilled with everything about our meal, but he's a very excited guy. I just wasn't that amazed by anything.

We came for an early dinner on a very rainy Friday night. The decor was nice, maybe a little overdone, but lots of wood, iron railings, heavy furniture, and a giant matador mural.

We were seated at a tiled table upstairs by one of the windows, and handed embossed leather menus. I already knew I wanted to try their tableside guacamole, and the cheese plate. Then I figured we'd get a selection of tapas for dinner. I ordered a white sangria, and my husband had a Diablo Margarita, which featured papaya and habanero pepper. We ended up with the following:
- Guacamole: I love when they make it at your table for you, but in this case the waitress came out with a bowl that already had some salt and cilantro in it, and she just mashed and mixed a couple avocados on top of it. There was no lime, onion, or anything else, and no way to adjust the flavor. I love avocados, but this was a bit bland. I'm also not a fan of their chips - they are very thick with layers that flake apart, while I prefer the thinner, crispier kind.
- Cheese plate: we selected the Queso de Cabra, a goat cheese; Mahon, a very sharp cheese; and Idiazabal, a hard to find smoky cheese. They were fine, but there was such a small amount of each, as well as ridiculously tiny deposits of nuts and things for garnish. I was also not a fan of the chewy bread served with it; again, it would have been better with something thinner. Weirdly, we were not told which cheese was which when the tray was brought out, but luckily we could figure it out, and our waitress came by a minute later and confirmed.
- Patatas Bravas: I was so excited for these, being a huge fan of the ones at Amada. Once again, there was just something lacking here. They were pretty much just a solid, bland cylinder of potato, with a tiny dollop of the seasoned aioli.
- Champinones en Verde: Plate of sauteed mushrooms... My husband is a mushroom superfan, so he loved this; I did not try any.
- Pulpo a Fiera: Octopus with potatoes and hot paprika. Again, my husband loved it, I did not try.
- Chuletillas de Cordero: Two lamb chops with a red pepper sauce. Another one that was just for my husband, which he loved.
- Ancho Chile Relleno: Chicken and dried fruits cooked inside a pepper. Once again, the chicken just seemed bland to me. The fruits were a nice addition, it could have used more of them. There was barely any of the cream sauce. I asked in advance if it was spicy and was told no, but the pepper itself still had a bit more heat than I would have liked.

Finally, we had dessert. I ordered the Tres Leches cake because I cannot say no to a tres leches. It was good, because it has to be, but nothing amazing. Would have been nice to have an addition of strawberries or something. My husband ordered a blood orange sorbet, because he can't say no to blood orange. For once, something with intense flavor!

Overall, it was a nice experience, and the service was mostly fine. However, if you're looking to impress someone with a tapas experience, there are better options. We spent as much here as we would have at Amada in Philly, for less of an experience and worse (in my opinion) food.

I've never been a huge fan of Panera, but this one is convenient to my office and my friends like to go here for lunch sometimes, so I deal with it. Every experience I've had at this location has had something weird about it, and at first I chalked it up to this being a new store and maybe the employees are still getting up to speed, but they've been open for a few months by now, so I expect a little better from them.

The most recent time I was there, one of my friends ordered the Big Kid Grilled Cheese, which is a grilled cheese sandwich with bacon. The first sandwich she was given was not really toasted on the outside, and didn't contain bacon, so they made her another. This one looked toasty and had a couple flakes of bacon, but the cheese was completely raw inside. Finally they made her a third sandwich, which still wasn't completely satisfactory, but she ate half of it because at that point, our table was covered with sandwiches and it was getting ridiculous. There didn't seem to be any manager presence, either.

As for my own meal, they always seem sort of stingy with the salad toppings, but that's probably a Panera thing, rather than a problem with this location.

This place is brand new (as in, just opened yesterday), so I don't want to be too hard on them. It's a really neat concept, however I think RapiDOUGH could use a couple tweaks to really become a place I look forward to going. I tried it for lunch today with a couple friends from work.

RapiDOUGH is all about this sleek, streamlined system of ordering. When you walk in, two tables of iPads are ready to take your order via a custom app. You can either start with a pre-made pizza, or one of their plain pizza or salad bases, to which you can add or remove ingredients. You pay there, program a numbered buzzer, then take a seat, and a staff member delivers your meals when they're ready. The ordering system was a little confusing; everything is done with pictures and icons, there are no words, and it's not always clear what to do next. I'm sure that now that I've done it once, it'll make more sense.

In the spirit of keeping it simple, I guess, all they serve are salads or pizzas (or calzones, if you have your pizza folded in half). I wish there were a little more variety and a little more flexibilty. For example, they could have something for dessert. I'd like to be able to customize my selections, like add extra cheese (the regular cheese, just more of it; you can only add each topping once). And they should definitely have some more unique pizza toppings - if I'm going to pay that much for pizza (the plain base pizza starts at $8 for a 9" pie), I want some gourmet options. How about prosciutto, fig, gorgonzola, and balsamic?

Strengths:
- Pizza was pretty good
- Staff was extremely friendly and helpful
- Service was efficient
- The 3rd Coast Soda was delicious

Opportunities:
- Pizza was just ok
- Toppings are standard
- Staff was kind of all over us - helping to order, explaining the order process, checking on us while we ate
- iPad ordering was little confusing, even for us tech-savvy young people; I'd hate to see my grandmom try to eat here
- Pizzas were not matched up to buzzer number; waiter had to guess which pizza was whose at our table (we each had a buzzer)
- Need a little trash can by the beverage station for straw wrappers and such

I'm sure we'll be back, but I'd like to give them a little while to get into their groove first.

My husband and I came here for lunch while we were out doing errands, using a BOGO coupon his parents gave us after they'd tried this restaurant. Similar to a Subway or Chipotle, you start with your choice of base (roll, salad, or rice bowl) and then add meats and toppings as you move down the line. The employees were extremely friendly and walked us through all the options, even giving us samples of the soups to try with our meals.

I really like the concept and like being able to fully customize my meal. However, the strange array of options could easily leave people feeling overwhelmed and worried they might make the "wrong" thing. At least at a Chipotle, no matter what combination of ingredients you choose, you're going to end up with Mexican food. At ShredWich, there are some things that seem to go together - for example, you could put together a decent pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and a horseradish sauce. But if you just go down the line and choose your favorites out of each category, you could easily end up with a weird combination. And because the most of the ingredients are included in the price, if you choose to forgo something, you may feel like you aren't getting your money's worth. (There are some pre-written "recipe" ideas posted in the restaurant, but even some of these seem kind of strange.)

In general, the food was good, but not mind-blowing, and certainly nothing I couldn't have made for myself at home. I ended up with a white rice bowl topped with chicken, sauteed peppers and zucchini, cold sliced mushrooms, cold roasted red peppers, and avocado lime cilantro sauce. My husband had a sandwich of chicken, sauteed mushrooms/onions/peppers, hot peppers, and barbecue sauce. We got an order of the homemade chips, which were good, but some of them had kind of lost their crunch.

I know this is a new business and they're still making changes, so I'm curious to see how it will evolve. We'll be back to check it out again!

I don't understand all the "like Honeygrow but better" reviews. It's more like a poorly executed knockoff of Honeygrow's model. The ordering app is confusing and badly designed. It's difficult to customize your meal (for example, you can remove ingredients from one of the pre-designed meals, but can't add other ingredients it didn't already come with). The entrees are boring, and the overall selection of ingredients is unexciting. Service was slow (I waited 10 minutes for 2 salads and I was the only customer in there), and nobody said a word to me until they came out to hand me my bag. They only earned these stars because 1) my salad was fresh and tasty, even if it wasn't anything I couldn't have thrown together myself, and 2) the matcha smoothie was good and worth returning for.

Ok, first of all, the pizza is really good! But second of all, the owner, Tony, and all the staff I've interacted with are fantastic. I volunteer for a weekly evening program for high school students, and we're going on five years using Pizza Stop to cater our meals. Tony is flexible, responsive, easy to contact and work with, and the students and volunteers look forward to dinners every week. The quality of the food is always great, and there is enough variety that we can serve anything from finger foods for more informal meetings, to sandwiches, to a full pasta dinner - though usually we stick with everyone's favorite, pizza and a side salad :) Pizza Stop also provides beverages, plates, cups, etc., and they are able to deliver everything to our location, when we need it - the fantastic delivery drivers even carry it into our building and up the stairs!

9VmRAGrRt_y-5XstJVJO7g.review_text: Food was good but the service was awful.  When I mentioned that I'd ordered sausage, the rude waitress grabbed the bacon right off my plate with her bare hand. It was so disgusting to watch, six people waiting for service left the restaurant.

Awful service! A long wait, bored staff who are more interested in texting then serving, espresso ground and packed for two cups but drawn into one  and the list goes on. Outside tables and atmosphere is nice and baked goods smell wonderful but if you want espresso, AVOID THIS PLACE LIKE THE PLAGUE!

Food was good but the service was awful.  When I mentioned that I'd ordered sausage, the rude waitress grabbed the bacon right off my plate with her bare hand. It was so disgusting to watch, six people waiting for service left the restaurant.

This used to be my go to hotel in the city of Brotherly Love but my last stay was like spending a night in the ghetto. Hotel staff woke my wife and I at midnight by pounding on the doors and calling the room phone incessantly. The issue? They'd screwed up by booking us into a suite instead of a single and decided to make an issue of it midnight. AWFUL! Worse, GM seemed to think the solution was for me to simply let the Cro-Magnon enter my room. After 20+ years of faithful Hyatt rewards membership when I called to cancel my platinum level rewards account, the answer was "ok". And that is the state of the Hyatt Nation and one of their marque properties.
No longer open for breakfast :-( and them has changed from upscale deli style with great food to upscale restaurant. Disappointed.
Worst Italian Hoagie in Philly.  If you like a grocery story roll with 6 slices of meat this is the place for you.

Food was decent enough but service was abysmal. My first time here and also the first time I've ever had the owner openly argue with a customer over a relatively benign matter that could have simply been ignored.
Staff are friendly enough but, lets be honest, if you're going to open a place centered around cheese, you'd better have some wicked good cheese. They don't.
Outstanding meal in a lively, upbeat atmosphere. We really enjoyed it and will be back.
Just average.  Pizza crust, while giving all the appearance of a true VPN, was tough and chewy.  Disappointing.

I honestly don't know what all the complaining is about. This is a corner bar. The food is solid, not gourmet, but solid. The beers are cold. The crowd friendly. The service and prices, great. Judge it and accept it for what it is.
Best cafe in Philly! Great espresso and cappuccino, fresh baked goods, farm to table style breakfast and lunch, all served in a tranquil, open setting. You can't ask for more.

C'mon, Nomad! I love your pizza. I really do. I could even somehow find a away to justify the automatic 20% tip (off of the net check BTW not the pre-tax amount) but for that kind of guaranteed cash your waiters had better bring their A-game,. But they simply don't. In case you were unaware you aren't located within the borders of a Socialist State. This isn't Communist Red China; this is America.  We pay for performance here but your waiter staff simply don't perform at the level necessitated by an automatic 20% tip. 

BTW I spent my formative years waiting tables, 25℅ is my minimum, except when I'm being exported. Then it just feels like you're being used. 

Oh, and watch out - Nomad sees fit to still include a tip line so the unsuspecting can toss in an additional 20%. 

Shane on you.  At least kiss me before you try to...
Oh. My. Buddha. This place rocks. May be the best egg sandwich on the planet.  Tiny place with limited seating but eat it on the sidewalk like a dog if you have to. It's that good.

Just ordinary.  Waffles are whole grain which is fine if that's what you want.  But, if I want a waffle for breakfast, out, I'll take it "hold the healthy" - of course that could just be me.  Other than that surprise, the service was slow.  And, I'm not a fan of the steel cups; it changes the taste of the coffee and I didn't see a campfire in sight.

This is THE spot for a cup of Joe and a light breakfast whenever you're in Old City or Society Hill. Place has a laid back, homey, farm-to-table style vibe with plenty of room to stretch out or people watch from the tables overlook mg Washington Square.
A functional, albeit uninspired coffee shop near the hospital. The bagels are small, the eggs basic, the coffee decent.
Meh, following the latest trend, these aren't bakery donuts. They are cake donuts with a variety of sugary confection toppings. Thus, there are zero filled donut options   I prefer bakery donuts.

This place really pissed me off. 

The food was great. The atmosphere, fantastic. 

So, why, then, did I leave with such a sour taste in my mouth? The automatic 20% tip that was applied to the chèque. 

Look, if the management feels their waiters - their employees - provide such consistently outstanding service that a 20% tip should automatically be included, then raise your prices by 20% and pay your employees a reasonable hourly wage. Don't offload this burden to your customers. This isn't a socialistic society; it's capitalistic, we pay for performance. 

As a former waiter I typically tip more than 20% for even average service. Yet I do appreciate the option to tip 10-15% to show my displeasure when the service is poor. 

To make matters worse, a tip line was still included on the check. How many people fail to catch that a 20% tip was automatically applied before they later an additional 25-30% on top of the tithe management has applied?

This is a disgusting and deceptive business practice. You should be ashamed of yourselves. Remove the auto tip or pay your employees more. At a minimum, have your servers tell customers, up front, that their management has decided the customer SHALL pay their wages regardless of how elk they perform.

9gSuVhKyOx3Qn4oI6EQMaA.review_text: I wanted to rate it 3 1/2, but since I had to round down or up, I went up...  Having said that, TJ Flats is solid Mexican food.  Its burritos are filled up with the traditional ingredients - meat, rice, beans, sour cream, cheese, and even jalapenos.  And for those who like to spice up their food, TJ Flats has an extensive sauce bar to choose from.  Also, the wait-staff is super friendly, from the minute we walked into the restaurant until we finished our dinner, the staff checked in on us about 6 different times.  Overall, TJ Flats hits the spot!
Very mediocre Chinese.  You'd be better off eating at Panda Express.  Also, there are very few tables to sit at, it's mostly a take-out place.

Went there for lunch and was pleasantly surprised, as having recently moved to Tampa from Los Angeles, I have been disappointed by the food.  However, I give Ploy Thai 4 stars, not just by Tampa standards, but by good food standards.  The food was very flavorful and the ingredients very fresh.
This is my go-to sushi place in Tampa, though it's in Brandon.  The fish is fresh and the service is unbeatable - 'nuff said!

We actually decided on the restaurant for the outside ambiance, but ended up enjoying the outdoors and the food.  Oystercatchers serves a variety of seafood, as well as, beef and lamb, in a creative and visually stunning way.  The house bread was delicious too - straight out of the oven and very soft.  We had oysters and calamari fries as appetizers, I had the Bluenose Seabass as my entree, and the chocolate lava cake for dessert.  The meal was wonderful from beginning to end!

Ordered take-out from there today, so I can't comment about the restaurant itself, but the food was delicious and had me craving for more!  I ordered the 1/4 slab of ribs.  The meat was nice and tender and I liked that the BBQ sauce came on the side so that it didn't overpower the flavors of the meat.  Good stuff!

This review is only for Sunday Brunch and for $18.95 you get what you pay for.  There was an omelette, stir fry, and carving station.  As well as, sushi, fish, fried chicken, and biscuits and gravy.  So, it's a mix of foods, and nothing is outstanding or awful.  Sitting outside on a sunny afternoon would certainly enhance the meal.  My only complaint is the $6.50 they charged for a cafe latte, a little ridiculous...

While the sushi was good enough for me to return, the service wasn't.  From the waitress to the sushi chef, I was very disappointed by the neglect.  At times, the sushi chef would leave the bar - I have never witnessed that before...  They have a variety of rolls to try, but watch out for the ones with mayo - there's a lot of it.

I would give it 3 1/2 stars.  Also, the restaurant is on Snow, not Swann.

The restaurant doesn't have any extensive menu, but there is plenty of choice between pastas, salads, and steak.  They also have a decent selection of beers and wine.

We had the fish tacos as an appetizer and I ate the Cajun pasta for my entree.  Both, the tacos and the pasta, were flavorful, but the "wow factor" that would make it 4 stars was missing.  My husband and I were unable to finish our pastas, as the portions are pretty significant.  Also, while the wait staff was nice and helpful while present, they weren't as attentive as they could have been.

I may go back if I am in the area, but I wouldn't drive out to the Old Hyde Park Village especially...

Maybe it was just an off night, but I found the BBQ to be very mediocre.  I ordered the 1/2 slab w/ mac and cheese and fried okra.  The meat was really tough, the hot BBQ sauce was off, and the mac too cheesy.  It was my first time eating fried okra and I seemed to like it better than the rest of the meal.  I did try the sausages that came w/ my husband's dinner and those were delicious...  Don't think I'll return though.

Although a chain, Capital Grille sure knows how to deliver good steak.  I had the 14 oz sirloin w/ the Kona coffee rub and ate every last bite even though I was partially full by the delicious Fried Calamari appetizer that is prepared w/ Chinese hot peppers and jalepenos.  We also had the Flourless Espresso Chocolate cake for dessert - another delicious dish!  Also, the waiter comped our bottle of red wine and was super helpful and friendly.  The food and service will definitely bring me back.  So good!

Five Guys is the In N Out of the east coast.  Although the two have a distinct flavor profile, the yumminess and freshness of the ingredients, get you hooked!  Also, the Five Guys fries are tastier than those at In N Out.

I am surprised to read the negative reviews.  We recently moved to Tampa from Los Angeles and have been disappointed by the lack of good Chinese food.  Although Panda doesn't qualify as good Chinese food, whether in Cali or Florida, it is a good back-up when you need to satiate your Orange Chicken or chow mein craving.  While it is odd that chain restaurants can differ in taste from location to location, this Panda outdoes the Panda in the Brandon mall.

I would actually give it 3 1/2 stars...

Similar to Noah's Bagels or Western Bagel, Einstein Bros. serves up many different types of daily baked bagels w/ cream cheese or as sandwiches.  They also serve wraps, salads, soups, and coffees.  While I would return for the Spicy Elmo (bacon, green chilis, spicy red chili cream cheese, and Swiss cheese) egg sandwich on a roasted garlic bagel, the latte was forgettable!

At first I was going to give it four stars, but then I thought about the food, ambiance, and service and realized that I had no complaints.  

I was there on a Saturday night and the place was pretty happening!  The guests and staff were dancing on the tables to a live DJ.  

They have a pretty extensive menu of Greek food.  I had a shrimp dish which came with rice pilaf and sauteed spinach with goat cheese.  The shrimp were BIG and the flavors wonderful.

At last - a quality Chinese food restaurant in Tampa/Brandon!  While I can't comment on the restaurant itself, since we ordered delivery, the food was delicious.  The ingredients were fresh and the food was nicely flavored.  Will definitely be eating here more often, rather than driving the 15 miles to Panda Express in Riverview or PF Changs in Tampa.

While I've never had stuffed crust pizza in Chicago, my standard for deep dish pizza is Zachary's in San Francisco.  Giordano's was good, but it wasn't excellent.  However, what was excellent was the 1/2 price pizza Giordano's offers on Wednesday.  Also, there is no limit on the number of pizzas or the size.  And remember, the pizza will take about 30-35 minutes to come out, so definitely order appetizers if you're hungry.

Grillsmith is the place to be on Wednesday evenings!  Live music (in the patio), $5 appetizers, and half off wines and cocktails.  You can't go wrong!  My husband and I shared the Spicy Thai Shrimp, Calamari, and Sticky Thai Wings (all appetizers).  We also probably liked each of those dishes in that order.

I just got back from eating dinner at Cilantro and being Indian myself, I have no complaints.  The okra (bhindi) was a bit oily, but the chilli paneer appetizer, Kerala fish curry, and goat rogan jhost were all delicious!  And a cold Kingfisher to accompany the food - can't go wrong!  I've found my go-to Indian restaurant in Tampa - will definitely be back for some food from the motherland!
I didn't love it, but I didn't hate it either!  I wish the meat was cooked fresh and there was more flavor to the food - a Subway style build-your-own gyro didn't do it for me!

After a successful Blackjack run, my husband and I decided to treat ourselves to a steak dinner.  Because there was a 2 hour wait, we decided to eat at the bar/lounge within the restaurant and am glad we did. Though the lounge area was more low key than the main dining room, the ambiance was wonderful.  The decor was modern/contemporary and there was a live acoustic band playing cover songs and originals.

Both my husband and I had a 10 oz bone-in filet; his topped w/ blue cheese and mine w/ wild mushrooms.  The steaks were good, but I had ordered it medium and found it to be a tad overcooked.  We also had half a dozen oysters and a side order of au gratin potatoes.  The oysters came w/ the traditional cocktail and horseradish sauce, as well as a shallot vinegarette sauce.  We enjoyed them.  The potatoes were too salty, but good otherwise.  For dessert my husband had the soufflé w/ chocolate sauce and found it to be average.  I had a trio of mini sugar-free chocolate desserts and found them to be delicious!

Although you can probably get a better steak at Capital Grille or Bern's, if you're at the Hard Rock Casino and are looking for good food and a lively atmosphere, Council Oak is a solid choice.

On Monday-Saturday they offer a lunch buffet for $10.  For that price and the quality of the food, you can't go wrong!  With a variety of cold foods like mozzarella balls, seafood, and salad and a variety of hot foods like meatballs, chicken parmesan, and pasta, there is a good sampling of traditional Italian food.  Good stuff! 

Will have to return to check out their dinner menu.

Ended up at El Puerto for lunch because the Laughing Cat was closed.  They offer lunch specials ranging from pastas to churrascas from $10-$15 w/ two sides.  The quality and quantity of the meals are definitely worth the high-ish lunch prices.

The meal is also accompanied with fresh, warm bread straight from the oven and two delicious, flavorful sauces.  

I ordered the churrasca and fried egg (steak and eggs).  The meat was 
so juicy and tender and was marinated for what seemed like the perfect amount of time.  I ate every last bite!  The egg was nothing special and 
frankly didn't need to be there...

El Puerto is a surprising little gem in the residential part of Ybor!

After reading the reviews on Yelp, I was very disappointed with my dining experience at Algusto.  As soon as the waitress came over, we were given our menus and told to hurry our order because the restaurant would be closing.  Within a minute or two, the waitress returned to take our order.  Since I didn't have enough time to peruse through the menu, I ordered the same as my husband - a carne asada burrito.  The burrito was filled with the same ingredients that came as sides - rice and refried beans and was pretty bland!  The only thing I enjoyed was the 
guacamole and hot salsa that we paid for when we ordered chips.  Will 
definitely not be returning!  The search for good Mexican food in Tampa continues...

Ended up here for lunch after attending a wine tasting at the nearby Florida Estates Winery.  

Although it's probably a good forty minute drive to Pancho's Villa from my house, I would definitely make the drive when craving Mexican food, rather than settle for bland and mediocre Mexican food that I have thus far encountered in Tampa!

The restaurant is modest with an extensive menu of Mexican goodness.  We were a party of three and all of our dishes were packed with flavor and fresh ingredients.  Also, the chips and salsa were complimentary, unlike other restaurants in Tampa that nickel and dime you!

Although the restaurant was packed, the service was great, as our waitress was very attentive and our food arrived after a reasonable wait.

I'll definitely be returning!

APNCUvK4nEEt3p9SYIp7Pw.review_text:
For my husband's firs trip to STL with me, he requested Pappy's after seeing them featured on MVF.

We of course ordered the Adam Bomb and OMG! The food is so beyond delicious! The sauces are all so flavorful, rich and complimentary to the courses served. Needless to say there was so much food we had 2 more meals and took some home on the place back to Portland!

I dream of Ted Drewe's....

Unfortunately I live in Portland, Ore and am only able to taste the amazing frozen custard when I visit STL in the summer :( 

No matter how long the line, it's always worth the wait! Ted Drewe's never dissapoints. The service is friendly and fast.

New to the area and in search of our new Chinese place - not sure this is it.

So we live in Kuna, and again are new to the area, but it appears our choices arent overflowing. I'd seen this place on the way home so husband and I decided to give it a go.

In total we ordered the Mandarin Chicken, General Tsaos Chicken, Mongolian Beef, Pork Fried Rice, Chicken Chow Mein & Crab stars.

The Crab stars had great flavor but were under cooked. If they had been fried the right amount of time they would have been stellar.

The fried rice lacked any kind of flavor.

The Generals Chicken was good, it's the battered recipe. However I've definitely had better and as a general statement could have also been more flavorful.

Husband liked the Chow Mein, the Mongolian Beef and the Mandarin Chicken, I didn't try them. He did say the Generals Chicken was the best, which leaves much in my opinion to be desired.

Total for everything came to $55, which for the portions we received is a pretty good deal.

We'll definitely try it again, I hope next time they can bring the flavor :)

What a nice, clean & well stocked little grocery store! 

We just moved to the area, are used to much larger grocery stores with over worked employees and lack of merchandise. 

Glad Ridley's is going to be our new stop for every day basics and essentials.

We had just moved to the area, were STARVING and fell upon this place. Glad we did!!

They had just opened and since they cater to a more beer/cocktail centered crowd they were basically dead - so ok with that!

The interior is fun, industrial and well maintained.

The waitstaff is very friendly, patient with kids and very attentive.

My husband ordered the nachos. Those are some serious nachos! He said they were really delicious, only wished they'd been served on a more fitting plate size wise. One half paying attention bite and you'd be a mess.

I ordered the southwest club. YUMMMM! This is your classic delicious club but with a kick! 

We ordered our three year old a grilled cheese. Huge portion for a kid his age, but good deal!

Overall experience was good, will definitely be back!

Just moved to the Boise area, so glad to find a DB! 

Great staff, excellent coffee!!

I fancy myself a Target regular, in fact when I found out we were moving to the Boise area I google mapped how far I'd be traveling for a Target... 

This is hands down the worst Target I've ever been to, worse than one in Portland that was obvious would be shutting down after the lease termed.

The staff is literally non existent. They also work through you, not around you. 

The shelves weren't stocked well at all, products were in wrong places in a clear effort to make things look fuller than they were. My husband was a merchandiser for years, I'm not imagining this. 

The bathroom though.... I honestly wouldn't have taken the time to write this review if it weren't for the bathroom. I don't think I've ever written this before on Yelp, but WTF!? Last time I checked bathrooms were one of those things that were to be cleaned regularly and God knows for good reason. I don't think I could bet money this bathroom had actually been cleaned in days. The floor was caked in dirt, the trash over flowing, the toilet paper was running out, there was smears of God only knows what on the walls and bodily fluid covered things on the floor. Yuck. 

I realize the area isn't over flowing with Targets, but I can guarantee I won't be returning to this one. I literally gave my son an extra bath when we got home because he sat on a toilet.

Hands down excellent BBQ.

It was a LONG hot day and all my husband and I could think about was BBQ. Since we just moved here we haven't yet gotten our traeger and don't know where to go for grub. Hit Yelp and decided to check this place out. 

Again long day so we ordered take out.

Husband and I couldn't decide what we wanted SO we ordered the Family Feast with a full slab of beef ribs, a whole smoked chicken, 1/2lb pulled pork, 1/2lb brisket, potato salad, baked beans & corn muffins.

Beef ribs, yummmmmmm! So I'm a fan of St Louis style, no competition, but these were very good! Fatty but not too fatty, well sauced, tender and excellent smoke flavor. 

We haven't hit the chicken yet, saving that for dinner tonight 

Pulled pork was some of the best I've had from a non traditional BBQ joint. The flavor was exploding with season and smoke but still super moist! Not an easy accomplishment. 

Haven't had the brisket yet, that's for lunch tomorrow 

Potato salad, ok seriously best potato salad outside of homemade I've ever tasted! I'd go back here JUST for the potato salad. If I didn't know better I'd believe it if someone told me it was homemade! 

Baked beans were stellar! Possibly a competitor to my husband's, don't tell him that though! 

Only thing not great, the corn muffins. Hoping we got a bad batch because with the superiority of everything else it's hard to believe these were as bad as they were. Dry, dry, dry & dry... 

All in all, we will SOOO be back!!!!

Good food, will eat here again but not mind blowing...

For burgers we tried The Classic and The Heat, both beef and all the fixens. The smoked sauce on The classic was good, but otherwise a very meh burger. My husband enjoyed The Heat. 

For fries we ordered The Purple shoestring & Regular cut Russets. The purple had excellent flavor but were quite wet from the fryer, they were pretty messy. The Russets were good, but just your average fry. 

I look forward to trying other things here and really like the concept.

I am so happy to know excellent Pho exists in Boise!! 

Coming from Portland, I was weary about great food selections, but this place is excellent! 

We ordered spring rolls to start. Very fresh and flavorful. 

I had the chicken and shrimp rice noodle bowl. Yum!!! Chicken and shrimp were perfectly cooked and very well seasoned.

Worth the drive and wait! 

Found this place on Yelp, decided to give it a whirl, glad we did! This review is for a take-out order....

For a Sunday, they were very busy, but that's a good sign and worth the wait. Total time for a to-go order was 35min. 

We ordered a feast, I'm 35wk pregnant so no judging! We got an order of the Thai chicken wings level 3 spicy, Red curry with duck level 3 spicy, Pad Thai with chicken no spice, Shrimp salad/fresh rolls and Chicken satay.

The wings and curry were mostly for my husband. He loved the curry, said he ordered due to the other excellent reviews. Level 3 spice wasn't too spicy for him, he said he'd try level 4 next time. The wings were delicious, I had one of these and though they had a kick to me (preggers!) they were very good and didn't burn too badly :) we of course compared them to PokPok but nothing is comparable to PokPok in terms of Thai Chicken Wings... Without such a comparison though, these were very delicious and we will get them again.

The pad Thai was your average pad Thai. I've had better and I've had worse. I will order it again, it's the spaghetti of Thai food after all :) 

The fresh rolls we very fresh, very delicious! I was disappointed they don't come with peanut sauce though. The sauce they come with, an oil vinaigrette type deal with peanuts was very good BUT I am obsessed with peanut sauce and it's not replaceable in my opinion. Next time I'll ask for some.

The chicken satay was for my toddler. He enjoyed them and I had a skewer for lunch leftover and it was very good. The satay did come with peanut sauce, so that made me happy! 

The portion sizes are ridiculous, in a good way! We had our fair share for dinner as well as full sized portions for lunch today. Definitely a great deal. 

One thing I'd like to see changed is access to a menu other than in restaurant. There's no menu on Yelp, their website doesn't work and they don't offer paper menus to go... Please change this!

Came here after our hike this weekend, just what the doctor ordered!!

So I have only had BFC one other time and was not impressed. This experience though 100% makes up for it.

We were a party of 6, 4 adults (2 very pregnant mamas) and 2 3yo. The atmosphere is very accommodating for toddlers, overall family friendly. It was very busy as they also opened up their Waffle side that day, but still a pleasant lunch atmosphere.  

My husband ordered The Heat, all the fixens and beef. He actually never made it to the burger because he ordered a large special fry, I can't remember the name, but they were deep fried in duck fat and tossed in truffle salt - OMG can you freaking say DELICIOUS!!!?

I ordered the Original, minus onion, with a turkey burger and had a side of home style Laura's. My burger was stellar, very moist and well seasoned. The garlic aioli is so yummy, it's also my favorite sauce to dip fries.

My three year old just got a no veggie cheese burger, he ate it all - which in itself says a lot ;)

Great experience, glad we gave it another shot, will definitely come back!

This place makes me nostalgic tummy rumble!!

Ok, if you're looking for authentic off the boat Chinese then move on! If you're looking for flavorful, fried, tacky booths and decor American Chinese then rejoice as you've found the place!! 

Don't get me wrong, I'm a foodie and love me some fancy and authentic Asian cuisine but anyone who can't get down with some fried deliciousness paired with BBQ pork and egg flower soup then we probably can't be friends.

Ordered here for the first time last night, got it DELIVERED! This is huge for me, Portland has NO Chinese that delivers and it's just wrong!!

I'm 37wk pregnant and really just wanted a tub of pork fried rice. We ended up ordering the Special Fried Rice, Fried Shrimp, Fried Wontons, Spicy Orange Chicken and Potstickers. It was everything is dreamed it would be! 

The fried rice was delicious. It was actually fried, which these days seems like impossible to find. I loved the amount of veggies. I would have liked larger shrimp and more pork, but overall tasted great.

The potstickers were also delicious. A tad dry, but I also don't like to dip my potstickers in anything so if you do then it probably wouldn't have been a big deal. The stickers were well cooked, crispy but not chewy or hard. The filling was a well seasoned pork mixture and also cooked thoroughly.

The Wontons were, again, delicious. There were probably slightly over cooked but it didn't take away from anything. The filling was really good. 

My husband ate the Orange Chicken. Not sure how it comes in the restaurant but the sauce came on the side. This wasn't a bad thing at all, actually makes for a less messy transport and you can decide how saucy you want your food :) the sauce is the jelly kind, I know some places differ. I did take a bite, it wasn't too spicy but had a good kick. I thought the chicken was cooked well and the sauce had great orange flavor. The side of rice it comes with is silly though... For an entire order of orange chicken you get less than a cup of white rice. This really should be changed, I did see a previous complaint about it. Next time we will just order more.

The fried shrimp were also delicious, but I mean how can anyone really screw up fried shrimp!? They were cooked well though, the batter was cooked thoroughly and not dried.

Delivery took about 40min and food arrived not only got but the fried stuff still crispy! 

So far, this has made its way to No. 1 go-to quick fix Chinese for us!

Probably won't eat here again....

Hubby and I were stuck at St. Luke's as I just had a baby and we were sick of hospital food. This place was super close and sounded great so we gave it a try. Wish we'd just ordered hospital food...

We ordered the Mongolian Flat read, Hand wrapped potstickers, Louie's Loaded Nachos & Uncle Fu's Fried Rice.

My husband ordered the flatbread & nachos. He was disappointed with both. He said the nachos were ok but barely had any chicken despite the item description stating they're loaded with chicken. He ended up giving away the flatbread after one piece, said it lacked flavor.

I enjoyed the potstickers very much, but they are very rich.

The fried rice has a lot of potential but the meat ruined it completely. I ordered the special, which is a combination of meats. The meat was so salty that I party contribute my recovery swelling from it  and the rice, while basically very good was also greasy.

Our bill came to over $50, definitely not worth overly salted, greasy and food that doesn't live up to its description.

Can't say we'll ever eat here again

What a great place!!

My mothers visiting the Treasure Valley for the first time, and as we're also new, I wanted a place that had great food in a good family friendly environment and that is just this!! 

Came here on a Thursday mid-morning. It was surprisingly busy, but in a good way! The place was full of families and what appeared to be regulars.

Mom ordered a special, had Bronco in the name lol. Basically hashbrowns with cheese, eggs, meat & veggies topped with gravy... Basically the thing breakfast dreams of! She said it was spectacular!

I had the B&Gs. I've had better, but they were by far super yummy! The gravy has excellent flavor, the biscuit is soft, eggs (over medium) cooked perfectly, hashbrowns cooked perfect & the sausage was amazing! 

We ordered the eggs & meat kids plate for my 3yo, great portion sizes and he ate most of it (he is 3 after all..)

Waitstaff very friendly, patient & knowledgable on the menu.

Atmosphere is really great too! It's an open room but isn't too loud, but at the same time some how seems to lesson the loudness that is a three year olds normal inside voice. The decor is simple but cute, chairs are comfortable and overall vibe is very comfortable and relaxed.

For three breakfasts, two coffees & two milks we spent less than $40 with tip, and we're not skimpy tippers! 

Definitely check this place out!

Excellent breakfast!! 

So we tried coming here a few months back on a Sunday and the wait was way too long with kids. We came here this time on a weekday and got right in :)

Both husband and I ordered the Farmhouse breakfast. It comes with eggs, sausage patty, biscuits, gravy & hashbrowns. 

Eggs, cooked over medium, we're done perfectly. The gravy was well seasoned & perfectly thick and tasty. The sausage patty tasted homemade, yum! The hashbrowns were cooked well, both crunchy but also soft, my favorite! 

The only thing I would change was the biscuit, also the reason for the 4 stars. The biscuit was airy and lacked density. I like a buttery, dense biscuit and the only way to describe these is they lacked substance and flavor - I'm glad they were smothered. If I had one of this as a side I wouldn't have eaten more than a bite :(

I loved that they offer flavored creamer for coffee.

Before eating here today, I had lost hope in Chinese food here in the Treasure Valley....

Ok, haven't tried THAT many places, but still!!

I only orders a quick lunch; pork fried rice and spring rolls - yes, I know, VERY authentic choices but I gauge my trust in a random Chinese place with basics!

I was pleasantly surmised. Spring rolls were freshly made and contained fresh cooked veggies and actual whole shrimp pieces. They were perfectly fried.

My friend rice was also extremely fresh! Sautéed veggies and Chinese pork complimented with actually pan fried rice! Rice had that perfect greasy texture from the pork without actually being greasy.

Atmosphere is that of your perfect hole in the wall. Looks like an old Taco Bell on the outside. Didn't spend too much time away from the counter but appeared clean.

Many people get their food to go, they use an old drive thru window for pick ups! I ordered there though.

Service is both fast and friendly. Prices are reasonable and portions are good!

Stopped in for a cup to go...

What a cute little place! Lots of people, but in a great Sunday morning social way. Their food looks amazing, like gigantic cinnamon rolls and scones! 

I was only looking for a cup of coffee though. Ordered a mocha. Simply wonderful!

So this place is amazing and I'm kind of upset I know it exists....

It's close to work. They're fast. They're cheap. Ugh, I'm about to get so fat from eating here too often :(

I ordered the chicken yakisoba. Yummmmmmmm

Noodles, cooked to tender perfection!
Veggies cooked but still had crunch.
Chicken, tasted like it had not only been marinating prior to cooking but also slow cooked for hours.
The dish itself had this wonderful nutmeg like taste to it.

Simply wonderful food!

It was an "eating my emotions" kind of day and ended up here for lunch....

Got myself the one with cookie dough, can't remember the name. 

Amazing. Duh.

Store is clean and well kept.

Staff super nice and friendly

Got room service from Emilio's while staying at The Grove Hotel.

Ordering room service was a breeze! The staff that took my order was very nice, knowledgeable and let me order a dish off the main menu that wasn't listed on the room service one!

Food arrived within 20min

Food comes with all condiments you'd need as well as salt and pepper.

For dinner:
I ordered the Vegetable Pakora, this isn't on the room service menu, and the Kobe cheeseburger. 

The pakora was amazing! It had a wonderful Middle East/Indian flavor to it. The paired hummus was out of this world! The two together, wow. 

The Kobe, although not as fancy as pakora, was just stellar. Well cooked, I ordered it medium well, and added bacon. The tomato jam was really quite a great touch. The brioche bun was slightly over toasted. The french fries were good.

For breakfast:
I used the order form found on my bed, hung it on my door before bed and voila breakfast arrived when I requested it!

I ordered the eggs Benedict with hash browns. Woooooooooow!!! Eggs cooked perfect. Ham perfect. Hollandaise was to die for!

Ok, gave this place another try and SO happy we did!! Our first visit must just have been due to recent opening mishap or something.

Food was really good, I mean this is now our top choice for Chinese! 

Everything had great flavor, was super fresh and our to-go order was processed timely.

So being from Portland I consider myself a coffee lover and feel I have a taste for not only good tasting coffee but also appreciation for good coffee people. This place has both!

Stopped here after church last Sunday. Husband ordered an iced coffee, boooooring, haha but said it was good. I was feeling more adventurous and ordered a Java Chip Granita.... ohhhhhhh emmmmmm geeeeeee! Best part was the price, I felt like we were stealing our coffee!

Service is outstanding.

Ohh and you get a chocolate covered espresso bean. Sold.

Wow, what an experience!

This place was referred to us as a fun experience with excellent food, decided to treat my husband for his birthday.

We made reservations ahead of time but we arrived around 7 and reservations weren't necessary. We were seated with no wait and host staff were very friendly and welcoming.

The restaurant itself is just cool looking. The decor is eclectic and fun but in good taste. The view of the water is quite nice.

Our waiter was very friendly, knowledgeable and attentive. 

We ordered calamari to start. Probably some of the best I've had, and I've had it all over the world. 

I ordered a special pasta, not sure it had a name lol, but it was really good. Had seafood and meat. However, one bite of my husband's steak and I was disappointed I hadn't ordered that.

My husband, as just mentioned, ordered the bone-in ribeye on the rock. Ugh, my mouth is watering just thinking about it. Hands down one of the best steaks we've had, and we are great steak seekers! The steak was gigantic and he tried but ultimately failed at eating the whole thing.

Our night wrapped with a complimentary birthday dessert of a mint cotton candy served on a plate drizzled with chocolate syrup. Wow!

When I first moved to Kuna I preferred Ridleys, but not anymore.

I hate how the store is organized, I don't understand why this Hispanic aisle is with the toiletries and how frozen is clear across the store.

They have little to no produce and seem to not carry items I'm looking for.

The deli is basically always empty or grossly old.

And the prices aren't worth the quality.

I was taken here last weekend for my birthday by some friends and had a blast!

We had reservations, which appeared to be a good idea; 7:30 and the place was packed.

Atmosphere is super cool. Well lit, good music but you can still hear your party.

Service was good, could have been better but was good. 

All of my friends, who had all been before, ordered a version of the coconut chicken. I decided to stray and ordered the fish tacos - wish I had gotten the chicken. They weren't terrible but I guess growing up along the Oregon coast I just have a higher expectation. The sweet potato fries were delicious though and the aoili they're paired with was booomb!

We shared a few pitchers of the coconut mojitos, sooo yummy! Then I had an effin cucumber mojito that honestly stole the show.

I definitely plan to come back, maybe next time go for the coconut chicken (or shrimp!)

This place is a hole in the wall unexpected BLAST!!

My party arrived still semi early (9:30) but before long there was a line down the block. 

The atmosphere is weird but in a good way. It's like a dive bar but younger. 

The music is a mix of old rock and hip hop, stuff that makes everyone have a good time. 

Drinks are great and cheap, I had an assortment from lemon drops to vodka soda to long islands... all good.

(Only downfall for me, and obviously not allowing it to lower my rating since I wasn't directly effected - BUT - one of the waiters took her tray into the woman's bathroom with her. ) sooooo order at the bar!

As a native Portlandian that grew up spending weekends at Saturday Market, I am absolutely thrilled my new home offers a thriving weekend market as well!!

My visit was on the 2nd weekend of opening. It was JAM PACKED!! While this was exciting to see so many locals purchasing local goods and being a welcoming community, it was more packed that I would have liked. If the market could get a permanent space of its own or spread out a bit more, the experience would have been top notch!

There are tons of vendors. Tons of different things to choose from; food to clothes. Great live entertainment. And despite the crowdedness, it's exciting being a part of downtown.

I definitely plan to go back, maybe this time leave the kids at home and I'll be able to enjoy it more.

I am legit surprised this place is as good as it is!

Husband wanted BBQ for Father's Day and we opted to try something new. Dangerous, I know.

Because our kiddos were napping I ordered our food to-go. We ordered a 3-meat plate and a 2-meat plate both with ribs and sliced brisket, and a pulled pork sandwich plate. For sides we tried BBQ beans, macaroni and cheese and baked potato casserole.

When I got to the restaurant to pick up I was worried the bag was so small, for $40 I felt like there could have been more. I was also disappointed drinks weren't included since they're pictured, but I understand I shouldn't assume.

As I plated our meal when I got home, I still felt like there wasn't a lot of food for the price. My husband said something similar - HOWEVER - we both agreed that in the long run we were grateful considering we're usually in a food coma after BBQ.

The food was honestly really good. The brisket was well seasoned and tender. A good balance of meat and fat. The ribs fell of the bone, no dry spots or bland meat. The kids ate up the pulled pork sandwich. The sides were all really good as well, I was pleasantly surprised with the baked potato casserole.

So while I can't see us ever dining in, it's a great spot to hit the drive-thru and get BBQ to-go. The portions could definitely be bigger but they are probably closer to how much we SHOULD eat lol
One of my favorite DBs around. Super fast and friendly service, obviously used to catering to a commuters morning coffee need and rush.

I'm beyond ecstatic this location has opened, I finally have a coffee shop on my way to work!!

The Human Bean legit has ahhhmazing coffee, they're small shop quality with the logistics of a large chain.

I always order a granita, no straying here. Today I ordered the snickers and I feel like I could solidly never get coffee anywhere else.

The app is nice too.

This review is for catering off-site.

I facilitate large quarterly meetings for the state and this place was suggested to me as a lunch option.

The ordering process is a little old school, it's done over the phone, but the staff are extremely patient and helpful and very knowledgeable.

We ordered an assortment of foods including the enchilada casserole and appetizers and create your own taco/burrito bar.

The food was spectacular. Kept warm and packaged easily to set up ourselves. The staff were accommodating with our needs for itemized receipts and meet every other need with flying colors.

I highly recommend them if you need an excellent and delicious catering option for meeting or party.

Diggs Pizza is hands down a diamond in the rough! 

Their ingredients are always fresh, their dough is soft and crunchy all in the right places and well seasoned. And their prices are great! 

Support local!

What a cooooooool place!

Came here for a work party a few weeks back. Loved every thing about the place; the atmosphere, the location, the staff, the food, the fun, the drinks!

Love that it's kids friendly to a point and then also no kids allowed after a certain point. Parents should be allowed to have fun with their kids too! But I also respect the flip side and understand not wanting kids around all the time.

I ordered the burger. Super simple yet tasty. 
My husband ordered the brisket, which he greatly enjoyed but did wish the serving was more for a mans appetite and not just a taste.

I also ordered a mojito, which was surprisingly strong (in a good way). 

Definitely check this place out!!

I am surprised by how much I genuinely love Big Als. It really is a perfect place to hang as an adult or bring your kids. 

I've come with just my family and also a corporate event, and both times were impressed and left having a great time. 

Their pizza is really good, definitely not large chain quality (mean that in the best way). And their burgers are also great. 

Honestly, Big Als is 100% worth all the hype it gets. I definitely recommend! 

My only complaint is the price. It's crazy expensive... but if you budget and plan than it's worth it.

This place is soooooo yummy! We were having a working lunch meeting and ordered lunch here and yummmmmm!! 

I ordered the Turkey Bacon sandwhich and a Lean Machine smoothie. Both were superb and so fresh.

The sandwhich comes with a side option, since I was getting a smoothie I knew I wouldn't eat chips/salad so I opted for fresh fruit - which I love in an option in general!

The smoothie was spectacular! I forgot how much i love smoothies. It was so fresh and well blended (this is important y'all!). 

Best part is this place doesn't break the bank! I highly recommend.

Wow, just WOW!

Imma cut to the chase on this one, come and eat here! Restaurant is like a log cabin in the middle of the city, super sweet and cozy. Service is great, despite the Covid weirdness. But the food...

Fresh beignets we on the special, so we snagged an order a an appetizer. We got an appetizer or brunch, yes.

My husband orders the chicken fried steak, home fries with a side pancake. To call it a side pancake is beyond hilarious because this is a dinner plate size pancake, lol. The home fries reminded me of homemade pan fried potatoes growing up as a kid, they were perfectly crisp and soft and well seasoned. The chicken fried steak look like a real cut of meat, if you're a CFS eater than you know some resemble a flat tire (though still taste amazing!), but this was beautifully battered and fried and cooked exactly as ordered! 

I ordered the Joe Bennie with home fries. The hollandaise tasted fresh and home made, you know it's good when you get that hint of lemon. The ham was fresh and soft, the eggs Ooooh emmm geee! Then of course you take the extra hollandaise and toss the home fries and you're in fat lady heaven!!!

AX77orc7Yron8Kb8xTZLmQ.review_text: I visited a few weeks ago to find an excellent wine and beer menu and was impressed by the ambiance in such a quaint taproom in rittenhouse. Upon returning tonight I was less than impressed by the beer selection and we eventually left after deciding the menu did not include  what we were looking for (a traditional saison or IPA). They were heavily featuring seasonal porters, dark ales, and tart IPAs/ "pumpkin" saison. I do, however, plan to return in the future and think it would be a good place for drinks with friends or pre-date night drinks.

Excellent BYOB in Conshy! You are missing out if you have not been here before. We passed the cafe upon moving to the area and we're delighted to have dinner on a Saturday evening. The atmosphere was relaxed yet sophisticated and reminded my husband and I of our honeymoon in France. The service was also wonderful and the food was amazing--a good selection of classic French dishes prepared with love and attention to detail. We will return!!
Decent diner with a fun and relaxed atmosphere. Coffee was great. Slightly overpriced for what you get though. Not sure if eggs toast and a side of meat is worth $8

Inviting dinner atmosphere with great tapas and an excellent wine collection. We liked the option of being able to order throughout our meal as opposed to all at once but would have liked the meals to come out more methodically. We had the ham coquettes, green salad, scallops, asparagus, and mushroom flat bread. We loved everything except the coquettes and would have gotten something else off the traditional menu instead. Would love to try the paella. Would recommend for dinner with friends, family, or a date night! Can be as inexpensive or expensive as you'd like and plenty to choose from!

We had been trying (I mean diligently trying) to get a reservation at Zahav for 4 months. With their 60 day wait on Open Table, we were overly ecstatic to finally score a reservation at a reasonable hour. We selected the Mesiba Tasting and had an incredible bottle of Lebanese wine. Our room was filled with large birthday parties and with us being the only 2 top in the room, it was very loud and difficult to hear each other or the servers.

First course, Salatim (vegetables) and hummus. excellent. Worth a 5 star rating just for the vegetarian starters. and Who doesn't love their famed hummus?

second:Fried Califlower was decent but nothing to really write home about and slightly salty. The Pastilla was a phyllo dough filled with feta and other herbs with an apricot sauce, it too was very salty but paired well with the apricot.  There was an additional fish Mezze which was smoked, not my favorite but my husband enjoyed it. 3/5 stars

The roasted lamb shoulder and rice pilaf were good but by this point in the meal we were full and felt we couldn't fully appreciate it. 4/5 stars, again it was good but not the best thing I have ever had (surprisingly so since it is their 'famed' entree)

Dessert was perfect, 5/5 stars and homemade mint tea!

Overall, I think it is an experience you have to do at least once. Will we be back? Most likely. Is the tasting menu worth it, I'm not quite sure. I would stick to ordering a la carte next time. But a million yes's for splurging on a whole bottle of one of their unique wines.
Excellent! A wonderful restaurant for a special occasion or just a nice night out.
Decent Ethiopian food with a welcoming atmosphere. Got the vegetarian platter, enjoyed the spiced lentils but the other items were a bit bland. Good injera!!

I haven't been to a Chinese restaurant in years or eaten any Chinese other than that off a wegmans hot foods bar but this was incredible! The sesame chicken was flavorful, crisp, and saucy without being overly greasy. The vegetables were nicely steamed. The Mongolian beef was flavorful and a large enough serving for two. The steamed vegetarian spring rolls were average but the rest of our meal made up for them completely. The BYOB was a huge plus (do yourself a favor and go to tired hands before to bring some amazing beer with you). Would definitely recommend and will be returning!

Great service from larree, friendly and welcoming atmosphere. Awesome late night specials for drinks. Food was mediocre. Had gulf coast oysters, a little "watery" for my taste but overall a good choice. The crab appetizer was just okay, and Brussels were very good. Crawfish sandwich was also decent. Overall, good to get away from the bustle of CBD and bourbon, hipster and relaxed feel.

Service: 5/5
Atmosphere: 5/5
Food: 3.5-4/5

Local ice cream shop with fast and friendly service, even on a very hot night with a long line. Have been here twice now-- soft serve was standard vanilla, chocolate or twist and was very good. Great size for the price even for a kiddie! Second time I tried the VEGAN soymilk vanilla almond bark and was very impressed! Love that they are offering two vegan/ dairy free options that taste amazing and have a great creamy consistency. Will definitely be back.

Really wish yelp let me give 3.5 stars because this place is definitely not a solid 3 but isn't quite a 4 either. We went last weekend when it was ridiculously hot and we asked to sit outside. Our seat was well shaded and service was prompt. They kept our water glasses full which was also a plus. We ordered two drinks-- I had the Electric Relaxation which was really good, and easy to drink. If we were staying longer I easily could have had 2-3 more. My husband had the Aperol spritz which was not as great. The ratio of aperol:prosecco: club just wasn't quite right. But oh well. The carrot hummus was TO DIE FOR.

What really fell short was our waiter. He answered every question like it was the biggest inconvenience and gave the most obscure answers. If you don't know the answer, just say so! He was also ever so slightly confrontational and acted as though we should have stayed longer or ordered more. 

I'd go back but only if other friends requested we go there. Kind of a go once, see what the hype is about and keep moving on after.

Finally, great Chinese/ Sichuan food near conshohocken! We have only had take out but had a great experience overall. The first order included Sesame Chicken, broccoli with spicy garlic sauce, Dan Dan noodle and dumplings. All were amazing, especially the Dan Dan noodle. Tonight we ordered sesame chicken, gluten free broccoli with spicy garlic, and gluten free fried rice. They were more than accommodating for my gluten free requests and were very helpful with navigating the menu. Service is quick and friendly. We will definitely continue to get our take out from here. Highly recommended! ....they are also a BYOB which we can't wait to try!

Lives up to its hype. AMAZING vegan restaurant; wonderful ambiance, excellent options prepared incredibly well and lovely presentation. Wonderful cocktails. I highly recommend checking out their wine and cocktail list, all wines are organic or biodynamic I believe which was a great touch. Favorite dishes: Fancy Radishes, pretzel with rutabaga... literally everything is amazing, you can't go wrong.

Ambiance: 4/5. For a cold night in the winter, Kanella was warm, cozy, and friendly. We were seated by the window which added to the appeal and was not drafty. The restaurant was packed but never got too loud. 

Service: 3 out of 5. The service was a bit "awkward" but friendly. They ran through the specials and quickly went to another table before having time to ask questions. When asked about dessert we said yes and hoped for a menu. About 15 minutes went by with no menu until another server came up and asked if we were ready for the check-- by that time we were ready to leave. 

Food: 3 out of 5. The food really didn't do it for me. For being on the Philly top 50 list I had higher expectations that were not met.  We started with the dip platter of the day. None of them were great and the fava bean dip was just awful.  An additional dip tasted exactly like veggie cream cheese. The pita was sub par and very generic.  I got the falafel platter for my main which also failed to impress. The falafel were decent, moist, and crisp on the outside but hardly tasted authentic or unique to kanella (for the price you could go to mama vegetarian and get the same thing). The salad on the platter was just not good as was the hummus.  My friend got the eggplant special which is the reason for the 3 stars of redemption-- the dish was well balanced, great flavors, and good consistency.

Overall impression: not sure what the hype is about, wouldn't necessarily return, wouldn't go out of my way to get a reservation.

Looked decent when we first walked in with friendly service and good looking bagels but it fell short, very short. Our bagels were supposed to be toasted but they came out less toasted than your stereotypical "toasted" Dunkin' Donuts bagel. They were dense, incredibly dry, and almost inedible. They also do not make their own cream cheese. If you're looking for a great or even a semi decent bagel, I'd keep moving past the bagel cafe.

Friday, Saturday, Sunday- Every time I mention this Restaurant to someone they follow up with, "whatever night works best for you."  I took that to mean it must still remain a bit of a hidden gem in the city despite it's known presence for many years.

Running 30+ minutes behind to our reservation on a busy Friday​ night, I was pleasantly surprised when the host graciously accommodated​ us and still allowed​ us over 2 hours of dining time. We were sat upstairs in the beautifully quaint and romantic dining area. It had this illustrious feel of a classic bistro amidst a museum. 

The service was impeccable--our server suggested we go with something out of our comfort zone for drinks, which we did, and we were so pleasantly surprised. My Husband got The Emperor's​ New Laundromat and I had the Control State--both completely different but perfect in their own way. We later followed with two suggested glasses of wine by our server which were equally as wonderful.  overall, great wine list and cocktail menu (I'd go back just for drinks at the bar with oysters). 

For dinner we started with a 1/2 dozen oysters, the frozen mignonette​ really made all the difference in terms of presentation and overall taste. The famed mussel toast had a flavor profile that unexpectedly fresh and herbaceous. The endive and treviso salad was excellent, a definite must have if you're looking for greens.  

Despite the hype, I didn't love the confit carrots; they tasted somewhat bland and lackluster compared to the other items we ordered. Also, the roasted gnocchi​ were decent, but I wouldn't run back for more, they were gnocchi​, perfectly fluffy potato pillows but I had three and felt satisfied. 

For dessert we had the trio of sorbet, the perfect ending to a well rounded first dinner here. 

Overall a good date night spot or a double date, i'd say any more than 4 people per party could be pushing.  Enjoy it for what it is--a classicly intimate restaurant with incredible wine, cocktails, and a variety of food options.

Chiangmai is a great go to spot for when you're running late from work, exhausted from grad school, or too tired to cook on a weekend. Eating there at least three times a month I'd say, it's a solid 4 stars. Service is fast and also friendly. 

I've only ever ordered take out and have never been disappointed. I love their Red Thai Curry with extra vegetables and no meat or tofu--needless to say, they're amazing at accommodating changes to the menu. The pad Thai is also good; not the most amazing pad Thai in the world but very flavorful and very good for conshohocken!

I'd love to eat there and take advantage of the BYOB in the future.

Great neighborhood brewery that is super dog friendly! Love being able to walk here for a beer in the summer along the SRT. Also a great place to stop after a long day of cycling. They have a great selection of beer including some favorites, the blueberry Berliner is great year round but especially on a sweltering summer day and the MC5 is a good well rounded IPA. Some of their more experimental beers miss the mark but the vast majority are worth trying. The food is also really good especially with this being their smaller location.  Really friendly staff, incredible patio when it's nice out and all around a great place to be any night of the week.

I wanted to like this place, I really did. It was packed when we arrived and we were seated quickly at the bar. I took note of the all you can eat breakfast buffet but my mind was set on a veggie omelette with Swiss cheese and some crispy, flavorful hash browns.  Our server was quick to greet us and bring us coffee, pretty decent coffee for a dinner that has an all you can eat buffet (my expectations were somewhere between old brown watered down coffee and Dunkin' Donuts), id go for a second cup if that means anything to you. 

The omelette itself was pretty good, but $10.75? This isn't a Center city diner here folks! Overpriced. The hash browns were heaped on the plate but this was one of those quantity over quality situations. Flavorless and mushy, needless to say I wasn't thoroughly impressed.

Overall we did have excellent service which would have been 4 star but the food just didn't hit the mark, hence the 2 stars.

I've been to Rebel Yoga at least a handful of times by now and recently purchased a 10 class pass.  I keep coming back for the amazing atmosphere of the studio itself--I love walking from the boutique to the studio and being surrounded by exposed brick, candles, and essential oils or incense. I had been to a few classes when they first opened and was surprised when I was always the only one at a class on a weekday morning--a pleasant surprise to have a private class but I also love the energy of having others in the room.  Since coming back almost 1.5 years later, I can say they have really grown into themselves. I haven't found a studio quite like Rebel in the suburbs yet--compared to other classes that completely eliminate the "om" or others that are constantly repetitive​ in their flow, Rebel has them beat.  

If you want a warm/ hot room, instructors that genuinely care about the practice of yoga and what it can bring from a spiritual view, to a great workout with really good music, Rebel is where you want to be.  I almost hate writing this review because I like that it is still kept somewhat secret! 

A tip--weekend morning classes can get packed so get there early to get a good spot! Also, make sure to try their Yomi bites and Inspired Brew kombucha!

V Street proved itself to be another incredible restaurant by the owners of Vedge and Wiz Kid.  Unbeknownst​ to me, Wiz Kid actually transforms into the dining room for V Street at night!  We arrived as a party of three and were quickly seated. Though our service was a bit awkward at times (they forgot our KFT tacos) and our first dish came before our cocktails and wine arrived, the meal was otherwise well coursed out and presented well.  They were also apologetic of these mistakes and none of them detered from the meal itself.
