Our server suggested we order 3 dishes from each section of the menu (1 per person); we ended up ordering 5 dishes total and thought it was plenty. 

Overall, V Street was impressive. The atmosphere was warm and inviting.  A good spot for a night out with friends or a more casual date night. I'll definitely be back!

- Charred Broccoli: Served cold and with a spicy chili sauce, they were good but not my favorite. I didn't get much charred​ flavor throughout the dish. Not a necessity. 

- Kung Pao Cucumber: A good lighter dish, not spicy and overall well rounded. If you want something lighter that isn't going to fill you up but give you some greens, go with this!

- Cauliflower​ 65: This was amazing! The flavor profile was incredible and the blend of fried cauliflower​​ and Asian​ inspired flavors was so well done. I would get this every time I come and order it as take out if I wasn't dining in. 

- Mushroom Shwarama: Another really good dish that had less of an asian inspiration and more middle eastern/ Mediterranean​. The lemon tahini lightened a dish that could have been quite heavy with​ the trumpet mushrooms but was so well balanced.  Another must order! 

-Dan Dan Noodle: SPICY! but good. If you love spicy, I'd​ order this. If not, I'd stay away. The sauce was heavier than I would have expected for a Dan Dan Noodle and the combination of that with using ramen noodles (or so it seemed) surprised me and I can't say how I feel about it--I guess undeterred but also underwhelmed​? I'd eat it again if someone was dying to try it but wouldn't drive 30 minutes for it.

5 stars for the bike shop/ coffee shop combo.  Friends of mine have been dreaming of starting something similar in our hometown and I would suggest they model their vision off Riverbend. The employees are extremely friendly and knowledgable of road bikes and cycling.  They genuinely want to help you get the best gear and best life out of your bike and aren't just trying to push a ​new product on you or anyone specific brand. 

Living nearby it is easy to walk for a coffee--Serving local Green Street coffee is what makes this one of my favorite coffee shops in Conshy.  There really isn't a better coffee shop in terms of coffee quality and service.  The downside that other yelpers have mentioned is that there really is no indoor seating, but in the warmer months, the outdoor seating is great.  

Run, bike, walk, blade your way to Riverbend​ on a warm (or cold) day and stop in for some friendly conversation​ and a good cup of coffee.  They do also have small snacks and sandwiches.  Your weekend will thank you.​

Really an incredible experience.  After learning of Cadence on the Philly Top 50 list, I knew I had to give it a try.  We went as a party of 3 on a Saturday night, the only seating available was counter seating but it was well worth it.  Watching everyone work behind the counter was just as exciting as our meal. Truly earning their spot on the Philly Top 50, I'd​ say Cadence can definitely compete with other mainstay restaurants​ like Vernick.

We opted for the 4-course​ tasting menu for $65--it was well worth the price and allowed us to sample a good portion of the menu. Everything was well paced and beautifully presented and paired well with our biodynamic Beaujolais​ we brought in (Cadence is a BYOB which we forgot about until we walked in the door, luckily there is a Fine Wine and Good Spirits across the street).

First: Venison tartare was to die for; the beet rye bread combined with the huckleberry and egg yok made it a decadent dish. The scallop was much lighter with slight hints of butter.  There was a shrimp dish that was also on the more decadent side but equally as light and flavorful. 

Seconds: Confit potatoes were okay but not my favorite, lacking in depth of flavors.  The smoked trout was something I normally would not try but our server suggested it; the everything spaetzle with beet really rounded out the dish and mellowed the smokey flavor of the trout.  Again, the octopus is something I wouldn't try but this was equally as good as the venison​​ tartare and the smoked trout, really well done! 

Thirds: Roasted maitake, beef, and pork were all well-rounded​ dishes with an exciting flavor profile.  

For dessert,​ my favorite​e was the chocolate maple tart and citrus date frozen nougat. 

The dishes here push the boundaries of conventional and really bring forth an experimental but well-rounded​ taste. I loved the flavor combinations in all dishes listed above, none were too overpowering and really paired well together. I suggest trying the tasting menu if you are going with a group to get a good feel for the entire menu.  Again, the staff was wonderful, they genuinely looked like they were enjoying their work, and we felt welcomed (not rushed) through our entire meal. Will definitely be back!!

This. Is. Pizza. Not your average neighborhood papa johns chain or some lack luster doughy mess labeled pizza but real pizza that has real depth and character. 

It's square (hence the name), it's friendly, it's a BYOB, it's messy and greasy, it's almost closer to a deep dish than a flat lifeless NY slice, and if it's good enough for Joe Beddia, it's certainly good enough for me. 

The atmosphere is friendly, casual, and fun--like your best friends opened a pizza shop except you don't know they're your best friends yet. The mushroom pie was our favorite but the sausage also looked equally as good if you're a meat pizza lover. A good Italian salad to start was also a good choice to make us feel less guilty about the damage we did to the pie itself.

The food is what gives this place 4 stars. The mezze platter was really well done between the fresh pita, creamy and flavorful labne, cashew dukkah egg and additional items. 

We also ordered a green salad with falafel which was way too much food but also equally as good. In the future I'd opt for the beet salad without the mezze platter with a side of falafel or just the mezze with falafel. The green salad was somewhat bland compared to the beet salad and other flavors throughout the platter.

They serve stumptown coffee which is another plus but the downside is that it is $4 a cup. I love stumptown as much as the next coffee aficionado but $4 was steep without any offer of refills, which leads me to...

Service. Ugh, Suraya you were doing so well with the food and bright modern atmosphere but I can't understand the service. We ordered a beer which was no longer offered, decided to switch and get a mimosa which never arrived. Halfway through our lunch I was over the idea of a mid day mimosa but was then a bit surprised when the bill came and still had the beer on it. The server was pleasant and admitted to the mistake thus removing the beer from our tab but it made the flow of lunch so awkward--first anticipating beer, then a mimosa, then disappointment of having neither and then having to navigate removing it from our bill.

However, I'd return for sure! this could have been an off day service wise. Regardless of service, the food lived up to the hype that has been built up around this place and like others have said, blows zahav out of the water.

This Wegmans really is a disgrace of the Wegmans name and brand. Growing up in Rochester, NY where Wegmans first opened, I have a certain expectation and level of quality I expect from Wegmans products, store experience, and employees. I genuinely gave this Wegmans store a good chance for the past two years but I am continually disappointed in the overall quality of their produce, arrogance and rudeness of their employees while restocking the aisles or forgetting to put your groceries in your bags, and the lack of variety in food products as compared to Whole Foods and Mom's. 

It's honestly such a disappointment that I've driven to Glenn Mills and North Wales just to get what I need while avoiding employees that could care less about the Wegmans reputation. 

This has become an issue of using a good name to their advantage while running a subpar store and forgetting about the quality they should be expected to deliver.

Stayed here recently for a school event. The room was clean, spacious, and well laid out.  The modern aesthetics and bright paint made it feel extra "new" and comfortable.  The staff was extremely friendly and helpful throughout our stay.  The valet was well worth the $45 splurge for the night and made parking easier than finding a lot down the street for $30 and walking everything back to the hotel.  The one downside was the elevator situation, they took an extremely long time to arrive and you had to pay close attention to make sure you got the right one for your floor. 

As for the event itself, I'd have to give a 2/5.  The food was not great by any means. I'd say mediocre would be an overstatement at best. I also found it slightly disturbing that they were passing dishes like crab cakes and sesame chicken without offering a toothpick or something to eat it with.  Not sure who decided a mixed drink would be $14 either but I don't know who would pay that price for well vodka.

Serpico is a gem for Philly. Ranking #9 on the 2019 Philly Top 50 from Philadelphia Magazine really doesn't do it justice.  Serpico has been around for a while, and for a good reason. From the moment you walk through the door, everything is incredibly well thought out--Friendly and knowledgable service, great variety of wine and cocktails, and out of this world menu options.  

They suggest you order a lot of dishes, but I've​ been twice now with a total of 4 people in our party each time and have found that the perfect number of dishes is 8 (including dessert). You​ HAVE to get dessert.

The main attractions are the scallops, duck leg, hailbut, and dessert though the eggplant is also really well prepared.  Any of their wines pair well with all three courses and their cocktails are equally as exciting.

Diver Scallops: 10/10 stars if that's even possible. these are a must. Don't pass go, do not collect $200 until you've had these scallops, once you do, you can die happy. I'd even go so far as to suggest going for a few glasses of wine or cocktails and just the scallops at the bar. They're smooth and savory but equally as light and subtle.  

Hamachi tartare: Good as an extra dish for the table but not the main attraction (again, refer to the diver scallops, they're the star of the show).  The tartare was light and fluffy but lacked in depth for me. The rest of the table loved this dish.

Japenese Eggplant: Interesting dish with a great flavor profile that is both unique and exciting.  Great for a vegetarian option.

Deep fried duck leg:  If you're coming for a cocktail and scallops you should also order this. It's equally as incredible as the scallops but on a totally different level.  Flavorful, slightly greasy, and naturally heavier than the scallops but when shared amongst the table, just the right amount of duck. Also a 10/10 and a must have.

Chicken and snail lasagna: This fell short for me and just didn't bring much to the table.  It seemed unique and interesting on the menu but didn't stick out as an exceptional dish compared to the others. You could do without this.

Halibut: One of the best preparations of halibut I have had in Philly (or anywhere for that matter). The carrot topping is decadadent and flavorful as is the halibut itself. The side of greens adds a brightness to the dish. Also a must have item on the menu.

Definitely not last and one of the most mind-boggling​ dishes was the Yuzu tart (sadly not currently on the menu as of April 2019, it could be seasonal).  This dessert was the perfect​​ combination of sweet and tart, light and fluffy, with an almost indescribable​ flavor profile. I would beg them to make this even if it's not on the menu.

Good "health food" find in Ucity. The staff were friendly and quick, which is perfect during the lunch rush. Great options and add ins though less than some other açaí and juice places in the city. Overall a good place to stop if you're in the area but I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way.

This. Is. Philly. Parks on tap symbolizes the start of summer and is one of my most anticipated openings each year. This year brings new locations including Historic Rittenhouse. Tonight was a gorgeous warm spring night. The food is average but that's not what you should go for--go for the beer (good local beer and decent food), go for the dogs, the atmosphere and the friendly vibes. Again, there's really no better way to put it than this is what Philly is all about. Parks on tap has a simplicity and relaxed vibe that other beer gardens just can't achieve and it highlights some incredible areas around the city that you may otherwise not venture to--do yourself a favor, check the schedule and go.

5/5 for beer. Hands down. Tired Hands is the best brewery experience and beer that I've had.  They're creative, push the boundaries, and unique.  They're also friendly.  You have to have friendly people serving you a ​beer to really enjoy it.  The beer options here often differ from those at the Fermentaria but are just as good, if not better.

4/5 for food.  I personally prefer the food options at the Fermentaria (right down the road) more, but that's just me.  You go here for a different experience and more "pub" food with a plethora of paninis (Tuesday is Panini Pandemonium with a special panini each week). 

I'd go to this location for a relaxed, casual, beer and panini or unique sides.  I'd also go for just a beer--the upstairs is a great spot for bar seating and this location has been less crowded than the fermentaria when we have gone (usually during weekdays).  If you want the "brewery" feel go to fermentaria.  They also have a wider selection of food options. 

Moral of the story- you can't go wrong.  It's the best beer in this region (if not the entire east coast in my opinion). Do yourself a favor and go ASAP!

We booked Hiroki as soon as we saw reservations opened and we are so glad we did!  This was not just a dinner but an experience, an excellent one that left us wanting to return again and again.  From the moment you step in front of the beautiful circular door to the time you leave, you are treated with excellent service. 

The first thing I have to note is that we chose to sit at the bar---This was the best decision.  If you have any interest in how meticulous the chef and staff are in the preparation of your meal, sit here.  If you want to​ watch their knife skills, sit here.  If you want to be mesmerized​ as to how they continue the flow of the meal, sit here.  This added to the experience in a way that I cannot fully describe.  I would even sit here as a group of 4, yes there is potential for less group conversation, but the interaction with staff is so vitally important to this meal.  To be able to watch them prepare your course and then offer it to you immediately afterwards is an experience in and of itself.

The meal itself was incredible and it is hard to put into words how great it truly was.  You honestly need to go and experience it for yourself.  Everything was meticulously well prepared and even pieces I normally wouldn't try I found very impressive.  

Great addition to the Philadelphia sushi and Japanese food scene.

Being open and honest here-- I just returned from a marvelous trip to Japan that included quite a few bowls of ramen that were out of this world.  

I wanted to like Terakawa, I did. But it fell short. Yes it was "decent" ramen but I found the broth to be a bit oily with basic flavors.  The bamboo didn't add much to the dish and the pork was fatty but lacking in complexity.

Gyoza was a big miss-- they almost tasted as if they had been frozen or bought in bulk.  I could go to a grocery store and do just as well but get a full bag instead of 5 for $5.

Overall, it was, as I put it... decent.  Terakawa gets the job done when you have a hankering for ramen but are okay with a very Americanized version. I'd probably go back but I wouldn't go out of my way for it. If you want unique or more authentic ramen I'd suggest you may want to try elsewhere.

I'm going to give Minella's a solid 4 stars-- they are a true "diner" if you will.  My last diner experience was less than stellar and left a bad taste in my mouth for diners (literally), but Minella's has me wanting to come back for more.

The atmosphere is...diner-y.  We walked in on a busy Saturday morning and were immediately shuffled to a table for 2.  Service was fast, a little ornery, but isn't that why you come to a diner?  It was lively, family and kid friendly, and welcoming.

The food was also solid diner food.  Homefries were more of a hash brown (which is what I was looking for anyways) and were crisp, not soggy, and not greasy/oily.  The poached eggs over medium were "perfectly poached" (not overly soft or hard and sitting in their own egg water).  Canadian bacon-- good! Toast came dry with a side of butter (better than having to ask for "dry rye" which tends to get stares from my husband).

Service was attentive and we were in and out with our stomachs happy!  I'd definitely recommend this place for a solid diner breakfast experience.

Came for the Bills Backer Bar and had a good time this past Sunday.  The bar area had multiple TVs including 1 projection screen size.  Other customers were pleasant and we all seemed to get along despite the Eagles crushing our beloved Bills.  Beers were cheap--Blue Lights for $3 and Genny Cream Ale (a personal favorite).  Wings were actually pretty good--I've still been searching for good wings down here in Philly.  We placed an order and received 8 wings (not sure if that was the number we were supposed to receive) but they were flavorful, saucy, and had a good amount of meat.  Will definitely be back to cheer on our Bills but not sure if I'd go here for any other reason!

Ordered take out wings after the game--they were salty and not saucy.  Just not what we were looking for.  The blue cheese was also more of a watery consistency and lacked in blue cheese chunks.  Carrot sticks instead of celery--maybe a personal preference but when I have wings I want a nice crunchy celery stick not a carrot.  Would maybe go back to try their bar atmosphere and beers but skipping the wings next time and will drive the 15 minutes to Manayunk for better wings.

Wow, ok Neighborhood Ramen did not disappoint!! From the moment we walked in the door to when we left we were impressed.  The host was incredibly attentive and genuinely excited to be working there (as were the other employees) and was knowledgeable about the types of ramen offered.  We tried one bowl of Shoyu and Shio along with Gyoza (spicy cucumbers were compliments of the kitchen since it was our first time).  The Shoyu was complex, flavorful, and balanced.  The pork and egg were cooked perfectly. I would love to see a homemade noodle or slightly thicker noodle for ramen personally but these were still great.  The portion size was also perfect.  The cucumbers brought me right back to a recent trip to Japan and paired perfectly with the gyoza-- I loved the gyoza, fresh, lightly fried, with scallions.  My husband is more of a purist and didn't love the scallion topping but didn't hate it either.  I liked that we ordered and then waited in line for a few moments for our table as well-- a more authentic ramen experience.  This place far exceeded our expectations and I'm excited to go back and try their unique specials.  Really really awesome spot-- get yourself there to try it!

I haven't been to many brunch spots in Philly but Fiore was incredible.  Immediately upon walking into Fiore I enjoyed the laid back and relaxed atmosphere that subtly hinted at the fact that this is a local place.  If you're looking for the hustle of Rittenhouse and flashy Parc vibes, this aint it--and that is precisely why you should venture to Fiore.  The bar area was occupied by a few locals drinking luxurious coffee drinks and eating beautiful handcrafted pastries and cake (at 10:30am)...you do you.  We chose to sit in the main dining area-- at 10:30 on a saturday I was surprised and happy to discover that we did not need a reservation.  We had The Saltie, The Breakfast Sandwich, Brussel Sprout Toast, and Fregola Salad. Coffee was from local Rival Brothers. 

The Saltie was this beautiful combination of fresh focaccia with softer scrambled eggs and ricotta.  Rich and decadent and while incredibly tasty, very filling.  I saved room for some bites of Fregola Salad. 

Fregola Salad was surprising--each bite incorporate something sweet and savory between roasted squash, some fruit, sesame seeds, and soft boiled egg.  Really out of this world good and something unique to the breakfast/ brunch scene in my opinion. 

Brussel Sprout Toast was also equally as surprising as the Fregola salad.  Definitely on the much lighter side than the Saltie but lighter does not mean that they skimped on flavor and complexity. I only had one bite but was intrigued by its uniqueness and had my husband not eaten all of it, I would have had more. 

The Breakfast Sandwich looked beautiful and our friend said it was amazing and commented on the texture and quality of the housemade sausage--she also left no leftovers to try. 

Will I return?  Yes.  Will I go back and try dinner?  Also yes.  Fiore really hit it out of the park and deserves its coveted spot on the Philly Top 50.  Overall a wonderful dining experience for brunch, off the beaten path, and worth the walk or drive.

Really want to give this a 3.5, I sadly cannot really justify a 4/5 for Res Ipsa given their spot on the Philly top 50.  They just didn't hit the mark for me as being one of the top 10 restaurants in the city.  It was good- yes.  The dining experience was unique- yes.  I would go back- yes. But something was missing.  I would really love to come back and see what more they have to offer in terms of experience and food.  

Some positives:  I loved the casual atmosphere that Res Ipsa has created.  They make you feel welcome and relaxed, like a casual neighborhood restaurant serving really good food.  I also appreciate that they are BYOB--it keeps the price down and allows guests to enjoy their own bottle of wine with their food.  The food was good (I could stretch my imagination and say great but again, something was missing).

Appetizers: We had all of the vegetable appetizers on the menu and they were all good. The Mushroom Caponata was one of the most notable appetizers that stood out to me and has to be one of the best dishes I have had in Philly.  The Cauliflower was also enjoyed at our table, it was not my favorite. The Blood Orange was okay but not something all too memorable. 

Mains: If I had to select 1 pasta to get again it would be the Fazoletti--It was unique and decadent.  The full size was a good serving for 4 people and it stood out as one of the better dishes throughout our meal. Spaghetti Alle Vongole was pasta with clams, again, nothing I'd sit and write home about; somewhat disappointing given it being one of their signature dishes. It was lackluster in flavor and left me wanting something more unique. 

Fish: The whole fish with vegetables was really the star of the show.  This fish was cooked perfectly and was both decadent and unique.  The vegetables were an nice added touch that our table certainly enjoyed.  If you go to Res Ipsa, make sure to get the fish or chicken.  You won't be disappointed.

Fiorella did a great job of pairing covid friendly outdoor dining with a luxurious experience of eating great Italian.  We were surprised how wasn't and cozy the tent atmosphere was on a cold night in February and were pleasantly surprised that we weren't freezing the whole time!  Service was friendly and prompt and the food was excellent!

We stopped by the museum last weekend and it was the first visit we had made since covid started.  Wow!  Their procedures were very impressive from cleanliness to temperature stations upon entry.  It was also so nice to have space to breathe and take in the art without fighting a crowd- this is the sort of social distancing I could get used to!

Af1Z4hO-Jif083b5V-SJFA.review_text: Delicious food and great service! I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for Latin cuisine in the city. We got the papusa and tostada combo with elote and plantain chips. Everything was great and the portion size was good! Make sure to get the churros as well :)

My boyfriend and I went here Sunday night and the food was great! We had their burger and duck fat French fries and I'd highly recommend both! The restaurant also has a really cool vibe and is perfect for a date night. The only slight negative is that  it's a little loud and hard to hear your company when the restaurant is packed, but other than that, it's definitely a great spot.

This place is perfect for a big, hot bowl of ramen. It's relatively new, so I wanted to try it out, and came here on a cold night in March. Their selection of ramen bowls is excellent. I'd been to Japan before, but I almost think the ramen they do here is better because of the diverse ingredients in their bowls. I got the Shabu shabu beef ramen and it was great!! It was spicy, but didn't burn my mouth. I'd definitely come back!

This is my favorite ice cream in Philadelphia! My favorite flavor is their chocolate caramel pretzel, but you really can't go wrong with any of them. They're a little on the pricy side, but it's worth it and they definitely don't skimp out on the scoop size!

These cookies are amazing! They're on the undercooked side, which is my favorite! My favorite was their Heath bar cookie. If you like toffee, you'll love this flavor. And definitely try coming towards the end of the day between 5-6pm for their happy hour pricing when all cookies are $1!!

El Rey has a cool environment. The restaurant is a little unsuspecting, as it's kinda farther from all the other restaurants around Rittenhouse, but it's still worth a try. My favorite here was the ceviche. I had the enchiladas too, but didn't think they were too memorable. It's also a little overpriced for Mexican food, but if you want to eat in a fun environment, El Rey is a nice outing. I've heard they have a good happy hour as well, but haven't tried it yet.

I've been wanting to try Helium Comedy Club ever since I moved to Philly and it did not disappoint. We went to a show on Sunday and there was a decent crowd. The headliner was hilarious and the host was awesome too. They guy before the headliner was just okay, but he wasn't on for too long anyways. It was a little disappointing though because the kitchen messed up our food order, so we never got our food, and when the waiter came to ask us if we needed anything else, we kept having to explain that we never got anything, so we missed a couple jokes. Other than that, it was great though and I'd definitely go back!

I thought this place was good pizza, but I honestly wasn't blown away by it. My four stars is for the kale salad! I'm not one to be blown away by a salad, but the kale salad had excellent flavor! It had an amazingly flavored creme fraiche and toasted pine nuts. The menu description doesn't do it justice, so I'd recommend ordering and finding yourself pleasantly surprised :)

The food at Spasso was okay. I didn't find anything spectacular about it. I gave them four stars though because the atmosphere was amazing and the service is outstanding. Our waitress was very nice and let us make whatever adjustments we wanted to for our dish. I think there are other places I would try before going back, but it's definitely a nice outing.

I've been wanting to try Angelo's for a while after hearing so many great things about it. I called around 6:30pm on Wednesday; I had to call a few times because the phone was busy. I finally got through and picked up my order ten minutes later. They were closing early at 7pm, so I think I was one of their last customers for the night. The pizza was delicious and a good ratio of cheese to sauce! I wish they served slices but, other than that, it's a definitely a solid pizza joint worth visiting.

Vic's is my favorite sushi place in Philly! It's a small place on Samson that if you blink, you'll miss it.

I've always had great meals here and find it reasonably priced. It's definitely worth going with a couple of friends and getting their combo platters. Also, I'd definitely recommend the tuna dumplings, which are unique and delicious.

I first went to Stephens on State as part of an office holiday party. The food was amazing, so I was excited to try it again. I found an awesome Groupon that gave me $50 credit towards Stephen's for the price of $20, so I thought there couldn't be a better opportunity.

We ordered the crab cakes and seafood bucatini and both were excellent. The restaurant is a little on the pricy side, but I thought it was well worth it given the amount of seafood on our plates. The crab cake was full of fresh crab and the bucatini had plentiful prawns, scallops, and mussels. I'd definitely recommend this place for others looking to have a nice night out at a quality restaurant!

Crave creamery is my favorite ice cream shop in the Philly area! It has a wide selection of flavors and carries both gelato and ice cream. I've never had the gelato before because the ice cream is so good and I can never pass it up, but I'm sure the gelato would be delicious as well.

They have great flavors and the ice cream is super creamy.  They also have an assortment of fun cones. I got one with m&ms and it was okay. I would recommend going for the ice cream and trying one of their fun cones if you're interested, but pass on them otherwise.

Carl Venezia is amazing! It's a small shop that, if you blink, you'll miss it. My favorite is their turkey salad. Whenever I go, I always grab a large container of it. It includes big chunks of turkey, dried cranberries, celery, and dried apricots. This place is definitely worth a trip if you're looking for a quality deli shop.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Media! I especially love their soup dumplings, but their noodles and appetizers are also great. I've never had anything I didn't like at Dim Sum Mania. It's also really well-priced and you can get a lot of food without spending too much. Great food and great value--can't beat that!

I've been meaning to try this bakery for a while now after seeing several articles about it online. I ordered a lox bagel and a slice of babka. The lox bagel was yummy, but I wish it had more of the fixins like tomatoes and onions. But if you like heavy lox, this is a good choice for you! Personally, I preferred the babka over the lox bagel. It was soft, fresh and not overly sweet. I'll definitely need to go back to try the rugelach and apple cake.

Insomnia cookies are soooo good! You wouldn't think they're that great because it's a chain, but these cookies are seriously some of the best I've ever had. You can't go wrong with the flavors. Also, their ice cream is really yummy too. I'm not sure where they get they're ice cream from, but it's super creamy and rich. There's plenty of locations around the city, so you should definitely check it out if you get a chance.

I've been to Bare Burger a few times before and it's decent, but I feel like there are better places in Philadelphia to get a burger (like Village Whiskey). The bun wasn't as fresh as I remembered and the bacon was really fatty. Also, I wish there were tables set up in front so we could eat outside, but they weren't. Overall, it's decent for a fast burger that's a step above fast food.

I know Ocean City Coffee has quite a following, so I've been wanting to try it. I'm not much of a coffee drinker, so I got the pumpkin spiced chai. It was good, but pretty sweet. I'd probably tell them next time to include less sweetener. Also, I wish it was served a bit warmer. We also got an iced Irish Cream coffee which had great flavor. Overall, it's worth trying because they have a long list of flavors and friendly staff.

If I could give McConnell's ten stars, I would! This is probably the best ice cream I've had in California (possibly ever!) It's super creamy and rich. All the flavors looked amazing. 

I ended up getting the sweet cream and caramel brownie, which is one of their more popular ones. It's a pretty sweet ice cream flavor, so if that's not your thing, you may want to try one of the other flavors. My favorite thing was how many brownie chunks were in the ice cream! They definitely don't skimp out. This place is a must-go if you're in the area!

This place is great to grab a healthy, quick bite right by State St in Santa Barbara. Their açaí bowls were huge and super filling and they have a lot of unique smoothie flavors. Also, I tried one of their breakfast bowls and they were great! Definitely a more sophisticated version of your average oatmeal. If I went back, the bowls would definitely be my first choice.

My sister recommended this place to me having been here several times before. Everything was really flavorful and the portions were super filling. My favorite thing (maybe surprisingly) was the Los Agaves Salad. It was filled with great flavors, everything from the chicken to the beans and even the dressing were all delicious! The cheese enchiladas and nachos were also great as well, but something about the salad made it a standout.

This place is great to grab a quick bite. I loved their menu--they have everything from plates to bowls to salads and everything's fresh and healthy. I got the avocado lentil salad which I would highly recommend. I added the falafel, so the salad was extra filling and probably could've been split between two people. I'll definitely be going back when I want something quick and healthy.

B3o-d34B7mFEzbc8pWWW5Q.review_text: My wife and I were visiting from NY and heard about this place from an aunt who lives close by.  Phenomenal food, decent prices. Wait staff could be more attentive. The seafood was way better than expected, living right on the coast we didn't think they would be fresh seafood places in the Midwest, we were definitely wrong.
Horrible. Never again. Pizza was ridiculously mushy and cheese along with ALL toppings slid off as slices were lifted.
We normally do drive-thru, but my wife and decided to go in and sit down, we had a fantastic experience and our waitress Katie was absolutely phenomenal!

This was the first time my wife and I went to a Five Guys and we feel it is absolutely amazing! Hamburgers were delicious, fries are to die for. Staff was incredibly helpful and nice. Would definitely recommend this place.

Mediocre food, prices are above average. I ordered the triple delicacy and asked for no mushrooms...  Of course there was mushrooms in it when I got it. Ordered a side of white rice and it wasn't even fully cooked. Won't be giving them business again. Don't recommend.

I ordered a #6 no tomatoes, medium with a coke and small chilli. 

What I got was a #6 with tomatoes, with a Dr Pepper and a small chilli. No spoon, no ketchup, no straw and 2 napkins. 

Ya...  And they want $15 an hour.
Food is really good, prices are average, would definitely recommend this place over the other Asian restaurants in the area.
Can't even get simple orders right. Come on, it's really not that difficult. Clean atmosphere, so that's a plus.

Being from NY it's been hard for me to find good pizza in Indiana. This place came recommended, so I called to order a large pie, which apparently isn't how you order pizza out here. So I asked for a 20" to be delivered with 3 toppings and a sausage calzone. I was quoted $42... Huh?? That's just ridiculous. No thanks. It's actually cheaper for me to have pizza overnighted to me from NY, literally cheaper.
It's ok...  Ordering can be difficult if you don't order one of their pre-made menu sandwiches.
Prices were decent, food was great, service was attentive and prompt. I would definitely be coming back for more!
Great food, great atmosphere, service was attentive and prompt, good prices (lunch prices are phenomenal), what else can you ask for?? I will definitely be going back!
Prices were decent, food was great, service was attentive and prompt. I will definitely be coming back for more!

My wife and I ate here for the first time with a recommendation from a local doctor.  Food was phenomenal, top notch! Prices were great and our server's name was Nina she was phenomenal! I will definitely be returning and recommending!
Really slow service, had to repeat my order 4 times, at least the fries are fantastic.

Nothing more annoying than dealing with incompetent cashiers, I was asked if my card was credit or debt so I said credit...  I had to swipe three times because the teller said my card was invalid. Turned out she didn't specifically ask if it was master card or visa so she was running it as a visa and getting error messages.  

Other than that fiasco, the place is pretty cool. The pretzel dipper thing is amazingly good! 

Side note, there should ALWAYS be a manager on duty 21 or older during business hours.
Came here with some co-workers for a lunch meeting, I didn't care for the atmosphere much and felt the burgers were mediocre. Our waitress was great, fast, attentive and accurate.

Decided to try ordering from here again, we ordered two sausage calzones...  What we got were sausage, pepper and onion rolls. That's not a calzone. Calzones are almost half circle shaped and puffy with lots of ricotta and mozzarella cheese plus anything you want to add. 

At least the ordering process was way less painful this time.

My first time at a Dairy Queen other than New Jersey over 15 years ago, food could be better, service needs more intelligence and actually pay attention to the customer ordering, rather than staring at me saying "uhh, wait, what?" two or three times. Prices are a bit high for the quality. Won't be going back.
Food was meh, service definitely needs improvement, the language barrier is there but speed, listening and accuracy is also missing.

Service was slow, hostess had an attitude, California rolls had BROWN avocados, hot food was warm, and cold food was also warm... Food quality was definitely cheap tasting compared to other buffets in the area. Food trays were either empty or completely dried out and most of the food description tags were in the wrong spots.I'm sticking with Journeys.

The food is amazing, service has a language barrier but it's manageable. The wait time for lunch/dinner rush is ridiculous...  5-10 minutes just to order, 10-20 minutes to actually receive your food, and good luck trying to find a seat.

Less than mediocre food quality, the new England clam chowder and filet migon was the best of all the choices. The desert quality definitely made up for what they lack in the entree quality. 

Watch what you're being charged for, they tried to charge us 12.49 instead of 11.99. Fifty cents may not be much, but think about how many people on a daily basis they're overcharging....  It adds up.

This place is awesome! Been looking for a movie theater like this since we moved here. Food is good, theater itself was very comfortable and nice size movie screen. Service was friendly and attentive. Prices are a bit steep, that's my only dislike.
Food is pretty damn good, especially the calamari. Service was great, atmosphere is a bit louder than expected. Prices are overboard, $28 for a 12oz ribeye is ridiculous.
Food and service are mediocre, prices were higher than they should be, the seating is small and tight. Atmosphere is average.
Delicious food, decent prices, great service! Will definitely be returning and recommending.

I ordered here for the first time and I had one pretzel dog and one large pretzel...  The total was a whooping $10... 

While the pretzels were good, the prices are absurd. Service was nice, a bit loud when greeting customers.

Went here with my wife for the first time and I gotta say, I'm impressed with the place. The DIY style is awesome, the flavors are great, and there's a plethora of toppings to boot.  The prices are a bit high, but I'd go back.

Went to eat here for the first time with my wife. The store is a bit smaller than expected and very stuffy, it was 90+ outside though and prices are a tad high. 

With that being said, the food was great, service was ok and very polite. We both ordered the Brownsburg Cheese Steaks, I had potato salad (which was phenomenal, btw) and my wife had the mac & cheese.
Food wasn't that good, service was extremely slow and what they charge for the quality is not accurate. Won't be going back.

Great food, great prices, great atmosphere. Love it! Will definitely be returning and recommending.

I would much rather support a small local business than a chain, especially with these qualities.
We had a great experience with our waitress,  Samantha.  She was fantastic. Food was pretty good, prices were cheaper than expected. I would definitely go back.

Food is decent, prices were better than expected. Our server, Juan was horrible, he would disappear for long periods of time, at one point we had to ask the hostess to find him.... Twice. Atmosphere could use some changes, I get the decor, but it's too much... bull.

Won't be going back.
Amazing burgers and great customer service  plus free peanuts lol.  Prices are a little steep though

Mediocre at best. Chicken parm was bland,  baked ziti was decent, meatballs weren't good at all, the sausage was great however ridiculously expensive, $8 for 2 links. 

Service was pretty good, attentive and refilled drinks without asking, so that was awesome. 

The place is kind of small and cramped..  The decor is too much, random pictures everywhere. 

One of the strangest things I've ever seen in a restaurant, you walk past the kitchen and food stations to be seated. Food sitting on counters could be easily contaminated by something contagious with a cough in the right direction.
Food was absolutely delicious, service was on point and prices were really good too. We would definitely be going back!

Had to wait 25 minutes for our food, they brought me the wrong dish twice, so they had to refire my ticket twice.. Another 15 minutes. 

Service was mediocre, prices of course are ridiculous. 

Would NOT recommend.

My wife and I went here for the first time and we were really concerned with the amount of negative reviews.

We watched our movie and ordered some food.. We had potato skins and 2 burgers.

The theater overall had an awful smell and the floors were dirty, one of our menus had a gun drawn on it... Not sure why the employees would not throw out a defaced menu. I asked the young lady at the counter if she smelled that sulfuric smell but all I got was a blank stare. We later found out that the smell was coming from the restrooms... Backed up sewage maybe? 

The food was shy of being mediocre, the burger serving dishes should be flatter to easier grab the burgers. 

Service was decent, although one of the waiters yelled at a table next to us from across the theater "Hey H10, I'll be over there in a few minutes" which I found pretty rude during a movie. 

The sound and picture quality was great, so that's a plus.

Absolutely THE worst Dunkin I've ever been to. They get orders wrong continuously, they run out of stock on items constantly, and asking to correct the order is like watching paint dry. I think the combined intelligence of the entire staff is that of a box of rocks. Never again will I give them another shot.

Out of all the times I have been here, there is always a female employee taking up a paying customer's seat, today she actually had her laptop with external speakers hooked up to it!

If there's down time, that's fine... But when customers come in to dirty tables, seats not pushed in, and have to wait for you to refill food as they order, it's unacceptable. Get off your lazy butt and take care of your store then go play with your laptop.

Food is delicious, service is decent, prices are pretty good.

Food is good, small portions and expensive. Service is slow and not attentive, I literally watched 4 employees stand at the end of the bar just chatting amongst themselves before I had to make a loud noise to get attention, after the second time of waiting 10+ minutes for someone to check on us. 

The atmosphere is nice, very well lit and laid back.

It's an average place. The "award winning" ribs were a disappointment, the sides would not be worth ordering again. We paid approx $20 per person which is decent, and service was ok.

I would not recommend Pit Stop, but I would also not detour someone from going either.

Food was amazingly delicious! Service was good too, and orices were not wallet breaking.

I would definitely return and recommend.

Below average quality of food, prices are "ok". They charge $2 per can of soda, so be warned. 

Very loud and crowded atmosphere.

The sushi seaweed is very chewy and thick, spicy tuna rolls tasted very "fishy" which is not good. The staff was pretty friendly though. 

Overall, we wouldn't go again.

Been here a few times over the past couple of years and also had orders delivered via DoorDash.

Never had bad service, and the food is absolutely delicious, prices are decent for the quality and I would absolutely recommend McAlister's if asked.

If you like potato salad, get theirs, it's to die for!

Upon entering, you immediately get punched in the face by the smell of stale cigarettes. I was a smoker for almost 25 years and thought it wouldn't bother me, but I couldn't believe how bad this place smelled and got worse the longer I sat there. 


Food is below mediocre, and that's being nice. If it were free, I would probably still pass on it. 


Prices are outrageous for the quality of the food, service and atmosphere. 


Service is very slow, and definitely not up to the speed of a lunch crowd. 


When I was finished eating, I literally sat for almost 20 minutes waiting for someone to return to the bar so I could get my check and go back to work. 


I would not recommend Jimmy B's nor would I return here.
I've ordered from here with doordash many times. The food is great and amazingly consistent, prices are very reasonable. I would definitely recommend!

Bezh6tDmCrL0-SnsV6CneA.review_text: I could see myself coming here a lot for happy hour if I lived/worked around here. They have awesome HH specials. The decor is modern and chic. Service is fast. I had an early dinner here with a few friends. We got two happy hour appetizers and shared 3 small plates. That was more than enough to fill us up. Portions are generous. We had the california ahi tuna burgers. They were substantial mini burgers. Also tried the spanish peanut crusted goat cheese with crackers. Not bad, but probably needed more lavender honey. The baked penne was nice and cheesy with bechamel. It was about $60 for 3 of us including HH drinks.

Yummy gelato. We came here after dinner. I'm glad I don't live near any gelaterias, because I'd go ALL THE TIME. There are tons of flavors. Make sure you sample! I ended up with the bananas foster and pistachio. Pistachio was smooth and nutty. Consistency was creamy and rich. No complaints here! $5 for a small. Not too cheap but it's very filling.

I had to visit because my cousin was raving about their chocolate croissants (like another reviewer, he also associates chocolate croissants with the bus stop), it's only a few blocks from my hotel, and I LOVE patisseries. 

It closes at 6pm on weekdays. I wasn't able to stop by until 5:40pm after work. As I predicted, the delicious chocolate croissants were sold out by now. But, a few almond croissants were left, as well as a lot of muffins, cookies, and madeleines. AND they were all 50% off (I'm not sure what time this sale begins every day). I didn't want this trip to the patisserie to be in vain, so I purchased an almond croissant and madeleine and happily went my way. 

The almond croissant was so fresh, airy, and flaky. The almond filling was not overly sweet. I'm definitely going back for the chocolate one... The madeleine was the underdog of the evening. It was simply AMAZING. I've had a lot of madeleines in my lifetime and this was the most perfect madeleine I've ever had. It was moist, cakey, not dry at all, and slightly crispy on the edges (I totally dig crispy). $3 for the croissant and madeleine. I highly recommend both! But, really, don't overlook the madeleines!

Also, the service here was great. I also saw tons of beautiful tarts and cakes that would be perfect for a birthday celebration.

**Update: I did make it back for chocolate croissant and it was as consistent as the almond croissant. I also tried a vanilla macaroon (which I spied in a huge apothecary jar near the cakes). It was too voluminous and crispy. Not chewy enough. Wouldn't recommend, but they sure are pretty to look at.

I had a happy hour/early dinner here last night. This place had a lot to live up to based on all the reviews I read on Yelp. Tria did not disappoint!

I started with a glass of  gamay, a "lighthearted red". The tuscan white bean dip was good and flavorful. Came with toasted baguettes and they even brought extra for free! The truffled egg toast was yummy. The mission figs with gorgonzola and proscuitto and bruschetta with brie and cherries were two sweet and savory dishes. Both were well balanced and flavorful. We also ordered the smoked duck salad with strawberries and pistachios, which was amazing. And they split the salad into two, without asking :) We shared the blackberry pudding for dessert. And I have to say that this was the most disappointing part of the meal. It was bland and unflavorful. Even with the chocolate syrup... 

Good portion size and great service. Great prices and portion sizes. I'd highly recommend coming here for good food, drink, and ambiance. I'd prefer to give this place 4.5 stars because of the dessert, but since Yelp doesn't give half stars, Tria gets a 5.

I love Chick-fil-a. Unfortunately there isn't a real CF in NYC. Imagine my excitement when I saw someone carrying CF on the streets of Philadelphia. 

I stopped by the Liberty Place Food Court about 10 minutes before closing. I was a little worried that I might get turned away due to the late hour, but nope. I got served in a minute. 

MMM. I love my chicken. The fries could've been a little crispier though.

A visit to Acme Oyster House is requisite for any oyster lover. 

Granted, the first time I came here during my 28 hour trip was for jambalaya. My friend wanted jambalaya and we got that along with some gumbo and oyster shooters. The jambalaya and gumbo were good but not out of the world amazing. A tad bit too salty for me. The oyster shooters were strong (maybe we should've mixed them better). 

After we ate here I met up with Angela C and read her review for the Metairie location... I will jump on her bandwagon and STRONGLY recommend the chargrilled oysters. When my friend and I were perusing the menu, I said "Ew, I don't want to eat cooked oysters" when I saw the chargrilled item. I bite my tongue. As Angela later described to me in person, as I was salivating, the oysters are shucked and placed on the grill in its half shell and then some delicious things are placed on top of the hot oyster, French escargot style (which I also LOVE). The chargrilled comes in 1/2 dozen or a dozen. The 1/2 dozen was more than enough for me...

But, that did not stop me from ordering the 'peace maker' fried shrimp and oyster po boy. This was my last stop before the airport and I needed to maximize my NOLA food intake. The peacemaker is huge. Angela and I shared one. Its hefty height makes eating messy. I like the tabasco-infused mayo and the oysters here are so fat and juicy! Also recommend. 

Don't come here if you're looking for something healthy. A lady sat next to me and asked the bartender if they had steamed veggies or salad. "Is cole slaw salad?"

I will mention that the two times I came here during the late weekend afternoons, I went straight for the bar. We had excellent and friendly service from the bartenders. The second time I came, I thought I'd arrived just in time - they had a employee holiday party starting at 5pm, but they continued to seat people through 4:40pm ;)

This is a great place for a good, cheap bite.

I planned a last-minute weekend trip to NOLA which coincided with a medical conference. I could not get a reservation here. We were determined to try this place, so we decided to drop by anyways, and snag seats at the full service bar. 

We got here around 7pm on a Saturday. The three of us had just sat down in our just vacated seats when the hostess informed us that there had been a cancellation and if we would like a table. Not surprising considering how many empty tables were in the dining room and the medical conference people are flaky.

The three of us are girls with decent appetites, but we did not want to do ourselves in at one place. We shared three appetizers and two entrees. They also gave us an amuse bouche of seafood egg custard sabayon with truffle foam. It was very fragrant.

Appetizers:
- P&J Oysters cooked three ways. Fried with creamy dressing, cooked in a foamy broth, and horseradish crusted in a spicy sauce topped with bread crumb (it looked au gratin). I think this one shouldn't be missed.
- Gnocchi in a creamy truffle sauce topped with shaved truffles. This was amazing and a good portion! (I was semi-surprised later to see that it was $19, but I digress.)
- Mushroom soup. Asian mushrooms in clear broth. I didn't mind it - it had the Asian medicinal taste. My friends hated it. Definitely an outlier of the meal.

Entrees:
- Duckling. This was so succulent and well flavored. It came with a side of grits, roasted duck foie gras, and candied quince. I highly recommend this dish.
- Scallops. We ordered the scallops from the tasting menu. I thought they were also awesome - they were stuffed with fatty bacon and had a side of bone marrow! My friend didn't like it as much. We later found out that her scallop wasn't as well cooked.

Service was attentive. We did not linger too long because we had more places to hit up. The wine list was extensive - we had two glasses of a full bodied Italian red. Our check came with meringue cookies and some brittle. 

If I visited NO for a longer period of time, I'd visit again and order the degustation menu.

This place is a big institution in New Orleans. We went for the Sunday Jazz Brunch. There were probably 10 people who welcomed us as we ascended to the second floor. There were only two other tables seated on the second floor so we weren't happy about being 'put in the corner', away from the live music. Eventually the place started filling up and we found out the musicians travel room to room. 

Despite the overabundance of staff, it took our waitstaff (we're not really sure who our server was) 30 minutes to give us menus. Perhaps this is the Southern, relaxed way of eating that us Yankees are not used to. 

The garlic bread was excellent. We asked for another round, especially since it took a while for the food to come and we weren't that interested in cocktails. 

When any of the courses are served, everyone is served at the same time (and maybe that's why it was hard getting our servers' attention.)

Note: All entree prices include appetizer and dessert. 

I started with the soup du jour which seemed to be seafood roux based. Not bad. My main was the Eggs Couchon De Lait which were delicious and perfectly cooked. The portion size is huge! The poached eggs and pork shoulder sat perfectly on biscuits with a generous drenching of Tabasco hollandaise. My friend got the Whiskey Smoked Chicken and Eggs which were similar except with a stronger kick. The third got the shrimp and grits with BBQ sauce (he doesn't like BBQ and did not like the grits - poor guy).

The desserts we tried were amazing! Make sure you save stomach space! We diversified and shared among the three of us. Some desserts take longer to prepare so they said something about preorder, which we did when we placed our order, but it still took a while. We tried the Creole Bread Pudding Souffle (add $3) with hard sauce. SO good. I wish I could eat some right now. The chocolate molten cake was standard - would not recommend. The praline parfait was a delight. The ice cream is wrapped in a round wafer "house" with two round windows so you can access the ice cream. And the cream and sauce steps it up a notch. 

In retrospect we should've ordered two meals for three because we got hit with a major bout of food coma afterwards. If you're in town for a short trip, know that this meal can't be rushed - budget time for it. 

Four stars because the soup wasn't that good and I wish service was faster (in getting us menus and the check). It was definitely attentive - we timed how long it took for an 85% full glass of water to be topped... 5 minutes.

I was a tourist and gave into the Hurricane gimmick. Set the tone for the rest of the night. It was good and cheap. We people watched for a while under the heat lamps - there was some holiday party going on. Bathrooms are really clean.

My friend swears she saw a creature running around in the outside area the other night. What's more surprising is that the bartender said he's never seen one of 'em around.

Visiting for the weekend. Got a pourover and a coffee. The pourover took a while and they didn't start preparing it until well after I got my coffee - so don't get that when in a rush. Good coffee.

Negatives:
It was a hot day outside and it was hot inside - definitely did not feel like there was A/C. 
There were bugs flying around the pastries. Looks like someone else commented on it too. 
The door behind the coffee bar was open - doesn't look the cleanest back there.

I love pie. I barely did any research for the trip and saw it in the WHERE magazine while I was browsing at the hotel. We had brunch next door, so finding out that the one other place I wanted to go to was next door was a win-win. There is plenty of seating inside; the interior was tastefully decorated and clean. 

I internally balked at the price of $5-6 per slice of pie and got two slices (caramel apple and butterscotch bourbon) to go. Both pies were good and more than enough to share with some family since everyone just wanted a few bites. Pricey, yes. Quality, yes. Sweet but not overly sweet.

Per their Instagram, they have some dine-in specials on some evenings.

Sunday brunch. Arrived late morning to a half full restaurant. You order at the counter, find a seat (unless someone sits down while you're in line), and they bring the food to you. The number of brunch specials was equivalent to the size of the regular menu. I got shrimp and grits - spicy, polenta was drier than expected, very large portion. He got carnitas benedict - also spicy and huge. Decor reminded me of Ikea. Pretty casual. You can easily combine tables for a larger table. 

Two entrees + two OJs (freshly squeezed earlier) + two iced coffees = $40. Everything was delicious but wouldn't have minded a smaller, reasonable portion size.

Two night stay. On Friday, the AAA breakfast rate was in the $160s with breakfast, so we did that. On Saturday, it was $300+. We didn't feel like paying or doing cash and points and used 15k Hyatt points (via Chase). No status.

After reading all of the reviews, it was apparent that this is an old, historic hotel with renovated and unrenovated rooms. The renovated ones naturally got higher marks. We got in really late on Friday night. I asked for a renovated room (which I think is translation for an upgrade - not sure if they have any smaller, non-suite rooms that are renovated as of this time). They didn't have availability for a renovated room for both nights. We were fine with changing rooms and ended up getting a huge one bedroom suite for Fri night (their largest one, I think it's called Arte) and a normal unrenovated room for Sat night. 

Needless to say, we were very impressed with the suite. It had really high ceilings, its own Keurig with tons of capsules, a Mac computer, rainfall shower, iPod speakers, a dining room area, a living room area, and closets. Not much of a view. 

Pros:
- Location. Central enough that we could walk to the places we wanted to go in 20 min or less. It's also attached to a shopping center and Starbucks. 
- Free wifi! Elites get premium for free. The standard speed was good enough for streaming Netflix. 
- Parking. Use the garage. Give your ticket to the attendant. You get in-out privileges. We ended up not using the car at all during our stay because we could walk everywhere. (Price was not a pro - $30 for self parking.)
- If you get breakfast in your rate, the buffet is a nice touch, however, is not at all impressive... will review that separately. 
- Great lighting in the two rooms we stayed in. 

Cons:
- Hyatt website directions. When I looked up parking on their mobile website, I was pretty confused on where to find their parking garage. Pull up to the garage right next to their main entrance.
- Creaky. Both beds in both rooms were super creaky.
- Beds weren't comfortable.
- Vents blew on where your head goes on the bed. One of us got sick.
- Needless to say the unrenovated room conditions were meh. (You can console yourself with the history of the hotel.)
- Shower in the unrenovated room. It was like a hose - that much pressure is unnecessary and not at all eco.
- Noise. The unrenovated room was a few steps from the main elevator bank. It's in an alcove with two rooms facing each other and a lovely armchair. Anything that is said in that tiny alcove is heard in the room and the bed is right next to the front door. The armchair encouraged someone to take a phone call from there. 

All in all, we felt neutral about our stay there and would probably stay here again since it's convenient and we can use Hyatt points.

Sunday brunch. Around 9:52am, I happened to go on OpenTable and see spots open for 10am (opening time) and 10:45. I snagged the 10am and we got to the restaurant a little past 10am. There was a long line out front (at least 10+ deep) - and it quickly became apparent that it was the 'no reservations' line. We checked in with the hostess and were promptly seated. 

Remy was our server and very gracious. We got our drinks right away and the jalapeno cornbread. Our entrees were a little slower (pretty sure the table next to us got their order in after ours) but nothing crazy like some of the reviews I read here. 

- Jalapeno cornbread. These were 5 little muffins and came with butter. Came warm, not bad but not great either. We were hungry so finished all of them.
- Eggs Atchafalaya. They did not skimp on the crabmeat. In fact despite having crabmeat in each bite, I still had some leftover once I finished the eggs. This was a satisfying but not grossly so type of dish.
- Softshell Crab (Special). It was good but a little too artery clogging. It came with some greens and green pepper grits.
- Grits (Side). Huge side... I had some and couldn't do more than a few bites. 
- Alligator Sausage (Side). 70% alligator and 30% pork. Not bad. Definitely worth trying if you've never had alligator and wouldn't otherwise. 

We thought the food was good/ok but not raving good, and probably wouldn't come back again (if we visited nola again).

We walked over here after Sunday brunch. There was a super long line inside, but we waited. Since we were so full, we grabbed 4 donuts and a buttermilk drop to go.

For those who also mentioned NYC doughnut plant, I don't think it compares... but the donuts here are quite good. I had:
- Buttermilk drop - too yeasty/doughy. That was one HUGE drop.
- Black cherry coconut - I couldn't taste the cherry or much coconut. It was kind of blah.
- Butterscotch pecan - I liked this!
- Boston cream pie - This was great. The cream was very light. 
- Cinnamon bun - After taking my order, the cashier went to prep the bun which was a highlight of my visit. He sprinkled cinnamon and then torched the top for a nice brulee. The topping is very cream cheesey.

The black cherry and butterscotch donuts were like most of the other ones - round and glazed on the top.

Check Instagram for their daily donuts.

I also got a cold brew, which was good. Wish there was time to try the sliders... but next time.

We came here because it was on the James Beard nominee list. We were able to get a later reservation of 7pm for Saturday, but had to sit by the bar, which was fine with me. 

- Beet salad: This was my favorite dish. It was spicy and I loved all the pistachios.
- Gumbo of the day: Chicken/Andouille sausage. In general, I don't find the appeal with gumbo, it is salty with no depth. This was no different At least the chicken was not tough at all.

And then it got worse. After the two starters, we waited a long time for our food. I didn't time it. We also didn't see our waiter walk by. Then, all of our small plates arrived. We had ordered 3 of them as an entree for two. Our dishes were warm but not hot. 
- Gnocchi with Pancetta and Parmesan Broth. Whoever said this was the best ever... hasn't been around much. The gnocchi was overcooked and tasted like a pile of dough, not in a good way. The seasoning was fine.
- Beef Short Rib with Potato Rösti, Salsa Verde and Horseradish Cream. The rosti was drowning in horseradish cream and there was a pool of it on the rest of the plate. The beef short rib was cooked fine but the overflow of horseradish made it underwhelming. 
- Housemade Spaghetti with Guanciale and Fried-Poached Farm Egg. The pasta did not taste homemade and also tasted limp and overcooked. The fried-poached egg was a fun touch, but overall, not a tasty and an underwhelming dish.

For dessert, we got the apple pie profiteroles. The puff didn't take fresh, more like fridge-fresh. It would've tasted better if there was more sauce, because otherwise the flavors did not taste grounded.

Overall, the meal was a disappointment. We're glad we didn't bother ordering any of the entrees.

Out of all of the places I dined at on this trip, GW Fins was my favorite. The mister had to work, so I made a reservation for one on OpenTable. I was seated promptly in a booth in the main room. 

Got a glass of white, the smoked sizzling oysters, and scalibut. It was my last night, so I was pretty decisive on what I wanted.
- Oysters: my only warning is that when it arrived at the table, it was very hot and sizzling. I pushed it further away and seconds later, touched one oyster (meat) with my fork, and some oil splattered, including on my forehead. I was obsessively checking forehead on my iPhone to make sure I didn't get burnt. The good news is my forehead is fine, and this dish was delicious! Really a great way to make these plump Gulf oysters shine. I didn't use the butter sauce, but it also didn't feel grossly heavy.
- Scalibut: it was a pricier entree, but hey, it's vacation. It was very well executed - the halibut was perfect and there was a thin layer of scallops to serve as the 'fins', seared just right. The lobster risotto was a nice complement. What I liked most about this dish was the portion size. Too many times I go to a restaurant and have to force myself to finish an entree because I don't want to waste (American portions). My hunger was satiated, and I devoured every morsel. I also like that there wasn't too much of the butter sauce (hate when it drowns the dish) and that there were some greens.
- Biscuits: these are baked freshly and doled out from the baking sheet. I had a little over one... the butter also comes are the right temperature.

Service:
- My waiter was nice but I couldn't tell if he was annoyed that I was seated at a table that could've fit a few more people (= more tip). He seemed very busy. Definitely didn't feel a connection there. I overheard another waiter animatedly recommending dishes to an adjacent table - they are definitely skilled at that. And as a solo diner, I was glad to wrap up my dining in an hour. 

I could tell it was a family run restaurant and looked it up before I wrote this review. All in all, I highly recommend making a reservation here if you love seafood!

My second time here. A must-visit to this classic NOLA institution if you want some fine dining and live music. 

I've only been here for brunch and couldn't get a reservation so walked-in at the Sunday brunch opening time and got seated right away in a corner table after a walk through the kitchen (everything looked so clean and organized, by the way.)

We did the pre-fixe menu:
- Bayou Brunch. Soft shell crawfish and oyster dressing. Yummy. 
- Shrimp and Tasso Henican. I think this is the shrimp app we had - tasted the acidity. I didn't care for it as much. 
- Pecan crusted gulf fish. Sweet corn sauce and poached blue crab. Like creamy things? You will love it. Very hearty.
- Louisiana Wild White Shrimp. I thought it was ok. Didn't care for the trinity. 
- Strawberry shortcake. Sounds simple but it was so good.
- Creole bread pudding soufflé. The whiskey sauce is drizzled upon serving. Can't go wrong. 

There is a dress code!

Summary: I would go for the gumbo, but the other stuff - meh. 

Pretty last minute reservation on OpenTable. Couldn't get anything between 5:45 and 9:15, so 5:45 it was. Need time to digest. Great location, nice decor. Stellar service. 

Apps:
Death by gumbo. Definitely the top of my gumbo experiences. Split into two bowls for us to share. One huge quail. 
Fire roasted oysters. A lot of breading. would recommend this elsewhere.
Crab beignets. I thought it was ok. 

Entrees:
Bouillabaisse. I thought it was ok. 
Napoleon. I also thought this was ok. Not that exciting. 

Dessert: 
Crunch peanut butter ice cream - love how the portion size was so small because we were so full. 

They also give you a dessert box of chocolates and cookies and such. 

Great service. Stool for your purse for those we hate to put your purse on the floor and it won't hang on the chair. 

Dress code: 
We saw lots of jeans. Maybe even a fanny pack. Smart casual.

Pro:
- Location. A brief walk from the action.
- Elevator access was fast.
- Doormen were friendly. 
- The rest of the lobby area/seating had the classy Ritz ambience. 

Con: 
- Paper thin walls and the gap below the front door was too big. I think we stayed next to a suite and their kids sounded like they were in our room. So loud. 
- The top of the toilet seat was not clean, if you know what I mean. That grossed me out and made me question other things in the room. They sent someone promptly to clean it.

Been here once, but don't think I'll be back. I had read about this place in Bon Appetit so I had high expectations. As a visitor to New Orleans, there is a lot of competition for stomach space.

I had a late lunch on a weekday. There was a film crew here taking up a corner of the restaurant. The place was pretty packed. 

I ordered the fried bologna and deviled eggs. 
- The fried bologna was good, but I got sick of the sweetness halfway into the large sandwich. Textures were great.
- I liked the fried chicken skins on top of the deviled eggs more than the eggs. Doesn't everybody? 

I was a bit confused after I got my order where the utensils or even napkins were. The film crew equipment had mostly obscured the shelf/wall that housed this stuff and since I was dining alone, I couldn't easily step away from my food to ask and there was a queue. 

It's a fun stop, especially if you like to try new places/highly rated places.  Take more people with you if you can so you can try variety.

We walked in for dinner once in September and sat at the bar. The meal was memorable despite the bar seating as the in-season corn was featured in every dish we ordered. I still think about that meal from time to time as a corn-lover. That was a 5 star experience.

TABLE: Fast forward a few years, we were planning to be in the area so I made reservations. They were for a Friday late evening in June. We arrived just before reservation time and was asked whether we wanted to sit inside or out, we said inside. I saw multiple open tables for 2. We were seated right away at what looked like the worst open table -- a table next to a pillar after you ascend the steps, the pillar didn't even run the full length of the table. Anyone getting up or walking by a table in our vicinity would block all the light. 

FOOD:
- The complimentary buns were delicious. 
- Food came out really fast -- the apps came out in 14 minutes and were the star (tuna crudo and garden salad). The tuna crudo had amazing balance of flavors and textures with the onions, radish, crunchy puffed rice, and whipped avocado. The garden salad had beets and strawberry along with some baked cheese. 
- Roasted duck was not bad. 
- The pappardelle pasta with lamb ok. 
- The side peas were a disappointment. 
- I normally go for dessert but I wanted to get out of there asap due to the uncomfortable table. 

We got our check within 50 minutes of sitting down. This experience ruined my memory of Talula's.

C5SZP7PSXx86tRe5bXulsw.review_text:
High quality food. The shrimp are SO GOOD. I like that it's a byob. 

My only disappointment was the small amount of pad thai in the take out order.  I was still hungry after eating.

Our number one bakery. My husband loves their red velvet cake and I love their strawberries and cream. 

I ordered a groom's cake for our wedding and it was gorgeous! It was so beautiful I gasped when I first saw what they created. I told Elizabeth I wanted a New Orleans cake and boy did she deliver! New Orleans skyline, vintage saints logo, and the cathedral compete with Andrew Jackson on horse!

I've been here a few times.  The coffee is good but the prices are high. The staff is very slow so if you're in a hurry to get to work don't bother coming here. 

If you're looking for a place to get coffee and sit  (if that's a spot even available! There's not much room) try the crepes. They are fresh and delicious.

Vegetarians! Get the Shroom burger. It's delicious! 

For those vegetarians who miss the experience of biting into a juicy hamburger, you have got to try this one. It's stuffed with Portobello mushrooms and cheese. I ate one last night for the first time and I'm already craving one again.  

Also try the custard dish (the exact name escapes me) with lemon curd, strawberry, and termini brothers canoli shells. It's delicious AND Shake Shack donates 5% to New Leash On Life- a program to better the lives of shelter dogs and inmates.

Casual, fun atmosphere. Lots of vegetarian options. Any meat can be swapped for tofu, Portobello mushroom, or vegan black bean burger. I had the Tennessee blue wrap with black bean burger swapped instead of chicken.  Good quality ingredients. 

Try the vegetarian chili, very good.

I left a comment on the other Bryn & Dane's yelp page, but yelp has two Bryn and Dane's locations? I think there's only one. 

Here's what I wrote: 

Casual, fun atmosphere. Lots of vegetarian options. Any meat can be swapped for tofu, Portobello mushroom, or vegan black bean burger. I had the Tennessee blue wrap with black bean burger swapped instead of chicken.  Good quality ingredients. 

Try the vegetarian chili, very good.

Good ice cream. I got the mint chocolate chip. My husband got the pralines and cream and wasn't impressed. We both agreed the praline had no taste. 

I gave an extra star because Bredenbeck's is the only ice cream shop open Sunday night after 9 p.m. It drives me crazy that things close so early around here, but Bredenbeck's was open and ready for our sweets craving.

This is my favorite Chinese restaurant in the area, hands down!

First of all, they have a vegetarian soup. Not a soup with veggies that is made with chicken broth. No, an actual vegetarian soup. This is a big deal to me because I grew up eating soup as the first course at Chinese restaurants and now that I'm a vegetarian I can never get soup anywhere we go. Try the vegetarian noodle soup. It's hot, filled with thin noodles, and stocked with real vegetables.

Try the mock general tso's chicken. It's delicious and vegetarian. Vegetable lo mein is greasy in all the ways you want lo mein to be.

Great coffee. Lattes are expertly crafted. 

Their  iced coffee is delicious and unique- they give you coffee ice cubes and you self-serve the hot coffee over it. I was skeptical when I first got the cup of ice cubes. I hate when I ask for iced coffee and the place pours hot coffee over ice. But Night Kitchen's is different. The coffee ice cubes really work their magic.  And because of this way of making iced coffee, you can also get decaf which is great for me.  

Try the yogurt parfait.  It's delicious. The granola is not skimpy and has pecans.

The pastries are also delicious. You really can't go wrong there!

Very small mussels. Like, really small. 

I was very excited to try this place out from all the good reviews on Yelp. We went Saturday night. It is a cozy place, just like the reviews said, but we found a space at the bar. The bartender, Tina I believe is her name, was really friendly and made a tasty vodka martini. I also liked that they served oyster crackers with horseradish as snacks at the bar. It reminded me of the seafood restaurants I would visit as a kid. 

The place is small, but well lit around the bar. The walls are decorated with fun sea life characters. The back booths were dimly lit so we opted for the bar because it looked depressing to eat back there. Since it's a small place, it can get loud. 

The food was ok. The butterfly shrimp were really the best- very big shrimp, nicely seasoned and fried. I ordered the broiled plate which came with tilapia, shrimp, and mussels. The sauce was buttery, which was delicious, but it was hard to eat the fish outside of the sauce and sometimes you want to just taste the fish! There were only two shrimp on the plate, which was disappointing because the shrimp were delicious. However, the biggest disappointment were the mussels. Really small. 

I'd go back. The drinks were good and the shrimp was great quality. Just would maybe not order the broiled plate again. The staff was very nice which also makes me want to go back.

Cool atmosphere . Service was friendly and fast, especially for a Saturday night! 

I had the Love Park sandwich. It was decent, nothing too spectacular. I liked the thick cut of mozzarella cheese on it, but could have done without the hummus. 

Great for an inexpensive and light bite to eat.

My friend and I went here today for lunch. The cafe is convered in art and felt very welcoming. There's a cafe space and more seating for eating in a separate room. 

They only had one menu that day. Apparently they're changing food and ordering more menus. It's a good thing we were the only ones in there or else we'd have to share with the other tables. They didn't have soup that day, or regular coke. This is definitely a quirky place!

Hummus platter: hummus is homemade. Not the typical creamy kind, more chunky and drier. Pita served warm. Feta cheese and kalamata olives were fresh and delicious. 

Halloumi salad: MUST try. The Halloumi cheese was so fresh and smoky. Delicious. 

Try the infused teas. Particularly liked the roobus chai tea. 

Will return!

I came back to change my review. I was a little hard on the place (blame the I need more caffeine headache!) I've been here more regularly since  then and it's become my favorite neighborhood coffee shop. Pricey, but well brewed. The cafe treats are fresh and well made as well. 

Lattes are great!
