Delicious!  I ordered the short stack with nutella and they did not skimp on the nutella. So good. Pancakes were light and fluffy. Lox, egg, and onion omlet was great as well! 

The staff is friendly and quick. Inside is clean and comfortable. It's byob, so we will definitely be back for dinner.

Great workout! The class pushed me past my comfort zone in the way I needed. Lauren was a skilled instructor with a warm and encouraging energy. The studio is clean and well lit, with a cold water filter to refill your water bottle.

My cheese garlic bread was like greasy cardboard, no flavor and soaked in oil, and the pizza was soggy in the middle and then dry and hard at the crust.  I am super disappointed because we ordered this for work about a month ago and it was great.  This order has me wishing I spent my $30 elsewhere. :(
I have only actually eaten here one time and everything my date and I had was delicious!  It was pretty busy and we had to wait for awhile to sit down, but it was worth it.

The food is always amazing and the sides change up all the time.  I have always had a good meal here.  Sometimes there is a bit of a line because its cafeteria like and you move down the line, pay, then seat yourself, but so yummy!  The workers are always friendly and enthusiastic.

The food was food but the service was just ok.  We ate late lunches so my boyfriend and I split a meal before a boat cruise to ride us over, but were wanting to have a few beers and relax. The older heavy set waitress with the flood pants was more concerned about the 5 top of people sitting next to us that were drinking water.  She did not ask us if we wanted another beverage, she just brought us the check so we paid and left. No wonder the landing has gone down hill

We had time to kill so we stopped in here seeing a sign that it was new and they had specials.  We went to the patio area and ordered 2 drinks.  The bartender/waitress brought food out to the only 2 other customers and said she would be back with our drinks. We waited almost 15 minutes then decided to leave because it doesn't take that long to open a bottle of beer.  Wish sho mes was still there because this was an awful experience. The bartenders were nice and attentive and there was live music, but it was so dirty and disgusting. Disappointed that the landing is falling apart.

The last visit took over 25 minutes with only 3 cars in front of us.  2 of our items were wrong and taco bell locations in are area are going way down hill. It really should not be hard to pit an order together.
Waited so long for an order that was wrong. Taco bell is going down hill in our area.

We went the first time and my steak had no flavor, the scallops were good, and the crab soup was good.  I expected a steak house could make a better steak than I can at home.  
Gave them another chance, they sat us at a table in the way of everything near the door.  There were people all over, kids running around and falling out of chairs (no place for young kids) and the wait staff would congregate around the hostess stand which is placed in a bad location.  At one point there were 5 employees standing there when we were waiting for water and alcoholic beverages.  My boyfriends potatoes which were the special very well could have been instant and the $15 lobster mac and cheese portion was not worth it either, very oily.  I am not sure we would consider a 3rd dinner here. Possibly drinks and apps only.
Well, it was a unique experience, but I would expect a German restaurant to have good food....nope!  Beer is great, but the food and service sucks.
We love this place.  Great food and good Bloody Mary Bar, but it could use some dusting.
Slowest location ever and god forbid they make a plain cheeseburger plain.  Rude staff
Ok if you like to hang out in Belleville.  We try not to.
Good food.  Good music. Just need a couple extra bartenders on busy nights.
Too many college aged people that like to fight.  Need bartenders that pay attention to tipping patrons.
Great cheap food. good music.  fun dive bar.  always welcome.
Great food especially tacos!  Yum!  fun bike nights
Better than the other location.  Service could be better, but food is always hot and correct
Nice little bar.  Good apps and great drinks
Nice atmosphere.  Wish the bar was bigger.  Fair prices and good food
Good fresh food.  Service could be better and the place needs a lot of cleaning and updating
Food is hit or miss and the service could be quicker and more friendly.  It has gone down hill since bikers dont go anymore on Thursday nights

So much better than the China King across from Hucks.
Food is hot and they deliver
Sometimes the service is awful.  WE used to go here often, but have cut way back due to that and the fact that 4 out of 5 of us had meals that were incorrect last time.
Best mexican food and service in the area.  We go here all of the time.  Ask for Angel and get a drink made by Freddie

CDh82JL-0-pZ_MedykEV_A.review_text: wow! Great Pho and outstanding service! the new owners are doing a great job look no further for a great bowl of Pho!
I have been here several times and the food is fabulous! all of the sauces are spot on and they really take pride in their food. the service is often a bit slow but it is surely worth the wait

Unfortunately this is my second time at Ella's only to confirm that it is a poorly run restaurant and bar. Without getting to detailed they screwed up our reservation for 10 and are out of 5 menu items at 4:56 PM on Sunday's (mind u there are 12 items on the menu) So that being said I would NOT come to Ella's hungry as odds are half of the items in their menu will be sold out! I  tell u what you do get really drunk and eat a lot of food and then comes to ellas to drink water and sober up!

I have been coming here for nearly 2 years and the food and service are second to none! All of the food here tastes like your long lost India mom made it from scratch! I have eaten India and Curry all over the world and this place cannot be beat! Monte is a top notch guy and makes sure everyone leaves happy!

OMG referred to this restaurant by a friend, and I was blown away! Brunch on a Sat offered awesome specials and drinks! Everyone at the table had different dishes and we all were giddy sharing each others food raving at how good everything was. Skip any other local breakfast lunch place and head right here for a fantastic meal,drinks and atmosphere.
2nd time at Jack's great little spot for some British old fashion treats. The Shepard's pie and meat loaf are awesome treats! Good prices and can always catch a football (soccer) game on the TV!

OMG everything at this small Spanish restaurant is unreal. I cannot go to Start Petersburg without popping in for the Lechon sandwich along with the orange ginger soda, it is my favourite! Although I have eaten nearly everything on the menu.

ah it was like being back in NY. A super high end organic food market and butcher! They also have a very diverse selection of foods to go, Ramen, sushi, aged beef burgers, poke bowls and special meals daily! You really must go eat and shop! Has the aged bone in Delmonico steaks were fantastic!

Awesome restaurant! Ever changing menu, with lots of super unique tapas type dishes. Had the quail, scallops and gnocchi each was equally awesome. Lots of great wines and beers. Very friendly staff and comfortable contemporary atmosphere. The prices are on the high side dinner for 2 with 1 drink each about $100. I found it to be fairly prices for the quality of food.

Very good New York style pizza! Location is a bit hidden you see the back of the shopping center from Fort Harrison but worth a bit of hunting. Great pizza and good prices. They sell zeppoles which I have not seen in a very long time!

Heard about this place so had to come try it. I love Indian food. This restaurant is awesome. I had the chicken 65 app, lamb korma and chicken vindaloo each was excellent . Restaurant is beautiful inside and out.

Wow! Upon arrival we were greeted by a bellman in the parking whom opened the door for my girl. Chatted us up while he escorted us up to the restaurant. On the way he took us for s quick tour of the pool! 

My first impression was Damn! This is one really comfortable chair! The burger selection is broad, I got the house beef with jerk rub, onion straw, smoked cheddar and arugula! OMG serious awesomeness! This is my second visit, and I'll be back again.
Awesome local produce and meats with a small but strong daily menu of specials and wonder drinks. Stop by for some unique simple foods, but be prepared to wait unless you come during off hours.
OMG good old fashion southern restaurant, I had the dark meat fried chicken mash potatoes and green beans. Was very juicy and crunchy! Have the banana pudding for desert! Good prices for great food.

Sandy's is a beach dive resturant. It is good for some quick bacon and eggs or a Sammy. I would not say anything is awesome, but everything is good and the prices are inexpensive. The place needs a face lift and a freshening up across the board

Looking for some BBQ decided to try this place. Yea well is generally sucked, was below average at best. They were out of ribs, got rib tips were fatty chunks   of hard meat with some store bought BBQ. Mac and cheese was bland and the collards tasted like someone spilled vinegar in it. I mean really give me tender meat with yummy BBQ sauce, I am not even picky with BBQ

The BBQ here is above average, I had the ribs which were good, two people had brisket and smoked turkey. The meats were good but their BBQ sauce is just not good, sweet too sweet. Spicey was not and the house is blah tomato. They should go to the store and buy some Rufus Teauge BbQ and serve that.
I have been here twice the food and service are excellent. Try their chicken tikka masala, quite good. They tend to be very cautious on level of spicy, so ask for it HOT if you want spicy medium
Very nice new wave German food spot. Several different food selection, helpful business owner. Grad a quick smoothie or a full german meal

WHOA super nice atmosphere, super friendly staff and awesome selection of foods. Lots of home cooking items with a twist. Chicken and Waffles, pot roast, cubans everything i have had was awesome. Be sure to ask for Nicole, awesome service!
Possibly the best burger i have ever eaten! I habe been here 12 times and when i leave i feel like i just won a war versus the yummiest prime burger ever!

Called to place order, was on hold for 5 minutes at which time I asked the person to hold for 1 second while I grabbed order, they put me back on hold for another minute. Then I attempted to order ribs, which they told me they had none, they would have them in an 1.5 hours. On top of this the last time I was there, the BBQ was like watery and gross. I was ordering to go food, so I can use my own BBQ sauce. I will NOT be back!
The best healty food in St Pete. Everything in the meun is Fantastic! The salmon and hanger steak is off the hook. Everything is Gluten Free!
STRAIGHT OUT OF NY. They have legit NY pizza. Awesome sauce, perfect cheese, NY water and crispy crust. Get some.
GREAT FOOD, and excellent location. Ability to eat outside, gets lots of small dishes for sharing. One of my go to places for casual fine dining.
Awesome variety of Asia foods. You will normally have to wait but not long. They have lots of outdoor seating which is COVID FRIENDLY.  Great for sharing dishs and trying lots of different dishes.

If you are from NY or have visited an italian  market there this is the answer. Lots of prepared foods, awesome selection of baked goods, fresh pasta and a cheese room! Can get insanely busy of the weekends, try to go on off hours during the week.

CONgXa5bkxl2wHzw1WEE4A.review_text: The food is amazing....I had the lamb is was so tender and good. I will definitely go here again
Grass fed burger really good cooked to order. Drinks were just okay...service was kinda slow but it was lunch time...
Great happy hour celebrated my nephew birthday here had an amazing time.  Food and drinks were really and the prices also
Ate here for lunch today ordered the Jungle pork it was amazing. Victoria was so nice I will definitely eat here again...
Food was not good..drinks were horrible I had the bartender make the margarita over and it was worse...
I went here on a Friday night the food was excellent. The crowd was very young but music was good...
All I can say is Omg...Freaking amazing prices were cheap for the quality and portion size . I live in the surburs and it was worth the drive into the city.

Went here on Friday night nice crowd..live bands we sat outside drink menu was a little odd never had heard of any of the drinks so i played it safe an order a Mojito it was okay. There wasn't much on the dinner menu so we ordered appetizers which were very good. Nothing really special about the place so I probably wouldn't return. Wait staff was very nice an attentive.

Went here for lunch my niece and I the place has a mildew smell . I guess because it's very old. This place is in a great location but needs to be updated. The food was just okay not worth going back twice. The waitress and hostess were very nice. I didn't take any pictures of the food it just wasn't worth it..

Went here for lunch after visiting someone at Temple hospital location is right around the corner but anyway on to the food..it was hot fresh and a very large selection. We had Curry chicken an Jerk chicken with 2 sides platters were $10 which I felt was cheap for the portion size. I will definitely eat here again.
Had lunch here today the food is always good no matter if its pizza or a full entree. Its tucked away in a corner but this place is a definite go to for real food
Just grab a jerk chicken burrito from here it was really good.  I also order a side of rice it was also favored nicely. I will definitely frequent this place when I'm feeling like Mexican food.

Went here for lunch the food was seasoned nicely. The restuarant is definitely a little upscale nice place for a first date. We had chicken, new cod fish special, mac an cheese, brussels spouts. All was very good.

Ordered Mediterranean pizza it was better than I  could expected. The topping very overflowing and had a lot of flavor. The girl at the counter was pleasant an so was the cook. I will definitely order from here again...

Stopped here for a late lunch after shopping and glad we did. The staff was friendly and prompt. The have variety of beers and drinks also the bar is huge. We ordered appetizers they were so large we had to take our dinner home. Nice place even if have children with you.
Ordered from here a couple of times. Food is good however I find most things are too salty.

I've eaten here two times in the last two weeks. The food is authentic and very flavorful. It's a place you must try. I was so happy to find this place in Levittown. Sorry I didn't post any pictures of the food but if you like Pho you will love this place.
Went here again last night. Amazing as the first time. Had the lamb and eggplant took a bottle with us also love this place.

Best salads in town. I have eaten here for years everything is freshly prepared. I had a tuna salad for the first since I'm watching my weight line and it was really good and enough for two days. I also ordered a chef salad for niece it was also good an enough for two days. So if you are ever in Levittown check them out you won't regret it

Did the lunch buffet here it was really good. If your unsure of what to order at an Indian restaurant this is the place to try. A lot different option hot and fresh with name tags above with complete descriptions. Not to mention its 6 days a week. I will definitely be back again...Sorry I forgot to take the pics....

Went here on Monday around 4pm it wasnt crowded at all. There were a lot of different selections especially if you like seafood. I'm not really big o n buffet but this was actually pretty good. I forgot to take pictures but it had to be over 100 different choices. My boyfriend loved it since he eats crabs, mussels, salmon, sushi, shrimps, crawfish. I would probably go back again on an off day when everything come out fresh right at the start of dinner. They also had coupons for $3 off but it was cheap without it. The buffet was $13.99 per person. Perfect place if you have kids since there was something for everyone and I'm allergic to seafood.

Stopped here for lunch on a Sunday haven't been here in over year but only because I live the suburbs. This place is so damn good. I love pork so I had the Pernil sandwich with everything. I ordered French fries made to order also nice hot an fresh. They had my favorite cake Tres Leche so I was a happy girl. So don't sleep on this place it is so good. You can eat in or take out either way you won't be disappointed.

I went here for take out after work. The food was good however I felt the price was way to high for the portion size. I think I would take a 20 min drive to the city for same food but cheaper and platters much bigger.

I  went here to grab lunch for my nieces . Place was very clean staff very nice. We ordered take out which consisted of buffalo chicken cheese steak, hot wings, chicken fingers and fries everything was good I i will return again. Oh and FYI I love the way the name the steaks after streets in the city kinda  cleaver. Sorry no pics I forgot to take them. But try this place out you wont be disappointed....

We have eaten here twice and the pizza is so good. I'm a pizza girl and this is my new favorite place. My man always goes in for take out and he said Adam who works there has supreme customer service. I've only had pizza so far but I'm sure we will be trying a lot more. Sorry no pictures I'll post some next time I go. Oh and prices are great and the slices are huge!

Went here for a girls night out on Friday. The food and drinks were so good. Nice size potions and drinks were strong (which I love). We order clams, mussels, salmon, filet Mignon (land and sea)) and Chicken Marsala. The service was great and they have outdoor seating and a full service bar. This place is good for a date night or a family dinner. The only negative I can say it is a little tricky to get to with all the construction going on but well worth the drive. I would definitely go here again!

Great spot for breakfast. Gets crowded very fast but definitely give this a try. I went on Sunday morning the food was fast, hot and fresh and the waitress I had in the back was very thoughtful she even came over and turned up the air conditioner. This is my new go to breakfast spot!

This little spot is my go to for Spanish food. I've been here several times and the food is always good. The prices are cheap and everything is always fresh. I live about 35 minutes from this place but it's definitely worst a try. If I lived in the city this place would be a problem for me  since I know I would frequent more often.  They also cater for parties if your having an event. Sorry no pictures to post. I couldn't wait to eat my food! Lol
Went here on a Saturday afternoon for lunch. This place was packed but the line moved fast. We ordered so much food everything was good authentic Mexican tacos.

CrGpKBx77VoAr4SbSQf9Lw.review_text: This was a first for our Foodie Club. And we gave it 5F's (which is a good thing ). The fondue was fun. The food was Delicious (not so much the crepe with cream spinach, but can't wait to go back for the smoke salmon crepe!!). The atmosphere was lovely. The service was excellent.

Decided to explore and try something off our beaten path.  This is truly a hidden treat for the nearby locals and tourist who stumble upon it.  The food is the freezer looks like it might be good. As for my son's All That Jazz sandwich it was too salty he reports and my half shrimp and oyster was all over-fried bland oysters. I blame myself because I watched the man put all oysters on my sandwich and when I asked if it was half and half he said yes. So I left the store knowing it wasn't.

Took advantage of the $35 for $50 deal.  They were having register issues but the manager was so kind and accommodating.  I'm a sucker for good service.  The corn pudding is a treat for my family, bbq is decent for a chain restaurant.  Still hats of to the ladies managing the store keep up the quality service.

Our 5F crew (Fourth Friday for Friends and Foodies) went to Brightens.  Top notch customer service.  Gotta say the seafood platter was just ok for me, other crew members enjoyed.  Just seemed a little unnecessarily over pricey.  But great atmosphere, we didn't feel rushed, until we needed to be nudged with a move it along ladies.  Overall we give it a 4F's.

Our 5F (Fourth Friday for Foodies and Fun) group went recently. Luckily we made reservations because it was a busy place.  Everyone was friendly, food was good.  A couple of our dishes was on the salty side but overall we all enjoyed our food and the bill was extremely reasonable for dinner for 4.
First time visit.  It wasn't bad but we weren't blown away.  We had a shrimp plate and shrimp salad.  All staff were kind and helpful.

Came here with friends.  My first visit.  Thoroughly impressed with the food.  Very flavorful and enough for take home. The egg rolls are the bomb. Chef visited our table, which was very nice.  Our waitress was very attentive and kept my glass full.  I pray this local dining spot success for New Orleans East sake.

Finally BBQ on the Westbank.  Greeted with a kindness as soon as I entered the door.  Had trio, double ribs and brisket.  It was good.  Also had 15 wings, had to go so when I got home they were a bit soggy.  But a good taste.

I've been here before and never commented.  The food is decent the punch although extremely sweet is the bomb.  However, I refuse to patronize businesses that have poor customer service.  You already have to place your order through a prison style window, you shouldn't have be treated like a convicted criminal too.  I wanted to order a wings but refused after dealing with the nasty attitude.  So I took my gallon of remix and bounced.  She put my punch in the slide through and turned her back.  Planning to never return.
Yummy yummy unhealthy goodness.  Thank you to the kind store clerk who let me try before I buy.  Good customer services brings me back every time.

Went here on Mother's Day with my son. Found this place through my pal Yelp.  I've been craving BBQ so this was perfect, walked right in, no wait. Food was delicious. Would give it 5 stars but my son found a hair.  They quickly addressed.  All and all this is really good BBQ.  "I'll be back" (Schwarzenegger voice).

The food was delicious.  I can't wait to go back and try more items on the menu.  However, better than the food was the service.   I hope  the owners know that our waitress is priceless and no matter how good your food is, it is the customer service that keeps people returning.

Our 5F (Fourth Friday for Friends Foodies and Fun) selected Restaurant Rebirth for our dining experience this month and we are giving it 5F's (that's a good thing).  The food was DELICIOUS.  Our waiter was friendly, patient and attentive.  The manager Manny added the personal touch by coming over and greeting us.  The young fella outside took our photo with a smile. That food tho....the southern cooked greens and hominy and crawfish and tasso maque choux were sooooo good, I think all of the sides may be winners. We all had seafood and it was delicious.  Do try the shrimp and eggplant appetizer!!  Truly one of our favorite and most memorable dining adventures.  We'll be back (Schwarzenegger style).

Feeling ill today so I picked up some chicken pho to go.  It did not disappoint. I ordered a large and really once I put in all in a huge bowl at home it was enough for two.  I don't think this is the best pho in the city, but it meets your need if you're craving pho.  Feeling better (enough to write this review).  

I've been here several times and the staff are ALWAYS friendly.  Service trumps food for me.

Soooo this is my second visit to this new Italian pie on General Degaulle.   My first visit was ok. The staff were nice, accommodating with my order and the food mediocre.   So after receiving an advertisement in the mail that they would be selling donuts, I decided to pop in.   When we walked in we were met by a staff on her cell phone.  She continued her conversation and did not look at us until I picked up the menu at which point she looked like "what are you doing" and said sharply we're not open (note the business above).  I said oh ok, we were coming for donuts.  She turned to look at the empty donut display to confirm there were no donuts and told us we don't have any donuts.  I'm just saying.

Our 5F (Fourth Friday for Food Foodies and Fun) ladies decided to Eat Nola Noir this week choosing  Half Shell on he Bayou for our dining experience.  We're giving it 4 stars for those fresh cold and salty oysters!!!  The atmosphere was relaxing with great R&B song selections playing on the radio......woe oh oh oh ooooh on the radio (I digress).  Also ordered was charbroiled oysters, gumbo, crab cakes, stuffed mushrooms, grilled chicken wings, a seafood platter, BBQ shrimp and margaritas.  The food was good, well seasoned, and real NOLA Gumbo There just needs to be some efficiency improvements, one of our ladies got her wings when we all were mostly done with our food.   The staff were friendly, even stepping outside to take our pictures and calling on the owner to come out and join the photo shoot.  If you're looking for good seafood you won't go wrong here!!

I like it when a restaurant chooses one thing and does it really well.  I ordered to go and my fish was freshly fried, crispy and delicious. I wish they would make their own specialty tartar and not give out those nasty tartar packs that is basically mayo; the fish deserves only the best condiment.  Service with a smile would have garnered 5 stars.  Perhaps on my next trip.
Best kept secret in New Orleans East.  Quaint, small and friendly atmosphere.  The food is consistently good and easy on the wallet.  I'm wishing them much success.

This was my experience today at Cajuns. I go to this store often and never leave without spending $50 to $100.  I had previously noticed their sign of a 3% surcharge when using a credit charge.  Disappointed I made a mental note to bring cash.  Well today I wasn't prepared so I asked the cashier if I could not be charged the 3% surcharge. The sweet cashier called what I am assuming was the store manager.  I'm going to wrap this up.  A jerk came out and laughingly said I'm sorry I can't do that for you, I'd have to do It for others.  I expressed I think it's unfair you pass this cost on to your customers.  To which he responded you can leave your food, and he said it repeatedly to make it clear to me he did not care or want my business.  I'm sure you're saying you should have left.  But I was with a friend and was celebrating their birthday and I didn't want my protest to affect them.  But I will never return.

CsBCxUumiMviu7uhRD5wRg.review_text:
We were greeted nicely upon entering. It is an open
 airy and comfortable feel. The food was fresh. They didn't have one of the specials of the day for appetizers that we ordered. The food was good. They also had a yummy specialty lemonade. We were offered a complimentary dessert. It was tasty but the spice was weak or artificial tasting. The bread pudding itself was tasty.
This is a nice cool spot. The hurricane drink is their specialty drink. Great music - live piano.

The gumbo was great (lots of crab)! Real down home cooking. They gave us a warm greeting upon entry. The fried chicken was tasty and they have a buffet with a nice variety.  Some of the food was a little salty to taste so drink lots of water. The price is reasonable. I would visit again.

This restaurant has phenomenal food. We went to the bar for pre-dinner drinks which were great. It took about 45 minutes to get seated. We had the barbecue oysters with blue cheese - tasty! We also had the shrimp and grits, catfish, Shrimp étouffée grilled red fish and oysters. The food was really good. The reason for the 3 is for the service. Our waiter "Bill" wasn't pleasant at all. He strained himself to bring such items as straws and hot sauce to the table. He expressed displeasure with not getting a "good" tip from a nearby table. He complained openly about the customers. Maybe customer service isn't a good line of work for him.

The manager was really nice though---Customer oriented.

The food is good, in general. The variety is good. They have lots of options. The biscuits and corn bread are good. There's plenty of tasty meats and egg dishes; fresh omelets and poached eggs. The service is impeccable. It's worth the money. The only thing is that the red beans weren't tasty at all and a little thin; very saucy with less beans. I would visit again.

The food was really fresh. The grouper was excellently prepared. It was accompanied with fresh broccoli and a salad. 

They ran out of food such as salad dressing and desserts after they were offered. 

We waited a little over an hour to get seated at the bar/counter.

We waited 1.5 hours in 94 degree heat and it felt like 104 degrees. The chicken is good - seems like a light cornstarch based batter-- a little greasy and lightly battered too. The red beans and rice went down easy. The corn muffin had the texture and flavor that I enjoy the most. We also had mashed potatoes (real fresh potatoes); max & cheese; candied yams, and they give you a side of sweet peas. Refills on the unsweetened tea and some had it sweet. Thanks
The beignets are ok-- crispy, square and sort of flat. The flavor is ok and they came out piping hot.

Luke was our tour guide. He was very knowledgeable and friendly. Enjoyed his stories on this walking tour. Lots of folk tales. We took the 8 pm tour so it was cooler in temperature at the time
of day.

The food was ok. I had a shrimp pie boy and it was the tiny cocktail sized shrimp. Also came with fries and fried onion strings. Lots of fried. The waitstaff- Trey was very nice. There was an annoying employee who brazenly came to our table to ask my daughter out for a drink after he got off of work.

The cheesesteak is tasty. I noticed the sandwich is prepared inconsistently. Some patrons get a nicely portioned sandwich and others a smaller portion. I practiced giving my order as to not hold the line and the server still did not get it right. I asked for three sandwiches and for some reason, he heard two. The sandwich was just ok and had more diced
meat than steak strips. The place has been renovated nicely. It is clean and there's seating upstairs.

This cheesesteak is yummy. The bread is a real Italian bread. The meat is shaved/thinly sliced meat as opposed to chopped meat. It's tasty. I ordered one with white American cheese and no onion. They also provide a full array of hot peppers which is an added touch. I walked a mile after eating the whole sandwich. I would eat these again.

This place is great. There's lot of yummy foods to choose from here. There's a grab and go bar for beer and wine and all sorts of foods and sweets. There's also a fresh produce and meats section.
Something for everyone.

I give this place 3.5 stars for the gelato alone. I usually don't like gelato, however, the concierge at our hotel gave us a complimentary tasting. The gelato flight included about 5 or six varieties which were all delicious. I tasted the mango, almond, chocolate, black cherry, and pistachio. The cherry was my favorite. I had the veal braciole over noodles with Sunday sauce. It was ok. The cocktails just ok. Go for the gelato.
The sever was pleasant and attentive. The food today was just ok. I had the unsweetened iced tea with my meal. It was a good test stop.

We were told the wait would be 25 minutes. We waited at about 35 minutes. I was told there were 3 parties ahead of me when I check; however, 5 parties were seated before we were. I actually wanted pie but they didn't have any. I guess there menu is on a seasons rotation. The employees there all seemed unwelcoming. Maybe they were overworked. Our server's uniform looked so dirty. The whole place looked dark and didn't seem so clean.  We decided not to eat and left. Employees were standing around like they didn't know what to do. I should remember not to stop at this location. It seems poorly run.

D1PjyzlSaA3tXRrADZCi_g.review_text: I went to Commander's for restaurant week and was not disappointed. Every course was delicious. I had the tuna for my main course and it was cooked to perfection. For dessert I had the classic creme brûlée. It was huge and could have definitely been shared. Commander's is a must if you are in New Orleans. The restaurant itself is a huge house and something to see. Lastly, the service is great!

I was hesitant to go to milkfish after reading the menu, but everything was delicious. It was easy to change your meals too. If you are not a pork eater and would rather sub pork for chicken it is an easy change.

Great atmosphere and food. I went for a girls night out and shared a few dishes. We did not have a reservation but they were able to squeeze us int. I think it is definitely better to go with a small group because the restaurant was loud and hard to hear one another. Menu changes, but we really enjoyed the scallops.

The food was great and Mopho has a great atmosphere. Must order the brussels sprouts! Don't let the menu scare you, just order something it will definitely be flavorful and different than anything you've had before. If you are going with a larger group try to make a reservation before hand.

The restaurant is small so there is always a wait during prime dinner time, but the food is worth it. I ate the falafel platter and added Brussel sprouts. All of the salads were delicious. In addition the sauces were fun to try with the falafel. I would definitely eat at 1000 figs again!
The cute little house had delicious food. The sauces and flavors made each dish special and worth going back to!

This place was so cute and delicious. I was so excited there were numerous gluten free options. My friends and I sat on the floor in a comfy little room. I highly recommend this place for a cute breakfast or lunch.

The Volcano roll is the best sushi I have ever had! The sauces paired with all the specialty roles are incredible. The vibe of the restaurant is trendy and fun. If you are in the warehouse district for the evening stop by here, but you might have to wait for a table on a weekend night. It is now my friends and my go to sushi restaurant.

This hidden gem is fantastic. On a nice day it's the perfect spot to grab lunch with friends. I had the curry chicken salad and it was a great combination of flavors. Also, Pagoda is very vegetarian and gluten free friendly. There's something for everyone to eat.

I really enjoyed my rainbow bowl. It was filling and I felt I got a well rounded meal. The food came out pretty fast and the set up was cute. I was hoping for some special gf treats but they didn't have any baked goods. My friends each ordered a smoothie (coffee and PB&J). I had a taste of each and thought they were super flavorful. I was surprise the place wasn't busier around lunch time on a Friday, but I think the place is still new and people don't know about it.

I really enjoyed my meal at Maypop. They were very accommodating with gluten free options. When you look at the menu it's hard to figure out what everything is. We took the waitress's suggestions and everything was great! Get the fried oysters to start. I had the tofu dish for my entree. The flavors of all the food was spot on. I also really enjoyed the truffles they gave at the end. The room was a little noisy but definitely a fun atmosphere!

I went to Arabella with a group of friends because I knew it was casual, fun, and everyone could find something to eat whether they were gluten free or vegetarian. Unfortunately when we arrived they said they were out of gluten free pasta. Therefore the only option was to get vegetables in a sauce for a gluten free meal. 
Otherwise, the sauces were good but nothing so amazing I would drive out of my way to get.

Mizado was excellent! It was a fun place to have drinks and dinner with friends. The queso was unreal! The brussel sprouts were also amazing. They were super crispy and light. The menu had lots of options from tacos (can be made on lettuce wraps) to plates, tamales, and salads. Don't miss out on the appetizers and sides. They are all as good if not better than the entrees. Lastly, if you order a mojito or margarita, try the foam salt.

This place has such a fun atmosphere. My friends and I stopped by for dessert the other night. We ordered the mint chocolate dome cake dessert. It was delicious! We sat at the bar and the staff was super friendly. My friend wanted him to surprise her with a dessert drink and he made her a grasshopper. She said it was the best drink she has ever had!

This is my favorite restaurant. I have never had better hummus. I always get the chicken hummus plate and manage to finish the huge entree every time because it is so delicious. You won't have a bad dish. I have tried the falafel, kabobs, halloumi cheese, vegetable soup, and so much more. This restaurant I always recommend even after leaving the uptown New Orleans area. No matter what time of the day it is, the restaurant always is busy. The food is reasonably priced; the staff is pretty friendly; most importantly, the food comes out fast. If its a nice day you can sit outside, but don't worry it's shaded. They event make large platters for catering!

Hansen's is an iconic New Orleans place so you have to try it. The cream flavors are the best. I got the coconut cream. If you want the souvenir cup buy the bigger size. However, the small is plenty big. Bring cash or you have to pay a credit card fee that is almost as much as the sno ball. 

While I was there someone came in with a big bucket and they filled it all the way up with rainbow flavors. It seemed like a fun idea if I was sharing with a large group/having a party.

Be prepared you never know if there will be a long line or not, but it's worth checking out.

Tsunami is a great addition to the CBD. It is walking distance from the Superdome. The food came out pretty fast. I dined in on a Saturday for lunch and it was very quiet. I am assuming it is busier during the work week since it is between a bunch of office buildings. 
The baked salmon with crab in the middle was great for something different than a roll. They have classic rolls and a few fancy ones.
I ordered the seared tuna on a salad that came with a delicious ginger dressing. For dessert we had the flour less chocolate cake which was divine.

Uptown New Orleans needed a good salad place! I had the salmon salad and it was great because it had so many different things in it. The dressing was delicious but not too heavy. They were a little slow in getting the food out.  The salad was a little pricey but was very enjoyable. You can pick up to go or eat there. The space is very clean and new. Parking is on the street but during the week there wasn't a problem finding a spot.

This place is over rated. I don't understand how there are so many locations because there are so many better breakfast places in New Orleans. There is always a super long line. I think it is a little bit of a tourist trap.

Last time I went I got the Costa Rican and it was just fine nothing great. I've never had the pancakes of french toast so maybe that's why I just don't understand the frenzy.

I had been waiting to try this ice cream for the longest time but took awhile since they are only open during the day on the weekends. We had to wait in line but about 20 minutes but it was delicious, especially on a hot day. You can choose lots of different flavors/toppings to be mixed into the cream base. I had caramel and coconut and then they drizzled extra caramel on top. It was a lot of ice cream and worth the $5. If you have cash it is easier especially with a long line. 

Also it's at a great location. You can eat it as you walk up and down magazine or sit in the fun outdoor dat dog seating area. We went on a Saturday and there were a bunch of vendor tables set up in the seating area to shop.

GW Fins is my favorite restaurant in the French Quarter. I always choose to go there for any special occasion. The food is always consistent and the staff is very friendly. If you are celebrating an event and tell them beforehand, they will decorate the table with confetti and make you a custom menu with a congratulations or happy birthday printed on the top. 

I always order the famous scalibut. The mix of scallops and halibut with the sauce is delicious. The fish is always fresh. I can't eat the biscuits because of gluten sensitivity but they always smell amazing and the people I have dined with can never get enough as the staff brings fresh biscuits throughout the entire meal. We ordered the chocolate dome for dessert. It was not too rich for me, but I love chocolate!

I was excited to try Breads on Oak because they had a few gluten free options. I had the buckwheat biscuit sandwich. It was ok. I was not a big fan of the taste of buckwheat, but it was exciting to eat something with the consistency of a biscuit. However, I would not order it again.

The cafe itself was cute and had a couple of tables. It was not noisy and a good place to sit and do work on your computer.

Amazing brunch!! They take the basic brunch dish to the next level. I'm not sure what the sauce was over the vegetables but it was divine. In addition the egg was cooked perfectly that it was crispy and still a little runny. The hash brown squares are the better version of potatoes and tater tots. My boyfriend got the fried chicken and was heaven. Also, the restaurant vibe was very cool. Great service and food! You must try.

DOBkkhx_iS0gWh0glk9pqw.review_text: Myung Ga is AWESOME!  I go in for lunch all the time with my coworkers.  the food is fantastic, the owner Sam is great.  The food is always great and I've yet to find something that I don't like.  Everything is very authentic.

Went in for dinner on a Friday night. We were seated near the bar where a rather odd live musician was performing to a very happy crowd of 60-somethings. Aside from the weird entertainment, the food was very good and the service was spot on. I will return.

My family and I went to Flavor of India based on the rather strongly positive reviews we found on Yelp.  Either we went on an off night for them or the level of quality expected of Indian restaurants in this area is significantly below par.  While the wait staff was very friendly, the Friday night dinner buffet was marginal at best and bordered on plain bad.

There was a selection of 5 main dishes and 3 sides.  There were another 3 appetizer items.  The food was all warm, but certainly not hot and they were clearly sitting there for a while.  The flavors were muted and dull.  The offering of fresh naan when you arrive is a nice touch, but it doesn't overshadow the rest of the meal.  

The price, $13.95 per person, is very reasonable for a buffet of higher quality food than was on offer.  I don't see Flavor of India earning a second try from us.

There's really not a lot needed for this review. The ice cream and water ice are fantastic. I've yet to find a flavor that wasn't stellar. Two things cost a half star: fee for a credit card and minimal seating outside. 

You can't go wrong here. Try something familiar or grab something exotic you will certainly be happy.

First time at Victory and also our last time at Victory.  I won't bother with a long review. The service was slow (10 minutes before our waiter even came to the table and they were not busy). The food was lousy. Mine was salted more than a salt-lick and was cooked to death, everything was mush. My wife's was about on par with fast food. My daughter liked her hotdog though. The manager did stop and ask how things were. I told it was bad and she took it away. The waiter came by 10 minutes later and we got the check. Nothing was taken off. We paid and got up to leave and the manager said she wanted to cover my beer but we checked out before she had a chance. Really? You had plenty of time. Now I see why the service is bad. 

It is also terribly loud. You can't hear the person sitting next to you. Poor design inside. Everything is a hard surface and it just echoes. 

Do yourself a favor, skip this place and go to the Mexican joint across the street.

We have been going to Luigi's for a couple years. It has been our go-to pizza shop for the last year or so. In the last few months things have been very inconsistent. Pizzas have gone from overcooked to undercooked and back again a few times. We used to dine in regularly but we've stopped altogether now. Service is always friendly but it has become painfully slow. It shouldn't take an hour to complete a meal. We are going to take a break from Luigi's for a while and give them a try again over the summer.
Holy, Roly Cow! Incredibly good. Super nice staff. Plenty of parking near here and they have coffee too. Gonna be a great late night stop. Great for kids too. Nothing more to say. Go. Go now.

Really darn good dim sum! We went on a Saturday afternoon for lunch and we were able to get a table for 7 without much trouble. Service is fast if a bit cold but you're there for the food not to make friends. Soup dumplings were awesome. Hand drawn noodles were great. The fried dumplings were pretty greasy which surprised me since they're panfried not deep fried. 

We will definitely go back.

How the mighty have fallen. As the Lunchbox Cafe, this was one of our go-to breakfast spots on the weekend. We went after the name change and discovered it was way more than just the name that changed. The coffee was a big plus for us. It's just meh now. My latte had coffee grounds in it. 

The next best thing they had were the waffles. They were just about perfect. Now? Awful. 

I got a burrito and it was just eh. It came with flavorless rice and cold beans that tasted like they were spooned out of a can. What a shame this place crashed so hard. We won't be back.

I've eaten much better food and paid a lot less for it. $60 (with tax and tip) for lunch for two adults and a kid with no alcohol involved? Better be some darn good food!  This was not. This place wants to be upscale but it's service and food fall far short. Their burgers are greasy, uninspired patties with names to make them sound more deserving of their $12 price tag. Soggy fries are a mere $5 extra because who would expect fries to come with their $12 burger?

On the plus side, their iced tea and lemonade are great. My wife's banana royale shake was a hit for her. 

Honestly, just go to the Five Guys in the same shopping center. You'll get better food at half the price.

I don't give out many 5 star reviews. I think they should be extremely hard to earn and utterly well deserved. Freddy's gets a rare one from me. This is quite possibly the best fast food burger out there, the fry seasoning is awesome and the sundaes are great. Top all of that off with super friendly staff and you get my five stars. 

We have kids so juggling kids and food can be a process. Every time we have been in the restaurant someone has brought or offered to bring us a high chair and moved a chair out of the way to make space for it. On top of that, they're at the table as we are getting there with our food to take the giant trays out of the way for us. 

We will be back again and again.

I was super excited to hear that a real BBQ joint was finally opening in the area. At our first opportunity to get there we took the family for dinner. I'm going to break this up into three sections: staff, prices, and food. 

Staff: 5 stars all around. Everyone is extremely friendly and always smiling. Top notch. 

Prices: Whoa are they high. With everything a la carte, the bill adds up in a hurry. The Philthy Combo is good to share for two adults at $24. Three meats and three sides. 

Food: Man, this hurts me. It's really sub par BBQ. I've had the real deal all over the country and this unfortunately misses the mark on nearly every count. The pulled pork was dry. The brisket was over cooked mush. The sausage has a ton of anise in it. The flavor of the chicken was good but also way over cooked. You didn't need to chew it. Just press it with your tongue. It's probably because everything is held in some sort of liquid in a steamer cabinet. 

We will give them some time to work on their processes and try again in a few months. For now, I can't recommend it.

Drinking. Chocolate. Are there any two better words to string together? This old timey shop is a fun place to stop in old city. They have a nice little candy shop up front where you can get bon bons, chocolates, gummy candies, etc but what you really want is in the back. 

Drinking chocolates made to order. The varieties change occasionally but they're always good. 4oz is $5. While it seems small, it's just the right amount. With all of the hand made focus on the store I was really let down by whipped cream from a spray can :( Other than that it was a wonderful experience.

This place is really a dive. If you're looking for or into that alone, this is your spot. The food is expensive, portions are small and it's bland and boring. We, against our better judgement, figured we'd give it a try one day after Longwood Gardens. Bad move!

It took 15 minutes to get water. Another 10 for someone to take our order. 20 for the food to come out and 10 to get someone to take our check. This should have been 30 minutes tops!

There is no reason to go to the place. Seriously. Go somewhere else.

Nice new addition at Christiana Mall! It's about time!

The service is extremely friendly and efficient. There are always people checking in on you and food comes out as soon as it is ready. The dumplings were very good. I prefer more soup in my soup dumplings but that's probably more about personal preference. 

My only gripe is about the soup broth. I got the shrimp wonton soup and the wontons and noodles were great. The broth was really flat. I wound up adding quite a bit to it. I was really surprised. 

Prices are high if you're expecting food court rates but they're right where they should be for a restaurant.

When we pulled up, we could smell the smoke from the smoker. I was hoping for great food, but as far as BBQ places go, this is just middle of the road and expensive. 

I ordered the combo ($20) so I could give everything a try. It included brisket, 2 ribs, pulled pork, cornbread, cole slaw, and one side. I should have taken a picture of the brisket. It had a 2" thick solid chunk of fat on it. The fat weighed more than the brisket under it. The brisket itself was meh. One side was overdone and rock hard. The rest was standard brisket, but nothing to write home about. Next were two ribs cooked nearly to the point of being jerky. One attempt at taking a bite and the entirety of it came off the bone. It was rock solid and the run on the outside stuck to my teeth like taffy. The pulled pork had a nice smoke ring. It was dry and bland. 

I got the brisket beans for my side. They had way too much something in it. I think paprika, but I couldn't quite put my finger on it. The best thing on the plate was the cole slaw. It was fantastic surprisingly. I would have done just that for my side had I tasted it before. 

Service was friendly and efficient. Outside seating was a plus. I was really let down by the food. If you're going to charge $20 for such small portions they better be damn good. This just is not worth the price when there are so much better food options in Media for less money.

First time ordering from Cafe de Thai. It was takeout (thanks covid-19), so no review on the dining experience or staff... just the food. We ordered online through their website and it was an easy experience. The food was ready in 20 minutes.

First thing we started with was the Thai Iced Coffee. We were on our way home from a hike so I was looking forward to something cold. It is suuuuuuuper sweet. It is supposed to be sweet, but this was melt your teeth sweet. After the sugar hit, it just tasted like stale coffee grounds. I've had quite a few Thai coffees in my day and this didn't live up. This is the only reason they lost a star.

On to the food! I got the drunken noodles with shrimp (medium spice level). It was fantastic! The shrimp were perfectly cooked (I think there were 7 in there), the noodles had a great chew, just the right amount of Thai basil. It had just the right kick to it too. It was definitely spicy, glad I didn't go for the #4 spicy!

My wife had the pumpkin curry with tofu. She liked it, but thought the pumpkin gave it a little too much of a gritty texture. It was a lot of curry and plenty of rice to go with it. The nice large chunks of tofu were great too. She got it mild. It had just a slight tingle of heat to it.

Got the steamed chicken and veggies for the kids. I should have taken the name more literally. There's no sauce, just steamed chicken and veggies. They were happy with everything, but it would have been better with a sauce (not to me for next time).

Finally, the mango sticky rice. It tasted very good. I don't usually like it, but I thought it was good. My wife ate the rest :) It's a pretty small portion for $7, but I imagine it is more about the preparation when you're in the restaurant for dine in.

TLDR: Great food, drinks were a let down, we'll definitely dine again.

I've eaten here twice now. Once for lunch pre-COVID and recently for take out. We got the meal for 2 combo thinking it would be a nice combination of choices. 

The salad for 2 was about half of a side salad for 1. The lettuce rotten and clear. We threw it out. Sides were supposed to be plantains and roasted potatoes. The plantains were perfect and a decent portion. The potatoes were literally 4 tiny circles. Maybe half of a small potato. 

The steak was cooked properly and was the highlight of the proteins. The chicken was insanely salty. We've had a lot of Peruvian chicken, this is not how it is supposed to taste. The beef skewers were fine, nothing special. The sausage was dry as a bone. 

Top it all off we all had intestinal issues that night. 

We won't be back.

We were really excited to try this place after reading the reviews. We pulled into the small parking lot and were figuring out what we were going to order. Then I noticed the cook not wearing a mask and talking on his phone. Then someone delivered something to the store wearing a tshirt with the store's name on it. Also not wearing a mask. Then a third guy came out of the back in the restaurant not wearing a mask either. 

NOPE! We pulled right out of the lot and left.

Really solid spot for Mediterranean food. Went with the small platters for dinner. They were a great size. Plenty for an adult for dinner. Hummus was a little thin, but tasted great. I wish it came with thicker pita and more of it. Lots of meat on top, not just a giant bowl of rice. Only let down is the beef and lamb are the preformed stuff you usually see on a gyro, not the freshly made kind. 

Prices were great and the order was ready when we got there (ordered online). We will definitely be back to try more of the menu.

Eh, it's fine for a franchised poke place. Ingredients were fresh and the store was clean. Only one employee but they were wearing a mask (Thank you!) 

Like most of these chain poke shops, they drown the bowls in sauce. I got the spicy tuna and it was more like a spicy teriyaki sauce and super salty. 

It's fine if you want something quick but we wouldn't make a trip to go there.

Cute small ice cream shop that's inside a record store. The owner and staff are very friendly. Ice cream isn't house made but that's OK. Prices are fair for the portion sizes. We'd stop in again if we're in the area.

Edit:
I stand correct about the ice cream being house made. It indeed is :)

After spending two weeks on tour with my band eating crappy food (a.k.a Subway), we were craving something that was fresh and had some sort of nutrition. Luckily, a need to hit the Nashville Guitar Center placed us in vicinity of Calypso Cafe. 

I ordered their signature salad, the lucayan, with dressing on the side. It was a heaping mound of goodness with great flavor and hit the spot. My malnourished body took to it right away! My poor band mates opted for chicken sandwiches and a rotisserie half-chicken which all ended up complaining that they were dry but my food didn't have any issues. 

Services was quick and friendly, the prices fair... it was a good lunch spot. If I lived in Nashville as opposed to Portland, OR, I'd probably eat there pretty often.

After just coming from TX a few days earlier, I didn't have high hopes for a Texas Style BBQ place in Nashville, even with all of the props they've received from the Food Network. That being said, even my lowered expectations were not met. 

The service was great but the food just fell flat. I ordered a plate with beef brisket, ribs, chicken, and a side of green beans. Everything just tasted bland and dry. The brisket tasted like it was microwaved, the only moisture in the ribs was due to the bbq sauce I covered them with, not due to the meat itself. The sweet tea was awesome though and the green beans were pretty good. 

They do have a 72 oz steak challenge - if you can eat it the 72 oz steak within an hour, you can have it for free. However, if the other dishes I tried were any indicator, I don't think I'd even be able to stomach more than a few bites.

It's too bad, perhaps they should have stuck with Tennessee styled BBQ instead.

The location and atmosphere for this place are incredible. We walked into a party with a live band, dancing, and all kinds of fun for a Monday night. It was right across from the River Walk. 

Unfortunately, the food wasn't quite as fun. I opted for one of their large combo platters featuring grilled crayfish, shrimp, catfish, calamari, and oysters. Despite the nice variety of items, they all tasted about the same - over salted and dry. Some of the other appetizers like the onion rings and gator bites were pretty decent though. It's sad when I can say I've had better cajun food in nearly every experience outside of this one in New Orleans. 

In the end, I felt like it was a restaurant that catered primarily to tourists as opposed to the kind of food that locals would enjoy and come back to. At $20+ a head, you'd hope that the quality of food would be much better but I suppose with their location, it isn't necessary.

Korean food in Nashville?

I was a little skeptical, even when the recommendation came from a friend. After growing up in Southern CA, volunteering for a Korean organization, eating food in Korea, and having many a home-cooked Korean meal, you could say that my standards were pretty high. However, my worries were lifted the first moment I tasted some of the delectable pickled side dishes served.

I ordered the Dolsot Bi Bim Bap, a staple in quick Korean lunches and wasn't disappointed. When I mixed in the over easy egg and chili sauce, it cooked together with the rice along the sides of the hot stone bowl, giving everything a nice crisp texture without drying any of the ingredients out. The meat was sweet and full of flavor, the veggies crisp and tasty. It was a winner!

Now I just wish we had a place as good, with the same pricing, here in Portland!

Like solo people who enjoy driving in carpool lane during rush hour in Nashville, I thought maybe checking out this strip mall joint would be a little questionable. I mean the odds were stacked: Nashville's Asian food that I've tried to this point hasn't been spectacular, the lights for "Corner" in the restaurant name were out, and they didn't place chopsticks on the table by default (an inside trick to suss out authentic Chinese food). That being said, I was pleasantly surprised. 

I was the only person that ate in - almost everyone was picking up take out. In fact, this surprised the wait staff, who initially thought my sitting at a table was just waiting for food to be given to me in a plastic bag like everyone else. I wasn't. I wanted my food on a plate. And I'm glad I did - the food was much fresher, the crispiness of certain dishes were retained, and I could eat dish as soon as it was ready. 

Despite having the name, "Corner Asian Cafe," don't be mistaken: this is Chinese food (mostly). Of the Szechuan variety. Sure, you have your Americanized staples that are safe for anyone who thinks Panda Express is the real deal: General Tso's, Broccoli Beef, Crab Rangoon, etc. but the more interesting dishes are the specialties. For real..."Crab Rangoon," with it's cream cheese filling is about as legit Chinese food as Taco Bell's Doritos Tacos is Mexican. Probably less so. 

I got to try the Salt & Pepper Pork Spare Ribs (excellent: great crisp, nice spice level, soft and warm in the middle. Definitely get these dining in so they don' get soggy on the way home), Shrimp & Asparagus (pretty good...shrimp, asparagus, brown sauce...very standard), and the Braised Pork Belly (also pretty good: it's thinly sliced and tender over a bed of veggies. Could use a thicker glaze for sauce and the veggies could stand for some more pickling for a tart kick). 

I'm looking forward to trying some more dishes here!

If you enjoyed this, check out my Nashville food blog at dineosaur.net

Initially, I pulled into the parking lot to buy groceries at Kroger so I could make some dinner. However, I was lulled by the glowing lights of "WASABI STEAK, SEAFOOD, & SUSHI." More importantly, there was a large banner proclaiming 30% off Monday-Thursday from 4pm to 6pm. Even though I felt that the "seafood and sushi" portion of their name was redundant, I enjoy like a good value so it was enough to deter me from my path. 

The place was empty. I suppose it was only 4:30pm, but that basically gave choice of seating and it meant quick service. A couple of things were ordered up:

Steak and scallop hibachi combo meal (of course - 30% off!) and the sashimi dinner. 

If you didn't know, the hibachi (Japanese: 火鉢, "fire bowl") usually refers to a hot, round bowl filled with charcoal and used to heat. It was not meant for cooking. In the U.S, we hijacked this term and it usually refers to a flat metal griddle (or teppanyaki), where the food is cooked on. That's mostly because people though 'shichirin,' what these cooking tops were modeled after, was too hard to pronounce for English speakers. In any case, the workers were speaking in Mandarin Chinese so there wasn't very much Japanese about the place anyway. 

Back to the food. 

The Steak and Scallop  hibachi combo meal normally around about $20 and comes with a small salad, miso soup, veggies, fried rice, and two shrimp. I skipped the fried rice and opted for more veggies instead. The miso soup was pretty standard (soup w/boiled water), though my bowl had a few mushrooms, and even more curious, a few pieces of rainbow rotini pasta noodles! I avoided those and moved onto the salad, your traditional mini bowl of iceberg mix with gingery-sweet dressing on top. They gave a bowl of something that resembled Thousand Island dressing on the side. 

The steak and scallop were decently cooked (ordered the beef medium rare and they honored that), the sauce was peppery and covered everything on the plate, but that wasn't necessarily a bad thing. The vegetables were crunchy and added a nice balance of texture to the soft meats. The two shrimp were delicious, though scarce. They were more like really, really good garnishes than an appetizer (which is how they were labeled even though it was served with the main entree). 

The sashimi ($18) came with a glowing wine glass. Seriously, it's hard to describe...other than a wine glass on its side that glowed green on the plate. I think it was meant to be fun, though it was more confusing than anything. The 18-piece sashimi also came with two sticks of imitation crab and a shrimp (though those did not count towards the 18 pieces of fish). The fish included tuna, albacore, red snapper, hamachi, and salmon. The albacore was the best of the bunch....the red snapper was lackluster and should be avoided (often, sushi places use fake fish to pass for red snapper. Only 6% of all sushi restaurants in the U.S serve the real deal). The salmon had a strange, buttery texture - most likely, it was Atlantic farmed salmon, not actual fresh caught. It's hard to find real sushi anywhere: most restaurants in the country use fake fish, this was no exception. 

In the end, I probably wouldn't recommend this restaurant unless it was during Happy Hour for the reduced rate. I found it a little overpriced and the delivery was underwhelming. However, it makes a great distraction if you're too lazy to go to a grocery store to buy and make food yourself. 

(If you enjoyed this review, subscribe to my Nashville food blog at dineosaur.com)

My wife and I have been on a diet. And after a week of healthy eating, it was time to break that miserable pattern of unhappiness with something full of starch, carbs, and gooey cheese. Really, Italian food has got to be one of the most efficient ways of killing a low-carb regime. Pasta, bread, cream...it is a gladiator that has been trained to slaughter any cultivated ideas of wholesome nutrition.

Villalba Italian Restaurant is nestled in a strip mall with a few other restaurants (Bojangles, Las Palmas, Subway) and a Publix. Inside, the scene is mostly older folks or those with families (many children were there). They happened to have a jazz trio set up in a corner playing live music, which was nice. It was comfortable - the kind of comfort that seems appropriate for a couple who've been going out for a few months, not necessarily a first date kind of vibe. And definitely a bit too comfortable if one has been trying to stick to healthier eating.

The menu was a mix of standard Italian American pasta dishes with some pizza and calzone options. There was a modest wine list, most available by glass or bottle. Every meal is served with a small loaf of their buttery house bread and a warm bowl of their red sauce to dip it in. The best part of the the bread was the sauce. The bread itself mostly served as a plain delivery vehicle for something that exploded with basil, oregano, and crushed tomatoes.

We ordered up two dishes to share: lobster ravioli in an Alfredo sauce and the lasagna.

The presentation of the lobster ravioli couldn't be more boring. Sure, it was fairly symmetrical, but the pasta dough and accompanying sauce made for a large plate filled with a similar, off-white color. At the very least, it could have used some fresh crushed black pepper or some parsley garnish to give it some more color. That being said, the flavor was rich with chunks of lobster, the pasta was cooked perfectly al dente, giving it a nice chewy feel. The sauce was liquid butter and cheese - exactly what it was supposed to be. The six ravioli on the plate was very filling from the sheer force of the butter alone.

The lasagna had a similar profile in that they must have used an entire dairy farm's worth of cheese to create it. 

I didn't know that in advance so when asked if I wanted some freshly grated Parmesan on top,  I gladly indulged. I rarely pass up anything free, it's a good value! Except this time, it was more than I bargained for.

This lasagna is filled with spiced sausage, meat, cheese, and their house red sauce. It was rich in a different kind of way: peppery with lots of basil, fennel, and Italian herbs. Because it was served so hot, the grated cheese on top melted instantly and was absorbed by the gooey mass of cheese underneath to become one large cheese monster resting on the lasagna. It was freakin' delicious. However, after the many bites of lasagna, the buttery-cheese ravioli, and the bread, that richness became overwhelming and we had to depart on semi-sweet sorrow. The sorry would really be how I felt later the next day after consuming 45 pounds of cheese.

If you're looking for some Italian American comfort by way of cheese, butter, and tomato, this may be your jam. It's better than the Olive Garden and it's definitely better than anything you'd eat on a diet.

If you enjoyed this review, check out by Nashville eating guide at dineosaur.net

Lucky Bamboo gets an extra star for being the only dim sum restaurant in Nashville. That being said, it didn't help much. 

I really wanted to like this place. Dim sum is one of my favorite things on earth and when I saw the photos, I thought this could be close to the real thing! However, the food can be described with one word: disappointment. I've reheated frozen dumplings that have turned out better than this (and I do believe these are just steamed frozen entrees). 

I arrived right at opening (11am) and walked into a fairly empty restaurant with someone mopping the floors. Shortly after being seated, someone rolled up a cart with selections to choose from.

I ordered a number of yum cha (dim sum) standards: har gow (shrimp dumpling), shu mai (dumpling with ground pork or chicken), shrimp rice noodle roll (cheung fun), pork rice noodle roll, and sticky rice wrapped with lotus leaf. I skipped the xiaolong bao (soup dumpling), as it looked questionable and they didn't have much else to choose from. There were no spare ribs, tripe, chicken feet, egg tarts, or anything like that.

The har gow skin was far too thick - the chewiness and starch of the rice flour overpowered the flavor and texture of the shrimp. In fact, it almost had to be drenched in soy sauce and chili oil to have any flavor at all - and even more surprising, it was cold (despite being served right at opening).  The two variations I had of the shu mai (both pork and chicken) weren't much better; they lacked the bouncy texture that the dumpling is supposed to have but instead had greasy cartilage inside instead. 

The cheung fun (rice noodle rolls) were probably the best items I had that morning, salvaged mostly by the sweetened soy sauce. The bbw pork was decent, it had some red flavor and the portion of noodle was appropriate, though these were served lukewarm as well. 

Unfortunately, the sticky rice was also disappointing as well. It tasted like the quail egg was cracked in, so the texture became granular, almost like biting into bits of sand with the sticky rice and the lap chong (Chinese sausage) was under cooked, so its sweet fat didn't dissolve into the flavor of the rice. 

Normally, I leave no dumpling untouched and certainly would never leave anything on the table at a dim sum restaurant. However, I walked away without bothering to ask for takeout containers...it just wasn't worth it. 

It seems if you want decent dim sum, it isn't going to be found in Nashville (yet). You're better off reheating some of the frozen entries from the K& S International Market next door than eating the stuff served at Lucky Bamboo. Or even better: drive to Atlanta and get the real thing instead.

If you want more Nashville restaurant reviews with guides to underappreciated places, check out dineosaur.net

This is my favorite sushi restaurant in Nashville so far. 

Having come from Pacific Northwest where I had access to incredible, fresh fish and traveling the world eating at some of the best sushi restaurants on the planet, I've been spoiled. I've tried looking for a solid place here in Nashville, both high end as well as an affordable go-to option. Yuno is definitely a solid, affordable option for sushi. While you won't be getting an "authentic" Japanese experience (I suspect that it's Korean-owned like most sushi places) or innovative rolls, they have decent fish here and ultimately, that's what matters. 

I've tried the sashimi combo (just raw fish, no rice - $26), their tuna tartare ($11), and a number of rolls ($4-$15) here now. 

The sashimi plate is a go-to test for checking the quality of fish at a restaurant. There's no hiding behind fancy sauces, there's no dilution from the sushi rice or any other ingredients mixed here. Here, you get a selection of fifteen pieces of five different fish. Almost anywhere you go, that will include salmon, tuna, and hamachi yellow tail. Sometimes, that includes red snapper (even though 96% of red snapper served in the U.S is fake). Personally, I think the $26 is bit overpriced but the fish presented here is pretty good. 

The tuna tartare is their appetizer that has tiny cubes of sushi-grade tuna mixed with some avocado and tobiko, and includes a house sauce. It also included some unnecessary crunchy flakes that actually took away from the dish. The fish was soft and the small pieces gave it a nice, buttery feel and the sauce wasn't overpowering. 

For rolls, I went with the rainbow roll (different kinds of fish over crab rolls  $10), the avalanche (a house special with white fish, spicy crab, and avocado with a house sauce - $13), and a spicy salmon roll ($5.50). 

The avalanche was interesting: I wasn't expecting it to be baked. The warm spicy crab was comforting, though it didn't mesh with the cold, raw fish on top and definitely could have done without the crunchy toppings. The rainbow roll is pretty standard across the board: imitation crab, cucumber, and basic fish on top. Didn't really stand out but wasn't bad, just met expectations. 

For $5, the spicy salmon roll was the best bargain. Marinated salmon mixed with some cucumber and rice. It's basic, a a good value, and could be paired up with other basic rolls for an inexpensive but decent sushi dinner.
