Also, very reasonable prices. Make sure you bring cash as they don't accept credit cards. Also, be sure to eat one as soon as you buy it, they are best enjoyed fresh and piping hot!!

I usually love stacked pickle but we ordered takeout from here and were not super impressed. I came after they said the food would be ready and waited a long time to be helped. Then, when I got the food it was cold and all mangled together in the box. Word to the wise, just eat in.

While the atmosphere and concept of this place is very cool, i was sadly disappointed and it didn't live up to what I expected. There are fun drinks and snacks available for purchase but be ready to pay a fair amount since everything is rather pricey (tax and gratuity is included though, so it makes it easy). The puppy chow was pretty good (it has a touch of cinnamon which was interrelation) but the drinks were not the best. I went with a group and nearly everyone was disappointed. If you want to get in the Christmas spirit though, this is a great place to come.

Went here for the first time last week and don't know how I just got around to it. It is the cutest little shop and the baked items are delicious. Not to mention they have local meats, cheeses, specialty sodas/drinks. I would recommend to go right when it opens to ensure you get what you want. When we went they had a bacon and cheese scone that was all gone by the time we got there (only 45 min after opening!) you won't regret making this a Saturday morning tradition!

Had the best New Year's Eve meal at hedge row last night! We ordered a few apps, main course dishes (highly recommend the short rib) and even sides (the Brussel sprouts are totally worth it) and left feeling very full. We also were given the best couple and their daughter to sit next to. At the end of the meal they graciously paid for our whole entire meal and we were dumbfounded. We hope that they see this review and know how extremely grateful we are for their kindness and generosity! We will be paying it forward in the next few weeks. We will also be back to hedge row soon. Service, food, ambiance and drinks were spectacular! Happy 2020!

Went here for dinner on a Friday night and expected it to be more full. We were seated right away, which was nice and had great service from the friendly staff. We ordered the wings and a take on a Philly cheesesteak . Both were good. My husband had the grapefruit IPA and really enjoyed it. Giving this 4 stars as the food was pretty average and didn't blow us away, but still very reliable. Will most likely come back!

Very reliable Thai food in fountain square. Best in all of downtown Indy in my opinion. They also have great takeout and you can order straight from the Yelp app which is always convenient. Their Pad Thai is always reliable, along with their spring rolls and curry. Cozy atmosphere if you're dining in. Come early though, this place fills up on weekend evenings.

Been wanting to try this place out for forever and finally went during devour. The food was amazing! We had the cheddar spread, brisket melt, turkey and thyme sandwich and the bread pudding. I would have given it 5 stars, but the service was a bit off. They don't have a host stand or anywhere to wait really so you never really knew when you would be sat or how many  people were in front of you. They were really busy, so  wondering  if it was just an exceptionally busy night. Also, there was no spacing between our courses and they brought everything out with 5-10 minutes of each other. So the ice cream in the bread pudding was unfortunately soup by the time we got it. Will definitely be back and hopefully the service will be better next time!

Wow! What an amazing neighborhood gem. Love everything that I've gotten so far in the few times I've been in. Also a great place to grab some baked goods and bring to a party or grab a piece of coffee cake and a drink to get some work done. Inside and outside seating!

Talk about a good cup of coffee and a welcoming environment! I've been here a few times and am always greeted by the friendliest smiles and great conversations, even during covid. Their seasonal drinks and lunch menu is to die for. You can also order breakfast all day. Cannot wait to come back for a happy hour when this place opens back up after all the covid craziness is over.

The best neighborhood ice cream shop with some
Delicious flavors at affordable Prices! Everything is aviation themed, right down to the flavors! Such a cute place to stop in for a weekday or weekend treat!

You guys, taxman city way is the place to go for takeout (or even socially distant indoor and patio outdoor seating). They have the best bar food. The burgers have the most amazing flavors combined to make something so delicious you'll eat it twice in a week (no joke). Also, they have crispy fries which, let's be honest, how all fries should be. Get some beers to go and you have yourself a nice little evening!

Went to Healthy Happies in Carmel for the first time and it was delicious! It's a bit confusing, but if you want a shake, you also get a tea to go with it. I won't say no to 2 drinks but if you just want a shake, I believe you always get a tea "to-go". I had the flirtini tea which was actually amazing. It has collagen in it, so definitely a healthy, light choice. I also got the peanut cup shake and it was amazing! Will definitely be back to get a sweet fix that's healthy! We need more of these in indy!!

Always a delicious experience at the Eagle! They have the best chicken sandwich and surprisingly, their chicken salad is something I get frequently! However, be warned, it's always packed. For good reason obviously! But if you go at 6pm on a weekend, be prepared to wait! You can always visit some nearby Mass Ave restaurants/bars fir a drink while you wait!

Everything here is amazing. There's a reason for the hype and if I was rich, I'd eat here weekly! The filet is cooked perfectly and the customer service is out of this world. We dined inside during Covid and felt very safe. The tables were spaced out appropriately and the waitstaff allowed us to have our space, but also kept us happy. I don't like shrimp, but if you do, the shrimp cocktail is a MUST!

My husband surprised me with a date night to Bluebeard 2 weekends ago and we sat on the patio and it was like a winter fairytale. The patio has heaters and fire pits to keep you warm. They also are featuring some warm drinks (the mulled wine is the BEST!) to keep you toasty all night. The food is delicious, so you can't go wrong with anything from Bluebeard. We also get a charcuterie board and it never disappoints.

I cannot wait until this place is open for in-person dining again! I received a gift card for Christmas and have been a few times now in the past few weeks and am loving their seasonal menu (Fireside Latte and Ginger Spice Latte are both delicious)! They also have a Tiger Eye Latte (basically a dirty chai) which was very good but couldn't really taste a ton of chai, so if you're wanting that flavor, ask for a little more!

Such a fun night out at the Fowling Warehouse! If you go during the week you can pay $10 for unlimited play and we were very distanced from anyone else. The space is HUGE. There is a big bar with a mystery  drink machine. Basically you pay anywhere from $2-$5 and receive a mystery beer/seltzer. So fun and a great way to experiment new beers!! We will be back. The staff is also very helpful and friendly! We even took our 10 month old and he loved watching us play!

Such a cool spot in broad ripple! The staff is so friendly (we had Noah as our bartender/server and he did everything to make sure we were enjoying our drinks) and the drinks are delicious (I got a French 75 martini, one of their champagne drinks)! Will 100% be back here again

So excited for this to fully open! They have a carry out window which is perfect for a quick coffee or treat on the weekends and will soon be open for brunch! I had the pecan pie latte and a pear and pumpkin macaroon and they were all so delicious! The gallery pastry team does it again by bringing us another amazing spot!

This pizza is delicious! Only reason for the 4 stars is due to price. I'm all for supporting local and will definitely be coming back, but it's not my everyday pizza place (unfortunately). If you're in the market for high quality pizza this is your place. Staff is incredibly nice. Also, highly recommend the spotted pig, Detroit style.

This is a great date night restaurant right in the heart of Mass Ave! I would highly recommend their margarita to sip on throughout the meal. So delicious and not overly sweet. I also love their guacamole and you cannot go wrong with any of the empanadas! They have outdoor seating and we've also sat at the bar several times for dinner and have been super impressed with all of the waitstaff!

Oh my gosh, I really don't know where to begin. went here for a date night with my husband and we had the most amazing meal. Started off with some cocktails and the Bao Buns which were amazing! My only complaint is that I wanted more slaw with the pork belly, but still would recommend. My husband got sushi and really enjoyed it as well! Then to the main entrees. I got the short rib which was so tender and delicious and perfectly marinated. My husband got the Tangerine Chicken and it was really good but super spicy, so you have been warned. I was nervous the bill was going to be outrages but we left spending less than $150 which I thought was reasonable. Very friendly staff and cool atmosphere!

Best bagels in Indy by far! Don't waste anymore time, go grab a bagel from here today! Favorites include cinnamon sugar sesame and spicy everything! They now are also toasting, slicing and schmearing bagels!

Eb8p_6274pnNXqG8I65tmA.review_text: My family orders take-out all the time from here.  Best spring rolls and potstickers.  Also house special is awesome.

Stoped by for lunch and had the lunch special which consist of 2 tacos beans and rice.  Good portion for $6.99.  Had a chicken & pork taco, both ok, guacamole was excellent.  Beware they only have spicy salsa.

Visited olive and oak with some friends.  Overall everything we had was very good, drinks, crab dip, shrimp appetizer, cheese curds, chicken wings, catfish dinner, cookie with ice cream and coconut cake for dessert.  Out of everything we had my least favorite was the catfish.  Wish it had more flavor.  The last thing is this place is a little pricey.  But don't let that stop ya!
Food is always good but service was super slow.   Waiter seemed distracted and it took forever for the food to come out.  Not the norm for first watch.

We have been coming to the restaurant for years and they have always been consistency amazing.  Since they have only been doing take-out due to Covid, they have not been consistent.  The 1st time we ordered the family meal, amazing.  The 2nd and 3rd time, not so amazing, everything was over cooked.  We may try again once they reopen.
My family and I love Mi Ranchito's.  Whatever you order will be amazing.  Best Mexican restaurant in St. Louis area!
First time trying DD's, really enjoyed the bowl with the spicy peanut sauce and the special  fried rice.  Will definitely be back!

Pro....staff friendly and helpful,  fries good
Con...ribs were dry and brisket was fatty

First time trying Nudo.  Food was very good.  Only negative there wasn't a staff member at the door to help you figure out which pick up order is yours.  Pickup is done by order number not name.  A little confusing for a newbie.

Eaten hear many times before covid and was always good.  During covid ordered take out several times.  Love that it's consistently good.  Love $5 burger Monday's, bacon flat bread, shrimp tacos and Sunday brunch.
Tried Orzo a few times, love their salads, gyros and bowls.  Like that you can make salads and bowls your own way.

Love love Prasinos....Before covid we would eat here also every week.  Since Covid we have only eaten here a few times.  Food is still good but not the same.  Plus they took some of my favorite items off the menu.  Hopefully when covid is gone things will go back to normal.

Met some co-workers here for lunch.  First time at Sasha's.  I had the Brie BLT and a sangria.  The sandwich was recommended by the server and just ok, don't expect an ample amount of bacon and the tater tots were not the normal ones.  These had a soft weird texture in the middle.  The white sangria, I wouldn't order it again.  My co-worker had the red sangria and liked it.  Maybe that one is better.  My bill was almost $30.  Definitely not worth it.  Don't think I'll be visiting again.

Stopped in for a Sunday brunch with family.  B Louie's was one of our regular brunch spots before covid.  You can't go wrong with $10 unlimited mimosas.  What has happened to B Louie's?  Service was horrible, while we are ordering, the server tells us they are out of chicken.  That would have been nice to know when he came to greet us the 1st time. Once we get our food, the server ask if we need anything.  Silverware would be nice.  He informs us silverware is in short supply.  All the silverware was being washed.  My daughter noticed her glass was dirty.  Something white was floating 
inside her glass...gross.  To top it off there were beverage napkins on the floor though out the restaurant.  Will be thinking twice about visiting again.

Stopped in with family for brunch.  I love the ambiance of this place.  Just wish the food was better.  I had the chorizo skillet it was ok, lacked flavor.  Everyone else had street tacos that they couldn't eat due to the corn shells totally falling apart.  Chips were ok.  Service was good, server was very attentive.  We may give them one more try.

ElN0bVArCpXS0jvvqMc5vQ.review_text:
I wish I could give this less than one star. My fiance and I ate here today because we had an Entertainment Book coupon and it was the worst "Mexican" food I have ever eaten and I have eaten at both Chi Chi's and Taco Bell. Actually, it might just be the most disappointing food of any kind I have ever eaten. We should have left when we were given the chips and salsa that CLEARLY came from a jar.

Everything was terrible and tasted like it came from a package. My fiance said the refried beans were comparable to the ones you get with a Banquet frozen enchilada meal. My margarita was so terrible I didn't even drink it. It tasted like straight up margarita mix you get in the grocery store, and had a sugar rim even though I had requested salt. I ordered the Enchiladas Del Mar and it was basically unseasoned frozen, thawed shrimp and crabmeat in corn tortilas covered in a bland green sauce, NOT with cheese and guac as the menu specified.

Shitty service rounded out an overall shitty dining experience. It took our waitress almost a half hour to take our orders and then at the end she brought our check without asking and then said she couldn't take our coupon, so we had to wait around for the manager to get there and take care of it, because HELL if we were going to pay full price for that crap. Worst dining experience of my LIFE. I still can't get the nasty taste of the margarita out of my mouth.

I would give them five stars for their food but they're getting one for their service. I can't tell you how many times I have been reduced to near tears when I foolishly call in during their, oh, you know, HOURS OF OPERATION, craving a burrito fix, to find that they took off early or decided not to open for the day. Tonight I called in a full two hours before they were set to close and the jerk answered the phone, "Mexicali! We're closed!" I said "I thought you were open til 9?" He goes, "Not tonight!" Why bother answering the phone then?? I'm done with these people. I HATE YOU MEXICALI.

What a surprise! An underachieving pizza place in Manayunk! My office just ordered from here and no one was happy with their order. My wrap that I requested a spinach tortilla, goat cheese and no dressing (all OPTIONS) came on a white tortilla with no goat cheese and soaked in nasty dressing. When we called to complain they wanted us to pay extra to send a new one. My coworker ordered a buffalo chicken salad and he got, literally, a large container of Romaine lettuce and a side of chicken to put on top. No vegetables, nothing. Just lettuce and chicken. Furthermore they couldn't be bothered to mark anything, so no one knew whose food was whose - and a few of us got wraps. Nothing more fun than picking through coworkers food to try to determine who it belongs to! This place can go to hell.

Damn. I love me some Dock Street. Brie, pear and walnut pizza? Just shut the hell up. This place makes the best pizza in West Philly with fantastic beer to boot. On this occasion, however, I'm knocking off a star for being closed the night before the recent holiday.

*Gets up on soapbox* Come on now, Dock Street. West Philly hipster types don't go farting out to the Jersey Shore for summer holidays like the rest of Philly, and the night before a midweek holiday is essentially a bonus Friday night. Friday night = pizza and beer. As one of the few non-BYOB establishments in West Philadelphia, you have a responsibility -- NO, DUTY -- to serve beer to the thirsty.

My friends and I tried to get there early anticipating a crowd, and arrived to locked doors. Then we had to hoof it all the way out to Local 44 in the heatwave, by which time we were all sweaty, it was decidedly no longer early which meant that our party had to wait 30+ minutes for a table, and we all got the hangries.

Is this what you want from your clientele, Dock Street? The HANGRIES? I hope you consider this next time you decide that you want to have a day off. I'll probably update this to five stars next time I'm in a happy pizza coma, but until then you have a good long think about what you did.

Really disappoints me to have to give this place two stars. My husband and I went a few weeks ago on a Friday night, and like everyone else we had the Groupon deal.

The first course, a shared gazpacho, was incredible. It had two different kinds of tomato and topped with a sweet basil gelato which was out of this world. Unfortunately that was the high point of the meal. For the next course we got the spinach manicotti, which was covered in a spicy squash sauce. The sauce was good but there was too much of it and the manicotti themselves were sad and deflated looking with not much filling.

We both got the baseball cut steaks. My husband ordered medium-well and I ordered rare, because, well, I am basically the man of the house. Unfortunately, there was not much difference in the doneness between our two steaks with them both being pretty pink in the middle. That describes neither a rare nor a medium-well steak. Just plain lazy. Underneath the steaks was an "asparagus puree" and some kind of messy brown sauce, and the whole thing was just kind of sloppy and unappealing. There were also some kind of diced potatoes which both resembled and tasted like home fries. Yuck!

I should note that the service was good (although there were only two other tables besides us while we dined) and the waiter was very nice and accommodating. I felt bad for him; as we were leaving a bunch of asshole college kids came with with a party of like, twenty, carrying horrid jugs of Carlo Rossi wine which they immediately started filling up in the water glasses before he could bring out water or wine glasses.

It bums me to say we won't be back, because it could be a really nice spot in our neighborhood. I just really wish the food/value was better. If we had paid any more than the Groupon value I would have given it just one star.

I'm a city gal working in the chain restaurant hell that is Bala Cynwyd and it was literally the happiest day of my professional life when Corner Bakery opened its doors across the street from my office. Yes, I know Corner Bakery is a chain restaurant, but it is a chain restaurant that actually serves fresh, healthy (and even meatless!) options unlike the reconstituted dog food you get from Qudoba or Potbelly.

Since they've opened, I've always found the service to be quick whether getting takeout or eating in. Sometimes you have to deal with Bala senior citizens who ask you things like "HURRR, what does hibiscus tea mean?" but other than that, it's usually quick in, quick out.

Four stars instead of five because once I dined in and my tomato soup with croutons seemed like it was originally a takeout order they slopped in a bowl, because the croutons were soggy and immersed at the bottom. I've got my eye on you, Corner Bakery, but we good for now.

My husband and I have been to Hop Sing a couple of times now, most recently on our one year wedding anniversary a couple of weeks ago. We absolutely love this place. Mr. Lee is a gracious host who personally greets and seats his customers, and was especially kind to us on our special night. I love the speakeasy vibe. The last time we went was a quiet Sunday evening, but the first time was a busy Friday night and to gain entrance we had to get past a bouncer who looked like Huell from Breaking Bad.

And of course, the drinks are amazing! Nice diversity of inventive and classic cocktails with fresh ingredients. The wait staff is knowledgeable and helpful when it can be hard to decide what to order. For $10 a pop, these cocktails are very reasonably priced, as far as craft cocktails go.

We're planning to come back tonight with a friend who is moving to NYC. This is a place we definitely needed to hit up with him before he leaves Philadelphia!

As many others have recommended, the tasting menu is the way to go. Best hummus I've ever eaten, and the selection of salads were amazing. I loved the ground up spices wrapped in the laffa bread. My husband and I visited recently for our first wedding anniversary and ordered the chicken liver, (favorite) raw lamb, (second favorite) duck hearts and sweetbreads, as we tend to be adventurous eaters who like all of the animal parts. Entrees and desserts were great too but we enjoyed the first and second courses best.

My only complaint about this place is that it wasn't exactly the most intimate or romantic dinner setting, as it is one of those place that cram the tables about three inches apart from one another. So as long as you don't mind the overweight blonde woman sitting next to you with frosted tips and a mismatched denim jacket/skirt ensemble pointing her finger at your food and asking what you ordered, then by all means. Next time I would probably prefer to go with a group as the larger tables seemed to be a bit more private.

Abyssinia is the best Ethiopian joint in West Philly and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. My favorite dishes are the raw kitfo and the vegetarian combo. Make sure you order the kitfo raw though, because otherwise -- sorry, hate to break it to you -- you are a huge pussy.

Yeah, sometimes there's gon' be a wait for food. Deal with it. Or better yet, visit more often and be nice to the wait staff, because I've found that the more they like you, the better the service. Either way, as long as I've got a cocktail I don't mind waiting a bit longer for my food. I think the longest we've waited was 45 minutes on a busy night. Assholes will wait for brunch at places like Sabrina's for up to two hours so I don't know how this is any different.

Oh, and it goes without saying, but Fiume upstairs? GIANT PLUS.

I love living in West Philadelphia, but my main gripe is that there's nowhere to get good sushi. You've got Nara, which is overpriced, mediocre and skanky; and Pod, which is overpriced, mediocre and pretentious. But Mizu? Is perfectly adequate.

If I want a really good sushi meal, I'll head over the river to one of many places I enjoy: Fuji Mountain, Yakitori Boy, Raw, Umai Umai, etc., etc. If I'm sitting at my West Philly home on a Wednesday night and I get in the mood, I'll order takeout or delivery from Mizo to satisfy my cravings. The sushi isn't spectacular, but it's decent -- and decent value for your money at $6-$7 rolls with 12 pieces a piece. I reiterate the takeout or delivery, as I would never eat in because college kids are awful. Seriously, once I stopped in and ordered without calling ahead and I think I legitimately lost IQ points overhearing the U Penn conversations. Better yet, just order delivery and avoid them all together.

Anyway, sushi does the job at a decent price. Thumbs up from me.

Man, does this place ever suck. My cousin, who was in town for just a short amount of time, went ahead and made this reservation for a group of six of us on somewhat short notice. I had never eaten here, so I checked Yelp and saw all of the terrible reviews and immediately asked her if we could go somewhere else, like nearby Fuji Mountain. It was to no avail, and we all ended up at Serafina.

Everything about this place is The Worst. They gave us a hard time about seating us a few minutes early, even though they literally told is that our table was ready, and tried to get us to wait in the overcrowded bar area. When they finally took us to our table, the table itself could have easily accommodated four patrons. But as I mentioned, there were six of us. The table was also jammed against the wall and two other tables, so we were all sandwiched in, to the extent that taking a deep breath would have been an endeavor. Being that I am claustrophobic, I especially did not appreciate this.

The food was as middling and underachieving as everyone else has pointed out. I paid $20 for lobster ravioli that contained no actual lobster, but a vague seafood-ish flavor, in a "lobster bisque sauce" that was basically just some sparse orangey-ish cream sauce with hunks of celery sitting in it. I tried some of my cousin's pizza and it was flavorless crust with uncooked mixed greens sitting on top. The hell? Special requests from others at the table were ignored, being that the service was even worse than the food. It took over an hour for us to actually get our food, and not once did our server come over to apologize about the wait or let us know what was going on. Someone from our table had to actually get up and go find him when we had all been sitting around with empty glasses for ten minutes and he was apparently just standing around.

They did end up giving us $15 off the bill due to the insane wait, but I would have rather had my two hours back. Yeah, I understand it was busy, but if your kitchen and wait staff can't accommodate that many patrons, than maybe, say, don't cram as many tables into your tacky-ass restaurant as humanly possible. Because customers like breathing as much as not waiting over an hour for their food.

I just can't say enough bad about this place. I hate it and I'll never, ever, ever, ever, ever go back in my life. You shouldn't go either.

Wow. Just ... Wow. My husband and I went to Marigold Kitchen last night for a special occasion and we were completely blown away at how amazing it was. We're both hardcore foodies and have eaten at some of the most hyped places in the city, yet this was easily one of the best -- if not the best -- meals we've had in Philadelphia.

Our dinner was more of an experience than a meal. We opted for one of the tasting menus, with five courses including hot and cold appetizer, meat or fish, cheese plate and dessert. Everything we ordered was exquisite and wonderfully plated. Some of our dishes included a tuna tartare, which was lightly seasoned as not to obstruct the flavor of the tuna itself (a problem I find with many tartares) and plated with micro fruits and tobiko; an amazing corn dish that included a croquette, tamale and holy balls amazing Mexican Cotija ice cream; diver scallops served in a decadent cream sauce with English peas cooked just perfectly and wild mushrooms; and my husband's filet, served topped with seared Foie Gras. My husband's dessert was also outstanding and notable -- he ordered "Chocolate in a Variety of Textures and Forms," which was served with the long rope of a stiff pudding around the plate which they called "flexible chocolate." Very cool, to say the least.

But what really transcended this from a  meal to an experience were the amuse-bouche one to two-bite courses, of which we counted ten (10!) total. In fact, some of the highlights of the evening were in these tiny bites, such as a bitter chocolate dusted corn ravioli, celery root vichyssoise with thyme foam bubbles and, of all things, a thick cracker filled with decadent, molten sharp cheddar which made me melt a bit when I ate it. I also can't forget to mention the impeccable service. Our servers were attentive and knowledgeable about explaining each of our courses and amuse-bouches to us.

I've noticed a lot of reviewers have recently given Marigold poor reviews for ostensibly misadvertising their UC Dining Days promotion. I can completely understand diner frustration, but to be honest, we paid $72/course for our meal, and it was worth every penny. While it's unfortunate that the promotion was misrepresented, you are simply not going to have the same experience for a $30 fixed course meal, and it's really just not fair to use that as a factor to rate the outstanding quality of this restaurant.

Thanks to Marigold for such an unforgettable evening. We plan to return again sometime with friends to share this amazing experience!

***Edited because I forgot to add how awesome the music was. Lots of low key brit-pop like New Order, Joy Division, XTC, as well as other stuff like Rolling Stones and Elvis Costello. Made for a nice ambiance.

I'm reluctantly writing an update to my review, as the first one I wrote in a fit of anger. When Mexicali is good it's REALLY GOOD but unfortunately the menu, hours, and quality are still inconsistent. Two weeks ago I ordered a Cali burrito and it was aces. One week ago I ordered a Cali burrito and it was close to closing time and barely had any guac (I'm assuming they were running out) and contained way too much rice. I guess they don't care so much about consistency since most of their clientele are college kids who are too dumb to know better and have high customer turnover.

I hate crowds, I hate people, and I hate lines. But despite that, basically, this is one of my favorite places in the world. As many times as I've been here I still feel like there's always still so much to discover, taste and experience. Some of my favorites are the L. Halteman Family meat and cheese stand, the 4th Street Cookie Company, the honey stand that keeps me in giant vats of honey... The list goes on.

There are two types of people who come here: Tourists and drunk people. The two groups are not mutually exclusive. I've many times been a part of the latter group, and from what I can remember, these are excellent cheesesteaks. Go to Jim's if you're sober. Just never go to Geno's, because they're racist.

My husband and I were looking for last minute reservations for Center City restaurant week, and this place was one of the few that had an opening with a decent-looking menu. Luckily we were not disappointed! It was $35 for a generous four course menu which included appetizer, soup or salad, entree and dessert. We thoroughly enjoyed everything we ordered; out of eight things brought out not one was a miss. I think the highlights were the chicken and waffle sliders, pumpkin soup, pork ribs and sticky toffee pudding. I ordered some fruit thing for dessert because I thought I would be too full for something more decadent. Rookie mistake! If a choice is sticky toffee pudding, then son, go with the pudding. Beer, wine and cocktail selection was also great. We don't find ourselves in this neighborhood very often, but we would happily go back.

This fucking place, man. I don't know why anyone would voluntarily come to eat here. I work in the building and every month or so for one reason or another, I've got to grab lunch in a pinch, and convenience trumps sanity and logic. Hey! You like totally crappy-to-mediocre food and you like paying way, way too much of it? Katz's is your place! If I ever order from here and they actually get my order right, I'm pleasantly surprised. And mind you, I never order anything terribly complicated, so a restaurant really is not worthy of "pleasantly surprised" accolades for like, remembering to toast a bagel. I would think that it is pretty standard in the deli industry that when someone orders a bagel, unless they specify some other way of preparing the bagel, they want it toasted. I don't pay five goddamn dollars to toast my own bagel, here.

I digress. Today I am sick and hadn't eaten in over 24 hours so I went down and got some chicken noodle soup. Guess how much the soup cost? No really, guess. SEVEN DOLLARS. For chicken noodle soup. And there were hardly any noodles and the ones there were all mushy and disintegrated. It should also be noted that the soup was tremendously salty. Ugh, you suck, Katz's.

You know who eats here are assholes like Hurricane Schwartz (true story: his picture is on the wall and I have literally seen him coming from here) and Main Line senior citizens who probably think that paying too much for food = quality.

I was on the fence between one star and two, but one time I ate a salad from here and it was decent. So a big, patronizing BRAVO, Katz's, enjoy your one extra star for not fucking up that one time.

I am really not sure why all the hype for this place. We had an absolutely mediocre and disappointing dining experience at fine dining prices. First of all, we came explicitly for the tasting menu only to arrive and be told they were no longer serving it. Two months later, they still are advertising the tasting menu on their website.

Ala carte items were disappointing. Lobster cauliflower soup was thin and laden with overpowering dill; one chunk of lobster at the bottom of the bowl was still quite cold despite BEING IN SOUP. Seafood stew was average at best. Shrimp were unpeeled, so I'm not sure what the reasoning for that was, like I want to go rifling through a stew to peel my own shrimp. Gross. It didn't come with a spoon or bread (traditionally served with seafood stew) or any way to actually consume the broth and when I asked for bread I was brought a small piece of ice cold focaccia. It seems the trend here is that everything is prepared and comes straight from Majolica's refrigerator. The dessert was completely forgettable, as in, I forget what it was beyond the point that it was dry and bland and served with ice cream. The cheese board was fine, I guess, so good job on putting some cheese and accompaniments on a board.

Maybe it's just me, but when you're paying well over $100/couple at a BYOB, I really just expect not to be let down after the meal. If this is just what constitutes "good" upscale dining in the suburbs, I'll stick to the city.

Local 44's slogan for all intents and purposes is: "gastropub. We kind of hate that word." Don't worry though, Local 44, no one will ever accuse you of being one of those if the definition of gastropub is "an establishment that serves food of quality higher than poor." Seriously, I get that you want the emphasis on the beer not the food, but it is actually possible to have a decent rotating beer selection and at the same time offer food that isn't utter crap for people to enjoy while drinking it. (News flash: People like to eat while drinking!)

Around late summer, we heard that there was going to be a new chef and hoped for a menu that wasn't 80% deep fried (Black bean burger? That's gonna be deep fried. BOOM! You're welcome) but somehow the food managed to get even worse since. One evening my husband and I stopped in for a drink and snack -- he got the new bone marrow appetizer and I got the grilled shrimp cocktail, $9 and $8 respectively. OK, first of all, there was MAYBE a full tablespoon of marrow in my husband's dish and my "grilled" shrimp cocktail consisted of lukewarm, clearly microwaved, previously frozen shrimp like the kind that comes in the shrimp ring at Pathmark, sitting on top of a sloppy bed of cloyingly sweet ketchup-heavy "cocktail" sauce and -- WAIT FOR IT -- covered in lettuce. THE. HELL? We also stopped in for a perfectly serviceable brunch on New Year's Day which was fine, I guess, other than the fact that it took an entire for our food to come out after we ordered it.

On the last point, and I do realize what I'm saying here, but the wine selection also has much to be desired, especially for the $8-$9 per 70's style small goblet that they charge for it. I get it, I get it -- again, it's a beer bar. However, I have stomach sensitivity when it comes to beer and I don't think it's too much to ask that my husband and I can go someplace where he can have a good craft beer and I can have a nice glass of wine, as we can countless other beer-centric places in the city -- Johnny Brenda's, Prohibition, Memphis Taproom, POPE, to name a few. It's just disappointing that Local 44 is really the only place we have like this in West Philly, and it's not, well, "better." C'mon guys... Can't you set the bar just a bit higher?

Came back to Marigold for a second time to share the experience with friends and everyone had an excellent time. We had been talking about making plans to go just before the now infamous 50 Best list came out, which made it somewhat more difficult to acquire a reservation. Despite the influx of clientele the service and food were both still incredible. Officially now my favorite restaurant in Philadelphia -- I can't wait for our next visit!

Prohibition, my greatest wish in life is that I could pick you up and transplant you to where I live in West Philadelphia, because you are everything Local 44 is not. Great rotating beer selection for my husband, an amazing wine (and sometimes cocktail) list for me, and stellar food. We don't get here nearly as much as we'd like just because it's a destination-type of place for us, which is a shame!

Staff and service is amazing. During our last visit the manager asked how our food was, and I told him, in a totally truthful manner, that I preferred the way they had prepared a certain menu item before they changed their menu, and he insisted upon taking it off the bill. This was totally unnecessary -- I wasn't even complaining, I was just being honest hoping they would bring back the old menu item -- but still the gesture was still appreciated. I also love your Wednesday-Saturday waitress who is a ringer for Lindsay Lohan (pre-downward spiral) and will chat celeb gossip with me. (PS: Did you read that NYT profile of her on the set of The Cannons? AH-MAH-ZING!)

I've been to Distrito dozens of times for dinners and happy hours and have never had a bad experience. It's not Jose Garces' best restaurant but it's a fun experience with great food. All of the tapas portions can add up, so check it out during University City Dining Days promotion to experience a good portion of the menu for $30.

PRO TIP: Order the Esquites, for a creamy, cheesy, spicy corn parfait. Kick ass.

I finally just got a chance to head over to Hibiscus last weekend, and I'm ashamed that it took me as long as it did. This place is amazing. My husband and I went for lunch with our neighbors and between us we got: two jerk tofu wraps, the seitan fajita wrap and the chickpea and kale platter. Everyone thoroughly enjoyed their food (even my carnivore husband!) and we all vowed to not be strangers. The owners are so warm and friendly as well.

Seating was kind of limited (we had to push a few tables together to accommodate our party of four) so in the future we'll probably do takeout. So happy to have this in our neighborhood!

Hooray for Honeygrow! This place is a savior in Bala Cynwyd, which has a dearth of fresh, healthy food. I was excited when Corner Bakery opened, but that turned out to be pretty underwhelming. Now that Honeygrow is here I've got no reason to step another foot in Corner Bakery.

I was a little apprehensive when my order totaled nearly $15 (including the bread and fountain drink) but with the generous amount of premium toppings I had ordered, it really only came down to a couple of bucks more than a salad from one of the local delis or catering places. Or hell, even nast Saladworks. So really, paying $13 for an absolutely delicious salad with grilled shrimp, avocado, blue cheese and portobello really wasn't all that outlandish. Next time maybe I'll try the chicken or tofu though, and keep it closer to $10.

Echoing some of the other reviewers, I also really love the self-serve kiosk ordering system with credit card swipe payment. It made the experience so quick and efficient, I didn't have to even talk to anyone before I picked up my order.

If they would do wraps too this place would be perfection, but still they get five stars.

I've been ordering from this place once a week since they opened. Since the Penn kids went home the delivery has been lightning fast (I am talking under 15 minutes on more than one occasion, which is insane), but I'm just glad to have a sushi delivery option in West Philly. (Mizu doesn't always delivery out to my block, and they're not on Grubhub anyway.)

My only complaint is that I wish they would add non-crunchified spicy rolls to their menu, but I always request without tempura crumbs and they're happy to accommodate.

Maybe I made a mistake by ordering pizza. Maybe my expectations were too biased toward a delicious Lou Malnati's or similar Chicago-style pizza. But we wanted some pie, and not that "St. Louis-style provel thin crust" shizzy.

Despite the recommendations, Pi's deep dish is not high on my list. While the sauce was nice, with a bit of sweetness, the crust was tough and the toppings sparse. A chicken pizza should have more than one bite of chicken per slice. The dead giveaway should have been the DRIED herbs on top... no respectable pizza place dares to stray from a bit of fresh basil for a shaker of pizza seasoning.

Next, the salad was disappointing. For around $10, I expect something more than a small dinner salad with a few random toppings. There wasn't even enough dressing to flavor-up the iceberg. All said, $60 later and we were not impressed. Maybe it's a great bar or wing joint, but it won't be on my pizza list.

In the end, this was the first pizza I actually left in the hotel room. No one enjoyed it enough to finish it off or bring it with - and that is a rarity!!

Pappy's BBQ is second only to Bogart's in St. Louis. The ribs are amazing, the pork and brisket tender, and the sides above average.

Unfortunately, I dropped one star for the service. Not the chefs, servers, or order-takers, mind you, but the odd behavior of whom I presume is the manager. Everyone was friendly and jovial; our server brought out our (huge) tray of food, boxes, sauces, and basically hooked us up. Yet, this one fellow stood over our table like we were going to pick up the picnic bench and throw it in the rental car. Did he know we were from Detroit?

He moved a bit, but never left the vicinity in the 1/2 hour we were there. Nor was he a friendly character and even engaged in some heated discussions with other staff. The biggest disappointment... I left an extra $5 on the table for the runner - and he picked it up and shoved it in his pocket. I mentioned this to her (the runner) on the way out and she said he'll probably give it to her later. I sure hope so. But given the show he put on for us, he really ruined a great food experience with his negative vibe. And to assume he's cheating staff, well, I just don't want to support that.

Just. Go. Here. Now!

Not only is the food and service amazing, but the owners' passion comes through in everything they do. Bacon-wrapped Easter ham, perhaps? My new favorite is the Cuban Sandwich. This should be on "America's Greatest Sandwich" - with pulled pork, smoked ham, fire and ice pickles... OMG, I want one now!! But they're only on Wednesday (or something like that, check their facebook page). And I do mean service - they will take care of you here and make sure everything is perfect!

Ribs are absolutely amazing; they use a thicker cut and you could chow down with or without any of their tasty sauces. My #2 ribs in the US. The prime rib isn't my favorite, but other meats are occasionally offered and you really can't go wrong. The brisket has the perfect chewiness/tenderness ratio and the pulled pork melts in your mouth. The sides are everything others have said below. Try the beans! Try the Deviled Potato Salad! Try the BBQ Chiccaron! And you can't beat the Soulard district on the weekend. 

I have stopped here every time I am in the area. Usually twice or thrice. Or I have my family ship me a pack of ribs and brisket. It's just that damn good.

I need to finish writing my Gelato List... and this would be near the top, if not first!

Perhaps the most authentic gelato I've found in the midwest... light and creamy, not too rich, with superb flavors in an amazing environment. The coconut gelato with pineapple sorbet is to die for! Each flavor we tasted was delicious... portions were a good size and prices were quite reasonable.

I didn't try them yet, but the baked goods looked super fresh and homemade, too. Our server was so nice and welcoming that I can't wait to get back and try more. Chill atmosphere makes for a perfect date-spot, or to hang with friends. Decent street parking.

So close to five stars. The value is amazing, the service is great, but the wait can be long and the A/C could be, uh, turned on.

A 16oz. bacon-wrapped filet w/sides for $25? Heck, yeah! Decent quality, tasty house salad (get the house dressing), free bread (in case there's not enough food elsewhere), etc... it's just a nice place to eat out. Servers are friendly and helpful, while runners keep your drinks filled, too.

The fish sandwich is probably a foot long (must be half the haddock in there). And worth it. Apparently there's a Friday lunch deal where you get this huge sammie and a drink for under $9. Wish I knew sooner... 

Best bet, go early and try to get a bigger table for elbow room. And then it's also less noisy and a bit cooler.

Not sure what to expect? Well, it's a little corner joint, kinda like a grocery set-up where you can order some food to go or buy frozen products to cook at home.

We tried the toasted ravioli and the fried artichokes. The ravioli were quite tasty, we're even still trying to figure out the delicate flavors in the meat mixture. Very nice and didn't really need the sauce. The artichokes were the favorite... drizzled with a bit of oil and vinegar, kept well with the nice flavor of the artichokes which were perfectly fried. 

I can't imagine going here when busy since it's so small and it appeared understaffed. But, it's definitely a contender in the fried foods category. Next time, I'll try one of the tasty looking sandwiches.

I would only give their baked goods three stars. I bumped the review to four because the staff was so helpful and friendly!

In short, it's a decent local bakery, but none of the products were worth writing home about. I can find tastier cannoli and cheesecake for the same price back home. Others mention the prices were a bit high; though they seemed in line with prices found at Detroit area bakeries, I deemed them to be reasonable. 

We tried an assortment of products. To me, the cookies were the standout. Lots of good flavors (from fig to "toasted ravioli" to german chocolate) and you can tell they were fresh. I'd probably be a regular if I was in the area, but it wouldn't be my go-to bakery. And yes, I'd spend more if they took credit cards.

Great pizza! 

Even though I'm more of a deep dish kinda guy, La Pizza has one of the best NY style pizzas in the midwest. Sure, it's a bit pricey, but they definitely load it up with quality ingredients and a dash o' love. One of my brother's faves whenever we visit.

Good service and plenty of leftovers.

My original few experiences at Mai Lee were mixed. Service was slow, food was inconsistent, and parking was a pain.

They've come around in my book, though... 

It's becoming a favorite place although it can get pricey quick - only because we want to order everything on the menu! From the crepes to spring rolls to pho and traditional dinners, you really can't go wrong. Service has improved and they also help explain things a bit more (and usually make good recommendations). I think it depends a lot on who you get. Tons of fresh condiments provided to flavor your meal exactly as you prefer. Carryout is usually pretty good, too.

Even after multiple visits, there are still a few occasional bumps in the road. It's definitely above average, but I can't give five stars until I know it will blow me away EVERY time.

I try not to review "chains" unless they are exceptional - or exceptionally bad.

This one is a conundrum. After multiple tries, I have found a consistency though. The servers here are AWESOME. They are friendly, knowledgeable, and will help in any way possible. When helping someone relocate, they were kind enough to share their thoughts on the neighborhoods, city life, etc. And were superb servers at the same time - keeping drinks and bread full, timing entrees perfectly, basically everything.

The managers seem to be a different story. On my first visit a few months back, the manager glared at us the entire meal. Yes, he kept walking by and eyeballing us - and his watch - apparently because we were the only table 1/2 hour before they closed! He never approached us, asked about the meal, or found out how much we loved the server. Instead, he made us feel unwelcome and unappreciated. Many visits later and the managers seem to have the same vagueness and animosity this one did. I don't get it. Bravo does a lot of things well, but hiring managers (at many locations unfortunately) is not one of them.

So, I don't want to penalize the servers by downgrading the restaurant; that part of your meal and experience will be good. Just don't expect any help or kindness from their "leaders". And no, I don't work here.

SERVERS = 5 STARS!

MANAGEMENT = 1 STAR!

Maybe this place could grow on me. Maybe. I've been known to drive 100 miles or more out of the way for a tasty treat. This visit wasn't worth the 4 miles. 

The ice cream is decent. First time I've had Chocolate Shoppe ice cream from Wisconsin. It's not the world's best, but it'll do and prices are reasonable. 

The biggest disappointment with the ice cream was the LACK of flavors. I understand you rotate them, that there's only so much room, etc. Yet not one of the flavors I was looking forward to (from reviews, website) were available. The flavors we tried were just too boring. Was there any peanut butter in the Yippee Skippee? Overall a tease. 

The other disappointment was in service. While some of the help seemed friendly and bubbly, not our guy. I thought maybe you were going to offer me a sample of that butter pecan -- nope, it was for you!! Can't even wait til we're gone!

The store itself is cute and fun in a hokey way. Seems like it would feel more at home in the middle of nowhere, not next to a major metropolis. Limited parking around corner.  

This is my first review in a long time. Figured I needed to start contributing again instead of just using. Especially when the reviews paint a very different picture vs what you'll actually find. 

Good luck, Wylie. I think there's a lot more potential here to impress and wow your guests. I won't be back anytime soon to update though.

Nada. Nothing. It's that impressive. 

Well the bar is cool. The chairs less so, with that slide-right-off charm. Had high hopes with the tremendous reviews. Dashed again. Was everyone drunk writing those???

The food. Average. Nothing that says I'll come back tomorrow. For breakfast, lunch, AND dinner dammit. Crispy fish tacos and decent pastor, but bland chicken and grocery store flour tortillas. Note to staff: when the limes are dry toss them. The bar limes had more juice than those with tacos! Salsa trio and guacamole was interesting, but our chips seemed bottom of the barrel... the majority were cracked into slivers of their former selves, not big enough for a scoop of guac or a hearty dip of salsa. So really, nada. 

The service. From the bumbling host to our server, we did not approach the level of service one should expect from a place like this. You feature craft and local beers but know nothing about them. Except that you're out of one. Recommendations? Help? Check in? I hate giving less than a 20% tip -- why are you trying so hard to make me?!? 

Overall a lackluster experience. I should really knock another star off for the price. Not worth $40/person. 

More like nada, eh?

If I drove a semi, I'd have to knock a star off for the tight parking lot. But I don't, so I have to fully recognize a restaurant that does everything else right! (Of course, decor is subjective here but I think it adds a certain whimsical charm in this case.) 

Good food, friendly service, reasonably priced. Go with the combos if you're not sure what to order - comes with sampling of many dishes and condiments. Or ask for recommendations, they're happy to help. My favorites are the lamb, chicken legs, and lentils. Be prepared to eat with your hands and leave full though. 

I'd be repeating many of the other reviews if I continue. Just go. Have fun. And yes, try the honey wine.

Given its location, Shapiro's could be a five star gem in the midst of Indy. It is not Katz. But it is a really good kosher style deli. 

Grab a tray, skip the first ten feet, and order up a pastrami on rye or a Reuben. Maybe some latkes or a matzo ball (in your typical bouillon base). Definitely a Dr Browns.  And you've got a nice meal. 

Plenty of parking. Line moves fast.

This review is for Helfer's paczki. 

For STL paczki, these could be 5-stars, though they fall short of my favorite ones from Metro Detroit (Note: I no longer make the trek to Hamtramck since they keep getting smaller and pre-made well in advance of Fat Tuesday). 

I was glad to find a reasonable paczki in St. Louis. At 6am, Old Town had none, but they were coming out fresh at Helfer's. Highlights: good traditional prune filling, fresh crisp dough, good size. The lemon and custard ones were good too, but the raspberry was too jelly-donut like. The dough could be slightly richer, perhaps more egg (especially for the price - they were a few dollars higher per dozen than Michigan's best). Also, my family prefers a variety of glazes versus the simple roll in sugar.

All in all, glad I stopped in. Staff was friendly, and there's plenty of parking. Will definitely be back to try more goods.

Their website proclaims "Philadelphia's tiniest bakery" and they're not kidding. This tiny corner-store bakery offers up a select few baked items including cupcakes, cookies, brownies, buttercake(!), cheesecake, dessert cups, and a couple of vegan items, too, among the few. I do have a peanut allergy, so normally I am hesitant to trust, but the sole worker was able to tell me which goods were nut-free. Note: peanut goods will be stored in the same fridge though not touching. 

Alas, I ordered two Birthday Cake cupcakes, a Red-Velvet cupcake, and a brownie. I thoroughly enjoyed the red-velvet cupcake with cream-cheese icing. The cupcake was moist and full of flavor while the icing held a firm texture that simply complimented the cake. After devouring the cupcake, I couldn't resist on holding off on the brownie. It did not disappoint! The brownie was moist, chewy, and fudgey with a lovely texture delivered by the added by the chocolate chunks. Big fan! My only regret is not enjoying it with a scoop of vanilla ice cream! 

Overall, definitely a great local spot to check out and grab scrumptious sweets at a reasonable price. They do offer custom cakes, cookie cakes, and baked trays - will give them a shot in the future for an event!

With plenty of good breakfast/brunch spots in the Fishtown/Northern Liberties area, it took me awhile to get to around to Honey's Sit-N-Eat. They, however, did not disappoint. 

My group of three arrived at 8:30AM on a Sunday morning and were immediately seated. I should warn though that a decent sized line started to form at the end of our breakfast - for good reason! Once seated, we were promptly greeted by our server with bottomless La Colombe coffee and recommendations from their daily special menu.  The restaurant staff was very attentive throughout with the table's coffee and water supplies never reaching the bottom. I was pleased with the friendly, homey environment. 

For the most part, the food was fantastic. We ordered the freshly baked blueberry muffin from the specials per the server's recommendation. Wow. Absolutely delicious. The muffin was short on blueberries, however, the crunchy top combined with a moist, buttery balance on the inside made for a scrumptious starter. My order of the Country Fried Steak was the only reason Honey's gets 4-stars. The steak was fried to a perfectly lightly flaky consistency, but the gravy and breading seasoning were absolutely bland. The steak only served as a plate filler for the sides, which were much better. My sides were a latke, buttered biscuit, and eggs-over-hard (that was a silly mistake on my end). The latke was so delicious - crunchy outside with a delicate, cheesy(?) inside! The biscuit was good with a little extra butter to add to the moisture. 

Now, I did try the Fried Chicken Chipotle Benedict that another member of my party ordered from the specials. AMAZING. The set-up was on mini buttermilk pancakes with a light honey glaze. When taking a bite with each element of the dish, it was simply bliss. The balance of the fried chicken with the cakey pancake, the spicy kick of the chipotle sauce met with the sweetness of the honey glaze, and the moisture from the poached egg was executed flawlessly. Highly recommend if they have that again!

All in all, a great place and will definitely be back again!

In the newest edition of me ruining my diet, I zoned in on FARMiCiA after seeing their brunch menu included nachos to which I could add to my running list. After two weeks of mentally preparing, I readied myself for a huge, delicious brunch feast. I definitely recommend what was to come!

My group of 4 made a reservation at 11:30 during their Brunch Happy Hour (11AM - 2PM, beers and cocktails 50% off!!) a day in advanced. Upon arrival, I noticed that you can save 10% off your bill by paying it fully in cash. Great deal!! We were promptly seated and were quickly greeted by our server for our drink order - I got the Always Sunny. Highly recommended if you like ginger brew based cocktails. 

My food order alone consisted of the small Nachos, Apple Cherry French Toast, Buttermilk Pancakes, Turkey & Avocado Club, and finished with the Apple Cranberry Crisp. Get ready.

The nachos were a decent offering for their price...coming from a big nacho critic. The portion for the small was enough to be shared as an appetizer for 4. I really enjoyed the subtle saltiness of the chips and solid crunch of the chips. In my opinion, the cheese should have been more warm and gooey to contrast the cooling of the generous amount of sour cream and salsas. If they offer meat as a topping, it would surely elevate these nachos. Solid. 

My favorite part of the meal were the items from the griddle: the Buttermilk Pancakes and Apple Cherry French Toast. The French Toast was topped with a delicious baked combination of the fruit that added to the lightness of the bread. Adding a fork bit of the whipped cream elevated the sweetness to a fantastic level. On the other side, the Buttermilk Pancakes were so light and fluffy with an exceptional taste. Really hard to find a good pancake, but they did a great job. 

As my main course, I ordered a Turkey & Avocado Club. Yet again, they executed this course flawlessly. My favorite parts were the fresh herb taste in the mayo combined with the avocado and the bacon. OMG the bacon was so crisp, so good! A generous portion of fries accompany the dish - be careful as they're addicting. 

My least favorite part of the meal was the ending - the Apple Cranberry Crisp. The inside was soupy and the outer was hidden under the ice cream. Not much crisp going on. Also, my only gripe with the experience would be the lack of attention from the server. I often waited 10 minutes between check-ups with an empty glass of cocktail or water.

All-in-all fantastic food. Highly recommend!

What a nice new little gem tucked away underneath Girard Station! I finally got around to hitting up Da-Wa after eyeing it up from its opening in January. Delicious food with friendly, attentive service.

My order consisted of the Braise Pork Bao Buns and Cha Shu Ramen. The Bao Buns were absolutely fantastic. The soft, chewy texture of the bun combined with the succulent melt-in-your-mouth pork and freshness of the toppings made for a musical symphony in each bite. Pro tip given by the waiter: add the chip garnish to the buns to add a crunch to enhance the experience. 

The Cha Shu Ramen was a solid meal. For $12, the portion was generous and the contents were presented beautifully. I really enjoyed the perfectly spiced broth. 

All-in-all, I can't speak to the sushi, but great spot for quality ramen and bao buns! Definitely a spot to check out if you're in the neighborhood.

There's always a lot of hype about this food truck for street festivals, but The Cow and The Curd was Udderly (get it) disappointing. An order of the curds (with a dipping sauce) costed $10 which was a bit steep for 8-9 curds, however, due to the hype and the appearance from others orders, I figured they would be worth it. Sadly, I was mistaken as they do not come close to a standard Wisconsin curd...like at Culvers. 

From the outside, the curds are huge pieces fried to a perfect golden brown - look perfect. As the story goes - you can't judge a book by its cover. I had so much anticipation going into the first bite, but when I ripped into the curd all I tasted was breading. There was no cheese. NO CHEESE in a CHEESE curd. The breading was great for what it's worth, but they failed to maintain the cheese during the frying process. Of my 9 pieces only 2 contained the cheese; the others left a small pool of cheese at the bottom of the cup. 

For what it's worth, the two complete curds were fantastic and their Chipotle Ranch sauce was delicious. However, I expect each and every curd to be filled with delicious WI cheese at the minimum. Oh well...

After hearing positive reviews from friends, I decided to do a birthday brunch at Cafe Lift. We had a group of 16 people (broken into a 10 and 6 top) which only required a 35 minute wait at 11 on a Saturday morning. Note: they do not take reservations. However, they will text you when the table is ready, so you can walk over to Prohibition Taproom or walk around if you'd like. 

Our table's waitress was friendly, attentive, and provided her recommendations when people had difficulty deciding. She was quick to open our BYO champagne and bring glasses for the table. Additionally, she was able to accommodate for allergies. Great service!

For my order, I got the popular Cannoli French Toast and the Philly Cheesesteak Breakfast Sandwich. The Cheesesteak Breakfast Sandwich was definitely the highlight. A pretzel bun stuffed with delicious steak, onions, cheese, and a fried egg with breakfast potatoes on the side. The sandwich itself was ample amount off food. If anything, I'd like the bun to be salted to amplify the pretzel taste. I was disappointed with the Cannoli French Toast based on my expectations. The bread itself was tasty - soft delicious inside with a crispy outside. I thought the ricotta topping and the chipped chocolate lacked in flavor. If anything, it was a bland dish that is not worth it. 

I did sample a few other dishes from my table. The lemon ricotta pancakes, blueberry pancakes, and a special B.E.C Sandwich on a "Philly Bun" were all solid. No one found anything that was a must have. 

Overall, solid brunch spot with some tasty brunch dishes.  Service and the vibe are what bring it from a 3 to a 4.

While shopping around for a birthday cake, I was looking for a place that could offer a to-order chocolate drip cake with great taste, reasonable price, and could make it nut-free. I was shopping around mostly in the Center City and Fishtown areas, but ended up stumbling upon Bredenbeck's in Chestnut Hill. 

Tish responded to my inquiry in a timely fashion. I was happy to hear that the equipment used to make my cake would be sanitized and ingredients would be nut-free - of course, there are nuts there, but that was enough to make me comfortable. From there, the ordering process was simple and easy. I asked for a chocolate cake, cookies & cream filling, vanilla buttercream icing outside, then topped with a chocolate drip to serve 12-15 people. Tish recommended the 9" cake and asked if asked if I wanted any additional garnish to which I said maybe Oreos to add to the cookies & cream style. Price was $20 cheaper than the same 9" cake from other bakeries. 

Brendenbeck's SHATTERED my expectations. The cake was beautiful, huge, and, most importantly, delicious. They went above and beyond with the icing garnish, Oreos, and chocolate bark. The cake was moist and tasted like a big, cakey Oreo. Everyone loved it. 

I will be back for future delicious, beautiful cakes at a very reasonable price!!

Jerry's Bar is tucked away off the main strip of 2nd Street restaurants in Northern Liberties. When walking or driving around the neighborhood, you'll likely see the loads abandoned cars, billboards, and signs advertising the restaurant. We headed over for Sunday Brunch. 

On Sunday mornings, this place is nice for grabbing a drink, sitting out on the sidewalk or in the well-lit downstairs while listening to live jazz music. However, the service and food (for its price point) was disappointing. 

I ordered the Brisket Omelette with potatoes and Strawberry Cream Stuffed Brioche French Toast. I will say the omelette was mouthwatering. The brisket was juicy, the eggs were light and buttery. On the side, the breakfast potatoes lacked character - no taste and still a bit firm with no crisp. Unfortunately, the French Toast came out 20 minutes late with no sight of Strawberries and Cream. We didn't complain as it was comp'd, but I think were given the Vanilla Brioche French Toast. It was really thick brioche with a nice outside crisp and soft, delicate inside. Yummy for sure, however, still disappointed with it not being what we wanted. 

Overall, tasty food and nice lively spot. Service and the wrong order brought it down a level.

Tucked away off the I-95 Girard Ave exit is this Fishtown neighborhood gem. If you're looking for a local spot with simple, tasty food at a reasonable price, Sulimay's is the spot for you. Nothing flashy here, but very happy with my experience. Note - cash only!

We went on a rainy Friday morning with almost all the restaurant to ourselves. I ordered the Biscuits and Gravy with poached eggs and breakfast potatoes plus split an order of the Blueberry Pancakes. The plate had two large fresh, moist, homemade biscuits topped with a well seasoned, perfectly balanced sausage gravy. Easily in the top two I've had in Philly. If anything, there should have been a bit more gravy to cover the heaping pile of biscuits, but the poached eggs made up for it. Breakfast potatoes were pretty standard that served their purpose as a side show. I thoroughly enjoyed the blueberry pancakes. Light, fluffy with a great pancake batter taste shining through. The blueberries were scarce, but added a subtle sweet taste. Highly recommend!

Overall, great spot with mom and pop shop vibe. Nothing over the top, but done just right.

Note: Review based on Brunch

After going to Frankford Hall several occasions for nights out for drinks and hanging out with friends, I noticed they serve brunch on the weekends...with Blueberry Pancakes! Though it is a lower key bar with a great outside for any season (fire-pits in the winter) and tables inside for playing jenga with friends, I would have never expected a brunch menu. Alas, I was wrong and I should've expected it from Stephen Starr.

With only four additional items, you'd hope they all be good. The Buttermilk Pancakes were surprisingly fantastic. The pancakes are moist, light and fluffy with notes of pumpkin spice. The blueberry compote and sweet butter give the pancakes a lovely sweetness and flavor that make syrup an unnecessary accessory. The other item ordered - Sausage & Egg Sandwich - was definitely a looker but did not bring the punch. The open faced sandwich is topped with spicy bauernwirst, gruyere, a tomato, and a fried egg. In theory those all sound great together, but the sandwich lacked flavor and character. Not worth it, in my opinion. 

Overall, the brunch atmosphere is what you'd expect - not much. The Buttermilk Pancakes are worthy of coming back for though!

North Third is an exceptional spot in Northern Liberties. The atmosphere is welcoming with a quirky interior that hits home on the local spot feel. 
I have been here twice - once for dinner and once for brunch. 

Though I have no evidence of pictures for the dinner in the Fall, I was thrilled with the meal. My Crispy Chicken Sandwich was an A+. Chicken was juicy, crisp, and tender. The tomato was fresh, bacon crisp, avocado and mayo flavorful, and delicious roll. We had a fantastic piece of Chocolate Chip Bread pudding a la mode for dessert. I accompanied the dessert with a warm spiked apple cider - great balance of flavor and alcohol. One of the best meals in the area. 

Brunch on the other hand was just OK. The server recommended the Chicken and Waffles which were calling my name. The chicken, like on the sandwich, was excellent and carried the dish. I believe it was the syrup which carried the tabasco addition, maybe the chicken (I poured it over the chicken and waffles from the get so I couldn't decipher), but I was thrilled with the balance of sweet and spicy flavors. Unfortunately, the waffle was a bit mushy and needed a bit more umph. The eggs and potatoes are a complete side show...nice to have but not needed. Additionally, I ordered a single Banana Foster Pancake (malted vanilla an& banana pancakes topped with carmelized bananas, cinnamon & rum sauce, and whipped cream) from the specials menu. The dish was smothered with the Banana Fosters topping so the pancake did not really shine through. The sauce flavor was good but a bit too thick. Overall, it was good but needed more of a friendly balance of sauce and pancake. 

Overall, the experience here from Dinner makes it a 4-star. Brunch was more of a 3-star. Highly recommend for a low-key date night.

One Shot is a great spot tucked off the main 2nd Street strip in Northern Liberties. What makes it special is the atmosphere and interior. It's great for grabbing a coffee and snack then either enjoying the hustle bustle downstairs or the calming upstairs with a mini-library while you crank out work!

The food from the menu itself is OK. Again, it's the environment that makes this place special - so the food is more so a side bar. I ordered the Huevos Rancheros and French Toast. The Huevos Rancheros was presented nicely, but the execution of the dish was off. There wasn't any particular ingredient that delivered a distinct flavor - no zest in the guac, no spice in the beans, no fresh taste of salsa. They all blended together to give just an ok dish. On the sweet side, the french toast was decent. The bread was not standout, but I did like the subtle taste of the added Dulce De Leche syrup. The sauce could have used a bit more thickness as it was runny and hard to soak the toast in. 

Overall, food is ok. However, the main purpose of this spot is what makes it great!

After a few years of the hype, the closure of his old spot, then the opening of the bigger restaurant - I had to check it out. Was it worth the hype and price? Definitely not. 

Since we did not have a reservation, we walked-in at 4:45 on a Wednesday. Upon being seated at the communal-style bench table, we were greeted by our waitress, put in our drink orders, and two pieces of the tomato pie. Thought was definitely put into the draft beer and wines as the Tired Hands Lager complimented the food quite nicely. 

The tomato pie was solid - dough was thick, I enjoyed the balance of the oil and the acidity of the tomato sauce. Gosh the crust was perfect though! Crispy, flavorful, and complimented the inner pie nicely. I took a portion home for leftovers which held up to the test and stayed delicious.

The main dish - a pizza - was a let down. We ordered the #1 (tomato, whole milk mozz, royer mountain). Maybe it was because of the magnitude of the hype for this to be life-changing, but I was disappointed. The cheese and sauce lacked character in the flavor which reminded me of a standard mid-class pie. I really like my dough crispy, but this was floppy with a weak hold. Crust was nice and thin, but forgettable. 

The Sweet Cream Soft Serve for dessert was enjoyable. Thick and creamy to properly finish off a meal. 

Overall, average pizza. I really enjoyed the tomato pie and soft serve. Is it worth $22 for a 15-inch cheese pizza? No. Nice spot though!

While at the Manayunk Food Truck Festival a few weeks ago, I was allured by the cute multi-colored blue truck offering eye-catching cupcake flavors. Boy, am I happy to have found this gem. 

At first, I ordered a peaches n cream cupcake - a vanilla cupcake topped with icing, peaches, and a crumble. It blew me away. The cupcake captured everything about a true peaches and cream dessert. The icing was light and complimented the sweetness of the peaches. 

I couldn't stay away from the truck for long and ordered a Cookies n Cream and a Red Velvet (not for myself). Cookies n Cream was fantastic for any lover. 

Overall, highly recommend for their cupcakes. Now the quest is to find them on the streets!

***REVIEW ON NACHOS ONLY****
One snowy day in Philly, Distritowas offering $5 (small) nachos and $5 margaritas that entire day. Their nachos (including their larger "Super Nachos") are topped with queso mixto, rajas, black beans, chile de arbol, and creama. Not mentioned, but important to the flavor, are tomatoes, fresh jalapeños, and radish. The nachos are based with a thin, subtle flavored chip that is sturdy enough to withstand their toppings. In addition, the cheese adds an underlying connection between each of the ingredients - it doesn't pop out for someone that is looking for just cheese, but, from a nacho perspective, it definitely molds the flavors. My favorite elements of the nachos are the complimentary flavorful kick of the chile de arbol salsa and jalapeños with the fresh and cooling tomatoes and radishes. These, like Taqueria Feliz, are top level happy hour nachos for sure...explains why I got two orders. Only downside is there are just too little!

I recommend this place especially during snow storms or for a date while you sit in their car booth. Also, recommend their Super Nachos (which I have, too, had).

Nacho Rating: 8.2/10

Tried Jerry's Bar for dinner this time. I ordered the Fried Chicken Sandwich with fries. The chicken is dipped in hot-n-honey sauce then topped with charred scallion aioli, lettuce, and tomato all on a brioche bun. I found the chicken too thin with mostly breading and the sauce had a nice tang, but a little too heavy. Maybe the classic slaw and pickles would be better topping than the lettuce & tomato as they did not add much.

This was the pizza spot that Mt Airy wanted and still wants to succeed, however they're having a hard time fulfilling that. 

The pizza and food is actually good. The pizza has a decent crisp and light flop. Maybe my favorite chicken tenders in the neighborhood (albeit probably prepackaged frozen) for a reasonable price. If you're looking for a relaxing kind of night, they have two pool tables for fun. 

What hurts this place is the service is unbearably slow with poor communication amongst the staff. While waiting for my to-go order, I watched a mom and son order and pay for two slices of plain pizza, only for the person to ring them up have a different staff to tell the patrons 5 minutes later they didn't have cheese. Another guy came in for pickup and was told 5 minutes by the cooks - only to sit for another 15 minutes. In a neighborhood like Mt Airy with a critical crowd, the operation needs to be smoother.

The Better Box food truck was featured on Thrillist and instantly caught my attention. It took me awhile to actually get there, and, by the time I did, it was the newly opened store location. 

The menu is definitely eye popping with mouth watering egg rolls, sandwiches, and fries. I ordered the Angry Chicken, the Cajun Jawn, a General Tso's Chicken Cheesesteak, and the Chocolate Explosion Cookies. 

My favorite hot item was definitely the Angry Chicken. The flavors blend well with the fried egg roll shell. The Cajun Jawn was OK as I was expecting a little bit more cajun seasoning to enhance the flavor but it was mostly overpowered by the grease. My least favorite was the General Tso's Chicken Cheesesteak. The Thrillist video painted a picture of this packed, sauced sandwich ready for annihilation. However, the flavor was underwhelming, cheese was not melted enough (see back of sandwich in picture), and wasn't a great roll. 

All that being said - THE COOKIES ARE BOMB!!!!  I was in pure bliss eating the cookies. I would go back over and over for them. Unreal. 

Overall, it's a spot worth checking out for the experience. I think the egg rolls were actually pretty good cold. This spot should definitely open in a place like Manayunk or somewhere with nightlife because it would hit the spot at 2AM. Again, COOKIES ARE FIRE!

After hearing my two friends glow when recalling their dinner experience at Barclay Prime, I had to try it out. Barclay Prime is tucked in the corner of Rittenhouse Square which is nice to come to after a stroll in the city. 

The initial intent was to go in for Happy Hour (which I heard is amazing), however make sure you sit at the bar area specifically to get the offers. In my case, we got sent straight to our table so we missed out - oh well. 

The bread to start off is quite enjoyable with a nice outer crust, (mostly hollow inside) doughy inside coupled with butter. Aside, we ordered a Waygu Beef Carpaccio as an appetizer. Absolutely fantastic. The beef paired with the refreshing citric acidity of the lemon paired well for a symphony in my mouth. If anything, brush the Parmesan away to get the most from the beef. 

I ordered the 40-day dry aged 20 oz Ribeye. A nice little touch on the experience is when they offer a selection of international knives to choose from as "your weapon." I chose the German knife. The steak itself was perfectly seared to capture the peppery but also buttery for the taste bud indulging flavors. I would go as far as saying it has been the best steak I've ever had. 

The sides were solid, but nothing earth shattering. The Truffle Mac & Cheese was perfectly creamy. The truffle added just noticeable flavor. The crumble on the top is barely a compromise for the desire for the dish to be baked. The other side, Tater Tots, were just well cooked tater tots and nothing to waste the experience on.
