To end the meal, I got the Warm Cookie Skillet. A blend of three cookies - sugar, chocolate chip, and oatmeal raisin - topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a side of chocolate sauce. One of the better cookie skillets I've had - crisp outside and warm, soft inside. My favorite of the three sections was surprisingly the oatmeal raisin.

Overall, fantastic spot for steaks and that should be your primary focus. If you want to try the other stuff, happy hour is the time as you'll get your bang for your buck. Maybe even stop by for dessert just to indulge yourself. Will be back at some point for the $120 cheesesteak.

Holidays tend to call for a surplus of money which means time to splurge on a higher end meal. At the same time, my debit card offered a 10% cash back for Del Frisco's Double Eagle so it was destiny. 

We went for a lunch which is lighter on the pockets, however we balled out. The day after Christmas did not bring in much of a crowd so there were few tables, low noise and we were able to just soak in the environment of the building's architecture. 

Our server, Marco, promptly greeted us and took our drink order. The VIP cocktail was fantastic as they let the vodka soak infuse the pineapple flavor over the course of a few days. Throughout the meal, the cocktail glass was replaced for a colder one. Great service by Marco throughout!

We started off with the Cheesesteak Dumplings. The dumplings crust were crisp and the inside was juicy. The spicy ketchup was a nice touch. Solid overall. 

The main course was (obviously) steak paired with two sides. We ordered the 12 oz Filet Mignon and 12 oz Prime Strip with the lobster mac & cheese and brussels sprouts.  Marco and the other staff member portioned out the sides with our steaks at the table. The steaks were nicely seasoned with a great sear around the edge. The flavor was good, but personally thought Barclay Prime was juicier and seasoned better. Mac&Cheese was some of the best I've had - creamy and packed with flavor. Brussel sprouts were perfectly charred and added flavor from the bacon and lemon. Overall, solid entrees and sides. 

For dessert, we ordered both the Lemon Cake and the warm Banana Bread Pudding. My favorite of the two was the Lemon Cake - it is a culmination of 6 layers of cake with lemon buttercream and lemon glaze. Although delicious, I would have preferred a stronger lemon taste to really hit the lemon craving. As for the banana bread pudding, it was lackluster in flavor and barely considered warm - would not order again. 

Overall, Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse offers delicious options and their steak is one of the best in the city. Service was great and drinks were good. Great for a date night or, if you're looking to save a few dollars, lunch is a good option. Would go again.

My friend and I were looking for a double date option for CCD Restaurant Week and found The Twisted Tail. For their restaurant week menu, there were several options that served to the table's dietary restrictions. 

We arrived for our reservation 5 minutes early but ended up having to wait 15 minutes past for a table to be opened up. If this is the case for you, the bar is an option for pre-dinner drinks.

Once seated, the three meat eaters at the table, including myself, game-planned how to make the most of the menu. A few overlaps, but enough desirable options to get a variety of tastes. 

First course - (2) Wagyu Beef Tartare and Crawfish Mac & Cheese. The beef was flavorful and melt in your mouth. I liked the side of crisp bed to compliment the bites. The crawfish mac & cheese was the table favorite. Generous amounts of crawfish with the perfect amount of creaminess and thickness. 

Second course - Chorizo Taco, Grilled Quail, Spicy Salmon Wraps. I enjoyed all three of these. The chorizo was in its unchopped link form packed with flavor and enhanced by the queso fresco and tomatillo salsa. Spicy salmon wraps were perfectly refreshing with the raw salmon, a nice bite of spice, and added crunch on top. The quail was solid off the bone and juicy. 

Third course - Braised Short Rib, BBQ Smoked Ribs, Grilled Hanger Steak. To start, my short rib was my least favorite. Was not tender and lacked the flavor from both the meat and the demi-glaze. The ribs were surprisingly delicious - tender, slightly charred, and a solid BBQ sauce. Obviously not the best relative to some of my favorite BBQ spots, but delivered for a spot like this. The steak was another solid pick with great flavor from the meat and chimichurri sauce. 

Fourth Course - Beignets and Chocolate Pot de Creme. Not my favorite part of the meal. The beignets were okay as they are cinnamon sugar topped vice the normal powdered sugar. The caramel sauce added a nice touch, but still forgettable. I thought the chocolate pot de creme was okay. It was thick and coated with whipped cream on top. I did like the ginger cookie to go with it though. 

Overall, definitely a great spot for restaurant week with a few people. But also a great spot otherwise. The food was great and definitely worth getting again! Will be back.

My friend and I headed to Angelo's after hearing about how amazing it was from another friend. Coupled with the glowing from Barstool Pizza, there was definitely a high expectation for the pizza. Maybe not their best day, but I know there is definitely high potential for the pizza. 

We headed over on a Friday around 1 PM with a solid line. We ordered the Cheese Pizza (a must as a baseline), the Diavalo, and the Drunk Cutlet sandwich. We killed our 25 minute wait time by walking a few blocks over to Isgro Bakery for some sweets. By the time we got back, our order was just coming out - perfect timing. 

Since there are only a few tables outside, we took the food to my car and posted up on the trunk. The long awaited moment to dig into the cheese pizza was finally here...

I was personally let down. I had built it up in my mind that it would be a crunchy, crispy bite but instead it was more doughy. However, it was still very good pizza. Cheese was flavorful and the crust was crispy. Apparently that day on Instagram it was said that the oven was acting up; I'll let them slide for now. 

On the other hand, the Diavalo was too spicy for me, so I cannot knock Angelos - that's on me. The Drunken Cutlet was very tasty! The bread was crunchy, there was a plethora of chicken, the garlic slices was fantastic, the blush sauce added a nice wetness, and the spinach and ricotta were both refreshing touches. 

Overall, solid cheese pizza that could be better (when done how it was on Barstool) and the sandwich was fantastic. Need to go again!

While searching for a dinner groupon deal, we stumbled upon Bistro Albertino. Reviews gave the small BYOB spot a promising rating, however the reviews did not hold up. 

We had an 8PM reservation for 2 which took about 20 minutes to be seated. The complimentary bread served at the table is nothing special, but I was told the pesto (allergy for me) was actually really good. 

Our first course of the Caprese was a total flop. When I think of this dish, normally its fresh and bursting with natural flavors. The individual components - mozzarella, basil, tomato, and olive oil - all were bland. Needed a good amount of salt and pepper to bring any life to the dish. 

The main courses were Linguini alla Pescatore and Bistecca Albertino. For my Bistecca Albertino dish, the pasta was fine, but the steak was on the tougher side - I would've enjoyed a more tender bite. The Linguni all Pescatore was similar to the Caprese, as it lacked overall flavor with no shining ingredients. Oh well. 

Overall, only worth checking out with a groupon to get a discount. However, not planning on heading back anytime soon. Need to revamp their ingredients.

Butcher and Singer was next up on my Stephen Starr list and steakhouse in Philadelphia. A late Valentine's Day celebration was the perfect time to check it out. 

When we arrived for our 5:30 reservation, we were promptly sat and asked if we would like our jackets hung - politely declined. The server was very attentive and gave his recommendations right off the bat. Tip from the server: the kitchen cooks their steaks a bit on the lower side, so a medium is generally a medium-rare anywhere else. Very happy about the service! 

We put in our order - crab dip for an appetizer and the 28-Day Dry Aged Porterhouse for two with the stuffed hash browns and macaroni & cheese for the main dish. While we waited, we were given warm biscuits and butter. The biscuits were delicious - flaky and moist, albeit a little on the saltier side - with the creamy butter enhancing them. They were quickly finished and the server said he'd get us more...never trust anyone who says no to more!

While we waited for more biscuits, the crab dip came out. Definitely a highlight of the meal for me. If you like heaps of crab and gooey, baked cheese, you're in for a treat. My only qualm was the shortage of crispy bread for dipping. Do not fret, however, because those extra biscuits came in for the save. Recommend as an appetizer!

The main course was where I make my assessment of Butcher and Singer - it's a steakhouse! When the steak arrived, we were asked to ensure it was to our requested temperature, which was a perfect medium-rare (aka a MEDIUM in their books). The Porterhouse cut consists of two cuts on the bone: the tenderloin and the top loin (aka New York Strip). The New York Strip side was dominated by a smokey-charred taste - big let down. The tenderloin portion was less charred, but still lacked a good seasoning to compliment the perfect, moist meat. We ordered au poivre which definitely came in handy to mask the charred and allow the meat to shine a bit. Still disappointing. 

Sides were okay but plentiful. The stuffed hash browns definitely needed help from the au poivre to enhance the flavor otherwise lacked flavor. I did really like the mac & cheese, however. It was creamy and noodles were cooked perfectly - really good for leftovers consistency. If you don't like breadcrumbs on your mac & cheese: beware. 


For dessert, we ordered the Baked Alaska and the Key Lime Pie. Again, our server made a clutch recommendation: if you don't finish, take home the key lime and freeze - it's better! It was my first time having Baked Alaska so I don't have a baseline, but a let down in my books - would not order again. The key lime pie - better at-home, frozen - was dense and yummy, especially if you like a strong lime flavor like me.  

Overall, Butcher and Singer does not live up to Starr's Barclay Prime or Del Friscos. Service was great though! Might give it another try in the future.

Stopped by Charlie Was a Sinner for a pre-dinner cocktail during happy hour. We sat at the bar and grabbed a quick round. Drinks were tasty and made with fresh ingredients. Recommend as a place to grab a cocktail with a friend or a date.

BEST BRUNCH IN PHILLY! You heard it here first. The Sunday-only Brunch here flies under the radar especially if you do not follow them on Instagram/Facebook and do not venture to the Mt Airy area. Jansen is known for it's white tablecloth dinner experience (which is a more than fair price, in my opinion), but they deliver an incredible, affordable brunch menu that tops the frequently visited/trendy Center City area spots. 

My friend and I came in with a single intention: the Sticky Buns. If you check out their social media or have ever had one of their desserts made by their pastry chef, you'll understand. 

We arrived shortly after opening with a reservation two and were promptly sat next to the fireplace. As a cool historical note, Jansen is housed in Cresheim Cottage which was built in the 1700s and oldest in the area! My friend and I immediately started drooling over the menu options with stomachs ready - we were in the middle of our kick that included a 4-course meals from Twisted Tail and two pizzas plus a sandwich from Angelos (see my reviews) within a 4-day span. Our server promptly tended to us and certainly fed the fire saying everything was delicious. We were undecided.

Our final entree order? Chicken and Waffles, Monte Cristo, Huevos Rancheros, and French Toast. Told you - undecided. Our server laughed and asked if she could interest us in the fresh breakfast bread and pastry spread to start. We caved, of course. 

The breakfast bread and pastry is nothing eye-popping, but, boy, does it deliver. The spread consisted of peppered biscuits, buttered rolls, biscotti, and caramel glazed banana bread with honey butter and peach jam on the side - all homemade. The biscuits were flaky, moist and, when coupled with the rich and light honey butter, some of the best I've ever had. The rolls were fresh and melt in your mouth. Banana bread was moist, not overly sweet from the glaze, but a little light on the banana flavor. We treated the biscotti - which was a bit bland - as a vessel for the perfect peach jam and extra butter. Great starter!

To our amazement with our aggressive entree order, the kitchen offered us a sample of breakfast egg-rolls. My taste buds are still dancing thinking about them. The bite-sized egg-rolls were filled with light, fluffy eggs, breakfast sausage, wrapped by crispy, flaky, lightly fried roll and topped with a dollop of ketchup. Pure bliss and enjoyment!

After devouring the egg-rolls, we were greeted with our first entree: Chicken and Waffles. As a note, it does come with candied pecan, but, since I have an allergy, they gave them to my friend on the side. The dish itself is a masterpiece with thoughtful flavors. In addition to the standard sweet/savory compliment of chicken and waffle, the waffle itself contains bacon and homemade toffee for added compliments. The fried chicken itself is tied for the best I've ever had. Period. Crisp, tender, and rich with flavor. The waffle was sweet and crisp. As mentioned, the toffee and bacon was like a symphony in my mouth. The fresh maple syrup is nothing to bat an eye at either! We agreed this was our favorite dish! 

Next up was the Monte Cristo and Huevos Rancheros. I started with the Huevos Rancheros which was a well executed rendition. The bean and salsa concoction was light and flavorful. Tortillas were crisp and light, so no issue cutting into them with compromise of the crunch. I really enjoyed poached eggs vice the normal sunny side up. The dish was a masterful blend of flavors and textures. Careful with the fresh jalapenos though. After eating my half, I moved onto the Monte Cristo. It's good, but definitely the first one out if we had to reduce our order since it's heavy. The dish is taylor ham (PORK ROLL!!!), turkey, gruyer cheese between two pieces of thick french toast then topped with two sunny side eggs and mornay sauce plus a side of syrup. Although its a heavy dish, the flavors kept me chugging through the dish with the 4th on the horizon. 

By the time the Brioche French Toast came, we were all but ready to tap out. Still had to try and, again, it was well worth it! The french toast was lightly dipped in batter so not overly eggy, but enough to get that perfect crisp outside without compromising the soft, chewy consistency of the inside. The berries and syrup added the perfect additional amount of sweetness. Great for leftovers, too! 

In the end, we did not get what we came for: the Sticky Buns. Don't worry though, I came back for them the next week. Again, phenomenal! 

Jansen is THE BEST BRUNCH IN PHILLY. Hands down. I cannot wait to go again - just need someone available on a Sunday morning. Check it out! If something sounds good, it probably is. Mimosa and Bloody Marys are creative at reasonable prices if you want to make it boozy. Will go again!

Went to Heritage with a couple of friends on a Friday night for a catch-up dinner. While it doesn't look big from the outside, the restaurant is quite spacey inside. The volume can vary depending on the music the given night - the music did not invade our conversations and provided great background tunes. Lighting is pretty dim, so definitely going to be that person with flash when the phone inevitably eats first. 

We were greeted shortly after we arrived for our drink order - I got the Strawberry Swing - and our food order. The drink was refreshing and not too sweet. 

For food, we started with the PEI mussels and wild boar meatballs. Mussels were made in a red sauce and solid, run of the mill. The bread was crunchy and flavorful: perfect for soaking the juices. Meatballs were solid, too. They are topped with a fresh marinara sauce and served with a side of creamy fontina polenta. The polenta was a unique addition that was welcomed. Overall, solid appetizers. 

My main dish, after my friend said his good friend boasted it as the best, was the red wine marinated duck breast. Duck was rimmed with fat, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, and packed with flavor.  Loved it. The mushroom & truffled pearled barley served as a complimentary side. It was creamy and enhanced to the texture and flavor with each bite. The roasted carrots were more so to say "here's a veggie." Overall, great duck!

The dessert was advertised to us a cinnamon banana bread pudding served with a homemade vanilla bean ice cream. Definitely not banana. If anything, the fruit was apple and plums. Either way, it was just ok. Would not get again. 

Overall, Heritage was a solid dinner with a pleasant ambiance. Only qualm was the server's lack of checking for more drinks unless we waved him down and telling us the wrong dessert. But the food itself is worth coming back again! Good place for a date or spiced up dinner with family/friends.

FDNFzcsE2WI3Qd2UEjGp6A.review_text: If you haven't stopped by Pork Belly, you are seriously missing out. I always order "The Rachel" sandwich and bow tie pasta. Delicious and addictive as always. I have referred several friends and family here and not one person has been disappointed.

Caramel macchiato was bitter and barely warm.. I got a ham and Swiss sandwich and there was a huge fatty piece in it, took up a large portion of the meat unfortunately.. cashier was very polite and I didn't have to wait very long but not worth the money.

One of my favorite Mexican restaurants and close to home. Polite staff, delicious margaritas, great chips n salsa, and cheap food. I've been here several times and I've  never had a bad experience. It's usually always busy but even when it's pretty packed it hasn't taken very long to get food.

In love with this place! I walked in and the line was long but the guy working at the bar offered us to sit and promised our food would be our very quickly. We ordered and our food was it out in less than 5 mins. It was amazing. The food tasted great and I will definitely be back.

I love the sandwiches and wraps here, the only reason I've giving 4 stars instead of 5 is because more than once I've asked them not to put mayo on my sandwiches (or tomato) and they still did it. Not a huge deal because I can take it off but still the food is a little pricey. One time they gave me coffee that was luke warm but happily warmed it up for me without any problems. Overall really good, nice staff, lots of sandwich variety. It's a frequent spot to stop for me.

I was very pleased with my dinner at cheddars. We had great service and delicious food. I ordered the red fish on rice with mashed potatoes and macaroni. I had zero complaints about the food, the fish was very tasty and exactly how it should be. Our waitress was very nice and attentive. The only complaint I have about my experience was that we were seated right by a back door that opened up to the outdoor seating. The reason being is because it was very hot and humid and they were in and out constantly. It's just not a very good seating spot in general but it was tolerable. Overall I'd definitely go back and have that fish again, so delicious!

Walking in the restaurant, it looked pretty neat and fun. Our waitress was very sweet and attentive, answered all the questions we had about drinks and food options. I ordered the chicken pot pie and it was pretty tasty. My husband ordered the shepherds pie and he enjoyed it very much and couldn't stop eating it. I had a cappuccino, which was so delicious and had a thick frothy top. I also ordered the iced layered cappuccino..it was good except it was a tab bit too strong for me personally. My husband finished it for me because he likes stronger coffee flavors. We ended our meal with the banana cream pie. Oh my lord, it was delicious! I wish I had an entire pan of that banana cream pie. Overall, I would absolutely be back, we were kinda disappointed we hadn't discovered it sooner.

I've been here two or three times and the food has been just as delicious each time I've went. I always get the pulled chicken, sweet potatoes (with coconut shreds on top) and the black beans. It's not far from home so it's a stop I plan on making more frequently. They have very polite staff who always greet you when you walk in.

Really fun atmosphere to walk into, very loud and fun. Staff was very nice and welcoming, the waiter helped my husband pick out a delicious beer also. I only really had one complaint, it was our first time coming here and the waiter offered us some apple sauce for our baby. We thought it was just a polite gesture, but we were charged 3$ for this apple sauce. Had I known it was a "side item" I wouldn't have gotten it. Our baby is 8 months old and only ate like 5 bites off of it. Either way we told him we didn't mind paying for it but I wish I had known before hand we would be charged 3$ for something I thought was just complementary. I got the Oktoberfest chicken which was pretty tasty, I didn't like the red cabbage that came with it but that's just my opinion. My husband loved the red cabbage. He got the Rouland and he said it was delicious. We ended it with the apple strudel dessert. OMG so delicious. I will probably get that dessert everytime I go back. It was a pretty pricey place but it wasn't bad for an occasional visit. We enjoyed it overall.

First time I came to try The Pharmacy it was so packed it was over an hour wait.. so today we finally got to try it. I got the special, a burger with barbecue sauce and bacon. I asked for crispy bacon (hate chewy).. it was still pretty chewy so I ended up giving my husband the bacon off it. The burger overall was delicious. I got a side of the corn and black bean mix. Soooooo good. I could eat a huge bowl of that stuff. I wanted to try a new beer so I asked the waitress for a recommendation, ended up getting Founder Sumatra mountain brown. It had a STRONG coffee flavor to it. Not really my thing, but I'm a picky beer drinker. My husband got the biergarten platter. He liked it, wasn't a huge fan of the jagerwurst because it was dry. We plan on going back, it was a nice place to dine at.

Love this place! You better get there early if you want a seat, it always stays busy. There was a line outside the door 10 mins till it opened. I love their sausage gravy with biscuits, cheesy eggs and house fries. So so good. Staff is always very sweet and never had any issues with service. Great breakfast restaurant, always enjoy eating there.

Cool environment, food was delicious. I asked the waitress for a beer suggestion and she picked out a great beer for me-Mill Creek landmark vintage and my husband got the Tailgate sweet tart sour (mouth watering ). Me and my husband both got burgers that were very good. I will definitely be back to this place. Been here twice and enjoyed both times very much. Definitely worth visiting.

Cute little restaurant with a milkshake bar. Nice place to hang out and enjoy a soup and sandwich. I got the harvest melt with a pb milkshake, husband got the artichoke grilled cheese and the hopscotch milkshake. Both sandwiches were delicious but I like the artichoke one better. The pb shake was perfection . Overall it was very good but a little pricey. They recycle and use recycled dishes which is a plus for me!

I got the 2 meat platter with pulled pork and the jalapeño cheddar sausage with high hopes. The jalapeño cheddar sausage was nearly impossible to bite through because the skin is so hard to bite through. The pulled pork was descent, had a lot of fat on it (which is hard for me to stomach), but I ate around it. The sides were very good. The mac and cheese was bomb, and I kinda wish I had gotten 2 sides of it. I loved the ice cooler of many old school sodas like cream soda, big red, and the bottles coke and such. You have 6 unique sauces at each table- husband tried and liked a few of them. Overall it would be a place I'd try again but no wow factor.

Nice restaurant as far as looks go, dim-lit, clean appearance. Server gave us no time to look at what drinks we wanted so we ordered water, and did the same for food. He was nice and backed off a little after that. I got salmon with Mac n cheese with mashed potatoes. Everything tasted great except the salmon was a little heavy on the salt. My date said the same thing about the chicken. Too salty. I would try it again, but first experience was kinda eh. Nothing special and a little pricey.

Such a cute restaurant! I've been here twice and both times were delicious. They're tortilla chips are very thin and crispy. Yum! I love their Baja tacos, and would recommend them. Wish they came with more than just two for a plate. Salsa was on the spicy side, which I love but not everyone does. Definitely will go back for lunch sometime.

Their cupcakes are so addictive. My favorites are wedding cake, and sweet potato. They always have weird and unusual flavors which makes me so unique.I try new flavors every time I go. Sooo worth the money if you are wanting a delicious cupcake!

Holy cow! I am in LOVE with this place. Me and my husband love Indian food, and decided to give this place a try on our very rare date night.. great choice! This place is a little pricey but damn it is so worth the money I promise. We literally had to make ourself stop eating our food before we got sick. I ordered the chicken koorma (I think that's how it's spelled?) and it makes my mouth water just thinking about it. My husband got the chef special and to be honest I don't remember everything that came with it but he was super happy with all of it. His food came out in a tier of bowls. I tried his also, and it was just as delicious as mine. For drinks we tried green tea (very good but nothing crazy), and the masala chai tea. I had to put some sugar cubes in my masala chai and made it very tasty. It had a creamy feel to it with a light nutty type flavor. Kinda hard to describe the flavor but I'd definitely get it again. Another plus to this restaurant was that the restrooms were so clean it was unreal. It's very rare I see a bathroom that's so clean I take my time and don't rush out of there. Seriously if you love Indian food try this place out. We very much plan on returning!!!

Fun little sports bar for darts and pool. Every time I've been it hasn't been super crowded so that's a plus for me. Bar staff is really nice, drinks are great, food is great. I love their fried pickles and they give you a huge portion. I've been a few times and plan on going back.

Tried the black bear latte and my husband tried the lavender latte. Both very delicious. Not overly sweet and subtle flavors. They have a few t-shirts and cute mugs you can buy. Staff very nice also. Will return at some point.

Me and my husband tried the flight of ferments, and it was delicious. My favorite was the root doctor turmeric and his favorite was the chaga cocoa. We ended up ordering sugar plum fairy potion and the salt of the earth potion. Both were perfect. We couldn't help but get us some little baggies of sample teas to go for home. Such a neat little place for any tea lovers! Will definitely be back to visit ! Also brownie points for welcoming ALL people-sign on the door for LGBT, races, religions, etc etc.

Not disappointed in their lunch buffet, had a good selection to choose from. I was a little thrown off that the server didn't direct us since we've never been here before- he seated us and gave us a water pincher and left lol. Shortly after we found someone and asked if it was just the lunch buffet that was available, he told us we could have a menu if we wanted one. We ended up getting the buffet, and they had several creamy sauces with chicken and lamb. Would come back to try this place again.

Ugh, I hate to even write this update. My favorite dish -the red fish, was taken off the menu permanently... so heartbroken. I use to come here all the time mostly for that fish plate. Now I come occasionally for drinks mostly snd their chicken with Dijon and mushrooms are pretty good. The most recent time (few days ago) we were seated and literally had no server.. a girl serving another section came over to help because we didn't have one. She said "idk where your server is, or if they're even here".. well ok. My food was wrong when I got it, they fixed it thankfully but I was sad to see the white fish (the correct order) had a rubbery mouth feel. Probably won't go back for awhile. Really hoping they'll bring back the red fish with the crab sauce.

A little pricy but worth the money. Me and my husband got the grasshopper latte and the Cuban-my personal fav. So very good. The Thai chicken wrap was a little dry but otherwise delicious and the quiche of the day was AMAZING. I bought two lol.

This place is a frequent meeting spot for me and my best friend since we live so far away form each other. I love they're coffees and baked goods. Cuban is my fav classic coffee, and they're holiday coffees are yummy also. My daughter always gets a seasonal cookie when we go.
We love this little shop. It's worth a visit.

Hookah is great, music is great, food is great. The only complaint is the service.
So damn slow. The place was fairly busy so at first I excused the slow service, but literally died down to less than half the building occupied and it took like 30 mins to get my card and receipt back. Several times me and people beside me were having to practically stop the server because she didn't pay much attention to anyone except for one guy. It was very difficult to order food because of it. Was wanting to order food for at least half an hour and she never stopped to ask if we needed anything. We ended up staying way later than intended purely because of service.
So if you go make sure you plan on staying for awhile and order like as quickly as possible.

Me and my husband visited for the first time today. I had the Tantanmen with mushrooms added and he had the szechuan miso. Mine was a little spicy, and very good flavor. My husbands was creamy and he loved his. Pictured is the Tantanmen. YUM.
We didn't get any appetizers because we knew we wouldn't be able to eat everything, but brownie points for carrying Sapporo beer! My favorite beer and difficult to find in restaurants! The only complaint I have is the temp control in the back room.
I went from burning up to freezing back and forth, because people were opening the back door often and the heater would kick on full blast. It was tolerable but not exactly comfortable. Other than that, our experience was nice and we'll definitely be back.

Cute little shop, tried the autumn leaves coffee. Literally tastes like fall in a cup. Also tried the Iced London fog to go- also pretty tasty. The guys that worked there were very nice and laid back. We plan on visiting again soon.

Best boba place around. Fortunately for me, this place is the first place I ever tried boba and I fell in love. So I began tryin other places closer to home and random places. They're all powder and artificial tasting. Literally they all taste like melted ice cream with tapioca balls. Super sweet and depending on the flavor very artificial flavor. It's like comparing Sunny D to fresh squeezed orange juice. Best comparison I can make. If you want real boba this is the place to go. 
I absolutely love it, it's mine and my husbands go to place.

Best boba place around. Fortunately for me, this place is the first place I ever tried boba and I fell in love. So I began tryin other places closer to home and random places. They're all powder and artificial tasting. Literally they all taste like melted ice cream with tapioca balls. Super sweet and depending on the flavor very artificial flavor. It's like comparing Sunny D to fresh squeezed orange juice. Best comparison I can make. If you want real boba this is the place to go. 
I absolutely love it, it's mine and my husbands go to place.

This is my go to coffee shop when I'm near Smyrna. They always have BOGO coffees and typically that's what I get. My absolute favorite is the lavender latte with whip cream. It's a tiny little shop with lots of local art. Which is a plus in my book. All the staff has been very nice and I really don't have any complaints.

I will update my review if needed when I visit again, but I wish my experience was a little better. The guy at the counter helped me pick out a coffee-which was nice.. I asked for my coffee to go because I just wanted to relax at home. He gave me my coffee in a small to go coffee cup with my creamer/milk in a small glass and "extra" coffee in another glass coffee mug. That's cool I guess? But I can't take the glass mug home.. 
so I tried to drink some of my coffee down so I could just use the extra and take it home. Couldn't do that unfortunately. I drank about half my cup and realized I still have so much extra coffee I couldn't put it all in my to go cup, so me being ready to go I just asked the guy for another to go cup. He gave me another to go cup.. with no lid ‍. So again I had to ask for a lid for my to-go cup-figured that was common sense. I was never offered more milk/cream or even sugar. Unless I'm just blind and didn't see there was a station for sugar and milk. 
Either way, the coffee tasted great, and the guys working there were nice but didn't seem to be paying attention to small things such as offering more cream when I clearly used all of the small amount I was given or especially a LID to my to-go cup. I'd like to add I was one of the 2 people sitting at the coffee bar.. not during a busy time. 
I'll try again on another day.

My one and only go to salon! A friend recommended this place a long time ago and when I decided to go I couldn't be happier. Ashley is my hairstylist and I love her dearly. She transformed my hair into something I never thought I'd have, and it still feels very healthy and soft. She definitely has a customer for life, because she makes me feel confident and beautiful!

Oh boy. 
I was hopeful for this place because I really wanted a nice seafood place to be located in Smyrna. Let me tell you my experience..
To begin with, the owner is very sweet and very nice man, and it wasn't very busy so that's always nice.
However, when we were seated, our server (an older lady named Emily) was constantly asking us what we wanted. We barely had time to look at the menu because she asked us if we were ready probably 3 times in 10 minutes.  
That was a little frustrating. Then once we ordered, there were about 5-7 employees behind the counter beside us arguing with each other. It's out in the open and everything could be heard. Not sure why it was necessary but definitely doesn't make it an enjoyable experience to have arguing employees in front of customers. 
Our food was decent, nothing spectacular, but not bad either. I went to grab a bottle of the tobasco and realized something.. odd. 
It was a lighter red color and looked very watery and thin. I looked around at other tables and realized how much darker the bottles were. ‍ they watered down this bottle to stretch it. I couldn't believe it. I wish I had gotten a picture but it would have been awkward for me considering all the staff was Right beside me behind the counter like previously stated. Needless to say, we probably won't be back till the business improves quite a bit if ever.

We were interested in trying something new and we found it. Everest had great reviews and after our experience, we can see why. The atmosphere is calm and relaxing, the staff was super nice and helpful with helping us choose dishes. 
Speaking of- the pork jhol mo-mos were AMAZING. We absolutely loved them. I got the butter chicken- which was creamy and delicious. My husband got the mutton thali, and he was impressed. We plan on returning without a doubt.

Bartaco will forever be one of my favorites. I LOVE their roasted duck tacos, they are a must try if you've never had one. We usually eat 4/5 tacos each since they're smaller like street tacos, and the corn. One helpful tip- if you fill out the little paper on the table about your experience and hand it to your waitress they'll give you a free taco coin. We never leave without one. My only wish is that their cocktails were a little cheaper because they're in smaller glasses than my experience at other restaurants but they are super tasty.

I was pleasantly Surprised at how big this place was. From the outside of the building it doesn't look very big, but inside it has several rooms to go in. They also have a gated area in the back full of plants- not really my thing for those interested it's available. They have so many crystals, jewelry, soaps, candles, books and statues... it's so much to look at. I could easily spend hours in this place. I ended up taking home several crystals and soaps. I adore them and they go perfectly with my collection of other crystals. My only complaint was the staff wasn't super attentive to me and My friend. We had a few moments of trying to get someone's attention but kinda gave up on it. Not a big deal but would have loved more info on certain elements in the store. I will definitely be back, and for someone whose into crystals, tarot, etc should give this place a shot.

I love tailgate and their selection of beers and pizza. The taco pizza is to die for and I'm a sucker for sour beers. My only issue with this location is how incredibly small it is. I'm hoping they relocate to a bigger building nearby in the East Nashville area but maybe that's wishful thinking.

Fun drinks and fun games. I went with a friend and we had aLot of fun but I hate how it's kind of a pain to get to the facility. All their drinks are inspired by games, and they've all been tasty. The times I've went it hasn't been overly crowded but I will say it's unfortunate that there is nowhere to sit except the bar unless you have reservations. Like, every seat needs a reservation, which is insane to me. That's my biggest complaint of the entire experience. I had a few games steal my coins and that is pricy considering each coin is a 1$. The most accurate rating for this place is probably a 3.5 overall. I would go back but it's probably not a place I'd go super often.

FGxqIgtWft0oatKbuvvKnw.review_text: I was totally irritated from a long week at work and dealing with traffic until I walked into Chelsea Bistro. The environment, friendly service, and hand-picked wine immediately changed my mood. The duck confit was a risk I was comfortable taking after a quick conversation with the server and it turned out to be unbelievable!
Don't be fooled by the fancy decor. I ordered the surf and turf - which was terrible. The shrimp/pineapple dish was mediocre, but over-priced/small. The drinks were pretty good.
This place was amazing! Had the lamb chops and my girl had the lasagne - both excellent!
Not cheap but worth every penny. Shrimp and grits: the best. Duck spring rolls: amazing. Brunch margarita was way better than the mimosa..
Best Indian food in the city! Lunch buffet is amazing, but I always order palak paneer and gobi manchurian gravy for dinner. P.S. You can bring your own wine if you want!

This is my favorite Mediterranean restaurant in the middle Tennessee area. Great food. Quick, professional service. This place runs like a well-oiled machine. Nothing fancy. Just a great place for lunch. I usually just order the gyro plate or chicken gyro plate.

Really remarkably good food here. That goes for breakfast/brunch as well as lunch. Some of my favorites are the 'chickichanga', chicken salad sandwich, the turkey burger, the quinoa bowls, and the butternut squash bisque (seasonal). The potatoes are not spectacular, but they are fine. I usually try to sub the soup of the day - which is always terrific. Great service, as well.

Over here on my lunch break. I ordered the club wrap and it's quite good. I'm looking forward to trying some of the other wraps! There are several interesting items on the menu - including some relatively healthy options.

Bellinis.
Grits.
Free muffins and biscuits with marmalade. 
Totally amazing service and environment - especially when the weather is nice and the bar area is opened up! Pretty much the best brunch ever and totally reasonable prices. Jeah!

Cashew cheese dip. Never heard of that before tonight, but I gotta say it's delicious. Order that app. The entrees were good, too, and very healthy, I'm sure. That cashew cheese kinda blew my mind, though.

Best tortilla soup ever!
All the food is great. Fish Tacos, Chicken Tacos, Elote (corn). Sweet Plantains.  I still haven't made it for tamales on Wednesday yet. Love the atmosphere and service. Now there's a bar, too!

I was a huge fan of the chef's previous restaurant, so it's really no surprise that this place is great! I'm saying it's the best Indian food in town and the best vegetarian food in town. We are enjoying the lunch buffet and noticing the fresh decor and great patio seating.
Let the haters hate. I'm over here drinking Long Island Iced teas for $1 each and smashing this sirloin stir fry. How many you think before they stop serving us?

Fantastic. Everything. I'm usually there for the Pho, but the sushi, appetizers, everything is just better than anywhere else close by. It's also the little things. Even the hot sake is better than whatever other run-of-the-mill place you might order something like that. Great service, too.

Fantastic food. Great service. Enjoyed some mimosas with brunch in a cool, re-decorated building in a great neighborhood. The line looked a little long when we walked in (11am on Saturday), but it was very well managed and we were eating pretty quickly. Can't wait to return!

I'm really excited about this place. Convenient to my home and basically a prefect neighborhood bar with FANTASTIC food (I had some tomato basil soup and chicken pot pie on my first trip and I'll be trying some other items very soon). The draft beer list is cool, too, with some local favorites. Great service, lighting, all that.

This is the best Ramen restaurant in Nashville. It's run by great, creative people who care a great deal about what they do. My brother said it's his favorite restaurant in town, period. Great environment, food, and craft cocktails. Thanks to them for being one of the restaurants that make this city great!

Just ordered some take-out. WHOAH! This is just what I needed. I'm talking about this food turned my whole day around. Split some plates with my girl so we could try two meats and bunch of sides and EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS FIRE!

FTaNwFkvoHOX8DkGya7NKQ.review_text: Delicious and affordable Indian spot in strip mall just across the dumbarton bridge. It's worth the toll fees. Found my new to go Indian spot

I was in the area to eat Vietnamese nearby. I saw this place at the far end of the strip mall and after a quick search realized they serve Somali food. I like to consider my palate well travelled, but this was my first ever opportunity to dine at a Somali restaurant. It's definitely a hole in the wall, I was the only non Somali in the place, but everyone was super welcoming. The food is a bit like North African meets Ethiopian/Indian. The rice was excellent with strong cardomom notes. I had the chicken steak and it was well flavored. The green sauce they'll serve with the food is HOT and I love spicy food. The white is your classic yogurt sauce. 

Note the special breads are only served for breakfast along with the stews. Dinner you'll be choosing from fish, chicken or goat to go with rice. 

I'll be back to try some of the other items along with their version of Ethiopian injera bread.

10/10 just be aware it's a total hole in the wall dive.

Authentic Pho spot here in NASH. Coming from CA it's nice to get an authentic bowl is unpretentious digs. Too many restaurants plaster on a hipster veneer with branding to make it appeal more to the masses. I like an authentic viet restaurant when I see one and this is it.

I just moved here from CA and this place is better than most Mexican spots back west. Cali burrito with machaca meat is my go to special request. Highly endorse this place as someone who has spent time around legit Mexican taquerias on the West Coast. 10/10

This place has legit Pollo a la Brasa. As a DC native who grew up with a large local Peruvian population I know good Peruvian chicken when I taste it. This place is just a rung below the best spots in the DC area. Considering this is Nashville I'm thrilled i can get my Peruvian cravings fixed when I need them. Will 100% be back to try the Lomo Saltado next

Solid, but i dont get all the hype. This spot reminds me a little of Philppe's french dip in LA. Massive hype bc its been around forever, but ultimately just decent. I wouldn't wait in line for it, but if you can walk up and get a cheesesteak in 5 min its a pretty good one.

So wandered in here on a random Tuesday. I wasnt expecting too much, but god damn are the banh mi good. HUGE sandwich, and really cheap. They put it on a class cheesesteak roll which is a little different from the french bread im used to, but it works. Great flavors, efficient service, and dirt cheap prices make this a must try if downtown

Our go to local spot since moving into the neighborhood a few mos back. Large beer selection, friendly staff, and a nice mix of everything from burgers to mussels. Chicken sandwich is a favorite of my girlfriend. I like the mussels.
Love my hole in the wall chinese spots. This isn't gourmet eating, but its good chinese for cheap. My go to spot for to go chinese in grad hospital

Spicy pork here is outstanding. Owner is Korean so naming is changed to hibachi on the menu. If you like korean bulgogi and KFC (the better version - korean fried chicken) then you need to try this spot. Lived in CA for half a decade and the korean here is on par with good Korean spots from the Bay and LA. Get your korean fix here. Star is the spicy pork and the KFC
Love this place -- hidden gem in N.Nash. Everyone there is super friendly and the strawberry wings are awesome and unlike anything else. Must try if you love wings:)

This place is a hidden gem and the best new food I've tried in Philly in 2021! Seriously, if you don't try it you're making a terrible life choice. This is amongst THE best tasting food you'll come across, period.

For those not familiar, Afghan kebabs are like Persian, Turkish, or Greek kebabs on crack. The flavor profile blows all of them outta the water. Get the chicken and thank me later. The meat is also way more tender than other types of kebabs bc of the marinade they use. 

Couple it with the accompanying mildly spicy green sauce and the amazing garlic yogurt sauce and you will find yourself in heaven.

I'm fortunate to have lived all over and the flavors here rival those of the very best Afghan kebabs I've had in the Bay Area. 10/10 you don't love yourself and your tastebuds if this spot doesn't join the monthly food rotation.

The guy running it does everything, so cut him some slack as he shuttles between the kitchen and service. It's a little hidden, tucked in nextdoor to a new Chinese spot so keep your eyes open. Brand new spot so leave this guy reviews so we can keep enjoying this new gem

This place is worth any diabetes I may encounter in another 40 yrs. Who knew the shitty poptarts in the foil drew their inspiration from places like this.  I say prayers for the cherry poptarts before I stroll over their way, and know it'll be a good sugar powered day when they have them. I'd eat here more often but I'm trying to drag out what insulin producing capacity I have left so I can enjoy these for another decade.

Love this spot in Devil's Pocket. The food here is consistently excellent and I think I speak for all of us in this little corner south of South St in saying we're grateful to have such a great local restaurant. For anyone that loves Thai this is worth the trip to our little off the beaten path corner of the city. 

Staff is always super kind, and the food itself is great quality.

Best Pizza this side of New Haven. Rest of the menu is also excellent, but pizza is the star. Slightly chewy and charred crusts, just like Frank Pepe's up in New Haven have my heart as the best pizza around, and Sally can hang with the best. Patio is adorable and staff is always excellent.

Bomb -- I'm a Bay Area transplant and these sandwiches/Banh Mi can hang with the best spots in San Jose. Get here and eat, sh*t is delicious.

10*

FnQvnUkRopiaz9lcmz0Jew.review_text: Octopus was everything it was cracked up to be, as was the almond jalapeño pesto.  Portions are small and felt a bit rushed by bus-boy staff but happy belly nonetheless. No kids menu, but they will do pasta w red or butter sauce on request.

Not only did this cake totally hit the mark for our coffee aficionado's birthday, it also hit the mark for moist chocolate butteriness and smooth and not overly sweet frosting. Totally custom based on ideas I threw at them. Thank you BoB!

Meh, had a lot of high hopes for this to be our go to place for bbq and ramen. Ramen was underwhelming. Broth not hot enough, and while noodles and charshu were great the absence of the umami mouth feel made it feel like a glorified miso soup. Chicken katsu side dish was big and plentiful, but would suggest they cut out the fatty pieces from the chicken thigh. Wasabi shumai for $5.25 was the biggest rip -- same tiny shumai you can get from the Chinese grocery.  

For the prices (over $12 per bowl) we were very disappointed. Compared to Hawaii or NYC or NJ this won't, unfortunately be our go to place.

Stopped in for a cup of coffee the other day and was so surprised at what I found! Open, modern, cozy transformation of a former Train Store that serves all natural food. So today I brought in my husband. All natural does not mean zero taste, bland, cardboard btw--giant pop of flavors!  See my pic of a hearty açaí bowl, - giant portion with super sweet berries, complimented by a date/pistachio granola that is above and beyond any old bagged stuff. Coffee is Vermont-sourced and will be my go to on the way to the office (low acid super robust) from here on... give this place a try -- we tried it for breakfast but will be here for lunch/dinner (yes they serve meat!!)

Came totally excited to try the much acclaimed warm Dutch Apple dumpling, baseball sized, carmel covered yummy ness. Multiple forks in hand, we quickly sat to dig in. First, it was not warmed. Nor crispy. But the pie dough like outer crust was still moderately tasty. But upon digging in to find (or try to find) the inner appley goodness was a disappointment. Inside was a round glob of uncooked dough, nary an apple in sight. We poked and prodded, then threw the $4 mess away. 

It may have won awards years ago but I wouldn't recommend it, at all.
This place has gone downhill. Used to be a fan favorite for weekend eats, before the merger, but have tried it twice and have had stomach aches after eating the poke and signature rolls.
Food is better in person than take out. Loved the soup dumplings! Was it a fan of the won ton which had a lot of seaweed flavor to it. A+ on the dry fried pork and Dan Dan noodles!

I love the way that this Mexican taqueria treats me like family every single time I walk through the door. My favorite thing to eat is the steak fajitas with my daughter. My husband always gets the burrito and eats all of it. I love how all the proportions are perfect and they never mess up our orders.
Get the chicken. Falafel is probably healthier coz it's not fried but it is dry and hard as a rock. Nafnaf beats them on this. Otherwise good flavor on the hummus and salad.

Pleasantly surprised at the healthfulness and quick service offered by the cafe. I got the Baja bowl and while it looked simple, packed great flavor in the right proportions with chicken, guac, beans, rice, cheese and a bed of salad. Comes w a side of your Choice Very nice young man suggested the "add on" smoothie for $3ish and I'm glad I did it. The detox green was refreshing and not too heavy or sweet. Only deducted 1 star because of the guac was a little too salty. Will be back!

Decided to do takeout and try a new place- it was Awesome! I had the chicken shawarma platter with hummus, swapped rice for vegetables, and an extra mini Tzatsiki and pistachio baklava. Chicken was flavorful and tender, veg came dressed in a nice sauce, and the combo of spreading a little hummus, tahini, tzatsiki and hot sauce before layering my bite of chicken into the side pita bread was to die for! Baklava came with 3 pieces - super fresh, buttery and crisp. Will totally be back for more. So glad you guys opened!

Pickup lunch was a Stockbroker and the famous Chicago dog. Did not disappoint! Packed neatly and served with fries, it was a perfect diversion from stay-at-home meal making. Toppings were spot on in flavor and balance, piled high. Bun held up so nicely, no soggy wet bread here! Sorry to say I ate mine so fast no pics to share. One point of feedback I'll have to remember for take out next time - get the mustard on the side. The decorative topping made for a bit more napkin use than I'd expected!

... this year was a teenager cake (1st cake) covered in ribbon stripes with hearts. BOB never disappoints. Absolutely loved the chocolate cake with mocha buttercream covered in fondant. Thank you bakers for matching our inspiration pic

If you're in doubt but have an idea - run it by BOB and they'll make it happen!

(Ps- cake topper I made myself).

Soup dumplings, Scallion pancake, Dan Dan noodles, three cup chicken are our favorites. Have had the whole fish (pricey but good) and the green bean entree is amazing. Friendly waitstaff and quick service. Could take or leave the dry pepper chicken, a little too breaded for my taste...
Hard to park/pull over spot but pizza was well done. Nice to have a spot close to home. Iffy on delivery, so try for pickups instead if you want it fasty

GMXl9-YviSIFq7VS-NmSOw.review_text: This is a nice place. However the owner is much less than friendly which is why I choose not to patronize it. He was very rude to me pretty much laughing at me when I asked if he had any specials for people who golden tee there all the time. I don't patronize places where an owner would act this way towards a customer. And a former somewhat regular customer I might add. I would also point out that I have played golden tee there before without a waitress so much as give me a glance. So I won't be going back.

I usually don't write reviews on here. And most people that do are uninformed people who don't really know much in my opinion. I have seen some mixed reviews about this place. I also think you need to try a restuarant more than once to give it more of a chance and try their food again before trashing it on yelp. I had a good experience and the food was pretty good. The waiter and all the staff were very attentive and friendly. Anyone on here who has a negative review about this place, I would try it again and see if you have the same experience. I also usually don't complain about prices. If you don't like it then go somewhere else. Restaurants are getting more and more pricy these days so deal with us or cook at home. Overall I had a very good experience at this place. i don't have the income to visit here very often as I won a gift certificate at work. But if I did I would visit here more often.

The service and food were excellent. We had the sea bass and Laredo queso. The sea bass was charred to perfection. Great drinks as well. It was kind of funny that one of the specials of the day was already on the menu which confused us. But we will be back and soon.

I cant say there is nothing this place couldn't do to be better. But the food and service here are always great. And who is ever perfect? The mustard basil shrimp is especially good. Everything here is really fresh and very delicious. Not sure what some of the below posters were eating. They obviously were not eating at Gerard's. This place doesn't cost any more than any other fine dining establishment in St, Louis either. So not sure what those complaints are about. And you supporting a local establishment. And for the record, I have no interest in this restaurant. I just really like it, and I think you will too if you try it. The owner is really nice and very knowledgeable about food and wine as well. The waiter even pointed us to a less expensive bottle of wine rather than a pricey one. I am not rich at all but I try to come here a few times a year for some great food and wine. So that says something.

Very good food but wear your parka even in the summer. Make sure you have a sweatshirt or more at all times of the year. It is an ice box in there at all times. Caddilac fajitas are awesome and feeds four.

The food here was excellent. However the waitress didn't know what kind of oysters they serve. But the service was great. And I cut my hand on the crab legs and they didn't have band aids. What restaurant serves crab legs with a lot of pointy edges to cut yourself on and doesn't have band aids? and what restaurant doesn't have a first aid kit for employees. I am from Missouri and it's a state law there. But I guess not in Florida. If the owner or manager of this place reads this I suggest getting a first aid kit as I can't be the first person to cut themselves on crab legs. I realize I am clumsy and cut myself often on crab legs. But this is the first place that didn't have a band aid for me. And I am certainly not the first one to do that.

The food here is really good and the pint and a slice is a really good deal. But felix's used to be a solid 1:30 bar to cater to the later crowd. Obviously it no longer caters to that crowd. They close at 11 on weekdays and if you go in there past 10 o'clock, they will be spreading cleaning solution all over the floor that you can breathe in while you are enjoying your slice of pizza. That unfortunately does not appeal to me. And if you get there past 10:30 they are very quick to get you out of there. And don't expect to get good service past 10pm either. They are too worried about closing up. I guess this is their business model now. But they definitely are losing out on a lot of profits not being open later and very aggressive in getting people out of there sometimes well before 11. So it is a great place to eat and drink. Just don't go there past 10pm like you used to be able to do for many years.

All those good review about the wings and they changed them to a sweet glaze? I didn't know this before I ordered them. If you're into a sweet glaze then you'll like them. And they're still cooked perfectly. But no thanks to a sweet glaze for my wings. The old wings were awesome. Menu online still says trashed with buffalo sauce and jalopeno ranch fyi. People might be surprised when they order these. Might want to change that. Not sure why the change either when people all over here were raving about them. Any to the other reviewer who called Felix's a sports bar. That is not correct. If you don't play the sound of at least the local games you are not a sports bar. Sports bars don't close at 11 on weekdays, nor close on Monday for the monday night football crowd. Again Felix's has great pizza and food (but dissapointed me with the new wings), just don't go there past 10pm on a weekday or 11 or so on a weekends and it's a good place. And it's not a sports bar. It's a pizza pub as it says on the door. And the owner does give a lot back to the community. I love that.

I had been to Main Street a few times and always wanted to walk in here. So we did yesterday. Right from the start the owners were welcoming and said thanks for coming in. They obviously take a lot of pride in their food and their establishment. It was 65 degrees on Jan 27th on Main Street so of course it was crowded. But I don't doubt this place is always crowded. The salsa might be the best I have ever had. We had the fajitas tia I think it was called with chicken shrimp chorizo bacon and steak. Be warned we got the small portion and it easily would feed four people. I can't even imagine how big the large portion is. It was up there as some of the best fajitas I have ever had. It came with a side of lettuce guacamole pick de gallo source cream and lettuce. And a generous portion. Had tomatoes onions and bell peppers mixed in. It was awesome. The service was great and you can tell the owners have a passion for the place. And they both work up front working their butts off just like everyone else working there. We live pretty far away from Main Street so may not be back soon. But next time we go to Main Street that will be our stop no doubt.

If you live anywhere near the post and you go to Buffalo Wild Wings or anywhere else to watch sports at a bar, what is wrong with you? Hands down the best sports bar in St. Louis. You can't watch march madness anywhere else. They are always on top of the tv situation and all spots. It's how a sports bar should be run. The service is also always great. The spicy garlic wings are awesome. And you can get them bakes so they're a little more healthy. I think overall the food could be a bit better. Hence the four instead of five stars. But for bar food I think it's very good. Until I open my spot which I hope to do at some point in my life, this is the best sports bar in St. Louis. And you are supporting a local business and not a corporation. Please dine local always!
This place is great. Awesome food and atmosphere. The staff is always friendly and attentive. Simply one of the best bars in St. Louis.

Went there Sunday for lunch. As soon as we walked in the door we were greeted by the chef who could have been the owner. Sorry I didn't ask and I should have. But he said welcome to Krab Kingz and immediately let us know about the menu. We got the #2 with crab shrimp, sausage potatoes and corn. It was extremely delicious and obviously fresh. We tried the Cajun, lemon, and spicy butters. They all were fantastic. Our waiter Eddie was awesome and super friendly. All the employees there were super friendly and made you feel welcome. Which is super important. We will definitely be back here and bring some friends and or family next time! And you are eating local instead of going to chain. Wherever you decide to eat next make sure you are supporting a local family not a chain like this one!

Went here last week. We split the ribeye and had the twice baked potato. The steak came pre sliced which was different but I though was nice. It was a fantastic steak cooked to a perfect medium rare. The bartender was really nice and friendly but not overbearing. Someone who I think was the manager also came by and asked us how our meal was. I made sure to let him the steak was fantastic. One of the better steaks I have had in the area. And $40 for a 20 ounce 24 day aged prime steak and a side is not a bad deal. A lot of the other steakhouses serve you a $60 plus steak a la cart. I want to come back here and try some of the other food. I would have to come here again but it seems like it is ran very well. You definitely should check it out.

This place is fantastic. Might be my favorite steak in town. Make sure and add the lobster tail and split the meal for a great date night. Splitting food is a great option. Not too many people can eat a 20 ounce steak by themself. The mushroom risotto is fantastic. Everything on this menu is awesome and the service is great. And $54 for a prime steak with two sides is a pretty good deal that for that good of a steak.

I went here on Saturday night. As mentioned before it's a small place. But very nice and I loved the decor. The waitress was awesome and very attentive. Most of their herbs and vegetables are grown in a greenhouse out back. So that was very cool. And most if not all of the ingredients were local. So it's not the cheapest place but it's kind of what I expected. i got the dry aged ribeye for $62 which comes with a side. Now it was $3 extra for a butter. But they do have their own sauce complimentary. I had the garlic butter and it was fantastic. The steak was 35 day dry aged and the best steak I have had in St. Louis no question. It just melted in my mouth. A 22 ounce dry aged ribeye at other high end steak houses is more than $62 and does not come with a side fyi for any one complaining about that. And for the best steak in town I would say worth it. My dinner companion had the dry aged bone in strip and it was also great. We had garlic mashed potatoes and asparagus with bernaise sauce for the sides and they were fantastic. The smoked salt that they light on fire was pretty cool too. So it's a higher end place to go to but very good. It's small but you know what you're getting into when you go there. The bar is very small so if you want a seat there just get there early. I want to go back and try some salads and more of their delicious food.

Gcxm0XlnMIW0sUwiYgo4dA.review_text: Great great French fries... So thin and delicious. Loved the aioli. Good Cheesesteak and decent burgers.

Went here for Valentine's day. Very crowded but our reservation was on time and server was good. Grilled seafood app was the highlight of the meal. Grilled scallops, calamari, shrimp and cherry tomatoes over arugula perfectly dressed. 5 stars.
Had filet and pescatore for entree. Filet was good but not amazing- 3 stars. Pescatore was delicious- 5 stars. Lobster slightly dry, but  calamari and scallops and garlic white wine sauce were more than enough.
Dessert was a hit and a miss. Chocolate souffle and vanilla ice cream great- warm and chocolatey and gooey. Chocolate peanut butter cake was dry and cold and seemed like it was bought from a grocery store.
Overall nice dinner for two.

Haven't eaten here yet, but love the bar and atmosphere. Quite excellent beer selection and the nitro option is always a nice surprise. Bartenders friendly and you can usually find a spot and see a TV.
Love their pizza. Ordered takeout and eaten here once. Good crust. Great ratio sauce and cheese. Had both plain cheese and pepperoni.

Ordered and ate at restaurant on a Friday- big mistake. Crowded and extremely slow. BUT pizza was amazing (or we just famished...). Really dirtied the pizza up with toppings. Got the cheeseburger one. But thick filling pizza and a lot of toppings. Definitely will go back but order delivery and at a different time.

Not embarrassed to give this 5 stars. This is our go to to order a cheap, quick, delicious meal. Ordering online for 20 min delivery at 50% off can't be beat and yes I love the garlic sauce. Tried most pizzas- pepperoni, pepper and onions, bbq chicken, buffalo chicken, plain. All delish.

Solid sushi dinner. Great service- friendly and quick. Spicy tuna roll, shrimp tempura roll, island roll (salmon and mango) and dragon roll- all good quality and fresh. Also had fried banana dessert. Could have used a little more honey and a touch of salt, but pretty good.
Would definitely come back.

Review is only for sitting at the bar during sporting events.  Great TVs, lots of seating.
Attentive service, cheap beers/pitchers, again great TVs so get the four stars.
Food is just ok- taste and price.

Service is slow and horrendous and agonizing,,,
but the BAGELS ARE AMAZING!  So awesome, worth the frustration and wait.
Love the bagels- chewy, fresh, tasty, so good.
Cream cheese is also great.

Had a lot of varieties and breakfast sandwiches.  Can't go wrong.
Will update when I've tried lunch here.

Only use cards over $5.

Dinner outside for two. Really, really nice atmosphere.

Server seemed a little uninterested.  Recommendations weren't great.  Food ok.
Will give it another shot though bc we live in town.

Super fancy and you're going to pay for what you get.
Staff is so friendly though and throw samples at you.
Fun to look at browse.

shrimp cocktail was actually worth it.  horseradish cocktail sauce was amazing.  bread was amazing.  filet was amazing.  wine was amazing.  service was slightly over the top but great vibe. Brought out a small slice of chocolate cake for me.

Loved, loved, loved.

Server was great, very friendly.  It was a busy night for them too.

Mussel app was incredible!  Really, really good and enjoyed the broth tremendously.
Duck breast entree was overcooked and ruined.  Artic Char was just ok, did like the orange in the couscous.  Mussel, shrimp, seafood entree again just ok.  Same with steak frites.  Best part of the meal was the apps.

Great great atmosphere, food and service. The warm Cuban bread is amazing and the empanada app was delicious. Paella didn't disappoint.

The dining room is gorgeous and all the history was really fun. Would love to go back for lunch.

Ate dinner, breakfast and lunch here. Food was solid. Spicy Burger with blue cheese was really, really good. Loved the chocolate thunder cake and the key lime drink. Also loved the bloody mary- just the right amount of spice. Service was definitely not quick, but very friendly.

Outdoor dining on the water can't be beat. Live music was great. And amazing spot to watch the sunset and spot some dolphins.

Such a cool little spot. Very authentic Greek cuisine. Service was awesome- very friendly and informative but not too much. We did the sampler dips. The feta red pepper one was amazing! As were the other five. We then also split the mixed grill entrée. The lamb melted in your mouth. Chicken kabob was great. The hot sausage is hot but loved it. We didn't get dessert BC we were catching a movie, but we'll definitely be back. Also recommend making a reservation.

GdFOEbcrJcoV11nP4ObzKg.review_text: Great service and food :) Bartender was awesome and they service Sun King beer. Which is always the best part!
The server promptly took our order and brought us out our meals. Then my sister found a hair in her pulled pork. I don't mess with food that has hair in it.

My boyfriend and I enjoyed the 2 for $40 during Devour Downtown. The entree portion was sort of small, only draw back. This was our first time at Iaria's, the staff was nice and was very informative with the menu. Great for a date night or family night out.

The setting was small and intimate, which was exactly what my boyfriend and I were looking for. We visited during the winter time, but the deck looked big so summers there would be great! 

My boyfriend Nic had the Farm burger and mac and cheese. He enjoyed both, but the burger was a little on the messy side. 

I enjoyed a original burger and fries. I LOVED the burger so much, cooked to perfection. 

Our server was great and attended to us several times. During our visit there was live music, which was pretty loud.

First off our waiter, Thomas was great! He was full of humor and class :) It's always great to have a good laugh at dinner. Our waiter attended to all of our needs! A+ dude!

We used a free coupon for a small alfredo pasta. It was good and the serving size was perfect for my boyfriend and I. The garlic bread was so-so, not much flavor. I suggest using olive oil with it. Thomas asked us if we wanted some so of course we said yes! 

The atmosphere was great. We went at 4:30 so it was rather quiet.

I've been to Bru Burger several times in the last few years and every time it gets better.

Great beer selection, they do serve sun king :) Burgers are all different and unique- yummy too! I've enjoyed the patty melt and garlic burger. Warning- the garlic burger has a lot of garlic to it, but still good to my taste buds. 

During the warmer months try to sit outside, it's lovely :)

I've been here for a night out and lunch.

The night out atmosphere was loud and more "club" like than a lounge. The drinks were okay, I've had better. The sushi was okay also.

The lunch deal is average, the amt of food you receive is enough.

I enjoyed a tenderloin :) It was delicious with onions and mayo. We were able to get seated right away. Our server was very helpful. We had a groupon and she assisted us with that. 

Also the coleslaw is awesome :)

All around a wonderful experience!  We had 2 toddlers with us and we greeted with open arms. They made sure the table was ready with high chairs before they brought us back. Our waitress was great, she brought out the kids food before our food. Which was the greatest ever! 

Food was amazing! My sister had a club sandwich- she isn't a big lunch meat fan, but was pleasantly surprised. I had the patty melt, the caramelized onions were the perfect touch! 

The manager who came around to ask how our meal was, was great- so nice!

I give Edwards a 5 star. 

I've been going to Edwards since I was little. It's always been great. Recently I went back with my sister (first time in a few years) and a toddler. 

Our service was great. All employees were very friendly and helpful consisting our loud, whiney dinner date. 

Onions ring are always the best! The hot dog and corn dogs are great as well! 

Edwards is an overall wonderful diner!

My boyfriend and I ate here on a friday evening at the bar.The hostess was super helpful to make sure the bar was available. When seated at the bar, our order was taken right away. 
**They have local craft beer which is a huge plus for me :)** 

My boyfriend order a chicken sandwich which was- okay. He said it needed something else. I agreed because my parmesan hamburger needed a kick to it too. Both were delicious and filling, the fries were good too. 

Great service can take a business a long way!

My boyfriend and I have been to Cheddars twice since opening. On both occasions the food and service were excellent. The only downfall of the restaurant is the wait time. We live pretty close and drive by a lot. There are always tons of cars in the parking lot, so we haven't figured out the best/ slow day to go yet.
Hands down, the best Mexican restaurant on the south side. The service and food is always great! Their guacamole is the best I've ever had. Also the restaurant itself is well kept!

I myself has been here once already before my boyfriend and I dined a fee months ago. We sat at the bar, bartender was awesome and very informative. My boyfriend is not too familiar with craft beers but the bartender gave us the 441! Their burgers are the best and their Mac & cheese  is delightful!

This city BBQ is great! They service Sun King beer and you also get a Sun King glass you get to take home with you! So cool! The prices were a little high, but we are talking about pork here. Fast service and also good desserts :)

My sister and dined at High Velocity before the Indian's game last night. Even though there were 3 other major events going on that night, the service was quite speedy. 

We sat at the bar and all of the bartenders were friendly and helpful. I enjoyed seeing them work together to please their guests at the bar. 

My sister ordered the cheese fries and I ordered the cheeseburgers. Both had large portions and were filling. My sister commented that the fries had a little TOO much cheese on them but the other toppings were sufficient. The cheeseburgers were nothing special- could have offered a special sauce to go on top. They honestly tasted like the soy burgers you were fed in Elementary school and were very dry. The fries on the other hand were great!

Other all our experience was pleasant and the managers made sure we were happy. I believe when a manager takes time to come around a greet you and ask how your meal is going make the experience worth while.

We enjoyed Between the Bun on Halloween this year. Costume contest was being held and festive cake pops were given out. These special touches made our experience a fun one.

First off they served local beer, which is always a plus for me! For dinner we had the Mac Daddy burger and the Italian Stallion burger. Both were cooked medium and were perfect. The Mac daddy is definitely a Mac and cheese lovers dream. I suggest subbing the ranch on the burger for BBQ sauce!  The Italian stallion is pizza on a burger, my boyfriend thoroughly enjoyed it! The buns on both burgers were nicely toasted also- great touch! 

Service was swell, server informed us of her favorite. This helped us narrow down our decision- there were a lot of delicious burgers to choose from! 

Overall this place gets 5+ stars!

I eat here all the time! 

They are typically busy and you may have to wait a few minutes for seat. Especially after church on Sunday, be prepared to wait! 

Friendly and helpful staff makes the experience a great one. 

Breakfast and lunch are both equally as yummy. I personally enjoy the of the skillets and the patty melt.

Always helpful staff on hand to answer most of your health questions. 

They carry essential oils and diffusers. (the reason for the first visit over a year ago) Now I shop there for anything from frozen foods to body lotions. 

Overall I am always satisfied with my visit to this health food store.

My boyfriend and I ordered carry out on a Thursday night. Ordering over the phone was simple and fast. 25-30 wait, which is typically for a Japanese restaurant. 

The lady at the front desk was nice and helpful, my soup and salad was ready when I got there. The lady explained that my chicken and rice would be out in a minute. I waited maybe 3 or 4 minutes. (Fresh of the grill- warm dinner so I didn't mind) 

The atmosphere was electric- literally! Loved the lights on the ceiling. Can't wait to try a dine- in experience.

The takeout portion of soup was rather large in my opinion- not a bad thing! Also the hibachi was a decent size and was cooked to my tastebuds perfection. Spring rolls and crab rangoon were a tasty appetizer as well. 

Overall, a great experience! Can't wait until next time!

I just want to say the staff here is FANTASTIC!! I usually do my grocery shopping early in the morning, anywhere between 6-7:30 am. All the workers greet me with a smile and say good morning! Truly makes my day! 

I am also impressed with the Clicklist feature. (Online grocery order, workers put groceries into your car) The service is great for my boyfriend and I if we are super busy that week and don't feel like wasting time in the grocery store. I can only imagine how beneficial it could be for a parent of young children. $5 charge for this service, which I think is reasonable if you are buying $150-200 worth of groceries. 

On the other hand, I give this Kroger 4 stars due to the outside cart areas being jammed packed. Not so much early in the mornings, but if I stop by after work I usually can't even fit my cart into the covered area.

I've been here for lunch in the past. Enjoyed the Milktooth double burger, which was amazing! Also their Bloody Mary was refreshing as well, but not as spicy as I would have liked. 

I gave this grand restaurant a 4 star because of... This morning I arrived at 7:45, knowing that they opened at 7am.
