To my surprise the first employee I saw explained that they only serve pastries, coffee and tea until 9am. As far as I know this is not mentioned anywhere on their website or FB page. While eating my pastry, I witnessed 20+ people walk out of the restaurant due to the kitchen not being open yet. None of this would be a problem if it were advertised as so. It definitely left a sour taste in my mouth. 

I did however enjoy my pecan roll. It was baked perfectly- not too soft and not too tough. The caramel syrup was also light and delicious.

Gy1UDGNUZLuZJAVBArjWnw.review_text:
I've gone here a handful of times over the past few years and I've been pleased with the food (the Spicy Basil with Chicken is my usual). But my most recent visit has convinced me never to go there again.

I went with a group of five friends. It was around 6 p.m. but they were by no means slammed during dinner. We waited over an hour for our food. Two of my friends ordered the same dish, but the kitchen only made one and so we had to wait for a second one to be made, which extended our wait even more. Our waitress was attentive with bringing water while we waited for our food, but she disappeared after the food came. No water refills, no rice refills, nothing. I ultimately ended up complaining and they gave us a 10% discount, but I don't think I'd go here again. Any one of those errors might be excusable, but all of them combined just made for a terrible dining experience.

My favorite restaurant in town. The food is unique and flavorful and delicious. Great for two people or a larger group. Get the combination platter to try different things. Bring your own wine!

Cons: Service is sometimes slow, don't accept reservations, little parking. But it's SO worth it.

I like this place. I've never had Pinkberry before but I do like the tart yogurts here. On top of that, the customer service is quite good. They were practically out of kiwi when I got there near closing one night, but the lady behind the counter cut up a fresh one for me. I've been going at least once every couple of weeks.

I'm pretty new to Peruvian food, but I'm definitely sold on this place. I had the lomo saltado (not entirely adventurous, I know) and it was delicious. Flavorful and a generous helping. The only other Peruvian place I've been to is Inca's and while theirs is good, the portions are considerably smaller. The main drawback to Don Pedro's is that it's so far away from central city, but I'll definitely be looking for excuses to come back.

Reilly is easily in my top three favorite restaurants in town. I was hooked from my first visit. This restaurant is dangerous because you want to keep ordering food regardless of whether it's a good idea or not -- everything is THAT good. This is my go-to place to bring out-of-town guests and all of them have been impressed by it. the pizza snobs have been particularly impressed by the crust. I also love the mix of old and modern in the decor. The former funeral parlor aspect adds a fun twist. I love coming here and I can't wait for them to open the beer garden!

Favorite salad: Apple + walnut brittle + gorgonzola
Favorite pizza: Yukon gold + pecorino
Favorite pasta: Papardelle (braised short rib + mushroom)
Favorite dessert: Tiramisu in a jar
Favorite cocktail: Gentleman's G+T

My favorite bar in Tucson, without a doubt. Ordinarily a place like this would get points off for being small, dark, and sometimes noisy (especially when UA's in session) but the quality of the drinks overrides all. I've stopped ordering off the menu and just ask for custom drinks from the bartender (although I tried a boba drink that's currently on the menu and it's definitely worth getting again). I wish I knew this particular bartender's name, but he's always made me delicious, interesting drinks and always has interesting tidbits to add to your conversation (he openly admits eavesdropping on everyone, because how can he not?)  Bonus points: He weighed in on our conversation about whether DS9 or TNG is the better Trek series. 

Love this place and I always look forward to trying something new here.

I desperately wish there was a location on the north side of town. This is my favorite Mongolian bbq joint in town. There aren't many options, but there are a few things that set C.I. Chu's apart:

1) Bigger bowls. Everyone knows that creating a super stack is part of the fun of Mongolian bbq, but there are some places that have microscopic-sized bowls, making it more of a necessity than a fun challenge. Here, you get a hefty-sized bowl that lets you stuff yourself to your heart's delight.

2) Base ingredients for your sauce. I've been to others where you choose from pre-made sauce mixes and it's not the same. I haven't gone wrong with the sauce recipes at C.I. Chu's and I can adjust as needed... more of this, less of that. There's less mystery about what exactly is going into your stir fry.

Tip: Grab your meat FIRST before the veggies to make sure you get a solid amount. It's near the end of the line and if you load up on other stuff beforehand, you'll only end up balancing a few slivers of meat atop your overflowing pile. Meat first, then go back to the beginning for veggies to make for a more balanced mix.

I love the concept of Mongolian bbq, and while this does the trick as far as being conveniently located, I've had better. Genghis Grill sort of feels like the Applebee's of Mongolian bbq. There are options for making bowls of other styles such as Mexican, Cajun, etc., so I imagine there's a little something for everyone. I come here looking for Asian stir fry, so I ignore that aspect of it. There may be potential for some fun fusion for the creative types.

PROS:
1) Lots of ingredient options, including marinated meats and a wide variety of starches.
2) You can always take leftovers home... you're not limited to what you can eat in the restaurant, unlike some other Mongolian places.
3) Full bar.

CONS:
1) REALLY small bowls... smaller than any other Mongolian bbq place I've been to. Ridiculously small. Piling isn't just a game, it's a necessary to get your money's worth.
2) Terrible buffet area. For one, it's often dirty with ingredients on the floor and the ledge in front of you. Secondly, it runs three deep, such that if I want to get something that's in the back I have to stick my head pretty far under the sneeze guard to reach it. Admittedly I'm short and have short arms, but my friend who's more of a normal-sized person had trouble reaching things in the far back too.
3) Mystery sauces. I'd rather have the raw ingredients instead of trying to figure out what "Dragon Sauce" and "Khanzu" are. They've added tasting spoons since they've opened, but I often have to sample a lot of them to figure out what I want and it's pretty inconvenient.

Not my first choice for Mongolian bbq, but proximity sometimes wins over quality, and that's the main reason I come here.

For lovers of the original Zemam's, there is one major reason to try Zemam's Too at least once: You can choose the Gored Gored as part of the sampler platter. I'd always been curious about it, but I just couldn't abandon my beloved sampler platter. It's so good. Anything on the menu is fair game for the sampler, including some fish and lamb options, which you won't find at the OG Zemam's.

For the uninitiated, Zemam's Too is a great restaurant for people who 1) love bold flavors and spice, 2) are open to an interesting non-Western dining experience, and 3) aren't too fussy about ambiance or getting their hands dirty. Like its predecessor, Zemam's Too is now in the top tier of my favorite restaurants in Tucson. I prefer these restaurants over Cafe Desta--the Zemam's dishes really hit you with flavor like a truck, which I absolutely love.

I didn't expect to find satisfying poke in the Midwest, but I did, and it's here at Ali'i. For me, it's comparable to poke I've had in the Bay Area and Hawaii (although nothing can REALLY top poke in Hawaii).

All the fish tastes good. I especially appreciate that they have marinated tuna, which reminds me of the poke I've gotten on Oahu. They have a wide array of toppings--everything I usually look for and then some. One of my favorite things about this place (and please, PLEASE never change this!) is that they don't charge extra for avocado. Having moved here from California where avocados are practically currency, I very much appreciate not having to pay extra to get a fix of the green stuff.

Another thing I appreciate here is the variety of sizes. Bowls come in Snack Size, Regular, and Large. I was told that you're only able to get a few different toppings with the Snack Size bowl, but sometimes that's a nice option to have. I usually order a Regular and it's plenty of for for a hearty meal (and there's no limit to how many toppings you can get).

They always have a dispenser filled with delicious infused water if you're eating in. And if water's not your thing, you can capture that island feeling with a can of UCC coffee or some lilikoi juice (which they didn't have last time I was there, but I *have* seen it on occasion). The hearty "mahalo!" greeting when you walk in the door makes me nostalgic for Hawaii.

It's a satisfying poke bowl every time and one of my favorite places to eat in the area. You can bet I'll be back.

A couple observations:
-- They are VERY heavy handed with the sauces. After discovering this the first time I went, I now ask for them to go light on the sauce and it works out much better. I want to taste my fish!
-- It would be nice if recycling was available. Since all the bowls are served in plastic clamshell packaging, it would be nice to try and reduce the amount of waste.

If you want a well executed, gorgeously plated, memorable, fancy dinner, then Vida is a solid choice. I'm impressed.

I came here for a celebratory dinner on my husband's recommendation since he had been there before with colleagues. The four course $65 seasonal dinner is a worthwhile splurge. Each of us ordered different items for each course in order to maximize sampling potential, and I'd re-order ANY of those items on a future visit. In particular, my husband's venison was quite delicious, but let's also talk about my duck entree. Mediocre duck is disappointing, but this duck was on point. Perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned. If I could do it again, I might skip the ricotta donuts in favor of something else. They were delicious, but didn't feel as high end or indulgent as the chocolate bombe (which checked all the boxes).

This place also gets an "A" for ambiance--warm modern decor, nice mood lighting, and folks make an effort to dress on the nicer side. All in all, a pretty classy feel.

At this price point it's not a place I'll be going on a weekly basis, but I'd say an emphatic "yes!" to coming here again next time I feel like splurging on myself.

It's a regular-priced grocery store in the downtown area (cheaper than Whole Foods or Needler's), so that counts for something. There's also a free parking garage where you can usually find a spot easily (without circling more than once or twice), so that also counts for something. It's clean and it looks newer inside. Could be a lot worse. But have you ever gone to a grocery store and found no grocery carts in sight? Yeah, that happens at this Kroger. You'd think that there would be wall-to-wall bodies inside the store when that happens but nope, it's always just a regular evening, not terribly packed. You can look for one in the garage but it's pretty hit or miss. Why so few carts, Kroger?? This has happened to me many times.

It's not the best, but it's far from the worst urban grocery store I've been to. It's spacious enough and the selection is pretty good for most items, though they do seem to run out of random things. The cheese section is pretty robust (including fun odds and ends cheese bins) and I appreciate that they sell beer singles in the alcohol department. They just opened a Starbucks inside this location and I hope that doesn't increase foot traffic. After all, carts are scarce. I'll fight you for one.

Will be back! I'm not a BBQ or Southern food connoisseur, but my partner and I happily devoured everything on our plates. 

We ordered the pulled pork sandwich and rib tips as mains, with mac and cheese and green beans as sides. The meat was tender, moist, and delicious and I would happily eat both sides again. (I was hesitant when they suggested the green beans but I decided to trust the recommendation and I was NOT disappointed.)

The staff was friendly and the wait was only about 5-8 minutes. All in all, it was a solid food truck experience. Looking forward to next time, Backyard BBQ!

FYI, credit card minimum is $5.

Happy to find good Ethiopian food in Indy! I ordered the Axum Special Chef's Recommendation for 2 and it is definitely a large meal for two people. It smelled amazing inside the restaurant and the takeout box felt like a BRICK--there was a lot of food packed in there! I couldn't wait to get it home and tear it open.

At my request, the chef's special was half meat dishes and half vegetarian. Everything was as I've come to expect from Ethiopian food: big on flavor and deeply satisfying. There was plenty of injera included as well. I thought the prices were reasonable and I'm definitely looking forward to going back!

COVID-19 note: I had a safe, comfortable pickup experience. Hand sanitizer was available and I was able to stay appropriately distanced from the staff.

The food quality is on par with other Five Guys locations I've been to. But on a Saturday night with maybe 8-10 people ahead of me, I waited about 45 minutes for two cheeseburgers and regular fries. At least the shake I ordered came out within 5 minutes or so. I could've made my own dinner or gotten food from almost anywhere else in less time. No "fast food" to be found at this location - will not return based on this experience.

WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER. I live fairly close to the Oxford Oaks Shopping Center so I've stopped in here for breakfast a couple times over the past couple of years. Every single time, I end up regretting it. I don't even know where to start.. 
During one visit, I went in to grab a panini for lunch and waited over 20 minutes for a single sandwich (I would understand this long wait if the store were busy, but I was the only customer in the store at the time) and when I brought it back over to the Starbucks next door to eat, I bit into cold pieces of chicken. I went back right away to let them know about my experience (I didn't even ask for a refund- I simply wanted to help them by letting them know about my experience for future reference) and the employee just stared back at me and stated that he was unable to refund me. Keep in mind- I didn't even ask them for a refund. I gave them back the sandwich from which I had taken one bite and told them they shouldn't be serving undercooked food. 
On a different visit, I walked inside and waited over 5 minutes just for my order to be taken because the woman working (with long, curly hair which is always down, which is disgusting considering she works in a food establishment and her hair could easily fall in the food) was on the phone, yelling at whomever was on the other line, and refusing to acknowledge my presence. Finally, after 5 minutes of waiting without a single greeting, she yelled over to a younger employee who happened to be doing something in the back room/kitchen area, and demanded that she come out to the front to help me. They exchanged a few words, saying that they were each busy doing something else and that the other person should help me. Seriously?! After the younger employee took my order, I went over to the register to pay for my bagel and waited another 5 minutes before the woman with the long hair would hang up the phone and ring me up. 
There isn't one instance in which I left this bagel shop satisfied. I'm honestly surprised that this place is still around considering their rude employees.

i was elated as a long-time yardley resident when i heard that shop rite was coming in to replace superfresh because i was getting tired of having to get my groceries from giant! i almost always walk out of here satisfied. the only bad thing i have to say is about an employee named corrine. she is simply rude and unwelcoming! avoid getting rung up by her at all costs. i don't know why shop rite would want an employee like her promoting and representing them.

pizza's average.. not the worst but definitely not the best. somehow, they always charge me a different price whenever i go in for a couple slices. i always order the same two slices (because i'm constrained to only two different types there since i'm a vegetarian) but they literally charge me different totals every single time.. i guess the managers like to spontaneously change up their prices depending on their moods...?

their udon noodle salad and hipcity ranch burger are to dieeeeeee for! there's almost always a line at this location and never any seats up for grabs, but it's honestly worth it because the employees try their best to ensure your order is taken and you're out the door ASAP! and their employees are super welcoming and inviting as well!
i absolutely love their portobello option! great for vegetarians and i love their "topping" selection as well! the "sushi burrito" is definitely a cool concept!

this place is nothing special, imo. the food isn't that great, and the staff is usually pretty unwelcoming and they don't really try to put in the effort to be pleasant. i honestly feel like it's just a low-class restaurant trying to act upscale.
amazing location, atmosphere, food, and staff! it's right beside rittenhouse so it's the perfect place to get some sunday brunch and people-watch!

love the food here (i've tried the tofu banh mi, fresh spring rolls, pho, tofu fried rice, and the vermicelli noodle bowl) but they're ALWAYS packed, which obviously isn't their fault. but the fact that they're always busy on top of the fact that they're usually understaffed (there were two employees waiting on tables alongside the manager/owner on a busy saturday night the last time i went) led to some mistakes in the order that we had placed during our last visit. nevertheless, the employee handled it nicely and brought out our correct order within a couple minutes. definitely one of my favorite places to get viet food!

i'm in this shopping center at least twice a month because i get my nails done right next door every other week, but i only recently decided to check this place out and i'm so glad i did! the first thing you notice when you walk in is the setting of the store. it's a bit unconventional compared to other fro-yo places, but that didn't prevent me from falling in love with this place! it's super clean (which is a big plus because most other fro-yo places are almost always dirty!) and has a fresh/modern feeling. they work on a self-serve system, but that didn't stop the employee working from checking in on me and offering me sample cups and even recommending some of her favorite combinations. she was very welcoming and friendly! they had 16 or so different flavors, which is A LOT to choose from, and they had really interesting and unique flavors! i decided to go with nutella, watermelon, salted caramel, and tart! i know it's a weird combination, but it was still amazing! i've never seen any other fro-yo places offer nutella-flavored fro-yo, so you can imagine how excited i was when i saw this! and their watermelon was a sorbet flavor and it was SO refreshing. they also had a good selection of fresh fruit and a myriad of other unique toppings available, but i decided to go with just the fro-yo that day. overall, i'm simply mad at myself for not having checked out this place earlier! i'm looking forward to my next mani appt so that i can pamper myself with some fro-yo after!

amazing coffee, staff, and atmosphere! the only downside about this location is how busy they can tend to get. the only time i've been able to score a table and seat in order to sit down and study was when i went super early in the morning, around the time they open. nevertheless, their staff is super accommodating and the atmosphere is super chill and laid-back!

I used to order from here through Grubhub all the time; I even had a go-to order and everything. However, I ordered and paid for a 2-Liter soda one night and the delivery guy forgot it, and promised to give me credit for it, whatever that means. I didn't pay that much attention to it because it was only $3 and the delivery guy said he would take care of it. But I never received a refund or anything for it, so when I went to place another order tonight, I called the restaurant and told them what happened the last time. The girl on the phone said ok, and then called Grubhub, claiming that I never placed an order from this restaurant before (is that a joke?! this restaurant is one of the only 2 restaurants I order from through Grubhub, and it clearly shows on my order history on the app) and they were trying to claim that I was scamming them out of a soda. A THREE DOLLAR SODA! All this after the incompetent delivery guy left a mess on my front porch the last time because the mango habanero pizza I ordered was leaking sauce everywhere (which he never even apologized for; all I got was a stupid, blank stare). I will never be ordering from this place again. Save your money and go somewhere else.

Hit or miss. I usually get the same bagel from here in the morning before I catch my train-a toasted pumpernickel bagel with butter. Dude didn't even bother to toast it so now I'm stuck with a slab of solidified butter on a cold, hard bagel which I'm throwing away once I get into the city. And the 2 gentlemen working in the mornings are not the friendliest. You're better off somewhere else.

first off, the quality of the chicken hasn't been the same lately. it's been inconsistent, dry, and lacks sauce and flavor. second, the girl with the glasses who works downstairs at the register is incredibly rude. i went in to pick up my order today and i didn't get a greeting and i caught her rolling her eyes multiple times. i asked her for an extra bag as i had orders for 2 separate people that i was picking up and she rudely rolled her eyes right in front of my face.

i decided to give this place another chance after multiple disappointing visits. i placed an order hours before the scheduled pick up time. i got there 5 minutes before i was supposed to pick it up and i let the girl at the front know that i was picking up an order i placed earlier and she said it'd be a 5 minute wait, which was fine by me. so i stood there and waited. 20 minutes passed, and i'm still standing there with no update whatsoever. meanwhile, a dozen people came in and out with their orders while i just stood there waiting. by the time i got home, my garlic knots were hot and fresh but my pizza was cold, and they only gave me 2 small containers of hot sauce which was not enough for 25 wings. i was very disappointed with this experience, as i always am when i try to support their business. i won't be going back again.

the drinks are standard KF tea drinks. you can't go wrong with your regular KF tea order. but the food is absolutely horrible. the teriyaki chicken onigiri had such a bad taste (raw chicken taste) that i just threw it out. the rice balls are 90% rice and the rice is so gooey that it falls apart when you bite into it. go for the drinks, but definitely avoid their food items. the girls working at the register are also sometimes very rude and lack customer service skills.

If you're planning on eating here, this is just a heads up that the servers don't wear their masks. Not only that, but the cooks who prepare YOUR FOOD in the back kitchen don't wear their masks properly nor do they wear gloves when preparing your food. I got take out from here and threw everything out after what I witnessed.

Their management sucks. We directly spoke to the manager when placing an order for a cake, and asked for a cake that said "Congratulations" to celebrate a graduation. When we picked up the cake and brought it back home, the cake read "I love you, mom." This isn't the first time they've made a mistake like this. There are other Korean bakeries in the area, so I would suggest going there instead of wasting your time and money here.
Their black cherry water ice is to die for!! We also got an ice cream cake to celebrate a birthday and it was also very good!

This used to be my favorite Dunkin and I used to go out of my way to go to this location since my house is further away. They recently hired a bunch of young high school/college students and it hasn't been the same since. In my last ~10 visits, there has not been one time when they didn't mess something up in my order. I ordered and paid extra for an iced latte, and they gave me an iced coffee instead. A few times when I ordered mocha lattes, they forgot to add mocha syrup so I just received bland lattes. The last time I went, I paid for 2 breakfast sandwiches and only got one. I've wasted so much money at this location just to receive the wrong item or not receive it at all. I'll be going to different locations closer to my house from now on.
There was the longest piece of hair in the french toast I ordered. I threw up and threw it out. Never again.

HNyPFluvz2o7BGq0_LvWwQ.review_text: Best last night spot in Uptown. Three different areas, the patio, the bar and the upstairs area for when you need room to dance. they have great cheese fries and their drinks are cheap. best nights are thursdays in my opinion but will be happy to come on fridays or saturdays as well.
best dive bar in NOLA. open 24 hours and has cheap drinks. good music playing and has an air hockey table. the bathroom is also interesting with all the mardi gras themed tiles.
favorite bar in new orleans. always a good late night spot to ride out till the morning. great staff and very friendly. nice happy hours as well.

very convenient store with good po boys. my room mate loved their french fries but they were just normal fries to me. the hot sausage po boy was really good and so was the shrimp.

also has everything a convenient store would have and not over priced. 
they sell beer and alcohol and mixers, all well priced.

their steak n egg breakfast sandwich is the best. awesome hangover food and they delivery. not only do they deliver their deli food but they will also deliver anything they sell in the store, which is also like a mini convenient store.very little seating available though

perfect late night snack right before bed. even had it sober a few times and it was still good- granted not as good as when you've had a few drinks but better than the crepe place on the other side of The Boot. 

this is not a sit down place unless you take your pizza and eat it inside the boot or in the one table they have outside. 

this is only for their pizza, didn't even know they had other kinds of food till after i graduated.

great drinks and good food,  i love their alligator sausage po boys. perfect place to come and watch a game with a big group of people. they have a bunch of TVs all around the place so you will have a good view from wherever your sitting.
So many cheeses to choose from - and a great selection of them! Delicious salads and sandwiches. Take some special cheeses home and enjoy with a nice bottle of wine, perfect dinner for me!

This place is a staple in New Orleans history. An institution. The greatest sno balls in the whole world... Is that too big of a statement? I think not. The ice is perfectly shaved and so soft. 

The line usually goes out the door and around the corner. This says something. It is a must try for anyone who hasn't gone and for visitors. 

My favorite flavor is wild cherry with condensed milk. Anything with condensed milk is amazing. This place actually made me love condensed me. I wish I never knew how good it was with sno balls. It's amazing. 

The strawberry shortcake is also great. So is the cream of almond.... They're all great. 

They accept credit card but there's a $1 extra fee. Just bring cash... The servings range from $1.50 to $18 - there's a size for everyone. Toppings range from $.50 to $1.50. It's all worth it. 

Just do it. You won't regret it!

It is good for what it is! Great place to grab fresh seafood... service could use some improvement. Love that they now take credit cards. Hard to run a business without this now a days. Came here on Easter Sunday and they still had plenty of crawfish and live crabs. 

Their prices are fair and are relatively competitive compared to the surrounding markets. Worth the drive - crawfish in NOLA is much more expensive. 

Plently of parking!

i love this place. you can't go in expecting the best - you have to take it for what it is. cheap drinks, good music, sloppy behaviour and NOLA debauchery. if you are looking for a classy place, this is not it - this city as a whole may not be it either. come here after a few drinks and if you are looking to boogie. music is usually pretty decent - top hits kind of vibe with lots of throwbacks. this is the kind of spot that should be your last stop in your night. i promise you'll have fun!

also, one of the last places that still sets your flaming dr pepper shots on fire! if you've never had one, get one. they are delicious!

It is important to note that the times they have listed on their yelp page are not correct. they are only open from Wednesday to Saturday!

this is a solid bar choice in NOLA and it often goes overlooked. i have never had the food so this review is just based on the price and the experience. drinks are cheap, good and strong. the bartenders are all friendly. the crowd that comes here are also very friendly and chatty. you feel like a local when you go here. 

on wednesday nights they have open mic night. this is always a great time. if you are ballsy enough to get on stage DO IT! i haven't mustered the courage but it seems like a lot of fun!

I visited for the first time last week with a few friends and overall it was a good experience. The food was tasty and the staff was excellent. There was a lot of hype around this restaurant given its star studded management but I wish I hadn't known that before. Going in with that mentality, I sometimes expect over the top, mind blowing food. Do not get me wrong, the food was great but it was not 'blow my socks off' great. I would recommend it to friends but as a 'try it once' kind of place. I guess what I am trying to say is that I did really enjoy it but was a little pricey for what you were paying. I think my idea of Mexican street fare is very different as having been to Mexico several times over the years. Again, the food was great but this was very fancy version of Mexican street fare. I love Mexican food and it is hard to find in New Orleans - I guess I am very spoiled by the options offered in Miami. 


If you do go, I do recommend the corn side dish. This was very tasty. It was presented differently from the normal street corn you'd find in Mexico but this is a HUGE plus. It is already off the cob - making it so much easier to eat!

We also got the tamale with duck. This was really tasty! The tamale was perfectly made and the meat was very tender. It had lots of flavor!

The queso fondido was alright. This was the least impressive item but it was still good. Kind of hard to mess up queso... actually I take that back as I have had several experiences with bad queso. This is good queso! LOL

We had a torta and this was great. Fresh ingredients and very well made. Expect a very fancy version of a torta. 

My friends had the shrimp dish which they said was very good. I am allergic to shrimp so I was not able to try it but they said they really did enjoy it!

This place is great! I came here with my friends on a Sunday morning when the weather was perfect and sitting outside was plentiful. There was not a long line by any means and we got to order our food rather quickly. I had some questions and the man helping us at the front was very knowledgeable of the menu and everything the restaurant had to offer. I ordered the poached big toast with bacon in addition to the breakfast tacos. Please note that both the bees menu items are really big open easily be shared, especially if you aren't too hungry. The poached big toast was delicious! It was a little hard to eat with a fork and knife so get ready today again. My favorite by far were the tacos! It came with a great hot sauce but I couldn't get enough of. I highly recommend this place for a yummy breakfast or brunch with friends. You won't be disappointed!

great service.
great pho.
clean facilities.
quick service.

No complaints here! All the people that work here are very nice. Their product is solid and very healthy portions. No way I was able to finish the small pho in one sitting. Will definitely be coming back!

This place is wonderful. I came here for an early dinner Friday with two friends and we had a GREAT time! The food was spectacular as well as the service. We sat at the table closest to the sidewalk. They keep the door open so it was a nice and cool breeze. Couldn't ask for better weather. 

We started off with the happy hour menu. I got the gumbo. It was probably one of the best gumbos I've ever had. My only complaint is that I wanted more. Next time I come I'll definitely get the normal appetizer size. I suggest you do the same. 

For my entree I got the jambalaya risotto. This was the real star. So creamy and perfect in every way. It was very rich so I suggest sharing this with a few people but it is definitely a must have. 

To cut the richness of the risotto I ordered the side dish of the kale salad with some fresh citrus. This was equally as good and I also highly recommend! It's a very unique flavor and definitely a crowd pleaser. 

My friend ordered the salad which was great. Can't remember what it was called but it did have homemade croutons which were REALLY good! 

For dessert we had the foie gras king cake. I wish they had this on their menu all year long and not just for carnival season. I was told they have fun desserts all the time so I'm excited to go back and see for myself! As for this king cake, it was unlike anything I've ever had before. It wasn't too sweet and had a faint foie Gras taste with three big pieces in the middle of the plate. Definitely one of the best king cakes I've ever had. Totally worth the hype! 

They had a great beer and wine selection for happy hour as well. Next time I come I want to try out their cocktails. The table next to us was raving about them throughout dinner! 

The only downside is parking BUT you're in the quarter so that's expected. I suggest ubering to the restaurant! 

As for the service, our waitress was amazing. I wish I could remember her name but she was so friendly and very helpful in navigating through the menu. The food came out at a normal pace. We weren't in a rush so it was perfect. We got to really enjoy ourselves, the food and the great weather.

This is not The Bombay Club I remember when I came here for college. This place has had a huge makeover and looks better than ever. First off, this place has live music everyday, a great bar area and a super cute patio. Great place to come with friends  or to get away for the bourbon craziness to catch your breath. 

The drinks here are fairly priced and most importantly STRONG & TASTY! They don't mess around with their drinks here. They also have a great happy hour! Definitely check it out. 

As for the food it's much much much better than I ever remembered. I had some bites off the happy hour menu. Started off with the pretzel... so warm and you can tell it was freshly made. Perfect amount of salt. The cheese dip it's paired with is to die for. I wish I could put it on everything! 

I also got the pork belly tacos! That slaw was really good... usually I'm not a big kimchi fan but they did it the right way that's for sure. 

I also came here during carnival season and they had the bacon king cake. I love bacon and I love king cake. Combining these two loves makes for one of the best king cakes I've ever had. It's meant for two but it's big enough for 4-5 or leftovers. I took mine to go... I ate it before the night was over. I wish they had this all year long! 

Looking forward to coming back here for a proper meal! Also, they have valet which is key! It still may be easier to get around the quarter in an uber!

This place is awesome and has quickly turned into this gals top brunch spots in the big easy. 

THE LOCATION 
I love uptown and finding gems like this makes me appreciate it so much more. The street it's located on has tons of greenery and plenty of street parking. 

THE AMBIENCE 
It has such a cute store front. It has a very relaxing feel to it. Try to snag a seat outside if there are any available. 

THE FOOD
I had the open faced breakfast sandwich. It had a healthy amount of veggies and a nice cream cheese like spread with more veggies. It was topped off with a fried egg - to which I added hot sauce! I also had a fresh pressed beat juice which was equally as good. They had a ton of pastries at the cash register that looked really tasty too! My friend had the breakfast sandwich. Considering that she never offered me a bite, it must have been really good. 

Will definitely be coming back!

I love this place for sno-balls! The sizes are very generous - and they pile them up high! I have gotten a few of their flavors and have never been disappointed. I have also gotten condensed milk and they are VERY generous with their servings with this as well - next time I think I will ask them to put some in the middle as well. 

The service is fast. You usually get your sno-ball within 5 minutes. They accept cash and card - which is really nice! I don't think they charge an extra fee for using credit card. 

There is no designated parking but there is plenty of street parking near by!

I have been here two separate times and had two VERY different experiences. The first time was absolutely lovely. I sat at the bar with a friend and we had the time of our lives and a lovely lunch. The service was spectacular. The bartender was very attentive, friendly and engaging. It really made out experience superb. Te lamb hummus is INCREDIBLE and I wish I could eat this every day. This was a few weeks ago and he had just started working there. I wish I remembered his name because he was awesome. I would have given Shaya 5 stars back then.

I visited the restaurant for lunch again with my family who was from out of town. We came in for lunch and it was a very bizarre experience. Our waiter was very patronizing. He got upset with our group when we did not follow his recommendations. He doesn't know our situation or what our likes/dislikes are so no one should ever take this offensively. When we sat down, I had asked him to put in an order of the lamb hummus with extra bread to be sent. He had suggested us not get bread to start off with because we will fill up... I told him it would be okay (my family loves bread and this does not fill us up). He then proceeded to bring us an absurd amount of bread. It was ridiculous and coming nonstop. This was an exaggeration... we'd have two loaves of bread on our table and they'd come out with two more loaves. It felt very patronizing. My family had asked me to order for everyone since I had already been there. I placed an amount I thought would be perfect for us and his response was that this was enough for 2 people.... we were a group of 8 people, 3 of which were not eating. We felt pressured to order more and ended up ordering 2 more chicken sandwiches that were absolutely disgusting... this might have just been our personal opinion but I would not order this again. We ended up with WAY more food than we could finish. Maybe he was hoping to get a bigger tip because we ordered more? I don't know but we definitely did not appreciate getting that pressure to order more food. 

What was very bizarre about this situation was our waiter. There really was no need for such a weird treatment. It really made my entire family feel so uncomfortable. I can't remember his name but he spoke with a British accent but was from the states. I'd expect them to be much more sensitive to how they treat their customers considering all the bad press they have been receiving lately. This experience totally turned me off to the restaurant and I will not be returning anytime soon.

I can't say enough good things about this amazing restaurant!
The service is amazing. They are all so friendly and accommodating. My family and I came in on Thanksgiving day and were welcomed into the restaurant so warmly. I was so surprised at the fact that there was no wait because this place really is amazing and blows all the other usual suspects out of the water (by this I mean all the classic NOLA restaurants).  

We had ordered a bunch of steaks, drinks, apps and everything was great! I really do want to point out the calamari salad. This was probably the best salad I have ever had. It is a must try if you like calamari. Really yummy! The steak was also amazing. They dry age the steak in the restaurant and you can see it in the entrance. 

I highly recommend this restaurant for a date or if you have friends/family in town. They also have a great bar so that would also be a good option. Worth the trip to the quarter!

Colin's milkshakes bring all the customers to the yard...

Seriously though, Dat Dog makes great milkshakes.

This place is iconic and a must for everyone visiting this city. Local tip, go for lunch during the week to take advantage of the $.25 martini special! They have a few different flavours to choose from. 

Weekend brunches are incredible because they have the jazz brunch! A great band making its way throughout the whole restaurant serenading the crowd. Perfect way to enjoy your day. 

I absolutely love the food here. You can't go wrong. Don't expect anything bland or healthy... you're in NOLA so indulge!!

Omg everything about this place was incredible!! The atmosphere, the menu and the food!! Seriously good food!!! The place was PACKED with other locals. I had a great time and wish I could eat here every day!! 

Also the staff is great. I asked what their favourites were and they did not disappoint!! Amazing oysters, fried chicken, Mac n cheese, sweet potato... don't walk, RUN!! Go there ASAP!!

This is my favourite place to get chargrilled oysters. It's the perfect blend of seafood, butter and carbs! Get your own order, they're so good you'll definitely eat the whole dozen (or at least I do every time I go). 

You can also go to the hotel lobby bar and get the oysters from there. Last time I went with some friends, we ate there and it was SO fast! We had a few people order takeaway from the restaurant and ate with us since the bar has a limited menu.

Get the milk and cookies!!! Wow it's so good... there's something about the milk - I hate it normally... but this milk is soooooo good. 

The food here is all good! My favourite is the beat salad and the fried chicken sandwich. The fried chicken and honey biscuit is also really tasty!!

I'm Cuban so I'm very critical of other restaurants that serve the food I grew up on. 

It's pretty spot on. The croquetas are PERFECT. Just how my aunt used to make them. The media noches are also truly authentic! They even got the bread right!! Rabo encendido was amazing!! 

Only reason I give this place a 4/5 is because of the price. This is normally CHEAP food. It's soooo overpriced coming from Miami. I'm assuming it's because of the high rent on magazine street. Please keep in mind, I have been here 3 times so it hasn't put me off all that much - I will pay anything for croquetas lol

I love this place so much!!! 

All the arepas I've had here are incredible. Seriously, you can't go wrong. They get the arepa bread so fluffy and moist. My favourite is the steak one - the mechada! It's the perfect combination of all my favourite things!! The carnicera is also equally amazing!! 

Their empanadas are always so good too! And the Maíz de la Rueda! Corn and cheese - everything you never knew you needed!! 

Make reservations because it gets PACKED! Every night of the week. It's worth it!! 

Friendly staff. Great drinks. Amazing food!!!!

Hq_iRg_7i-nl_LFuGrv6Kg.review_text: Naturally there are higher-rated gourmet pizza joints, but Italian Pie has a special taste that reminds me of my favorite pizza in the country-- Ecco's Pizza in Long Beach, CA. However, be careful: the Italian Pie downtown on Rampart is much different from the one located in Mid-city on Carrolton. This Italian Pie-- the one located on Rampart St. is delicious and good enough for a lazy weekend. The Italian Pie on Carrolton tastes like microwaved pizza! It's atrocious!  Anyway, the service here is friendly and quick. I typically call in my order when I'm around the block at Rouse's grocery (when I used to live in St. Roch), and find that my pizza is hot and ready to go within ten minutes. Not too shabby...

The veggie burger had two patties and they expect you to add your own condiments: nothing special. There is your average mustard, a bottle of ketchup, and there may be a packet of mayonnaise, but I'm not entirely sure, so don't quote me on it. A dry bun is a very dull veggie burger, indeed. Maybe it's just me, but I prefer to have a "special" sauce or spread added my burger, but I probably won't be returning here anytime soon. Overall, the food is healthy (if you're into that), and the prices were more than affordable for your average Joe veggie burger. I sure do miss Astro Burger in Los Angeles!

Sacred Grind's is my new favorite morning haunt. I'm lucky that it is located rather close to my humble abode. It is a coffee shop located literally on a cemetery, hence the name. Attached to it is an apothecary with various oils, incenses, and votive candles for purchase. One of the few coffee shops where you can treat yourself to a tea, purchase a candle, and dedicate the morning to the Hoodoo spirits in the cemetery immediately after exiting its confines! Don't forget to have your card punched, as the 8th drink is free.

Cafe Niño is a family-run authentic Italian cuisine. Hands down, the best pizza in New Orleans. You can order a whole pizza, or take several slices already made, to go. They offer weekday specials with various hot meals already made (cafeteria style) and ready to be served. Chicken or eggplant Parmigiana or Veal, Chicken Cacciatore, Chicken Marsala, Catfish, hoagies, calzones, salads, etc. But best of all is the pizza. The service is incredibly friendly-- it's going to be one of three: the owner, his son, or the cool black guy. Remember: cash only! I learned my lesson during my first trip, but they let me have my meal on the house, providing I came back and payed the following visit. I've returned more than a several dozen times since!

One night my car was being worked on at the mechanic, yet I was starving without wanting to go out in public. I remembered a flyer that I had received in the post and decided to try their "gourmet pizza". The pizza wasn't exactly gourmet, and it unfortunately tasted quite a bit like Pizza Hut, however they provided ranch dipping sauce, making me nostalgic for Virginia pizza. In Norfolk, Virginia, there is a delicious pizza chain that insists on using ranch dipping sauce. Don't get me wrong: Magazine Pizza is decent for a night-in, curled up watching a foreign film, however it was rather ordinary pizza to begin with. Perhaps if I try the Grilled Shrimp pizza, I will have second-thoughts?

Say whatever you want, but I am a Whole Food's shopper. I can't find everything on my shopping list here, but I certainly find my fair share when I am in the mood. Whole Food's caters to my caviar needs, which makes me happy. However, their selection of exotic meats is basically non-existent. For alligator, turtle, and rabbit, I must go to my local Rouse's, but I forgive easier than I probably should. This Whole Food's is a bit out of the way for me-- living in Mid-city-- though the Whole Foods down the street on Broad St. Is opening in February, so I'm incredibly excited about that. 

With that said, this is a small Whole Food's. For the warehouse-sized Whole Food's see Metairie on Veteran's. I won't complain too much, as all of the cute girls shop at this Whole Food's. Located on Magazine St., it attracts all of the pretty hipsters that are fun to look at. Being a gastronomist, I find that Rouse's supplies me with the majority of my needs, however Whole Food's is there for speciality items: I purchase my gourmet cheeses and wines here, caviar, mango juice, and so on. I find that the majority of Whole Food's shoppers are vegetarian, and being that there is an entire store filled with vegan and vegetarian products rather than one aisle at a local grocery-- that's what attracts that crowd to the Whole Food's lifestyle. Otherwise, I eat gourmet style and most of my shopping is done at my local Rouse's. I will admit that I am overly excited about the Whole Food's opening up down the street in just a couple of weeks. Instead of driving all of the way uptown, I can walk several blocks away for my Whole Food's speciality items.

When it comes to Viatnamese/Chinese, this is my go-to cuisine, located in the Vieux Carre Quarter. The prices are incredibly affordable and the size proportions are very large. I typically order the Orange Chicken Tofu with fried rice and shrimp and vegetable egg rolls, which is the best I've had. The Viatnamese Po-boys are also very good and extremely cheap. 

The employees here are as friendly as one can be, and they're very good about taking orders for pick-up. I believe they deliver inside of the Vieux Carre Quarter, but as I live further away in Mid-city, I typically call ten minutes ahead of time for pick-up. Dining-in is also a viable option, as the ambiance in the evening is dark and a good place for a date. It's the best type of hole-in-the-wall-- it's not particularly a dive, but it's nothing close to fine-dining either. A good place for more of a casual date, or the perfect Viatnamese take-out for a quiet night in.

Absinthe is a bit of an obsession of mine. The Old Absinthe House is a historical landmark within the rich history of the emerald muse. It is here in New Orleans where absinthe took off in 1869, when the Aleix brothers opened a bar named the "Old Absinthe House" at the corner of Bourbon and Bienville streets in the Vieux Carre Quarter. The Old Absinthe House attracted an impressive list of visitors, including presidents William Howard Taft and Theodore Roosevelt, Mark Twain, Walt Whitman, Aaron Burr, William Thackeray, Jenny Lind and Oscar Wilde. In 1918, Aleister Crowley, the British magician, proclaimed: "Art is the soul of life and the Old Absinthe House is the heart and soul of the old quarter of New Orleans." Indeed, this is the bar where the cocktail was said to have been invented. In 1916, while sitting at the Old Absinthe House and waiting for a woman friend, Crowley wrote his famous essay, "The Green Goddess"-- adorning its main theme, the emerald muse, with the philosophical reflections suggested by absinthe with descriptions of the inn, its guests, and the city. First published in The International, the essay extols the inspirational virtues of the hazy green liqueur, while speaking out against the rising tide of prohibitionism that was sweeping the country as the first U.S. "war on drugs" began.

So for the absinthe connoisseur, the Old Absinthe House is a special place to stop-- most preferably at l'heure verte ("the green hour")-- while taking in its history and colorful past. As an absinthe connoisseur, you're not going to find the best brands of absinthe here, but the Old Absinthe House is more about the history & lore than it is about the absinthe specifically these days. 

Public service announcement: just please, do not burn your absinthe. The sugar cube is not meant to be burned. For a good authentic absinthe louche, ask the bartender to slowly pour cold water over the spoon. As for sugar, that is specifically up to the drinker. Personally, I take sugar with my absinthe. Therefore it is absolutely horrifying for me to witness a bartender burning the sugar cube. I once saw this at Pirate's Alley, however whether or not this is on their agenda on a daily basis, I am unsure. When you order your absinthe, just kindly let the bartender know how you want your absinthe served.

I also recommend a good absinthe frappé to be ordered on a hot summer day!

I'm going to echo Joi B. here concerning Pirate's Alley and its European decadence. This is one of those places in New Orleans where you stop and suddenly realize that New Orleans is truly one of the last few decadent cities in the entire world-- along with cities like Cairo, St. Petersburg, and Naples. New Orleans is also one of the last sin-filled cities in the United States along with Las Vegas and maybe Manhattan on a good night. The Pirate's Alley is the perfect afternoon haunt to sit outside smoking a cigarette with a glass of absinthe, looking upon the shadow of the St. Louis Cathedral and the European-esque alley.

Pirate's Alley is owned by an older couple and the bartenders are a group of several or so females, who all enjoy drinking absinthe. Kesha is my favorite-- she's a sweetheart if you get to meet her. I sat with her the other day, absinthe in hand, just talking about life and art for an hour and a half. Pirate's Alley holds a certain nostalgic quality to it. People from all over the world are attracted to this bar and frequent it when in town because of its odd charm and for some, the "occult" vibe that is permeated within. This bar is supposedly haunted and has been the subject of various television shows and documentaries, and there have been dozens of sightings during operating hours-- such as a ghost baby behind the counter and other old souls and pirates of New Orleans that still fancy the establishment in the afterlife. The Haunted Ghost Tour typically stops at this sight, so that's usually when the pirate crowd comes along and does their thing. 

As for absinthe itself, you may want to read my review for the Old Absinthe House. Finding good brands of absinthe in any bar nowadays is difficult, as it's more about the concept than the drink itself. I recommend drinking either Lucid or the more expensive Nouvelle-Orleans brands of absinthe-- Lucid isn't the best, but it also isn't the worst. Made by Ted Breaux, who can sometimes be seen at the Pirate's Alley, Lucid had a significant role in re-legalizing the emerald muse in the United States-- and was the first imported absinthe to be legally sold in the U.S after they changed the regulation in 2007. Honestly, it's better to have a brand like Lucid in stores, rather than some of the terribly made artificial absinthe brands out there. The Kubler 53, a blanche absinthe, is also a decent absinthe behind the counter at Pirate's Alley, if you're in the mood for something lighter.

When visiting Pirate's Alley, you're always bound to meet someone interesting if like me, this is your kind of vibe-- artists, Cajun old-timers that search for buried treasure, Dada-enthusiasts, writers and the like.

This is my neighborhood grocery and my typical go-to spot for the morning and evening hours. I've been to multiple Rouse's since moving to Louisiana, and this was by far the best of them all, and remains the top-runner. One is able to satisfy their impeccable gastronomic desires here with their wonderful variety of meats: I purchase my rabbit, turtle meat, octopus, alligator, and sometimes shrimp at this location. The seafood department is also incredibly helpful, and their catfish, swordfish, and oysters are just as good as Whole Food's. They also provide a variety of salmon with different seasoning and sauces. In the late afternoon/early evening hours, cooked catfish, Cajun-flavored corn and potatoes, and Cajun-spiced shrimp are all available and kept warm. 

The produce section is large and fulfilling, and everything is exactly where I know I will find it, as they don't mix and move around their aisles, as some stores ever so terribly do. The employees all know me by my face, as I frequent the store quite often, and they're all incredibly friendly. I also like that the crowd tends to be in the early twenties to fourties range. I've never dealt with any assholes at this grocery store, which is quite surprising because there seems to always be "that guy"-- but not at this Rouse's.

First off, this is the botanica of all botanicas. F&F Botanica is an occultist's dream warehouse. This is the ultimate supply of votive candles, folks. Every imaginable prayer candle that exists will be found at F&F Botanica-- but most significant of all, this is the cheapest place to find candles. Not only are they the cheapest candles, but they are made from 100% wax and are top quality. It's really a shame that touristy shops like Reverand Zombie's sells their candles for $7 and above, when at F&F, one can find the same candle, but in better quality for $2.89. In fact, why not take the $7 that you spend at a touristy shop in the Vieux Carre, and come visit F&F where you can buy a "dressed" candle for the same price? Felix, the owner of F&F, explained the difference between a dressed candle and a normal votive candle: "It's like being handed a plate of plain rice. A dressed candle is like being handed a plate of rice with meats and vegetables." This couldn't be further from the truth. F&F Botanica dress their candles with the appropriate oils and herbs for each particular candle and its purpose. Even though twice as expensive, it's the difference between performing a spell the correct way and halfway finishing a spell because one is in a hurry to finish.

F&F Botanica also carries prayer cards, pamphlets, spell books, saint statues, oils, sprays, cleaning supplies, pendants, necklaces, bracelets, and other altar paraphernalia. Again, anything you can find at any other botanica, one will find at F&F and much much more. Felix, the owner of F&F is an incredibly friendly and knowledgable older man who has owned the store for what is now going on 31 years. Years ago, there were 15 botanicas in the area, however F&F was the only shop that prospered and is still around to-day. When I first met Felix, he made it clear that his intent at F&F was to sell the best quality products for the most affordable prices. 

It's nearly impossible to walk into F&F without purchasing anything. I feel very lucky to live only a few streets away from this magical shop. The first time I visited F&F, I even noticed jumbo votive candles--- something I had never seen before. I assume these candles are 30-day prayer candles. When visiting for the first time, be sure to ask kindly for parchment paper for your candle, and if you're unaware as to how to perform the devotion, it probably wouldn't hurt to ask Felix, or another available employee. F&F Botanica is the premiere botanica in all of the New Orleans, and is a special place for many people around the world. "People come here from Europe, just to come to this shop," Felix once said. I believe it! This is the real deal.

Being an absinthe connoisseur, I'm giving Sydney's Wine Cellar a review solely based on their absinthe selection, considering there aren't many great places to find good absinthe in New Orleans. Also because I don't really buy anything other than absinthe here anyway. For the first time absinthe buyer, it would seem as though there are plenty of brands of absinthe to choose from, however if we are talking good absinthe, then there are 3 or 4 good brands here among their selection of 15 or so absinthe brands. Here you will find Pacifique and Heritage-- two of the better brands out there. Also available is the more expensive Nouvelle-Orleans made by Jade Liquers. All three of these brands come highly recommended by The Dandy of New Orleans. 

The girl that works here seemed a little angry and frustrated at the world, but whenever I buy absinthe here, the guy seemed to know what he was talking about. He agreed that the brands I mentioned are the best available-- at least at Sydney's Wine Cellear. When in the Vieux Carre, stop on by and treat yourself to some good absinthe.

I absolutely love this place. Upon walking in, you should be greeted by the casual crack smoker, singing a song about life on the rough streets smoking the crack pipe. Inside it's like a ghetto shopping mall-- excuse the language, but anyone would agree with me. There is an electronic department to the left selling phones and other stuff that nobody really wants to know where it originated from. The meat market serves meat specials that you can't beat-- literally, anywhere. 32-inch shrimp Po-boys for $12.99. Those things would feed an entire village in Yemen. I like to stop by for the more reasonably-sized 10-inch shrimp or catfish Po-boy-- usually marked at $5.99, but the guy behind the counter was so high that he sold it to me for $3.99 last time. 

The Banks Meat Market is open 24 hours 7 days a week, but I wouldn't recommend coming here alone in the evening. I once lived in St. Roch so I have some serious street-cred. When I roll by, I usually run into my homies and we catch up over a cold one. This is the closest to fast food that I would ever eat. When I'm in the mood for some junk food, this is where I stop for a stuffed Po-boy.

As I live in Mid-City, I've been excited about this Whole Foods ever since they started building it. Now I can avoid the long drive uptown and literally walk a few blocks down to this Whole Foods. Upon visiting on the grand opening day, there were so many people that I thought I was going to die of too many people overload, but that most likely won't be the case as time continues on. The parking lot is rather small however, for a Whole Foods, so a word of advice: park on the street right next to the parking lot. Not only will you find a spot, but you'll exit much easier and faster. 

For the quality of the store itself, see my review for the uptown Whole Foods. Everything is really the same as in any other Whole Foods. This particular one is bigger than the uptown store, but still smaller than the large warehouse-style store in Metairie. Upon visiting the new Whole Foods for the first time, I found everything that I usually find in Whole Foods-- just new aisles to get used to and a new store layout to become comfortable with. The employees are friendly here, the vibe was good... just too many people, but I wouldn't really expect otherwise on a grand opening day.

I decided to walk to The Parkway Tavern for lunch, and as far as their food is concerned-- I was definitely impressed. The Parkway Bakery was founded in 1911, so they've had plenty of time to invent the perfect recipe for the Po-boy. They bake their own bread here and serve your Po-boy in a fresh loaf. Even the vegetarian Po-boys are good, but there are too many good choices here to be wasting time with vegetarian stuff. I'm definitely going to return for the Alligator Sausage Link Po-boy. 

The bar is probably the best feature of the tavern, and as long as you sit at the bar, you're going to have extremely quick service. The outside patio kind of reminds me of a homeless food shelter for some reason, but maybe that's just me. The bartender girl was a sweetheart here. I hear they have a no facial hair policy here as far as employees go, and in all honestly-- it's incredibly lame! What are they... The New York Yankees? So I sort of boycott this place, but at the same time, it's difficult not to pop in every now and then for a good Po-boy with fresh French bread made at the in-house bakery.

This is probably my favorite place to go for drinks, if I were to choose a single venue in the city for an evening out with friends. The restaurant manager, Charles, is a cool guy, therefore knowing that someone relatively interesting is managing the bar makes up for the expensive cocktails. Being a cocktail barman myself, I must say that their cocktail menu is one of the best in the city. Not to mention they provide an absinthe drip here too, for someone like me that literally goes through withdrawal from the emerald muse and needs a little green in my glass every once in awhile. 

The ambiance is lovely. The Bombay Club is beautiful and the music is always good. When you enter the premises, you know you're going to be hearing good music-- jazz and lounge singers-- instead of some of the terrible music one would hear elsewhere. This place is right up my alley. The music typically begins at 9PM, so it's better to arrive fashionably late. Also, don't take too much offense to not being seated in one of the curtained booths. Honestly, if I were the bar manager, I would only seat the upscale spenders and VIPS here myself. This is probably the closest one is going to get to an authentic speakeasy-style bar in New Orleans. Unfortunately we don't have a Mata Hari's like Savannah, Georgia, but there are several places, such as the Bombay Club that halfway meets the requirements for that old-timey speakeasy that I personally would prefer any day of the week, rather than the many hipster dive bars that people my age are supposed to haunt.

I work at a strip club on Bourbon St., so take my word for it when I say that Vieux Carre Pizza is the best "pizza by the slice" available in the Quarter. Certainly my favorite stop during my lunch break. Forget Jester's pizza and all of those cardboard bread pizza slices up and down Bourbon. The bread at Vieux Carre is nice and thick, and the pizza is delicious. I recommend the chicken and spinach, but they're all good. Not only is the pizza fabulous, but the prices are also the cheapest. A slice of cheese will only cost you $3.00, where as slices with toppings run from $4.00-4.50. 

Probably the best place to stop in the Quarter for an extremely quick and cheap eat. Service is friendly as well. All of the guys that work here are rather nice.

My barback recommended I try this place after work one day since they offer a discount for Bourbon St. employees, and I definitely wasn't disappointed. After a long day at work I was incredibly starving, but the food itself was really great. The shrimp is delicious and the sauce is perfectly spicy. The rest of their seafood is above average, and their Po-boys look wonderful, even though I admit to not having tried one yet. 

Even when busy, the service is friendly and tactful, especially if you sit at the bar as I always do in a restaurant. Just a very convenient little seafood cookery. Definitely a touristy destination, but it's difficult to find a non-touristy place to eat on Bourbon during the Mardi Gras season. I took some photos with some out of town girls like the celebrity I am, but it wasn't all that terrible. There's no doubt that I will be back. 50% off Bourbon St. employees is a lovely thing, indeed.

I'm from Los Angeles, so I'm really picky when it comes to good, authentic Mexican food. Juan's Flying Burrito is surprisingly refreshing and delicious. I've only been here twice, so I don't really understand the whole "punk" theme thing they have going on here. Some of the burritos have names like Veggie Punk burrito and the Squatter Punk Burrito or whatnot, and the bartender looks the part, but living only a few blocks away-- this is definitely a great place to come for a good meal. The frozen margaritas are pre-made in a daiquiri machine, and are really great as well. 

I recommend sitting at the bar for speedy service, but this is usually the case for any food joint. During the evening hours the waitresses are tattooed and sexy, but I don't have time for all of that. I sit at the bar and my burrito is typically made within 2 minutes. Not bad!

People saying this is "the best burger they've ever had" probably have never been to Los Angeles or New York, which is understandable. In-n-Out burger in California is exceptionally better, and about a 1/3 of the price of the overly expensive $9.00 Company Burger. A double-double at In-n-out is somewhere around $4.00 and a burger at New York's Shake Shack is somewhere around $6.00. The Company Burger is an overhyped burger restaurant aimed at hipsters with money to spend. There is even a small bar in the restaurant, which was incredibly arbitrary to me. Personally, I wouldn't want to sit in a Wendy's and drink craft beer with friends while the couple next to me is eating a burger and fries. Maybe I don't get out as much as I should, or expand my horizons beyond bars I'm already familiar with and comfortable with, but fast food and a bar doesn't really interest me at all whatsoever. 

More importantly, the food itself was mediocre. The double-pattied "company burger" was wet and soggy with a weird sweet taste. So many reviews have raved about the miraculous "mayo
bar" but the company burger itself already has so many disconnected flavors that the thought of slapping on any kind of mayonnaise to the already overwhelming burgers just sounds like overkill to me. The french fries were decent but nothing special. Kind of bland actually. In the end, I payed $14 for a burger and fries and felt completely underwhelmed even upon the first couple of bites. Next time I'll take that money and dine-in at an Italian or Thai restaurant, spend just as much, but will have an overall greater food experience. When it comes to burgers in New Orleans, I recommend Five Guys or Atomic Burger. Who even eats burgers anymore though?
