Quesadillas named after me? (Peter's Quesdillas) were yum, spinach/cheese was in good balance and seared torillas had nice spicy crispness - decent & proper

Sadness was Disaster of vegan jambalaya - am unsure if they forgot to spice it at all but a blander bunch of overcooked rice and small bit of vege would be hard to find - at $11 entree price, this was poor thru & thru (and now a couple hours later my stomach hurts..)

Fried pickles are fun, and tasty mustard helps.

Service is friendly amateurish, water/iced drinks served in cool mason jars,  coffee was burnt and bitter.

Never crowded, so I wonder how much of food is prepped days/weeks? ahead of time and thawed to order - but no matter, if I survive the night, I'll be happy to walk on by with the bacteria in my gut rightfully kept in check -

perhaps it was the dog... he was missing tonite... where was he?

For Philly this is the only choice...

It's a travesty that for an area with a large Jewish & other forms of loud, hungry mouths to feed, this is the ONLY spot to find a bagel crafted according to old-world norms (thanks to the hard-working, of course, Spanish-speakers toiling continually in front of the viewable kitsch-en ovens).

In NYC these would be OK - the dough isnt all that flavorful, the CC's are a bit salty and not always real tasty/fresh, and the variety of flavors in name does not match their respective tastes.

Coffee service is a pain: creamers lately have not been chunky - somehow they stay below bacteria-happy levels in their little cooler-thing - and the tease of fresher coffee in two usually-empty glass pots can frustrate.

Staff works hard, it turns over a lot, and the clientele is rather brusque on the strange lineup.

The owner seems to be a mensch who strides in quickly at times, swoops behind the counter, barking out some orders, questions - makes a few apologetic phone calls, then takes an order or two mixing in jokes right outta Loch Sheldrake or Monticello.
He might be a better entertainer than bagel purveyor - but in Philly his virtual monopoly is desperately needed.

A plus are the "men's" magazines on display in back of the cash register - showing sexy Israeli chicks with bold Hebraic fonts - this would be a nice style touch at 4th Street Deli !

To sit inside and enjoy a b'fast or lunch bagel one must stake out turf and plant hard on one of the two available seats (plus a Victorian era couch Dateline has postively tested for many things)...

It's more nervy than exciting inside - but the point is the bagel - and the fact so many want them toasted... well, what else do u need to know?

Another Jewish-core establishment, which overarches through chai-bravado to maintain stereotypes of food, personality - and succeeds at times despite itself.

Baked goods are uniformly excellent - babka, h'taschen, breads are yum - the lox, whitefish, pwetzels all look fresh, smell good, not cheap, and shouldn't be!

Eat-in is where diciness comes to play - huge portions don't cover up somewhat slipshod, aloof service... Excuse me, but, just because you pay me to come here - must you be so sneering & insensitive to my gastric needs?

Every dish is overfilled, overwhelming to point of displeasure - get something modest (eggs on a bagel perhaps) and SPLIT IT... thats more than enough!
Food tastes fairly bland but is solid enough - but you are PAYING for a huge portion - those photos on the wall need a lot of glass cleaner.

The chrome and fluorescent lighting when you enter don't equate with Gemuetlichkeit, nor modesty - so take out whenever you can, and leave the cooking to Gramma

ah the attitude!

so cool, so dark, mystery abounds!

but the food is bland - the menu a snore - and the buzz could be yellow jackets teeming outside.

Once was a decent place to eat, with modest pretension - now just tension, reheating, poor service - and pricey!

Yes the cash will flow out, and your tum will fill - but is it worth it?

Nah

Coffee is a litle burnt and treats are hit or miss (muffins are interesting when different berries enter mix, cookies are pedestrian, a little stale / al dente..)

Worst part is the "wi-fI" experience... i think a caf w/o wi-fi is a blessing.. no porn, IM, people writing code for hours to be uploaded, etc etc - a serene, reading/talking establishment...

The fakery of claiming to have wi-fi, then the shock, with winsome smile of "wow - ..." followed by a silly technical reason for why it's not working is rather annoying.

Four times I have asked over past year "Do you have wi-fi.. i need to send an email, etc" and every time staff has said "YES!" Unequivocally!

Every time - nothing!! Router connects, then nothing... once a staff person went into back office to reset something... perhaps the index card order for illogical response... alas it did not help.

I did get a response via email from the owner recently..  friendly a little, more smarmy...

"I am replacing the six year old Wi-Fi as soon as possible.

 The Wi-Fi is a complementary amenity that we offer"

MMMMM - yeah - thank God for yelp!

Really a nice spot for caf in this part of the city... easy to carpark usually during the day as well (try the side streets - free!!)

coffee is yum and not burnt, almond croissants are among best in city (flavorful, nice vanilla taste with ample marzipan)

seating can be tough, as local families love having their childs with them for hours of droning home repair horror conversations...

Owner has  nice brooklyn edge to him - had foresight of making "clients"use password to connect to WIFI - better step would be one hour timer per purchase - and as PW never changes, it doesnt really do much...
 
slightly pricey compared to others in Philly, but about worth it

The thin, middle-ager maiden with hair of magnesium runs the place, along with her golden sleepy sidekick who always lay out in front of the "bar" for crowd control... with the assorted non-talented kooks who stride in to self-fanfare, I feel real safe with the behaved pooch!

What a day when something outside gets his attention!  He roars to life and bellows deep, DEEP - until someone takes him off the leash and shows him the outside world. Today it was leftover Ritt Square wreaths decorations, an awful shiny grey plastic, which were being attached to the lamposts.  Other times it is a loudmouth who bumps his way in and betrays his lack of importance in deed and tone

Once in a while a decent pencil/pen sketcher sits at front window table drawing RUSH-era nutty fantasy drawings circ 1979... he seems happy if duly medicated

Less than half of the people ever have a laptop, almost all the rest read or hit on the proprietora

This keepa happily obliges most conversation attempts - she has a filofax of stories from S Street going back like 20-25 yrs... or so her addition makes it seem... some tales are taller than others

O Yes - the coffee is usually quite OK, bathroom downstairs is life-threatening - and the cocoa quite good.... entertainment!

claim, reclaim, disclaim!

I owe u quite a few dollas - o yeah! the stack of singles would go to the drastic stratospheres... yes i signed with freewilly... and i do promise to pay u back, as I have been, every month til 2525...so help me xxxxx

why do i then leave extra dosh with u in the ether... i dunno, i guess it's the FREE drink one receives whenever one makes a deposit..

PEET coffee is good - and it is me !  Dutch treets!

thank god i dont have to go to wilmington to keep in touch.. geesh - yucckie poo! what businesses will do to avoid having to pay taxes

Ing, my ING - u were one of the first to go pure play virtual/online, your rates were once the tops.. and the potentially delicato in/out  maneuver$$$ have always been ride-a-bike EZ.

And these cafes are nice - (Philly is nicer than NYC's!) but ever since they appeared... well- upon reflection, really since the ING merch machine multiplied to NBA store levels, the RATES offered by the BANK have not been top top notch...
close, but about a percentage BELOW the growing field's best...

Painful to profess, as the Internet experience inside is decent, one computer in five is dedicated to ING business ONLY.. the rest are first come, first squat...

ah yes, the squatters - and the lack of real order as to who gets on, who must hop off... an "honor" system in this town requires a sheriff of ninjac ability..

why not institue a 30 minute timeclock? why not let people who actually give you real business have some priority??

These are mere trifles, my iNG darling - I dont want to upset you!! I don't - please leave my lovely homes alone!

I hope when my ARMs reset, well, you'll remember this kind (of) re-view - and five stars are always a possibility

The waitstaff are pleasant, prices reasonable, and I've seen several down-on-luckers receive free menupickings...
No one prizes smelling, observing homeless folks - especially when the gamut of scorn/pity/rage/guilt infuses your food-filled fork and slides thru the gape into your tummysoul - how uplifting to see a few  treated gracefully here!

The register folks maintain an alien, outer-Kevin-spacey mood... modest snarls, Mona Lisa smiles - nary much beyond dark greys - titanium...

Why would you eat anything beyond breakfast here?
(Rhetorical)

Decent selection of NY papers - marked up a quarter+ or so - I opt to think it's for a good cause.. worthy of  an extra star, don u think?

Where can people turn for decent, true and reasonably-priced Amer-Ital food??

A Warehouse of Splendid Taste!

The cosm of all that is this place - vaulting soaring cathedral space plus-decorated to the hilt with artifacts of fifty-hundred years past.

Interesting old trolley car in center seats 10+ tables, fourposter gold bedframes ring a center VIP area - along the Spring Garden side windows present decent urbanesques extending the tiered, satisfying experience.

The food - the sauce - is fine - above average!

IS the pasta freshly made daily - can u tell the diff??

Simplicity! Complicity!
Pasta with grilled veges, ravioli, etc - mmmmm

Eggplant parm is too bready - the portion on that one range to obscenity.. but not vulgarity!

Unlimited depths to refillabel salad approach speed-of-light travel! Not crazy leaf variety, but you find some carrot, some red cabbage.
Warm sourdough bread is acceptable, spiced butter not so mmm.

O the people you will meet there - likely the only restaurant this size, other than a diner, where all classes, colors, ages, trans-fat-positive or negative converge.

And laugh, and smile, and eat, and seem so so happy!!

Nay-sayers, denizens of popular pretended taste - do stay away!!... once inside your faulty fulcrums will heave you asunder -

Its better that way

expensive and pedestrian - bring your own bland

unappetizing truffle dish

olive oil without taste was better than 
"italian" bread dipped out of closed-down wa-wa

samples of spaghetti w/ scallops showed nothing refined, no taste beyond the chew... same for fish specials served as right triangle shingles

lasagna had mozza cheese a la Polly-O with a couple of roma tomatoes, slice of eggplant and some green napoleanic discs i think made of starchy plankton

small portions at least relieve guilt of either eating or wasting too much

for four , without drinks, bill soaring past $100

i can't believe that this is what the world has been waiting for

tasty and suprising that amid the trestly male prostitution one could devote such care and spice shadings to border(f)landfood

vegg tostadas have a crunchy shell - flavorful corn/wheat mix - and the plant cuts are crisp and balanced... feels good in mouth & later on in the tumm

black beans & rice & guac & salsa & burros & whateva else always surprise... as if you made them (well if u could cook) and you cared about what u ate...

never dull, watch the flowering burgeoning love on 10th street, and enjoy the Scoville scale live - true catholic Mexican !

The days when to experience a diner meant inexpensive nee cheap, and service came quick, chipper ---

Relive it without fright nor tears and enjoy simple over-medium eggs, toast, gentle cups of caf... maybe even w/ barbaric scrapple (pride of Franklinstein) near the Famous 12th Street Testo-Trestle Funzone

It is fun to sit at the counter and see the "oldtime" crewmales work the grill: thin moustaches, slender frames, thickrim glasses, pinkish skintones... clean shaven, always

Waitress is buxomic and hairsprayed. She is spot-on with efficiency of refills, order precision. She proffers few tenderbitten words... clean shaven, always

Cash register womanned by a middle-ager blonde whose delicate fingers work fast thru the three singles breakfast lays u out. The manicure impresses.

If interested in gossip: lots of uniformed and uninformed patrolpeople gather at the booths, and speak unrehearsed about the streets, the patrolhouse, the wives, the indecent.... eyebrow raising.. usually worth the eavedrop & bit more in the cup

parking is ample - but walk among the getting madder crowd - inhale the chromium rust, wonder about mutations via the huge PECO transformers, and just enjoy a great place to start a day

Dirt is vital for proper plant growth.

Earth-shaking botany is way down on reasons why people visit Yelp, so there's no need to overdose my floral background/talents.
I just know - I went to university for a while - that nutrients (nitrogen?) and other yecchy stuff comprise excellent qualitative dirt. 

Probably in the old times, seventy-six years ago, you could eat a decent pile of materielle and not get sick... you might even feel good about it.
These days, who is so certain about anything?

Thru continual research over and under Philadelphia, I have been noting several intriguing sub-varieties of dirt. 
The exact data are to be published soon on my website blog. Please trust that most species are unhealthy - a couple are downright carcinogenic, a few severely poisionous, several quick-into-the-mud pasture piles.

Please don't panic. 
Not all dirt will kill you, nor others on your lists... you potentially murderous lot, you know to whom I refer... I  feel the behind-the-click violence ionizing en masse here - I mean on Yelp - and soon...
(this is logical as there exists no obvious way to berate, vote down or castigate viewpoints and the atrocious reviewers behind them)

do keep that to yourself!

That's all besides the points, I guess. Few people would use dirt to dispatch someone.

So I ate yesterday at Govinda's. 

research notes:
*  Prep areas, tables, servers and receivers of food, floors, bathrooms (sic) possess layered colonies of dreck - fourteen original flavors, never sampled before in this area... a Galapagos for smudge Beagles

* overarching lack of sensibility, confused spicing and stuck-smiling servers may lead to dearths of gastric pleasure
 (the acid rain outside tasted much better in comparison)
 
* Cashish did get absorbed into the collective sponge behind the counters without apparent hesitation.

Thank the lord of your choice for Wild Turkey - smart person research has determined the brown flow to be antidote against many harmful bacteria, virus, mold and spore - I do suggest, I implore you to bring a jigger or two and ingest it immediately after any Govindan maneuvers


Fundamentally, I still believe in dirt - it provides a home for beautiful vegetables and fruits - each dignified and amazing in taste, texture and life, respectively

However, distorting nature to fit one's preferred kingdom seems egotistic, wasteful, hypocritical - non-natural

Imagine a citizen claiming to be "pro-life" took a doll or mannequin-baby and smeared fake blood on its surface - solely to make some awful "point" or whatever

Exactly

Most things dig a proper place in this world, cliches as well. 

mock meat is herbicide 

products of this good Earth deserve proper sanitation

do we need another cult to further muck up our perilous spiritual/culinary situation?

Not quite the caf d' Golden Cote I imagined.

Nearest casino is the coastal Chester Royale, next door is a torture chambre for all sorts of live poultry - and up the road works noted fan of Romance Literature, Geno (the Rainier of bloody meat)

This shouldn't affect my love of RIM - but if you've visited any sparkling beach filled with glam vitality, passionate virtual nakedity and wonderful natural scenery - the road to this locale is troubling.

Once seated, coffee is passable OK, but croissants appear rundown, as if trod on by M. Renault, other foods miserable to non-existant... 
the decor is drab (some regional maps, silly Cannes postcards, overpriced marmelades, the smell of mould)

Much better would be to forego 150-200 visits and instead grab an Air France a Marseille o Aix... 
a croque'd madame, cotton blanket and clacky seabirds fit together much better over there

This is the type of place Alyson thinks I'll get murdered in some day.

At no extra cost, the food happens to be tasty and inexpensive - and breakfast is served all day long. For $4.95 you get a full plate - 3 eggs, home fries, toast, juice, coffee, water (and meat if you want it!)

The people come clean here - pretense minimized to annoying cell phone conversations and equally loud rants at the waitress for her poor description of the soup o' the day.

I asked the hostess what the name "K-Diner" means - and she wasn't sure, but she felt it had something to do with the K Laundromat across the street. Some runes scrawled in crayon along the back wall outside seemed to indicate this eatery was once termed "Meemee's Luv-In Diner".

This place is worthy of a sunny day bikeride - or bus-schlep, if just to admire the nether regions of Philadelphia County.  I don't think shoes nor shirts are required.
Great spot for a coffee or relaxing meal. They are very friendly there and have daily newspapers available. Best spot in Gladwyne, they make the mornings bright.

This came highly recommended by a few people.
Let me start the service was excellent after we sat there for 5 minutes before being acknowledged and given water.  The crab au gratin was excellent, the combination salad excellent, then it starts to fall apart, the filet gulf poisson aux ecrevisses cardinal was dry, the chicken aux champignons was dry and very peppery, but the peach melba was excellent.  Again the chocolate cake was extremely dry and over priced .

Great history and ambience, you might was well try the oldest family owed restaurant in Nola.

Nine table hole in the wall and ohhh soooo good.
I was hesitant at first because the sales person at a local tour company suggested it with a 10% discount card so I thought she was sending me to a connected restaurant and not the best that I was looking for.
We went for lunch that day and the line was down the block we decided we would go the next morning. On Friday and Saturday it's open 24 hours.
We went Sunday morning at 8 ish which was perfect all the drunks from the night before were still sleeping off their hangovers. We were the 2nd table to be seated. I had the eggs lafitte and those poached eggs were cooked perfectly!!! The entire plate flavorful and delicious . I also had the blueberry brandy glazed French toast which was a grilled cheese French toast...Amazing!! I couldn't believe I was eating a grilled cheese for breakfast what a delight.  The wife as usual had her boring egg white scramble with dry toast...she liked it.
The place was cute inside, super clean and the service was excellent .  I would give a 10 if I could.

The blackened catfish special on cornbread with collard greens was awesome . The abita amber beer a local beer was really a good compliment.
The French bread was good.
The wife enjoyed her Greek salad with blackened chicken. The four ounces of wine served to my wife was marginal.  As was the service, nice kid but just not on top of things as promptly as it should be.
The bread pudding was one of the best I've ever had.  The wife loved her pecan pie.

The place is fairly clean.
The food was highly recommended and did not disappoint.

New Orleans has great breakfast places and Cafe Conti is another perfect example.
The place is clean, the food amazing, the service perfect.  Enjoy!!

When you board grab a table and chairs on the port side of boat (left).  This is the side of attractions that the skipper talks about for the first half hour.  The music is fun .  
Overall not a bad way to kill 2 hours in New Orleans on the Mississippi River .

Almost missed this experience based on the appearance of the place.  Don't judge based on looks.  It's not the cleanest place in town and could definitely use a fresh coat of paint but guys behind the food counter are hilarious and so welcoming.
The place attracts a lot of locals and us tourists, everyone seemed to be in a great spirit with all us customers joining in the conversation with the locals.
We went for lunch and a tourist said they are known for many of their dishes but recommended the hamburger.  It was an excellent fresh patty cooked to perfection, our server was awesome and on top of all requests.
I would have gave it 5 stars but the cashier tried to charge me for extra meat....I believe an honest mistake.
Thanks for yelp and the 4 stars they were given we tried it. Don't judge a place by its cover :-).

Worth the hype, worth the wait in line, worth the money.
Ribs were Amazing, perfectly cooked and seasoned.  The ribs were lean and meaty. There is no need for sauce but if you like,  there is a choice of four BBQ sauces sitting on the table to smother all over those delicious ribs.  The pulled pork was excellent, they were out of brisket, can't wait to try it on my next visit.
There is usually a line out the door, it goes fairly quickly but if you want to make sure you get the type of meat you are craving, then earlier is bet then later.  Service was quick and friendly.
I had the green beans (perfectly cooked and seasoned), the vinegar slaw (different) and the applesauce ( chunky, fresh, topped with cinnamon and oh so good).
A huge selection of fountain drinks to serve yourself and if you want an alcoholic drink there is only Budweiser beer, my motto is "when in Rome...."
Don't forget the fresh baked chocolate chip cookies sitting in a basket by the cashier, yummy.
I get it and I loved this place!

The Brewmaster tour for $35 takes around two hours and is completely worth it.  Tim, our tour guide was awesome.
The Biergarten wasn't too bad either, I had the Shocktop salad with chicken which was pretty good.  
Well organized tour. You get a hat and a souvenir glass as part of the package.

Sam our waitress was the best.  Great neighborhood restaurant on the hill aka little Italy .  The restaurant is deceiving from the front but once you enter the restaurant it is much bigger and beautiful than I expected.  The place was completely full on a Wednesday night, and for good reason the food is fabulous.
If I lived here I would eat here weekly.  The lemon chicken soup was the perfect blend of noodles and chicken. The salmon dinner was cooked perfectly, pasta with pesto was good.
The place is clean and it offers patio seating and the prices are good.  Highly recommend. Enjoy.

Excellent tacos, appetizer trio, salads and the premium margaritas!
Happy Cinco de Mayo!!
It is a bit loud in there.

We were looking for a quick bite to eat, The hamburger was really good, nice soft bun, flavorful and my wife loved the French onion soup.  Service was good, the only thing that could use improvement were the uncomfortable metal chairs inside.

Trendy restaurant that has a separate bar area as you enter.  Overall really nice experience, the service was really good and the food was good.  The octopus & shrimp bruschetta fell flat for me, the bread was excellent, the flavor was good, there just wasn't as much meat as I expected. The sourdough bread and flavorful butters were excellent, the cauliflower was really good.  I had the fish special which was good and my friend had the lamb which was excellent.  The wives had the filets and they were both disappointed, the meat was over cooked and too salty.  The chocolate bar dessert was excellent.

Solid breakfast place, open 24 hours. Sitting is only at the bar.  Excellent service and a variety of interesting options:
Breakfast Tacos
Donut breakfast sandwich 
Chicken and waffles
Feeling good breakfast burger
Steak and eggs
And many more options, check out the menu.

Worst experience.  Whatever you do eat before you come to the Opry house.
I asked what their best meat was and they responded beef brisket.  If that is their best.......?
The meat was cold and looked like leather smothered in BBQ sauce.  Eat at your own risk.
If you get stuck their without eating, good luck.

This is a great Irish restaurant/ bar.  The entertainment was excellent, service and the food were good.
I loved the coleslaw that came with the fish and chips, the negative was the fish was undercooked and greasy.
The Shepard pie was good and the bread pudding was amazing!!
Cheers!

Fun, hip place.  Great place to meet and socialize with your friends or business contacts. Huge square bar in the middle, lots of seating, great service and food.  Bowling lanes, outdoor game area.  Can't wait to visit again when back in town.

Loved the pies, we had the great white pizza and a bowl of mushroom soup, which wasn't too bad either.  The service was really good and the band " the Mexicans"  were really good. They played Pink Floyd, Santana and a host of 80's and 90's rock and pop songs in the land of Honky Tonks lol.

Stopped here on the whim while I was in the area doing some apartment tours. And I am so pleased with this place! A full day of apartment shopping made me and my parents hungry and this place was more than generous with their portions! The food y'all. The food!!! No one left hungry that's for sure! We ordered the smashed avocado, and truffles fry pile, ham and Brie sandwich and the Aston hot sandwich. Everything was really to die for!! Y'all  have got to try the truffles fry pile!!! We ate it all so fast there was no time to take pictures (sorry!). I'm sure if o did your mouth would be watering. As soon as the plate got to the table and the aroma of Parmesan and truffle oil hit my nose, my hands were on those fries. No hesitation. 

The beers were also a big hit. We ordered the saison and 2SP up and out hazy IPA. AMAZING!! Will definitely be taking a separate trip to visit their Brewery. 

What a great find!!!

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday dinner. It's now one of my favorite places to go for sure!! The atmosphere of the restaurant was fun and unique. And the food!!! Absolutely delicious. The best part, they give you complementary limoncello shots! Ive heard of complementary bread, salad, you name it. But I've never heard of shots! How unique. It's a little twist that's different than other places and adds all that much more charm to this amazing place. The drinks we fabulous, the main course was fabulous... and the desserts. THE DESSERT! My boyfriend and I ordered the chocolate ganache cake. If you're a big time chocolate lover and your sweet tooth needs a fixing this is definitely the choice for you. Omg my taste buds are watering thinking about it. What I would do for another piece of that cake!! I wish I took a picture to show how delicious it looks but before I knew it my fork was in the cake and it was gone! 

All in all I'd recommend this place to anyone. Wants some amazing pasta? A tasty drink? A mouth watering dessert? Then this is your place! Look no further. Enjoy!

I'll make this short and sweet for you. Go here. Get the Mac and Cheese. And don't forget to enjoy. 

You will without a doubt not regret this choice. Since my last visit, I'm trying to figure out when I can go back ASAP!! Delicious food and delicious drinks! Never had anything like this Mac and Cheese, and my mouth is watering just thinking about it again. You must order this dish! They have a great happy hour menu as well! Enjoyed my time here, loved the food, atmosphere and the amazing happy hour!

Popped into this place for a Friday HH with a group of coworkers. I thought the atmosphere was so fun! An old warehouse building turned brewery with a fun industrial twist! I enjoyed my time here and the drinks were good! I cannot speak to the food as I didn't order anything, but I had other friends tell me their food isn't bad! 

Only one thing to note, as the place fills up it gets very noisy and can be hard to hear your friends. Wasn't a dealbreaker for me but just something to keep in mind if your visit is going to be strictly convo based! So for that I'm giving 4 stars. All in all not a bad place to visit for a HH!

For the longest time I was craving a milkshake. I came across this place because their website mentioned milkshakes! And let me tell you, these are some seriously good milkshakes! You pick a cookie dough flavor and an ice cream flavor, so you pretty much get to mix and match your milkshake with whatever you want. SO DELICIOUS. If you're in the area and have a craving for something sweet, do not look any further. Go here!! 

Their website mentions a quote from a customer about driving from out of state just to come here and no doubt, I believe it! I'd probably do the same!

I visited Dew Point for Father's Day. My family and I had a nice experience in the spacious garden. Beautiful weather and nice music included! 

I know they do bring in a food truck when there is an event going on but we decided to pack our own picnic lunch and snacks which is welcomed by the owners! 

I am knocking off 1 star because there was no guest WiFi and service is fairly non existent - most of the time I had no service at all with Verizon. 

There were no yard games (corn hole, frisbee golf) set up but I attribute this to the current Covid-19 situation so I won't take another star away. I do believe the yard games would have made the experience that much better so I hope they offer this again soon!

My friends and I met up for brunch on a Sunday. 

Drinks: Mimosas were a hit! They have different flavors like mango! They also offer other cocktails and wine. A full drink menu with lots of options. 

Food: Not bad! I wasn't knocked off my seat but I wasn't displeased either. Maybe it was just what I ordered! My friends had delicious looking plates full of goodies. I would definitely eat here again. 

Parking: Plenty of street parking is available around the place! Shouldn't be a problem. I was able to park on. Sunday for free not far away. 

Overall: I was fairly pleased with my experience! Drinks and food were decent. I am knocking off a start because I did think it was a little pricey for what I got (Blueberry French Toast). It was a little lacking in flavor not much filling or fresh fruit served. I also had to ask for syrup. I think the dish would be more exciting if they offered blueberry syrup of some kind. I've had other French Toast dishes that's truly wowed me with flavor and tastiness! Out server was friendly enough. No real complaints other than coming to check on us for drinks and clearing plates was a bit slow.

Best. Sushi. I've. Ever. Had. 

I'll keep it short and sweet for everyone. I'm a big sushi fan. I love it. All kinds. All flavors. Give it to me all. So it's safe to say I know good sushi from bad sushi and mediocre sushi. I really don't have much else to say here except for this is the BEST SUSHI IN THE AREA. Go here. Order. You will not regret it. I've been wanting to try this place for a long time and not am I SO glad I did. The end.

One of the best local spots for brunch in West Chester! But be forewarned: the wait is long and it's a little chaotic inside and hot! All in all I'd recommend this place but give yourself extra time for the wait. 

There's always a wait and it's not an ideal waiting situation! They do not take reservations and it is first come first served, so if you're starving and need to eat right now or else the hangry version of yourself will appear within seconds!! I'd opt for a different spot in West Chester. But if you can wait, wait! Because it's worth it. I am knocking off a star due to the there not being much room to wait. If you don't want to feel cramped and have others in your comfort circle, I'd suggest waiting outside. However, you might miss your name called. At least one person from your party will need to wait inside to listen for your table. 

I'm also knocking off a star for the mass chaos and confusion that seems to go on here. I'm all for supporting the college students with jobs but they need a little more training. The host/hostess isn't great at making sure they have taken everyone's name when they walk in or checking of the person is there for pick up and giving them their order. This probably contributes to the long wait times. I waited a good bit of time before they addressed me and took my name for a table. And I had to ask those around me if they have been helped yet so I didn't cut them in line. 

With all that said and done once my party and I was finally seated the food was great!! No complaints there. It did take a few odd minutes for someone to come over and give us a menu and take our drink orders. Nevertheless, the food did come out quick and was hot and ready! And that's what we're all hear for anyway right? 

Parking: The location is convenient, right on the corner next to the S High St parking garage. There is also street parking out front of the restaurant all along Market St. 

My suggestion for management: I think part of these wait time problems could be resolved with taking less take out orders from DoorDash, Uber Eats, etc. The drivers are running in and out and contributing to the mass confusion going on inside. These orders are also creating longer wait times for those coming into the restaurant to eat. If there was a way to limit the amount of orders that'd be great for those wanting to dine in. Train up your staff so they know how to shuffle customers around efficiently and quickly take their names for a table. A texting system would be super useful. Other restaurants will take the name and number of a party and text them when their table is ready. This way people could wait outside and not be in the way of those coming in to pick up orders or be seated.

Bottom line: LOVE IT! Great food. Refreshing cocktails. 

As big Oyster fans, my boyfriend and I have been eagerly awaiting their opening for months. We came the first night they opened and were pretty pleased with our experience! They were able to seat us straight away but the waitress took a little while until she finally came over to introduce herself and take our drink order. After that she was fairly attentive. 

I really liked how they offered Oysters from different areas! We tried some from British Columbia, Washington State and Connecticut. We also ordered a Mussel pot with red sauce to start, which was yummy! The cocktail drinks we ordered were Awesome with a capital A! They were unique and delicious. I ordered the Cucumber Gimlet. Can I have another?? 

Looking forward to coming back!! Keep up the great service and yummy food/drinks! And please please please consider creating Oyster Shooters as a drink option! No where else in town has them and I think they'd be a HUGE hit. My only minor complaint is that is was pretty noisy inside and hard to hear from across the table!

You have my vote! SO YUMMY. Might be making this our new go-to spot. 

The food was delicious, seriously. Each dish had its own unique twist and was superb. I always say you can tell if a restaurant knows what they're doing in the kitchen if they can cook a good Octopus and boy did they ever! The Octopus app was done perfectly, not chewy, not over done, just right!! I think that in itself sums up everything you need to know about their food. They can cook a delicious Octopus dish, therefore everything else will be good as well (and it was). 

I heard they plan on having a rotating menu and the dishes offered will change from time to time, which is exciting!! Love trying new things from the same place. I truly believe everything they offer will be delicious! 

Only reason I'm knocking off 1 star is because we had a reservation but still waited 15-20 minutes to be seated - bummer!

Wow!! Delicious Gelato. Their flavors are distinctive and tasty! This is a fun place to cool off on warm days and grab a sweet treat.

They have plenty of seating (indoors and outdoors), even a small area in the back to kick back and relax. You could study here, do some work, read a book, etc. Additionally, there is a seating area enclosed in glass for a quieter experience if you're there for study/work. 

Their menu is fun and flavorful! So many options for things to try. The staff is incredibly friendly as well. 10/10 would recommend to anyone looking for a place to hang and enjoy something sweet! They also offer coffee and other desserts as well.

I've been here on a few different occasions now and each time I'm pleased with the food and service! The staff is always very friendly and quick on their feet. 
You really can't go wrong with anything off the menu! One of my favorites off the menu is the stuffed pork chop. The lobster ravioli is at the top of the list as well. 

Wait times can be somewhat long and a reservation a few days in advance is definitely recommended!! 

There are plenty of parking options near by. Whether it's street parking or either of the 2 parking garages within a block!

First, I'd like to apologize for not taking any pictures of this delicious pizza. I opened the pizza box, smelled all the good smells, and BOOM before I knew it the pizza was gone and no pictures were taken. 

I ordered a 12 inch Pear and 12 inch Brussel Sprout pizza for 2 people (we had 3 slices leftover!). Both pizzas we exceptional but if I had to pick my favorite I'd go with the Brussel Sprout (you can't go wrong with either). The pizzas were packed full with toppings, they don't skimp out on you that's for sure! Each bite of pizza was flavorful and oh so delicious. The crust was perfectly crunchy and not overdone or burnt. 

I also loved how many options of unique and flavorful pizzas they have on the menu. I sure had a hard time deciding because they all sounded so delicious. I can't wait to order again! 

Dare I say this might just be my new favorite pizza spot in WC?? Yep - I dare. So glad they opened up shop! If you're craving pizza, I recommend giving Cirillo's a try!!

Lastly, I just want to add how they kept my pizzas warm in the oven while they waited for pick up! I thought this was a super considerate and nice touch!

What you need to know:
Drinks - great
Food - even better

My boyfriend and I started with drinks. We ordered a pomegranate mojito (omg yum!) and a lavender lemon martini (so refreshing!). The waitress apologized for the bar being backed up but I still thought the drinks came quickly!

We both opted for pizzas, I went with an already crafted one while the mans went with a create your own. Both were delicious in their own way! Mine was more on the sweet side as I ordered a Shannon which had fig jam, prosciutto, feta. He created his with (just about everything lol) but it was top notch!! Both pizzas were flavor packed and baked to perfection! 

We also ordered a cheese plate to start, which was fine. Nothing fancy or extraordinary! It was your pretty basic cheese board. However the bread that was included was probably the best part of the whole dang thing. Loooved the bread. 

The wait staff was also very friendly and kind. I really don't have anything negative to say. The only reason I'm doing 4/5 stars was that it was just an average old yummy pizza place with good drinks! There wasn't anything worth knocking my socks off about.

Oooooh baby I've been wanting to try this place for so long!! I wish I would've done it sooner. 

My boyfriend and I stopped here for some bourbon inspired night caps! And boy were they delicious!! The Smoked Old Fashioned was truly phenomenal and perfectly crafted! Tasted like I was drinking a s'mores or sitting by the campfire. Loved it! Our other drink was a Peanut Butter Manhattan, which our bar tender said he concocted just that night. It was very good and I think he did an impressive job (sorry I forgot your name to give you credit here)! We also decided to order a Tiramisu with 2 Espresso Martinis to end the night. Espresso Martinis tend to be our thing so we were excited to try a new place's martinis! SHOOOT. We were blown away. These were the best we've had in WC! Truly incredible. The Tiramisu was good and worth mentioning but nothing exceptional. We've had some yummier homemade and local versions. 

All in all great experience! We will definitely be coming back to check out their dinner menu... we have our eyes on that Seafood Bake...

Hi! Hello. Let me just stop you right here. 

I. Am. Obsessed. My hair!!! My hair. I LOVE IT. My girl Morgan hooks me up. I've been visiting this salon for a little over a year and a half and each time I've left more than happy with my cut and color. 

Morgan takes her time to ensure she is meeting your wants/needs. She keeps notecards on her clients to make sure of this! If you have a hair goal she will do everything she can to help you achieve it! She really is the sweetest and has you and your hair's best interest at heart. If she doesn't think your hair will be able to achieve something you're asking for she will let you know. She wants to ensure your hair is/stays healthy. She is a phenomenal stylist and colorist. She specializes in blondes! Morgan also is very good about making sure you are aware of how much services cost. If she needs to add something or do extra she will let you know that it will be more so there are no surprises! 

I simply just love her and her work.

Check out her Instagram for pictures of her beautiful work @morganleighhair
Second time visiting and I'll be back for more! Ingredients are always so fresh and tasty. The stir fry bowls are deliciously flavor packed each time. Yum yum yum!!!

I just love this place!! I've always had a great experience here! The food is yummy and drinks are tasty! 

Kildare's is a super fun place to hang out and grab a few drinks. Enjoy a sports game on TV, catch up with friends, etc! The inside of the restaurant/bar is uniquely designed and laid out in such a fun way. It really feels like you are stepping back in time when you walk through the doors. They took the Irish pub atmosphere seriously! The wait staff has always been super kind and upbeat. Never a bad experience!! I suggest giving it a go! You won't regret it!

Yum!! Fun!! 

I'll keep it really simple for y'all: The beer is always tasty. The food hits well time and time again. You can't go wrong stopping here!! And you won't leave hungry!

The Social's shaker drinks are so fun!! You get almost 2 drinks out of them. And they are so so yummy!! I'm writing this review about a week later so I forget what drinks we ordered but I do remember that both were delicious! This is a great place to grab some drinks and apps.

Ps. Their wings are lowkey amazing. Sorry for not getting a picture, we gobbled them down before pictures could even be taken and I'm not even ashamed about it. Every bite was tasty!

Looking for a mom and pop place with an upscale restaurant flare in West Chester? Opa is your place! 

My plus 1 and I love ordering the Saganaki to start. You can never go wrong with one of their authentic, Greek Gyros. And their drinks are always very delicious too! I wish I could share a picture of their tasty food but we always gobble it down before snapping a pic! 

You can't go wrong with anything on their menu. I love taking my West Chester visitors here. If you're looking for an authentic Greek cuisine, Opa is your place to go. I wouldn't lie to you!

The pizza lover in my is giving the West Chester Pizza Cafe a 5/5. For the first go round I ordered plain waffle fries and the Vodka pizza. The fries alone were phenomenal and ever so tasty! The toppings on the pizza are generous, the sauce is delicious, the crust is crisp... the whole pizza is mouth watering. They knocked it out of the park! I look forward to coming back and checking out their fry bar options some more of their yummy looking pies. 

This is a fun little place in WC that's not in town but close enough! I recommend giving them a go!

Wow! Amazing sushi. Their all you can eat sushi is a great deal, but definitely come hungry! 

They give the table a sheet that you can check off which apps, soups, rolls, etc. you want. They will give you a new sheet for each additional order. There is a limit on how many specialty rolls the table can order. But they have so many other good options for rolls that it doesn't matter. 

My boyfriend and I drove 30 minutes just to come here for their sushi. One of the best places I've been and I'd definitely come again! Yummy yummy yummy!

Update: We are back! And we got a picture this time!  The Jalapeño Popper is deeeeelicious! Definitely a new fave!! We added a drizzle of ranch on top! Ps. It's also not spicy like one may think! 10/10 this pizza knocked my socks clean off.

Super cute place!! They do pup cups and give a decent size amount. My little boy was so happy and definitely enjoyed his frosty treat. Thank you D'Ascenzo's! 

I had a Carmel Sea Salt which was super tasty too! They also have an adorable little alley with additional seating on the side of the building. I'm a fan and Wiggles is too!!

I've been here twice now! Once for dinner and once for brunch. Each time I've been blown away by how delicious their handcrafted plates are. They offer the typical dishes you'd likely find at other places around town but their's always have a special twist to them that make them unique and better than every where else. Ive always enjoyed my visits here. The wait staff has always been friendly and pleasant to interact with. They are helpful and accommodating as well!

Wow!! I just absolutely love this place! Can I give it 6 stars? 5 isn't enough. 

What you're here for: food. Phenomenal, truly. Everything on their menu is a home run hit. My boyfriend and I came here for brunch. This might honestly be my favorite brunch spot yet. I know for a fact this is my new favorite place for French Toast. Holy delicious! We also ordered the Fried Avocado Benedict and added a drizzle of hot sauce with a side of bacon to share. The Benedict was a master piece of flavors combined with fresh ingredients. Everything was delicious and I really can't wait to come back again and try something new! I just know anything on this menu will be an excellent choice. 

Let's talk vibe and esthetic! The feeling is so chic, natural, warm, and welcoming. There are live plants in every corner you look. Lights strung across the ceiling. Wood and nature vibes throughout. 

Make this your new go-to brunch spot! Give it a try!

I was pleasantly pleased with my experience at Village Whiskey. My party of 2 was able to walk up and be seated outdoor immediately. Food was good! Only giving 4 stars because I've had 5 star experiences and it just wasn't quite there. However you wouldn't be wrong by choosing them as a place to dine!

I don't think they are open anymore. First I tried doing their online reservation from the link on their website, which I didn't work. So then I tried calling the number multiple times but each time it would ring and no one was on the other end or had a pre voice recording that they were closed, busy, etc.

Absolutely wonderful experience!! 

The hostess was super friendly and cheerful upon arriving and accommodating. Our waitress, Francesca, was also very kind and attentive. She was great!! Just absolutely loved her.

The ambiance was warm, inviting, intimate, and romantic. The space was quiet and well insulated so notices and other table's conversations didn't carry. The restaurant was lit perfectly to give it that intimate and romantic atmosphere. 

Our food was phenomenal. We started with grilled octopus and 2 glasses of sparkling. We ordered the rigatoni and duck for main dishes, which were both delicious and ever so tasty! To end our night we ordered espresso martinis without the Kaluha since we don't like our coffee super creamy. We also ordered the tiramisu and it was incredible! Not served in the traditional form but none the less it was great! 

We had a great experience and absolutely loved everything we tasted! 10/10 recommend this place!

Been to Nudy's multiple different times now. I always enjoy my experience! They have sweet and savory options on the menu. And SO many options at that. Pumpkin French Toast? Cinnamon Bun French Test? Ahi Tuna Florentine. Lobster Eggs Benedict! You name it they probably have it. They also have your classic diner options. Their coffee is good too! 

The wait staff is always friendly and attentive. The wait is usually about 20-30 minutes during a busy hour for a party of 2-4. 

This location has a small parking lot out front. It's usually full but you may get lucky and snag a spot! Otherwise there's a parking garage close by and street parking is always an option as well.

Stopped by Stove and Tap's Malvern location for a quick bite on a Saturday during lunchtime. We sat at the bar and our bartender was very friendly and kind. She chatted with us and offered suggestions based on what we like to drink. A bartender who knows their offerings is always a great bonus. 

We ended up ordering the chicken cheesesteak and their burger. Both were good don't get me wrong but nothing to rave home about. Therefore knocking a star off.

However we enjoyed our experience and the atmosphere with our bartender so keeping 4 stars. Parking was easy which is also a good bonus in my opinion.

Honestly, I was not at all impressed with the girls behind the counter. They were unfriendly and came off pretty rude. Their hours are also really tough. There have been multiple occasions where we've said "let's get Lorenzo's" but they were already closed. Big bummer. However their pizza slices are massive and pretty dang good.

Absolutely loved it! 

We ordered Gyoza and Seafood soup to start and for dinner we both ordered a Stonepot. Very delicious!! 

Every one there appeared to be friendly and they had an efficient process going on, balancing take out, dine ins, and the sushi bar. We didn't have to wait long at all for a table or for our food. 

Our server was very friendly and attentive. He accidentally spilled some soup when placing it on the table but handled it super professionally and it was not a big deal at all. He was still a great waiter and we enjoyed having him. 

I'll definitely be coming back and enjoyed my experience! Check them out! I recommend.

I've finally been!! I always have seen this place walking but but I've never been in. My boyfriend and I were in the mood for Chipotle but instead he suggested Taco Mar so we gave it a go! 

The man at the register to take your order was extremely pleasant and friendly! Great guy! He was kind and welcoming. The girl who made my taco bowl seemed friendly enough too, I just didn't have as much interaction with her. 

We ordered a food to go (a taco bowl, taquitos, and burrito). The taquitos were great! Can't speak to my boyfriends order. And my taco bowl was good. I can't say great, it seemed to lack a little flavor especially in comparison to Chipotle. But it was still good and I'd come back again (but maybe try something else)! 

Ps. They are BYOB which is fun as heck!!

HvtXvzLjiwNrW1q38EW0UQ.review_text: Better than a lot of Thai restaurants I had in the city! Amazing food! Definitely try pak per khing
Came across this takeout place by accident. The food was not oily at all and you don't feel heavy after eating it. The place is very clean. The girl who takes the order is so sweet and so friendly!
Finally a great Korean restaurant, long over due! Great food, great service, very nice environment!

While I appreciate the great service, fresh decoration flower on the dish and freebie calendar, I am just disappointed that the spicy soup base was bad. Spicy soup base is probably one of the key pillars in hotpot and they simply don't have it. It is almost like they just use hot water and dump some spicy oil in it, completely flavorless. 

Besides the disappointing soup base, beef is ok, fish is smelly, mushroom is bad and not fresh at all, pork ball is good, fish dumpling is decent, sauce is standard.

Please fix the quality of soup and food before you spend all those money on fresh flower decoration or freebie. People come to your restaurant for food. If you want to charge a premium in Chinatown, at least present some decent good food.

It is no wonder that there was no line on a Friday night :(
I should have just gone to my usual place teado for bubble tea :'( maybe I just didn't have a good luck, but the bubble tea is bad that that I have to throw it away.
You can't beat this place! Authentic good Taiwanese bubble tea, love it! I will never experiment other places for bubble tea again! I'll stick to this one to avoid any disappointment.

Best burrito ever! 

I tried to come here once but parking is always impossible in this area. We decided to park our car at a Chinese supermarket on Washington street and I'm so glad we did. The food here is absolutely incredible and the staff is so friendly. This is gonna be my go to place for Mexican food going forward.

We ordered spring roll, egg roll, pork chop and beef soup, and everything is incredibly delicious. Little detail like the peanut sauce for spring sauce is also amazing. Great job! Will definitely drive 30 mins again next time to come back here.
The food is just ok. However, given there is no nice place in this area, it is sort of your go to place for brunch if you have friends in town.

Service - 2 stars 
Bento box - 1 star
Soup - 3 stars 

Given the quality of food as well as the location, this place is way over priced, very disappointed.
Unlike many other Chinese takeouts, their food is not as oily. The restaurant is also much cleaner than most takeouts.

Simply love this place for always being so clean, offering delicious dim sum at reasonable price, friendly people, great service! This is the only place where I know I definitely don't need to share a table with others!

We moved down here from New York and have been looking for a nice coffee shop in the area. After one year of no luck, we are so thrilled we finally have a nice cute coffee shop in town. What's even better is that the coffee is really good. The ice coffee is cold brewed (the owner should call it out by the way!) and the croissant is just great. At the end of the day, how can you beat great food at good price? The owner is very friendly and I love her risk taking entrepreneurial spirit and story. She also provides free wifi. I hope this place can eventually become those places where you can come in with your laptop and work for half an hour with a cup of great coffee. P.S. If you think her coffee is great, don't forget to tell her that! She took the effort to get coffee beans from Italy!
It's a decent restaurant but the food portion that this restaurant serves seems to be smaller than what the other Han Dynasty restaurants serve in Philly (they are all owned by the same guy).
Their spicy pork burrito is so delicious! Super friendly staff and great food! Thank you guys :)

Food is ok, probably 3 stars out of 5. However, service is horrible. They have no basic manner. We came in during lunch hour when more than half of the restaurant was empty. When we asked how long is the wait (there were about 10 people waiting in line), the waiter just turned away without even responding.
Came here the second time and just love the food as well as the great service! This place is a hidden gem! Thank you for the amazing food.

The lady who took my order was nice and friendly but the food.... is just surprisingly bad. When you walk into a Chinese takeout, you kind of expect similar menu and similar taste (since most of them get their ingredients from the same company) that will satisfy your craving for unhealthy food, but this one's food is just.... bad. If you are expecting some typical Chinese American food from a typical Chinese American takeout, this is not for you. If you are dying for some Chinese American food and just don't have the time to drive a bit further and will eat anything as long as it is something Chinese then sure 

3 stars for the service.
1 for the food.
With the great reviews on Yelp, I decided to give it another try. The staff is friendly for sure but the food seems a bit plain, which is not an issue if you are into healthy eating.

Ordered eggplant salad, mushroom soup, potato dumpling, beef kebab, chicken kebab, and everything, literally everything is delicious. Great service, great price, great environment, perfect portion, and of course fantastic food! Will definitely come back again for the delicious and high quality food for sure! 

If I have to be unreasonably picky, I'd say please use Georgian soda :)

The food tastes so bad and the quality has gone down dramatically after this restaurant has a new owner. It is no longer a place for authentic Taiwanese food but rather some cheap food. I ordered spicy wonton, cold cucumber, pork minced rice, Taiwanese burgers and beef with pepper, and the only thing that is eatable was the cucumber. Avoid their meat dishes, because they taste so bad, seriously worse than those Chinese takeouts. The chef isn't even Taiwanese, so what's the point of coming here? Sad.

I just love this place. Food is amazing and the staff here is even more amazing. The restaurant manager is just an incredibly guy. He is one of the main reasons why we keep coming back. We are here at least once a week!

Making good boba is not easy and that's why many places' bubble tea is undrinkable! This place has great boba. The boba is sweetened with just the right amount of sugar (or honey) and well cooked through. I'll definitely come back again!
Came here excited but left extremely disappointed. Food, particularly shrimp, is low quality. 0 star for the food and 3 star for the staff.

Service is great but chicken tikka masala was very bad. Chicken didn't seem to be marinated and taste so plain. It is almost like they just use boiled chicken breast and dumped into the curry sauce. Disappointed.

Since I learned about this place a week ago, I have been here twice already. I am beyond happy that we  finally have an authentic Indian restaurant, a GREAT Indian restaurant. This place is so much better than many highly rated Indian restaurants in north jersey or even NYC. Great food, and the female owner was incredibly nice too (I saw how she professionally and friendly handled a tough customer while I was waiting for my takeout). Love this place! I am hooked!
Best Georgian restaurant even compared to those in Brooklyn and Manhattan. I've eaten in numerous Georgian restaurants but no one even comes close to them. Everything is freshly made and delicious.
Rice is cold, beef basil is cold. I used to love this place but they start sacrificing quality recently.

[Update] 10/8/2017
I used to be a huge fan of this restaurant. However, I'm getting really sad and frustrated with their deteriorating quality. For example, the chicken dish I ordered tonight seemed to contain some really old and bad quality chicken with terrible after taste. This is the third time it happened in a matter of 2-3 weeks. I hope they are not like one of those failing restaurants who start to sacrifice quality and fall into vicious cycle and then eventually shut down the business.

Really want to like this place but the overpriced food just doesn't taste that good. Wonton soup is probably a 1, pickles are probably a 2, short rib is a 4, dumpling is a 1.

Worst Starbucks employees here. Why would you use ACME employees to cover Starbucks? They are the slowest among all Starbucks I have ever been, and all their cashiers still need a booklet to check every single price for the products you purchase. They love to chitchat and they would still be doing their own thing even when customers arrive. If 8-9 out of your 10 visits suck because of speed issue, maybe there is a speed issue? 

Starbucks, you are not saving any money by installing a mini store inside ACME. You need to have a real store and hire real people who know what they are doing. This is the worst Starbucks ever.

Finally something other than Han Dynasty is in town. They have the best fish in hot sauce, not too much coating with the fish, just simply delicious. Really great food and great dining environment. I also find the owners, a young couple from Szechuan, to be very friendly and professional. The owners seem to have so much passion for what they do. They explained how they brought some of very unique utensils and bowls from China. Love the spirit. Please keep your passion. I'll be back very soon again!
Hot pot soup was ok, soy sauce was too sweet, beef was low quality, seafood wasn't fresh, just an average place for those who are craving for hot pot and don't want to drive into the city.
What a hidden treasure! Love the food here! Great price, great service. Will come back very soon for sure.
Love this place!! This place is a hidden gem, will come back for sure. Thank you for the great food!
Not sure what happened to this restaurant. It used to be so good though the people working there are still very friendly.

Food tastes much better than other diners, so not sure about the 3 star review. The woman at the door greeting people is lovely and friendly. The atmosphere feels very homey, just a nice place to come!

Been to many big name steak house restaurants but nothing compares to this place. Everything is simply delicious, from appetizer to steak to seafood to dessert. I do have to call out that while they have amazing steaks, their seafood is unbelievable! Which is typically not the case in most steakhouse.
Amazing place, probably by far the best hot pot in china town. Very friendly staff, high quality food! Love the fact that we don't need to get up to get our sauce. Will come back for sure!
Absolutely love this place! Super authentic food and friendly people. They won't check on you every 15 minutes but they definitely have amazing food and great staff.
Love this place!! Amazing food! Must try! Will come back again! Great food, good service, nice environment!
Great environment, decent food, fantastic people! Will come back again! Love this place!
OMG, unbelievably delicious food! I'm definitely coming back again! They use good ingredient like chicken and amazing sauces! Will come back for sure again!

I3ywvvRizXINMzOXdYaozw.review_text:
My girlfriends and I went for the early bird special after work.  $10 dinner plate if order placed before 6pm.  

The crab cake with zucchini & mashed potatoes were delicious.  Haven't had mashed potatoes that good in a while.  One of my other friends tried the chicken parm and found that quite good as well.  

The chocolate cake was just okay.  

I'll go back and try it again.

Beautifully restored restaurant.  

Great selection of local/imported beers.  I was particularly enthused by the Belgian beer selection (the wide range of Belgian I have only found at one other restaurant in area - Monks in Philly).     

Food is okay.  First time we went there I had the crab cake dinner, which was bland.  Caesar salad had interesting taste - some may like it and some may not.  Second time I had their beet salad for dinner, which was good.  Salad dressing was light and tasty.  Over cooked the beets a bit however.  Burger was good, but nothing out of ordinary.  

We will go back due to beer selection and continue trying to figure out out which items on food menu are acceptable to eat.

Found this BYOB gem a while back.  Not too much to look at from outside but quaint on the inside.  We order out/dine in at least once a week - standard favorite if we don't want to cook ourselves.

Food is really good.  Think between my husband and I have tried most things on the menu and haven't been disappointed yet.  Favorites are lobster ravioli, farfalle gorgonzola with sliced chicken added, penne abruzzi, calzones, florestina pizza, panini sandwiches, eggplant with veal sausage topping - although not a big fan of the pasta & sauce that is served on the side (sauce is a bit too sweet for my taste).  Balsamic salad dressing is addictive.  

Only thing I'd change - ask for oil/parsley combination that comes comes with bread on side since bread can get over saturated from sitting too long and quality of cappuccino depends on server making it.

We've only gotten two things from this pizzeria - cheese steaks and chicken parm sandwiches.  Always with fries of course.  They have these two items nailed down.  

Never tried anything else since we always opt for our favorites.

The old Macaroni Grill should have stayed because this is not authentic Mexican food at all.  Not even a good Americanized version.  Met a friend there for lunch today.  Only thing that was good was the server.  Margaritas were so so - tasted like they used a powder mix.  My shrimp chimichanga was small & flavorless.  Sides were slopped on the dish so very messy presentation.  My dining friend ordered a combo dish #20 (burrito, taco, chile rellenos).  The chile rellanos tasted like it had been frozen and then thawed - 'twasn't even warm when served and again food just slopped on plate.  With so many other good mexican places close by even if a little bit more expensive - can't say we'll be back.

Food was hit or miss.  The real issue was that we sat for 2 hours and in that time only 1/2 the table was served,  Finally got up & left b/c they hadn't started the other dinners as of yet after repeated reminders from waiters the table wasn't complete.  Ended up at Firehouse down the street & found some other patrons who ended up there too after waiting 1 1/2 hrs themselves.  Unless dinner service improves, this place simply isn't worth the wait.
Food was a bit bland.  Might be explained by the older crowd. Best thing we had was appetizers. Restaurant itself is very cute & cozy.

Restaurant is now under new management but serving same menu.  I found this out after making comment that food is not quite what it used to be & wondering why.  Some of my favorite dishes aren't quite the same- sauces seem to be a bit less robust.  Overall still decent but I find us going there less often now.   Looking for other venues for our weekly comfort food.

Have been to this newly opened restaurant 3 times now (dinner & lunch).  The place definitely has good food & decor, attentive waiters & BYOB is a bonus.  Portuguese inspired dishes is more of a terminology than an actuality.  There are hints of it in menu dish names & a few ingredients but most of menu spans a wide range of typical restaurant choices.
Finger licking good!  Have had both the brisket & pulled pork sandwiches to date with slaw topping.  Both extremely good.  I won't be satisfied until I try everything on the menu.

To be fair we went to this restaurant for first time on Night Market night, so it was very busy.  The good:  1) bartender rocks the drinks - very yummy, 2) the shrimp/feta salad was delicious.  The bad: 1) shrimp/fish ceviche was not good.  Tasted like they simply put cocktail sauce over it & lavished it heavily to try disguising fish that was chewy & shrimp that didn't    make any impact at all.  2) fried chicken with spinach & corn bread salad was 50/50.  The corn bread salad was definitely a plus but the fried chicken was under-seasoned & the spinach overcooked.

I have mixed reviews.  My lobster ceviche appetizer was decent - the lobster was fresh but lacked a certain wow factor ...  the salad/mandarin around it definitely saved this dish.  My husband's calamari tempura salad was really good.  My seafood taba yacki was a pretty bland - the seafood itself was fine but the citrus butter sauce didn't really add anything interesting to dish.  Plus they need to crack the crab legs a bit better or give you a cracker/pick.  My husband's entree of beef, side potatoes & fish salad was definitely flavorful.  The sake menu was a definite plus.  A wide range to choose from.  Dessert - green tea tres leche a bit strong on green tea flavor & my husband's peanut butter/banana/bacon ice cream was a good attempt - to indicate bacon though you need to have more than two bits present.  Overall, dishes seem to be hit or miss.  If I go back, I might just try the sushi bar & see how that goes.  Or just meet people for drinks since sake menu was definitely a plus & atmosphere itself was trendy.

The litmus test of Italian food is whether we could bring my Italian dad here or not without hearing him critique the place.  It passed with flying colors - authentic delicious Italian food.  Went for lunch before performance at Kimmel Center. Definitely would go back and it is BYOB so double bonus.

I dined at Dettera when they first opened and it was a horrible experience.  Under cooked scallops, slow service,  huge TV at bar blasting sports (which for a supposed wine bar was not appropriate) and a staff that was not knowledgeable about their wine for pairings.   Professional restaurant critics apparently agreed with me.  Maybe a year or so later I tried them again during summer when they had their outside dining between building renovated.  'Twas a totally different experience.  Food was good and outdoor seating with fireplace cozy.  To determine if this experience was a fluke or not , my husband and I went back during Jan 2013 restaurant week.  Have to say it was fabulous - amazing beet appetizer, succulent beef shoulder entree and pot of cream dessert that was just right.  They have improved tremendously and we will be back.

The food is very good.  That being said - the service itself needs oversight.  Agee with another reviewer that service was chaotic and many things overlooked (perhaps due to the young wait staff not having much experience).  The chef chatted with the various tables which was nice.  The quality of the food coming out of the kitchen needs to be reflected in table service for an overall good experience.  Otherwise you leave pleasantly full but frustrated too.
