Just visited tonight at 6pm for the first time. It was a terrible experience. And here is why:

-we got there at 6pm and didn't get our food till about 7:20pm. 

-one plate came out about 15mins before the rest of our party got their order. It was a plate of nachos so there was no reason to even plate that order till the rest was ready. 

-we had to sit at a "high top" table in the middle (we were a party of four) and had random couples next to us. The seats are very small and uncomfortable. Not conducive to sitting forever for your meal 

Service was terrible. It seems the servers are all brand new to being a server. Took forever to get a refill on waters and they ran out of coke before 730pm. 

Won't be back again.

We had the breakfast sandwich on the English muffin and they were delicious. We also had a mango coconut handroll which was very tasty. Also a spring roll was strong flavored and very refreshing. We will def be back again!

We came here on Saturday afternoon after going to the Trop for the home show. There were a total of five of us. 4 of us ordered burgers. We ordered them medium well and one ordered well done. After waiting for the burgers to be cooked, they came out and we started eating. However biting into the burgers we found them to be still raw. It wouldn't be a problem if it was pink but the meat was cold and raw inside. Thinking it couldn't be the whole burger I ripped the burger in half and saw how bad it was. The others at the table did the same and found their burgers to be raw inside as well. After getting the manager out there to talk to us she didn't want to take the burgers off the bill. She only wanted to give us 25% off our entire bill. When you go to a burger place and 4 out of 4 burgers come out still raw it is a problem. My fiancée and I had been there before and had a great burger but after this time we will not be back. You can't screw up burgers that badly and think we will be back. It would've been one thing to be still pink but to be raw and bloody isn't acceptable at all.

We have been to this place a few times now. I almost hate to post a review because it's a perfect spot. You almost feel like you are on vacation here. The location is perfect right on the water. The food is amazing. It's hard to find a fish dip at a place that isn't filled with fillers and mayo. This dip lets the great fish speak for itself. The conch fritters are amazing. The peel and eat shrimp are amazing. You can't beat royal reds. We have had the grouper sandwich and they are amazing. The fish is amazing and fresh. You can watch her behind the counter filleting the fish out. I don't want to tell people to go here because I don't want it to lose its charm but it's such great food people shouldn't miss out!

We had been here a few times and really loved it. However the last few times we have been here, we have been let down. The service has been slow, and the food quality has gone down. We have had way better pizza at tikanis. We use to get the deep dish but the toppings have seem to gotten smaller and not nearly has plentiful as they use to be. Maybe in a few months we will try and see how they do.

We have been there two times. the first time we went we went we just ordered off the menu. It was excellent. The second time we went it was all you can eat pizza and it was totally worth it. It was amazing to eat all kinds of pizza. The crust is perfect. The toppings are fresh! Def one of the best if not the best pizza places around.

This is a great place to grab a few drinks. The food here is hit or miss though. We do like the conch fritters. The food though we have had better seafood at other places around the city but for a great casual place to grab a drink this is the place!

We ate dinner here on a Saturday night. I had a water, seaweed salad and a Mexican roll. The waitress kept my drink filled. The seaweed salad was delicious. It even had cucumber in the bottom. It was a nice side with my roll. My Mexican roll was yummy. The size was perfect and very filling. I would def come back!

Horrible service. After we sat down we decided to time how long it took to get service after reading some yelp reviews. It took 9 mins to have someone come to the table to greet and get drink order. After that it took 8mins to bring an ice tea and the smallest sangria glass. We then placed or order and it took 30+minutes for it to arrive. We will not be returning. There are too many great places around this area to give our business to.

We try and come here once or twice a month for breakfast. It is always so good! We always get the mic mic sandwich and depending on what the muffin of the day is we split a muffin. We are always so impressed with the food and quality. Keep it up!

My fiancée and I love this place. We even hosted our wedding rehearsal dinner here. The food and prices can't be beat. Plus you can bring your own drinks and that def helps lower the cost of the final bill. The owners are always so friendly and welcoming. Usually I stick with the gumbo but one night I did branch out and get a special one night of crab and chicken wings. It was one of the best meals I have ever had out to eat. I hate to write reviews for a place so great like this because it could get over-run. However this place deserves all the accolades it has and everyone needs to go here!

I would give this location 5 stars but how can I ?? The location is incredibly TERRIBLE. There is a Home Depot, Total Wine, Nordstrom's Rack, PetsMart, DWS Shoe Warehouse, Sweet Tomatoes, Dunkin Donuts, Rooms-to-Go, Home Goods, a bridal shop, and other stores ALL in the same shopping center. Add in 5 years of road construction to the daily mess and you're setting yourself up for road rage. 1 star off for that. Another star off for the super premium prices that Whole Foods loves to fetch. Sure, your organic black tea is made with imported Arctic glacier water and the chicken in the salad was massaged everyday of its life but should that really command a credit check??? My advice is go to Whole Foods once and take pictures of everything that you want. Next, go to Fresh Market or Trader Joes and purchase those same items for a LOT less. The bonus? you will get to skip the traffic jam.

This place is right up the street from our house. It's a great place if you are craving a home cooked meal. It's not for the diet conscious but it is good cooking. There's a reason it was featured on diners, drive ins, and dives. Their biscuits at breakfast are soooo good! Their eggs were a bit runny,but I like my eggs cooked really well done. I've come for lunch also. Their burger was yummy. I would love to comeback to try their chicken. I've heard great things about it.

The food is ok. But it can be a pain to remember to bring cash to it there. And the food is not worth the effort. It can be a nice place to go for a drink when the weather is nice out. But during the summer it is just way too hot to eat outside. Even with the awnings draped overheard. There are better burger places all around st Pete. So Yelp it up and check out a place that's worthier of your business!

Excellent! We were looking for a place to eat dinner while driving from Sarasota to plant city and found this place on Yelp. We were not disappointed. It's in an unassuming strip mall. We never would have stopped had it not been for Yelp. They don't have alcohol but we saw in another review that you can bring your own, so we stopped by total wine and grabbed a bottle of wine. They even had wine glasses for us. Perfect!

We each got a seaweed salad and then some sushi. I had a mexican roll, not technically sushi haha but I love shrimp. It was excellent! My husband also had two different rolls. Everything was beautifully presented and excellent in flavor. If only it was closer to our home in st Pete. We will be back if we are in the area!

We came here on a whim after dinner. We were surprised at what we found. Tucked in a strip mall is this tiny gem. Sadly we haven't had their food, though it looks so delicious. We had drinks there in their bar. It's a quaint little place with excellent drink prices. If you want a great little bar to go to for some drinks one night don't pass this place up. They have an excellent selection of beers and a full liquor bar. The sandwiches, salads and wraps all looked delicious. We want to come back and try their food. But on drinks alone, this is a great place to go!

It's a Walmart. We come here for the decent prices on groceries and such. However the clientele here at this location is not the best. If I am walking alone in the store, I am almost always cat-called at and approached by random creepy men that ask way too personal of questions. But prices they are good. Some times we do still end up at publix because the shopping experience is so different.

I love coming to this place for lunch. I'd come for dinner but they don't have my favorite menu item at night. It's the gigantic shrimp burrito. It's so huge. I shouldn't eat the whole thing but it's so hard not to eat it all. When we come, we usually get chips and salsa. Their salsa is very delicious. Also a pitcher of sangria. It is pricey. It it's great. It's very refreshing for a mid day pick up. I would love to try other items on the menu but I can't seem to stray away from the burrito. It's that good. Def try this place out for lunch. I don't think you can go wrong.

While my husband and myself didn't particularly like the food here we could tell it was fresh and would be great if we had liked tat type of cuisine.  We tried it for something different one night. The hummus was excellent and the pitas were so warm and delicious. The food wasn't what we were expecting however if one is looking for this type of place they will love it. That's why I'm giving it 4 stars. Not my cup of tea but still I can tell the quality is excellent.

My husband and I went here a few weeks ago after having dinner, when I was craving something sweet. I love having dessert after dinner so this was the perfect opportunity. We opted for 3 of the minis since we had just come from dinner. At a dollar a piece they were reasonably priced and the perfect size. We got the coconut, carrot and chocolate cake. Normally I'd be all for the chocolate caramel but it seemed very dry to me. The carrot was my favorite out of the bunch. They have excellent comfy chairs that recline back. It is very relaxing. They also have beer and wine so it's an excellent place to go for a small dessert and drink. Def check it out.

We came here for lunch on Black Friday. Based on the reviews we were excited to finally try it. However we were disappointed. We had the grouper fish sliders that were he special for the day, fried oysters and my husband got the boneless chicken bites. My grouper sliders were just ok. The amount of fish was lacking. There was so much more bread and toppings than actual fish. The fries were ok but that was because they were super salty. The fried oysters were good. The chicken bites were very dry. We were expecting so much more. If you want excellent fresh seafood the go to Maximo. They can't be beat.

My husband and I went here on Saturday night. We were excited to try it based on the great reviews on Yelp. However we were very disappointed. It took a bit for someone to seat us even though there were plenty of tables and staff walking around. 

Once we sat down, our waitress came by and gave a sigh when we just had water to drink. We ordered our food and I got the chicken red curry. Not once did the waitress ask what spice level I wanted. That is whenever she seemed us worthy enough to stop by our table and check on us. We never saw her and she rarely remembered to fill up our waters. When my dish came out it was barely lukewarm and the presents of peanuts was overwhelming. Every bite contained peanuts. Not something I want in my red curry. I was so upset with my meal. We can't figure out if maybe people in the area just don't know good Thai food or what it is. No matter what we will not be back. Service was horrible and the food wasn't hot or fresh.

I came here with my parents on the night before they opened. We were very impressed with the food. We got three different sandwiches. All were unique and delicious. The dressings and soups are all made in house. The beer cheese soup was amazing. We tried 2 of their dessert donuts. They were excellent but def super sweet. they would be a treat just every so often. I can def see coming here after shopping at the mall for a comforting meal. The place can get very loud and be a bit overwhelming. I do wish they had a Coke freestyle machine like you see at a lot of new fast food places instead of just a regular soda fountain machine. I can def recommend the flying pig sandwich. It was loading with meat and cheese. A home run! If you have kids, this is an excellent place to go. There is something for everyone because they have many options of breads (even a gluten free option) and many cheese options (including a vegan option). You can create your own sandwich as well. So you can do meat or no meat. As well as add lots of veggies!

We went there for my birthday celebration with my parents. We loved it. Plus how can you go wrong with all you can drink mimosas??? The best part of this breakfast buffet is the small plates. Not only do they have shrimp, crab legs, mussels,oysters, a carving station, and different salads, but they have small plates. These are excellent. Instead of different items being out on the buffet, you order certain items when wanted and its brought to your table. Today we had a chicken dish, blackened swordfish, lasagna and seafood dish. Everything was excellent plus it wasn't getting cold on the buffet line and no one was breathing or touching it!

The deserts were nice and small. Perfect to be able to try a lot of different items. The bananas fosters was excellent. My husband who isn't a huge fan of desserts even loved it. The mimosas started at 11am. We ended up doing mostly champagne by the end of the meal  

The view can't be beat. It's almost like being on a cruise ship, looking out onto the water. Plus inside there is lots of wood and fireplaces, it's easy to forget that you are in Florida. We will def be back for Sunday brunch. The value for what you get can't be beat!

It is a great way to spend a fun low key night out. I went with another friend the other night. It was a lot of fun. My final product wasn't quite close to what the original looked like but it was a lot of fun and a lot of laughs. It's great that they allow you to bring your own snacks and drinks. There was only one male in the class, however our instructor was a male. So it is def a female oriented crowd. Don't let it stop you though from doing a date night here. I look forward to coming back and trying to paint another piece of artwork.

My husband and I love coming to this place for pizza. The pizza is so good. We always get a spicy chicken sausage and pepperoni. We also split a carafe of wine. It's not the best wine but it's yummy and you can't beat the price. This is some of the best pizza in the area. They never seem to be super busy because it's on the side of the mall next to dicks. So while maggianos and such have a long wait, we usually can get right in here. We have had lots of pizza all around this area and this pizza is very consistent and delicious. Also sign up for their VIP email club because you get a free one topping pizza for your birthday. It's an amazing deal!

My husband and I have been here a few times. We found this hidden gym about a year or so ago looking on Yelp. We love coming to this place. It is in a converted old motel. It looks a bit shady but you have to stop and check it out. I always go with the wet burritos. Amazing. The chips and salsa is always fresh. The burrito is the size of the plate and very filling. But they are so good I almost always end up eating the entire thing and being stuffed by the end of dinner. 

I have had their sangria and found it very refreshing and delicious. The prices are on point with other Mexican restaurants. We have a Mexican place right up the street from us but we always make the extra effort to come here or D'Mexican. If you want awesome Mexican, do yourself a favor and check this place out. You can't go wrong with anything here.

We came here on the way home from thanksgiving dinner. Not a lot of places are open on that day so it was nice to find one. We did have the place to ourselves. They had a lot of different options of cider and mead. The bartender was very knowledgable about them both and was helpful in answering any questions we had. To pass the time, they had Cards Against Humanity. Got to love a bar that has games. They offer flights and glasses. The flights are nice to try a lot of different ciders and meads. They also have a few craft beers to pick from in case you don't want to drink cider and mead all night long.

We went here a few weeks ago. I had bookmarked this place to try for breakfast. We had a short wait when we arrived which is usually good when a place is busy  there was one large party and we ended up at a table that was oddly placed near the front door. So when people are waiting just inside the door they were brushing up against my chair. This could probably be changed by reconfiguring the layout. The cash register is in the middle of the place so when people go to lay they had to go there or worse when they wanted to be put on the list. It should be in the front to make things flow a bit. The food was good but nothing special. I had ordered the scramble and my husband got the yogurt and fruit bowl. They didn't even come out at the same time. Oddly enough his took the longest. Another mark against them was at one point my husbands coffee cup was empty, for a good 10+ minutes. Our waitress never checked on us so he went out on his own to find a coffee pitcher and fill it up himself. They seemed to be short staffed but it's a small place and everyone running around should always be checking on drinks. It was an ok breakfast but we have had better. Sadly we can't figure out what all the great reviews are for.

My husband and I stopped here while we were riding on the bike trail. It was a very convenient stop. Our waitress was very nice but that's where the positive review stops. We started with the fish spread. It had too much mayo in it. Plus all the side items that come with it just try and add flavor to it. The fish spread should be able to stand alone. Sadly it doesn't. After we stopped here we continued to Dunedin and we had some of the best fish spread there. It was full of fish and barely held together on the cracker. You could taste the fish with every bite. We also got wings. Not good again. I had bbq and they were just coated in a sweet bbq sauce. And by sweet I mean overly sweet. I love sweet bbq sauce but this had that fake bbq sauce taste. We def won't be back. We will pass this place to continue to eat at Dunedin when on the trail. Maybe we caught it on a bad day but there are too many other great places to eat at.

Based on my meal I would give it 3 stars. However everyone else enjoyed their meals so I'll give it 4. We started out with the fish dip from the check in. A bit too much mayo, but my husband has made me a fish dip snob haha I had a blackened grouper sandwich with fries. There was very little blackening season on my grouper. The fries however were excellent. My grandmother had the grouper sandwich fried and I believe that's the way to go with the grouper. Skip the blackened style and go all out with the fried fish! My sister in law had the fried chicken and loved it. It was a full half chicken. It was a ton of food! Needless to say I wasn't super impressed with my grouper sandwich, but everyone else in our party enjoyed their food. So go and check it out for yourself!

My husband and I went here for lunch on Father's Day. We got married in Jamaica back in October and try and find great Jamaican food around here. Very hard to do. While this was good...it wasn't out of the ballpark delicious. But if you haven't been to Jamaica, it is good. We had a hot beef patty (it was good) and then my husband got the curry goat and I had the jerk chicken. Everything had good flavor but there was just something missing to put it over the top. In a pinch we would probably go back. But if you are looking for decent jamaica food it's good.

Amazing. I had the pulled pork sandwich. I couldn't stop raving about it while eating it. Hence why I don't have a picture. It came out hot and ready to go and I dived in. I loved this place. The beer is decently priced for cans of craft beers. And I love a place with outdoor seating so I can people watch. And the people watching didn't disappoint  my husband also got a sandwich, the jerk chicken, it was good too but I think mine was the winner. I couldn't put it down. If you are looking for a place to sit and eat a good sandwich, check this place out.

Absolutely the best Jamaican food i have had here in the states. Run don't walk to this place. Don't let the horrible parking and very shady location stop you. Except maybe don't go at night alone haha my husband and I were in Jamaica in October to get married and the jerk chicken ruined us for all other jerk chicken. That is till we found this place. Even walking in felt like we were back in Jamaica. We got curry goat and curry chicken and ate it in the car as the ac is barely working if at all at the place and no seats really. After we polished that off with lots of praise, my husband went back in and got an order of the jerk chicken. Oh man, I can't describe the amazingness that was in each bite. We couldn't stop raving to each other about how it was just like being back in Jamaica. If you don't like spice then maybe not for you but it has been a long time since I have had a meal that I can't stop thinking about. Definitely check this place out. It is totally a hidden gem. I'm sure everything on their menu is a hit!

I really liked the look inside of the bar area. I'm a sucker for pallet wood on the walls. And they have a ton of it. The beer selection is very nice. I liked the big windows that looked into the brewery. It's not super close to where we live but I would definitely go back.

I love this place. Whenever my husband and I are craving Cubans or just an easy meal we come here. Best Cuban around. I try and only eat half since they are so big that way I can get two meals out of one sandwich, however I can never stop eating the sandwich. It's just that good. I am sure everything else on their menu is great but I can't stray from the awesome Cuban. This place can be packed when there is a Rays game so be warned. But it's def worth it!

This place is amazing. If it was any closer to our house we would be eating here a lot! This was some of the best bbq I have had. The pulled pork sandwich is always my go to at a bbq place and this didn't disappoint. While eating it I kept saying that we would have to come back soon and also bring my parents who move great bbq. You would think it wouldn't be so hard to find great bbq but it is. Most is tough or bland or just not fresh. If you want great bbq then def check this place out.

My husband and I have given this place way too many chances. Somehow we just don't seem to be able to hit the place to get the great food that everyone else races about...except the first visit. The first visit was amazing. The second visit they didn't have food ready for lunch and the 3rd visit they weren't open(and that time we brought friends with us). The 4th time was this past Friday. Bbq sounded good and we had found a coupon to save a few on the sandwich so we figured we would try it again. My husband's ribs were so burnt there was barely any meat left on it. My pulled pork sandwich was just ok. I had to add flavor with the sauce. The meat itself was just "eh". No real flavor. The Mac and cheese was decent. The baked beans were the usual. Sadly it just wasn't enough to wow us like everyone else seems to be. We've given them plenty of chances but sadly it doesn't live up to the hype for us.

We stopped here while we had to get my car worked on. You can tell this is a new outlet mall. Everything is kept up nicely and has a good amount of stores. If you are looking for an outlet mall and don't want to drive down to ellenton then check this one out.

My husband and i had been here before it changed hands and it was horrible. When we heard it was under totally new ownership we decided to try it one last time. We were pleasantly surprised. We had a fantastic dinner with yummy margaritas. We have since been back a handful of times. Every time we have had a great meal! The only "complaint" is sometimes the side of rice and beans that comes with the entree is cold. But the main entree is always delicious. It is way better than the old place. Even if you have written this place off because of how bad it was, give it one more try!! Plus their happy hour specials are great!! Have a margarita for me!

We had passed this spot on previous rides on the pinellas trail and always wanted to try their breakfast. So this past weekend before our trail ride we did. It didn't disappoint. I had their French toast and it was fantastic. They had a selection of fresh baked items which we didn't try on this visit but can't wait to try on the next. The scones looked amazing!

We have been here two times while visiting the area on our bikes. We love this little bar. They sometime have yummy fresh popped popcorn to snack on or you can buy some delicious fish spread. The clientele is friendly and the bartenders are as well. They have a decent selection and their Yelp check in offer is fantastic. If you are in the area you need to stop in!

Tried this place on a Friday night. When we first arrived it was pretty busy but it died out pretty fast. To the point where we even asked what time they were closing because it seemed really empty for a Friday night. I had their red ale and it was quite delicious. I didn't try a flight because I was happy with my red. But my husband enjoyed trying a few different ones in a flight. It will be an excellent addition to the other breweries in the area even though it is a bit further away from the others.

I had been wanting to try this place since having their food at a yelp event. The location however isn't too close to where I live. Luckily I was in the area recently and grabbed a quick bite. It was delicious. The guy that took our order was new and so that was a bit time consuming but the food was good. The burrito I had was delicious and full of flavor.

Iy7gBdaaM291508wqoqzVw.review_text:
Tuesday special lunch chicken salad pita was very disappointing. Almost tasteless content, except for the decent pita. I should have had a real sandwich or a soup, but I always try to have something different or featured. Not again here at B. B.

Chocolate espresso brownie was very good on day one. Nice texture and flavor, even for a non-coffee person. By day two it had lost its oomph, and was barely edible. Find a friend or two and consume the entire brownie when it's fresh.

Oatmeal raisin cookie was the opposite. Loads of raisins, but on days one and two way too flaccid and crumbly. By day three it became more crisp and enjoyable.

The young man behind the counter was unintelligible. I had to ask him twice to slow down and repeat. Even then, it was tricky. My hearing and brain are fine. He needs better training before he can manage a busy lunch time counter in this loud place.

I purchased a ciabatta loaf to be used for dinner. It can't be sliced in their machine. Bread was fine, although a bit bland. Much better in french toast two days later.

Late lunch on beautiful sunny coastal day while traveling. Several other diners were with dogs on the large patio with seats in both sun and shade. Warm welcome by hostess, who brought bowl of water for our poochie. Service was prompt, and food arrived quickly. My wife had delicious seared tuna dinner with tasty chunky vegetables and astonishing sweet potato fries. I had excellent salmon burger on fresh brioche bun with really good salad inside. Tomato vegetable soup was peppery and better than average. This is a destination restaurant for locals and tourists, and we can't wait for another chance to eat the amazing sweet potato fries.

Large birthday group at long table near east entrance. Very good service and food. We ordered mostly lunch items instead of brunch, and everyone was pleased. People want to repeat annually. My salmon with potatoes and veg were well prepared and a little bit peppery, but that's okay. A quality experience from start to finish. Wish they had more dessert items non-dairy except sorbetto.

I have eaten here twice before. First time the pasta and mushrooms were the best, but seafood stew was way over-seasoned.

Second time was outdoors on patio for happy hour. Some of the very best happy hour food ever, especially the pizza and soup.

When it cools down a little bit I'll return for more patio happy hour food, plus possibly a beer.

UPDATE 9/20/14: Happy hour meal with three companions yesterday afternoon. Staff were attentive, helpful, and professional. We ate out on the lovely patio as the sun set behind Armani to the south.

Beer was fine, drinks were okay, soup was tasty but not hot, chicken salad was somewhat dry, garbanzo fries and calamari were yummy, and pizza was disappointing. Probably our last happy hour at Tavolino, although we continue to recommend it with the good choices for both food and drinks at amazing prices in an attractive atmosphere, with live piano musician.

UPDATE 8/16/15: Delicious lunch birthday celebration. Place was *very* quiet on a hot Sunday afternoon. Outstanding service from a waiter new to us. My chicken dinner was the best of several that I've ordered, including outstanding potatoes and spinach. My wife's veg sandwich was disappointing for the first time. Three other friends thought their food was very good to excellent. 

Bonus! Birthday desserts complimentary to all three celebrants. My wife and I split an order of the three best sorbets we have *ever* eaten: two berries and a very puckerish lemon. These sorbettos alone are worth coming to Tavolino.

Been here many times since opening years ago. Just had dinner as party of four tonight. Dining room ridiculously loud. We ate out in the patio. Much better, including sunset views and ability to converse. Water misting system kept us cool on a warm late summer evening until 8:30 departure.

Service is pleasant, professional, and proficient. Menu items are plentiful and diverse, with nothing pretentious. Two of us ordered the trout special, one ordered scallops and rice, and one ordered beef dinner. We mostly cleaned our plates and enjoyed our entrees. My trout and veggies were a little bland, but it's always nice to try the nightly special. My wife's scallops were excellent, she says.

Calamari appetizer is outstanding. Prepared perfectly, and large portion. I don't typically like or order it, so tonight's was best ever for me. All four of us shared it.

I had a light local beer that was great for a summer night. Arnold Palmer drink and after dinner coffee were disappointing for my wife.

Two shared special peanut something dessert that I didn't try. My chocolate dessert was very good but not great, although it is a signature dish at Wildflower.

This place does a good job of satisfying locals and visitors.

Pleasant patio lunch last week with four friends. I had baked potato chips this time, that I don't recommend over regular chips. Salmon special sandwich was good. Will order it again next Friday when I eat at Oracle location.

Lunch on patio yesterday with three friends. I had turkey wrap. Over-seasoned and a bit dry. Will not order this item again. I have eaten here five times, and I really like PJungle. Dog friendly on patio. Good service. Large and generous portions. Each time I try something different. Some meals are better than others. With such good value and great location, I can forgive occasional duds.

Returned with two others for dinner tonight. Baba ghanous appetizer was different than in the past and not better. Won't order that again. Place was very busy for a Wednesday night. Two servers were really moving fast, and did a good job, but they could have used some help in the dining room and on the patio.

Friend had spicy bean burger with potatoes. She liked and ate all of it.

Wife had fish salad. Tuna was not prepared properly, and salad dressing came too late. She was disappointed.

I had salmon dinner. It was good, as were smashed potatoes. Had grilled veggies also, which were okay but unremarkable.

I'm glad PJ is so busy, but we have had better dinners there in the past.

Four of us had dinner here last night. We decided to eat inside in spite of lovely night because mosquitoes are numerous this year for a change, and people smoked on patio last time we were here. We were only people in large middle room. Easy to talk, in spite of music that no one was listening to.

Tempura veg were well prepared and tasty. See photo below.

Shrimp curry with veg was really good.

Soup with fish and shrimp, plus rice noodles, was excellent.

Eggplant with garlic was a little bland, but still tasty.

This is a good restaurant with a diverse and creative menu. 

Service was fine too.

Just had brunch on the patio today, a beautiful late October Saturday. Easy nearby street parking if you can back into your angled space. Great location at south end of 4th Avenue, adjacent to downtown. New streetcar trolley stops very close by. Comfortable chairs, plenty of water on the table, and exceptionally friendly servers. Bizarre misting fan creates wet, windy environment when day becomes too warm and buggy (the latter is rare).

Wife and I had poached eggs, roast micro-potatoes, fig tartine, olive oil mini-cake, and coffee. Food and drink were excellent.

We definitely will return, and bring family/friends. Coronet is excellent addition to growing food scene in the area.

Three of us ate early dinner here a few nights ago. Megan is an excellent server. We sat in the little room on the left, just past the toilets. A bit too easy to hear conversation at adjacent tables, but the air conditioning was not intense in that room.

Split personality pizza was great. One half had shrimp with goat cheese, and the other half was loaded with mushrooms. Crust was best I've had in Tucson: crispy and chewy. See photo. 

Other two dishes were pepper loaded with chicken meatballs and smothered in tomato sauce, plus eggplant parmesan. Both were good, but not outstanding like the pizza.

Had lunch with new friend on the covered patio yesterday. She had Friday salmon special salad, and I had Friday salmon special sandwich, plus regular potato chips. Staff were friendly and helpful. Chairs were comfortable. It's nice to eat in their hybrid outside/inside space at ambient temperature.

I realized afterward that in future I need to ask for the bread to be warmed or toasted. Cold bread surrounding warm salmon isn't my favorite. Suggestion: offer toasted/warmed bread with all hot sandwich contents.

We have eaten here *many* times with friends, and C. P. is consistently good. Two nights ago we had big WAR WANTON soup for four people, plus eggplant sauté in garlic sauce. Yumm. But eggplant was not fully ripe, and we got slight MSG headache a little later, probably from the soup. I know they don't use MSG, but I think some of their purchased ingredients have it.

Previous time with total five of us we ordered a bunch of stuff to experiment, items we had not eaten before. Noodle dishes were extra good with skinny rice noodles. Tiny salted spicy scallops were a little peculiar, but I liked them. We will continue to try this method due to their large selection of menu items.

We have eaten here several times. Food is good to very good, and definitely unusual for Tucson mall restaurants.

Yesterday late lunch the sun was streaming onto us as we sat on the outer perimeter of the patio area. It was cold, but we were bundled. In the past I thought it would be weird sitting there with mall shoppers walking past on the other side of the black railing, but it was fine.

Wife's chirashi bowl was spicy and tasty. She ate most of it and had the rest with dinner leftovers at home.

My bento chicken box was yummy. I had ordered the salmon box, but when the hot chicken bento arrived I was hungry and didn't want to slow down our meal experience. The chicken bento was better than I would have predicted, including nice variety of veggies and other meal items.

Out waitress, Megan, burst into action when we told her about the missing salmon as I neared completion of my lunch. Two minutes later she appeared with a full salmon bento, but I said no thanks to her heroic rapid response to the kitchen's error (not hers).

We will return, especially to eat lunch outdoors in the sunny Tucson winter season. The hostess turned down the **LOUD** music at our request, so ask. Dogs are not allowed on the patio under any circumstances.

Went for guys lunch yesterday. All three of us enjoyed our meals. Lunch specials are fabulous bargains. Food is delicious and very fresh. Service is excellent. Room is attractive and easy to converse. Chairs are all wood -- supportive and comfortable. Will definitely return for both lunch and dinner. Will also try carry out, living just 10 minutes away.

Another terrific meal at WGarlic in its funky, humble location. Evening was cold on Sunday but the large enclosed patio was heated fully with attractive and efficient propane monsters. Service was slow but friendly and efficient. The place was bustling.

Wife and daughter shared super yummy mussels [ see photo ] in delicious sauce, then the cabrillo dinner. Plates were cleaned and lips were smacked. I ate the excellent stuffed salmon special that was larger than the front section of the Titanic. Enough remained for a full lunch on Monday. Plate included soft rice base plus veggies and a salad. Would have appreciated more potatoes and less kale in the hot veg segment, but that's a small grumble.

We have dined here many times at lunch and dinner. Will continue to do so. We had a ton of ideas of where to eat on Sunday, and WGarlic was the best choice by a large margin.

[ Sorry I took a bite out of my salmon creation before snapping photo below. ]

Sunday early afternoon. Sparkroot is quiet, yet full of calm customers, most on computers while sipping and relaxing. Sun pouring into upstairs loft, where three of us sat and discussed improving downtown cuisine scene.

Wife had Americano (pretty good) and daughter had pour over (nothing special). Notwithstanding coffee non-excellence, we really appreciate having Sparkroot where it is and how it is. Will continue to keep this place in business, especially on sleepy summer morning and mellow Sundays, when parking is free and plentiful.

Hint: pastries are better elsewhere, or home made.

My wife wanted some sit down restaurant pizza after we toured the central arts district galleries last night. Impossible to find parking on Congress Street near a famous pizza place. So we headed home and went to Z-78 for a quiet, tasty pizza and soup experience.

Their house tomato cream soup is splendid. Our attentive waitress helped me order a custom pizza: caramelized onion, mushrooms, pesto, and goat cheese over marinara sauce. Crust was thick and chewy; a bit too dry for my wife's taste, but well-prepared overall.

Glad you were there for us, Z-78.

Chewy, gnarly, hand made, fresh, great location, good variety, friendly service, East Coast style genuine bagels arrive in Tucson -- finally. Tell people about the Joint. They need customers lining up from Oracle Road. Tried raisin and poppy today. Slightly under baked. Took them home and toasted them to perfection, cut into halves. Extremely filling and tasty. Great with real butter, and also with crunchy almond butter from Trader Joe's up the street.

First time eating happy hour food here. Have eaten lunch and dinner at Wildflower many times. Four of us sat inside. Noise wasn't too loud with the dining room less than half full. Quieter outside, but too stuffy and hot this time of year for outdoor dining in the afternoon, even if their misting system was running full blast.

I wanted to try something different, so I had asparagus bruschetta, bbq chicken tacos, and crispy shrimp with veggies. The latter was the best item I ate. I should have had a bowl of soup instead of the other two dishes. Shrimp was batter fried to perfection. I typically don't order or eat fried anything, so I'm glad I branched out.

Service was good. Price was reasonable. Parking was easy. Gelato shop was steps away for cool dessert on a scorching late afternoon.

First time in the new hilltop location. Definite upgrade, although not as intimate as at St. Philips. Outstanding service. 

Bread was amazing, and I am really fussy about bread. We sat in the main dining room between two pillars so the four of us could converse. All three of their locations have been noisy, so be aware of this ahead of time when reserving.

My wife and I split the lunch seafood soup. It was better than ever before, and we've eaten it often. Generous split portion, and excellent value.

It was raining (hooray) that day. On a typical sunny day the patio looks inviting. Will try it there next time. Well done, Vivace.

We've eaten dinner here several times. Tonight we were guests of old friends. Arrived early when not many customers were there yet. Rock music was LOUD throughout the interior, mostly from the 70's (Billy Joel, Van Morrison, similars). Asked for music to be turned down, and it was a bit.

Staff is young and pleasant. Extensive menu. I ordered wood fired salmon. Other three ordered trout. I tasted the trout. It was better than my salmon, which was bland. My mashed potatoes were a bit cool and dull. My waffle style sweet potato fries were the best thing I ate, in addition to the trout. My chicken orzo soup was okay; somewhat spicy and rather tasty.

We shared a flourless chocolate cake for dessert. One portion was sufficient. I kept thinking WHY DIDN'T WE GO TO WILD GARLIC GRILL instead? Far superior food and dessert and waaaaay quieter.

I complimented the manager on his staff and food, and asked him if in future he can possibly choose a different genre of music, such as classical or jazz early in the evening, especially for the *old* crowd of early diners. Nope, he said. I'm the only complainer from thousands (his words) of customers over the years. And "it's part of our concept," or something like that, meaning they like the classic rock LOUD to attract and retain a certain type of customer.

Not us four. This was our last time here. Food can be good, chairs can be comfortable, staff can be professional, but the music makes it unable to hear or converse for older people.

Best meal of our entire vacation. 

 We just came back home from spending two weeks eating delicious coastal California cuisine.  We needed a place to stop and have a decent meal on our way south before we got to Los Angeles because we were spending the night down in San Diego. 

 My wife used yelp to find this exceptional and authentic joint as we headed down the hill from Los Olivos.  We ate outside on the modest front patio area which is very dog friendly. I ordered the fish special and my wife had a scallop pasta dish.  From the salad to the spinach to the pasta to the seafood to the potatoes every bite was explosive and delicious. 

 This humble eatery and deli is definitely a local's place. Once the traveling public finds out about it watch out. It will be on the radar instead of under it.

Charming new pastry, breakfast, and lunch spot; much needed in downtown! Very helpful and friendly staff. Nice variety of tasty desserts and savory items. Good coffee. Parking is tricky during the week so plan ahead if you are thinking about meeting someone. Much easier to park on the weekend.

The large and attractive main room is enjoyable for sitting except the seats themselves are not comfortable. If you have a bony rear end bring a cushion.

We ordered several different flavors of pie and chocolate desserts. All were tasty. The chocolate was extremely intense. The crusts on the pies have sugar on the top which I do not prefer so if you are ordering a custom order of pie request removal of the sugar.

Great location when you're attending a performance at Fox Theater next door. If the show begins at 7:30 make your reservation for 5:30. Parking is easy on the street or in an adjacent lot. Service is *unbelievably* slow at this restaurant, so be extremely patient. Food is good. I enjoyed pasta with seafood, plus minestrone with pesto (it's white, not red). Friendly and attractive ambience with comfortable chairs and quiet acoustics for easy conversation. But remember about the glacial service.

Stopped here on the way back from a driving trip. Pleasant welcome. Ordered four dinner items carry out. Prepared fresh in 20 minutes. Hot when we got home --- eaten quickly. All gone. Curry was just right not too spicy. Pad siew tender and flavorful. Glad it's here.

Mixed experience here today lunch. Service friendly and professional but arrival of food was  V E R Y  slow. What was problem in kitchen?

Nice jazz vocal music playing on sound system. 

Appetizer Brussels sprouts were flavorful. Main courses were tasty. Chocolate bits dessert was delicious with lovely presentation. 

Cioppino was unusual. Fish and seafood items were well prepared. But the base was more of a THICK spaghetti sauce than delicate cioppino broth or similar. No bread is provided so you need to buy $$$$$ bread to assist with consuming the thick and intense seafood sauce creation. 

Suggestions: faster food delivery, include bread, lighter cioppino base. And provide cushions for the uncomfortable chairs. 

Mercado is alive, finally. Check out all the shops there now.

Best gelato in Tucson. Way better than Frost. Excellent and classy style and design of this upscale shop in an unusual location. I tasted two flavors of sorbetto and two more of gelato and they were gooooood! Strong recommendation. Friend had capucinno and he loved it. Can't wait to go back and enjoy more delicious flavors. Keep this place in business. Make it a destination. Bravo, Giovanni!

Tasty taco special yesterday featured perfectly cooked shrimp with a watermelon glaze. Enjoyed every bite. Rice on the side was a bit ordinary, and they can make it more tasty I hope. Service was friendly and attentive. Give this unusual storefront cafe a try. Breakfasts look good too. But bring your own booze.

The vibe definitely is hipster and trendy yet this is a high-class establishment. Better to eat indoors than outside. No soundproofing so bring your outside voice for inside talking. I had the chicken and mushroom black rice stirfry for lunch today and it was very tasty and perfectly prepared, especially the mushrooms. My wife had the salmon Benedict and it was just fine except there was too much balsamic vinegar oozing over the eggs. Good desserts--cookie and pie.

Challah bread. $4.75. Serious disappointment. Looks good, but that's it. "Tough, tasteless, and salty," according to my spouse, who loves challah bread (normally). No egg was ever within a mile of this challah, which is supposed to be an egg bread, light and luscious. How about, for the same price, half the size and twice or more as good, loaded with eggs, at the very least? We really wanted to enjoy this challah, but it is more of a blallah. Are those really sesame seeds on top, or just chunks of salt? "Sold to me as sesame, and there were none. If I knew it was just salt I would have got a poppy seed loaf."

WHOA, said the owner, in a quick Yelp response to me. She apologized for the error. We were given a pretzel bread by mistake. Hint from me: double check before you leave the store to make sure you don't get a pretzel bread when you want a challah.

She arranged for a replacement challah to be available today. We picked it up and ate leftover turkey sandwiches with it.

Ordered the seafood pasta special last night. Companions had shrimp scampi and salad. Latter two unremarkable. My dinner was amazing. Explosive tastes. Had my food customized with wine sauce instead of alfredo. Excellent preparation and presentation. Portion just the right size and mix of gnarly, thick, juicy handmade noodles and seafood combo. Bit heavy on the black pepper and cayenne, but I survived. Packed a punch in every mouthful. Sat on heated patio, which was fine on warmish and windy early winter evening. Service was okay, except dessert took forever to arrive, and it was not worth the wait. Get there early. Crowded solid by 7:00 on a Saturday night.

Farmers market. Last Sunday. Rillito Park. Early arrival. Hot morning. Requested pesto pizza with goat cheese substitution from FIAMME booth. Certainly. Baked fresh and HOT in 12 minutes. Delicious. Beautiful to look at. Scrumptious to eat. Six hearty pieces. $12 good value. First time eating their pizza. Will definitely do it again and again, plus visit to the restaurant. Extremely agreeable staff and baker. Thanks.

This place has a serious problem. We really like Asian food and noodles, but we don't eat pork, beef, or very spicy food. Everything in the noodle/soup menu has pork, beef, or is spicy. Oops. We chose the wrong place. (Keep reading.)

We ordered and ate a plate of duck that was somewhat tender and mostly chewable, plus pan fried pot stickers and fried spring rolls. The two appetizers were tasty if a bit greasy. The duck didn't have much flavor overall although some parts of it were better.

That's not the problem. The problem is that *nowhere* on the menu did it say we could have had shrimp and chicken instead of beef or pork. Nowhere. Only in offhand conversation with the friendly staff person did we learn this substitution is possible, by accident, after we had eaten.

If we had known that in advance we would have ordered their signature noodle/soup with chicken and shrimp. It took us most of the afternoon to regain our gastric equilibrium after what we did eat. 

Hey, NOODLEHOLICS! Have a big sign on the wall and a big notice on your menu that shrimp and chicken area available, please.

9 out of 5!

I live around the corner from THE PARISH and - gasp - today was my first time eating here. I was told the food is too spicy and everything tastes like bacon. WRONG. The food is outstanding and the flavors are exceptional. 

I had trout with fries. Best ever both. Perfectly prepared and HOT from the kitchen. Generous portion. 

Wife had pasta with lobster sauce and seafood. It was very tasty, she says. I ate most of her saucy pasta and WOW it is amazing. I'm going to order a side of that pasta each visit. Best pasta n Arizona. No contest. 

Daughter had two dishes - oysters and frog legs. Oysters were her favorite in lemon butter sauce. Frog was good but not as great. 

Friendly and efficient service. Easy to talk. Banquettes on south wall okay for very straight back sitting only. 

Will definitely return and recommend. Will bring two large groups in for Sunday brunches soon. 

Bravo, chef Travis and crew. 

See four photos also of our servings.

Four of us geezer techies just had delicious pizza, sandwich, and salad today for early lunch. Food was great. Staff are outstanding. Location is good, right next to Trader Joe's. I created a white garlic, goat cheese, onion pizza that was super yummy from crust to topping to mouth to tummy. Will definitely return. See two photos.

Sorry to be a party pooper but I can't recommend HS. Our entrees were tasty, BUT--

The noise level is unbearable. 

Chairs are uncomfortable. 

Group tables are not large enough. 

The waiters are incoherent attempting to describe certain items. 

Portions are dinky and prices are stratospheric relative to the actual value. 

Side dish offerings are pathetic. 

Over $30 for a piece of farmed salmon with not much else is insulting. 

Menu is too limited for people with any special food concerns. 

Substitutions? Don't get me started. 

----

Positives are --

Attention to beverage levels is good. 

Bread is fresh and compatible with the main courses. 

St. Charles streetcar location. 

Desserts are good not great. 

----

We had two other outstanding meals at NOLA restaurants that are waaaay better in every feature than HS. You will also.

GO HERE FOR LUNCH. Sit in the sunny inside spot because interior is dark. Food is some of the best in NOLA and everywhere! Staff are charming. Location is exquisite. Spend the afternoon or morning on a self tour of nearby GARDEN DISTRICT wowzer. 

FRIES PHENOMENAL. 

FISH FABULOUS. 

SALADS STUNNING. 

SANDWICHES STELLAR. 

Nuff said. Top quality everything.

Some hints. 

Make a reservation. It gets full at dinner. Or go off hours, early and late. Better service and less noise. 

IT'S LOUD! Wear your hearing aids. Another reason to go when it's not packed. 

Food is delicious but salty. Have some orange or apple slices in the car for the way home. 

Favorite items last night were fish pot stickers, green beans, grilled eggplant, and lamb skewers. Seven of us shared nine yummy dishes at a round table.

Ask for silverware and napkins as soon as you sit down because otherwise they may arrive after your food.

Your hot dishes come to the table as they are prepared so don't wait for what you think will be your favorite. Just dig in the and other stuff will show up soon.

Get here early. 8:45. Line will soon reach past Broadway. Wear a big hat. Park in the shade. Bring sanitizer and tote bags. Help Don with his canopy. Buy Don's mega seed and half a locavore. Skip the walnut unless you make French toast. Go home and eatttttt!

Delicious food from a charming place. We had a big lunch sharing the chicken eggplant tomato rice entrée. With super yummy baba ghanouj. Will keep trying different stuff including the kebab next time. We were actually down at the Loop Trail down the hill and we had no idea if the meal experience would be worthwhile getting food from here but we picked it up and yum yum yum.

Ordered yesterday from the car after loop trail walk. Easy to use online menu. Picked up 20 minutes later. Hot and fresh. Clean and efficient. Reasonable prices. 

EGGPLANT WITH BASIL. CHOW FUN SHRIMP. STEAMED CHICKEN DUMPLINGS. WHITE RICE. 

Delicious. Especially the eggplant. Good portions. Will have leftovers for lunch today. Will get other dishes next time and keep exploring.

IyLBcbpdOP-MjBeDSzdjEw.review_text: Was good when it opened has gone down every time I've gone. Good for the area, but if you are looking for top notch, visit Pho Quyen on West Hillsborough.
Like any other Chinese buffet. Nothing good about it. Below par food, and they curse at you in Chinese behind your back because you don't understand what they are saying anyways.

Some dishes are Amazing, some are below par. Great portions for low prices. Lowest place for Thai tea in the area. Nice and very friendly staff. Overall good, just find your favorite dish. Plus specials every Monday if you text their messaging advertisement.

Service is slow at night
Prices are higher than average
Atmosphere was oriental and comforting
Food was above par
Overall is lacking in most aspects but the food makes up for some of it.

Service is decent, could be better
Prices are cheap to decent compared to others
Atmosphere was odd because you have the sushi chef staring at you constantly
Food is above the average sushi. Even comparable to Kobe Steakhouse's sushi
Overall it's a really good place, could be better if they opened a bit earlier.

This place doesn't deserve my normal review type. Always a disappoint meant every time.
The Chipotle on Countryside is a better choice.

Service is slow and could use a lot of work
Price is average for any barbecue joint
Atmosphere is about the same for any bbq place
Food is just average, nothing more nothing less
Overall they could put a little me effort in to make it a better eatery.

For some who is Chinese and has worked and owned Chinese take outs. This place is the only Chinese place I go to. I've tried others and they were a disappointment.
At least this place is average, average is still better than terrible.

They have not disappoint me so far. Everything has met my expectations for a Five Guys Joint.
At this place I've always gotten fresh fries and fresh burgers.

Was Five stars first time I go, but disappoints more and more each time. Stayed a consistent three starred rating until the last time they poured water I. The broccoli cheddar soup. It was more of a drink than a soup.

Service is slow like any other Korean restaurant in the area 
Price is much higher than Korean places in the area.
Atmosphere is nice and homey
Food is probably the best in the area
Overall it is very close in comparison to one family Korean restaurant but has just that one upper notch in food.

Service is slow like all Korean restaurants in the area
Price is average for most Korean restaurants
Atmosphere is nice and comfy as well
Food is on par with Korean food, nothing short.
Overall it is a close tie with Sari One Korean Restaurant but just doesn't have that little wow factor that Sari One has to offer.

Service is not perfect but well above it
Price is amazing for its portions versus other places
Atmosphere is bright and clean
Food is at a minimum average, at a maximum almost heavenly addictive (certain foods better than others). 
Overall a well liked and frequent often place. Only complaint is the Shrimp has decreased dramatically in size, otherwise it would of been FIVE STARS.

Service ranges from below to above average depending on your server
Price is very affordable compared to most restaurants
Atmosphere is bright in the day and dim at night
Food is above average but somewhat salty. 
Overall this place has great food at a good price. Although it is very addicting, be prepared to drink lots of water to counter out the sodium intake.

Let's start out with this place cracks me up.
Service? What service? The servers are dancing/horse playing or giving each other massages. I refill my own drinks. Word of advice, double check your bill, they charge you extra or beg you for tips.

Price is actually very cheap compared to other Chinese buffets in the area. Just don't bring kids, very not children friendly

Atmosphere.......Look at the whole building. Honestly how much do you expect?

Food actually decent if you come at the right times. Very small window time frame of good food. 
They say they open til ten but they no cook no more food for you after nine because it too late(Chinese accent)

Overall the chinos no likey you they likey the dinero. No Bueno no Bueno. Honestly look at the exterior building, how much do you even expect? No tip no service. Best quote is "aye papi, no propina para me?"

Honestly, best IHOP I've had (I've had a lot).
What makes this stand out more than others is the servers. Most of them go out of their way to make sure you are happy. (As long as your server isn't Paul)
No biased judgement, pure experience, Paul has been the only one to disappoint me so far.

Service here is always pretty good. Most of them will do what they can to make sure you're satisfied. 
Food here is honestly a hit or miss situation. At times it could be finger licking good, or a "wtf is this" moment.

It's hit or miss on everything. At times your drink is perfect, sometimes it is half full or they didn't mix it right or something (Hit or miss).
Sometimes they run out of straws or run out of cups or run out of sugar. (hit or miss)

This place is honestly hit or miss on food and service. 
If you got a good server and chef, everything will come out fresh and happy.
Most of the time though you get servers who ignore you or leave your food sitting there because they are too busy chatting with other people.
Or most of the time your cook will give you frozen chili or stale fries even cooking with no gloves on.
Stay away if possible.

This place is getting better and improving. The employees really strive to bring you satisfaction. 
Give them a chance and let them know if something doesn't suit you and they will help.
Plus they have Thai tea!!!

Service is decent, in my opinion it is kinda annoying how servers rotate and check on you every couple of minutes.
Price is cheap with all the competitors on sponge dock.
Atmosphere is quiet and kind of hot.
Food is really mediocre at best, all my fried foods were way over fried, over battered, greasy not really edible. The Parthenon gyro is edible but not good, the meat was well over cooked and tough and chewy.
Overall it's cheap and edible if you're willing to settle for low quality.

Went after 10:00 for happy hour.
Service is nice, they are a little slow but nice how they don't keep bothering you.
Price is cheap compared to other sushi places. It's really cheap during happy hour.
Atmosphere is a hit or miss depending on where you sit honestly.
Food is amazing for its price.
Overall I frequent this place often. At happy hour you can get rolls for about 5 dollars each. I believe the place is run by Thai people but I am not sure. The food isn't perfect, if you want better go to some place like Kobe. But if you want just some cheap good food then this is the place.

This is the first time I've seen a place that deserved a 5 star to now a 1 star. I've been regulars here and know all the staff members. I literally used to come here everyday since it was convenient for the way home. It went from 5 stars to 4 stars and now it deserves nothing more than 1 star. The quality of the food is failing(burnt edges of meat, tiny or half of shrimps). The quantity went from a good hearty meal to half portion sizes. One of the best workers Alex left the place. It's now fill with incompetent and untrained staff. Owners can never seem to make your order right. Sunny side up becomes well and crispy or burnt. I'm gonna boycott the place for a bit and maybe it'll go up. If it was only once then I can understand, but after many chances resulting in failure it needs and intervention.

This place looks nice and has a modern atmosphere. The service is better than average. The price is decent.

The problem I have is with the food. Gordon Ramsey would be really upset with this place because it is LACKING SALT!!! Everything I ordered is FLAVORLESS!!!

Simply put, if you're wanting to drink alcohol and hangout, then this place is good for you. But if you want food, I wouldn't recommend this place.

Bunga Raya, the name itself drew me in to try it out. The food is sub par at best though. It is opened by Chinese people in attempt to come up with a modernized Asian Fusion. All of the food are edible but nothing stands out. Considering their prices, I don't recommend the place for that reason alone.
Overall if you've got money to blow for non standard Americanized Chinese food brought up a level then this is the place for you.

I live close by here so I frequent this place often.
Their food is authentic and good!!!
The problem is how long it takes to get the food. 
I understand Chinese so I hear them talking and their problem is that they're understaffed. The chef/owner is constantly swearing and shouting because he's overwhelmed and the owner's wife/server is on the slower side so it is hard for her to keep up.
I keep going back to this place only because of their quality of the dishes they make. Even if they're backed up, they don't rush and push out a mediocre dish.

What can I say? 
Always busy, always fresh.
Better than the chipotle on 19.
Only thing that could of used help is service.
Felt more rushed than normal.
Overall good experience.
Will be back to see if it goes up or down.

Definitely one of my favorite Whole Foods on the east coast.
Hot food has its ups and downs depending on the day.
Usually always a great array of produce.
So far only had one negative experience.
One of the cashiers threatened me regarding mixing nuts together in a bag.
They were of the same price and same mixed nuts genre.
I apologized and said I didn't know and will pay for it separately.
He word for word said to me, "If you do this again I will charge you the highest price"!
All in all I just avoid him and go to another line now.

New fresh addition to the Pinellas area.
Went in for lunch on a Friday and it was pretty empty.
*Notice*
1. This is a Chinese BBQ opened by Chinese people.
If you have been to normal Chinese BBQ elsewhere like 99 hotpot in New York, you will understand.
2. You are cooking your own food regardless of whether you get hotpot, bbq, or both.
This right here shows the difference between Chinese and Korean BBQ. In a real Korean BBQ they come and cook/cut the meats for you.
3. Lunch menu is cheaper but doesn't have the more expensive foods that you might want or see.

Now about the food itself. But the Hotpot and BBQ food isn't bad. The food taste fresh hands down no questions asked. The BBQ meat needs to be marinated. If you've ever had an unseasoned steak, that's what it taste like.
My advice to to grab some of your favorite sauce on the counter and marinate it yourself. Don't get me wrong the food is good, but if your going to be paying the price and you don't eat much, then by all means make it taste the way it should be!
Now for the service. I really think it needs work. It was dead on a Friday afternoon.
When I was present I saw that they hire non Chinese employees as well. Well our server she was great. Attentive, made sure we got more food constantly.
She wasn't the knowledgeable regarding the actual food but it wasn't a problem. My biggie with was her attitude. Even though she was trying to be sweet and calling people honey, she had the meanest and saddest look to her face. Like someone died but not close enough for her to cry.
That's the end of that, now for a run down of how it goes.
You go in sit down and decide if you want to cook BBQ or Hotpot. Then go grab some veggies at the salad bar and sauces at the sauce bar. Come back and start cooking away.
Personally myself I will not come back for lunch since I don't eat that much and I can get higher quality food elsewhere. I might come back for dinner since they have a wider array for selections. 
Overall it is a nice addition to the area for those who haven't experienced it before. If you've been to NYC or LA you've had better.

THIS PLACE IS SEAFOOD HAVEN.
It's been awhile since raved about a place so much.
I've have Poké before in New York.
Authentic ones and wide array of ones.
It's been so long since I've felt excited eating food.
I don't know how to describe this place further.
I've never had better food than this in Florida.
On a scale of 0 to 10 it's a 20!!
This place is LITTT
Hole in the wall treasure.
I can't emphasize this enough, if you are an avid seafood eater and tell quality and fresh, you will enjoy as much as I do.
Now I'm done with my spiel.
The price isn't bad considering you're getting seafood.
Only if you're piling on all the good toppings, it might go up to the 20s.
Atmosphere is small, but that's what makes it good.
They've only been open a few months and are expanding.
If you don't hit it you miss it!
Just awesome people over.
Ps be nice and tip them.

This place has gone down a lot since the last time I've been here. I don't know if they've changed owners or something. 
The lady in the front is plain rude. Food was bland or over salted. The best things were mediocre.
I had high standards for this place but I won't be coming back here for awhile.

Food wasn't bad. Better than a lot I've tasted.
Personally I believe this place is sort of like an acquired taste.
Had I'd have more of Lebanese type foods, this restaurant would have excelled.
But since this isn't my forte, all I can say is that it's not bad.

After deciding to wait a bit and letting the place have some time to get used to opening, I finally tried this place.
I didn't expect much since it's Florida.
A lot of people were complaining about it being flavorless, personally I didn't have that problem. It tasted fine and the ingredients were like the standard norm of ramen. 
My beef with it is the pork. See what I did there lol. The two slices of pork were burnt black. Nothing like I've ever tasted before. Gave it a rich flavor though, which I kind of liked. Another thing was the broth was too greasy which didn't appeal to my liking.
Lastly overall I didn't like the wait. Even though there were no people I had to wait a substantial amount of time to receive my food.
Good food but some minor improvements would help.

This place is okay. I've had many different Pho from all around the states.
There is a Pho Quyen right down the street. Personally for me that is a better place, but my girlfriend disagrees. She thinks this one is better because it isn't as salty as the other one. For me I think this VN's broth is flavorless and the stock is much better at Pho Quyen. 
Someone here mention about the meat being low quality and I disagree with that. The meat I had was fine and I actually preferred it over the other place.
It's not bad but it's not good either. I'm very indifferent about the food. I've had better but I've had worst. My problem I feel is that they sacrifice quality for quantity. I'm six foot 180 pounds and I didn't finish the food.
This place isn't strictly Vietnamese and I feel it's because of that, it isn't as good as it could be. Same feeling when I'm Chinese but I go eat at a authentic Chinese place but it is cook by nontraditionals.
In my best opinion, this place is a lot nicer than Pho Quyen.(there's a strange guy in a white shirt that always stares at you with a weird look.) For service come here.
Lastly to finish this review off, they best and most authentic Vietnamese restaurant is Tasty Pho down in Pinellas Park. That place is bomb! Plus the boba tea taste so much better. #QualityNotQuantity

I don't understand all the hype about this place. I came here based off of a recommendation but it's far from even meeting my expectations. It wasn't bad but it wasn't good. More mediocre to me than anything. Honestly I would choose Mike's sushi or Kobe's sushi over this place. They do have a slightly wider variety but not really. A lot of their rolls are similar, for example most of their special rolls contain jalapeño, which isn't a normal sushi ingredient. Variety is good but don't sacrifice quality for quantity.

This place goes down every time I come here. The first time was amazing. But they keep making small changes that is making me not want to go back anymore. The last one being that when you get the combo meal; the rice is now inside the box instead of a separate pint of it. Plus they seem to be running out of items more and more each time as well. But this time they ran out of the Ninja XL chicken which is the signature dish. How do you run out of the most popular dish? Plus they were out of calamari as well. They are also putting less and less I've in their drinks. When it is 90 degrees out but there's no ice and you're drinking room temperature tea, it's not good. I'm taking a break from this place to hide them some time to get their act together. I'm from New York, where the tea originated in the states. From Kung Fu Tea to GongCha to Quickly to Coco all the way to Mi Tea. I know tea and they are running the KFT name.

Came here all excited to try it out. 
Low and behold they were closed due to some AC problem they were having.
I get it; technical problems happen. But at least post a temporary notice on Google business or something to give others a heads up. I drove nearly an hour to try it. Wasted my time and went to Chewy Boba which wasn't better. 
Very disappointed and will stick to Kung Fu Tea next time.

First off let me say I would classify myself as a Bubble Tea Master. Having tasted Bubble Tea from all around the world and from coast to coast of the United States. 
I've never had anything sweeter than Chewy Boba. It was so sweet my teeth started to hurt and I couldn't drink it. It felt like 80 percent sugar, 10 percent tea, and 10 percent boba. 
I really don't have much to say besides the fact that I would never come back here again.

This place has completely changed. The owners aren't the same family they used to be. The quality of everything has gone down. I will have pictures to show for everything as well. Korean food is very well known for their filtered water. Well when they brought me the carafe to pour from, the didn't wash it and there were dirt all over the lid. The cups smelled like chemicals. The food portion became less. They normally put lots of fish cake in the tteokbokki. The food was cold and unappetizing. I will not come back here again. Do yourself a favor and go to SaRi One

This place has really gone down. The food has gotten terrible. The menu is getting smaller. They tried remodeling and it went downhill from there progressively.
I went one to get Duck Leg Egg Noodle soup. It's my favorite dish and always get it. They hired a new cashier that told me they didn't have it anymore. I questioned why since it still had it on the menu. All she was able to say was that she didn't know she was just told they didn't have it. What does that even mean?
I get the beef combination instead. It was super salty and felt like I drank pure salt. I was so thirsty afterwards from it. They ran out of peanuts for the spring rolls. Not only that, the spring rolls got smaller and smaller because they are barely stuffing it. 
I will no longer come here and will take my business down to Tasty Pho in Pinellas Park. I suggest you do the same.

Nearly perfect!
This place is always packed and now I know why. The the food is superb! Everything is great, the people are nice, fun atmosphere! Pricing is a little expensive for four dollars a taco but it is well worth it. My only complaint is the food got cold really quickly. I am not sure if it was because it was sort of cold in there but after my second taco, the rest of it was all cold.

I want to start off saying that this place is not the same owners it used to be. I've been coming to this place for 8 years. It has always been a great place to get authentic Korean food as it was family owned.
The last three times I tried it; it had been subpar at best. With that being said I will not be returning to this establishment again after this last visit. The food was no longer the same. 
They mixed up sugar with salt. Decreased portion sizes. Dirty cups. Lowered food quality. To make up for all of it; they now use some abstract dish ware in attempt to brighten up the ambiance.
I will now make the trip down to Sari One even though it is further.

A hole in the wall take out Chinese restaurant.
The ownership has changed multiple times and I believe this is at their best.
The issue is their best is really only worth about two stars. The food was greasy and soggy. Everything was overly sweet, even when it wasn't a sweet dish to begin with. The reason it got two stars instead of just one, is solely based off of the fact that they have a more extensive menu versus your standard Chinese takeout. The problem is that the food was terrible in every single dish I tried.
The wait was terrible as well. I ordered ahead on the phone and was told 10 minutes. When I arrived and let them know if my presence, they told me it would be right up. But then someone who came after me, had ordered food and got it before I did. After that multiple people kept coming inat first kept picking up their food, but mine wasn't ready until near another 20 minutes. I get that it's was busy but don't tell others a shorter time if you can't make it by then.

I want to start off by saying there isn't a lot of dim sum places in the Tampa area. With that being said this place isn't as bad, but it is far from being good. 
The food took forever to get someone's attention to order, the cart barely had any food, the wait to get seated was unreasonable with the amount of tables available.
I grabbed nearly one of everything in the cart and ordered a bunch of random food from the dim sum menu. 
Just to note that I've had a lot of dim sum from New York and California. This place isn't even comparable in the slightest, but with the limited options in the Tampa Bay Area, I would visit again if it is on the way and I have a craving for it. Otherwise there are a few better in Tampa itself versus St. Pete

It's a chain store Kung Fu Tea. What more could you ask for? Welp it's also Token Ramen like the one over in Riverview. It is not like the one in Tampa on Dale Mabry where it is Cheers Cut and Kung Fu Tea. The good part is? They have a lot of the food there that they also have at Cheers Cut. The bad part is, the quality isn't the same. I'm a big fan of seafood so I always get the fried squid and fried shrimp.
Although the sauce is the same. They dont offer the spice flavor option and also the breading is lacking. It is still good but it is slightly different that you would notice on your palate. 
The ambience is similar to the one in Tampa but it is a darker theme to it. The are some games that you can play as well. 
This is not like the one in Tampa. They would actually put the food on plates and give you silverware here. The Tampa one just puts everything to-go. 
Also don't forget to try the ramen as it is pretty decent for its price and for being in Florida.
The cons: the only thing I didn't like was that the mince meat rice was lacking in flavor and meat.

I am a big fan of Panda Express but this location is one to avoid. I got some food from here to-go and when I got home to eat it; the portion size was literally half of what they usually give you. I get the same thing everytime I go. Noodles with Walnut shrimp and Beijing beef. Normally when I go to the one in St. Pete or the one on Waters in Tampa; they would fill it up with noodles  and place the shrimp and beef on top. It would be a lot and I would have leftovers for the next day. This time it was so littlle that I finished it all with no leftovers and I was still hungry. Not only that. The food was so cold that I had to heat it up in my microwave. The problem is this panda is the closest to me; how was the food so cold? 
I will attempt to give this place another attempt but if it isn't up to par with the Pandas in the area, I would be going to other locations in the future.

I've never wanted to give someone a negative review before. This is the first time. The atmosphere is terrible. I went with a group of my friends and as they went to seat us they sat us in the back of the restaurants. As I sat down and peeked around, it was all African Americans sitting in the back section, I was the only Caucasian since I was in the group. As I went up to grab my food I noticed all the other races sitting in the front. This is wrong on so many levels. 
Next all the food was cold. I asked this Chinese guy walking around like an ape or gorilla but he was no help. We each ate not even a full plate each and left.
For a place that has been on dirty dining, you would think they would try harder. Avoid at all cost.
