I went here with my sister last Sunday and I must say we had a good experience. We got there somewhat early, so there was no wait- yay! The place is pretty open with booths around the perimeter and even a bar top you can sit at to eat- which must be nice for single diners. 

The Pros- Our waitress was great and was on top of everything without stalking us. 

I am usually in a food coma for the rest of the day if I go out to breakfast (which is why I hate going out for breakfast), but our server recommended one of their omelet breakfast specials. For the special I could get any omelet on the menu with one pancake and hash browns for $6.25- hallelujah! The omelets for the special were made with 2 eggs instead of 3 which is perfect for me because I can never finish my breakfast anyway and who wants leftover omelets? Not this girl. It was great because this was probably one of the few times I've ever finished my meal when I've gone out to breakfast because the portion was perfect for me.

The Cons- They did not have pepperjack cheese for us spicy lovers and I really must have cheese on my veggie omelet- so I settled for American. I also have to pay for my dairy addiction and I believe it was $1.25 more for my cheese. :(
 
I also needed a banana pancake which I paid another $1.25 or so for. :(

Coffee is not included- sad day- but they do have flavored creamer which is a necessity for me so I'm okay with paying. Some breakfast places I'm familiar include coffee with a meal, but this might not be the norm everywhere.

The main lobby area is very small and crowded if there is a wait. It was difficult to get to the register to pay and even more awkward and difficult to get out the door. I imagine when the weather is nice it wouldn't be so bad as people could wait outside too. 

Overall- Again, I will say we had a good experience. The staff is great and very friendly. I would go back and would recommend.

Okay we've tried this place at least three or four times so I feel as though I have a fairly good grasp on Wild Eggs. We usually come on the weekend so I know sometimes days and times of visits make a difference in level of service. 

1st- expect to WAIT. Not just for a table, but for your drinks, coffee, etc. I'm not usually too bothered by this, but I always feel the hostess gives inaccurate wait times either way longer or way shorter than quoted. Also- the food is sooooo slow to get to the table I'm talking about 20-30 minutes for eggs! I have small kids so they panic when hungry!

This is also our first meal of the day when we go there so I'm more than ready to eat immediately upon entering the building- so there's that. 

2nd- way too expensive for breakfast food. Paid over $70 for 3 adults and two small kids meals. I think I don't perceive the value to match that price. While I do appreciate the hipster meets Mexican flair breakfast menu items (i.e chilaquiles), again, not for that taste/price.

3rd- I love that I can get espresso and I like that they serve breakfast cocktails. I haven't got a cocktail, but I did love the espresso bar. 

4th- received both mediocre (at best) and epic levels of service here. Not a lot of consistency. 

Overall, while I do appreciate their approach food wise- to brunch- I can't see this being a regular breakfast spot due to high cost and lack of consistency. I do recommend trying once though!

Definitely American Mexican, but has been fine to eat because it close to us and is kid friendly. It's over priced as I've had way better Mexican food at half cost- but, coming from a bigger city than Indianapolis, cheaper and better is expected I guess. 

I will say they usually have coupons in a mailer or online for a few bucks off your meal and the service has always been great when we've came.

This place had the best Mexican we've found up in Indy so far since moving from Chicago! Which is a monumental statement guys. We just happened to come on Monday too - which is $1 taco night. We ordered several of the $1 tacos, steak quesadillas, house-made chips and guacamole and a couple kids meals. 

There is a salsa/ topping bar which you can add the topping you want to your tacos- which is right up my alley. It's a order and serve yourself spot which I find usually are the best type of Mexican spots anyway. 

Super lowkey, unassuming, and clean little spot. Thanks to other Yelpers for the recommendation.

*****UPDATED REVIEW - if you are not coming in in $1 taco night this food gets expensive. Ordered guacamole/chips app, one quesadilla, and six tacos To go for $40!! Insane for what is supposed toy be cheap food. I hate that you have to add what is supposed to be included for extra charges on a taco ( cheese, onion, cilantro).) Also, they give these tiny ass containers. I'm talking the height and width of a quarter, maybe, to fill up with sauces at taco bar. I feel nickeled and dimed eating there. I didn't enjoy my food as much the second time around and regretted spending so much on what was supposed to be a cheap, weeknight dinner for my husband and I.******

Really like this local spot. Come here at least once or twice a week for a donut for my kids and coffee for me. Cinnamon cream coffee on Mondays and Tuesdays are my favorite! Super quick and friendly staff always. 

Donuts are are buy one get one free around 12pm!

Customer service means so much to my husband and I. If this were the Wingstop in Illinois I usually go to- this would be a two star review. I never even gave the energy to write them a review out there. The wings were good- but the customer service at that location was just so, sooooo bad. 

So imagine my surprise to call and make an order to the Keystone location here and talk to someone actually kind and offering me suggestions to save money AND he even repeated back my order. I get off the phone and I just couldn't stop thinking about how different of an experience I had. I'm just used to prepping to be on the defense or prepping to speak to a rude person when I make a Wingstop call. 

I get there food is ready - we ordered a lot- and it's in a box to - HELP ME CARRY IT ALL.... I'm SHOOK ya'll. 
They got me drink carriers to help as well and made sure they fit in the box. Manager- Please keep doing whatever you are doing or keep whatever employees you have right now that are making your particular location GREAT.

Ate here and have to agree with another reviewer- probably some of the most taco-bellish Mexican food I've ever had. I give two stars because the service was wonderful. If you are more into Tex-mex Food -this might be okay for you! This food just tasted uninspired and inauthentic to my husband and I.

We were very happy with BurgerFuel! We went on a whim because we were in the area and loved pretty much everything. We really appreciate the care in quality ingredient sourcing and environmentally conscious packaging for their products. The staff was super helpful when we had questions or needed something extra. We loved the Bastard and pickle fries best! The house-made aiolis were amazing. We will definitely back next time we are in Bripp.

Went here for the first time last night. It was a lively atmosphere- prob good to get a drink and watch March Madness or games. I give two stars because I came for the food. It all bar food and it is average to sub par- at best. The ingredients seem cheap and offerings left something to be desired. We tried the pork nachos, chicken tenders meal, and Shewman special burger. 

I did actually like the peanut butter on my burger and that was pretty cool that I did. The nachos seemed like something I could make at home and the guacamole we paid extra for was some avocado paste - ew. The chicken tenders were like the frozen kind you get at the store. My husband doesn't usually get those- but had a craving for whatever reason- but did ask me how can you F up chicken tenders!? 

Overall the service was good and the atmosphere is good - we just wont be back for the food.

First time here. Great wine, we came on a Sunday and got a half off bottle of wine. We tried something new and it was really good and we didn't finish the wine and they were able to recork so we could take home. 

I recommend the duck fat frites, steak frites, wings and scallops. I honestly wasn't a huge fan of the loaded tots and their ranch has a very dill herb taste to it that I wasn't a fan of. Our server was great and everyone that works there is friendly. 

Next time I go it will be more for wine and maybe one snack vs trying to make their tapas into a meal because I ordered way too much lol and it's pricey! Also- PLEASE offer a kids meal/kids price. We made their sliders into a kid meal and spent $12 on just two beef sliders (bun, patty and ketchup only) for our daughter on Mother's Day. :*(

This is a MUST! A STAPLE! Probably the best ice cream I've ever had. Service is great.

I recommend the 4 scoop sampler, because who wants to try just one flavor lol? It's big enough to share too which takes some of the guilt out of it. Key lime pie and spouse like a house are the current favorites. Highly recommend if you are in the area!

Arguably one of the best burgers I've ever had! You can totally taste the homemade difference and fresh ingredients. They moved to a new location and they serve you instead of self serve like before. We had a new waitress and she was sweet, but we had a lot of questions that she she was unsure about, she always offered to go find the answer though. 

We had the pretzel bites for an appetizer- it was so amazing! I just wish there more! I had the Flamme Burger with pretzel bun and their fries and it was sooooo bomb. 

I am sad they are not downtown fishers anymore because they are further from me and new location they are at is so hidden away compared to before. But all in all- this will not stop me from going back. Highly recommend.

So they are a new place and I can tell they are still working out the kinks! The staff was friendly - but waiting outside until there is a table is a bit extra. Also being told- we only can stay a certain amount of time was a little different. 

I would have preferred to know we were being seated on the patio Bc last night was very chilly. When we asked the host- he said only had a table outside or we could sit at or we could sit inside with a shorter time limit. We were catching up with friends and didn't want to be on a time limit and pushed out too soon. 

The food portions are very small. I understand the creative foods- but it would be nice to see a burger and fries on the menu too for my husband who is less adventurous. Overall I may come back once they get a bit more established and we can sit inside- it was very beautifully decorated!

Super disappointed. I used to order takeout from here about 3-4x a week since 2016/2017 and had to take a break because my family wanted to switch it up- not Mcalisters fault they USED to take very good care of getting our order right. 

Fast forward to a few weeks ago- I was craving it again and was coming here once again 3x a week. The staff is totally different. We used to love
Getting take out from here it was affordable and easy dinner option because my husbands works until late at night

I am on a strict diet and make some changes to my salad and my husband's so it can fit our dietary restrictions. They mess up at least one thing on my order every time and i guess it's my fault for not checking the salad before I leave . Previous staff used to pull the salad out of the bag to make sure they got it right. I complained last week because they forgot the chicken on my salad. 

I'm upset because my husband comes home late ready to eat his salad and instead of chipotle ranch dressing I ask for for his salad they gave me chipotle peach bbq sauce that goes on one of their sandwiches - He dumps it on his salad without thinking it was a wrong sauce and maybe the sherry shallot that comes with it. 

I really don't know why they gave me a sandwich sauce. And not a dressing - ANY dressing. I called to talk to a manager and he acts as if I am a dumbass Bc the sauce tastes like a bbq sauce and says "they don't have bbq sauce". Instead of trying to help us problem solve and correct the problem. We can't eat this salad with this bbq tasting sandwich sauce - so we have a ruined salad. I asked if he can replace it and said he would only give us more salad dressing not a new salad. 

Your store got our order wrong - not me! So make it right is all I ask. For his rudeness I will NEVER eat Mcalister's again.

Our first time and our food was fiiiireee. We got wings, chicken and waffles and fries . Appreciate it was open late it can be hard to find that. Very good customer service as well- which can be a nice surprise at 1am! :)

First breakfast spot my husband and I tried when moving to Tucson. We have been 3 times total now and plan on many, many more. Everything we've had has been delicious: food and drink. The servers are always attentive and kind, make good jokes and really make you feel welcome. We have always gotten there around 7/7:30 on the weekends so there has been no wait, which is great! Sign up on their website and get some coupons emailed to you occasionally!

Food:
Seasonal quiche: this might be the best thing I have ever had anywhere. We came back a 2nd time to have it but it's not on the menu anymore. Hoping I'll see it back as the "seasons" change. 

Biscuits & Gravy + Eggs + Fried Chicken: SO DELICIOUS. The gravy is flavorful without being overly salty. The scrambled eggs were perfectly cooked and the fried chicken added a nice crunch. 

Chicken & Toast: Ordered this for the fried chicken and that did not disappoint. The french toast was not great but I think my childhood memories of french toast are of a delectable breakfast that does not actually exist. I don't judge them too hard for the french toast, just won't order it again. 

Can't wait to go back to try more and try the pastries!

Came here with a group for dinner on a Saturday. We were seated quickly and our waiter was very friendly. 

Everything the table ordered was delicious. The garlic naan was some of the best I've had. You can choose the spice level on the dishes which is great for picky eaters and kids. I had the Saffron Mughlai with chicken. It was amazing. Enough for leftovers and those did not disappoint either!

We will be back and will bring family and friends!

Been twice since moving to Tucson. Food and drinks have been great and service is pretty good. 

The servers have always been very nice but not quite as attentive as I'd like. 

We've had the mac burger which is delicious and the fries are great too. I had the kale salad with smoked salmon. The salad was great but the smoked salmon was verrry smokey. I should have known. 

We also had the happy hour antipasti plate. It was DELICIOUS and generous.

My husband and I came on a Sunday for a late lunch ~3pm. The place was pretty empty but we were greeted with smiles and sat at a tall table. 

The ambiance is open and welcoming. It's not too loud in there but also not so quiet that you feel like everyone is listening to every word you say (I hate that!)

We started with the goons (stuffed fried mushrooms). My husband liked them, I thought they were underwhelming and neither of us said we would order them again. They had a bunch of other delicious sounding appetizers so we'll try something new next time. 

For my entree I had the Loaded Fries. I don't remember their menu name but they were amazing. I mean, I haven't been so satisfied with something at a restaurant in a long long time! The fries are perfectly seasoned and cooked. The beer cheese sauce is delectably smooth, and the grilled jalapenos add a great kick. The pulled pork was so flavorful that I found myself unable to stop eating! Even after eating to my hearts content, I had at least half of the bucket left and brought them home. Even reheated they were delicious. I would recommend this dish to anyone!

My husband got the bucket burger with chipotle mayo and was very happy. I tried a bite and was also impressed. The meat had great flavor and a nice crisp on the outside. The toppings were messy but delicious. 

We will definitely be back to try more items on their extensive menu!

Overall good experience. It was about a 25 minute drive from our house so I probably wouldn't come all that way again but if I'm in the area I'd go back. 

Chips & Salsa were good. Salsa tasted fresh
I had the Numero Cinco. The enchilada and chile relleno blew the shredded beef out of the water, which kinda sucks when the beef is their specialty. It had good flavor but was a little dry. I loved that their chile relleno wasn't fried and the enchilada sauce had great depth of flavor!

A little pricey for mostly run of the mill mexican food but overall good experience

We dined at the Kitchen. We were welcomed by the host and the night never stopped being fantastic. Our server was Jackie and she might have been the highlight of the night! We started with some cocktails and perused the wine list. Jackie was happy to give recommendations and help us choose. 

We ordered 2 appetizers to share with our group; the diver scallops and the mushroom toast. Both Amazing! The scallops were huge and so flavorful, perfectly cooked! The mushroom toast was unique and the goat cheese really elevated the dish. I kept going back for more. 

Our entrees were the whole trout, the fresh fish (grouper) and half roasted chicken. 
Everyone was highly satisfied with their choices. Simple but delicious flavors and great portion sizes!

We will absolutely be back and will always ask for Jackie!

I have been here for lunch twice. The service is always prompt and friendly. 

I really enjoyed the roasted corn & avocado salad with salmon. The salad was fresh, generous portions of avocado. The salmon was perfectly cooked. I honestly crave this salad regularly now. If it wasn't $20 I'd probably go at least once a week.

My other favorite on the menu is the wings. The sauce is amazing, just the right amount of kick with loads of flavor. The homemade ranch could be dumped on everything I eat from now on and I'd be happy. We chose to have our wings over tots instead of chips and I'll never go back. The tots were perfectly done, had bits of the wing sauce on them, and were so good dipped in the ranch. Plan to bring everyone I know here, just for the wings alone!

I was not as impressed by the cuban. I felt it was really lacking in the pickle and mustard, which, in my opinion, is necessary for the cuban flavor I was expecting. The bread was good but could have been toasted or grilled. The fries on the side were good but I should have gone for more tots :D

Lobster pot pie was OK but probably would not order again. The breading was great but the pot pie itself was a little thin and didn't have the greatest depth of flavor. 

Overall good food, some great, prices make it tough for a regular lunch spot, but a special treat for sure.

We came on a Friday night for drinks and snacks. Server was kind but a little short and slow. 

The outdoor area seemed cramped, not my favorite feeling. 

We ordered the pretzels appetizer. The pretzels came out hot and the cheese dip was delicious with them. We also ordered the fried cauliflower. Good flavors and nice breading. 

We had the breaded chicken sandwich. It was kind of like breaded nuggets which mostly seemed to be dark meat, which I wasn't expecting. The roasted tomatoes and arugula were a nice touch but I think the aioli was a little heavy for the sandwich. 

Might be back if a friend wants to go but probably wouldn't come back, unless I have a hankering for some delicious pretzels.

Went on a Saturday around 11. Joined the wait list on the yelp app before leaving the house, 25 minutes later we checked in with the hostess and were quoted another 25 minutes. I expected there to be a wait so no big deal, except we ended up waiting almost an hour. I know the hostesses can't predict how long people will stay but I would say, assume double what they tell you. 

We were seated outside and no server came to us for almost 15 minutes. Luckily we had gotten water and drinks at the bar during our wait, although they were almost out. 

When she did finally come to the table, all she said was, "Ready to order?" I usually feel so at home here and never rushed, but this experience was different. 

This was also the second time I was slightly disappointed by what I ordered. I ordered the avo & herb and have made better avocado toasts at home. I will not be ordering again. Guess I'll keep searching for another favorite until the quiche comes back.

The one time I was disappointed in the service and food here, both owners reached out to me and were eager to make it right. I was very impressed by their dedication and we did come back and give it another try, twice now! 

Both times we were impressed with the service and the food. The servers were personable and fun. The food was unique and delicious. If they have any type of quiche, get it, you will not be sad you did!

My takeaway from all of my Prep experiences is that if you want to come for a leisurely, relaxed breakfast, get there before 8:30. I feel that after that it gets too busy to allow the servers their usually pleasant interaction with the guests. 

We will be back again!

Husband and I recently discovered the fish tacos and cheese crisp. Both are crave-worthy and we have been back a couple of times just for them. 

Enjoy this place a little more each time we come. Can't wait to try a margarita once our baby girl makes her appearance!

Came in to check it out as a possibly soccer watching location. We sat outside and were a little confused on whether or not there was table service. Took awhile to get a waitress but once we did she was very nice and I had no complaints. Wings and fries were good. We'll be back for soccer season. 

Pretty basic bar overall

Went here for lunch. The fries were the highlight of the meal. Disappointed in the pizza, I had the lunch mushroom, it lacked flavor and was very greasy. 

Might come back for dinner because the building itself is cool and the appetizers were good.

Don't know why we didn't try this place earlier. 
Our first visit was on a Friday evening and we got the Barros special medium pizza and 12 wings. The girl that took our order was very nice and helpful since we were first timers. 

The restaurant had plenty of seating and didn't feel too loud or crazy. 

The pizza was amazing, the perfect crisp crust and heaping with toppings. I imagine their other specialty pizzas are delicious as well. 
Wings were good, we had hot and honey hot. Honey hot was our winner. 

We loved this place so much we ordered to-go the next Friday. We stuck with our same order since it was such a winner and again, not disappointed!

Went on a Saturday night. Walked in, nobody was up front, and there wasn't a sign or anything saying whether to sit wherever or wait. The entry is tight so it makes it a little awkward when you are standing next to a table of people eating wondering what you should do. We assumed it was seat yourself and no one told us different. We didn't get helped for awhile and they were slow with my water refills and the beers. 

Food was fine, have had much better bar food elsewhere

I am soy and dairy free for my 2 month old daughter. I ordered directly from the allergen menu, feeling confident that I would be fine. Unfortunately my daughter had a terrible reaction and I no longer trust that was is being told to their customers is true. Will not be back

I don't understand how they only have 3 stars. We've been a few times on the patio since the pandemic and have great food and service. The wings are my favorite and they have an awesome beer selection. We will continue coming back.
We won't order pizza from anywhere else. Pizza and wings (boneless or bone in) are always amazing and the delivery folks are nice! Comes faster than they say almost always.
One of the only places we've eaten in person since the pandemic. I feel save here and they still have such great service. Awesome food and atmosphere, will continue coming back!

Everything here is very good.
  My only compliant today was the tall blond boy with the tattoo of " Molock " the owl god on his arm who was tending bar.  He really does not seem to be happy in his work and it shows ; he has a bit of an attitude problem. Perhaps his place should be back in the kitchen.
Great selection of high quality meats , including wagyu.
The pulled pork sandwich was really super and the black eyed peas are beyond good.  You will be happy you came here.

This place offers the healthiest food you will find in New Orleans , but don't let that statement fool you into thinking " yuck". The food quality and presentation is at the apex. The prices are very reasonable and the portions are such that you will not leave hungry.

The food here is very good , but , be prepared to wait 15 to 35 minutes for it to arrive at your table. This seafood house is run by very small crew which may lend to a couple of problems. 
  First , you will rarely find more than one person behind the counter taking orders , and the person behind the register is often the one who will also bring your food out to you. As the patrons pile up at the door you may be looking at the longer of the average waiting periods. 
  Second , because they are operating on a shoe string , a great deal of pressure can be put on the employees , this can sometimes equate to a little shortness of temperament . Suggestion, go there during off hours , the wait will be minimal unless they are boiling a new batch of seafood. 
  You will love anything you order and the crawfish are especially good during May.

This is the latest endeavor  by Susan Spicer  and it shows. With the plethora of incredible restaurants  opening in New Orleans no one can open a place that is in any way second rate and expect to make it. This place will defiantly make it. 
  Understated charm is the watchword  in this turn of the century building which once acted as a court house and jail for what was then an outback of New Orleans .  You won't be disappointed !! The decor is simple , so you won't need to dress up. The drinks are world class and made from the freshest ingredients as is all of their food .

The food here is very , very good , but , be prepared to wait up to to 35 minutes for it to arrive at your table during peak ours. This seafood house is run by very small crew which may lend to a couple of problems. 
  First , you will rarely find more than one person behind the counter taking orders , and that person behind the register is often the one who will also bring your food out to you. As the patrons pile up at the door you may be looking at a longer than average waiting period. 
  Second , because they are operating on a shoe string , a great deal of pressure can be put on the employees , this MAY sometimes equate to a little shortness of temperament . 
   Suggestion, go there during off hours , the wait will be minimal , ( 5-10 minutes) , unless they are boiling a new batch of seafood. 
  You will love anything you order and the crawfish are especially good during May.

We are here for Sunday brunch and found it to be a top rate eatery. I can not recommend more highly the crawfish pie eggs Benedict.  The French toast was also incredible.  Drinks here are all made with superlative ingredients . 
 The only negative would be the style of some of the music and how loudly it was played. It really interfered with the overall enjoyment .  I want to relax when I eat but the music did quite the opposite . Perhaps they are trying to turn tables faster?

This eatery was started a few years ago by some of the people who used to run Houston's on St Charles . They have done a great job in creating their own version of that now venerable establishment .  
  The ingredients used here are very good to excellent in quality . The drinks are top notch as well as top shelf and are made without the use of bottled mixes. 
  The service is friendly , professional , and timely .  The ambiance is bright and pleasant accept that the music can sometimes make it too loud an atmosphere .   
   My only compliant today concerns  the blue cheese dressing on the salad.  I'm sure they are not lying when they say its home made , BUT , it sure had a bottled taste to me. They would do well to improve the recipe by adding ALOT more blue cheese and offering ALOT more of it . 
  The fries were very good , BUT , I had the impression that they were probably pre made/ frozen and likely coated with that stuff that lesser restaurants use to make the fries more crunchy. Perhaps they could improve by making the fries from scratch using a proprietary oil or method . 
  Small things like this go a long way towards standing out in a city that has exploded with so many incredible new places.  The competition is pounding at the door fellas , stay awake .  
  All in all , this restaurant is a winner.

We heard this was a place that stayed open a bit later than most places , (10:00pm). We called ahead and got a recording that said that indeed they were open till 10:00 pm. Based on that info we drove half way across town to have a late dinner there only to be greeted at the door with " sorry , we are closed " , this was 9:00 pm.  Upon telling the little girl about the recording ,  she replied , " yes we've been meaning to change that ".  As we left , we turned around to see her having a hardy laugh with the manager about our dilemma .   We checked the recording the next day to find no change in the greeting.  
  This was our last visit.

This is one of the New burger places that opened in New Orleans after Katrina and thank goodness it did. This town was starving for a really great hamburger and this is one of the best.  The onion rings are some of the best you will find anywhere as well and unlike the chains , they have a rather full bar menu.  The prices are not cheap but do reflect what a real burger costs these days.

This is one of the best places I have been to this year and is on par with any of the best of the new restaurants that have opened during this renaissance of the last 10 years. 
  Don't let the name fool you , the food here is on a much higher plain than your average beer hall.  You will not find any of the pre made , frozen , Monsanto crud grub that most beer halls serve ,( Abita comes to mind).  The food here is farm fresh organic everything .  The turnips are especially good , you would swear they were just picked.  The pot roast sandwich is another item that you will be very happy you ordered.  
  The only problem with this place is that everything on the menu is so good that your going to need to make multiple visits in order to experience all of the menu. 
  It will also help if you are fond of having a number of really great beer choices on tap.

Maybe it was just a bad day for them , but I doubt it.  My father , myself and a guest arrived at 2:00 pm and we were seated quickly.  We were one of only four tables in the place , but despite this , the service was very poor.  It took 30 minutes to get two trays of raw oysters. Then it took another 20 min for next entre to arrive which made the rest of us have to sit and wait for that person to finish.  
  In a nutshell , the service was terrible!

This is the third time that have been here and faced the same problem of their being out of multiple items.  Today they were out of ribs , sausage , and chicken.  How can you run a bbq place and consistently be out of all of the key items sold by a bbq establishment?  If you go here be sure to sit at the bar, because the server/bartender must engage with you , the service will be better. The other waiters will often use the excuse of being too busy to avoid you when ever they can , wich will happen even when there are only a few people in the place. 
   On their behalf , the food , when they have it , is spectacular. 
   Because of their poor service and daily outages of basic items , I doubt they will last another year.  Blue Oak BBQ just up the street is a better pick.

This place is amazingly good!!   The beef is of the highest quality and the portion is much better than Shake Shack. The Fries are some of the best you will have anywhere and eclipses those of the afore mentioned chain. . Also , Atomic offers a huge Portabella mushroom burger that is incredible!   
  I urge you to try this place and compare it with the fore mentioned , over hyped national chain.

This little out of the way place is a true sleeper of an eatery.  Don't let the neighborhood put you off ,  the breakfast here is as good as any of the great brunch and breakfast spots in town .  Their hamburgers are also at the apex of quality , along with their fries.    At the end of your meal you have choice of any number of great deserts as well , ( this being their specialty).  
 Highly recommended !!

OVERLY Hyped Hyped HYPED!!! 
   Don't waist your time and money. Unless your comparing it to McDonalds or Burger King , there is absolutely NOTHING about this place that makes it stand out as something special. 
 The burgers are good but not great. The fries are from frozen and have the appearance of Orida. 
 There are any number of great New burger places in New Orleans all of which eclipse this place.   ATOMIC burger just up veterans and is FAR better presenting one with much more choice.  Lee's also is a far better burger place , but for the very best go to Company burger on Freret or True burger on oak.

One of the great old Metairie establishments! I had my first snow ball here back 1964 , and it always brings back great memories to return. 
   Having lost McKenzies, K&B drugstore , Woolworths ,  Big Shot soft drinks , Masion Blanche , Wise and A&G cafeterias , Jax beer , Sclafanis  ,  it's nice that some things from childhoods memories have not disappeared.

I'm sorry , I wanted to like this place but they made it too difficult.  
  Myself and my 93 year old father stopped by to have lunch. There were no cars in front at 12:20 pm which should have told me something right then. My dad uses a walker ; as we were slowly making our way to the door it went through my mind that since there were no customers , wouldn't it be nice if someone would come to open the door and help/welcome us into the establishment. Instead ,  the two workers just sat there watching as we made our three minute approach to the front door.  It would have been a nice gesture to help at the door , but i guess that would have put them out. Why help if you don't have to.  
   As we entered , the first thing we noticed was the heat. It must have been about 86 degrees.  There was also a bit of an off smell , a kind of sewerage like odor. Perhaps the heat was causing something to rot? 
    The male behind the counter was not friendly or happy at all and didn't seem as though he really wanted anyone to come in and bother their peaceful lunchtime with no customers.  The girl was very sweat and friendly to her credit. 
   After ordering I made a trip to the restroom to wash up and was then met with the smell that I noticed when I first went in , sewerage.  Apparently they have a back up somewhere ; it was all I could do to keep from getting sick. I told the two attendants when I returned but they giggled a bit and didn't seem interested. 
  It was obvious to me now that these two workers are here on a temporary interlude through life and couldn't  care less about making a patrons visit special in any way.        The cook attended his work with what appeared to be a methodic disdain . Disdain for his boss , for the customers and perhaps with his life in general. The Boudin was warm , the fries and pies were WAY too salted. 
   Nothing about this dark , dirty , smelly place makes me want to make any return trips.

The food here is typical of out of the way New Orleans eateries.  Sysco vegetables from a can are too dominant . Cheese fries like dishes abound ,  and many dishes find themselves swimming upstream through heavy lakes of cream . Chicken wings with sugary sauce are also an offering.  
 No wonder we are all getting cancer and having heart attacks from obesity.
Perhaps they could green things up a bit . 
 How about collard greens that are not cooked down with molasses or sugar until all nutritional value is gone? They could also add salads with a variety of different lettuce as apposed to just iceberg.

An OK place to eat.   There is a reasonable variety of dishes to choose from though fried foods tend to overwhelm the menu.  The batter used is something that would benefit from a change though.  The consistency of the crust is tough , chewy , and rubbery , and the same batter is used for everything.   This batter is especially bad for the onion rings.  Perhaps as a draw , they could develop two or three different batters for the various things that they Frey up ; but this would likely be thought of as too much trouble.  The catfish meunière is probably the best thing on the menu , HOWEVER, each time I've tried it , the fish has never been cooked all the way through and has in fact been raw in the middle. When asked if it could be cooked longer , Ive gotten some attitude from the waitress , they do have it rough here in that they are always packed.  Parking is another issue ; you will be doing some walking so it's not a place to take your aging parents to unless they can walk a distance without help. All in all , it's an ok place for a decent meal.
   They may also benefit from hiring more waitresses or perhaps paying the bus boy just a little extra to be be in charge of filling water and tea glasses ; this would allow the waitresses more time to tend to the customer.

I went back for the first time in a while and had a better experience in terms of service.  
  It may have been because my 93 year old father was with me ,( sympathy factor)? Or it may be because we were one of only two tables there , but it was better. 
  If they can offer this service on each visit then I would have to say that , yes , they will be around a while.  The food here is exemplary.

This place is one of the best "sleeper" / time capsule establishments in the city . 
       You don't hear much about this restaurant but it is a true gem .  It's location is a bit out in left field but you will be very glad you went.  The steaks are prime and are always cooked properly.  There are a lot of sides to choose from which are all fresh , so you won't find s lot of Sysco from a can food here.  Their wine selection is very good as well.  The atmosphere is that of an old family establishment like something from The Godfather , but without the mob hits.  Give it a try , you'll be happy you did.

Stoped in with my father for lunch.  "Out of Oysters".  Only cooked oysters were available and they were so small that all you had was a mouth full of batter.  The catfish was so thin cut that all IT was was corn meal.  The fries were typical Orida from a frozen bag. All together a very disappointing lunch .  Find someplace else. This place is resting on 70 year old laurels that have gone by the wayside.

A superlative eatery!  This chef really knows what he is doing, ACCEPT when it comes to French fries.  
  I seem to recall that in the past the fries here were a great proprietary creation but as of late a change has taken place ; one that I hope will not infest the other dishes .  
   It seems that the chef has seen fit to trade in the original house made fries for Orida/ Sysco from a frozen bag fries that are identical to the style of fries one would have seen on any plate of seafood in the city about 30 years ago.  
    For the price that you pay there should be a wow factor to every element of the meal.  The fries fall short. I hope he changes this soon.
The food at Atomic Burger is much better AND they are locally owned .  Why give your money to a giant mega chain.

Now that " Molok " the owl god boy is gone , I can safely say that this place deserves the highest accolades for all that the do here. The drinks and food are of the highest quality .  You will not be sorry that you came here.

I've been to Agave at least 6 times and it has quickly become one of my favorite restaurants. Part of the reason is because of its prime location - I live close to the Monon trail and it's nice to have a Mexican restaurant within walking distance. I even trudged there through 8 inches of snow this winter, and that pitcher of agave margarita made it worth it!
That being said, this place is still trying to "figure it out." The space is quite unique - a converted art gallery with two floors. It has a nice Chihuly-esque piece that is mostly visible from the second floor. Speaking of which, the 2nd floor is where the bar is. It's not very large and doesn't have anything on draft (not the kind of space for that) but it works.
The service tends to be on the slow side here, so you have to have some patience. However, once you order the food tends to come out pretty quick, which I think is fantastic.
The biggest fault of this place is that is does not do well at handling seating when it's busy. They do not have a host - most of the time seating is done by their older gentleman who I assume owns the place. There is extremely limited standing room inside the restaurant, and with only single door entry, expect to get a bit chilly sitting anywhere near the door in the winter. In the summer, there is a lot of extra outdoor seating right next to Main Street that is great, though!
Their food is quite excellent, and pretty much anything that uses their shredded chicken is always a slam dunk for me. Highly recommend the Los Tres Burritos.
The restaurant would greatly benefit from a host on busy nights who is better able to communicate with the customers and take care of seating.

This place is a regular go-to lunch spot for myself and my coworkers. They are quick enough to get you through your lunch hour.

The variety of food is fantastic. I've tried the Vietnamese Pho, their Japanese sushi, and a variety of their Chinese dishes.

The actual food I've had here over the 10 or so times has been consistently good, even if it is nothing that particularly stands out.

A few of the other reviews mention "mushy" rice, but I've never had that happen here. I get white rice, and it is always perfectly sticky, completely manageable with chopsticks.

My recommendation would be the Sesame Chicken.

This location has long been a standard within my family, especially for family events. Birthdays, rehearsal dinners, Mother's Day, etc.

Sometimes family style can be a challenge to find items that everyone likes. I particularly am a fan of the Chicken Carbonara, but many times I'm the only person interested in getting it - in which case I have to skip in order for something else, because a Small for $21 that feeds 3 but only I would eat is not worth it.

However, all of their food is great. Their cheesy garlic bread is fantastic - big cloves of garlic on it.

I don't frequently go to Italian restaraunts, but when I do I like to take advantage to order food that I wouldn't normally cook at home. I recommend all of their specialty pastas.

However, my biggest recommendation is the Apple Gorgonzola salad. The mixture of flavors is out of this world, and the dressing for it is what really makes it taste amazing. I was the first person in my family to order this salad years ago (they still used to order the regular salad), but now everyone in my family ends up eating it.

The biggest reason to go here is because they are understanding of large parties and have many spaces available to accommodate for them. They take reservations in advance as long as it's not a special day like Mother's Day or Easter.

I tried this place after purchasing a Groupon (because the picture looked SO good). I had heard good things about Greek's in other Indiana cities, so I was looking forward to trying them out.

Overall, I was not very impressed. I got Carryout - a pepperoni pizza and breadsticks.

The breadsticks were fantastic, even if they were a bit greasy. The pizza was good - I am pretty sure that they use the same dough for their breadsticks and pizza.

The biggest disappointment was their marinara. I got this for my breadsticks (which it was actually slightly cold), and it was on the pizza. Basically... it was tomato paste. There was pretty much no flavor to it at all, and that's one of the most important aspects of a pizza to me.

I will say that I enjoyed the price. This place has some great specials every day of the week.

My opinion would greatly turn around if they could make their marinara sauce more interesting. In the meantime, I will probably go to Hotbox or Bazbeaux instead.

This place was great! I had never really eaten much Greek food in the past, but I am glad I started here!

All over the restaurant you will see Saganaki being lit on flames every so often. And the reason why is because it tastes AMAZING. The seared outside of the cheese with the melted inside is perfect on their amazing pita bread.

We also ordered the Tzaziki and Baba Ganoush. I preferred the Tzaziki over the Baba Ganoush, but both were good, and we were provided with an extra plate of pita bread when we requested it from our server.

I am not the most adventurous eater, so I stuck with the Chicken Gyro, and it was a slam dunk. All of their dinner meals come with rice, Mediterranean green beans, and Greek potatoes (the best of the three).

Overall, I had a great time here. There is nothing major I could really point out for improvement (hence why I think it deserves 5 stars).

I visited with friends, but I cannot wait to visit again and hopefully convince some family members to go with me.

Usually I never have a bad experience here, but last time some odd things happened. The person taking the order just completely spaced out and did not get it correct at all. They did not add Parmesan chicken as ordered.

Seeing as how I've been here many times and this was the first time anything like this happened, I'll assume that was a fluke caused by a busy Friday evening dinner rush. I expect it to not happen again, though.

I had just gotten the Thai Hot Pot the day before this, and it was perfect. Custom ordered without peppers or mushrooms, and they nailed it. I had a blast trying a new food item, and I enjoyed it so much that I will definitely order it again.

The restaurant overall rests on the grave of Ponderosa (RIP) and it really is great to have such a high quality place around. Their food is top notch, and they also sell liquor at this location in case you want a glass of wine along with your noodles.

One of the nicest things about this Noodles & Co is that they have their large menu to the left of the register you can really get a good view of it without having to hurt your neck looking at the one high above the registers.

Noodles & Company has always had the unique serving method of ordering at the register, but then an server brings your food out. I really prefer this method and it works out well for the restaurant. It's nicer than fast food, but still a quick restaurant.

This location has one of the fancy soda machines with over 100 variations. Overall, I like these, but when it's busy and you have someone taking too long to look over the possibilities, a line can quickly form. Still, it's fun to have around.

I highly recommend the BBQ Pork Mac! It is one of the best dishes they serve. Also, I always get their tomato/cucumber/onion salad. It's simple, but so flavorful. If you purchase a dish you can add some of the select sides for $1, so there really is no reason to not get one of those sides.

Overall, I usually have a great dining experience here, and I love the variety of dishes they offer.

I'm updating this review. Because I have d-e-f-i-n-i-t-e-l-y been here more than 2 times by now.

This place is THE. BEST.

I've tried a couple of their hot sandwiches, and they are pretty good, but I'm never as impressed with them as I am the cold cut sandwiches. That being said, the cold cut sandwiches are the best subs in the Carmel area by far, especially if you get it "Mike's Way." Still haven't tried the wraps, it's on my to-do list, but I heard that they are also really great.

I really wish they offered sliced cucumber, though. One of my favorite things to get on my sandwiches is absent from their potential sandwich additions.

Cafe Korea was an excellent little Korean restaurant. It's tucked away in a strip mall on the NW corner of 116th and Allisonville. It might be small, but it has a lot of personality.

I'll begin with the best part: the food. Everything I ate was delicious. I went with a couple friends who had been before. Apparently their banchan is always the same: Oi-sobagi, Sigeumchi-namul, Sukju Namul, Kkakdugi. We split an order of Kimbap for an appetizer. It was great! I ordered the Dol Sot Bi Bim Bop, which was amazing. They always give you some fruit at the end - this time it was some watermelon cubes.

The restaurant has a great ambiance. It is obviously frequented mostly by the Korean community, but my table wasn't the only non-koreans in the restaurant. There is recent k-pop playing in the background, which I loved. There are a good number of TVs that they show sports on.

This is not a restaurant to go to when you are looking to get in and get out quickly. There are very few servers - apparently either one or two. I went on a Saturday afternoon and the place was somewhat busy. When the tables were done, they weren't bussed even an hour later. I could not tell if this was normal because the restaurant has a mid-day break between 3-5pm or if it was just because that one server was too busy taking care of tables.

Overall, my friends and I were there for two hours. The k-pop playlist is apparently only so long - we heard "Mr. Chu" by A-Pink at least 5 times (not complaining, I love that song). However, we did get service (seobiseu), which is free stuff basically, in the form of Pajeon (korean pancake). So that was nice, and delicious.

Cafe Korea is not a place to go for a quick meal - this is a place to go for an experience and to socialize with your friends. I had a blast and will be returning.

Awesome food, lots of beer choices, good prices, great service.

I ordered the PBB&J burgers (peanut butter, strawberry jam, strawberries, bacon, Monterrey jack cheese). It was a fantastic burger.

I also had the sweet potato fries, which were lightly covered in cinnamon sugar. The highlight of the meal was the sweet sriracha dipping sauce, though. It was perfect with the sweet potato fries. I ended up asking for more dipping sauce because it was that good.

Overall a great addition to Main Street - will definitely be returning.

Went here for lunch, started with kimchi pancake (kimchijeon). It was four individual round pancakes with a sweet sauce drizzled on top. Each about the size of a sand dollar. Overall, pretty good and the sweet sauce was really delicious. Only complaint would be that Kimchijeon is not that difficult or expensive to make, so I felt like they could have been a bit bigger, or there could have been a couple more of them.

For my entree, I had the (dolsat) Bibimbap. It was faaaantastic. It had bulgogi (beef), tofu, carrots, bean sprouts, zucchini, and a poached egg on rice in a hot clay pot. It also had a spicy chili sauce on the side. I'm used to having a hot pepper sauce (gochujang) for my bibimbap but this one had an awesome sweet kick to it. I would definitely get it again.

Overall, the food was good. I look forward to trying one of the sushi rolls next time. I know that the restaurant is "modern asian" so they really try to Americanize some asian dishes to make them more appealing to the non-asian people of Carmel. However, it would be nice to see a few more traditional options. That's part of the fun in going an an Asian restaurant sometimes. "Samgyeopsal? Oh that sounds awesome, I will try it." I really wish they had some type of ssam dish. Like bossam. That would be pretty awesome. Or some kind of modernization of ramen (the good Japanese kind, not the kind you eat in college).

A couple notes about the experience. No banchan with the bibimbap. But I went for lunch, so I wasn't very surprised. I asked for a spoon for my bibimbap and was given a normal spoon. Would really have preferred sujeo. I'll probably try asking for a soup spoon next time instead. Or maybe just take my own because I'd prefer stainless steel chopsticks to their wooden ones anyways. Also, the music was like soft rock or something - felt a little off. The waitress was awesome, though!

Definitely planning on returning in the near future. Maybe next time I'll get "service" like a couple of people have posted in their pictures. ;)

Food is pretty good, but it used to be better. Still, I like the pretzel bites a lot, their chicken salad is good, and their burgers are huge.

I'm mostly giving this a low rating because I have consistently had poor service here, and this evening was the worst of the bunch. Waited 5 minutes just to have her show up to take our drink order, then when she gave those to us, she ran away as fast as possible when we were ready to order. Waited about 10 minutes for her to come back to take our order. Sure, she had a 9-top that ordered a full spread with drinks, steaks and desserts, but she had plenty of time to check on us, but failed to do so ONCE after we received our food. My dining partner could literally see her standing around and kiki-ing in the kitchen area. When she came with the bill, I had my credit card in hand and tried to offer it to her, but she threw that bill down and booked it away from us and didn't come back to pick it up for another 5 minutes.

Overall, we were there about 30-40 minutes longer than we really needed to be, especially for a table of 2. This was a worst-case scenario, but it certainly seems to be a sign that they were either understaffed or need to train their staff better.

Definitely one of my favorite new go-to places in Carmel.

Building your own pizza for a set price no matter what you put on it opens up so many possibilities to do it your way, and I love experimenting with different flavor combinations each time I visit.

I love the aesthetic of the restaurant, it is very unique.

The staff is extremely friendly and helpful, and there are a lot of them!

There are quite a few cons I can point out though. The acoustics inside the restaurant can be rough, and the place can get very loud if it's very crowded.

During lunch rush, this place can be absolutely crazy. There is not a very good waiting area for receiving your pizza when it's up, and because you never know exactly when they'll pull your pizza from the oven, you can't always expect them to get pulled based on who was in front of you in line, especially if you had a simpler pizza than the person in front of you. This leads to a lot of people waiting in a small space for their pizza. And when it is up, if you aren't there to immediately receive it, they have to yell across the entire restaurant to try and get you to go get your pizza.

Like someone else mentioned, for the best experience here I would highly recommend coming around the primary meal rush times, if possible.

But, I really do love this place and that's why I keep going back.

For the record, I was the first one who suggested we try Piada, and NOT my mom. So now it's officially on yelp in writing. (except she really did suggest it first, but don't tell anyone that).

Glad we did try it, this place is great!

I read some other reviews where people were saying the owners didn't really like being called the Chipotle of Italian food, but SORRY BOUT CHA, that's what it is. Assembly line-style piadas (think like a wrap or burrito but Italianized), pastas, and salads.

So far I have tried each at least once. I prefer the pastas and salads over the actual piadas, though.

The prices are good for being able to create your own dish. Plus, they are adding some new items to the menu soon and including a deal where you can get a sandwich & side for a good price.

One of my favorite parts is that they have a berry and orange italian soda (on the opposite side of the Coke). They are sweet but really flavorful!

Do yourself a favor when you come here, and always try a little something extra. They have some delicious soup options, yummy piada sticks, and my favorite part - cannoli chips! These little items are only a couple bucks extra, but soooo worth it!

Chipotle has always been one of my favorite places to eat ever since the first one in Carmel opened in Merchant Square (rip). This new store is very nice and the decor feels perfectly in line with their aesthetic. It feels a little small, and I'm worried about how well it will fare in the lunch rush because it is in a high traffic area around a bunch of businesses. I think that this restaurant could be overwhelmed for its size.

There will eventually be outdoor seating.

I had a burrito from there, and it was perfect, and the staff was very polite and kind. Some of them were obviously new and still learning, but they got everything perfect as far as I was concerned. Can't wait to return here over and over.

My friend and I got kbbq here - it was awesome.

We ordered the mixed meat special of chicken, pork and beef because we wanted to try a little of everything. Everything was super delicious - the chicken was surprisingly spicier than the pork and beef.

There's noraebang in a back room, that was super fun because there we could hear a party doing it in the back while we ate.

While we were there, a group of like 10+ high school kids were eating here. It looked like the restaurant did very well with them, so I'd say this place is great for a larger party of people - you just get two barbeques put together instead of one.

My eating partner and I quickly found out that I sucked at cooking the meat (I wasn't very organized with my "meat layout") - but I'm sure I'll get the hang of it in the future. It was still fun to try.

There were a LOT of banchan, and we knew what most of them were. Only one we didn't recognize, but tried it anyway. 

Definitely will return, the experience was fun and the food was delicious! Worth the money. If you go here, try to keep an adventurous attitude.

The Keystone food court mall rework is A-MAZ-ING.

The staff at this Chipotle was super friendly, probably one of the friendliest staffs I've ever met.

This is probably one of the quickest options for the food court, which is why it seemed to be the most popular option people were eating.

Pretty much everything about this Chipotle was a slam dunk - fast, friendly, delicious.

I've only been here once but it was a great experience. There is a side room that is perfect for a get-together. It has a few tables and chairs for dining, plus a tv and couches by a fake fireplace. I was very impressed.

Our server was super friendly.

Best of all, this place had Zombie Dust on tap! It's one of the best beers on BeerAdvocate, and it was delicious.

Good for large parties, great for small ones too. I'm glad this place is here, and based on how difficult it was to find a parking spot, it seems to be doing very well.

Once the new Brewflix brewery/theater is right next door, Wolfie's will be PERFECT for dinner before going to a movie or a place to have another drink once the movie is over.

This subway is very "business-minded" - and it's right in the middle of one of the heavy business areas of Carmel so that makes sense.

Based on other reviews, the employees here seem to get a lot of flack for not being the most personable. But I don't go to this Subway because I want to chitchat or make small talk and giggle with the staff. I want to get my sandwich and then get back to work.

This Subway can get very busy at lunch time, and they usually do a very good job at getting their customers through the line in a timely manner.

If you are looking for a Subway where it's the lunch rush hour and you want to take your time and ask a bunch of questions - this isn't the Subway for you.

They have a promo right now for a basic cheeseburger with fixings & unlimited seasoned fries for only $5 on Thursdays. Pretty good deal, I've been there a few times for it, and enjoyed it every time. Last go my dad's burger was undercooked, but that's the only time we've really had an issue with the food here.

The tortilla chips here are really delicious, slightly addicting. If I'm not getting the amazing knockout nachos, I'll usually get an order of chips & guac.

Food is good, the price is right. For a sitdown restaurant, those are two things I can appreciate.

Service was definitely faster in the main dining area than the bar. I've sat in the bar section a couple of times and it was very slow both times.
Quick, delicious food. Very filling. Always splurge for extra bread. It's worth it. A little more plain than some of the other locations but nothing wrong with that.

I've been to this location a few times now for lunch, usually after the big rush is done. Service is typically friendly. Had a weird credit card machine issue one time, but the next time I went there a couple days later it was no longer a problem.

They usually are done making my sandwich while I'm getting my drink. Soda machine has Cherry Coke - always a plus.

This is a nice, quiet place to relax for a bit during lunch.

Ice skating was a lot of fun.

But the layout of this place was HORRIBLE. The amount of space between the ice rink and the side vendors was way too small - there were constant traffic issues trying to get through.

To make matters worse, all of the really good vendors - like the food and drinks (stuff people really wanted to purchase) were along the inside of the rink. Which meant that lines for food were wacky, and constantly having issues with thru traffic.

They need to place food and drink vendors on the outside of the rink where there is more space. There was a lot of space closest to the Palladium that was underutilized.

Also would recommend some sort of better ticket/signup system for ice skating times when it's popular. The group I was with almost didn't make the cutoff for the time we were there and would have had to wait an extra two hours for the next time slot.

It was nice while it was there, but I'm glad it's back to normal now.

This place is pretty casual. Food tastes good for how simple it is. Prices for hotdogs and hamburgers are good. Drinks and fries prices are way too high though. At least the fries are pretty good though.

I particularly like  the Atlanta dog. Chili, cheese, and onions on the poppy seed bun. Very tasty.

SKIP THIS PLACE. It's some of the worst Chinese food I've ever had. I got a meal at lunch time, which was busy. I almost could not find a place to sit.

The counter service was mediocre. The person working the register acted Iike she was over it.

The egg drop soup was good, but everything else afterwards was tragic. The rice was dry and undercooked, the sesame chicken was breaded terribly (clearly just something that was frozen that they microwaved. It was chewy and soggy. The egg roll was pretty disgusting as well.

All I could stand eating was the soup. Wasn't worth the price of the meal. I don't usually take pictures of my meals but I did this time because it was so god awful.

Don yourself a favor and avoid this joint. It may be cheaper but you get what you pay for... in a bad way.

A couple years ago Arby's really went all in on their image change and efforts to rebrand. And I have to day, they did a great job.

I've been to this Arby's a good number of times now, and it's so good that I will keep going back as long as I work close to this location.

The management does a good job at keeping the place clean and running smoothly. The food is EXCELLENT, and fairly priced. The sliders in particular are simple but cheap and delicious - and who doesn't love some hot, fresh curly fries??

I haven't been to McDonalds since I discovered this was just down the road. 


Only criticism is that sometimes the indoors is unusually chilly. But it's worth it for the awesome food and service.

Updating my review to five stars. Any place I've checked into 20+ times in 8 months deserves it.

This place is great. Food is made very fast and tastes great. It's a clean space, even the bathrooms. Quiet place to chill and de-stress while eating.

Plus, CHERRY COKE. I mean, what else do you need?

Small criticism... I wish there were napkins more easily available. Only really find them behind the counter which is kinda weird.

I'm moving to a downtown office soon and I will definitely miss this Jimmy John's.

Had a Tofu Rich Girl. Came with blue corn chips and salsa. I have to say it was absolutely delicious!

Food did not take long to make, and I loved trying something new.

This is a great stand in City Market and I will definitely be back.

Great place - reasonably priced for the fantastic food quality.

I ate lunch with a friend inside the restaurant, had a great time and great service.

However, last time I was here I went to the food court window. First, they had free samples. Second, you can just order the same amazing meatballs while everyone else can go get whatever they want to eat.

The food court window is basically the best thing ever. My mom got Noodles & Co, but after seeing my food said she wished she had gotten Mimi's instead. She particularly loves their mashed potatoes, which are very good.

Do yourself a favor. GET THE BRUSSELS SPROUTS. Even if you don't think you like them. They are perfection.

Sorry no photo for this review. The food is so good I usually can't wait to start eating. Whoops!

This Steak 'n Shake has gone DOWNHILL.

Memories of this location were great, a go-to location for after late night events like Carmel football games.

However, I went a couple weeks ago and the entire experience was awful. The restaurant seemed like there were only three employees working. The manager running the to-go orders, one cook, and one indoor dining server, who was serving about 8 or 9 tables by herself.

I dined in, and the place was a complete mess. We're talking about 5+ tables with their dirty food plates not cleaned up.

The burgers, fries, and shakes were decent - only reason I'm giving two stars. The chili looked awful. My dad tried to send it back because it tasted bad and he wanted baked beans instead, and the server wasn't sure if she could do that, had to get a manager for it instead of just taking the chili and getting him some baked beans.

The food deals they have are good, but if they can't staff properly, this place is never going to get better.

The Westfield location is much better. Go there instead.

Located on the northern side of City Market, Gomez BBQ has a fantastic menu using their excellent barbecue meats.

Upon first visit, I was suggested the pork rice bowl - which was great. However, next time I tried the pork quesadilla and I've pretty much been stuck on it since. Perfect blend of pork, cheese, tomatoes, pickled onion, and bbq sauce.

Seriously - try this place out if you haven't. It will not disappoint.

Years ago I used to visit a Tropical Smoothie Cafe in Dayton, I always had wished there was one close to me.

WELL NOW THERE IS, AND IT'S AMAZING.

The smoothies are great, the food is also awesome, and fairly priced. If you get any food, try the kale apple slaw - it's a delicious side.

My go-to smoothies have always been the Mocha Madness and Peanut Butter Cup. They are both amazingly delicious.

Recently, I've been craving the Detox Island Green - it's packed with fresh, healthy ingredients, and it's naturally sweetened.

I'm also a huge fan of the flatbreads. I tried a chicken caesar wrap last time, and it was tasty, but probably not as good as the flatbreads. Either way, the food is warm and delicious. I'm sure a lot of people go here for smoothies, but seriously - try the food. It's awesome.

Presentation-wise, Public Greens is awesome. The interior of the space is clean, modern, and pleasant. Their food is has huge social media sharability. It looks gorgeous.

Where Public Greens fell flat for me was the food. I recently got the sesame chicken bowl. The plate and presentation was beautiful, though a bit unexpected. The ingredients listed rice - but it wasn't your typical rice. Which I thought was pretty good.

Unfortunately, the chicken was tough - like it was overfried. Some pieces you could barely even cut through. The sesame sauce was globbed onto the chicken and it was thick, so you couldn't really spread it out through the bowl. This meant when there was a bite with the sesame sauce - it packed a bit too much of a punch.

For $15+, I was a bit disappointed overall. I think the dish had huge potential, but execution was way off.

The staff was pretty awesome - they were super friendly and they had someone by the menu to explain how it works and answer any questions. I really appreciated this.

The interior of the place is aesthetically pleasing, and the menu has great selection.

I will probably give Public Greens a second chance as I usually do, but I really hope they step it up next time.

I've never had an unpleasant donut from Square Donuts.

The yeast donuts are really the highlight here - chocolate glazed, plain, or my favorite with strawberry icing. They are pillowy and melt in your mouth. The amount of glaze doesn't overpower the donut either.

The cake donuts are a little different - I think part of their 'old fashioned' style of making them. It's not my favorite cake donut, but it's nice to have something that tastes like a more traditional-style donut.

The donuts may not be gigantic like Jack's (which I think are doughy), but I think that the quality at Square Donuts is far better.

House blend drip coffee tends to be unusually strong.

Price points are decent. Doesn't break your wallet to take a couple dozen donuts to work once in a while.

I'm not typically one to complain about price increases, but Tamale Place recently made some menu changes, and the price increases for their food is INSANE.

Tamales - $3.49 to $4.25
Tacos - $2.99 to $4
Nachos - $7.49 (only one size, I assume a large) to $9 small / $11 large
Half-Pint of Rice/Beans/Salsa - $1.75 to $3
Tamale Combo - $9 to $12
Taco Combo - $8.49 to $12
Even just the bottled drink went from $1.50 to $2.50.

I could understand some small price increases every once in a while, but these new prices are pretty ridiculous.

I understand Condado is around and charging $3-4 per taco, but their tacos are actually interesting and have variety.

The food at Tamale Place is good, but those combos are not worth $12 compared to other lunch deals in City Market for $9-10.

I don't know what to say other than this "restaurant" is garbage and the owner is a corrupt politician, being a Carmel City Council-at-Large.

The food is bad, I've had dry chicken and meatloaf. The interior is dark and depressing.

There are a bunch of other restaurants in the area. Matt the Miller's, Anthony's Chophouse, Bazbeaux, Muldoon's, Pint Room, Burgerhaus, and more.

Go to one of those instead.

Been to Wild Eggs a good number of times. Tried a few different dishes, but ever since I had their biscuits and gravy I never get anything else now. It's really good. They have two different gravies, and you can get it half and half if you want (highly recommended!!)

Only issue I have is that they don't season their breakfast potatoes at all. Seems really weird to me.

Last time my family and I went on a Sunday and they had $2 mimosas. Umm.... yes please. Service was great too.

I would say that I still prefer LePeep, but Wild Eggs is really great too.

Graeter's is THE BEST ice cream in Indy, no competition.

I grew up in Cincinnati eating Graeter's for a treat when we were good.

Their signature black raspberry chocolate chip is to die for. But any of the chocolate chip flavors are amazing. I get coconut chip or coffee chip.l occasionally.

Calling it a chocolate chip is an understatement though, these flavors have CHUNKS of dark chocolate.

One knock is that I got the black raspberry chip cake to try with some friends, and it was ok. Not great. Especially for the price (it was quite expensive). Maybe will try the pie instead next time.

Some of the Ohio locations started putting in bakeries. Wish we had those here!

Had to check this place out after seeing the Yelp reviews and it did not disappoint.

Getting into the parking lot going west on 96th was a nightmare. Had to pass it, turn around in Kroger and come back the other way to get in.

The food was fantastic. The owner guy brought out two sauces to add. I didn't think the food needed them, but tried both of the sauces anyways. The red sauce was insanely hot. Almost ruined the meal.

Prices seemed a little high if I'm being honest. Counter service Mexican for $10-12 per meal seemed steep. But the food was good, at least.

I've been to multiple Mimi Blue locations: Carmel, Keystone Mall, and this one on Mass Ave. I've been to the Mass Ave on the most though.

I have to say that it really is fantastic. Their meatballs are phenomenal, the sides are all delicious. The Brussel sprouts in particular are standout. I didn't think I liked Brussel sprouts before I tried them here.

Location is great and will only get better once the coke plant gets revamped. Easy to make an evening out with dinner at Mimi Blues and then going anywhere else on Mass Ave (Kingmakers is right across the street, highly recommend).

Recently the Mass Ave location expanded into the other space for more seating and it looks really nice! Great indoor or outdoor seating.

I've been here a few times now, and I love it.

First time here I went by myself before a show at the Murat, which is just a little further down Mass Ave. Sat at the bar, service was great. One of the bartenders made a little too much of their pineapple margarita and gave it to me pro bono - it was AWESOME!

As far as their tacos... I'm all about that Lucy shell. No matter which taco - get the Lucy shell (hard shell inside, soft shell outside).

Another perk of this place is that they are open late. Nothing quite like going out on Mass Ave and getting some late night tacos.

Love Condado, will return often!

I thought the food at CoreLife tasted good, but I would not say that the price was right for what you got.

The scoop for their meats is TINY. I got a double-scoop of steak on my black & blue salad, and it was about the same amount you find at other comparable places.

I guess they have cool in-house drinks, but I was already dishing out something like $13+ for a quick-service salad, so I skipped that.

If I return, next visit I'll likely go for a grain bowl or soup bowl instead.

Had a great time at Winterfest! There definitely were a lot of people and lines got kind of crazy but overall got to try a bunch of different beers and had fun.

The venue was indoor which was fantastic, but also meant that traffic got a little odd at times. Hard to go behind some lines, so people just cut through. Good number of consessions scattered around. Water was easy to find.

My only beef was that the venue website's FAQ specifically said you HAD to print out your tickets, but that wasn't true at all. A majority of people we saw used the tickets on their phones.

KpacaqqLR5bU_AGTV0E0Xw.review_text: The food and service are good but it is over priced.
This is an excellent restaurant, amazing food, staff and fair pricing.
This is good if you like this kind of cuisine.  Priced fair and good service.
What can you say about a burger joint?  The service at this location leaves a lot to be desired.
Kind of a hoe in the wall.  Wondering what the kitchen looks like.  The pricing is excellent and I have never had a meal here that I did not love.  Definetly Worth a try.
This is a really nice bar.  Great food, service and the pricing is acceptable for what you get.
Fantastic place.  The food and service is awesome.  Be ready to dig a little deeper into the wallet for eats here.

This is a great new place.  The cuisine is New Mexican. and some Mid Western meals.  The New Mexican food is very near to what you would get if you were in New Mexico.  Great flavors and pricing.  It takes a bit longer than it should to get the food out to the table.  The friendliness of the wait staff leaves a little to be desired.

This is a net little dive / geriatric meat market.  If there is a young person in this place they are out with their parents or grandparents.  Since I have grand kids I actually like this place.  Very relaxing.  Great prices and Service.  You can't go wrong.
