Best Stuffed Philly Cheesesteak Pretzels and nuggets are soft and tasty. The honey mustard sauce is great and they have many options on the menu from salty to sweet.

This place is a hidden gem, they have a wide variety of donuts from Bear Claws, Oreo, Caramel,   filled Donuts but my favorite is the regular old fashioned glazed donut it is so light and not overly sweet like most donuts. The lady that works at the counter is so friendly and helpful. They also sell breakfast sandwiches and drinks. They even have a drive thru for those who want quick on the go.

I ordered the Drunken Noodles with chicken and did not enjoy it. The crab ragoons were okay, the chicken had a strange aftertaste with the chili sauce i personally would not try anything else off the menu disappointing.

LV2aVDnPrl87Bfl8Mc4AtQ.review_text: Checked out Soul food Sunday with friends. If the weather is good get there early for seat outside and decent parking.  We had the Southern Salad and it was delicious. We also got the brisket and sliced pork with a side of smoked beans. The smoked beans were like spicy baked beans and were good. The pork and brisket were both very fatty, but the BBQ sauce was good.  We snagged bites of the mac and cheese and fried pickles, which were both amazing.  We would definitely come back, but would steer clear of BBQ. Loved the atmosphere and the place was packed.

Took my best friend here for a birthday lunch. We had reservations and were seated immediately.  The place was gorgeous, from the coffee bar, book store and unique shop we spent hours just taking it all in.  I had the chopped spinach salad and subbed hard boiled eggs for the Gorgonzola. It was good but they left off the pear and pumpkin seeds. I still licked my plate clean. My friend got the chicken burger with sweet potato rounds. The sweet potato rounds were roasted and perfectly seasoned. The chicken burger was good, but needed a sauce or aioli as it was a little dry.  Since it was my friend's birthday they brought us a salted caramel macaroon, shortbread cookie and mini chocolate cupcake. The macaroon was to die for....the cupcake can be skipped.  We can't wait to come back for tea time or brunch.  If you're looking to take a vacation from Tampa without leaving the city limits this is the place!

Pizza fusion is one of those places that I frequent a lot, but I'm hardly ever blown away by the food. It's not awesome, but it's never bad.  I was originally drawn to their commitment to organic ingredients and great weekday lunch specials.  My favorites on the menu include the chicken Caesar salad.  No dressing needed, as they lightly dress with lemon, shredded Parmesan and well-seasoned chicken. It is always fresh.  I am also a fan of their multigrain crust, which pairs nicely with any of the pizzas.  I would rank it higher, but the service is always a little chaotic and none of the wait staff seems to give consistent information regarding menu items and prices.  This is a solid meal with a great downtown location close to Curtis Hixson, the straz, and the Tampa Theater.

I've been an Evos junkie for years.  I used to work by their location on 4th St. in St. Petersburg and I went so much they knew my order when I walked in.  I appreciate their vegetarian options and their commitment to providing healthy fast food.  I love their spicy thai chicken wrap, baked air fries with mesquite ketchup, and their nitrate free hot dog.  Their vanilla milk shakes are also yummy and their veggie chili on a cold day is the perfect light bite.  The reason I am giving them only three stars is that this particular location has been pretty bad in terms of customer service on my last 3 plus visits.  They've gotten my order wrong several times and completely forgotten portions of it on a take out (which I didn't realize until I was home).  I'm just not sure who is running that place anymore.  Last time I walked in around 7pm at night the entire staff except one person was congregated at a table talking and watching some kind of video on one of their phones.  I probably stood at the register for about 3 minutes before someone acknowledged me and when they finally did only one person came over to help before someone else reluctantly went to the kitchen to make my food. Luckily I checked my order before leaving because they forgot items again.  I have been loyal to Evos for years though, so I will keep coming back as I know they have good people working for them and despite these customer service issues the food quality at this location has not been lacking.

I am a big fan of Gourmet Pizza Company.  I normally always get their pizza with spinach and artichokes added.  Their crust is just amazing.  It's thick on the outside and thin and crispy as you move to the middle.  They are always very generous with their amount of toppings, the cheese blend is thick and creamy and I love that when I bite into it a huge string of cheese follows me from my plate to my mouth.  I am not a fan of pizza sauce at all, but they never put too much on and I actually don't mind their sauce.  I recently discovered their breadsticks which I might like even more than than the pizza. There is so much great cheese and on top of that cheese is sprinkled more parmesan.  My husband loves to dip it in the marinara sauce on the side.  They have tons of options for the meat lover, vegetarian and vegan alike.  They also have gluten free options.  Their location right off of Armenia and Swann is convenient for S. Tampa peeps.  I have only ever actually eaten inside once as we usually get take out, but the time that we did was great.  It wasn't too crowded or noisy and the staff is always friendly.  They deliver too if you're in their radius and they always have great specials online.

I drove by this place a million times before I ever stopped in.  Let's be honest its curb appeal is pretty lacking, but don't let the exterior fool you...there is good food inside.  I've been there for breakfast and lunch and even though it is tiny inside I've been able to get a seat without too much trouble.  I love that they have organic and vegetarian options and have a commitment to using fresh and local foods when they can.  It's a funky little arty spot with art on the walls, open mic night etc.  I've had the ham and pickle sandwich.  I love that it's on the toasted Cuban bread and the salty ham combined with the sweet and vinegary mango chutney and sharp cheddar really wakes up the taste buds. I've also had the VLT, which is vegan bacon, tomato, lettuce and veganaise.  Again I love the Cuban bread, but next time I would add some avocado as I just felt like something was lacking.  For breakfast I've had the A to Z which is avocado, turkey, provolone, tomato and eggs.  I had them put it in a wrap but you can get Cuban bread too.  The food I've had is solid, but never knocks my socks off.  I often stop in to get some tea as they have an extensive menu.  I'm a fan of the naturally sweet rooibos teas, particularly the hawaiian divine and chai.  The price is right for what they are doing here.  Support Local!

Tijuana Flats is one of my husband's favorite spots for lunch so when we are in Brandon we often go here.  I like that they have a Light Menu, whole wheat options, and use hormone free meats.  I can also tell that their sour cream is REAL sour cream and a little of that goes a long way.  Their chicken is good, white meat and is never fatty.  I do appreciate the seasoning they put on it.   I do not enjoy their always cold chips with sporadic seasoning...some chips have no salt and pepper and the others are covered with it.  I usually ask for them to just leave them off.  I'm a fan of their chicken and black bean burrito or quesadilla and the husband likes their chicken soft tacos.  Is this mostly stuff you could make at home? Yes. But it is good for on the go and is consistently good quality food at a reasonable price.  Also, they do have good service as someone always greats you when you come in, hands you a menu and offers suggestions if you want them.  They also have people walking around to refill drinks, remove trays etc.  This location is usually busy but is also clean.

Royal Thai has been a staple in my south Tampa diet for years, as I do love to support local restaurants.  I stopped in tonight with friends after about 2 months away.  Thursday night is pretty slow, which is good since parking is at a premium.  Tonight I had the tofu pad thai and my husband had the chicken fried rice adding broccoli.  I like that Royal Thai lets you order items to your spice level liking, basically not spicy at all to Thai Hot (5).  My tofu pad thai was good.  It is a pretty small portion, but a has a decent amount of triangles of pan fried tofu over the pad thai noodles.  The flavor is always good.  My husband's chicken fried rice had very little chicken tonight and he was charged two dollars for adding broccoli, which seemed ok as it was a lot of broccoli.  The servers are attentive, as my water glass was always full.  I gave this 3 stars because I am never thrilled with my meal here, but I am never disappointed either.  I also wish that they would stop putting groups directly next to each other in a practically empty restaurant.  Finally, I seem to remember the portions being larger and felt that 11.95 for my portion was a little pricey compared to some other places in Tampa.  

PS-I recommend the Amazing chicken, but ask that they give you broiled chicken not fried chicken unless that is what you prefer.  It comes with mixed vegetables and peanut sauce over rice.

I've been to Ribit's BBQ several times since it opened, including a visit tonight.  I always want this BBQ to be really good.  As a Kansas City gal in a former life, sometimes my mouth just starts salivating at the thought of good BBQ.  But, every time I go I am underwhelmed.  Is the location on Howard convenient and unique in a converted gas station...heck yes. Is this probably a good spot in your early twenties after you've been drinking too much? Heck, yes.  Is the price right for a pulled pork or beef brisket sandwich?  At $7 for the amount of meat and size of the sandwich...heck, yes.  Tonight I had the Porky platter which is one meat and 2 sides for 10.95.  I went with the brisket, collard greens and macaroni and cheese.  The brisket had good flavor, smoky and lean, but it was dry and needed some BBQ sauce.  Ribits has several to choose from...spicy, sweet, tangy, and NC sauce.  I'm really not a fan of any of them.  Sweet is how I was raised...and there is nothing here that comes close to that.  But, I went for their version of the sweet and it was good on the brisket.  The collards had a good bite to them, but were almost flavorless.  I could taste vinegar and nothing else.  I wish they had some spices or meat to give more flavor.  Lastly the macaroni and cheese had that plastic shine to it and again it was completely lacking flavor. 

My husband had the pulled pork sandwich on a large sesame seed bun.  He devoured it with the spicy sauce.  The pork was a little more juicy and was not fatty at all.  Points for that.  He got a side of potato salad though and the flavorless theme continued.  Somebody throw a little salt on something here at least.  Dinner for two came to $24 dollars.  I suggest sticking to the meat here only.  The sides can be skipped.  

Ribits gets three stars for convenient location, good meats, and friendly staff.

Wrights Gourmet House is a well-known Tampa staple for sandwiches and cakes.  I've only ever had one bad experience here and I think it was just an off day, possibly a new person making the sandwiches etc.  Every other trip has been good.  If you're coming during the lunch rush get ready to wait.  You stand in line, order at the counter and sandwiches are literally made in front of you (some take up to 15 minutes to press).  

What I love about Wright's Gourmet House....they have fresh mint for their tea and water!  They have the best cake in Tampa.  We had 5 different cakes from there at our wedding (think chocolate chocolate, red velvet, carrot cake, yellow cake with chocolate frosting etc).  My favorite cake is their Alpine cake.  The yellow cake is moist and melts in your mouth.  It is two layers and is loved up in the middle and all over the outside with a delicious, yet simple chocolate frosting that is thick but not overwhelming.  Lastly there are white chocolate shavings on top.  You can buy it as a cupcake, a slice of cake (very generous serving) whole cake or sheet cake.  Make sure you save room to at least try something!
I also love their California Reuben that is pressed with shaved turkey, Jarlsberg cheese, cole slaw and Russian dressing.  A tip...these sandwiches are huge and you can order them by the half which I normally do so I have more room for cupcakes.  

What I don't love about Wright's Gourmet House....salad dressings are very heavy and the flavors just don't agree with me.  Soups that I have had are pretty salty.   Parking during the lunch rush can sometimes be difficult.

I haven't been to Mellow Mushroom in years.  Today I met a friend at the Brandon location.  It is a quick 15 minute jaunt from downtown Tampa, located in a strip mall close to Costco and the Brandon Mall.  Location is good in terms of ease getting there and convenience of other items around it.  The inside of Mellow Mushroom is decorated a little cheesy for my taste, but I know a lot of people love bright, varied colors.  My friend and I both ordered small make your own pizzas.  I appreciated that they had a wide variety of topping selections, including tempeh and tofu.  I ordered a spinach, artichoke and tofu pizza.  My friend ordered pepperoni with an appetizer of spinach artichoke dip.  The dip came out about 30 seconds before our pizzas.  It came with toasted baguette portions that appeared to be buttered and topped with garlic and parmesan.  Overall I felt that everything was too greasy and heavy, but my friend enjoyed it.  My pizza had lots of potential.  It was covered with spinach, artichoke and tofu.  It was 10 inches and had a huge pillowy crust surrounding the exterior.  I loved the crust, brushed with butter and garlic, but the marinara sauce was really thick and chunky and I'm not a sauce gal.  Also the cheese was just ok. I appreciated all the toppings and felt like I got my monies worth on those, but at almost $13 it seemed a little pricey overall.  Our waitress was attentive and I appreciated the huge glasses of water!  I would go back but I would try a different sauce and cheese blend, or perhaps a salad.

This is one of my favorite places in all of Tampa.  So, why not five stars then.....well, it's not Sail Pavilion's fault but I really cannot handle cigarette smoke and since this is outdoors you're bound to smell it.  Ok, back to why this place is so great.  It is right on water.  Hold the presses, I know a cool place on the water in Tampa....didn't know those existed.  This is a round pavilion overlooking the water directly across from Jacksons by the Convention Center.  They have their own bathrooms on site, which has been a great addition as you used to have to walk into the convention center to use their facilities.  Don't come here hungry because they don't really serve food, but the drinks are reasonably priced.  If you want to relax and listen to music or play some cornhole this is the place to do it.  Just got done taking the dog for a walk, pull up a chair.  Want a quick drink before you head out on the town, this is also a good spot.  Young and old, dressed up and in sweats this place is just right for all.  We've been known to hang out here for hours during the day or in the evening.  It's just the best!  

Not sure where to park...sometimes you can park in the little parking lot next to it, but other times you may just need to park in convention center or Tampa Times Forum lots and make the quick walk.  

Oh, and they are going to start having food trucks again on Fridays so walk down for dinner and stay for the great atmosphere!

Food truck gets 3 stars...

The good: My friend's mom "rented" the truck for a day after the wedding lunch for guests at her house.  Very cool.  Stylish truck that looked clean on the inside.  Bread is from Pane Rustica so it is fresh and delicious.  Owners are very friendly.  

The bad: I ordered a Philly cheesesteak sandwich and I watched them microwave some of the components.  Major turn off.  

The ugly:  Nothing was ugly, other than the remains of my picked through and half eaten sandwich.

Overall the flavors in my sandwich were good, but I just couldn't look beyond the microwaving of some of the components and it was a touch greasy.

As a competitor to Whole Foods in Tampa, Publix Greenwise was a welcome addition to the Soho area of S. Tampa.  I am here more than I care to admit....call me a lazy consumer, but this is closer to my house than Whole Foods and often results in me having a lower grocery bill.  I like that the parking is indoors, particularly on rainy days.  This store is always very clean, well staffed, and has good lighting.  I appreciate the stronger commitment to organic and natural products, but compared to Whole Foods the selection is not as good.  Yes, the Publix brand of organic items is much cheaper than its counterparts, but I worry about BPA in the cans and the rigor of their safety and organic standards.  If you're looking for more obscure items or speciality items Whole Foods is still the place to go, but if you're looking for organic staples (milk, eggs, tofu, butter, cheese, veggies, fruits, meats) this store has a great selection.  I often buy the bulk of my weekly groceries here and then supplement other items from Whole Foods.  

Also, the staff here is great.  I have been able to return items with no hassle, ask for assistance without having to search for someone, and am generally greeted by multiple employees throughout my shopping experience.  Although I don't take them up on it I do appreciate them offering to help me out to my car with the groceries.

Whole Foods was a big deal when it came to Tampa.  I know a lot of people call it Whole Paycheck, which it can be if you shop hungry!  

The good:  A great selection of food and specialty items, health and beauty, household supplies, and yummy hot food and salad bar.  365 brand and Whole Foods ever increasing standards of quality for organic and natural products, eliminating the use of BPA, and commitment to local producers and businesses is impressive.  I also enjoy that I can recycle my Brita filters here and that staff are super knowledgeable in their areas of expertise and always willing to help.  Bring your own bags and you can donate the 10 cents to a local charity!

Off the hot bar I love the chicken and dumpling soup, the garlic tofu, and orange beets.  They also have delicious slices of cheese pizza with pillowy crust and seasoned with herbs for less than $2 a slice.  

The bad: Getting to this Whole Foods can be a feat of great patience, so try to go at off peak hours.  Parking can be troublesome, but I always go to the second floor which is usually pretty empty since it's on the level between Whole Foods and Target.

The ugly:  The price if you get sucked into the gorgeous looking prepared foods or super high dollar specialty items.  Check out the specials and coupons before going in and stick to the bulk bins or 365 brand items for most things and you should be ok!

So, I'm ranking this Starbucks as a 3 compared to others in Tampa.  Why so low?  The parking here is a nightmare as is getting in and out of the actual parking lot.  They are seriously out of two of my favorite things....vanilla roobois tea and rice krispy treats (or rice dream bars as I think Starbucks calls them) at least 75% of the time.  I've asked them multiple times why they are consistently out of these items and no one seems to have a great answer.  The bathroom is normally pretty dirty too.  

Giving them the benefit of the doubt though this is a very high volume Starbucks and their staff have always been warm, attentive and pleasant.  They are efficient as well for the volume of people they push through on a daily basis.

I hate scoring places so low but this place was a disaster.  Maybe we were there on an off night because I have friends who love this place and to be fair other people in our party of 5 were happy with their meal.  We showed up a little after 7pm and sat ourselves since we couldn't find a hostess.  From there our server screwed up our drink order and basically disappeared for most of the night.  We had to go to the bar to get water refills and we had to go to the pizza counter for more salad dressing when our salads appeared with basically no dressing. I started with the small Fire House Salad. It stated that it came with roasted tomato and fennel, candied walnuts, figs, mixed greens and shaved provolone.  It was pretty big and I appreciated the mixed greens, however the lettuce wasn't cut at all so I spent a few minutes making manageable bites.  The candied walnuts tasted stale and there were two tiny tomato chunks on the whole salad.  For my main entree I ordered the mushroom gnocchi that came with peas, bacon, and a sherry cream sauce.  I also added chicken, which oddly came sliced on a plate on the side.  The gnocchi had an overpowering smell and flavor of maple syrup which I'm assuming came from the bacon.  It was just so pervasive that I couldn't enjoy the entree and I sent it back.  I was then glad the chicken breast was served on the side because I did eat that.  

Other issues: My friend was charged more for subbing a side that was actually less expensive than the side that came with his entree.  My husband's waffle fries were cold and his burger, which was supposed to be medium came out well done. The pizza was average and a little soggy.  Lastly our server barely spoke two words to us all evening.  

The actual space is pretty cool and the bar area was hopping! I think this would be a better place for drinks....they have a full bar with specialty liquors.  Also, two people in our party got the cornmeal crusted chicken and mac and cheese and enjoyed it.

Since this was my first visit I'm willing to give it another try, but it might be awhile until I get up the courage to go back.

I drive by this place all the time and have never stopped in, but today I had lunch catered by them and now I will be stopping in!  I had the chicken salad sandwich.  It was served on a soft, whole wheat bread.  The chicken salad was not too gloppy with mayo, but not too dry either.  It has a hint of curry spice and a nice textural contrast due to the celery and almonds.  I also happen to be a huge fan of golden raisins and was pleased when I discovered those in the sandwich as well.  I also tried the spinach salad that came with tomato, cheese, walnuts, fresh mushrooms, golden raisins, hard boiled egg and bacon.  Everything was very fresh and the flavors worked well together.  Lastly, I had a bite of the chocolate brownie and it was moist and fudgy.  I cannot wait to actually go into this deli and see what other offerings they have to try!

I've eaten here about 5 times, both for lunch and dinner in the sushi bar side and the hibachi side.  I'm ranking this 2 stars because I have definitely had better food elsewhere and my last two experiences there were not good at all.  

I've had the mango girl which is described as spicy lobster with asparagus wrapped in mango with a sweet chili sauce.  What they don't tell you (even when you ask the waitress) is that it is also drowned in some sort of mayonnaise sauce, which negates the fresh flavors that might have been found otherwise. 

Other times we've dined here the food has been overly salted, cold, very fishy smelling, and pricey.  The service is also just average.  I've been known to go the bar for a refill of my water.  

The last time I ate here I got carryout.  I ordered the salmon teriyaki with miso soup and white rice.  When I got home I took one bite of the miso and couldn't go any further.  It was so salty that it was inedible.  The salmon was completely overcooked and salty as well, they gave me fried rice instead of the white rice I asked for and the veggies that came with the salmon were comprised of onions....maybe a carrot thrown in for good measure.  I called the restaurant and the manager said that the next time we came in that dinner would on them.  Good customer service, but I've had enough bad experiences here that it's not even worth it to me.  Hibachi can be a fun experience, but the food is a let down.

The Parkshore Grill is a great spot for lunch with a view in St. Pete.  I love to sit outside and people watch along Beach Drive and nothing is better than an after lunch stroll by the water.  I find the inside are is quite a different vibe and do not like it at all.  Outside is the place to be, unless you get stuck by a smoker.

I've had great service at lunch when I've been here, including an attentive and knowledgeable waitstaff.  

The prices seem a little high to me, about 15 for a lunch chicken Caesar salad, but the food is always good.  I wouldn't say they food has ever been great, but it has been fresh and well seasoned.  

If you find yourself in St. Pete on a beautiful day and are hungry for some decent food and great views check it out!

I stumbled onto this place when I used to live in Pinellas.  I had heard some rumblings about it, but couldn't imagine that something in a strip mall would be good.

I've been there for breakfast and lunch and can tell you that the O'gratin grits are cheesy, creamy and delicious.  The grilled cheese and ham sandwich with tomato bisque is the perfect cure to any rainy day and anywhere that has an artichoke and hearts of palm salad on the menu is a blessing in my book.  

They have good options for vegetarians and meat eaters, plus I am pleased that they have hormone, antibiotic, and preservative free meat.

Don't let the exterior fool you...inside you will find a nicely decorated restaurant with comfy booths, friendly waiters, and good food.

I've been to Boca both for dinner and brunch and was underwhelmed at each experience.  Most recently we had a large party for brunch.  We got a beautiful table right next to the windows and I really do enjoy the interior at Boca. I also appreciate their commitment to local foods.  Our service was decent, but the food was painfully average to sub average.  I got the salad #9 because I was going to share the buttermilk pancakes with my husband who also got a side of scrambled eggs.  The salad was small and I was disappointed because the description on the menu didn't fit what I got.  The corn was not roasted, there was no avocado, the pineapple salsa consisted of 4 chunks of plain pineapple and the salad contained shaved red onion, jicama and arugula which were not in the description at all.  Unfortunately I am not a fan of the last three ingredients and specifically ordered the salad for the avocado, roasted corn and pineapple salsa.  My husband's buttermilk pancakes were 4 deep and good sized.  They came with the tiniest portions of chantilly, syrup, and mixed berries (blueberries and raspberries).  The pancakes were very dense and dry.  We had to ask for more syrup three times and the berries tasted like they were drenched in alcohol (not ok for a pregnant lady).  The scrambled eggs were rubbery and overcooked.  Fluffy scrambled eggs are a lost art form in my opinion.  Other members of our party were happy with their lobster eggs benedict and hangover panini, but again didn't rave about them.  I really want to like this place a lot and keep being disappointed when I just don't.  

I'm giving this place three stars though for ambience, commitment to local foods, and the fact that even though the food is average it is always fresh.

Cafe Dufrain gets points for being one of the few restaurants on the waterfront in Tampa.  They also get points for their emphasis on fresh, seasonal, local ingredients.  However, they lose points for sometimes very average food. I've been here several times and it is hit or miss.  They also have a limited drink menu if you're into that, with many popular liquors not making an appearance on the menu.  The service too can be a mix of people who seem to have no idea about the menu, to decent service from knowledgable staff.  

Tonight was a good night.  My husband and I shared the 4 hour pork bolognese with ricotta and gnocchi which is considered a "sharing" item and the grilled chicken sandwich with smoked cheddar and a molasses bbq sauce.  We also added a side of fries on the side.  The grilled chicken sandwich was really good.  The chicken was moist, on a lightly sweet bun with smoky cheddar and a spicy bbq sauce.  All the flavors melded well together.  There were homemade chips on the side, but I was more interested in the fries.  The fries themselves were tiny and a mix of crispy and slightly soggy.  My husband and I both felt they were overly salted, but had they not been they definitely had potential.  The gnocchi were perfect little pillows swimming in the pork bolognese and ricotta.  This was good, but I wished there was some sort of textural contrast as all the items were soft.  Overall, it was a good meal and including two drinks came to a little over $40 for two.  Tip:  the fries on the side were $6, so make sure you're committed to eating the bowl for that price.  

I would come here again for the atmosphere and that chicken sandwich.

I met a friend for lunch at Piquant this week.  

Highlights:

1.  The remodel of the interior is clean, sleek and open complete with a stunning pastry case.  
2.  The bread was very fresh and delicious.
3.   I liked that they brought an extremely cold bottle of water for the table in a beautiful glass carafe. 
4.   I love the location in Hyde Park Village and that you can sit outside!

The things that disappointed me:

1. I had the roasted turkey sandwich on a french baguette.  I literally bite into a huge piece of fat that was at least 2.5 inches long on my first bite. After removing that there was barely any turkey left.   Also, the mango chutney was disjointed and overly sweet.  

2.  The sandwich was $11 and was tiny.  I mean seriously tiny.  It came with a side of homemade veggie chips which were pretty oily and lacked flavor.  Overall the value for what I got was disappointing.

3.  Our waitress hadn't tasted very many menu items.  We asked about 4.  She had tried none.  I know the restaurant is new, so hopefully this will improve over time.  

Although I scored this very low on my initial visit I will say that I have seen Piquant being very gracious over social media stating they are taking all customer comments to heart and are committed to making this a great place.  Additionally, I will be back to try the pastries and the yummy quiche that I saw someone eating on my way out (I hadn't seen it on the menu otherwise I would have ordered it.  Our waitress told us it wasn't available at lunch).  Be sure to check back when I update this after my next visit.

Cru Cellars is a great spot right in the heart of Palma Ceia, one of my favorite areas of Tampa.  I don't even drink and I love this place.  I've been able to try stuff off their new dinner and brunch menus enjoying both the indoor and outdoor seating.  First let me say I love their space.  It's open with beautiful wine rack displays and rustic wood tables.  There is a more private room for a group, a dining area by the bar and a charming little outdoor area perfect for brunch.  

Food that I have loved includes the mushroom orzo, the blueberry waffles at brunch that come with ricotta and lemon zest, cinnamon cream syrup, and a side of fresh fruit (think blueberries, blackberries, oranges, and raspberries), and the burger on pretzel bun.  My husband got the croissant sandwich with cheese, scrambled egg, and thick slab bacon.   He got roasted yukon gold potatoes on the side.  The sandwich was amazing (I stole a few bites, of course), but I could do without the potatoes.  They were oily and room temperature.  

I look forward to going back and trying more items off the dinner and brunch menus as everything that I have seen coming out of the kitchen looks delicious.  Oh yeah, and if you do drink talk about a wonderful selection with a knowledgeable owner who is more than happy to talk wine!  

PS-We walked right in at 11am for brunch and were seated immediately! Much better than some other brunch spots in the area.

So the Refinery....what can you say?  A James Beard nominated chef, a dinner menu that changes weekly, a brunch menu that changes seasonally, a chalkboard with listing of local farms goods featured that week, friendly staff, mason jars for drinks and a newly finished covered deck....oh yeah, and the food is pretty darn good.  I've been to the Refinery about 6 times over the past few years.  I've been for brunch three times and dinner three times.

The most recent time I went was to take a friend for a birthday brunch.  We made reservations, which I recommend since the dining room is small and the upstairs outdoor deck fills up fast.  My husband and I shared the brioche can bread french toast with carmelized plantains and chantilly cream, as well as scrambled eggs and a biscuit.  The french toast was a huge round piece of brioche covered in syrup with a dollop of chantilly cream and a few small slices of plantain.  It was so rich and sweet, like dessert for breakfast.  It was amazing, but we were glad we had the scrambled eggs to balance the sweetness.  By the way, I have this thing about restaurants being terrible at making scrambled eggs, but these were actually fluffy and flavorful, not like the dried out thin strips of egg I usually get elsewhere.  The biscuit was good, very buttery and you could literally peel it apart by layers.  My only complaint was that it wasn't warm when I got it and despite my sweet bites of french toast I was wishing for some homemade, seasonal strawberry jam to go with it.

Don't let the location fool you, this place has some of the best food in Tampa.  If you're not an adventurous eater the dinner menu at first read can be intimidating, but trust me when I tell you that chef knows what he's doing, so my tip is just to ask your server for recommendations and dive into the menu.  Vegetarian and vegan options are available, and for goodness sake, don't go modifying your order.....again, chef knows what he's doing and all those things are on your dish for a reason!

Stopped in for our own little Easter brunch complete with a creative loafing deal that gave us $15 worth of stuff for $2.50.  We were already off to a good start.  The pastry case looked amazing and we settled on splitting a vanilla cupcake with nutella frosting.  Yes we decided on dessert first....don't you?  My husband had a croissant sandwich with egg and cheddar that came with an orange slice.  He loved it.  Fluffy egg, freshly baked croissant and thick melted cheese.  I had scrambled eggs that came with three slices of toast and an orange slice.  I also got the side of fruit which was a rather large bowl of strawberries, blueberry, kiwi and green apple.  I could tell it was fresh from that morning as the apple was still true to its color.  The scrambled eggs were just ok.  I got a lot of them, but they were a little dry which was a perfect match for my dry toast.  I guess you have to ask for butter or jam.  We also had a hazelnut latte that was delicious and enormous.  It stayed piping hot through our meal and was so big that we got a to go cup.  My husband said it was the best latte he's had in town.  Oh, did I mention that had chocolate samples?  We tried all three, white, milk and dark chocolate.  They were delicious but when we asked how we could buy some they didn't know.  They didn't think they were selling it which we thought was odd.  Onto the cupcake.  It was a mini version which is good considering we ate all the above.  The cupcake was moist and the frosting was chilled, thick and creamy.  We couldn't detect the nutella, rather it tasted almost like a frosty in frosting form.  It was good, but not great.  We were hoping to get some brioche, but showing up at noon on Easter Sunday is probably the reason we didn't get any.  Oh, and if you're wondering we got all the above for $5.50 thanks to our great deal. I will be back to try lunch someday and to sample more of their baked goods.  

Just a few tips---parking is in the Ventana garage immediately on the right when you enter the parking lot.  There are about 5 reserved spaces for the restaurant and we were able to pull right in.  It's sort of self-service...you place your order at the counter, get your own water, come back to get your food, and put your plates up in the bins on your way out.

If you're a tea lover like me then you will be kicking yourself, much like I was, that you did not check this place out sooner.  I'll admit that driving by the storefront on a rundown, strip mall laden area of Fletcher right off 275, that I had my doubts.  The second I walked in though I was happy.  Their tea menu is very extensive and I had my eye on the red raspberry leaf tea.  I decided to purchase it in one of their tins, as loose leaf tea needs to stay air tight to maintain freshness.  The person helping me said that she could give me 2 oz of the loose leaf tea, but that she would need to give me the 4 oz. tin since it was such a fluffy tea.  I was not charged for the larger tin, which is great customer service.  I decided to sample my purchase in the Iced version while I was there.  They let me know it would be a few minutes so I walked around looking at all the great tea products.  They also had books, magazines and board games to help pass the time.  There was plenty of seating, plus an area much like you would find at a Japanese restaurant behind sliding paper lined doors where you remove your shoes and sit down at tables where your feet drop below to the floor.  They also offer yoga and many other events...check out their calendar online.  The food menu, though, small looked and smelled amazing.  Again, I was kicking myself for having eaten before I came because I wanted to try everything.  The vegan cupcakes were calling my name too and got high marks from the staff and customers alike.  The tea was delicious in iced form and I appreciated that the staff took the time to explain to me (even though it was on my label) how to make the tea for iced vs. hot purposes and large vs. small batches.  

Friendly staff, reasonable prices, clean space with an inviting, serene atmosphere.  I will definitely be back.

When I stepped into Dough yesterday, the latest brain child of Datz I sort of felt like a grown up entering Willie Wonka's chocolate factory.  The decor is fun and whimsical and the pastry counters are brimming with beautiful confectionary creations.  It was about 11:30am and the place was semi-full.  I was a little confused about where to order and the 3 people behind the counter were no help....classic Datz...bad service abounds.  After about 5 minutes I finally asked someone if they could please help me....no one ever acknowledged my presence.  Having read some reviews online I really wasn't sure what to try.  My husband loves chocolate cake donuts so I got one of those that had some chocolate and vanilla glaze.  I also got the maple donut that is the shape of an eclair with pastry cream on the inside and a thick strip of bacon on top of the maple frosting.  They were also sampling mini key lime tarts (at least I think they were...one staff member said they were not samples, another did) so I got a few to share with my family.  Two donuts were about six and a half bucks, a little pricey but I'm ok paying for quality.  PS-My mom tried to order a latte, but the lady told her that she could start it but someone else would have to finish it.  Again, no one acknowledged her presence or asked her if they could help her.  She had to ask.  She left without purchasing anything. I took my treats home in the white box they provided and shared them with my husband and mother.

Chocolate cake donut:  Dry and shockingly not very sweet.  We thought it might have been better if they put a glaze on the whole donut and then the chocolate frosting, but the donut itself could use some work. 

The maple bacon donut:  This was decent.  I liked the maple frosting, but did not like that the bacon fat was making the donut a little soggy.  The cream filling also seemed more like cottage cheese in consistency and I prefer mine to be smooth.  I might order it again if they are fresh.

The key lime tarts: These were a HUGE hit!  I don't even like key lime that much and this were the perfect punch of tart key lime flavor.  The meringue on top was beautiful and a nice light contrast to the crunch of the tart shell and tartness of the key lime.  We would definitely order these again and I had wished I snagged more samples.  Yum!  

I'll be back to try some other goodies another time.  I'm hoping that the service is better and the overall food product is as well.  I think the place has promise though and I love dessert!

SERVICE, SERVICE, SERVICE.  We made reservations for our second anniversary online 10 minutes before we arrived last week.  We told them it was our anniversary and that I was needing to eat dairy free.  When we got there they had a hand written card for us, a dairy free menu and offered either a champagne toast or free dessert.  Multiple people told us happy anniversary and thanked us for choosing to dine with them.  My water glass was never empty and everyone was very attentive. 

The atmosphere is great here too.  It is always impeccably clean in the dining room and the bathrooms.  I love the open kitchen and the plethora of booths.  

The food is always average to me.  I've never really been blown away there, but I've never had a bad meal either.  What was good...the vegan tasting menu...think tofu with mango salsa, steamed snow peas, asparagus, golden beets and killer quinoa salad.  My husband loves the buffalo chili and the peanut butter mousse dessert.  I stuck with the fruit dessert (only option for dairy free folks).  

Overall we had a great experience!  We've been here a bunch and will be back.

Zudar's is a local staple for great lunch.  The prices for the portion sizes are spot on and in the over 20 times I've eaten here I've never had a bad meal.  

Some of my favorites are the Cobb Nosh sandwich...think bacon, avocado, and fresh turkey on your choice of bread.  I also love the cobb and cuban salads.  They are huge and usually last 2-3 meals.  Their honey mustard dressing is to die for...if you like it sweet and thick like me! If you're craving some great pie look no further.  I've enjoyed the coconut cream pie many times.  The slices are big and always fresh!

It's usually crowded for lunch, but the service moves fast, so don't be afraid to wait a few minutes.  If you're really in a rush call ahead or grab one of the prepared items from the cooler, pay at the counter and be on your way.  You won't be disappointed.

Doormet. I always have high hopes and usually walk away feeling.....meh.  We ordered delivery for the first time tonight.  What was good....orzo pasta salad and spinach salad done vegan.  The spinach was fresh and I'm a sucker for anything with golden raisins. Plus, the honey Dijon dressing is perfectly tangy and sweet.  The price is reasonable and our delivery person was punctual and friendly. What was not good....the meatball sub.  The meatballs were inedible due to salt overload and If you're expecting ooey gooey melted cheese you won't find it here.  Same goes for the spaghetti and meatballs which was salty with a healthy dose of fennel.

I've previously had overly salted soups and average pizza from here.  I've also had the classic salad adding grilled chicken which is a great blend of grapes, strawberry, mixed greens, candied walnuts and honey Dijon.  As you can see it's been hit or miss for me. The concept to deliver gourmet food is awesome, but again it always just leaves me saying....meh.

I am happy to report that my return visit to Piquant was a great success. We took my dad for his birthday. He got the chicken salad sandwich on a croissant and raved it was the best croissant of his life. My mother said the ambience reminded her of Paris.  I got the purple spinach salad with pistachio, shaved apple, smoked chicken, barley and avocado. It was a great blend of flavors..smoky chicken, salty, crunchy pistachio, and sweet apples.  I particularly loved the chew of the barley.  Desserts highlight was the chocolate mousse and lemon tart.  Skip the chocolate chip cookies.  Can't wait to go back.

This is by far my favorite restaurant in South Tampa for lunch and dinner. The place is always hopping during the lunch and dinner rush and the ambience is both classy, comforting, and inviting.  There is a set lunch and dinner menu, with specials that change daily.  My favorites include the Baked Rigatoni (I get it with chicken instead of sausage), the watermelon salad, danish bleu salad, tomato bisque, turkey sandwich as a salad complete with sweet onion jam and homemade aioli, and really anything off the specials menu at night.  I might argue they have the best burger in town!  Seriously, try it.  Or try the ever popular roasted acorn squash stuffed with the chicken salad of the day.  For dessert, I love the espresso cookies and the Barry White cookies.  The former are like a cookie-brownie hybrid.  They are rich, but do not taste like espresso, it is simply there to enhance the chocolate flavor.  The latter are a toffee cookie with chocolate ganache filling.  Extremely rich, but satisfying.  If they're out of those two dessert options go for the summer cake at night or one of the delicious tarts (apple, peach or blueberry), black and white cookie or chocolate cupcake.  And people, this is a bakery first and foremost so enjoy the bread! I've tried them all and the only one I don't like is rye, but I don't like rye bread anyway.  My favorite is the complimentary warm bread at night that comes with the most palate pleasing white bean hummus topped with roasted red pepper, basil, and olive oil.  I've been known to ruin my dinner on this alone.  I've hosted several parties here in the private rooms to rave reviews.  The service and food are always on point.  The owners, Kevin and Karyn are there daily and are truly invested in their business.  They, along with managers Julie and Brian, are there to make sure you have the best experience possible.  Say hi to them and thank them for their hard work! 

Even with perfection though comes room for improvement.  I'm not a huge fan of their breakfast pastries or frittatas and parking can be a nightmare during peak hours, but it's worth the hassle once you get inside. 

Enjoy!

M5QAuzQB9ee0ntf9RKkx7Q.review_text: One of the few decent restaurants in Delaware. They have a great lunch special and the food quality is typically quite good. The restaurant has a very quiet and comfortable atmosphere. For a spot to grab a solid bento box for lunch or sushi, Sakura is a great choice.

An unexpected gem for the area. The Creamery is honestly a really awesome spot to post up and chill with some friends. There's cornhole, bacci ball, jenga, and live music. Definitely a nice pop up beer garden; I'd highly recommend checking it out if you're in the area. For those who just want the beer, there's a solid selection of craft beers in the main hall.

My girlfriend and I love this place. The interior is very unique and cozy. The food is all spot on and really well made. I think the service takes the crown, though. Our server was very attentive and even told us about how special some of their cutlery is. The whole restaurant just has a nice, intimate feel to it.
Overall a good bakery with really well plated desserts. From the desserts I've tried, I think the flavors could be a little richer personally. Will definitely stop by again though.

Pretty good sushi for the area. It is located in a charming Main Street at Collingswood and is a good spot to go if you're nearby. We have gone a few times and the service has always consistently been fast. The sushi isn't anything extraordinary, but it's enough to satisfy a craving and it's always played really well.

Overall I'd give Harp & Crown 5 stars for the experience. I came here on Valentine's Day with my girlfriend and we weren't disappointed. Here's my breakdown on the restaurant:

Service - definite five stars here. The entire restaurant staff worked cohesively. We didn't go more than a minute without a full glass of water. Our plates were also cleared and replaced between each dish.

Food - we got the lamb meatballs, garlic prawns, scallops, hanger steak, and pear tart. The lamb meatballs were a small tapas style dish, but it was probably my favorite. The scallops were really tasty but unfortunately had a bit of sand in them. The hanger steak was also quite good, although a little chewy. For dessert, I'd highly recommend the pear tart - I could eat that all day.

Drinks - easily five stars. Will definitely be back for the drinks. The longfellow sour is dangerously good! If you come here, you need to get this drink

They must be reading the recent negative reviews because the service was definitely on point when we stopped in. We made a reservation for 8pm, and were seated in about 2 minutes upon arrival. Our server also checked in on us periodically and the manager even walked around to each table to check how everyone was doing. 

Now for the food. We ordered a mix of shrimp, crawfish, potatoes, and sausage - all in the boiling house special blend. I would've liked there to have been more of the blend/sauce, but it was pretty good overall. I also got a Thai iced tea, which I normally have a hard time finding one I like, but the one here was especially good. If you're craving seafood around the area, the Boiling House is def worth checking out.

This has easily become our go to spot for pho. There's no frills or anything extra about the place, but it's exactly what I want when I crave pho. Plus, your food usually comes out super fast. Definitely get yourself a Vietnamese iced coffee while you're here as well.

This bar is definitely a nice go to spot for a casual chill night with the crew. The layout has several sofas and chairs, with kind of a 90's basement hangout vibe.. 

In regards to the actual drinks - the cocktails are fairly priced, but I didn't think they were anything amazing. Kinda felt that it left a little more to be desired overall. I had the 'heather on the hills' and the Paloma, so take from it what you will.  It also took a really long time to get a drink order in despite sitting at the bar with only one other couple.

Overall I'd say it's worth checking out if you're near the area.

If I reviewed the ramen broth alone - it's easily 5 stars. Seriously some of the best noodles and broth I've ever had. I'm extremely picky with how I like the actual noodle consistency/firmness in ramen, and they nailed it 100%. 

My girlfriend and I had the spicy chicken ramen, and the spicy pork ramen with miso. Meat wise I'd say definitely go with pork as it complements the ramen more. The chicken was kind of like pieces of grilled chicken, which although tasty, I felt like didn't work with the ramen as much. I was hoping it would be more of a thinly sliced and roasted chicken. Honestly though, I'd be more than okay eating the spicy ramen without any meat at all based on how much I liked the flavors. Also it should be noted that the spicy ramen comes in different heat levels based on preference (i.e. 1-5). We tried the 1 and the 3 - both of which weren't too spicy. If you like a bit of an actual kick I'd say go with a 3. The spice does just enough where it doesn't take away from the flavors or make you sweat profusely..

In regard to the actual restaurant itself, it's a very quaint space but I didn't mind it at all. The service was really good as well, as our sever (possibly owner?) seemed very personable to all of the diners.

I'm always kind of weary of trying Southeast Asian restaurants in smaller towns, especially if I'm craving something more on the authentic side. Safe to say I was pleasantly surprised by Pinto Thong's dishes and menu selection. I ended up getting the duck fried rice because of all the rave in the reviews and it definitely didn't disappoint. The portion size was quite large and I honestly thought it tasted even better the next day when I brought the leftovers for work. 

I wouldn't say it was the best Thai food I've had, but for the random location it's a gem. Worth checking out if you're near by or passing through!

This is honestly one of the best low-key gems in the area. From the outside it's an unassuming barn, but on the inside it's a portal to France. We got the Marie Antoinette set for a light lunch and it was just enough for the two of us. It comes with several tea sandwiches, plenty of baked desserts, and unlimited tea.

If I could only rave about one thing here, it'd be the quiche. It was seriously the best quiche I've ever had. It was baked on puff pastry so it had the perfect blend of flakiness and moist egg greatness. They have mastered everything here, and I honestly can't wait to come back.

Took my dad here for Father's day and really glad I did! The location was a little out of the way from where the majority of restaurants are in the area, but don't let that deter you. You could easily tell all of the pasta and sauces were house made with how fresh it all tasted. I got the risotto with grilled shrimp which was cooked to perfection. The presentation of the dish was also very impressive with it's contrasting colors. As an appetizer we got the calamari and I am not exaggerating when I say that it was some of the best I've had. Honestly I've had my fair share of overly chewy calamari, so I was really happy when they nailed it here! Overall 4 entrees and an appetizer for about $100 was extremely reasonable. Don't forgot that you can bring your own wine and beer here (note: $8 opening fee for wine)! We also got some complimentary limoncello shots at the end which was a nice touch. Definitely a solid restaurant to satisfy your Italian food cravings. Looking forward to coming back when I'm around!

I've been wanting to go here for the longest time ever since I saw it on Food Network way back. I wasn't really craving anything to heavy at the time unfortunately, so I ended up getting the veggie burger. I'm by no means a vegetarian, but they did a really good job with the veggie burger patty. I think it could've used a little more zing (maybe some jalapeños blended with the guacamole?) and perhaps some pickled toppings, but overall not too bad for what it was. Definitely looking forward to trying there actual meat burgers next time though, which I'm sure are incredible. 

On a side the note we got a cocktail that was a mix with vodka, passion fruit, and a few other ingredients and it was insanely delicious. Can't remember the name unfortunately, but if you see that description on the drink menu I would highly recommend !
Still easily the best ramen spot in Philly. The pork is always cooked perfectly and the broths are extremely flavorful. Shoyu ramen is definitely the way to go if you want something light yet tasty.

Best hand drawn noodles in town! I always get the braised beef noodle soup and scallion pancakes. I tell myself I'll try something else some day, but the braised beef noodles are just too good to pass up on.

The all you can eat is such a good deal here. You order whatever you want and as much as you want, just as long as you finish it. You're only charged extra for dishes you don't end up finishing/wanting to take home, which is honestly very fair to avoid people over ordering. They have a large variety of rolls, sushi, and appetizers all included in the choices. Seriously for about $24 it's hard to beat. Order two of the specialty rolls at any other sushi restaurant would already cost you about the same. The quality of the food here is pretty spot on as well, so definitely give this place a visit if you're in the area.

Came here around 9:30pm on a Tuesday night and got seated right away. We got the oysters, jambalaya, and swordfish entree. Being that the restaurant wasn't too busy at this hour, everything came out very quickly. The two servers for our table were extremely attentive and friendly; they seemed genuinely interested on how we enjoyed the dishes.

I'm not huge on raw oysters just due to the sliminess and texture, but I honestly really really liked the P&J oysters here. For those in the area during the day they have a happy hour for $.75 oysters from 3-6pm. 

Regarding the main swordfish dish - it was easily the best I've had. I've only had swordfish a handful of other times, but it was always too dry for me. The Tasso rubbed grilled swordfish here, however, was seriously cooked to perfection. It also sat on a puréed corn/ polenta kind of sauce, which was really bomb. The spicy peppers also complemented the dish very well. Personally I would've liked if the swordfish had more of a salt crust, but that's just nitpicking. Overall really enjoyed all of the food and experience at Luke's.

Much more than Ok. The Martabak was great, and the owner was really cool. I ended up getting the beef Martabak with mozzarella. I would recommend just getting the traditional beef without the mozzarella though honestly. And make sure you ask for their dipping sauces! Will be back to try the sweet ones soon.

Terrain is easily the most aesthetic restaurant in the area. Its also an amazing store for all sorts of plants and interesting items (e.g. honey, soaps, books, etc.). Would recommend them to open up a small ice cream cart during the summer incorporating their locally grown ingredients to come up with some interesting flavors.

Food was great, and the service was even better. Came here with my family and the entire staff was very accommodating. It's a new restaurant so there doesn't seem to be too many people get, but the interior is very clean and chic! There's also a bunch of quality pastas and goods you can purchase off the shelf, this the market aspect.

I was planning to write a long review, but honestly you just need to know one thing.. The breakfast potatoes are THE best you'll ever have. Perfect amount of crisp and seasoning. I've also never seen an omelette made so smooth and aesthetic haha. The wait can be pretty long on weekends which is the only downside, but that's how you know it's good. Plus there's a fireplace you can sit by while you wait, which is always nice for the winter days.

Best fried rice (got the Indonesian FR) and Hong Kong milk tea I've had. The prices are also pretty reasonable as the fried rice came as a pretty large portion. I'm always skeptical of ordering fried rice at restaurants since it's a fairly easy dish to make yourself, but this definitely didn't disappoint. Will have to come back and try some of their other dishes when I have a chance.

Just a quick tip: make sure you bring cash as there is a $15 card minimum.

Been here three times so far, and have yet to order anything I didn't like. So far I've had the beef rendang with curry, fried chicken with coconut rice, and roasted pork noodles. I would go as far to say that this is one of my top 3 favorite Asian restaurants in philly for overall value. Goal for this year is to try every single dish at least once. 

Also just wanted to note that the owner and all staff are extremely nice.

Didn't have a chance to try anything other than a latte when I was here, but I was pretty impressed overall. I'm not a huge fan of overly sweet drinks, so I was pretty happy that the green tea matcha latte was just the right level. 

The cafe itself is actually a lot roomier than I imagined; definitely a good spot to post up and do some work if you're in the area.

Very intimate and classy bar without being pretentious! The staff and bartenders have always been really great every time. The new spring cocktail list has just come out so def recommend trying them. The Man Made Mile was essentially an adult strawberry milkshake with a mezcal base. The RH is also a solid drink if you enjoy cocktails with egg whites.

Might be a new favorite lunch spot during the work week for me. The falafel is definitely the best I've had in the city. I got the Mama's Falafel sandwich, which is stuffed with 5 falafel and a mix of veggies - all for only $8. They also have a little free standing cart in the store where you can add additional toppings and sauces.

As others have probably mentioned it's cash only here, but they do have an ATM inside.

Probably my favorite macarons I've had in Philly so far. They're not overly sweet which is a big plus for me. If you only try one I recommend the Orange Blossom, definitely the best macaron flavor combo I've come by!

Definitely some of the best Korean fried chicken wings that I've had. I almost always go to bonchon if I'm ever craving them, but figured I'd give it a try here since I walk past it pretty often. In all honesty I think this arguably better than the wings at bonchon. I only tried the spicy soy flavor, but the wings were really crispy and the inside had a lot of meat. Will have to come back and try it again to confirm, but I was definitely pleasantly surprised by how good it was. I also got the beef melt sandwich, which was really good. It was very banh mi-esque in terms of the bread and vegetables, but just with a lot of cheese. Wish it had jalapeños but other than that it was a good choice to balance out the wings.

Solid spot for a quick lunch during work. The portion size for the bowl is pretty generous, and it comes with pita (relatively standard now). The falafel here is probably my second favorite out of the surrounding restaurants (current falafel rank: 1. Mamas vegetarian, 2. Naya, 3. Naf Naf, 4. Cava). In terms of all of the rest of the toppings and bases, I think overall I still prefer Cava for its variety.

Hands down one of the best brunch spots I've been to so far in Philly. When walking in it almost has a leasing office layout, but the main dining area has a really nice ambiance. You can see the kitchen and everyone making the food which is always a nice touch. All of the staff here is also super nice so that's a huge plus. For those wondering, the wait here at noon on a Saturday was about 25 mins (worth it).
Food wise we got the crab cake Benedict and the chicken n waffles. Both were really well made and the portion sizes were pretty generous. I would go as far to say that these are definitely the best chicken and waffles around. The chicken meat is insanely juicy cause it's braised and then fried.

Super aesthetic cafe with very reasonable prices. There's a lot of hype around it being that it's led by the pastry chef from Zahav, but I'd say it lives up to it from what I experienced. That being said though you'll want to get here really early (at opening if possible) if you want to make sure you get what you really want. I got in about 3 mins after it opened on a Saturday and there was already a decent line (~15 minute wait). I ended up getting the pistachio sticky buns, which were amazing and not overly sweet. 

For anyone wondering you can only get a max of 3 of the same item, but a total of 12 pastries.

Awesome spot that recently opened right above Di Bruno Bros in Center City. Finally got around to trying it and it was definitely worth the visit. The interior is really aesthetic and has a really laid back vibe. We only ordered a few light bites since it was an odd hour of the day, but everything we got was delicious (charcuterie board and pizza). The pizzas are more personal sized, but they're fairly priced and well made. Our server was also extremely knowledgeable about all of the food and took the time to explain everything that came on the board we ordered. 

If you're just stopping in for a casual bite I'd say get one of the pizzas and the affogato. The affogato comes with cotton candy on top, which then gets melted by the hot coffee poured over. Will definitely be back to try some of their main dishes soon!

Really solid spot based on my first visit. I'd say it's one of the best new spots to have opened up recently. The staff of El Cafe and the POD hotel (where El Cafe is located in) were all extremely nice.  The actual area where you order is pretty small but once you walk further back it's a huge open space where you can pretty much sit anywhere. The space across from the bar/Condesa is really chill, and honestly seems like it could be a good study or work spot to post up at. 

In terms of the food I only got the chorizo breakfast taco and a horchata latte. Both were really good, but I'd say the taco ($5.50 for the chorizo one) is relatively small. For the quality of the ingredients the price makes sense, but you'll definitely want to get two tacos or one of their pastries if you're hungry. Will definitely be back to try some of their other stuff.

Finally tried this place after years of staying loyal to Nan Zhou Hand Dawn Noodles. I got the beef brisket noodle soup with the spicy broth. Honestly the broth flavor is probably one of the best I've had and I love the slight numbing spice. The noodles were good too, but I think Nan Zhou slightly takes the edge on that. The beef brisket itself was flavorful but most pieces were a little too fatty for my personal preference.

Overall I'd definitely come back, but I think Nan Zhou is still my preferred spot for the beef brisket soup because of the noodle texture and heartier pieces of beef.

Had dinner here recently and absolutely loved it. The interior is so well designed with middle eastern accents that you almost forget you're just in Philly. Unfortunately I came late in the evening on a rainy day so I wasn't able to check out the garden area in the back, which is supposed to be really nice.

For food we did the tasting menu and it's definitely A LOT of food so just keep that in mind if you're only going with one other person. The tasting menu allows you to select several small dishes either cold or hot, which easily fill you up (not to mention the massive pita breads that come along for dipping). 

For dessert you can either each choose a single item or combine to get one kanafeh for sharing. We were already extremely full so we ended up just getting the tehina and carob mousse along with a cup of their Lebanese chai latte - both extremely good. If I'm ever in the area I'd definitely grab on the chai lattes, easily the best one I've ever had.

Pretty cute spot to just chill and grab some tea/dessert. We got the Trio Combo Mix and Match which was a good way to try several items. Our favorite was the black sesame creme brûlée. Usually I find black sesame to be a little strong of a flavor but it was made really well and had a more subtle taste.

The charbroiled oysters were incredibly good here. We started with one dozen and then ended up getting another dozen since we liked it so much. We also got a few pounds of crawfish since they were only about $5 a pound. 

If you're over in the French quarter there's tons of places with charbroiled oysters and crawfish, but if you find yourself on this side of the river near Algiers point then this is definitely a solid choice. I honestly thought the oysters here were even better than the rest we had in the main touristy spots. The jalapeños they broiled the oysters with gave then a really nice kick.

Really solid spot to grab some pastries and is located right next to Dock Street Brewery. There's a small communal table inside for seating, but that's about it. Hopefully they'll add some seating outside as it warms up.

In terms of the actual pastries everything looked amazing so it was hard to choose what to try first. I got the pistachio tea cake and the apricot praline; both of which were really well made. I usually prefer more dense and less sweet desserts, so the pistachio tea cake was perfect. Pricing was also very reasonable at about $3.50 per small pastry item. Will definitely be back to try their other stuff.

Recently moved nearby and walked passed here several times before finally caving in to the temptation. I got the St. Antney's, which has sausage, peppers and onions. This was made fresh upon order and arguably one of the best pizzas I've had. It's not overly greasy or heavy on the dough, yet has all the flavor. The thinner crust let's me feel slightly less guilt eating an entire pie. Will def be back to try the rest of the menu for research.

Such a cool spot! The interior is really unique with some sweet denim couches to sit on. Right outside are a few seats as well with plants all around them. Walked past here several times thinking it was just a standard cafe, but finally popped in and realized it was a Vietnamese cafe with banh mi and viet iced coffees. Only had the chance to try the Vietnamese iced coffee, which is super well made - the ice is even made of frozen coffee so it doesn't dilute your drink! Will be back to try the banh mis for sure.

I have been going to the Gryphon for well over 8 years. I love the place so much I wouldn't hesitate to name my first born, Gryphon. I'm a complete tea snob and feel utterly at peace inside the Gryphon. Mostly because I became a tea snob inside these very walls. 

But where to begin!? As I've mentioned, their tea is to die for. I know it sounds dramatic but they have dozens of loose teas to pick from that are served in individual mismatched tea pots. (I prefer the brown pot with a yellow lid, and yes some barista's remember weird quirks like this!) I know nothing about coffee but my friends seem to enjoy it and I've never heard any complaints. As for other beverages, they serve a wide array of italian sodas, hot chocolate, and delicious limeaid. The baked goods are also tasty. 

What draws me to the Gryphon is the connections I've made over the years. I've gotten to know tons of musicians over the years from the Monday night open mics, and the live music on Fridays and Saturdays. Everyone has been warm and inviting and maybe that's because the place is small. Sometimes you have to share tables with stranges which result in friendly conversations with old, and young alike. Looking to have a quieter conversation? Check out the room upstairs with a large table and some couches, perfect for if you're with a group. 

Now for the artwork, there's always something to look at. I'm not always a fan but hey am I supposed to like everything I see? I just appreciate that a place like the Gryphon is connecting artists, musicians, and consumers. It's a beautiful place to be.

I stayed here in the fall and well it was interesting to say the least. Each room in the hotel has a specific theme. Check out the hotel's website so that you can really get a gist of how different each room is. The hotel is the opitomy of old school New Orleans, which means it has that kind of eerie feel to it. A lot of the rooms have those paintings that follow you with their eyes, which would be okay if it wasn't a painting of children across from your bed. 

All in all, The Columns Hotel was an experience that is unique to New Orleans.

FunFact: Pretty Baby (1978) was filmed here.

It surprises me that people are so alarmed by Christopher customers and their children. If you're not a fan of sharing a restaurant with children, try dining on the later side you'll enjoy it more. Anyway, I've really enjoyed coming to Christopher's. I've mostly come on Monday nights around 10pm. The bartender always remembers a face even if it's been 6 months. 

The space is split into two sides bar and restaurant. One of the last times I was there were 19 of us in a giant herd. They were great about letting us sit in the restaurant section even though it was well past the dinner rush. The bar area has a modern "jukebox" and one of those game machines. I think I'm partly lured here because of Photo Hunt competitions with my friends. 

One of my favorite things about Christopher's is the Dum Dum lolly pops. Sometimes the waiters will hide the bowl of lolly pops if people get too greedy aka when people take hand fulls.

My friend mentioned she really wanted wings from Theresa's which confused me wings at a "Belgian" bar? When I got there I realized, she did not mean your standard buffalo hot wings (for the record I'm not dissing them!). While 6 of us squeezed into a booth, I wouldn't suggest it. 4 to 5 is good group size at TND. Anyway, back to these "wings". They were spiced with rosemary and roasted. Delicious! I still wouldn't call it typical Belgium, for have one of their Belgian beers on tap or bottled and the mussels. I would suggest the Chimay. 

As for the decor, it looks good. I enjoy the look of the stone wall inside, and the modern (maybe custom?) sinks. Booths line one side, and the bar lines the other. Plenty of room for a good time. The service was good, the waitress was attentive and brought us drinks without too much of a wait. All in all, an enjoyable experience.

I took my nephew here when he was 3 to hang out and do something special and what kid doesn't like ice cream at 10AM. My sister tagged along for the experience and to eat the mid morning snack. We walked right in and started checking out the dozens of flavors. My nephew announced that he wanted to eat Green ice cream and seemed less concerned by the flavor. He instead hopped around and would've done cartwheels if he knew how out of sheer excitement. The lady working was really nice and let us have several tastes of ice cream especially since there were several Green ice creams flavors. My nephew had the Pistachios with M&M's in a cup and a cone, I had the Gold Medal Ribbon (Vanilla, Chocolate ice cream and caramel) in a cup and a cone, and my sister had cookies and cream. As we left Baskin-Robbins, we realized they weren't even open yet! But the lady behind the counter probably didn't want to deal with an angry 3 year-old and let us enjoy all the ice cream we wanted.

I hesitate to admit I've been here. My friends enjoy spending their birthday's here and I'm not sure why. Maybe because of dozens of Q102 ads for Maddie's in Malvern? There is usually a manageable cover around 8 bucks give or take a little. I've always seen live music which is why they are getting 2 stars. People seem to dance in interesting ways... especially the "older" crowd, I'm just saying. I have nothing against a place that welcomes people of all ages and well I guess it is quite entertaining. 

Maybe I've lived away from the area too long but I hate indoor smoking. Ugh. There's nothing worse than leaving a bar and reeking of every type of cigarette there is. I have nothing against smokers but I would just prefer people to do it in non enclosed places like Maddie's.

If you live in the Malvern area, you don't have that many options to go out. The Pig can definitely be considered Malvern's watering hole. You'll run into people you haven't seen in a long time whether they're 45 or 21. 

The beer selection is great. There's something on the list for everyone. There's always plenty of tables free while the bar stays more crowded. There's also a couple couches that I don't think I've ever seen anyone use. 

I was here once during a power outage which was quite an experience. They used the generators to keep the beer cold and the Christmas lights glowing. It was kind of funny but hey why sit at home in the dark during a massive power outage?

So we all have seen Phoenixville's commercials. You know, the ones that say how cool it is to hang out in Phoenixville. Anyway, Steel City has been around since before Phoenixville was the new hip place to be for young professionals and just married folks. 

In high school, my sex-ed teacher told me to go here. I avoided the place like the plague purely out of fear but then I looked the place up and realized it really was up my alley. Turns out he was spot on, so I also owe him a thank you. 

Steel City has that coffee shop vibe. They have live music and open mic nights. Sometimes you have to pay a cover of a couple bucks. The musicians play on a tiny stage in front of a massive sculpture/painting of trippy city. It's the type of place where you can lounge, eavesdrop on your neighbors, people watch and most importantly inhale caffeine. 

During the summer Phoenixville hosts lots of different outdoor events. Steel City has bathrooms. If nature is calling, stop in for a little relief and a fresh beverage!

This is one of those places where there are over 200 kinds of beer. It's like being Goldy Locks and getting to taste something different with each visit. It's a large place that's divided into three areas which means there's always a spot to sit but doesn't feel like warehouse. 

Several nights during the week they have a different activity ranging from your standard quizzo all the way to bingo which is great if you want to practice before you turn 65. There's also some arcade games in the bar area to keep you busy. Like many bars in the area, if you went to Conestoga or GV you will run into people from that era.

My experience was mildly confusing. My friends and I sat down at a table and ordered a drink. About 15 minutes later the bartender came by and told us that if we wanted anything else we needed to order it from the bar. Then 5 minutes later he came to take our drink orders again. Either way it worked out for us. 

The place was clean, and looks relatively new. It seems brighter than the establishment that was there before. I would have liked to see more of a New Orleans feel to it but hey it's Malvern (which is nothing like NO). The only real downside is the place closes at 11.

The place looks great partially because you can tell it's new. That being said it still has personality in the shades of burnt orange and browns. The tables are gorgeous and are made of solid wood. In the center of the place there are some comfy couches and a coffee table with games, which gives the place a sort of living room feel. It looks like someone put a ton of thought into the decor but sort of failed when it came to the ceiling tiles.... I really hate ceiling tiles. 

I had the Blackberry Chai and a bagel. The chai tasted wonderfully sweet and the bagel was good too. A little skimpy on the cream cheese but I'm sure they would've given me more if I had asked. They had several chalk boards with the menu and detailed thorough descriptions for each item.

I was sad to hear the Gryphon is no longer playing music which is why I'm glad Burlap and Bean is still going strong. If you're interested in seeing live music they often sell tickets in advance. Don't worry you won't be paying hefty prices. It's just a cover to keep the music/coffee world working in sync.

I spent hours in my car. Hours. Seriously, I drove from Beantown down to the MALVERN to visit the fam. I thought I was going to set a record (not a #1 but at least in the top 5) until I hit NYC and Jersey. Jersey smelled like moth balls, rotting garbage, burning rubber and freshly cut grass. I finally made it to Malvern and was staaaaarving (or as they say in Boston staaaaahhhvin). My parents let me pick between Indian and Chinese. I picked the Mandarin. I had been through enough with Jersey's series of strange smells.
