The best part of the Mandarin? It's BYOB which means more money to spend on chowing down on some good food. First they bring out some roasted peanuts and picked cucumber, YUM. All three of us had the spring rolls because great minds think alike. I had the tangerine delicacies. It was a little too tangy (think Tang) but this is the first time I haven't scarfed down my plate at record speeds. My parents' food was great. It's definitely the best Chinese food in town. 

I haven't had anything off the Japanese menu except Miso soup which was fine. I'm not sure that one could mess up Miso soup. Anyway, there's a Sushi bar where one couple was seemingly enjoying a romantic night out. 

Lesson learned: Jersey blows but the Mandarin rocks.

It was one of my Besties' birthdays. He is one of those sassy hipster cats who drinks PBR tall boys because it's righteous. You'll definately fit in here if you have a septum piercing, skinny jeans on, wear plaid, are a graphic designer/artist or have some funky tattoos. Even though it was about 30 blocks away from the birthday boy's apartment, he picked this Sugarmom's. If you've never been, it's this basement style bar. Think secret club meets suburban basement party (you know you went to at least one in HS!). The place was surprisingly big and was organized really well. It's a great place for groups because there's clusters of coffee tables and chairs AND BUMPER CARS! Yes, I said it bumper cars that double as seats. Talk about a photo op session waiting to happen. There's also a pool table, juke box and pinball machine for more festivities. 

As for the bar itself, there was the standard 2-5 minutes wait to get a drink where you sort of look eagerly at the bartender. We mostly drank the $1-3 PBRs and had a round of Kamikaze shots. They were the biggest shots I've had in long time but tasted really good. Perfect for a birthday celebration.

I walked in with my best friend and felt at home. You might wonder why I felt this instant connection to a new cafe and well it was quite simple. The cafe has the same IKEA Klippan love seat that is currently sitting in my living room. You can't blame me for my love affair with IKEA, I have chosen to live in a show room. Anyway, I'm also a sucker for art. As the name implies, Artisans Gallery and Cafe has art displayed around the room. There's a decent selection of ceramic mugs, saucers, plates etc. 

Even the mugs that our beverages were served in were handmade. My bestie ordered a Chai Latte and a Scone. I had the Peppermint Tea and S'mores. The barista was kind enough to heat up the Scone and S'mores. My friend made me promise to write about her Scone. She was almost tongue tied trying to explain how delicious it was. The few things she was able to convey was that it was almost like a cookie but not like a Croissant, didn't taste old/stale, and was one of the best Scones she's ever had. My S'mores weren't too shabby either. 

Artisans Gallery and Cafe also accepts VISA, which if you're like me you have to appreciate. I hate cash and rarely carry it on me. 

The end.

Anyone can make a cupcake but Gigi's fixes (yes, that's my excitement for the South coming out!) a cupcake just right. Every day, Gigi's has a different variety of cupcakes. There are also some staple flavors that are always available like wedding cake, and birthday cake. My advice is be bold, be daring, try something different. I had never seen a green cupcake before and figured I had to go with it. It was the key lime cupcake and while the color was a bit unnatural its flavor was heavenly. It was a great place to stop and grab an afternoon snack and in traditional tourist fashion, I documented every moment.

Oh yelp, how you rule every decision. When the countdown to my trip to Nashville hit single digits, I went bananas. I spent a significant amount of time just checking out all the places I wanted to visit. The 12 South neighborhood had a lot of spots I wanted hit while I was in Tennessee. While yelp is fab, I was happy to discover the Taproom without its help.

My friend and I drove by trying to survey the area before picking one restaurant. I totally misread the sign twice and thought it was "Tarpoon". Inside, the walls are decorated in arabesque swirls made of bottle caps. The waiter was great and after pretty much playing 21 questions with us we ended up with Yazoo Pale Ale and Heffenweizen beers and chicken quesadillas. The waiter was even kind enough to take our picture. 

Seems like it would be a local spot because there were tons of poster advertising live music. The chalkboard advertised happy hour drink specials.

I have a confession. I had a one night stand with country music. I have the Blue Bird to thank for this mysterious occurrence. I went to Nashville to visit friends. I realized there was no way I could avoid Country Music but I never expected to like it. I was mistaken! My friends took a bunch of to the Blue Bird and I had a fantastic time.

I wouldn't say that the menu and/or anyone's food was that spectacular. There's your standard bar fair food that includes Mozzarella Sticks, Chicken Fingers, Fries, Chips and Salsa, etc. The beer list was pretty limited too but no one's really there for that, it's the music that draws the crowd. 

There were four different musicians sitting in a circle. They each took a turn playing one song or reading. It felt more like I was a fly on the wall in recording studio, or watching musicians truly appreciate one another. I have never seen people listen with such intensity and appreciation. If you're in the Nashville area, the Blue Bird is definitely a place you have to stop, and listen. You'll get lost in Country Music, if only for one night.

I didn't think I'd being going to a plantation tour on my trip down South, nor did I really expect to enjoy it. Our tour guide was amazing. He was dressed in period clothing which I have to give him props for. And believe me, no one wants to wear heavy wool clothes in June in Nashville. 

As the tour progressed the guide explained the family tree which was mighty confusing. All I remember is one guy named his children with his second wife after his dead first wife! The actual home was decorated for a wedding from the Civil War era. They had a whole food spread along with a wedding cake and groom's cake. 

After touring the house, my friend and I walked around outside. They have some horses grazing, a gift shop, stables and what was the former slaves' home. They even have those fun cutouts to stick your head through for photos! Overall, the Belle Meade Plantation is well maintained and can be a fun stop for locals and tourists alike.

I was in NOLA for a wedding. A wedding means one thing in my family, it's going to be a whirlwind of ridiculousness! The Funky Pirate was the first stop in this whirlwind. My brother let me know that our family was stationed at the Funky Pirate. His directions were typical. Our conversation went like this 

"It's on Bourbon street" 
"but where on Bourbon street?" 
"on Bourbon street" 

I still couldn't tell you the cross street or what number it is but it's near where the neon signs end on Bourbon. I guess it's obvious we're family. Anyway, my friend and I throw away our slushy drinks and head into the bar to see a site. This incredible site is Big Al and boy is he BIG! I'm talking like 500 pounds big. He's part of a pretty rad band. 

Now are you ready for the hands down best moment while at the Funky Pirate? Seriously, are you ready? If you're not take a deep breathe, it's that good. Phew, I'm glad we did that. 

So, Big Al is singing and I'm perched on my bar stool nodding along. And then he stops singing and points at me. I over course assume "who me?" and turn around looking for the person behind me. But, Big Al wanted me! (ick) So I reluctantly come forward and step on stage, of course Big Al remains comfortably on his chair. So Big Al proceeds to tell me that I have great ta tas but he used a more vulgar word the exact moment my brother steps into the bar. His eyes have never gotten so wide out of shear anger/surprise/disgust. I'm surprised he didn't bum rush the stage and attempt knocking him off his chair. But alas all Big Al wanted was for me to go collect his tips. I made my rounds and gave my brother a meditation CD. Okay, I didn't but I did have to talk him out of a tree. 

It was first of many experiences to come on this trip to New Orleans, but why not put your best foot forward. Why go somewhere that isn't totally memorable regardless of what state you're in on Bourbon Street?

The Carousel Bar is a spot in New Orleans you've got to visit. It's not your standard hotel bar mostly because it spins around, around, and around. When you have a seat there's a moment where you think "did i have too much to drink?" "Is the room spinning?" No, the room isn't spinning. The bar is! 

The bar tenders don't stand still either. They move from guest to guest but never seem to be in a hurry. The drinks are tasty and strong. The bartenders also climb over the bar to get inside. There are no openings for them. Last time I was there, I was asked to move out of the way for just a moment to let one of them in. It's always a goofy site. 
Fun Fact: Hemingway wrote about the Carousel Bar.

I've never actually had the luck of finding a table close to the piano players. I've popped my head and they sure do sound nice. My last visit, my family and I sat outside in the courtyard near the fire pits. It really is a great place if you're with a multi generational group. Between the piano bar area, and the outdoor seating, there's plenty of places to hang out. Also the bartender came frequently which was great for our big group. There's nothing worse than a thirsty, grouchy group! 

The bathrooms are upstairs, and is not handicap accessible as far as I know. So if you're in need of extra assistance, check before hand what the exact details are.

I've been to a New Orleans about half a dozen times, and I've never disliked any food until Mother's. I almost feel bad for saying it too. Mother's is one of those places that survived Katrina with stride. Mother's had quite the line of hungry customers when I got there. It moved quick enough and before I knew it we were through the door. 

After checking out the menu, you order at the counter and have a seat. A waiter will find you and bring you your food. I ordered Shrimp Gumbo and salad. The salad was fine, I mean really how could you mess up a salad? The gumbo tasted terrible. I didn't have more than two bites! It tasted like pool water was used to cook it. Yuck. My roomie had the Jambalaya and practically licked her bowl clean. I was sad to leave a place with such notoriety hungry.

After my work out, I decided to reverse all my hard work by indulging in some yummy cupcakes. I'd been wanting to stop in Cupcakes Gourmet for sometime now. As a yelper, I dutifully asked 25 questions about their cupcakes and am ready to report back! They make their cupcakes daily in house. Most of their icings have cream or cream cheese in them, so it's something you should be prepared for incase your lactose intolerant. They also do frequent "eater" cards, so it pays to eat a lot of cupcakes. Earn 10 stamps and get cupcakes for FREE! They also have some cute packaging if you're looking to gift them or bring them to a party. 

I ordered two mini cupcakes (red velvet and chocolate peanut butter) and a hot tea. I didn't feel like the red velvet was that special. I wished the icing was cheesier, a little more rich or something. The chocolate peanut butter was great. The cake portion is chocolate, the top has a creamy peanut buttery top that's covered in a layer of chocolate. It was perfect for a chocoholic like myself. 

All in all, their cupcakes are good but not mind blowing. While their shop is cute to pick stuff up, it's not too cozy if you want to hang out. I guess my heart belongs to another cupcake shop. ;)

I would go to Prohibition Taproom for the staff alone. They're friendly, personal and authentic. They don't do the fake smile and bother customers like a lot wait staff in other joints. The atmosphere is hella good. Relaxed. Chillaxed. It's the kind of place you can see yourself hanging out in. The bartender's a rad guy who likes to add his own personal twist to drinks, and is totally cool with it if you're not happy. Luckily, I loved his idiosyncratic drinks. As for the food, I keep getting the burgers which come with fries. They make some fry sauce which I can't remember the name of but tastes good and gives you killer bad breath. It's probably not the best condiment if you're on a date. 

Better yet, they have a jukebox. It's just one more way to control your experience. Good food, good music, what more could you ask for?

Yum, yum, yum. I came here with a friend on a Sunday afternoon. At first, I felt like we got the cold shoulder. After all, it was past 1 and they closed at 2. I think this minor detail sped up our service which was great. We both ordered the Burrito North of the Border and it was bananas. Just the right amount of cheese, egg, pepper, chicken, etc. combo. 

The decor is interesting. My friend pointed out the owner and you could tell that the place was a definite reflection of her. Apparently, the artist that painted one of the murals in back room just left is mark in the White House.

"S" is for SALSA! The girls wanted a fun night out to celebrate a birthday but we didn't want to do the usual. Thanks to handy dandy Yelp, I found Brasil's. Check it, the situation was perfect. We got there around 9 when the place opened, and had time for a drink before the dance lesson. 

I have since forgotten the instructor's name but he was amazing! You could tell he was used to teaching novice salsa dancers like us and was really positive. The lesson started by practicing basic steps alone in line formations. Then, the men paired up with ladies and we were in a rotation system. 

By the time the lesson was over, I was able to do a couple steps, badly. But hey, I was being a good sport and dance the night away.

My tummy has found a new best friend -- the cook at Blackfish. The portions are small but amazing. They're rich with thought, precision and flavor. The only downside was that I had the scallops. They were perfect not weird and gummy like at some places. When I finished them, I was a little bummed there weren't more. Had I known that I would've loved them so, I would've ordered them for all three courses. 

The service is amongst the best I've ever experienced. Our waiter was really good at judging whether our table was ready/needed something or needed another couple minutes. He refilled glasses without bothering us, but simultaneously tended to our needs. With 7 of my family members that's no small feat! 

As others have said, it's BYOB! So don't forget to stop at the liquor store if you're a lush! ;)

It's the burbs. There's not too much to do but the ice cream hot spots are plentiful. Whirled Peace is setting itself apart even though it stands where Rita's used to be. They have 4 flavors of frozen yogurt and twists with tons of toppings but it's a do-it-yourself thing. At the counter you weigh your creation, pay and they hand you a spoon. The staff seemed friendly and there was indoor and outdoor seating.

I went here only because I couldn't find parking near Monks and I was in a hurry. I had the fish and chips... sorta wish I hadn't. The fries were fine and totally unmemorable. The fish was in a beer batter which I normally love but it seemed like the whole thing was sorta dried out. If I'm ordering friend anything, it better be delicious. 

This place would've only gotten 2 stars had it not been for their checker boards...

It's a Starbucks. It's exactly like the others, which is one of the reasons why chains are sometimes comforting. You know what you're going to get. My tall Zen tea is going to be the same wherever I go. So I'll break down this location's idiosyncrasies. 

Pros
-Comfy chairs, and tons of seating.
-Clean bathroom
-Relatively friendly/professional staff
-Next to the train station

Cons
-The parking lot blows. They have three spots for Starbucks' customers within the train station lot and two or three parallel spots along Rt 30. 
-No drive thru
-No personal touches. It's Starbucks, they won't be dolling out hugs.

Okay, I'll admit it... I'm not very good at bowling. My tiny wrists start to hurt within 15 minutes even when using a 6 pound ball. So the key to fun, painless bowling is lots of breaks and tatter tots! I got the North Sliders, which were alright. The chicken fingers were yummy too. They also have quite a few draft beers, wines and drinks. 

They waitress was little... uh... crabby. Although I was told that there were dozens of kids there all day for a party and they were prepping for a bar mitzvah. So I'm guessing (and hoping) that the crabbiness was related to an exorbitant amount of children in one shift. 

The bathroom is totally rockin! The walls were covered in glittery tiles, which made me smile. They were also clean and totally modern, which isn't what you expect when you go bowling. 

Pro: they sell socks for $2
Con: it's cash only...

Maybe I'm just used to a hole in the wall Mexican food place... you know... where everything comes wrapped in tin foil or wax paper. This not that kind of place. Instead this place is an intersection of modern city meets Mexican food. 

We got here minutes after the happy hour special ended (FYI 6:30), so no dice on drink specials. Their beers are priced reasonably though. The bar is this sort of jagged crazy shape, which is better if you're in pairs. We were in a group of three and it was hard finding a spot that didn't leave someone out. After a short wait, our table was ready. 

I just feel like they could offer some complimentary chips. It's not as though you're not paying for it. It's not that I thought the prices were outrages, but they are definitely higher than authentic Mexican places. All I'm saying is stop being stingy and throw in some chips while I wait! 

The food was alright. I had the fajita where you pick your own meats/tofu. The chicken was fine but they left the shrimp tails on. It was sort of a pain to get the tails off while everything was piping hot. They were seasoned well with a hint of lime and some spices.

Artisans Gallery & Cafe has become my new homework hot spot. It's sort of the perfect mix for doing work. It's not totally quiet, but people aren't squawking to loudly either. The best part is that they don't seem to mind that I sort of set up shop. At one point, I let the baristas know that I was going to move my car, and they kept an eye on my stacks of books and papers. This place is personal. The folks who work here get to know their customers. It's the kind of thing that only grandparents talk about but somehow it's managed to be authentic, kind and thoughtful in 2010. 

I've been loving their green tea, and have been slowly making my way through the baked goods. So far I've gobbled up the S'mores, Snicker-doodle cookie, chocolate chunk cookie, and a bagel with cream cheese. I'm not sure what's next on my list but I'm sure it won't disappoint!

It had been a long, long, long time since I'd been here. I blame time because I forgot how great this place really is. Don't let the same thing happen to you! This has been a Public Service Announcement. 

Anyway, it's interesting how having a table to listen, watch and hear music can make the whole thing a lot more relaxed. The waitress was really attentive and could've come by slightly less. Sometimes it felt like she was eyeing are table to figure out whether we needed anything the same way a dude checks out a woman with giant knockers (less than subtle). After the show ended, everyone stood around for a good 30+ minutes chatting away, but the staff didn't seem to mind. 

The women's bathroom was also super clean, which somehow surprised me. According to my amigo, the men's bathroom was clean too. So don't hold it when you're here. 

FYI: there's plenty of meter parking in the area but remember to bring quarters. Some meters are old school and some you pay at the kiosk with cash or card. Just make sure that you check the signs to avoid getting a ticket.

So, we were a little transfixed by the napkins. They're folded so beautifully, and while we all hold or nearly hold multiple degrees we couldn't figure it out. Luckily, the waitresses were kind of to show us how. The next day I was so proud of my new skill, I showed my mother with a paper towel. 

Girls night wasn't just fun because of silly napkins but also the food. We each had a different dish which left us begrudgingly sharing a bite only to taste someone else's food. The menu was full of options that can accommodate most people's palates (spicy, mild, meat, seafood, vegetarian, etc) and with reasonable prices what could be better? Oh wait, it's BYOB. That's what makes it even better! 

I will definitely be back to this cozy restaurant. Yelp has once again helped me successfully plan another night out with my girls!

Dumplings -- check, kung pao chicken -- check, fried shrimp -- check, broccoli and chicken -- check, lo mein -- check. You get the idea, it's your standard Chinese buffet. Grace Buffet has all the greasy options you'd normally order at 2 am for lunch instead and for around $7! 

I agree with Danan on the service. The waitress served us drinks and then was MIA until we waved her over. We figured that since she was basically ignoring us we couldn't figure out if we had to pay at the register or hand over the funds to her. One perk was that we sat and talked, and talked and talked. The employees didn't seem to mind that we had set up camp. 

The desserts were misleading. All the baked goods seemed pretty dry. I mistakenly thought the banana pudding was vanilla and was shocked when I ate a spoonful. I went back and scooped some ice cream instead.

The polar ice caps may still be melting but, I finally got my act together and  went to Silk City. It's a diner that has it goin' on with a dash of Magic Gardens (just search Magic Gardens if you have no idea what I'm talking about). Dancing + greasy diner food = hipster hang out. Okay, maybe that equation doesn't make a ton of sense but it seemed like there was a good percentage of folks who looked like their worlds were centered around the arts. 

Anyway, the food. Right, I'm reviewing a place that serves food. I had a cheese burger and the chocolate brownie ice cream thing for dessert. Yum. No complaints. The burger was cooked exactly the way I had requested it. The waiters and bartenders weren't necessarily super speedy but based on Silk City's vibe, I wasn't expecting a waiter to hover by my table. 

Next time, I'd like to come back for some dancing. I will report back!

Corner Bakery Cafe is easy and not in a sleazy way. It's certainly not glamorous with its plastic checker-board tablecloths but it might be handy if you have little guys in tow. Speak of which, they had high chairs available and we decided to eat in the backroom. It was a little quieter and removed from others more importantly, we didn't bother other diners. 

It's a fusion between cafeteria and sit down and eat styles of restaurant. You order at the counter, receive a number and are served. Anyway, I had a wonderful tomato, arugula, mozzarella sandwich. Normally, when there's a hefty sandwich and chips, I don't finish them but it was too good to stop! The snickerdoodle cookie was a disappointment. It was too dry around the edges. 

*They have free WiFi, which is perfect for the hardcore yelper wanting to post a tip or a check-in!

I'm a sucker for a chocolate croissant mainly because it is another avenue to consume my favorite food, namely chocolate. It was right on point. My other half decided to devour an almond croissant filled with almond paste and showered with confectionery sugar and almond slices. Somehow, I still made a bigger mess. We sat at a small table eying the artwork for sale as we ate. 

As a tourist, it was nice to take a break for the endless menus pushing heavier items and Thanksgiving sized portions. La Boulangerie isn't a place that immediately comes to mind when I think of New Orleans, but maybe that's what makes it special. 


FYI: Bring cash.

La Boca is slowly becoming a staple when I head out to New Orleans. Sometimes you need a break from friend seafood and rice dishes. Sure it's not exactly Vegan/Vegetarian friendly but DELICIOUS none the less. I've had the American Kobe Terras Major twice and loved it both times. Between the flowing wine and the perfect cut of meat, the only decisions left are what side dish to choose from and which steak sauce is your favorite. 

Besides enjoying the food, the ambience is great. The restaurant is relatively small and seems well staffed. There was a rambunctious group last time. They were politely approached and asked to simmer down. By far my favorite detail is when they come by and allow you to pick your own steak knife. They have a fantastic assortment of knives to pick from. My favorite has a silver bee on it where you can rest your index finger while the knife is in use -- genius! It's certainly more thoughtful than generic monstrosity known as a steak knife at a big chain restaurant. 

I can't wait to visit one of my favorite cities and enjoy a great meal.

McKenzie Brew House is a breath of fresh air in Malvern. The bar feels a little less towny than some of the other "hot spots" around despite almost every customer being a Great Valley High School alumni. Anyway, I've been here several times for drink only. As the name implies, McKenzie brews it's own beer. Their wheat beer is pretty tasty but is pretty forgettable.

It's a pretty large venue with plenty of seating for diners, bar flies and space outdoors. Last time, I was attacked by mosquitoes so spritz a little bug spray on before sitting outside.

MRFffcfww-fvhRX8zY3sew.review_text: Had an amazing brunch, service was great, the waiter told us that one of our choices was not the best and not to get it! Must love the honesty :) after changing our minds, all 6 of us LOVED our meal!

On Saturday nights they have their "Category 4" menu and it was amazing! It's a 4 course meal with small portions, so great for one person, with wine recommendations on the menu. Every Saturday is a new menu.  All 4 items were absolutely delicious and I can't wait to go back a different Saturday night for an entirely different menu! On top of this, they have live music :)

This place has a great vibe, the food was fresh and healthy and environment was fun and relaxed with games to play and comfortable couches to sit on. It fits perfectly in downtown Plant City. The staff was wonderful and personable.

Best crab cakes around! This place has a great atmosphere, definitely sit outside; with the water and live music, it's perfect! We had the Shrimp Dian and it was absolutely delicious! It had a kick to it, but wasn't too spicy. My husband and I also split it and had leftovers. We love coming here and will always recommend it to others!

This place had a nice atmosphere, great for a party or celebration. I had the pasta brio (their specialty) and wasn't overly impressed. It was very good, but not anything special. Same with the brio salad, it tasted like a typical salad. I will say, the desserts were awesome. Every single option looked delicious; I had the chocolate cake and mouse and it was fantastic. The rest of our table had the carrot cake and bread pudding and we were all raving about our dessert. 

All in all, I am glad we went and tried it, but I would not go again just because I would rather spend the money elsewhere. It didn't impress, but it didn't disappoint.

The margaritas were amazing, the guacamole was mad fresh at the table, complimentary chips and two choices of salsa...all delicious! We got the fajitas and easily split them. They were full of flavor and came with guacamole, sour cream and Pico. It was all wonderful. For dessert we tried the apple pie, and it did not disappoint! It came in a skillet and covered in cinnamon ice cream. Every single thing we are and drank was delicious! I can't wait to go back!

This is a typical diner. The food wasn't bad, but it was nothing special, I could easily make all of this at home and it would have tasted better and been cheaper. 
I ordered eggs with the waffle, the eggs never came but we were charged for them. When I was out of coffee, three people walked by and asked if I wanted more, I replied yes to all three and the last girl was the only one to ever come back. 
The service wasn't bad, but our waitress definitely did not care about us once our food came out. 
We were in and out very quickly and it was a pretty cheap meal, but I would not come back. 
We found this place by searching for brunch places on Yelp. I would not consider this s "brunch" place. They have breakfast until 11:30 and then they serve lunch. To us, brunch is mimosas and bloody Mary's with the option of breakfast or lunch. None of that is available at this restaurant.

This is a must in the Tampa Bay Area! This may be my new favorite place to eat. The environment is so cool and chill, very hip. Everything inside is reclaimed, which I love because I'm all about using resources.  Everything is local, even the refurbished items, and in season. We went last night and their beer was a strawberry beer and their ice cream was strawberry ice cream because that is what is in season right now. All the strawberries came from Plant City also. 
The food was amazing...and with four girls, we tried A LOT of food! For appetizers, we got the alligator puppies, the Mac and cheese, the garlic oysters, and the okra fries with house made ketchup. Every single item was fantastic! I would want all of that again. 
For dinner, I got the crab Mac and cheese. I am a macaroni and cheese connoisseur!  This was just the right amount of cheeses, very creamy, and not an over-powering amount of crab. It was perfect! The girls got amazing dishes as well. One got the special, which was Mahi with an apple and pear glaze, the cheese popcorn mashed potatoes and green beans. Delicious. Another got the beer pan chicken, which we all decided was nothing special, it just tastes like Publix rotisserie chicken. 
Of course we got dessert and they were amazing also! I had the key lime dessert. It was very tart, frozen, covered in graham cracker and with a side of toasted marshmallow-like stuff. It was my favorite on the table. We also got the homemade vanilla bean, strawberry, coconut, and chocolate ice creams. Every single one was mouth watering. The last of our desserts was the most interesting on the menu, but the least impressive. We got the candied duck bacon maple fried ice cream. It was covered in what tasted like stale cereal and was not as tasteful as we imagined. Don't get sucked into the fun name! 
All in all, this is my new favorite restaurant and I want everyone I know to experience this place!

What a great place to hang out with friends. Though the wait was long for a lane (45 minutes on Friday), there's a great, giant sports bar to sit and have drinks while waiting. The lanes are typical, but it's a fun environment, tons of things to do all around: the sports bar, which they have food in, a smaller snack bar to get a pitcher of beer and some snacks while bowling, then an entire game section with tickets and prizes. 

We got nachos and they were way beyond our expectations for a bowling snack. They were HUGE, definitely enough to satisfy all four of us, including our two big and hungry husbands! There were all the toppings, including guac, in a mountain of deliciousness. We highly recommend spending some time here and enjoying all the fun and delicious aspects!

The food is really good but it's a standard NY style pizza for a little more money. The sizes are great, a medium is a chain pizza stores' large. We do really love it, it's just a little expensive. Worth going to for sure!

This is a great, traditional Mexican restaurant. We give it a 4 out of 5 because it's more expensive than it should be. We came on Sunday and it was 2 for 1 margaritas, and they were pretty delicious! We got the Mi Casa sampler and the queso. For my husband and me, this was the perfect amount of food. And my husband is a big guy with a big appetite! We sat in the bar area and the service was quick. 

Don't be fooled by the outside storefront, even though it is in a strip mall, the inside is pleasantly shocking! It has a fun and colorful ambiance and is large inside. They also have an outdoor eating area that is covered.

This place is fancier than we thought. It's a classy wine and appetizer bar. While you can get a meal, don't go there with the intention of filling up. We had the caprese salad, hummus, and fig and prosciutto flatbread. All the food was amazing, but conservative on portions. The flatbread is something I will dream about; it was the perfect combination of sweet and salty and paired perfectly with moscato. 

The service was fantastic, we felt like a friend was serving us! Our server asked if we were going to a show at the Straz, when we said yes, he was highly aware of the time for us, giving us the time to really enjoy our drinks. 

I would go again but it would have to be a special occasion because it was pricy and small portions.

Everything from the setting, shopping, food to drinks is excellent at this place! Whether in the dining area or the atrium, you are transported to London instantly. The tea options are astounding and are freshly brewed to perfection. I've tried many things on the menu and I am always shocked at how delicious it is, no matter what it is I order. Brunch is my favorite time here because it is sunny in the atrium creating the perfect setting for a mimosa and some Nutella pancakes. 

Once finished eating, shopping is my next favorite thing to do here! Whether I'm looking for a book, accent pieces for my home, a gift for my toddler niece, or some stationary, OE will have it. Their indie/eclectic/classic style is everything I'm about and I could spend hours looking at everything in the shop. 

When you walk out to go back to the real world, you feel you were transported to a different time and place while in OE and now it's back to reality.

If I could rate food, experience and ambiance separately there would be different ratings, BUT, because of all the hype about this place and our experience of having drinks, dinner, and breakfast here, I'm sticking with a solid 2 stars. 

First: dinner. We ordered drinks and the Brazilian was delicious, it took a while to get to us and it was 5pm with no one in the restaurant. Our waitress was odd and awkward, not knowing how to leave a conversation or when to walk away. She was pleasant but seemed inexperienced. We ordered the calamari, and THAT would get 5 stars, it was delicious with an odd mixture of flavors that complimented each other perfectly. It was almost refreshing tasting. 

Once the waitress went over the specials, my husband knew he wanted the soup of the day which was a coconut curry soup. I ordered the yellowfin tuna. At this point, the waitress already told us a couple things on the menu that were unavailable, leaving us without an explanation. We overheard another waiter explaining it was because of the harsh winter in the north east effecting the availability. When our food came out, the waitress had a different soup for my husband, lobster chowder, saying she was mistaken with the soup of the day and hoped this would be an acceptable replacement. We elected to take it as my entree was now at the table.

I liked the tuna a lot, though my husband thought it was bland. It came with a mixture of chopped fruits as a salsa. It was a smaller plate, but I enjoyed it. Neither of us liked the lobster chowder, it didn't taste like there was any lobster in it and it was bland. It was obviously extremely different from the coconut curry soup he thought he was getting. 

We stayed for almost 2 hours and saw our waitress only a few times. We got 2 drinks and had to ask for them each time. We would have had more had we been offered in an appropriate time frame. Overall, the food was good, just not great; the service was ok, but the environment is beautiful. 

We are staying at the hotel, so after going to a show we came back and sat at the bar. We sat down at 10:15 and they close at 11.  When we sat down a waiter came by and collected all the menus off the bar. By 10:30 it was apparent they were trying to clear out and go home. We asked to see a dessert menu, ordered the Jumbo Choco Taco, then several minutes later were told they had just sold the last one. That made the third thing in one  evening that was unavailable off the menu. 

The next morning we had breakfast here. We had a different waitress who was very sweet with a youthful awkwardness and a glowing personality. We really enjoyed talking with her throughout the morning!  I ordered the Castile Parfait and my husband got the Castile Omelette. They each had a  beautiful presentation. The Parfait had a lovely mixture of yogurt, cream fruit and pickled papaya; however, I discovered a layer of candied nuts on the first bite, an ingredient not listed on the menu. I'm extremely allergic to tree nuts and peanuts (especially walnuts). I was able to spoon the nuts out onto a napkin but was left with a slightly swollen and itchy mouth. This was highly disappointing. The Castile Omelette was pretty standard but with some fancier ingredients and we would definitely recommend to anyone that prefers a savory breakfast option.

Overall Castile has a wonderful design with very classy ambiance and an intriguing menu. At just under a year old, the restaraunt feels like it's still figuring itself out  and stumbled on delivering an experience to fit the price point. It has great potential and I would not write it off, our experience was just below average in the end.

My only complaint is that it is always crowded and there is always a wait because it is that good! They are expanding soon though, so that should fix the problem. 

This is a great, very cool and hip bar that loves local and changing their selection often. The food is amazing as well. You MUST get the Juicy Lacey with smoked gouda. It is perfect. They change their menu often and we have tried almost everything that's new, our favorite being the French toast burger (perfect blend of sweet and salty) and our least favorite being the PB&J burger. Though this is a great idea, it just wasn't our favorite. Everything they create is a beautiful blend of flavors while staying creative.

This is an amazing ice cream spot like no other. It is a very trendy dive that also sells local artwork. The ice cream is phenomenal and changes almost weekly. My favorite that stays on the menu is the drunken brownie: Chardonnay ice cream with brownie chunks. I have tried a crazy amount of their odd mixtures, and NOTHING disappoints. The chicken and waffles, PB&J and Girl Scout  mixtures have been my favorite creations. 

The people who work there are always friendly and talk to you like you belong, like you are a friend. The atmosphere is kid-friendly and very home-y with sofas and chairs to sit at. 

Everyone should go to Revolution Ice Cream. It is now a staple I bring out of town friends to!

Burgers are fantastic, big and juicy, perfectly portioned. Great very cool, hipster-like environment that feels very "local".  Everyone who works here is extremely nice and pleasant, always personable. This is one place I want to take all my Tampa visitors!

Quick greek food. Set up like a Moe's or Subway where you order at a counter and you can take it to go or eat there. Service was good. We enjoyed our meal but wouldn't make it a habit to go there. Huge portions, my meal was easily two!

Famous for their deviled crabs and Cuban sandwiches, this place does not disappoint. It is very old Tampa, making it a great place to bring out of town guests. I also highly recommend the plantains, they are sweet, always hot, and cooked to perfection.

Anise was everything we expected it would be. First, we were seated right away, which we were not expecting at 7 on a Friday night! The service was outstanding. We were brought waters as soon as we sat down, our server, John G., was super positive and made all of our decision making easier. He deserves 5 stars for sure! 

To drink we got the RYE Old Fashion and the Hibiscus Margarita. Both were clearly made by professionals who care about the quality and taste of a drink. 

I loved the fact that most items were small portions because we love to try all kinds of things on a menu, and we were able to try four different meals! We obviously got the stinky buns (our waiter helped us mix and match with the most popular choices), which come highly recommended on Yelp. We were not thrilled with them as we expected to be. They were good, but not something I would say someone HAD to order if they were to eat there. 

We also got the lobster mac and cheese. I consider myself a Mac and cheese connoisseur and this was delicious. Of the four entrees we got, this was both of our favorites. It was creamy and had big chunks of lobster in it. The Sriracha bacon was a perfect addition to the flavor. It came steaming hot and was dropping with cheese. 

Along with those we got the tater tots and the shrimp tacos. Both AMAZING!

The bar staff is always nice when we come here, but other patrons crowd the bar and there are no servers, which can make it hard to get a drink. They always have a great rotating selection of their unique craft beers and the sampling is the best option because you can sample 5 of the beers (out of 8 options). The servings are enough to split with two people and if you want to keep drinking, you have enough taste to make a good choice. 
The ambiance is a clean barn style, encompassing the surrounding area of Plant City. 
The "You-Pick" is so much fun! I have picked the blackberries, but you can pick whatever produce is in season, and you walk down a beautiful path to wind up in a field of plants and trees. You have no idea you are near civilization. It is definitely something to experience. 
This is one of my top places to bring out of town friends!

We do not give 5 stars lightly, but Berns definitely deserves the rating. Everything from ambiance to food to wait staff was exceptional. The food alone was worth the 5 stars, but the experience itself was over the top. Berns Steakhouse has a pedigree within Tampa which is rare. 
The food is brought out with consideration to timing: it comes in courses with the waiter/waitress timing exactly when to being out the next course. The steak was perfect; the steak was trimmed with care and it was cooked to our exact specifications. The server cut it for us at the table and prepared our naked potato for us table side. It was a classically good meal. 
Definitely make sure to do the tour, read the stories in the menu, and go to the dessert room in order to appreciate your food and where it has come from. The tour is great for history and ambiance. 
The dessert room is a different experience all together. Upon entry to the separate level, you quickly realize it is its own entity within the establishment, you are greeted by a new waiter. Every seating area is separated, creating a warm and intimate space for the people dining. Included is your own choice of music, making it more personal than it already is. All of the desserts looked amazing; we got the brown sugar and chocolate, chocolate, chocolate, both of which I would have again because they were amazing. 
Valet is $5 and reservations are a necessity! We tried a month in advance and 9pm was the only available time. The dessert room is first choice to diners. The full experience is 2-3 hours, so plan accordingly! 
We highly recommend the macadamia vanilla bean vinaigrette dressing, the chateaubriand brushed with garlic butter, and a scoop of the macadamia nut ice cream for dessert!

I went to the family and friends soft opening. The ambiance and the food was amazing! Our server was really awkward and couldn't recommend anything, BUT it was a soft opening and the food definitely made up for that! 

We had the fish dip for an appetizer. It was one of the best fish dips I've had! There was plenty of dip for all three of us, but it came with six pieces of cucumber, not enough to accompany the dip. I highly recommend it, but ask for extra cucumbers! 

I had the crab cake sandwich, my friend had the grilled mahi sandwich, and my other friend had the fish and chips. All of the entrees came with a lot of food! None of us finished our meals. The crab cake could have used some sort of sauce, it was a little bland, but the portion was huge and it was very good. All three of us would recommend our entrees! Two of us also got the sweet potato tots...DEFINITELY GET THEM! They were the perfect kind of sweet! 

Do not leave this place without getting dessert! There are two options and we had both. The bread pudding was, no exaggeration, the BEST bread pudding I have ever had! I do not like bread pudding usually, but this was phenomenal. It came with vanilla ice cream and covered in cinnamon.  I will dream about this dessert. The second option was key lime pie. I LOVE key lime pie, and this was delicious, it came in a cup which was cool. I am allergic to nuts and the crust is crumbled nuts, so I just ate the key lime. This dessert was amazing, but i wouldn't ever leave without getting the bread pudding! 

I can't wait to go back and eat there again!!

This is the most efficient drive thru I've ever seen in my life. I come here on Saturdays when I am training, so the lunch hour I get is the typical 11:30-12:30. When I get there around 11:45, it is packed every time. I've never been in line for long though. They always have people in the line directing traffic, taking orders and taking payments. Not once have I waited long, nor have they messed up my order even though there are cars and employees everywhere. The communication is phenomenal on their end in order to get all the right orders to the right cars. I look forward to this efficiency every Saturday!

I wish there were more than 5 stars! Every option is creative, fun and food-trendy. The environment is eclectic and cozy, making you want to stay here longer. The options range from doughnuts to ice cream to quiche, and nothing disappoints. We've had almost everything and there's nothing I love more, making it easy to try something new every time. 

Today we are having the salted caramel latte and the campfire latte. I highly recommend both, and now I want to try all the other creative lattes!

Creative, trendy, delicious. Seriously, what else do you need? Everything I've had here is amazing and nothing is ordinary. They take fun combinations that don't always sound like they make sense, but end up being the perfect taste combination! Whether you are here for lunch, brunch, or dinner, you can't go wrong.  Try as much as you can, drinks included. 

In addition to the house-made desserts, Datz also sells baked goods flown in from a famous New York bakery. On two separate occasions, I've tried them, and it was disappointing both times. Maybe because I know what it tastes like fresh, but both times, it was dry. 

  *Food allergy warning: some items are not listed on the menu and I was shocked to have nuts on my chicken and waffles one time.* If you have an allergy, ask your server about your choices.

Great food, good prices, ambiance is lacking (as in non-existent). The best part is that it is BYOB, making the price of the night out go down :) There are only a handful of tables, so a reservation is a must. The environment, though small and lacking decor, it feels like you are in someone's kitchen; then when you taste the food, you know you're in someone's kitchen eating homemade Italian meals. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu!

This is my second time at this Chick-fil-A and my second bad experience. I've been on weeknights around 5pm both times and waited over an hour for food. The first time I was trapped in the drive-thru for over an hour; this time I ordered ahead and sat in a parking spot for almost an hour. My order was cancelled, I spoke to someone who had the order and said it would get made right away, then he came back 10 minutes later to say I had to order again through the app. All with 2 frustrated toddlers in the backseat. If it were convenient to get out of the parking lot, I would have left and gone literally anywhere else.
Real, authentic tacos and great environment for a quick, delicious meal. You get salsa and homemade chips to start and we both ordered 3 tacos with different meat in all 3. I will definitely be back!

MbBhClrXyu8-Mk5wW5y8tg.review_text:
So I've been to this place a couple of times and every time. I agree with everyone's comments that the wait staff is pretty lousy and definitely needs to improve but I do like the food. Actually, I've always gotten the same thing each time. The Arroz Con Pollo is delicious. Granted that I've never had it before and have never tried it anywhere else so far, it was very flavorful. It is supposed to be spicy (according the menu) but it is not as spicy as you would expect it to be. The crab cakes were nicely cooked and I liked the batter that they used for it. The drinks were ok. Had a couple grey goose dirty martinis. Unfortunetly, they didn't have any blue cheese olives.

This place has two different sections. They have their bar area which is pretty cool and have tv's everywhere. They also have a dining area which is nice and also has tv's everywhere. They give you a box if you want to watch tv in the dining area where you can change the chanel on the box and hear what's on tv. You just need to find the right channel for what you are watching but they will turn the tv to whatever you want if noone else is watching it. 

The main reason why I like going to this place besides the Arroz con pollo is that they have the NFL network and this is a Steelers bar when my boys in black and gold play. The bar area gets filled with Steelers fan and they set up a giant projector to show the game as well as put a lot of the other tv's onto the game. They also do show the other games too so you can still see your team play. And lose if you are a ravens/bengals/browns fan. Who have never shown up to this place when the steelers play btw. I would frequent this place every Sunday to watch my steelers play and for the arroz con pollo.

Oh. They will also let you hold Pujol's ESPY award if you ask so make sure you do because it is pretty cool. I doubt 95% of the people know about this but now you do.

So. I was driving through the mall thinking I'd hit up QDoba when I saw Noodles and Company and figured I'd give it a try for the first time. Well. I went in with little to no expecations and came out blown away. First of all, it's kind of like a fast food style place where you order your food at the front and wait for it while they are cooking. However, you go sit down and they bring your food out to you. I've tried almost everything on their menu and I now only get a large Thai Curry soup and a large Indonesian Peanut Saute with breaded chicken breast. 

The thai curry soup is a curry flavored soup with noodles and fresh vegetables. The thing that I love about this place is that all of the stuff that they use is fresh. The soup has fresh tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, spinach leaves all soaked into the soup. It is delicious. The soup alone could fill most people. I am not most people. The indonesian peanut saute is a spicier dish than what you would find on the menu which is good because I like a little more kick to it. They do sprinkle some crumbled up peanuts over the noodles and they have some sort of spicy peanut sauce that goes well with the rice noodles. They also throw in some brocoli, sliced carrots, cabbage and asian sprouts which are all extremely fresh. 

These two dishes are what I miss most when I had to move from St. Louis to Texas.

Well. The pad thai isn't exactly their best dish. I had it once and never got it again. The Pesto cavatappi with grilled chicken is delicious as well. I would sometimes change up the indonesian peanut saute with either this dish, the penne rosa or the japanese pan noodles.  I have tried the asian chop salad but that wasn't anything spectacular. The tomato basil bisque is also good but not as good as the thai curry soup. They also have some fried dumplings as appetizers but I have had better dumplings at non-asian restaurants. Wouldn't suggest getting these.

When you order your noodles, you can customize the meats that you put on. You can either get grilled chicken, breaded chicken (parmesian crusted chicken breast is what it's called on the menu), slices of beef or shrimp.

I kept raving about Noodles and Company to my coworkers (especially the thai curry soup and the indonesian peanut saute) that they finally went there and fell in love. They absolutely loved the indonesian peanut saute and how fresh the vegetables are.

Ok. The thing that I like the most about this Qdoba is that I signed up to get a Qdoba card and they keep emailing me free meals every month or so. And it seems to be just this place that does it because my friends don't get the same things with the other places. This Qdoba is very clean and was recently built. The staff was real green when they opened up so not all of them knew exactly how to make my steak fajita burrito but they learned pretty quickly and got real good. I'm a big fan of the naked burrito's now because the tortilla's are about 300 calories more but I will still get a regular steak fajita burrito every now and then because it's so good.

Well. For those who don't know what Qdoba is, it's a mexican fast food chain that serves fresh, moderately healthy, mexican food (burritoes/ quesadillas/ etc..) The burritoes are gigantic and weigh about a pound each. There is a ton of meat, vegetables, sauces in it. You can pretty much customize what you want in it which is the best part and they make it in front of you. They have 5 different spicy sauces from not spicy to very hot. I like mine hot. If you sign up for the Qdoba card (which is free) every time you get 1000 points, you get a free meal. 1 Burrito is 100 points. So if you order 5 burritoes for lunch for co-workers, you just need 500 more and you get a free meal. It's pretty awesome. 

There are Qdoba's all over the country. They are not in all states yet but if you do see one and are hungry, you will not be hungry after eating here.

The thing I love about St. Louis Bread Company / Panera Bread is that the bread is unique. I have never tasted a piece of bread more delicious than the slices of french that they rip off to go with your soups. I am a big fan of their tomato mozzarella paninni but their french onion soup is to die for. The croutons on that thing have some sort of garlic flavoring which when soaked in the soup and cheese, are just delicious. The breakfast menu is also really good. They serve multiple types of egg quiches mixed with bacon or ham or spinach, etc... that are absolutely amazing. The breakfast sandwiches are on the paninni bread which is really good. They also serve a breakfast power sandwich which is supposed to be the healthier sandwich on whole wheat bread. Not gonna lie, it's damn good.

This place has some really good indian food. I've tried a couple of the places in St. Louis and Saffron has to be the best that I've been to. The lunch buffett has multiple curry dishes. They always have a chicken tikka maasala but have a goat dish and another meat curry dish too. They have the tandoori chicken which is really good because they put it ontop of a bed of vegetables. 

Oh. They don't only serve white rice but another type of rice. Naan is brought to your table fresh instead of sitting at the buffet. The mango lasi is delicious and the best part of the lunch buffet. After everything, it's not even $12.

Pointers Pizza was ranked #3 on the Food Network's Top Five Pizzas with Pizzaz and #8 on the Travel channel's top ten places to pig out. 

Well. Pointers Pizza has a pizza challenge called the Pointersaurus Pizza Challenge. It's a 28" pizza which weighs in at about 10 lbs. A team of 2 has one hour to finish it and there has to be either 2 meat selections or 4 vegetable selections. If you win, you get $500. Only 17 teams have completed it and 2 of them were professional eaters. 

So my friend and I figured we wanted to try this challenge. Well. It was a friday and we wanted to practice for it so we got a pointersaurus pizza with just pepperoni on it. I've heard people say that if you're going to get the meat, go with something light like turkey. Well. The pizza box is enormous and barely fit into my rental mazda 6. I had to put the back seats down in order for it to fit. Actually, I almost lost the pizza carrying it to my car because the wind picked it up and almost flipped it out of my hands. So I bring the pizza to my friends place and we time ourselves. Well. We finished half the pizza in 30 minutes before the wall hit us. And my god did it hit us hard. We ate about 5/8 of the thing before throwing the towel in. There was no way we could have finished it in one hour. We actually got so sick of looking at it that we threw the rest of the pizza out. 

Well. The pizza itself was pretty delicious. It's a thin crust style pizza which really helps for the challenge because there isn't too much bread in it to fill your stomach up. 

We did not decide to do the challenge afterwards.

I really like this place. I think I'd rather go here than to Big Daddy's. The dueling piano players are awesome and know so many songs. They also are really good singers too. The music was kickin', the crowd was good, the women weren't bad. This is a really good place to go if you want to just chill out and listen to some good classics.

What can I say. This has the potential to be a really really good club. If people would just ever go show up. They've actually closed their upstairs section because they didn't have enough people. Every time I've been there, the place has been dead. I once go 2 bottles there and by midnight, there was another table with people and about 5 people on the dancefloor upstairs. Downstairs was a little more crowded but not by much. We ended up killing the bottles and leaving.

Great bar. They actually have two sections. An indoor section and an outdoor section which is really more of an indoor section but it has a roof and heaters during the winter. The outdoor area is awesome at night and I think it is actually better than the indoor section even though the bands usually play inside. There are two pretty decent size bars outside so you don't have to wait too long to get drinks. The space outdoors is also huge so it never seems too crowded.

The only reason why I went here was because my friend lived 30 seconds away in the Soulard Market Apartments and we left a different bar with a couple of really hot girls who wanted to go here. Just have to say that this place is a dump. The whole building is dirty and the place reminded me of my frat house. Spilled beer everywhere, dirty wooden floors, disgusting bathrooms, etc. If I wanted to drink at a place like this, I would have traveled back to Pittsburgh and crashed at my old fraternity house.

Talk about another dump in St. Louis that people actually really like to hit up to get trashed. You want to meet some real trashy people. Come here. They apparently have a strict dress code and made me take my hoody off. So I drop my hoody off in the car and roll in with jeans, t-shirt and sandals. Ridiculous. You don't want hoodies but you'll let me in with sandals?? If you're not gonna let hoodies in, why are you letting people in with backwards hats? Come on. Dress code my @ss. It's cuz I'm the only asian guy in there. If you roll in here with a dress shirt, you are way over dressed. And girls who wear dresses to this place, don't bother, you'll stand out like red on white. At least the girls here are semi-attractive.

I liked coming to Big Daddy's as a pregame to something bigger because it is always packed and is a great place to pick up good looking girls who want to go to a club and get bottles later. I've had a blast every time. They have a really large outdoor patio and an even bigger inside. A decent sized dance floor which gets really packed later in the night and plenty of tables for people who just want to sit and chill. When it does get packed, it takes a little longer to walk around because there are a ton of people. They have 2 bars inside and another one outside. Bathrooms are inside to the right.

Everyone gets carded at the door and they do have a dress code where you can't wear a backwards or sideways hat. So to all those idiot wannabe gangsters, just wear your hat normally, get in and then turn it sideways. You won't imagine how many people start getting into it with the bouncer for refusing to wear their hat straight on. It's a hat. We all know your going bald but seriously, just put it forward for 10 seconds then you can set it back to the side again. That's when people in line start getting pissed.

Morgan Street Brewery has a ton of different beers and actually gets really packed on the weekends. They always have new different beers so you can always try something new each time. I've never eaten here but I have stopped by for multiple beers on many occasions. One time, they actually refused to let me in because I was too drunk. (Don't remember it though because I was obliterated.) Apparently my friend and I ended up going back to Big Daddy's where my group was but they wouldn't let me in because I was too drunk so we decided to go back to Morgan Street Brewery where they actually let me in. I then go to the bar, get two beers and we polish them off rather quickly. I then try to order 2 more beers but the bartender says no because I'm too drunk. My friend then leans over and orders the same two beers and gives me one of them. Man. What a great place.

Been here a couple of times because I was craving Pho and it was the only place I knew where to go. Also got a large order of Pho with plenty of meat, tripe, flank, tendon, etc. The only way you can really mess up Pho is if you're trying to mess it up. This place does not. The bean sprouts are not always the freshest but they aren't old and moldy either. They're in between. Probably stored in the fridge for a little bit of time. I also usually get some spring rolls which are also not completely fresh but also not old. The price isn't bad at all and you do get pretty full off the meal. Service is usually really good but I've only been there on Saturdays around 2 pm for lunches because I wake up a little late in the morning from the night before.

Been here a couple of times before. Didn't actually feel like dropping money on bottles the first time which turned out to burn me because if you do get bottles, you get treated like royalty. Music was pretty good. They played some new songs at the time and some good classic hip hop ones that got everyone bumping. The girls that come here are pretty good looking but you'll need to catch it when there's a lot of people inside. I think I've only been here once when it was actually really really good and the girls were very good. Other times, it's been pretty dead.

Have only actually eaten here for breakfast because I used to stay at this Hilton a lot. Most of the time, I'd go for the breakfast buffet because it's pretty good. They're always refilling the platters so the customers will never run out of food. The wait staff is also really good about refilling my OJ and water because I tend to pound those after being completely dehydrated from drinking the night before. I like how they have a fresh fruit selection. They also serve salmon, sliced cold turkey, salami. The price of the buffet is about $13 a person.

Used to live in Arnold so the Kilt was a usually a weekend stop if I wasn't going clubbing in St. Louis. Gotta love the outfits that the waitresses wear. Everything is so revealing!! The girls here make those outfits look good. The food here isn't bad. I usually get a burger for the main course. The beer is cold, the shots keep coming, what not to like?

The only complaint I have is the wing selection. You'd expect a place like this to have a pretty decent selection of wings but they don't. They only have 3 flavors and the hot is not hot at all.  They even have a section for smokers which is awesome for non-smokers like me who don't want my clothes to reek of cigarettes while enjoying a nice beer.

The Kilt does show the UFC fights

Drove by there a couple times and never really had any interest of stopping in until a friend literally took me there. I thought it was some asian buffet restaurant that served fatty, greasy unhealthy food. Wow. Was I wrong about the buffet. As for the other half of that last phrase, all I can say is that they claim to be PF Chang's sister restaurant. The dishes are decent calories but the sodium content is enough to feed a family of 4. However, the dishes are tasty and a lot better than your asian buffet restaurant in St. Louis. You can also choose brown rice instead of white.

My favorite dish here is probably the Beef Mandarin Kung Pao. The chicken orange peel isn't bad but not as good. The beef noodle teriyaki is also pretty good but they do drench the thing in soy sauce. Also, the fried rice is drenched as well and I hate when restaurants overload the soy sauce on your rice.

This isn't a bad restaurant to hit up every now and then but because of the amount of sodium in the dishes, I try to only come here maybe once a month.

They claim to serve NYC pizza here. Was in the area for drinks at Ozzie's when it was still around with a couple of friends and we felt we needed some NYC pizza and went across the street. There are better NYC pizza's in St. Louis but if you need something quick and are in the area, this will kind of satisfy your craving. It's not exactly NYC pizza but they do try their best. The slices aren't as big as NYC slices but you can still fold the pizza. There is grease on the pizza which helps with the authenticity. They do serve alcohol here too so we continued drinking. They have a wide variety of pizza's here so you don't have to get the classic pepperoni slice.

This is one of he better Hooters that I have been to. The girls here are actually pretty attractive and most do not have a nasty gut that hangs over their pants. The wings here are very good and I'm not sure what is in the hot sauce but it is hotter than other Hooters that I've been to. The burgers are also good and the quesadilla's aren't bad. Even though they taste the same at every hooters. This location does serve multiple selection of wing sauces so you aren't stuck with hot, mild and nuclear. They've got a garlic parmesan which isn't bad.

They do show the UFC fights but come at least an hour before if you want a seat because it gets very very packed.

Located smack middle downtown. If you're going to a ball game, a hockey game or a football game. Or just want something to eat and pregame before hitting up Laclede's or Washington Ave for a heavy night of drinking, this isn't a bad place. The restaurant is actually really big and they have tons of tv's. The waitresses are really friendly (not exactly the smartest tool in the tool shed) but they are nice and will sit chill. They also bring other girls to sit at your table if it's just guys. Food isn't bad. Service isn't bad. It's your regular Hooters location so don't expect anything fantastic. If it is your birthday and your friends tell the waitresses, do plan on being completely humilitated. There's a reason why I never come to Hooters on my birthday now.

Want good steak. Ruth Chris is a sure bet to have some. Do plan on spending some money though. However, it's cheaper than other good steak houses in the city. I usually get a porterhouse for 2 and split it with another person. Medium rare of course. Sides include creamed spinach and some asparagus. A couple bottles of wine. Appetizersr aren't bad. I do like the crab stuffed mushrooms. Creme brulee for desert. Now that's a good meal!

Located across the street from the Hilton downtown. This is a place to swing by for some quick asian fusion. Don't expect a 5 star gourmet dish. What you'll get is food that fill you up and won't make you sick. Now if you're counting calories, you probably don't want to swing in here. But if you happen to check into one of the many hotels in the area and need something quick to eat and don't want to go to Hooters or anywhere else on that block, then this is the place to go.

Great Korean place. Probably the best in Indianapolis IMO. The food comes out very fast. I love how you can customize what you want in your bowl. Some of the other places don't give you the option to add additional ingredients to change up the flavor but you can do that here which is a huge plus. The location definitely has a fast food, get in, eat quick and leave type feel but the food is not greasy or unhealthy. I do like how they serve alcohol. My only complaint (super minor) is that I wish there would be some appetizers to order. 


Definitely gonna be coming back the next time I'm in town.

Mg9mEuK7oSk6a6kCaAtRig.review_text: Best Happy Hour and GREAT food!!! Half off apps and drinks Tuesday-Sunday 7pm- close...who can beat that, esp when the food is off the hook!! Love the Raviolis and the great Oreana Pinot Noir yummy!!!...

Love this place! Go there all the time for happy hour. They serve Oreana wines for their house wine for $5!!! Usually i go to places and for "Happy Hour " I get an off brand wine that is barley tolerable. Oreana rocks love their tasting room and all their wines! The happy hour food is really good too, lots of options and good portions! Definitely one of the top Happy places I would go to!!

Great place for a calm happy hour or to take a date for dinner. All their foods are bought locally (farmers market) which I respect tremendously not to mention the burgers are off the hook. I had a glass of Mission Point Chardonnay for happy hour which I had never heard of but loved it!! Come to find out its the same wine maker from Oreana winery which is also a local company here in SB!! Never knew Oreana was part of mission point!! Thats awesome!! Staff is friendly and lovely ambiance!

Savoy night club is the one of the top clubs in Santa Barbara if not the only one that has good music, good people and great drinks and entertainment. They also provide an amazing brunch on Sundays that is worth checking out.

Wow this place was quite Amazing. I have tasted a lot of foods and this traditional DANISH food is super yummy (It's not AMERICAN food). I have gone to Andersen's every time I needed a cake or pastries but never realized how amazing their restaurant part was. I love love their duck for dinner,   their crab sandwich for lunch is super delicious and  the crab Benedict for breakfast, well priceless. Their portions are overly generous and their staff is right their when you need them. I have met the owners (Mom and Daughter) and they are the sweetest people...I have definitely gone back multiple times and will continue to go!!!!
Awesome place, went there last night for first Thursday and the wines/ beers and service was amazing....it was hard to find but a hidden jewel for sure. Definitely going back!!

It was definitely Yummy, but little expensive for what you get (plan on eating dinner after :-) ha). 
When we arrived the young gentle man (Host) was extremely accommodating and informative. Our server was busy non existent so we asked him if we could order bottles of wine and food. He sold us on $300 worth of product (he was great) but upset me shortly after our Asian server she started yelling at him in front of us to get back to his station out front and that this was her table and not his job...felt it was rude and unprofessional... lets just say we had a good time but he definitely made our experience, would never want her as our server bad attitude and unprofessional.
Oh and the ambiance is top notch.
Best Thai food in Santa Barbara County by far!! Owners- service is outstanding and prices are great! Only Thai place I would recommend and I have been to Thailand so I am picky!
I was partially sad when I found out there was no meat... Then I ordered there pizza and artichoke dish and I was wowed!! Amazing food great Kava. And they have beer and wine! Can't wait to go back.

This is for Dave W.'s review: I just want to clarify on your review since I was also a guest during your dinning time. The so called Blacked out girls (2) out of the (3) were drunk from another club during "Sunday Session" they were local girls who came in to see a friend at work. Only 1 girl got served ( the sober one) the others were placed outside with water. Yes, I agree especially since Blk Sheep is small place the Management should have asked the girls to leave or asked to call them a cab. But they kept to themselves until one of the girls did sneek into the uni sex bathroom and I guess was throwing up. That's when I saw u open the door and freak out, right after management got her friend to help her and he called a taxi for them right away. It wasn't a huge deal and in no way was she unconscious or in danger she was just drunk and young. As for the food, well it's bomb! And well priced... If u think it's expensive then I wouldn't recommend Santa Barbara for u and def don't go to the Lark or blue tavern ( my other fav spots). All I can say is good luck! Ps they used filter water

If you are going for drinks and a California Roll u are safe otherwise don't go! I normally go to Arigato but got talked into going here. Not only was it same price as Arigato ( for certain rolls) the fish was not fresh and customer service wasn't the friendliest or quickest. Avoid!

I used to go to State and A but never made it to Maggie's bc of the reviews so I was excited when Benchmark opened up but service was slow, not knowledgable about anything. Example wanted vanilla vodka ( told me they don't have fancy drinks... As an industry bartender I turned my head and said look right there see the stoli,well vanilla vodka is located right next to it. Just write down my drink and give to the bartender lol. Food was eh ok nothing special... Ambiance was confusing.  Not a horrible place but nothing special. Skip

If you are looking a great pizza at a great price and are in a rush this is your spot. They let u build ur own pizza with no judgements lol and get it to very promptly. Definitely recommend. Also this pizza is great the next day, just pop it in ur oven or toaster oven and it's bomb!

Server was incredibly rude and come to find out she was the owner! Food was ok nothing special and still pricey. My friends and I will never go back. There are a lot better restaurants in SB to go too.
Great place for a nice glass of wine or a enjoyable dinner. Definitely recommend and servers are friendly, knowledgable and prompt. Five stars!
One of the best breakfast places u can go to in SB just plain yummy! It gets busy but staff handles it great!
One of my favorite spots. Not only great food but super yummy cocktails. Staff is friendly and nice too. Great for first date night

What can I say... 5 star restaurant with 5 star staff. Everyone is very knowledgable staff works as a team not individually and food is off the hook. Definitely high end place but worth the buck and great local wine selection

So I took my family to Andersen's for breakfast and yes I have been there plenty of times mostly for dinner to get their amazing duck but this time for breakfast and i ordered the Blackberry Sparkler and crab cake Benedict (Hollandaise was amazing! And I'm picky about my sauces). It also came with a complimentary pastries and some bread...a lot of food but super amazing. Staff was friendly and of course the owners were there working their butts off which is nice and warming to see.
I will def make this spot my new breakfast favs. Plus they have an amazing patio

Amazing fresh and delicious authentic Mexican food. I am not easily impressed with Mexican food here in SB but dang service was extremely nice and food was bomb. Ambiance is warm and inviting for dates, going alone or for families. Hidden Gem indeed has a tv too if u want to watch sports

Only complaint I have is I want more and they need to open for lunch bc I want more! Very awesome food, ramen is bomb, tacos delicious and the peanut sauce wontons are dreamy... Very yummy indeed! Also cocktail list and wine list are also top notch. I'm definitely coming back

Wow I was really excited for this Bar/ Cafe to open but am always nervous to go to opening day Bc brand new places can let you down....But I was extremely happy!! 
Staff was very helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. Prices are great and location/atmosphere is perfect.
They have amazing fun and unique Wines and Sherry's can't wait to go back and have lunch there!

Wow, I was blown away by not only the selection on local wines but amazing import wines! Staff and owners are extremely knowledgeable so if you do not know what you want they can lead you in the right direction or they can pick out great wines that you will love.
I was extremely statified and will be coming back. They even have a wine club program that I might just join!
Oh and parking is not an issue which is a huge plus!!

MoiL6eoTqhyU0zrgbw3qtA.review_text: Great place for a bite to eat even in the late hours. This is the spot to go for late night cravings.
Love the wings! Great weekends. Karaoke nights are highly entertaining and best of all the ufc fight events!
Small "hole in a bar" type of place. Quiet local crowd but not a place to have a good time.
Still one of the best little Italian pizzerias in the 08060 area. Been around for a long time and I still enjoy it. Best sicilian pizzas around too!
Best big-chain pizza in the area. Just needs a delivery service and it's a 5 star review for me!
I love it here!! Great Japanese cuisine and the plate presentation is superb! Overall a great restaurant. Try the Sushi boat!
I love having breakfast here. Their homefries are what gets me coming back for more. Big plates and servings always keeps me happy.

I love this place! For a dive bar, it has great atmosphere and crowd. The food is f'n unbelievable! You need to try everything in their menu. They have huge portions for those with a big appetite. The bartenders and staff are awesome. They'll get you what you want and will always check up on you to make sure you're taken care of. This is a great spot to go to and I suggest you stop by and experience it yourself.

This is the only Indian cuisine restaurant in the area that I know of and I'm glad it's only 5 minutes away from my house. They have outstanding food. Their BUTTER CHICKEN is to die for! That is my #1 entree of choice. Naan bread is also top notch. 5 stars for me across the board! * * * * *

I love it here! It's both a blessing and a curse that I live right across from the restaurant so I'm constantly here getting their homemade filipino cuisine. sundays are what i look forward to because of their breakfast! but they serve delicious food throughout the day.
