My hubby has raved about Tommy's roast pork sandwich for YEARS. YEARS, people, YEARS. 

Upon visiting Philly for the first time, Reading Terminal Market and Tommy DiNic's was our first stop. As expected, the line was wrapped around the entire booth during the lunchtime hour. I was surprised by how fast the line actually moved, gotta give credit to the fast expediters. 

We snagged up 4 sandwiches for us and some friends (+$40). Overall, the sandwich was just aight. My hubby would probably bitch slap me into next week for saying that, but I honestly wasn't that blown away. The pork was a little bland, the rabe a little too al dente, and it just lacked an overall wow factor. 

Would I eat it again? Sure. Would I rather experience John's Roast Pork or a Philly cheesesteak next visit? Probably.

Well, I'm probably digging myself a hole straight to the depths of Yelp hell, but the Reading Terminal Market is overrated. Maybe I don't appreciate what RTM has to offer... maybe I had this grandiose idea of what the place would be like in my head... maybe I just suck. Who knows. 

Too many people. Tight walkways. Lines wrapped around booths so you have know no idea where they start and where they end. No concept of walking on the right. Dirty bathrooms. Rude bathroom attendant. Eating areas are cramped. Meh. 

Hate all you want on the city of Cleveland, but they have the West Side Market. I imagined that the RTM would be similar, but man was I wrong. The West Side Market has high ceilings and a more open feel to it. Feels less congested and easier to navigate. Sorry Reading, but I'll take the West Side Market any day over your hot mess.

I've been to the Morimoto in Waikiki and absolutely loved the ambiance and food. Only took about 5 years to make it to the original location, but gosh darn it, I FINALLY made it! 

We decided to venture to Philly (and Morimoto, of course) to celebrate a few birthdays. We had a larger party of 10 people and I made reservations well over a month in advance. There was only one time slot available for our larger party, so I definitely recommend booking as soon as possible if you are dining with a group. They also require a credit card to secure the reservation and there is a charge if you cancel. 

The ambiance at the Philly location is very modern-- love the color changing lights. We dined in February and I was surprised by how warm the inside of the restaurant was-- not sure if it's the lights or what. Our server, Seoung (I think), was very attentive and gave a great description of the regular and seasonal Omakase. 

I am not a sushi eater by any means (I know, I know), so I typically stick with "safe" (read: basic) items. Morimoto has the best Rock Shrimp Tempura and Black Cod Miso (better than Nobu). The black cod miso melted in my mouth and was a pretty decent portion, I was almost too full for the last few bites. The Wagyu Dumplings, while expensive, are a must. So delicate and served with a rich broth. My husband enjoyed the seasonal Omakase and the scallop served with one of his courses was the BEST scallop I've ever tasted. 

Overall, Morimoto is a one of a kind dining experience. Waikiki and Philly have been checked off my list-- I'm eyeing up the Vegas location next!

WOW! Definitely a must if you are in the area! Located right next to Cochon, the Butcher has a more fast casual vibe. Order at the counter, receive a number, then seat yourself. Drinks can be ordered through the bar and you can keep a tab open (versus if you order at the main counter). 

The Muffaletta is legit! Meats were high quality and the bread was delicious! The Sausage and Salami Arancini were equally delicious, but only 3 come in an order. I heard this menu item is a new addition and hope it remains a staple!

Teeny tiny, legit coffee shop tucked away from all of the crazy. We popped in for a pick me up and were pleased with the handcrafted menu options and friendly service. The macchiato was bold and some of the latte options sounded interesting. Don't plan on bringing your laptop and staying for hours-- more of a grab and go set up.

When you see a line 50 people deep and snaking down the sidewalk (with a security guard posted out front!), you know you're in for some serious eats! A friend posted a pic of the chargrilled oysters and they looked divine-- as a side note, I don't even like oysters and these were delicious! I also got the New Orleans Medley- red beans & rice, gumbo, and jambalaya. Soooo good! The tables and condiments could use a good scrub, but this didn't deter me from indulging in some New Orleans classics.

Been a fan of Isaac since his days on TC. Toups was on the top of my list during a recent visit to NOLA and, dare I say, better than my visit to Emeril's *gasp*. 

Reservations can be made via Open Table and there is indoor and outdoor seating. It's about a 10-15 minute drive from downtown and situated in a quaint little neighborhood on the main road. 

The service was friendly and informative. The food was spot on! Definitely recommend the pickle plate and boudin balls to start. The boudin was one of my top faves of my trip! The shrimp & grits poboy was a cool fusion of two classics. Bottomless mimosas during brunch topped off my experience-- yesss!

Come for the ambiance of the spinning bar carousel, but don't stay too long-- tons of people want to try and there is very limited seating. A few tables and chairs and couch areas are available throughout, but it can be a waiting game to snag a seat during prime hours. 

The cocktail menu is quintessential French and they do serve legit Sazeracs. My hubby said it was the best sazerac he had in NOLA! My Fleur Des Lis cocktail was pretty good-- contained my favorite spirit combo of gin and cucumber. A complimentary bowl of bar snack mix is also provided. 

My one pet peeve-- the people that hog seats at the spinning bar that A) are not drinking at all B) are finished drinking and just dilly dallying around or C) think it's a sports bar and the place to watch footballl while drinking. In the words of *NSYNC, BYE, BYE, BYE.

Tucson has some great breweries and Dragoon was an okay stop on our weekend tour. 

+ nice space with lots of seating 
+ tucked away in an industrial area 
+ flights 
+ IPAs for days 

- not a lot of sours or styles of brews 
- food truck bailed the day we went
- 1 dude working and he was a bit curt 
- locals definitely received better treatment than out of towners

WOW, this pizza is fire! My hubby suggested we walk here from Pueblo Vida because of the high reviews. The walk was a bit sketch on a Friday night (under a bridge, through a construction zone, cue the Walking Dead), but I would totally do it again for this pizza! 

The walk up order window is pretty cool. We ordered, paid, grabbed some beers over at Crooked Tooth while we waited, and they delivered it over to us in no time. 

The Verde pie was so fresh, loved the pistachio crunch, and that CHAR! Omg. My hubby also ordered the Focaccia and wowwwww. The pepper jelly stuff on top was a great surprise.

Pretty decent Mexican food, not better than El Nene, but good nonetheless. 

+ Chile Colorado 
+ Carne Tacos 
+ Rice & beans 
+ Quick service and they gave us side salsas, napkins, cutlery 
+ Accoutrements (jalapeño, radish)

- Flavor and spice were pretty good, not the best I've had

The BEST food in Tucson. Hell, this is some of the best food I've had in awhile. So flavorful, spicy, delicious. 

+ adovada 
+ tacos
+ lorenzas 
+ Sonoran dog YUMMMMM
+ salsas and accoutrements were on point

I've been to Donut Bar in San Diego and Vegas. Super excited to see this location in Tucson. We visited at about 9 on a Saturday morning and there was no wait. The lady who boxed our donuts was very sweet. The maple bar was sooo good-- can't go wrong with a classic. My only complaint was that I couldn't eat all of my donuts in 1 day and they got super stale the next day.
Yessss. I always try to stop at the Cartel at PHX, so was super happy to see this location in Tucson. The coffee is legit, service was great, wish I was hungry enough to try the breakfast samplings.

This brewery was probably my favorite in terms of beer in Tucson. The sours were really nice (+1 for the Prickly Pear Lemonade sour) and the Order Up coffee stout was also quite good. We visited during Halloween and loved the video contest they were playing-- super funny! This would def. be a regular spot for me if I were a local.

This brewery is awesome, definitely one of my favorites during my visit to Tucson. The ambiance was on point-- loved the outdoor courtyard with lights and plants. The brews were great and I loved ordering Anello pizza from the window across the road and having it delivered and I enjoyed my brews.

Only gripe, no veggies, some places will add broccoli/onions & they don't add that or offer egg roll, or soup - just pop. Most places give options, they don't. Lunch here is just pop on side with your entree & pork fried rice for $6.67 (with tax). I can tell fried rice was a day old, better off to get white rice, at least that's made daily & left in warmer. 
Overall - if you work by 41/Palm St - ORDER! It's definitely a hidden jem!

Went around 5pm to celebrate my husband's birthday. We were seated instantly and our waiter was attentive. Noteworthy: other wait staff would check with us occasionally throughout the evening to see whether we needed something. 
We looked around the menu and decided the Chef's Tasting would be the way to go. We felt adventurous and don't have allergies or are disgusted with anything. The chef was very nice and turned out later - very creative. He prepared 4 courses for us and all were wonderful:

1. Bone marrow - Exellent! It is much different from your regular marrow from osso bucco, where the osso bucco is supposed to be cooked perfectly and the marrow just goes along with it. Very delicate in texture, served with tasty chimichurri, ciabatta toast and arugula. 

2. Aged copa - a plate of 16 weeks aged pork shoulder, thinly sliced. Accompanied by arugula and parmesan. On the side we got bunch of spicy pickles. I could do without those as they were really overpowering, but my husband requested them so we got them. They were not chef's choice.

3. Seared scallop and sole with mashed parsnip - That was just heavenly! The scallop was perfect and drizzled with delicate buttery sauce. The texture of the sole was also perfect and drizzled with different sauce - olive with something tropical, but not too powerful, little chunks of small nuts, and parsley. The perfectly creamy parsnip was surprisingly delicious. This dish was overall amazing and should be permanently on the menu. 

4. The last course had sliced sirloin topped with foie gras mousse on a bed of arugula, accompanied by fren chfries drizzled with truffle olive oil - The sirloin and foie gras - I don't even know where to start. What a great combination!!! The steak itself might have been aged (but I am not sure). There was a certain smokiness to it and maybe a drop or two of soy sauce. Coarse salt was a nice texture adding touch. Combined with smooth foie it was the best thing I had in a long time. The French fries were great too. I saw many reviewers complained about Campo not serving fries, and I would not have a problem with that at all, but I also have no problem eating perfectly-crunchy-on-the-outside-and-soft-on-the-inside fried potatoes. A little hint of garlic and truffles was a nice touch. 

I wish the desert was free for the birthday boy, but it's not a big deal.
Overall, it was fun and food was beyond delicious. I will go back for the Chef's Tasting experience. 
Also my two previous visits during lunchtime were ok, I was not offended, but would not go back out of my own initiative. Three stars at best. Last night, it felt great to be so positively surprised. 

Thank you!

Wish I could try the food. Service was ridiculous. We sat at the empty table for about 15 min and nobody even approached us. Not even with water. Please note the place was by no means full. We left and it is unlikely that we will be going back.

I love Martinis. Over the course of years I must have had all martinis that Roxy puts on the menu. Always perfect. Not too cold, not too warm. Not watered down. There is live music. And adorable older couples dancing. The happy hour is a steal. Sure there are few minuses, like cigarette smoke (seriously ban that shit already), the waitresses are tiny bit sluggish, and they might have done away with the salty almonds (or maybe I just missed them?). Either way, still four stars because the martinis are great!

The first though after walking in: This place is tiny! The staff is very friendly and engageing. VERY tasty coffee. I had a mocha and it was really nice. The use of whole frothed milk makes a difference. The chocolate was also the good stuff. I wish they had larger size of the serving. 12oz barely puts a dent in my morning fuzziness. We waited a while for my mocha, but no longer than you would have to wait at Starbucks. 
There are few tables you can sit at and hang out, but the place is poorly heated so at this time of the year, you can't even take your jacket off. 
Props for the owners who created something really worthwhile out of a garage - truly a great job.

I think I got my happy ending! This is a second visit to this place, but first time we actually ate. 
After the first review, I was contacted by the manager almost immediately. He apologized profusely for our unfortunate experience. He also provided a small incentive for us to go back and give it another chance. Tonight was the night!

We went around 6pm, were greeted and seated right away. Our server Liz was very polite and attentive. We had our 13 month old and were happy to know that L&L has high chairs (clean and straps were working too), as well as little cups with lids for kids. 
We ordered calamari for appetizer it was good, not over cooked, but I would like to see the sauces on the side. I like my calamari with lemon only. Also putting the sauce on the calamari makes it soggy in a very short time.

As for the main course, I chose the seafood pot with brown rice - let me tell you, that was a very happy dish. Chunks of various seafood (fish, shrimp, clams for sure) were swimming in a delicious coconutty-lemongrassy-oniony goodness. Definitely a hit! I have to point out that unlike many seafood stews/soups this dish was not overcooked. The presentation was very pleasing as well: the stew arrived in a iron cast pot. Since the dish was soupy, it would be nice if it arrived with a spoon. I had my teaspoon, so no biggie.

My husband had jungle princess beef (I think the name was). I did try it and thought that beef was perfectly prepared, not overcooked. Very pleasant taste, spicy.  

Both dishes were pretty large, so no room for dessert. The prices were reasonable.

To sum it up; L&L is a new place with a lot of potential. The food was very good, so was the service this time. We will be back for more.

Thank you

Could be a nice place if the sushi options had more variety. Especially during lunch time. I had AYCE and there are not that many long rolls to choose from and most of the choices were deep fried or had tempura item inside. I very much prefer fresh fish, so wasn't taken away. The plus - rolls were cut into small one-bite size pieces, which are easy to maneuver without making an ungodly mess. The fish seems fresh, nigiri was very nice and surprisingly large size.  
The place is clean and service is very attentive and polite, but not in your face. Might go back for dinner if in the area, but will not go out of my way to eat there.

I have always been a fan. Great service, great food; original dishes but not over the top. Last night we went for dinner and as usual, were promptly seated and our drink requests were taken. Initially, we got 3 menus for 4 of us to share, as they were just printing them at the moment. Didn't offend me as we arrived around the opening. 
Thing I noticed at the table next to us was: One of the guests couldn't read the menu - guess what??? - waiter jumps in with a bunch of reading glasses on a plate covered with a white napkin. I don't wear glasses, so maybe it is a normal thing in the fine-dining world, but to me it was a novelty. 
The waiter was very efficient, polite, and attentive. Same goes for a bus boy. 
The food was arriving at the table fairly quickly and at the same time for the whole table (big plus). This is what I had:

1. Started with maple glazed pork belly - good but not great. Bacon is good. Period. I felt like it was an easy out for the restaurant of that level. I could use a little more crispiness. The accompanying pickled okra and green beans were perfect.

2. Another starter was sherried mushrooms and goat cheese (?) on a puff pastry - A must! Perfect combination of textures, very flavorful. I could eat 4 and just call it a dinner.

3. Sunchoke and parsnip soup with garlic croutons - Yes, yes, yes! Very flavorful, perfect for the season. 

4. And the downer of the day - braised lamb shank - The meat itself was really good, so were the giant beans, but all was drenched in a ridiculously salty reduction. And I like SALTY. This was just such an disappointment. You cant really shift your reduction to the side and eat the good pieces. Everything was covered in the stupid salty reduction. Unfortunately I did not said anything. I figured, it would put a damper on the atmosphere at the table and I didn't want to spoil otherwise perfect evening. 

5.  The dessert - Bittersweet chocolate ganache torte - Another must! The pecan crust and perfectly smooth chocolate with exquisite caramel sauce - absolutely great!

Also another plus is the tea. Maybe the only place in town that offers the "good stuff". The tea is from mightyleaf.com - very good quality. I head vanilla bean black tea. Promptly ordered some on-line after getting home.

Overall, I would love to give 1 star for the reduction and 5 stars for everything else. I had to average this out somehow and 3 stars seemed appropriate since the mishap was my main course. 

Please note that this is not my first visit to the place and other visits were definitely 5 stars. I will go back for sure and probably update the review.

Thank you!

I like this place. A little out of my way but worth it. I went for late Sunday lunch and we ordered four different dishes to share. Overall, the menu was very creative with a lot of freshly looking options. The service was prompt , but then and VERY polite and accommodating, but then we were maybe one of the three tables that were busy. Pleasant décor, but I wish the owners separated the HUGE dining room into smaller, more intimate sections. The feeling of warehouse was dominant.

On to the food:

1. The tiny pork tacos appetizer - very pleasant, well cooked pork, not chewy at all - perfect texture. This could be a happy main dish.

2. Crab Croquettes - Really these were crab cakes, but delicious ones, nevertheless. There is some kind of corn salsa on these and red tomato/bell pepper paste. I liked this dish. It wasn't too greasy or doughy. Just right.

3. The cauliflower ceviche - A-ok. first few bites were good, and after that just got boring. I could use more flavor in this dish. Maybe few shrimp? Or pieces of fish. 

4. The parmesan chicken - Very tasty dish, but the chicken was OVERCOOKED. Also a pretty small portion. Liked the sauce a lot, the ravioli was good, and crème fraise was nice flavor enhancing touch.

5. Tiramisu - Nice and light.  No chocolate sauce (thanks for that!). Instead of heavy sauce, there was a light coffee liquor flavored sauce. Definitely loved it!

Overall - 4 stars. Good start, but some kinks should be worked out. Had it been established restaurant, I would have given 3 stars. 

Thank you

Such a fun evening! The service was great, food was even better! We were in a birthday party of four and ordered a bunch of little things to share:

1. Chicken coconut soup
2. Papaya salad
3. Fresh rolls
4. Chicken satay
5. Coconut shrimp

 Everything was delicious and perfectly cooked; no chewy shrimp or dry chicken. The fresh rolls were properly rolled and not falling apart. I cannot think about anything I disliked about last night's dinner.
Also, the birthday girl got a 20% discount coupon from the owner and there was no bullsh.. cake cutting fee. So yeah! Keep on rocking, Bangkok Cuisine South!!!

Thank you!

I didn't care much for the place. The food was good, but the service was poor. The waitress didn't refill my water and I had to flag her down. Also my friend's plate was cleared but not mine even though we both were done, all utensils across the plate and all. 
The good: the salads were as ordered, came out quickly. The food was fresh, the dressing was little boring. 
The decor was nice, but... The writings on the walls are unappealing. Some would be ok. However there are so many that it reminds me of a public toilet in Europe. And who wants to eat lunch while thinking about public restroom. Not my thing for sure.

overall ok, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat there.

Thank you

Edit on 2/15/2012: My review was replied to by the owner, who said the service issue was addressed. This level of care is worth of mention. Seems like a good amount of effort goes into maintaining the quality of this business and it would be a shame to write it off. I would give it a second chance if I was in the neighborhood.

Deceided to bail on the 45 minutes wait at Hiroba, where the service got complacent because "people come over anyways". I looked up nearby spots on the phone and voila! here's the new place.

I like this place! Good value, no wait. I had AYCE. There is a wide selection of rolls with a lot of them being raw fish rolls (thank you for that). I liked the ratio of fish to rice. Also the fish seemed fresh. The fancy boat dishes could probably go as they are not very comfortable to use; hard to dip your sushi in a tiny soy sauce compartment. 

The sushi chef, Steve, was very nice and helpful and oh so creative! he would come up with various "surprize" rolls that were not on the menu making the experience more fun for me. The mochi balls ice cream were GREAT. They are small so being full is not an excuse - HAVE ONE!

Very friendly service from the whole team, even though we were the last customers for the day and the restaurant was getting ready to close down. I didn't feel urged out the door. 

Very pleasant experience overall. Goodbye Hiroba, welcome Kitzmo!

Thank you

Nice place! Too bad it's hidden in such a low traffic area. Really good selection of high quality teas. The prices may seem high, but the quality is there. The prices match the internet pricing. You just save on shipping. 

I got following teas: 
1. Very Berry - Really tasty and aromatic. Would be great in the middle of winter!
2. Pink Lemon Zest - So citrusy, but not sour. Love it!
3. Tropical Green - Smells great, but I didn't get to this one yet.

The store has a lot of coffee too. I did not buy any though. Next time.

The place is manned by Steve - very friendly guy. You can easily spend 30 min just chatting. If you want to try tea before you splurge, you can have a cup and try it out(not sure how much it costs). 

The store has some unusual opening hours: Tue-Fri till 5pm, and Sat 10-3pm. 

The only minus is, you need to spend at least 20 USD before you can use your credit card. Also having a website would be nice. Those are small things though.

Overall, I think I will be a regular 

Thank you!

Oh Campo! You have made me happy yet again. Late Valentine's Day dinner was phenomenal! We did chef's tasting again, and got entirely different flavors this time.
I wanted to mention the service - I don't know how you do it, but even though it was slammed, our plates were cleared IMMEDIATELY, after each and every one of five courses. Big plus on the service! 

And now, on to the tasty goodness. I want to mention something I didn't say the first time; not everyone likes everything like myself. Some of the dishes I was served would be "gamy" to many of my American friends. But in order to avoid that the chef comes out and ask whether you are allergic to anything or whether there are things you don't want to eat so don't be scared. 

This time around we had:

1. Roasted beets and cauliflower on a bed of goat cheese sauce. Simple, but great. Veggies were cooked to perfection, little crunchy, but not raw. Complements of chef - I know how to make the cauliflower. Thank you for that

2. Seared scallop and head-to-tail pork patty with mashed parsnip - I still cannot get over how good this parsnip is. Incredibly smooth, with a little bit of sweetness - nice compliment to the breaded patty. The scallop, same as the first time, just perfect. The patty was new to me, but I truly loved it. It had some meaty chunks and some fatty chunks. I can't come up with something comparable, but it was surprising and tasty.

3. The spicy pasta with tomatoes and calamari - one of the better pastas I have ever had. The calamari was not chewy, pasta was al dente, everything was tasting fresh and just perfect!

4. The blood pudding, Linguini sausage, roasted butternut squash, and some funky greens - we loved this dish. For once, I have had blood pudding and blood sausage on numerous occasions, but to me this was a whole new take on the dish. there was some pork meat mixed in and it was baked. In the end the texture was perfect, the bloody flavor was there, but not too heavy. The curious thing about this dish was the composition of basic flavors - squash was sweet, greens were bitter, sausage was salty, and blood pudding was little spicy. Maybe the dish had umami somewhere too, but I wouldn't know that ;) Very elegant dish. I would love to see it on the permanent menu.

5. The dessert trio - I always get this for two reasons: I get to try three desserts, and it's big enough to share. This time we got the caramel pudding (honestly, this one will never get old), dark chocolate patty with ice cream and berry sauce (I licked the plate),   and bread pudding with cranberries and orange sauce (things should not taste this good). I can't tell you which one I liked the most. It's like trying to say which one of your kids you love the most. They are different, they are excellent. Can't pick one. 

I LOVED it again. Thank you for this wonderful evening!

This is just such a solid place. Lunch or dinner. 
They have good variety on the menu. Never had anything I wouldn't like. The quality of food and service is up to a par.

Last night we went for a happy hour. Few 5 USD wines and some appetizers. We god the antipasti plate split between two of us. It is HUGE and it comes with home made warm bread. Bunch of salami, other deli meat, pickled peppers and olives, some cheese and crackers. 

Our bartender was polite and professional. Maybe tiny bit frazzled, but it was very busy during the happy hour. We had to ask three times for our waters, but we were getting the wine refills immediately. And you know, that's the priority anyways.

Good times! I will be back for more!

Thank you

What a lovely product they sell! I am not a connoisseur of Chinese baked goods, but what I got was very much up to my standards. 
I had egg custard bun, chicken curry bun, and BBQ pork bun. Absolutely LOVED these! Also they were fresh from the oven, which makes it an extra tasty treat.
I topped it all of with honeydew boba (made of fresh fruit) and went back to work. The service was prompt and polite. The value is definitely there - $1 a bun. 

I will be visiting more often, for sure!

Thank you

Fresh organic food, different menu every day, very pleasant staff, huge portions. The food tastes like grandma's home made meals. 
You can also get half a portion for $3, which will be a satisfying meal to most people. You can also order healthy dinner take outs on Tue and Thu (example - buffalo meatloaf with salad).

You really have to try it to believe how good the value is.

Don't bring a girlfriend or a boyfriend for a date as this is not a romantic place. 

Local businesses visit MS café and have a feature lunch for few bucks. I had Sushi Pier and Cafe de Thai. Fun and cheap way to try different restaurants.

They do take outs, they have desserts, coffee, salad bar, healthy options, pizza, soups, home made chips, fresh fruit. You WILL find something for yourself.

LOVE THIS PLACE SO MUCH!!!

Hmmm... All the bad customer service reviews are very surprising to me. I always received a good customer service in Reno Costco.
The shopping is easy, it is almost a one-stop-shop. The quality of the products is nice, although salad greens are hit or miss; some lasted 1.5 weeks some went after 3 days.
Everything is a great value. I noticed that even if I have to throw a little bit away due to spoilage it is still cheaper than buying from a regular store in small quantities and using it all.

The few issues I have with this store or Costco in general are:

1. Open till 6 only on the weekends

2. Please stop rotating your products in the store. I know you want me to check out other things than what I usually buy, but if you doing it by trying to confuse me, trust me, I will do all there is in my power to buy ONLY what's on my shopping list. I am a regular shopper at your store and it infuriates me if I have to look for chicken breast for 10 min because you decided it somehow didn't like to sit where it used to.

3. Please don't put your sampling stations in a cluster. People who apparently don't have food at home usually make a main store isle impassable because they have to sample everything. If the food is not ready they will all wait right there with their carts. WTH people? EAT YOUR LUNCH AT HOME OR IN THE FOOD COURT! It really makes the shopping experience a pain in the a**. If the stations are spread there are more smaller clusters.

4. Accepts only their own credit card, otherwise it's debit or cash - 1950s called they want their cash transactions back!

Otherwise, I will be happy to continue shopping at Reno Costco as they are still far better alternative than other grocery stores.

Thank you!
WTH happened here? My favorite pizza place... Oh well...

I like SG for 2 reasons: 
1. Happy hour, which lasts forever (till 8? Vs 6 at other places). All drinks are 1/2 off. Someone below said that happy hour is crappy and there are better in town. But they didn't even give one name. Well, put up or shut up. Where are those places? Mind you, it's not a challenge. If there are better happy hour places I would like to know.
2. The decor - it is VERY nice looking place for a sports bar. Other establishments like bully's, sparky's, and other crappy's look sad and underwhelming. Not even mentioning the cleanness. The difference here is that I would bring my kid here. 

Another thing I would like to bring up is the smoking section on the other side of the bar. What a great idea! I hate cigarette smoke and it's good that smokers have their den. This way others don't have to walk through a cloud of smoke to get inside.
Thank you
The bathroom is the cleanest place in this establishment. No thank you, I won't eat here.

Midtown Eats, you gave me a headache. That is a good thing. It just means that your cocktails are delicious. There are different concoctions. Some are mild and sweet for those who don't like strong alcohol taste and some are potent. I tried several and all were interesting and tasty. I had atomic burger. It was just wonderful. Perfectly medium rare. Generous patty, flavorful meat. It has some habanero mixed in but don't be fretful it does not overpowered other flavors. I also had wild mushroom soup. Very tasty! Although cup for $4 - tiny, bowl for $6 - generous. Just get a bowl and split with your friends. 
my friend had a rabbit with veggies. It was good but not very big. She said the vegetables were undercooked. 
What I liked the most about this place was the service. Very professional and friendly. I love when waiter that is not assigned to your table checks with you. To me, I don't care whether it's your table or not. To me you are part of the same establishment and nothing bugs me more about the restaurant than poor service and waiters who try to push you off to one another because it's not their section/table.
They don't take reservations but you can call ahead when you are on your way to put your name down on the waiting list. 
overall, it is a very nice casual dining and I am rating it as such. I loved it, but if I'm going to celebrate birthday or some other occasion I would rather go someplace else, where I can place a reservation and nit wait for a table. Also the tables are very close to each other, so there is nit much intimacy. On the other hand it's conducive to meeting cool people! 
Thank you!

This is a solid place. I have not bought any wines here, but I ate a couple of times and had some glasses of wine here. Both times I visited I sat at the bar. First time it was tended by the owner, the second time there was a different person. Both times the customer service was very good; prompt, attentive. The food is good but rather small portions. I am missing some variety in the appetizer department. Lots of good wines on the menu. We had an antipasti platter and it was very average. Some olives and artichokes, crostini was too hard, small amounts of cheese and meats, small cup of fruit. All that for USD13. Not very impressive. Comparred to the platter at the Grill at Quail corner with their fresh unlimited bread, this one was a silly affair for sure.

As for the clientelle - I agree with some commenters before me; rather over 45 and skewed towards a male side. This is curious granted that the place is a wine bar. From my experience those are usually more popular with women. Is it because of the surrounding businesses? 

Overall I will probably go back (close to my home), but I doubt I will suggest this place out of my own initiative.

Thank you

I like the place. I genuinely do. But it's hard to find the value in their offer. I think it's a 4 star place (bartenders conspicuously forget you asked them for a menu and look busy) but the beer is pretty expensive. Also the recent beer menu is not as good as few months ago. The prices vary but the better stuff is about $7 for 13oz - rather steep. I tried Red Headed Stranger and Pale Rider. They were both ok, but did not got me overly excited. I used to like Hopalong Cassidy, but it's gone. Also passage to India was great - also gone. Please don't misunderstand me - I don't mind changes to the menu, I just don't like when the menu changes for the worse.

The food is still very good. We had Whole Hog Pizza; tasty, but rather low on meat and heavy on the cilantro. The Gorgonzola was almost non-existent. I got ONE crumble on my last piece out of 4 pieces that I ate. 

In the past, I had the braise, the Saint Pizza, Seared Scallops. Of all these, the Saint is definitely noteworthy. Very interesting and unusual combination of flavors, fresh tasting.

Overall, had I wrote this review couple of months ago, it would have been 4 stars. Last visit was a little lackluster. I will be back for sure because I hope it was a one-off underwhelming experience. 

Thank you

Even though the prices are low, it kills me how this supposedly logistics genius can't figure things out:

1. It is prevalent that the shopping carts are all over the parking lot to the point, there is hardly a place to park left.

2. They will open a small cluster of registers away from either exit/entrance. then they will put bunch of huge bins with useless crap in the place where the line naturally forms. You get in line and there is an old lady yelling at you from behind the bin that she is in line too. Shopping at WM is strange enough. Please don't make it worse.

3. The produce is shit.

I will still stop by occasionally, but there are plenty of other stores, I would much rather use.

Thank you

Such a hodge-podge of random stuff. I always wonder what are the criteria for the product to make it onto the shelf at this store. I have bought a variety of things over here - furniture, alcohol, sweets, other food, jewelry. Everything is good quality and a decent value. The employees are ultra nice and helpful. 

Bonus: I can occasionally find products from Poland, which is fairly unusual in this town.

Thank you

Decent grocery store. Not a great value, but acceptable. The noteworthy - the bread. Always fresh, good brands, like LaBrea and the other one from SF (the name totally escaped me). The employees are usually friendly and helpful. I honestly cannot think of one thing that is a con. It's just your average chain grocery store.

Thank you

This is a surprisingly good place. I went for a dinner with some of my friends on Friday night. The food was tasty and the portions were generous. The dinner dishes rather inexpensive at $10-13.  I had fish tacos, which were made with halibut - and loaded with it. This was unexpected since most places will put small chunks of fish in the tacos. These were true fish tacos with great fish in them. The only weird thing was the cheese in them, but they tasted great. I mean what doesn't taste great with cheese. Very pleased with the dinner plate. I wish they offered black beans, but it is just me being fussy, whole red beans were very acceptable alternative to the refried beans. I also had a margarita on the rocks and a beer - both were fairly cheap (especially the beer). The margarita was made with a drinkable mix and you could taste an alcohol - good!

As for the service, very prompt and professional with exception of one older male waiter who was ogling women patrons top to bottom and back up. C'mon! At least you could try to be discrete about it. Nope, no effort at all, full blown body scan. Makes for a very awkward moment.

This used to be a different bar. Nothing had changed really other than the ownership and the name. We went there on a Saturday night to see some bands. Overall it was a great evening, but the place itself has still a lot of work to do. Especially figuring out their staffing needs. If you have to wait for 30-40 minutes to get a drink/beer, the place is probably understaffed. I saw multiple people taking off and coming back with their own beer/liquor.  I did like the fact that they had a big ice water pitcher on the counter and you didn't have to wait for that. The water tasted funky though - not sure whether the lemon slices were old or the pitcher was in need of a good scrub, but just in case please take care of both!
Bathroom was pretty clean - surprising in a busy bar. 
I might check it out again, but not a fan yet 

Thank you

This place is a nice looking place for sure - very thought out layout, nice outdoor area with a big stage and viewing place designated for live music - love that part. There was a band playing too. And not a bad one at that. The minus - we were seated inside next to the speaker - had to yell to each other to have a conversation.
The service was prompt and courteous with frequent follow-ups, but the place was not busy at all. So it is hard for me to give a bonus points for this one. And we didn't get water. We didn't specifically asked for it, I just like the ice tap water to be there. I think it is mostly a standard around Reno these days. Good selection of beers on tap - we were told about 50. Big plus in my book! My friend had a Caesar's salad and I think she liked it, because there wasn't anything left. I briefly scanned the menu and the food seemed inexpensive. I did not eat though.
The people coming over to that place - hmm... I don't know. I think there must have been a slow night at the Men's Club. I think all the female employees called it a night and went to town.

I love this place! It is a great value - inexpensive ($14.95 lunch and $20.95 dinner), good quality fish, free sake Tuesday - Thursday. We went on Wednesday. We were seated right away. We ordered our appetizers and rolls. The dishes were being served promptly. I am not a fan of cooked rolls so can't tell you anything about these, but the fresh fish rolls were very well prepared. The ingredients were fresh, the ratio of fish to rice was very good. I hate when restaurants try to stuff you with bunch of rice. Not cool. We had Marinar, Flower, Volcano, The Chao, Mountain, and some nigiri. Really didn't have anything I wouldn't like. Also the sake kept coming. Before we finished a bottle, next one would be on the table. The service was very professional and attentive but not in your face. Just the right amount of attention. 
Also we stayed till the place closed. We were not rushed out. Even though the personnel was winding down they kept encouraging us to get more food or sake. We didn't as we were ready to go too, but I appreciated not being encouraged to GTFO :)
Made for a great dining experience. 
Thank you

I have always been a BIG fan. Gb did not disappoint this time either. The service was prompt and polite. Even though we were loud and obnoxious. The beers were great. Since we went out during cinco de drinko, they had chile beso on tap (chile spiced beer). I can't tell you how happy I was when the bill came - 2.50 for a pint for that heavenly goodness. So I had four :) 
I also had the burger with blue cheese. The patty was overdone, nevertheless very tasty. I chose a garden salad for my side and it came with fries instead. The waiter replaced it immediately. The salad was mostly greens, so charging extra dollar for a salad is silly, but not such a big deal. A friend had Thai chicken wings. They were good, but I have definitely had better in Reno. While the flavor was great, the texture of excessive, not at all crispy skin was meh. Ok on food but great on beer. I will be back for sure, although I prefer Reno location (pizza is great, Sparks does not make pizza).

Hi JOX! I used to be a regular. Maybe 8-9 years ago and still will stop by occasionally. Although, I don't know the bartenders anymore for sure. It is a divey bar. Yes it is, but i like divey bars. The only minus is the loud jukebox. It's manageable if it's a decent music, but sometimes it's a shitty music and there is no escaping. 
Food is good, very cheap. There are some machines on the bar and Jox might be the only bar that will give you some free drinks if you play the machines.
Bartenders are always nice and helpful. 
The smoking is part of the dive bar, so even though I don't smoke, I am at peace with that.
I am glad there is Jox in Reno among all the trendy places. It's nice to just go to a normal place and relax without having to be experiencing "new trendy" things all the time :)

Needless to say I will be visiting occasionally

I like it! I was reading the reviews and was very surprised with all the "expensive" reviews. The regular bacon cheesburger costs 7.59. That's for TWO patties and unlimited toppings (bacon is +0.50$, eveything else is free). I would not call that a bad deal. There are no bun and lettuce wrap options.
While I was disappointed that the on-line ordering did not work, I was happy with the burger. It was juicy, the toppings were fresh. Also the variety of toppings is really nice.
The french fries were very good. Not sure why so much salt, but the cajun seasoning is awesome. Also 1 5guys regular fries = 2 x Regular fries elsewhere. 
I will eat there again :)

Just tried to place the order for catering for 30 people. This is how it went:

ME: May I please place a catering order?
GIRL: Yes
ME: This would be for May 23rd. (4 days from today)
GIRL: Ohhh... Could you call on Sunday night to do that? I just want to make sure it will not get lost. It's big better if you call on Sunday.
ME: Ok, I'll do that.
GIRL: Are you sure? I can do that right now for you.
ME: Ok, let's do that. 
GIRL: They will not look at it till Sunday and it might get misplaced.
ME: Ok, I'll call on Sunday.
GIRL: I can also take the order now and leave it for them.
ME: Aaaaarghhhh! *click*

Going elswhere.

HEALTH HAZARD! I bought 8 items and 6 are past expiration date. I went today on April 17th, 2014. Some items expired this year but the beets expired in August 2013. I will not be going back for sure. Also attaching picture with receipt and a couple of expiration dates.

EDIT ON 9/8/2014 - Yelp removed the picture of receipt with date of purchase and the expiration dates of products I bought - apparently because "the content didn't appear to be broadly representative of the business (e.g., wrong business, close-up of patrons, etc.)"

Great location, I really liked the food, but the service was a joke. We were sitting at the bar and there were 2 sushi chefs trying very hard not to make eye contact with us. You can get away with this in a regular restaurant but when I am seated 2.5 feet accross from the staff, it makes for a VERY awkward 20 min. Luckily we had 2 hrs to spare, because once we started ordering, there were some items forgotten, it was difficult to find someone to pay for the dinner. On the plus side - rolls with snow crab were delicious!

Being a review # 100, I better do a good job. I will start with this place is effing awesome. As I might have mentioned before a ratio of rice to fish is big for me.  This place has got it right. There is a nice balance between the starch and the fish. Having said that,  the rolls themselves are truly wonderful; the flavors are well balanced, good variety, the fish is fresh. I had 7 rolls (don't judge me) and some nigiri. I had the jj#2, the war, the caterpillar, the knight, mango island, lion king, tornado. For nigiri, we had Donald duck. Let me tell you this mango island is a must. It has this wonderful fresh mango sauce that is not overwhelming.  Just the right amount of sweetness and not thick or sticky. Try this, very tasty. Jj#2 also a must. If you like ceviche, you will love this one. All the rolls topped with scallops, are also worth of checking out. I only had one appetizer - fried calamari - don't bother. Couldn't taste the calamari. Don't waste room in your belly. Use it for tasty rolls.
And now for the service - it was excellent. Thus business is almost entirely family operated and it shows. They all care that you are well taken care of. As a matter of fact, the owners are hesitant to consider a new location because they would have to release the control over managing of the place (the owner is one of the sushi chefs so you can talk to him). 
Overall it was a great visit. It is way out of our way, but we'll come back regurarly. 
Also a plus (almost forgot) - they take reservations. 
Loved it!
Thank you

I have been twice to the new location and both times were phenomenal. The quality of the food is unreal. The food is cooked to perfection.  We had duck breast, arctic char, charcuterie plate, apetizer oysters, and some wine and cocktails. Everything left you craving more. The absolute hit was the Grand Marnier soufflé,  which apparently is not on the menu. It was of wonderfully light texture with distinct Grand Marnier flavour. The only three things I would improve were the bread served before the food was ordered (you warmed it up but you're not fooling me; that thing was not fresh). Secondly, the sangria cocktail - diluted wine with very little flavour, you can do better than that, Beaujolais. Lastly, the hostess' nails; those crazy things were atrocious; chipped nail polish and black dirt underneath. I was watching to make sure those things were not touching anything I was about to eat. 
I purposefully left the best for last - the service. Our server was Steve. He was extraordinarily professional. I felt like he knew the exact time to appear, take care of things and go. I had not once needed to flag him, but everything was perfectly taken care of, in a flawless kind of way. 5 stars all the way, even despite the crazy nails.

I am very "on-the-fence" about his place. There were things I loved to the core (the beer, the service) and hated with my whole being (the food). I cannot say enough about the beer - extremely good, the service was not lacking either - prompt, attentive, accommodating. And then there was the food - a whole range of great ideas and terribly executed. I had a halibut, which was fried to a solid brick - AWFUL. Same with pork belly tacos - the pork belly tasted like wood chips, extremely overdone. The artichoke dip had unmelted chunks of cream cheese. The only redeeming feature was the shishito peppers - if you're into spicy appetizers, this one's a must!
I will go back, but only because I really hope these are the growing pains. It is a truly beautiful place and I hope it becomes one of Reno's "go-to's"

Few years later and I absolutely LOVE this place. The food improved greatly, the beer offer is broader and not all out. I think I had almost everything to eat (but oysters) on their menu and never had anything to complain. It is definitely one of my solid places I can go have a lunch or dinner and leave entirely satisfied, with a smile on my face!

I love this place. Disclaimer: I can only speak to the food as I have never eaten inside. I always do take out. It is my go--to Chinese place. So far, everything I had from there was tasty, well prepared, fresh ingredients. Not once have I wondered whether the beef came from an actual cow (you never know with Chinese places). Or whether it's a chicken or only "taste-just-like-chicken". I had general's chicken, orange chicken, spicy garlic beef, side vegetables. Never had a single complaint about the food and will continue to order from there every time I feel like Chinese :)

Solid four stars - I visit this place during lunch or for a happy hour - because the happy hour is awesome at this place. The food is fantastic (not your regular hotdog and taco and wings). They offer a wide variety of creative dishes during Happy Hour, Also the wine list includes more than house wine and the pour is generous. I like salads at TF because they are usually very creatively prepared and decent size too. The burgers are fabulous - perfectly done, juicy, fresh. Appetizers are really fun too: I've had the prosciutto pizza, queso fundido, champagne wild mushroom fondue, empanadas, Mushroom & White Truffle Mac N Cheese, and La Espanola Pizza ( I told you I liked their happy hour).
The service is really good too.
Now on to the reason for 4 stars and not 5 - the take out portions of salads are substantially smaller. When I pay $25 for a take out salad (I like to double my shrimp). I expect to be satisfied after the lunch. But not here, the salad was smaller, and I will not be doing the take out from TF again. 
TLDR: take out - BAD, happy hour - GOOD!

I started writing this last night but i passed out from a 2000kcal meal. So here it goes again: i went to the Depot again and once again the service was impeccable. I do not know what are their criteria for hiring the waitstaff, but I'm 100% sure I wouldn't qualify. The staf assissts you immediatly, regardles whether you sit at their table or not. The food is delivered promptly, the dishes are cleaned almost immediately. My favorite beer is still on tap (the IPA), and hopefully it is a permanent position on the beer menu. The beautiful building is teeming with people. I had a reservation through Open Table. All of us with lengthy names appreciate reservations over the Internet. We were able to get in before the happy hour was over therefore it was a good opportunity to demolish the happy hour menu. The deal is you get 2 dollars off  beers and 2-3 dollars of most appetizers, not a dollar menu, but these are full sized dishes. We had shishito peppers (of course), followed by duck confit sliders, pork belly tacos, meat board, and poutine. And beers. And coma. 
I will just get this out of the way: the tacos were prepared much better, the meat was tender with a little crisp on the outside. I was hoping for this dish to improve from my last visit and it definitely did. Everything else was above my expectations: the sliders are a must. Perfectly cooked duck meat, shredded with some delightfully sweet sauce on a not so little toasted brioche. They come in threes, so I was already pushing it,  but since my pants are still comfy, let's keep going. The meat board - I wouldn't be surprised if it came from the Provisions or cured in-house. Excellent quality. Not from Costco (I'm looking at you, The Grill, and Napa Sonoma). I don't have anything against Costco deli meat, but I eat it every day, so no, I want something different, especially at $20-30 per plate. And now the climax of the dinner - the poutine. If I could I would take a bath in that oxtail gravy. That dish was extremely good. I would not be surprised if this Canadian staple started showing up everywhere in Reno. I sure can't have enough of it.
As a bonus we got a mini tour of the Brewing and distilling area. Little bigger than our garage operation! 
Bonus: the brew master previously worked at Silver Peak and 50/50 in Truckee. And everybody knows that 50/50 is my treat. 
After 2 visits I have two different scores, I will update on the consistency in few months.

The selection of wines is amazing. The staff knows their stuff (this reads funny). If you want to unwind after a long day at work, this is the place. Just sit between shelves full of delicious wine and allow for the day to slow down. This place not only have good selection of bottles, but also by the glass. And has wine flights (3x3oz). The place gets packed in the winter, but when it is warm, they have a little outdoor sitting area that doubles the shop's place. The store has limited selection of appetizers, but you are encouraged to order from neighbouring Yosh's or SqueezeIn and the food will be delivered. This place was a much needed alternative to  Vino100 (not that nice of a place after change of ownership a few years back). Then the Summit wine place closed down, but Whispering Vine came to the rescue of South Reno!

Red Robin, you're such a mess... Disclaimer: My 3.5yo son LOVES the place so we frequent it. Normally it is between 3 and 4 stars, but today it was a joke. Someone thought it was a good idea to add the ordering machines to each table. They are a little tablets on a stand with a built-in  credit card reader and a printer. First of all the stupid thing has games on it. So my 3.5 yo tries to play with it. I do not like my family playing with electronic devices during meals. So RR actually encourages the use of devices at the dinner table. Meals are to socialize and have family time. I try to take it away and I am the bad guy. Thanks RR. Also RR is charging for the games so if your kid wins the race to the tablet, you're SOL. 
Secondly, the waiters are more confused by these things than the guests. 
Lastly, the devices are all mixed up. I am pretty sure we paid for someone else's dinner, but it was close amount, so I didn't want to prolong this painful experience and left. 
One more thing; my baby was sitting in a chair that was literally falling apart. I asked for a different one, the waitress acknowledged it and moved on her merry way. The chair was never replaced. 
My burger "Burning love" was ok. Spicy but oddly lacking in flavor. My husband's burger the seasonal smoky burger on ciabatta was excellent. That's why the second star. 
I think I'll wait a few months before visiting this confused place again.

Only had a take out, but man their food ROCKS! My absolute favorite were the crispy scallops. 8 decent size scallops gently covered in a sweet/smoky sauce. Loved it. It had steamed broccoli with it. Vacuumed up the whole dish. Other dish we ordered were orange chicken, also excellent. I loved the bits of orange peel in the sauce. Very flavorful and fresh tasting. We also had spicy pork. Chicken and pork were breaded, but you could clearly identify the meat inside. Good ratio of batter to meat. Maraschino cherry with sliced cabbage as a garnish was a bit of a surprise, but my 4yo really appreciated it. He chased it down with sweet and sour sauce and loved every bit of it. All this with a copius amount of rice. The only thing we were disappointed with was the lack of fortune cookies in our order. How will i know how to live my life until next Chinese take out? I would write more but I need to lay down.

I used to LOVE this place, but the Stone House Cafe decided they don't give a shit anymore. Two stars because it was a party of 8 and the waitress offered to split the checks - a star saver for me. Also the Stone House is a Pokespot. Don't judge me. Other than that it was a pheory of forgotten items, overcooked fish, and passive aggressive comments. It is fit for elderly community that it is located in, but not the newfound high quality and hip mid town eateries available a mile away. You bricked my halibut - i hate hard, overcooked halibut. Shape up or gtfo. Not likely to be back.

I really really really wanted to love this place. But I don't. Bluntly speaking, for the price this place commands, the service was slow and the cheese board is a joke. It is a wine bar, and in my opinion, the cheese board is the weakest spot. Let that sink in; cheese board sucks at a wine bar. And here is why; while the quality of the cheese is excellent, you get three slices of cheese. Literally ungenerous slices or half-slivers. And the best cheese they offer, which being my favourite cheese, I recognized it immediately (melkbus 149), you get a half a sliver. I get it; It's 28.99/lbs at whole foods, but when I'm charged  $15 per cheese board, I expect it's a cheese board, not a cracker board with a miniscule side of cheese, 6 olives, few slices of average salami, and 5 almonds, and 2 chocolate truffles  (mind you, the truffles were the best part about said cheese board). Just call it a filler board, charge 5 bucks and move on. To add an insult to the injury, i frequent the location in the south and the cheese board is way better. So what gives? 
But moving on to the positives; the other dishes I've tried were duck confit tacos, coconut shrimp, pork belly skewers, and hummus pappadui. My absolute favorite was the shrimp. and my favorite part of this dish was the slaw bed the shrimp sat on. The shrimp itself was perfectly cooked and not drowned in overly sweet sauce, like other
 places would serve it. Perfectly balanced with mustard seeds. The slaw is an amazing combination of flavors. Pretty sure it has mint , lime, and basil as main flavors. It's slightly spicy as well. I would order another one if I wasn't crazy curious about other dishes. Truly a must, but moving on to other highlights.
The pork belly is quite exquisite. The texture, the Korean bbq theme with gochujang... did I mention the texture? The reason this is number 2 is the cold bed of noodles, this deliciousness resides on. Why? It might be more authentic, but felt cold and awkwardly paired. 
The tacos were absolutely awesome. Nothing to complain here. The reason I put l dish as 3rd is my personal preference. I just love fatty pork belly better and the shrimp and slaw flavors were intriguing and compelling. 
Overall, I will definitely be back. I will skip the silly cheese board and double the shrimp!

It's ok. It has some nice produce and occasional good special, BUT... It is very expensive. The same Boar's Head deli meat can be found elsewhere for 2-3/lb dollars less. The deli meat staff does not know the specials, nor do they know where does the discount come off (the counter or the register). They are polite, but VERY slow. I waited 15 mins despite no other customers being present. There were multiple employees doing random things and avoiding eye contact. I might go back if I have a coupon, but otherwise it is just not worth it to me.

OlDJgnu-bzNPVAk7UYvWrA.review_text: I went on a a Saturday afternoon and it was totally empty apart from my friend and I.  The service was great, the food was awesome (I don't eat sushi, so I tried some of the beef and chicken dishes they had - so good), and as the Beatles are my favorite band, I thought the music was perfect.

I love Sugar Mom's, especially on week nights when it's not super crowded.  It's like hanging out in someone's basement.  The jukebox is full of awesome music, the food and drinks are cheap, and the crowd is usually pretty chill.
Best Indian food I've ever had!!  The Butter Chicken is absolutely amazing.  The naan basket is awesome.  The service is always great, the ambiance is classy but not pretentious.  I love this place.

An awesome place for brunch, whether you're a hipster or not. The 25 minute wait on Sunday afternoon was worth it - the specials are seasonal and out of the ordinary, the coffee never stops coming, the staff is friendly and fast, and the food is delicious.  I love that you can get potato latkes with your eggs instead of hash browns.  The multigrain pancakes with peaches and plums was amazing.  I wanted to try everything on the menu.

It's a little pricey, but worth it - I'll definitely be visiting again. I'd like to go around dinner time to try some matzoh ball soup and brisket.  Mmm.

Cosmi's has great Italian sandwiches, delicious cheesesteaks, and some of the nicest staff in the city.  Four stars out of five because I've gotten the completely wrong sandwich on more than one occasion. The menu is a little pricey, but you do get a lot for the money.

If you want seeded bread (and trust me, you want the seeded bread) call earlier than later because they are always running out, especially on big sports nights!

The Pub is, and has always been, my favorite restaurant.  Don't let the cheesy 70's decor and mounted deer heads deter you - this place is magnificent.  The lobby, bar, and staff hasn't changed in about a thousand years, and luckily neither has the food.  The salad bar can't be beat (Caesar salad and zucchini bread - mmm).  The fresh-baked bread on your table is hot and delicious.  The steak/chicken/what have you is cooked to perfection by chefs you can see from your table. The desserts are gargantuan. 

I can see being scared off if you're under retirement age, but power through, friends.  Once you've had The Pub, you wouldn't want it any other way.  (And don't forget to leave with a pocketful of spearmint candies.) A+++

Love the Royal Tavern. Go there all the time. The food (lots of heavier comfort food) is awesome and they usually have great specials. The beer list is always great. The Bloody Marys are good. Sometimes it's really crowded and you have to wait a while for a table, but if you're there early for brunch or most weeknights, it's fine. 

My favorite dishes are the meatloaf sandwich and the truffle butter popcorn (which is only available at dinner time!).
Try the Tempo Shandy cocktail, it's ridiculously tasty.  And only $5 during Happy Hour.  I tried two different kinds of hummus and both were delicious.

I went to Han Dynasty for a friend's birthday, so we sat in the basement, family-style, and tried a ridiculous number of things from the tasting menu.  I don't eat seafood, so I had to skip a few dishes, but what I ate was excellent and SO spicy!!  My friends and I were daring each other to eat whatever was put in front of us, it was hilarious.  I can't stop thinking about the cold sesame noodles. I need to go back asap.

This place is an authentic, old school Italian restaurant.  It always feels like one of the Corleone brothers could walk in at any moment.  The staff treats you like family.  The food is basic, but very good.  For those addicted to their meatballs, you can also pick up refrigerated sauce and meatballs to go. It's a little pricey for simple pasta dishes (it comes with bread, but no salad), but if you're looking for real Italian Market cuisine, it's worth a visit.

A+++ This place is a gem. I've eaten there several times, and I swear every single thing they serve is ridiculously good.  It's not like any Chinese food you've ever had - other Chinese restaurants are to Han Dynasty what Chef Boyardee is to authentic Italian food.  I've taken several friends to try it out, and everyone leaves saying the same thing: "Best. Chinese. Food. Ever."

A lot of the menu is crazy spicy, so if you're into that kind of thing, you've hit the jackpot.  Prepare to sweat, cry, and have your sinuses cleared. For those that can't or won't handle spicy stuff, there is plenty to choose from that is not spicy at all.  

I agree with all the reviewers that the Dan Dan noodles are AMAZING, but try the Cold Sesame noodles too - they will haunt your dreams!

This place has the best tomato pie I've ever had, and I usually don't even care about tomato pie. It makes my mouth water just thinking about it. Something about that sauce is absolutely delicious!

I've tried their other stuff and it was pretty good, but nothing to write home about. It's all about that tomato pie!
Went to Supper for brunch one Sunday. The food was good, not great, and I felt like it was overpriced. Not bad, but I doubt I'll want to go again.

My friends and I have a group we've deemed "The Parc Pact," and the four of us go to Parc for each of our birthdays for brunch. As long as you have a reservation, the brunch at Parc is a wonderful experience, especially if you're sitting on the park side when the doors are open. Everything on the menu is good, if not wonderful. The bread is amazing. The staff is always awesome. 

I recently went to Paris, and in each restaurant we visited, we'd ask ourselves, "Which is more French? This place, or Parc?"

The answer was always Parc. It seems ridiculous, but Parc beats Paris, people.

I was tasked with finding a dinner spot for a group of 20 on a Saturday night in or around Fishtown, which is apparently MUCH harder to accomplish than you'd think. Every restaurant either needed a a huge deposit, a room rental, or couldn't sit us after 6 pm. Luckily El Camino came through! It was as simple as setting up a reservation over email, no deposits, fees, or time constraints, done and done. We chose the Mexican family-style menu, which was $30/person. 

On Saturday night we were seated right away and were almost immediately inundated with course after course of delicious food. We really loved the fried pickles, the steak fajitas, and the mole enchiladas. There were plenty of options for the vegetarians amongst us, and the drinks were all great too. The waitstaff was awesome and even split our bill 20 ways, which we were not expecting at all!

I'd definitely recommend El Camino if you're trying to book a big dinner.

Hooooly crap this food is amazing. My coworker ordered some one day and it smelled so ridiculously good that I almost couldn't handle it. Now when she orders I order too, and you get SO much delicious food for not too much money, and everything is fresh and healthy and amazing. I can't recommend this place enough.

Or1J9ym667HxQrkKJqn7hA.review_text: Sweet Potato Fries and dipping sauces are my favorite.  Great burgers too.  I have never had something there that I didn't like.  Awesome beer.  Love the Raspberry Wheat. Clean.

My husband and I are new to Thai food.  We saw that Sukhothai was open on Eagle Road and decided to give it a try.  We ordered the Chicken Pad Thai, Panang Curry & Chicken Skewers.  For a first experience, I thought that these dishes were amazing.  The food was fresh, and the portions were large.  Since the first time we got take-out, we have ordered from this spot about 5 or 6 times. Definitely in our take-out rotation.

Great Beer selection for the area.  Mix and Match 6-packs are a plus.  Food is decent- great tuna hoagies, ok turkey and italian hoagies.  Have yet to try their cheesesteaks, but I've heard that they are worthy. Would try more stuff on the menu for sure.
I was there this past Saturday- one of the days it was about a 100 degrees- and the place was PACKED!  Lots of takeout orders and dine-ins.

Stumbled upon Barbacoa in Ardmore on Father's Day while trying to find a fab meal for my hubby.  We've been to a Peruvian restaurant in Queens and loved it, so I was super excited to try out the food, in hopes that it would be JUST as good.  It was.

I ordered "The Lancaster" only because I was having a hard time deciding. There are so many mouth-watering things on the menu to choose from.  I waited for over an hour, because the place was packed.  I believe that it was only their 2nd day open, and they apologized profusely, so I wasn't at all bothered. Also knowing that I was about to eat a delicious meal made it worth the wait.

My husband was SO surprised to see that I brought home something different than the typical Chinese, Sushi, Pizza and Hoagies that our area has to offer.  The portions were large, the meat was cooked to perfection.  The french fries were absolutely delicious (did not taste greasy at all).  For sides we got the mac and cheese (my 2 year old adored it) and the coleslaw (creamy and had just the right about of crunch.)  Corn bread was also included, and I can honestly say that it was the best I've ever had.  We had leftovers galore.

I definitely will go back and tell all of my local friends.  Take-out is easy when a little one is involved, but if we have a sitter, the place is adorable and really perfect for a BYOB date night.  Looking forward to trying out some other things from the menu.

I stopped at The Bagel Factory this AM after fasting for some blood work over at Bryn Mawr Hospital.  I was starving!  The lady at the cash register was SO nice and polite-  very genuine.  I assume that it is hard to find employees like her in this day and age! A lot of people in  food service are so miserable.

I ordered the Hame/Egg/Chz on everything bagel and it hit the spot.  I feel that their bagels are on the small side, but that is good for people who try to watch their carb-intake a little.  They also had a nice variety of cream cheeses and muffins, which I will probably hit up the next time I stop in for breakfast.  

Definitely recommend to fellow Yelpers in the Bryn Mawr area.

The smell of this place alone would make me come back!  Heaven!  I have brought my 2-year old son here a hand full of times this summer, and each time is a great experience.  The girls who work behind the counter are so sweet.  
I took my son last night and this is how it went down:

He wanted a chocolate sundae (surprise surprise), and the girl who waited on us made it just right for him.  I ordered soft serve  because it's easier for him to eat.  I took a few bites of the fudgey goodness and was impressed.  Son was not impressed that I was eating his dessert.  So good. 
I was torn between the fudge brownie and caramel apple ice cream for my treat.  I ended up getting a sample of the caramel apple and was sold.  It's vanilla with swirls of (you guessed it!) caramel and apples.  I thought I tasted a hint of brown sugar in there but I am not positive.   On a cake cone, it was perfect.  Eating it made me think of fall :-)

The cookies (choc chip, macadamia nut and cin. raisin) looked just baked and delicious, but I had some self-control and said "next time".  It's places like Koffmeyer's in Havertown that make me happy to be a resident.  We get bogged down with so many "commercial" eateries that it's nice to have a "mom and pop" place to go for superior service and quality food!

My co-workers and I have not had any luck in KOP finding a consistent place to order salads.  We are very impressed with Pasta Via and the quality of their salad options.  
All ingredients are fresh, chicken tastes like it has just been grilled on an actual GRILL, and the dressings come in nice portions and taste really good.

Delivery is a plus.

So far we have had the Monterey Chicken Salad, Zola Pear Salad, Cajun Chicken Salad, and Pesto Chicken Salad- and we have ordered them multiple times each.

Pasta Via is the perfect option for us- not too expensive (check out their daily specials), always fresh, nice portions, friendly staff.
Will continue ordering from here 1-2 times a week.

Quick Review-

AWESOME slices of pepperoni and plain.   Cheese is perfect, crust is thin.  I will go back again for sure.  I also heard the cheese steaks and cheese steak pizzas are excellent.

The only bakery I will use for cakes for special occasions.  Every cake I have ordered from the Bakery House has been raved about by guests at my parties and get-togethers.  The chocolate cake with vanilla butter cream is making my mouth water just THINKING about it!  I also recommend this bakery to all of my Main Line friends.

PS- The last time I was there I ordered a lemon bar because it just looked TOO good to pass up; it was heaven!  I love this place.

Eww. My husband ordered a Tuna Hoagie from what we supposed would be a great, new place to order from in Havertown.  He ate half of the hoagie, which he thought tasted above average.  This is major because he is very critical of everything that goes into a sandwich. The tuna tasted fresh, the roll was perfect, as were the add-on LTO and provolone.  It wasn't until later that he discovered chewed GUM on the other half of the hoagie, located on the outside of the roll.  A voicemail was left for them to let them know, and he has yet to receive a call back.  

Even though this could have been a mistake, or a random mix-up of some kind, we are very turned off that we did not receive an apology or explanation.  P&S will remain our #1 choice for hoagies in Havertown.

YES!  Definitely have been excited for this place to open up.  Clean and cute on the inside. Very spacious.  
Ordered the pita and hummus for my son, but I ended up having some too.  Looked too good to resist, and I was right.  The hummus was chilled and the flavor was out of this world.  One of the better kinds of hummus we've tried.  The pitas were soft and warm, and tasted well, like a pita.
Feta is really not my fave, so I ordered the chicken salad sandwich.  Bread was whole grain and fresh.  Chicken salad was made with white meat and the mayo wasn't very heavy. I would order it again.
Going back for the hummus for sure, and will try out some other things on the menu.  Great addition to the area.

My girlfriends and I spent a few hours here last night.  For 8 of us, the bill was only $95.  Being a BYOB helped :-)
The staff was nice and welcoming and put up with our loudness.  We ordered guacamole for the table that was fresh and SO YUM!  The salsa had a bit of a kick to it and the chips tasted homemade.
I ordered the Chicken Enchiladas with red (mole) sauce.  I wasn't the biggest fan.  There was entirely too much sauce and it was a bit spicy for my taste.  One of the girls ordered the chicken flautas which looked amazing (she said that they tasted delicious) and the other girls ordered tacos, fajitas, & burritos and were all huge fans.
I would go back, but I prefer Mexican restaurants where I can order a big fat margarita to go along with my spicy meal.

YES!  Another place in Havertown to get a delicious hoagie.  The Italian was as good as it gets.  We also tried a chicken parm hoagie which was awesome.  This is huge, bc we are VERY picky about chicken cutlets, because my mother-in-law makes the BEST.  
The highlight was the John's 9th Street Special.  OMG.  Imported capicolla, Genoa salami, extra sharp provolone, roasted peppers, imported soppresatta, prosciutto.  Can you say heaven?  And BTW, I didn't eat 3 hoagies....we cut them up and shared.

Their website looks modern and I love the layout:
http://centrellasdeli.com/

There are a lot of other sandwiches I want to try, which we will definitely be doing during football season.  Way to go, Centrella's!

I did not feel "guilty" or "fat" eating this pizza, so naturally it is my new favorite spot!  We got a half mushroom/half plain & it was as good as it looked. Thing crust, rectangle shape, cool looking box.  Called ahead and no wait when I got there.  The place was crowded and kid-friendly.  Next time we will be more adventurous and try something different.

Nice change from the normal area pizza joints.

My brother's wedding was held here and everything was PERFECT.  The owner, Jeff, was everywhere- even mixing drinks- making sure every guest was taken care of. Definitely recommended for a wedding venue.

Also a charming spot for date night.  Food is wonderful, wine flows and service is the best...love this place.

Things from Wegmans that I have tried and LOVE:

1. Buffalo Chicken Pizza- if you haven't tried it, I suggest you do so ASAP.
2.  Their sushi.  It's not the best, but it is damn good! I like the spicy shrimp roll.
3. The mac and cheese.  If my son likes it, it must be tasty.
4. Pulled Pork.  Serve on a roll with some provolone and you've got yourself a meal.
5. Coffee-  they make a nice cup, esp the flavored coffee
6. Breakfast Sammy on English Muffin- a lot less greasy than Wawa
7. Fresh Squeezed Tangerine Juice- so sweet and so refreshing

Those were foods that came to mind right away.  I am sure I have tried numerous other meals there and just can't remember...it's early :-)

Don't forget the AWESOME BEER SELECTION!  I am headed there this weekend to pick up some fun pumpkin brews.

2 words:

Guacamole and Margaritas.

Any kind, any combination.   Delicious and a perfect spot for a night out with your girlfriends.

Everything here is phenomenal.  I have yet to order something here that I did not like.
This is my #1 lunch choice for when I am near the KOP area.  I normally order the Cobb Salad (lunch portion) and I love it.  The sliders are amazing, and so are the fries.  Huge turkey club, awesome fried zucchini and fresh hummus.
The mango iced tea and raspberry lemonade are always my drink choices.  Portions are HUGE and the bread that they serve pre-meal is delish.

Of course every slice of cheesecake is heaven.  LOVE THIS PLACE.

When a new restaurant comes to H-Town,  we get very excited.  It's definitely not easy to line-up babysitters to go out to eat in the city, so anything convenient works for us.  My parents happened to have the kids a few weeks ago so we decided that we would finally hit up Brick & Brew.  I have driven by every day since it opened, so obviously I was anxious to see what they had to offer.
We got the prosciutto fries for an app.  They were perfectly cooked fries and the cheese was amazing-- but where was the prosciutto?  I don't even think there was one piece in our serving.  The homemade ketchup sort of made up for it though.  Applause for that yummy condiment.

The pizza was just OK.  If I remember correctly we ordered the 5 cheese.  It needed salt, which was odd.  It was lacking in some flavor but it was filling after a few beers.  If we were to go back for dinner, I am not sure that I would try this pizza again.

The beer list is impressive.  We would definitely come back to see what is on tap and maybe try another app and sandwich/pizza.

Cute date spot, cozy and really cool atmosphere.
Amazing beer.  Definitely hidden and not what you would think a "brewery" would be, but super chill.  I have high hopes for this place.

Highlights:
Pizza=YES!
Potato Salad= The best in the area.  And believe me, I am picky when it comes to PS.
Dill Salad= Simple and delicious.
Carlino's Lasagna= Rose sauce, chicken, blue cheese.....OMG! So good but probably SO not healthy!
Tuna Salad, Egg Salad and Chx Salad= All fresh and good quality

This is a normal weekend stop for us to pick up a few things. Staff super nice and helpful.

Went for lunch with my girlfriend and our infant daughters.  We each had a glass of white wine which was refreshing.  Our server was helpful and knowledgeable of the menu.

We started off with a flat bread- it had chicken, pesto, arugula and cheese....Delicious.  Was not too filling and had the perfect taste.
