My friend ordered the fish tacos- she loved.  I went with the bbq chx salad which did not disappoint.   It was perfect.  

I heard the piano bar is fun, so I would really like to go back and see that for Happy Hour one day with friends or the hubby.

We took the kids here for lunch on a Sunday and were seated right away.  The menu changed a bit from the last time we visited, it seemed much smaller.
We decided to get the hummus plate to start, which we all enjoyed- even our 11 month old could not get enough.  It was served with pita and some veggies.

The hubs and I both got French Onion Soup and Salads- nothing too exciting.  The FO soup was picture perfect!  Awesome presentation and taste.  Salad was ok- loved the ranch dressing- has a bit of a kick to it.

4 yo got the Burger.  I had a bite and it kinda made me wish I ordered one to begin with.  

This place has a top-notch beer menu- draught and bottles.  I noticed in the bar area some of the tables even have their own tap!!!....a draught beer you can pour yourself at your own table!!!  Sounds good to me!  

Back in our Happy Hour Glory days we would frequent this place quite often, as it is a fun atmosphere...especially in the summer with the outdoor bar area.  
Family friendly for sure!

Came in for a Mojito on mother's day...Out of this world Good!!
The only suggestion I have is to get a few high chairs :-)

Fun spot in town- love the selection of beer.  Had a delicious pulled pork quesadilla and truffle fries...which tasted like regular fries to me! I like the "dive-yness" factor and all of the dollar bills taped to the bar. Cool outdoor area. Was very quiet when the hubs and I stopped in for a quick beer and snack.

Lots and lots of hoagie/sandwich options.  Something for everyone.  All of the lunch meat is high quality and the rolls are excellent.  I ordered an Italian Hoagie and it definitely is one of the better ones in the area.  A co-worker ordered the hot roast beef sandwich, which she loves.  The only downfall: no option for wraps or salads.  I understand that this is a hoagie shop, but it would be nice to have some healthier options for those that don't want all of the carbs.  If you are looking for a legit Italian hoagie, try this place out.

I have always wanted to try Barre classes, so when I heard about Barre3 Rosemont opening, I jumped right in.  The first week of their Grand Opening, free classes were held.  I took advantage of their "Founding Member" special- $110/month for life (cancel at any time).  The instructors are awesome and the place is super clean and cute.
If you are sick of going to the gym and your every day routine, I  recommend trying one of these classes. Arms, legs, butt, core, etc....every muscle is worked.
Amazing.

Went with my cousin who recently turned 21.  We were able to get a seat at the bar (Saturday around 7ish) and did a wine tasting- 5 wines for $5.  The selection is awesome- something for everyone.  Glasses of Sangria are available for $5 and they also offer tapas. Olive oils and balsamic vinegars for tasting and purchasing as well.  I plan to go back in the winter- should be festive and I want that Alpine Spice wine :-)

Ordered wings for an Eagles game because I read that they were delish.  My sources did not disappoint.  These wings were meaty and flavorful and cooked perfectly!!
We got the Mild and Barbecue.   My palate cannot handle anything too spicy, so these  hit the spot.  They came with blue cheese, celery and carrots. Bonus points for the carrots.  Loved!  
Cute little pub atmosphere-- would definitely go back and dine-in with a pint of Guinness!

Popped in for lunch on Sunday with the fam- my hubby, me, our 5 yo and 2 yo.  We were IMPRESSED!!  We never know how our little one is going to act- she was actually an angel (which is rare) so we got to enjoy everything.
The bread and olive oil was brought to our table very quickly- and it was really one of the best tasting I've had.  I try to watch my carb intake but this bread made me cheat.

I ordered the pineapple painkiller drink- delicious and STRONG!

The movie clips playing on the wall was pretty cool, too. The kids enjoyed it,

My salad was fresh and the dressing was perfect.  A bad dressing could very well  ruin my whole dining experience.  The kids meals (burgers) were good, according to the kids. True because they ate most of it. The staff was very friendly and accommodating to us. 
The bar area looked awesome and the hostess mentioned that they are opening an upstairs deck bar area in the summer which would be fun for a night out, sans kids.

Had a wonderful experience here celebrating my Aunt's 50th Birthday.  We reserved tables upstairs for about 20ish people on a Friday night.  It was very chill and sort of private, esp because we got there on the early side of dinner.

The staff was friendly and helpful, always filling drinks and making sure everyone was taken care of.  There is a bar upstairs which is convenient.  

I had the crab cake sandwich was was delicious.  I also want to mention the pickles- spicy pickles- were AWESOME!!  So good.  Our party mostly ordered sandwiches, fries, etc and everyone was impressed.  I am excited for the summer to sit and hang in their outdoor area.

The coffee and smoothies are excellent.
All of the fruits and veggies are fresh, and a lot of the prepared foods are great for busy families.  I also love the section in the back with essential oils and vitamins/meds.

I am an iced coffee aficionado and LOVE that they have decaf cold brew.  The taste is amazing and I crave it often.  
The otter bread is to die for and their other pastries and baked goods are fresh and look so YUM.  Lucky to have a spot like this in Phoenixville.

Had the BEST chicken cheese steak stromboli (sauce on side) from there on Friday night.  Was packed with meat, cheese, and mushrooms/peppers and not greasy at all.  I also am a fan of their fries.  Have also had excellent cheesesteaks from Palermo's.
The blueberry mojito yogurt is AMAZING!!  So light and refreshing.  Def good for the summer. The facility is very clean and the staff is nice/helpful.

Such a cool new spot in Phoenixville.  The size of the place is really impressive and it has a very chill vibe.  Plenty of tables, long bar, and a cement indoor "beer garden" in the back that is kid friendly.  The beers are on point and there is even a food window to order some snacks.  We did not eat (just drank) but will definitely come back to try out the food.  The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable.  Have already recommended to friends and will continue to do so.

The smell of this place is amazing, and the coffee is even better.  I love the cold brew.  The baked goods are out of this world delicious.  It is hard to walk out of there without getting a sweet treat.  

Employees are very nice and helpful.  It can get a bit crowded at times but it's worth it.
We love Uncle B's- one of the only places in the area where we will get wings.  The new spot in town is spacious and kid-friendly.  In the summer, the outdoor biergarten is a plus.

OsGiWMCb3Q2OPva3-fTDGQ.review_text: I had the chicken curry and it was delicious. The chicken was cooked perfectly and the curry was full of flavor and went very well with the basmati rice. I will definitely be back!

This is THE place to get fried green tomatoes. They are amazing! My friend had the kale salad and said it was very good. I had the panini which was also good but everything on the menu looked great! The service was also very good. The server knew the menu well and was very attentive. We will be back!

Went here for a friends birthday celebration. They were very under staffed. Our server told us she was the only one working inside and had multiple tables to take care of which caused our drinks and food to take a very long time to arrive. They had a $5 burger special and the burger was decent. Not the best and not the worst. Management needs to pay closer attention to staffing needs. Other than that, it was a cute lively place and we had a good time.

I really like this location. The staff is very friendly and the sandwiches are consistently good. The Philly cheese is a personal favorite and in my opinion is one of the best Philly sandwiches in town.

Fun place! I love the fact that more places like this are opening in my neighborhood. The food was pretty good but the service could have been a little better. The server we had was not very knowledgeable about the menu or the beer selection. But I will definitely not let this stop me from returning.

I wish I could say this was an enjoyable experience but I got violently ill after eating here. My friend also got sick and we had two different items so I'm not sure what the food poisoning culprit was. Needless to say I will not be back.

I really enjoy the ambiance of this restaurant. The views of the water are amazing. However, the quality of the food is not great. I've been disappointed the last few times with the taste of the food. The fish is under seasoned and over cooked. If you just want drinks with a great view then I definitely recommend hula bay. I suggest finding another alternative for food.

I was really excited that a brewery opened in my area. They have a decent selection of brews to fit most tastes. However the atmosphere and service can use some improvement. We went on a Saturday night and it was practically empty when it should have been busy. There was no ambiance since the lights were turned up so high we felt like we were drinking in a spotlight. We sat at the bar and waited almost 10 minutes for someone to help us, even though there was a bartender standing right in front of us when we sat down. Both bartenders weren't the friendliest and we felt like they would rather be somewhere else. Overall not my first choice for a fun place.

I tried the club sandwich and it was pretty tasty. The menu looks really good and I will definitely go back to try more items. My only disappointment is that they don't make the fries in house. Especially since I love fish and chips. In any case, the food and service are great. I hope this place lasts!

This place has exceptional service from the minute you walk through the door to the moment you leave. I was so impressed I made a point to tell the manager how friendly and on point the staff was. I had the biscuits and gravy with house made gravy and sausage and it was delicious. I know it's a breakfast joint and closes early but I wish it was open later. Sometimes I like breakfast for dinner!

I love this place. I've been several times and each time received great food and great service. They also have a very good happy hour. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because of the parking situation. The plaza is shared with other businesses which makes finding a spot challenging. And you are forced to use valet parking if you're not lucky enough to find 1 of 10 spots to park in. If it weren't for that issue it would have been 5 stars.

I've only had the falafel here so far but it is amazing. I would even go so far as to say this is my favorite falafel in town. The service is always friendly and the prices are very reasonable. Next on my list to try is the baked hummus. I will definitely continue to order food from here.

This is my new go-to burger place. The food is great and fresh and the customer service is spot on. I love the truffle burger, the smashed chicken, and the turkey burger. The tots and fries are really crisp and delicious too. Great concept for foodies on the go! They have applied for a beer license and once they receive that they will also be serving craft beer from local breweries. Can't wait for that!

We really enjoyed this cute place on the water. It wasn't overly busy for a Sunday afternoon which was nice. We got the crab Benedict to split and it was really yummy. Then we also split the shrimp and oyster combo basket and everything was super! The seafood was fresh and cooked perfectly as were the fries (which were made in house). The server was a little flaky and forgot part of our order a couple times but she was very friendly so we weren't too bothered. We will definitely return.

While I like wings and boneless wings I was less than impressed with them here. I was excited about a sports bar opening close to me and being able to enjoy watching some games and eating some good bar food. But again, I was disappointed with the service and the food quality. I won't be making a habit of visiting here very often. There are many other places to go for some great food.

I went for the first time and was not impressed. I walked in as the only customer and saw a child sitting at the counter playing games. A woman was in the kitchen eating and completely ignored me until I said hello. She apologized for not seeing me but needless to say the negative impression was made. I ordered the bowl and an iced tea. The bowl was pretty good, although a bit over seasoned (there are better ones around) but the iced tea was horrendous. It tasted like bottled nestea with 2 lemons squeezed in. I ended up throwing the entire drink out because I could not drink it. After this experience, I'm not in a hurry to go back anytime soon.

Tried for first time and got the 5 item dinner. Everything was delicious! The owners were very welcoming and friendly. I got hummus, falafel, the couscous salad and white bean salad and all were very good. I will definitely be back to try more of the food as it all looked yummy. I'm not a vegan but I honestly did not miss the meat at all.

Checked out this place on a whim and the food was pretty good. We got the trio and really enjoyed the shrimp and grits (even though I wish we would have gotten more shrimp). The service was incredibly slow but the staff is very friendly. If you are in a hurry or pressed for time you might want to go elsewhere. But if you're not in a hurry and have a couple of hours to enjoy a meal than check it out!

Tried this place for the first time and overall was underwhelmed. First off, the place is very small and cramped. There is a $7 charge to park in their lot which seems a bit much. The wine selection is decent but not extensive. We ordered several items and all were just ok but nothing great. The shrimp were quite spicy and had a strange taste that I've never experienced before. The Caesar salad was over powered by lemon and unbalanced. Everyone at the table said the mushrooms tasted sour and the buffalo cauliflower left something to be desired. Based on this experience I'm not in a hurry to go back.

Second time here and YUM! I got the red beans and rice and it was delicious. The boyfriend got the seafood platter and it was delicious too! It's a soul food kind of place so don't expect something nice. There are
Signs everywhere that say no tipping allowed but then the workers tell you "the signs are old we can accept tips" so it's kind of weird, but the food is worth it! Delicious bloody Mary's too!
Had breakfast here on a Saturday morning with no wait! Food was good! Service was decent.
FIVE STARS! Yum! This place is absolutely delicious. We didn't look at the menu and asked the waiter what his top three favorite rolls were and got those. Absolutely delicious.

Giving four stars for the location and the awesome valet guy, Roy. We had to ask for towels both days we were there because housekeeping forgot to give us towels when they cleaned our room. We LOVED Roy. He was so awesome and SOOO helpful. Went far above and beyond a valet guy. He was absolutely awesome. The room service breakfast was really good too.

Location was very convenient since we were staying at the Prince Conti hotel. Our waiter Sam was awesome. Very attentive and friendly. We all ordered different things to try. I got the croissant breakfast sandwich and it was so good!!! It's very small so maybe not ideal for large groups, but perfect for our group of 4!

Found this place online and had good reviews so we tried it out. We got there around 7:15 and there was no wait. Very small inside but really cute! Got the croissant sandwich - pretty good! When we left around 8:00 it started getting busier.
Justin is awesome! I had a tour with him two years ago and got him again today for the Cemetery Tour. So informative and answered any questions we had!

We ordered from UberEats this morning for breakfast and it was delicious! We got the croissant sandwich with a sausage patty and French toast. The croissant was amazing! Melted in your mouth amazing! The French toast was a little too done but it was still delicious! So good!

Went her for dinner after we got married and it was a great experience all around. We made reservations for 6:30 and got there a little before and only had to wait a few minutes while they got our table ready. They put a white table cloth down for us and sat us in the courtyard to celebrate our wedding. The shrimp and grits was amazing! Definitely have to get the shrimp and grits if you go here! Our waitress was very sweet along with all the staff! The ambiance and vibe of the place is just really neat! Can't wait to go back!

We love The Ruby Slipper. We go at least once everyone we are in town! The chicken st Charles is honestly a little piece of heaven on earth. There is usually a wait so I would recommend going a little early! Their bloody Mary's are delicious too!

Such a great place with a fun atmosphere. The monkey bread bites were AMAZING! They come out warm and so delicious- you get 8 in an order. The artichoke dip was pretty good- I will probably try something else next time. Definitely a cool place. 

Only complaint was they told us 45 minute wait for 2 when there were multiple tables open. We ended up sitting at the bar instead!
Loved the appetizers we got! We got a tour of the restaurant and WOW- so much history! It's absolutely beautiful! Will definitely be back!

Holy moly - the pecan pralines  are amazing!!!!!! The lady that helped us was super sweet and let us sample different flavors. I am excited to go back tomorrow to get my mom some since she's on Texas!

Good service but the food was morning amazing. My burger was over cooked and the nachos were all crushed up and a mess. Hard to eat nachos with broken chips that are tiny pieces. The Cesar salad was good so that's a plus.

We met some friends here for brunch- had reservations at 9:15 for 8. Part of our party was there at 9:15 but they cancelled our reservation...? Not sure why. We eventually were able to get
A table for all 8 of us. We asked our waitress to snap a pic of us and she said no she was busy which is understandable but honestly it didn't seem that busy. I got the steak and eggs and it was pretty good. The grits weren't that good but I liked the steak.

The worst "fine" dining experience I've ever had (I've had worse experiences at roadside stalls in China, but I'm trying to be fair and compare apples to apples).  

I had an out-of-town visitor and wanted to take her to a traditional New Orleans restaurant.  I am a vegetarian, so I knew that my options would be limited at Commander's Palace; therefore, I called ahead and asked if they had vegetarian options at brunch.  The host was very polite and helpful and said they could accommodate any meal preferences and could make something off-menu if nothing on the menu was satisfactory.  

When we arrived at the restaurant and were seated, I told our waiter that I was a vegetarian and asked if special ordering would be a problem.  Like the host, he was said that it would be no problem and the kitchen could make any of the dishes vegetarian.  The brunch menu is a modified 3-course menu, requiring that you order a starter, main and dessert.  My friend ordered a salad with dressing on the side, a seafood entree and a dessert.  I ordered a salad with the dressing the side, a vegetarian omelet with tomatoes, fennel and watercress (these were the 3 ingredients listed with an on-menu seafood entree, so I chose them thinking it would make it easier for the kitchen instead of me just requesting random vegetables they might not have), and a dessert.

When the salads arrived, mine was as ordered, but my friend's was drenched in salad dressing, which she had asked for on the side.  The waiter apologized and said he would bring out another.  It took almost 10 minutes to bring out the corrected salad, and I was forced to awkwardly eat my first course while she waited.  Normally, this would be slightly annoying, but not something I would complain about.  But it was just the warm-up to the restaurant's big screw-up.

When our entrees arrived, my friend's was as ordered.  I looked at my omelet and noticed that there was nothing that looked like tomatoes or watercress in it.  However, I thought perhaps those vegetables were just hiding inside the omelette and the brownish pieces of something I saw might be well-cooked fennel or mushrooms that the chef had decided to add.  I took a bite and immediately knew something was very wrong.  It has been years since I've eaten meat/seafood/poultry, but I knew that what I had just tasted was not a vegetable.  I asked my friend to try it and she said, "That's crabmeat."  At which point, I almost had a minor heart attack, since I am allergic to shellfish.

We called the waiter over and told him that he had not only failed to bring me the vegetarian omelette that I had ordered, but that he had brought me something that I am allergic to.  He perfunctorily apologized but didn't seem to grasp that he had just really screwed up.  A few minutes later, the "captain" came to the table and apologized, again, in a fairly perfunctory manner.  About 15 minutes later - after my friend had finished her meal - the vegetarian omelette that I had ordered was finally brought out.  At this point, I wasn't hungry and was more concerned about the hives that I would soon be breaking out in.  

The waiter apologized one last time when he dropped off his check.  Opening the check, we expected that my entree (or some portion of the meal) would have been comped, since not only had both my friend's salad and my entree been wrong, but they had almost sent me to the hospital.  But no, a check for $102 awaited us.  We were both so shocked that this "fine" dining establishment that is supposedly all about Southern hospitality would do this that we just put our credit cards down and walked out in stunned silence.  

I fully understand that a restaurant like Commander's Palace is not designed for vegetarians, but both the host and the waiter went out of their way to emphasize how happy they would be to accommodate my vegetarian request.  So when they then not only served me meat, but served meat that I am highly allergic to, and then acted like it was no big deal and expected us to pay over $100 for a horrendous dining experience, I have no qualms giving them a 1 star rating (if I could give 0, I would).  Regardless of whether you are a vegetarian or not, if you have any special dietary requests, do not expect this restaurant to honor them.  They may tell you that they are happy to accommodate you, but do not believe them.  You will be paying a lot for whatever they feel like serving you, not what you actually ordered.

This is a great restaurant to go to if you are tired of Southern cooking (or if you don't really like it in the first place).  It would be a dime a dozen in NY or LA, but here it is a rare and welcome find.  Plus, it is a reasonably-priced upscale option.  

Domenica is ostensibly Italian, but feels more like a Mediterranean small plates restaurant.  Our table ordered several appetizers to share, such as burrata and heirloom tomatoes; watermelon/mint/feta salad, and squash blossoms stuffed with goat cheese.  For our entrees, two of us also shared a pizza and the other two shared a seafood dish.  There are several artisinal pizzas on the menu - it's not quite a Pizzeria Mozza, but it is good thin crust pizza with creative toppings.  

Everything was well-prepared and as ordered and tasted farmers' market fresh.  The service was also very attentive, and all of the cocktails ordered, as well as the very reasonable bottle of Italian wine, were great.

Oak St. Cafe (and the staff and clientele) looks like it was taken from the set of Gilmore Girls - small town diner with small town characters who are friendly and interesting.  It serves typical diner food which is hard to mess up - my eggs and potatoes were good, hot and greasy, and the coffee was strong but not bitter.  

Like other reviewers have said, what makes this place stand out is the live music.  There was a piano soloist and bluegrass-ish band the morning I was there.  They are just playing in one corner, like it's the most normal thing in the world to have live music at 9 am in a diner!  And somehow it does feel normal, in a very special way - you can still have a conversation at a normal volume or you can do work (I sat there for 2 hours reviewing documents for work, and they have wireless internet as well if you bring a laptop).  

As a bonus, they actually take credit cards, which a lot of quirky, cute places in this city don't.
The plain glazed and chocolate glazed donuts are amazing.  A little denser than Dunkin Donuts (which I unashamedly love), but still pretty great.  And the guys behind the counter are really friendly.

Oak probably averages out to 2 1/2 stars: 

1 star for the horrible acoustics - you have to shout to be heard by the person right next to you, and if someone is more than 1 seat away from you, you're definitely out of luck.  I'm fine with a bar being loud if I'm in the FQ, but at an uptown wine bar?!   And I don't think the 2-3 piece band playing the corner is the main problem - it was actually the noise of other people's voices bouncing off the walls and ceiling that made it intolerable.

2 stars for the weird layout - this is a huge space, and the bar is big, but there is a major lack of seating - nothing other than a few banquettes tucked along the walls and barstools around the bar.  More tables would definitely be an improvement.

3 stars for the wine - it's annoying that there are not a lot of wines by the glass (odd for a wine bar), but the wines we had were good and the bartenders' descriptions of the wines were accurate and helpful.

4 stars for being a needed addition to the Oak Street neighborhood.  Both times I've been here, it has been packed - there's no other upscale wine bar in the neighborhood, so it's a nice addition.  It'd be much nicer if they dealt with the acoustics and layout.

The food is as good as the cocktails which are as good as the music.  And it's non-smoking!!!

Our table ordered several cocktails and wine, all of which were delicious (especially the Muse and Pimm's Cup).  The food is an eclectic selection of small plates, everything from mac and cheese w/meatballs and crab rolls to vegetarian options like butternut ravioli and falafel sliders and feta fries.  Every single dish we ordered was delicious - like, nothing-left-on-the-plate delicious.  Perfect for sharing and inexpensive.  The homemade ice cream we ordered for dessert was a little disappointing, not as rich and creamy as I imagined homemade ice cream would be, but we had pretty high standards at that point because everything else was so amazing. 

It's not a very big space, and it can get crowded, but it's pleasant enough to wait in the bar area and listen to awesome music until a table opens.

Lovely space, good cocktails and wine selection and good, if small, food menu.  I agree with the reviewer who calls the decor "Mad Men on the cheap" - if you look too closely, the furniture seems a bit worn, but luckily the lights are dim and the actual room itself is well-designed.  And Bouligny Tavern has none of the noise level problems of another uptown wine bar.

Each time I've been there, the crowd has been on the mature side (30s and up) -  a mix of couples on dates, small parties and groups of women.  Menu is pretty limited, no entrees, just small plates, but everything I've tried has been good - the various crostini in particular.  Drinks are in the $10 range; the cocktails I've had were worth it - tasty and they didn't scrimp on the liquor.

A good sandwich starts with good bread, and bread at Milk Bar is amazing.  Fresh, warm, flaky and chewy ciabatta rolls.  The sandwiches on the menu have creative blends of meats, veggies and spreads (they also have salads, but bread is so good, it's hard not to order a sandwich).  And unlike most po-boy shops, Milk Bar has more than one vegetarian sandwich option (filled with fresh veggies and cheeses/spreads, not french fries and gravy - which is okay for special occasions, but hard to justify for weekly lunches).  I was there during the lunch rush at noon and there were several people ahead of me in line, but the guy behind the counter keeps the order line moving fast, and they have 2 or 3 people making sandwiches in the little kitchen.  Probably only took 7 or 8 minutes total to order and get food.  My only wish is that they were open on weekends!

I really want to like Maple St. Patisserie, but after a half-dozen visits, I've just got to face the fact that their bread will never be like bread in France.  I've tried several different loaves - the baguette, the ciabatta, the multi-grain - and while they were all fine, they weren't any better than what you could get at the grocery store's bakery department.  The french bread in particular lacks the crusty exterior/chewy interior that is the hallmark of good french bread.  On bread alone, Maple St. Patisserie would probably get 2 stars, but the staff is friendly and the one petit four I sampled (mini-chocolate coconut cheesecake, maybe?) was very good.

Underwhelming.  The space is nice, pleasant outdoor patio with cool breezes, but the food was not that great and the service was less than attentive.

Our table ordered french fries to share as an appetizer, and they came out cold and limp.  Like McDonald's fries that had been sitting out for several hours.  The bread that was brought out had also seen better days - I'm not sure if it was supposed to have been oven-baked and warm (it wasn't), but I'm pretty sure it wasn't supposed to be hard and stale (it was).  

Our entrees - goat cheese salad, french onion soup and omelette - were all okay, but nothing special.  I've had far better versions of the goat cheese salad and omelette at Coquette.  

Service wasn't rude or anything, but our waiter took a long time to greet us and never checked on us during the meal - we had to flag down busboys for more water and iced tea.  

If you're looking for french bistro fare, Coquette is a better option.

Definitely my favorite "southern" restaurant. It's comparable to Dick & Jenny's or Dante's Kitchen or Jacques-Imo's (but I like it better than any of them) - refined southern cooking in a disarmingly casual atmosphere.  The menu is southern-based, but definitely has other influences (including French and Middle Eastern).  

One of the reasons that M & N stands out from other similar spots is because it has WAY more vegetarian options - and really interesting and good vegetarian options (i.e., not just the boring steamed vegetable plate that Dick & Jenny's offers, or the side of grits and beans (definitely w/bacon in them) that was the best Jacques-Imo's could do).  And in case you're worried it is too vegetarian-friendly, no fear - the two meat-eaters with me raved about their crawfish and shrimp entrees.  

The service is also really friendly (if not particularly speedy) - our server answered lots of questions from my out of town guests, and they did not pressure us at all to leave their lovely patio, even though we were the last ones there at the end of the night.

Of the 3 uptown Middle Eastern restaurants I've tried (Babylon, Mona's and Lebanon's), I like Babylon the best.  Falafel is definitely better than the other two spots, and hummus is equally as good.  I usually get their pita for my sandwiches, but their homemade bread is pretty good too.  The wraps are good and cheap, although I usually get a plate b/c it comes with side salad and extra hummus.  Always easy to get a table at lunch or dinner, and they also will have take-out ready for you if you call ahead.

I *really* wanted to like this place and had such high hopes - whenever I tell anyone I'm a vegetarian in New Orleans, they have recommended Green Goddess.  Maybe my expectations were too high as a result, but when I finally got around to going, it was a very disappointing experience.  Food and ambiance were definitely lacking (but the service was very friendly, which is why it's getting 2 stars, not 1).

First, for a vegetarian-friendly restaurant, there weren't even that many vegetarian options on the menu (side note - 4 of the 6 pages of the menu were full of wine and cocktail options, not food.  I like wine and cocktails, but I thought this was a restaurant, not a bar?)  Anyway, the food menu - maybe 2 or 3 vegetarian options (total, including appetizers, salads, entrees - which is slightly above average for New Orleans, but kind of a stretch to call that vegetarian-friendly).  In fact, there were so few options that I still had to special order my soup and salad without the accompanying crawfish on top.  When the food actually arrived, it was fine, but nothing special - the other people with me ordered meat/seafood items and confirmed - not terrible, but not anything they would ever want to go back for - so forgettable, I don't even remember what any of us ordered and it was only a few days ago.

Second, the ambiance - there is lovely outdoor seating in an alleyway, but we were seated inside.  Which was the opposite of lovely.  It is about as big as a closet, with maybe 4 tables jammed in along a wall in between the kitchen and door to the outside.  Servers are constantly squeezing by and the kitchen staff is constantly shouting three feet away.  And the temperature was about 105 degrees (and it was only April and not that hot outside yet).  It felt like we were eating in the kitchen.  Actually, it felt like we were eating in the oven in the kitchen.  If there's a wait and they offer to seat you inside, I'd highly recommend waiting for an outside table - you're not that hungry.

Finally, the only redeeming factor - the service was very friendly.  Our waitress checked on us regularly and answered random questions about the menu and wine list intelligently, and the chef (or maybe owner?) stopped by each of the tables inside to see how we were doing and to apologize about the heat (something about the exhaust fan not installed).  Despite the nice service, I won't be coming back - there's other places in the FQ/downtown area where I wouldn't leave hungry (and with heatstroke).

Shockingly good bar food - not necessarily good for you, but more than just greasy burger and fries - fried risotto and parmasan cheese balls, homemade hummus, grilled cheese with gouda (w/ or w/o bacon), and a bunch of other stuff that looked good.  Beer options are v. extensive and fairly priced, and they do basic mixed drinks, but no wine or fancy cocktails.  The bar is roomy and with all the doors on both sides, it stays pretty cool.  Only downside is that they allow smoking - the open doors help, but my hair and sweater still smelled like cigarettes when we left.  Oh, and as some of the other reviewers pointed out, the women's restroom is totally weird w/it's half-sized stalls.

Very tiny cafe that serves very good lattes and iced coffee.  No real seating inside, but a few tables outside.  They serve tasty (though pricey) Intelligensia and Stumptown coffee, and the barista - who looks and acts like he was imported directly from Silver Lake - knows what he is doing.  Only two quibbles: (1) they serve iced coffee in paper cups - not cool, since after 15 min or so, the paper starts leaking; (2) they wouldn't fill a cup of water for a dog outside - maybe they don't want to waste cups/water/time on non-humans, but at least do what a lot of other shops on Magazine do, and keep a big bowl of water outside.

This spot definitely has the most NY-like bagels in New Orleans - crusty outside, dense, chewy inside.  Slightly smaller than the average Brooklyn bagel, but tastes pretty good.  Lots of flavored cream cheeses, but no light cream cheese, which is kinda weird, since even Starbucks has light cream cheese for their sad excuses for bagels.  The prices seemed fair to me - I think it was about $2.50 for a bagel and cream cheese.  And they have fountain soda - so rare outside of McDonald's and gas stations, but so much better than soda in a can!

Very friendly service, good breakfast food, HUGE portions (even for New Orleans).  I ordered the 2 egg breakfast w/2 sides - either they use XXL eggs or they gave me at twice the number of eggs ordered.  The hash browns are like thick fried potato chips - unusual, but tasty.  The coffee is standard diner coffee, nothing special, but totally drinkable and refills are free and plentiful.  Only bad part of the meal (which was really my fault for not remembering this is the Deep South where it's presumed you want butter or bacon on everything) - the greasy english muffin - order your toast dry if you don't want it pre-soaked with butter.

Like other reviewers have said, this is definitely the closest to East Coast pizza in NOLA.  Domenica has good pizza (and an amazing happy hour), but that's fancy pants pizza, not Brooklyn/Philadelphia corner hole-in-the-wall pizza.  Pizza Delicious has the real deal - giant, well-done pizza pies with thin crust and grease on cheese for $12 (cheese).   You have to go the side door of a random shotgun house in the Bywater to get it and have to plan ahead when you order (only open on Thurs. and Sun. nights and depending how busy it is, might be an hour or three before pizza ready), but it's worth the trek.  It might not be better than your favorite East Coast pizza place, but it's definitely pretty close.
They now have a big bowl of water outside for the pooches!

Pleasantly surprised - as a vegetarian, I expected to leave hungry from a French-German oyster bar, but the menu has 7 or 8 side dishes, all vegetarian, as well as at least 2, maybe 3, salads that are vegetarian (not even requiring special ordering to leave meat off).  In other cities w/more veggie-friendly dining options, that wouldn't be all that special but after 3 recent meals at other upscale NOLA restaurants where there was literally nothing vegetarian on the menu (Upperline, Atchafalaya and Tommy's), Luke gets points with me.  And the non-vegetarian with me also raved about her meal, which appeared to involve both fried oysters and bacon.

Also, the ambiance is pleasant - we went for dinner around 8:30 pm on a Wednesday, and the place was 3/4 full, with a lot of solo diners, presumably people (lawyers, judging by their clothes/reading materials) who work/live nearby.  Kind of like Paris, actually.  And apparently, they have a happy hour everyday (including weekends) from 3-6 with half priced drinks and wine (and cheap oysters if you're into that sort of thing).

Love the name but not a fan.  

No vegetarian options at all on the dinner menu and only one on the brunch menu (and who really wants granola with their bloody mary at brunch?!)  

Service is slow - took a long time for waiter to take drink orders and an even longer time to take food orders and get food.  

Overpriced for what you get (at brunch at least) - my friend ordered one of the egg dishes - it was almost $20 and the portion was definitely not that big (and most of the plate seem covered in bechemel sauce - last time I checked, cream and butter weren't all that expensive).  

They have live music but it is *really* loud - like too loud to talk to the person next to you who looks like they are going to die from their hangover loud.  There is outside seating - I recommend it - you can still hear the music through the walls.

Hipster coffeeshop (with wine) in CBD - it looks like it's out of a Scandanavian design magazine.  Lots of coffee choices (though they use Illy coffee, which I think is bitter) and limited menu of panini, crepes and salads.  I had the granola parfait - it was the best Greek yogurt I've ever had, which I think must mean it was whole milk yogurt.  There was a steady flow of traffic on the weekday morning I was there, but it never got crowded like the Garden District coffeeshops and I had plenty of space to spread out my work - lots of table/counter space and free wi-fi.

PQrxOTtaCOno4p3Nzz5xZQ.review_text: Used to be 5/5, but still a solid 4/5.  Great menu, delicious food, amazingly fresh ingredients.  Just they don't quite load up the sandwiches with as much meat as they used to.  Maybe that's a better balance of ingredients?  But its what we were used to!  Still highly recommend.  Try their hot subs too - amazing cheese steaks.
Excellent Pizza and parmisian sandwiches!  Highly recommend the eggplant parm - they cook the the bread just perfectly.

This place has a lot of great food.  It's a cult phenom too - as people will travel here.  There's also a sub-place that has a broccoli raab-cheesesteak that was featured on Diner's Drive-Ins and Dive's.  A great visit if you visit the city.

Rays has always been one of my favorite sub places.  Ewing has several of them as well - so you know it's quality!  Their signature belly-busters are a particular favorite, but their hot subs are amazing too.  

After they switched ownership, they stopped loading the subs up with quite as much meat - but maybe that's a good thing to make a more-balanced sandwich?  They also unveiled their 5 dollar menu - pretty awesome for high-quality subs.  

If you are in Ewing/Trenton/Pennington/Lawrence.. try this place out!  You won't be disappointed.
Fast, fresh, and delicious - this place is great. I highly recommend the Junk Monkey veggie wrap. Their hot stuff is great too. Give this place a try, you'll probably go back.
Solid bowling, nice bar, good times.  They have beer specials I think.  I like bowling. They have bowling.  Much nicer than your average dank pit.

Live in Ewing or Trenton? This is your Chinese takeout place.  I'm a fat guy that tried all the local spots!

The food is delicious and hot, the deliveries are always fast, and I've never had an incorrect order or long wait.  

I recommend the fried rice, anything with garlic sauce, poopoo platter.. Hold on a second, I'm starting to drool.

Popeye's is Popeye's, so I'll review the location.  Fast, courteous staff and I've never had a wrong order.  The other day, we were placing our order at the drive-thru (a bunch of random stuff) and the teller suggested we get one of the combos and saved us a buck!

She totally didn't have to, but it made us very happy.

The Hungry Barbarian's food is like taking your wildest dreams, rolling it in a cabbage condom, then simmering it for hours in actual magic.  

Half their menu is their daily specials, which are always changing.  The sweet old Hungarian couple is 100% of their staff.  The guy has awesome old-man tattoos and Barbara is everyone's lovable grandma.  A gem of Ewing, and worth every gold coin spent.

Watch out No. 1 China.. Theres a new ballgame in town!  

Friends recommended Royal Chef so we tried out their chicken & broc in garlic sauce and their orange chicken.  Wow delicious!!  Fresh, plump cuts of chicken!  Masterfully cooked broccoli..  Highly recommend this spot for your Chinese food needs!!

I'm looking forward to eating more stuff from their menu.  They also have a very impressive website for a Chinese restaurant.

Man, this is my favorite delivery pizza.

I wouldn't call it gourmet.  It is greasy, standard sized, but.. Theres something about how they cook it, or maybe it's the cheese?  Whatever the secret sauce is that makes this pizza "special" really does the trick.

I'm also a fan of their wings!  So many wing spots overbread the heck out of their wings bit special city has em just right!  

Try their plain pie though, you'll love that cheese!

Food is good but the worst thing you can do is forget to put something in the bag!

Two times in a row they forgot my cinnamon bites (those nasty little sugary grease balls that explode in your mouth).  They were probly doing me a favor, and I would sit there thinkin "If someone said they'd erase those 400 calories of sugar and grease from my life that I just ate, yes.. I'd pay $2.50 for that.."

So maybe it was a blessing in disguise?

The beef liver and eggs is the way to go.  It tastes like how a wet dog smells, in a good way.  You can also swap your hash browns for pickled beets. 

Pickled beets, beef liver, eggs.. Three super healthy foods together at last, to take me to Mount Olympus!
My only complaint with Halo Ice Cream is that there is no trough filled with Chocolate Peanut Butter Paradise to bury my face in.

We came in and a lady in a pantsuit (manager?) was in the middle of scolding her hostess. I stood there, a foot away from them waiting to be greeted until my SO pulled me away to not be awkward. A few moments later the lambasting concluded, manager stormed off, and hostess greeted us.  What the heck was that all about?

Anyway, I was a little shocked when the hostess told us it'd be 15 minute wait, despite it being nearly-empty, and recommended we wait at the bar. (Obviously a strategy to try and extract a few pre-meal drinks out of their patrons)

Eventually we were seated and chowed down. I had the Grouper, the ball-N-chain had the salmon - both were delicious. The salad, tho, was iceberg lettuce, soft tomatoes - amateur hour.  Everything was served on square plates, and like Jon Taffer says, that's an easy way to jack up the price.

I'd eat here again.

Disclaimer:  despite being a 6'5" 235 hulk that eats like Slimer, I can't really boast an understanding of fine dining like others and can't really comment on if it was re-heated frozen food - as suggested by other Yelpers. It filled my Viking veins with Nordic hemoglobin and that's whats important darn it!!!! *punches wall"

Got a "Super food Side salad" and requested no dressing, to go, with hot sauce packets instead. The poster in the lobby, the menu, and the internet all said that this salad was made of kale, broccoli, nut blend, cherries.  Sounds healthy!

Got home and there was no broccoli, no nut blend, and the cherries were bright red/soaked in sugar (the same ones they put on the sundaes, I'm assuming). Worst of all the small handful of kale was utterly soaked in an inch of thick brown sugary dressing! "No dressing" seems to be interpreted as "no broccoli & nuts and loads of dressing!". Gross.

This was my first and last stop to a chick-fil-a.

PSQhXkKgYyIPitbEyTee-g.review_text: We ordered red velvet pancakes, creme brûlée French toast, Mac and cheese, and Spanish fries. Too much two people, but very good!
Good place for karaoke, but food was slightly substandard - often cold/reheated. It really is a seafood restaurant so don't expect tremendous results from the other options.
Excellent place for authentic southeast Asian cuisine. Roti canai is a must have. Popular spot for BYOs.
It's nothing special, but it's quality food if you're looking for a quick bite to eat and are in the area. We enjoyed the flatbreads and lentil soup.
A bit pricey but overall the mushroom Mac and cheese and chocolate shot are worth the fanfare. It's a good idea to get an entree and desert but even better if you can split with a friend.
We went for brunch- I ordered the omelette with gruyere, grapefruit juice, and pastry basket. Such an amazing place to go! Every aspect was five stars.
I ordered the Apple Pie Pancakes at brunch. They were good, but a little too cakey for my taste.
The food was decent but a little overpriced. It's a nice location but maybe not the spot for a foodie- that said some of the fusion options are worth a look.
Amazing experience. I got a haircut and shave for $60 incl tip and was treated well by my barber, who gave good tips for how to style my hair.
Great spot to relax, study, read, hang with friends, really anything. Good food/beverage options and friendly staff. Definitely a place to check out.
Came here for restaurant week. Butternut squash soup appetizer and desserts were great. Veggie burrito needs work. Fish tacos were good.

I wouldn't recommend this place for its food, but it's definitely a top notch place for drinks and some appetizers. We tried their tasting menu during restaurant week and while there were some solid options on both the meat and vegetarian menus, overall I was left with an average impression. The service and ambience were great for after work but definitely not for a quiet dinner focused on the food itself.

We tried the antipasta, sheep's milk ricotta, and strozzapretti. The ricotta was perfect and the strozzapretti had so many flavors - definitely unexpected win. The dessert selections were not the best but we were completely satisfied with all the entrees. It's busy and popular, highly recommended!
I was really excited for this restaurant but turns out it's a little over-hyped. We got French toast, chili, eggs Benedict, and lemon ricotta pancakes and it was pretty average.

The bagels can't get any better and the guys are always very friendly. I always make it a point to come here when I can - although the carbs do add up! I recommend anything on the menu and of course you should always ask them for suggestions. I'm also a huge fan of their social media presence - their communication is very reliable.
Went here again and decided it's actually pretty good - especially the dessert cakes! It is definitely pricey though.

I had an amazing experience with Tony. The whole thing took about 45 minutes. I opted for the traditional shave and he was very skilled, which was important because I have acne-prone skin. I highly recommend the barber or any their products, they are top notch.

We absolutely loved the French toast, eggs Benedict and pancakes at this place! the best part was that it was relatively one panics for old city brunches. Check it out on any weekend - it's busy but there's no wait.

I love coming to Sabrina's for Sunday brunch. Their food is always really good and has great value (I always have leftovers for the next day). Usually I stick with the stuffed challah french toast, the classic option for first-timers, but this time I ordered the "Post-Hibernation Feast Special Breakfast" (accurate, considering the weather). They were kind enough to replace the the bacon with vegan sausage, and although I was a little wary about the "blackberry-apricot-jalapeno" but it turned out to be great with the eggs.  The cornbread french toast wasn't very good so I would stick with some of their standard french toast options. I also prefer the University City location to the one on Callowhill.

Could not have been more impressed with this place! I had been wanting to try Vedge for a while and only just got the opportunity - it did not disappoint. It's definitely the spot to check out if you're a vegetarian or a vegan, and all of the dishes are worth a try. Sharing is definitely the way to go here.

I really enjoyed this place! I got the chocolate chip pancakes and iced mocha and they were both amazing - although maybe too much chocolate for one order! It's relatively new considering other restaurants on Baltimore and packed for brunch. I want to come back and try some of the Mediterranean options.

I didn't find this place exceptionally more exciting than your standard cheap Asian place in philly - and it's not even that cheap! Still a good option for informal eats when you're craving ramen/sushi but want to eat in sweatpants.

I didn't particularly enjoy the Mac and cheese or the pimento cheese appetizer enough to give this place a 4 or even a 5. Their main attractions are the sliders and pork chops, and everything is meant to be shared, so it's a struggle when you're vegetarian. My friend who eats meat enjoyed it though!

I'm new to Korean food, but I decided to try U-Town because it was packed on a Thursday afternoon with a lot of Koreans. I tried the dak galbi (chicken) stone pot and the chicken dumplings and they were both very good! Definitely going back to try everything on the menu.
I came here with two friends, and we ordered two small plates to share among the three of us and an entree each. The ravioli changes daily, so I tried that. Everything was top notch!

Half priced bubbly is all the more reason to come here on a Sunday! We got the Muscat along with the asparagus appetizer, and I ordered the rotisserie chicken with vegetables. Highly recommended - check it out!

With four stars and hundreds of reviews on Yelp I have to admit I was expecting more from Distrito. Since it was busy during happy hour on Thursday night I'll say that it has an excellent ambience even though the food itself is not great. Steer clear of the adobo chicken tacos and opt for the veggie nachos to split with a friend.

I think Greek Lady is one of the most underrated places to eat near Penn's campus. It consistently offers a variety of solid options, and the best part is that it's a good value and the closest thing University City has to a diner. The chicken plates and breakfast/brunch are what you should stick with.

I was really unimpressed with this food truck especially because I was so excited to try it. I paid $8 for the sundried tomatoes option, but honestly if you're looking for decent Mac and cheese you should be at Wishbone. It's similarly priced but is totally worth it.

Federal Donuts should stick to what they're good at, because adding a slice of Kraft American cheese to wings on a cold bun does not a fried chicken sandwich make. That being said, the chicken itself was obviously perfect as were the donuts I ordered. I don't enjoy their special flavors any more than the standard three, so if you go I recommend sticking to a half order with one or two donuts.

I saw the show Flight Club (2016 season) and it was by far the best student production I have seen at Penn. The performers of Mask & Wig are incredibly talented and I would recommend seeing their annual off-campus show in the spring - it definitely is at the same caliber of any theater on Broad.

I thought it was a bit pricey for the amount given (comparing to food trucks) but it's a solid late night option. I ordered the chicken keema, chicken tikka, and paneer tikka rolls. They were all quite dry in comparison to the masala roll.

After Distrito, this was was my second visit to a Jose Garces restaurant, and I could not have been more impressed with Tinto! My friend and I ordered five dishes to share, and all except one were exceptional.
We ordered the monte enebro cheese, pulpo, chicken brochettes, wild mushrooms, and a soft-shell crab special. I didn't enjoy the special, but I'm still developing a taste for seafood (my friend thought it was the best course). The photos don't do the food justice. The mushrooms and octopus were by far my favorite.
I highly recommend this place and also it's very important to make a reservation if you plan on sitting at the tables. The happy hour specials are only available at the bar.

Three stars for this one because the happy hour vibe was great and the food was decent, but the service left a lot to be desired and the drink specials tasted like flavor water. Also, it was much more expensive than was called for. Overall unimpressed, go for ambience if nothing else.

Pd8fz73SG3few12bB6NypQ.review_text: Best tacos in Pasco County! Wish they had more seating, but the food is worth the tight quarters. Give them a try...you'll be back!

I've been going to Larry's for close to twenty years, and they're still making great subs and salads for a great price! As much as I love the Publix deli products, I can say that you'll get double portions at Larry's Deli for about the same price, and sometimes even a better price!

The last time I visited this restaurant my family was seated next to the kitchen. Normally that wouldn't be a big deal (other than the fact that it's quite obvious they segregate people with kids to the less desirable seats--as if our money doesn't spend like the other people), but there were crude jokes and language that was easily being overheard by my young child from the staff in the kitchen. In addition, the restaurant seems to be dirty and the customer service is not the greatest. In other words, you feel just like a number at this restaurant.

I've been eating at Hungry Harry's BBQ for over twenty years. I can honestly say that the food is as good today as ever. The one thing missing today that existed up until a few years ago are the little niceties that they used to provide when LOL was more of a small town, such as giving you a free drink when you're waiting on your to-go order, or knowing your name like some of the old timers used to, or just saying "thank you for visiting."

If you're a gear head, you'll enjoy the cool decor of the restaurant. The food portion (at least burgers) are HUGE. What I didn't like was the very loud music (felt like I was at a bar) which made it difficult to carry on a conversation. The customer service was OK, but it felt rushed and like being more of a "number" than a customer. It's probably a place I'd go back to, but not more than once a year.

Whaley's is basically a food truck with a BBQ pit out back. The pork is ok, but the sausage is great. My only complaint is that they are regularly out of menu items on a regular basis, and even though they open at 11, don't expect all meats to be prepared to eat until closer to noon. A picnic table for seating would also be a nice addition.

The actual bbq was good (not great, but good). The restaurant seemed clean and was nicely decorated. What we didn't like was the fact that we never got an offer to refill our drinks until we were DONE (as in, the bill presented). Had to get my own extra napkins, etc. And no, they weren't that busy. Probably will not go back.
Have been twice. Great food, great prices, great service. I like the fact that the owners are present and working, and introduced themselves as well. I'll be back a third time shortly.

I have eaten here several times over the years. UB's is a popular local spot primarily due to the fact that really no one else around has live music, and eating/drinking options along the US 41 area of Land O' Lakes are still very limited despite the population growth of the area. The food portions are big, but tend to be on the "greasy spoon" side. The burgers are the only menu items I'll order since, IMO, everything else is overpriced grease food.

Probably the best Cuban type food in Land O Lakes. Prices are reasonable, food tastes fresh and staff is friendly. They've done a good remodeling job with the decor as well. My only knock is that the food amount is a bit on the small side, regardless, best Cuban food nearby.

I've been to Pepe's many times. They make a very good Cuban sandwich, and their cafe con leche is very good (although overpriced), but that's all I'll order from Pepe's. My experiences of ordering other menu items has either left me with an upset stomach or disappointed with slow service and items that don't taste authentic.

Cafe is pretty much in the middle of nowhere, which makes it a nice place to visit, even though it's a bit of a drive. The building itself is a historic local landmark. CM has the best Cuban food north of Ybor. Food portions are big and authentic tasting. Seating can be limited (a sign of good eats), so come early!

I usually stop here or Hooters to eat when I'm in the Brandon area going to Bass Pro. I love the pork and the sides at First Choice. The macaroni salad has a kick to it, the fries are always made on the spot, beans are great. The only reason I knock them a star is because they're about the bunch of most unfriendly guys you'll ever meet. Be sure to know what you want for your order, because you're on your own if you don't.

Food is good, but overpriced. I've always found the door greeters to be very friendly, but my experiences with waitresses at this location is that they're not the most accommodating. Fortunately for them, I love a couple of their select menu items (shrimp, chicken, etc), otherwise I'd probably never go.

I feel that I cannot give Jazzy's more than an average rating based on average food, average customer service, and an average atmosphere. The pork sandwich was plentiful, but a bit dry and fatty. The mac n cheese was good, bbq beans are decent, and collard greens were not bad. Although I eat BBQ at least once a week, I've never found a reason to visit Jazzy's more than about twice a year.

Ate here today for the first time. I ordered the BBQ boat which they're known for. As others have said, the mac n cheese is delicious, and I thought the pork and bbq sauce was very good as well. I wasn't crazy about the BBQ beans as they tasted a bit hard (undercooked?) to me. The price was decent, but definitely not cheap. Customer service was first class. If I lived in the area, I'd probably occasionally visit, but wouldn't go out of my way to eat there.

Best smoked fish sandwich hands down. The ONLY reason I can't give 5 stars is because they are CASH ONLY, and I always find it annoying when a restaurant has a cash only policy, but conveniently has an ATM machine on site with a $3 fee attached to it.

Ate at Franky's for the first time this evening. First off, I miss Elsa's Mexican which used to be located in same spot. The food at Franky's was OK, but there's an odd assortment of foods and it's overpriced for the location and quality. Lutz is still in many ways small town USA, and this restaurant style seems to be attempting to mix that small town population with a South Tampa atmosphere. The decor is very modern/urban, the food is like a quasi country restaurant menu, and there's an odd assortment of country music playing in the background thrown in. It just doesn't work and feels forced. My guess is "Franky D" is a New Yorker (or thereabouts) trying to establish a place where people of all stripes can eat. I'd suggest sticking to one theme and doing it well.

Disappointed...had about a 15 minute wait (very limited seating), then served a meal with a cold biscuit (although they did replace with a hot one upon request). The skillet came with not enough gravy, so asked for some extra, only to be charged for it without being told. Only giving more than one star because the staff were friendly. Very unlikely to go back...plenty of other breakfast options in LOL.

Q0LFOm1i68HeBVc_Sv4_uQ.review_text:
This is by far the best Vietnamese restaurant. I have been a customer for a long time and they never seem to dissatisfy. It is a long wait at dinner time but it gives time to actually talk to the people you are with. I recommend to always get fried egg rolls and fresh rolls.
One of my experiences from there is, when I was there with my sister and father so we all ordered seafood with rice. I had broken rice with shrimp. My father got some shrimp too but I'm not sure what kind. My sister got catfish. Once it was all together it was delicious. The catfish and my father's shrimp (not mine) was served in separate plates from the rice so we all got to pick what we wanted. Overall, I highly recommend this place and this will always be my go-to Vietnamese food place.

When we first went there, we were very unsure because of the reviews. The waiters weren't very kind and the food was okay. Yes, it does have crab and sushi but it all could have been better. The utensils didn't look clean and I didn't have a very good time. Overall, I don't recommend eating here and am very dissatisfied.
One of my first times going there and it wasn't that bad. I don't want to say it was absolutely amazing or say that it sucks. I had a good time eating with my family and I will be going there again.
I was there for the lunch special which was fairly cheap for a soda and a meal

I went there with some family, not sure that it was going to be good given it's appearance - we were even sketchy as we got out the car! But once inside, we were instantly relieved as it felt so homey and the aroma of food was absolutely stunning. Service was very nice and they checked up on us often. When they served the food, the food was still very hot and the pan that it was on was still sizzling, which was comforting and looked so welcoming. Some of the things I didn't like was that everyone was so close to one another, and the surfaces that we sat on are similar to how you would feel sitting on a bench. Not sure if this is just preference, but after a while your butt does get sore..

Since they remodeled it looks so much better! We've been going here for quite some time (years actually) and we always get 10 pastries because they're just so d*!@ good. The custard buns, roast pork, and the most recent strawberry buns are my favorites. They also serve smoothies, Vietnamese rolls, boba tea (bubble tea) for a very relatively nice price. We ordered 11 pastries for ~10 dollars. The cakes are ~3 dollars. Extremely cute place, but the owner/worker there is kind of angsty and not very happy to serve you with a smile but she definitely gets the job done. Often customer. c:

Service was very nice. The place itself is huge and filled with goodies whether it's a quick sweet snack or a meal with clubs and sandwiches. Their selection is very amazing and vast and there's so much to get! Ordered a Cuban for 7 dollars and for a drink and fries/chips it was an extra 2 dollars. It was our first time there so we were quite confused when they didn't give us our drinks from the sandwich side.. (it's split between the deli and the bakery) Will be back again!

The atmosphere was cozy and everything in there was so nice and comfortable. It's a perfect hang out location to just chill with your friends or study while enjoying something. It's about 10 miles away from my house, so I probably won't be back but I definitely recommend it. My only problem was that my friends boba teas were perfectly blended while mine was icy at the top with liquid on the bottom, which I was not fond of.

We went here to eat after going to Busch Gardens for my birthday. The waiter was easily forgetful of our orders. Forgot to give us our fries that my friend's sister ordered multiple times and had to ask another waiter walking by to get us our fries. The food was absolutely amazing (though it slides right through..BEWARE) and the surprise birthday cake was beautiful inside and out. Would go back to try more of their new stuff.

We've been to this place a couple times to shop. My experience was average with the cafe where they have pork and duck available. They have boba as well. This place would probably be good if you're on a time crunch, and want to buy some groceries, and also get some boba or eat some food. This place is for Asians mostly because that's what most of the products and people are.

We needed someone who would bring us great food in the wee hours of the morning. Pita Pit were one of the viable options that were more on the cheaper side in the area and we had them deliver to us from grubhub.com. We actually ordered twice from the same Pita Pit -- once was flawlessly amazing (we're talking about the food and the curt delivery, it was 10 minutes earlier than expected and they called us letting us know they were at the door.) and the other.. well. Their delivery range was 3 miles and we were JUST 2.9. The second time around, we got a call back saying that we were 3.3 miles, just out of range and they weren't going to be able to deliver. Grubhub and The Pita Pit made sure that the money was refunded promptly and I was mildly disappointed but at 2 AM, I could've mistaken that disappointment for tiredness. It's okay Pita Pit, I still love you (and will be requesting another deliver soon)

Taco Salad was delicious! The flavor was right on! This wonderful place is also very close to my house. Plus, it does get better because I mostly sit in the booths, so when I look out the window, I can just look at the people at McDonalds ,and know I'm eating way healthier than them.
The service was really good as the waiters were always so attentive. The atmosphere was so homey. I don't have to worry about how much money it costs. The food... I can't even explain in words(especially the soup!). I definitely see myself coming back for more.

I'm always looking out for Asian themed restaurants, and plus I knew someone who worked there, so it caught my eye. I'm always a sucker for Vietnamese food so of course I thought that the food was superb. From the spring rolls, which was oh so fresh. From the rice which made it feel just like home.
However, the atmosphere could be better. It was dingy and dull, so it just didn't feel comfortable eating there. Which made me feel unsanitary, and made me be so picky. From whether I thought the forks were clean to the plates to the table. It was still an enjoyable night though because I was there with family.
To revive the evening at the end, we got some extra cherries in our drink which cheered me right up. All is good again. But, I don't think I'll be coming back because there are far more places I can dine that doesn't need to be here.

I was surprised to read the reviews being so negative here until I realized that it looked a lot different than how it looked when I came in. I myself am not a huge fan of being healthy, but I can't deny their delicious smoothie options, the healthy part is just an added bonus! I always get something from the Local options and it's usually something different each time. Workers there are polite and rather patient with us since we're not accustomed to the menu (and my sister is a picky chooser and likes to take her time) and the smoothies are made in front of us (think Subway - through a glass panel you could say?) and are ready under 5 minutes.  Good place, we need to definitely change the rating and get this place recognized! 

Forgot to mention: In the only picture here, their shelves look stocked, but you haven't seen stocked yet until you come back in to their new renovated place! As I stated, I wasn't a healthy person, but as they were making our smoothies I couldn't help but notice some really nice, healthy looking stuff! There were protein bars of all kinds, protein powder..things, and nice organic/raw/vegan food options there too. We ended up grabbing two large vegan cookies for the night to compliment our smoothies and left happy and promptly.

We came here after eating at Pho Quyen (recommended, by the way!) since we all knew that we had some space in our stomachs for yogurt. When we first walked in, the place was colorful and popped out at us enough. Personally, myself, I am not as big a fan of yogurt as my sister is so I was a bit skeptical of buying anything. Right away, one of the two ladies offered to give us samples as we took to the yogurt machines. I thought it was a nice touch to give the customers a nutritional values on some (not all) yogurt options. I ended up getting something simple, coconut yogurt (which I surprisingly loved) and candy cherries whereas my sister went a little bit more over the top with her choices. At .45 per ounce, I couldn't complain.

We live down the street from this place, so we finally decided to walk down there and give the place a try.

Inside, the place is very hot and stuffy, not to mention small. When we went there were a lot more people than expected waiting to order their food. I would guess that it's a family orientated restaurant, only being two in the 'kitchen' and a teenage boy at the register. I recall waiting in line of two/three people in front of me and the cook kept going in and out of the door and it was kind of regrettably uncomfortable moving around in the already small area, and I was blocking the small (and only, apparently) garbage that was already up to the brim in food. The food took about 10 minutes to make, and I was asked again what I ordered since there's really no process of keeping track of the orders. We ordered chicken and pork, and it wasn't until after we paid that the cook informed us that there was no chicken and we got ribs instead and I ordered green beans on the side but I got mac and cheese (which I'm not usually a fan of, but it was really good with the bbq sauce!). They didn't charge us the price difference, which was nice (not sure if this was intentional.) and the food itself was nice and filled us up. Will go here on the off chance that it IS literally right down the street and the prices are not too bad, but if it were a 10 minute drive and the prices were spiked, we wouldn't be returning.

Went here for my dad's birthday dinner and I was NOT let down! We went super early and from the outside it looked intimidating and I was afraid of awkward air, but it isn't anything like that at all. Music was playing very softly, the service was AMAZING. Even though we were early for dinner and there weren't a lot of customers the air was filled with the single server (who I presume is the owner) talking and making everyone laugh with his humor! The food felt authentic, it was on the level of my grandma's cooking, which is saying a lot. Unlike most places I've been to, there are seasonal rolls as opposed to just the traditional spring roll. I recommend the winter and autumn rolls as they were almost heavenly. I would differently eat here again..and again.

I just went here today, and I'm surprised not to see a better rating.I love places with booths, so this was right in my ballpark.

My friend and I came for a lunch date right in the middle of happy hour. I don't remember exactly when it was, but I'm pretty sure it's Tuesday to Thursday 3-6. There are multiple deals for happy hour, but the one we took advantage of was $1 off every plate. We got a lot off too, considering we had 7 plates(the total was around 21 dollars too, that averages out to be 3 dollars per plate!).

There were very unique flavors in the dishes, and we were stuffed when we left.  I also was trying to eat mostly vegan options. It was helpful enough for them to put a V for vegetarian. The rest my phone had to tell me. They also told me they ran out of vegetable gyoza, but immediately assured me and showed me other options. I like how as a vegan, I can still enjoy sushi. I ate a fair share of both things on the conveyor belt and hot stuff that you have to order. In my opinion, the sizing of the plates are perfect because you can pick it up for a snack like when you're shopping or have an actual meal. It also lets you know your limit, so you won't have to take home any leftovers. The only thing I'm iffy about is the vegetable firecracker rice. I should've known because I'm not good with spicy things. But, it was good enough for me to finish the whole dish, and know I'm not getting it another time. It was also the last plate we got, so trying to squeeze some more food in wasn't pleasant.

Overall, this place is awesome for small groups and I think I'll go to international plaza just for this place.

QLhKYnsmv07EwZ-JM5fl9A.review_text: Had the Supreme nachos.. pretty good and the sweet tea is really sweet! Which I love..
Rib tips are mmm mmm good! And so is the barbecue on bun.. the sides seem to be a little on the small side. The pies are yummy to.
Granite City.. had the bone in wings and a Cesar salad. Pretty good both were and the service was great

If you like spicy food and spicy chicken. This is the place for you! They have some really good chichen and seasoned sides like southerners do it! Yum Yum for my Tum Tum!
The only draw back is they are a bit slow.. lines can be long which means you will not be eating right away.. so patient!

Krogers grocery store has most lines open in the evenings.. biggie for me.. weekends all 9 lanes may be open.. longevity with employees.. nice neighborhood store for the last 8 yrs.. and they now Murray's specialty cheese in store. Murray's is a New York cheese based company. The staff have relationships with regulars..
Mmm mmm Good! Who does a burger.. service can be a little better but everyone gets a pass or two ;) restrooms were fairly clean.. management was freindly. Great location and they are open very late!

Visited this place today. The food was pretty good we had breadsticks, salad and wings.. Yummy! But the staff at the front door was kind of  obnoxious. As we walked up he put his hand out and said I need to see your ID. I was like ID for what? He says everyone that comes in has to show Their ID.. uhhh is this a nightclub or resturant? I showed my ID then proceeded. I asked the waitress and 2 other ppl in the restaurant were they asked for their ID and they said no..hmmmm??? Then a young women said we were her on Tuesday and they didn't ask for my ID. As we were leaving I seen this same guy asking 2 women for their ID and debit cards. Since they didn't have debit cards they were not let in. Ok not sure what this is all about but this will kill business. Well at least my business and referrals!

Simply quick and good mexican food for a pretty good price.
Try the nacho supreme! Delish..

Everything's God here! Mac and cheese, the tea, the chicken! Seasoned just right! Tasteful and tender! Prices are pretty reasonable we spent about $30 for 3 ppl. The only thing that bugs me about this place is the location (downtown) The parkings not great. You have to pay at a meter for parking if you find one and may have to walk a distance to get to the restaurant. But I can say the food is well worth it!
This place is your average express chicken and fish joint. Good for a late night eat and a quick drive through for lunch. Very reasonably priced.

Love this place..  it's like being at Disney land. The owner is very nice and greets customers with a smile. There's cakes, pies, cookies, bling, coffee, wines, sandwiches, crystals and very pretty decorations that change seems every month. It makes you feel like a princess when you walk through the door.

The closest as you can get to Nawlins style eating. Huge portions and the meals are flavorful not salted down. The staff are friendly you can tell they love what they do. I love the shrimp and grits..yummy.. a square grit cake and huge shrimp in a creamy sauce it is delicious and the portions are huge. Ample parking in a strip mall. Clean.. and they have wifi.

Love the pancakes at cracker barrel. The service is great. Can get busy sometimes. The lines can get long but there's a reason for that. The food is good here. The maple syrup is yummy on the pancakes. I also like the fried catfish with 3 sides. The waitress and waiters are very friendly. One your finished eating you can browse the gift shop when you check out they always seem to have something on clearance and they always have Old Time Candy from way back when we were little kids. Parking is free.. the atmosphere is pleasant. Management will check on guest to make sure they are enjoying their food and if there's a problem. Management will get it fixed right away.

Today we stopped at Popeyes to get some sodas. I was impressed with the cleanliness of the place. Upon entering 2 of the employees spoke up and said Hi! What? Ppl still speak when you walk in these days? Anyway  we had shrimp and chicken. It was fresh and delicious! The restrooms were clean and we didn't have to wait long on out food. Very impressed!

Ok.. now I'm really a pretty patience person and understanding...hmmm? 
 Ok so I meet a friend at long horn (which she suggested) for dinner.
