The best Indian food...period.  

So it took a year (since moving here from Chicago) to find and Indian place worthwhile.  When I asked an Indian fellow who lived in Broad Ripple which was the best place there to get Indian food, he shot me a horrid look, as if he found out his blind date lived in Carmel.  It was in fact Amber, and boy I'm glad I asked.  This place would stand out on Devon Avenue in Chicago any day.  Authentic, delicious and priced very reasonably.  The garlic naan is to die for.  My wife and I both had lamb dishes (kinda silly but ya want what ya want) and they were cooked to perfection.  You can choose from 3 different levels of spicy.  We chose medium and that left a nice light burn on your tongue, and no issues on the way out.  The Palak Pakora is a must app for $3 too.  The meals were the Amber Biryani and the Amber Special lamb.  The portion sizes left both of us lunch the next day, and the service was fantastic.  The staff line up against the back wall, like the Royal Guard and just wait for any sign that you might need something.  Oh, and the place is immaculate.  Good luck finding that in Chicago.  We are going back for the buffet on Monday.  Look for me, I'll be the guy with the "O" face!

Went for dinner here with my wife tonight and I must say, the place is better then I expected. We started with Asian wings that had a great balance of sweet and spicy. We shared the full rack of ribs that were very moist and flavorful. The BBQ sauce was a little sweet for my taste, but that is forgivable. The sides of very cheesy Mac n cheese and sautéed green beans were good. What struck us was how incredibly nice the owner and waitress were. They also have beer specials that are amazing with lots of local craft beers. We will be back to try the sandwiches and the fried chicken cause it looked delicious on our way out.

Hipster Haven w/out the hipsters...thank god!

Ok, as far as the food goes, it is fan frickin' tastic.  The double cheeseburger with crispy thin patties, slightly greasy on a modest size bun with all the old school trimmings was worth every calorie.  Perfectly cooked fries (if you like them seasoned and well done) accompanied the burger and a chalice (36oz) of ice cold bud washed it down.  Get the goblet, it comes from the freezer and really completes the meal.

The service is top notch.  Old school charm, with experience written all over the waitstaff and proprietor's faces.  It's a family owned operation for decades. The years have given the place incredible charm and the original floor has what Antiques Roadshow would call "patina." Two original cig machines are there (empty of course), with a worn sign requiring $2.25 a pack.  Brilliant decor throughout.  Here's the best part, it is an ultra hipster joint without the hipsters.  I guess the place is too far or Belmont is too pothole ridden for the vermin to ride there bikes or Vespas.  A huge win!  Oh, if those walls could talk, they'd tell quite a story I'm sure.  Check er out!

This is the best restaurant we've been to since moving to Indy...and we tried a bunch.  We went here on a Thursday to celebrate our 10 yr anniversary and Meridian did not let us down.  Our service was top notch, as our waiter gave us concise, yet comprehensive tour of the menu.  We started with a locally produced meat and cheese app that was amazing.  No combination was wrong, and worthy of the $18 price tag.  Honest.  My wife had the tomato soup which is her favorite to both eat and criticize, and it did not disappoint.  I had the corn puree (voted the best soup in Indy I'm told) and it was one of the very best I've ever had.  Unreal.  I would have licked the bowl clean, but I we were surrounded by the blue blazer crew, so I thankfully refrained.  Which, by the way, I wore nice jeans and a button down and felt under dressed (probably 'cause I was.)  Not sure the dress code, but people played dress up.

The dinners were great.  The shrimp and pork was to die for, very complex and full of delicious surprises.  My duck 2 ways was the only semi-flaw to an otherwise perfect dinner.  The crispy side was top notch, but the seared side was a bit underdone to my liking and a little tough.  With that said, it was in a delicious sauce that saved the dish for me.  We also splurged and had the au gratin taters that were unique (almost like a cheese cake) and down right amazing.  Don't leave without trying this.

When we finished, our server insisted that we had desert, but after declining several times, he brought us a little chocolate tart (for out anniversary) on the house and it just an oral orgasm.  Gonna being going back for desert there in the not so distant.  So, if you haven't been here, I strongly suggest you put it on your short list.  Not cheap, but what worthwhile is?

Here is what you get from Ambrosia in a nut shell; great ambiance, including a fantastic outdoor seating area, awesome service and good Italian food that is reasonably priced.  We had the Rustica, which was delicious homemade penne, sausage and sweet peppers.  It had the perfect amount of sauce, (not drowning the dish) and a generous amount of sausage.  The portions were plenty for us, and it's not Maggiano's where you can take home dinner for the Brady bunch, including Alice, Sam and even Oliver.  My wife had the Vongole, which was good, not great.  The wine sauce could have been cooked down a bit, but the clams were good and in both cases, the pasta was cooked perfectly.  I think our dishes were $15 each and there was more than enough food for a meal. If I could just say, the Glenlevit pours were about as generous as you could ever hope for.  I had 2, so I don't remember how much they cost, but  I do recall thinking the first was a kill the bottle pour, but the 2nd was filled to the rim (in a big glass) as well. It's a great neighborhood spot, especially if you're not interested in traveling to chain store row on 86th St.  And it's far enough to keep most Carmel patrons away..usually a good thing.  I'll be back.

I should have known...period.  I've driven by this place hundreds of times and it is almost always empty.  But, I live nearby and against my better judgment, my wife and I chanced it.  We sat downstairs, which is like a metrosexual's man cave.  The TV above us had "Departed" on IFC with commercials and all, and that was the most interesting thing to look at.  I'd bet a bowling alley bar in Mooresville had 10x more people then this place, and it was Saturday night, 7pm.  I had the Nasfuratu, which had a frothy egg white to camouflage the Death's Door gin and a syrupy red mess at the bottom of glass that could put you in a diabetic coma.  My wife had the Moscow Mule that was super tart, but she managed to get it down.  The boursin cheese dip was good, but at $11 you can keep it.  The music was excellent, if you like '90s shoegaze and the wait staff was friendly.  Ummm, they have a great web page?  Other then that, this place needs a complete makeover.  Sorry, I really wanted to like you.

I can't give this place 4 stars because the burrito I ordered, steak was just ok.  For $7 it was bland and light on the meat.  HOWEVER, the place is called Indy Taco's for a reason (other then a hopeless lack of creativity).  The Taco I ordered was terrific.  The Mole (which is a flavor that can easily be mutilated) taco was amazing.  Finally an authentic taco in Indiana.  It was packed with fresh, tasty ingredients and the sauce was fantastic.  I will go back and try the other tacos, if I can get past the Mole, skipping the steak of course.  2 to 3 tacos would make for a filling lunch, which is cheap in my book.

Some strengths and some weaknesses for our first visit.  Starting with the positives:
The breakfast burrito was one of the best I ever had.  You can fill it with options and they were stuffed with high quality cheese, bacon and sausage.  The sausage is to die for.  The iced coffee (nice option) is quite good as well.  My wife had the grilled cheese sandwich that was cooked to a perfect golden brown and again, the cheese was top notch and plentiful (3 different kinds)  The outdoor seating was quit nice, and the spacious.  
Weakness-  The service was terrible.   We waited forever to get seated, and then it went downhill from there.  They may have been shorthanded, but the staff seemed pretty unconcerned and annoyed that they had a lot of patrons which was a bit perplexing.  The biscuits and gravy where pretty crummy.  The gravy was way too thick and biscuits were dry. The tomato vegetable soup was more vegetable then tomato and the earthy flavor was a bit much.  I could see how some might find this wholesome, but for us it was a flavor that didn't sit right.  It is not tomato soup in any way IMO.
I stand behind my four stars in that when it was right, it was fantastic.  The service may have been off that day, so I'm not going to doc them as everybody has an off day.  I look forward to giving them another shot.  I hope I can get past the burrito and try something new...but i doubt it.

Full disclosure...I'm writing this review for self interest reasons ONLY.  This should be an absolutely jam packed place from open to close but, because its in Indy, and Cubans didn't immigrate to the US to wind up in Indiana, the place was half full on a Saturday night.  This needs to change, STAT.  

My wife and I started off with a beef empanada and chicken empanada.  The chicken was juicy and the crust flakey and not overdone.  We also split a Cuban chicken soup that was to die for.  Rich, hearty and seasoned to perfection.  Again, the shredded chicken was just perfect.  Oh soooo gooood.  We split 2 dinners, the Ox tail stew and  a yellow rice, cheese and chicken casserole thingy.  The Ox tail was incredible.  The meat was rich and flavorful and plenty of of it.  It just fell off the bone, and the tomato stew juice was so rich from sitting in the fatty meat.  Oh man oh man.  Even the side of veggies that came with it were buttery and fantastic.  A little over cooked for my taste, but I like a crunch.  The casserole had olives in it which gave it a little special something' but I don't recall the menu mentioning it.  Anyway, it too was quit good.

Service was good but this is not a quick grab a bite place.  Picture Tony Montagna's mom in the kitchen cooking family favorites from scratch.  It takes some well worthy time.  They also applied for their liquor license, so that should add an interesting element at some point.  All in all, a fantastic find...A+

If you've had Chinese food elsewhere (i.e. a major city like Chicago, LA, NY or even say Cinci) you've had way better.  For Indy, it's a better than any buffet and most other places I've tried.  And the bonus of delivery is huge.  The food is meh.  The egg drop soup was tasty, not too much salt (rare) but a tad gelatinous for my taste.  The vegetable fried rice was bland, but not overcooked and the veggies were still crunchy which was nice.  The sesame chicken was way too sweet, but a HUGE portion.  The Egg Foo Young patties were actually quit good, but the brown sauce wasn't very thick and the had a strange bullion taste to it.  Different, not terrible.  They accidentally (?) threw in an order of rangoon and that was lucky, I know not to order it in the future.  Very little crab creme and lots of breading which was flakey but undercooked.  Finally, the chicken wings were great.  Nothing chinese about them, but they were huge and breaded perfectly and a good value.   Not #1 happiness but not terrible either.  Will do in a pinch.

My friend, wife and I happened upon this place and I must say it was a great find. Our waiter, Sean was fantastic. He came across sincere, not one of those "ok, excellent choice" b.s. Slingers you find in these type of places.  We started with a bottle Malbec ( which was terribly dry but paired well with our entrees) and the mussels. The broth of the mussels was so amazing we had to order more bread as to not miss a good soaking opp. It was under the small plate menu but three of us were satisfied as a starter. 

The entrees were on the small side, but they were soooo delicious. I had the steak, and my wife and friend had the chicken. My beef was cooked perfectly and the side of potato salad was a perfect comfort side that was one of the best I've had. The greens too were cooked perfectly (not over cooked which happens all too often). Both my wife and friend raved about the chicken. A rich dish with a perfectly cooked soft boiled egg. They sounded like they were orgasming in unison, which made me a bit jealous...for the food! 

Anyway, there are a lot of places you can go in this price point, but P&A ranks real high on my opinion. Three dishes ordered, all spectacular and a fantastic server (Sean) makes this a must return destination.

Wifey and I went last night.  The place is kinda a cross between a chain mexican place like Qdoba and an authentic taqueria.  First off, we grabbed one of the last possibilities to eat outside and the seating there is plentiful and comfortable.  The inside bar which is located away from the dining area and had its own entrance looks to have a nice assortment of tequila and different specialty drinks, but not to cheesy.  Speaking of cheese, finally a place like this that doesn't smother everything in creamy cheese whiz.  

We started with a small guacamole app and it was ok.  I've had better and by small, they mean small. For dinner, my wife had the combo plate w/ 2 enchiladas and a taco.  The taco is huge and is loaded with very tasty and authentic mexican cheese,  The enchiladas were solid, but not exceptional.  The fajitas were the hit in my book.  I had the Texas mix, which had shrimp (which were quite large) chicken and  steak,  The steak was very tasty and it didn't have that sweet tereaki flavor that often ruins this dish in other places.  It comes with a side mix of guacamole, pico de gallo and creme that really makes the dish come alive.  It comes with three flout tortillas, but you can easily get five out of one order, so the entree can easily be shared. One of the best fajita dishes I've ever had.

Our server was good, but the place was packed on a Wednesday.  Our dinner took over an hour from order to arrival and that is just ridiculous. It's new and they have to get the kinks out, so I'll be back in the next month or so.  Aside from that, I think they may break the curse of that particular location and be a successful joint.

Honestly, sometimes I just marvel at what people expect from a restaurant.  No, they are not there to talk you off a ledge, listen to the dreams you had the other night or provide happy endings.  They have great food and the service was fine.  Excellent actually.  Maybe they listened to what people wrote here, or maybe (as so often is the case) the Indy crowd is cookoo bananas.  In any case, we shared a cup of lentil w/ smoked sausage (my wiife loved, I liked) and the best damn clam chowder I've had in a very long time.  I mean,  chock filled with clams and a creamy velvety richness that almost brought me to tears.  BAM!  But wait, there's more!  The double cheeseburger was ah-maaaa-zing!  Crispy thin patties that seriously give Workingman's Friend a run for their money.  Since I was sober for this burger, it may of been better actually.  Jury is still out.  My wife had the best damn BLT ever.  I'm sorry people, if you want Oscar Mayer bacon, go to Marshes and fix yourself a sammy.  The meat was thick and well seasoned...amazing.  And the tomato jam on it really completed the dish.  The portion of coleslaw was a bit chauncy, true that.  But great horney toads is it f'n amazing.  Dip into your wallets and splurge for the bigger size.  

The place is not cheap, but it can't be any less expensive if you want the quality they provide.  That goofy Guy had it right brining this place to the masses.  Now, it's our turn to keep it alive and right where it is...

We love this place and come here regularly. The portions are huge, prices low and service friendly and attentive. D Nice is the friendliest person I've ever met. The restaurant is also very clean and inviting. As far as the food goes, we love the Judys plate (insane amount of good food) and the Western. Order anything with bacon and you get like 8 slices worth and it very good. Great sausage too. The lunch potions are gy normous. The tenderloin and Groupon sandwiches are massive beyond words and like under $7. The BLT is amazing and should be world famous, but I'll settle for best in Midtown. The only items I personally don't care for our the daily specials like meatloaf or chop steak, but that's me.  The menu items are the way to roll. I hate waiting for a table so please feel free to ignore this and move along. Move along!!!

This place is about as average as you can get. I give 3 but it is a true 2.5. The chips are no better then store bought but are a little warm. The salsa on the table is fresh and blended with fresh tomatoes but nothing to write home about. I had the steak Colorado which was smokey and tender. Not a bad choice considering. It came wth a side of flower tortillas that were warm and a side of gauc that was fresh but bland. I mean, the consistency was good, just no flavor. The retried beans and rice were ok. I've had better, but certainly have had worse. At least the rice was warm and not sticky. The service was average as well. No real attention and my server seemed to care more about why the chicken crossed the road. It filled the void but that's about it.

There's a lot to like about this place. The owner is very cool. The food is pretty great. The rib tips (only on weekends) are fantastic and he seems to always run out. The chicken is always perfect, not over breaded and moist and succulent inside. If you like thin burgers with the crispy edges, he's got it.  Kinda  like what you'd think steak and shake once was way back in a day. 

Now, why not 5 Stars?  I don't know if this place is a passion project but he's never open around meal times. I drive up and down 46th all the time and the dude is almost never open. Forget the posted hours, that's just a suggestion. I can go on because this really drives be bat sh&@. but let me just suggest you call first and we can leave it at that. 

Those who come here... you know what I'm talking about!

So I've been here twice and my experience was not the same. The first time was for lunch and both my friend and I ordered the meatballs as recommended by our server, and drank ice teas. The ice tea was fantastic. Very flavorful and dark. The meatballs were also exceptionally tasty. They are brought in a bowl with a delicious marinara sauce and sit on a bed of polenta and topped with broccolini. Despite the wait for the food and a crazy long wait for the check and for them to run the cards, it was a very nice lunch. Great ambiance and friendly staff, although the "community" service idea (any and all staff can help you once the meals are ordered) is a hot mess. 

I brought the wife the following weekend. There was a long wait but luckily we were able to belly up to the bar and ordered bourbon specialty cocktails. The cherry old fashioned was our favorite. Too notch cocktail. The peach bourbon was a bit sweet but not terrible. This was by far the only redeeming aspect of our dinner. When we got seated I immediately ordered another old fashion, that never came. Well, not until we got up to leave. My wife had the burger and it was terrible. No, really.  Well done is an understatement. I had the shrimp bowl and it was disgusting.  The breaded tiny shrimp (you know, the ones you're afraid to eat at a buffet) were terrible and the combination of flavors didn't work at all. Not what I would expect from a place that has wait times approaching 2 hours on the weekend. Not for long I bet. The staff was doing their best but were in the weeds big time. I can let that go. Anywhere else we would have sent both meals back, but we hardly had the time to wait for a redo. They couldn't even get us a drink.  I hope they get it together. I really want to make this place a regular spot, but they got some work to do.  The give it 3 stars as a blended average.

Awful!!!  I went with a friend for lunch. He had the briquet sand which is served on Texas toast. It was terribly dry and tasteless. I had the half slab of ribs (award wining no less) and they were basically meatless. It was eating dry bones with bbq sauce slathered on em. The sides sucked as well.  The Mac and cheese tasted like the box Kraft stuff.  The baked beans were decent, so that's basically iwhat I could eat. I went due to the 3 1/2 star rating but man, I don't get it. The only redeeming feature was the service was friendly and I didn't get food poising. Avoid!

3 1/2 more like it, but definitely not 4. Stopped in for lunch and had a the egg and chorizo special. Worth the $7. The manager was very friendly and it was pleasant atmosphere. The tortilla chips brought were very good but the salsa was average. A bit watered down and bland for my taste. The entree was decent. Portion size reasonable. I rolled 4 small tacos out of my portion. Eggs and rice were good, but the beans tasted they came out of a can. Bland, nearly tasteless. The soda was the size of a super big gulp which my only complaint being I hate wasting food and there was no way I was finishing it. They are very generous in that department.  Indy offers better Mexican food for sure, but I've had much worse.

No longer the only game in town


This place is great when they are open. WHEN THEY ARE OPEN. I have gone now 5x during posted open hours and and they haven't been there. 10/5 2pm closed. A Friday late afternoon etc etc. the first 4 times I laughed it off, but I'm done. Their pie is amazing but there are now other options. Great meals like the salmon, and fantastic fruit. The tomatoes and peaches are also fantastic when in season. Expensive but worth every penny. I've adored this little gem but I'm done peering threw the glass doors like the fat kid outside the bakery. Post a sign if you're gone for the day hmmmm? I'm sure the poor shlubs who travelled to be there would appreciate it. This one is spending his dough where it is needed more. Adios.

Thank you for your delicious food, amazing brew and dedication to the safety of the health and well being in our community. Your chai and plain black coffee is top notch. Full of flavor and your staff attentive. Will be back soon.

I really enjoyed our lunch. The smash burgers are epic. Crispy patties with lots of flavor. I would recommend the house burger but you can build your own with very fresh options and unique sauces. Both the fries and onion rings are top notch, and the side salad was great. The salad was not your usual dinky side, but flavorful lettuce and veggies.  Cool decor and greet service makes this place a complete lunch spot.

This place is like the Hill House for diabetics. The donuts are the best I've had in Indiana and are in the same zip as the best around Chicagoland. Ive only had the iced coffee because it's summer, but I always get it when I'm there and it's solid. The highlight for me however, is the bread. I've had the wheat, cheese and bacon and white and I can't express enough just how incredible they all are. Bread is available on Tuesday and Fridays I believe and are about $5 a loaf, which isn't bad considering the quality. I popped in on a whim and am now a regular.

This place is fantastic. Because it's a small operation with huge demand, it's going to be a wait, especially on the weekends. I've ordered here a half dozen times now and every time told an hour for orders to be ready and at best it took 115 to an hour thirty. If this kind of thing bothers you, move elsewhere. They do their best with what they have to work with and the quality is always excellent. 

Specifically, we always get the butter chicken, tandoori chicken and garlic naan. All of which is very flavorful and consistent. When we venture out of our comfort zone, we've tried various apps and dishes and they never disappoint. I'm great full to have such a fantastically authentic spot in our hood. The Broad Ripple options are by far the weakest compared to Carmel, Caslteton and Lafayette Corridor and this place ranks right up with the best of them. 

Be patient and good things will come your way.

R7oqm48wW0h0n2veJOdJlw.review_text: I visited Manakeesh on a whim with a friend for lunch. It was my first experience with Lebanese food and I was more than a bit reluctant. But wow! The food (we ordered sujuk, falafel, & tiramisu) was phenomenal. Very nice atmosphere, spacious yet cozy, decent prices, and a seemingly friendly staff. Will most definitely be returning!

Seriously, the best pizza you will ever have.. No joke.

I have been visiting Cacia's since I was a kid on weekend trips to South Philly for Cacia's pizza and Cannuli's cheese sausage (also great). Their prices have always been much cheaper than any other shop around. My favorite is the white & pizazz. They also have great roast pork sandwiches on the weekends. My only dislike is the small space.. On the weekends the line is usually out the door.. and it moves painfully slow. My best recommendation is to call ahead and place your order. They're also cash only.

I visited Bistro La Baia with a group of 11 for a holiday work party. The staff was extremely accommodating even when we called 10 minutes prior to our reservation and said we were running late and needed to add an extra head to our table. We were seated immediately and were assisted in opening our wine bottles. Orders were taken promptly and appetizers and bread (amazing or maybe I was just starving by this point) were served. Our food came out in a rather reasonable time for our large party. But it's the food were the lack of star comes in.. 
Prior to my visit to La Baia, I peaked at their menu and yelp profile and knew I wanted to try the lobster ravioli as it seemed to be a fan favorite. I found mine to be lacking, literally. There were a total of 5 ravioli on the plate. I actually had to pace myself while eating or I would have been done in minutes. The light cognac sauce had the similar robust flavor of canned spaghettiOs. Absolutely dreadful. However most of my group appeared more than pleased with their meal. The pricing was also standard at about $20 a person. 
If I do return to La Baia, I will be trying something else on the menu. Suggestions?
Like most have said: cheap, quick, and good. Serves only pho but you will not be disappointed. Attentive staff, spacious, and good parking.

This is probably one of my hardest reviews.. I have serious mixed emotions about Federal Donuts, allow me to explain. The first time I had their fancy donuts, I was in love. I've tried piña colada, lemon poppy, passion fruit brown sugar, apple walnut, indian cinnamon, vanilla lavender.. All phenomenal, no exaggeration. However I was fortunate enough to have these donuts brought to me from a friend. So when he suggested going to Federal Donuts for chicken, I was totally up for it given I had no idea of what I was in store for.. It was a massacre. Lines, chaos, complete and udder disorganization. Note this establishment is NOT for the anxious. We waited well over an hour (#43) for a half chicken and 3 donuts in a cramped space. We ordered the Za'tar which is one of their dry chickens. It was quite good but most definitely not worth that kind of wait. I for surely will never make the trip to Federal Donuts again, send someone else in for the dirty work.

Came to Carman's with a friend for brunch. Small space, a few tables and barstools, and strange decor - there were quite a few penis and breast decorations. I ordered the butter milk pancakes (sweet summer corn, apples, dates, and crushed walnuts in the batter) and my friend ordered the lamb stew I believe. Prior to coming, we were driving around looking for a quick but satisfying meal and my friend assured me that Carman's specialized in quick yet satisfying brunch foods so off we went. However we weren't served so quickly in fact a couple who entered a good 10 minutes after us were served first. But when our food came so did a complimentary kale omelet for our wait. The pancakes were above average but nothing to write home about, my friend seemed to thoroughly enjoy his meal and I just couldn't get over how delicious the kale omelet was. It was a tad pricey for breakfast at about $20 (with tip) a person but if you go for brunch ( having this meal take the place of two) then it's worth it. Though there seem to be quite a few people who have made Carman's a regular breakfast spot of theirs, I'm not sure if I'll return.

One word comes to mind when I think of Silk City.. Overrated. Admittedly diners do usually fall low on my "where to eat" list and it took a bit of convincing from a friend to actually enter this establishment, it was still a dive experience from the get go. We ordered the garlic crusted mac & cheese as an appetizer, it was mediocre at best. On to browsing through the menu.. I was pretty set on ordering the grilled portabella sandwich only to be informed by the waitress that they no longer offer that sandwich. Call it a pet peeve, but it bothers me beyond belief when something is listed on a menu but not available to order. I settled for the grilled chicken sandwich, dry chicken - soggy bun. I have no comment on my friend's order aside from the fish n chips reeking of grease. Their fries is what earned them two stars in my book.

Agreeably, Cafe Lift is a decent brunch spot.. But there are much better options in the city. The wait to be seated wasn't so bad however the wait to served was quite long. Prior to going I scoped out their yelp profile and knew I wanted to order the eggs florentine (served on focaccia bread with crab meat and a side of potatoes) however it was not actually listed on the menu. They did accommodate and serve the eggs florentine along with my friends eggs benedict. I don't know if it was because of my "special order" that our orders took so long to come to us.. Or if it was because the wait staff was more interested in chatting with one another rather than serving. My OJ was also forgotten. The meal itself would have been fantastic had it been more than slightly warm. But again this could be chalked up to the inattentive staff. Ill be going elsewhere for breakfast and brunch in the city, you should probably do the same.

What a pleasant surprise. Yet again, being the reluctant, stuck in my food ways and the restaurants I feel comfortable in, I drug my feet and whined like a child "but whhhhyy can't we go to Sam's!?" to my boyfriend the entire walk into Teri's. We were going for brunch and able to be seated immediately. What? No wait? Unheard of at any other brunch spot on a weekend. The menu is a little lacking but what they do serve does not disappoint. I ordered the banana walnut pancakes and the bf ordered the spinach bacon and feta cheese omelet. My oh my... Absolutely amazing. I'm drooling at the thought. Infact after I finish this review, I'm going to go eat my leftovers until I fall into a delicious food coma. I can't wait to go back to try their omelets and to have another peak at that gorgeous waiter. Plus so much more reasonably priced than other spots in town. Highly recommended.

Walking around town on a Friday night looking for a place to eat with no reservations and it being restaurant week, I was sure we would be eating at a dive or heading home to make tacos.. Not the case! We stumbled upon Xochitl and my boyfriend remembered hearing good things about it so in we went. We barely waited 3 minutes before being seated. Pretty decent given the circumstances. As it was restaurant week, Xochitl had a fixed 4 course menu at $35 a person. The meal started off with a customizable guacamole (we added red onion, roasted garlic, and cilantro) so yummy and the tortilla chips were perfectly crisp with just enough saltiness. Then on to the first course: we chose the cheese filled empanadas and some type of flat bread with mushrooms and cheese. I must admit that though good, the first courses were a tad bland. For example the flat bread could have used a little squeeze of citrus. For main courses, I ordered the short rib (served with a potato gordita and roasted veggies) and bf ordered the pollo frito (served with cornbread and greens) at the waiter's recommendation. The short rib was fantastic, perfectly glazed and tender but the potato and veggies were alittle lacking. I can't comment on the pollo frito but the cornbread it was served with was the best I've had yet. For dessert, we ordered the flan and doughnuts (served with both chocolate and strawberry dipping sauces). Both were very good. I also cannot comment on the drinks but if I visit again, I will most definitely give them a try. If you haven't been to Xochitl, I recommend giving it a go.

With all of the positive feedback and review Los Gallos is receiving, I know my personal review will hold little significance but it is not stopping me from writing! I have visited Los Gallos on multiple occasions and have even had their to go service and was more than pleased every time. My favorite is the Al pastor(no cheese, please). The portions and pricing are on point. The service and cleanliness are too. Highly recommended authentic Mexican!

Had a great Saturday evening dinner at Memphis Taproom. To start we ordered the pork rillons and watermelon salad, light and refreshing - perfect for a summer night and at the waitress' recommendation, their signature beer battered dills - it is an absolute MUST order.
 The small plates alone were enough to satisfy but onto the entrees.. I ordered the chicken fried portobello sandwich (the basil mayo is like the icing on the cake) and my friend ordered the fish and chips. Both very satisfying as well. We actually left with a good bit of leftovers being so full from the appetizers and I found it very thoughtful that the waitress took the time to mark each container with what was inside. Maybe it's just me, but it's the little things that can really make or break a dining experience. I wish I remembered her name to give her a big, public thank you. 

Ps - I also recommend asking your waiter/waitress about the bottle specials of the night. Great deals all round.

I have had Porcini bookmarked for months with the intention of giving this cute little byo a go, and last night I finally had my chance. We actually made the "reservation" on the drive over through open table via yelp (super convenient - other restaurants need to get on board). We started out with the grilled octopus and baby calamari appetizer.. Light and refreshing. I ordered the ravioli in a pecorino cream sauce and my boyfriend ordered the spaghetti and seafood (shrimp & scallops) special. My dish was excellent and similar to the appetizer, I was surprised at the freshness of the seafood in my boyfriend's entree however his pasta was over cooked. We also redeemed the check in offer for the free dessert but I couldn't tell you much about it as the boyfriend ate it all to make up for his lack of entree. Poor guy. The staff here is all seemingly very friendly and I'm sure they would have redone the dish had he asked. 

Overall, I may come back but I do think there are better byo options in the city on a similar price scale.

Strolling down Passyunk Ave today, my boyfriend and I were browsing the neighborhood brunch spots to grab a bite to eat. Passing Plenty, we both remembered hearing good things so we decided to wait the 15 minutes until they opened at 12pm... Fast forward 25 minutes or so, and in we went. We were both craving breakfast-y food so we fixated on the breakfast menu. Plenty offers around 5 breakfast options, different variations of egg sandwiches and a greek yogurt. However when my boyfriend went to order, his first request to change the fried egg to scrambled (which is offered in other breakfast options) was responded with the cashier asking a fellow coworker "are we still doing no order modifications?" um okay... She then went to check with the cook if they were even serving the breakfast menu, they weren't. The cashier then pulled down the breakfast menu.. Us knowing that we wanted breakfast decided to go elsewhere but my boyfriend proceeded to pick up a chocolate bar and went to get a drink out of the beverage cooler to which the one coworker said to the other "I guess I'll wait all day to finish this transaction". Mind you, we were the only potential diners at Plenty during this entire "transaction". His grabbing of a drink took probably 25 seconds and our entire experience maybe 4 minutes. Not that it needs to be justified.. Their sandwiches may be good but I wouldn't know as I will never be returning. I'll stick to Paesano's where the sandwiches AND customer service are great.

Before the close, I was a Border's gal - I mean I never even stepped foot into a Barnes & Noble until Borders was packed up and gone. But eventually one must move on... I'll start with the location, absolutely fantastic - especially if you happen to be in the Starbucks on the second floor - great view of the park. However this is unlikely as this bookstore is typically PACKED (free wifi, open outlets, heat/ac, etc). If you were to order something from the Starbucks (which I wouldn't recommend - every order I've placed here has been messed up in some sort of way), you probably won't get a seat so that view I mentioned - enjoy it while awaiting your order. 

Moving on... The layout is kind of all over the place and a bit cramped. I also wish they had the computers for patrons to use to search a book and find it's location. I always feel like I'm bothering the employees asking where something is located, only to find out they don't have it in stock anyhow.

On the plus side, they have a public bathroom, cute knick knacks, and the greeters are always super friendly.

UPDATE: They have a 3rd floor! It's a real bookstore after all. +1 star!

Hmph. My boyfriend and I had a little dinner date at Mercato this past Saturday night. It being Restaurant Week, I was sure we would have a wait but we were seated right away. Though chilly, we opted to dine outside as the restaurant itself is very loud. We started off with appetizers: charred caesar salad and a bruschetta plate - both quite good especially the anchovies in the salad however I would have appreciated a tad more dressing. For our main dishes I went with the pappardelle and my boyfriend ordered the diver scallops. This is where the night took a turn in the wrong direction... The lag between appetizers and entrees was a whole bottle of pouilly-fuissé and at least an hour later. The entrees were just okay and the vanilla bean panna cotta was disappointing to say the least. Thankfully this was all at the restaurant week $35/pp 3 course menu. I doubt I'll return to pay full price for the quality Mercato serves.

Rembrandt's has become my go to brunch spot. The wait, if at all, is never an issue. The menu is classic yet has a few interesting bits (try the parmesan truffle frites - they'll serve them as a side) and of course their alcohol selection is a plus. But what really makes this place is the servers.. Last weekend when my boyfriend and I stopped in for brunch, his coffee took a little long to come out but we honestly hadn't even noticed until our waitress, Hannah - I believe, said it was on the house. You can tell Rembrandt's truly cares about pleasing their customers.

I have been to my fair share of pubs and such for brunch and unfortunately Standard Tap doesn't do it for me. I agree with Jill L.'s review below and the 3 fatal flaws of Standard Tap - no Internet publishing of their menu, no in-hand menu at the pub (you read off of a chalkboard), and no descriptions. 

My Saturday brunch included a ham & pepper scramble (no further description necessary) and a mimosa. All very... Standard. I do however like the two floor set up and overall atmosphere.

On a scale from Monsu to Modo Mio, well Popolino isn't even on it. However if you have not yet dined here, I still recommend giving it go. As others have mentioned, Popolino is not your mom & pop red sauce Italian restaurant. The dishes here vary, from safe to adventurous. Play around, Popolino (like Monsu and Modo Mio) offers a turista - a great way to explore the menu. Also don't forget a bottle of wine or three.

Another stroll down Passyunk, led my boyfriend and I to a late dinner at Sophia's. We were standing outside peaking at their in window menu when two diners came out exclaiming how great the food was.. All I can say now is, I feel mislead. The restaurant itself is beautiful, the staff is all seemingly friendly, the bar is stocked and the drinks are fantastic however the food is just okay. Every plate we tried seemed like something was missing or just off. Thank heaven for dessert. The pastry chef they are working with right now knows what he/she is doing! Yum. Btw I normally don't mention cost in my reviews as I don't mind paying for quality however I'm still trying to wrap my head around our bill.. Either our 1 dessert was $35 or we were overcharged.

In Riva has been in my YELP bookmarks for months and this past weekend, my boyfriend and I finally made the trip to Manayunk to check it out. For starters, I love the lay out - we were seated in what I believe is called "the library", a little nook section with a few tables. We ordered the crispy pork belly as an appetizer. Super yummy and I question whether they serve 3 pieces.. so that couples fight over the last piece and then just order a second plate? (We split ours). Moving on we ordered the pizza margherita with white anchovy and nastrini pasta (both to share). The pizza was a let down, very doughy and had a burnt aftertaste as the crust was burnt. I had hoped we just had a bad pizza but I noticed others were coming out like this as well. To be honest, I had MUCH better pizza at California Pizza Kitchen. The nastrini was good but not memorable. For dessert we shared zeppole, I thought it was great - the boyfriend wasn't all too impressed though. A very mediocre experience with an expensive wine bill overall.

Dear Bobby's,
Please consider different buns to compliment individual burgers. 
Signed, Caroline

Stopped by Bobby's with the boyfriend for a bite to eat not too long ago and have been meaning to write a review.. I ordered the napa valley burger w/ ground turkey, very interesting indeed. The flavors worked great together and I really liked the utilization of goat cheese. I just wish there were different buns, Bobby's appears to serve all burgers on the same seeded plain bun. Boring and doughy, I almost went bunless but would have lost all of the yummy lemon honey mustard. We also split an order of sweet potato fries - a must order - and a black and white shake - overpriced and under stimulating. 3/5 stars for Bobby, I've had better but I've for sure had worse.

Recently I had a late evening dinner with my boyfriend at The Mildred and was very impressed. We went in without reservations and were still able to be seated immediately in the bar area by the fire, very warm and inviting indeed. The wait staff was very prompt and polite so needless to say the service was impeccable. 

I ordered a glass of wine while the boyfriend tried out their mixed drinks with the "peasant's revolt" - he loved it. For first courses, I had the winter lettuce and my boyfriend had the escargot. We shared the scallops, just wow. And for entrees, I had the tavern steak and my boyfriend ordered the chicken breast. Words will not do this place justice, give it a try. I cannot wait to go back and taste their bouillabaisse!

I truly adore Little Saigon. It is a small, family owned business that makes you think you are the first customer that has ever walked through their doors with the way they greet you. I have been there on numerous occasions and have ordered quite a few different bits off the menu and everything is done extraordinarily well. (Pretty generic but try their spring rolls - they are better than anywhere I've tried.) Another review stated the line "made with love and served with care" and I could not agree more. The older gentleman (grandfather, I believe) that buses the tables, is always there filling your water glass after each sip, bringing napkins, etc..  

My only peeve with Little Saigon is that because it is a family owned business, they can open/close as they wish. I cannot tell you how many trips I've made to a closed restaurant and had to settle for Pho down the street (I call ahead now). But other than that, Little Saigon is a gem. If you're in the suburbs and need a pho fix, this is the place to go!

I'm not one for ball park food: A) it's way overpriced B) the lines are ridiculous and C) the food is usually mediocre at best. Well while watching the Phillies be absolutely destroyed by the Mets (seriously boys, what's goin' on?), I couldn't help but notice my seat mate's food, a Campo's cheesesteak to be exact. After another home run by the Mets, I thought to myself the food can't be any worse than the game. 

So we made are way down to Campo's and as expected, there was a long line. But it wasn't as bad as I thought, I was surprisingly entertained by other game goers and interested in how they order their cheesesteaks. How do I order mine? American, onions, and sweet peppers with a sprite please. This totaled $16, a bit steep as expected but you can pay by card at the ball park and my sprite came in a snazzy phanatic souvenir cup. 

After a few squirts of ketchup, I was ready to dig in. Have I mentioned yet I'm not a big cheesesteak fan? Born and raised in the suburbs of Philadelphia and I've had them all Pat's, Geno's, Steve's and I would always honor my own mother with the best cheesesteak award however Campo's comes close. Yummy, well cut goodness not greasy or sloppy and dressed with cheese perfectly! Not to mention these things are ready for you in the blink of an eye.

Next time you're at Citizen's Bank Park, I recommend stopping at Campos!

I want to like Hawthorne's, truly I do. I like the  concept ("bier cafe"), the decor (and who doesn't like oj in a mason jar?), the staff is all seemingly friendly however the overall experience is inconsistent. Hawthorne's is a bit larger than other brunch spots in the city and they also have outdoor seating but you will still have a wait (Average 10-20 minutes for a 2 top).

 If you haven't already been to Hawthorne's, check out their online menu - their selection all sounds drool worthy however what is actually served is not. The final straw being brunch this past weekend in which I ordered the steak & eggs (served with a mozzarella salad & balsamic vinaigrette). The steak was well and tender but the over easy egg was over cooked around the edges and under cooked near the yolk, practically inedible. Sorry but I'll stick to a brunch spot that can cook an egg.

Yikes. In 2012, we frequented Teri's as our go to spot for brunch and I even wrote a four star review. Fast forward to this weekend in which we walked out (after paying for our OJs of course) after waiting 50 minutes to be served. This may be the norm for a heavily trafficked brunch spot in the city but not a diner with no more than 5 booths. 35 minutes after ordering our waitress comes by to ask what we ordered again as the cook was asking the couple at the bar if they were "in a rush" as it may be awhile. I have never experienced such poor, careless service. What happened Teri's?

Like some of the more recent flockers to Brigid's, I had my first meal there after hearing it had "consultation" from Mr. Peter Mcandrews. And after my second visit, I'm ready to review. 

I don't know where to begin to properly explain my love for Brigid's... Perhaps it's that you can in fact walk in and be seated right away on a Saturday night. Or that the servers are all extremely knowledgable of the menu and full of recommendations. Or maybe it's the menu itself (Check out the online publishing!), even the bar menu is impressive. Every bite I've had here has been extraordinary - from the bread, to the braised snails, to the panna cotta. If you haven't been to Brigid's, what are you waiting for? And if you have, I'll probably be seeing you again!

I made our reservation for La Calaca Feliz via OpenTable, which is always a plus in my book - I wish other restaurants would get on board, for 6:30pm. We actually ended up with more time than expected and after browsing through the neighborhood, we decided to head into the restaurant around ten after and wait at the bar. We put our names in and the hostess offered us a table, very accommodating. La Calaca has an interesting set up and beautiful decor along with patio/out front seating, we however dined inside. We started with the ceviche rojo and guacamole. We were a bit nervous about the ceviche with beets but it is very well done and perhaps my favorite yet. The guacamole was just okay, I've had better (but most definitely have had worse). We shared the chorizo and carnitas tacos. All tacos come a la carte but they will add rice or beans if asked. The tacos were very good and the meat so flavorful but I think a slightly thicker tortilla may make for a more sturdy taco. We also ordered a side of plantains for a bit of sweetness, they were everything I had hoped for. I cannot begin to describe the amazing-ness that is their white sangria and cinnamon churro vanilla ice cream, both are most orders so save room for dessert (we boxed some taco).. BF even liked the coffee and he is quite the coffee snob. 

Side note - I never once felt rushed as other yelpers have mentioned, in fact we ended up dining for well over an hour and a half.

I absolutely adore this store! I have visited this location since I was a kid with flare eczema.. And now after switching to a GF diet (migraine trigger), it is basically my go to food market (and the prices for GF items are more reasonable than in the supermarkets).The selection is HUGE and they are always stocking new, local, interesting products. The staff is so helpful and friendly. And they have a monthly magazine! I can't rave enough, check it out for yourself! You'll be exploring for at least an hour!

Quick recommendation:
Canyon bakehouse rosemary & thyme focaccia

Oh Giorgio, I think I love you! Okay maybe not you (he is a sweet guy!) but your menu. I was convinced that I would never be able to order pasta dishes at restaurants.. Not only could I but given a full array of gluten free options (peak at their menu online). GF bread, GF dessert.. I was in food heaven. The staff is super friendly and menu aware. Oh did I forget to mention, we made our "reservation" 2 hours prior to dining? Giorgio said "no problem friend." I'll most definitely be back and I recommend this place to everyone not just those who are gluten free!

Quick and convenient yet original and keeps its regulars. I started visiting La Va for brunch about a year ago primarily on the weekends when in town with the  BF. However BF has been coming for years and rates La Va highly amongst other coffee shops in the area. I normally go for the Greek omelet with an OJ, consistently good. 

So that long wait across the street at Honeys? Forget it - walk right in to La Va.

I dined at Azie (Media location) recently with a few coworkers on a weeknight. I have to say that this is probably one of the loudest restaurants I've been to. I quickly gave up attempting to actually listen to the table's conversation and instead focused on my wine glass, nodding in agreement every so often.  

The table ordered quite a few different appetizers for sharing including the rock shrimp tempura, spicy tuna tartare, and miso chicken lettuce cups. The tempura and tuna tartare were okay but I have had better elsewhere. The presentation of the lettuce cups reminded me of high school lunch room food.. Needless to say, I passed on these. 

I ordered the diver scallops without bacon (the waitress assured me that the bacon was primarily for flavor so I felt comfortable nixing it). Scallops are served on a crepe like bed with arugula, sautéed calamari and cherry tomatoes. What is not included in the description (just double checked on Azie's website) is shaved cauliflower. I know not too horrible but it was practically inedible in the way it was prepared and served (large shavings that were hard to cut let alone swallow). All in all, I did enjoy my entree and would recommend this to others if you're planning to dine at Azie. 

For dessert I had creme brûlée and again okay but I have had better. In conclusion if given the opportunity, do not settle in the suburbs.. We all know the food is better in the city.

When my BF told me about this awesome hot chocolate he had that cost over $10 I asked if he got to keep the mug... $10+ for hot chocolate is absolutely absurd, right? WRONG! 

Rim cafe and it's owner Rene make for one unforgettable experience. Upon first walking into Rim cafe, your eyes do not know where to glance first. The decor is dark and the place is a bit cluttered (so if you're reading this before visiting, walk in - continue straight and then turn right!). The music is always on.. 'Applebottom jeans', 'Naughty girl'... It's like tacky tracks of early 2000, Rene knows all the words, dances along & I adore him for it. 

Rene will spot you walking in and if you have any questions, want a recommendation, whatever - he is on it! Then you will watch your drink be prepared! He'll go through each and every chocolate he is shaving - which I thoroughly appreciate (peanut allergy). We normally get the salted caramel and it is out of this world.  I tell everyone about Rim cafe and think it's the perfect spot to bring out of town visitors. Check it out!

I almost do not want to review Porto to keep their greatness under wraps. But all is fair in love and food so here it goes... Porto is a cozy little brunch spot with a drool worthy menu. BF & I visited last weekend and ordered the cinnamon raisin bread (great value at $6) and the Porto special (scrambled eggs, pierogies, and kielbasa for breakfast?! Yes please!). Both dishes were done very well. Their staff is also kind and upbeat which always makes the experience that much more enjoyable (I believe I was here the same day as Carter P. during the transformer blow). I will most definitely be back and hopefully I don't need a reservation (yep, it's that good)!

I've been to Victor Cafe quite a few times in the past few years and the service has been average. I have always visited as a 2 top so getting a table was never an issue (practically no wait time) and now that you can make reservations on OpenTable, it is a breeze. Parking is standard for South Philly so the complaints about that are kind of laughable. Waiters and waitresses have always been friendly but seem a bit flustered (I think this is because I typically go on a Saturday evening - one of their busier times). The music, though phenomenal, is very date night-esque and a bit touristy IMO. For someone who is just going out for good Italian fare, I might recommend you go elsewhere - you could end up with a migraine (been there, done that). 

I was unimpressed with the calamari appetizer (very chewy) however their salads are good (I personally like the arugula salad). The crespelle is also very good and makes for a nice sharing app for two. The reason for my continuous return is the meat tortellini bellini. Fantastic. And I don't even care for bacon or peas on their own but in this dish - yum. The BF however has had a few poorly done dishes. On our most visit recent, his entree was served with a side of risotto. The risotto was way undercooked. Poor guy. I haven't tried anything on their dessert menu, I have glanced at it and nothing sounded all that interesting but who knows! 

Overall unless you're going for the music, I'd suggest elsewhere for Italian especially with what you'd fork out in $$$ at Victor's.

I had dinner at Nonna's this past Saturday. A party of 4 and able to make last minute reservations via OpenTable is always a plus. This was my first time dining here and though it wasn't our first choice for dinner, others in my party had dined here in the past and spoke highly of it.. Unfortunately this will also be my last time dining here.

Agh where to begin.. Drinks. I ordered the Nonna's cocktail, I don't remember the dazzling details of what this cocktail was actually to be composed of but what I received was raspberry lemonade and gin. I think most would've sent the drink back but I love raspberry lemonade so I didn't mind much. 

For appetizers we had the calamari. This was not my choice and after my questionable cocktail, I wouldn't have trusted Nonna's with squid. To my surprise, this dish was quite tasty. I will note that in the description online it states there is an option for grilled or fried, we were not presented that option and served fried. 

There wasn't much of a selection for entrees dishes... BF and I both chose the lamb bolognese but what we were served was ground beef. Yes most definitely ground beef. The pappardelle was cooked to perfection and the sauce flavorful but each bite of meat was close to infuriating me. At $19 (still one of their cheapest plates), I should've said something but did not. Our fellow diners and WC residents, informed us that Nonna's is under new ownership and will soon have a new name, Avalon.. Not a good impression even if still under the old restaurant's name.

We've visited One Shot a handful of times for weekend brunch. It's not nearby but when in the neighborhood, we'll stop by. I'd consider them a coffee shop that *happens* to do food very well. I've noticed others getting frustrated because they are expecting more of a waiter type experience... You will not find that at One Shot. You will however find knowledgable, polite, time efficient baristas. 

I love the Moroccan scramble and was absolutely devastated when Fall rolled around and so did One Shot's new seasonal menu sans the scramble. However one must move on (at least until the spring/summer menu is back). On our most recent visit, I had a daily special (I checked their online website for name but it's not listed) which was basically an egg white, cherry tomatoes, avocado, arugula, and goat cheese sandwich. The sandwich is normally served on brioche but they were out so I chose rye toast and still found it to be pretty tasty. I am always tempted to try their pastries and desserts which look fantastic but we shared a samoa cookie and I wasn't impressed. There was far too much caramel, it weighed down the cookie and was wet. 

Also I wanted to quickly mention the overall set up and decor of One Shot.. It's awesome. There is seating downstairs, upstairs, out front and along the side - it's a place where you'll definitely be able to get in right away. Others have brought up One Shot's costs.. I think they are comparable with other places in the area. You're not going to find decent breakfast food for much less, sorry friend.

This review is solely for Margaret Kuo's MEDIA location. I say this first because I have only heard great things about their Wayne and Malvern spots however MK Media just doesn't equal up. 

I came with a rather large party (12 heads) and our reservations were made about a week in advance via OpenTable yet there was 1 server for our large party... In fact, he seemed to be the only server there (Friday night). Our drink orders weren't taken for about an hour into our visit. Then it was a continuous struggle trying to get his attention to place appetizer and entree orders (A few in our party actually left because they hadn't anticipated spending 5 hours out for dinner). 

When the waiter was taking my order, I repeated myself a few times because he seemed to be drifting off into outer space and he also was not writing anything down. So I was not entirely shocked that when meals were served there were a few entrees missing. However when we asked the waiter about this I was shocked by his careless reply, "you didn't order that"... Um okay. Not even a "I'm sorry" or "Can I put that in now for you?".. Very awkward. 

Also what is actually served is kind of laughable. Two in our party ordered the Chilean sea bass, one's fish was literally twice the size of the others... The only difference? The sauces they chose. I wasn't impressed by the majority of the menu and it is definitely overpriced for what you are getting. 

Skip the dessert menu. Everything that is worth ordering they no longer have and the rest is awful.

... Just do your wallet a favor and skip Margaret Kuo's Media entirely.

Coworkers and I order from Double Decker probably once a week for lunch. Their service is always consistent.. Fast, fresh and good. This may sound like total blasphemy but I don't get the inside outs... The individuals that do and then later complain about how sick it made them - you chose to eat large amounts of fried dough! Fools. Anyway I recommend the pita pizza - it's the perfect sized individual pizza (cheese and sauce on rolled out pita). I also really enjoy their gyros and salads (I like the Greek).. 

They are upfront about their delivery times (I've learned to call a little earlier is all). I don't believe there is a minimum CC charge and you can add driver's tip to the CC as well... Next time you order out give Double Decker a try!

If you're looking to decompress and enjoy some authentic Mexican in the area, Plaza Garibaldi is where to go. The answer as to why is plain & simple... They have a bar and Karla can make a mean margarita or should I say 7. The service has always been consistent and quick. The food fresh, plentiful and good. Don't skip by this little hole in the wall... You'll regret it!

I've been to quite a few vineyards mostly throughout Europe but have never experienced the hospitality that Va La offers. If you don't know much about this vineyard or its owners, I recommend taking a peak at their website and maybe you'll see what I mean (seriously do it!). The owner Anthony and his wife are both very sociable and mingle with vineyard guests all while offering a little wine 101.

During the tasting, a few of the wines are accompanied by an assortment of chocolates and cheeses. These are all local and available for purchase within the vineyard. My personal favorite combination was the silk wine and wine infused chocolates. Very good. It is a bit pricy but you're paying for quality all while supporting a local business. I'll most definitely be back!

3.5 stars... 

I came with 3 others during Restaurant Week to celebrate a coworker's birthday. We made reservations via OpenTable without issue however it seems they overbooked for that random Tuesday evening and we ended up waiting about 25 minutes on top of our reservation to be seated... We dined outside where we could hear each other and enjoy the crisp fall air. It was nice. 

We started with drinks... I ordered the lavender margarita - awful. I mean it got worse with each sip. However others ordered different cocktails and loved them (ie: coconut mojito.. I had a sip of this. It's amazing!). I ended up ordering the sangarita and enjoyed that.

The RW menu had some great picks.. I started with the baked brie (grand marnier-soaked cranberries, pears, hazelnuts, toasted baguette). It was so so good, I highly recommend. For my entree, I opted for the scallops.. These were a bit of a disappointment as only two scallops  (& relatively small in size) were on my plate. It was one of those moments where you take a look around the plate to see if your eyes are deceiving you... Nope just 2! However my dessert - the rum bananas & ice cream -made up for it and my friends all seemed to enjoy their entrees and desserts. 

All in all.. It was a nice experience and I'd go back for drinks and appetizers just maybe not during RW.

Hot chocolate! Hot chocolate! Hot chocolate! I don't care what the weather is like outside, I'm always in the mood. Cafe Crema serves up delicious concocted blends of whatever chocolate you select. I am a fan of the parmesan and caramel chocolates. They compliment each other so well and make for the perfect evening drink. My only complaint is that they are minimizing some of their chocolates because of the warm weather - this took away the parmesan and made for much less tasty hot choc. Baby come back?

More like 2.5 stars...
I wanted to like Brigantessa. Their rustic Italian menu is mouth watering however what's actually served tastes like disappointment.

I dined here on a random Wednesday evening with a friend. We sat upstairs. There was only one other table dining so the service was decent. We started with the burrata and octopus appetizers. The burrata which tasted fairly good itself was paired with carrots and a pistachio purée of sorts. I was curious to see how this was executed... It was very strange especially with nearly raw carrot. The flavors just did not flow. Avoid this dish or at least the carrots in it. In the octopus appetizer, there was arugula, tree nut and you'd expect some sort of fruit but no.. I found sliced potato. It again made for the most awkward combination of flavors.

For main we shared a margherita pizza and the truffle ravioli special. The ravioli was over cooked on the edges however the cream sauce and filling were good. The margherita pizza was just okay. I've had better and I've had worse. I also tried their housemade limoncello. Very strong and a bit pricy... 

Overall I can't say I'll be coming back. There are far too many restaurants in the area that do it better.

Sorry Brigantessa.

I wanted soup. My friend brought me to Good Spoon. I came in, scanned the place and immediately wanted to leave. The words "vegan","vegetarian", & "gluten-free" caught my eye one too many times. I asked my friend if we could leave, I wanted my soup to have flavor after all. He was insistent on staying so he ordered food while I stared at their menu in disgust. 

He ordered the turkey and white bean chili which came with a side of bread. Once I caught a whiff of the chili, I had to have a bite. Then I couldn't stop. It was so good! And the bread. I needed more. I wish I got one of those containers of refrigerated soups on the way out because now I'm craving their turkey chili. 

I'll definitely be back. And will order myself next time.

Oh Modo Mio... 
This cozy Italian BYOB has been a strong and steady for so many years. I can't think of one bad experience I've had here. There are so many positives to this place... BYOB,  the wine and spirit shop directly across the street, the service, turista menu & the food never disappoints. 

A few of my favorites over time would have to be both of their versions of lumache (red wine & lemon), rabbit agnolotti and panna cotta dessert. 

The reason for only 4 stars and not 5? Well 1.The portions are small (keep this in mind - do the turista or you'll leave disappointed/hungry). 2. Because Modo Mio is a smaller restaurant, it tends to get VERY loud in here. 3. No online reservation booking. 

The mentionings above will not discourage me from returning. Modo Mio is among my favorite restaurants.

My go to spot for pho in Delco. Pho 4 Seasons has very convenient hours, parking and delivery. They have an extensive and unique menu with things that I haven't seen at other spots along with daily specials. The restaurant itself is super clean and cute. Staff is always friendly. I highly recommend their Thai tea with jelly & pork summer rolls. Give this place a go for your next pho fix while in Delco, you won't regret it!

Cocco's is a Delco institution. I have ordered from all 3 locations but Primos is my favorite. I recommend a slice Sicilian tomato pie but you can't go wrong with an XL plain cheese either. I have never been disappointed. Traditional, consistent, clean.

The Good King has been in my Yelp bookmarks for sometime and I finally had an opportunity to check it out. A friend and I were in the neighborhood and were lured in by the very tempting menu posted out front of the tavern. 

Unfortunately some of the items on that menu are absent from the current menu. However what is served does not disappoint. I don't remember all of the tasty bits we tried as I also did not neglect their drink menu but the stand outs were the bone marrow and steak frites. Mmm mmm mmm. Try it, you won't regret it. 

-1 star for the menu trickery.. Not what I'd expect from a Good King. Tsk tsk.

Rc3nVXEoEGc8mjL3s5eYyQ.review_text: Terrible food, Sushi was tasteless and tuna and salmon were stale and dry; spicy tuna was mushy and very inedible I did not even eat it ... the sushi rolls had too much hard rice and hardly any fish. The shrimp inside the rolls were all pieces of breading ... so disappointed even the green tea ice cream was awful and old with ice on it - they ran out of mochi ...  so disappointed and service was lacking too!!' I will never go again with the high cost of sushi and the. To be so disappointed!

Poor, slow service when it was empty dining room at 12 pm on a Sunday. We ordered awful greasy fried over-breaded shrimp tacos with no taste.. overly salty colored stale chips. Sad that with an empty dining room you can't get good service on a weekend when most folks golf or take lessons at a country club restaurant with a beautiful view! Plus we were told we could not sit outside On the balcony with those gorgeous views no reasoning ... is it too far for Services's to deliver food or refill water glasses ???
Great pizza for Canasta night with friends... nice thick crust and fresh ingredients....

We had the worst service tonight and were treated so poorly. I made reservations for 5 persons for 4:30pm tonight since we were going to the Little Reno Theater to see Peggy Sue gets an Apartment at 6:30 pm. Brunch was great, but bacon under cooked and fatty not quality thickness bacon... oat, apricot pecan pancakes were yummy

Tasty hot and sour soup, crispy egg rolls and spicy Kao pao chicken... good food and same family owners for over 15 years. It's been a stable for my family on a busy work night with not enough time to cook for the family.

Terrible service and sushi ... not fresh at all... color of sea food and fish off, I had to return a couple of plates ... very cheap on appetizers with no taste... mussels cold with no flavor ... tempura veggies were 3 small pieces the size of a coin... the place has really gone down hill compared to when it was with previous owners!!!
Great food, service and atmosphere !!! Hats off to chef and his delicious menu!!! Flourless chocolate cake was decadent !!!
Great place for breakfast !!! Fun atmosphere and fabulous coffee!!! Located in cool midtown shopping center with great ships to browse

Incredible meal and service !!! The food is very fresh, tasty and healthy if you order correctly!!!

Great service and the pizza is delicious the garlic knots or not bad either .... love the close convenient location in the south of Reno and they use All very fresh ingredients. The crust is So yummy especially dipped in honey !!! The toppings are all first quality and staff is very friendly and kind!!!
Great Steak house with yummy side dishes, hor derves, salads, desert abd wife list. Service is incredible and food is cooked perfectly ... ambiance is fun too!!!
