I had not been to the Egg and I for a couple of years. The food is excellent. I had the bacon spinach omelette with hollandaise sauce. It was well prepared and well cooked without being overdone or dried out. Everything was hot and fresh. The wait staff was friendly. My one little complaint is the hostess is set off to the side where you can't really see her when you first walk in. The register is immediately in front of the door when you walk in so we went to the cashier for seating. It wasn't until the people who came in after us were seated ahead of us that we realized where we were supposed to go. 

The prices are not too bad about eight to $10 for the entrée. And coffee for two or three dollars. Decor is really cute and very attractively done. Can't wait to go back!

I ate here one Saturday while I was doing pet psychic readings next-door at four muddy paws. I had a chicken bacon wrap that was really good and was very surprised when the guy told me it came with a side salad. The food was excellent the side salad was big and it had a lot of stuff in it mixed greens cucumber onion cheese tomato very tasty. I'm only giving it four stars because the building is kind of a big echoey type barn and when you get some people in there that are noisy it's not pleasant. Otherwise it was great the employees were friendly and really nice and I'll be back.

Trader Joe's and Whole Foods really missed the boat as was evidenced the very first day this place was open. The parking lot was packed at 7:30 in the morning and pretty much stayed that way for at least two weeks any time I went. It's still pretty packed on weekends and evenings but daytime during the week is not quite so bad.

One big disappointment was how water soaked the fresh produce is. One of the best kept Grocery secrets is that they over water the fresh vegetables so they rot in your refrigerator faster. It was disappointing to see the store following that path.

Their sales are really good. I tried out a fantastic whole food supplement that was on sale for 25% off. I loved it and will be going back to stock up before the sale ends on April 1.

You do have to watch some of the pricing, however. I noticed in the bulk section the white yogurt covered pretzels were $2.99 a pound while the prepackaged white yogurt pretzels were $3.99 a pound. The prepackaged flavored yogurt pretzels were $3.99 pound while the bulk ones were $3.49.

I love that there is a place like this now on the Illinois side of the river but will continue to patronize Trader Joe's in Brentwood. A lot of the things that I buy like butter and toilet paper are cheaper at TJ's. Also I like TJ's soy cream a lot better than what I found at Fresh Thyme.

Having said that, I will say emphatically this place is great and it's long overdue for Illinois!

Great little coffee shop! Sharon and the rest of her family are very hospitable and always make me feel welcome. The food is good, as is the  coffee. Very quaint feel to it very comfortable with couches. Stop by!

I had an hour to fill yesterday, so I stopped and got a sandwich here. I intended to go to the St. Louis bread Company on Central and then saw this place so I decided to check it out. I had a BLTC sandwich toasted on a whole wheat sub bun. It was perfection! Fresh and hot. In fact so hot, I had to let it sit for a couple minutes to cool off to the point where I could pick it up to eat it. LOL

The place looks clean. The staff were friendly. I highly recommend it next time you're in Clayton!

Nice place! Clerk was very friendly and helpful. It looks like they also sell a lot of the Aura Cacia oils and aromatherapy oils then I usually buy at Whole Foods Market in Brent wood. I went in to buy a muslin bag for decocting herbs. This was more like an expandable mesh bag that was cheaper than what I would pay in St Louis for a regular muslin bag. I think it will work very well for what I need.

I found a glass bottle that would work well for something else I was planning on making. The price on the bottle was $2.95 but it rang up at $3.95. when I questioned the clerk on it he said I had to pay the higher price because that's what was in the computer. After some discussion he did finally call the owner who told him to go ahead and sell it to me at the lower price, which is what most places usually do when the price on the item doesn't match what's on the computer.

I will definitely be back!

Definitely made me step outside my box. I was expecting a more traditional type of barbecue like a sweet honey barbecue. They do have barbecue for every person's taste .... Just not the sweet honey barbecue I was expecting.Their house brand the righteous pig sauce had a very fruity taste to it. Once I was told it was Apple cinnamon, I really enjoyed it!

I like the idea of having the barbecue sauces on the table and adding my own. It gave me an opportunity to sample the different sauces... An opportunity I would not have had if the meat had been cooked in the sauce itself.

I got the small pulled pork barbecue sandwich minus the bun since I'm trying to watch my carbs. It came with two sides for eight dollars. I got the barbecue beans and the applesauce. The barbecue beans were a little on the hot spicy side for my taste. The applesauce had a very unique flavor to it. It was kind of hard to tell what that was. Very tart and tangy. Delicious!

They have nice outdoor seating. The weather on the day I was there was absolutely gorgeous... Sunny and clear and a little bit on the cool side.

They also offer a military discount which is a definite plus and brought my bill to under eight dollars.

And of course the friendliness of the staff put this place over the top.

I highly recommend this place! I will definitely be back.

More than likely this will be my last visit to Cheryl's Herbs. I have always purchased the Young living oil Release blend from Cheryl's Herbs because it was less expensive, and I could buy smaller quantities.

This time when I ordered it, the price had gone up about seven or eight dollars. When I got it home, it smelled horrible. It was not the YLO blend. 

I called and was made to feel at fault. I was questioned as to whether I had specifically requested the YLO blend which they call Rel. I was told that they have always had two blends, which I never knew and had never been told, even though I have bought this particular blend there for a number of years. I'm pretty sure I specifically requested the YLO blend, but even if I had not, you would think the clerk would clarify which blend I wanted. The person I spoke with said that they would redo the order for me.

I happened to be in St. Louis a day or so later (I live about 30 miles away) and called to see if the order might be ready. I was told it was not and was questioned as to whether I received a phone call stating that it was. No I had not, I responded, I just thought I would give a call to see if it might be ready since I live a ways away. I was told that there were other orders ahead of me to which I responded, well do you think they could put a priority on this? I'd already bought the stuff.

I was almost home, got the call that the blend was ready. I went in this morning to pick it up. I was told I would have to pay an extra $.70 for the blend. After I started to ask for clarification, the woman who I think was the manager told the clerk not to bother charging me.

I think it's time I signed up for Young living oil.

This store is definitely NOT user-friendly for the handicapped or senior citizens. While they have wheelchairs, which is fine if you have somebody to push you around in it, they do not have motorized scooters like most other stores have available. The first time I visited and asked about them, I was told that the powers that be at IKEA have concerns that someone might drive one down the stairs. As a senior with arthritis in my hips and back, their concrete floors are a real pain to walk on for any length of time. 

I would give them one star, except for the fact that they do have a wonderful cafeteria. I usually stop in for Swedish meatballs for lunch when I'm in the neighborhood. Also I like the little market place on the first floor. Otherwise, I don't bother with IKEA.

Disappointing! Judging by the name, I thought this was going to be some kind of a bakery. Instead, the food is mostly nacho type dishes that seem to be mostly spicy hot and rather expensive. I think there were  only two or three sweet things on the menu.

A group of us went there after church one Sunday. It was very noisy. They were able to get us a table in a quieter section of the restaurant, which was not too bad.

I ordered the beer batter shrimp with french fries and creamy coleslaw. The shrimp was spicy hot -- The type of hot that the more you eat the hotter it gets in your mouth. I made it through about two pieces and then told the waitress that I could not eat because it was too hot. She told me it wasn't supposed to be. I told her well it was. She asked if I wanted something else. We had already waited 45 minutes to get our food, so I said no... I would just make do with the fries and coleslaw and stop at Wendy's on the way home for a sandwich.

After about another half hour, and I was done with eating what I had, a manager came out and talked to me. And again I get this business of well it's not supposed to be hot we don't put spices in our beer batter. I told her, well, maybe the pan it was cooked in it been cooked with something spicy previously, but it was hot and it got hotter the more I ate it.

I was going to give three stars but after the manager argued with me I knocked it down to one star. I don't know why people can't just say, I'm sorry you had a bad experience what can we do to make it right? I hate when they have to make out that it's your fault because, well we don't cook our food that way. Well, apparently there must've been something in that beer batter that was spicy. Just because you can eat spicy food doesn't mean someone else can!

Absolutely delightful! Lots of nooks and crannies where you can sit to be somewhat alone. Very low-key and quiet. It's a wonderful place to meet my clients. Oh! Yeah! The coffee is fantastic! A little pricier than some places around here, but well worth it.

A couple years ago, I bought a bottle of flower essences from the store that was two years past the sell by date. When I took it back, the manager said the price had gone up and I had to pay the new price on the new bottle. I didn't write a review that time, but I sure am this time!

So, today, I decided I would give them another chance since they are the only store in St Louis that sells the product I'm looking for. I needed it in a hurry and preferred to support a local business rather than Amazon. I called and asked if they had a particular flower essence blend. Young lady who answered the phone asked if I would call back later because they were extremely busy. I called back about a half hour later, only to be met by a huge sigh once I started talking. Again, she asked me to call back after explaining that she was the only person in the store, and it was very busy.

I forgot to call until about 40 minutes before closing. A man answered the phone who was very abrupt, bordering on rude. He said he would go look and placed me on hold. After five minutes, the call was dropped. I called back, and this time he did get back with me, only to tell me they don't carry the product.

I live in Belleville. This place is definitely not worth battling the Central West End traffic and parking. Amazon here I come!

I upgraded from one star to 2 stars. The music playing while I was on hold was very nice. I'm not a fan of piano music, but this was quite decent. Very soothing.

I love love love this place! Whenever I'm in Nashville, I stock up on all sorts of goodies ... Spell candles, incense, crystals, tea. The biggest thing I appreciate and love about this place is that not only do both owners walk their talk, but so does the clerk I saw yesterday. Every single one of them has their own personal altar. There also are altars specifically for the store. There are so many spiritual shops... New Age and metaphysical shops... Where the owners just got into it to make money and don't actually practice anything that they're selling.

I can't wait to go back.

Their baked goods may be wonderful but the Caesar salad I got here was ATROCIOUS! I was at an event across the street and went over to get something for lunch. The chicken on the salad was somewhat dried out and had hard brown spots on it. I took it back. I was told the chicken was cooked the day before and was probably overcooked. They gave me my money back and then offered to make me another salad. I suggested i just take the one I brought back, but, "No. No. Let me make you another one." This one was worse! The chicken, I think, was even older -- completely dried out and thoroughly brown. One small piece was so hard, I was afraid it might break a tooth. On top of it, there were even pieces of lettuce that were old and soggy. The only reason I'm giving them two stars is because they were accommodating and didn't give me any attitude.

For some reason, an order of sausage & eggs is not on their all day breakfast menu. I don't know exactly what that means, since you can get eggs and sausage in the regular big breakfast or on an Egg McMuffin. Anyway, I went ahead and ordered a salad since it was just 10 minutes into the lunch hour. When I got home something seemed a bit off with it. On further investigation, it looked like somebody spit in my salad. Yuck!

This place just opened... It is wonderful! I had some business at the courthouse and stopped in afterwards... Walked out with a Chai latte that could probably use another shot of espresso which I will ask for next time I'm in there... It's a cute little place... They serve breakfast and lunch along with coffee. At the time I was in there, they were having a special Caribbean lunch deal... I did not have time for lunch, but I sure do like my latte! I definitely plan to return.

Very disappointed! When I googled restaurants in Brentwood and this place came up, I was really excited to find healthy food that I could take back to the office with me... before I even got there, on the drive over, I was thinking about purchasing extras to take home and trying and maybe getting on board with their service. When I went in, about the first half dozen meals I picked up had either hot chilies or Chipotle in them... I asked the young lady at the register if they had anything that did not have hot spices in it... She said she had no idea and that I would have to look at each package to see. Then she went back to whatever was occupying her on her cell phone, which obviously was more important than helping a customer... I went to a different section of the refrigerator that looked like it had savoury items in it... I picked up about three or four different items... Same thing... Everything had either hot chilies or Chipotle in it. Needless to say, I won't be going back...

Foodwise, this is the worst Wendy's! I would say about 1 of every 3 visits, I get old (brown) lettuce in the salad. Twice, I've gotten baked potatoes that were brown. The potato I had tonight was not only brown, but hard.

On the plus side, the staff are usually pretty nice.

I've been affiliated with Mystic Valley since I bought my aura camera in 2002 (Loving Rose, Psychic). It is a great place to shop! There's always something new & different. The staff are knowledgeable. If they happen to be temporarily out of something, they will special order for you (a lost service at most places!) Also, it is one of the few places that takes Covid precautions seriously with plenty of hand sanitizer & watching the numbers in the store. The coffee bar is still up and running with plenty of hot (and cold) drinks to take with you in this chilly weather.

If you are looking for Irish fare on this side of the river, this might not be the place to go. I've lived here almost 20 years & just never got around to stopping in. Yesterday was the day... My sister was visiting from Nashville, TN, and we decided to check this place out. She raved about how much she liked shepherd's pie & couldn't wait to try one of theirs. I should have looked at their website menu before we went. While the ambiance of the place had an Irish look to it, & there were some Irish beers & drinks, the only thing on the menu that seemed Irish was the Reuben. It came with a LOT of meat, so that was great. It was very filling. The fries also were very good. It was just disappointing there was nothing truly Irish food-wise.

I had just gotten done doing pet psychic readings at Lola and Penelope's and decided to check this place out for some lunch. The outdoor seating especially attracted me... The first table I sat outthere was an obnoxious odour... I think it was near the garbage dumpsters... So I switched to the other side of the patio... There was a lovely cool breeze blowing. I ordered the soup and salad... Selected the red pepper Gouda soup... It was exquisite! Very creamy, very rich, very flavourful and seasoned to perfection with no hot spices in it, which I greatly appreciated... The salad was a bed of mixed greens, black beans, sunflower seeds, tomatoes and croutons with a cucumber ranch dressing. It all came with a basket of crackers which had cheese spread instead of butter... A nice touch... I live 35 miles away in Belleville Illinois, and I would be thrilled to drive over here for another meal instead of waiting until I'm in the area. In fact, as I'm typing this up, I'm getting hungry and thinking about going back over there tomorrow... It was that good! The staff were friendly & attentive.

WJnyWEe_YK7JO47fcovBVw.review_text: Great local lunch spot in downtown St. Louis.  I had the Vito - Italian sub - very good!  Plus quick service.  Jimmy John's came recommended by locals - always a good sign in my book!  Very close to convention center if you are in town for a conference and need to get a good and quick lunch off-site.

Sushi Pier is the best!  Better sushi than I get on a regular basis in Calfornia - who knew Nevada had the best Sushi?  I had been told this by Reno natives, but was happy to have the opportunity to test their claim a few weeks ago.  Not only was the sushi fresh and melt in your mouth delicious, but the chefs are so creative and try to outdo themselves in creating delectible treats to delight you!  AND all this for an all you can eat price!  Look no further - this is the place!

Good choice in Union Station St. Louis.  I had the Ponchartrain (server said it is same as Tilapia, though that was also on the menu, so why two names for the same fish, I have no clue).  The Ponchartrain was quite good with mushrooms and a cream sauce.  We also had the shrimp cocktail and lump crab cake appetizers....both fine, but not wonderful.  Drinks and service were perfectly acceptable.  We dined outside on the patio since the weather was nice - inside looks comfy and a bit less casual.

Definitely OK tourist spot  - I came here with a group - so the experience is always a little different than if you come on your own.  The atmosphere is great for a festive group.  We happened to come during Restaurant Week and ordered off the Prix Fixe menu.  Overall the food was fine, but not noteworthy.  I had the Cajun BBQ Shrimp appetizer, house salad, 7 oz Filet and Cheesecake for dessert.  Nothing was outstanding.  My steak was cooked how I like it - medium rare - but lacked flavor.  I will say I had a great time here....the food is fine,  the atmosphere is good for a party group, and I enjoyed the company of the people I came with!

Too weird - same restaurant  - same city.- same trip - two locations anyway. Don't ask - the why is not interesting!  Good downtown restaurant.  I came here with a group and we were seated on the patio. It was a great locale for a party group, and the food was good. It was Restaurant Week if that matters to anyone reading this.  I got the Filet - ordered medium rare, but came medium well.  I almost sent it back, but it was tender and tasty in spite of the non-rare status, so I kept it.  Way better quality of meat than I had at Jake's the night before (see my review on that) Overall, a good choice in downtown St. Louis.

Don't miss out on the Shrimp Ya-Yas! 

Just arrived in N.O., and stepped out of our hotel into a parade!  Then properly festooned with Mardi Gras beads we followed the crowd and our noses down Bourbon Street.  I had noticed La Bayou driving in, so when the first couple of places that had been recommended had long waits, we opted for La Bayou and got right in though it was crowded and busy. 

Loved the atmosphere which is festive and fun and the front is open to Bourbon Street and all the activity going on - at least the week before Mardi Gras there is great energy going on!  

An appetizer called Shrimp Ya Yas caught my eye.  Yum!! Succulent shrimp sauted in a sauce of garlic, butter, shallots, wine and pinenuts served with perfect french bread for dipping.  The bread was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside with just a glaze of seasoned butter.  

The Blackened Redfish served with jambalaya on the side was really good too.  Our waiter suggested a delicious upgrade of a topping sauce with shrimp and crawfish.  

I might have to come back and try one of the Po Boy sandwiches...They look really good, plus the aforementioned bread...yeah, gotta come back!

Out and about in the French Quarter looking for a likely breakfast spot? 

Fleur De Lis is a good choice for a casual breakfast.  Nothing spectacular, but just what we wanted. You know how sometimes you want something really special and sometimes you want to just belly up to the counter and get some good plain food.  

We had the two egg breakfast with bacon - just fine - though I wondered if I should have tried the Hashbrown Heaven which sounded wonderfully decadent.  Guess I better go back some time and try it!

I think I am just lucky - I have a knack for stumbling upon the most amazing places!  The Bourbon House is fabulous - my mouth is still happy just thinking about it.  

Our first night in the French Quarter we wandered out and cruised down Bourbon Street looking for a good meal - it's not hard to find lots of great looking and smelling places.  We liked the looks of the Bourbon House and went in to find out there was an hour and a half wait, which suggested that this might be a really good place to eat!  

Being too hungry to wait that night we went elsewhere but I had "bookmarked" the Bourbon House and when I decided to put together a group dinner a couple of nights later, I made a reservation.  

Here's where it gets really good!  The Jumbo Lump Crab Cake appetizer is absolutely to die for - really unusual in that it is served in a pastry filled with jumbo lump crab with Creole butter and crab claws.  

I followed this wonderful delicacy up with the Crispy Gulf Fish served skin on with shrimp, crab, oysters and bacon with a vermouth cream sauce...heavenly!  

The Martinis are good too, and of course my man had a Bourbon as he couldn't go to a place called the Bourbon House and not try the Bourbon!

First of all, my boyfriend liked the sign for GW Fins when we saw it as we wandered about the French Quarter.  Then, of course I remembered that the concierge had recommended this restaurant, so when we decided to ditch a party (which would have been fun, no doubt) in favor of a quiet dinner with a client so we could continue an interesting conversation, we opted for GW Fins.  

They have a daily menu which is cool, especially when they get in some special items like the wonderful Blue Fin Tuna we had which you don't often see on menus.  The Blue Fin was seared rare and sliced over a bed of something good, (potatoes I think, but I was focused on the tuna obviously) and drizzled around the edges with a veal jus - interesting and surprisingly good with the fish.  

The appetizers were equally tasty...we had the Lobster Dumplings and the Smoked Sizzling Oysters, both super yummy!  

One would hardly think we needed dessert, but our waiter told us the Crème Brulee was like silk.  It just melts in your mouth and is probably the best we've ever had.

We had to try a real New Orleans Po Boy sandwich before we left.  What better place than The Market Café in the French Market?  

Sitting outside on a beautiful February afternoon watching people and listening to a great jazz quartet while we ate was just perfect.  

We tried a fried shrimp Po Boy and a fried oyster Po Boy washed down with a beer.  Both sandwiches were good, the oyster more flavorful, eating half of each was a perfect combo.  The bread was really fresh and just the perfect texture.  

We were even in the mood to enjoy our ditzy waitress...who was still in slow motion from too much partying the night before and kept forgetting what she was doing.

Combining business with pleasure in The Big Easy?  The Marriott New Orleans is a good choice.  

Right next to the French Quarter, you can be on Bourbon Street in a couple of minutes, and the Mardi Gras parades pass right by the hotel.  We arrived just in time for a parade and started our visit by catching beads from a passing float.  A festive way to start experiencing New Orleans!  

The rooms are a bit on the small side but plenty comfortable.  The bathrooms are really small and there were no towel racks except in the shower which was a bit inconvenient, but minor.  

Really the only thing that was a problem was the internet which was wired not wireless, so only one person could use it at a time AND it was $14.95 per day, which just really bugs me.  You really ought to be able to get internet access for free everywhere.  

Room service is somewhat leisurely in its arrival, but we found that laid back approach to service in a lot of places in NO, so we learned to just adapt to it and not be so uptight.  

There is a nice bar and lounge area off the lobby which is nice for late evening drinks and conversation.  

For the business traveler there is also an especially good business center provided by FedEx Office right in the hotel.  The convention center is within walking distance though a bit more than you might want to walk after a day on your feet, but most conventions are going to have buses that run back and forth to the hotels anyway, or barring that it is a quick cab ride.  Better to be more convenient to the French Quarter than the convention center in my view!

Melt in your mouth cheesesteaks!

Yummy!  I had mine with white american cheese as recommended by the girl at the counter as her favorite.  Wash it down with a local brew - a perfect lunch for a day of walking around olde city Philadelphia.  

Family owned and the whole family seems to work here - great food, fun atmosphere - loved it.

Guess I'll review this twice since it has two listings and is worth knowing about!  

Melt in your mouth cheesesteaks!

Yummy!  I had mine with white american cheese as recommended by the girl at the counter as her favorite.  Wash it down with a local brew - a perfect lunch for a day of walking around olde city Philadelphia.  

Family owned and the whole family seems to work here - great food, fun atmosphere - loved it.

A delightful and thoroughly delicious experience!  We were dining with a group of 15 but it still felt like an intimate dinner.  

The atmosphere is cozy but open, and the menu is wonderful.  We tried the mussels and pan seared scallops as appetizers and the Berkshire pork chop for the entree - everything was cooked to perfection!  

A great bottle of wine and congenial company made the evening!

It appears the fashion is to show a lot of ennui about this place based on many of  the reviews...but I really enjoyed the dinner my boyfriend and I had here.   

I didn't even go up to the roof top bar so was not subjected to the oft lamented lame plastic glasses.  By the way folks - though we may find plastic glasses ridiculous with Grey Goose, the harsh reality is that rooftop restaurants all have to comply with regulations these days - we have the same thing in San Diego, so it's not really fair to slam the restaurant for plastic glasses -ok, done with my rant now :)

I had a couple of vodka martinis that were just right.  We enjoyed the tapa type dishes most of which were quite delicious, particularly the ahi tuna tartare, lump crab cake and pan-seared hanger steak.   

We also tried - on a whim - the cheesesteak eggroll, which is a bit much.  It's tasty enough but a little too much of a good thing and a bit gimmicky, but still a fun thing to order.  

Our server was a bit rushed, but it was a busy night, and I have to say the dishes came out fairly quickly and one at a time which worked well since we were never quite done with one when the next one came out.  

Had I known about the Olde City location, I would have liked to try that one since other reviewers seemed to like it better, but I enjoyed myself just fine at the Continental Midtown.

Strolled by Parc on late Saturday afternoon in May and decided we must have some refreshment on the sidewalk patio seating overlooking Rittenhouse Square on such a beautiful day.  We were lucky enough to get a table that had just vacated as it was pretty crowded outside.  

I felt in the mood for a Mojito - the sunny afternoon and the fact that we had passed a Cuban place a block or so back maybe had something to do with it.  

The Mojito was decent, not the best I have had, but definitely good. We had a Shrimp Cocktail to tide us over until dinner and that was fine too.  

The service was a little iffy at first, as we sat for some time before our drink order was taken until we caught the eye of a server, who was not ours, but at least she tracked down ours.  Our server was not super-attentive, but to be fair, it seemed like they might have been a bit short-handed, as we saw the manager running back and forth quite a bit too.  

Would definitely love to try Parc again for a full meal next time we're in Philly.

No one should be surprised that an old-school diner is just that - a diner.  You know you'll get OK eats served quick and no-nonsense about it.  

Just what I expected when I went there for a Saturday breakfast before sallying forth on a day of sight seeing in Philly.  

Eggs and hashbrowns just fine, and I tried the Scrapple just because...

I agree with Russ C.  The Elephant & Castle serves its purpose, in this case to be attached to the Crowne Plaza and therefore served as a place to have a last drink at the end of the evening and chat with friends who were also staying at the hotel.  

We arrived in Philly really late after a long day of travel with little food, and seeing as how we were on West Coast time, felt like it was time for dinner.  Happily the E&C was still open and we were able to get some pretty good halibut & chips.  

We stopped in for a night cap the rest of the nights we were in town and got decent drinks at a decent price, and our server even remembered us & what we liked to drink.

Absolutely loved Devon!  Could have had something to do with a balmy May evening on our last night in Philly as well as the excellent food and an attentive server.  

We had reservations for 8 PM and had to wait a bit to get an outside table but it was well worth waiting for.  The bar was crowded and the bar staff not super attentive, but we did get a good drink and were at our table before we finished it.  Loved overlooking Rittenhouse Square and people watching as we enjoyed our dinner and a bottle of wine.  

As appetizers, the prosciutto crusted scallops were to die for, and the duck trapped smoked salmon excellent also.  

We split a filet and crab cake entree, but added a second crab cake on the advice of our server - and very good advice it was!  

Awesome place - I highly recommend it!

X1eug0jtqLeW3ZuTD6FA-Q.review_text: Great tasting food, horrible service. We went in as a party of 7 on an empty day we have our server take our paper and then she never put in our order of nigiri but did however bring our rolls. We then tried to get our servers attention and we were ignored, we waited for our nigiri for an hour and the waitress failed to bring us anything. We then had to stand up to get her attention. It was honestly the worst service I have ever received in my life, and it wasn't like she was busy because the restaurant was basically empty. I really wish my experience wouldn't have been ruined by such utterly bad service.

They're always busy but that's because they do an amazing job. They definitely are worth the wait and every time I go I have gotten an amazing service experience. They always have great suggestions on what cut would look best. I have never been dissatisfied, and I will continue to be a loyal customer. I love how they shampoo and dry your hair once you're done with your haircut making you feel refreshed and clean. Definitely money well spent.

I had one of the most delicious Italian subs I have ever had. The meat was perfect very juicy and went great with the peppers which complemented the sub perfectly. I was not expecting such an amazing culinary experience from a food truck. Everything I have ever wanted from sub, it was actually pretty big so the fact that I actually finished it just goes to prove how insanely delicious it was. 10/10 would eat again, the man from the food truck was also very kind and helpful.
Ok quality food, ok service. Reviews boosted by discounts for people that do reviews on yelp.
Terrible service, and pompous staff. Great location, and good beer selection; thanks to the terrible staff you will never catch me spending my money at this bar ever again. Terribly dissatisfied.
Great service and good quality food however besides the showmanship the food was decent but nothing to write home about.

Sakana Sushi, is my favorite sushi place in Reno due to their quality of fish and great sushi.

They do not include all you can eat mussels in their sushi but they have lots of different appetizers and the quality food make up for their restrictions on all you can eat.

Service can be a little slow at times, however I have never had a bad experience at Sakana in the 20x I've been there.
Trendy, delicious, different. Would recommend to those looking for a nice lunch spot with tons of delicious options.
The Depot has an amazing selection of beer and liquor, great happy hour specials, delicious food, and friendly staff.
Two Chicks for brunch is a Sunday brunch staple in my book. It can take a hot minute to be seated on a Sunday (as expected) but it is totally worth the wait, great food and great service.
Great place for Sunday breakfast, tons of different breakfast options. Expect a wait if you're trying to go for breakfast during the weekend.
Delicious Thai cuisine, more modern than the other Thai places I've tried in Reno, but very well priced and very tasty .
One of my favorite Midtown eateries, great dinner options and wonderful outdoor seating.
Great place in Midtown to grab a quick bite to eat, their house salad is great, great variety of sandwiches and soups. They also have a nice selection of canned beers.
Sakana Sushi is by far one of the best places to eat sushi in Reno. Quality sushi, and a great variety of rolls & nigiri.

One of cleanest places I've ate AYCE sushi at, they have quality fish and a great atmosphere.

They do not include certain appetizers (like mussels) or ice cream like other restaurants that do all you can eat. However the a la carte Ice Cream we ordered at the end was great and I'd rather end up paying a little bit more for the great sushi & amazing ice cream.

XMQzB1pun4pcgrlP5wCj-w.review_text: I can't even begin to tell you how wonderful this restaurant is. At the recommendation of friends we took a day trip from new york (yes, we went from ny to philly for food and was exquisitely worth every penny and minute it took to get here) just to eat at this restaurant and try out their tasting menu. We intended to do just 5 courses but at course 3 we couldn't believe that it would be over soon so we asked to do the 7 instead. Every dish was well crafted, well thought out, was perfectly in sync with what had come before, was all home made (from scratch), was perfectly cooked and seasoned and left us licking our plates clean. The waiter knew everything about our dishes, wines and beers and was just as excited to tell us about our food as we were to eat it. The waiter was also kind enough to relay our request to meet this genious chef who did come out for us to endlessly complement. We were never rushed and always well attended to but not overly. There was a live band who played beautifully and not so loud that we couldnt have great conversation over great food. In fact, i went in with a migraine and i left happy and pain free. I would travel from florida to eat here again. If you have something to celebrate or just got your paycheck, go here!! You will not regret it and neither will your pallate.

An absolutely delicious restaurant. We all shared and wanted it all. Even the bread was outstanding. I like the BYOB Philly scene since I like my wine and I like to know what I'm getting. The decor was minimal and felt like you were in someone's dining room. Bathroom was clean, kitchen looked very clean as well. Wait staff was helpful and attentive, but not overly so. A table next to ours didn't like their order and it was replaced with something else free of charge. Pretty cool place.
Delicious fish, as expected. Wanted more from the tasting menu, ended up ordering of the regular menu as well. Good wine selection for fish. Exceptional service. Fancy bathrooms.

Absolutely delicious ribs. Chicken was good, ribs were better. Baked potato was standard, corn on the cob was bland, cole slaw was good, apple sauce was bland. Music was very loud, but it seems like that's why people come and everyone was enjoying themselves.

For a hole in the wall chain, this place is great! We ended up here unexpectedly and had a great meal for four people for $25. The chicken really is delicious and juicy, not too spicy. I'd skip the rice next time. Maduros and yuca fries were on point. Not such a huge fan of the dipping sauces.
A great local Indian spot. Service was quick and attentive. Food was perfectly done and they were happy to bring more rice. Warning that the puffed rice appetizer is not gluten free.

Amazing! They even make their own gluten free bread (and butter)!!! They were very ready to accommodate gluten free needs without removing the flavor from the food. Their mocktails were creative and full of flavor. Our waiter was kind and available when we needed him.
The grilled oysters are a must. As is the oysters app w creamed spinach and bacon. Don't bother with anything else. But definitely come for the grilled oysters.

I cannot believe I almost passed this place up! So far in NOLA, everywhere we've had to wait on a line has been worth it. The fried ham was good, a bit dry, great with some black beans and rice. We made a half-and-half with lemonade and iced tea and a spare cup. The grits are just in water. Seems to be the way they're made here. But the real star was the fried chicken!! This was the most amazing fried chicken! It was not at all dry, it was perfectly crispy, with a thin coating of beautifully seasoned dredge. I'm still wishing I got more.

Very creative and fun dishes. Amazingly friendly staff. We had the pork nachos, the boudin balls, and the Crawfish and artichoke dip. I appreciated the dip the most. The boudin balls could use more flavor. The nachos were just fun, could use more pulled pork on top. I appreciated the drinks, also very creative. Id be back for the drinks and the dip and the friendly people.
Stunningly delicious. We got the pork belly sandwich and the pulled pork sandwich. They were delicious. I wish they were as big as po'boys. Their Mac and Cheese was also yummy.
Delicious ice cream! Fun flavors, including the cones themselves. We'll be back for more.

This place was a bunch of fun to walk around, get a bit from each place that intrigued us, and then sit down for an eclectic lunch. If we lived nearby, I could absolutely see coming here for favorites during lunch, especially on a weekend! Each spot was delicious and friendly.

I don't understand how this place hasn't made a Michelin list somewhere. My goodness how delicious. Words can't even describe. We tried 8 different tapas plates amongst us and each was better than the next. The octopus was the softest, most flavorful I've ever had. Ever. The dates wrapped in bacon and stuffed with cheese were scrumptious. The live music and heat lamps made the evening as special as the food. I would come back to the area just to eat here again and again. Come to think of it, I think we will go back this afternoon just for the ice cream!
Yummy, well rounded food. Great views out on the deck. Fun drinks and friendly staff.

XovVS25QvXlRrc9oOxt-KQ.review_text:
I live on Whyte Avenue, and have walked past this restaurant time and time again. Each time I would think "Wow, that place is so busy! I want to check it out," and just never got the chance to go. I'm very happy to say that I finally went, and it was fantastic! I can definitely see why it's always so busy.

I would recommend making a reservation, but even though we didn't have one, they took our names, we left and went for a walk on Whyte Ave for 15 minutes, came back and it was good to go! The restaurant itself has a great vibe to it, a sort of urban-southern-diner style, with great employees and excellent service.

LOVE the biscuits with the mint/chili jelly that you get upon seating! Delicious. For our meal we got an appetizer of calamari, which was good, but I would definitely go for the Oysters next time. For the main we shared the ribs and fried chicken, which was a lot of food! I can't imagine getting that to myself but if you're in for a big meal this is definitely a good choice. The chicken was deliciously crispy, couldn't get enough of it. 

Bonus- Electric lemonade- delicious and dangerous! ;) Don't order if driving, that's for sure. 

Overall I really loved it here, great atmosphere and good food, will definitely be coming back.

I am astonished that people have given some bad reviews! I am a baker, and definitely have high standards when it comes to cakes, cupcakes, and cookies, and I can say that these are the best cupcakes I have ever had (and that's saying something!). 

I love so many things about Fuss, so I'm just going to list them:
- The atmosphere. It's cozy, and the staff are so sweet and welcoming.
- The location. I live off of Whyte Ave, and it's a nice tradition my boyfriend and I have on the weekend to walk Whyte and of course, grab one of the cupcakes of the week at Fuss
- the cupcakes! They are the most moist cupcakes I've ever had. There is nothing worse than an overcooked or dry cupcake, which I find in a lot of bakeries due to mass production. I don't know what the secret is at Fuss, but it's working!
- the icing. If you like super sugary sweet, cost-co style icing, this is not the place for you (and luckily, I don't!). That being said, the icing is sweet, a lovely balance of flavour (whether their buttercream or cream cheese icing), and just the right thickness. They are the perfect balance to the delicious cake flavours. 
- They add 6 new flavours each week, and switch them out! What other place does that? It maintains the fun of going to a bakery, and seeing what you have to choose from, instead of the monotony of having the same choices all the time. I can't wait for the rotation with the Creamsicle to come back!

Highly highly recommend! We always get 2 cupcakes, which come conveniently in a two cupcake take away container. The perfect treat at the end of a long week :) I would suggest the Godfather, the Creamsicle, or one of their everyday favourites: Cloud 9 and Chocolate Cheesecake!

I've been here many times, and the food is always great! Nice atmosphere, and a great place for lunch and dinner. I've taken food to go and it is just as good. The daily specials are great if you want to try something new, the Basil Chicken has great heat to it. My go to Thai food is usually either a curry, or Pad Thai. At this restaurant I've had the Green, Red, and Yellow curries, and they never disappoint! Definitely get the coconut rice if you're coming here, you won't regret it. 


 The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was because it is usually very busy, the service tends to fall back a little. Even then, that's not a big deal, I'll be back many more times!

You have to go here!

This place is so much fun, has a great friendly staff, looks amazing, has a great selection of board games, delicious treats to eat and drink, and an overall awesome atmosphere. 

This is a fun spot to go on any day at any time, and a great place to meet up with friends and play some board games - they have all your old favourites, along with some interesting new games, everything you'd want to choose from! It's in a great spot on Whyte Ave and it's filling such a needed niche here in Edmonton. I got some of the vegan chocolate chip cookies (a MUST!), a chai tea, and played games for 2-3 hours. Very excellent price for all of this (less than $15).

I've only been here twice, but I loved it and will definitely be back!

I've been to both locations, downtown and on Whyte Ave, both many times! It's a great spot for the after work crowd, good vibes, and really great prices.

Happy hour has great deals on drinks as well as some food specials. Wing Wednesday is an amazing deal, and their wings are great! They have so many different types to choose from so everyone ends up happy. I love pubs and this has a chill atmosphere, and it has a big layout so you can almost always find a spot really easily. 

I've found the service to be a little better in the Whyte Ave location, but from the times I've been to both I think that was only because there seemed to be more staff/less patrons, but the staff are very friendly and the service is quite efficient, even when they're busy. I've seen all types of people in the crowd, but I suppose it would generally be those in their 20s-30s. The people who come here are here for fun and it's so great to talk and meet with people.

The platters are a great deal, especially if you're with a group. They have 3 types, we always get the one that comes with wings (bone in and no bone), nachos, french fries (amazing fries) and chicken fingers. Have never been disappointed! If you're looking for a nice pub, good atmosphere, good price, this is a good spot to check out. The deck at the downtown location is also great in the summer.

I really like this place! I love Indian food, but this isn't your traditional Indian style restaurant. Though it maintains a similar atmosphere, and a lot of the amazing flavours of Indian cuisine, it has it's own special and unique spin on the dishes.

This is conveniently located on Whyte Ave, and a great spot to pop into at almost any time. Generally busier around dinner time, but I haven't had trouble with waiting for a table. I thought that the service we received was fantastic, and felt very catered to. One of the dishes that I will forever rave about is their butter chicken poutine! It seems like the oddest combination, but it works and it works well! I would go back again and again just to have this dish. 

The foods are reasonably priced, and you can have a nice meal with several different dishes for $50-60. They also have Groupons from time to time (just bought another one!) and they are an amazing deal.

The Common is an excellent place for delicious food, friendly and attentive service, with awesome vibes and great atmosphere. I feel like it's a mixture of  high end gastro pub with a definite foodie scene. 

There's a reason I keep coming back! I've been many times and will continue to come here. It's great for after work drinks with friends, more of a scene on the weekend with great music and people, and the food never disappoints. 

The chicken and waffles is a MUST, as is the truffle popcorn, simply to die for! I've also had all of their salads, fish and chips, brie cheese app, tandoori calamari (YUM), bread and cheese, etc! All were absolutely delicious. They change up their menu every few months and add fresh new takes on their classic dishes, and even sometimes change up apps or entrees, The prices are very fair for the high quality food and service you'll receive. Their drink menu is really good too!

If you haven't been, it is a definite must!

So I've been here many, many times! I've been wavering between a score of 3 and 4 stars because I really enjoy it here.

What I like the most about Julio's is the open atmosphere when the front windows are open. In the summer it is one of the busiest patios, but it is worth the wait! If you can, definitely make a reservation because this is a happening spot every night of the week in the summer. It's a great place to enjoy some drinks, Mexican grub, with in your face views of Whyte ave and some great people watching! Oh, and complementary chips and salsa when you're seated - how can you resist! The decor here is also great and it has an awesome vibe. Every server I've had has been funny and attentive. 

The bar here is AMAZING. If you want to have drinks on Whyte, come here! They have excellent margaritas, beers, and liquors. My personal favorite is the bulldog, a margarita with a corona in it! I'm kind of getting thirsty for one right now... 

The only reason I didn't give it 4 stars is because the food, while good, isn't anything out of the ordinary, but it's definitely still good.

Come down to Julio's, have a (few) drinks, and you'll have a great time!

I've been to Khazana several times, but only for the lunch buffet. I have to admit, that I absolutely love coming here! Whenever a friend suggests a lunch, I'm always hoping that they'll want to come here.

First of all, I love that you can make reservations online. I would suggest 11:45-11:50 if possible to avoid the lunch time rush if you're in a tighter timeline! This place is really busy during this hour. That being said, I've never felt rushed or that I had to wait a long time to get anything.

This place has a very cozy feel, with fires lit and beautiful decor. I love the service here as well, even when it is busy, I find that my water is constantly being re-filled and the naan bread comes almost as soon as I'm seated with my plate of food.

And since I mentioned the food! I think I have tried almost every dish they offer at the buffett (that's the point of buffet.. Right?! My waistline may disagree!) As far as my memory serves me, I've had the aloo gobi, chicken tikka, butter chicken, saag paneer, channa masala, daal, vegetable pakora, basmati and saffron rice - all divine! I have never been disappointed, the food is always flavorful, hot, and fresh. 

If you're in downtown Edmonton make sure to check out Khazana!

I honestly love coming here, it is a truly a gem on Whyte Avenue. And in Edmonton, too, for that matter! Since I moved here I thought there was a lack of local, unique, comfortable, and fun atmospheres.Block 1912 is definitely all of those things. I love the vibe inside this cafe, and there are so many chairs, couches, and tables, all unique with an antique feel but somehow it goes together perfectly. 

If you get anything upon visiting Block 1912, GET A DESSERT! They are simply amazing.  Beautifully decorated, hand crafted, unique creations, I have never had a disappointing dessert. If you can get anything with cheesecake, you will not be disappointed. The homemade gelato is also a must, especially in the summer! They have crafted a lot of flavors and there are so many! Their items are a little on the pricier side, but you are paying for something that a lot of effort has been put into, and the effort definitely pays off. 

I've been wavering between giving Block 1912 a 3/5, and a 4/5, but ultimately went with 3- though I would give a solid 3.5 if possible. The reason behind this is down to one simple thing - The service. If this place relied simply on service, there would be no business. It's a good thing they have such a great atmosphere, amazing desserts, good food, or homemade gelato. I've been here countless times, and I'm really sad to say that I don't believe I've ever had good service. The staff seem unhappy to be there, annoyed to serve you, and are slow and disorganized. 

But, please do not let this stop you from coming here! You will miss out on amazing desserts and a great place to meet with friends, family, or even to relax and chill out on your own. I've been back time and again, and it remains one of my favorite places on Whyte Avenue.

When a friend suggested this for lunch downtown, I immediately asked, "Where?!" I've walked by it so many times, and didn't notice it was there. This HAS to be one of the best kept secrets in downtown Edmonton (though I'm not quite sure the secret hasn't been let out, it's always so busy!).

This restaurant has been here for years and years, and coming inside is kind of like a time warp- in a good way. It has an authentic diner feel to it, because, well, it is an authentic diner. 

I ordered breakfast, ham and eggs, which came with toast and potatoes. It was SO good! The kind of home-style cooking that just makes you feel happy. And the price? Out of this world for the portion and quality, $8! The service is great as well, with very friendly staff.

I also ordered the blueberry pie for dessert,warmed up with ice cream on it, because you have to treat yourself every now and then, right? It was definitely a treat! Tasted just like my grandma's old fashioned blueberry pie :) 

I would definitely recommend checking this spot out, for (all day) breakfast and lunch. Make sure you come a little bit early if you want to grab a table, this is a busy spot- especially at lunch! 

Can't wait to go again!

It's all in a name, right?

Well, if you want meat, Meat is the place to go!

This is authentic, cooked with love, homestyle food guarenteed to please. I think that Meat is definitely best enjoyed with a few people! The dining is family style, where everything you order comes out on a platter, with additional dishes for sides. Also this is a great way to try a lot of items on the menu :) Since they don't take reservations, you may have to wait for a table (depending on the time of day) but it is well worth the wait! Luckily we were seated immediately and got a table outside. 

I absolutely loved the ribs and the chicken, I don't think I've ever had meat that was cooked to be so tender and full of flavour. We also had the brisket and pulled pork and it was just so delicious. Their house made BBQ sauces are also a must try! I can't remember their names, but there are 4-5 on each table and they are so delicious. The meat that you order doesn't need sauce, but you're missing out if you don't try these. 

As for the sides, we had the potato salad, coleslaw, garlic fries and green beans. If I HAD to choose, well honestly I'd get them all again, but the potato salad and garlic fries were just so good I had to coach myself into not eating until I burst!

I'll definitely be coming back here, next time with a stretchier waistband to make room for dessert!

Meat lovers, you've met your match.

One word: YUP.

You simply cannot take a stroll down Whyte Ave without grabbing one of these babies! Fat Franks does hot dogs and smoked sausages, and boy, are they GOOD!

The honey ham smokie I literally dreamt (and drooled) about for days, it's that good. You have a lot of different options for condiments (get the curry mustard, yum!) as well as additions to your frank (hello banana peppers). 

I've never had bad service here, whether it was a busy summer day, late night on the weekend, or off season when there isn't much foot traffic. The staff is very friendly! I think the one downside is that they only take cash, and if you're like me, you don't have it very often! But when I do you can count on me grabbing one of these!

I remember walking by here multiple times prior to it opening and wondering what it was going to be, I thought it was just going to be a brewery but I was happily wrong! It is a unique situation, a brewery/pub, and if you're on Whyte you HAVE to come here!

The location is perfect - almost tucked away just off of Whyte ave, enough to feel like a genuine find. It's not a chain (which have been dominating Whyte ave lately) and it definitely has a great vibe. I love that it has it's own brewery, and you can sample a lot of their beers for an amazing price!! (a flight of four 5oz beers for $10!). They brew on site, so you can see where your beer is brewed and it doesn't have to travel far to find it's way to you! I tried the WTF Raspberry, Afternoon Tea Saison, Page Turner IPA and Random Acts Pale Ale. Honestly they were all great, but the Raspberry and Saison were just so refreshing and light I just had to get more! 

The food is also fabulous. It's a step up from regular pub grub, but not fancy as to feel out of place in a brewery. We had the frites (hand cut deliciousness), pretzels, and carnitarian pizza! Everything was delicious and timed really great, especially since it was a busy Saturday night. I can't wait to go back and try out some more menu items - aka dessert ;)

Let me start this by saying I LOVE Indian food - so I may be a little biased! 

It's not your typical Indian restaurant though, despite having a lot of similar decor and the always delicious flavours. Naan-O-Licious has it's own unique take on a lot of classic Indian and North American favorites, and there is a large menu guaranteed to please everyone in your party. 

Their Naan is AMAZING - I absolutely die for the garlic naan bread. Also, make sure to try their butter chicken poutine! It is out of this world (and a great price)! 

The service is really good, though it does get a lot busier on weekends they do a good job. The food is freshly prepared and you can see the chef cooking - which I don't always need to see, but it's definitely a nice perk. 

Bonus, it's right next to the Magic Lantern Princess theatres so you can quickly grab dinner and a movie!

Xqka4P-7nMUQRRaBWB0RLA.review_text: $10 for lunch, gyro drink and 3 pieces of pita w/ hummus. Food ok, service ok. I prefer the gyros from the drive thru stand on overland near the freeway in the ace hardware parking lot. Cheaper, better flavors, more food.

Love it. Absolutely the best in town. Wonderful combination of textures and tastes. Fresh ingredients, slight crispiness to the meat, soft pita bread, tang of yogurt sauce, hot sauce if you want.  The side of hummus and pita wedges with two incredible olives on top (my favorite) is almost a meal itself. Other side choices include salad or tzaziki (sp?).
Worst pad Thai ever, swimming in sauce. Waitress said sorry, sometimes wet sometimes dry. Didn't offer to take it back. I will never be back again.

Never again. So inconsistent.  My family likes the hawaiin bbq chicken but many times it comes with almost no sauce.  When I order with extra sauce it comes swimming in sauce so that the toppings won't even stay on.  This last time I specifically identified my concerns and asked for just a little extra sauce - again swimming in sauce.

My son and I both had burgers - bbq and mushroom.  Neither of us was impressed, pretty bland and pretty sure it was a frozen patty.  I asked for mustard.  Pretty much any fast food joint has a better burger in my opinion.  Wife had the salad bar which seemed OK.  .  Best part was the banana split which our server initially said wasn't an option.  Service was pretty good.  Sizzler a better option in my opinion.

Had a contest combo pizza delivered. Something very off about the sausage, definitely tasted old and bad. Combination of ingredients was not well balanced, onions were hard and inedible. Ate here one night for Gourmet Night and was not very impressed that time either. Off my list of pizza joints.

first vist, general's chicken.  Chicken was cooked perfectly, golden brown and crispy with nice green onion slivers on top. Portions on the large size but almost $10 for lunch. Sauce was a little on the runny side for my tastes and too sweet. I like my generals chicken a little spicy with some bean paste. Received my order very quickly. Will try again.

I always get the teriyaki beef with rice and macaroni salad. Nice and thinly sliced beef that is full of flavor. Almost $10 for lunch for the small by the time you add a drink and tip. Lived in Hawaii and wife is Japanese so I know a good plate lunch. Comes in a Styrofoam tray though so the flavors don't mix like a true plate lunch. Used to love it when a teriyaki sauce would meld with my mac salad in Hawaii.
half a sandwich and a few bites of salad for $10 without a drink. Won't be back anytime soon. And this was the lunch menu...

Third time coming here, never again. Drink service was terrible and I walked up to the counter to pay since we never got a drink refill or a ticket. Wasabi was brown and crusty, lots of empty boats. We ordered a roll and ate off the meager selection of boats. Left $50 poorer and still hungry. One highlight was the taco (octopus) salad. Grabbed several plates of that.

I've only been here for lunch! The service has always been pretty good and a good value if you get the lunch special - salad, 1/2 sandwich and fries for under $10. The capone, french dip and reuben have all been pretty good. Order off regular menu and you'll be in the $15-20 range.

Just went here for lunch. Was told they let the pizza dough rest for three days before using. My memory is not so great but pretty sure I had the million dollar pizza?? It had bacon, jalapeno, cream cheese and a sweet chili paste??  Looks like their website is still in the works, so I couldn't verify. But the pizza was very good and I'll be going back again. Very reasonable prices too, $8 for a signature pizza or build your own.

New chicken burrito is dry and too spicy for my tastes. Really, who decided to add this to the menu for $9 to the lunch menu?? They definitely ate a different burrito than I had. This location has  been very stingy with the fries for a while and now this has put me over the top. Been sticking with the chicken quesadilla for a while and it is acceptable.  Definitely better lunch options out there. My friend had the double hamburger and it looked very disappointing as well.

Never again. Walked in for a quick beer (one) with a buddy. Walked up to the bar to see what was on tap and the owner was standing there talking to a couple. He ignores us for about 5 minutes and then finally asks us if he can help us.  We tell him we want a beer and he waves us to a table and tells us to wait for a waitress. We walk out and I will not be back.

Service here has always been sub-par but why have a bar if you are not going to serve beer from it? There are a lot of places more deserving of your patronage.
worst subway ever. Skimpy portions, poorly made sandwiches. Second time with poor service and substandard sandwiches. Won't be back

Great burger and beer. Carmelized onion and bacon burger was great! Nice thick patty with plenty of cheese and bacon. Felt like there could've been a few more onion rings. Jess was great, basically working bar and tables mostly by herself on a busy Friday evening.
$12 for two pancakes, two eggs, bacon, and coffee? You gotta be kidding me. Bacon was soggy. Cashier said something about I must have ordered special pancakes. Crossed Eddie's off my list.
