I don't know whose mother this is, but she can't cook.  If I could do zero stars, that would actually be more appropriate.  

Food was terrible and tasteless.  This restaurant was recommended for good NOLA food, especially the red beans and rice.  I took first time NOLA visitors and was embarrassed by this food--I've had better food from a can.  The jambalaya tasted like rice with tomato soup poured on top.  I don't know why the line here is always so long, but don't waste your time or money.  On top of that, rude staff who didn't want to clean a table for us.  

If you want good NOLA food, head to Market Cafe near the French Market or Creole House on Canal.
Good food fast.  A bit pricey, but it is the Quarter.  Friendly staff, kinda off the beaten path.

Great burgers, great for all ages in the family.  A bit greasy, but lots of flavor.  Burgers are served single or double with cheese, onions and pickles (at least that's how mine came). It was hot, juicy and cooked to perfection.  Get there early because at 8pm, they were sold out of onion rings.  

I tried the garlic and basil mayos.  I'm not a big mayo fan, so I didn't slather this on my burger.  Very nice concept though.

You won't be disappointed by the thick, delicious shakes--OMG, they are good!

Lively atmosphere, fast counter service and food is delivered quickly despite the big crowds.  If you've ever had Twisted Root burgers, The Burger Company is a good rival.  Definitely my burger joint in NOLA.

Great BBQ in NOLA.  It was well seasoned, smokey and the right balance of sweet/savory in the sauce.  I had a brisket sandwich and my husband had a dinner with brisket, brussel sprouts and beans.

It was all good, big portions, fast service, loved the location.

We brought the kids here after bowling last night and this little ice cream parlor was bustling.  The kids had Lucky Charms and Cotton Candy in waffle cones and I shared the brownie sundae (vanilla ice cream) with my other kid.  

Everything was great--rich, delicious, creamy goodness.  My husband said that Hagen Das is real ice cream--Creole Creamery makes Hagen Das taste like the grocery store commodity brand for 99 cents.

A great selection of traditional flavors and then some for unique palettes as well.  All goodness.

5 stars for the chargrilled oysters.  They are truly heaven on a plate. I've tried Superior Seafood, Felix's, and Blind Pelican chargrilled oysters and they are good, but Drago's knows what they're doing on those open flames.  I could eat the entire dozen myself (and I've attempted), but either my son or husband never let that happen,

These chargrilled oysters are like eating popcorn, you eat them effortlessly and without thinking, then they're gone before you know it!  I've also had the chicken and andouille gumbo here and it's probably one of their other key menu items.  

Also, don't be fooled by the expensive desserts--hubby and I ordered the brownie sundae, which is presented as a half foot high creation--it's all whip cream!  We dug down to a 2-inch squared brownie with a good scoop of ice cream, chocolate topping and nuts.  It was actually a good brownie sundae, but horribly overpriced for the $10+ you pay.  

We've tried a few other dishes off their menu, but I haven't been particularly impressed--sticking with Drago's for those addictive chargrilled oysters only.

One of my NOLA go-to's.  This little place is great for sandwiches--hubby and me typically choose the turkey.  It's delicious, flavorful, and a balanced combination with the aioli spread and avocados.  The potato salad is really awesome.  I recently had the Brussel sprouts and they were decent--a bit too vinegary/acidic, should balance them with just a hint of sweetness.  Kids love the Mac and cheese.

The bread and butter pickles are great--you can purchase a jar to take home.  

Be careful because it's kinda pricey--family of five with sandwiches, sides and drinks = $100!!!!  OMG!  Stick with a sandwich and share a side if it's just a party of two.

Love the childhood nostalgia.
Best gumbo and RBAR in the Quarter.  Very flavorful in an unexpected dive bar atmosphere.  Good prices and service for the quality of the food.

This is an awesome, whole in the wall, bonafide barbecue joint in the Bywater.  The food is flavorful, and not overly seasoned.  I thought that I couldn't find good barbecue after moving from Texas but this is really good.  We shared the brisket plate with baked beans and potato salad--I wish I had ordered my own except I would've just been eating out of greed.  Good size portions, friendly service. Can't wait to return when I need my barbecue fix.

Very good Mediterranean, a bit on the more expensive side, otherwise I would have given it at least 3.5-4 stars.  Had the chicken schwarma and hubby had the gyro.  No pickles and pickled veggies on the side, which was okay.  Still good, authentic Mediterranean fare.  We shared the falafel appetizer with three different sauces.

Superior introduced me to my ongoing love affair with chargrilled oysters.  Amongst this NOLA delicacy, they serve up a varied menu of seafood, chicken and other American food.  My favorite part about Superior is the location and lively atmosphere--its always bustling and lively.  Make reservations or you'll find yourself hawking for a table at the bar area.  Everything we've tried here is great, hubby likes the salad with grilled shrimp.  Desserts are big enough for sharing.  

This will always be one of my go to spots in NOLA.

I really enjoy Herbsaint each time I've eaten here.  The food is incredible, unique without oddity or trying too hard.  My favorite is the drum fish, their salads and appetizers are good as well.  Can't beat the location, beautiful atmosphere.  Go to place for business dinners--private dining pricey but nice when you need it.

I'm a big dessert person, but found the pecan pie to be extremely rich!  Good, but save your calories if you're going to indulge.

Can't get any better than French fries and homemade pies! Well, I didn't indulge in the fries because I had just eaten at another establishment, but always room for dessert.  Hubby and I shared this hand sized treat, The Lush Nut, a pecan pie served warm with pillowy, made on the spot whipped cream--naughty little thing. 

Fry and Pie is a walk up window with outside seating.  Drive slowly on the one way street or you may literally miss Fry and Pie, it's so unassuming tucked away off St. Claude.  I was in another world after being invited into the secret, Red Room courtyard. 

Fry and Pie has a seasonal dessert menu, so can't wait to see the fall/winter line up.  Delish, gone in less than a minute.  Don't share your pie with anyone, you'll be very upset and have to get another one.

Busy Freret corner cafe that's been on my South Shore wishlist.  We went on a whim during the week and seated right away.  I liked the location, good service and good home cooking.  

I had the smoked chicken with sweet potato salad.  The chicken had a great smokey flavor, a little bit drier for my taste; and the unique twist on traditional potato was, well unique.  Hubby got the burger, to my disappointment.  The burger was good, flavorful, well seasoned.  The side of fries were hot and crispy.

I'd go back and try something different, but my judicial pallete is still out in this one.  I had high hopes for High Hat, so hubby will try the bar and see if it's a winner.  I'll be back!

Another boxed checked off my South Shore wishlist.  We were out house hunting a few weeks ago and St. James on Prytania was hopping.  I waited in line for 15 minutes only to be told that it would take another 25 minutes to get the Hooks Cheddar.  

I was hungry and couldn't miss the appointment with the realtor so we dashed that Saturday and returned this past Saturday.  I ordered the Hooks Cheddar sandwich AND the Cantal Salad with turkey.  I tried to stay on my raw diet but had been dying to taste from the menu.  More bread than bite on the Hooks Cheddar, turkey with cheddar, of course.  Also fully dressed with basil, mayo, lettuce, tomato and avocado.  Still a bit more bland although it looked great on the hearty ciabatta bread.  I like the turkey sandwich better at LaBoulangerie because it's BIG on flavor and taste.

The salad was big, too much cheese, and not as flavorful as expected.  

Four stars for location (we walked a few feet to Creole Creamery for a single) and their other product selection.  Amazing selection of cheeses from around the world, anything and everything to build an amazing charcuterie.  Lots of kitchen tools and accessories, going back for that reason.  

Just one tip for SJCC, don't let people smoke in the awesome courtyard patio, it's harmful to babies also dining there on mac n'cheese.

One of my favorite cuisines at its best.  Lebanon's came recommended after a tough day of house hunting.  Right on Carrollton, it's an ideal location for a Saturday afternoon meal on Lebanon's sidewalk dining.  I had the chicken kabob sandwich and hubby had the gyro sandwich, we shared a huge Greek salad.

Classic, simple, fresh, satisfying, tasty Mediterranean food.  The Greek dressing was mostly a red wine vinegar and it was so delicious, perfectly dressed and not a bit overwhelming.  

My chicken kabob sandwich was the kabomb!  Probably one of the best flavored poultry dishes I've ever had.  The grilled onions, herbs and seasoning were right on.  Of course, I let hubby taste my kabob and he said he liked it better than his gyro (never a fan of gyros, but it was well seasoned and had a great flavor).  

Lebanon's is a keeper and will be my go to for Mediterranean.

Another recommendation checked off the South Shore wishlist.  I gave Neyow's five stars on atmosphere and location and 3 stars on food.

So, I'm about 75% raw vegetarian and spend my other 25% on NOLA foods that I can't seem to shake.  So I did the fish with potato salad and hubby got RBAR (red beans and rice).  He hates when I say RBAR, but hey it's my word now.

Anyway, decent food and flavor, but my white fish was horribly over cooked.  It was no longer a light, flaky texture, but I really had to dig in with my fork and knife!  The potato salad, pale in appearance, was okay.  Hubby liked the RBAR with sausage but ordered a second helping of rice.  

The flavor was better than many, but if you mess up RBAR in NOLA, then you really shouldn't even call yourself a cook.  

BTW, I had to try the chargrilled oysters, big on flavor, but apparently size does matter (hubby said he's had nose goo bigger than Neyow's oysters, he really did say another word, but I don't want to gross myself out).  

I'd go back for the lively vibes at Neyow's.  Plus the daily specials--challenge on.

Nothing like a neighborhood pizza place.  We saw G's from a news interview with an athletic coach and glad we tried it.

Brought the kids here during fall break and everyone was happier with this pizza experience.  Pan style with classic toppings offered--you have to master the classics even before you want to get fancy and high-fallutin'.  G's Pizza did it.

Good service, skip the dessert, not worth the calories.

Finally, a delicious, affordable and health conscious place for us semi-vegetarians.  I fell in love with smoothie bowls over the summer in Gulf Shores, AL and was happy to find the Daily Beet.

Hubby and I shared the big açaí bowl, filled with good fruit and granola, topped with honey (sans coconut flakes). Our bowl was big enough for two, even with him usually taking than his fair share of the serving.  It was thick texture, just right.  I've never used apples in my smoothie bowls at home and this was okay as there were plenty of other fruits included.

I'm being more judicious with my stars these days, so if you're a smoothie or bowl person, then it's really a 4-4.5.  Awesome location, earthy environment fit for hipsters and Xers alike.  Daily Beet has a plethora of other healthy menu options.  My go to place for bowls.

Loved our experience at Fulton Alley--we took the kids (teens) here on an early evening during a holiday break and we all had fun.  I like the smaller, intimate bowling alley, good music without being too loud that we couldn't hear each other talking.

I liked the areas to lounge and dine, play games, and continue the experience.  Fulton area is just fun in general most times, the Alley is an awesome addition.  Just be mindful of the hours are limited for the under age 18 crowd.

Good bar foods:  we had wings, burgers, fries.  Served hot, didn't appear to be too processes.  Good family fun in NOLA.

We were craving good gumbo and did a yelp search for the area we were in and tried Gallier's.  This place is a bit off the beaten path, not in the Quarter price trap, but a short walk across Canal.

Gallier's gumbo is big on flavor with smokey undertones; and the serving size was big for $11.  It was probably about a 12/14 ounce bowl.  It's a dark, very thin roux, which isn't bad, but definitely a bit more soupy texture.  There was plenty of sausage and chicken in every spoonful.  We ordered our gumbo New Orleans style, which is with potato salad (on the side) for an extra $2 each.  I was skeptical about gumbo and potato salad but some of my employees had previously encouraged me to try it--I must say that the combination was magical.  The potato salad was southern, a bit sweeter but offered a great balance with the savory gumbo.  Served with buttery garlic bread.

We also tried the chargrilled oysters, $13 for half dozen.  Heavy on the cheese compared to other restaurants, like a sharp cheddar vs. mild Parmesan.  Not ideal for me, so I'd pass next time and stick with only the gumbo.

Parking is a bear, so walk over after you've had enough of Bourbon Street.

Cherry Expresso is a cute neighborhood eatery, coffee house on Laurel, not too far off Magazine Street.  It's so quaint and laidback and had this very eclectic crowd--from young families to a sophisticated group of four sexagenarians.  

We decided on a brunch selection--hubby had the breakfast sandwich, substituting the jalapeño hummus for avocado; and I had the breakfast plate with sausage (I had asked for bacon).  The sandwich looked good, but I didn't taste it because, well, I guess hungry people don't like to share their food.  I liked my dish, not typically a sausage person, but this was not Jimmy Dean's from back in the day--it had sage, and paprika, not spicy but definitely homemade.  I also liked the toasted challah bread, served with apple cinnamon preserves.

The only disappointment was that hubby thought he could get his one free refill to go--not so.  Free refill only if you refill your original mug.  That's a bummer, but we had to run so he had to buy ANOTHER coffee to go.

I was definitely expecting more from Fogo de Chao based on my experience at the Fort Worth, TX location.  For starters, their salad bar was skimpy and kinda sketchy--not a lot of variety at all.  Once we flipped our markers, it took a bit to get started with our sides and then they brought out two mashed potatoes for a party of five!  It also took a while to bring out the filet, all the other meats were flowing well.  All the meats did have a good flavor, which was pleasing.

I couldn't tell who was actually our table staff, but it was annoying to have to keep asking for more things and them not having an active presence for the price you pay at this restaurant.  

I wasn't disappointed because our three teens enjoyed the experience, but for the $300+ (including tip), the poor selection and hesitant service, not worth your money.

This will be one of my go-to NOLA restaurants.  After being in-the Quarter so many times since we moved two years ago, we finally made reservations at Tableau.  The atmosphere is classic NOLA and simply stunning.  We shared the Crystal Shrimp upstairs while waiting for our table.  OMG--I should have fought harder for the last shrimp.  I conceded to hubby and he offered a pitiful "are you sure you don't want it" to ease the guilt.  I had the Redhead mocktail too--refreshing.

For dinner, we shared the Maison Salad and it was large enough for two.  I had Chicken Tableau and hubby had the Drum.  Both were good, filling portions.  My only dislike was the amount of mushrooms in my dish.  It's not stated in the description so if you don't like mushrooms, ask to leave them out as I will next time.  

For dessert, we chose the bananas foster cheesecake.  It didn't appear to be made in house, but it was okay.  In all fairness, I don't remember eating much of it because I think hubby devoured most of it.  

At any rate, you can't go wrong with this NOLA classic.  A great menu that would appeal to a variety of tastes.

You can't beat a good, full plate of teriyaki chicken, steamed rice and veggies for less than $9. Chill Out Cafe's name doesn't allude to this little Asian joint in Oak Street Area.  You can walk right past it, thinking it's some hipster place with bowls or something.  But it's fast meals served up from their great menu.

What I liked about the teriyaki is that it wasn't too sweet over over-sauced.  The balance of the savory soy flavor was spot on, the steamed rice was not sticky and the veggies weren't over cooked.  

Hubby and I were both really satisfied after the cheap, yet find at Chill Out.  We've gone a second time and it was equally good.  Fast service and they also offer takeout.

Another referral from a local that we tried while passing through Prytania.  This is REALLY a grocery store with a food counter.  If you need groceries, you can buy anything from melons to matchsticks!

We went there for the sandwiches.  Hubby had the turkey Po-boy dressed and I had the chicken salad on toasted wheat, also fully dressed.  I didn't know that I could get a "regular " sandwich fully dressed, but you can and you should.  The turkey Po-boy was good, but I would have to vote for the chicken salad at Zara's.  Nice chunks of white meat, good amount of onion and not too much celery. So perfect to me.  What I liked about the chicken salad is that it wasn't swimming in mayo, but it wasn't dry either.  

No complaints, just wish I had another because you know who ate a good portion of my other half.  Soooo, off to creamery 504 to fill up my tummy since I was still a bit wanton.  

I would go back for that sandwich and others.  I think that Friday is also fried fish day, so someone tell me how that works.

We were starving and had Domilise's on the wishlist and my roast beef PO'boy was amazing.  Hubby had the shrimp and both were dressed with mayo, lettuce and pickled.  Hot sauce and mustard are options as well.  They serve a crazy big curly fry which were hot and crispy.  

So these are Italian grandmas working the counter and kitchen at this neighborhood dive.  You go in, take a number, and wait to be called, then you order.  Your number is called again, which means your food is ready, then you pay.  This is not everyday stuff, eat these well proportioned sandwiches when you deserve an indulgence--treat yoself.  Too much goodness for just an everyday meal.

I don't always eat po'boys, but when I do, I will always go to Domilise's.  Stay hungry, my friends.

Four stars for atmosphere and ambience, the food was good, but probably not largest portions (which is probably not a bad thing).  Trenasse is tucked away on St. Charles, within the Intercontinental Hotel.  It's a beautifully chic interior, but not loud and ostentatious.

Hubby and I had the special of the day, which was a white fish, I believe the drum.  Very light, flaky and served with tiny, crispy cubes potatoes and an a flavorful vegetable medley.  The wedge salad with green goddess dressing was equally flavorful.

No complaints, just wish there was more as we left still hungry after our salads and entrees.  They do present they menu in about 4-5 courses, so maybe next time we'll follow the plan and get satisfied.

I don't typically get into breweries but Parleaux was a fun crash spot after a long day.  It's in the supercool Marigny Below Bywater neighborhood and we stopped in just to unwind after stumbling upon the location.

Parleaux has a good beer selection (that's what hubby says), his was actually really good and the beautiful color was impressive.  There is counter service with open indoor seating; and what won me over was the outside seating.  Casual tables all around with umbrellas and a pergola with a big hammock swing thing.  

Little kids and fur babies are welcomed both inside and outdoors, just as long as they're leashed (dogs only, kids can run about). 

Can't wait to visit when it's a bit warmer out, would be lots of laidback fun.

Finally, a plant based restaurant that taste super without trying too hard.  Max Well is in the Audubon area, on Magazine Street.  Great, simple interior with amazing bowls and salads.  I had the California salad, simple greens with red peppers, cukes, avocado, carrots and a flavorful miso dressing--the unexpected Asian fusion was a wonderful touch.  I actually got a chance to taste hubby's NOLA bowl:  red beans, brown rice, sweet potatoes, Cajun slaw and other goodness topped with a millet muffin--those flavors work so well together.

He also had the fresh squeezed orange juice (no pulp, yay!)--smooth, refreshing, delicious. A bit pricey at $5 for an 8/10 ounce but worth it. 

Everything is fresh and they source some products from Whole Foods.  On top of that, nothing goes to waste--the OJ pulp is used in the miso dressing; and they compost other food items that they can't use.  Max Well is good for the planet and good for stomachs!  

I wish I could eat here everyday to fulfill my plant based diet (PBD) dreams.  It's really that good.  If you're wanting to give PBD a try, this is an awesome place that will make you want to never eat meat again.  So glad to have this PBD joint on the NOLA scene!

Nothing about this place says Chicago.  You walk into the most generic of places. We were seated and 10 minutes later had to literally get up and go find out server for dinner...   the pizza though is pretty good just not Chicago pizza.  We had breadsticks and cheese.  The server warned us the cheese was bad but let us try for ourselves. Stop serving this if it's not good.  Or find a better product. Kind of plays to the entire restaurant.  Cheap silverware.  Sub par service and pretty decent pizza. Rather not go there and get delivery though.
Not good at all!  Stick to your Mexican hole in the wall neighborhood joint!  This place is not Mexican!

Service is A+ food is A+ great location and overall great experience.  We all shared everything.  It was one of the best meals we have all had in a long time!  Just recommended it to an employe and they have not stopped talking about it!  Amazing!

Sunday's are amazing at Blue Sushi!  We always get great service and the discount menu is great!  Really our favorite Sunday spot now!  Love this.  Highly recommend it!  Great variety of options and won't set you back too much.

Average at best.  For the low cost steakhouses this is the bottom of the barrel!  The place is in a dirty strip mall and doesn't get better once you enter.  One of the worst steaks I've had tonight.  Full of fat and cold.  Not good.  Texas Roadhouse is so much better.

I enjoy this place.  The location is super convenient, but I don't always have the best experiences when I go..... and I keep trying!  Their beers are pretty good and drinks are tasty.   The atmosphere is fun and great for groups. The food has a great idea but poor execution.   I only ordered a wedge salad with pulled pork this past time and the pork was fatty and not shredded.  I was disappointed in the overall flavor.   The fries were great we had for an app though.  Service needs increased and food should be checked prior to coming out.  They have a great concept. But room to grow here!

Very cute place in the up and coming fountain square district.  

But....   

The food was average and would not recommend going back or wasting a good Italian dinner here!  

Few warnings... they do NOT make fresh pasta... but since they are just using hard pasta.. they should know how to cook it... both of our dishes were over cooked. 

They do not make fresh mozzarella.  

The service is slow.... we had empty drinks for far too long!  Not what you expect when paying over 100$ for dinner.

They no longer serve fried meatballs, but still have on menu... because they can't get consistency they said.  

That all being said...   the caprese and meatballs were good.  My fiancé liked her ravioli besides being over cooked and once I dumped their tasty red sauce on one of the driest pasta dishes ever.. it was delicious!

Tried for the first time last week and we enjoyed it!   The calzones were very large and they have lots of options and different sauces.  If you build your own, like we did... it gets pricey!    The Caesar salad is so good!  Highly recommend you get this!  The apple pie was NOT good.  Do not get this one!!  Overall pretty decent place.   Overpriced....   but we would go back if we are hungry and close to it.

2  is a generous review.  


We ordered tea and a draft beer...  they are out of tea and the beer we ordered. Also... the manager had to run to get cheese!  Red flags for poor management here!!  

Service was a negative star!  He was non existent and we were done before he even thought about checking on us!  Had to get our own drinks. 

The food wasn't bad.  Pizza a little greasy. But the rest of us has pretty good food!  I like the complete package though.  Service should match the dood.  And cleanliness should increase as well. The tables were sticky.  They have some work to do.  Could be a good spot since the food was pretty good.

Wild Ginger....  used to be my favorite sushi spot!  Close to home.... cute inside... great service.... decent sushi....  but after my visit on Friday, I just can't go back.  Everyone goes the the overly fried and famous - mistake roll, but that isn't really want most people are looking for when they go out for sushi.  It's tasty.  Their gyoza is tasty too, but the sushi just isn't fresh.  I made my fiancé not eat the soft shell crab roll because of the distinct flavor and smell, I knew it was bad.   We have had far better experience at other places in the city, I'm sad that I won't be going back!  I do hope they improve though because fishers needs them!

Office had lunch here today and we really love this place.  The service is always great.  Not just one server helping... everyone goes around filling drinks and taking up empty plates.  I ordered the large spinach salad and breadsticks!  The spinach salad is one of the best salads I've ever had.  Warm dressing, tomatoes, bacon, eggs, mushrooms.... so good!   The breadsticks are some of the best as well.  I had hummus and creamy parm with them.  They make both in house.  Coworkers ordered pizza and everyone was really happy with their meal.  Great place. Great service.  I recommend this place if you are in the area.

Great dinner tonight at Harry and Izzy's.... after a bad experience the last time we visited... we are sure fans again after tonight.   First let's talk about our server Alex... I'll be requesting him in the future if possible.  He was absolutely amazing. We had terrible service last time so Alex really made us enjoy our dinner so much more.  Jerry the helper was very good as well.   We had a simple dinner but the execution was exceptional as always.   The jalapeño margarita topped the list tonight though!  Wow.   Highly recommend.  Ask for Alex.

We really stumbled upon this place last weekend and were pleasantly surprised. Don't let the roads deter you!  The inside of the place hasn't changed from the past two bars that have been here.  I don't think they have an identity.... but we were going for food!   I tried the bloody like always and it was pretty good. I had the tenderloin and some kind of loaded fries that were great and she had a buffalo chicken wrap. We both left stuffed and happy!  I'd recommend this spot!! Enjoy.

Going to bring this review right back to reality!  With two reviews so far.... guessing that to be employees or owners!  

First time stopping in today and they did a great job with the atmosphere and decor. It was very clean and inviting.  Lots of tables and tons of room!  The service was good. Two guys and nobody else there.... so it was fast and friendly.  

The reason we went this morning was the the donuts part of this place.  We had to try them because we love us some donuts.  

They have a variety of classics and different flavors... basil in some! 

We tried the lemon basil with blueberry filling.  The raspberry filled chocolate and the chocolate filled long john.  

We were left feeling sad and depressed after eating these three donuts.... and wanting some thing to take away those memories. (We went to Starbucks) but seriously. I was excited to go.... disappointed I went after though.   

They got the 2 stars for the nice place and friendly service.  I hope their beer is good.  Go for the games.  Not the donuts.   Sorry.

Please don't go here for breakfast.   It was terrible!  Not the greasy spoon you want!  We had sausage gravy.  Eggs.  Blt.  Nothing was good.  We tried the donuts.  They aren't too bad. But that's all I would get.  Even the coffee was terrible.   Do not recommend this spot.  Been wanting to stop here for years.  And wish I would have just kept driving.

Unfortunately.... they'll come for the food and leave because of the service.  Probably the top restaurant of my childhood and I was so excited we finally got PK in Fishers... but I was left with a bad taste in my mouth!  

You walk in and seat yourself.  The decor is really nice.   But only being open a short time, the music already didn't work and all you heard was the phone ringing, because they sure don't answer!  

You actually order, like many old school PKs, from your table!  I like this but after 10 minutes waiting for drinks and only 3 tables in the dining area... I got up and asked to get drinks for our table.  Two sodas and two waters.    Our breadsticks came out but the sauces we asked for didn't come. They gave us bbq sauce!?  Who does that??   The pizza was great.  We got the royal feast and I love it!  The crust was a little thicker than usual.... but still had the great flavor.  

While we were there one guy yelled at the workers and stormed out.  

We had to ask for adult plates. They gave us saucers for our meal.  We didn't get enough napkins.  We didn't get peppers and cheese for our pizza.   It was just a cluster and will NOT stay open.  Come back to this post in 6 months and i promise.... they will have closed signs on the door if they don't get it together.  They need new management ASAP!

Tried it again... yes that is rare for me and I'm even more pleased with the food and service. This place is just great.  They even surprised me and had a Veterans Day menu that I took advantage of!  Wow. This is a great spot. They are hanging in there during construction.  Try them out!!

Tiny spot on a strip with amazing Mexican and subway... this is pretty good!  The decor inside needs some work.  The music is bad and the tv wasn't on....   the booth had been patched up and there were gnats flying around.....  

We ordered spring rolls and basil chicken.  Spring rolls were pretty good but the sauce needed help.  The basil chicken was the bomb.   We both really liked our main dishes.  I'd probably just get it to go next time.

Absolutely one of the worst experiences!  

I was super excited to try these... driven by for years and never stopped but my coworkers have said they are amazing and we were having a Christmas breakfast with our leadership group at work.... I said I'd order these for our team and they were responsible for drinks, plates, and napkins. 

I went online and ordered a breakfast tray or assorted varieties, scheduled delivery, paid $70 and that was so simple.  

It was supposed to be delivered at 7:45.... I called at 7:55 with a meeting at 8, asking where they were.   The store told me they had been read at 7:20 and just sitting there!  I was not happy. I do not recommend this place.   I was so excited and now I'm so disappointed.  Customer service was absolutely terrible along with their lack of accountability with the 3rd party delivery that they schedule.   Don't order these.

Another one of my favorites falling short here...   second time going, first time reviewing.... and unfortunate for them!  NYE dinner wasn't what we expected!!  Our service was absolutely terrible! Not sure if everyone was having an off night or what... but our first visit was so perfect.  We were upset we wasted our first NYE here.  Won't be going back to this one!!

Omg delicious!!  Stopped in this weekend to grab a few and wow!!  I don't have pictures because they were too good, ate them before I thought about it!!  So many options!!   I had a hard time choosing!  Really good spot in a great new location. Cinnamon rolls are so good too!   Must try in Fishers!!

I'll start with the amazing...  food, service, atmosphere, all are amazing.  We went for our fIRst visit and had brunch! We will be going back to try the rest!  The wife got shrimp and grits and I got biscuits and gravy... mmmmmmm mmmmmm was that a good  meal.  She had a mimosa and I had the fresh Bloody Mary!  They were all so good! And oh yes. We had the little donuTs for an appetizer, and I washed it all down with a glass of cold chocolate milk!  From the brown cows!  This place was great, my only request or specification would be to sit inside.  We sat on their enclosed patio next to a small space heater and froze!

Sunday's are amazing at Blue Sushi!  We always get great service and the discount menu is great!  Really our favorite Sunday spot now!  Love this.  Highly recommend it!  Great variety of options and won't set you back too much!  We have made this our go to spot and even tried others and just can't.  The place  is amazing and weird enough have one oF the best bloody Mary's.  We will see you there!

Let me start out with the one positive and reason they even get one star.... out service was wonderful.  Brandon did a great job!  We really appreciated him and his detail and dedication to his job.  

The food!  Devour has been said to be the reason this meal was terrible... but I don't think that is any reason to not put your best foot forward.  We compare this  steakhouse to the standards of Ruth's Chris and Harry and Izzys.  

We ordered the seared pork belly with fig Demi glaze and grits.  Sounds good right?  Terrible.  We both took a bite and left it.  Instant grits are terrible and the pork was all fat.  

The salads...  I ordered tHe Caesar and the wife ordered a seasonal. I dislike salads but she loves them and can eat a salad everyday.  My Caesar was an average salad and she actually hated hers.  Said the flavors did not mesh at all.  

We ordered the filet 8oz, famous potatoes and asparagus....  I order my Steak medium rare and this was the driest steak I've ever had.  Texas Roadhouse is never even like that.  I was so disappointed.  The potatoes come in a square from some reheated pan... and the asparagus had 0 seasoning.  

We did like our desserts, only guessing that Fleming's does not make those!  

We do not recommend this restaurant at all.  Don't pass up Ruth's Chris or Harry and Izzy's, both under a mile away.  We won't be going back!

The famous St Elmos and Harry and Izzys little burger restaurant doesn't meet the mark when you know the quality and service you  get  at the other establishments in the family. I expected high end service and great food...   I got neither.  

Planned a nice evening for our Valentines dinner and left disappointed.   Let me start by saying how they handled the situation was great and it's what I would expect... but serving a rare hamburger when you ask for medium is unacceptable.  I ordered the double major she ordered the espanol .  Mine was cooked fine, they were thin like Steak 'n Shake.  They didn't add the extra cheese I asked for but that's ok.  The salads were really good.  The chopped side salad but we both had issue with the tiny bowls and trying not to have half our salad on the table.   The fries are good.  But even though they comped the burgers and fixed hers, they just aren't great.  I even like Bru burger over that... and Fords garage was a lot better quality and service.   I say to stick to what they are known  for.  We won't be going back when there are so many other options.  This will be a tourist spot.

Tried this spot today for the first time.  We were one of two tables so we decided to sit in the bar. The bartender served us and he was great. Service was fast and friendly and we appreciated him.  We both had a beer, small salad,, and split a 10" pie.  She had the Greek salad no oLives and I had the chop chop salad.   I do have to say that the food gets different reviews!   The salads are huge, even for a small, and really tasty!  I did have a bone in my chicken - but I kept going! Haha.  I found out I don't like Gorgonzola cheese.... tastes like blUe cheese to me!  Nonetheless, they were  good.  The pizza was about average.   Once we got the ranch though, that helped out and I really liked their ranch.   With the service and the food, this is a solid 4.  We would go back to grab a quick bite.  We will stick with just a salad next time.

Night in was a success!  Texas Roadhouse never fails and they have adapted and overcome some large obstacles during this crazy time we are now in!   They had two girls out front directing traffic - one line for online and one area for call in!  People running food and running money in and out made this very organized and convenient!   The food is always good and they always take pride!  Service was awesome and you can tell how much they truly appreciate the community still showing up to support them!   Great experience!!  Tip big people!!

Yelp dine IN was great here for lunch!  Try to go here every year for my birthday because it's my favorite sammich!  Today was different with the pandemic, but that didn't stop us!  They had a great system and were really busy!!  A 20 minute wait and we were on our way!  I had the boilermaker with my changes and the wife had a turkey bagel!  Both were great with dirty chips and a scotcheroo!  So good!

The carry out is the second time in two weeks and it's been great! Tonight we learned they even serve margaritas to go!    Yes.  You read that right!! Margaritas to go!!!!   Haha. The staff here is great and always friendly! Tonight we got 6 chicken tacos and salads and queso, and man was it good!   Really great experience!  They have a fiberglass screen up over there counter and are being really safe!   They are cranking out food and being great about it!   I'd ask consumers to not use coupons!!  They are all hurting, let's spend the extra few bucks to help business and TIP big!!!!

Nobody answered.  And that continued for over an hour!  The car next to me, 2 hours!  Poor planning and terrible execution!   It'll be awhile before we go back to our once favorite sushi spot!   This was the worst and I'll choose others that had their shit together during this time.

Tried to go here today!  They are supposed to be open!  I parked and tried to get in, they pointed to a note on the door saying you couldn't go inside, but had a big sign on building saying open!   Guess they are a victim of fear and didn't want my money!   Went to the Westfield location who was open and ready for business like they are supposed to be!!   Great location in Westfield!  Don't go to this one!  Poor customer service and false advertising.  Difficult to get in/out as well!   Skip it!

I have heard nothing but good things from everyone who has tried this place.... so being a follower, I decided I must try it as well!  Haha.  Walking in it's a different feel and very bright.  It's more cafeteria style seating than anything.  The seating said cafe and the food said fine dining.  But who cares about decor and seating.... the food is what matters!  Service too though!  Our server was awesome. She had a sense of humor and took great care of us!  We started with the Crab Baguette.... omg that was delicious!!!  Our server told us the specials And talked me into the lasagna!   I'm so glad she did!!  The wife got the pasta Italiano and just loved it.  The gooey butter cake for dessert it s MUST as well!  Portions are large!  Go hungry!!  Enjoy!  
Missed one star because this place was not.  I hate being hot when I am eating indoors.  Next time I'll just wear a cut off shirt and I'll be happier. Haha.

I've been for dinner and that's hands down a 5. But this review is for brunch!  It was pretty empty in there today so that was nice!  The speaker was out above our table and it clicked loudly for the entire meal!  I would have turned them off!  Started with drinks and they were great! The cinnamon rolls were just flavorless and not good.  The consistency of the frosting was just not good!  We ordered.  The wife got the shrimp and grits- fabulous!  I ordered the filet Benedict.  One was great and one had a hard boiled egg on top!  Haha.  I need them to know how to properly poach an egg at this point!  Tasted great!  Filet was cooked perfectly.  Will be back for dinner.  But never brunch!

I find it really hard to believe this place is getting an average of 4 stars, c'mon Yelpers.  I hope I'll be able to update this review, but for now here's where I'm at:  I've been here twice now, once in the afternoon for some appetizers and (craft) beers during a Sunday Eagles game and a second time for a girls night out dinner.  In short, the first time my boyfriend and I ordered the spinach and artichoke wontons.  Out came a few, heavily breaded and fried, "wontons".  Okay so it wasn't what we were expecting and that's fine, but the middle of each wonton was barely warm.  Thumbs down.  Also this place claims to have a great craft beer selection, but really, it's mainstream stuff so don't get your hopes up.

A couple of weeks later my friend and I wanted to try somewhere new for dinner so we headed to 8 East.  We started the night off ordering a lemon drop martini each.  Hands down, this was the worst lemon drop martini I've ever had.  It tasted exactly like what I imagine paint thinner to taste like.  So we suffered through it adding a few ice cubes and a pack of sugar to tone it down and moved on to the food.  I ordered the buffalo chicken salad which came out without any dressing.  When I asked the server for dressing, she brought back a vinaigrette dressing, not the blue cheese dressing it's supposed to come with.  Then she disappeared for a while, finally returning after both our meals were finished to ask if we wanted another drink.

Like I said, hope to update this review in the future, but for now I'm disappointed.

Went here a week ago for the prixe fixe restaurant week dinner menu.  The food was fantastic.  I had the scallops to start, veal as main course and then the four of us shared the four desserts which were so so except for the mango sorbet which was fantastic.  My fiance had the skate and loved it.  One word of caution, which is probably no surprise and just the way things work, but the wine markups here are ridiculous or at least it was ridiculous for the bottle of Meritage by Lythe vineyards that we got.  Price of the bottle at the restaurant was $50...we found it at Canal's this weekend for $14.

In my constant attempt to try differeent pizza places in and near Conshy, we gave this place a try last Friday.  To sum it up, you can get a much better pizza for less $$ somewhere else.  First of all it took just under an hour for them to deliver a large cheese pizza to me, 8 blocks away.  Second of all the pizza had no flavor. NONE.  No spices in the sauce, and the crust was chewy and slightly soggy.  Won't be ordering from here again.

My fiance took me here for my birthday dinner this year.  What can you say about a place where the steaks are cooked to perfection with a beautiful spectrum of red visible in every slice?  The creamed spinach is right on par, rich by nature, but not so overwhelming that you can't eat more than one bite.  The service is impeccable and if you ask for wine recommendations within a certain price range they will gladly suggest a bottle of wine to go with your meal that is in that exact price range and most importantly, fabulous.  This was our 2nd time here and everything was incredible each time.  Tom, our server, was the best!  If it wasn't so expensive and I wasn't opposed to taking out a second mortgage on my house I'd eat here every night or at least more than once a year :)

One Saturday afternoon this summer my husband and I decided to check out some local wineries for fun.  We discovered this little gem via a recommendation by the folks at Penns Woods Winery.  We were absolutely blown away by the quality of their wines and the warmth and knowledge of their staff.  My husband and I are by no means wine snobs, but we were married in Napa Valley and have visited there a couple of times so we never have high expectations for Pennsylvania wines.  Galer really proved our expectations wrong.  Their wines are carefully crafted and absolutely delicious.  You really get a sense for the passion behind their wine making from MaryBeth in the Tasting Room.  She was extremely welcoming and walked us through the history of the winery as we tasted each of the wines.  We even got a tour of the production areas! After our tasting we didn't want to leave so we purchased a couple of glasses of wine and sat on their scenic patio chatting with another couple who kindly shared some cheese and crackers that they had brought.  Galer is truly a diamond in the rough, and we can't wait to return for another leisurely weekend afternoon.

I miss Viggiano's, the tasty BYOB that preceded this mess.  The food here was mediocre, at best.  It was entirely too salty and the sauce tasted like it came straight out of a jar.  Seriously.  I'd rather eat at Olive Garden.  They did have a nice wine selection so that's where the one star comes from.  Service was extremely slow, and the waitress was not attentive (my water glass was empty for at least 20 minutes). The grotto seating was pretty cool until the folks behind us lit up their cigarettes and the wind blew it in our direction. Yuck.  This place needs work on the food and service.  I will not be going back.

Went here with some friends from out of town for lunch yesterday to try their burger which has been touted as equals with Rouge downtown.  First impressions at a restaurant largely center around service for me, and Stone Rose missed this big time.  There were 2 people seated near the bar and 6 patrons outside when we arrived.  We walked in and stood at the bar looking for someone to seat us.  A hostess, manager, server was nowhere in sight.  We stood there for about 5 minutes and considered leaving just as a lady finally came up and asked if we needed something.  It's not what you say, it's how you say it and she acted as if we were a huge inconvenience to whatever conversation she was having in the back room.  We were seated with a snooty greating and a halfhearted "I'll be taking care of you today".  She took our drink order and came back a few minutes later with beers for each.  Then she took our food order and disappeared for at least 35 minutes before finally returning with our food.  With respect to the food the burgers and fries were absolutely fabulous, but unfortunately the poor service we received prevents me from giving any more than 3 stars, and to be honest, 3 stars is being generous here.  I'm sure we'll be back because it's close and they do have a nice happy hour special, but it would really be nice if they showed a little more customer appreciation by decreasing the attitude and stepping up the service.

My husband and I decided to try Pasta Via for some pizza one Saturday afternoon.  So we headed over with a bottle of red wine inside.  We sat outside, which was great for people watching.  The pizza was lackluster, at best.  It just didn't really have any flavor.  I would not go back for pizza since there are plenty of other great pies in the area, but I do want to go back to try their entrees which I've heard are very good.  I'll update my review once we've been able to try it, but for now, sorry Pasta Via, you're only A-OK. in my book.

I love local businesses.  I don't drink coffee, but I am obsessed with chai tea lattes and Feine makes a great one.  I love that the baristas offer you different milk options too. I've tried both the almond milk and 1% milk version.  My preference is the latter, but props to them for even offering almond milk as an option.  This place is great and I hope it's here to stay in Conshy for a long time.

In a word, this place is fabulous.  Fantastic, unique dishes priced just right.  And the fact that it's a BYO is icing on the cake.  The service is fabulous and the servers really know what they're talking about.  I've been here twice now, once with my husband for date night and then with larger group for his mom's birthday. The food was fabulous both times. The only thing that some people may consider as a drawback is that it can be quite noisy since it's  smaller place and typically packed.  I wouldn't let that deter you from enjoying the great food and service for a really reasonable price. The tab for the two of us came to a mere $60 and we had ordered 2 appetizers, 2 entrees, dessert and coffee.  Definitely, a must visit for the foodies at heart.

One of my fellow diners summed up our experience best by saying "I really wanted to love this place."  I did! But alas, we left feeling anything but love for The Twisted Tail.  In fact, this might be one of the worst dining experiences ever.  In summary, terrible service and so-so food led to a painful 3 hour meal.  For those of you interested in the details, read on.

Our group of 5 had a reservation at 7:30pm Wednesday night of restaurant week. Upon arrival the hostess asked us to go to the bar After 30 minutes one of us went to check in to see if our table was ready. Nope.  Another 15 minutes later we went back and conveniently the hostess was "just coming to get us".  It wasn't crowded so I'm not sure why we couldn't have been seated elsewhere instead of waiting 45 minutes for the previous group of 5 gabbing girls to leave.  As an aside, said group of girls received their check well before they actually got up and left. It would have been nice if the hostess would have politely asked them to move along to the bar because another group was waiting. Famished, we sat down and started to salivate in anticipation of the pending meal. Another few minutes passed before we met our server.  After some brief deliberation over menu items we each ordered all four courses at once.  Thirty minutes later the first course made its way out to our table. (Some complimentary cornbread to hold us over would've been a nice touch as it was an hour and a half after our planned dining time). Silence fell over the table as we scarfed the crawfish mac 'n cheese x 3 (there were 2 crawfish in one bowl...TWO), the shishito pepper salad (literally a bowl full of grilled peppers...my stomach is still burning a day later), and mussels.  Overall it was just okay. Anxious for the next course conversation resumes at the table and we wait ANOTHER 30 minutes. This time we have the mushroom salad, corn on the cob, empinadas, and sausage x2.  The flavors of each were unremarkable.  ANOTHER 30 minutes passed and the entrees arrive (are you kidding me? What are they doing back there?!):  2 orders of crab cakes and 3 chickens in a bag.  The crab cakes were tasty and a way better deal than the chicken in a bag which basically looked and tasted like KFC. On the menu the chicken in a bag was to be accompanied by sweet potato fries.  There was a whopping TWO fries in each of the bags. At this point we still had dessert on deck...cue another 30 minute wait except this time they surprised us and it was only a 20 minute wait.  Either way, we were all ready to be done and get the heck out of there. Unfortunately we forgot to ask for our check as soon as dessert came and then it took another 10 minutes for our server to reappear.  Finally, at 10:30pm, THREE HOURS after our reservation we walked out of there.  This was the most egregiously long and unfulfilling dining experience I've ever had, and that's why I'm giving it one star.  If I could give 0 I would. It should be noted that half of that one star goes for the good music and people dancing but that's not nearly enough to make me go back. Ever.  What a disappointment.  If anyone from the management is reading this PLEASE learn to manage your customers' expectations and improve your service. Throughout this whole ordeal we received ONE apology, a semi-sincere "Sorry about the wait" when we were seated.
Service is consistently poor and food is just okay.  They are one of few places with outdoor seating in Conshy which is pretty much the only thing that keeps me coming back.

Stopped in here for a quick brew and snack with my husband and we were both pleasantly surprised. The ambience is really cool since it's in an old bank. The beers are pretty solid. We had the hummus plate and the red and yellow pizza. The hummus plate was amazing. I would come back just for that and a beer. The red and yellow pizza was okay. The tomatoes were a little mealy and should have been wrung out before being put on the pizza because the pizza was really soggy. I can see where parking might be a bit of an issue at times however they have a sign out front directing patrons to the lot across the street which was super helpful since we're not from the area.  Bottom line is we'll definitely (and happily) be back!

I would love to be able to give more stars and a better review, but Blue Bell Inn you just don't deserve it.  The ambience is awesome especially with the outdoor patio but the food is sub par and service is just okay.  We popped in for Sunday brunch and sat outside on a gorgeous sunny day.  That was the best part.  We ordered the cinnamon rolls to start and some coffee. The cream cheese frosting was amazing but the rolls themselves were dry and the cinnamon goo was not as hot, warm or runny as it should've been.  The coffee was warm, not hot.  Next up, huevos rancheros which the menu would have you believe come in a tortilla however in fact they came on a bed of greasy tortilla chips.  Not what we were after and the portion was pretty scant. We also had the French toast which was equally underwhelming and not very flavorful.  It was two slices of thick bread with Nutella spread in the middle, hazelnuts sprinkled on top and half of a banana, carmelized.  To sum it up, overly expensive sub par food in a really nice setting with so-so service.  Wish this place would step it up and match it's atmosphere and ambience with good quality food.

Beers are always so-so. This was our third visit. We may or may not return. The brew pub is cool. Wish there was more outdoor seating. The deviled eggs need work. They were rubbery and tasted like hot dogs.

I have been a regular customer at this grocery store since it opened few months ago. From the very beginning the things seem unorganized and service appalling. The people working at the deli meat counter also work at the restaurant so I usually have to wait for sometime before anyone comes to help me out. Their cafe drinks r bad, most r made from a Nespresso machine. 

During my last visit few days ago, when I was checking out the guy at the counter said, "you have a free coffee with this purchase", I was like "oh thank you". But then I realized that he had actually over charged me and didn't even tell me. Instead he was going to give me a coffee if I wanted! I was shocked, never had anyone overcharge me and not let me know about it. Now I wonder if they did the same in the past and I just never bothered to check. 

If you do go there, do check your receipt!

Love their pizza! Please note that the rating is based on their pizza dish only. I haven't tried any of the non pizza stuff, other then few appetizers. 

I have tried many of their thai pizza and love it. The service is not bad and the lady who works at the kitchen and I am guess manages the restaurant is very nice!

Love their store brand ice-cream! 

They have large variety of great precooked food selection! Love their bakery section too!

Love their bakery selection! Love their coffee drinks. Always well made. Oh and great service! 

Some of their prepackaged sandwiches are not reasonably priced. So just order from their main menu and get freshly cooked food at about the same price.
Mediocre burger and the restaurant itself feels more like a lobby. Parking was a pain since they share the same parking area as the residents living in that building.
Great selection of beer. Never been to a place where they don't serve food but allows you to bring your own. I love this idea. I am sure to come more often!
They served the president few times. But other than that, I don't understand what the fuss is about. I didn't like the pizza. The restaurant is decorated poorly. Service is OK.
I just didn't find anything that makes their menu standout from any other desert menu at any mediocre restaurant.

Great wine selection but the food was mediocre. I would suggest going to their other restaurant next door Taste Bar. 

They both provide valet parking, if needed.

Service: Came here with a friend for a cup of cappuccino today (Jan 17). Told the barista that we are having our drinks at the cafe. So when I got my drink he gave it in a to go club and said "sorry, we don't have any large cups". I said its perfectly fine. But I thought it was odd because after all its a cafe and it should have cups for what they serve. Then I saw at least fifteen coffee cups of all sizes on the expresso machine. I am not clear of his intention but my best guess is that he just didn't want to be bothered with cleaning up the coffee cups assuming he is the one doing it since he was only one working at the store when we were there. 

Cappuccino: I can say from my experience that this cappuccino was one of the worst I have had in a long time. I cappuccino from Starbucks would probably taste better than here and cheaper too. 

Food: They had no bakery products left, I came around 4:30pm and they close at 6pm so it is entirely possible that they ran out of food. So I don't have any comments on that side. 

Vibe: Its very crude. It seemed like they were roasters who had some extra space so decided to put some tables and chairs. They have a great outside space that has good potential. So if the whether is good, outside is definitely the better spot. 

I came here entirely because of the great Yelp rating they have. I am disappointed.

Saw this place while walking around Loop. Obviously can't stop myself from trying out new cookie store, so I went in. It first reminded me of Dominos pizza delivery store, it seemed like majority of their sales were delivery. I don't have any problem with that after all I wasn't planning on eating it there. 

However, I do expect a good service. The girl at the counter seemed annoyed when I came in. anyway, I got three different cookies, she took it out from a draw. I think its a place where it stays warm, so I have no idea when it was made. All I know is it was warm. I tried the white chocolate and macadamia and it tasted great, however after few bites it had this strange aftertaste. I felt like it was made from poor quality ingredients and/or sitting in that draw for little too long. I am no expert on cookies but I have had very unhealthy level of cookies in my lifetime. 

Anyway, after trying the first cookie I gave up. Didn't try the other two. 


Tip to Customers: If u do go to this store, know that the little larger cookies are twice the price of the smaller ones, so get two smaller ones. However, I think some of the cookies are not in smaller version.

Tip to the Owner: You are selling cookies not chicken wings, appropriate environment with proper seating and smiling employees will go a long way to build loyal customer base. Review your pricing, use better ingredients and you can charge more.

I have been there for few gatherings and only had drinks so the rating is mainly for the service and their drinks. They have decent drinks and service is good. They place is relatively small but cozy. 

Parking was hard and I would advice bringing some quarters since most parking lots around that area only accept coins.
I went there to get some take outs. I tried few different burgers after a friend recommended this place. The burgers are good but I won't call them outstanding. The prices are reasonable.

The burgers were very mediocre, I have no idea why this place is known for its burger. The fires were just OK. The quality of the pretzel bun n meat were of average quality. I paid $13 something for the Three Kings Burger on a pretzel bun, I don't think its worth the price tag.

Been there several times and I think its one of my favorite spot in STL. Reasonable price for the quality of the food, service and the vibe. I especially love their breakfast pizza. Their italian donuts are great too. I wish they serve them warm!

Have no idea why they charge $25 for a haircut when they don't even shampoo! They serve you beer, which is a good and actually most salons do provide refreshments these days but the only reason people come here is to get a haircut. They neither do a good job and nor is the service worth the price.

Great place to have coffee or tea and get some work done. There are several large and comfortable single chairs, perfect place if you are coming by yourself. 
During my visits, I had no problem finding parking on the street.

I am have no idea why this café has such a high rating. The place is terribly decorated with uncomfortable chairs. I had a mocha and a cookie (they had only 3 baked goods, truly a MICRO-bakery). The mocha was barely warm (Price: $5). The cookie was hard and bland. I won't recommend this place to anyone.

This café is my favorite in St. Louis. I live 20mins from their location but I like it so much that I don't mind the drive. I have never been disappointed by their coffee drinks, baked goods or gelato. Oh and they make their own gelato! Its very good! Love their big french windows and the staffs are friendly. 

Free parking can be hard in this location, I suggest bringing some quarters.

I have been there several times and I found it very unexceptional. During one of my morning visits, I ordered a mocha and biscuits with butter. The mocha was mediocre and they didn't even warm the biscuit. Seats are not very comfortable.

It is unfortunate that there is no good cafés in the Loop area even though there is a large pool of potential customers.

This Starbucks is located within the Olin Business School at Washington University in St. Louis. It has all the drinks and snacks that you can find at any other regular Starbucks. The hours tend to vary depending on the school schedule. During regular school time it opens at 7am and closes at 8pm on weekdays. 

I love this Starbucks because of the amazing baristas and the other people working there. They are all friendly and always have smile on their face even when they tend to get overwhelmed by long lines of students. 

The people in green brings smile to all the students who come to get their caffeine fix. 

I will miss you guys during the summer break :(
