Brother John's satisfies my bbq craving without having to drive too far. Great atmosphere and fantastic staff. Seeing as this was a whiskey bar, I felt inclined to order a drink. After revealing to the bartender I was more of a beer guy, he was happy to help me find a drink to my liking with just a couple questions. I ordered the brisket sandwich with pit beans and a side of mac 'n cheese. The sandwich was a little thin and a little dry, but I threw some pit beans on it and was quite pleased. The mac 'n cheese was delicious, but also a bit smaller than I had expected. 

Overall, despite the high prices/small portions, it was an enjoyable experience and I would go there again.

10/10. I've been a customer at D's since their food truck days, when I would drive all over town looking for their parking spot. The fact that they were able to open their own restaurant made me so happy, but hesitant. I was worried they wouldn't be able to stay open for very long (new restaurants often fizzle out here in Tucson), but here they are two years later and killing it. 

The special was a BBQ pork sandwich day, so I went for it. First of all, the price was great. $8.99 for a huge sandwich, fries, and drink beats most lunch deals in town and comes with a lot more food... but I digress. As I said before, the sandwich was huge.. and oh so delicious. I usually get the jerk pork, but this was a good change of pace and would definitely get it again. Festivals are a must!

Hands down my favorite hot dog cart in town, also happens to be a few blocks from my house. Buns toasted perfectly and onions grilled just the right amount. Bacon always cooked to crispy perfection.

Price did go up from $2.5 to $2.75, but you won't hear me complain.

Great beer, good food, and a friendly staff. Been going there for years and have seen things change over time. Prices aren't too bad, so you can sit around and eat for a while and not hurt your wallet. 
Great for happy hour and/or Sunday football.

My first choice on Bar night. Plenty of bar space, plenty of bar games (darts, shuffle board), 4+ pool tables, air hockey, and pinball. Good prices and friendly staff. 

Plus they're down the street from me, so that's an added bonus.

A couple friends and I recently went to Throwbacks for the UA-ASU basketball game and unfortunately came away disappointed. 
Beer prices were good and there were plenty of the to watch the game on, but that was the bet part. 

Despite the rather low number of customers, service was slow and I had to ask for silverware more than once. Meals came out and things looked fantastic. However, my medium green chili burger came out well and my friend's grilled cheese came out soaked in oil from the Parmesan fries. Friend sent back fries rather peacefully and the sandwich she got back was the same sandwich but with new bread. 

Overall, I'm willing to try Throwbacks once more in hopes of a better experience, but this one trip earned the proverbial two strikes.

Hands down my favorite restaurant in Tucson. I've been coming to Boca for years and have never left disappointed. From the local craft brew and awesome tequila selection to the delicious tacos and house-made salsas, this place is a must for all. The staff (most of whom have been there for years and greet me like a friend when I walk in) are crazy friendly and hard-working. 

My most recent visit happened to coincide with Exotic Taco Wednesday, which has slowly made Wednesday my favorite day of the week. This week brought us sea urchin, which is something I'd never think of trying. It was definitely... peculiar, but when can you say you've eaten sea urchin? I also ordered an octopus taco because it's the best one on the menu. A little chewy (not a complaint, but more of a heads up) but fantastic.

The definition of a dive bar, but I mean that in a good way. My friends and I usually go on Sunday for the $.50 taco bar and can easily kill three or four hours just playing pool and listening to the jukebox. Prices are right, bartenders are friendly, and the place is always clean.

Hot damn. This was hands down the best donut I've ever eaten. My roommate came home with a 6pack of gourmet donuts and I've never loved him more (in a completely heterosexual and strictly food manner). He got me an apple pie/peanut butter monstrosity and it was breathtaking. The s'mores one was almost as good, but nothing is ever as good as that first bite. 

10/10 
Need to go back
May develop gnarly addiction

So normally I'm not a huge fan of the college bar scene and try to stick to the many dive bars around town.

However, when I'm feeling fancy or want to take my girl out on the town, hermano's is almost always a stop for us. Their tap list consistently has a plethora of great beers to choose from (and that's coming from someone who is rather picky about what he drinks), whether you like IPAs, Sours, Milk Stouts or just fizzy yellow beers. The couple of times I tried it, the food was incredible, but I'm really only there for the beer haha. 

Great date spot

9/10

Very friendly staff and good beer selection. Dropped by here with some buddies for an hour or two and was pleasantly surprised. They had a number of pool tables, both inside and outside on the patio (which was pretty cool), plus they had darts and other bar games. Good bar munchies.

I'd go back, and I'd bring friends.

Hands down my favorite hot dog cart in town, also happens to be a few blocks from my house. Buns toasted perfectly and onions grilled just the right amount. Bacon always cooked to crispy perfection.

Price did go up from $2.5 to $2.75, but you won't hear me complain. 

UPDATE (7/24/17) 

They added another location across from the Mitsubishi dealership on Speedway and it's still awesome. 

Go check them out!

I don't hit 4th too often, but when the woman wants to go out we usually head to the Flycatcher. Decent beer selection and good staff, plus they usually play good music (the Mrs. loves the Emo and Heavy Metal Nights). $4 for a Budweiser in a bottle is a little disappointing, but otherwise it's the place to be.

Love the new location. The bar is fantastic and a much-needed improvement from the origins location. Great rotating beer list with delicious local beers (cheers to the Crooked Tooth Sour and the Elysium StarDust the Mrs. and I ordered tonight). 

I ordered the octopus (of course) and the ETW (which happened to be Wild Boar this week) and they were both incredible, like always. Apparently not too many people got the Exotic today, so I might have to go back for more tomorrow. This being the Mrs. first time, she got the tofu and the AM, to which she said "It was actually really good!".

I've never been a huge fan of pho, but this place was fantastic. I got the shrimp, crab and squid bowl and I was not disappointed. The Mrs. ordered the veggie bowl and even that was great. Hostess/server was very friendly and helpful. 

Only downside was the price, as two bowls ran us about $25

This place... I'll admit I was pretty skeptical. I've been a meat eater all my life and growing up the idea of an all-vegan restaurant was just unheard of. Meanwhile, the Mrs. has been vegan/vegetarian for a long while and this is one of her favorite restaurants in town. So one day she decides I need to try and you could say I was less than excited. 

Walking in, I immediately noticed the smell. It was a light and almost healthy smell (with a hint of Chinese?) and I was reminded how hungry I was. Looking at the menu, a few things stood out to me. One was the buffalo cauliflower hot wings, which I immediately called "blasphemous". I mean come on... How could that possible be good? The next thing I noticed was the BBQ Bacon Cheeseburger. Veggie bacon? Nope, not happening. Then I spied what was basically a Philly cheesesteak, but with grilled mushrooms instead of steak. That sounded fantastic, but I saved that for my next trip (and yes, there will be a next trip) and went with the veggie burger with homemade BBQ sauce (but no fake bacon). I was surprised at how much I liked it, and how good I felt after eating it. I'm glad the woman dragged me to this place and I'm looking forward to our next visit. 

Oh, and those buffalo cauliflower wings? Holy sh*t. They blew my mind and I considered going back for a second order. They tasted almost exactly like boneless chicken wings!

A buddy and I needed a place to watch the MNF game, so he recommended his neighborhood chain bar. Walked in and was amazed by the number of TVs they had... They even had my Red Sox game on! Their draft beer selection was surprisingly good, albeit a little pricey. 

The food is where they lost me, however. My buddy ordered the mozzarella sticks (which I enjoyed) while I had the fried brussel sprouts (which were honestly terrible). The chicken tender dinner was $13 and was not worth it. Three decently-sized tenders and two little winglets, plus a handful of fries? While the fries were good, there weren't enough of them to make up for the price. 

My buddy swears by the place and keeps going back, so I'm hoping I just ordered the wrong things and that my next trip will turn out a little better. 

**My phone died near the beginning of the game, so I was unable to take some pictures. I'll take some next time.

Finally decided to go in after weeks of walking past it and was not disappointed. Quaint interior and friendly(ish) staff. Good prices and quite the beer list, including one from my favorite hometown brewery (Port Brewing). 

Daily specials were homemade Meatloaf Burger and Veggie Burger, so naturally those were our orders. Good size and came with a crazy amount of fries (great seasoning as well). I thought the meatloaf was fantastic, deliciously grilled onions and the sauce was spot on. My better half really enjoyed her veggie burger, although I found it to be a bit... peculiar haha.
Probably the best Indian buffet in town. I appreciate the number of vegetarian options, but I'd also appreciate a few more meat options. Friendly staff and great price.

My favorite place to stop when I need to spoil myself. Prices can be a little high, but when you're the best shop in town you can afford to be pricey. 

They have an incredible amount of options and almost all of my favorite beers, although I can really only speak about the beers. I'm yet to venture into the whiskey section, but they appear to have a plethora of bottles and brands.

"I like coming here to drink until I can't feel my face and dance to the music I used to cry to." 

-Anonymous

The Mrs. and her roller derby folks really like coming here because it's the only alternative bar on 4th. They have air hockey and very friendly bartenders. Not to mention the $4 Rock 'n Shot (shot of whiskey and a Rolling Rock). 

They have an occasional $5 cover charge, so that can be a bummer.

I've always been a fan of food trucks and had been hearing great things about this one. While at work I decided to drop by and grab the strongly suggested pork burrito. Enjoyed the atmosphere around the truck and didn't mind the slight wait and also though $6.50 was a pretty good deal for the size. 

Got home 15 minutes later and dove in to find a damn good pork sandwich (complete with Cole slaw)... but in a tortilla. Pork tasted fantastic, tortilla cooked perfectly, maybe could have used a little (more?) sauce (maybe in the slaw) but I still really enjoyed it.

Looking forward to trying this place again.

Really good  with lots of vegan options. Vegan cauliflower is da best. Super friendly staff and plenty of seating. Kinda wish they were open later than 6pm. 

Side note: The burritos are huge and cheap. Like chipotle but better.

3.5/5

Huge (and delicious) pancake, potatoes were a little too crispy (the Mrs. liked them), and there wasn't any creamer for the coffee (they were a bit too busy to ask). 

Semi-friendly staff (probably due to the rush) and great food. Great for a hangover or breakfast date with the better half.

One of the better hotdog stands in Tucson. I just moved away from the Pima/Alvernon area and had been missing my usual hotdog guy, but Los Ponchos fills the void quite well. Friendly staff and good prices, plus they have a quesadilla with hotdogs inside. How can you beat that?

Meh. 

OK beer selection and comfortable seating, but the music is too loud, staff is not really that friendly, and it's really just an OK kind of place. I'll go if someone specifically suggests it, but otherwise....

Che's Lounge is a great hangout spot on fourth avenue. It has a large smoking patio with a small patio bar and a stage. The inside is fairly small and that's usually where all of their bands play, so it can get very crowded. The staff is very friendly and down to earth. Drink prices are standard. The "Tucson Water" cocktail is to die for- it even has a salidito inside of it 

Che's also has probably on of the best juke boxes in Tucson, along with a two player Ms. Packman machine and a sticker machine with stickers made by local artists. It's rad!

One of the many great restaurants at the Grant/First intersection, this little gem was fantastically delicious. 

Dropped in for a quick lunch and noticed there was one server (and one sushi chef) for the entire restaurant. It took a little while for the server to make it to our table and pretty soon he was nowhere to be found. 

I ordered the Oyaki Don (chicken, veggies, and egg over rice) and a spicy crab roll and both blew my mind. The crab roll was better than any roll I've had in Tucson and the chicken bowl was incredible. Chicken cooked perfectly and just the right amount of egg. 

Overall, this has become one of my favorite new restaurants and feel the need to share it with others.

Great breakfast date spot. Walked in on New Year's Day and immediately found a seat for the Mrs. and I. The service was fantastic and we'll definitely be back. 

I ordered the #12 omelette with potatoes and sourdough toast. The potatoes were incredible and the toast buttered to perfection. The omelette, however, I was a little disappointed in. I feel like there was still a bunch of water in the veggies, so the omelette itself was a bit watery. 

Overall, I won't let the watery omelette ruin my experience and I'll just order something different next time.

Hot damn. 

The Mrs. and I were craving pho this morning but, upon discovering our favorite restaurant was closed, decided to try K Japanese as it was within walking distance of my house. We walked in at 11 (which is when they open) and found the place empty. The entire staff greeted us and were super friendly and the menu was detailed and easy to read. 

The food was fantastic. We ordered a Monkey Ball without knowing exactly what to expect and had our minds blown by what we received. This sushi thing was huge! Perfect amount of tuna and the fried outer layer wasn't too thick. We then split a red dragon roll, tootsie roll, and an unagi roll and were not disappointed. The rice/good stuff ratio was perfect and this was the freshest eel I've had (in Tucson, that is) in ages, the tuna was flawless, and you can always count on a tootsie roll. 

Total bill came out to be $36 which is a little pricey... but considering what we ordered, it was definitely worth it and I'd pay this over the $25 all you can eat at Sushi Garden any day. 

Overall, I'd give it a 4.5/5. This could possibly become my go to spot for sushi (especially since they're next door) and I hope their business is steady enough to keep the doors open. It'd be a shame to lose this place.

4.5 stars out of 5

I went a couple of times back in California and have been craving it ever since, but was S.O.L. considering we didn't have one in Tucson... 

UNTIL NOW

What a burger. Hands down the best fast food burger in Tucson. Unfortunately the only location is on the opposite side of town, but that'll keep me from visiting too frequently and risk losing it's appeal. 

I ordered the portobello (it says portobella on the menu...) with garlic aioli and it was phenomenal while my buddy ordered the bbq bacon burger (two of them, actually...). He was blown away by the service (compared it to a Chick-fil-A) and said he'd come back to try the portobello burger before EVER visiting a five guys or In-N-Out. 

Jesse- 5/5 "Let's go back"

Fantastic hidden gem just off 4th Ave. 

I noticed Revel had opened some time ago but was never really a wine guy, so I figured why go? However, the Mrs. likes wine and has me trying new wine from time to time. Last night we had a date night and I thought "Shoot, let's try somewhere new and fancy" and we found ourselves at Revel. 

It's a super hipster place with a great atmosphere and vibe, plus the staff was incredibly friendly and helpful. The wine selection was extensive and had options I'd never heard of and, while the beer options were limited, I enjoyed my Belgian.

The Mrs. and I went on a lunch date the other day and randomly decided we'd give Yard House a try. I had been there countless times before and always enjoyed myself, but this was her first time so I was hoping it'd be extra great. 

The server was super friendly and patient with me as I took a little too long ordering my drink. When the food came out, it looked incredible. I ordered the bbq bacon burger and when I took that first bite... I came away disappointed. My bacon was delicious and the bbq sauce great, but the patty itself was pretty darn charred. The majority of my burger was this way, so I ended up taking half home with me only to end up eating the toppings and tossing the patty. The Mrs. ordered the black truffle burger and to my surprise her patty was ALSO charred and carbony. We really enjoyed our fries/onion rings/lobster and crab dip, but definitely came away wishing for more from the burgers. 

Maybe it was just a one time thing and next time will be better?

Crazy good breakfast joint. Not your typical greasy spoon breakfast, as it's lacking in the grease (which is definitely a good thing). When the Mrs. and I go out to breakfast, I normally leave feeling lethargic and fat, but hat was not the case this time. I definitely felt full, but there was no grease hangover. 

I got the biscuits and gravy with bacon and eggs, and those were some darn good biscuits. The gravy? Heavenly and probably made by someone from the South. The bacon was cooked perfectly (I like mine a little on the softer side) and the eggs didn't even need hot sauce (but I used it anyway, cause some like it hot). 

The Mrs. ordered the Snickerdoodle pancake and oh my... I've had "specialty" pancakes before where it was so rich that you couldn't eat it (looking at you, ihop) but this thing was insanely good and definitely not too sweet. The only reason we didn't finish it was because we got full, but you can bet we took that sucker home. It even tasted great cold and straight from the fridge! 

In short, the food was crazy good, it's walking distance from our house, and the staff was friendly and helpful. We'll definitely be back to try out the menu.

It's about time. 

I moved to Tucson just about eight years ago and all I've ever wanted was some darn good BBQ. Everyone gushed about Brushfire but it just never did it for me. I was constantly on the hunt for something worth my money and time and now my waiting has paid off. I decided to try this place on my own before dragging the Mrs. to just another brushfire. 

This place is located in the old burger stand at First and Grant and is very much worth a stop. The first thing I noticed was the smell. Hot damn, what a smell. The super friendly staff helped me pick out the brisket sandwich and it was incredible. Great sauce and not too dry, plus the bun was toasted perfectly. My dad always told me "You can tell a good bbq joint by how good their beans are"... so naturally I ordered a side of beans. One bite and I was in love. I threw some on the brisket and came away soooooo satisfied. 

Tldr: 9/10 Would definitely go back

I think we just found our new "feeling fancy spot". 

The Mrs. and I were celebrating and decided to try somewhere new. We choose a restaurant we'd been wanting to try for quite some time and thought this would be the night. We are seated and about 8 minutes later decide "Nah, we'll pass". So we get in the car, drive across the street, and pull up to Dante's Fire. 

As soon as we walked in we knew this was the place to be. There was just something about the place - be it the staff looking dapper in their black and bow ties or just the overall vibe of the place - that told us we'd made the right choice. We look at the menu and everything sounds good. The drinks sound delicious and the food... It took me 15 minutes to decide what I wanted, as there were way too many great options. 

She went with the Ajo Asado Pasta and I chose the red sauce pasta dish (I can't recall what it was called) and both were incredible. The crab in my pasta was delicious and the noodles were perfect. Like, from now on, I want all my pasta to be served with these noodles. Her dish was like a beef stroganoff, only waaaaaaay better. It had that home-cooked and comfort food vibe, but with an elegant and hearty take on it. 

We're already taking about going back and you should definitely make a trip down there. Easily one of the best restaurants in town. 

9/10 
Pros: Everything 
Cons: A little pricey, but worth it

It's about time. 

I moved to Tucson just about eight years ago and all I've ever wanted was some darn good BBQ. Everyone gushed about Brushfire but it just never did it for me. I was constantly on the hunt for something worth my money and time and now my waiting has paid off. I decided to try this place on my own before dragging the Mrs. to just anothebrushfire. 

This place is located in the old burger stand at First and Grant and is very much worth a stop. The first thing I noticed was the smell. Hot damn, what a smell. The super friendly staff helped me pick out the brisket sandwich and it was incredible. Great sauce and not too dry, plus the bun was toasted perfectly. My dad always told me "You can tell a good bbq joint by how good their beans are"... so naturally I ordered a side of beans. One bite and I was in love. I threw some on the brisket and came away soooooo satisfied. 

Tldr: 9/10 Would definitely go back 

UPDATE FROM SATURDAY 10/13:

I ordered the two meat combo and chose the pulled pork and the tri tip, with beans and Mac n cheese on the side. The tri tip was great, but the pulled pork was horribly disappointing. It was dry, full of charred pieces, and had very little sauce. I'm sure more sauce would have covered up the char, but the combination of dry and charred left me sad.

On a good day, it's really good BBQ. On a bad day... Let's just say you won't regret dropping by but you might end up wishing you could have ordered something different.  

7/10

Heartbroken. 

This place was incredible, from the salad bar to the sandwich deli, but ever since Time Market took over... This place has been on my "avoid list". The salad bar was the only reason I would come in, but the UA-themed decor and friendly staff kept me coming back time and time again. Now this place is soul-less and just Time Market but worse.

Stop the press, we've got a new king of barbecue here in Tucson. If you're a BBQ fan, you have to stop by. 

In the old Mr. K's location at Park and Silverlake is easily THE BEST BARBECUE IN TUCSON. It's a little hard to see, but I'd be driving past it and wondering for quite some time. Today I finally stopped by and boy am I glad I did. 

I was met by a friendly man and woman (his wife?) and ordered the sampler, asking him to pick the meat options for me. He chose brisket, ribs, and a hot link and -upon trying each of them - I knew I had made a good call having him decide. All three were delicious and the sauce was spot on.

Great food; one of the best bbq options in Tucson. 

It took me a few months after they opened to actually make it down there, but I'm glad I finally did. I usually get the bell ringer, which is two meats and two sides. Their pulled pork is damn good and their brisket is mouth-watering, but the killer would have to be the ribs. Only available on Fridays, they are definitely worth the trip. Their sides are bomb, from the beans to the bacon slaw. 

Plus they have RC Cola and Hires Root beer, so you can't go wrong there.

A must if you're a coffee person. Super chill vibe and a beautiful location, you could easily sit there for hours and get lost in a book or homework. Super friendly staff make the experience that much better.

The Bomb.com. 

It's a little known place with dang good street tacos, awesome Sonoran hotdogs, and a good beer selection. Great location and the owner/cook is super friendly. 

Try the jerk chicken tacos!

Literally the worst Carl's Jr... No, worst overall fast food location I've ever been to. It always takes roughly 15 minutes to get your food, no matter what you order. I've received moldy buns, wrong orders, and rude customer service. 

Major shame its the nearest Carl's by miles, so I'm not left with many options.

A really solid option for a quick and light lunch. 

The location is a little bit of a deterant, but they say you can never judge a book by the cover and this is a prime example. The staff was super friendly and welcoming, the chicken fried rice bowl was simple and satisfying, and the egg roll was perfect. 

Like I said, a really solid and simple lunch option. Stop by, you won't regret it.

Z8Dv-N42EfoCkQ_MP6npmA.review_text: The food is great, but the wait can be daunting. I always try to go during non-peak hours if it is on a weekend. I love the décor, they have cleverly used the upstairs as additional seating. It has a nice vibe and I've always had delicious food. My uncle came into town and had done his research, he demanded we eat here, and he was not disappointed. I wish they would open a second location so more people could enjoy the place.

One of my favorite places to stop in. As a 30 something, this place is on my must take list when friends visit town. The beer selection is incredible- all of my favorites: Delirium Tremens, Frambois Lambic, Stella, etc plus domestics too. The staff is quick, to the point, and friendly. There must be only four or so of them, because I'm always seeing the same faces. The place is small and I love to sit at the bar, which is sometimes the only seating available. The menu is limited but all items are on point, and I find myself craving the croquetas. The lamb grinder is also a great choice. I felt welcome and at home the very first time I visited thanks to the friendly atmosphere and dive feel (said with love).

Maybe it's because I am originally from Texas, but I have never eaten a steak here that blew my mind, and certainly not for the price they charge. After three visits, I had the best experience with a fish dish. I'm giving four stars because I do like the upscale option downtown and the food is good, just expect to pay.

Ambiance in the main floor is great, interior design is very pretty. I've been here twice and cannot seem to get a good server. We ordered a wine that they were out of and were disappointed with the recommended wine replacement. It was in no way similar to the original we had requested, aside from color. We were sat in the upstairs section which has a great view of the beautiful wine storage, but was far away from everyone in the restaurant, right next to a door to the kitchen so we could hear everything, and so hot I was half undressed by the end of the meal. My first experience was unremarkable, and I have not been back. I would love to see more attention to the loft seating. I could see that area as being desirable for its feature of being tucked away, but I mostly felt forgotten.

This is my go to for neighborhood, I don't feel like cooking tonight, what are we ordering, honey. I've probably eaten here 50 times in two years and I the only complaint is that once I had a few pieces of crunchy rice and once they forgot my soup in a to go order (which they made a note in their system and I got for free the next time). My parents will NEVER try anything new- I took them to Gernika and they ordered hamburgers...and they both liked this place. I get the kabob sampler with a rotation of lentil soup, hummus, or baba ganouj as sides. The chicken shawarma is also excellent. And I absolutely abhor cucumbers but their tzatziki is so good, I put it on everything. Lovely local business worth a try. You will be back.

Fantastic food, wonderful beer selection. I tried the Swill (I think it was called) and never want to drink anything else in the summer months. I've had the BLT with egg and avocado, the steak salad twice, and pizza; all of which were absolutely perfectly cooked and delicious. The service is quick and efficient, the staff is young and friendly, and it is on my list of places to take friends when they visit from out of town. So glad this is in our community and helping to expand the downtown. 100% recommend after four visits with absolutely no complaints.

I have always eaten here for brunch. I love the patio in warm months. If you like spicy, you must try the Spicy Chicken and Bacon Benedict... HOLY COW it's so good. Service can be slower on the patio, probably because you are outside of the regular restaurant. I also like the Irish coffee in the morning after a night out. Again, I always sit outside, but usually am waiting for a coffee refill.

The sushi tasted fine, but I assumed from the design of the place that this was more of a quick sushi take away type restaurant. I thought that meant lower prices and faster service. The prices are comparable to other sit down sushi places and our rolls kept falling apart. Service wasn't particularly quick, but they were making all food to order, so it didn't sway me. I would eat here again, but Sushi Joy is my staple.

I prefer this store over the one on Milwaukee- it's larger, cleaner, brighter, and seems to be more well stocked. I am ALWAYS asked multiple times if I am finding everything I need, so it's nice to know there's someone around to ask. But if you're a regular at Target, you aren't usually confused on where to find things- seems all of the stores are sectioned the same way.

I love their salads and white pizza. Tonight I had their cheese steak for the first time and it was delicious! Currently under construction, but in March they are teaming with Kilted Dragon and will be offering more beers and take-a-way growlers! Always very friendly staff. The wait can be longer than you might think for this type of place, but I've never been disappointed with taste.

This place is closed. I love a dirty venue and this one was nostalgically punk. Went to see Nekromantix but band broke down in another state. The bar waited until all opening bands had played before announcing headliner wasn't coming. Then they only refunded half the ticket price. Kind of misleading and cheap.

This is our anniversary and valentines day go to. Their butter chicken is incredibly delicious and the chicken vindaloo is nice and spicy. Not a fan of the desserts I've had, but would love to try the lunch buffet some time. Staff is so nice and very helpful. I pray this place never goes out of business.

The service and ambience are great, the food was fine. We ordered the nachos and the chicken grinder. Nachos were good (although I will NEVER understand why Boise puts olives on nachos). The grinder had a spicy sauce I didn't like but the husband did. The chicken on both was good. Very attentive servers, we went on an afternoon and they were extremely welcoming to our small kid. We really liked the decor of the place and the bar is huge. Husband had the Locomotive Dry Stout and was happy. They have some limited outdoor seating and offer four for $4 beer flights. Glad to have this place on the west side of town, definitely a good addition to the fairgrounds area.

The owner was fantastic. He bussed tables, served, and took a LOT of time to not only make suggestions from the menu but to describe different dishes. The food was perfect. We ordered the chicken chau chau, the matter paneer, the chicken korma, and three types of bread (garlic naan, onion naan, and one with nuts that I can't remember the name of). Absolutely 100% recommend this place for taste. This is the type of restaurant only locals know about and there is an intimate feeling. By the time we left, all tables were full but the service never missed a beat. Five stars for food and service.

Great coffee (the Big Titty Blend is my go to: it's named for breast cancer awareness :)). Their scones are insanely large and one even has full slices of bacon baked in. Their sandwiches are good and the biscuits and gravy weigh about 5 lbs in a to go box! Really great decor, retro signs and strung lights, plus located in the heart of the Linen District. I love to bring out of town guests here for the mood and good food.

I love the patio and the fire pits are great at night during the colder months. The food is delicious and really allows the ingredients to shine. Our server was Tifany and she was great- attentive without hovering.  I had the beet pierogi and my husband had the beef with kimchi, both on the brunch menu. The presentation is beautiful- just like the building, very modern- and the food tastes even better than it looks. The portions seem small at first but are filling when you've finished. The menu is reasonably priced for the quality of food; we spent about $25 for two, at brunch, with coffee. And the coffee is from Flying M, so of course, it's also wonderful. I love the Modern and appreciate its presence in Boise!

This place is Ok. The jalapeño pepperoni pizza was good, I also had the BBQ chicken which was fine. A little greasy, definitely New York style, thin crust, with a large bread rim; I'm a Chicagoan- so not my preference- but it tasted just fine. A bit pricey for pizza considering you can make 10-12 sales from baking one pie but, the slices are large.

Wow! You will not believe the food coming out of this place! We had the artichoke dip to start and it was piping hot, creamy, cheesy, and the bread was perfectly toasted but chewy in the middle (yummm). My husband had the steak salad and I had the pork loin. Holy smokes! Two super thick cuts of pork that were tender, juicy, and easy to cut. The wild rice was delicious and the asparagus was fired perfectly on the grill. Plus, the prices were amazing. We weren't drinking, but the beers were in huge handled glasses. I saw two tables order the bread pudding (I think that's what is was) and the server delivered it and then poured an entire cup of caramel over the top! I'm absolutely coming back to try it- we were too full to even entertain dessert. Our server, Cameron, was attentive, quick, and friendly. I can't believe the quality of food for the deal of the price. Definitely recommend.

Chris and Aimee were so helpful when I needed a birthday cake in a pinch! I had planned on baking my four year old's cake when I was suddenly hit with the scale of the party we were undertaking. I called Amaru on Friday morning and was able to pick it up the next day before the party. Their cake was delicious (as always) and looked amazing for my Super Hero theme. I recommend this place to people constantly- I have been hard pressed to find cakes that taste this good! Always professional, helpful, and the storefront is just as cute as can be with hot pink walls and vintage stoves. Their cakes really are delicious, plus they offer dietary restricted options (you would never know because taste isn't sacrificed!). A+ will continue to use them. They make wedding cakes and cupcakes as well!

Z91nGczF9M-Odi3Bv6XWvg.review_text: Quarter View is simply fantastic! I regularly frequent this establishment and have always enjoyed my experience. The menu is vast and expansive and the portions are more than generous. In addition to a wide selection, service is always top notch and the owners are incredibly friendly. Although I'd argue Parkway has the best PoBoys around, Quarter View is a close second, especially when you consider price and total wait time. I would recommend this restaurant to any local or visitor. Try the fried pickles and the French fry PoBoy- you won't be disappointed.

Absolute best Middle Eastern/Mediterranean food in the city. The prices are right and the restaurant serves sensible portions. The Shawarma (Beef,Lamb,Chicken) is marinated and presented perfectly. I have never had a bad experience at Lebanon's. Like many places in the city, they allow you to bring your on alcohol. However, unlike most places I've seen, there is no corking fee.

Hidden gem right off of Causeway Blvd.
There are a handful of other Mediterranean restaurants in the immediate area, but ZoZos is by far the best. Every menu offering is fantastic. Even their American fare is great! Really great shwarma and pita! The owners were very nice and more than accommodating. I will definitely be making this a regular stop.

Recently paid a visit due to an available Groupon and I have to say that this place was incredibly underwhelming. First, it is located along a service road next to I10 making is difficult to access. The area surrounding it is full of warehouses (not the best place for a restaurant). Inside, the restaurant smelled like cigarette smoke. Normally, I wouldn't have thought it a big deal but the smoke smell was repressive. There was only one other group inside during our lunch. We ordered two standard Italian fare dishes (Chicken Parm and Lasagna). In all honesty, the food was absolutely terrible. The pasta that accompanied the Chicken Parm was quite literally the cheapest white spaghetti you can buy and the sauce tasted like it came from a Ragu jar. I can't imagine anyone thinking this is what Italian food tastes like. I will not be coming back here.

Great local Asian/Chinese food! The service was good, but the menu offerings were even better. I had the General Tso's chicken and the plate was more than adequate. Generous portions, great hours (open early and late), and very conveniently located,

Warning: This is NOT a restaurant. Rather, it's a bar with bar-food. Most of the menu offerings were fried. The food that was ordered completely lacked flavor. Moreover, the portions were not very large. If you're looking to drink, I'd imagine this would be a good spot. However, I'd skip it if you're just looking for something to eat.

Went on opening day and I must say that I am BEYOND thrilled about it's new presence in the area. I've eaten at Cheesecake Factory many times before, but this is the first Cheesecake Factory in the tri-state area (Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana). It's in a great location and the dining room is bigger than many other CFs I've been to. As always, the menu selection was amazing and the food that was ordered was flavorful and nicely presented (Dynamite Shrimp, Buffalo Blasts, Greek Salad, Chile Rillenos). Id also add that the service was exactly what I expected: phenomenal. Cheesecake Factory attracts a certain clientele that is sure to really make the area flourish. I really hope this resturant does well and I hope it continues it's success!

Great offering in Fat City. Reasonably priced when considering the variety of choices given when ordering. Their cheese-stuffed burger is an absolute guy buster, but is oh so worth it. Other recommendations: sweet potato fries and their buffalo burger meat

Delicious "build your own" burger offering. Really fresh ingredients and good quality meat. I am a frequent visitor (it's hard to stay away). They definitely offer a better product than their competitors.
Fantastic! Tucked in a neighborhood and difficult to locate, but totally worth it. The cheesy chicken potato is complete hit.

I strictly came for the donuts. Overall, selection and diversity in the product was severely lacking. Nevertheless, the price was right and the donuts we did select had a great taste. Best part about this place is that they never close.

Sensational! One of the best new-aged restaurants in the city. The food is both artisanal and casual all at the same time. The meats are perfectly cured and seasoned. A must for any serious foodie living in the area or visitor passing through.
Nothing really to say expect that this place is beyond dumpy. Service is absolutely atrocious.

As aesthetics go, the space is nice and warm. However, I was incredibly disappointed by our overall dining experience. Most of the main entree dishes are 30 (+) dollars, so virtue of that alone, service should be excellent (e.g. Most restaurants in the city in this price range are complemented by great service). With this restaurant service was everything but great. Our main waitress was incredibly standoffish and seemed inconvenienced by questions and a secondary waitress was just completely rude and nasty (she snatched a fork out of my hand and dropped my drink on the table with massive attitude). I noticed that the servers were much nicer to the older table next to us, so it was hard not to think this was a case of age discrimination. This was definitely not a case of bad customer - bad service, just really bad service. The food was decent, but service alone was so abysmal that I wouldn't even bother. It's New Orleans after all and there are many, MANY more places to go without having to deal with rude and nasty servers. I would suggest to management that they review their current wait staff and future hiring practices.

Excellent overall! A hidden gem with a great selection of grocery/deli products. Their dine-in menu is large and seems to rotate regularly. As someone who longs for more authentic delis in the area, I must say I was very happy with my experience. This is definitely my new go-to.

Ordered: Rueben and a side of coleslaw

I will start this by saying that I love Moe's - the ingredients are more than good for the price. This location, however, is complete and utter garbage. Customer service is non-existent and the employees look like they hate life. If your idea of a good food experience is getting food thrown together by terrible workers, you will love this place. It doesn't take much to not be rude, but that's WAY to much for these people. I'll take my business to Felipe's.

This place is not good. I honestly can't believe people think this is even comparable to Dominica  and I'm shocked that Shaya (was/is) the operator of this place (he is normally a brilliant chef). It is overpriced, the service was horrendous, and frankly, the food was not good. The meatballs had the texture of meat that's been frozen and turned to a frost-bitten stage and the pizza - while fine - was overpriced and insubstantial. New Orleans has FAR TOO MANY restaurants to even be bothered with this place.

Very underwhelming. For being from the same creative team as Turkey and the Wolf (which is obvious based on the decor), the menu is very half baked. Half baked, however, is not how I'd describe the food. The bacon was black and flavorless. The McMuffin imitation sandwich was good but in no way worth it's relative price. I imagine they are still working the details out and it will improve over time. At the moment, though, I'd skip it and come back in a few months.
Complete trash. It's been more than a year since I last came here and boy, this place has changed radically. I will NEVER come here again. It's very sad to see a former great go to hell.

Za3ZzbjPUBFovzm-OQ1acg.review_text: I probably shouldn't have gone to this popular burger joint to eat a steak but I was curious. Ordered it medium and it came medium surprisingly. A bit bland, but again this place is really known for it's drinks and burgers. However the baked potatoes were great, not to hard and not to over done. Seating is rather limited in here. We arrived around 10pm on a Monday and it was kind of a squeeze. Nonetheless the were accommodating. Not quite sure when they started serving bread but I love my carbs so I was fine with that.

Variety! And amazing food. I usually get the stuffed catfish with their roasted garlic potatoes and Mac and cheese because it's absolutely wonderful. The cream sauce with shrimp that's served ontop the stuffed catfish compliments everything so well. It's ALWAYS packed during weekday lunch so be prepared for line but the staff is friendly and you sort of feel like family when you go in.

I'm a chorizo fiend. When I saw they had chorizo Mac and cheese I damn near lost it. I had that and the shrimp tacos. Not to fond of corn tortillas but the the sauce that the shrimp were cooked in was amazing. Happy Hour is the time to go. It's like this place doesn't belong in NOLA...it belongs in LA or ATL from it's feel. I'll definitely be back!

I don't know what the negative reviews are for. I've been here twice, once for lunch and once for dinner at the bar area. 

Lunch was a pleasant experience. There was no wait and my server greeted me immediately. The Sangrias here are really good along with the Shrimp Club sandwich which is HUGE. 

For dinner me and two friends say at the bar because it was slightly crowded. We ordered appetizers (a salmon dish, Mac and cheese balls, calamari, and a southwest egg roll style dish). Again we had THREE rounds of their Sangrias. 

Next time I'll be sure to actually try some cheesecake lol.

Came for brunch......I do appreciate the bottomless mimosas but this place might be understaffed for brunch. We sat at the bar with Justin. The food was WONDERFUL. Had a filet Benedict with shrimp added and cheese grits. My friend had the French toast on ciabatta bread and it was also wonderful. Service from JUSTIN was wonderful. 


Here comes my slight complaints. 

The servers were struggling to keep up the refilling of mimosa to the rest of the small restaurant. And it happened to be 52 degrees today and one of the staff has decided to prop a door open to the patio area. I didn't choose to sit outside I chose to sit INSIDE. The parking situation is good on the weekends with street and lot parking 

I'll probably come back.....not quite sure at the moment.

I'm giving this place 4 stars because I attended a birthday dinner and we basically had the restaurant to ourselves. The restaurant is at a BEAUTIFUL location with an amazing view of the water and boats, parking is lacking but it wasn't an issue that night because like I said, we were basically the only patrons there. Service throughout our three course meal was exemplary from this nice married couple. However when we first arrived I went to the bar to get a drink. They had a speciality hot coco that I decided would be good to start off with. The bartender had no one else in the restaurant but it seems she just thought I was standing there for my health. After a couple of minutes of side eyeing me to see if I actually wanted a drink she asked me what would I like. I asked her opinion on their speciality drink for the holidays; the hot coco. She said in a flat dry tone, "I wouldn't know i haven't tried it". I was slightly taken aback at her tone and the fact that she was serving items she honestly knew nothing about. I paid for my drink and politely over tipped her hoping that her crappy attitude would subside. The turtle soup was pleasing..... I had the pecan crusted catfish which was AMAZING. THAT is the dish that will probably keep me coming back. Everything on that entree from the asparagus to the sweet mashed potatoes to the catfish itself was absolutely delicious. I'm not a fan of bread pudding but others at the table throughly enjoyed it. I wish I would've gotten the two servers names who took care of us, they were so accommodating. I do plan to return soon, maybe when it warms back up and I can take full advantage of the outside patio.

Never again. I went to this place around three in the afternoon thinking I was avoiding the lunch rush. I was extremely wrong. The place was packed and it is rather small. We decided to sit at the bar to avoid waiting in the long line waiting to be sat. We waited almost 15 minutes for the bartender to acknowledge us because he was dealing with takeout orders. Quick suggestion to whoever runs this place get a second person to man the bar while the other one handles to-go orders. I decided to go for the stuffed shrimp plate with sweat potato tots and Mac and cheese and my friend went with the charbroiled oysters. My food was a disappoint but hers was delicious. It's kind of hard to mess up oysters though. Presentation is such a strong thing for me. My phone came out on a plate looking like it was made for a toddler at lunch time. The sweet potato tots were good but nothing to be overly excited for, the Mac and cheese gave me a "box made" feel and the stuffed shrimp had entirely too much stuffing on that small shrimp. At one point I was down to the last shrimp out of hunger and I just pushed my plate away. I won't be back here ever.

Racist establishment with subpar, mediocre food. Their catfish has a terrible after taste, and I found a fruit fly in my drink. After telling a waiter about it it took him almost 15 minutes to get me another drink. There are better restaurants around the French Quarter. Funny thing is the day we went the had an incident with a server putting the word "n*gger* on a guest check. It was the same boy who completely ignored our table. I thought he was just rude I didn't think it was because he was racist but now I know better. Not EVER going back.

Only reason I can't give this place 5 stars is because of the lack of parking, and the fact that I stick with the same things everytime I go. 

Watermelon mint margarita, queso dip to start off with and a Velvet Steak Taco, and a Shrimp Taco. 

I literally overindulge in their watermelon margaritas because those two things together are just heaven. 

The Velvet Steak taco has this tender steak almost like a pot roast consistency. It literally melts in your mouth. 

Some restaurants have that fake tasting queso, nope....this tastes like REAL cheese and its THICK. 

I wish they opened before 4:30pm on some days, and I wish the parking was better but other than that this is one of my new favorite places. 

The waitstaff is attentive, and the bartenders are quick. What else could you ask for?

Way better location than the French Quarter one. Parking galore (which you don't have to pay for) and outdoor seating. 

I ALWAYS sit at the bar when I go and they ALWAYS have an awesome, friendly bartender behind the bar. 

The queso with the chorizo mixed in with chips is just my go to thing along with a frozen margarita. Service is always speedy, drinks are always strong, and you meet some pretty cool people just sitting around the bar talking. 

Thanks for not being a snob in the small Mexican restaurant population that we have in NOLA Felipe's! You're appreciated!

I want to be biased and give them more stores because I'm cool with people who work here but they need to straighten out some kinks. 

I'm usually sat in a more private area with actual comfortable couches but some of the sitting areas are like sitting outside on concrete. The chairs are hard and flimsy. 

Service takes awhile, so find a menu and tell your server EVERYTHING you need at once because there's a good chance you won't see her again for some time. 

If you're going to order a hookah I recommend doing it with a grapefruit on it. It gives it a better flavor. 

Only come here on Fri-Sun if you have TIME. It gets packed (which is good because I remember when they had tumble weeds in here). 

Enjoy but follow my tips!

Much better atmosphere than the one near city park. It's smaller but I enjoy the intimate setting and the fact that it's on Magazine near other bars. I didn't have any of the food this go around but some of my friends did and they seemed to enjoy it. 

The offer "bar food" so nothing extremely extensive. I'm an apple cider girl who hates beer but they had a nice selection. Two on tap and a selection of bottles. I went with a strawberry cider that was DELICIOUS. I've actually been searching for it since that night. 

It's a good place to just hang out with friends.

Went here before a movie, and the service was kind of slow. There weren't that many people in the establishment for it to be like that. 

I ordered a steak sandwich of sorts. The steak was rather tough, and the fact that the wait was kind of long we barely made it to our movie. I wouldn't have stopped in here if I wanted to wait like an actual restaurant.

My friends all seem to flock here for "Taco Tuesday" so my interest was peaked. I happened to go on a Friday and sat at the bar with a friend. I ordered a drink and got a menu looking over the different choices of Tacos. 

Queso dip....I'm a fiend for some good cheese dip but this stuff didn't exactly do it for me.

Saw many a friend check in here so I ventured to this spot one afternoon hoping for the best. I checked in and got some free mint tea which was a plus. I decided to order the Doner Kebab and for the most part it was good. The spicy hot sauce they gave me was a plus but the meat was a tad bit dried out. I'd honestly eat their bread just by itself because it's so delicious. I'll be back again to give it a second try because that's just how I roll in life.

Firstly let me say this, I've been to Fogo's in other cities and had great experiences. I was a tad bit taken aback that I wasn't having yet another great one at the Nola location. 

After shopping a friend and I decided to stop in for dinner. The restaurant seemed to be a bit busy for a Tuesday. We were told it would be a 20-30 minute wait to be seated. I was fine with that because I wanted RED MEAT and a lot of it. Twenty minutes passed, then thirty, then forty and soon an hour. I asked the hostess what the issue was and she said only a few more minutes. Here's the thing...if your restaurant is so packed with reservations you should tell guests that or that you can't take any walk in's at that moment. 

Ten minutes we were seated at literally the noisiest table. We were near the exit where the meat was coming out so I tried to look at the bright side. I thought I'd be able to get first dibs on some things. Wrong... We saw the same 4 meats come to out table until we actually ASKED for a better variety. The chicken was dry, the beef almost tasteless. The lamb chops were the only enjoyable meat, and I couldn't get a second one to save my life. At that point I decided that my meal was going to consist of smoked salmon and fresh greens. I'd given up hope. Our server (who I won't name for their sake) was completely inhospitable. I understand....I get it....the restaurants packed but you could at least ask me if I'm enjoying my wine or if I needed a refill on my water. The plates were only taken once from the table. The plus side, one of the managers saw that we had a toddler with us and immediately got mashed potatoes to the table for her after that long wait in the lobby. 

I won't be back, at least not to this location. Houston's service, and meat selection are what I'm used to, it's unfortunate I didn't find it here in New Orleans.

I'm giving this 4 stars only because New Orleans has like all of four BBQ spots in this whole seafood driven city. I ordered the three meat combo with Mac and cheese and potato salad as my sides. 

The ribs were delicious, and the sausage was honestly the best part of my meat combo. It's spicy, juicy, and flavorful. The brisket was kind of a miss for me. I think I might've gotten the end of it because it was honestly more fat than anything. All the meat was seasoned well though and I really enjoyed the barbecue sauce. 

The Mac and cheese wasn't really exciting but I like the fact that they used that creole mustard in their potato salad and used red potatoes. 

I wanted to get a drink while I waited for my food but the bartender was busy with a phone order I guess. I was slightly disappointed in that but life goes on. I'll probably go back a few more times. Being from Texas living in NOLA is hard on my barbecue loving soul.

ZbSO0cWBjlqJDsfw3iDSug.review_text: Excellent Chinese. It is off the beaten path, so everyone goes there because they like it.  I usually don't order off the menu but ask the owner to fix me something so I skip all the sauce and get meal like you would get home cooked in China. That way it's healthy too, but you are never sure what you will get.

I had lunch a Super Cuca's today. There was a customer who decided to give is a loud and protracted political rant and would not stop.  After 10 minutes of a ruined lunch I asked the manager help us enjoy our lunch. Failure to intervene ruined my experience. I understand this is not "fine dining" place but a modicum of peace is expected.
Authentic, very Italian atmosphere. Good and reasonably priced food. Very small and quaint.

This intimate place is unpretentious and friendly with excellent food. The prices are the lowest for sushi I know of, yet the sushi is smoking the best in town. The place captures the ambiance of a real Japanese sushi bar. 

Try the Green Iced Tea, it has a different twist you may or may not like, but it grew on me.

Food was decidedly ok. There are better and there are far worse Thai choices. Waitress who might have been the owner , was a tad surely but the guy who brought the water was professional. Place was clean but there were a few crumbs on the table.

We came in from out of IV for this. 

Good value for the money. Good college town food. Service is good. The owner and the staff is very friendly. Owner prepared us hot tea even though it is not on the menu. Food is definitely Korean, except the macaroni salad.  Food is better than average is you ignore the styrofoam.

My friend, who grew up in Korea, says it feels like she is in Korea.

This is a gem buried in IV. While not elegant, the food is superior and service excellent. I had pasta, which was authentic and fresh tasting. The salad contained a variety of greens and in the authentic tradition was plain with a tasty oil and vinegar. The pasta had sparing tasty sauce with fresh flavored. I am sensitive to salt, and the pasta had flavor without too much salt. I rate the pasta as better than Silvergreen's across the street, which is very good, if you crave authenticity. The bread was more than I needed, and nicely but heavily spiced with basil, etc. 

The owner must be the server because he really seems to care that you are happy. He came by twice to check on us which rates as attentive without hovering. 

If you want pasta cooked ahead with plenty of salty sauce, there is a great pizza place right around the corner.
Ordered a milkshake so I could rest my injured foot. Clerk refused to bring it to my table although I obviously could barely stand.

Good compliment to El Sitio. Good burgers, and sandwiches. Salads look good. Did not try the pizza but saw a lot go out. Unlimited refills on soda. 

Atmosphere is small and clean. 

Are there on the 3rd day and the 6th day they were open. Service is pretty good.

Generally creative and healthy sandwiches and very creative salads. I recommend it. 

Hard (impossible) to park at lunch time within about 1/2 mile. Tad noisy. 

Staff is friendly even if over-worked.

Extraordinarily creative sandwiches and salads. Much more then peanut butter and jelly but they do have that. 

Space is small but I never have gone without a seat. 

Ample vegetarian selections but plenty of meat also. 

Thumbs up.

Just ate at their little restaurant. As fast as I know that part of the business is new. 

The food was fresh and flavorful. I think they have a minimum of out of the jar sauces. Prices are not high. $10-17 for dinner.

I recommend it.

Just ordered lunch. I quite like Sam's to Go. But I ordered a combo, with chips a drink. Ignacio apparently heard wrong and when I grabbed chip, instead of telling me he he had misunderstood, he decided to insist I had told him the incorrect thing. There are some serious customer service issues here.

You know it's pizza. Everyone has a different idea of what's best. 

But it is fun. They have lots of topping and you can have whatever you want at no extra charge. If the crust is not for you, you can do the same unlimited options on greens for a salad. 

And the pizza is a good size. Plenty to eat but you do not "have to" take any home.

It is back open with a new building. 

The building has a great new layout with much improved access for both cars and people. 

Previously friendly staff is gone. Manager used to work to improve staff customer performance. Now that manager is gone and I am often great with a I will be with you in a few minutes sort of I am busy greeting. Food is also put up on the counter and just left until you wonder what happened to my food. If you want a clean table, you can get a napkin and clean it yourself. Let's hope that improves because they are not making use of the great new venue.

Ok, it is fast food ... but  it is about the best fast food around.

I found the food fresh and tasty, and it was not overly salty.

The staff was friendly, know how to interact with a customer, and make eye contact. If the corporation is teaching these skills, then kudos.They supplied plenty of refills on soda and sauce when asked.

The place was clean (great restrooms) and they took care of used tables promptly.

The veggies were quite good.

We ordered onion rings appetizer. The coating was crispy if a bit greasy, Inion favor was fresh

The roast pork was on the dry side, which they covered with sauce, which was way to salty. (Why do gourmet chefs always add so much salt)

We also ordered meatloaf which was delicious but had a similar too salty sauce.

The real rub was the water.  They told us that it was against restaurant policy to check if we wanted more water. We had to go get the waitress and ask for more water if we wanted more. That was explained as doing their part to save water. Somehow Denny's down the street finds a way to bring a customer a glass of water. Then they told us it was against the law to bring us a larger glass of water or more than one glass.  (really!!!). I think it is just bad service.

Food is picking up from there old natural but bland style. If you try s special, they are creative and tasty, except pasta because they think "al dente"something a body shop beats out of your car. 

Besides pasta, things are very tasty. Desserts are terrific

Not fresh. The marinated meat is not to bad, but you got to hide the taste. The onions or habenaro salsa help. 

Drinks are bottles or can. Definitely a plus.
Good variety. Good fresh food. They do well with fish but the other stuff is good too. My favorite is the fish and chips. I also get a soft ice cream cone

This is a great place. Not a 5-star restaurant but it has the basic burger or taco. If you want a quick bite, it is one of my go to places. 

French fries are good, staff is attentive, owner is polite in his introverted sort or way, the place is clean the condiments (salsa, peppers) are good.

No Problem.

Food is McDonald's.  What need be said?  You expect McDonald's food. We went for the french fries.

But the place needs some staff training.  I guess they were busy, but they acted like they could not be bothered. Upon taking my order, I said, "Thank you", and the reply was "No problem".  Really, glad to hear that taking my order was "No Problem".

Like I said the food is McDonald's food, but having the staff be courteous should not be a extra cost sort of thing.

No problem.

Hidden away in the University Plaza Shopping Center. Simple coffee shop/bakery with no frills.

They have great breakfast burritos and sandwiches for lunch. Always quiet there.  I pop in for lunch every now and again.

They have great bread and pasties with a Mexican bent, but I try to stay away from the sweets.

When you are in the neighborhood, this is a great place to get some Mexican food. They have all the basics and some creative specials. Even the few vegetarian options are pretty good. 

The decor (or undecor) is plain. 

SALSA is good. Wish they gave you more chips.

The new location is great. Right across the parking lot from the other one. Great place to chat with friends for a while over a beer. I specialize in the 3 ounce size. They have a nice variety 

Last time I was there on pizza night. Albeit a tad pricey is is great pizza that fits with the beer.

This a great place for a craft beer and good food. The menu has enough choices ranging from healthy to not. 

Service is good. If you get a heater, outside seating is nice.

It is fast food so ...

I found the food fresh, good variety, healthy, low fat, very salty. 

The restaurant, tables, and restrooms are plentiful and clean. 

I going down the cafeteria line the staff tends to yell at you about what you want from 10 feet ahead of you. This really hurts the experience because:
1) you don't know what you want because it is yet to far away. 
2) you can't hear because they are screaming at you
3) it raises the tension because the server in front of you is screaming at the person 10 feet behind you. 

It contributes to a hurry and get it done attitude rather that a friendly "how can I help you" atmosphere. I am sure these highly compensated employees time is valuable, but not screaming is nice too.

This I bright and spacious. The staff is friendly and seems to have been trained in courtesy. I like that the attempt to wait for you to pick up your food, nice touch. The food is about the best you are going to do with fast food. Not much fat or sodium. Restrooms are always clean. Unfortunately there is a dog in here. I am sure it is probably some sort of emotional support beast, but that does make it any cleaner.

Closed " until further notice"
