Great service. Tasty fresh food albeit a tad spicy. I was there early but as business picked up, it is a good casual date spot (if you are not going to drop rice on your shirt with chopsticks).

Tea was tasty. 

I got a sizzling plate which was good, I want to try a hot pot next time.

Great burger and salads. It takes the burger joint to a new level. 

The is not tremendous variety but all the combinations are well thought out and capture your pallet. 

My friends always turn up there nose at eating at a burger joint but once I drag them there they always want to go back.

I like Dejavu for then you want a big hot sandwich with French fries. There is often a college student or 6 here doing there thing. Often noises. But the food is good and plentiful. 

The staff is always nice.
They would do better if there were polite. I have been there twice and not gotten as far a ordering food because there are so many choices with good service.

They have a nice deli, but the prices are high and the quality not commiserate with those prices. 

The dry goods are also a tad high, although they have a quality selection.

I am glad we have this place. The food is adequate for a high-price venue. I found the service excellent. I 3 times, I got a bright witty server, who paid attention to our needs without hovering. The wine selection is good and you can get a modest priced glass of wine.

I like this place. On the downside, the car service line is often backed up into the street. But once you can get in, the place is clean and fresh. 

I find the food a refreshing choice from the usual burger place. 3 star food. 

But the service is outstanding. 3 times during my visit I asked for something and said "Thank You" when I got my request. The server replied, "My pleasure".  Repeat "My pleasure".  Now that is service!

Chicken is fresh and tender. Fries are different, but still fries. Rest rooms are very clean. Staff cleans tables fast and well.

I find this a pleasant and quiet place to get a healthy light meal. Always people inside chatting but it is not loud. Efficient environment, not fancy. 

The food satisfies me. I do not feel over stuffed. As with all soup, a tad salty for my tastes. 

It is on my "go to" list

The food is what you expect from Carl's Jr.  Tasty but way too salty. 

I think the drink guy might be speaking English but I am not sure. I think he is refusing to give me another drink refill. Not even if I pay for it. I thought I was minding my business after eating lunch. I guess he is too busy with his other duties of standing around the drink machine doing nothing. 

Fortunately, McDonald's is a couple of blocks north and Habit (which is actually pretty good) is a couple of blocks south, so it is not hard to find a place where people want to work.

You know, it is McDonald's. The food is the same everywhere 

But I have to say, the are doing a great job with COVID-19. The are friendly and clear about their procedure. They have someone manning the drink station with your drink ready. They have someone cleaning the table when you finish. Most the places I have been just leave the tables dirty, so what is the point of everything else. 

The still have the practically useless paper straws, but rules like that why we eat in Goleta. 

Under the difficult circumstances, Kudos.

Not responding well to opening up. You get the food but they have strict limits on condiments and no drink refills. Hard to understand everybody with masks but when the employees act dumb it makes it worse. No evidence the clean tables between customers which would help more than not giving me a refill. Well just have to drive down to Mesa 

Saves the employees a lot of time but now I have to drive down to Mesa Burger or over to Home Plate across the freeway. Sad because this is right in the neighborhood.
Everyone has to eat outside during Covid. This place had customers waiting taking up tables at adjacent eateries. How rude.  It is a sign of bad management. I will check back and see if the fix that.

They have been great during COVID and it is a old-time friendly barber shop

And I get a good haircut.

No problem

I hate it when I tell the clerk "thank you" and they reply "no problem"



Food is from Jack in the Box

At least when I gave them $20.07 for my $4.07 total, the guy gave me $16.07 change then wanted to argue that it was not $16.00 change I was owed. 

You got to laugh.

Very good customer service. Servers are the most polite of anywhere I know like they have actually been trained. 

Food is very good for fast food. Chicken is not overcooked. Always tender.

Zna994E0FpeKVhMEENtytg.review_text: I LOVE this place. Order food from an amazing menu, from burgers to steak and everything in-between. Enjoy a full bar, waiters and soda for the kids. This is a family experience, mom and dad can kick back and enjoy an alcohol drink, order great food and watch that special movie u have been waiting for. Only complaint is the lounge chairs are nowhere as good compared to the seating at RegaL CINEMAS. IF THEY JUST CHANGED THE SEATS, I WOULD HAVE GIVEN FIVE STARS.
Eat here a few times throughout the year. ALWAYS consistently good, service is up and down, I've had great waiters and lousy ones. Overall though, Guppy's is liked by my friends and I.
Came across this by accident. Decided to bring the other half and we enjoyed the food, fresh crab, but the service wasn't what we are accustomed to.
Good food, decent service, always busy, nice middle-class patronage.
Lenny's is the best diner on the planet. It's more of a restaurant, GREAT FOOD and VERY REASONABLE prices!
Not bad.... expensive, I think, for what they give. It's worth a try but don't expect cheap prices.
They claim their hot dogs are 100% beef. I have never tasted beef that tastes like this! The dogs are very salty, are hard to the bite, not sure this is the right place for you to spend your money.

I happen to like this pizza and I am a PIZZA aficionado. Growing up in Manhatan, eating pizza has always been an event! Here in Florida, they just can't duplicate the taste, oil on top and at least a decent crust of New York Pizza. However having said this, Cristino's Coal Oven Pizza is pretty damn good if you can get a table. TRY their authentic spinach ravioli, you will be blown away by this restaurant's high quality and freshness, the preparation and presentation is immaculate.

Good food, always a wait at the door, but the food is worth it. You want a place where you can let your hair down and just enjoy a quality breakfast & Brunch? Want to unwind in a tropical setting? The vide and food is great here and the prices are AMAZINGLY LOW.
I've been a satisfied customer of Amici for ten years. The chicken/veal/eggplant parmigiana is very good. The deserts are to die for... and lastly the service is impeccable - ask for Linda.

Honestly, Acropol is one of the best Greek restaurants in the area. In fact, they are the best I have eaten here in Florida. Make sure you try the monster Gyro, finish with their danishes, cookies, cakes. I always buy all their white chocolate macadamia cookies (BEST ON PLANET EARTH) .... go have lunch or dinner... you won't regret it.
Best damn burrito this side of Mexico ! Very good! Didn't expect it to be this awesome!
I've been here a few times, nothing special, the food sometimes comes out cold and I wouldn't recommend this place for breakfast instead go to Kim's restaurant two minutes away.

The food is not bad, the waitresses are awesome, however the vibe isn't good. The new owners don't seem to know what they're doing and the cooks keep quitting. Instead go eat at Kim's restaurant two minutes away!
Always good food, the owner KIM is amazing and the waitress ROBIN rocks. Definitely my new go to place for breakfast and lunch!

Is it just me or do they put the same seasoning on everything? It just seems like everything is over seasoned and it's the same stuff they use for the blooming onion, steaks and burgers... it's just too much, I can't stand the taste of the food...instead try Longhorn!

ZybKys6Kg37xX2LMfvcntg.review_text: Delicious, fresh, and friendly volunteers. Yesterday was my second trip to Hollygrove farmers market. The produce is fresh and organic. The volunteers were nice and helpful. Their tomatoes and curly kale is delicious. Oh and the cucumbers were yummy, big, and crisply fresh. I also purchased zucchini and fairytale eggplant, anhich I haven't tasted yet

Eh.. their pizza is better than some big brand pizza deliveries but I still feel that it's over priced. Why? Well my $10 gourmet spinach salad wasn't so fresh few crisp spinach leaves here and there but the rest we soggy and limp. The pepperoni pizza I ordered was fine but wasn't buzz worthy to us. Sane goes for the sausage pizza. The tomato sauce didn't taste freshly made. And the delivery driver put the nail in the coffin by mentioning a tip which I already had waiting for him. But couldnt hand it to him quickly because I was trying to gather everything because he didn't want to take the pizza out for me and I had my one yr old running around. So instead of giving him a 20% tip I gave him a 10% tip. Be a gentlemen and help a lady sir. But most importantly the food wasn't what they hyped it up to be.

I've been here many times and I'm always given great service and good food. Ive had various rolls and dinner selections. I love their Saigon salad. I don't favor one roll over another so I can't suggest which is the best. Our waiters/ress have always been prompt.

Hmm I'm torn. I really want to give them three stars because of the spinach and artichoke dip with pita. We've ordered delivery from them about 5 times now. Here's a couple's review. He ate the shrimp platter (from appetizers menu) and also the bbq chicken sandwich. The shrimp platter is way overpriced for both quality and quantity. I understand it's part of the appetizer menu but geez hardly any shrimp and barely any fries like maybe 8oz of fries, maybe. Ive tried the bbq chicken sandwich, spinach dip, hummus and pita, chocolate seduction cake, vegetarian chili, and regular chili. The bbq chicken sandwich is a 12in and loaded with chopped grill chicken breasts. There was bacon in mine, I think the hostess misunderstood when I said to add extra bacon to his bacon cheese burger. And I ended up with bacon on mine as well. Lucky her because though I don't like pork it was yummy. So try the bbq chicken with or without bacon I feel it came with too little of fries. But enough to keep my taste buds comfortable. The spinach dip was yummy-very cheesy and rich. The pita was delicious too. The hummus taste good. The veggies that came with the hummus were fresh. The soda cans are over priced in my opinion. The vegetarian chili was ok no serious let downs it was my first time having vege chili so I can't compare. THE 'REGULAR CHILI' WAS TERRIBLE. It tastes like canned chili, Hormel brand to be exact. I couldnt stomach it. The cake was chocolate so I'm good there. But if you want a serious slice of chocolate cake for only a buck more,actually I think it's the same price, go to Hoshun. Huge slice of cake. We've never dined in. Only delivery, which the drivers delivered in the promised amount of time. And were kind.

I give it four stars for fast quality delivery and good food with low prices. I ordered from the dinner special. We had the kung pao shrimp and moo goo gai pan with shrimp fried rice as its side. Also we ordered veg egg rolls and cream cheese wontons. The food was great, hot and fresh. The lady who took my order actually called me back after my phone dropped the call. My only problem is that they do not offer any desserts. Not even any fortune cookies! Argh. I need desserts and cream cheese wonton won't do it though it's sweet. I'm talking cookies and cake, where are the cookies, cakes, slices of pie or ice cream?!

Cashier Theft! And I wouldn't make an accusation without cause. See this how you wish. Our total was $25.59. The drive through cashier falsely documen on our receipt that we gave her exact change by cash. FALSE! We gave her $40.60. She was supppose to give us back $15.01. She gave us one penny. When my fiance went in to get our correct change back they gave us hell. In fact implying that we were lying. So basically ended up with them having to count their registers. Which showed she was only over about $10. We weren't buying their bs. I told him to request that pockets get counted. He pulled out his wallet to prove all he had were twenties. And the cashier who was visibly nervous took money out of her drawer which was the correct change of what we were owed. I called corporate and left feedback as well as my contact info. They were not friendly, not efficient, and apparently untrustworthy. Be very careful if you purchase here. Only give exact change. I've cashiered before I've seen what untrustworthy cashiers do. I've busted some before for stealing from customers and businesses.

I like that there are many options here. I do not like the Ghetto Punch title. Seriously?! Either way, my wings were tough and unevenly cooked. Hush puppies were dry and hard. The fries were ok. The inside looks like a prison office desk area/courthouse cashier. They protect thems behind this glass (which is pto bullet proof) they seem to want the money from the townsfold but not the trouble. I guess I cant be angry at that. This is the south so I'm sure people are use to this treatment and I think many will end up liking the food.

I have a like-dislike for this place. Those the menu is limited I think it tastes pretty good. Not the absolute bestie in Nola. The chips and Pico are greasy with seafood seasoning topped. I know because I use the same seasoning at home. The chips are too greasy with unevenly topped seasoning. It's my first check in but I've been here many times. The 3 taco deal is good for the price. Greasy but I think it still tastes good. The fillings are always limited though. Always out of something. The bartender is sweet. The petite 30-40something year old lady. Really nice. But the waiter/"cook" isn't all that great professionally. The petite guy with bandana. He usually have an attitude. Few days I caught him being nice though. It's a hole in the wall joint. 95% of the time they play rock music, lots of biker, hikers, and musicians frequent the place. Could be better especially the waiter attitude. But eh when I'm not close to home and starving I come here.

Friendly and courteous hostess/server. She and the rest of the staff were clean, kind, and professional. We ordered to-go. And our food was fresh, warm, and came promptly. I absolutely love my Buffalo Tofu Salad. A bit spicy, very flavorful but not overbearing. I also ordered a gluten free chocolate chip and raisen cookie not pictured because I devoured it quickly. Sooo yummy.

It wasn't bad but it's not a place I would go to again if I have other options. My Spicy Shrimp Tacos (flour tortillas), were a bit too salty. They were very spicy, which I loved. But you can't taste the extra salt in the grilled shrimp. The margaritas were good. There weren't many drink options. But they have what I'd call for others, the essentials, I saw some tequila, Bacardi rum, and beer. It was my first time there. I'm a dark rum or mezcal lover. But you can't go wrong with a margarita. So I still like this restaurant. I do feel they could've been a bit more organized. It was a very slow day hardly anyone was there. My table and two others and they forgot our food twice. But once they got the hang of things everything else went smoothly.

It's okay. The food wasn't terrible. Bland but not horrible. The service could've definitely been better and my menu was dirty. But I don't think they knew to flip through the menu to check for splattered food. The margaritas were good. I had the mango and my sister had a mixed Margarita. They do not allow to go boxes for your paid food  after dining in on taco Tuesday....

I'm here trying the Lambsbread Taco which is Caribbean inspired. It's amazing. Great contrast between fresh taste of plaintains and lamb. My drink of choice tonight is the Erin's Key Lime Coconut Rum Punch. My meal tonight is a YES. The staff is professional, kind, and prompt.
I would review my food IF Id ever recieve it. It's been about 40mins simce seating. Lets see where this night goes.

You ever felt so excited to eat something that you forget to snap the photo before eating the sweet treat to review? We began eating these delicious donuts as soon as they arrived. I ordered 4 gluten free blueberry donut holes and 6 glazed donuts. These are by far some of the best donuts I've tried in NOLA.

Vyoone's has amazing food and great customer service. Everything was fresh, delicious, and at the perfect temperature. This is definitely one of my favorite restaurants. Vyoone, as well as her restaurant, is top notch!

Foods good but the cashier is very arrogant , condescending and rude ! Music is wayyy to loud , if I wanted to go to a bar I go to one ! The owners of this place need to wake up and stop their staff from treating their customers like dirt and running the place as it suits them
This keg can be good . Buts it's VERY hit and miss . One visit perfection . Next visit complete incompetent disaster . Wish they would get it together !

Best steak in Edmonton ........ Usually . 

Most consistent steak place in Edmonton IMO . Priced at the upper end of reasonable and the oyster bar is great ! Usually have the Cajun ribeye Chicago style , vons seems to be the only place in Edmonton that even knows what that is . 

Unfortunately on our last visit all our steaks were very salty . Not sure why

They are very capable of great real Sichuan style food . No idea why their name is Beijing lol . But don't bother unless you can read Chinese or speak mandarin as all the good dishes are not on the English menu . The staff don't seem to want to explain them either .
Went back twice recently and was impressed. Staff were attentive and food was great ! Still quite pricey but I have no problem paying when it's good like this !

Worst dim sum in Edmonton ! Surely staff who abscond you if your not an expert on all their dishes . Also they barrage you with food carts at the beginning and never return again . Very poor management
Wow . A restaurant owner that actually cares if people like his food ! Great fresh food in a clean enviroment with attentive staff . 5 stars from me !

Comfort food ! If cold bland and listless is your comfort food make sure to try this place . Overpriced poor service (not from a lack of staff as there are plenty ) they have the gimmick down pat but there's no hope for the food here . No management in sight and a staff that just aren't interested in serving good food
I'm surprised to read others think their prices are reasonable . For what you get they are expensive . Food is ok but pricey for the quality and portion size

Great supermarket ! Family owned and competitive . Supporting places like this will help encourage more instead of only the chain grocery stores . 

Food is good and priced great . Try the Vietnamese sandwiches !

Fantastic beef satay soup ! 

Consistenty good food . Great service at reasonable prices . Great lunch spot but can get busy from noon till one . Better to go after 1

Terrible mucho burrito location . Used to be a loyal mb fan . Driving from the west end to down town several days a week to eat mb . Spicy satay soup broth is very tasty and not oversalted like other places .

Decent food and service . Friendly staff and attentive owners . Happy to see Thai express in Edmonton . Unfortunately the taste is better in the Thai express I have tried in Vancouver . Not sure why ? Improper training , different ingredients ? Hope they can improve  as I like the concept !

Came here for brunch . Reminded me of a 5.99 Vegas brunch Buffett . Had all the usual items including dirty glasses fake crab and dodgy sushi. glassware was dirty and overall the cleanliness of the restaurant was not good . 
No hostess to greet and waitresses that couldn't be bothered either. 
 Absent manager and terribly undertrained or non caring ( I couldn't decide which ) staff.  Odd brunch setup in the cold breezeway Lobby making all the warm food not warm . Berries for the waffles/pancakes were obviously old and fermenting ! making me feel unwell after .

Good sandwiches . But unfortunately the place is not as clean as I would prefer . Used to be better and in the last year or so standards have definitely fallen.  Hope they can bring it back !

should be 3.5 stars . happy to see healthy options in edmonton . like the concept but the follow through is dissapointing . staff not careful in handling food . new businesses hiccups ? Hope they can improve

Good donairs . I like the romain lettuce and big tomatoes ! Pickled radish is a good idea but too salty for my taste ..  regular donairs are big as other places supers :) would be interesting to see some other veggies available.

_C82sNHU4fOaZw6gULZ3Vg.review_text: Little gem off the main road featuring fresh favors!! After reading the reviews, I ordered the chicken Cesar wrap and an Asian beef noodle soup. I was impressed! They give you not just saltines but oyster crackers and their known for homemade soup so of course I had to try it! The Asian beef noodle soup has peanut butter (for allergy purposes) but it's such a tiny amount it really rounds the whole soup out. My wrap was delicious and fresh but the ratio of chicken to croutons was off. My boyfriend got a turkey sandwich which was delicious as well. We got two drinks and I think the bill was around $30 for lunch. I'd definitely recommend this place!

What a pleasant surprise! I would have never found this place if it wasn't for our new friends :) so thank you for introducing us to a neighborhood breakfast dive in with great food! It is packed so expect to wait and safe to assume that I have not stumbled upon a secret. The people know where to get great breakfast food!! There were four of us and we probably waited 25 mins on a Sunday around noon to get a table. Definitely worth the wait. We literally had everything off the breakfast menu. Pancakes, French toast (must have), eggs,scrapple, bacon both turkey and pork, hashbrowns (the GOOD kind where it's slices not shredded), toast and breakfast sandwiches. I was starving by the time we ordered so of course I'm going to eat everything on my plate and I was not ashamed. Proud was more like it! I did enjoy everything but I was not a fan of the sausage (Seemed a bit over cooked because it was dry). A tip I learned from the friends who have been going there since he was literally born, the tickets are individual not by tables. When you first walk in, the chef is at the griddle and it's not huge so whenever he finds room to make more food is how it goes. Honestly, the chef must be rocking it hard to be getting all the food out so quickly. So be patient because you'll get great food and you cannot beat the prices for sure! Can't wait to eat there again oh and I totally have a soft spot for breakfast/brunch food!!!! 
P.s.- I have to apologize for not taking pictures since I was that hungry. Next time (maybe)

Pleasantly surprised and what a gem! I found this place on Yelp since my friend was coming into town and we both love Indian. Unfortunately, the lunch buffet is only available on weekends and not during the weekday BUT they have a great lunch special deal for 8.99 which includes dessert and naan! It was perfect since you get a selection of 5-6 dishes so it's your own personal buffet anyways! The chicken tikka and paneer was delicious as well as everything else that came with the lunch deal. I had leftovers for days! Seriously I had 3 different meals with the leftovers (we ordered the paneer as a separate dish since it wasn't on the lunch special) but still! WOW! Indian food is the ONLY food I'll eat leftovers from. I have yet to check out the buffet (which I will asap) but for lunch buffet in my eyes so far is karma in old city. You're welcome :)


So ironically since I wrote my first review I had a craving for Indian so we got takeout from this place! I (myself only) got paneer tikka masala and chicken tikka biryani and of course garlic naan. They ask which level of heat you'd like on your dish which is a definite thumbs up (got extra hot) which it was so that was very nice. The biryani was a tad dry but the chicken was moist. The paneer was not fresh but still edible. Just disappointed because I've experienced it's hard to get really fresh paneer because the texture is softer. All in all I really enjoyed everything! I'm just going to mix the sauce with the biryani and I had meals for the next couple days :)

THIS IS MY FAVORITE BAGEL PLACE EVER!!!!! They know me by name because I am addicted to their amazing bagels :) *drool* my favorite is the garlic so if you pick a popular flavor make sure you get it early! I get bagel sandwiches (Oh MY SOOoooo good) and dozens of dozens of bagels to go and they store well in the freezer and you just take it out and microwave it for 30 seconds then just toast it up and tastes fresh just like that day. The chicken salad and egg salad are delicious as well! The owners (local couple) are so sweet and they're definitely a neighborhood gem spot. Tell them Esther sent you when you go in!

We used to be obsessed with this place when it first opened. Awesome food and the price is definitely right especially in the sushi world. Honestly, we haven't frequented there lately and now I'm questioning myself why. Next time I get a craving though, this will be my go to. The staff is always friendly, courteous and professional. I definitely recommend this place!

I've been waiting to try this place for ages and finally got to go with my dear friend who came to visit. I was so ecstatic to show her around town and amaze her with this place but our experience was subpar to say the least. The ambiance is out of this world gorgeous and our waiter was very friendly and receptive to our questions. We started off with the crawfish gumbo and it was a great start to our meal! It wasn't as spicy as we thought but the flavor was really good. The bread loaf comes in a paper bag with their logo on it, which I thought was very cute and special. I ordered the crawfish etouffe while my friend got the jambalaya. Both were lacking seasoning and spice :( we were disappointed with the entrees. We ordered the carrot cake, which was good and we didn't leave hungry so that's also a plus. Try it out if you're in the mood for New Orleans cuisine but I know for sure there's much better out there.

I was very surprised with this place! I'm very happy about what they're doing there- dishing out great food and in a timely fashion even when it's crazy packed! Good job guys :) keep it up and we will see you soon

Definitely a noticeable difference between a regular Chinese joint versus the good ones. If you eat in, you're there for the food, not the decor. So let's talk about the food. The honey ribs are fall off the bone tender and the sauce is delicious. You're going to need to order 2 orders because it's not a lot of meat and it's just that good. The crab wontons are a hit and if you eat in, they provide the fried noodles with a lightly pickled cabbage side/salad, which is palate cleansing. There's an option to make your own entree (pick your meat and veggies and sauce). It was delicious :) the service can be a tad on the slow side so just try to get their attention. The staff is very nice and they will start knowing who we are by order (honey ribs).

Great place for pizza and drinks! I've been going here for quite some time but haven't gotten around to writing about them. This place gets bumping especially in the summer since they have a bocci court and they've won awards for their court actually. This neighborhood joint serves really great pizza and beer. I usually get this huge sandwich I believed named after the restaurant which has prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, tomatoes and roasted red peppers and onions YUM! I'm a SUCKER for fresh mozzarella. It's two meals in one. Great place to meet up with friends so check it out now that the weather is nice. Bonus plenty of parking.

Even if you're not in the mood for a hot dog, try it out and you'll be very happy. The owner is very friendly and there's a huge variety of different hot dog flavor combos that will fancy your taste buds. There's also a hot dog challenge so if you want your picture on the wall, prepare yourself. I'm actually going to try to out soon so I'll keep an update about that soon! Tell him Esther sent you!

BEST cheesesteaks around this town hands down. Why? Because of the fresh baked seeded roll baked right next door (connected to a bakery) with flavorful meat and cheese. This is my go to place for cheesesteaks around here (different story if you're in willow grove check out the steak and hoagie factory). More often than not, I can't get them since they close early (9 pm). Definitely check this place out and if you happen to go there, pick up some bread for the house. You won't regret it. Oh and they also have a deli meat counter (limited selection).

Delicious little gem off Huntingdon pike. It's a healthy cafe so they have turkey bacon and other delicious delights. I usually get the barista wrap- turkey bacon, avocado, chipotle, eggs, pepper jack and spring mix. It's delicious! I've also had one of their spicy Moroccan chickpea salads to go and that was also yummy! It hits the sweet (roasted butternut squash if I remember) and crunchy, spicy chickpeas, just love. Order it. They're definitely not a secret because they're always busy.

WOW! I am blown away with his authentic real Brooklyn style shop! I LOVE my bagels (and carbs) so if you're with me, read carefully. If you're into NYC style bagels, this place is a must. They serve breakfast sandwiches all day along with other sandwiches and you can buy deli meat-only the best, boars head brand. My boyfriend got the New Yorker (#5) and it was overflowing with meat! I got a breakfast sandwich on a garlic bagel (sausage,egg and cheese) and it was delicious. I was starving when we got there and ordered home fries but sadly I couldn't even finish my sandwich! Real problems of a hangry girl :/ Anyways, the owner's name is Steve and we had the pleasure of being in the presence of his two adorable daughters, Chloe and Bella. They're really friendly and it makes you feel that much better to be supporting the local community. You know Steve works hard through the food. He gets in by 5 am daily and even by midnight for the weekends. Sick! The difference between mom and pops vs corporate places is obvious. People like Steve have the passion for food and it's not just a job- it's their livelihood so I'd say they're quite motivated! My first visit and I was just blown away and you will be too. We ate in late Sunday and after talking with Steve and his beautiful daughters, we grabbed some deli meat to go and he handed us a bag full of assorted bagels!!!!!!! I just couldn't stop smiling after that. That totally made my day :) Thanks Steve for making us feel special and can't wait to see you again next week!

This cozy mom and pop shop is a mix of a country kitchen with many pictures of famous people from previous decades. The decor is eclectic but I think it adds to their unique style. Our server,Valerie, was extremely courteous and took our orders quickly (we already came in starving). If you get her, she's a toast fanatic and will make your toast perfect :) My boyfriend and I both ordered breakfast (he got a breakfast sandwich on a Kaiser with bacon, egg, cheese) and I got a breakfast platter. I LOVE breakfast food and grew up eating diner style breakfasts so I'm always psyched to eat breakfast food. I asked for the home fries well done (I love the crunchy part of home fries). Not only were they crispy but extremely well seasoned :)!!!! Bonus: they serve breakfast all day! Support your local community and check this out this cute place for good food and great prices. Our food plus two coffees were $13.99. That's a deal!

Great neighborhood spot! My boyfriend and I were going to go to ben's deli but they were already closed so we stumbled upon this pizza joint. I had a pepperoni slice and he had two slices of cheese, along with fries well done and garlic knots. Damn those garlic knots are amazing! Light, soft and fluffy with the perfect amount of garlic, butter and herbs. Fries are beer battered (my fav) and pizza was good. I highly recommend this place if you're in the area. Sorry we were too hungry to take pics! The service was also great- friendly and food comes out quickly :)

_Rhoq_IK0YExhXOAJOfs-A.review_text: Yum yum great food! Was a little leery at first because the restaurant was in a strip mall, but we went ahead and tried it...Hey, 450+ yelp reviews can't be wrong, right?The restaurant was small but clean and cozy; facilities were also very clean for a restaurant so close to the beach. It had a really good vibe and decor/atmosphere.  We sat outside (which had 4 four-top tables), so not really sure if they had any music. Our party ordered a bunch of appetizers so we could try a little bit of everything: Coconut Shrimp, Avocado Ceasar Salad, Black Bean Soup, Shrimp/Lobster Bisque and Oyster Shooters. The food came out fast and everything was really good. The shrimp (my favorite app) and oysters were very fresh. The service was also great - Shawn (spelling?) was our server and she was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. I tried the Blackberry Sangria...personally I've had better but it was decent.  Hey got rid of straws for 'environmental purposes' just to note...I personally don't like drinking straight from the glass lip, but when in Rome...I would definitely go back anytime I am in the area.

Decided to try this place out. Had varying Yelp reviews but dog friendly and it was in the vicinity of where we were headed. They had two sides to this restaurant/bar. To the left it was more traditional seating and to the right was the 'bar' side with high-top tables and stools; obviously a bar too. Had a few 'biker's'. Overall eclectic variety of patrons for a 12-1pm lazy and relaxed Sunday crowd. I would give this place 3.5 stars if I could. The Bloody Mary special was pretty good and the the clam chowder was actually pretty decent. Some Yelpers reviewed the chowder as being 'awful', but it actually was pretty good. Nice size clam chunks...Could you taste bacon? Yes - but it wasn't a bad thing. I'd order it again. Also had the tacos. Pretty good stuff. Typical local dive bar. Music was good and most the TV's set to sports. Service was friendly and fast. Definitely just a relaxing place to eat.

Went here solely based on Yelp! reviews and it was fantastic. A very eclectic group of patrons on a Friday night around 10pm. Staff was extremely friendly and knowledgeable about the menu and the food was served fast and hot! The facilities were clean. It was a very busy place for how small it was on the inside; maybe 10 tables if I'm being generous. They do have some outside seating. As far as parking: most signs said tow away zone or pay around the corner/pay to park, but we didn't pay or get towed. Either pure luck or my disabled parking permit...There was no close parking unfortunately, at least during this day and time. We got the 1/4 chicken dark, 1/2 chicken white (mild & hot sauce on the side) greens, fries, mac&cheese and potato salad. It was great fresh southern food. Will definitely come back!

Upon entering we weren't sure what to expect... went here on a whim because we had errands in the area and was starving! We entered through the bar area - not sure if this was by design or if there was another entrance around the side (didn't see one, but also didn't look), walked past the fully patroness bar into a larger room, with an even bigger 360° bar but it wasn't as loud or busy. They had a selection of booth type tables (wood bench seats, no squishy butt vinyl seats) or bar seating. We grabbed a table in the corner and began to peruse the menu. The front of the menu said: Beer - Burgers - Sushi. Interesting combo, but whatever. The menu had a variety of items but we were starving so once we honed in on something we chose it. We had the BLT Tots for a starter, then Sushi (crab Rangoon roll & crunch white tuna roll) and a BBQ Burger. For whatever reason all our food came out together: not really a big deal, we were hungry). The Tots were great very filling, but I would expect it should be for $13 for potatoes...The Crab Rangoon Roll was really good, but the White Tuna Crunchy roll was less than desirable. It was edible, I ate a few pieces, but decided to stop, it honestly didn't have any taste. I was full from the other roll and tots so I was happy regardless. The Burger was satisfying - no complaints. I didn't use the facilities so I can't comment, but the tables/restaurant itself appeared clean. Typical bar/after work atmosphere, same for the patrons. IDT I would take my kids here, but that's ok! Plenty of TV's, neon signs are 'bar' aesthetics. Our server was pretty good. We had to remind her about a couple of things, but she appeared quite busy as we were dining right around 5. She went out of her way to make a fresh pot of coffee, which was nice.

Excellent food!!! Wonderful atmosphere and great servers. The hostess on duty was a bit ditzy and a little weird, but it didn't impact my dining experience. When we walked in and up to the host/hostess stand she just stood there looking at us for an uncomfortable amount of time before asking if she could help. Usually during typical dining at a 'nice' restaurant, you are greeted  by your host/hostess immediately as you step up to the counter, but this sort of starting contest went on longer than needed. Again, it didn't really impact my experience, just a bit odd... On to the food: I had the pleasure of trying the prime rib, sea bass and a little gem chopped salad. Honestly it was one of the best salads I've had in a long time and it was big enough to split between two adults. The prime rib was juicy and cooked to perfection and the mashed potatoes it came with were creamy and delicious. The sea bass melted in your mouth like butter and had a lovely flavored dressing/topping with a side of spinach. The atmosphere was dark-ish but had ample lighting so you could read the menu and see your dinner mates but weren't totally blinded. It was clean, and had a nice vibe. This was my second visit (first visit everyone in my party all ordered the prime rib) and I would definitely come back. Enjoy!!!

Typical $15+ burger joint. Went on a Sunday afternoon; they were pretty busy but luckily we were able to be seated immediately. Odd half booth / half table seating with semi-uncomfortable wood seats and backrests to match the wood tables. They do have odd long pillows you can sort of use for added backrest/comfort. Lots of kids/families! Our server was great and all the other servers who helped her out. Everyone was very pleasant. I had the mushroom, onion & Swiss burger with sweet potato fries and a side of regular fries. The burger was decent...it could have been cooked less and it would have been much better. Sweet potato fries were good, I just wish they didn't pre-salt them - a little salty for me. The regular fries were also just ok, honestly they didn't taste super fresh. I can't say I would never go back here and try something new, but just keep in mind you can get similar burgers at half the price at competing restaurants.  The ambiance was 50/50. The overall decor was nice. Loud, but it was full/packed with customers. The seating/cushions were filthy with food remnants.  If I do go back I'd like to try something new and request the burger to be cooked at a different temp.

I've been here several times and have always enjoyed myself. The food (sushi) has always been fresh and tasty. Some things I have tried: edamame, miso soup, tuna & white tuna sashimi, shrimp tempura, spicy tuna, etc. The ambiance and servers have always been great. I honestly can't complain. For a chain restaurant, I'd have to say they are doing above and beyond. I have always gotten a variety of their sushi. All has been wonderful (again for a chain). I've tried a bite of their jambalaya and it was good as long as you like a bit of spice. Clean restaurant and clean facilities. I would definitely come back.

Tasty and trendy restaurant with a nice location.  Checked out this joint on a Friday about 1-2 hours before they closed and they were still quite busy. Only had to wait about 5 min before we could order, then took a number and found a seat. Upbeat ambiance, clean, nice facilities. Food came to the table fast, hot and delicious. Tried the famous Bonuts, S.E.C. (sausage/egg/cheese) and the Blacklock Hash. (Highly recommend EVERYONE try the Bonuts at least once). What is a Bonut you ask? Well it's their rendition of a biscuit and donut combo or as they call it: fried biscuit dough. Kinda sounds weird, but fantastically good and unhealthy ;). Everything was incredible. The only minor 'complaint' was when I asked for lemon the girl at the order counter said they were all out of lemons. I looked behind her and then asked again (noticed there were several cases of lemons behind her), She reluctantly said, "well we have lemons but ran out of the cut ones". Ok, I get it there only 1.5 hours till close...was a very funny moment but is it really that hard to really cut up one lemon? Ha!

Excellent food!!! Wonderful atmosphere and great servers. The hostess on duty was a bit ditzy and a little weird, but it didn't impact my dining experience. On to the food: I had the pleasure of trying the prime rib, sea bass and a little gem chopped salad - honestly it was one of the best salads I've had in a long time and it was big enough to split between two adults. The prime rib was juicy and cooked to perfection and the mashed potatoes it came with were creamy and delicious. The sea bass melted in your mouth and had a lovely flavored dressing/topping. The atmosphere was dark-ish but had ample lighting so you could read the menu and see your dinner mates but weren't totally blinded. It was clean, and had a nice vibe. This was my second visit and I would definitely come back. Enjoy!!

Food was pretty good. Sushi was absolutely terrible, which is why I didn't give 4 stars. I will go ahead and preface the server did take the spicy tuna roll off our tab immediately, which was very nice considering how terrible it was. Other than that we had the Lettuce Wraps and Thai Steak. The meal presentation on all our food was good. As I said before, both were good, hot and edible. I really wanted to like this place as I have only been able to find very limited 'good' Asian food in Middle Tennessee. The interior was nice, modern and clean and the server was great. Other than the sushi everything else was perfect. I would maybe try this place again, just to see if it was a fluke evening/night for their sushi. We did come in about 40 min to closing, but you would think sushi would be easier to prepare (as far as freshness) than hot meals & steak.

Wow! What an interesting find. I had an unrelated appointment in the surrounding location so I yelped nearby restaurants and found this gem. It was about 10-11am on a weekday. Still a few patrons, but there was plenty of seating. It's an old house converted into a restaurant; quaint, charming and unique. All the employees were very pleasant. I got a veggie & meat omelet with a side of Gouda grits. I also tried the stuffed French toast. Wow! The toast was out of this world. Absolutely fantastic. The omelet was hot and fluffy, and the Gouda grits that came along with it were fabulous. I'm not too much of a grits person, but I truly can appreciate this yummy dish. They have a fine array of homemade jams and their biscuits are good. Will keep going back!

Was in the area and decided to try this place via yelp. Would give this place 3.5 if I could. The cashier/server was nice and helpful. It wasn't too busy around 10am on a Wednesday. I tried the breakfast sandwich: scrambled egg, cheese and bacon on an everything bagel. Can't really go wrong with this 'traditional' fare. The coffee was ok, I didn't get anything fancy; just black. There is both inside and outside seating. Plenty of light and seating inside. Interesting mural on one of the interior walls. Clean and upbeat vibe. I would go back, it was definitely good, just nothing out of the ordinary.

Decent burgers...fries were delicious. The Parmesan truffle fries and sweet potato fries were fantastic. Super good with equally delicious dipping sauces that accompany them. Would go back just for the fries...The burgers were good, but nothing I couldn't produce at home. The prices were actually good - approx 7-11$ for most burgers, of course all sides are extra/a la carte. I was pleasantly surprised their burgers were not the typical $14-15 burger. I got the Goodnight burger and also tried the Classic with bacon and cheese. You walk in and order at the front counter. They give you a table number and your food is brought to you. The atmosphere was pleasant. Neon decor adorned the interior. Variety of seating options: outside, inside table/booth/hi-top/bar. I liked the foot rests attached to the booths. Nice touch. Ice machine was out of ice, but other than that, there were plenty of condiments about.  There is a parking deck right around the corner so parking is pretty convenient. I would go back if I was in the area.

Went on a Sunday about noon. They were not serving a "brunch" menu or foods, just a regular lunch menu. No worries, they did have reasonably priced Bloody Mary's that we're good :). I had the lobster roll and my partner had the burger. They were pretty good. I can't say it was the best most super amazing lobster roll ever as I've had plenty around the US but for middle TN, I'll take it!  Burger was hot and juicy. Fries were good and the side salad was decent. We sat outside in the back patio. It was hot, but it's July so duh. Surroundings were clean. The inside was nice and tidy. They had a stage for music/performances. Service was great, very friendly. They do wear masks and appear to practice new health guidelines.

I hate when my partner takes me here, I gain 50lbs just looking at the menu. Ha! No seriously, this place is absolutely amazing. Went there for the 4the time last week (1st time since Covid). Food was still fabulous. We tried the peach pancakes and original pancakes/egg combo. Super good stuff. Fluffy, tasty, goodness. The peach pancakes were: To. Die. For. Eggs were eggs. The side hash browns were decent, expensive for what you get. This particular time the service wasn't as good as it usually was but that's ok. We were not in any hurry this particular day. Tables were neat and clean. They now have a QR code at each table to access their menus online. No more standard/traditional menu's for now. They do wear masks and appear to be practicing new standards. Ate my food too fast and forgot to take pics!

I have mixed reviews of this place. The first time I went, I had the eggs Benedict and I enjoyed it. Can't remember the second and the next time I had avacado toast and a side of eggs and it was average....nothing to die for. Super expensive for what you get. I don't mind spending money as long as it's one of a kind, tastes good, is phenomenal, etc. Not when something is just average / blah. Coffee is decent, can't really mess that up. Service seems to be ok. Restaurant is almost always busy with a wait - at least the 3 times I've been. Tables and facilities are clean. I'd be willing to try this place one more time.

We finally had the chance to try Brothers and were not disappointed. I had the Fun Guy and my partner had the Jumpback Jack. Both were amazing. Burgers are made to order (and doneness) and came out perfect. The regular fries and sweet potato fries are both pretty dang good. I can't speak for the cleanliness of the interior of the restaurant as we sat outside, but the patio area was nice. The only minor odd thing that happened is another customer walked by us and noticed we had an ashtray at our table so he reached between us to throw away his lit cigarette. Ugghhh, lol. Note: we don't smoke, the ashtray bucket was on the table when we sat down and we didn't bother to move it. BUT, other than that strange encounter everything was perfect. Our server was super nice - I forgot her name. We will definitely be back.

Wow! So good. Glad this local gem is pretty close to our home. We had the steak sandwich and Italian sausage with fries. Everything was fresh and delicious. Fries were hot and crispy. Not sure if they have restrooms; didn't look for them. The area inside was clean and neat. Our table had a few crumbs on it but no big deal; We could have also went to another table. The gentleman working was pleasant and friendly. Seems liked he genuinely cared about our experience. I would like to definitely come back. Looking forward to trying one of the burgers - they look amazing.

_m0Sxb2_kUFtic4wGwIGzw.review_text: Staff are very friendly and the beer here is delicious. I also took a brewery tour, and the tour guide, Ron, was highly informative and taught me a lot. I had the loyal lager, the Jefferson golden ale, and the Pynk which is the picture I took. They were all delicious and unique tasting.

I got the Ny Strip, Medium Rare, and egg breakfast with some coffee. It was delicious and the staff was all friendly. I have been here before a couple of other times as well and the food and service have always been consistently excellent even when it's late at night past midnight. I highly recommend checking this diner out if you have never been there!
I come here a lot and get there Rice and Beans Bowl. Staff are always friendly and consistent. The atmosphere is great too!
Their food is always delicious and huge. It's a great place to get some hispanic food here in the St Petersburg area.

I came here for lunch on Friday, the 24th. I sat outside and it was pretty busy, I ended up getting the trifecta which was a soup of chicken pot pie, some pasta, and a small shrimp roll. It was pretty good, the server Denny was attentive and filled my water whenever it was running low which I highly appreciated. The atmosphere of the restaurant was relaxing and beautiful outside with the weather.
Came here for dinner with a friend. I got a Margarita and a burger here and both were delicious. Server was very attentive and gave great service. Will definitely come back again.
I got the corn beef hash with scrambled eggs, breakfast potatoes, and a biscuit which cost around 8 dollars plus tax. It was pretty good, I would recommend coming here for breakfast.

Been here a couple of times. Great diner with good service. Plenty of breakfast options for great prices and fast service. I highly reccomend this place if you're looking for a diner, somewhere affordable to eat in downtown, or for a quick meal.
I love the burgers at Engine No. 9. They're always delicious and savory. I honestly believe they're the best burgers in St Pete.

Ate here with a couple of friends. I got the grilled chicken ramen which was pretty good, a bit too salty though. Bushido sake was good. Service was okay, the server wasn't around as much. Overall, it was pretty good.
I had the bolognese here, it was amazing. The server, Miko, was also really nice and knowledgeable about wine and the pairings. This place has delicious pasta and good wine.
Ate at at the bar, I got the bolognese. Forgot to take a picture of it but it was really great, bartender was nice too.

Recently came back here for dinner and the bartender Ricky was highly knowledgeable of the menu and drinks. I ended up getting a the new york strip with their birch and vine set and was able to substitute some fingerling potatoes to it as well as order some fries. Everything was cooked at the right temperature and it was all delicious. The bartender was also attentive to my water and wine (I got a bottle of cakebread chardonnay) and made sure to fill it up whenever it got low which I appreciated. It was also Tuesday night which they do half of wine bottles under 150$.

I came here on a Friday and Saturday night and my server, Loriel, was amazing, friendly, and had great drink recommendations.  I got to try their spicy margarita,  prohibition sour, and pinot boiler cocktails. They all tasted great, my favorite is the spicy margarita.

First time eating here and I got the scallops which were very delicious. The bartender, Nick, was very friendly and made sure I have everything I've needed for my food and drinks.  I also got to try out 3 of their cocktails. The teak punch, 240 carrot, and the disa pier ing act. All three of them tasted great. The teak punch and 240 carrot were nice and sweet while the disa pier ing act cocktail was more on the bitter side similar to a smoked manhattan. The view from the pier was also astounding and the atmosphere overall was amazing and memorable. I highly recommend checking Teak out if you are in St Petersburg.
Came here a couple of times. The Chick n cone is pretty good and the staff are really friendly. The Buffalo Blue Sauce is my favorite!

I got a peanut butter boba and the Spicy Hue Style Noodle soup when I came here. Both was good. The soup was pretty big which was a nice surprise. It had a mild spice to it, which I was expecting it to be more spicy but other then that, it tasted great.

First time eating here and I got the Lardo Wrapped Octopus and the Pork Campanella. Both were delicious, the bread they provide is also great. The bartenders Harry and Joey were very friendly and also had a lot of knowledge on the menu and described the dishes I got perfectly.

The Galley is a great place to get food and drinks. Today I got the Cuban bowl which was so good, I had to get another one to go. Their Cuban sandwiches, chicken sandwiches, steak and eggs, as well as rice and beans are some of the delicious food that they have. They're bartenders are also really nice and friendly. I highly recommend coming here.

The food here was really great and I was surprised to see that they had a meat platter with plenty of steaks for such a great price. They were phenomenal, I highly recommend coming here with some friends and sharing it.

One of the best bars in st pete. The staff here are always friendly and they have a variety of drink options here. The atmosphere here is always clean, nice, and fun. They also bring in amazing live music , highly recommend this bar if you're looking for a chill fun night with some friends.
Nice hidden coffee shoppe on central. I had their iced crislip coffee and it was delicious. The place itself looked really cool and clean. Staff was nice.

I been coming to this spot regularly for a couple of months. The coffee here is always great and the staff here are always friendly and helpful. It's also a great spot to get some studying done. They also have some good food and snack options as well
The food here was pretty good, I got the Mangosteen noodles and added steak while my friend got the duck tacos. Both were delicious. Their thai ice tea tastes great as well.
I got the large Havana pull pork bowl and a fountain drink. The food was good, and it was quick to get. The staff were nice and friendly too.

Lord knows how many people drive by here every day, not even knowing it exists.  Little do they know they're passing up the best pastrami in the city.  This place is a little slice of heaven with a friendly staff and a small but good variety of specialty groceries.  It's not cheap ($7-9/sandwich), but once that pastrami melts in your mouth you'll know you paid for quality.  

Every time I go in here I feel like I've stepped into a corner deli in NYC, but they should only be so lucky to have a place like Protzel's.  I hope more St. Louisans discover this place like I did and give it a shot...you'll never go to Bread Company again.

For years as a native St. Louisan, the rule was the best BBQ in town was probably in your own backyard (or front yard to some of us).  Memphis and KC both laughed in our direction as mediocre joints opened and closed left and right.  Then along came Pappy's to show us what we've been missing out on all these years.  

Warning: The wait can be arduous, 30-60 minutes during peak hours, but the payoff is so worth it.  The meat is so moist and flavorful that their sauce is an option, not a requirement (although I prefer the hot sauce...they also have sweet and original).  The sweet potato fries taste as good as they sound, and the fried corn on the cob doesn't even need salt or butter for the incredible taste to emerge.  

St. Louis's rich BBQ tradition deserves not just a joint, but an institution that both locals can be proud of and tourists can visit.  Dare I say it?  Pappy's is the Arthur Bryant's of St. Louis...A legend in the making.  Combine the taste with the friendly waitstaff, central location (sorry suburbanites), and fun atmosphere, and you get a lynchpin of St. Louis barbeque.

...but I'll have to keep making my own pork steaks.

When I think of Cicero's, I don't think of the big beer selection, or the cheap plastic outdoor seating, or the somewhat arbitrary distinction between the smoking and non-smoking area...I think of a rock.  

Cicero's is like the dependable 3rd starter on a baseball team.  Every time you go you pretty much know what you're going to get.  You're never going to get your socks blown off, but rarely will you leave disappointed.  Above-average food, average to above-average service, about a 15-30 minute wait, a parking headache, $8 for a decent sandwich, $12-14 for an ok entree, good people watching, bing, bang, boom.  Like clockwork...every time.  I would call it the perfect neighborhood joint, but it's not really that either.

It's not too trashy, not too fancy.  Somewhere in between the too-cramped concerts and the frat boys playing pool, Cicero's wraps me up like a warm blanket........Excuse me, someone is calling.  What's that, ribeye steak sandwich?  You want me to order you?  With provel cheese on top for an extra dollar and a Fitz's draft?  Why must you always tempt me so?

Dewey's is alright, I don't really get why everyone seems to get worked up over them.  It's middle-of-the-road pizza, nothing too special about it.  Comes in only 1 type of crust (the bland "hand tossed" style, which inspires yawns all around).  You can see the workers in the back throwing the dough around during your long wait for a table, or you can squint your eyes to watch their lone 17" tv in the corner (why even have a tv if it's going to be so small?).

If you like lots of weird junk on your pizza, they can accommodate.  But that's not really a calling card, since almost every pizza place takes pride in the weird stuff they put on their pies.  Like most other pizza joints nowadays they have wacky names for all their specialties.  The service is alright but seems overworked.  This is a good place to go to if you're with a group of people that can't come to an agreement on anywhere else.  

That being said, the pizza's not bad, but let's not get worked up here.

Ahh, Ruma's.  One of the last bastions of "old" St. Louis delis.  And by "old" I mean big thick pieces of french bread, mostaccholi by the bucketload, and more provel cheese than you can choke down.  So why are their sandwiches so addictive?  I have no idea, but when the phrase "Gerber Sandwich" enters my brain (a hot ham and cheese open faced sandwich on french bread), I start drooling like Pavlov's dog.  

Their cheese will stick to the roof of your mouth, the place is perpetually dark and the atmosphere is dungeon-esque, but I'll be damned if this isn't one of the best places to get hot sandwiches in St. Louis.  It's understandable if you don't feel the same, it's the type of place only a native St. Louisan would appreciate.

But when you order, get carry-out.  The interior can be a tad depressing.

Man I have no idea how to rate Coffee Cartel.  Ok I'll try to break this out for you:

Scenario #1:
It's late and you're bored.  You (and/or your companion(s)) don't want to go to a bar or diner, you just want to hang out someplace and chat.  It's a warm night so you can sit outside.  The wide variety of people will keep the conversation flowing, from the faux-fashionistas strutting around to the panhandlers.  
Verdict: 5 Stars.  For late night people watching, it doesn't get any better than this.  Plus you don't have to deal with the obnoxious smoke.

Scenario #2: Same as scenario #1 except it's cold.  You have to sit inside and try to wrestle a table away from some sulking hipster or yammering sorority girl.
Verdict: 3 Stars.  Not fun, and the choking cigarette smell permiates the joint, so there virtually is no "non-smoking" section.  Plus the odds of you getting a table in the non-smoking portion is next to none.

Scenario #3: You're there to concentrate, it's cold, and you have to cram for a test.  You don't smoke and you want a quiet place to hang out and FOR THE LOVE OF GOD CAN THAT STEAMER GET ANY LOUDER???
Verdict: 1 Star.  This place isn't for you.  Go to Meshuggah's with all the book nerds or Kaldi's with the pretentious wash u students.  They'll be too busy with their nose in their book to pay attention to you.

I love contemporary art.  I really want St. Louis to be on par with Miami and NYC and Chicago when it comes to displaying art created after 1970.  I am so sad to say this museum does not deliver it.

I've viewed almost every exhibition here for the last 3 years or so, and can say that with the exception of one or two, every one has been disappointing.  The museum itself is similar to walking into a warehouse.  The "galleries" are humongous rooms with not a lot of wall space, and concrete abounds.  This would not be an issue if the curators would use the space more effectively.  

Instead of filling the space in with more, they keep everything to a minimum.  By no means do I advocate cramming in as much art as possible, but at least provide a sense of place.  When I attend an exhibition, it feels like they need to keep space available for the pallets of groceries they store at night.  You'll walk in a huge gallery and see 1 or 2 works in a 15' x 15' space.  This is especially true of what I call the "back room", which seems like it houses the castaway art of the exhibitions.  Note to the contemporary: You have a lot of space...USE IT TO DISPLAY MORE ART! 

As far as the exhibitions themselves, regrettably they are not on par with what you would see in other contemporary museums.  They have a knack for picking up touring exhibitions that are either very small or insignificant.  Many of the solo exhibitions they curate are the artist's first for a reason.  As an example, currently their solo exhibition features someone who salvaged refuse from construction sites with no alterations.  Construction garbage hangs from the walls and sits in corners, while the dossiers carefully watch to make sure you don't touch or "damage" them.  Don't get me wrong, I love challenging art as much as the next guy, but it's also derivative and bland.

The Front Room gallery is a nice addition and usually has good works on display.  I just wish the rest of the museum takes a cue and uses its space to do away with the needless minimalism.  Don't even get me going on the wasted space upstairs, either.  So much potential, so much underutilized space, so many artists you've never heard of, nor will hear from again...

St. Louis.
Summertime.
Saturday Night.
Out for a cruise with your fam or your best girl.
Driving down Chippewa.
Hordes of people standing around.
Line of cars backed up to get into the lot.
The friendly neighborhood cop directing traffic.
How do they fit all those cars in that tiny lot?
Stare in amazement at the menu.  The combos.  The possibilities.
Man this line is going to take forever! (it doesn't)
You order.  No pen, no paper.  They remember it all.
They hand you the order upside down.  You might freak out.  Don't.  It ain't going anywhere.
The taste combinations explode in your mouth.
You look around.  Doctors, lawyers, policemen, factory workers, newborn babies, screaming kids, teenagers, old married couples, white, black, brown.  Even dogs and cats.  Everyone is here for this and everyone is happy.
Pop open the hatchback and turn on the Cards game.  What's the score, Mike?  
Well, we better get going soon.  Get out before the post-game rush.

Ted Drewes is the great uniter of St. Louis.  There may be better ice cream, but the experience is pure.  Everyone goes to Ted Drewes, and everyone loves it.  You remember when your parents took you as a child,  you remember going there on cheap dates, and you remember taking your own kids there.  Rarely will you see such a spectrum of people, kind to each other, getting along as one.  Anyone can make good ice cream, but a trip to Ted Drewes may just restore your faith in humanity.

A *gasp* chain restaurant has the best burgers in St. Louis???  Say it ain't so!  Oh it is so, it is sooo so.  You can have your Blueberry Hill charburgers, and there are nice things to be said for O'Connells and Seamus McDaniels (probably the best non-chain burger in STL), but when it comes to burget ectasy, look no further than Fuddrucker's.  With the closing of the Westport location, this is the only Fuddrucker's left in St. Louis, so cherish it.  

Everything you need from a burger is here.  Various sizes to choose from?  Check. (Quarter pound all the way up to a full pound, I recommend the 2/3rds pounder).  Great buns?  Check.  (buttered and toasted and freshly baked every day).  Toppings?  Check. (they have a toppings bar, so top to your heart's delight).  And the burger itself?  Tender, juicy, flavorful, everything a burger should be.

I'm tempted to deduct a star for the mediocre sides and atmosphere.  The fries are average and sometimes undercooked, and it's a "family-style" place, so there are sometimes kids running everywhere, but truthfully the burger outweighs those negatives easily.  Actually, I often order the burger to go, so the atmosphere doesn't really concern me anyway.

There are a lot of burger snobs in St. Louis who will probably turn their nose up at this review, claiming that no chain is worthy of best St. Louis burger.  True there are many non-chains that have a valid argument for the trophy, but for my money's worth, I still go to Crestwood for my burger fix.

What do you want out of a diner?  Do you want a place where you can grab a $5 meal when you're drunk off your ass late at night, or do you want a pleasant dining experience with home-cooked meals?  Well sorry to tell you, but this place is neither.  I've been to the City Diner (or as I will forever call it, South City Diner) many times, and each time I wanted to like it because well, I'm a diner guy.

Here's the problem: This place tries to be everything to everyone.  They have a crappy side of the menu which consists of overpriced standard diner-fare, and a nice side of the menu, which consists of fancier food for people who want to pretend they're not really in a diner.  In both cases, the food is pretty mediocre, if not substandard, with the added guilt that you just paid $8 (plus tax, tip, and drink) for a cheeseburger w/fries at a diner.

The decor is nice, but the hipster tattooed waitstaff is frequently absent-minded.  I've had servers forget about my table, and also flub an order.  It's a diner guys, not rocket science.  It seems every time I've gone I've been slightly disappointed with the experience.  I will say that as far as people-watching goes, it's very entertaining.  SoCiDi seems to attract the crazier side of STL, including drag queens and pierced metalheads.  

I was about to give this place 3 stars, but then I remembered the last time I went I paid $13 (w/tax and tip) for a mediocre patty melt, crappy fries, and a coke.  I starting thinking what other great food I could have bought with that and realized it will be quite a while before I suggest coming back here, even if it's to grab a late night snack.

Seamus McDaniel's has the best bar food in St. Louis.  There, I said it.  The burgers are heavenly, but the chicken sandwiches give them a run for the money.  The fries are meh, but the onion rings are incredible.  It's the perfect place to meet up with your buddies and catch up, or hang out after a day in Forest Park.  Inexpensive, quick, good service, nice atmosphere.

So why 4 stars and not 5?  To tell you the truth, I'm not sure myself.  But there's something that stops me from giving it that 5th star.  Maybe it's the fact that they allow smoking, maybe it's the disappointing fries, maybe it's that locals tend to make a HUGE deal out of this place when in fact it's not mind-numbingly amazing, merely great.

Or maybe Seamus is the type of place that doesn't need fancy stars to let you know how great it is.  Unlike some other "great" burger joints in St. Louis *COUGHblueberryhillCOUGH* it hasn't been overhyped to tourists as a must-eat St. Louis restaurant, so it's populated mostly by locals.   Good for you, bad for the tourists.

Kaldi's is like the cool little secret that got out and now is ruined forever.  It's too popular to be considered a quirky small shop, and too small (and inconvenient) to be considered a go-to daily destination.  I live within walking distance of it and don't go that often.  I'll start with the good points:

- Nice service, generally friendly staff
- The quality of the food and drink is alright, no complaints
- Good people watching (Wash U book-nerd hottie central)

Ok, now let's go with the negatives:

- Cramped as hell.  They push as many table and chairs as possible so if you want to go to the back room (or anywhere else) it is inevitable that you're going to bump up against someone. 
- It's kinda loud during peak hours.  You know how you like to go to coffee shops to study and/or have private conversations with a friend?  Don't even think about it when it's busy, you often have to share personal space with a complete stranger.  Not to mention the noisy machines that interrupt you every 30 seconds.
- It's expensive.  Don't get me wrong, I'm no cheapskate (don't quote me on that), but seriously someday I'd like to get out of there without spending at least $5...on just a drink.
- Hard to get in and out of.  The logistics of Demun would be comical if it wasn't so awful.  Limited parking, one-way streets, blind turns, etc.  It's not a problem for me, but for the 90% of patrons who don't walk there, it's a huge hassle.
- No Free Wi-Fi.  This is the most damning of all.  So you're telling me after I find a place to park, wait for my $5 drink, accidentally hit someone in the head with my laptop bag, and sit within 2 feet of a TMI conversation, I can't get wi-fi?  This is really inexcusable in this day and age.  They offer free wi-fi at the laundromat, and I can't get it at a local coffeeshop?  At this point, I might as well sit in Starbucks.

Sorry to be so harsh.  Maybe I'm agoraphobic or cheap or not social enough or something, but Kaldi's doesn't really offer anything that I can't get somewhere else better.  If I want quirkiness I go to Meshuggah's.  If I want social conversation I go to Kayak's.  If I want space to breathe I go to Starbucks.  If I want to people-watch (along with black lung) I go to Coffee Cartel.  Kaldi's, you're great for my neighborhood, but not great for me.

Bandanas has the unfortunate priviledge of now living in the shadow of Pappy's, the new BBQ king of St. Louis.  Bandanas BBQ is good, even great at times.  It's a local chain, so there are places scattered throughout the region, and they all serve pretty good, but standard, Q.  

When I go I usually get the 2 meat platter with beef and pork.  Maybe it's my untrained palate or perhaps the fault of Bandana's, but I can never really tell the distinction between the two.  The sides are pretty standard stuff.  Beans, slaw, fries, baked potato.  The fried corn on the cob is pretty good, but costs extra.  They serve huge slices of garlic bread with their meals as well, which are incredibly awesome.

For what it's worth, I actually prefer their sauces to Pappy's.  True it's nothing fancy, but they pretty much cover the gamut with their 3 styles (hot, sweet & smokey, and mustard-based).  For a sauce guy like me, it can make up for boring meat (even though it shouldn't).

The service is usually good, and the prices are fair.  In the St. Louis BBQ scene, Bandanas tends to get lost in the mix.  They're just kind of there, nothing too exciting.  I don't think about them too often, but maybe I should.  I'll never put up an argument if someone suggests Bandana's, but when I'm in the mood for BBQ I can't forsee a scenario in which I wouldn't prefer Pappy's.

Pi's pizza is good.  Really, really, really good.  If you like deep dish pizza, you gotta give this place a shot.  The crust they use has corn meal in it, so it has a little extra bite to it than traditional crusts.  This also gives the crust a little more rigidity, lightness, and less of the doughiness that a lot of other deep dishes have.  Not saying it's good or bad, just different.  And different is good here.

This place is in the East Loop across from The Pageant, so that means good luck getting a table here on a show night.  In fact, good luck getting a table here in peak hours period.  Once it became known that this is Obama's favorite pizza joint (and it is, no joke...the owner flew to the White House to make him pizza), it's not unusual to wait 1-2 hours for a table.  It's worth it to try it once...whether it's worth it a 2nd or 3rd time is up to you.

I took my parents here, who are not down with the hip culture of the area, and they didn't think it was all that great.  All they noticed was the cooler-than-thou vibe and weird music coming out of the speakers.  So I suppose this solidly counts as a yuppie hang-out, and I'm ok with that.  Just know that going in.  This isn't a mom-and-pop place with candles and all that.  It's a noisy place to see and be seen, and there's a good chance that the people at the next table have better taste than you (or at least think they do).

So in summary: pizza = good, atmosphere = ok (depends on your perspective), value = ok.  I find it's a tad overrated by people, but judging on the merits of the pizza itself, it's very good.  Give it a shot.

Man, this place has some pretty devisive reviews for being a hole-in-the-wall pizza joint.  Alright, here's the bottom line.  If you're a carb fanatic who likes thick crust pizza (count me in!), Black Thorn has among the best (if not THE best) pizza in St. Louis.  They have 3 styles, but you really only need to pay attention to the pan-style and chicago-style pizzas, which are both amazing.  

Listen Chicagoans, I'm not going to pick a fight here.  Is it real Chicago style?  I dunno.  I'm not going to get all nit-picky with the types of tomato they use and how they layer the cheese and what ingredients go where, so save your snobby "this isn't real chicago-style!" arguments for someone who cares.  Is the pizza good?  Yes, it's good, bottom line.  2-3 slices are all you need to fill you up, and a large pizza will serve 3-4 people.

Oh, and the pizza isn't cheap either.  This isn't Little Caesar's where you can pick up a large for $5, or even Papa Johns where you can find a deal for $10-15.  Expect to shell out $20-25 for a large pizza.  However, bear in mind that their pizzas are very filling and that it will feed 3-4 people, so net-net, it's not a big deal.

However, there are a couple things I can't argue with when it comes to this place.  The service is consistently not great.  I don't mean bad, just not great.  You're going to a pub, not a Zagat's million-star restaurant.  That means you got to stand in line to place your order, you have to deal with a bartender who is usually too busy to take your order, and you have to wait 2-3 times as long as you'd expect for a pie.  On a light night, it's 45 minutes.  On a busy night, it's 2 hours.  Yes, it's annoying as hell.  Yes, you can call in your order ahead of time.  Yes, you should definitely do that if you have other stuff to do that night.

Also, unfortunately I happen to live in a city that has not yet had the common sense to ban indoor smoking (yet), so if you're a non-smoker, this can be a problem.  I'm almost to the point where I can't stand to be someplace while someone is smoking, so if you're like me, you better order Black Thorn to go, or at least get away from the bar area.  By no means is the smoke thick, but there are enough smokers here for it to be really annoying.  It's not as big a deal on a quiet weeknight, but on weekends it feels like I just crawled out of a dumpster when I leave.

So anyway, yeah, it's pretty much a dive bar that sells kick-ass pizza.  5 stars for the pizza, 3 stars for the atmosphere, 4 stars overall.  You can't go wrong getting it to-go, but if you dine-in, beware the hazards listed above.

Zia's is one of those places that St. Louisans love but I just don't get.  When people talk about eating out in The Hill, someone always inevitably brings up Zia's as their favorite or near-favorite place to eat.  I've been there on a number of occasions, and I'll put it simply: This is not Italian food, this is bar food with tableclothes.

Not to say I'm a food snob, in fact I'm far from it.  If it's deep fried, I'll probably eat it.  I'd rather have a good burger over a good steak, and I've been known to opine on the pleasure of eating fistfuls of slim jims and potato chips straight from the bag.  But Zia's?  I just can't do it, man.

Zia's is probably the kingpin of "old" St. Louis Italian, and for those unfamiliar with what that means, it basically translates to: Deep-fry the meat and/or smother it with enough sauce to eliminate the taste.  I really hate to say this, but just because you serve a side of pre-cooked pasta with an entree does not make you Italian.

Almost everything about Zia's screams "expensive bar food", from the appetizers (9 out of 12 are deep fried!), to the needlessly low lighting (what kind of weird carpet stains lurk in the darkness?), to the loud and crowded space they cram you into, to the wild fluctuations in quality of service.

All of this would be forgivable if only Zia's food didn't taste like chewing on an old leather boot.  Again, don't get me wrong.  I like some fried food.  I like some food with sauce.  I like provel cheese.  But all of these in heavy doses drain the dishes taste to the point of blandness.  There are some restaurants on the Hill that get this combo right.  Favazza's, Pietro's, and Cunetto's (to a certain extent) are all noticably better in atmosphere and taste IMO and still fit in the "old st. louis italian" category.

The fact that people treat this place with reverence is even more mind-numbing.  People wait an hour for the honor of eating toasted ravioli and veal parmesan with sauce that tastes identical to Ragu.  Cmon St. Louis, you can do better than this.

This may be my most torn review yet for Yelp.  There's a part of me that wants to give this place 5 stars because it helped revitalize the Loop, has Chuck Berry perform every month, and has a cool, laid-back vibe to it.
