This restaurant is really beautiful. We were invited to the grand opening, but came down with something and couldn't make it and were super bummed. We felt like jerks for RSVPing and being no-shows, so when we called to apologize, management insisted we come back another night. So, that we did.

The service was great and the staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. I ordered the Wagyu steak, which goes for a whopping $100. I wanted to know why it was $100 and I was informed that the cows are Australian, are fed only beer, and receive massages all day. (I want to be one of those cows!) Anyway, the steak was excellent. As was the caprese salad, which I always order anytime I see that on a menu. 

This place is pricey, but doesn't disappoint. A word to the wise -- do not take someone here on a first date. There'll be nowhere to go from there!

Okay, I've never been to Fogo de Chao, so that means nothing to me.

I thought Chima was super fun and delicious. Let me warn you though: Having your card turned to orange (meaning you want more meat) is friggin' dangerous. Those guys in their little suits come around with huge hunks of meat on swords and they come flying. They're like vulchers in reverse. It's pretty awesome. I feel like they should have wheelchairs by the door to cart you out on after you've stuffed yourself full.

The bacon wrapped chicken and the lamb are my favorites along with the creamy veggie soup and the turkey spread.

A good time and great food. I dig it.

This place really is all that it's cracked up to be. It's actually the first restaurant I'd ever been to in Philadelphia, but people had prepped me that it was a classic restaurant and that I was lucky to be going there.

The food was freaking awesome, the restaurant was beautiful in a very old society way, and the serving staff were great. We had the top floor reserved just for our one table for a private meeting. (Yeah, I'm lucky.)

Hopefully, I'll be lucky enough to go back.

I love this place. First of all - take out beer, bitchin! The homemade mac & chee is to die for. But, what really made me love this place is the staff and the environment they create. When I asked the cashier for a recommendation, she told me that her dad makes the meatballs himself and her mom makes something else herself...I just thought that was the cutest thing ever.

Campo's rocks.

Great place for adventurous eaters. Don't get me wrong -- it's great for the more conventional palate as well, but they do have some interesting (and many traditional) plates. I still have dreams about the pork belly. The baked egg is pretty cool too.

I love this place. It's walking distance from my house and has great food and beer, plus a cozy and fun atmosphere.

Eat: Try the Cuban sandwich or the smoked turkey.

Drink: The beer sampler rocks. You get a small glass of every kind of beer (for only $8).

BEST cheesesteaks in the city. I like mine with mushrooms and American cheese and plenty 'o hot sauce. The shoestring fries are irresistable and I highly recommend whipping up yourself some spicy ketchup (equal parts ketchup and hot sauce). 

The people who work there are nice and I like the no-frills environment. They're also open late and I think they deliver.

Plus, when you have Rosie the Riveter on the wall, you just can't go wrong in my book.

This is my absolute favorite sushi restaurant in PA. It's quaint, clean, and the fish is fresh. The sushi chefs and waitstaff are super nice.

The square sushi is really fun, but my favorite thing to order is the sushi/sashimi combo. You get an awesome variety of fish and they take the time to explain to you which pieces you're getting. I also ordered a spicy scallop handroll. It was on the expensive side since the scallop was live. And I do mean live -- literally still twitching. It doesn't get more fresh than that.

The best thing they have is the white tuna. Do not go here with out trying the white tuna - sushi, sashimi, it doesn't matter. What does matter is that it's what makes life worth living.

If I could give this place an extra star I would!! Seriously, one of the best meals of my life. Adventurous eaters: You MUST (and I do mean MUST) order the foie gras and the sweetbreads. I command you! 

As a native Californian, I am not a fan of, nor do I understand, the BYOB thing, but I have to admit, the bill was far less than expected due to the lack of alcohol. 

I won't be selfish and tell you this place sucks so that you won't make me wait for a table when I want to eat here (which will be often), but I will share with you the goodness that is Matyson. Enjoy, my Yelpers!

I really like this place. It's comfortable, affordable, and gosh darn it, I think it's fun. Plus, it doesn't hurt that it is literally around the corner from my house.

I always like places that offer all kinds of sauces to experiment with and Q's has 3 just sitting right there on the table. The street tacos are good (I prefer the pork and chicken), and the coleslaw and the macaroni and cheese rock my world. Great drink specials too. This place reminds me of LA in a non-pretentious, "we are close to Mexico" way.

I love this place. It has a cozy, homey vibe and always an interesting menu. My boyfriend and I were excited to find that they serve chicken livers, which are delicious. I also thoroughly enjoyed the butternut squash soup. It's a great spot for dates or business dinners and is perfect for those who want to try something new or for those who simply enjoy American cooking.

Okay, I know it's chain and maybe that doesn't make it "cool." So it's not a secret yet to be discovered. It's right on the very beaten path. But, the food is consistent and their drink menu is so darn fun!

There are several reasons I go to Eulogy: It's across the street (basically) from my house, they have an insane beer selection (and I do mean insane), video games at the bar (yes, I actually do like these), take out beer, and really good food.

My favorite beer is the Rodenbach Grand Cru. I think maybe it's an acquired taste because it's one of the sour beers. They have beers to please everyone though. They also have the best grilled cheese sandwich I've ever had...a crunchy roll, fancy cheese, and a yummy tomato. If a dream were a sandwich, this would be it. A friend of mine drives across town just for their meatballs. 

Apparently, one of the guys from one of the 'Real World' casts from like 10 years ago works there/owns it...? The funny thing about this little fact is that the person who told me actually referred to this person as a celebrity. 

Anyway, I love this place.

This place is pretty awesome. You'll probably be fairly unimpressed by the decor, but pay no mind. The skewers are really good and really cheap. Plus, they cook them right in front of you. I recommend the tofu, hearts, gizzards, beef, lamb...I guess I liked them all. I think the chicken skin was my favorite. Did I mention they all come on sticks? Who doesn't love to eat stuff that comes on sticks??

I really like this place. I'll admit, it's overly theme-y and can get extraordinarily loud. It's also fun and has yummy food.

I highly recommend the Mexican chopped salad (I got mine with chicken and cumin-lime vinagarette). It's big and has all kinds of cool ingredients. The taco tasting platter is fun because you get to try a bunch of different things, but I think the sea bass tacos are probably the best. All of the guacamole are ridiculously delicious, although rather pricey. 

Having recently moved to Philadelphia from California, where the best Mexican food is easily accessible, I was disappointed with the Mexican cuisine in this city. El Vez is pretty freaking good.

This is one of my new favorite places. It has everything -- great beer selection, awesome staff, great food, and good atmosphere. Oh and it's walking distance from my house. That rocks.

Some of the friendliest people work there, including the chef who is more than happy to cook things exactly the way you like them and he has great recommendations. The menu has a lot of fun things on it (like octopus, the butcher plate, etc), but also has classic bar food. 

Three cheers for PB&R!

This place is super fun. When I think of sushi/karaoke bars, I automatically think "not for me." I was wrong. It was pretty awesome.

The food is really good and the menu is fun to look at. I am a tough critic when it comes to sushi and I had no complaints. The yakitori was pretty awesome too. Just imagine -- gizzards, giblets, hearts, livers, chicken skin (my fave), meatballs, etc grilled and on sticks! God is good.

Having recently moved to Philadelphia from Los Angeles, I've been really missing authentic Mexican food. As far as I know, real Mexican doesn't exist in Old City and much of Center City. I was definitely happy to have found this place. It's in a questionable neighborhood (think skeezy people hanging around on every street corner) and has absolutely zero parking, but those are really the only downsides. 

I had the carnitas burrito, which was gigantic (I could only eat like 1/3 of it) and was filled with lettuce, lots of yummy rice, and delicious crunchy pork. My husband had the steak tacos, which he loved. Our grand total came to like $15. Plus, the guys who work there are super nice. We'll definitely be back in the near future.

On my quest for legit Mexican food, I came across this place. Pretty authentic and pretty good. Skip the chorizo burrito and go for the pork one instead. Yummy rice, yummy beans, yummy sauces, and a pretty fair price.

Best pizza in the city, no doubt. There are so many good things about this place. Where to begin?!

I guess we'll start with the backbone of the operation -- PIZZA! My favorites are the three meat (delicious sausage, crispy prosciutto, and pepperoni), any of the white pizzas, and the indulgent Sicilian pie. 

Next, the calzones and strombolis. Man alive, are they HUUUGE! I usually get mozzarella (a given) , ricotta, ham, and onions. They come with a cup of sauce and never disappoint. 

The garlic knots are pretty damn good and the salads are loaded with fresh and, dare I say, fancy ingredients (artichokes, feta, green olives, etc) and are bargain basement cheap. The house salad is all of $3.50 and it aims to please. 

Plus, the staff are kind and polite. Gianfranco for president!

Farmicia is great for brunch. All of their food is super fresh (which is not always the case for brunch at some restaurants since this is a meal that is served once, maybe twice a week) and the ingredients are local. The eggs and grits are fluffy and flavorful and the sandwiches are really good, I think, because the bread (sourdough!) is so damn good.

They also have great drink specials and fun drinks. I always go for the "barn burner" -- a great Bloody Mary.

My husband and I are obsessed with this place. Not kidding -- obsessed. Stella might even be considering getting a restraining order. We've tried each and every pizza at least once...and within a 10 day span (if it took that long). 

So, here's the pizzas in order of my favorites:
1. Sausage - the best pizza ever
2. Margherita - might sound boring, but it's pretty amazing
3. Mushroom - yummy creamy garlic sauce, yummy shrooms, yummy ham
4.Tartufo - you won't believe how good this smells, let alone tastes
5. Marinara - delicious cheeseless pizza, whodda thunk?
6. Pepperoni - can't go wrong with this one
7. Piccante - the favorite of most of the employees
8. Spinach - the pine nuts are a great addition
9. Zucchini - a much better topping than you'd think!
10. San Daniele - love the arugula 
11. Quattro Formaggi - the tomato sauce is freaking gooood 
12. Pistachio - a buttery sauce and thinly sliced red onions
13. Panchetta - very bold and delicious flavors

By the way, just because one has to rank last by no means should that indicate that I didn't like it. I love each and every one as if they were my babies (and if I ate babies, which I do not).

You got me on my knees, Leila!

This place is good, man. I was skeptical about a salad with bread in it, but the fattoush salad is amazing -- get it with the pita toasted, not fried. The baba ghanoush has a delicious natural smokiness to it and is an absolute must. The tabouli is crunchy, fresh, and darn good and worth the side effect of breath that could singe your fellow diners' eyebrows off. 

I ended up getting a chicken gyro. Now, I wouldn't normally go with the chicken, but the very, very nice owner dude recommended it and, boy, was he right. My husband had the shawarma platter, which was full of tender, flavorful meat. And, for no apparent reason we were given a free dessert. Don't mind if I do!

aiJG7jeyygfXg-oznRe5-w.review_text: This place is really good for somewhere I've never heard of until just last week. Unlike some other sushi restaurants, JJ doesn't do unlimited mussels. They also blended our orders (there was 10+ of us) but that wasn't an issue as much for us. Just a warning in case others care about that for big groups. The food was pretty good and the service was fantastic. Would definitely go again but probably in a smaller group.

I love this place a lot. The service is a bit poor but it is definitely made up for by its authenticity and decent drinks. It is, what I consider, a default place, when my friends and I crave Asian food because there are a lot of options. They are a bit pricey but I think it's worth the price. My favorite are the soups---especially if you want something brothy but filling.

Hands down, best pho place in Reno. I go here all the time. I get the #5 soup and it's never disappointed me. The service is outstanding and the prices are fantastic. There's no change in price for the past 3+ years. Their spring rolls are also really great and they have generous portions... As for their condiments, I think they have the best chili (the darkest red one) to go with their soups out of every pho place in Reno.

The food there was phenomenal.  We had dumplings in red curry and I really enjoyed it. It's definitely an interesting spin on dumplings and their respective dipping sauces. 
I would recommend any of the Chefs Specials, especially the Thai chicken. It was just the right crisp and the spices were great. I also loved that a "4" was actually an 4, unlike some places where a 4 could be too mild for my tastes. The service was great and I would definitely go again. For beverages, I had the Thai tea and it was a bit overly sweet for my tastes but people with a sweet tooth would love it.

I kind of wish they could do 3 1/2 stars but I'll bump it up to 4 because I think their attentiveness was very nice. The waitress was a bit forgetful at times but I didn't think it made my experience worse. The atmosphere was great and it could be good for causal or a first date type of place. 

Personally, I really only wanted calamari and wings, which are both appetizers. They were both average in taste, with the calamari being a bit too crispy, but good for "bar food." My friend had a brewhouse burger and it was very good according to him. 

Lastly, we saved room for dessert with the Pizookie Trio which was fantastic. I love the concept and the taste solidified that love. Neither of us are intense sweet lovers so the trio was a bit overwhelming but I loved the crunchiness and the moist middle. We had the salted caramel (my favorite), cookies and cream (his favorite) and the chocolate chip.

I love, love this place. The place is consistently good, from their burgers to their sandwiches to their snacks. You feel like you've stepped into a rustic, steam punk-esque location where your water comes from a mason jar. The lighting is very good and it's never too crowded feeling. I wouldn't go here for a dinner, but would come back for lunches. Their service is fantastic and the food comes speedy. Their selection is a bit limited.

Just as good as the place look, Midtown Eats reiterates its uniqueness and quality by how great the food is. Their sweet potato fries is a must and I love their varying snacks. 

All in all, it's a great place to get together with friends for a nice lunch or snack with great waiters and a lot of beverages to choose from.

When I came, I came for the seafood unbeknownst they had sushi and I wasn't in the mood for sushi. I had the bacon wrapped prawns with sweet potatoes and my friend had fish. He also got the New England clam chowder but I didn't think it was good for a seafood place. Also, it was very pricey (over 100) for just okay food. 

The desserts were terrible too. The creme brulee was terrible. I'm not sure if the sugar under the melted sugar plate was intentional but it was disgusting. It was too, too sweet and not smooth. The cheesecake was alright and pretty big but not good for such an expensive place.

So, let me start off with the fact that the best part of their food options is the fact that they have a dessert cart and their desserts are complex, there's lots of options and it's super good without being overly sweet. Their service is good and their thai tea isn't that bad.

However, with the abundance of Thai food places in Reno, I'm pretty picky about how good Thai food is. Their spicy is not that spicy (but maybe that's because I'm asian) and their flavors are lacking. 

I felt this way the first time I went, but tried again a year later because the desserts are so good, but it was just as disappointing as the first time. Their atmosphere is really cool and definitely have a "date like" feeling but if you're a fan of Thai food, this is not your place to spend all that money.

If I could give this a 3.5, I would. Let's start first with prices:
Compared to Poke King, it's the same price for the poke bowl. The bowls (3 scoops at $10.95) seem more worth it than the burritos, but burritos are cheaper (with 2 scoops of protein at $7.95). You can get small bites or signature burritos if you don't want to customize it. However, you have to pay $1 extra for masago, cream cheese, and seaweed salad, which for me is ridiculous as Poke King doesn't make you pay extra for masago or seaweed salad. You also have to pay $1 for water.

Onto food: the protein isn't bad and there are a lot of options. It's interesting that they have purple rice. The rice is cold. I like my rice warm. I like that they have a lot of toppings but they were out of some things when I was there. The sauces were okay, but they do not toss the protein in the sauces - it's just placed on top of all the sides and such. They get a 4.5 for how many sauces they have. It's really neat. For me, I like my protein to be flavored so I had to ask for extra sauce on the side to dip in/mix into my protein. 

Additional things: the location is quite nice and the layout of the seating area is good. They have super tall glass windows to order over/through, but because I'm short, I had to yell (and this was when there wasn't a ton of people). The trays are very slippery when you put a plate on it, so be very careful. 

Overall, it's okay. It seems like the burritos may be the better reason to go - at least if you rather have a burrito than a poke bowl.

I love everything about Poke King. The prices are decent and the scoops of protein are reasonably sized. The bases are either: wonton chips, spring mix, white rice, or brown rice. I normally get 3 of them and they're generous about it. I love the less creamy sauces and Poke King is great in that the protein is tossed in the sauces before being placed onto the base. I love all the toppings available and they're very generous about how much is added to the bowl. If I get the larger bowl, I could eat it for 2 meals. Their atmosphere is nice and they offer free water!

How is it that half stars are still not a thing for Yelp? I'd give this place 3.5. Presentation is 5/5. Food is 3.5ish/5. Service is 5/5. 
Get the mint latte. It's incredible and I could have had 10 of those if it weren't for the caffeine crash I'd suffer later. 

They definitely hyped their chicken & waffles way higher than they should have. The waffles lost their integrity within the first fork poke. The chicken was good, however the chicken to waffle ratio was lacking (too little crumbling waffle, too much chicken for said crumbling waffle). 
The green tomato chicken salad was surprisingly my favorite. I'm not a fan of dressing and I did feel like the chicken salad was drenched, but with a crunchy green tomato, it went well together. 
For the French toast, it had the banana taste, which was all I really wanted. There wasn't anything particularly special about it, though. Chez Louie is better if you're looking for some mouth-blowing French toast.

Honestly, I hope this place never closes. I love Chinese desserts because they aren't overwhelming sweet and maintain their fluffy, spongy (when approrpiate), integrity. I always get my birthday cakes here because the frosting is a buttercream that keeps its structure and tastes light. This does limit the designs they can do, but I hate fondant for its disgusting taste. They have 39 designs to choose from so there's a lot of options. Also, get their pastries. They all taste incredible, especially the sticky pork buns and cake rolls.

Second favorite poke place. They give 4 scoops for a regular bowl, with chunky fish pieces. I like the pieces a bit smaller but it's not too bad. I also like that the rice is a bit warm. I also like that the fish are tossed in the sauce before being placed into the bowl. The employees are always very nice and helpful. 
What I dislike is that the owner is apparently stingy because now extra scoops of crab salad and seaweed salad is 50 cents. Also, the employees were told to give only a bit of seaweed salad per time. I need to ask for more sides each time I go, per side. Their sauces do not live up to the variety of finbomb but the fried garlic soy sauce is super good. Actually, I just like garlic anything so I might be biased. 
Overall, it's pretty good and I love that Reno is getting more poke locations.

To start, I came on a Thursday so it wasn't a special night, which cost me $25.99 per person. This is about the price of all you can eat sushi and add tip, it's all you can eat Korean bbq. I love the latter two a lot more so paying that much for a buffet was me keeping an open mind. 

The service was the best part of the buffet. Our drinks were continuously refilled and our plates never piled. 2nd place goes to the decorations. They had meat roses and beautifully carved vegetables and fruits as decorations. 

The food was memorable in a bad way. Everyone told me this was their favorite buffet so I thought something there would stand out. The most standout ish part is that the carving station had more than just the generic prime rib and ham, and there was cotton candy. The desserts aren't as good as The Nugget Buffet or Harrahs and I'm a girl who is obsessed with desserts (and knows which desserts are quality). 

Go to a buffet if you have picky eaters to host. Go to a buffet if you can't figure out if it's a  Mexican kind of night or Chinese kind of night. Don't go if you want quality over quantity for your money.

As a recent graduate, I was skeptical about choosing a place that isn't all you can eat. Nevada is basically the capital of AYCE. When we went in, we happened to go during the busiest time of the night, which was a relief to me because that meant they were doing well. Mark was our sushi chef of the night and he was a great conversationalist. With a new trending restaurant, it's nice to see the employees care about you. The limited space is actually a plus, because that means every employee can give you the attention you deserve as a customer. 

Actually, this should probably be more about the food. Salmon is my favorite raw fish and they did not disappoint. They even made me a handroll into a long roll (Reckless) which was absolutely divine. The rolls are long so you do get pretty full after 2 or 3. As everyone else has posted, their poke bowl appetizer was great. I've been to many sushi places around the world, and to say I'd go back to a non AYCE place is a huge compliment. I'd go back here many times over with my friends because of how tasty their fish is. The rice is soft and warm. The nigiri came with the perfect ball of rice. Also, having a salmon skin handroll is an A+ in my book. 

They have vegetarian options that isn't just grass - their options are unique and make a fish lover like me want to try all of them. They also have teriyaki chicken bowl and beef bowl as alternative options to sushi. We had their beef bowl which was very authentic and delicious. The flavoring was spot on. 

Desserts are standard. Green tea ice cream, mochi, and tempura banana. All these options are a great way to end the meal. I felt full and not stuffed, which allowed me to go about my night being productive.

Holey Sugar! They definitely chose the right location for a donut shop.Their donuts taste very fresh and have the perfect amount of crunchy. I really like the glazed ones, actually. If a donut shop can't do glazed properly, they're really failing. Luckily, this place does glaze pretty much better than any other donut shop in town (maybe except for Doughboys). The specialty donuts are very good and there's a great variety for everybody's tastes. Also, the decor is beautifully done and the place is spacious.

I feel like this place has gone down in quality. Their popcorn chicken isn't as crispy and their spicy isn't as spicy without the add-ons. I asked for extra, extra spicy and the food tasted bland. Also, their "traditional" Chinese dishes are just insulting. A majority of them are Americanized Chinese dishes, like orange chicken, lemon chicken, etc. The authentic Taiwanese dishes are great, though. Also their appetizers are incredible, to the point where I'd eat them as main dishes sometimes

If any of you remember the crepe place that was overtaken by Poke King, this place is nothing like that. When I saw that this place had opened, I was hoping for more Asian options: green tea/matcha, red bean, pocky sticks, etc. 

Their options are good nonetheless. Since there isn't a solely crepe/cafe place in Reno, it's nice to see that this place had opened up. The staff is great. It was not busy when I went (around 1pm on a Monday). They have unique specials often, like a sweet cherry cheesecake crepe, and have great speciality drinks like snickers latte, to fulfill anyone's sweet tooth. Their variety is great, if one wants a sweet crepe and a drink with varying degrees of sweet. I like that they have specials, because that keeps me curious enough to come back to check on that. They have 11 savory crepe options to choose from, too, plus specials. 
It seems they are cookie butter/biscoff oriented as they sell biscoff supplies, have a cookie butter sweet crepe as a house special, and a biscoff latte as a speciality drink.

I really liked my sweet tooth crepe. The hot tea was very hot which is fantastic because I despise lukewarm teas. Fingers crossed for a matcha option in the future!

This place is great in all aspects: food, service, cleanliness, and prices. Their place is small, which is how they keep prices low and effective. The food is super good and filling. Their plates are huge. If you're in a rush, this is not the place to go. I like the experience of going there and love being able to watch the chefs cook all of our food. They are super fast at cooking and maneuvering around the tiny kitchen. However, I'd get takeout if I wanted somewhere less hectic to eat at. Also, they always make sure we have the things we need, like water and sauces. Don't be afraid to call out to the waiters though - don't wait around for someone to ask you how your food is, how you're doing, if you need anything, etc. Just speak out.

This restaurant is really a give and take. Gives lots of toppings, takes lots of money. Gives lots of options, takes lots of money. Gives generous amounts, takes reasonable bowl sizes. The rating is for the poke bowls. I'd give the acai bowls ONE star. 

Let's start with price, first. Their generosity in quantity of toppings was on par with my generosity of paying the steep prices. I wanted more fish, so I got their large which was $14.95 for 3 scoops. Their scoops are a bit bigger (about 6-8 pieces per scoop). I could eat it for 2 meals, so it's not too bad. However, Bluefin has similar fish sizes and is way cheaper (4-5 pieces per scoop). They make you pay $1 extra for mango, which is kind of weird. Also, their acai bowls are $8.95. I wouldn't regularly pay so much just for an acai bowl. Also, they could use real pineapple rather than canned ones for that price. The sizes are similar to Jüs and Basik, more expensive than Jüs and cheaper than Basik, but have more toppings put onto them than both places.

Secondly, quantity and quality. Their fish pieces are quite big. I only add sesame ponzu to get the taste of the fish which is good. They have blue crab and chicken, which is different. Their pineapple-citrus ponzu is unique and delicious. They have a ton of toppings, including unique ones like beets, pineapple, corn, and red bell peppers. They have spicy crab salad. I repeat, they have spicy crab salad. It's super good. 

I got the tropical paradise acai bowl. The flavoring is lacking. The honey helps (subbed instead of agave syrup). I didn't like that there's whole pineapple pieces mixed in because I like my base smooth. I would recommend Jüs over this any day. 

Lastly, service is great. The staff was very open to my odd requests of food placements. Also, the girl who helped me knew to put masago on after most toppings on poke and which toppings go well where. I love my food photos so it was definitely appreciated.

I am OBSESSED with this place. This is a board games place with very passionate customers. Glass Die is definitely getting a bit too crowded for its size now that it has gained so much popularity (which is great!). Sometimes we go in and cannot find seating/only find seating at the bar and would have to wait 2 hours to get a table for 4. Obviously afternoons are a bit less crowded than night time, but 3:30pm on a Saturday was surprisingly busy! We try to arrange to go when it's less crowded as it's hard to hear each another sometimes. I recommend calling in and asking if it's busy instead of trying to show up and not being guaranteed a table.

Despite the crowd and loudness, I wish this review could be done via voice because I'm so, so happy this place was created and is still in existence. There are a ton of board games, organized perfectly by maximum number of players. Everyone seems to really respect the games because each game is pristine and there's never any pieces missing. There is good alcoholic options that are often changed, great loose leaf teas, and snacks available. The fact that they use loose leaf teas makes me squeal in excitement. I super recommend getting a flight of six 4-oz beers/ciders/sours to try out because that's the best price if you want to try a chunk of their selection. There is no entrance fee so I really recommend everyone to get a drink to support the place.

I give a 2/5 for edibility. I can eat their food and wouldn't throw it away so there's that. They have AYCE dim sum, with limited choices. For Reno, that's pretty good. I was disappointed that they didn't have egg custard buns when I went, but the fact that they have steamed and fried options for buns is pretty neat. 
I tried their ShangHai Dumplings, which took 30 minutes for them to make (typical), and they were a hit and miss with each bite. I was given 6 dumplings, and some were juicy and correctly steamed and others were dry and lacking in flavor. They are made by the owner so it's nice to know that they're made locally. 
I had their chow fun and asked for extra spicy. The waitress assured me that it would be extra and it was not. There was no spice, and even the basic elements of chow fun was missing. The noodles were dry, stuck together, and somewhat crunchy. I would recommend Chin Chin in Sparks for good, solid chow fun.

I thoroughly enjoy shopping here! The place is super clean, well organized, and have great options. This is a place that combines the prices of Trader Joe's, the selection of Natural Grocers, and the deli at Safeway.I would prefer Winco for the salad/packaged veggies section and their bulk foods section as they are way cheaper than Sprouts. They also have their own brand which helps with the price. Often times, they have sales so I do agree that they uphold their slogan of healthy foods for cheaper prices. They are also very clean. 

Onto their selection specifically, Sprouts has gorgeous orchids! They have beautiful blue ones that catches your eye as you walk around their bulk foods section. As someone who does low-carb, it was great to see them have riced cauliflower, broccoli, and veggie noodles that are very well priced. I also appreciated them for having nuts with all sorts of flavors - cinnamon, plain, salted, honey coated, spicy, etc. I enjoyed their sushi selection, and they have Poke bowls for $8.95 now! I do not believe in pressed juices but their juice bar is super cool looking. 

Overall, great place to go shopping at if you're in the area (which I am not). The staff are all very friendly and helpful.

Honestly this place is so great for many reasons: 1) the aesthetics are amazing; 2) all their food options are solid and it's hard to go wrong; 3) the service is great and the servers are very accommodating; 4) their menu has many options to choose from; 5) their lunch menu is diverse and cheap.

I would like to highlight a few things on the menu: the drunken fried rice is to die for. It is so, so good and I typically don't like fried rice so I was extremely surprised by how good it was. I also really like all their appetizers, especially their spring rolls.  For drinks, I enjoy the iced green tea with ice cream. I think their Thai tea is too sweet for me though. 

They do use a 1 - 5 star scale but after going there about 6 times, they rarely ask me for what number I preferred. Sometimes I do go with a number and sometimes I let them decide. For example, their 4 stars is not that spicy when I ordered the pumpkin curry (from someone who eats a lot of pretty spicy food so take that as you well). However, I didn't tell them a number for the drunken fried rice and it was decently spicy despite us not giving them a number to match. If you do not want too spicy or cannot handle any spice, make sure to let them know if there's a chili sign next to the food. Despite not being spicy, their flavors still are pungent without being over-seasoned or salty.

ayee68jM2pRkWuOmRISKag.review_text: This is my first Yelp review. I am so compelled to write this review because this was the best Mexican food I've EVER HAD. My boyfriend and I went in starving and ordered a feast for take out. Literally, for $34 including tax we got: 3 bags of chips with a large cup of queso, large guacamole, and large Pico de gallo, then 2 Saturday specials (1 w/ chicken & 1 w/ pork) which included 3 soft taco shells each with large portions of cheesy beans, veggies, lime wedge, and moist flavorful rice. Lastly, we had 2 Tamales- 1 with chicken mole and 1 with corn and cheese. Everything listed above was simply the best EVER. As in the most flavorful, satisfying, authentic Mexican food ever. And the portions were great. The 2 huge bags of food covered our 4 person dining room table. We will be back!!!!

I love the atmosphere here. I enjoy coming to study or just grabbing a coffee or cup of tea to relax. The interior is visually stunning and i really appreciate the incredible efforts made to recreate an Oxford style building. The Bookstore is marvelous and contains am eclectic mix of books handpicked for their unique covers. The tea here is excellent but I have yet to try any food. I will be back again and look forward to tasting their menu!

I would rate this place as average. They had quick and friendly service for take out but the 3 rolls i tried didn't really impress me. They were actually kind of dry and lacking in flavor. I will come back once more to try the more "gourmet" rolls as they look delicious...I will add an update once this happens. The prices seemed average and fair.

This is mine and my brother's "go to" for sushi in Tampa! We love it so much. We've ordered take out as well as had plenty of sit down meals inside the restaurant. The sushi is incredibly fresh. The sauces are on point and bursting with flavor. The sushi menu offers typical, traditional, new and unique rolls so there is something for everyone. I have brought several friends and family members here and everyone always loves this place a much as I do. If you go on a weekend, be sure to make a reservation. However, it's worth the wait!!

I just tried this place for the first time and it was such a delicious experience! I've been trying to find a decent sushi place near me and this is it! I tried the blue crab roll, citro roll & summer of love roll. The flavors complimented each other well, the sushi was very fresh, and the service was excellent!

Tried this place last weekend with my boyfriend and we were enthralled. Foodie heaven. We ordered breakfast and also lunch to go. It was that delicious. I had the lemon ricotta pancakes & my bf had the eggs benedict. We were sharing both meals because they both were so phenomenal. That had to be the best eggs Benedict I've ever had. We also ordered the salmon cakes as a side and they were very moist on the inside, perfectly crispy on the outside, and packed with flavor. The sauce they come with is delicious too. I ordered a bacon, egg, & cheese sandwich to go for later and he ordered one of the lunch sandwiches ( don't remember which one as i didn't see it or try it). He was equally as impressed as i was overall with our massive breakfast and lunches to go! We will definitely be back. Oh- FYI they let us bring our greyhound inside as we waited by the door for our food. :)

I've been here twice now and both times I've had a 5 star experience. Most recently my best friend and I came on a Sunday and had mimosas with the chicken and waffles and the veggie burger. The flavors were outstanding, the service was great, and the atmosphere was perfect.

I came here for the first time last night with my boyfriend. We had a wonderful evening and thoroughly enjoyed our experience. We tried 2 red wine flights with a small cheese board. Mike was our sommelier. He did an excellent job presenting the wines to us and really seemed to care how we were doing with our samplings. He was very knowledgeable and made great recommendation for our flights. We got to sample 8 wines with generous portions (would have been 10 but we cancelled the last 2 glasses as we both were really feeling the wine by that point). We will definitely be back and will order more food or eat a larger meal before coming in. The cheese board was good but next time we will ask if we can have other options for cheese as we both prefer harder cheeses and our board had 2 soft/1 hard. The value was great though and we really enjoyed everything. We sat outside at a candle lit table for 2 underneath a live acoustic band from the bar above. The night was perfect!!

This review pertains to the Sunday Brunch. I have never had lunch or dinner here, but the $16 all- you- can-eat brunch is pretty awesome. They had a great selection with something for everyone. The buffet was piping hot and they also had a DIY Belgian waffle section with fresh fruit toppings. The waffles were delicious and I tried almost everything at the buffet. I also enjoyed one of the $2 peach mimosas. It was perfect- not syrupy or overly sweet. I came here with a few friends and the place was packed. The service was kind of slow as we had to wait for our drinks and had to ask for refills on water. I would come back again though because the food, drink specials, length of the buffet (11am - 3pm) & overall price was worth it.

I ordered take-out sushi with my brother and boyfriend and we tried more rolls...everything was phenomenal and the boys were both impressed with the quality and flavor of the sushi. We tried: the sweet potato roll (HIGHLY RECOMMEND), blue crab roll, spider roll, lobster roll, bagel roll, Tokyo roll, the Ladies roll, Key West roll, and an order of the blue crab Rangoon which was delicious and flaky! If you are looking for excellent sushi in the area, this is it!

This place serves genuine NY style pizza. I tried them a few weeks ago for the first time with my boyfriend. We both were impressed. The mozzarella is REAL, the crust is crispy and doughy without being greasy- true NY style. The sauce is delish and the toppings were very fresh. And the size- legit NY slices!! We ordered an 18 inch pie- it was heavenly and put all other "xtra large" pizzas to shame. Goodbye forever to all pizza chains in the area for us!!!

My boyfriend turned me on to Which Which last weekend when we went for a strenuous hike and got 2 sandwiches to go for our picnic lunch. I was blown away by the topping options and by the hearty and flavorful black bean patty sandwich. I was ecstatic to see options like hummus, caramelized onions, jalapeno hummus, spicy mayo, spinach, and quinoa on the menu. It's such a breath of fresh air compared to the standard "lettuce, tomato, pickles & onions" toppings offered at places like Jimmy Johns, Lennys subs, Subway, etc. I have now tried 2 subs and 1 wrap in only a week. Everything has been delicious, fresh, made perfectly the way I ordered it, (love the ordering system) and fairly priced. I will certainly come here over any other sub shop in the area!

The menu is limited but the food was delicious and fresh. Definitely worth the value and the wait. We were disappointed they didn't have cups/sides of guacamole, salsa, queso, chips, etc. They just don't make it. Also we were dying to try their tamales but they were completely sold out by time we got there. Arrive early for dinner!

The spiced chai tea late with almond milk and boba was devine! It was quite possibly the best chai tea I've ever had- and I'm a chai tea addict. I also had the house spring rolls & Naan For You entree. Both were bursting with flavor and were very fresh. I ordered carry out as I was in a hurry and the service was warm, friendly, and very fast. I can't wait to come back on a day where I can stay and relax with a book and sip more delicious tea!

My boyfriend and I have been on the hunt for THE BEST Italian place ever...and we've found it here at Ginos!!! We've tried the Sampler #1 (the eggplant parm is DEVINE), Sampler #2, Shrimp gnocchi appetizer, the savory and delicious garlic bread (a LOAF comes with your meal!), the Shrimp & broccoli tortellini, both and house and ceasar salads, and the tiramisu. Everything has surpassed our greatest expectations and has brought us into this fantastic food paradise with every bite. There is cheese on top of cheese, on top of cheese- on everything. The portions are legit (huge) and in line with the kind of Italian mom & pop joints I'm used to from upstate NY. We have eaten here twice and man...WHAT A TREAT. We can't wait to go back and will eat here as often as our wallets and waistlines allow!

bC3BA14cO5xVn4FifRFjdw.review_text: Super good hot chicken, first time ever coming to a Hattie B's, we got there around 4:00 on a Wednesday and there was no line at all! We got our food fast and it was delicious! I had the chicken tenders with Mac and cheese and fries. My spouse had the white plate with southern greens. The service was friendly and helpful, we found Hattie B's driving to our Air Bnb and were happy when a local told us that was "Nashville" as we were on our way and it was worth it!

Came in here really hoping to enjoy ourselves. Some of the poor reviews aren't really the restaurants fault (I don't blame them for not wanting to start serving an 8 person party that walks in 10 min before close or because of a Postmates order that wasn't fresh). We were planning on spending the long haul at this restaurant and racking up a decent bill, we got big margaritas and were really excited and hopeful. The chips and salsa that come free we're pretty good. The guacamole was kinda disappointing but still guacamole so we ate it and were fine. But our server, was not a good server, he was rushing us through every aspect of our experience, he wouldn't look at us and rushed through our drink order (two margaritas) to the point where he had to come back because he didn't write it down and forgot it. When he brought our guacamole he just set it on the table and walked away, we were out of chips from the chips and salsa and sat there for two minutes wondering if we were expected to eat the guacamole with our fingers because there was no silverware on the table even. He came back with chips two minutes later which was fine, but it bothered me that he couldn't take 3 seconds to say "I'll be right back with your chips" we were trying to take our time he walked up to us SEVEN times in fifteen minutes to ask if we were ready to order (we made no inclination that we were ready to order, we weren't looking for him, my fiancé was still looking at his menu) to the point where we decided to not eat there and told him we'd have our guacamole and margaritas and have dinner somewhere else, we thought he understood when we said that. He didn't. Five minutes later, he came back and said "Are you guys gonna eat or no?" We said no, and he said "Well you can't have a menu then" and reached over us to take our menus. No other employee was running around the way he was and everyone outside of his section seemed happy. Really disappointing experience overall (also the "large" guacamole is TINY)

Our server, Don F. really was the reason we were so upset with our experience here.

Being right down the street from Hattie B's Hot Chicken has got to be a both a blessing and a curse and I'd say everyone here at Bolton's does a good job of making it more of a blessing. The service is friendly even when it's over 100 degrees inside. You can tell Bolton's definitely caters a little more to the locals than the tourists because their medium spice is pretty equivalent to a hot or extra hot other places. It's still excellent though, they do a good job with their tenders and are honest with people about how much ranch they'll need. The only thing I'd say needs some work are their sides. They don't taste fresh like the chicken and reminded me of soggy grocery store deli sides.

We came here because it was walking distance from our Air B&B and I would say it was okay, they had one really refreshing and delicious drink that had cucumber in it. But he food was only okay, nothing really all that special, in fact, the experience was kind of forgettable. My fiance got a burger that he was really excited about and ended up getting another burger the next day from somewhere else because he didn't feel his craving for burgers was satisfied. I had the pork mac and cheese and it was oddly sweet. I was not a fan at all, half the noodles were crunchy and the flavor was just not pleasing to me. The girl who served us was pretty nice and we liked that there was live music playing while we ate, but, that's pretty much every bar in Nashville

I wish I could say more good things about this place. I think it was a little expensive for what you got, we ate at other places in Nashville that had the diner feel to them and had better food that was less expensive. I would say definitely go somewhere else if you're looking for a diner like experience, there are places on 12 South with better food that costs less.

I did really like the Mimosa I got, so that's why they're getting an extra star. I got Strawberry St. Germain Mimosa and it was delicious!

I was really impressed with this place! It's not what you'd expect from a sushi restaurant (it looks like a hole in the wall), but they had some really good rolls for a REALLY good price. The Crazy Roll was our favorite, we also really liked the Nimza roll. They had a lot of good variety and it was a small place which made it feel homey (a weird thing to say about a sushi place, right?) the service was pretty good, and we were happy we came here. Definitely worth going to if you're wanting some decently priced sushi in Nashville.

I would have given this 4 or even 5 stars if the service had been better. We did the take out option and it took almost 30 minutes to get two pulled pork sandwiches with fries. They weren't even that busy. We watched someone order their food, wait for 20 min and then leave because he had to get to his flight. The guy who took our order left immediately after taking the order to the point where after 15 minutes of standing there the lady who had taken everyone else's order asked what we had gotten and discovered that there was nothing put in. So, we had to wait another 15 minutes and then scarf our food down as fast as possible so that we made it on our flight. 

The food was not half bad, the fries were pretty good and my fiance enjoyed the cole slaw. The pulled pork sandwich wasn't the most amazing thing I've ever had, but it's an airport and it was good for airport food. 

Overall, for airport food, it's not bad. But it seems like they have an issue getting people their food at a decent time (all of this happens at the to go counter, by the way). It's one thing to be understaffed, it's a whole other thing to not tell people how long they'll be waiting before you take their money. I think we could have sat down at a restaurant eaten, and gotten the check in a shorter amount of time.

Loved the environment here as well as the staff and the drinks! We never ended up doing a tour, but the next time we're in Nashville, we definitely will! We enjoyed it here so much that we came back three times in three days. Each day the staff was friendly and helpful, we learned how to properly try whiskey, learned about some of the best places to go in Nashville, and even some of the best places to live (we're thinking of moving there) The distillery cat, Copper was feisty and pretty much always around to make sure you didn't forget about him, because he was darn cute. And the staff here seems to all really care about what they do and who they do it for. We didn't get a chance to see their other location and their other distillery cat, Pizza, but we're sure we'll stop by there at some point. Until then, we're more than happy to swing by Corsair anytime we're in town, and all the time when we move there. The drinks are excellent and reasonably priced and the gins and whiskeys are unique and flavorful (and I am not a whiskey person)

Talk about a place you would not expect! We came here on our way out of town because it was a beautiful day and we were craving some ice cream. Bobbie's had better reviews on Yelp than the other place we were gonna go so we thought we would give it a try. We each had a 16oz shake and could not believe the price! They were $4 each (which you don't find in MN) overall our shakes were pretty good, though we think we might have been happier with actual ice cream. The location was super cool, it was full of color and just screamed joy as soon as you drove/walked up. Being just barely across the street from Hattie B's has got to be good for their business because who doesn't want ice cream right after hot chicken? 

It was a very unassuming place with lots of options and friendly people, definitely worth it to check out!

Can we first just talk about the pricing? We compared this place to the closest thing in the twin cities which is called Lagos Tacos, and not only is Bartaco a dollar cheaper for each type of taco, but the environment is super cool and the staff is crazy friendly and helpful. 

We were pretty happy with our tacos, but weren't blown away by any of them. The key lime pie dessert was excellent and so was the guacamole. They serve their chips as just basically tortillas and you break them apart on your own, that was something new to us. But we liked it. My fiance really enjoyed the hot sauces they had which looked like they were made in house. I wasn't a big fan, there wasn't a lot of flavor to them. We both really liked the duck and the cauliflower tacos. He enjoyed the chicken pastor too, but wasn't blown away. Overall the tacos were good, not great. And the ambiance was pretty awesome. Plus super friendly staff!

I had my first ever Bison burger here at Burger up and I was pretty happy with it (it tasted like a regular burger to me, but I still liked it) everything was seasoned perfectly, and our waitress was so friendly and really attentive. I'm not a huge fan of mustard and can't eat mushrooms so the aioli that the Bison burger came with was not for me, so when I ordered I asked if they made other aiolis and turns out, they had a jalepeno aioli that worked PERFECTLY with my burger. The fries were seasoned and cooked really well and they had unique burgers that you don't find everywhere which I really enjoyed. 

The only thing I would say that bugged me a smidge was that the table didn't have salt and pepper on it, I had to ask and I'm kind of a saltoholic so I notice those things. But thankfully it wasn't a big deal to get me some of my salt :) :)

Love this little coffee shop/cafe! it's quaint and quirky at the same time. The monkey themed decor really got my fiance and I excited! We both got the banana monkey (not sure if that's what it's called, my memory isn't the best anymore! But it was a banana flavored mocha) and since it was so hot out they made it a cold brew. We really appreciated that since it was like 100 degrees outside. The place was super busy and had the feel of an old house being converted to a coffee shop, which you don't see in Minneapolis (where I'm from) a lot. Except on Grand Ave in Saint Paul. The people there were friendly and the service was timely despite them being really busy. They seem to be able to accommodate all the people they were getting with both indoor and outdoor seating.

We didn't eat here, but the people who were sitting next to us did, and their food looked delicious, so I'm excited to try that the next time I'm in Nash!

I liked it here well enough, we went based off a recommendation from someone who worked at Corsair Distillery (she did say she was biased because she used to work there). We were fresh off an incredibly disappointing Mexican place across the street from our Air B&B (see my review for Cilantro to find out what happened there :() So we hadn't had our Mexican food craving satisfied yet. 

We got an order of guacamole, which was super good (but honestly, overpriced for how much you actually get) and fajitas and a chicken quesadilla. The fajitas were a pretty standard Americanized fajita. Though for some reason restaurants are incapable of realizing that 3 tortillas is never enough. And all my tortillas were really hard on one side, like they were trying to warm them up, but really just toasted them instead. Because of that, they were a little bit hard to eat. My fiance got the chicken quesadilla which was also really good, though it tasted exactly like Taco Bell's Chiptole Chicken Grillers (EXACTLY) and we both really like those, so we were happy, though we could have spent 1/4 of what we did and gone to Taco Bell and gotten the same thing. 

Overall, the food isn't bad, I don't advise getting the chicken quesadilla because you can get the same thing for sooooo much cheaper at Taco Bell.  The fajitas and service were good, and I was happy with my meal, but I was not happy with the price tag that was attached to it.

This place is sooooo good! We were in and out super fast, there was no line when we went and we got to try a bunch of different flavors (I almost got decision fatigue while there there were so many options) I absolutely love that their sample spoons are metal and therefore reusable! The girl who was serving us was super nice and ice cream was much needed on a 100 degree day!! It was a wonderful way to end our walking tour of the 112 South Neighborhood and their waffle cones are super good. It was super messy and melted quickly because of the heat, but the pricing was super good, and the ice cream was even better. I understand why y'all have almost 200.000 Instagram followers :)

This place has all the makings of a popular breakfast place, and what do you know! It is one! We got there on a Saturday morning and were lucky enough to only have to wait 15 minutes to be seated. They have an excellent way of making sure that everyone is seated and gets their food efficiently, by providing menus, ice water, and even sunscreen to those waiting outside and having them order before they sit down. it's the perfect scenario for a place that gets as busy as they do. And their biscuits are bar none the best I've ever had. I had the East Nasty with the buttermilk chicken and sausage gravy and I was so happy with the meal I didn't eat the rest of the day because I was so happy. My fiance got the Lily to satisfy his ever hungry sweet tooth and we were over the moon content with our meals. The service was quick and friendly and the place is decorated to be a prime Nashville spot. Highly advise anyone in town to come here if they need some yummy brunch to soak up all the alcohol they consumed on Broadway the night before :)

bIsW255vsUMdZYk_IV7Xhw.review_text:
Probably one of the best cheesesteaks to be found in the 'burbs is served up at the Trolley Stop.  I called up the deli for take out, as its been a few years since I've been back to this joint.


"Do you still make cheesesteaks?" I inquired.

"Yeah, you want red sauce & onions on that?" 

"Of course" I responded.

"Give us ten minutes"


There is no other logical option than to say yes to the red sauce & onions.  Sure, traditionalists might fringe at something more than just meat and cheese, but trust me it's well worth it.  They cook the meat, cheese, sauce and onions all together on the wok, which lends to a well balanced sandwich.  Every bite you take, you taste a little bit of everything.  

it's a popular lunch spot and the deli line grows quite long around noon, so I'd suggest getting there before the lunch rush.  The hoagies here are legit too.  They will make pretty much any kind imaginable.

Came here for a late lunch, just a little past 2pm on a Wednesday with four of my friends.  Perfect time to avoid any crowds.  Maybe it was due to the holidays, but it was nearly dead during the swing hours.  Nevertheless, that did not take away from the experience.  Quite the upscale bistro for the area.

Service - 5 stars.  Very tentative, knowledgeable and not pushy.  

We all decided to order one of the lunch specials, all of which included salad and miso soup.

The orders:

Salmon Teriyaki Bento
Chicken Teriyaki Bento
Grilled Chicken Salad - (no side salad included)
Tuna roll & rock shrimp tempura combo

I didn't get a chance to sample the above orders, as I went with the Chirashi.  The fish, over a bed of rice & veggies, was pretty fresh and consisting of 2 cuts of salmon, yellowtail, halibut, trout, and one of octopus.

The only gripe I had, which was echoed by my dining companions, was the excessive use of pepper.  It was everywhere!  Both bentos were heavily peppered with thick black pepper, including the gyoza, meats, and CA rolls on their plates.  The chicken salad had a ton pepper in it.  When I got down to the rice in the chirashi, there was a layer of pepper over it.  Tuna roll & shrimp tempura escaped pepper free.
  
Overall, the food was pretty good, but the chef needs to let the food speak for itself.  I'd come back again, but ask to hold back on the pepper.

One word can best describe the pizza here - Oregano. 

I've never seen pizza made with so much oregano.  Instead of being a topping to add yourself, its already an integral ingredient when you are served.  Don't get me wrong, I like a little on my pizza like everyone else, but the amount covering the 2 pies we ordered were just overkill.

If you don't like a sea of green covering your pie, I would suggest asking to nix it upfront when you order.  Otherwise you will inhale an overwhelming aroma with every bite.  Other than that, the pizza was just OK at best.

Would I come here if I had been drinking?  Probably.  Would I come here sober? Probably not.

Good Vietnamese in Philly? Far and few between.  
Good Vietnamese in the suburbs?  Forget about it.

That's been a long standing assumption for some time but that's starting to change with the opening of Saigon 2 a few months back.  I didn't get a chance to try it when it opened, so I made sure to make a visit when I was recently back in the area.  Let's just say that the food was good enough for me to come back two days in a row for lunch.  That's saying a lot considering I'm spoiled with pretty good Vietnamese options in L.A.

As for the eats:

Pho tai nam - The bowl of pho with beef and brisket was quite large.  The broth was decent, though adding some siraccha & chili paste helped.  Though I would preferred the broth to have come out piping hot, it was still warm enough to do the job.

Goi cuon - pork and shrimp spring rolls.  The accompanying dipping sauce was pretty good, but reminded me of a Thai peanut sauce.  Crushed up peanuts and daikon topped the thick, peanut buttery sauce.  At the bottom of the bowl there was some chili paste, which spiced things up a bit and gave it a sweet flavor that went well with the daikon on top.

Cha Gio Re - These fried spring rolls were a nice crispy treat, with a nice warm pork filling inside.

Charbroiled Pork Banh Mi - plenty of pate for starters.  It had all fixings you'd expect to find. The pork was very fatty pork, with a lot of grissell and was a bit of a let down, but the rest of the sandwich was good.

I ordered a black coffee on my first visit and let me tell you that it was strong!  Served in a mini automatic french press that sits and brews atop your cup, the coffee is strong enough to be confused with a heavy stout flavor-wise, minus the alcohol.

Authentic, tasty and pretty affordable sums it up.  All of the pho & entrees are in the $7-$9 range, banh mi's between $3.50 - $5.

Note that there is a $15 minimum for credit/debit cards.

It's not your typical "looks great estetically, but no real substance" kind of joint.  Nothing but quality, fresh fish, in this modern, chic Japanese restaurant.  The lunch specials are pretty legit.  For $11.50 I chose the 3 three roll option, which came with a salad and miso soup.  Each roll has six pieces.  18 cuts of fish came to just about the perfect lunch portion.

- The salad wasn't anything fancy, but the miso soup had a good flavor.

- Eel Avocado Roll - The eel was good, though the avocado was a bit weak, maybe just old.

- Salmon Roll - Fresh cuts of salmon were delicious.

- Spicy Tuna Roll - The best of the 3 rolls that I had.  What I really enjoyed was the thin layer of crispy rice on the inside of the seaweed with a thin layer of white rice on the outside.  It made for quite the tasty roll and if I come back, I might just order 3 of these.

Not the best rolls that I've ever had, but still pretty solid and a worthwhile meal.

Hidden deep in a residential neighborhood, Famous George's is one of the better pizza spots in KOP.  

The pizza is pretty good and affordable (large pie starting at $10), though their stomboli's are what bring me back time and time again.  Treat yourself to a bbq chicken (nice a hot, barbeque onion flavor), or a steak 'boli (like a cheesesteak wrapped up) - trust me, you'll be savoring the flavor and have enough food to last for two meals.

Delivery can be spotty - I'd recommend take away.

This South Street staple is not only the cheesiest pizza in the city, but the cheesiest I've had anywhere!  That being said, it's the only type of pizza they sell, by the slice (gigantic) or whole pie.

Forget about toppings, forget about the sauce.  It's all about the ridiculous amount of cheese that makes the artery clogging induced ecstasy worth the just as ridiculous long wait in line.  3pm or 3am, expect to stand in line through the hole in the wall joint and snakes out on to South Street, especially on the weekends after the bars close, since they are one of the few eateries open to 4am that's not diner fare.

For health reasons alone I wouldn't make it a routine stop, but once in a while post bar grub run always makes for great eats.

Ah, the age old debate in Philly - which is better, Pat's or Geno's?  While I can't say that either of the two are my favorite cheesesteak joints in the city, I'd have to chalk it up to Pat's.  

The sandwich itself is alright.  The meat is chopped nice & thin, which is key in marrying it to the the cheese & onions.  I'd also recommend the pizza steak, which is pretty much just the addition of red sauce.

You won't get as much lip service as across the street at Geno's, but do be prepared to know what you want at the counter, as they will give you a hard time.

Newer is always better, but not in this case.  

Not much has changed in over a 100 years of service at Ralph's, and that suits me just fine. Sure, it's got the prestige, the history, the classic neighborhood feel, all of which really complement the food & huge wine cellar very well.

Besides the suggesting the pastas, some notable orders I would recommend:

Meatballs - delicious traditional seasoning
Eggplant Parmesan
Calamari in red sauce
Mussels in white sauce

Five stars for italian fare, you ask?  Why yes, because the food is that good.  There's few italian spots that I really recommend, but Ralph's does it well and should be a must try for anyone willing to shell out a couple bucks more than you'd pay at a chain restaurant.

A bar in the barstool district?  Who even knew there was a barstool district to begin with?

Sugar Mom's discreet location, basement level bar, and exposed brick walls give it a unique modern saloon charm.  By modern saloon I mean that it's kind of divey, but wouldn't go so far as calling it a dive bar.  Especially considering they've recently jacked up the prices up a good deal.

I'd suggest hitting up their happy hour, which features half off on all drafts...pulling some of those beer increases back down to reality.  Otherwise you get a steady stream of 90's music, pool tables, jukebox, and a very chill atmosphere.  

Sadly, I can't say that it's quite the same as it was a few years ago, though still worth popping in if you're looking for something a little more relaxed in Old City.

If you have never dined at a Brazilian steakhouse, you will love it here.  Then again you could say that for any place you go to if it's your first time.  For someone who was been around that block, Chima is not too bad, but not that impressive either.  

Some items were good, some ok, and some not so great.

 - Parmesan pork loin - pretty nasty, I'd not recommend
 - Bacon wrapped filet - small beef cuts, above average 
 - Flank steak - couldn't tell the difference between restaurant prepared or prepped at home
 - Lamb chops - gamey, not recommend either
 - Filet mignon - probably their best cut

We were looking forward to the ribs, but they were out on the day we went.  They also have some fish on the menu too, but we opted to just stick with land animals.

Overall, the meats were inconsistent from being too salty to just right, some overcooked to just right etc, so some rounds of the same meats tasted better than others.

A few bucks cheaper than Fogo, but then again not quite up to the Fogo standard.

I'm sure you've had one of those Friday's where you're just getting off work and all you want to do is throw back a couple of drinks?  Then head to Roosevelt's.

Friday night happy hour is really the only time & reason you need to be here.  $10 cover gets you penny drinks/beers from 5-7pm.  If the place isn't too packed you should be able to get your covers worth and then some.  No, it's not top shelf stuff (well drinks, light beers), but what can you say for $10?

Of all of the places in Philly to get a cheesesteak, Geno's ranks at the bottom of the totem pole.

Sure they guys behind the counter can be assholes and soup nazi-ish, but that really doesn't phase me - that's just how it's always been.  I just don't think the food lives up to any of the hype whatsoever.

Why not?  It's just not that great.  The rolls aren't half bad, I will give them that, but really, the thick slabs of beef just don't do it for me.  When I think of a classic cheesesteak it's got that chopped beef.  That's the whole schtick to the cheesesteak, so when you throw on those onions & cheese on the wok, they all just caramelize and infuse together, enveloping the meat.  This just doesn't happen to the meat with the thick slices of beef.

Go ahead and do the tourist comparison with Geno's cross street competitor, but I'd recommend heading elsewhere for a better made and tasting cheesesteak.

For any meat lover, if you haven't heard of Fogo then you need to get out from the rock you've been living under.  

Like any chain model, the usual salad bar, sides dishes, and all you can eat gluttonous experience is pretty much the same as the other locations that I've been to.  I do think it's a step above the others because when I ask for a medium cut, I can get a medium cut.  

The bar is pretty legit too.  Nothing less than a heavy handed pour.  I might even (how dare I say it) just come back for the drinks alone.

Wurst House RIP...you had great food, service, and a great beer selection.

Best House - far from it's former self, this reincarnate of the Wurst House, just as the namesake did, took a 180 spin in all facets.
 
The food's great, if you enjoy what amounts to congealed cold food that was supposed to be served hot.  Nice guys at the register, but delivery is seriously lacking.  If a few block delivery didn't take forever and a day, the food might pass as acceptable.  Sure, I probably wouldn't care if I were plastered drunk & would eat anything, but I like pizza served hot, not stone cold.

The steaks are missing that something as well....oh yea, flavor!  Completely devoid of it, bland, super salty, and overly greasy.  Would be great if my taste buds were completely burned off, which is kind of how my mouth felt after eating one these.

I will say acceptable for a slice of their pizza (for sustenance alone) in the rare occasion that there is nothing else open past midnight, or the fact that you're too lazy or drunk to hit up Wawa on 38th St, but thats really about it.  

Too many misses and no improvement over the years to say that it's worth warranting another visit.

Finding an all you can eat KBBQ spot in Philly is no small task.  There are better odds that you will walk into work tomorrow wearing gold dollar sign chain around your neck and quitting because you struck it so rich you'll never need to work a day in your life ever again.  

Though plenty of Korean restaurants are in the city, the all you can eat variety has yet to catch on.  This is as close as you're gonna get.  Not that it's Korean in particular, but more Pan Asian fare than anything else.  

Papaya salad?  Check. 
Hot pot? Check.  
Spring rolls?  Check.
Loads of meats & veggies?  Check.

You get your own grill and they start dolling out the meats (or hot pot, or both).  You ask for, you get it.  You want more, you ask and they bring it out.  For under $20 a person, you really cant go wrong.

They have also a menu (heavy on Vietnamese fare) for other dishes if you aren't going the barbeque route.

When my friend suggested we hit up this suburban location up for a dinner that was central for a group of friends, I had no qualms.  I love the original Ralph's that's actually IN South Philly.  Really, I do.  Those traditional meatballs, the pastas, the seafood, the superb wine selection to the feel & ambiance is the epitome of a traditional italian joint.  The south Philly joint knocks it out of the park.  The suburban location, however, not so much.  

By comparison it's cold and desolate.  And I'm OK with that.  You can only do so much leasing the space in a Sheraton, but I did have higher hopes for something a bit more than over priced banquet faire.

Being a party of 12, going family style on a numbers of dishes just made sense.  Both chicken & veal parmesan dished were probably left in the oven too long, jerky like consistency for both.  The chicken marsala came out pretty horrible unfortunately.  Nothing like lukewarm chicken to get those taste buds in gear.  The calamari was solid, though a little heavy on the oil.  Meatballs were a joke, at least compared to the OG spot.  Edible yes.  Worth the coin you're shelling out?  Nowhere near.

As pedestrian as our food was, the service was good.  Our large party was seated without a hitch, the drinks came in a timely manner and so did the food.  

Sadly, I've had better cuisine at my grandfather's VFW.  As a higher end spot, do save yourself the trouble of paying for an underwhelming experience and drive 20 miles down to Bella Vista to get better quality at the original location.

It's a must stop anytime in Reading Terminal Market for a quick snack, if not for a large order.  Let me just preface this review that I've only come here for their cannoli's. 

Their cannoli's are sick.  The ricotta cheese with chocolate chip reigns king here as the go to order, though I'm a personal fan of the vanilla flavor.  The custard to carb combination is just one of a kind and has a great mix of texture against the cannoli shell.  The chocolate cannoli's come in at a not so distant third to the other flavors.

A bit pricey for each, but worth the coin for a quick snack or dozen.

I've yet to be let down by Steven Starr's fusion concoctions.  Still a great spot to get some comfortish food if you will, with a bit of sophistication.

Some staples:

Rad Na - huge portions, easily enough for 2 full meals.

Chicken Masala - prepare to ask for another side of rice, as the portions provided is trumped by the amount of masala.

Lobster Mashed Potatoes - still one of my favorite dishes from the first time I stepped in here years ago.  Exactly what is says it is, I've made a meal out of this appetizer a few times.

Even though the menu changes from time to time, the food never disappoints and is a solid dining option, not mention the rooftop bar.

Best cheesesteak in all of Philadelphia?  No, but in West Philly, hands down! 

Everything on the menu is pretty solid, with the exception of their fries.  They are kind of crappy.
 
Before the days of man vs food, I accepted a friend's challenge which was worthy of Richman gluttony.  An 18 inch cheesteak with a side of mozzarella sticks.  Why?  Because when it comes to greasy comfort food, this is probably the best they have to offer.  Just good a, greasy cheesesteak with all the important items checked - fresh rolls, tasty meat, cheese and sauce.  
 
The mozzarella sticks are made just right too.  Not over cooked and the cheese just oozes out.  The chicken cheesesteaks are on par with tops in the city.  The hoagies are alright, though I would head for Wawa for a better one.  For a heartier meal, do the chicken parm.

bjDGX06VVzDG6GEKmNstYw.review_text: Yikes! Would be rating the coconut curry shrimp but couldn't get past the poor customer service. Vendor attendant simply shrugged his shoulders and said, "it's good" when asked about the dish and walking away as if he were annoyed. Oops, guess I was wrong to think it looked DELICIOUS!

Great menu, awesome drinks and knowledgeable staff. This place was standout for venue and quality. Highly recommend for a nice dinner. It was the best meal either of us have had in a long time (coming from a Houstonian and New Oleanimal that says a lot).

My favorite shop to study. Their coffee is great, and pour overs are affordable. They have a good selection of bagel sandwiches and muffins if you're looking for more than a quick caffeine fix. Porch is great for a nice day and the quiet backroom is awesome for studiers.

I've been an avid French truck goer for nearly a year now. Not only is their coffee (holy moly iced coffee is #1), but not a single roast has fallen short of wonderful. They know the art of coffee here.
This place is absolutely perfect for a light brunch. I love the outdoor seating and the crisp design. Great menu and of course, the best coffee in Nola!!
This place is all I need. Cocktails, sweets, and games. I love that is equally approachable for a day cocktail or a drink before a SwAnKy night out

PSA 4 months after eating at AVO, I cannot stop bragging about this place. I'm basically a walking spokesperson. At parties, my introductory statement is "have you eaten at AVO?". I stop strangers on the street to tell them to go here. Are you catching my point? This place is amazing. I love their contemporary presentation on traditional menu items. 
What I got: 
Appetizer: Charred octopus
Pasta: Rosemary fettuccine 
YUMMMMMMMNM

Incredible cuisine. Lives up to very high expectation. I am currently in a food coma from dinner but still thinking about my next trip. We loved that our waiter provided many honest and specific suggestions. This made choosing from their (everything looks great) menu much easier. An overall wonderful experience with venue, food, price and service.
*What we had:
Arepas sampler
Cerviche 
Empanadas
Blackberry (freshly muddled) margarita
Looking for a great place to dance on a Saturday night? Here's your place.  DJ Soul Sista on the tables with funky jams

Juan's is a great go-to place for a good, quick bite. The margaritas are up to standard and are a fair price. I recently discovered that their tacos are $2 if you buy them individually. This has changed my taco game. AFFORDABLE TACOS FOR ALL. Their Queso with chorizo is great too.

In NOLA, there sure are a lot of poboys. I have yet to find a spot for a hot sandwich on good (ciabatta) bread with a variety of cheeses. 

What I had: "clooneys choice" and iced coffee. 
-Didn't care for the iced coffee. Tasted to me like hot brewed coffee that had been left out and then iced.
-Sandwich was just as good as it looks.

Curried goat is just incredible. It's been a few months since I've been here, but this meal still sticks out as one of the best meals I've had this far in Nola. 

Andromeda cocktail is wonderful. Easy to drink without giving up flavor or adding sweetness.
Fully committed to their mission of providing delicious, organic products. This place is just adorable. Thank you Breads on Oak!
This is my favorite coffee in the area. It's considerably cheap, the drive thru is extremely convenient, and their lunch menu is perfectly "lunchy"

Not your "everyday" coffee shop on the corner, but very forward in the coffee movement. I appreciate the shop's aesthetic that creates more of an experience. 
I had an iced coffee- black. Distinct flavor with fruity notes and a nutty finish.

This might just be my favorite casual watering hole of NOLA. Their taps are full of unique and interesting beers, minus any pretentiousness that often accompanies this combo at other bars. I GREATLY appreciate their descriptive beer menu and unhurried nature when
deciding/ordering. 
Just a great spot for good beer, laid back atmosphere, and outdoor patio option.

And.. Ok... Those loaded cheese fries....

1st UberEats order! Finally the convenience of trying a Nola heatmap restaurant during the work week. I've been trying to make it here for months.
