I'm giving Talayna's 3 stars mainly because our server was super friendly and attentive.  If  not for her I might knock it down to 2.  

My boyfriend and I had a $25 gift certificate from restaurant.com for Talayna's, and had to meet a $50 minimum in order to get the discount, so we ordered a lot of food.  We got the calamari appetizer, which was definitely edible but just very blah.  It wasn't seasoned at all, the marinara dipping sauce was bland and it didn't come with any lemon, which is my favorite part of having calamari.

The house salad was pretty decent, and I like their sweet Italian house dressing a lot.  It reminds me of the salad at Zia's.  The croutons look house made and pretty sinful, as in, packed with so much oil/grease they're pretty much oozing.  But I must admit, they tasted pretty good.

Ah, the entrees.  I ordered the tutto mare, which was described as "thin, flat noodles, a variety of seafood in a red sauce".  Um, no.  What I got was linguine with shrimp, 3 mussels and a bunch of imitation crab meat in the heaviest cream sauce I have ever had.  The sauce had no taste but THICK, HEAVY CREAM with a hint of parmesan.  Not good.

My boyfriend ordered the grilled salmon, which was so overcooked and dry you couldn't even tell what type of protein you were eating.  It could have been grilled chicken.  The char taste from the grill was nice, but unfortunately that was the ONLY taste it had.

We might come back here for pizza, since I've heard that's decent.  And one major plus is that they don't exclude alcohol from the restaurant.com gift certificates, as most restaurants do.  So I can definitely see us coming back with another certificate and enjoying some pizza and beer...but we'll stay away from the overpriced (for what you get) entree/pasta section.

I looove this place.  For the type of place it is, it's totally perfect.  The best time to go here is on a cold night (and we have been here once a week since it started getting cold outside).  It's a small bar/grill with lots of wood & brick, giving everything a very warm and cozy feel.  They have a large fireplace with plenty of fireside tables around it.  The customers are mostly regulars and everyone has always been super nice & friendly, despite being located in the middle of West County a-hole central.  

We always just get burgers and fries, which are nothing spectacular but done right.  The burgers are always juicy and cooked perfectly, and the fries are hot and fresh, crispy on the outside and with just the right amount of salt.  I did stray from my usual burger once and got a salmon club, which was delicious, although the ciabatta was a little tough for the delicate fish.  However, it was a special and not a regular menu item.

They have a decent selection on tap too, not just the standard Bud & Miller.  Although they do offer the usual suspects, you can also grab a Stella, Schlafly, Guiness or Fat Tire.  And the domestics are on Happy Hour until 7pm, so you can grab one or two or three for 2 bucks a pop, along with a half price appetizer.

I'm giving The Country Club 5 stars not because you'll get the best food you've ever had, but because their food is really good, the beer is really cold, and it always makes me feel better to go there after a rough day.  

P.S.  Did I mention that they have a really cute outdoor seating area with a chiminea?  And they fly the firewood in from Colorado because it smells so nice when it burns.

Dressel's is amazing and we have NEVER had a bad experience here.  The one thing that I don't like about going here is parking in the CWE, as it's super annoying, especially on a cold night when you have to park 4 blocks away...but that still just makes it even better when you get inside and it's warm and cozy and there's a fire in the fireplace.  This place just makes you want to sit around with friends and consume mass quantities of beer, bread and cheese.  Or maybe that's just me.

Over the years their menu has evolved a bit, but I've always been able to find something I absolutely loved.  One thing we never skip is the homemade pretzel braid with Welsh rarebit.  That is a contender for last meal on earth, just like 2 or 3 of those pretzels...and the cheese sauce...oh my.  I'm getting greedy just thinking about it.  Also a favorite, though I'm not sure if they still do this, is the Sunday chicken pot pie.  I've never seen it on the menu but we used to go in on Sunday nights to get this wonderful creation--a gigantic dish with a puff pastry top, filled with creamy chicken, potatoes, carrots & peas.  

Sometimes we'll just get pretzels and cups of their stockpot soup, which changes frequently but is always so delicious.  I've had Guiness beef stew, spanish pork stew, french onion, bean...I've never had one I didn't love, and they're always served with warm bread.

The back bacon, egg & blue cheese sandwich, cheesy porchetta on baguette, lamb burger with apricot chutney and goat cheese, and of course the truffled grilled cheese with tomato bisque are all very excellent reasons to check out Dressel's IMMEDIATELY if you haven't already.

We moved out of the Tower Grove area about 6 months ago and it hit me earlier today how much I really miss being so close to Mangia!  The atmosphere is great--casual and unpretentious--and lighting, especially in the evening, is rather dim, which makes it feel more intimate.  The servers have always been extremely nice and attentive.  And in a city that's famous for not having a lot of late-night dining options, Mangia offers a good portion of their menu until 1:30am.  

My boyfriend and I usually get the calamari appetizer, which is wonderful and comes with a spicy arribiata sauce and lemon wedge.  Every once in a while we'll get the toasted ravioli instead, which is great because it's a little different than the standard STL toasted rav in that it comes with 3 dipping sauces...spicy red, cool pesto and creamy garlic aioli.  

For lunch, we usually stick to sandwiches or pizza.  My favorite sandwich is the Marcus, which is roast beef, olives, roasted red peppers, cheddar and a jalapeno cream cheese which is fantastic!  I would ask for that cream cheese on any sandwich I got, actually.  As for pizza, the classic margherita is delicious and I LOVE the Brutus, which is a blend of pecorino, mozzarella, bleu and goat cheese with marinated tomatoes.

They have a good selection of pastas too.  My favorite is the spinach manicotti but I also love their seafood di Mare, vodka pasta and porcini tagliatelle.  

Now if you'll excuse me, I have to go beg my boyfriend to take me here for dinner tonight.

This is one of my favorite places to drink in the spring summer as long as it's not too hot...they have a really nice patio.  The drinks and bartenders are all great, and I recently discovered they actually have killer food too!  The fish tacos and shrimp pico de gallo are very yum.  

Atmosphere is laid back and fun.  I always wind up chatting up some person at the bar and having a good time.  Good beer specials too...sunday nights, cans of Stag are only $.50 and PBR is $1 on Wednesdays.  It's the perfect spot for an after-work happy hour.

While you won't find super-authentic Mexican food at Chava's (or almost anywhere in STL), you'll find food and drinks that are pretty awesome, a loud but fun atmosphere, and friendly wait staff.  

I always get the fish tacos, which come with beans and rice and are amazing.  My bf gets the fajita soft tacos, which he ordered on accident the first time we ever went there and has never looked back.  

I usually get a margarita (plain/lime, on the rocks, no salt) but was recently talked into trying a mango-raspberry frozen marg.  It was super fruity and flavorful, and had a nice kick to it.  And because I just love their plain margaritas so much, I had to have one of those too, and well, my bf definitely had to drive home.

This place is great because they have their own parking lot (something I love, since I STILL can't parallel park even though I'm 30) and the place is always really clean, especially the bathrooms, which are mega cute.

Their patio is also really nice (and dog-friendly)!  We try to avoid going on Friday/Saturday nights (they get packed) but weekday evenings are usually fine.

One of the things I love most about going to a Mexican/Southwest restaurant is the chips & salsa they set in front of you, like, the second you sit down.  And it's free!  The main reason we would typically order an appetizer is because we want FOOD FASTER when we're really hungry and just sitting there waiting is BORING.  But when places give me free pre-meal snacks they're saving me money and quieting the roar in mah belly.  And the chips &salsa at Canyon Cafe are definitely the best in the STL area, in my opinion.  Blue & white corn tortilla chips, flatbread crisps with some kind of sweet & spicy mix on them and sweet potato chips, which I didn't think would go well with salsa but oh man, they totally do.

We did order an appetizer once, the sedona spring rolls with roasted BBQ sauce and tossed greens...reeeeally good.  But we usually go straight to the entree.  We both love the canyon burger, which is gigantic!  It's served on a jalapeno roll with bacon, cheese and just a light drizzle of BBQ sauce.  Tip--their fries are totally fine, but go for the grilled/sauteed vegetables instead.  Amazing.  Zuchinni, squash, carrots, bell peppers and mushrooms.  It makes you feel way better than if you just had the fries, which, to me, are nothing to write home about.

I've also tried the seafood paella, which was one of the specials.  I sincerely hope they bring that back soon...it was HUGE, with whole lobster tails, shrimp, clams, scallops and a spicy saffron sauce with grilled asparagus.  

I've never had to wait here but we also tend to avoid coming here on Friday night, etc.  They have plenty of tables and the service is great.

Very friendly, family-owned place.  Food is comparable in taste to any other Chinese takeout place but is cheap!  I especially love their bourbon chicken.  A typical combo meal with fried rice & egg roll will run you about $5.  Definitely worth it!

The main reason CJ Muggs gets 3 stars is because they're open late and we usually have the same waiter and he's great (hi, Carl!).  I tried half the things on the menu before I finally found something I like, and that wound up being the pizza.  I've tried several--wild mushroom, sausage & caramelized onion, pepperoni & mushroom, 4-cheese--and they were all great.  Actually, so are just about all the appetizers we've tried.  My favorite is the hummus plate, which comes with flatbread wedges, feta and some olives.  BF is partial to the chicken strips and chicken quesadilla.

They also have a nice outdoor area that is perfect for mild spring/fall evenings.

Nice beer selection, comfortable table layout, relaxed pub atmosphere and great bar food!  I love their pub pickles & pretzels, fish & chips and "adult" grilled cheese.  It's the perfect place to meet with friends for a few beers.

Even though they have new owners now and don't offer as wide a beer selection, it's still one of the best in the city.  I discovered a Unibroue wheat beer that I loooove, that I never would have come across if my waiter hadn't recommended it to me after asking me about some of the other beers I like.  

I haven't eaten there since they changed owners, but their food has always been very decent.  Not fine dining, but some seriously good grub after a handful of drinks.

Their back patio is maybe my favorite in the STL area, and I LOVE a good patio.  I drug all of my friends here for my birthday back in September and the weather was perfect.  The outdoor bar is a plus too.  This is just a great, laid back place to have some laughs and meet good people.

Civil Life just rocks.  It's this classic beer hall with loads of character, the owners are super nice, the beer is fantastic (I love the german wheat!!) and they have a really cool outdoor area (the real key to my heart is a great patio and a great beer).

I want to go here every day...I get so excited when I see local bars & eateries that carry Civil Life!  Go here and have an awesome time!

Update: One thing to note is that (at least the last time I was there) they do not accept credit cards.  But there is an ATM conveniently located right inside the front door.
Great food at reasonable prices, and they have a terrific happy hour with cheap drinks and appetizers.  Decor is a little tacky but we do really like coming here.
My favorite patty melt in the city!  This is a good place to go after sleeping in on a Saturday.  Lots of great places to sit and it's right across from the park.  The prices are very reasonable.

I have had a LOT of pizza in St. Louis but nothing compares to Black Thorn.  It's hands down my favorite.  I'm speaking in particular about the Chicago style.  We usually get pepperoni, mushrooms & green peppers.  Their sauce is spicy and a nice change from any pizza sauce I've ever had.  It's worth the wait for sure.

And you WILL wait.  Even if you go in on an early Tuesday evening and there's no one there, you're looking at probably 40 minutes before your pizza comes out.  The longest you'll probably wait is 3-4 hours on a Saturday night.  It's kinda nice though, because if you go there to hang out and drink beer with your pals, you can put the order in when you get there and just about the time you'll need some food to soak up all the beer, it's ready to go.  

This place is an awesome dingy punky dive bar that also happens to serve pizza.  It's a great neighborhood place that's a little off the beaten path (a bit away from the main stretch of Grand) and the people who come here love it.  You will too!

A couple DOs and DON'Ts:

DO bring something write on the wall with.  It gives others something to read while they're waiting on their pizza!

DON'T get up and leave your table without having someone there to hold it.  There aren't a whole lotta tables at this place and they are highly coveted!

DO plan on leftovers.  It reheats fabulously, especially if you stick it in the oven.

DON'T throw this pizza at anyone because it weighs like 50 pounds and would probably seriously injure someone.

This is BF's favorite place to eat, so we go here every year on his birthday.  We usually don't make a reservation but this year, after winging it every previous trip, we decided we wanted to try and get a great table for once, and it was a special birthday.  I called a week in advance to make the reservation and asked for a nice, private table for a birthday dinner.  I made the res for 8:30 so that a large portion of the dinner crowd would have already vacated.  

I called the day before to make sure they had made note of my request for a private table, and I was assured that would be no problem.  When we arrived, we were seated right next to 2 large parties and weren't able to hear each other talk.  It was a tiny little booth, and once we had gotten our waters, cocktails and appetizer, there was already very little room left.

The food, as always, was very good.  I got the filet and seared scallops with lobster mac & cheese...BF got the filet and lobster tail with yukon gold mashed potatoes, and we shared a shrimp scampi appetizer.  Everything was cooked and seasoned perfectly.  After our entrees were cleared, our waiter said "And what kind of dessert would you like?" which, to me, implied that they were offering a complimentary dessert for his birthday, as they have always done in the past.  However, when I received the check, I saw that we'd been charged for it.

The total including tip was just shy of $200 (one appetizer, two cocktails, two entrees and a slice of key lime pie)...we're not people who can afford to eat out at a place like this very often.  It sucks to feel disappointed after dropping $200 on what was supposed to be a special dinner.  It makes me a little hesitant about going back.

We stop to pick up a pan pizza here once a month or so.  The last 3 times we've been in have been terrible.  The pizza's fine (if you like Domino's) but there's a guy in the back who screams at his employees the entire time you wait.  Not "where are those pans?" in a loud voice but like, SCREAMING.  "Why don't you idiots stop standing there with your thumbs up your asses and do some work for once?!?!  Why do I have to do every goddamn thing every goddamn night?!!!!!"  Like reeeeally loud.  

I just assumed he didn't know there were customers waiting, but once when he walked past, he looked right at us and kept screaming.  I felt terrible for the employees, who looked like they were trying their best to hustle.  We're probably going to start using a different Domino's.  This dude has MAJOR anger issues and it makes me mega uncomfortable.

Couple small imperfections but I can't help but give this place 5 stars because it actually made my day BETTER today.

This was our first time going there so I wasn't exactly sure how it worked.  The guy behind the serving line pointed out the regular menu and the specials, and recommended the burnt ends sandwich (one of the specials), which is what I got, with jambalaya and cole slaw as my sides, plus a Lucky Club Cola from the fountain.  The cole slaw tasted really good but was swimming in sauce...but we went in at an odd time (3:00) and I might have gotten the end of a batch.  Not a big deal, still tasted awesome, even though I dripped on my shirt.

The burnt end sandwich was incredible.  And sooo tender.  The jambalaya had huge chunks of chicken and sausage and veggies, and was also pretty amazing.  BF ordered the double burger w/ cheese & bacon, and fries, which came out piping hot, perfectly salted and actually tasted like potatoes.  We were both really happy (and extremely full) when we left.  Next time we go there won't be a lunch break from work, because I think I desperately need a white Russian milkshake.  Yes, I'm pretty sure I do.

Went here for lunch today and it was PACKED.  Still didn't have to wait for a table for 2 though, which was awesome.  Apparently they specialize in fish, as our waiter told us that their Walleye is their most popular item, and BF and I spied a sign that said Tuesdays they offer discounted clam strips, which I plan to try very soon.  

BF and I ordered a chicken club and a cheeseburger, respectively.  The food won't blow you out of the water but is damn tasty.  Their fries are delish!  Our server was fast, efficient and a smartass (but in a friendly way), which I appreciate.  The prices seemed about average--my burger was about $8 and BF's club was $9-something.  The entrees and seafood specials were a little pricier though. 

I'd definitely go here again, though the atmosphere isn't all that pleasing to me.  Very cramped and heavily fishing-themed.

I love the warm lighting and intimate atmosphere we've experienced all three times we've gone.  The food, service and wine have always been fantastic as well.  Between us we've tried the crispy duck breast, lamb chops, my personal fave the bacon artichoke flatbread, the cilantro grilled shrimp and a few different desserts.  On our first trip they were still offering mini desserts (the passionfruit cheesecake was awesome) but have since switched over to a few fullsize desserts.  Most recently we ordered an insanely rich and delicious dark chocolate amaretto cake with chocolate ganache and brandied cherries.  

I just received a birthday email from them for $20 off my entree so I think we'll probably be back soon.  The only thing that worries me is they've never been busy when we go there.  Even on Saturday evening at 8pm there were plenty of open tables.  I worry that being in the Colonade shopping center isn't really helping their business.  Not having to endure a packed restaurant is definitely nice but I would hate to see them close.

Huge selection, great prices and the staff is extremely friendly and helpful. We're here about once a week and just love it more each time we go. Note that there's no cold beer, so plan ahead and make sure you have time to chill anything you buy here. Helps keep the prices down, though, which is worth it to me.

csA8AdkS22FYxK8Pd053Ow.review_text: So cute!! Lots of tables and outlets!! I went there to study, good atmosphere. They have live music in the afternoons,  students come and share their own prices! Great matcha lattes too!!
Super cute inside, love the bowling alley. Friendly staff, they have community seating as well. The only thing keeping me from giving them 5 stars is that my food was a bit dry.

The sushi was great, some of the best I think I've had! It's a a bit loud, and kind of dark inside but it works! Prices are on the higher end, but the quality of food and friendly staff make it worth it. 4 rolls and 2 drinks were roughly $125 for price pointing.

I was recommended this place by a native Chinese person. I was very impressed, the steak noodles were delicious and I was surprised there was lots of steak. The best milk bubble tea I've had since coming back from Asia. Fair prices and authentic food. Will definitely go back
Tasty, but the wait was long and I ordered donuts that were available at the time of order and then I watched them being sold to customers that came after me..
CASH ONLY!! Average cheesesteak- kind of dry and the bun is tough. Nice that it's 24/7 though.

CASH  ONLY!! Pretty good spot for breakfast! There was four of us and we waited 5 or so minutes to be seated. We ordered a few different things- we had a three egg omlet with bacon, onion and cream cheese. The kitchen sink and the pecan pie French toast. The food was extremely filing. Staff was nice. 18% service fee on tickets more than $50

Then restaurant is nice, I like that they're taking covid precautions and only letting 50% capacity sit inside. They also offer outdoor seating. Loved the assorted bread basket. The drinks were good, the oysters were great!

I was told this was the best in the city. Luckily I only had to call twice to place an order for pickup, the bun was good- meat was more seasoned but why were out of cheese whiz so I had to opt for provolone. Overall I thought it was okay.
Came here craving some bubble tea. Ordered a large taro- it was alright. Tasted very watery. I appreciate they didn't put too much boba in it. Not amazing, but not awful by any means. Average prices.

I don't think there's anything here that's bad!! We ordered a variety of things and everything was amazing! The staff was really friendly and I would definitely come back here! We had the veggie empanadas, el pastor nachos, Mexican cheesesteak, southwest chicken cheesesteak,  and the el pastor pizza!

We waited a little bit but it was worth it!!! The staff was funny and really nice! I wish we had one of these places in Kansas City! I loved their spicy Xiao long bao (soup dumplings)- a must try!! Everything was literally soo good!! We had the pork soup dumplings, the spicy ones, crabmeat + pork, fried beef and potato cake, pork bao buns, pan fried soup dumplings!!

Average food with that typical east coast attitude service. You can only have parties of 4 to be seated together. Nice little 'pod' seatings with TVs inside of them, not to mention giant TVs everywhere! The ice cream cake was pretty good, and filling. Crab fries are a bit deceiving as they're crinkle cut fries with seasoning + cheese. The Cobb salad was a lot larger than expected. Wings were your average joe wings. We ordered calamari and never got it- just gave up because we didn't want to wait. Staff consistently forgot things we asked for- had to ask for more water multiple times!!

5/5 stars if staff hadn't been so stuck up. We had no idea what the seating policy was like. They acted like we were stupid for not knowing where to go. Gelato was incredible!!! Tiramisu was rich, but delicious. Medium gelato was 2 scoops. We had two orders of gelato, and a piece of tiramisu and it was around $23. I would 599% comeback to try all their gelato.

This place was a nice place to come to watch a game as they have multiple TVs on all the walls. It was a bit loud. Food was alright, but the thing to get here are the cheesesteak empanadas!!! I think they tasted better than some of the other cheesesteaks I've had in Philly! The salmon sliders were average. Staff was decently nice- they repeatedly came and asked if we needed anything else towards the end of our time as if they wanted us to leave even though there was no one waiting. Prices weren't bad.
Nice and clean!! Friendly staff and quick service! Good pit stop for water, coffee, etc.

I was excited to try Mac Mart out while in Philly! My friend recommended saying it was a favorite. I ordered the cashiers favorite which sounded really good! It was the heart attack + ranch. Obviously due to covid I had to get it for take away. I thought that the staff was nice it's super cute inside but the mac and cheese itself was just ok. It wasn't anything to recommend to anyone else. Maybe I just got mac and cheese that had been sitting but it didn't taste fresh. I would consider coming back though.

Some of the best boba I've had!! I got the black tiger milk tea. It was a bit sweet so I made sure to stir all of the sugar into the milk. It tasted like Carmel milk. It was really good, the boba itself was perfect!! Not too hard not too soft. 100% recommend, and will come back if I'm in Philly again.

d1TBexam8SBAlWlqyrpXwA.review_text: The jerk chicken is tasty if you get bone in. The boneless chicken was dry. The sides are decent. Fried plantains were delicious...I'd order them all the time!!

The manager is phenomenal. My fiancé and I went for the first time and ordered our own pizza. I can't remember what we ordered but we didn't like It. The manager allowed us to reorder and gave us free pizza. 

Our next visit we ordered BBQ chicken pizza and Slaughter House and we loved it. Great portion sizes. Let's say I had left overs after day 1 lol.

Turkey manhattan was delicious. 
I can't recall what the sides were. If I could I'd give It a higher rating but I can't...
The food was reasonably priced. Had the pasta that started with the M and it was delicious. Sorry I can't spell It lol. The tres leches was delicious!!!

Breakfast Benedict was not as flavorful as it looked. Biscuit and gravy with the sausage was perfect, literally. 
The stuffed French toast was very unique. It wasn't the typical bread we have for French toast but was rather thick. I absolutely enjoyed it!

On Tuesdays they have the best deal in the world for steak.Their steak is wrapped with bacon. Big loaded potato, salad and chili or soup  for all under $10 . 
And their hermanaki chicken is the bomb!

Decent portion size and greatly seasoned. However, It doesn't taste marinated with butter as id like. I prefer crab legs that are smothered in butter beforehand ... anyhow It was good. Fresh and non fattening  is how I would describe It.
Their jalapeño Mac and cheese is to die for. The only thing I fixate on getting. The burger was mediocre but the Mac and cheese makes up for It.

Best seafood in the city, hands down! 
Their crab legs are always juicy and flavorful. Their potatoes are cooked to perfection. I don't like the shrimp with the peeling on It because It takes away from the shrink being well seasoned but their sausages makes up for It. 

Forgot to mention how their exotic fries are the best loaded fries ever. I added crawfish and It now is probably my favorite selection from exotic

Birthday cake 
And sweet potatoes or pumpkin cheesecake (I can't recall). If go back! The sparking drink was tasty!

My favorite Hibachi place. No matter how big or small your party is they seat you timely. 
If you go during lunch specials (before 3pm) you can get a meal for about $11-$15. Typically it's nearly $30 during dinner . Be smart and go during lunch because you get the same portion size for less. And the food is always great!!

Food is great but overpriced and takes too long to be seated and served. If you try to make a reservation they will make you pay a deposit. Ironic huh ? Go to Izakaya cheaper and taste just the same. And the experience is the same where they cook in front of you as well as entertain.
I almost always get their fried cabbage. It's so delicious. Sometimes they don't out enough sauce and makes It less flavorful. Be sure to ask for extra sauce. I didn't care for their crab Rangoons.
I would never debate that Longs donut isn't the best donut place around. Unparalleled. Made with love everyone. Half dozen of yeast glazed every time!

It takes longer than expected for food to be prepared. It seems calling in serves no purpose because you still have to wait a decent amount of time to even get your order. 
If you're impatient like me you'd be upset about the time but the taste and quality of the food makes up fo It. I either get  Philly cheesesteak or chicken teriyaki. Both are delicious!

Best friend chicken I ever had in my life. The honey is always warm and a perfect add on to the chicken. The sweet potato crock is perfect... not too sweet and definitely not bland. This Mac and cheese has a crunch to It and It will make you crave It randomly if you ever try It.

My favorite lunch spot. My husband and I go once a month. We always get Spicy Miso soup. It's always on point. We often get a side of gyozas and they are likewise , always cooked to perfection. The lunch portion is fair and I can finish it easily. Whenever I don't get the lunch size I'm not able to finish and have left overs. That says a lot about their portion size. I recommend this place to everyone I know. Great food. Great environment. Great staff.

Watami Unlimited sushi deal will certainly satisfy anyone. I started off with the American dream , sexy girl, dynamite and shrimp tempura roll . They're all flavorful. I'll definitely be back. It's cheaper Monday-Saturday in comparison to Sunday's $21.99 rate.
I had an omelette. It wasn't  as flavorful as I hoped for. The home made potatos weren't either. The fruit was fresh so that satisfied me. Unique environment and friendly  staff.

I love that this establishment moves at such a fast pace. The wait time flies by. The food is delicious. I can't recall which skillet i had both times I went but nonetheless it was delicious and I had enough to take home for leftovers.

I tried Swai fish for the first time here and it's so tasty. They cook it to perfection, it's light and flavorful. They have really affordable lunch specials. I believe it's $5.99 for meat, fries, and a drink. I also ordered fried tomatoes and they were so delicious! I'd definitely go back.

My goto: cheese head fried and spicy garlic chicken wings! I get the same thing every time. I occasionally get their deep fried Oreos . I've never been disappointed. However, I've been on a Wednesday where they have discounted wings but the wings are significantly smaller. Go with a bang. Skip the special!
The sauce is very flavorful. I had a seafood boil and I'd Deff get it again. The prices are very affordable in comparison to the boiling downtown.

The first time I went I shared a boil with my husband. We ordered 1/2lb of crab legs, 1/2lb shrimp and. 1/2lb of sausage (it comes with corn and potatoes). We chose yummy sauce and medium so one level. It was so good I went back again by myself and ordered the same exact thing lol. Worth the $26bucks!

This place is right near all the bars in broad ripple! Accessible parking. It's a cool place to check out for breakfast or lunch. I can't remember the price but i went 2x that I can recall so it must be good and affordable for me to have gone again!

Best andouille Mac n cheese ever. There pasta is also flame. The drinks are good as well. Funny story, my surprise engagement was here. This venue has a room for private events and they allow you to make a tab that is to meet or exceed $1000 from all the guest in order to get the room without charge.

Who doesn't love a fried chicken sandwich? I love their sandwiches. And their nuggets. Their new BBQ sauce is not comparable to the old sauce. Waffle fries are good and are always cooked to perfection but they aren't the type of fries you'll randomly crave.

Their red velvet waffles are a must have! I always get it with their chicken and waffle meal. You are able to select two sides and I always get their bourbon corn. It's delicious. Along with their greens.

The customer service here is awesome. I went once and the corn didn't taste the same and the manager herself sampled it , from the back, and acknowledged it then took it off the menu for the day. They serve all of their food with love and keep their reputation on the line. I love it.

I ordered the smokin chic pizza. It's a specialty  buffalo chicken style pizza and it's delicious. It comes with cream cheese, ranch, green onions,  blue cheese and pizza sauce.  

They have an inside and outside dining option. Convenient parking. And today's music playing for entertainment!

One of my favorite mexican restaurants. I typically order Cancun special, shrimp diablo or chili enchiladas. 

I've never had a bad experience here. And they offer lunch specials with drinks often.

I ordered the smothered fried chicken, scrambled eggs with cheese, hash brown casserole  and fresh fruit. Let's just say the only things i enjoyed were the fruit  and hash brown. The eggs were hardly scrambled and the cheese was just sitting on top of them not mixed what so ever.

My first time having rice king and I'm not head over hills. The rice is dry and has no flavor. The shrimp is cooked well so it makes up for it. At any rate, I don't think I'll order again from rice king. The ordering/ waiting process isn't the quickest either unless you call it in.

Play boy roll is a must try!!! Between my husband, my sister and I we've shared the ultimate roll, the play boy roll, the play girl roll and the lion king roll. The play boy roll was the best, hands down.

Best chicken fried rice ever. Fresh, moist, and flavorful. 
The jalapeño stuffed peppers were also great. 

We didn't care for the sushi so much but the side were large and filling that we didn't have room for the sushi anyways. I would go back everyday just to get their chicken fried rice and or the stuffed jalapeños.

The best food and vibe establishment in Tampa. 
7th + Grove not only offers delicious food and mimosas ---their management and the establishment vibe is superb. It's a perfect balance of ambiance + vibe + and lit. 
The deviled eggs with okra is so fire!!! 
The shrimp and grits were delicious and moist. 
The egg rolls were very original and tasty. 

The catfish bites were so fresh and moist. 
The chicken wings were alright. Moist but the flavor wasn't outstanding. 

I'd go back for sure!!!!
So many flavors of tacos to choose from. It's hard to pick a favorite. They make every taco fresh.

The chicken was delicious. I didn't really enjoy the rest of my meal. The steak was dry and flavorless. The appetizer was also distasteful. I can't recall the name of it but it was pork belly on top of a fried green tomato. The wording on the menu makes it sounds great, but it doesn't taste that way.
Biscuit and gravy was dry and not proportioned. The shrimp and grits was watery. The fresh fruit was the best option out of everything I ordered.

Best food place around! The drinks are tasty. The Cajun dilia is to die for. So flavorful and juicy. The red beans and rice and gumbo are very good. I would go back and get the same thing every time. I forgot to mention the appetizer. It was a wrapped shrimp with bacon and a jalapeño. So delicious!!!
The mozzarella salad is delicious. They have a great soul and salad lunch special. The chicken wings are not satisfying. The wings are huge and don't have much flavor.

dOKVBEfssYdjQF02Q7W2cg.review_text: I was so excited when i found out they opened a Mr. Wish in KOP! Their drinks are super authentic, tastes almost like the ones I would get in Taiwan. Just a little tip, if you don't want your boba tea too sweet, make sure you order 50% sugar or less. Their bobas already have sweetness to it so cutting back on the sugar in the milk tea makes it perfect. Their fruit teas are very refreshing, and has lots of fresh fruits in them. Totally worth every penny!!

Saw there were lots of mixed reviews about this place so I thought I'll share my thoughts to help people decide if it's worth going. 

Yes, it's true their service is slow but the food is just so so good, it's worth the wait if you have time (haven't had a drink there yet so can't say anything about that). The people there are always really friendly and loves to chat so I think that's probably why it's slow sometimes. But again, it can be kinda annoying when you're in a rush...

I've been there many times now and every single time I would bring home their bread. Their apple walnut loaf is my personal favorite, and they have 50% off day old breads! 

Ice cream is very creamy and the waffle cone is very delicious. 

The glazed donuts are fuffy and light. If you love dark chocolate you would definitely love their glazed chocolate donut. Normally the chocolate glazed on donuts would be very sweet but this one is different! It tastes exactly like a dark chocolate bar.

These donuts not only taste good but they're super fun to order as well!! It's made to order so you get to pick one glazed, one add on and a drizzle. If you don't know what goes well together no problem cause they have lots of options of their menu as well. 
What I love most about these donuts is they're still warm when you get them. It sometimes causes a mess ( and not really good for pictures after some time) since it melts everything on top but warm donuts are just so so so good!! Just remember if you want good pictures make sure you take them asap after you get them!! ;)

This is probably the best all you can eat sushi in the area! The pictures pretty much speak for themselves, if you're craving sushi this is the place. 
My personal favorite aside from the sushi is the teriyaki beef, so juicy and tender, a must have when you're here!!

i've been here so many times and it's hands down my favorite Vietnamese place in the area! the restaurant is large, clean and comfortable. the servers are always friendly and the food comes out pretty fast so that's a plus! the portions are pretty filling for an average hungry person. 
they have lots of options on the menu for those days when you just want to something other than pho. if you're around the area definitely come give this a chance.

you know some smoothie places that adds way too much water making it super watery like you're drinking juice? this place is definitely not like that!! the smoothies here are wonderful with very good and fresh ingredients. 

my favorite is the "detox island green" which has spinach, male, mango, pineapple, banana and fresh ginger. it's naturally sweetened and you can taste the ginger in the sips! 

the place is very bright and clean with friendly people. they also have sandwiched, flat breads, bowls and wraps on their menu. haven't gotten a chance to try their food yet but will update when I do.

Malvern Buttery is a very unique place, you pick what you want and pay at the end before you leave. decorations here are beautiful with an open kitchen so you can actually see them baking the goods. there are note pads and pencils on the table for you to write down what you are in case you forgot. Different kinds of seating are available from sofas to picnic benches.  A perfect place to catch up with friends or family. 
food overall is a bit over price but it's all delicious. they have soup, sandwich and salad for lunch and some sweet baked goods perfect for dessert.

five of us went in around eight on a saturday night, the place was packed with people but the wait wasn't too bad, around 15-20 mins. 
they're currently having a lobster week till April 24th, so some of us ordered from the lobster week menu. from the lobster menu we got lobster bisque and whole steamed lobsters. both were very delicious. definitely recommend the whole steamed lobster, one pound with potatoes for $18. 
from the regular menu we got cheesesteak and quarter pound cheese burger. friend doesnt really recommend the cheesesteak($14), the portion is on the smaller end. 
other then the cheesesteak disappointment, our server was friendly and the overall atmosphere was nice.

a friend brought me here awhile ago and i've been coming here many times myself ever since. it's for sure my favorite korean place! the overall atmosphere is great and the food is so so sooo delicious. 
their seafood soondubu is a must if you're a seafood lover like me. it has real seafood in it not those small frozen kinds, it even has half a crab, definitely a must order!

you can't really go wrong with Chick-fil-A! there were lots of people since it is a saturday but the line went by fairly fast(ordered in store). never been thru their drive through but seeing how the cars were coming in and out it seems not as bad as the pervious reviews. 
my favorite drink of theirs is the half lemonade and half iced tea drink, basically the best of both worlds. for the sandwiches I always go with the original chicken deluxe and it's always wonderful.

the food overall was good but the chicken pot pie was a bit disappointing. at $17 i feel like there should be more and the taste was just okay. my entree was the "beer can chicken" and it was very delicious. it was the same price as the chicken pot pie, and you can see from the pictures of the two dishes why we were disappointed at the pot pie. two of us got the ribeye steak and it was pretty good! 

we told our server we were here to celebrate a birthday and a graduate, he was very kind in treating us to donuts for the occasion. we also got the liberty bell ice cream as dessert and it was the best idea!

delicious pizza! we had the large Hawaiian pizza($15.75) and the large White Chicken Pesto($19.00). waited around 10-15 mins for two large pizzas on a saturday, which isn't bad. it's faster if you called ahead to order and come pick it up. they also have delivery with a minimum of $10.

really really good Sichuan food! been here so many times but it's actually the first time i remembered to write a review. 
personal favorite is the hot sauce style fish, have to get it every time im here. it's fish with some veggies on the bottom soaked in hot sauce. their hot pot style items are really good too! depending on what hot pot style you get there will be a main item with lots of peppers and some veggies, all mixed in a pot that's still burning with fire when it comes. (the fire dies down after awhile, no need to worry about that) 
they give out free white rice, which goes perfectly with all the spicy food and if you run out you can always ask them to bring more.

Absolutely love the interior design. This place is huge, perfect for hanging out with a friend or for doing some work. Just remember they don't have wifi but there is xfinity if you have that! 

We ordered a macchiato and a latte, very amazing. We also got the pancake to share since we already had lunch. It was so delicious! It wasn't just a stack of pancakes but it came in a skillet pan,soaked in the perfect sauce and topped with tons of amazing toppings. (see pictures for details)

been eyeing Suraya for so long and finally had the chance to check it out. came here during a wednesday noon and there was already a big line when we went in. It is such a cute restaurant with a great atmosphere. when you first walk in you order at the counter and take your number sign to find a seat. water and utensils are self served. 
we ordered the traditional hummus(comes with two pitas), two extra pitas and the Lebanese chai latte. the Lebanese chai latte came in the cutest mugs and was good but the main star for us was def the hummus and pitas. they were are absolutely delicious!!! could have it all day if i can, no joke! 
cannot wait to come back and try all the other amazing foods they have.

for those of you who don't know, this place is also green eggs cafe 8am-4pm! we saw the green eggs cafe sign when we passed by once but couldn't find it on yelp, thought it was weird so we came back today and we're told it's two restaurants sharing one place! 
one thing to have in mind is green eggs cafe is a cash only place, they do have an atm inside the store but they do charge you some fees if you withdraw so if you can have some cash prepared beforehand that'll make things easier! 
place is clean, simple and lots of natural lighting. food came out pretty fast and is delicious!! we got "the kitchen sink" and "creme brûlée french toast".  
the kitchen sink is a bunch of savory breakfast goodies all in a skillet. there are eggs,potatoes,sausages meat, cheese topped with gravy and biscuits.  
i loved their creme brûlée french toast a bit more to be honest, it's just the right amount of sweetness with lots of berries!!

a very cute little ice cream place with super delicious ice cream! my personal favorite is the "mint cookies and cream". it's the classic cookies and cream ice cream but green mint as the base. it's absolutely delicious. 
they also have milkshakes, ice cream sodas, cookies etc. definitely try this place out when you're around the area and you'll for sure come back for more!

a very trendy and bright cafe with a good atmosphere. the food overall was alright not amazing but it is a great place to catch up with friends or a cute date with your other half. they give free bread pots with special butter for every four people in the group.

The first time i tried Tiger Sugar was in California so when I found out they were opening one in Philly I was super excited. The wait when I was there was around 10-15 mins, they check your temp before letting anyone go in. 
We got #1, it really is just like drinking a dessert. overall it was really good for times when you have those sugar cravings. One thing I would do differently next time is to get less ice. When you finish the drink there is still around 1/3 of a cup of ice in there

dU7i1wjAQ1q_-7a7JRVqZw.review_text: We really wanted to try this place but after 30 minutes of looking at their online menu and deciding on 50 dollars worth of food we tried to call a to go order in only to find out that they have a carry out menu with NO sandwiches on it. Not willing to help we decided to take our business to City BBQ!! Dumb business move!

Well after wanting to try this place for awhile I was really hoping to like/love this place. Unfortunately I neither liked nor loved anything about this place.

The hostess was nice and greeted us quickly and was looking for a table, even thou it was 5:30pm and the place was less than half full. I offered we would sit in the bar at a booth if that made it easier for her. She agreed and seated us.

My boyfriend and I are average size, I'm on the shorter side but trying to squeeze in the booth was challenging. Once in the table came up to my neck. Not a comfortable seating arrangement to eat comfort food!

The server arrived and took our drink orders. Drinks were served promptly and I did like the glassware and decor. We order the Crab cakes for a appetizer.

Crab cakes arrived and for 12.95 the size was unimpressive. Two half dollars sized extra crispy on one side (if I cooked them I would say burnt). I fished out many pieces of shells and chucked it up to that's what you get for eating crab cakes. Not impressed

My boyfriend odered the catfish poboy with okra. I decided on the special top sirloin with the sweet potato casserole and mac and cheese. The server told my boyfriend it's the best poboy and you would think your in New Orleans. I asked about the mac and cheese and she stated it was better than her grandmas.

Also, i must say we never got any complimentary corn bread or knew about it till leaving.

The food arrived and this is where truly I'm shocked. The catfish was straight out of a box as well as the okra ( if guessing coming from GFS located behind the restaurant). My sweet potato casserole was most likely yams from a can mashed with a sprinkle of brown sugar. The mac and cheese was boiled macaroni with shredded chesse then heated. I will say my steak was cooked perfectly and tasted decent.

After eating we had empty drink glasses never asked to be refilled even though the manager passed by our table several times. The server was the bartender and was busy but the manager who was dressed inappropriate could have asked us if we needed refills.

By this time I just wanted the check. After 57.00 plus tip I can honestly say we will never be back. We paid for tasteless, greasy, and food that could have gotten at a local gas station. 

Don't waste your time. This restaurant has a great theme but if you want to be a Southern food joint buy some seasonings and spices. Prepare the food not just take it out of the box and deep fry it or heat it up!

Smee's is our place!! We come here very often for lunch and dinner. It's casual, friendly and the food is good. Never had a problem. I recommend the Mary Lou! The only reason I am giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is because they have removed the Buffalo Chicken dip. We had recently tried this and loved it! We went back the next week and it was taken off the menu. We instead had the salmon dip and that was delicious but would really appreciate it if you brought the Buffalo Chicken dip back!!

Love this place. My favorite is the chicken pad thai. Wonderful staff. You will always have your water refilled.  The portions is great size. Love going here for a relaxing lunch. If you like Thai this is one of the best in Indy and if your new to Thai this is the place to try!!

Well we come here often. We enjoy the seating and food. We would have rated it a 5 but a few times we have had teouble with the wrong food order and checks being wrong. They fixed the problems immediately and it was fine. We are here now watching Ted 2 and before being seated, there was a incident in the lobby with a previous customer. The manager was trying to apologies for a wine spill on his pants. The manager stated they would be happy to pay for his vleaning bill but that did not satisfy him. The customer had already received free movie tickets for the accident but he was obviously wanting more. His pants were your basic khakis and nothing special but he was still extremely upset. I was impressed how the manager handled the situation and even stated to our server that she handle it well. Accidents happen and when a business is willing to fix the problem that is commendable.  It is always nice to see a business stand behind fixing the problem but not going overboard to satisfy the customer beyond what is deserved.  We will be back!

By far my favorite place to eat!! As soon as you step through the door, you are met with bright colors and a laid back atmosphere.  The food is simply GREAT!  I enjoy Cuban food when in South Florida and this place beats every place in Miami I have been to. The plantains good to perfection,  the black bean soup full of flavor and The Cuban well it was so yummy. We got the Coconut Flan to go and it was beyond great. Great people, great coffee, great food!! Support this local eatery. The only thing I can hope is a bigger space but then again this little Havana is perfect!!

Ok I know this is just a gas station but I felt the need to review my experience there yesterday on 7/14. I was there to purchase a cold Starbucks and a pack of smokes (my vice I know it's bad, trying to quit). Standing line with one person in front of me, another cashier comes over and announces come over here you will be the first in line. He was very animated and loud. Remeber it is early morning. I ask for a pack of Marlboro lights 100s and he grab a pack then proceeded to ask if I would like to donate a 1.00 for some charity.  I say no thank you, and noticed it was the wrong pack of smokes. I asked for the right one and he again acted silly, loud, and crazy. Again this is not what I like in the morning.  I paid cash and again he asked if he could keep the change for charity. At this point I was completely annoyed and just wanted to get out of there. FINE, keep it, even though I already said no thank you, not at this time. After I left I was beyond ticked off, not about giving money to charity but to be felt strong armed to give anything. Charity is a choice, and a gas station early in the morning is NOT the place I want to feel put on the spot to give to ANYTHING. Please tell this dude it is wrong, not professional,  and he makes your customers uncomfortable. I for one will go elsewhere!

We had a family gathering after a funeral at Seasons 52. We appreciated the private dining area. The servers were friendly and helpful. The food was nice and tasty. Enjoyed the music from the piano bar. Not to loud but able to enjoy the music and talk to family. We knew nothing about the food or ambiance but were very pleased. Thank you for making a tough situation a perfec place to relax. We will be back!

I dined here before seated in the bar and just had appetizers and their flatbreads. Those were great choice. We went back and were seated in the main dining room. We ordered the sweet potato fries as a appetizer and I had the Guac Burger, and my boyfriend had the Pulled Pork sandwich. Sweet potato fries were great with a great sauce for dipping. But they lost us when our food arrived. We both ordered rosemary potatoes as a side and we got extremely overdone home fries that were seasoned way to much with salt. Both sandwichs were extremely spicy but flavorless. Server was great, we did not complain, we ate much as we could and wrapped it up. We may try this place again but I'm not craving this place!! I'll stick to the flatbreads

Great place for breakfast. I have not tried it for lunch. Good food, great coffee. Nothing bad to say about the place. We enjoy going early on the weekends,as it can be quite crowded but that only shows that it is worth checking out. Decent price for the amount of food you get. We will be back.
Best gyros in Indy. Little hole in the wall joint but true greek food. Love the owner and his family. They make quality food.

Not that impressed. Decent food I could get cheaper, better elsewhere. It hasn't been open long and the place is falling apart. Table wobbles, toilet splashed water at me as it blew from the wall. Service was not great, or good since there was only about 5 to 6 other tables. I will not be back. For a celebrity chef he should visit his establishment.

I had high expectations for this place but the dry, cold and flavorless biscuit truly showed me no love. I ordered the East Nasty and coffee.

My food arrived before my coffee, which this was a weekday morning not a huge rush and lots of employees so not sure what happened there.

The biscuit was cold and flavorless. Dry and would just crumble. For all the hype I was expecting something amazing. The fried chicken was good. 

I'll stick to Pillsbury for biscuits.

Stopped in for breakfast. Great atmosphere and great staff! Food was good, only complaint, if you order pancakes or in the need of syrup start trying to pour it as soon as you sit down! Cool looking bottles that do not work! Please for all of us who had to eat their pancakes cold get new syrup dispensers!
Excellent food and service! Was not expecting much from the outside of the building but a great surprise! The bbq salmon was beyond delicious and look forward to going back!

This place is a true hidden gem!! If you are interested in dessert give this place a visit. I am still not sure how to describe the offerings. Shaved deliciousness of flavorful creations! We had the Dulce de Leche and absolutely wonderful. The staff was super friendly and offered us a sample of the Strawberry cheesecake and it was so great!! Low calorie and delicious this place has it all!!

eBawjpoDxDHJHiHg_UrS6w.review_text:
Best Burger in town - and yes - it BEATS Five guys - barely but it does.

The environment was clean.  Service with a smile and I wish I could have had the the shake if I wasn't working on the spare tire.

If you are from out of town - it is worth the drive from Nashville.  Franklin actually has a lot more shopping and places to eat than downtown nowadays.

I've been coming here for a couple of years now.  As I've told many co-workers - Wolfgang's is the best bang for the buck in the entire Franklin/Brentwood area.  Spend 5 more bucks than you would at a fast food place and less than Friday's and the other chain crap.

The 4 Cheese mac and the BBQ chicken quesadilla is what I most often have.

Had a bad experience at the Calypso over near 100 Oaks years ago and I swore this place off for a long time.

I've been back at the healthy side of things and this is one of the better options in Cool Springs nowadays.  I was surprised to enjoy a great chicken breast/sweet potato combo for lunch.  It was filling, did not taste like "foofoo" food as a I call it and the staff was a little hipsterish they were pretty cool and helpful.  No complaints.

One of my regular spots in Cool Springs nowadays.

It isn't just a salad place but they really do have quality ingredients for any salad that you would like.

Tip:  Try the Chef Salad, replace the turkey with chicken and add the honey mustard sauce that they keep hidden.  They'll know what you are talking about when you are in there.  I hit this place probably 2-3 times a week now and I've almost thought about getting them to prepackage me a few salads at a time so I can keep them at home for whenever my hungry desires.

One more note:  This place builds the closest authentic Italian caprese sandwich on this side of the hemisphere.

I like to try to keep my ratings simple.

Best sushi in Franklin and close to the top in Nashville.  Very very fresh foods and I've brought people who have remarked it is the best calamari they've ever had.

Oh Genghis - how I love thee.  I run into here once every few weeks with friends for lunch.

I don't know how it would ever be possible to have more than one bowl and if you learn your stacking techniques, you can have a BIG filling and then some.

The service is stellar, the food is usually fresh and they make an effort to keep the area very clean.  It doesn't hurt that management is intentional in hiring pretty good looking young females to work there.

The one less star mark comes because I hate the rush time in there and it will take a long as a sit down place when its packed to the brim and the waits don't help either.

Sorry guys - I did not like this place at all.  I enjoy good chicken and was willing to try this out.

The place is DILAPIDATED and overall kind of nasty.  If you only like eating at prim places, this place is not for you. 

I guess a forewarning is, I don't mind spicy but - this was just too much and it wasn't about it being hot.

The chicken tasted like cardboard that had spicy seasoning on it.  It was so over-fried that you had to crack off the skin to even try to get to any meat, which apparently, there wasn't that much.

The parking sucks and it was not a very inviting atmosphere.  I guess there might be some people that thinks there is some allure for it being in the area it is in but not for me.

You would think that a place so popular on review sites would make an effort to make their place more appealing.
For St Louis and considering this is South American - I'm gonna give it a 5.  Enjoyed it - used the Yelp check-in for a yummy Sangeria and the Avacado salad was awesome.

Been wanting to write a review for this place for awhile since I went over a year ago.  In short, it is way too gimmicky with their food and while it is novel to get "southern" gourmet food, it is in fact, not at all gourmet in taste.  

The environment and the actual location is the only redeeming factor for this place.  The service wasn't bad but - I'm more of a food vs environment type of person but it was such a disappointment for my girlfriend's birthday dinner.  To think I had to actually wait to try to get reservations for this place make it worthy of the 1-star.

Had the shrimp and grits, meh.

Pimento cheese and wafers, meh.

Bone marrow, meh.

I can't even remember the dessert.

If you are reading this and waiting in line, please be patient.  Even after a 1.5 hour wait, I have to say that it exceeded my expectations for brunch today.

I, myself, had the Cinna-French Toast and while it did come out looking like dessert and something you shouldn't eat for your main during breakfast, I didn't care, it was great.  They also know how to serve the proper syrup which means it wasn't the processed stuff that everyone else overlooks.  Kudos for that

The side turkey sausage was spectacular and for me, I love mixing my sausage with my syrup and it was just yummy!

The service was great, they made sure to come out to reassure us a few times while we were waiting and let us know what may not be available just in case since we did the brunch a little later in the day.

For a Nashville Brunch - this place was great and it isn't the same thing as all of these exposed duct-work, reclaimed wood edison light charging too much for the experience because it looks cool and they spent way too much money in trying to create that atmosphere.

This place cooks with love and it shows.

Overall, I can't complain about the place.  The food hummus was good as well as the boneless chicken wings.  I can't give it an AMAZING review but I was satisfied.  

Be aware, the boneless wings ARE BIG - I accidentally ordered 10 of them and felt like a glutton.  

Clean store, the drink options were lacking.

As a halfie-Venezuelano, I always make it a mission to try out any Venezuelan places that I find in my travels.

That led me to Are Pitas.  I was completely satisfied and then some by their Venezuelan arepa and it went past and above the standard arepas I've had before.  It was delicious.  I had to get myself another one with the turkey/gouda and that too, was soon devoured. 

The mango juice was on spot and if I had not been working, I would have likely gotten a bottle of Polar for old time sakes.

The staff was professional and nice and I while I'm only in Tampa for work for a few more days, this place may have earned one of my coveted revisits.

Proud burger enthusiastist and travel around the world eating burgers so I may have a slight obsession.  

With that being said, I have had issues with most of the burger places in Franklin failing at a few core things like the bun or beef used, etc.,. 

This is the most complete and best burger in Nashville if not considering simple fare burgers (Gabby's gets that title).

This place isn't about the ambience or any hip things, just good beer and a killer burger.

The bun was toasted just perfect, the mix of the beef was on top and everything worked right including the size of the bun to Patty ratio.  Will come again for sure.

Been here a few times already.  They keep things simple and consistent.  Just appreciate that.

Everything on the menu has great taste and is accurate to what you are expecting.

Service is fast, no complaints about any of that.

#Protrips Local Edition: Micheal Mina's Bourbon Steak

Steak - Wagyu style Austrian Filet

Cut and quality: 9/10
Cook: 9.5/10

Foie Gras Donut: 7/10 - the beignets were an odd pairing, the actual foie was cooked perfectly and no problems with it but just an off mix. It went better by itself with the steak vs the style the did.

Fries: A nice on the house start, fries themselves were not anything special but done right, the house made sauces made it. 8.5/10

Rebel Old Fashion: 9.5/10 - Best old fashion in Nashville I've had.

Service: 8/10 - I didn't sit at a table but just went to an open seating and it took me about 5 minutes to get my order in. Otherwise, service was steller.

Overall, it's a tie with Kayne Prime. I do think the location, design and overall restaurant is prettier, better setup and more fashionable where Kayne is a little more cold, it wins for that. For a pure steakhouse and cuts of meat per the menu, Kayne wins.

Cost of an app, drink and steak: 120 on the dot.

Overall I enjoy this restaurant for a late lunch.

The decor, layout and styling of the restaurant was great.  Nothing about the seating arrangements were awkward and most seating spaces will be comfortable in here.

There wasn't a wait for a 2:00 lunch on Friday so that was nice.  The hostess was attentive and let us choose since it was low occupancy.

The server Garrett was excellent throughout the service and had a great attitude and was friendly.  

Now for the food - I tried the gumbo and the chicken fingers.  Both fairly simple dishes but I'll give credit that I felt like the spicing was excellent for the gumbo and tasted more upscale versus a traditional NOLA style and the ingredients tasted better.

The chicken fingers were on point.  Again, another simple dish but easy to mess up.  The portions were more than enough and it had the perfect mix of crispy and moisture.  I think the honey mustard was the star and the fries were overall of a good quality.

Would visit again and try out dinner to see how they do.

I think for Nashville, the burger is legit.  The container type of architecture is cool and no complaints on the service.

More on the burger?

Bread was spot on, I thought maybe it could have had a little more edge on the Patty because it was not an easy burger to manage and sloppy. The kick was nice but could be a little much for others. The meat, bread, sauces and everything was spot on but how easy it is to eat a burger also weighs in my rankings.  The fries were a no-go, some others may like the waffle style but meh.  Nothing special on the  ketchup side, little things like that help.

Service was excellent and prompt.

If return for lunch, not dinner.

Poke for Dinner?  That's how I roll... or don't roll...get it?!? :eyeroll: I know

Well, at least while doing keto anyways.  Franklin has not been all that great for Poke or it has been pretty much non-existent so I found this just doing the YTG (Yelp-Tripadvisor-Google) trifecta search and didn't see anything that was bad and it's new so I figured why not?

The store is clean and organized with character and actually less sterile feeling than a lot of other poke places I've ran into across the US.  I give credit for that, someone put detail into how the layout was.  It fits the area as well.  With that being said, most people like to think the prim of Cool Springs area is the only place to eat.  Don't neglect the folks off 96 - they got good stuff out there including Ice Point.  With the amount of traffic in Cool Springs during lunch, you'll probably get out in less time from this part of town.

Off the rant - how was the food?  Everything was great quality, the ordering process was smooth and I like their POS system which helps for a speedy transaction.  They had my keto option which was just mixed greens as a base then the fish on top.  Great options for all of the base/protein/sauces and the options with crab meat and avocado.

I enjoyed it!  Yea, 5 is strong but considering being the first in the area, the store layout, the overall price and impression.  They deserve it!

tl:dr - This is the first time I'd ever think of putting any restaurant in the Southeastern USA in this high of a regard to it's service quality. This place is special and would skip reservations to the Catbird Seat everytime to visit here. I got around 140+ Michelin stars under my belt and dining in over 97 different countries so hear me out. 

What is this place? Is this Nashville? Is this real life?

Did I just experience my first true Michelin level dining experience in Nashville, TN? Food at the 1* and the service of a 2*? 

An 8 course tasting menu by a James Beard awarded Chef husband and wife combination and paired by a true sommelier. All for what would be considered a value (Per my former NYC resident date).

I can't say enough about how much of a pleasant surprise it was for us to visit tonight on a random Tuesday. This wasn't planned and I had a friend text me about it two months ago before they opened.

I imagine most people can guess and understand what I mean when I reference 1* for food, it's just a cut above the rest and something worth visiting if you live in the city. 

2* service is something that is rare. I'll try to explain the small details I've learned over my 100+'s and years 

Attentiveness - predicting/watching and knowing when you are done with your course and taking the plates away under 30 seconds. Keeping the table cleaned between each course. On the money.

Cutlery - Each course had specific utensils with each course and not a single one had so much of a blemish of use. One course had a butter knife style but with a depression that made sense for that course. It was also a beautiful brass/copper color that matched throughout all courses.

Plating - every single piece of ceramic appeared as handmade with all of it fitting each course in a purposeful and display-like manner. The pasta dish even had a special spot to twirl. This is next level.

The service from the opening of the door to the Joseph Hotel to Sommelier making a pairing that would ensure me safely driving home while getting to show off his skills while saving me some money. Being able to prepay with a set service charge is something I'm personally in love with.

A lot of times I feel that we try to review one time places that we visit and there are places we visit regularly that don't get love.

I figured I'd give some love back to this Starbucks as I've been coming here on the regular since I moved to Buchanan Arts District.

I almost always order via the mobile and I can't say that I have ever had a problem with the speed it comes out.  I have less than a 5 minute drive and it's been rare that I've encountered having to wait for either a food or beverage item.

Throughout the recent snowstorms, they were on the money and I totally appreciated the store and staff and being able to make it in despite the conditions outside.

Tried this place after hearing some buzz last night and wanted to really see what the deal was about.  For me, the food was a 5 but to be honest, while I think most everyone will love the interior of the place I felt like it was a little trying too hard.  I get it, maybe I'm older and not as cool but that's how I feel.

Having been to every country represented I can say that all the dishes we tried that night were actually pretty authentic tasting.

Summer Rolls - a pretty simple dish, hard to mess up but good.

Golden Wontons - Much more meat than I had expected, good.

Po Po Lo's Curry - This was a star of the menu and one of the things that makes me realize I really liked a dish is when I sit there trying to eat every single piece of rice and notice with disappointment when it's gone.

Service was good but the place was loud.  As far as COVID - my date is more aware than I need to be (Vaccinated/recovered) but she felt safe in there and felt like they were taking proper precautions.  There were still a lot of people so I'd recommend trying to go in at a slower time if you are trying to be careful.

This is my second visit here and I don't have much to complain about except the parking situation being a little annoying although parking at the bank after hours seems like the best thing to do if you don't like valet parking.

The interior of the place is well designed and I am impressed by most of the layout in there and you definitely feel like it's a high level place.

That's where I'm only going with a 4 - for a steakhouse, I can't say that the cuts I had were anything that blew my mind but everything was cooked to perfection and the menu was excellent as well as the choices.

In the two visits, the service did feel more than less than experienced.  The FOH service was great but the servers felt a little careless or inexperienced, no fault to their own but I've found that there are places that people want to work at and take pride in and others where people are just trying to find a job while going to college.

The one star example I can talk about are the scallops, between Etch and E3, it's a hard pick to say which dish holds the title to the best in Nashville but for purist, I think Etch wins but for the daring, E3 with the extras like that delicious cream is out of this world and I intentionally ordered it a second time.

The more I think of it - the seafood has been better than the steak here and they do the seafood portion better than most any "seafood" spots in Nashville and I give them a big thumbs up on that.

eDtBMIh3RTxtqViJDcIjag.review_text: We were disappointed in our experience at Giovanni 's. It is a lovely space.  And the wait staff was attentive  The food,however, was not what it should have been at this price range. For appetizer we had cannelloni and a shrimp in a tomato sauce. The cannelloni was barely warm and the shrimp while tasty was a bit over cooked and tough. The house salad was overdressed. We each had different entrees. The veal dishes were just Ok. Likewise the salmon and swordfish were just ok. We were hoping for and paying for  better than we received. We went a night after a snow and the valet was "unavailable "  So their chance to make a good first impression was missed.

The staff was friendly and efficient. It was wonderful sitting outside at the communal picnic tables enjoying the day. The food however was disappointing. Ribs were VERY fatty. Could see people at other tables  with meatier ribs meaning that consistency was lacking! Brisket was just average and also fatty. Beans were tasty as was the potato salad but the fire and ice pickles deserved to be a garnish not worthy of being a side dish.

Used to love their knishes. Brought one home today to find they had changed the recipe. Added rice to the beef filling. Felt like they got their fillings confused...tasted like it should have been in stuffed cabbage! Corned beef was not up to par and sliced too thick. Very disappointing trip to the deli.

Side dishes may be creative but really should be edible. Potato salad had no flavor  and green beans were so peppery we couldn't eat them! Slaw was really just fair and served in so much liquid that it was not pleasant. Very disappointing meal !!!

VERY disappointing. Two employees who were working were not up to the task. Although they were trying. Service was slow! Bill was incorrect. The gyro meat was good...the only redeeming feature. Pita was mediocre, falafel balls over cooked, lettuce was browning, fries were tasteless. Trash can was overflowing and we got to clean our table before we sat down. If the owner wants return customers (at dinner)  he may want to be on site or staff the restaurant appropriately.
Crepes were as tasty as crepes in Paris. Technique of crepe makers was not as refined or fascinating to watch as we had seen on our trip. Nice variety and well worth more visits!

Have always liked Lester's and have eaten there and carried out bulk orders many times.  Called yesterday and sat on hold for over 11 minutes. Called on another line and was put on hold for a couple of minutes, again! (Even after telling the manager I had been waiting so long) When he finally came on the line I gave him our order with a pick up time. Guess what? Order not ready at requested time. 
They are either currently staffed inappropriately or staff training has gone way down hill!! Very disappointing!!!

For the second visit in a row...we had another WONDERFUL meal.  Our server, Tom, was helpful, attentive and just plain old nice.  From start to finish food was great. Loved the assorted antipasti plate.  The wine recommended with my entree, a valpolicello, was very nice. Both the fusilli with four cheeses and the veal tortellini were delicious. We finished the meal enjoying the limoncello torte. It was a perfect meal.

We usually like Sugo's but tonight we had a really exceptional meal. We started with the cheese and olive appetizer. Nice selection of olives and blue cheese was really tasty tonight! A house salad was followed by a nightly special, linguine with lobster broth, shrimp, olive oil, basil and a little cheese.  It was really good!!! With the addition of house red wine and tiramisu it was a wonderful  dinner.

Terrible experience of a night out for pizza!! First visit was marginal but we thought we'd give it another try after they had time to work out the kinks!! They haven't and the way it seemed they might never get there. Many tables were dirty. Trash can was overflowing. After making our pizzas we were informed the charge machine was down. That should have been relayed BEFORE we ordered. Ok-we had enough cash. After waiting longer than we should of considering the amount of the business they had, we went to the counter where our pizzas had been sitting!!! They were too disorganized to have brought hot pizza to our table as promised. Instead we carried our own barely lukewarm pizzas back to the table.  Would have asked for them to be remade but they were out of red sauce after making our second pizza. They either need to get their act together or Pieology won't be in the neighborhood for long!!!!!

Loved, loved, loved our meal and experience!! Salads-great! The salmon my husband said was one of the best he'd ever eaten. They made eggplant parmesan off the menu for me and it was wonderful. Black Forest cake for dessert was to die for!! The ambiance made all the worries of the day fade away and the waiters were excellent.

Soooo disappointing.  Arrived requesting a table for six people.  We were told 10-15 minute wait.  After 30 minutes we asked how much longer and were told they really couldn't say.  If a restaurant with so much history isn't able to give honest guesstimates I don't know why ANYONE would choose to stay there.  I know we will never put our name on the wait list again!!!!

So disappointed!!! I RARELY go to Starbucks.  Went yesterday to a different location and tried an iced caramel macchiato and it was delicious! Came to this location and it is a totally different experience.  Drink is bitter with very little caramel flavor and an expensive letdown.  Last purchase at Starbucks for a long while.  Way too inconsistent taste, quality and value.

We just had possibly the worst restaurant experience of the  last 5-10 years!!! Terrible service. Slow!!!! Mediocre-at best- food.  Waited a long time to get barely warm, runny spinach artichoke dip that arrived with semi-stale chips. And after a truly inexcusable wait the two children's meals arrived. But our wait wasn't over.  The other food took longer.  Cole slaw had chunks of pineapple in it.  It was not what was expected.  Patty melt was tasteless served with a not pleasant sauce.  Everyone did enjoy the French fries but that is certainly not enough to ever try this place again!!

Hadn't been to frank & Helen's for a long time.  Did curbside pickup.  Woman who took order was professional and had a nice voice. The broasted chicken dinners were great!!! The kids' chicken tenders were devoured. The house salad dressing was quite tasty. The only improvement could have been the salad.  There were two pieces of core in my salad and a bit more care with salad would have made the meal perfect.  
We'll be back!!!
