This restaurant seems to be inconsistent.  Friday evening was crowded, the waitresses were busy.  Our order didn't come out as we ordered.  My husband ordered a chicken quesadilla, but the waitress wrote it as chicken burrito.  I ordered 1 cheese enchilada with rice and beans.  A waitress brought a chicken burrito to my husband, and he explained he didn't order that.  The waitress had 2 plates which I assumed one could have been mine.  She took both back to the kitchen.  When our order was brought out the second time - my plate (even though waitress used a hot pad) was cool to the touch.  (Very unusual for a Mexican plate).   The cheese inside the enchilada was hard because I'm sure it sat in the kitchen until they made my husband's quesadilla.  I was able to eat the rice, but could not eat the cold enchilada or the beans that had cold cheese on them.  I'll think twice before we return.

Our lack of service was noted by all at our table (there were 5 of us).  Apparently no one knew who was to be waiting our table.  Finally the host came up and said the waitress was busy so he was going to take our drink order.  After a substantial wait, a waitress did arrive.  I ordered the house salad with dressing on side.  Salad arrived with dressing already on salad.  The unlimited honey wheat bread became limited.  Coffee was served, but a portion of the pour ended up on the table.  The waitress had to be called back to clean up the spill.  The service wasn't good.  Felt as though she was pre-occupied with another table.  I ordered a loaded baked potato.  The potato was very dry after eating the  top stuff.  No extra butter was provided.  Although we were celebrating our 50th anniversary we talked about dessert, but since none was offered we decided to go to McDonalds.  Might add service at McDonalds was great.  Certainly can't say that I'd recommend this establishment to any of my friends.  I, too, will not returning.

My husband and I went for lunch at Olive Garden.  That was a mistake.  Our waitress had the personality of a rock.  I doubt that she makes any tips. We had soup - and she couldn't tell the difference between Minestrone or Vegetable. Our "endless breadsticks" arrived after our entre.  Our waitress claimed that the breadsticks were in the oven.  The lack of service made our lunch unpleasant. I'm sure there are plenty of other restaurants in the area that offer good service and friendly waitresses - not at this Olive Garden.

Hard to believe that the Safeway Store on Duval Mine Road can charge more than a store in Tucson.  Not only are Green Valley residents paying more for their gas, but now we find out that groceries are cheaper in Tucson.  A recent ad showed that the ads were the same, but the prices were higher in Green Valley than in Tucson for the same product.  I bet that Safeway wouldn't honor the Tucson price here in Green Valley.  Stop shopping at Safeway - go to Frys or Walmart - but stay away from Safeway unless you like being higher prices.
The coffee was good.  The music was too loud, and certainly not my taste.  Employees who weren't working  were hanging out in the small seating area.  Seating was at a premium the day I was there.

Bravo - Great Job - Wonderful ........

This restaurant spent Easter morning passing out to go "Free Breakfasts".  

What a wonderful thing to do during these troubled times.

TStopped in for a quick lunch today.  There was a large sign stating that the soda machine was out of order.  However, the cashier told me that the Pepsi machine was working.  I ordered the drink and received the cup.  Their ice machine wasn't working so they had to put ice into the cup at the cashier place.  We headed for our seat, and walked over to get the Pepsi that the cashier said was working.  It was not.  I took my receipt back to the cashier and told her that the machine was not working, so I wanted a refund on the drink.  She said "well let me go and check".  Apparently she didn't trust me.  She came back and said, "no, it's not working."   Well, duh.....I told you that.  Then my husband went into the bathroom and he came back and said that the urinal was out of service.  Seems as though Panera is letting the places go - don't know if they are having a hard time or not - but if other things don't work - and they aren't taken care of no one will stop in the restaurant. Very disappointing.

fr7ac23SbYpBNl-Z-nyv3Q.review_text: What a  cool place (really the. A/C is great on a hot day like today) OK besides being a nice temperature, this building is way cool ! Walking in is a real surprise as from the outside it looks like an old original style downtown building.  When you open those front doors though its like being in a high end Scottsdale bar! It's both old and new and the combination really works, I love this design! Anyway, the place is really well done. I had the chicken Parm sandwich and my wife had the margarita pizza. We were both happy with our lunch and the service, it's nice to have a different cool place to go in downtown, I'll be back soon, as I want to try one of the other pizzas (that by the way they make in plain view of the dining area) you should check this place out, exactly what Tucson needs to help energize the downtown area!

Wow, what a friendly and delicious local Tucson treat! I have been eating lunch at Chacos for at least the last 6 years and have never had a lunch I didnt enjoy. Being a Tucson native Im partial to good Mexican food and I will say this rates at the top ! I have tried most everything over the years and am partial to the Carnitas (on Friday) and the Carne Asada tacos (anyday). The Machaca is another winner, really I love it all. You wont find a nicer family run place for a fast and resonably price meal. If you want the glitz, glitter and expensive decorating, you wont find it. If you want to be greeted by a friendly owner who will take good care of you and totally satisfy your craving for good Mexican food, get over there ASAP !

Great locally owned Barber Shop ! Owner (Dale) and crew have been making people look good (believe me, I need all the help I can get) for over 40 years in Tucson. This new location on Speedway is modern and convenient and the staff are all really friendly! Over the years I have sent many friends in to see Dale and his staff and have always had positive feedback on their experiences too! If you are looking for a good place to relax and have a professional give you a nice hair cut, take a look at El Continental!

Ok I have been here a few times as I really love BBQ and I love to see local folks do well but Im afraid they (the owners) need to pay more attention to whats going on in here. Each time Ive been here its just been 'ok'. On this recent visit the food was not hot, I cant give an honest review on the taste as I was unhappy about the eating a luke warm dinner. The corn on the cob tasted like it had been sitting there for a couple days, when i took it back to complain they said 'no problem' and just threw it in the trash. How about 'gee im sorry, that shouldnt have happened' (not much concern that the rest of the corn sitting there may have been exactly the same) They did offer another side to replace it. I may go back and try it again someday but if they dont get it together next time, they will never see my bbq stained t shirt in their door again.

Im sorry to say these guys have closed the location at Stone and River. I did go back several times after my first review and I must say they had gotten it together and really improved the customer experience so I raised my rating to 4 stars, The food was really improved too. I guess I will visit their other location on the Southside for my bbq fix now.

I'm late doing this, I'm trying fulfill my New Years res. for giving credit where credit is due. I love this place! great food and fair prices, I've taken my parents out to dinner here several times and have never left unhappy. Nice people, clean and nicely decorated with modern colors and original artwork. I know they have been under construction for a remodel for the past week or two so I cant wait to get back for dinner to check it out. ps. I have eaten lunch there and been able to get in and out and back to work without the boss yelling at me. Maybe Ill take my boss with me next time....on second thought, nahhh

Ive seen some negative reviews on this location but I eat in here maybe once a month and I actually don't hate it. Tonight it was 1/4 chicken white with mashed potatoes and garlic spinach, my wife had the same with the mixed veggies. The food was good, tasted fresh, we liked the veggies too. The people were friendly, maybe a tad pushy with the add on's but not obnoxious. Id say for a fast food chicken place its pretty good and for $7.00 pretty reasonable. Ill go back.

I've always enjoyed going to Rosas, they have fast service, have a good variety of the usual favorites and deliver a  nice meal for a fair price, what else do you want ? I usually get a  combo meal  because I'm lazy and it gives me a little variety of the food I've eaten in Tucson for the last 50 years (yes I'm old as dirt). We showed up tonight with a group of 7 got right in, ripped through the chips and salsa, had a couple of tasty orders of guacamole and then enjoyed our meals. Ill go back whenever I'm in the mood for my Mexican fix.

Hey I usually rave about these guys, boy this week was the exception. I ordered 2 slabs of BBack ribs, baked potatoes and creamy cole slaw. The coleslaw was tasty, the potatoes were cooked nicely and lathered up with butter and seasoning (I know, I know, the little Mrs. already yelled at me) but the ribs were not good. They were not cooked all the way and were really chewy. I forced down 2 ribs thinking they had to get better but then gave up. I should have called and let them know but i think I was there on an 'off' day so ill give them a pass. I will go back as normally I really enjoy their BBQ, I probably wont order the ribs though.

This is a fun little local bar ! Friendly people drinking in and working here. I must say I've never thought I had too many weird or  perverted tendencies but there is a mannequin in here that is absolutely stunning...as mannequins go that is. I know i sound like a freak, sorry maybe i am and need to get some help, but go in there and get a beer, wander into the back room and check her out. There are a couple of these plastic Angels in the bar but there is one in particular that will get your attention, If im lying im buying! Feel free to get your picture taken next to her..actually I noticed some flash burns from all the photos She has been exposed to. Exposed...good choice of words, ouch! the little Mrs. just smacked me with a ping pong paddle.  I like this place  and will be back when im in that neighborhood and need a cool brewski !

Sorry to do a 2 star review here as this was one of my favorite places years ago. I have been a couple of times in the last few months and its just not the way it used to be. 
We were there for dinner a week ago, 5 of us, we got seated pretty quickly then we were just sat and waited. The server was really busy, I'm assuming they were understaffed that night. She was friendly when she got to us but honestly it was a little annoying as we were hungry and didn't want to be there too late.
 
It was a pretty good wait  to get our food, my sons plate came out even a few minutes after the rest of us had ours. We could have still been been fine here as we were not looking for things to pick on, hey i know we don't live in a perfect world but  once we started eating nobody's food was hot. I'm pretty sure it had been sitting for a while waiting for the server to grab it.

Btw, the Mariachis were pretty good at first. The music was not overbearing, they were not too close and they did sound good! The girl with the fiddle was a real treat!
Then they got closer and louder and you know the deal, no more talking as you cant hear unless you shout, oh well.

Sorry i forgot to specify this, it was the Oracle rd. location.

Update: I was back in this location a few months ago as it is convenient for me and as I mentioned in my previous review the La Parilla locations were always at the top of my list for a tasty dinner . The staff was friendly, we got seated and waited on quickly, the food however was disappointing. I really hate to slam the place again but I really think the owners should spend time trying to figure out whats going on here. There is fantastic Mexican food in Tucson as we all know and these guys should be as good as anyone else, especially given the amount of years they have been around.

Wow what a nice find ! Driving by it didn't look like much but do yourself a favor and don't judge the book by the cover! I've eaten here at least 6 times in the last few months and have never been disappointed. Maybe a different lunch menu would be nice? Try them out, you'll be a fan too!

Wow, I have had no less than 6 great meals from this Dickeys ! I love the brisket, and the pulled pork but really i haven't had anything that i didn't  enjoy. The staff has always been friendly and efficient.  i have done take out as well as eaten in, its been a great experience each time. I usually don't have left overs because im known to eat everything on my plate and usually my wife's but saving a little brisket for the next mornings eggs is hard to beat too! Give them a try when you are craving for some nice BBQ !

Great People, experts at hair styling, will take care of the whole family with one stop! Check these guys out they will impress you with the quality of their work and the friendly atmosphere they do it in !

I have been a fan in the past and have always enjoyed my meals here, hey what can I say, I like to eat ! I feel the quality of food and service has gone down lately. The last 3 visits have not been amazing relating to service and food. I'm sure Ill go back again as Mrs M woofs down the salmon like it was her last meal but for me just so so. Maybe because of their popularity now they are overwhelmed ? I hope it gets better, Ill report back.

Had a nice lunch here the other day, the place is happy and clean, food was pretty good we all had something different and everyone was satisfied with their meal. The buffet looked pretty good too, not fancy but well stocked with your usual favorites. I saw several rather large folks squeezing their way through the door that leads to the buffet area. I think the folks I saw were on their second or third trip to the buffet,(all you can eat) they looked happy as they were all smiling, so either the buffet was good or maybe they had just stuffed a few tamales down their pants for later? Either way, I would say give them a try, they have a nice staff and fair prices too.

I do like this restaurant, I've had several dinners here. I really like the building & design a really nice Southwestern feel with great western decorations. Always a friendly staff, the food is pretty good too.  last time we were in they sat us in between 2 crowded tables, it can be a little tight in there so we decided not to be part of the other patrons conversations and we asked to be moved outside which was much better. I had the New York strip which was tender, not cooked perfectly but I woofed it down. The misses had the salmon, she enjoyed it too! The patio has heaters, so on a cool evening you are quite comfortable. If you are young and energetic you might be able to 'dine and dash' through the oleanders to your get away car on the other side...I don't know why I said that, sorry folks I'm just nutty like that. I would never do that as I'm too old to make a run for it and I would surely be caught. Anyway please pay your server before you dash as I'm sure they prefer it that way and give Hifalutin a try!

Ok I've been here enough times over the last few years to write a review, i should have done this sooner but I have put it off as I hoped it would get better. I remember the original Sams on  29th st that is long gone now but 'in the day' had the best pastrami sandwich in town, in fact you might have called it 'Famous'. 
This week we were in for lunch and the first thing i noticed was when i sat down in a booth.. well, lets say I would sit down very gently or you will need to visit the nearby Asian massage parlor to work out the kink you just put in your backside. Hey guys Fix the Booths they are terrible! The server was efficient and friendly, She has been there for at least the last few years we have been going in. The food was so so, my pastrami was an improvement over the last one I had there, a little too greasy but good flavor, it was actually ok. My buddy had a salad that was a little rough, maybe not their strong point. another buddy got a pickle with his food that looked like it had been munched on by someone else or possibly the roving vendor trying to sell his wares while we were dining. I wish the owner would take a serious look at trying to improve this location. I'm not sure how business is here overall, maybe its OK as they don't have much competition in the area but this could be a much better experience.

Nice place, not crowded, comfortable seating, nice outdoor space with great view. I've been here 4 or 5 times and i have not been disappointed. They have fresh warm tortillas as free appetizers that are really tasty. Cold beer, nice food selection, I usually get the enchilada casserole (that's not what they call it) but that's what i call it and they always know what i'm talking about. The beans are really good, blended with cheese and other good stuff ! The little misses usually goes for the Salmon which she loves and gets every time. Hey give them a try!

0k I know this is a chain and you don't expect the same quality as many of our local Tucson favorites but I must say we had a good lunch in here a couple of weeks ago and a really good overall experience! There were 4 of us, each of us had something different, pls don't ask me what everyone ate, I can't even remember what I ate...but i'm kind of old and have a mind like concrete  'all mixed up and permanently set' can you relate? Anyway here is what I do remember: When I was finished with my salad I put the bowl on the ledge behind me, I know that's not polite, I have poor manners too. My table was crowded as 2 of my buddies are rather large in stature..ok they are fat, anyway room at the table was snug so I did what I did with the salad bowl. 
Shortly there after, a waiter (not ours) strolled by, saw my bowl that was virtually licked clean, ok there were a few little scraps of lettuce about the size of a quarter left in it. He scooped it up to get rid of it and asked me in passing "did I want a to go box for my salad?"  Ok I know he was being a smart a_ _ as he saw how I had cleaned that bowl out but I like a smart a_ _ cuz I am one. So I played along and said "Yes box it up for me." Ok I laughed a little and kept on enjoying my lunch and a few minutes later here comes the smart a_ _ guy with a tiny plastic cup about the size of the Lucky Wishbone secret sauce that comes with their steak fingers. It had a tiny plastic lid on it and inside was my 2 little scraps of lettuce and a tiny piece of carrot that must have been hiding under the lettuce. This is stupid I know and I apologize to you folks who were hoping for an expert detailed review like most of my others. Long story longer, I'm still chuckling about this and I will go back and hope for more good food and a waiter with a good sense of humor. Try them out, its worth a bite and maybe a laugh!

Update: I went back yesterday and as soon as a saw the menu I remembered what I had last time. (and I had it again) They have a bargain combo deal for this Buffalo chicken wrap, baked potato and a big side salad.so I took the pic this time.

I've been here no less than 5 times for lunch since they opened this location. I've eaten the chicken salad sandwich, the rhino wrap, had several different breakfasts (for lunch) I really like everything I've had but the D's potato cake and huevos rancheros is really hard to beat. Try these guys out, nice menu, not too big, fair prices, tasty food. What else do you want ?

I say go for the ice cream, its good, the people are friendly enough, hey its an Ice Cream place and who doesn't love ice cream. My gripe is really on the food. I've been a couple of different times and the food has always been just so so. I could go into more detail but my opinion is they put way more effort into the ice cream than the food which is fair enough. Ill still keep taking my grandson in for ice cream on those special occasions but from now on Ill eat ahead of time.

Wow, how can you not love this place! I've had many lunch's and a few dinners here and have never been disappointed. I usually do the 'chefs pick' and let her serve me whatever she desires and the darn food is just flat outstanding every time. If you have not treated yourself to Cafe Poca Cosa, get there quick , definitely one of Tucson's treasures!

Ok since living in Tucson pretty much forever, I can tell you I have eaten at the Hoagie House locations on many, many occasions. My 'go to' sandwich is the Carmichael, i have tried a few others but I love the Carmichael! I really think this is one of the best sandwich's in town. The place, well lets say if you are expecting a 5 star dining experience with great decorating comfy furniture and a fully uniformed staff you may be in for a shock. These are older not so perfect buildings and decor (lets just call it kinda of dumpy) but during my last visit to the Oracle location last week, I was greeted by two friendly ladies who took my order, collected my money and made me a great sandwich. What else do you really need? Give them a try, they are one of the few remaining long running Tucson treasures for a great sub.

Boy I like this place, nice people, delicious food and when i'm in trouble with Mrs. M,  I can stop by and pick up a tasty dinner to take home and cook. I'm kind of a basic sort of guy, not too smart, not much of a cook (Mrs. M says that's why I got married) anyway I look a little better to her after I heat up that nice pasta dinner i bring home from Roma. Yes I can use the micro wave. Anyway try these guys out, maybe you'll look better to your other 1/2 if you come home with a nice dinner!

Hey we went to Opa for dinner last night, I've been here on a few other occasions and have always enjoyed my food. Last night i had the # 61, traditional Gyro platter with the beef and lamb and the greek salad, it was delicious! The meat was super tender, honestly it was probably as good as I've ever had.

Mrs. M had the salmon special platter, also with a salad and she really enjoyed it as well. In fact she liked it so much she kept bugging me to try it. I'm not a big fish fan, sorry honey you eat it. Well she is pretty hard headed and doesn't like to hear no so now i'm on the bad list for Santa again.

The waitress gave us a heck of a fire show too. As she delivered another patrons meal she lit it up like a booni bon fire! I saw the flames shoot up near the ceiling and I was glad i didn't have to test my fire extinguishing skills with outdoor garden hose, I guess she has done this a few times before and knows what she is doing, just a little alarming when i'm not sure my toupee is fire resistant. Nothing worse than seeing a flaming racoon diving for the water pitcher.  

 Anyway the staff is very friendly and the prices seem pretty normal so next time you have an urge for Greek and a fire show, give them a try!

We ate lunch here a month ago or so as one of my compadres knew about the place. When we arrived of course I recognized the building as one of the original Lucky Wishbones in Tucson. Brought back many greasy memories of garlic toast coated with butter using a paintbrush. If you've been around for a while you know what I mean. Anyway forget the left over memories and heavy artery residue that I will no doubt take to the grave with me as I want to tell you about Holy Smokin Butts!

Plain and simple, go in there and get some of this BBQ! We had brisket, pulled pork and ribs and it was all delicious! Big portions and cooked like BBQ should be. The folks were friendly, and the food came fast. The ambiance..well lets say you are not going to be overly impressed, but the food makes up for it period.Try it if you are a BBQ fan!

I've been going here on and off for Whiskey Wednesdays with a few knucklehead buddies for years. Ok, honestly Mrs M. would not be happy if she read this as i'm not sure I always told her where I was and for some reason she thinks Ill get into trouble if she is not there to corral me..imagine that. Anyway the food has always been good, not a huge menu but a nice happy hour selection, I've eaten the pork sandwich and burgers more than anything and always have enjoyed them. Boy I'm on a roll with BBQ lately. The fries are always delicious (I really need to quit eating this stuff and turn to health food..nahh) Honestly the thing I really enjoy about Union is a Tullamore Dew on one of their Ice balls. I just love those ice balls, a little whiskey, a splash of ginger beer or ginger ale and I'm a happy camper. Its a little noisy in there in the evening, alot of youngsters, not sure why a crusty old guy like me is there but maybe it makes me feel a little younger..Ill go with that! Check them out and don't forget your balls!

First of all,I like doing business with local Tucson family business whenever I can. Jerry Bobs on Valencia is one of those examples. I eat lunch here at least 2 times per month and I have always had an enjoyable meal. I really like the Mexican food, the enchilada plate(4 of them,you better be hungry) or the machaca & eggs are some of my favorites.If you are looking for a hearty meal at a reasonable price served in a friendly atmosphere, (sometimes you may experience some friendly harassment too which I personally enjoy) then try them out!

Here is a little hidden gem if you happen to be in the airport area. I would normally not go to a hotel restaurant for lunch (even if i was staying there) but this place is the exception to the rule! I've only eaten lunch here as I don't wake up early enough to eat breakfast and I'm only in this area around lunch time.
The menu is limited which makes picking a selection much easier for me. Please remind me to throw myself in front of a speeding, overweight heavily smoking driver in a yellow cab if I ever have to look at the Cheesecake Factory menu again. The sandwich's are all good, I eat the club, the grilled chicken sandwich, the Ruben, always happy with my choices. The sides are normally generous and tasty.I had a huge side of cottage cheese with my club yesterday that could have been a lunch by itself! (Not that anyone would want a mountain of cottage cheese for lunch, I'm not as dumb as I look) Salads are a good choice too, Mrs. M keeps telling me that, not quite enough grease for me me but I try to keep the little lady on my good side from time to time. I think the prices are fair, maybe a touch high but not out of line and they do change the menu from time to time so the chef here is on the ball. Anyway I'd would give these guys a try as its not your typical airport hotel restaurant, see what you think!

Is it just me or do you have trouble finding meat ravioli any more? When you go to the foo foo Italian restaurants they may have some version of ravioli but its all modernized with some other concoction. I just want my dang ravioli without the modern modifications! Roma is where you can get it and its delicious, the marinara sauce is authentic and I lick the bowl when I'm finished, there I said it. Of course there are many other delightful treats..You will find what you are looking for. I've eaten here dozens of times, its always great food with lots of carry outs available that are equally is good. Yes its in a weird spot, you wont see it when you are on your way to an Uncle Kracker concert but you are not far from it! Follow your smart phone ap and get over there and make sure to hum Smile. Smile. on your drive cuz you will be smiling when you are making a pig out of yourself while eating here.

Here ya go, another local good little place to grab some Mexican food!
I've eaten lunch here and at the original location on 22nd st for years. Never had a bad meal! The people are friendly, the food is tasty, the prices are very reasonable as you'll see as I included the receipt for my lunch bill today: 3 people, a guacamole appetizer, 3 drinks, out the door for $32. A little over $10 bucks per person for a decent lunch is not bad folks. I had the enchilada plate with beans and rice (1 shredded beef, 1 chicken) and a few extra onions and peppers on the side which you'll see in the pic. To sum it up: the food is good, the place is clean, the chairs at the 29th location are a little tough as they are unpadded metal, but don't let that stop you from going as the service is fast and your butt wont have to endure the iron too long.. Maybe the owner will think about a chair upgrade someday soon, my skinny a_ _ would sure appreciate it ??

I haven't been to BJ's for a few years as I was never overwhelmed by the food or service but I tried them again this weekend. I must say the service was fast and friendly, we were seated quickly the overall experience was a good one! 
We tried a couple of different appetizers, The brussel sprouts and the old stand by spinach, artichoke dip with tortilla chips. Both good choices, the brussel sprouts would get the nod if I were to go with one. 
I had the mahi tacos which were enjoyable, I'd order gain, Mrs. M had the bread bowl with clam chowder that she enjoyed. My 4 year old grandson requested Mac & Cheese, a salad and ice cream. He did a good job of eating most of it (all of the ice cream) and when he was finished he laid on the booth cushion and said he wanted to go swimming so I think that was all a good sign.
OK, finally, we couldn't resist the chocolate peanut butter marshmallow with vanilla ice cream pizookie, if that doesn't give you a sugar charge and put a smile on your face then you don't like sweets!
So if you are on Oracle near the mall and are hungry for a variety of tasty treats give them a try!

Wow, all I can say is the Machaca Huevos Rancheros was fantastic! It was hug and delicious! I'm kind of a big portion eater but this thing was so big I didn't quite finish it which doesn't happen with me. Get in there and try it, you wont be disappointed! They know how to do breakfast folks, it all looks good, I cant wait to get back there and try another dish. I Love this place!

Hey this is a heck of a good place if you are a Greek food fan! Good food, big portions, reasonable prices  fast service, nice enough environment, so as long as you are good with all the basics Id try them out. 

If you need the ambiance of a traditional Greek restaurant with the aerial view of Santorini covering the walls it may fall a bit short as its kind of  plain inside but don't hold that against it. They do a nice job overall, stop in for your Gyro fix and see what you think.

OK we have had two parties in the last three weeks where we have picked up food from Pappoule's. Both meals have been a variety of the usual Greek cuisine and both times have been really good. The food has been ready on time (hey I had 20 free loaders licking their chops waiting for the food to arrive so I wouldn't want to walk in late or Id never hear the end of it from Mrs. M.) There was nothing wrong with anything on the order. I especially like the Greek salad and of course the delicious Gyro meat and the chicken was tender and spiced nicely as well. Id say the only problem with this place is that Mrs. M calls it 'Pappa Louies' Well she is a country girl and sometimes has trouble calling things by the right name but I love her anyway and she puts up with me so what the heck. Try out Pappoule's (Pappa Louies) friendly folks, fair prices and good eating!

Hey you want a quick meal to go at a reasonable price try these guys! I have had several dinners to go from this location and I have always enjoyed them. I usually get the burrito bowl with chicken, I love their chicken. They load the bowl with all the good stuff you chose and my friend that is a big meal. The other item i really enjoy is the queso and chips. I have to tell you I'm kind of a queso snob. I've been to Austin too many times and sampled the worlds best queso and trust me this is not it. Haha but its not bad either, some of the best I've had lately that's for sure! Definitely a good choice if you are a fan of the cheese. 
Go to Torchys in Austin if you really love your queso (just saying) Hey I like Chipolte I have tried most everything here and the steak is another good choice in your salad or tacos. Reasonable, fast, take it home and sit in front of the TV and eat yourself silly.

gEhxkSS-_H8yS9K1cA7TQA.review_text: I consider myself a pretty picky foodie especially when it comes to Asian cuisine...and living in the suburbs there are only a handful of places I would actually recommend going back to....I was trying to figure out where to take my dad for his 70th birthday and after working a late day...I found Zen Asian Bistro and Bar that was open pretty late. We went there and was greeted by an older man (I'm guessing the owner) who truly had wonderful hospitality service. Very friendly and throughout the entire night checked up on us to see how everything was....at the end he surprised my dad with a special cheesecake decorated beautifully and sang to my father for his birthday. From the delicious food, singapore noodles, a black pepper beef entree (in their traditional menu) and tom yum soup - our meal was 5 stars and matched with the service etiquette. I will definitely be going back there - plus the bill was 50% off with a yelp deal I found....SCORE!!!! Handsdown a wonderful place to go to for great food and service. A definite winner and I wish this new restaurant it's about 5 months old nothing but continued success. =)

I first heard of Spice Kitchen after visiting their original location in Trooper, PA (which is closer to my parent's house so I went there pretty frequently). Since moving close to the Lansdale area, I heard they opened their second location recently and was anxious to try it since I had a good experience at the other location. I invited my non-Indian friend (who loves Indian food)with me since she and I have been wanting to explore a new Indian restaurant together for awhile. Since this was going to be the last time I see her before she moves, I decided to pick one of my favorite North Indian restaurants and hope the experience would be just as good if not better than their other restaurant location. One negative right away is the fact that after plugging the address into my GPS it took me to the intersection of Forty-Foot Rd and Allentown Rd...since there was a shopping center near there, I decided to trust my instincts it would be in there. I drove around and most of the shops were empty, so I almost was going to turn around. Fortunately, my friend got there a few minutes before me and I called her and she helped me find the restaurant since it was not labeled/listed on the shopping center sign from the entrance  I came in from.Upon arriving we were greeted by a very personable and bubbly blonde haired American woman (whose name I later found out is Johanna). She really brings the restaurant to life with her charm, stories, and sense of humor as she keeps you entertained throughout your meal as she frequently checks in on the guests in the restaurant. (A definite positive to keep me coming back here), can't believe she's only been there for less than a year - she makes you feel like family and is a natural at what she does. A true gem at this restaurant.
The ambiance is small and charming with a classy interior design, perfect for a quick get together during the week for dinner with friends, date nights, or family outing. We sat down and shortly after we got settled in, an Indian gentleman, named Mr. Sharma came to our table and brought us papadam that came with 3 assortment of chutneys - most other Indian restaurant in the area don't do this - so bonus to this location! He was very nice as well and personally took the time to meet each guest it seemed like him and Johanna have been working for years together, they are quite the entertainment with their funny comments flowing back and forth throughout the night. My friend who came with me is a vegetarian and found it easy to pick something off the menu with a large selection of options to chose from. She ended up getting the Kashmiri Dum Aloo, and aloo tikka chaat as an appetizer. I, being a Punjabi (North Indian) was craving my favorite, chicken tikka masala (which comes with rice) and I decided to split some fresh naan with my friend. The food came out without waiting too long although one mistake that occurred (which is minor - and my friend didn't make a big deal about) was that her dinner came out before her appetizer. The portions were definitely generous (another reason I would come back) - because not only can you enjoy the meal in the restaurant, chances are you will have enough to take home for lunch/dinner the next day. We both thoroughly enjoyed our meal. I thought the chicken tikka masala was perfectly cooked, in the rich tomato, buttery gravy with aromatic spices. I enjoyed it with the rice and also ordered a side of raita since I always eat Indian food at home with some sort of yogurt on the side for digestive purposes to calm any sort of spice level. The restaurant was nice and cooked the food to my tolerable spice level which was another personable touch I liked. The only thing I wish was since this was the first time I was there - I was a little taken aback when I was charged for the raita when my bill came. Usually, for something small like that I thought it would be complimentary to gain my repeat business in the future, oh well. As our evening was wrapping up, Mr. Sharma brought us some boxes to wrap up our leftovers, although I do suggest instead of just assuming styra-foam would be sufficient to pack the dinner, Mr. Sharma was kind enough upon special request to dig up some Tupperware since I did have some of the raita and chicken tikka masala to wrap up without wasting any of the delicious food by using styrafoam alone. I really wanted to get the rasmali for dessert, but I figured I would try it out the next time I came in. Before leaving since it was a special goodbye dinner planned with my friend, the staff was super nice to take some pictures of us and then I even had Johanna get in a picture with me too for the memories. The staff really goes above and beyond for their guests to make it a enjoyable experience. Overall, the prices were reasonable, and I left the restaurant with a positive impression - and can't wait to bring my family here to try some new dishes together from our native region. Good job, Spice Kitchen Lansdale!

I came here tonight since I have been craving some good authentic Indian food that doesn't taste as if I went to a  typical Indian buffet meal (filled with oil, or loaded with butter to substitute natural Indian quality and  flavor). Most Indian restaurants in the North Wales/Lansdale area - are average in taste and flavor, so when I saw a bunch of positive reviews for Biryani Bowl I wanted to give it a shot and see if it lived up to the hype based on the positive reviews that were posted. 

First off the restaurant is a stand alone shop next to Napa Auto on Broad Street.
It looks like a family owned business - based on the staff. There was an Indian Uncle and his wife who greeted me. I took a look at the menu - and the first thing I noticed was the ridiculously over priced dishes - I mean who pays $10+ for a dosa, that's insane. I know and have been to quality places that don't charge even close to that. Since it was cold and snowy, I didn't feel like driving any more so I decided to fork out the money and give something a try.

I ordered the chicken dum biryani and tomato daal - which came to about $24 and some change. (Holy cow! That better be some really good biryani for that hefty price tag). I waited for my order - which was fairly decent turn around time, only took about 10 minutes to prepare. 

I handed over $40 cash (and a younger guy who processed my order was a bit unprofessional (was on the phone the entire time) and didn't have the best customer service when handling my business). So that didn't sit well with me, when I am a first time customer. I even asked if he could give some extra raita for the biryani since i noticed the raita portion was in a really small container and would never be enough with the biryani that was packed in a round container. The guy was still on the phone so I decided to wave to the "Uncle" who seemed more friendly and appreciative of my business. (I'm assuming he must be the owner)...who would give me some attention and handle my request more professionally. He was happy to give me the extra two small containers of raita and then I thanked him and was on my way home to try out the food.

I opened the food when I got home and was pleased to smell the aromas of what looked like real authentic hyderbadi biryani. I took a bite and holy crap was it spicy!!!! I ordered it to be mild, becase I know true South Indian dishes can be awfully spicy because they use different spices than North Indian food. I am used to eating real typical biryani since I have lived with some South Indians from Andra Pradesh and Hyderabad - so I know the cooking is far different than North Indian cuisine. But I don't enjoy Indian food if all I taste is the heat and less on the actual dish I ordered. I ordered the food mild too, and could barely feel my tongue from all the masala they used to cook the biryani. Thank God I got the extra raitas. 

All in all, it was okay - not your typical Indian restaurant, so I will say it was better than average, but definitely not my favorite. I will give it one more shot and try their buffet to get a more accurate read on this place. 

I wish this place was not so greedy when it comes to their prices and tapered down the heat so you can actually enjoy the dish properly. If they are willing to do this I will give this place a 4 star instead of just 3. Good luck and be ready to drink a lot of water or milk with your meal.

I recently moved to the area and wanted a quick lunch while fighting a cold. It not very common that I found a Chinese/Thai restaurant together.  I ordered their lunch special Singapore noodles and tom yum soup. This was hands down the best and most reasonably priced food I got. Perfect to the last bite. This definitely will be my go to Chinese/thai restaurant that I highly recommend eating at or for a quick local take out.

Hands down my favorite suburban go to for delicious Chinese food. My family and I have been going here for years. The owners are so nice and want to get to know their customers, and the rest of their staff and service go above and beyond to accommodate their customer's needs.  Delicious hot and sour soup and Singapore noodles (my usual Chinese favorite dishes to get). Keep up the great work guys, I hope you're around for many more years! :-)

I heard about this place from my neighbor and being a foodie I knew I had to check this place out since it was close to where I live ..since I love good brick oven pizza. Their concept is original and the staff is super attentive to each customer that comes in from the time they order to when they leave the restaurant.service goes along way for me. And the crew definitely is on point making every guest feel welcome and appreciated. Think of it as when subway meets fresh quality brick oven pizza. You can custom create your own Pizza or choose from their one of their favorites. 

The place is great for a casual meal or for a quick grab and go take out. Family friendly and plenty of tables to relax and catch up with a friend  over some delicious pizza. The pizza is small and airy enough that makes you feel satisfied without overdoing it frim eating. I definitely will be back and wish these guys the best. Can't wait to try more pizza creations with my friends.

Generous, fresh quality, and delicious portion sized dinner entree take out, quick deliver, and friendly staff. Since I work in the area...this will definitely be my go to spot for Asian cuisine.  Can't wait to eat leftovers for lunch tomorrow. Highly recommended trying out this place.

First off , after getting to the restaurant with reservations at 7pm...my dad and I had to wait 10 mins for a table (not very happy about the wait)...oh well...when we got seated to make up for the wait they gave us prime seats almost in the center of the restaurant and  closest to the lovely gourmet salad bar. (Okay, I forgive you now)...our head waiter pulled out both of our seats and made us feel important immediately. The staff was always very attentive and it didn't take long before the gaucho styled dressed men started coming to our table with the array of delicious hand carved selection of high end meat.They give you coasters to flip : green means keep feeding me more meat, and the red means I am full. My dad loved the lamb chops and I was in heaven with the Picanha (the top house special steak).They brought us cheese bread to the table , mashed potatoes, plantains and polenta fries. The salad bar was amazing - everything was spot on and oh so fresh. Did I mention they had basil dressing ...that was heavenly and made the salad so much lighter and refreshing (especially since we went on a hot summer night). Another section they had was a rice and bean bar. (I decided to skip that section)...oh and to round off the evening they brought my dad a complimentary birthday dessert of his choice...we split a tres Leche cake with drizzled strawberry glaze. By the end of the meal, I was thoroughly satisfied....and would definitely come back. The staff really treated my dad like a king and made his 74th birthday special. Oh yeah, for those of you who don't eat meat...call ahead and let the staff know they have seafood options for you too. The bar selection was very good...and oh my goodness the mango refresher drink I got was a perfect pairing for this experience. Before we walked out of the restaurant the head waitress was kind enough to take a photo of my dad and I. Oh did I mention even as you are about to leave ...they have Belgium chocolate candies as you head out the door. This restaurant is a perfect addition to the burbs and I am so glad they found their home in KOP. I give it two thumbs waaaay up. Oh and if things couldn't get better sign up on their website to become a Fogo member and get $15 off your bill. I will definitely be going back! Enjoy to all my suburbanite friends who want to dine with class and safistication. Well done!!! :-)

Amazing food tucked in the Valley Forge towers complex in King of Prussia, pa. Complete authentic Syrian family run restaurant. Good for families or even dining alone without feeling odd. I loved my chicken gyro...very fresh quality food, non greasy, healthy, and filling meal without feeling heavy or over stuffed afterwards. Super attentive/ small, but personable staff who truly appreciates your visit, business and sees that you are enjoying your meal. Patrice was my waitress and provided out standing service and very friendly throughout my meal. She is a new addition to the restaurant and quickly became a friend who is full of wonderful foodie knowledge. I hope to see her again and try the kafta kebabs on my next visit. Well done Aroma!!!

I have been wanting to come here ever since it first opened ...and finally made it here with my best friend. I was so excited after hearing such great reviews from different food blogs and KOP magazine write ups...as a true foodie I had to check it out for myself. The wait time was only one 15 mins..it was pretty packed for a Thursday night out so I was pleasantly surprised the wait time wasn't bad at all and the hostess was very friendly and gave us menus to check out while we waited. Upon seating ....we were greated by our first waitress...I told her it was my first time here and she made some recommendations. I have to say after that we didn't see much from waitress #1...so throughout the evening we asked for things from random staff that walked past us...I was a bit annoyed by the rest of the staff made up for the lack of attentiveNess from waitress number 1. Amongst the staff that came to check on us one waitress really shined on us and I have to recognize exceptional talent in the tough food industry when  I see it...her name.is Molly. Not only did she check on us multiple times, she was truly a genuine gem of fill in waitress. When I felt a bit disappointed to the lack of check in from our original . waitress. Molly really went above and beyond..she explained her true passion for working at this beautiful restaurant, her love and passion for good food being a graduate student studying and pursing her masters degree in food and wine, and personal stories about her visits to South America and love of the culture after experiencing it first hand. Molly even offered  my best friend a military discount after getting to know and take interest in the people she was waiting on and checking with the manager to see if it was okay. We were impressed that this place is military friendly a big plus in my book that it honors and respect our service men year round not just on certain holidays.
..way to go! As far as the meal goes our entrees were delicious ...I got the mojo chicken breast platter that came with cilantro rice, black beans, and roasted tomato salsa. The flavors were incredible and I couldn't have asked for a more delicious and satisfying meal. My best friend had the chimmichuri chicken sandwich and fries. Saving a bit of room for dessert, Molly recommend how tasty the sweet potato warm donuts were that was paired with a cheesecake vanilla sauce for dipping. Since they came out nice and warm ...and dipping it into the sauce and taking my first bite ...I felt like I was dancing in heaven on a cloud. Since I was impressed with the meal already , these sweet potato donuts certainly throws my reviews off the charts and if u could I would give our experience 2 thumbs up. Towards the end of the meal, I asked to speak.to the service  manager of the restaurant, who is Katie. She was very friendly and I had to let her know how well Molly treated us considering it was her first day training on the job, and I told her I would never have known she was in training because of her professionalism, kindness and making sure her guests were happy during their visit. I told Katie, she hired an excellent waitress who has a bright future here the restaurant. Katie was very happy to hear my positive impression of my first time dining experience at the new establishment. I told her I certainly will be back for drinks and more good food to try out. I am very pleased with meeting Katie and seeing how  well she helps run the restaurant and she went out of her way to extend her appreciation for my compliments about Molly and offered me a drink on the house when I come back. I am so glad this restaurant is part of the new KOP town center. I certainly recommend checking if out. Your taste buds will be in for a treat for a deliciously good time. .

Tim Paulsworth was an amazing waiter tonight, you can tell he really cares about his job and goes beyond just a normal waiter. Because our pizza took a little longer, he brought us some chips and salsa while we waited. When our pizza did come out itwas delicious and impeccable service from beginning to end. We def will ask for Tim when we return.

I came to walk around this fun new dining area in KOP with my friend after visiting Valley Forge Park. I wanted something light and healthy after a good workout - I stumbled across this place while we were looking for HoneyGrow. I'm so glad I decided to check out the place. I immediately spotted next to the registers a small fridge filled with all these crazy concoctions of fresh juices. When I asked the guy who was helping out at the register (later I found out he was the GM of the place) - he came around from the back and started talking to me about the variety of flavors. He was kind enough to take one of the bottles out of the fridge and offer me a sample without even pressuring me to buy some, etc..he just had a such a genuine friendly above and beyond customer service approach with the people visiting the healthy fast food restaurant. He even said try whatever you want over at the fountain fresh lemonade area as well. Since I have been in the service industry for 15 years now, I can't say how refreshing it is to meet someone as genuine as Shirone Parker (the GM) who really treats each person who stops by with passion, excitement, and an honest review of the products at the healthy, smoothie juice bar and restaurant. He just seems to want to see people happy. I love supporting businesses that go above and beyond the way he does to make their customers feel special, valued, and appreciative of their business and leave a lasting positive impression. As I was making my final decision amongst the juices from the fridge - after sampling some of them, I was literally blown away by the unique taste, that definitely hit all the right notes with my taste buds. While most are grilling hot dogs, burgers and ribs this Memorial holiday weekend..leave it to this foodie to find this hidden gem that I found walking through Ambler tonight. This visit to the Ballwin location my just be my last. Time after time the service is poor at best. I'm writing this review while I wait for my food. Her first words, after we sat at the table for a few minutes were, "do you know what you want?" 

The manager was playing on her phone in the bar. All in all the food was good. I had to get a new bun too because my original one came with greasy fingerprints on the top. Once I got a clean one I was fine. Fries weren't hot. 

I've given up. Ballwin is off my list. Ellisville is not great either for service. Maybe I'll give the franchise a break for a few years. Service seems to be lacking everywhere.

The one time I decide to use the drive-through to pick up my prescription is the last time. I waited for 28 minutes for birth control and Xanax. Two prescriptions that I was told was filled the day before. So, I give Walgreens a full 24 hours before I go to pick up my prescription. I'm only giving one star because this place has some of the worst service around. I walked in today, was looked at my three employees and after 5 minutes standing up front with no one to seat us, lead me to this review. 

First and foremost the food is fantastic! However, I've been served margaritas with no alcohol to margaritas with rum. 

We used to go once a week because we love the food so much. However, the service has been appalling. We've waited upwards of 40 minutes for an order with only three or so tables sat besides us. Never has our food order been messed up but we have had our drink order messed up a lot. 

We have given this place a chance to redeem itself over and over. Today, after standing up front for 5 minutes and have 3 employees look at us and not greet us or seat us was the last straw. We will not be going back.

Love the crab Rangoon. Best in the area. Lovely staff. New car your place close to home.

Waited 15 plus minutes for a small order of cheddar bites and onion rings. The employees came out to the car in front of us three times with no food. Just talking. Car behind us left and we decided to as well. This place is NOT worth it.

Clearly I'm not the first one to write a review saying this location tells you they can't take orders. Today I went and was told their system was down and they can't take orders. This strikes me as odd, because I've visited this location three times in the last year and all three times I've been told their system was down and they could not take orders. Coincidence? Lazy employees that would rather sit outside and smoke than actually work. I'll go to the location at Grand and Chouteau from now on. That location hasn't failed me for nearly 20 years. The location on Vandeventer is the worst in St. Louis.

Pro tip: place your order and step aside after you pay. This way the employee can take the next order while yours is made. Don't crowd the window and look like a tourist. You only drive the locals crazy.

Went in at 7am on a Sunday and the bathrooms were worse than a truck stop in the middle of Kansas at three am. They claimed to have just cleaned the floors. Doubtful. There was shit on the floor next to the clean floor sign and tp all over the floor. Two stalls were permanently closed because it looked like someone had shit all over the inside. Friendly staff and consistent food. I've only been here half a dozen times but have never had a problem. The drinks aren't the strongest, but you should t expect less from any franchise. 

The manager working around 9-10pm in the bar area on 9/21/2016 did a fantastic job and if he reads this, then he'll remember the former apples employee he helped out that night. Thanks again!

Came in on a Thursday night. 10/13/16 @9pm to be exact. Only stating this so they can look back and see who was working. We ordered two small chocolate dipped cones. As we were wondering why it was taking so long and why the "manager" felt the need to give us a handful of napkins after the employee just gave us a handful of napkins; we realized all he wanted to do was come to the window to catch a smell of our car. "Oh, I can smell it now" as he and his employee both chuckled. 

Well, mr "manager" we're just as clever as you in your obvious quest to smell our car. Now that we know children work there, there's no need to come back. It would've been better had you just enjoyed what you came up to the window for.
Sold warm beer in the cooler. Didn't think I had to grab the bottles with my own hands to make sure they were cold. Not going back to this location. Ever.

Walked in at 9:00pm on a Saturday. Not a single clean table. Once sat we waited 6 minutes and left after we saw an employee go in and come out of the bathroom, and unless he was going in there to send a quick text, there's no way he washed his hands. The place was gross.

Sat in line for 10 minutes watching one of the employees hang outside with his girlfriend and their kid at 11:30 on a Saturday night. Two cars pulled up behind us and left. When we backed out of the line, we realized he was the ONLY EMPLOYEE.

Overpriced hipster tacos. Mission failed. Cheese dip was served cold. Took about 15 minutes for our first round of drinks. Second round of drinks took about the same time. That is extremely long to wait for drinks. Drinks weren't even that great. 

I had the house margarita, and it came in a pint glass with an ORANGE? What a disgrace. I had to ask for limes because that is the proper garnish for that drink. I can understand a "Mexican" inspired place getting a Long Island or a manhattan wrong, but a margarita? I didn't order a blue moon. For $8 I expected to taste SOME tequila. Inexcusable and embarrassing. 

The tacos weren't that great. Very small amounts of protein. We knew they'd be small but I feel they are just robbing you. We left hungry because we didn't want to waste any more money. Ended up in a drive through about two hours later. Great. 

I would've complained about the drinks but honestly didn't want to hurt any of the employees feelings. They all looked extremely sensitive. 

Oh, they must've forgotten to actually coat the churros with cinnamon and sugar. Seriously, how do you mess up all three courses? Embarrassing. Too bad most locals can't see through the bulls#!t

Worst service ever. Not busy whatsoever. Our server, who had red dreadlocks (only mentioning hoping her manager reads this) didn't even greet us, she just asked if we were ready to order from across the restaurant. Never refilled drinks and her and her fellow employees were all standing around the service station bickering with each other while patrons waited and managers worked while complaining that the employees were lazy. 

I told a group of 6 in the parking lot to go somewhere else. First thing they said was, "poor service tonight?" Hmmm wonder what made them think that. 

I hope you enjoyed getting stiffed. Don't bother looking for us, we won't be coming back. Too bad too, we just moved to the neighborhood and are normally really good tippers.
Sat in an empty drive through line for two minutes. After saying hello and waiting some more I left. This was on a Sunday at 2:30 in case managers want to see who was NOT working during that time.

Might as well abolish the dual ordering line if you're only going to use one. Never seen more lazy employees in all my life. You're lucky your fries are good. Your employees are the worst pieces of trash ever to "have jobs". What a joke.

This pretty boy is always more concerned with himself than anything else. I've been in here several times, thankfully he's never waited on us, but he's loud, obnoxious and sits around in his uniform when "off the clock". gizcDkj8-DcAIOyq7JR0HA.review_text: I received some gift certificates from my friend for my birthday, which I appreciated, along with a menu. I heard how great this place was from her so I figured I would try it. I called the number on the menu and placed my order with the girl. When I went to the Berwyn location to pick up my lunch I was informed that there was no order placed under my name. It was then I realized I had called the wrong location. The guy behind the counter told me I would have to drive to the Wayne location. I informed him that I was on my lunch break and did not have time. He then said that I could order a sandwich there but I would have to pay for BOTH sandwiches! He explained that he had to do this because they have had a problem with people ordering at the wrong location. I told him that he can also charge me for neither sandwiches and I walked out. My guess is that most of these people were first time customers like myself. Well, I am also a last time customer because I will not be going back.  Instead of making me a happy customer he decided to lose a new one. Also, if they have had a problem with food being ordered at the wrong location, why would they not answer the phone with the name and location you are calling...or confirm that you are calling the right location. This is what Nudy's Cafe does.

I used to love this place. However, I believe it has changed management. There are many new faces, the food is just mediocre, they did away with the weekly specials and the service sucks, except for Jill. She is the lone server kept on from the previous staff. The last two times I was there we had awful service. The last time I was there, we had a new server who should really consider a career change. Not only did my wife's appetizer come out AFTER her meal, but I got the wrong meal! I ordered the tri-colored tortellini, but got the cajun shrimp and processed chicken (used to be real chicken breast) over linguine. Since we stopped off here before heading to the shore, we were on a time schedule so I just accepted the incorrect meal and dealt with it. Our visit before that we had four people at our table. 2 of us got our meals. The other two waited for about 25 minutes before we had to say something to our server. We then waited another 10 minutes before our food came out. One of those 'meals" was just a slice of cheese pizza, which is smaller and does not taste nearly as good as it used to.  I have been a loyal customer since it opened, but I am now considering taking my business elsewhere. I will give them one more chance. But three strikes and you are out!.

Eh, it was OK. The quality of the meat was good, and It came on an Amoroso roll. However, they do not use real Kraft Cheez Whiz. It is "cheese sauce". I have eaten enough times at Jim's Steaks in Philly where they use real Cheez Whiz. Our Deli in Paoli also uses real Cheez Whiz. Trust me. I can tell the difference. If they used real Cheez Whiz, I would definitely give them a better rating. I would even pay a little more for it. The cheese makes a big difference.

Also, the side of pizza sauce that came with the stromboli tasted burnt. The stromboli itself was pretty good though.

My parents go to Lucky Dragon all the time and they love it. So I figured I would try it with my wife last night. I called and ordered the sweet and sour chicken, the only Chinese food my wife eats. We get to the restaurant to pick up our order and my wife goes in to get it. She gives the lady our order number and says that it is an order of sweet and sour chicken. The employee (who my mom says could have been the owner Paul's sister-in-law) told my wife she was wrong. It was an order of General Tso's chicken. My wife explained to the lady that it was supposed to be sweet and sour chicken. So now the employee is copping an attitude with my wife and says "maybe you should double check?" My wife says with who? And the employee said with the man who ordered. My wife then had to explain that it was her husband that ordered and that it was the sweet and sour chicken that I had ordered. The whole time my wife was in there, the lady had an attitude and was quite rude. Whatever happened to the customer is always right? Why would my wife be lying about our order? When we finally got our food, it was sub-par. The chicken was hard and rubbery/over-cooked. It almost seemed like the chicken was cooked and then dropped in the fryer again to heat it up. It was not very good. This was my first time and last time ordering from there.

Being a man who believes in second chances, I tried John's Village Market again. I can now say that my first visit there was just an off day. I have had better service every time I have been in there since. Their corn beef special sandwich is excellent.

Live review here. It has been one hour and 12 minutes since we placed our order. At the 61 minute mark, our server brought us a stale scone. Still waiting for our meals. I understand today is the first day and there are kinks to be worked out. But we're going on an hour and a half. Ridiculous.

Update: At 2:00 after waiting one hour and 22 minutes, we decided to leave. After getting up to leave, the owners who are very nice, talked us in to staying. They comped our meals. They said the meals were coming right up. After waiting about 10 more minutes we finally got our meals. Neither of our meals (the Irish Fry) had the fried tomatoes. My meal was supposed to have scrambled eggs, but came out with a fried egg over medium. We waited so long I didn't want to complain and have to wait any longer. 

Again, this was their opening day and I understand things have to be worked out. But my blood sugar was dropping and I was getting "hangry". 

Now for the positives. The food was very good. Once they work out the kinks, they should be fine. The owners are very nice people and our server was too.

After seeing the 4 star rating, my wife and I figured what the heck. We will give it a try. Boy, were we disappointed. We started off with soups. She ordered the chicken noodle soup and I ordered the soup of the day. Her soup was just ok. Just be forewarned that they put potatoes in their chicken noodle soup. Neither of us had ever seen that before. I don't know if that is an Italian thing or not, but it really takes away from the soup. In my personal opinion, a soup should not have two starches. I'm no soup expert, but that's just how I feel. My soup (I forget what it was called) tasted awful and looked like dirty dishwater. The bread they brought to us tasted musty and was hard, like it had been sitting in someone's basement for a couple of days. For our meals, I ordered the chicken marsala. It was ok. Not great but not bad either. My wife ordered the ziti with meat sauce and a side of meatballs. My wife is a very picky eater. So when she said that she did not like hers, I had to try it for myself to see if it was just her being picky. I will say that the sauce was decent and the pasta itself was good. However, the meat sauce seemed to be of a low quality beef/pork/chicken variety. Also, the meatballs she got were not cooked through and had pink in the middle. All in all, not a very good meal. Ending on a positive note, our server was pretty good and the owner seemed nice.

Stopped in yesterday with my wife, and the owners were very friendly and informative. Plus, the beer is very tasty. I highly recommend it. I really hope this is the beginning of good things to come for Spring City's Main Street.

The food was very good. I only have a few minor complaints. We were served our appetizers which were all quite tasty. However, the tiny Styrofoam plates they give you for the apps just aren't big enough. Again, I know that is a minor detail. Also our server did not clear any of the plates that the appetizers came out on before serving us our meals. So we were stuck playing Tetris with all the plates to make our entrée plates fit. She did clear them after she dropped off the dinners, but she put the cart before the horse. My other complaint is that the seafood bisque is $1 more than the soup du jour on the menu. However, if you ask for the seafood bisque with your meal, they upcharge you $2.50 instead of $1. This makes no sense to me. Other than those little things, our meals were all very good. I would definitely go back there for dinner.

I have been to John's Village Market numerous times. My first time there a few years ago started off rocky, but they have more than redeemed themselves. Their food is consistently good and service is great too. However, I have just tried their Soul Food Friday (presented by Chef Derrick "DOO" Jackson) for the first time. And I must say it was delicious! I ordered the jerk chicken platter which comes with rice and beans and your choice of two sides. The options were collard greens, mac & cheese, potato salad, coleslaw, string beans and sweet potatoes. I went with the mac & cheese and potato salad. Both sides were excellent. The food portions were also generous. I could not finish all of it for lunch so I will be definitely eating the rest of it later. I am looking forward to it. Put it this way...I have tried some very good jerk chicken when I was in the Caribbean. The chicken I tried today from JVM beats it hands down.

I have been to Bar Lucca twice now. The first time was for a Christmas party this past December. It was nice and the food was very good. So when I asked my wife where she would like to go for her birthday she asked to go back to Bar Lucca. So I went to their website a couple of weeks before my wife's birthday and submitted a request. I waited for one week and never received any response by phone or email (and I even checked my Spam folder). So I called the restaurant but the event manager was not there. So I left my name and phone number for her to call me back. I waited two more days and still got no response. So I called back again and spoke to a nice girl who told me that once again the event manager was not in, but she would go ask her manager if we could have the Chef's Tasting private room. She came back on the phone and said that we could have the room and that everything was reserved. Great! Until a couple hours later when she calls me back and says that she spoke to the event manager and now we cannot have the room because they had a party in there from 7-10. Our reservations were at 6:00. So our options were to eat in the main dining room, move our reservation up to 5:00, or go somewhere else (my idea not Bar Lucca's). I asked my wife and she decided to keep our reservation for 6:00 in the main dining room because 5:00 was too early and we did not want to have to reschedule with all of our guests. The girl was very apologetic on the phone and blamed their new computer system, but sorry only gets you so far. 

So we get to the restaurant and get seated. We tell our server that we wanted a beer similar to Stella. She says that they have a beer called La Rossa and it is very similar to Stella. Ok, that sounds fine. She brings it to the table and it was dark! Nowhere close to Stella. I tasted my beer and it was good for the style (Doppelbock). The two others that ordered it did not like it nor drank theirs. 

So now it's time to order our food. One of our friends asked the server about the Risotto. The description on the menu says that it contains "Shrimp, green chillies, lobster, mushroom, basil oil, grana padano". The server proceeds to tell my friend that there is actually no lobster or mushrooms in the risotto and she's not sure why it even says that on the menu. As long as there were no mushrooms, my friend was ok with ordering it. When our food arrived, lo and behold my friend's risotto had mushrooms in it! She did not notice until she was halfway done eating it. Thank God she is not allergic to them. One of the other servers offered to take it back, but she did not want to wait any longer for her food. 

When I received the sirloin steak I had ordered, it tasted very good. I just wish it was hot. Scratch that...warm. I don't like piping hot food. My food was cold. But we waited so long by this point, I did not want to send it back and wait more because I was starving. So I just dealt with the cold food. 

Needless to say, no one at our table was impressed. I highly doubt any of us will be going back any time soon. 

Oh, and beware of the overly salted bread. The bread itself is good, but the crust is way, way, way too salty!!!

From the reservation process to the entrees (we did not order dessert- can you blame us?), nothing was impressive.

My wife and I Went to Liberty Union for the first time last Friday around 7:15 p.m. We were told that there would be a 20-25 minute wait. I understand that there is sometimes a wait on the weekends. I am OK with that. But as we stood there waiting, I noticed that there were at least four 4-top tables and two 2-top tables set and ready to go with no one sitting at them. That irritated me a little bit. They seemed to have plenty of servers (at least 6) plus a few bus boys/girls working. I don't know why they could not seat us right away. Maybe the kitchen could not handle all the tables at once? Who knows? But we waited patiently anyway.

Once we were seated our server was quite attentive and friendly. The complimentary tater tots are a nice, tasty touch. My wife got the Cap n Crunch breaded chicken fingers and I had the New Orleans pasta. Both of us were happy with our meal selection. Overall, it was a decent place. Not great but not awful either.  I would go back again.

I went to Snoozys for the first time today, and I was not impressed. Pulling into the parking lot I was greeted with a huge pothole. THUMP! Not a big deal since this is PA and potholes are a way of life. Just wasn't a great first impression. So I get to the table and our server takes our drink orders. She seems nice. She returns with our drinks and gives us a few minutes to decide what we want. When she returned, we ordered our food. It came out relatively quickly. So far so good. However, after she delivers the food to our table, she also puts the check on the table and disappears.  I take one bite of my SOS and it tastes like "S". It was probably the worst cream chip beef I've ever tasted. It tasted like it was out of a plastic pouch. I have had better SOS from a package of Stouffer's. The few other tables that were outside had left, and we were the only table left. So they were not busy. She never came back once to check on us or refill my coffee. She could have fixed the awful SOS situation if she had only come back to check on us like any good server should. When went to pay, we finally saw her again. Now she asks me how the meals were and I nicely informed her that it was awful and the SOS tasted like it was out of a package. However, this was too little too late. She informed me that it was homemade. I find this hard to believe though. 

Overall, not a good experience. We will not be returning unfortunately. I really wanted to like this place. 

I hope this info can help them improve, and I wish them well.

My wife and I were very happy to hear that Cutillo's was reopening on August 26th. However, we were not happy with their new menu. It is pretty much all small plates now that they say you can share with your friends and family. This is not a very good idea in the middle of a pandemic.  They have also increased their prices significantly. For example, chicken fingers that used to cost $8 now cost $18. I understand that food prices are increasing and that the restaurant needs to make money, but a 125% increase for chicken fingers seems a bit steep. The value that you got at Cutillo's is now gone, and they unfortunately have lost two customers. I'm not even going to go into the details of how slow our service was because I understand that restaurants are still understaffed. I will end with a positive comment though. The food was still very good.

Tonight I ordered the short ribs with rice and brussel sprouts to go. I really wanted to like this because I've had the brussel sprout pizza here before, which is delicious. Unfortunately this meal did not live up to the quality of the pizza. First off, it was not short ribs. It was rubbery skirt steak. The rice was bland. And there were only a few shavings of brussel sprouts. For $30.50 they could add don't more brussel sprouts. The sauce on the meat was tasty though.
