I know good bagels and these are them. Forget any place else in Bucks county, I have tried and failed to find a really good bagel. This place is wonderful. Service is personal. I walked in after two months away and they said, "Two plain with cream cheese?" And Ollie calls me "sir". I want to shake his hand that makes the wonderful bagels.
They had to move, 1/30/2011,somewhere near Galloway Road. Anyone with the address, please post it.

The food was homey like my mother's cooking. But mom wasnot a very good cook although the large portions remind me of home. And somehow we got upsold by a slick guy with an accent who managed to turn ten dollar entrees into forty dollars per person. The appetizer was tasty but cold in the middle, the chicken paprikas had a deep oil slick and not a lot of flavor. I make this stuff for my Slovak in-laws and I can truly say mine is better.. It was not a wonderful experience, just pleasant and expensive. If I go back I wil lorder differently, not listen to the old guy's suggestions, and make different menu choices. I think the Goulash and the schnitzel looked good.

Maybe four years ago my wife and I had a good meal at Ruby Tuesday in Princeton area. Apparently that menu is long gone and Langhorne store is shorter on service too. 
I ordered a raspberry iced tea. It came in a pilsner glass with more than an inch of raspberry seeds at the bottom. I got a throatful of seeds. I never eat seeds because they trigger a very unpleasant reaction and a gag reflex. My server seemed to think that I should be happy because the seeds were a sign of real fruit in the drink. I asked for plain water. It came with a twisted lemon wedge floating and seeds on the bottom. Right after I told the server about my seed problem. The new menu at the time had none of what we came for. The portions were definitely too skimpy for doggy bags. It took me two years to try again.
Our foursome of adults had a few minute wait and were led to a booth. We asked to be seated at a nearby empty table instead. She took us back to the hostess desk. We passed at least one other empty four-top on way. We were told the wait was now one hour!! I explained that we already had a table to trade. They could just swap us out with the people who they were going to seat at the empty tables. This concept escaped the head hostess. So Goodbye, Ruby Tuesday. At least one Assistant Manager and two hostesses need some re-training in customer service. I really don't want to go back again.
I also want to say the portions still looked skimpy in the dishes I saw. And many restaurants give you a salad or soup with your entree. Ruby Tuesday gives you a salad, makes you get up and get it yourself and charges you for the privelege.

For a pizza place, Yordana's does Italian food better than most. I am a regular. Pizza is OK, but then, I am from Hoboken where brick ovens made a unique quality pizza. I especially like the pasta boscaiola and my  wife, the veal parmagiana. one dish is good for two meals. The service is friendly. They recently spruced up their dining room with pleasant murals so it is less like eating in a pizza joint. We have met several people at the restaurant who tell us they dine there often. When people come back, you are doing it right.

truthfully, I don't get corporate chains like Fridays. They aren't a good restaurant and they aren't a good sports bar. They have right-sized portions, which means you should appreciate getting less food. It is the same bar food that you can get at many of the chains. You get better burgers at some burger places. You get better pasta at pizza/pasta places. You get more sports and drinks at a sports bar. Yet the place is crowded mostly with young folks who will wait an hour for a table. I guess being mediocre make you unobjectionable. So when you try to decide where to go, everyone finds something they can eat or drink, even if it is low level satisfaction.

Cracker Barrel is a mediocre chain which is popular maybe because everyone accepts the mediocre food because of its style or quantity or price or the phony-downhome decor. It is to Southern cooking what Olive Garden is to Italian food, the American corporate chain bland version, a shadow of the real thing. It took me a while to realize that they are just a cafeteria with the server retreiving your food from the buffet. Really. Notice their are no made-to-order omelets on this menu. The kitchen just pumps out scrambles or sunny eggs. An entree with three sides just means walking down the steam table and selecting the meat and the sides which are already pre-prepared. That is why Hien D. could be told no dumplings and then yes dumplings. The kitchen staff replenished the dumpling pan. And since they are scooping it out of a large pan, you only get as much chicken as your server takes care to fish it out for you. The blandness is the trend of chains restaurants to take some salt out of your food to have bragging rights about how healthy their food is. They menu featured their healthy selections. Look around the room, who is eating the granola and bran muffins?

One trick about breakfast. Food $6.99, coffee $1.99, orange juice $2.99. The beverages pump up the fairly cheap 7 dollar breakfast to not-such-a-bargain 12 dollars.

Still, I like this place. I like the service. I enjoy the mediocre food and I keep going back.

I have been disappointed several times in many ways by this Burger King. In general, BK keeps making radical changes to its menu.The new choices are always on the fringe instead of trying to please the most people. Becoming a cult fast food willnot keep them at the top and it is one reason why they have already fallen from the number 2 spot.
But beyond Corporate problems this BK creates its own. Managers have yelled at employees in the hearing of customers. They screwed up 3 of my last 4 orders. They are the meanest and most miserly BK I have visited. I rec'd coupons in the mail. In three tries, I have been given an argument about the discounted product. For a while I couldn't find the dollar menu. It turned out they didn't light it. Now they light it but they put it as far away as possible with small letters. And most items are now more than a dollar. But then this BK never liked the dollar menu.
So I have had it with them, My last two visits I cut their arguments over coupons short and went to McDonals. There are plenty of food options within just a few hundred yards. When the coupon says you get lesser priced item free on a two-for-one coupon, it implies that you if you order a large, you can get a smal medium or large free. If it meant that you only get a small for free, it would have said Buy one, Get a small free. But I am done with constantly putting up with their arguments.

I really liked the toasted sub. Beyond that, I visited the day after Hurricane Sandy. Firehouse Subs was one of the few places with electricity and there were long lines. Only two workers could get in to work, but those two guys worked hard to make everyone happy. It was an oasis for most of us without heat or kight or food at home. And even though they must have been pretty tired, they kept the quality of the food they served up to the usual great standards. Kudos to those guys. We will be back.

It's a lovely menu and not badly prepared, It is just so commonly pretentious. Look at all the foie gras, sweetbreads, and other supposedly high-quality ingredients. Everything has to be compkicated with a lot of ingredients, and different cooking techniques. There is a reason why the simple hamburger or even just a ham and cheese sandwich is so popular. Macadamia encrusted octopus beak with chicken lips sauce sounds so decadent and luxurious but wouldn't a grilled cheese satify just as well?

I use La Stalla for entertaining family and friends on special occasions. For instance if one person has a birthday, four or five couples might celebrate at La Stalla. It used to be that all the food was excellent and the Sunday brunch was a favorite. The last couple of times I have been disappointed with the quality of the food and the increased use of "bought' food rather than created "in-house". For instance anyone can defrost those little cream puffs and mini eclairs you get in a supermarket. I object to paying premium prices to have them served to me on a plate.

The Mother's Day Brunch was a real problem for us. Forget the hugely inflated price. The restaurant was overbooked so that tables were crammed together with no place to walk. The buffet was placed in a long narrow room with food displays on one side and carving and omelet station on the other.There was barely room to pass, so with the omelet station and waffles hopelessly backed up and people at the food displays, you had gridlock. There were handwritten signs 'Brunch In' and Brunch Out' to this narrow room. But if you know the layout, people in the main dining room would be at the wrong end to go in. They would have to travel to the front of the restaurant up two steps, pass the greeters podium, and down two steps to get in. Of course very few people took this long way around through the maze of tables. They entered the 'Out' door  and added to the gridlock for food. 

The food itself was not what it used to be. The fresh mozzarella on the Caprese was now a much more manufactured quality and cut into very small pieces so that people took a few small pieces and left a platter full of large tomato slices. The only bread was bagels. No rolls. No Italian bread. No biscuits or muffins. and surely no croissants. The carving station has three meats, overdone beef, dried out pork, and I didn't want to try what I think was ham..The only eggs were omelets, So you waited in line if you wanted an egg. A watery chicken Marsala, penne with ricotta and sauce, and a fish dish. They had pancakes and waffles apparently made in the kitchen ans brought out to the waffle station.. Truly I have never seen a restaurant bring a waffle out of the kitchen and stick it in the waffle iron to reheat it in front of the customer. My mouth was watering for such a 'freshly-made' delight.

On the good side, Service has always been friendly and quick Although today it was evident that all the employees were stressed by the crowd, and the complaints about the setup, the food and the price.

Now I cannot have another bad experience for my groups. they will lose faith in my judgment and I have lost faith in La Stalla. I will have to find another place to go. Maybe I will come back in a few months on my own to check out a dinner and a brunch.
The food is really a three star. Nothing fancy or special about it. The extra star is because they have generous portions and freebies.

It is telling that there is one 5 star review and all the rest are 2 and 1 star. The one guy who liked the place came for happy hour. Nobody has a 3 or 4 star opinion.
I was assaulted by the noise, then by the décor, then by the server. Really, this place is loud. The obnoxious fake Mexican music blares from unseen speakers and there is no escape. I couldn't escape the completeness of the cliché Mexican decoration. Everything was authentic fake reproduction Mexican. There is nothing classy at all here. I could understand if it was done in an obviously playful style, but this looks rather like someone's idea of what a restaurant in Mexico looks like. 
I also noticed the army of black t-shirt servers, runners, and bussers mostly standing in groups socializing.
They missed a great opportunity to make a good impression by serving warm, fresh tortilla chips. These are so easy to do in seconds when you have a big deep fryer. Instead I got a bowl of cardboard stale chips. The salsa was too spicy for me. I wish they had warned me, or provided an alternative.
The server was very attentive. I mean VERY attentive. His sole mission seemed to be to sell us alcoholic drinks. He made four quick trips to our table to suggest drinks, even telling us to allow him to select our drinks and we could send them back if we didn't like them. When we chose lemonade, he served them and his enthusiasm waned.
My enchiladas had a ridiculous amount of plastic cheese. Once it cooled just slightly it became stringy, not the good kind, these strings were tough enough to play on a guitar And it was unchewable. I was told it was Monterey Jack. It acted like Latex Jack. To his credit, our server took it back, offered another selection, and took it off the bill without being asked. I left him a 25% tip on the remaining balance.
I had hopes for this place. I enjoyed the Uno's that had been here before. Now I think with Sesame Place next door supplying new victims and the impression of cheap, fun food and drink, this place may be here a while. I hope not. It is taking up prime space where a good restaurant could be.

I went to the new Sport Clips in Fairless Hills. This was supposed to be the solution to all the old barbers leaving the system and the manly alternative to women's beauty shops. I guess men aren't  comfortable with other men cutting their hair anymore because all the hair cutters are women. ( and my observation is that unattractive women need not apply). In a men's barber shop the customers and barbers often talk together as a group. At Sports Clips you might get some small talk from your hair-cutter but otherwise the customers are all watching the Sports Channel on the flat screens. My haircutter had minimum barbering skill and no artistry. There is no comparison to real barbering. Selecting the plastic gadget for your clipper is not a replacement for competence. A hot towel and a girl massaging your shoulders( for which you must pay extra) is not a replacement for all the little touches like ear, nose, and eyebrow trimming, scalp massage, shaving the sideburns and neck, and a good dusting off with powder and maybe some good-smelling stuff. None of which you get from Sports Clips. A really innovative concept would be creating an old-fashioned Italian barber shop.

I don't want to like this place. My overall experience was annoying and I probably won't go back. But the food is good for Levittown. This is not your typical pizza joint. They don't deserve a bad review for their food. My impression of the dining room was a forest of tightly packed tables and chairs. unattractive green walls with large generic pictures along one wall and nothing on the other. The service center and soda machine dominate and are should be screened off. The lighting was dim and the menus are printed on parchment colored paper, so I had a hard time reading the menu. The waitress was relentless in upselling, drinks, apps, add-ons, desert. But when I declined a house salad and asked for some soup instead, I was quickly told the soup would be extra, and full price. Most places readily substitute house soup for house salad. I told the server I would take the salad home and she delivered it  in a container with the rest of the salads for the table. Where it sat. And it was dressed, so next day it was just a soggy mess. If it was a take-out salad, the dressing would be on the side. My plate was accidentally tilted and some of the sauce spilled on the floor on the way to my table. The food was shimmied back into the center of the plate but the sauce messed the rim on most of the plate and it looked unsightly. The room was cold. We finally figured that they had a door open in the kitchen and everyone going in and out let a blast of cold air into the dining room. So, like I said, the experience was annoying and not what I hoped would be a pleasant event.
But the FOOD is good. OK, I am finicky and did not love the gravy, but it is far better than the sweet stuff that seems to be standard in Lower Bucks. I was looking for better food and Scappa has it. The prices were reasonable and maybe better than some places with inferior food. The chef makes a statement. This is my style. It may not be your mother's style. I can understand that. My mother's family and my father's family made very different tasting gravy and soups. Scappa is the net level below. All my complaints had to do with eating in. Maybe this will become my take-out Italian place.

A hidden gem!! Good food, cheap prices, great service. Friendly and casual. Best grits this side of the Carolinas. I have now been here seven or eight times. When I ask my family members if they want breakfast out, Radcliff Café is now the only request.

Four of us tried this new place. The location has had a succession of failed restaurants including the excellent Ming's. It may be the location. You only see the back of the building and have to rely on limited signage . At first, I thought it was a diner-style restaurant without the huge menu. Once inside, it is clean and open. The menu is American and has a lot of choices but not many pages like a diner. It also has a limited selection of Turkish specialties on a separate card. The friendly owners visited with us when they heard that we knew and liked Turkish dishes. We ordered an eggplant appetizer and two entrees, including calves liver. Delicious and authentic! Americans might like a beef kebab option even though the lamb and chicken are truer to Turkey.
There were comfort foods. We ordered meatloaf and Turkey with stuffing. They come with two veggies like potatoes and peas. Also you get choice of soup or a really good, fresh salad bar. Oh, and delicious little garlic rolls too. And I almost forgot...choice of cheesecake or apple pie. The servings were extremely generous. We took a whole lot home. We liked everything about the food which is amazing for a fussy bunch like we are. 
Service was fast, friendly and enthusiastic. Our server was always there when we needed her and yet did not seem to be bothersome. She even had the thought to tell the owners that we were familiar with the Turkish menu. They have some flaws which were more from being overzealous. For instance twice we received small square side plates which took up a lot of space and weren't much used. The appetizers, soup and our salads were still on the table when the entrees arrived. But I would rather have a table covered with food than sit around with an empty table waiting for my dinner. They are new and will sort out these serving flaws over time. 
I would like this restaurant to survive because I want to keep coming back often. I wouldn't mind if they exercised a little portion control to maintain a viable profit margin. Their prices are reasonable. Just don't cut down the portion too far, guys, I enjoyed the leftovers a lot.

If you are a gourmet food snob or need a more formal setting, you have other options which will give you food less well-cooked at twice the price. But if you like friendly service, fresh food perfectly done, in a very informal setting then Erwins Country Kitchen is the place to go. Fine dining it is not, but it is absolutely a fine place to eat.

I have been here several times, for brunch, for an intimate dinner, for a party occasion. I noticed that the few poor reviews had some form of coupon or a complaint of food v. price. I don't know what they are looking for. Seems like they were looking for some kind of bargain. Lower Bucks is not a hotbed of fine dining, yet Bella Tori has darn good food in a beautiful setting that is really not matched in the area. So I had a really special occasion and brought a large table of 14 people this time. Our service was quick and attentive. The portions are ample. If you have a salad or appetizer, you will be hard pressed to eat all your entrée and dessert. Everyone loved their meal, rack of lamb, pescatore fra diavolo, beautifully done large sea scallops. My chicken marsala was not to my taste, yet it was well-made. that's just me being finicky. And one steak was a little over temp. It was whisked away and a correctly rare filetto replaced it. 
My plan is to come back for brunch soon with a group of friends.

Calling the décor retro is a euphemism for they haven't updated since the eighties. The service is good. There are so few customers you have your own private butler to serve you. However, the place is classy in a dated manner. Good white table clothes and fancy fan-folded napkins. Artificial roses in vases. It is pretty and romantic and attractive to an older person. The problem is this concept doesn't seem to attract customers in 2014.I am sure the lack of customers affects the food. The crudités were fresh and cold. The rolls were pleasantly warm. The house salad was also fresh. a little boring, but good quality and we liked the dressings. The soup was excellent. They can actually do duck with crispy skin and juicy meat. The other side is that it is difficult to serve some items fresh. Stuffed pastas all were straight out of a frozen bag (Celentano's?)  Meatballs too. Almost every appetizer is some form of seafood that could be kept frozen until needed. The entrees had an old-timey selection. Nothing much you couldn't get in a pizzeria or diner. The desserts are purchased and low quality. And finally, the chef has a real thing for sprinkling the edge of every plate with dried herbs, which is totally passe'. I saw good things here, but I won't go back to this version.
There is a cure. A relatively cheap renovation to remove the eighties décor and update the look. Do away with the tablecloths and fake flowers. Bring some color and character to the room. Ditch the fish tank which adds nothing to the restaurant. Stop sprinkling the plates. Re-do the menu to have fresh-made signature foods and a minimum of frozen food. Push the drink menu with attractive drink specials which will now be easier with the younger demographic hat the new décor and food will draw. Actually the place could be a family destination also. a la Friday's, Houlihans, etc.
And one more thing, this place is neither easy to find nor does it effectively promote itself. They will need a print and social media plan to tell people they are open, new, and fresh. A new name could help. (Gaby's American Bistro??)

I almost forgot. The red pasta sauce was inedible. It had an odd herbaceous taste that absolutely ruined the dish. Good sauce recipes abound.

I have been there several times. I have taken small groups of 6-8. My wife and daughter went. They then brought their girlfriends. My circle of friends is a diverse group who tend to strain the abilities of restaurants, for instance asking an Italian restaurant to eliminate all garlic from their meal or no beef in the Irish stew. Yet all these people love Cancun restaurant and have happily returned with and without me.

For my part, I clean my plate. In other restaurants I usually have leftovers and there is always a pile of detritus, little bits of the food that I find untasty and leave piled to one side of my plate. Turns out my wife, who usually eats half and takes half home, also cleans her plate. I am a large man and can consume quantities of food but I consciously take some home so as not to overeat. At Cancun, I cannot stop. The food is so tasty I finish, stuffed. About heat and spiciness, it is quite mild, but they will readily give you spicy sauce or salsa if you want more heat.

We have been actively looking for a good Mexican restaurant. I absolutely hated the Margaritas experience down the road from Cancun. On the Border is to Mexican what Olive Garden is to Italian, the Americanized chain version. Don Pablo's was better but still a chain. You can get authentic Mexican in ethnic neighborhoods of Trenton and Norristown. But you run the risk of uneven quality and service, especially from some really small local places. 

Not everything is excellent at Cancun. Some of the staff rush in a false effort to serve you quickly. And I think many of them don't quite have a perfect grasp of English. But they are friendly and helpful at all times. My group of six lingered over coffee and dessert, comfortably fed and enjoying our companionship. The restaurant emptied and I know we kept the staff waiting for us to leave. We did not feel any pressure at all to get out and we got cheerful goodnights when we did finally leave. Sorry for keeping you folks at Cancun. However, we will be back many times.

Finally, I noticed a high percentage of Central American looking faces and it reminds me that this food must be familiar as the food their mothers made. So I am guessing this is close to authentic.

I am certain that Zio Gio picked Levittown because of the scarcity of real, authentic, and well-prepared  Italian food in the area. I was excited. Now I am disappointed. Zio Gio is to Italian street food what the Olive Garden is to Italian restaurant food, the American corporate chain version. I was hoping for better. I was hoping for really tasty. Instead everything is taken down to the common denominator of the average customer's tastes.  Realistically, you are better off and have more choices at most pizza joints. Not that I wouldn't go back from time to time, but then, I also go back to McD's and BK.
Oh for a really good sausage sandwich with peppers and onions.

Panera makes very nice baked goods which are in short supply in Lower Bucks. However, he menu is pretentiously healthy. Pasta and half a sandwich might be 1100 calories. That's half my food for the day! And if I want a pastry, which is what really attracts me, forgetaboutit, I am done eating today.My real beef, though is that they stop breakfast. I never get there on time and usually leave in frustration without food. So no breakfast, expensive fake healthy, and a system where you order and have to wait in a crowded small area. I can do better at local sit-down eateries.

The most pleasant part of dealing with this Manhattan Bagel was getting our money back. I should preface this by admitting I broke my own rule. I had a previous poor experience about a year ago. But my wife wanted a bagel so I thought I would give it a try. I even determined to buy two different signature sandwiches in case one was not up to my standard. Apparently the woman  behind the counter, who seemed to be the owner or franchisee, did not understand English well enough to take an order. She didn't know her own menu and we had to explain exactly what we wanted even though it was right up on her menu boards. And she seemed to want to give us her idea instead of what we wanted. Terrible attitude. Listening is as important as speaking the language. when we looked in the bag, everything was wrong. Also, the quality was poor and the portion skimpy. Given the customer food he does not want , badly prepared, and being miserly about the portion is not going to build you a good reputation. Like I said, I encountered this last year and it is just as bad now.

I often lead a group of friends to various restaurants. Having a good experience is important not just for my, and friends, enjoyment, but because it reflects back on my own reputation and their confidence in me to pick a good place.
So Saturday 10 of us went to Café Antonio. We were not disappointed in any way. The place is nicely decorated and comfortable. It was a little noisy, but so are we. Ten people ordered a variety of appetizers and entrees. Delicious and tasty. Desserts are great. Service was attentive and friendly. The chef/owner? came out to say hello. Humorously, our server seemed to have a mental block about one of our guys. She forgot things he asked for and his food was always a little behind when we all got ours. When he didn't get his espresso we finally called her on it. The actually fact was that service was otherwise so perfect that missing this one person consistently seemed almost like a prank. But the server freely admitted her mistakes and we all had a laugh about the underlying humor.
Anyway, I will go back to Café Antonio and I think most of the others will also keep them in mind as a good place to go.

clean, friendly. I hate the "go sit and we will bring your food and clean up when you leave". It really is cafeteria food. I can carry my own tray.
Food was mid-quality, and unobjectionable. Lisa Simpson would say, "Meh."

You have to give credit for clean, friendly store and nice healthy menu. Just what I hate, but all the young women and healthy older women seemed to like it. My wife would have wanted more punch to the flavors and, truthfully, my pasta salad was bland compared to what I make at home. I saw few men. Maybe they were at the pizza joint or the Green Parrot doing beer and burger. Anyway, I have to admit, Zoe's Kitchen does what it does well. If this cuisine is your style, this is a good place for it.

Let me say I have not eaten here this year and here is the problem: Dining hours are Wed 11:30 am - 3 pm
Thurs  11:30    - 3 pm
Friday    11:30 am - 10 pm

Really??? I don't think this qualifies as a restaurant when you only serve lunch 3 out of 7 days and only serve dinner on 1 day. The menu fits on one page. It is basically a bar menu. This is all changed from the original concept of modernized Italian food with a feature meatball.

I tried several times only to find them closed. Now I am closed to them.

I am a handicapped man. Sometimes need a mobility scooter to get around. First three times here I managed to walk in. Episode one was no low tables, I had to sit at the bar with six others. Besides being a buzzkill for socializing, the barstool is not a good position for my legs. They food was ordinary. Frankly, except for people who drink alcohol, the place had nothing to attract me. Episode two, again no low table, had to sit at high table with eight friends. Episode three, got a low table, near the door, on the patio in the winter. The overhead fans created blizzard conditions. The waitress offered to turn off the one above me but the manager stopped her and refused to do it. I had to leave or freeze. Last episode, I need the scooter, wanted to see a hockey game and had a party of ten with me. I called to be sure we could get a low table for ten, so I could use the scooter and they would put the hockey game on near us ( there really was nothing else anyway, but we wanted to be certain. So we all made the trip. Guess what. They could not accommodate us...apparently not even if we waited a while. Sorry, maybe they should have called us back to let us knowThe alternative of a high table would leave me looking up at the table from a dog's eye view. Not good for socializing and also demeaning. I am not going to give them a fifth shot at me. . Note nowhere along the line did I play the handicap card to get better service. I was not going to use it to lever special treatment if they didn't have the sense to try in the first place.
 Bailey's was happy to have us, turned on our game, let us compete in their Quizzo contest, served good food, and was altogether a better experience than we could have had at the Ale House. So I guess I should thank them for that.

When I first went to Bailey's several years ago, I liked it. Over the years I have realized that the service has always been personal. The food has been really good. It is bar food, of course, But it is well done. Soups and burgers are great. I ordered a variety of appetizers for a group of friends the other day ad they were completely devoured. I called them and asked if I could bring over a group of ten right away at 9:30 on a Wednesday. I wanted a low table, room for my mobility scooter, and near tv to watch the hockey game. It was their Quizzo (trivia) night and they were fairly busy. But NO PROBLEM. They accommodated everything we wanted. They even let us play Quizzo, even though we missed the first round. Waitresses were friendly. They teamed up to deliver our food quickly and at the same time. I have to say, we always liked Bailey's. We had not expected much at the last minute. We had great fun. My opinion of Bailey's has made it a go-to place for me and my groups.

Had been a huge fan of this place. Normally grab drinks and smoke a cigar out on the balcony. Went last night to order food, and was for the first time totally sober. I ordered the wings and watched as the young lady in the kitchen rubbed her hands through her hair and bare handed my entire order into the deep fryer and then filled and placed two ziplock bags of wings in the fridge all without even attempting to wash her hands or put on a pair of gloves.

Maybe I should just keep getting drunk there and I'll ignore the cleanliness issues in the kitchen.

:-I

Actually was turned on to this place not too long ago. The owners are very down to earth and they make the wine buying experience very easy and non intimidating. The back bar and the outdoor space is now really nice. I honestly feel like this place is a hidden gem, with tons of personality and potential. 

Big time spot, with really great people. Will definitely remain  a loyal customer.

Came here tonight on a whim. Started with the Cadillac Margarita and it was huge. Shared it with my lady. I must say that this may be one of the best Margaritas that I've had in the city. A whole lot better than Juan's or Superior Grill.

We started with the wings and they were great. A great mix of heat and perfectly fried chicken. I had the Big Ass Burrito and it was awesome. My lady got the tacos. She liked the chicken tinga the best, the other varieties were kind of average. I would definitely come back here. Anxious to see what Taco Tuesday is all about.

Great spot for Mexican on St. Charles.

Our go to spot for crawfish. We get the crawfish and all of the sides that we like (Corn, Potatoes, Sausage, & Turkey Necks) Sometime the spice can get to be a bit unbearable, buy today they were spot on! I can't wait until we get further along in the season so the crawfish can be bigger.

Big props to these guys for sticking ONLY with Louisiana crawfish. Last week they wouldn't sell the Chinese frozen stuff because of our bad weather.

Normally I don't venture into these parts. But a friend invited us out for celebratory dinner and drinks, and we obliged. A bit stuffy for my taste but the service was impeccable. The table shared sweetbreads, scallops and oysters with brie, and the BBQ shrimp. The appetizers were just okay. My oysters were really gritty. 

For our main course we had the filet, lamb chops, duck and the drum. The drum was phenomenal. The lamb chops and filet were cooked well but left a bit to be desired seasoning wise. It was all accompanied by some Knob Creek and some awesome Cabernet. 

I'll probably stay away because I don't drive a Bentley nor ride in a limo. But this place was a cool change of pace.

Was headed to another spot and passed this place last night. I had always wondered what the vibe of this place was, as I pass it daily to get to work. 

Ended up turning a quick U turn to have a cocktail at Treo. I must say the entire scene on the inside of this place caught me off guard. From the fancy door as you enter, to the art gallery on the 2nd floor. It seemed like this was kind of an oasis in the middle of Tulane Ave. We didn't order food, but the menu looked interesting. We ended up going outside to relax and smoke some cigars as we talked and enjoyed our cocktails. This area was really nice. Adorned with wooden decking and also restored church pews, I immediately felt at home. One of the bartenders came out and talked to us and I remembered her from serving us at their sister bar on Banks St. 

I've read numerous reviews that reference the fact that this establishment does not cater to the neighborhood's members, and I totally agree. But I'm certain that the owners had no desire to do that. They are probably hedging their bets that this neighborhood will continue to evolve as many neighborhoods are doing city wide. Its a very sad reality, but this city is changing QUICKLY before all of our eyes. 

But back to the space. I would go back again. Mainly because I like places that are chill and allow me to smoke a good stogie and drink a brew. I'll update this review once I try something from the kitchen.

Came back this past Sunday to sit out on the balcony and have cigar. Waited for a while despite being one of two people seated at the bar. Ordered a round of drinks, and carried them out to the other folks in my party. All was well until one of the young ladies noticed her white wine had a lipstick ring that wend around the ENTIRE glass.  

I guess I'm just a sucker for ambience and a good outdoor area. I'll be back, but I'll eat before I come, and I'll pack my flask!

Came to give this place a try. Had just recently been to Grimaldi's in BR and wanted to keep the pizza itch going. This place was a disaster from the beginning. Our table of three was seated and we place orders. Well, to our dismay about fifteen minutes after ordering the server came back and informed us that they were out of wings. No problem, I totally understand that this happens in restaurants. Well it took almost an hour for a kids pepperoni and our other pizza to come out. The server brought us complimentary truffle chips for our wait. Well... these ended up being Zaps chips drenched in something, I'm not sure what the hell it was. They were absolutely gross. 
By the time the pies came out I was starving. The pizza had no flavor and the crust was the equivalent to eating a thin sponge. My seven year old hated his pie too. (And this dude eats EVERYTHING)

This was a huge disappointment. No chance I'll be back there.

Normally not a big fan of this place, first because I think it's super dirty, secondly I just have never liked the taste of their food.

BUT TODAY!!!!!! This was an awesome visit. Had to get some wings for my boys party this evening. As I drove up a guy tried to sell me a brake tag, a copy of 5 different movies that are still in theaters and a pair of socks. Before I pulled the handle of the door, a guy try to sell me some pralines. After I got the food, a sat there and people watched for about 10 minutes. This was definitely dinner and a movie!

I came to Kubi's for a networking event last night at about 7:15PM. When I got there to my surprise the place was packed. The turnout for this event was awesome. 

Kubi's has definitely a dive feel, and look, but I soon got over that. I ordered my first round of cocktails, which were taken care of by our hosts, and started to move around the room. About ten minutes I suddenly felt like I was in Las Vegas in August! It was sooooo hot in here I had to shed my jacket. I looked around the room and just about everybody was sweating due to the extremely high temperature in this place. After about 45 minutes I couldn't take it any longer. I went and stood near the door to try and cool off... But wait, we are in New Orleans in June! It was hot by the door too!

I'm not sure if we caught this place on a night where there were just too many people for the air conditioner to keep up with, or if this place is just that much of a dive. The drinks were fairly priced and the food looked okay, but I just couldn't get a good groove going because this place was absolutely steaming hot!

Went today to get that seafood fix. Naturally they only had frozen LA crawfish as the season is over.  Ended up getting a couple of pounds of shrimp that were a bit forgetful. 

I think I'll stick to getting their crawfish when the season is in, as that is definitely where Broadview shines.

I'm here pretty often. Below average food, but the Typhoon is just enough to get me where I need to be after a long day of work. 

The ambience is cool with the Catholic league football jerseys lining the walls, and some New Orleans themed art in the dining area. 

It's cool that you can really create your own vibe with the jukebox.

An absolute disaster. Pizzas took forever to make and it seems as if they threw the jalapeños on the pie after it came out of the oven. The wings were just sitting in the sauce, they were too lazy to toss them. And I watched as the staff argued in the back while bounce music played in the background. WTF?!

Never ever going back.

So disappointed, as I wanted to love this place. We got two pies and an order of wings. The pizzas tasted like any run of the mill frozen take and bake. The wings were soggy. 

I will try them again because they are so close to the house, but I'm a bit nervous to waste the money.

Had my birthday party at this place when they were in the old location. Visited today to check on this new location. Very nice and very spacious. Good selection of sticks in the humidor. Full service bar and the young ladies came to my table to take drink orders throughout my visit.

Would come back to see what this place is like for a Saints game.

Went over to watch MNF. The place was empty. The young man in the humidor was extremely helpful. I knew what I was smoking and he took care of me very quickly. I know it is the new law but I hate having to smoke outside at a cigar bar. The gentlemen that worked outside was great and he started two of the large heaters for me and I enjoyed the game. This place could be a great spot for the neighborhood. I'm looking forward to coming back to see how the food is from the kitchen.

Cool spot with a funky location on Tchoup. We were able to find street parking, but I'm sure this could have been a challenge if we weren't lucky. 

The ordering process was easy enough. I really enjoyed the margaritas. That's pretty much where it went down hill. I ordered a chicken bowl, and the lady ordered tacos. It seems as if there isn't any seasoning used in the entire establishment. Not sure if I'd go back, as there are more options in this category that actually season their food. 

The ambiance was cool, but unfortunately their food  wasn't up to par.

Wasn't bad, I went there after a work event at East Jeff Stadium. Ordered the jambalaya rolls. They were pretty good. I was the only patron at the bar and I found that to be a bit strange. It was early evening and all of the TVs were turned off. I found it odd that with all of the seating and such a beautiful bar, that nothing was being shown on the televisions. 

I later learned that the owner does not agree with athletes kneeling during the anthem, therefore sports can not be shown in the bar area.   Just a heads up if you want to eat at the bar and watch sports. 

Overall a decent place to grab appetizers.

ij9_0CYVnc04ekIH0pKr-g.review_text: We had the original grouper sandwich, which is deep fried to a crispy brown, beyond golden. The grilled grouper was delicious as well, and I would probably go for grilled next time-which says a lot for the fresh factor of this sandwich. Service was excellent, and the outside seating was nice. Impressed. Planning to return soon for grouper tacos.

Total hole in the wall, t-shirt 'n flip flops kind of place. Local clams steamed in butter and garlic and served with ciabatta bread, fish spread with crackers, and fresh-caught snapper tacos...will definitely return.
Dirty plates at breakfast buffet, so when we asked for clean ones, they wiped them out with a dirty dish towel. The view is great, might be good to go for drinks and appetizers.

Shrimp n grits, just average. Huevos Rancheros was really good. Service was excellent, coffee -meh, swampy. LOL if only these places would use filtered water, the coffee would be so much better. I would definitely return here, so many good choices on the menu.
Oysters Rockefeller and Chicago style oysters, along with hot peel n eat shrimp...great place, definitely will return.
I had the chocolate pancakes and Jay had the Lox Benedict. Both were way more than we could possibly eat, and scrumptious. This is another definite return-to place.
Fried grouper sandwich and grilled grouper sandwich -excellent. Fries were crispy. We sat out on the porch and watched the people go by.
Breakfast pizza was excellent, Greek omelet was, too. This one is right beside the public beach access, easy walking distance from most area hotels on the beach. Roomy, clean, mature wait staff.
Fried grouper bites, grilled grouper sandwich, and fried conch. All excellent. This place was featured on Diners, Drive-ins and Dives.

Grouper sandwich is huge! Fish tacos were good, there are two and they are priced just right around $7. Fries were not as crisp as I like, but still good. We will go back for breakfast (includes Bloody Mary and mimosas).

First, pulled into the parking lot and realized we came here last year, only it was PJs then. They have now moved across the street and LuLu has taken over at this spot. We scored a free appetizer (smoked fish spread) for checking in on Yelp. This is like tuna salad, but made with flaky smoked white fish, mayo and spices.  Spread it on a cracker and top with hot sauce...good stuff. Next, we had a dozen Chicago style oysters, which means they were topped with Parmesan and butter and maybe some Old Bay. They are small but delicious. For our entree we had scallops, grilled shrimp and blackened grouper. Everything was delicious and not over-priced. I thought the blackened grouper was really salty (and I'm usually the one who adds salt to everything). I would have gone five stars if it had been more peppery and less salty. The atmosphere  here  is very casual, ladies, no makeup required.

This little retro candy and ice cream shop is right across the street from Villa Madiera, so we walked over for an after dinner ice cream cone. I had the chocolate brownie and he had the praline pecan, and both were excellent.

This is a Jimmy Buffett margaritaville type of place. Mussel appetizer is delicious. It comes in a huge plate with a mildly spicy sauce and crusty bread for dipping in the sauce. My husband liked the stuffed grouper, but I was immediately turned off by the celery mixed with the crabmeat. I had one of the seafood dishes with mahimahi, shrimp and scallops over yellow rice and Cajun sauce. It was ok, nothing to write home about. The bread was served with real butter, so that makes up for a lot in my book. They sang happy birthday at least three times while we were there, all the while blowing into a loud conch shell. Very noisy dinner place. Service was good.
Cuban sandwich and shrimp/oyster poBoy were delicious. Best meal we have had here this week. We wish we had found it sooner.

We usually have pizza at home on Friday nights, so we decided vacation Fridays should be no different. This place was recommended above all other pizza in the area, so we had to try it. They have outdoor seating, but it was still 90 degrees at 6 pm so we ate inside. I love the fact that I can go into a restaurant in Florida and not freeze to death after a hot day in the sun. The temperature was just right, and w had a nice booth by a window. We had the small Greek salad, which is a lot like the salad from Olive Garden, but better. The small was more than enough for two of us. We ordered the small New York style pepperoni pizza, which was three small to average sized pieces each, and was plenty after having the salad. I loved the crisp crust, although I understand why some say it is tough if you don't eat it right out of the oven. They do not have sweet tea, so I only gave them four stars

Excellent meal on our first night in Belleair. Grouper Picatta was amazing, as well as the shrimp over fried green tomatoes with feta and black olives. Nice atmosphere sitting on the heated porch with Christmas lights on the palm trees. A definite change from the cold snowy mountains of East TN.
Excellent gnocchi , bread with olive oil, lasagna and spaghetti carbonara. No room for dessert.

Lox omelet could have been good, but I ate first half wondering where the cream cheese was, only to discover at least a half block of cheese was dumped on the other end. Jay's bacon Benedict was excellent. Huge serving a fruit looked beautiful on the plate but something they had cleaned the grapes with causes a strange reaction on my tongue, and did the same to Jay. Made it feel like it was burned, and very dry mouth.

imGIfSLkI7zslRrc8VfPcA.review_text: really imaginative takes on classic tapas dishes.  knowledgable servers and great mixed-drink list.  It can get a little noisy at peak hours, but well worth it!!

Place was just "ok."  staff was very nice, but overall it seems to be just somewhat fancier version of a neighborhood burger joint.  They have good "adult" milkshakes, but even those I felt I could make at home with a bit of effort.  I say best for a late-night drunk fix, but not worth the trip

Veggie wings were mind blowing!!!  People at our table were not even vegetarian and talked about how it was one of the best foods they have eaten in a while.  Really unbelievable flavor and texture.  Service staff was forgetful at times, and the overall vibe of the place is more like a local bar with tables.  However, those veggie wings are worth the trip anywhere!!

The food is strong. Well sourced ingredients and thoughtful preparation. I have never had a bad food experience at this owner's restaurants. The onion rings were served in a greaseless panko crust. The burger was well cooked. The salmon was smoked and flash fried, all well done and clearly made with care.

My review has to do with the service.  Upon arrival, they canceled our reservation without cause other than "someone called to cancel." When pressed,  the hostess could not provide details; who called, when, the name/number used. Only that we no longer had a reservation. It was placed on us to figure out what to do.
After a lenghty discussion. We were then seated in an empty room. We had to ask for bread. We had to ask for water. We had to ask for menus. We had to ask for our waiter, water refills, drink menus, etc. All the while, there were multiple staff members idling around.
The staff needs to be MUCH better trained for a restaurant that is not inexpensive.
The best cappuccino I have ever had in south jersey. Staff is knowledgeable and eager to help

FANTASTIC pizzas and salads. Everytbing tastes freshly made to order.  I especially like the kale Caesar. The kale retains its crunch and is nicles offset by The mustard-based Caesar dressing.  The pizza dough is made in house and has The right about of char when baked in the brick oven .The place is spotless. I go here 1-2 a week and have never seen any traces of clutter. All told, a really strong lunch spot

My friends and I have a club in which we hit every south-jersey area brewery throughout the year. Some we get to more than once, for others once is more than enough.  In my opinion, Berlin Brewery is one of the three best in SJ. 
They offer a strong selection of base beers,   not just two or three styles and the rest is a variation of a theme.  Their beers are also inventive and nuanced. Specifically,  their English Session and Hefeweissen beers are flavorful, and layered with subtleties.  These are not one-note pours.   
The same holds true when you get into their higher abv selection. The humble bitch and peach ipa offer a strong, refreshing drink with well considered ingredients.  If I had to offer any constructive feedback it is that they are not the most friendly behind the bar. When I have asked questions and tried to engage in conversation,  the bartenders and owners do not seem that interested in talking shop.
I'll focus my time on my friends sitting next to me and the beer.
 Cheers!

My friends and I have a club in which we visit all the south jersey breweries. Eclipse is one of the three best in the area.
Their selection is deep in style and broad in scope.  The owner is incredibly welcome and friendly. It feels that you are a guest in his home.
This is local brewing at its finest; a high quality product made with loving care
This is the best brewery in south jersey.  I think about their beers all the time; the complexity,  the quality, the diversity of their offered styles.

Fantastic breakfast sandwiches! Sourdough Bread is made  in house and is crusty and fresh. The French toast is custard-like; more a gourmet dessert than your standard.
Super friendly staff,  clean open kitchen,  wood fired oven.....eat here now!

We just ate here, on the way to the Rays Game. What a fantastic find! The falafel was fresh, full of a tahini sauce that offered a garlicy-lemon snap that woke us out of the afternoon heat.  We also ordered the babaganush; redolent of smoke with a nicely blended consistancy. The staff was a delight; offering free samples of the homemade hot sauce.
It's only two blocks from Tropicana Field...why would you eat anywhere else?

We were here the Sunday of opening weekend. Very well done takes on classics. The East Coast IPA was a nice balance of juicy with a slightly citric bitter finish. The West Coast IPA was sufficiently bitter, but not overpowering. The Oktoberfest tasted like buttered biscuits with jam....delicious!!
The vibe was more a neighborhood tavern than a typical brewery. Very friendly staff and plenty of locals.  I cant wait to see what they'll brew next!!

We have been here several times. The drinks are very well made with imaginative riffs on the classics. The food is also well done. The place is a bit pricey for the suburbs (3 drinks and apps ran us around $70 about a week ago).
How can you not LOVE this place???? Open year round and offering tasty custard-based treats. Cash only!

The selection of spirits is really difficult to beat. Wineworks has your standards, but also a very deep and broad library of esoteric bottles.  If you like making higher concept drinks, chances are that you will find the ingredients here.  
The beer inventory has, also, evolved nicely.  There is an elaborate display of cans (many local) as well as larger bombers. 
What stops me from providing 5 stars is that the higher level employees are not that helpful.  The stock and checkout workers are great. However, when talking to a purchaser or manager, there is the feeling that they would rather not interact with customers

The brown spirit selection is amazing.  The staff has done an.uncreeinle.job amassing a deep library of bourbon, scotch and whisk(e)y. Everyone is very friendly and eager to steer customers to the bottle that meets their needs

This is the best italian restaurant in south Jersey.  This is not an Italian-American red sauce type of place (there are plenty of terrific options for that in the area). Instead, this is an upscale restaurant for italian gourmands! You can taste the quality in the housemade pasta and the daily made sauces.  Each ingredient sings in the creative takes in italian classics
Salud!

We have been here before. Something changed....and we are not going back.  
It took 40min for the appetizer to arrive. We were offered bread but it never came.  Each of us was given just one glass of water for the entirety of the meal (i.e. no refills on water).
The hot food was served cold. The cold food was tepid. Brown avocados in a salad. Ceasar salad was from a bag. Fresh Vegetables on the kids meal was frozen medley (and poorly defrosted). Kid's portion of the wood grilled salmon was slightly bigger than a 50cent piece.
I get that, in these times, it's hard to staff a restaurant. Firebirds should, then, set a cap on reservations; every table was filled when we were seated. From start to finish,  all the flaws were glaringly clear. 
We ordered 2 adult salads and 1 child's meal. 1 appetizer, 1 drink...75.00 (not including tip).  We all finished the meal deeply dissatisfied and felt it was a wasted evening

Terrific food! We went here on Sunday (today). The falafel sandwich was a well balanced blend of crisp falafel, cool salad and creamy garlic sesame paste. The tahini shake was a real treat in the summer sun. The shawarma fries were covered with a spicy mix that provided a depth of flavor

 We'll be back (again and again)!
Super friendly owner and strong coffee made in a variety of authentic pours. The espresso was clean and bright.  The iced coffee was bold and flavorful.  Try the pastries!

We bought a red velvet cake for a backyard BBQ.  We walked in without calling ahead and had a nice fresh selection available.

Packing substantial flavor, these cakes mean business!  We were thrilled with the dense,  moist body and the flavorful, airy topping.  A medium cake served 8 with plenty left over for the next day's breakfast.

This is a newer entry to the Center City Dining Scene. With that said, there are a few kinks to work out (the staff is a bit forgetful, dishes were presented without some accompaniments). However, please look past those smaller items as this place is fantastic!
The chef and head bartender both bring a unique set of flavors to the menu (tamarind salmon with bitter herbs, smoked rye wild fashioned with cardamom syrup).  Even the water is infused with a hint of citrus(?) cucumber(?) rose(?) keeping in the intriguing spirit of the place.
The staff is super friendly and seem genuinely excited to work there; citing their favorites meals (and describing the dishes with passion). Go now before they get to successful and you have to wait for a table!!

This store offers a deep and diverse selection of wine and spirits. I will walk down the well-stocked gin, rum and tequila isles and find bottles I have never seen before (micro distillers, limited edition releases, etc). The shelves are well lit and features well detailed descriptions of many of the products.
The beer selection can use some work; there are not that many individual bottles (mostly packaged 6packs).  All told, a great store for both mass market as well as unique finds among the wine and spirit set.

A classic slice shop. The pies are hand-tossed with large, floppy slices. The sicilian reminds me of a Chicago-style deeper dish with a crusty, frico speckled rim. One bite, though, and it reveals itself as something wholly other;   made light and pillowy with buttery pockets of air.

iqM0wQ-ECvRdE6rA6c2tZA.review_text: Great experience!  Was at Silver Saddle for dinner on October 7th, and everything met my expectations.  Even though they were busy, we were seated right away, and our server was friendly and efficient.  She checked on us throughout our meal to see if everything was fine, and to see if we needed anything.  I started with French Onion soup, which was delicious, then ordered medium-rare prime rib, with baked potato, as my entree.  The quality of all was excellent!  I would highly recommend Silver Saddle.  The only downside would be the parking, which can be a challenge, but if you arrive early it should be fine.

After reading mixed reviews of Kon-Tiki, I went in not expecting too much, but was pleasantly surprised!!  Ended up going there twice with my brother during our visit to Tucson!  Both visits were mid-afternoon (October 6th & 8th).  Melissa the bartender was great.....attentive and friendly to everyone.  The manager, Louie, was also there during our first visit, and I had cool conversation with him about various tiki bars.  I got totally "bombed" during our second visit, as I ordered both a Blue Hawaii and a Scorpion for one.  Both drinks were great, as were the Original Mai-Tai and Planter's Punch I had during my first visit.  Also met some regular patrons, who had good things to say about the place (thanks for the great conversation Marcos!). Will definitely go back again (and again) next time I'm in Tucson!  Thanks again Melissa....you are a superb bartender!

Was at Guadalajara Original Grill on October 8th, and had a great experience!  All the food was fresh and delicious, and the service friendly and efficient.  The salsa prepared table-side is the highlight, and can be spiced to your liking.  I ordered the Plato Ranchero, which was delicious and filling.  I was impressed with the entire dining experience, and will definitely return next time I visit Tucson.

Had a cool visit to this place on October 4th.  Patrick was the bartender, and I ordered a Mai-Tai, which was excellent.  Decor and ambience is tropical/tiki.  We went early, so the place was pretty quiet, but overall was a good experience.  I would recommend The Hut for good tropical drinks!

El Charro definitely lives up to its reputation, and served some of the best Mexican food I had during my visit to Tucson.  I ordered combo #4, which is seafood....grilled shrimp taco, seafood enchilada, and green corn tamal.  All was prepared fresh, and quality and taste were excellent.  Friendly and attentive service by server Rob.  I highly recommend El Charro!

Had dinner at La Indita on October 4th, and was favorably impressed.  The restaurant is very simple in decor, and food is excellent! They also make their own tortilla chips, which are served with a special salsa.  I would definitely return to La Indita!

Stayed at the Best Western Royal Sun Inn for 5 nights, from October 4th-8th, 2016.  The motel is conveniently located for visiting central Tucson, especially 4th Avenue, Downtown, and Old Town areas.  My room (#210) was large, clean and tidy, and desk staff was friendly and efficient.  Complimentary breakfast is served daily to all guests in the adjacent Royal Sun Restaurant.  The desk clerk provides you with a daily breakfast ticket to give to the wait staff at the restaurant, where you can order from the special free-breakfast menu, or receive $2.00 off anything on the regular breakfast menu.  Street work was being done on Stone Avenue during my visit, which was a little inconvenient, but you could easily enter the motel from the back or side streets.  One downside is that freight trains pass by about 1/4 mile from the motel, and most seemed to be at night.  I would suggest wearing ear-plugs if you are a light sleeper.  Would definitely stay at this motel again when in Tucson, despite the train noise.

Visited Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29 for the first time on February 21st, during a week-long vacation to New Orleans.  The bar is located at the rear of the Bienville House Hotel, facing North Peters St.  I was favorably impressed with this place!!  My brother and I came back two more times that week, and got well acquainted with Sam the bartender.  Also met bartender Brad, who is also a cool guy. During my three visits I tried the Nui-Nui, Latitude 29, Hell in the Pacific, Rum Barrel, Mai-Tai, and Oaxacan Sour....all were EXCELLENT cocktails, mixed to perfection and beautifully garnished by Sam!  The bar has great tiki decor, and is a relaxing place to hang-out and meet people while in New Orleans.  Thumbs up to a great tiki bar experience!!  Definitely hope to come back again sometime!

Visited this bar while in New Orleans in late-February.  In mid-afternoon the place was quiet and relaxing, and the bartenders friendly.  Had a Roman Punch (sans the toasted marshmallow), which was a very refreshing cocktail on a warm day!

Pat O'Brien's is a "must-see" while visiting New Orleans. The place is famous for their Hurricane cocktails and the flaming fountain in the patio.  Visited here in late-February....my previous visit being in 1997 on my last trip to New Orleans.  Had a Planter's Punch instead of a Hurricane this time, and enjoyed the nighttime ambiance of the patio.  Music was a bit loud....and would have preferred jazz to the raggae that was being played!

Visited here in late February and was pleased with the quiet ambiance and the cocktails.  Tried a Gin Rickey for the first time, and was not disappointed.  Live piano music makes the place classy and enjoyable.

Had a very good lunch here in late-February....hadn't been here since my previous trip to New Orleans in 1997.  Dress code has definitely eased-up since my last visit!  Saw people in shorts & t-shirts here at lunch, which would not have been allowed 20 years ago.  We were dressed "nicely" since we planned to go to Galatoire's, but discovered that they couldn't seat us until 1pm when we checked-in at 10:30am.  Decided to eat at Antoine's instead since it was nearby.  I had the 3-course "$20.18 Winter Lunch Special" - Shrimp Bisque, Oysters Bonne Femme Biscuit, and Pecan Bread Pudding.  All three courses were very good.  After lunch we toured the restaurant, which is definitely worth seeing.  One of the maintenance men on the second floor took the time to guide us through the various upstairs rooms and explain the decor of each, and also took us out onto the second-floor gallery facing St. Louis Street.  The wine cellar is immense....extending for almost a city block!

Had a very good meal at Arnaud's in late-February, during my first visit to this restaurant.  The decor is classic and timeless, but the main dining room gets quite noisy as the restaurant fills-up with diners....the vintage tile floor is not the best for acoustics!  Since the restaurant is celebrating its 100th anniversary this year, I decided to try some classic items on the menu.  I started off with a Sazerac cocktail, which was a bit too strong for me, so I didn't finish it....I'm not usually a whiskey/bourbon drinker.  For a starter I had Turtle Soup, followed by the main entree: Trout Amandine, with a side of Souffle Potatoes....all were excellent! Dessert was Lemon Ice Glace.  Service was very good, if a bit on the more formal side.  This is a restaurant that ranks up there with Antoine's!

Heard many good things about this restaurant, which opened in 1990, and the chef/owner Susan Spicer, so had to give it a try during my New Orleans vacation in late-February.  Had a 6:30pm reservation, and within an hour the restaurant was practically full.  Asked to meet Susan Spicer, since she was in the kitchen at Bayona that evening....she was overseeing a large private party on the patio, but made time to come out of the kitchen to meet my brother and I and chat for a few minutes - she also made her apologies for there being a slight delay in the food arriving to our table due to the private party taking precedence.  I started with the Quail Salad, followed by King Salmon, and finished with the Banana Tres Leches. The food was excellent, and meeting Susan Spicer made the meal all the more special.  Thank you for a great experience, Susan!

Was last at Brennan's in 1997, and went again on my recent trip to New Orleans in late-February....so glad that I did!  My brother and I decided to go again for breakfast as we did 20 years ago.  Everything was excellent, and the service was impeccable!  Brennan's has an army of servers to wait the tables, so you are never in want of anything.  I started out with a Ramos Gin Fizz, which is very light and refreshing with a slight lemon flavor.  The waiter brought us each a sample of Asparagus Soup to try, which I followed with an order of Turtle Soup....the best Turtle soup I had while in New Orleans!  For my main meal I had the Eggs Hussarde, which was very good.  Brennan's is definitely a must-do for breakfast when visiting New Orleans!

Broussard's is considered one of the New Orleans "big four" (Antoine's, Arnaud's, and Galatoire's being the other three).  This place looks elegant, but has no dress-code. The food and service were excellent during my visit there with my brother in late-February!  Alexandria, who took my cocktail order, suggested the Hurricane, which is sweet and much better than the Pat O'Brien's version (in my opinion). Next I had the Lump Crab Ravigote salad, followed by the main entree of Gulf Drumfish Bonaparte, and Bittersweet Chocolate Pave for dessert....all three were delicious! Would definitely go back to Broussard's again for a meal....they seem to be one of the famous New Orleans restaurants that many visitors overlook, and I am so glad that we gave them a try! Thanks for a memorable dining experience!

My brother and I were here in late-February for lunch and I was most impressed by the service as well as the food.  I started with a glass of Sangria, which was perfect in flavor. I opted for the 3-course Creole Luncheon, which included Turtle Soup, Barbecued Gulf Shrimp, and Creole Bread Pudding Souffle for dessert.  The food quality was excellent, served by a well-orchestrated staff.  The manager came around to each table to greet and chat with everyone while we were there.  I would highly recommend Commander's Palace as a great New Orleans dining experience!

Had dinner at The Court of Two Sisters on my first night in New Orleans in late-February.  The evening was warm and comfortable and (noisy) fans were on in the patio, which were eventually turned off, making for a quieter dining experience. Started with the prepared-tableside Caesar Salad, followed by Crawfish Napolean as the entree.  The food was excellent and our server attentive.

Had a great lunch at Creole House on a visit to New Orleans in late-February.  Started with a Streetcar Punch cocktail, followed by Crawfish Etouffee as the main course. Food and service were excellent, and I would definitely eat here again!

Felix's has always been known for quality seafood at reasonable prices, and it is still so. Was previously here for dinner in 1997 during a trip to New Orleans. This time just went in for Char Grilled Oysters after dinner at Oceana Grill. The oysters took almost an hour to come out from the kitchen, since the restaurant was very busy, but were worth the wait. You can't beat Felix's for good food in a casual setting!

Had dinner at Mr. Ed's in late-February during my vacation in New Orleans.  Started with a Debbie's Rum Punch, followed by Crawfish Pies appetizer, and a Shrimp Po-Boy as the main course.  Food was good and service attentive and friendly.

This restaurant & bar is a New Orleans favorite, and I'm glad that I tried it for the first time back in 1997 on a previous trip, and returned again for lunch during my recent trip in late-February.  The Pimm's Cup cocktail and the Muffuletta sandwich are the things to order here....the Pimm's Cup is cool and refreshing, and the Muffuletta is delectable!  Great ambiance in both the patio and the restaurant.....I highly recommend Napolean House!

Had a very good experience at Oceana Grill during my vacation to New Orleans in late-February.  The restaurant was very busy at dinner and we were given the option of eating upstairs in one of the smaller and quieter dining rooms, which was a great choice!  Alex was our server and he suggested a very good cocktail to me - the Tropical Storm - which wasn't too potent, since I had already consumed two fairly strong tiki cocktails at a bar prior to dinner. Started with Crab Cakes as an appetizer, which were very good.  Alex offered the Soft Shell Crab Platter as an option not on the menu, when I mentioned that I really loved soft shell crab....the crab was good, but very slightly mushy since it was obviously frozen and not fresh, but had good flavor.  I would recommend Oceana Grill for its extensive menu and very good service!

Met a friend here for lunch in February of 2018 and was favorably impressed. Service was friendly and efficient and the food quite good. I had the Trio Salad - which includes separate portions of chicken salad, potato salad, and bean salad, served with french bread. We sat at a table located on the veranda overlooking Audubon Park and the experience was relaxing and enjoyable. Definitely give Audubon Clubhouse Cafe a try if you are visiting Audubon Park!

j8LUe66fZ5ckT9pf6s0ouA.review_text: Customer service is lacking. Waited at least 15 minutes just to be acknowledged. Waitresses were walking by and serving tables, but did not acknowledge us. After we finally sat down, we had to wait another 5 minutes to get menus. I noticed another couple waiting to get seated, but finally decided to leave. There were a lot of empty tables, so I'm not sure why waitresses ignored customers. I was excited to come try this place out, especially after the renovations. Just like my rating, "Meh. I've experienced better." I ordered my Cowboy steak medium rare, but it came out well done. Will not come back because of the customer service.

Great for the private karaoke party rooms. One of a few restaurants with karaoke that actually has up to date songs. You just have to make sure you get there early. However food quality can be better.
With unfriendly staff and average tasting dishes, I'd rather go to other restaurants in chinatown. They have nice private party rooms, but songs aren't up to date.
Food is excellent. I believe it's one of chinatown's best eateries. Only reason it didn't get 5 stars is because the service can be better. But it IS chinatown...
This is a big restaurant and it is always busy. Love coming here for dim sum. The line is worth the wait.
One of my favorite spots for dim sum. They have delicious dishes. It is worth the wait. Staff can be more friendly, but this IS chinatown.
Been here a couple times and was never disappointed. Service is great, just like their food.  Salmon burger is delicious.
Graffiti bar in the backyard is awesome. Friendly staff.
It gets pretty loud, but love their guacamole.
Margarita pitchers are great. Burritos are HUGE. Tacos are delicious. Friendly staff. Never once disappointed.
Hidden gem in south philly. Food is delicious. May be hard to find parking on weekends.
Ample parking. Pho is great. One of my top places for Pho in south philly.
Great Pho with good service. Plenty of options on the menu.
Pho is ok. I usually go elsewhere for Pho, but the food here is good. Parking is horrible.
Good food. Good service. Great place to eat outside when the weather is warm.
Saw a show on tv that renovated this place... they shouldn't have stopped. A side window was cracked. Service was sub-par. Food was ok. Will not be coming back.
Burgers here are delicious. The beer list is at least 10 pages long. Never disappointed. Recommended stop when partying in olde city.
Went here for lunch. Food is good. It gets pretty crowded since the place is so small.
Heard great things about this place. Maybe my expectations were high, but the burgers here were OK.
Lobster mac and cheese, calamari, and steaks were all delicious (especially the filet mignon). Steaks were cooked to perfection. Staff is friendly, would definitely go back soon.

Though I have been there a couple times, this establishment just opened up. Been to the previous thai restaurant there once and never went back. My wife and I was hoping this place would be the go-to thai spot in delco. After a couple visits and a couple different dishes, I would say I am impressed. Their Pad Thai isn't the best I've had, however it is really good compared to others. The drunken noodles are really good as well. Wasn't a big fan of their soft shell crab dish. Their curry dishes, I think, are their best entrees. Full of flavor and taste. As for apps, we like the fried calamari and spring rolls, but thought the beef salad and dumplings were sub-par. Lets hope this place sticks around because we would definitely go back. Service was great. Decor needs work, but they did just open. We'll see.

Went here for lunch on a weekday. Service was great. Loved the dog pictures on the wall. The Good Dog Burger itself was really good, however the fries that came with it was subpar. Maybe I got a batch that was at the end of the bag. However, I will def be coming back.

Since this is an all you can eat bbq restaurant, we were excited for our first visit and came hungry. After being here for an hour, we were still hungry. We made reservations and were seated within 20 minutes. Our first dish (appetizer side) didn't come out until 40 minutes after being seated. Don't really understand why since you have to cook your own food. I haven't yelped in years, but felt I had to for this experience since I found this place via yelp. It's hard to enjoy yourself when food isnt coming to the table in a timely manner. Good news once the raw selection comes out, it's only another 15 minute wait for the next dish.

jYOK8bu9lIxkVoKvwPC7ig.review_text: Really good fries...about a dozen varieties from Spanish, Irish, Mexican, pizza & more.  Wings ( their specialty) were great.  Our waitress, Camilla, was quick, attentive, friendly & helpful.  Plus she was as cute as a button.  Bathrooms were clean.  50% off wings if you check in on Yelp!!  We shall return.

Ok, never had roasted cauliflower tacos but they are GOOD!  3 corn tortilla with seasoned cauliflower, black bean corn salsa, lime cilantro sauce, topped with fresh lime & served with black beans & rice that was perfect.  Jenna does a great job with a busy bar on a rainy Saturday.  Almost makes it seem sunny out.

Went last month for Sunday brunch before Rays game opening day.  Excellent Bloody Mary & mimosas since you make them yourself how could they not be.  Nice selection of fruit & juices for the mimosas as well as all kinds of garnishes fir the bloodys.  Bar keeps are there to "suggest" but you literally make your own so YOU control the booze and everything else!  Food was good too.  I'm usually not a huge fan of buffets but this one was fresh with a wide variety of brunch items.  They kept it well replenished when needed.  I'd say the only down side is it gets very busy and the station where you make your drinks can get 6-7 people deep as you can imagine.  We got there before 11...(can't drink before 11 & they are very strict about that) not too bad ...but as we were leaving after 12 it was crazy busy.

Called on a Friday night around 5:30 to see if we could get or if we needed a reservation for 6 people for soon...the girl said if we could be done by 8:30 she could seat us but they'd need the table at 8:30.  No problem we could do that so we walked over.  Now know that we'd been in the French Quarter ALL day.  We were wearing shorts & t-shirts and had a pretty good buzz going.  When we arrived they initially were going to seat us in the dining area to the left, they thought better and took us through the lively bar into the "fun dining area" good call staff.  Our waiter was Renee' and he was hilarious  and knowledgeable about wine and the menu.  We enjoyed sharing stories of New York & family with him...he was our kinda guy.  This is what I'd call a steak place and all of our group got steak except me (not a steak person).  Everyone loved their steaks.  One couple got the porterhouse for 2, the hubs got a ribeye and the others got a ribeye & cowboy??  I got the fish special, a flounder with crab & shrimp on top...the flavor was great but I hadn't been listening that it was a whole fish with bones and I was frustrated after getting a 3rd bone in my mouth & quit eating...they took it off our bill!!  The sides and salads were unique as well.  Mac & cheese was especially tasty.  We were celebrating a birthday and they brought us a slice of cheesecake to share...it was big & rich...teehee...enough for all 6 of us!  I think I would have made myself sick if we had more.  The atmosphere was very nice as well...certainly an upscale restaurant.  We usually prefer a more casual place but this was a nice change of pace.

Went back today...it was great!  We were able to get 2 seats at bar right next to the mimosa/Bloody Mary station and were the envy of all!  Brent was behind the bar with plenty of help(sorry I didn't get names) he was ON IT!! Very attentive, fun and funny.  We wish we lived closer.  Until next time...
