My only complaint was that they took a long time to bring out our food. However, we were a large party with virtually zero wait time, so, really, CAN I complain?

Party Fowl was our introduction to Tennessean hospitality. Friendly and attentive staff. For my meal I ordered the "Brick-Tattooed" chicken, a chicken breast (surprisingly juicy) with sage and goat cheese. It came with a side of sauteed veggies and that was probably my healthiest meal to date in Nashville.

I also treated myself to a drinky drink: The Fowl Language, their take on an Old Fashioned. It was so smooth, had it asked me out on a date, I'd have said yes.

For kicks I also ordered a side of Piggy Chips. They were pretty good, if a tad on the salty side.

Overall, I was pleased with our first stop of our stay here.

Oh. My. Gosh.

This is one place EVERY tourist needs to visit and cross off their list.

This is the epitome of southern food, southern dining, and southern, well, everything. The house is huge and old-looking. There are some house rules that need to be followed (No cell phones at the table, and I heard from another person they were admonished for dropping an f-bomb at the table).

This reminded me of a Yelp event in that everything is served family style. You occupy a chair? You pay meal ticket price. You very well can be sitting with a group of strangers, but by the end of your meal you'll have made lots of new friends.

We came on a Tuesday night, so we had Sweet Tea, Lemonade, and water pitchers waiting for us. Then out came the sides: Green beans, collard greens, squash, corn pudding, coleslaw, mashed potatoes, biscuits, gravy, peach preserves, and probably other stuff I'm forgetting. The main meals were pot roast and probably the best fried chicken I've ever had.

Dessert was banana pudding.

The Science team is coming back here for lunch next week and I definitely will be joining them.

I did not try the food, which if what I'm hearing is correct, is a good thing. We came strictly to have a drink and experience a rooftop bar, and lo and behold, we ended up picking the "highest rooftop bar in Nashville." Of course, we didn't find this out until after we climbed all those stairs and THEN saw there was an elevator. I wanted to die.

The view, however, was stunning! You can see plenty of noteworthy buildings from your perch on the rooftop.

I can't fully give this place 5 stars, because I didn't try the food, nor did I pay for my drink--one of my coworkers did--and he kept pretty mum about the price. I'm sure if I had a better gauge of the flavors and prices I'd be able to rate more accurately, though.

But to me, as my first experience ever in Downtown Nashville, it let me impressed and with a sense of awe over how colorful and musical this city is.

One of the restaurants that kept popping up on my recommended lists on Yelp was The Pharmacy. I figured I might try it on my own during the weekend or something, while everyone here for the Math Committee would want to try something more tourist-friendly. Well, one of the math peeps mentioned The Pharmacy, and I immediately suggested that, yes, it has great reviews and we should go.

Our Lyft driver also said that it's a popular spot among the locals. Bonus!

So we get there and we're told our huge party of eleventy billion (aka 8) would have a 45 min to an hour wait, and this was also my first time using the reservation feature on the Yelp app. Well, we ended up only waiting maybe 20-30 minutes. Pretty rad.

This lovely lit restaurant has a gorgeous "backyard" and, oh, it was the best thing to see fireflies flitting around back there! I haven't seen fireflies in over 20 years!!

Our waitress was super patient with our large group. I got The Pharmacy burger with fries (though I meant to get the Farm one, cause it had eggs, but that error is TOTALLY on me, not the restaurant) and I also got a homemade cream soda. Good lord it was AMAZING. Like if ice cream and soda married and had a perfect refreshing baby. Some coworkers had the Orange Creamsicle one, and it also looked super good.

The original coworker and I shared our fries/tots with each other. The fries had a nostalic taste, like Rally's but if Rally's was better and not as fast-foodish. The tots were crispy and perfectly salted and fluffy on the inside.

My burger was outstanding, though I could only get through half before tapping out. I did take the rest home and eat it as a midnight snackaroo, though. The bun was soft, the meat was juicy, and all the veg was fresh. It was absolutely, definitely, most certainly worth the wait.

We almost gave up and went to the Mexican restaurant across the street, but remembered our "No Mexican food north of Dallas and east of the Mississippi" rule. Plus, once we got a look at the burgers, we were resolved to stay.

I'm in town until the 21st, and if I had to pick a restaurant to revisit with the Science team this week, this would be it.

You know I can't visit a new city without trying at least one coffee shop. I can't do it. I can't.

As soon as I dumped my luggage in my hotel room, I opened my Yelp app to find a nearby coffee shop. The Bowtie Barista was the first one that popped up that was less than 5 miles away. I resolved to go as soon as my meetings wrapped up.

After visiting a plethora if tourist-friendly shops, The Bowtie Barista was a small step inside local living in Nashville. Nestled in a strip mall with a Barber next door, this small and cozy cafe's most notable feature is a felt map of the US with pushpins. They encourage visitors to mark where they're from on the board. I put a purple pin where San Antonio is.

The barista was friendly and also originally from out of town, but had all the kindness and hospitality of a native Tennesseean. She made me a Tennessee White Mocha, and it was sweet and picture-perfect. I also inquired about the bags of coffee for sale, and made a separate purchase to take back home to my coffee club.

I loved the quiet hour I spent here, and although my remaining week here won't allow me to come back, The Bowtie Barista left me with such a positive impression.

Very cute and very subtle with the Harry Potter theme. It was cozy enough to have an engaging conversation with a friend I hadn't seen in over 12 years, and not a whole lot of background noise/chatter to cause a distraction.

I had a butterbeer latte and it was sweet for all the right reasons. It was also beautifully designed, showing the baristas here care just as much about the presentation as they do the flavor of the coffee. (Do it for the 'gram, as I like to say!) For an afternoon snack, I had the avocado toast, and I'm still perplexed over how green the avocado was. Could have used a little more salt, but otherwise, it was tasty and not overly priced.

I am going to try to swing by again before I leave Nashville, but at the very least I'm glad I got to experience another cool little coffee shop in this city.

I'm a Texan through and through, meaning I exclusively (well, 95% of the time) shop at H-E-B. Well. Those don't exist in Tennessee. And Kroger doesn't seem to exist in San Antonio or anywhere south of that. 

I will happily take Kroger as my Grocery Store away from home, though, as I really did forget I wasn't in an HEB while shopping here. There are minute differences, like the size of propel waters, and of course, the generic brands are different, and there's a distinct lack of fresh tortillas and pan dulce (though the rest of their bakery, down to the packaging, looked SUPER familiar!). But overall, it felt like home and I actually went there twice. Lucky me, I caught a cold while up here and had to buy some cold meds. (And allergy meds, just in case I misdiagnosed myself)

Great spot, it was easy to get to, and maybe $5 per Lyft drive.

Augh, gosh. I WANTED to like this place so bad.

My friend and I came here for a couple of beers and to enjoy some music. Lo and behold, the band playing was from Austin, TX! Nice to see some Texans, what with the states' common ground with their love of country music and all. They did a great job.

I had two beers, none of which were impressive to me, and split the burger with my friend. Unfortunately, both the burger and fries were just way too salty for us to enjoy. We were even brushing salt off the bun! I'm sure that was some sort of culinary decision, just not one I necessarily agree with.

Walk the Lime: Good, but I've definitely had better. 
1927: You know, even though IPAs aren't my cuppa, I thought I had developed an appreciation for them. I feel like this undid all of that. :( Sorry, TN. TX takes my Craft Beer Award.

On the other hand, the staff was remarkably wonderful and friendly, and even though I didn't like the beer they suggested, I appreciated their input/opinions anyway.

You could say this place is Legen. . . . . . dairy. Ok, that was an awful HIMYM reference.

After a less than impressive stay at a local brewery, my friend and I decided to quash our sweet teeth at this nearby place. The line was nearly out the door! But since we took a Lyft, we were essentially stranded, so we persevered and were able to order.

This was my first "extra" milkshake. That is, a milkshake so ridiculously overgarnished you HAVE to take pictures of it. (And also explains why it's about $7 more expensive than a normal milkshake)

I must say, though. If I was a boy, I would have been brought to the yard. I ordered the S'mores milkshake and it arrived covered in cloud-like marshmallows, dripping in chocolate sauce, and topped with a large roasted mallow and a graham cracker.

The ordering process was quick and easy, and is designed for minimal line stoppage. You pick your ordering sheet and circle either one of the pre-designed milkshakes, or build your own with the ingredients on the other side of the page. Then you give your sheet to the cashier, they ring you up, give you a number, and find a place to sit. Super easy, super painless, and super delicious.

My friend and I were in complete awe over our tasty little pieces of art. This was definitely one of my favorite stops during my trip to Nashville!

Pretty quiet but a bit on the expensive side. The food was good, too, unless they're catering Mexican food. I just . . . I can't do Mexican Food outside of Texas (or even north of Dallas).

Breakfasts were always fresh and hot. The croissants were far and away my favorite part! They were small and buttery and it was easy to pack away two or more and lose control.

Lunches were a bit more meh, since they catered out business lunches for the week. The BBQ pork, salads, and most of the desserts were quite tasty. (That flan is a crime against humanity, though)

In conjunction with room service, everything was outstanding. My favorite go-to dessert was this chocolate chip brownie with this bourbon vanilla ice cream on top? Oh my stars, that was heaven.

I also dined in Champions twice: Once for breakfast, and I got the buffet. It was delicious! And the other was for dinner, I got the burger. Also fantastic.

I was never too disappointed having to stay in, cause I knew a great (albeit expensive) meal was just a phone call away.

Even just the name "Darfons" sounds so exquisite and expensive!

Darfons is probably -the go to place- for fanciful dining for out of towners, or just the spot for any business gathering. 

My only complaint (and yes, it is my ONLY complaint) was my Old Fashioned was watered down. Everything else was top notch: from my meal, to the atmosphere, to the service.

I ordered the Filet mingon and it came with a side of asparagus and mashed potatoes. I ordered my filet mignon rare, and they did not let me down at all. In fact, my filet was SO TENDER, I didn't even use the steak knife. I had an easier time cutting my beef with a BUTTER knife. The potatoes? Probably the best I've had in recent memory. And the asparagus was a nice, light balance to all the heavy starch and meat.

For dessert I ordered the tiramisu, but I got to sample the bread pudding and the bread pudding was PERFECT. It turned into this silky custard, which is how you know bread pudding is done right.

I'm so glad I made it out to Darfons! If I ever make my way back to Nashville, this is a must-have spot on my itinerary.

Well, I was going to dock a star because they didn't have the mussels in stock and that made my cousin sad, but dammit, everything else was just too fan-damn-tastic.

First of all even though we arrived late due to traffic, they still honored our reservation.

Second, the bartender/waitress was fantastic, and she looked like my other cousin, haha. Her suggestions were top notch.

Starters: Bread with onion butter. The bread was charred but still edible, and that onion butter was divine. Sweet and not overly pungent. We might have hissed when people tried to take our plate away.

Nashville Hot Softshell Crab: HOT, according to my cousin. It LOOKED hot, too, and it looked delicious, too.

Brussels sprouts salad: WOW! I will never look at Brussels sprouts the same ever again. Amazing how frying some of them changes the flavor and texture of the salad. It was bitter and sweet and the cheese added some good sharpness.

My cousin ordered the scallops, can't say much on them cause I didn't try them, but they were lovely looking.

Pork chop: HEYOOOOO that was GOOD STUFF. Perfectly fatty in all the right places, HUGE, and had a super small hint of heat. I loved it. The nuts really elevated that. And the accompanying potatoes were just delicious.

For dessert we had these chocolate chip cookies, and a G version of how I described them: They're better than half the guys I've kissed.

My drinks that night were an Old Fashioned and the bartender suggested something called a Caledonia. I don't remember what was all in it, but she said "If you like bourbon, you'll like this." She was spot on.

Overall it's a bit pricey and the menu isn't that expansive, so I wouldn't recommend it for large groups, but do go if you're a table for 2 or 3. It's a great shareable experience!

This restaurant appears to be a favorite among the Science team, but agh, I was so disappointed.

We were promptly seated due to a reservation we made prior, and were in the music room. While enjoyable, conversation was difficult due to the loudness.

I ordered the Steak and Guinness pastry, which was a bowl of beef tips in guinness and topped with a flaky, fluffy crust of.. something. The flavor was quite bland, though. The pastry in particular, I might as well have been eating cardboard.

Service was also underwhelming. While our waiter was nice, we rarely saw him, and he never refilled my water. I think we maybe saw him a total of 4 times and he would never check up on us.

One of the tasty things I did enjoy were the mozzarella sticks. They were larger than the average stick, resembling a log more than a stick, and had a nice cheese pull. 

Also, it started raining hard, and we were seated by a door--water was leaking into the restaurant through the door. Yikes!

I had BJ Hot Chicken ordered for delivery through the DoorDash App. They can and will deliver to hotels, woo hoo!

For my meal, I had the medium hot chicken tenders (3) and a side of mac and cheese. Even though they were a medium, they still activated my sinuses! The only thing I didn't like was how shallow the container was that contained my mac and cheese. It was so good, I wish the little dish was just a bit deeper so I could keep eating . . . but I guess that's for the best.

This was the "hottest" chicken I allowed myself, and I was very satisfied! I ate it in the comfort of my own home away from home.

First and foremost I have to admit how weird and uncomfortable I am by the phrase "The Gulch." I don't even know what a gulch is, but just saying it was just. . . idk. I don't like it.

THAT said, a coworker and I planned on getting our brunch on at Biscuit Love, but upon seeing the massive line out the door, we took a left turn and ended up at The Pub, and I'm glad we did.

This British themed-pubsteraunt plays old and current tunes from across the pond, and serves up a surprisingly wide variety of food. I ordered the chicken and waffles, and I was pleasantly surprised with my meal. The waffles in particular had a nutmeg flavor I think, and reminded me of egg nog.

The chicken was also great, and I ended up taking a tender and half the waffle back to my hotel to eat as a PM snack.

Service was great, our waiter made fun conversation and worked in the fact that we were from San Antonio into his bit. (Yes, we have clean air, but you could never tell with all the blasted pollen in it!)

The trendy neighborhood reminded me a lot like either The Rim or The Quarry, or even The Pearl back here in SA, so that was pretty neato burrito. I wouldn't mind coming here again if I ever find my way back to Nashville.

My last legit dinner in Tennessee, and I wanted something definitely less "touristy" and far more "local." I found it.

Homegrown Taproom is a hidden gem, a hole in the wall looking place in a blink-and-you'll-miss-it street corner in a strip mall. This isn't your Tourist attraction. This is a nitty gritty local spot and I was all here for it.

Service was pretty good and remarkably friendly, and they served Austin Eastciders (pineapple)! That was the only Texas drink I've found here. I had an Oatmeal Stout, and it was very delicious and creamy.

For my meal I had the pulled pork mac and cheese. The pork's sauce had a super nice sweetness to it that went well with the cheese, and let's just say my leftovers didn't last very long.

I loved this spot, vastly more so than the places my other coworkers wanted to go. I live for local places like these, so to finally get a taste of one made my whole trip here worth it.

kyg3Hyu94OqG3TIEdctt6g.review_text: I would like to make a note about other reviews: there is no free wifi because they want to make it an atmosphere where people go to talk and hang out, not be working on their laptops and have headphones in etc... Anyway, I love the oxford exchange shops and the restaurant is great. Also the coffee shop (buddy brew) has long been a fav. They make the best lattes in Tampa. The interior design and architecture of the building is beautiful. Be sure to check out the bathrooms too haha (:
Great coffee, amazing lattes! Friendly personable staff. Cool architecture and design. (:

The staff is SO friendly. The menu is huge. There's never a wait time when I come in but they're usually pretty busy. I like the huevos avocado and Jose's omelet (: yum yum! Breakfast for lunch is the best. Love this place

They re-designed the place and it looks bad ass! Kind of hipster but not pretentious. Still the best lattes in Tampa. It used to be a hole in the wall kind of place but now it's hard to find a seat. It makes me kind of sad but I'm glad they're doing good business lol and the manager is super nice... They have beer too ;)

I love this place! It's got a very cool interior, the staff are very friendly and the food is sooooo good. It's in a weird location but it's worth it to make the trip over there. Great place to take visitors (:

My sister is visiting and I brought her in to have authentic Cuban sandwiches. They were delish! We ordered a dozen oysters that were HUGE! The deviled crabs are great too. The interior is very rustic looking and has a great atmosphere. I highly recommend! The only thing is the waiter wasn't all the great but we were young and poor and it's kind of a classy place. But if you look like a middle-aged tourist I bet you'll have a great experience hahaa

This place is so cool! There's an entire hidden back patio and they play reggae which adds to the ambiance. It's super shaded with lots of plants, trees... It's dirty but it's authentic! (: I played with his dogs and drank beer and had a great time. I will definitely be back to try the shakes.

A great new place! It's perfect if you don't want the hustle and bustle of Starbucks. Their interior has a modern rustic feel; a brick wall/ wood counter-type of coffee shop. The owners are so friendly; they gave us our first cup of coffee for free. The coffee is delicious too. I'm a big fan of Buddy Brew and Kahwa, and I'm predicting that this place will take off once the word gets out. Glad they're putting nice stuff in this area too.

I love this place. It's small and quaint. They brew all their beer right there in the back room. The owner is really friendly; the beer is SO good. They have flights and growlers too. Some of the big name breweries can be a bit too much sometimes with their cool architecture and interior design and fancy paintings... This place is perfect if you just want to relax and enjoy beer.

GET THE BREAD PUDDING!
I would never order any kind of dessert that's called 'bread pudding' but the waiter recommended it so I said yes. It was the best thing I've ever tasted. Because of that, my boyfriend and I are now regulars. We usually get half Cuban and salad. It's so good! The black bean caviar dip app is only $5 and its delish. Great mojitos and sangria too. And the view is unbeatable! They have live music Friday's and Saturdays. It's just a wonderful place to relax and have dinner. I highly recommend checking it out.

Maria Levou...? Or something? And the other half was the one bad pig. Both were the best burgers I've ever had. Best burger joint I've ever been to in my life! Why hasn't everyone in the st pete/Tampa area been here yet...?!

First time here! Not sure if it's a local artist but the murals they have inside are the coolest I've seen around here. Jase is awesome, one of the best customer service experiences I've had. Everything around this place is great, I'll definitely be back!
The food is so good! And the service is excellent! This is one of my favorite restaurants in Ybor. I suggest the Udon bowl (with poached egg) or the green curry. And don't forget hot sake. (:

Been dying to come here. I've been to Rubios all over SoCal. This location is SO nice. The restaurant is very clean and updated. Great service! The staff is extremely friendly. I had the mahi mahi taco and it was literally the best taco I've ever had. Their corn tortilla is the best you'll get in Tampa. And my fiancé got a free birthday entree! Everything was so fresh. So many great freshly brewed iced teas. The salsa bar is also the best salsa anywhere. I was sitting there sipping on just salsa haha... Might be my new fav restaurant.

This place is SO fun! You load up your plate with vegetables and meat and then cook it yourself at your table. Lots of vegetarian options. I got the miso broth and my fiancé got Chinese herb. The desserts are really good too! It's a very chill place. The staff is super friendly. The owner Sharon came over and asked how everything was. WE WILL BE BACK SHARON (: (:

This is the most beautiful restaurant I've been to. It's the first 5-star restaurant that I've taken my fiancé to; my soul mate. Everything from the romantic upholstery to the lighting, I had the most amazing night of my life. Thank you to our incredible waitress Christina who was very attentive to our needs and clearly a professional in the industry. We had such an amazing night, thank you Rococo for everything!

The menu is huge! Prices are great! Breakfast all day (I think)? Very very very friendly service. There were lots of cute old folk coming in and out. Family owned; they've apparently been in business for 35 years? I mostly loved how nice everyone was. I will defiantly be back. (:

Todd is a great bar tender! It was very busy when I came in with my fiancé but he was very patient and listened to all our bs in the middle of making all the drinks. You can definitely tell he's from Bourbon St! Very very friendly and made our experience memorable. I wish we lived closer! We highly recommend this place. Thank you Todd!

Margaret is always so pleasant. We'll walk by and if we see she's working we'll stop in for a drink. Have you ever been thanked by your server or bartender when they take your order? That's the kind of service she gives. Always exceed what we would expect as a simple bar patron. Great atmosphere; super romantic. The sangria pitchers are a must if you're with Bae. Don't miss out on the 1905 salad. And definitely fill up on the Cuban bread so you have leftovers to bring home. We love Columbia restaurant!!!
Best hashbrowns! Breakfast all day and it's 24 hour. Best grits too. Very very friendly service. I wanted to try one of their many assortments of cake but I was too full. I'll be back (:

Really really good tacos! The corn tortillas are so good and they don't fall apart like a lot of them do at other restaurants. I wish they had more vegetarian options but the carnitas tacos are some of the best I've had. I highly recommend (:

The seafood is great, we love old bay! The view of the marina is beautiful. I just wish they had some chicken wire or something outside along the bottom because I saw so much trash and saltine wrappers and such blow into the water just in the time I was there. Ick.

Really really great açaí bowls and smoothies! My bowl also had chia pudding and oatmeal in it, it was sooo delicious. I think the smoothies are slow-blended? Really really yummy. Wish it was closer to home (:
Get the risotto!!! It's soooo good. Turkey burger was the best I've had. Drinks are amazing of course. Really really wonderful atmosphere and vibe, we will definitely be back.

The food is really really good. Downside to the food is they leave it out all afternoon so it's kind of dried out. Still happy with the healthy selection though. 
They tried to charge me extra for substituting veggies for protein. And then they were out of all their toppings except cheese and guacamole (guac costs extra). It was all a bit expensive for what it was. Not super happy with my overall experience but I think they're still new so I'm not gonna give a terrible rating.

Delicious raw vegan options at a very fair price! The restaurant itself is very bright and clean and open. Staff are friendly beautiful people. My tropical açaí bowl was perfectly blended and sprinkled with toppings. It's been hard for my babe to eat vegan but this place has many filling options for the hungry guys haha. We are from Tampa but will definitely be back!

Best Indian food I've had in a long time. They have a large selection of vegetarian options. The okra curry was so delicious. The atmosphere inside is very nice. It's very clean and the staff are friendly. (:

lLKBshoFXqizrPt25Pc-7A.review_text: I had a party of 6 for lunch at Amada yesterday.  The tapas was great and the presentation beautiful however two of my guests never got their lunch.  The waiter never came back to check on us and sitting at the very front (in the rocks) put us out of the servers view.  Finally we asked and he told us they were made wrong and they were redoing their order.  After a long while he brought their lunch out in a shopping bag and they had to take it back to their office.  Definitely not the service you want if trying to entertain.  They took those two meals off the check but offered no apology for the mishap.

The most wonderful restaurant, beautiful decor, experienced staff and best of all the most delicious food.  We weren't sure what to order so we had the sampler including the lamb (cooks for four days).  Every course was better than the one before.  Just loved the whole experience.  Definetly highly recommend!

We went to The Barley Sheaf Inn for New Year's Eve.  The buildings were beautiful, the service very good.  The food however was designed for elves.  It was tiny.  Artfully presented if you like to spend close to $200.00 for a couple (not including wine) and leave hungry.  Salad of tiny beets, radishes and one tiny carrot.  Soup barely covering the bottom of the shallow bowl.  One scallop and two bites (one if you are a man) of short rib.  The best part was the tiny chocolate cake.  At least you could get four bites of that.

Had a wonderful dinner there with a group of 5.  The wait staff was all very polite and efficient.  The food was delicious.  The place is historic and charming.  What more could you ask for. 
 They got us out in time to get to the show next door at the Sellersville theatre.

I have had the opportunity to dine here three times in three weeks.  Not only is this restaurant in a great spot but the food is delicious.  The menu has so many things it would be hard to put it in a category.  The Sunday brunch is amazing too!  Everything is fresh and cooked perfectly.  The staff are so polite and helpful.  I highly recommend this restaurant!

The food at Ooka is always fresh and beautifully presented.  It is the best sushi in this whole area.  The menu is great and Harry the waiter is the best!  If I'm taking my whole family we do hibachi which is reliably good but the sushi side of the restaurant is amazing.  The lighting is good and the booths are big enough to be comfortable.  Highly recommend Ooka!

I had lunch there today with two clients.  The waitress Diana was so pleasant and knowledgeable about the food!  The food was delicious and the portions very good sized.  They have outdoor seating but we chose to sit indoors and the restaurant is large and well spaced out.  Highly recommend it!

Pumpernick's Deli is amazing.  I'm from NY and I love great deli food.  Generous portions and the pickle bar too!!  If they had delivery it would be on my table 3 times a week.  Hot pastrami and giant sandwiches are amazing.  They also have a take out area where you can take home what you are craving.  Love it!

These are the best donuts.  Ever!  Sometimes there is a line around the building so you know if people are willing to wait it must be worth it.  The peanut butter cup donut is amazing!  The staff very friendly.
The food is fresh and healthy!  Tastes great.  The location is easy to get to. Tonight they brought the appetizers out after the main course otherwise I would give this 5 stars!

This was my first visit to the new building.  I love the seating area with the garage doors open.  It was so nice and has a good vibe.  The chicken parm was delicious and with two giant chicken breasts I have dinner too!  My client liked it just as much as I did.

I dined with three friends on Friday evening.  We didn't get to dine in the garden but the structure they built along the sidewalk was fine. The food amazing especially the short rib and the creme brûlée. This restaurant never disappoints!

The location and service were great.  That being said the frozen drinks featured on the front of the menu were unavailable.  The other section said those drinks could be hot or cold but then we were told the one we wanted was only served hot.  The cheesesteak egg rolls were good, the same as everywhere else.  The shrimp wrapped bacon was inedible.  There were four and we left two - awful.  The martini's were good but served warm.  The food average.  The proscuitto pizza was the only thing that I could say was excellent.  It's a shame but I couldn't recommend this place.

This was a truly enjoyable experience.  The staff were very friendly and sat us at the table we requested.  A great start!  The watermelon jalapeno margarita was amazing.  The taco's were so good that I brought one home and ate it the same night!  My friend had a salad with chicken that was huge.  She got another whole meal out of it.  This restaurant is here to stay!  It has everything - great staff, drinks, food!

I had dinner at The Love last night.  The ambiance is excellent as is the staff.  The Labor of Love artisan cheese platter was presented beautifully.  The tuna appetizer was all presentation with very little tuna.  We all had different entree's so we could sample them.  The ravioli was amazing, the fried chicken as well.  The scallops were disappointing.  Thirty four dollars for three scallops and four stalks of asparagus.  Overall it was a very good experience and I would dine there again but would stick with the chicken!

I had lunch with a client there today.  The host was polite, the waitress was attentive and our glasses were refilled consistently.  The food was amazing.  The avocado toast was the best I have ever had.  The grilled artichoke with lemon hummus was incredible.  Presented beautifully and tasted even better!  The chicken caprese sandwich was tender and delicious.  I highly recommend this restaurant.  As a bonus there is plenty of parking!

I met a friend at BricknBrew in Havertown.  The service was good but not great.  The burrata salad was wonderful and served with greens and berries.  A great addition to the traditional.  We both had the lobster roll.  It was very good but just a little bit less mayo would have made it perfect.  The only real drawbacks are the sound level and the parking situation (there is none).

A client suggested I meet him here.  What a wonderful surprise this restaurant is.  The shiplap in the entryway, the patterned tile, wood ceilings and amazing light fixtures were amazing.  This place is straight out of HGTV.  Our server was John and he was engaging, very familiar with the menu and extremely helpful.  The autumn soup was incredible.  The apple gave it that bit of sweetness.  The short rib grilled cheese was to die for.  I hope you get the chance to eat here!  I will be back for sure!

Coyote Crossing was an amazing surprise.  Nestled on a residential street you would never guess that this incredible restaurant if it's hidden gem.  I walked in and the back wall was open to this amazing courtyard, lights on the trees, private and perfect.  The coconut watermelon margarita was like no other!!!  The carnitas nachos were incredible and the Tinga Burrito had more chicken in it than I've ever had at a Mexican restaurant.  I can't recommend this place enough.  It's the total package, easy parking, easy location and just crazy good food and ambience.

Had dinner with two friends last night.  Our waitress was amazing, attentive and professional.  Unusual now with the staff shortages.  The food was fantastic.  The pork dumplings were incredible and the humus was as delicious as the presentation suggested.  The pumpkin ravioli was amazing!!!  The food is freshly prepared and I couldn't recommend this restaurant more.

I just had my third client dinner at Eddie V's.  The bar is lively and has live music.  The restaurant is well appointed and the food is amazing.  The seafood tower was great and the lobster taco's were the best appetizer!  Our server was Alaina and she was knowledgeable and friendly.  A rarity these days.  The food is delicious whether you order seafood or steak.  I highly recommend this.  It's expensive and worth it!
