Congrats to swarthmore borough -- this is the dining establishment we've always needed! What a great ambience both outside (thanks to the heaters and string lights) and in. They've done such a nice job with the orangey/red paint inside and art on the wall -- easy on the eyes as you stroll through swarthmore village. 
Let's start with the food. It's tapas style, so we ordered a mix of "wine snacks," appetizers, entrees, and sides. Our favorites included the mushroom strudel, goat cheese stuffed squash, and brussel sprouts with braised apples. You really cannot go wrong with anything on the menu, though. The monkfish itself was great, but for $20, I was hoping for some sort of side -- maybe a pile of rice or something like that. Whatever the dish is, it's guaranteed to be better than what the ghosts of Swarthmore's restaurant past could offer you (i.e: Rudy's). 
Now for the slightly negative part: the service. In all fairness, it's covid times, it's a new restaurant, a waiter was being trained, and other factors made it hard for the service to be top notch or match the food quality. We had a reservation at 730, but weren't able to be seated until 755. It took a long while to receive our plates and the order in which the plates came out didn't make a lot of sense -- the brussel sprouts came out as our last dish. Unfortunately I had to give up on ordering the white chocolate and nut cookie skillet for dessert because we feared we could would be there until midnight if we ordered another course! This isn't anything that should keep you away from the restaurant -- just a heads up to bring a jacket to keep cozy while you wait for food! 
We are so happy to have village vine in our neighborhood and can't wait to return.

You almost forget you're in a shopping mall when you're in this laid-back, tropical-feeling environment (not tacky, either). I came for a casual dinner and was definitely pleased by the whole experience. 
We didn't call ahead or use the app, so we had to wait a bit for a table, but there's endless entertainment to be found in KOP! 
We were sat outside next to a heater and were then informed of the ordering style -- you scan a QR code and create a bartaco account to link your credit card to. This was fine for us youngsters, but I could see an older set of visitors struggling with this. Anyways, you do all of the ordering from there and they know exactly where to bring your food to. I'm not sure if it was a covid times invention, but it's definitely smart -- no real interactions with waiters, no menus that everyone's been touching, etc. 
My one complaint is that we didn't receive basic service expectations -- no water or napkins (or utensils, but we didn't really need those). 
The tacos are definitely TINY but they make you aware of that. I had carnitas style and tuna, which were both great, but I failed to notice that the tuna came in a lettuce wrap (sad). I LOVED the Mexican corn and the guac appetizer was definitely fresh and lime-y tasting. Also ordered a marg, which hit the spot and was also pretty strong! We noticed some ladies out on the town at the table over who were enjoying some tequila shots, what a fun idea! 
10/10 would return and the prices definitely aren't unreasonable!

A classy ambience they have going for sure! We came for an early dinner and felt comfortable as far as covid goes, even indoors. 
I can't speak to their cocktails because they were operating under governor's order to shut down alcohol services before 5pm on thanksgiving eve! We laughed about it with the server as she offered us some sprite and lemonade. 
We ordered a whole slew of appetizers -- pesto bread, beet and arugula salad, truffle fries, mushroom soup and the short rib hash. While I generally maintain a no salad ordering policy at restaurants (why pay for meh healthy stuff?), I had to bend the rules for the beet salad because it is phenomenal. My favorite dish of the night even. The goat cheese is divine and the croutons are to die for -- it just all came together so well. Pesto bread was fine, just not my personal favorite bread variety. If I'm going to pay extra for it, I want something warm and fluffy -- didn't get that here. Mushroom soup was nice and included a nice pour presentation. Truffle fries are BOMB, a white dog staple in my experiences. 
I didn't actually order an entree, but someone in my family had the falafel sandwich, which was pretty standard but yummy, and another had the Reuben, which they seemed to enjoy, but they did complain about the salad dressing. Oh! And the Brussel sprouts which another someone let me have a taste of were also out of this world!!!
Overall, it was a relaxed and delicious experience!

While I can't comment on the takeout option process because someone else in my household handled that, I CAN say that their sushi is nothing short of phenomenal. It will rock your socks off. Make sure to order the tomo roll -- they sure know what they're doing there! It's the freshest tasting tuna, not sure how they do it! Hope to be back shortly!

God bless THE ardmore station cafe. It is my absolute favorite for a variety of reasons: it has some character, is drastically different from its uppity mainline breakfast joint counterparts, it's affordable, and the food is to die for. They were open and accommodating on New Year's Day, and we called in some black bean breakfast burritos. Perfect for a non-meat eater like myself. I've enjoyed everything I've tried here in the past: the stuffed french toast is another definite highlight. The strawberry and Nutella variety is a classic -- you've just got to come hungry. Did I mention the prices?? $4.50 for an egg and cheese bagel WITH breakfast potatoes. Minellas is shaking in their boots. I'm one of your biggest fans, ardmore station cafe! I reserve 5 star ratings for only the best of the best!

I cannot think of any negatives about this special place to balance out my review. Simply stellar. They've really figured out a way to make enjoyable dining possible during covid. They have pods that are really quite warm -- I was even debating taking my winter jacket off. It's nice to be sitting out on the streets too, as there's some solid people watching available in center city. The wait staff is also incredibly attentive. Obviously the food is tapas style, and we didn't regret ordering any of our plates. As a pescatarian, I especially recommend the salmon skewers (so very flavorful) and shrimp pad Thai! The Brussel sprouts are consistently the star of the show, too. Thanks Sampan for all that you do!

UPDATE (visited again for happy hour):

Sampan's happy hour absolutely broke the 5-star scale for me. Can I give it at least 6 stars?? I was blown away by how much high quality food & drink we got for such a reasonable price. A huge bowl of fried rice for only $5?  You must be pulling my leg! The scorpion bowls are phenomenal and the right amount alcoholic for a lil evening fun! 
Our waitress was super kind and made sure we were able to place orders before the 5 o'clock happy hour deadline/ the cheaper plates expired! 
I have never been so anxious to return to a restaurant in my life!

My sister and I were really intrigued by a vegan spot opening up in our very own delco! Usually you'd venture into the city for this kind of cuisine. It's therefore pretty niche, and they delivered on their promise that even non-vegans can enjoy it. 
As a situational pescatarian (lol), I try to limit my animal-product consumption chiefly for the environment. I don't think Cheezy Vegan shares this priority, but that's okay -- these practices could also be due to COVID. They give you styrofoam takeout containers, plastic utensils in plastic wrap, plastic straws, cups, etc. I hope to see some improvement there, but by not serving any animal products, they're probably more sustainable than most restaurants! 
The ambience/ interior could use some work, but I know they're just a brand new biz trying to make their way. They had fake brick wallpaper -- very tacky. Above that was another panel of white wallpaper which could use some more character. 
We came for brunch on a Thursday morning and there was only one person on the wait staff -- she was sweet as could be! We were the only ones in the restaurant too, and they seemed a bit frazzled to have in-person diners (maybe more of a takeout-kinda place nowadays). I was surprised that they didn't have something as simple as an iced coffee when I inquired about drinks. 
Now for the food. I definitely ordered wrong and wasn't super hungry upon arrival, so when my plate of the ultimate biscuit arrived (it was listed under "foodie favorites" on the menu) I wasn't exactly anxious to jump in. I'll say that it certainly wasn't this foodie's favorite, but my sister really enjoyed her McReeky breakfast sandwich. Mine just smelled overwhelmingly of salt, and the gravy too much so reminded me of vomit. I was really impressed by the vegan eggs, they resembled the texture of real scrambled eggs to a 't.' The chick'n was the highlight of the plate -- it tasted so real it was fREEKY! (Haha, the chef's name is Reeky). Next time I'm going to try the chick'n and waffles, as that sounds more up my alley! We also got to try the bread pudding which was divine! 
I definitely want to try this spot again when I have an empty stomach! Thanks Chef Reeky!

Jules is a really unique spot! Not just the pizza -- you can tell it's a family-owned business. They come up with topping combinations out of your wildest dreams! My favorite pizza BP (before pescetarianism) was Kim's pie. It's not the greasy pizza you crave after a night out, rather it is a beautiful delicate slice of thin pie with meat, mushrooms, and fine cheese that should be savored. I'm glad I was able to dip my toes in the veggie pizzas -- I can't imagine not discovering the V11. The V11 has kale, mandarin oranges, apples, lemon juice, and cheese. It is AMAZING. It leaves you feeling satisfied and not gross and bloated.
I also tried the V9 -- a Mexican-style pizza. I didn't think the flavors really fit together and it was almost overly-tangy, but still an interesting concept that I'd give a solid 8/10. 
Jules is definitely pricey, but you're just rightfully paying for quality! Love it.

Handel's is a mainline staple. The prices are reasonable and the scoops are HUGE. Such a variety of flavors, too -- how is one to decide what they want! I went with the cake batter in a cup and was not disappointed. Maybe it could use the addition of some fun sprinkles/ jimmies (call it what ya want), but that's on me to spice it up a bit. It was an enjoyable treat even in January winter weather. My friend and I sat out on their benches and basked in the sun and left the worries of the world behind.

I always rave to people -- friends and strangers alike -- about sweetgreen. If someone says they don't like salad, I'll say "wait! but have you tried sweetgreen?" I guarantee their yummy salads will sway even the pickiest anti-'rabbit food' eaters! 
Recently I've gone for the veggie Caesar. It's just the right amount indulgent, yet still feels healthy. The ingredients are FRESH and my only complaint is that they forgot to put the tofu in my bowl the last time I was there, but mistakes happen! 
I love how they have compostable bowls. The hexagonal shape is pretty rad, too. It's a win for aesthetics AND for the environment!

I stopped into the fishtown location for a quick bite and a bit of a caffeine fix to power through my afternoon of thrifting. The staff was very accommodating and more than tolerated our indecisiveness about sitting down or not. 
Firstly, be aware that they only take cash (at least when we were there and indoor dining wasn't permitted). I ordered the Nutella latte (hot) and the cheesy hash browns because I didn't feel like dishing out big $$ for a full plate. 
Everything was phenomenal! My friend also ordered the latte and said "wow! that tastes like Nutella!" A very convincing review if you ask me. She was right -- it was spot-on. The cheesy hashbrowns were perfect, there was a cheesy kick and it was just the right amount of sustenance. 
Can't wait to go back and order a full meal. The fishtown location is super spacious, too!

I'll say it: I think El Vez is a tad overhyped. Don't get me wrong -- it's good, but when all things are considered, it's not special.
Keep in mind I only ordered sangria & chips/ guac during my last visit there, which is a pretty limited scope of their offerings. 
We were sat outside next to a heater which I had no qualms about! We were lucky that it was a relatively warm night, as I might've been uncomfortable in this set up in truly chilling temperatures. It was fun to (safely) be in the center of activity and see fellow diners (and even some drummers!) on the corner of 13th and Sansom. Honestly even more of a thrill than we'd get in non-covid times!
The peach sangria was a hit -- very sugary though. The chips and guac are always solid and have a great kick of lime-y freshness. It's nothing mind-blowing, though. 
Overall, I like El Vez, but I wasn't too enthused to pay that bill at the end.

Bittersweet is always a reliable spot for a solid brunch. It didn't seem like they were anticipating diners on a cold covid Tuesday morning, as I had to knock to get the  staff's attention inside. They then promptly escorted us to a table outside underneath a heater that they flipped on for us. It must've been a powerful one -- I was very comfortable temperature-wise! 
I ordered the vegetarian spin on their breakfast chicken enchiladas. The cauliflower and black bean was a lovely substitute and it made for a perfectly filling and yummy breakfast! No complaints! 
They didn't try to rush us out or make us feel us feel uncomfortable for wanting to sit awhile and enjoy the ambience! I really appreciated that.
Everything was great, but I just held off from the 5 star review because I don't think the food is anything phenomenal. 
Can't wait to be back!

I'm surprised that it took me so long to discover this place as I tend to scope out the ~trendy food spots in the city. 
This spot was worth the wait! It's first come first serve, so we missed out on a table in their glorified dumpster. Lol -- it's actually a very nice train-car looking thing (picture included below) that kinda falls into the category of indoor dining masquerading as outdoor dining. We were instead placed out in open air and next to a heater. I think our waitress could sense that we were chilly and was ready to move us if a table opened up in the boxcar, which was very nice of her! And what do you know -- as soon as one cleared, she ushered us over! They have some nice string lights in there which wakes for a cozy vibe. 
My two friends started off by ordering the peppermint mocha and were very impressed. I placed an order for the pumpkin pie cappuccino a bit later. 
The timing of my ordering was unfortunate, as my food came out with it. I therefore couldn't fully enjoy two things at once! My cappuccino was getting cold but I also needed to tend to my food! What to do! It was a lovely and comforting drink, though. 
For the food, we all ordered the huevos rancheros and then shared a plate of their infamous cannoli French toast. Honestly, I struggle to see why this is their all-star plate. The brioche was AMAZING but I had a slight issue with the cannoli side of it -- the filling had a weird lemon-y aftertaste and was really nothing like a true cannoli's consistency. I'm not sure what the pistachios had to offer, either. The huevos rancheros was awesome -- highly recommend this plate. 
They also have a 10% off deal for any student!! Make sure you take advantage of this when you check out this fun little spot!

I only ordered a drink pouch to go so that's what I'm basing my five stars on! 
We stopped in bud & marilyn's on a lively Friday evening in the city hoping to turn the fun up a notch! We saw many other people carrying these fun pouches so we had to track the distributor down! There wasn't much going on in there and I don't believe they have an outdoor seating option. Alas, they were eager to take our order and our adult juice boxes were ready in no time. We all got the gritty margarita! It was excellent! They're refreshing and it's a nostalgic/ fun experience to sip them! They were $13 which isn't too terrible, especially considering there's a hefty amount of liquid in there! 
I'm looking forward to trying BOTH their food and drinks next time!

Jaco's menu offerings are awfully niche -- tacos, burritos, and smoothies. I came for an afternoon bite and got two baco tacos with the $6.95 deal. 
You better like corn if you order this, because the dish is more like 'sweet corn with a side of a corn tortilla.' I do like corn thankfully, and thought the plate hit the spot. The guacamole tasted a bit off, though -- it had likely seen better days in terms of ripeness! 
One complaint is that they didn't include a fork in my takeout bag. But go off for saving the environment if that was the idea behind it!

I ordered takeout from here during covid and I truly can't complain! 
I wasn't overly hungry, so I decided to just order the chips and guac. Luckily, the chopped salad is so large that my friend was generous enough to give me half of it and I surely did not reject that offer! 
I can't say I've ever experienced guac with rice in it, but this was great! Kind of like an out of whack (proportion wise) chipotle, if you know what I mean (in a good way). The chopped salad was 10/10 and just indulgent enough with that sickkk pork belly (just take a look!).

This place slaps. I was at West Chester university for the evening and we were trying to decide which late night joint to take our business to. I asked what the authentic WC experience was, and was told my time in WC would be incomplete without an order from here. It's the real deal, folks! 
The buffalo chicken calzone was fantastic; I absolutely devoured it. It was dreamy honestly. Wish I had a picture, but it will live on in my memory!

Certifiably worth the hype.
For such an iconic and hot Philly restaurant, I was pleasantly surprised to hear sympathy over the phone when I said we might be 10-15 minutes late to our Friday evening reservation. Sometimes this would merit a cancellation on any restaurant's end, but my dining party was met with nothing but kindness! 
So we're off to a great start before even getting a bite in.
Their outdoor dining pods could definitely use a bit more insulation, but the patron near the heater was a happy camper. I had to keep my winter coat on, but I was by no means uncomfortable.
We started by ordering the fig pizza and mushroom pappardelle. These two dishes are jaw droppingly good. The fig pizza crust is somehow a perfect mix of doughy and crispy -- the stars really aligned here. And that's just the dough -- the fig, bacon and ricotta toppings nail a balance of sweet and savory. It's not your usual pizza, but I'd say it was one of my favorite slices ever. The pappardelle pays homage to talula's roots in Kennett square and has these intricate mushrooms tossed in. It's creamy and filling, but not too much so that you're unable to touch whatever entree you have coming next. 
I got the salmon. I'd say this was the most unremarkable of the evening's fleet of dishes, but good nonetheless! I would've liked to see it cooked to more of  a crisp. The brussels, apples and sweet potatoes are a nice, farm to table-esque addition. 
Lastly, I ordered the molten chocolate cake despite being stuffed to the brim. Man, I'm glad I didn't pass that up! Best dessert a dinner establishment has ever dished out of their kitchen. The raspberry sauce is to die for and you get the perfect bite every time with a bit of the cake, ice cream, and sauce. 
Epic meal!

We picked the perfect night to dine here -- we experienced a lovely sunset on the Delaware and it was a random weekday so were the only diners on their outdoor deck for the majority of the time. There was even a real (!!) fire that a staff member was tending to. Talk about ambience! 
If you're even remotely thinking about dropping some money on the bread, do it. The best thing $12 can buy. Especially those Parker house rolls. 
I couldn't justify getting both an appetizer and entree, so I got two appetizers. This was the right move for both my wallet and my tummy! 
I had the roasted carrot salad which comes with ricotta. These are some luxurious carrots within a flavorful dish! Keep in mind it's not a green salad, I was sure happy about that. Its remnants also made for an awesome dip for our leftover focaccia. 
I had the gnocchi come out next. This is the best gnocchi I've ever had. We're talking the melt in your mouth variety -- there's nothing like it. 
The wait staff was super attentive and even funny, too. Yes, Stella is pricey, but you're really just rightfully paying for quality and a relaxed evening!!

locpT-bSRrJotd8Tnmqlpg.review_text: Great food and ambiance. Their boeuf bourguignon is phenomenal! Service is always friendly and good but sometimes a bit slow. This place has a nice, warm and cozy atmosphere that I love. Makes me feel like I am in actually in France!

One of my favorite spots in St. Louis. There is a romantic and rustic ambiance to this place that I love. It's very dark and cozy with a nice candlelight touch. Service is always friendly and the bartenders take pride in their unique cocktails. Oh and did I mention the food is to die for?  A nice place for a romantic, splurge, forget-about-my-diet kind of night :o)

Went for lunch today and it was quite busy! Service was spectacular. It was fine dining service so there wasn't a ton of personality, but that is to be expected in this type of place. All needs were very well met. My guest's steak was phenomenal. I opted for the Chef Salad, which wasn't something to necessarily brag about. The steak that was on it was extremely tender as was the chicken, but the dressing was on the saltier side and the greens were tossed in the dressing and quickly became wilted. Definitely go for the steak! I was trying not to consume a heavy lunch (hence the reason I ordered a salad) but I realize that steak is definitely what the Tenderloin Room is known for and that's what I should have ordered. With some wine to accompany my meal, this easily became a $100 lunch for me and my guest. As long as you're willing to splurge, it's a nice place to check out!

Went there for their Sunday brunch and I was very much impressed.  Excellent service and food.  Their lobster mac n cheese, smoked salmon, and waffles were amazing.  I've been there before but regular dinner dining but this brunch was a great experience--expensive but highly recommend as it's probably one of the best brunch buffets in St. Louis.  Great for special occasions or if relatives/friends are in town.

The ambiance here is unlike any other in St. Louis--trendy, sleek, yet cozy at the same time.  I think I may have uncovered a new gem in the St. Louis area...and lucky for me it's extremely close to where I live so I am sure I will be a new regular. In the few weeks they have been open, I have already been in on three occasions. I still have yet to sit by their warm fireplace because it's taken every time I've come in! 

During my first visit on a Thursday night, I sat at the bar with some friends and the restaurant was PACKED!  Bartenders were friendly, helpful and drinks were made very quickly.  Lots of beers with several on tap as well as a fairly extensive wine list and a fair signature cocktail list. 

2nd time I was here I dined with several friends for my birthday.  Server was a step above mediocre.  It bothered me that he couldn't answer my question about what he recommended on the menu, but instead started to ramble on about wine pairings...when I had already ordered a beer.  He did redeem himself by the end of the dining experience by getting us a round of Birthday Cake shots. To note, he was never unfriendly, but maybe just not fully trained.   The hostess during this dining experience was exceptionally friendly and courteous.  Her name was Alexandria, I believe, and checked on us a couple of times throughout the meal to see if we needed anything and whenever a new guest arrived she was prompt to give my guest a menu.  She also helped my friend who had baked me surprise cupcakes by carrying the cupcakes into the restaurant through the back entrance so that I wouldn't see them and helped buss the table once we were finished.  As for the food, the Donald and Margherita pizzas were great, as were the cheese plate and side dishes that my friends and I shared. My friend didn't like her burger though.  Open kitchen = very cool. 

The third experience I had was last night where I also sat and grabbed a drink at the bar with my friend who was in town--she wanted to check out a new place in St. Louis and I told her I knew just the place.  The bartender's name was Devin and was extremely sweet, knowledgeable, and helpful and let us sample a couple of wines and beers to match our tastes.  She was excellent.  

Overall a very good experience in my first three visits!

Today I went for lunch and it was a great experience! Fantastic ribs and BBQ sauce. Fast and friendly service! Charismatic cashier guy! Best to get food to go since the place is apparently always busy and it felt a bit claustrophobic when I was in there--very much elbow-to-elbow!  Tried going there once before and they had closed very early afternoon because they had already sold out.  It's the Oklahoma Joe's of St. Louis.  Highly recommend!

Sanctuaria is definitely a unique place in St. Louis with it's darker, more gothic decor.  My friends and I were discussing how it reminds us of New Orleans' French Quarter. In terms of the restaurant itself, I thought the food and service were both just okay.  Drink list is extensive and very unique but definitely on the higher-priced end if you want to try one of their signature drinks (and being at a place that specializes in their special drinks, it's definitely a must-order).  I had one of their seasonal drinks called Fall Baquiri , which was phenomenal.  I love that this place takes pride in making exquisite cocktails.  Food was on the saltier side...lots of fried items, and on the smaller side in terms of portions, even for small plates.  Overall, a satisfactory experience but nothing extraordinary! It is a place you should visit at least once just to try out if you're looking for something new.

Fantastic food and bartenders.  This is one of my favorite spots to catch up with friends in a comfortable, cozy setting.  It's really nice at night when you're sitting at a candlelit table OR when the weather is phenomenal and you can enjoy the fantastic patio.  Jamie, who used to work there, remains to this day, one of my favorite bartenders ever.  He was a charismatic guy, quick to make a drink, and always remembered his guests' names. The bartenders who took over are not quite the same, but are fair in comparison.  Food is consistently great.  Table service could use some work.  I've had brunch here on a handful of occasions, and the service then (by this same female server) has never been super friendly or timely.  Nevertheless, one of my favorite spots in one of my favorite areas in St. Louis.

Wine and food = fabulous!!! My gal pals and I shared a couple bottles of wine and I had the filet mignon for dinner.  The filet was super tender and paired well with the mushrooms and mashed potatoes it came with.  I would have given it a 5-star rating but our server seemed a bit spacey and had some difficulty figuring out our checks even though we made it fairly simple for her.   Otherwise, a very cute place with great wine and food to match!

My kabobs were awesome but my friend ordered some kind of lamb stew that really wasn't that great.  I guess I expected the lamb to be a bit more savory and not so sweet. The service was okay from our server.  There was another server in the restaurant who was actually a lot more helpful than our own server.  The food came out insanely fast, but it was our server who was slow to take orders and to bring drinks.   Being a Friday night, the music was pretty loud.  The belly dancer was great and entertaining, but it was a bit hard to have a conversation with such loud music.  Decent food and service, but nothing above and beyond!
Good food, good service, really cute patio.  And the servers dress in kilts. So what's not to like?
Romantic setting both inside and on their awesome patio. Food is good but when I went a few days ago, service was on the slower side.  Otherwise, server was pretty attentive and friendly.

Best duck in St. Louis. The Peking Duck is a must-try item on their menu.  Seafood tofu hotpot is also delicious, along with pretty much everything else.  This is one of the nicer Chinese restaurants in the St. Louis area in the heart of our mini-China town.  Service isn't the best, but the food can't be beat!

4 stars for the food--the food is incredible.  The gyros (the deluxe) tends to be a bit pricier than some of the other gyro places around St. Louis at about $10 a gyro, but it is quite delicious.  Service was friendly but incredibly slow.  Had to wait fifteen minutes for our check to be picked up, when the restaurant was not very busy.  The ambiance is also cool. This is a Dogtown staple and despite the slow service, some of the best Greek in St. Louis.

Some of the best, genuine service I've had in a long time.  Food was great.  The toasted ravioli is to die for.  But everyone from the hostess to the server was extremely friendly and I could tell they really enjoyed their jobs.  Two thumbs up for this place!  This place was also featured on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives on the Food Network.

Scape is probably one of the most beautiful restaurants I've seen in St. Louis. Service was also fantastic. From the moment I called to make a reservation, a friendly hostess asked if we were celebrating anything. My date had just gotten promoted so I explained to her that is why we were having dinner there.  As soon as we entered and I gave her my reservation name, she greeted us with, "Congratulations on the promotion! So glad you are spending your evening celebrating with us."  We received a very similar response from our server who immediately greeted us at the table.  

We each had some awesome cocktails. I had one with gin and lavender and champagne that was beautifully sweet and surprisingly sour (it was a pleasant kind of sour!). My date had an awesome cucumber cocktail.  The oysters were fresh and the crab cake appetizer was probably the best crab cake I've ever had.  I ordered the scallops for dinner which was also superb.

Really, a fantastic place to dine if you're willing to drop a few extra bucks. Totally worth it!

I came here for the first time last weekend and I feel like I have seriously been missing out! Great food (French toast was to die for), awesomely unique lavender latte, and totally great service! Everyone who touched our table was super sweet and friendly. I can't wait to go back and try the other stuff on their menu. Highly recommend!

Very warm staff and awesome food. Great new addition to the Central West End and have already been a few times since this place has opened.  Papardelle is incredible. Make sure to save room for dessert!!! All of their desserts are to die for. Can't wait to try them for brunch :o)

if it wasn't for the two friendly bartenders and the quality of the food, I would probably have given this place 3-stars. The atmosphere is cool and resonates the look and feel of a big city restaurant.  However, the server seemed a bit pretentious which dampened the experience. The wait to be seated and the wait for our drinks and food to be served was also horrendously long.  There was a 1.5-hour long wait for a table (which was a correct quote time) but once seated, I can honestly say that my friends and I were there for an additional 2 hours. They don't take reservations which sucks for the guest but I can understand why from a business standpoint.  I must say the bartenders were awesome though--they were 2 girls who were very sweet explaining the menu and helping me with my beer selection and appetizer while we waited for our table. I would go back but would probably sit at the bar or at the bar where you can watch the chefs prepare food by the open kitchen (very cool!). My friends and I split 4 pastas and a pizza and the food was all delicious.

I dined here last night for Clayton Restaurant Week for the first time. Really cozy ambiance in the main dining room. The service was good but a bit dry (which tends to happen at higher-end restaurants) and the food was great.  I ordered the Arancini for my appetizer and the Beef Medallions for my entree. Both were delicious.  Portions for the dessert were tiny for Restaurant Week, however.  I ordered the bread pudding and it was incredible, just small. I would definitely go back to dine again.

This was my first dining experience in Nashville and I thought I had to try it out with all the great reviews.  Awesome set up of the restaurant with cool furniture, private rooms, and decor.  Food was good but the service was okay.  Took a very long time for our server to come to our, then come back to our table, and for the drinks and food to come out.  She was nice and seemed knowledgeable, but also seemed rushed and therefore not as available.  The General Manager was kind enough to take a picture of me and my friends, so that was a nice touch.  Good burger and shrimp and grits. I enjoyed the experience but the wait made the experience less than what it probably could have been.  Oh, complimentary valet also a nice touch.

Amaaaaaazing lamp chops! Server was friendly and knowledgeable and allowed me to order the lamp chops with the side items from the filet entree.  Overall a great dining experience with prompt and friendly service from the hostess, server (Justin), and the server's assistant as well.  The previous reviews did not lie!  I'm definitely glad I made this stop on my first trip to Nashville.
Delicious coffee and friendly service. Higher end coffee shop but can't beat the quality and friendliness and sleek, clean ambiance.  If I lived in Nashville, I would be a regular.

I was one lucky girl when there happened to be maintenance issues at the Sheraton and they had to relocate me to the Omni.  Everyone from the concierge to the check in/out desk to the service staff was extremely friendly. Immaculate lobby and nice rooms. I must give additional props to the shuttle driver Justin who not only drove us around but also was genuinely friendly and helpful and was great at recommending places to go. Shuttle service was fantastic. Thoroughly an awesome experience and I definitely hope to be back one day!

Delicious Southern food and just a really cool and unique concept. Community dining might not be for everyone, but it was definitely a fun experience for me! We met several people from out of state dining at Monell's because it's such a hotspot in Nashville.  Because it's so unique, this was definitely one of my favorite things to do while vacationing in Nashville. 

Mac & cheese is INCREDIBLE. So creamy and cheesy. The fried chicken and oven-roasted chicken were also superb. Those items made the trip entirely worth it. 

I must say, GO HUNGRY.  They aren't joking when they tell you to pace yourselves because it's a ton of food and I found myself getting full before the chicken came out!

Excellent food and service.  Very romantic, vintage, sultry--and it feels like I've been swept away into a decade from a very long time ago.  Filet mignon and scallops are superb.  I've dined here 3 times and have had an excellent experience each time!

I would have given a higher star rating if the server remembered to bring out my friend's birthday cake that I had to drive an hour to pick up.  I called ahead of time to let Sqwires know, then specifically told the hostess to relay the message to the server.  He already semi-ruined the surprise when he came up to our table after we were finished eating saying that he "had a special treat" then walked out with one of their house desserts. I had to chase after him remind him that I actually brought a cake for the table.  His response: "Oh yeah, the hostess did mention something like that..." Really?  Own up to the fact that you forgot, then tell me you are going to make it right, and have a sense of urgency about it.

Everything went down hill after that.  It took forever to get our checks, our checks were wrong twice, then he proceeded to tell me that checks could not be separated more than twice and encouraged my friend to pay my other friend for their tab difference.  The food was good but the service was bad. A restaurant should enhance the experience of a special occasion, not bring it down. Let me tell you, I have been in the restaurant industry for 8 years and it takes a lot to irk me enough to the point where I will write a bad Yelp review because I know how much these reviews can affect a business, but this experience was ridiculous.

The service from the server to the manager to the attendants at the pool was AMAZING. However, if I am to combine that with the quality of the restaurant's food, I have to be honest, the steak that I ordered for my brunch meal was not up to par for nearly $20 for the dish.   The steak cut was tough and bland and lacked serious flavor. The hashbrowns that it came with were hard as a rock.  I was definitely expecting more from the restaurant side as this was one of the worst breakfast/brunch dishes I have ever ordered at a restaurant.  This was my first time here and I will at some point try it out for dinner, but hopefully my food will be better.  If it weren't for the phenomenal service, I would have rated this dining experience with a lower star rating, but the service was top-notch.

A true gem in the heart of Lafayette Square. I hadn't been here for years but went last night for a friend's birthday gathering and the drinks were amazing and the service was friendly and prompt.  Haven't eaten here but the drinks are awesome.  A very cool-looking plush place with lots of red and black.  Nice patio area in the back as well--the weather was perfect last night for it.
Just grabbed drinks here. Service was quick and friendly. Staff actively worked to help clear tables. Beautiful setting. Can't wait to visit again when the weather cools down!

Service was great. Server = friendly. Ordered the Tonkotsu Ramen as recommended by the server. I was very excited to try it as there really aren't any ramen houses in St. Louis.  It was DISAPPOINTING! Way too "done up." There were so many things going on with the dish-too salty, fatty pork cut too thick, weird spices, etc. A piece of advice--keep it SIMPLE. Also the broth did not resemble tonkotsu broth to me, which is supposed to be a pork bone broth that is creamier in texture. The broth was also really oily...too buttery. I must say my coworker enjoyed her burger, so maybe I should have gotten that instead. I love the atmosphere. Very cool patio and amazing rustic wooden decor. These guys definitely know how to decorate right--as Blood and Sand is also amazingly beautiful.    I'll try this place again but will opt for a dinner entree choice.
Okay food and service. Pretty friendly staff. Nothing really wowing about the place but if you're looking for a simple egg-y breakfast, this isn't a bad joint.

Delicious food and adequate, friendly service. My jalapeno burger was yummy. The UK sauces add a touch of authenticity. It was a slow lunch when I dined, but I bet it would be cool to come for a game day.

The place was cool looking and the service was good.  However, we did have to wait nearly an hour for a table when we were quoted a half an hour.  The food was good. I enjoyed the mussels and The Hill salad.  I think it's a bit overpriced for what the place is, however.
Darling little place! Downfall is that it is super tiny.  But the fall spice latte was delish!!! Service was friendly.

Checked out this place recently to celebrate my friend's birthday and generally it was a pleasant dining experience.  The restaurant was bustling when we arrived at 8pm but died down halfway through our dinner.  We were seated upstairs for our party of 5 and I must admit being the only ones left upstairs created an absence in ambiance.  

The food was overall very good. We tried everything from the beet salad to the mussels to the "fat-fried cornbread," which was phenomenal. I was recommended the chicken pot pie for my entree, which was a little disappointing. Portion very small and the dish lacked a creaminess and heartiness that I am typically used to with pot pies.  The server surprised us with a birthday dessert for my friend which was a very sweet gesture.

I gave this place a 4-star rating because of all the other good food we ordered and the top-notch service.  Server was friendly, at ease, and confident. Just don't recommend the pot pie next time!  Also, Andrey the Beverage Director of the place, came by and chatted with us about wine which was a nice enjoyable moment of the evening.  Try it out for yourselves!

This place is a fast-casual restaurant with good, fresh, flavorful options.  It was my first time here for lunch today, and I was thoroughly impressed. With the exception of one employee who could not crack a smile, all of my other interactions with the employees who were serving and bussing tables were very pleasant. You get a LOT of food for less than $10!  The gyro meat, at least on this occasion, was not dry like what some other reviewers mentioned.  Unlimited toppings is a huge plus! So you can load up the tzatziki, tomatoes, lettuce, feta, you name it! And you can choose a side and hummus.  Check it out for a delicious semi-healthy option that's not your typical pub fare.

Food 3.5-4
Drinks 3.5
Service 3

This place is "cool" and I can see why it's a trendy spot in town right now.  Since James Beard's name was tossed around, I decided to give this place a try. I'm all about checking out new places and really do enjoy craft cocktail and small-plate type of restaurants. Publico is a cute place located in the Loop with fun décor and a sleek ambiance.  Don't get me wrong, the food was overall good. However, honestly, for the price, I didn't see much value.  I'm all about paying for what seems relatively right.  I know sushi and steaks are expensive, so I will pay beaucoup dollars to get delicious sushi and steaks.  I get that. The fish tacos here were delicious and bursting with complex flavors, but I don't think I can justify coming back to spend $12 on two very small grilled fish tacos. The guacamole arepas were good and definitely something different, but to pay $10 for some guac on little coaster-sized pancakes seems like a lot. I also had the baby octopus, which came out submerged in some stew--this one, not so good at all. The margarita I had was good but not the best, and also $12.  Service was adequate and maybe a little pretentious. No one went out of their way to be friendly, but basic needs were met. We sat at the bar where the bartender greeted us relatively quickly, but then took 20 minutes to actually take an order.  Once we actually ordered, food came out quickly via a food runner.  

Ultimately, go for the experience, because it is a relatively unique place in St. Louis. If you have the disposable income, go again and try more stuff! If you don't, then you'll probably be better off getting $3 tacos and better service at Mission Taco down the street.

Gorgeous restaurant with a really cool, sleek ambiance.  Overall the service was great, with my server being both courteous and friendly and checking on us several times to make sure we were doing okay.  Others came by and picked up empty plateware, so I know the teamwork here among the staff is good.

Loved the roasted brussels sprouts--they were bursting with flavor.  Oyster Rockefeller plate was okay--not bad, not great.  My scallop dish was good, but also not great.  The scallops were cooked perfectly, but the bed of risotto that it came on had several clumps of rice, which was a bit unappetizing. However, the flavors were complex.

I tried the Ain't No Ferns cocktail and it was delicious. Would definitely come back to try some of the other cocktails on the list. 

Food was good but I really think the ambiance and service were the highlights of the experience.  Both this concept and Basso (the neighboring restaurant, same ownership I believe), are cool places to check out in STL with distinct ambiances.

I just checked out Porano for the first time a couple of days ago. Service was okay but quick. The ambiance is modern, clean, and brightly lit.  The taste of the food was meh.  The Sunday Sugo sauce was recommended and I didn't love it.  The price is not bad--even though the bowls look kind of small (at least to me they do), they are pretty filling. Overall, this place was decent and I'd probably give it another chance, but it wasn't to die for or impressive. The quick service part is a plus and I can see why it's such a draw for business people downtown who need to be in and out of a place to eat.  Oh, also, warning--strange soda alert!  You'll have to observe the fancy sodas closely to figure out what they are....and you still may not be able to figure it out just by looking at the label.

That farmhouse burger!!! It was one of the juiciest burgers I've ever had. It is a "fancy" burger, but definitely worth a try. Service was good and friendly overall, though the second half of our experience we weren't checked on much. Hipster nation. Not sure if I was trendy enough to be there.
Service was great. Pizza was yummy. Place was packed at 5pm on a Sunday.  Nothing to complain about! Keep it up!

Tried the all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ and the flavor and offerings were good. However, the kalbi (a Korean marinated rib delicacy) had soooo many bone chips in it. I had to pick out several pieces of small bone.  This was a major factor in my review score.  The ribs should be rinsed with water before being marinated to avoid this. For a second, my friend thought she chipped her tooth because of this. Service was decent for an Asian restaurant. I was a big fan of the pork belly eaten as ssam (lettuce wraps). Otherwise, this is the trendiest Korean restaurant in STL-very cool modern decor. Worth checking out. Just beware of the kalbi.

I came to this place because of Yelp. The food is great. High quality ingredients and excellent preparation.
Two things were not clear to me, though. No. 1, the place is kind of small with a limited menu. What they offer is good.
The other thing is that they have few of the delicious looking baked items shown in the pix. I want me some lemon meringue! And everything else looks delicious. But they never have it.
Yelp steered me wrong here. I've tried Sup three times and it's not that good. I like Micheal's much better.

This food is real hit and miss. Some days it is really good. Some days I'm ready to send it back. Perhaps they have problems having a competent chef there seven days a week. 
The beer selection is good, but frequently they don' thave what is listed on the beer menu.
I've had the waitress disappear on me, too.
I've stopped going. That's why I rate it one star.
This is not for the restaurant. It's for the bakery and deli. They sell too much old food out of the bakery. Stuff that should have been thrown away two days earlier, it seems.

The food is good enough. Three stars for that. But it's overpriced for what you get. So the poor value brings it down to two stars. There's better places to spend my money.
Sometimes service is good. Sometimes it is poor.

I've only been here once, but it was enough to convince me not to return. The sushi was definitely not fresh. On top of it, they kept messing up my orders. There's too many other good sushi places in the area.

It seems Old Granite Street eatery has been in decline for a while. It started before the new chef came and the new menu doesn't seem to help. Some of the items on the new menu just taste bad. I miss some of the old items. And overall the food doesn't seem as skillfully prepared as it was before.

The first time I came here several years ago, the food was really good. The last couple of times it hasn't been that good. It tastes like maybe they're cutting corners on the quality of ingredients. And it doesn't seem to have been prepared with the same kind of care. 
Plus, I've never liked the margaritas here.
I'm wondering if they changed chefs or maybe even changed owners.

Two stars for the pizza. It's not the best pizza in town. The ingredients are not fresh. Just the overall attitude of the place brings it down to one star. It's a business. You're supposed to serve customers. Get rid of the attitude.
Oh, the wings are terrible, too.

Love the Awful Awful here. It's a great burger. The rest of the food can be hit or miss. Some times they don't even cook it properly. 
The full bar is also a nice option.

Usually the food is good. Sometimes there's problems. I've yet to have chicken here I like.
If they had a better beer selection, I'd definitely rate it four stars.
Service seems to be getting worse, though., There's a lot of people running around but no one is helping us.

Yelp missed the boat on this one. The burgers are okay, but they're not that good. I guess maybe if you like big fluffy bread, the burgers are good. 
Everything else seemed ordinary. Like you could get at any neighborhood restaurant.
I drove clear across the Truckee Meadows to try this place and it wasn't worth the trip.

The burgers are good but the price is expensive. I've been here four times now and I may not come again. What's supposed to make them different is that they don't have drug-injected beef like other places. That's good. But in the end the burgers don't taste better than other places. 
I've tried a couple of their specialty burgers and they weren't that special.

It's an okay burger, but what is supposed to make it worth the price they charge? Plus if you add toppings, it makes it messy and hard to eat.
The only reason it doesn't get one star is because the staff is usually helpful the times I've gone there. So the workers are good.

I think I'm going to stop coming here after my last experience. 
I found myself in this area right before I had to go to a friend's house for dinner and decided to pick up the groceries here. I had to buy a lot of fruit and vegetables. 
That turned out to be a mistake. These must have been the worst fruit and vegetables I've seen in a supermarket in a long time. I picked through everything the best I could, grabbed some other items and then went through check out. They only had two cashiers and the lines were going everywhere. It took forever to get checked out. 
The grocery store selection in south Reno is just terrible.
