I went to Woodlands yesterday, based on the good reviews here. Maybe I caught the swing shift; it was only 4 pm. The raitha was so watered down that it didn't even cling to my chapati when I dipped it. The mint sauce was likewise watery and tasteless. The waiter couldn't explain any of the dishes, except to nod his head and say "Yes, hot" when I asked if something could be made extra-spicy. The food was forgettable at best, and thesoup advertised as traditional spicy Indian tomato soup tasted exactly like Campbell's tomato soup from a can, with some black pepper added. 
I live just outside Nashville and am always in search of great food here. Perhaps the lunch buffet is better, but for "real" Indian food locally, Shalimar is still, sadly, the only game in town.

I eat here once a week. The pho is really good, and they'll bring extra vegetables without a murmur (unlike Kien Giang). The cold rice rolls are likewise very good. I have to admit that Kien Giang beats them on the pork with noodles front - the KG pork marinade is much much better, and the pieces are nice and thick, unlike Miss Saigon's thin small slices. Also, the shrimp they use in their noodle dishes are the tiny, horribly salty shrimp. AND... I was overcharged once as well, though I got the money back.
But. I have to admit, the vegetables are fresher, and the food tastier, than any other Vietnamese restaurant in town. So keep an eye on your bill, order the pho, and you won't be disappointed.

It's sad that so many Nashvillians actually think this is deli food; if this was New York, they'd have been stoned out of business long ago. 
And it's no wonder that their health rating is usually in the gutter. The tomatoes are always the cheapest, mealiest in town. Half the time the pickles were frozen and end up mushy. The latkes (potato pancakes) are usually grey from sitting out too long, and that's just breakfast. 
I really really wish Nashville had one great Jewish deli. Then again, I wish Nashville had one great Chinese restaurant too. It's a pity, because we certainly have a large enough population to support both.

Maybe we hit this on a bad evening; Miss Saigon was closed, so we decided on the basis of these reviews to try this place. The food was so bad that we left without doing more than taste it. Gummy, lukewarm, completely unappetizing to the eye and mouth. Like Erin D., I found the portions sadly lacking compared to Kien Giang or Miss Saigon, particularly the fresh vegetables (which looked 3-4 days old). Sorry, but stick with Miss S. and Kien G. if you don't want tobe put off Vietnamese food for life.

I go to Shintomi a lot, alone, and with my family - probably 5-6 times a month. The sushi, admittedly, is average IF you've had really good sushi in Japan or a major city here. (To be perfectly honest, the sushi at Ichiban is better.) The wait staff vary from speak-no-English-don't-care-when-your-food-comes to really friendly, articulate and knowledgeable. The food rating is a lot lower than I'd prefer. 
But for my money, they have absolutely the best nabeyaki udon in town, and one of the best in the country (even though they're skimpy with the vegetables and chicken). Their gyoza likewise is the best in town. Their prices are still reasonable, too.
The one thing I wish they'd add (are you listening, Shintomi?) is a basic sauteed vegetable dish - without sauces, just lots of broccoli, onion, whatever they have. And enoki mushrooms in the soup, instead of those bland American standbys.
I disagree that Peter's has better sushi. They have bigger rolls, but most are fried. And the sushi quality isn't really any higher. (Though they do have a fantastic green curry!) Given my druthers, Shintomi is more the local friendly hang, with good specials like hamachi-kama for $8.95 this week, and a huge portion of it, too.
My two objections as noted previously are the lack of plain vegetable dishes, both at lunch and dinner, and the low health rating (in the 80's.) But I've never gotten sick from eating here, as I have from Noshville, so maybe the health rating is just picky stuff. Who knows?!

I stopped in here for lunch yesterday - major error! The buffet was forgettable at best, the food high in grease and low in taste. In fact, it was so bad that after tasting each item once, I paid and left, in search of a decent lunch.

Let's face it. Da Vinci's was better back in the day, when the owners were a married couple and she pretty much ran the place. Pizza Perfect is sometimes okay, sometimes good, and sometimes awful, depending on whether the owner/head chef farms all the duties out to some Lipscomb students who could care less or a church set who don't care at all. Domino's does deliver, but that's about it. For anyone who's had real, thin crust pizza in New York City, Joey's is the real deal. My first meal there, I ordered a plain cheese pizza - my test. As I watched the steaming cheese slipping around on the perfect thin crust, I looked at my companion with tears in my eyes. No, really. It was that good, to know that finally, someone in Nashville was making pizza the old-fashioned way.
Okay, the salad is forgettable at best. Okay, some of the toppings leave a great deal to be desired. But if you want a real NY pizza fix, this is the place.
As to people complaining about the service - it's "Joey's Pizza". Not "Joey's Italian Delicacies." Not "Joey's Gourmet Pizza." You won't find lobster pizza here, no sir. Just great, basic, New York style pizza.

My family and I have eaten here twice, once to "check it out" and once as a birthday celebration. Both times, our waitress "Heather" was wonderfully knowledgeable, and extremely well-trained. Both times, everything on the table was fabulous - but I must mention the roast chicken, which is the best I've ever had. One of us is allergic to eggs, and the kitchen went all-out to make certain she wasn't served any, including making her fresh rolls as the normal ones are "brushed with egg white."
If I had one complaint, it would be that there doesn't seem to be a way to change anything in your order from what's offered - eg one of us wanted the steak, but instead of the menu vegetable, requested the melange being offered with another dish. She was told that could be done, but it wasn't. This happened to us the prior time, as well. While I understand the chef's desire to present all dishes as the chef dreamed, sometimes people just don't want a certain vegetable or potato with that dish. I think that those requests should be politely accomodated when it's only a vegetable substitution. 
That being said, I would also love to see another dish as simple as the chicken offered - but I will go back many times, you can be sure!

This was my second visit to a Ted's Montana Grill, and like the first, I was both satisfied and disappointed. The bio-degradable straws are a silly "feel good" measure when their chickens are not organic. (One of my party was allergic to the antibiotics, and after much time the manager finally told us they'd recently changed suppliers, and the new ones had probably been fed same. He did inform us that the bison was antibiotic-free, but that's not much help when you want chicken.) The waitress was overwhelmed and under-informed; we had to ask a passing waiter for everything from wine and beer recommendations to water refills. The rib eye steak was all right, but nowhere near as good as the one Bosco's serves. The short ribs tasted exactly like the pot roast, which we all found strange. And the crab cakes had so much breading, they weren't even worth eating.
However... the sweet potato was amazingly delicious and perfectly cooked. The pot roast, and accompanying sauce, were likewise wonderful, as was the bison burger.
I would go here for a lunch burger or chili, but don't recommend spending your money on a dinner, or a celebration meal.

Okay. Best rotisserie chicken in Nashville (and I'm a Whole Foods fan). Best black bean salad ever. Great service BUT - make sure not to go on the weekends, when the staff by and large appear hung over and not at all helpful. During the week, though, yum! I get the black bean salad with beef, and ask them to "nuke the beans and beef" so the cheese melts. The chips are homemade and about as good as it gets. The staff are friendly and helpful. All in all, a great lunch spot.

Let's forget about food for a minute, and talk about community. When CPK opened in Nashville, I saw black and white patrons by the dozens eating at the same restaurant. Now, this happened periodically before, but only at specialty restaurants (Swett's for ribs comes to mind). Suddenly, all races, all colors were together. Then came Whoile Foods. Astonishing. All races and colors may shop at Kroger, but they don't shop "together". Whole Foods has done more to diversify Nashville than anything since the Civil Rights Act. The different styles of the employees are a joy for one starved by a mono-chromatic culture -- there's the black oh-so-gay bagger, the formerly-Wild-Oats-vegan-Dad who's finally got good health insurance. The employees are incredibly friendly and helpful, and if something's wrong, they have the leeway to fix it. The Grill area isn't that interesting - the seating leaves a lot to be desired - but the food is good. If I had any criticisms, they would be that a) the food bars really, really deteriorate between 11 or 11.30 am and the start of the lunch rush - I've eaten food that tasted like it was cooked yesterday and just shoved out there to get rid of it, and b) the salad dressing containers are impossible. You can't shake them without it going everywhere, so the oil congeals on top, and you only alternative is to grab half a dozen napkins, close the hole with them, shake like crazy, then hope there's a nearby garbage pail.
That being said, the credo "If you want to taste it just say so!" has exposed me tomore new food than I'd ever have imagined. The cheese counter is a marvel. The vegetables and fruits are normally the best in town (though once in a while they fall down.)
In short, Nashville really needed this, and I shop there daily.

Oh dear. Could I have hit them on a bad day? Twice? The pork souvlaki, highly recommended by the waitress, came cut up in pieces with chunks of fat on the ends. The promised amazing spices were not. We had the calamari (tasteless, just battered and fried, no special sauce, no seasoning), and a pork souvlaki and a lamb/beef gyro. The salad dressings were salted to death. The pork and beef were tasteless. Folks, go to Athens, or for upscale, Anatolia. Maybe it was just because we came for early lunch, but this was about as bland and tasteless as I want to get...

The spread was quite amazing - everything from a raw bar (oysters, clams, crab) to huge amounts of quite good sushi (and I've even had it in Japan!) to dim sum (forgettable) to soups (my one criticism. The soups are terrible, and not hot. The hot & sour is all vinegar all the time.) The grilled vegetables with protein - I had shrimp - was fabulous. I've been here 3 times, most recently hristmas dinner with a bunch of Jewish friends. My only criticisms would be that a) the place was freezing on Christmas, and nobody bothered turning on the heat, and b) the waiters need to either learn a bit more English, or just admit that their English isn't good, and ask the host to translate. Otherwise, the buffet is fabulous, and the ikura sushi is the best in town.
Was I surprised? You bet!

This is probably the least predictable restaurant in Nashville, and not in a good way. We went there last weekend after a long absence in the hopes that things were better. 
I have to say, the service was fantastic, and because of the Christmas decorations, the whole place was a bit brighter. Staff are friendly and helpful, and it's a stunning atmosphere to eat in. 
I ordered duck because I love duck - the waitress warned me that the chef tended to cook it "until pink". I stressed that I like poultry cooked through, but it arrived red at the center. She kindly took it back for me, and it re-appeared, now pink in the center. No way was it cooked through.
I don't know who told a few Nashville chefs - the chef at Miel does the same thing - that they're cool if THEY decide YOUR food preferences - but I really resent it when I'm paying good money and ask for something specific, then get the chef's preference instead. 
I also don't know who decided that pork and poultry should be served rare, but that seems to be happening a lot here. I'm sorry; I don't care where the poultry comes from, or how carefully it's raised - I still like it cooked!
I wish places like Mad Platter, Miel, City House (who serve rare sausage) would hire chefs who could also cook a "normal" meal. I've had gourmet dining all over the world, spend a lot of time in Italy, and have to say, dinners like these make me long for your basic pork chop and baked potato.
Sorry, Mad Platter. Wish it had gone better.

My family and I have been eating at Calypso since they opened on Elliston Place. It would appear they now have four locations, and great consistency among them. This isn't really Caribbean food, it isn't really American food, it's just good food. Chips are always fresh, they have the crunchiest jalapenos I've ever had, wait staff are pleasant and competent (though I have to admit, on weekends the one on Thompson Lane tends to suffer in that regard.)
Black beans can be too hard or too soft, but Calypso's are always perfect. Their black bean salad with beef is a real stunner (though I always ask them to "nuke the beans and beef" so they're really really hot). Their rotisserie chicken is the best in town (sorry, Whole Foods), and there's plenty for my vegan son to eat as well.
The only problem I've ever had at any of them is noise level; go early or late, before the lunch/dinner crowd arrive, if you don't want to be shouting. But go, definitely.

This is by far the best Starbucks in the Nashville area - Cordell is always upbeat, the staff really go out of their way to make you happy. Drinks are hot, and the only annoying thing is that someone needs to put cones up between the two handicapped spots in front so idiots stop parking there!!! 
Nice seating in the back, comfortable for laptops or reading. No pressure to move on. And yes, a really great mix of types.

When it first opened, in the location across from what was formerly Green Hills Grille, Shalimar was amazing - brilliant food, and totally different from anything Nashville had seen before. Admittedly, I wasn't happy that evey single thing on the menu was a la carte - everywhere else I'd lived, Indian food came with a chutney tray, raita, etc. But the food was, admittedly, amazing.
I've tried to like Shalimar these past four or five years, truly I have. Worked to like the mango lhassi. Hoped for better tandoori chicken. Wished the tikka masala tasted like anything other than bland nothingness. Most of all, I've wanted the Saturday buffet to be worthwhile. 
Alas. How is it possibe that the tikka, tandoori, and vindaloo all taste exactly the same? or that the tandoori has no sliced onions, let alone lemon? or that, no matter how much money we spend, everything tastes bland bland bland?
I can't imagine that the original Shalimar owner - who seemed to be simultaneously owner, chef, and waiter - would let it go this far... but I now go to Cuisine of India for my buffets, and for my tandoori. It's sad, because Shalimar is in my neighborhood, but the old grey mare ain't what she used to be.
Too bad. In its prime, it was as fine an Indian restaurant as I've seen in the US!

Ohhhhh... used to be amazingly good, and (sorry for using this word) authentic. Grew and grew. Expanded. Cleaned up. Not as good now, alas. Still, if you're visiting, it's a great place for breakfast. (Though frankly, I'd send/take visiting folk to One Stop Cafe in Franklin for down-home funky eats...)

Oh yum! And clean!! Friendly and efficient, too - I've been there four times so far. The third time, my wife wanted green curry, but they'd featured it the day before. We were very disappointed, until the chef (a lovely older woman) said she would go ahead and make it for us. Amazing.
You have to be careful to really specify "Thai hot" if that's what you want - otherwise, they're prone to under-spicing (though they'll bring you more spice on request.) They even chopped up a bunch of Thai chili peppers for my wife.
As for me, I'd been told the Pad Thai was unusual, and great. It was no disappointment. For years, I thought I didn't like PT -- what I discovered here is that I'd just been having bad Pad Thai. This was a revelation -- not sweet, not sticky, full of bean sprouts and yum.
Smiling Elephant really does their own versions of classic Thai dishes. Their Yum Woon Sen is completely different from any I've had before - more a cross between a Yum Woon Sen and a Larb Gai (which, sadly, they do not have.)
Like I said, I've been four times, and each time was as good as the last. My only criticism would be that the restaurant really needs a few basic salad choices - cold vegetables, something crunchy and plain to cut through the heat!

This used to be my favorite local sushi restaurant - good value, good food. Unfortunately, the owner (Sonny) seems to have decided that recession equals rip-off. The food has gone so far downhill that my wife and I now regard Shintomi as our last choice. The Nabeyaki udon is still the best in town, but they've cut back on the shiitake and subbed American mushrooms. No more Enoki, either. The seaweed salad,at $7.95, is not only over-priced - it's poor quality. The same dish at Koi or Peter's is almost half the price and twice the taste. It's unfortunate, because this used to be a great place.
Oh, a word of warning. Their health score keeps going down, too...

In desperate search of a healthy burger place that will supplement the admittedly fabulous Whole Foods counter restaurant, my wife and I ate here this past weekend. 
The chicken wings were completely outstanding, although we could have done without the smoked paprika afterthought on the celery and carrot that accompanied. (Buyer beware - if you inhale too quickly, you can actually begin to choke on the darn stuff!) I wish the dip had been blue cheese rather than a watery ranch, but as a real buffalo wings lover, these were outstanding.
I loved that for an extra dollar, you can sub salad or any other sides for the fries.
The reviews that complain about slow service are somewhat correct, but our server (and all the servers we saw) were willing and helpful. Sadly, the host who greeted us was not so much, looking like we'd bothered him during an Extremely Important moment. (And this at four in the afternoon, not exactly a crush!)
The ambiance is lovely, though I'd imagine it would get a bit noisy when full. My wife loved the place settings, especially the napkins, actually small French-style dish towels. 
My wife had the bean and quinoa burger, surprisingly good and moist! I had the turkey burger, not as good sadly... the turkey itself was fabulous, but the couple of tiny, limp pieces of lettuce on it were a huge disappointment.  The grilled onions were sadly tasteless, too. 
 Their house ketchup is more a salsa than ketchup, and it would have been nice if our server had let us know (before we'd finished eating!) that "regular" ketchup was available. 
I found myself wishing for the average burger place's crisp raw onion, pickle slices, and fat tomatoes. I suppose, if I'd thought to ask, they'd have given me all of that. 
Still, the menu is about as varied as you can get, with lamb burgers (!) available, as well as vegan choices, and we will definitely be going back. Next time, I'll know what to ask for!!!
Oh! It's very kid-friendly, and with Las Paletas right next door, a fabulous dessert is just a heartbeat away!

We don't drink much, so the beer is meaningless, although when we've taken guests there everyone loves the "taster", where you're served around 10 shot glasses, each with a different beer. We go to Bosco's for the ribeye steak - absolutely the best in town, and we've tried all the "big deal" places - and the smoked pork chops. On two occasions, my steak was overcooked (I asked for rare; the first time it was medium rare but on such a hot plate that within minutes it was well. The second, it was just medium.) Without a murmur, the manager or waiter took it back and brought a new one. Seriously recommend this place.

Oh Arnold, we miss you! When you were a regular presence, the lettuce was fresh, the cucumber wasn't frozen. The sashimi didn't present as slabs of glossy flesh hacked out of a mountainside of fish, like strip mining at its worst. Where are you?!

My family loves PM. We revel in the atmosphere. One of our favorite things about it is the wonderful cross-section of humanity represented here, from elderly folk who've lived in the Sterling Court Apartments forever, to young almost-hip Belmont students. But lately, it's gone awry.

Perhaps it's the new menu? When first ordered a few years back, the seaweed salad was the best in town, and highly unusual - wonderfully delicate strands of seaweed sitting atop mounds of dulce and ocean greens I have yet to identify. Never greasy, always large enough for two. Now, it comes drowned in sauce - though I have to say, if ordered with the disclaimer "Please make sure it isn't drowning in sauce", most of the waitrons will drain it. Still, it's nowhere near the surprisingly fabulously huge and delicate repast we were used to.

Perhaps it's the sashimi? I'm not sure who trains Arnold's sushi chefs, and I realize this is not per se a Japanese restaurant, but if you're going to serve sushi, have a bit more respect for the fish! The chirashi is great value, no argument there - enough for two, at least - but I personally would prefer not to have to cut my sashimi into thirds and fourths before it fits in my mouth. What's the point of sashimi, if not the delicacy and the enjoyment of a succulent mouthful that melts on the tongue, rather than huge pieces with gristle and fat still clinging to them, interrupting all taste sensation with overkill?

Nashville has some of the best Vietnamese restaurants in the country, which begs the question - why on earth advertise "Vietnamese spring rolls" and then present these dried up wallflowers, with a sauce that plainly comes straight out of a bottle? Kien Giang at its worst could do better!

The final insult? the "salad" served on the side of the fabulous Thai wrap. The wrap itself is a thing of beauty, perfectly balanced, but the "salad" that accompanies it is a disgrace. We ordered it for the third time tonight, and it was no better than the other times - the lettuce had been sitting far too long, the cucumber slices looked like they'd been frozen, and over-all, the entire thing could have used some serious attention.

Patty Myint was there tonight, and I wih I'd taken the opportunity to show her my "salad" - the brown, curled lettuce edges, the barely-defrosted ice on cucumber slices. The daub of wasabi next to my sashimi, with an outside crust proving it had been sitting far too long. But to be honest, I didn't have the nerve. This woman has single-handedly re-shaped Nashville's dining - why bother her with minor details?

I love PM, believe it or not. It's in my district. It's kid-friendly, and the outdoor seating is lovely. Those of you following my reviews know we used to go to Shintomi, but no more - so where to go for sashimi in the 'hood? Ginza is embarrassing, Watanabe too far. PM is the obvious solution - but oh, Arnold, how we miss you! Please come home, Arnold!! Hollywood may beckon, but Nashville needs you!!

I've spent about a third of my life in Japan, so when I get a "jones" for sushi I really want sushi. I was extremely excited to see a new sushi restaurant opening near my business office, particularly after checking the reviews for Kohana in Hendersonville and Clarksville. My wife and I went with great expectations.
Let me start by saying that the restaurant's only been open a little while. Still, our waiter told us the owners had "imported" staff and chefs from the other restaurants, so the recent opening is no excuse.
We arrived the first time just after dinner hour opening, were greeted and seated by a friendly hostess. When we got up to look at the sushi bar, the sushi chef behind it couldn't be bothered to look up and greet us - not even make eye contact. We stood there awkwardly for a minute, then returned to the table.
We ordered age dashi tofu, which arrived in a huge mound of slightly-warm tofu with a dash - really, just a dash - of sauce. Nothing else on it. When we asked the waiter where the grated daikon the menu promised was, he checked with the chef, then came back to say "Chef says they've never, ever made it that way, he doesn't understand why it says that on the menu." The tofu was mealy, the sauce was forgettable, and without the grated vegetables, disappointing.
We ordered the gyoza, which were actually quite good - not fried to death like so many other restaurants. Reminiscent of the old Shintomi when it was still the best in this area. However, the gyoza sauce tasted like someone had thrown a batch of vinegar into a bowl, splashed a teaspoon of soy sauce, and forgotten any other ingredients.
(As an aside, until it went fervently downill my wife and daughters and I ate at Shintomi at least twice a week for years. They had the best gyoza sauce I've ever eaten, including in Tokyo!)
We loved the beautiful picture menu of sushi rolls. My wife adores crab, and was excited to see that certain rolls specified "crabstick" (surimi - imitation crab), while another specified "snow crab." Since she is allergic to imitation crab, she happily ordered the roll made with "snow crab." Ordinarily, if a restaurant lists the two differently, we don't double check, but the prior two dishes made me nervous, so I asked the waiter whether it was in fact real snow crab. "Oh, no. ALL our crab is imitation crabstick." What? Really?! With snow crab cheap enough that Denny's features it, you're substituting surimi? 
Yes. Fake crab. In a restaurant charging $14-$18 a roll!
Well, we cancelled the roll and moved on. I ordered ikura sushi, one of my personal tests of a good Japanese restaurant, along with seaweed salad. The salad was delicious. The ikura was embarrassingly bad. I would expect to see it at an all-you-can-eat sushi buffet.
Thinking perhaps a non-Japanese item would fare better, we ordered the calimari. Delicious.
I went back for lunch a few days later, and again asked about the crab, and was told the same thing. When I asked why the three menus at dinner and lunch differentiated between "snow crab" "crab stick" and "imitation crab", the waiter just shrugged.
If you want good Japanese food in Nashville, without the health complications of a corporate entity that cheaps out where it counts (and don't think the imitation crab rolls are inexpensive!), go to Midori. It's a bit of a hike, but the sushi's always good, and their Korean food is excellent. Or go to Koto, sometimes hit or miss but usually very good. Or try Miyako. Or even Hanabi, which has begun to slide but is still way more than decent. 
But don't expect anything except LA-style atmosphere out of Kohana Green Hills.

This was our fourth dinner here. Love that they don't charge a fee for splitting a dish, because portions are large. Good value for the money; bar doesn't overcharge. Oysters are delicious and it's wonderful that the Apalachicolas are affordable during "happy hour". Closer to the symphony than The Palm. Waitrons always friendly, and visiting the ladies room is a must - very cool decor and film! 
Re the "disappointed" reviews, I don't think The Southern pretends to be destination dining - that would be more like Debra Paquette's new place a block away, "Etch". It's cozy home cooking.
Wish list:
More "plain" items on the menu, like the asparagus. (Delicious!)
A plain ribeye steak on the menu.
A quiet area - maybe blocked off a little? - where a booth or table for 2-4 could actually hear one another talk after 6 pm. I know there's a private dining room but don't think it's available just for a regular dinner.

My family used to eat here at least once a week for dinner. Then they changed the menu - completely - getting rid of a lot of our favorites, halving the selections, and instructing the staff not to fill special requests (eg "Could we have garlic spinach with that instead of kale?" They used to go over to the vegetable area and just bring back spinach. No more.) The new menu is something you'd expect to see in an LA-wanna-be restaurant, not a local grill. They still have one of the best burgers in town, but on our last few trips we thought they were price-cutting rather than serving the kind of quality food we'd come to expect. The daily specials are usually good, and the fish tacos, but the rest is really cheap-looking -- even on paper -- and not worth the tariff. Very disappointing. I don't understand why they don't just go to a real seasonal menu, four times a year, with lots of choices. 
They WILL cook to order if you pick up something in the store - eg a steak - BUT there's a big up charge ($5 I think) in addition to their already high prices.
Very disappointing of late. We've stopped going and won't go again until the menu is sorted out.

Order "Thai hot". Person at counter takes order. Looks quizzical. You specify again "Thai hot" and say "I've lived in Thailand. I really mean it." Wait five minutes. 
Counter person brings your food to the table and says "Here is your order. Not hot." You say "What?!" She says "Not hot." You say Cook didn't believe me?" She says "Yes." You say "I ordered it hot, not mild." She says "Cook says when she wants hot, she adds this." 
Points to very old, very dusty, very out of date dried red pepper flakes you put on the table just in case. 
You point out that spices taste very different when cooked with the food rather than sprinkled on top. She agrees. You say you're very unhappy about this. She agrees. You say "Smiling Elephant makes it Thai hot for me. And it's delicious. Why did I even bother trying your restaurant?" She says oh no, you will like this. Even if it's absolutely not what you ordered and not the order she took.
You sprinkle a ton of the out of date dried red pepper flakes on the gelatinous mess she's put in front of you, just to make the point. Then you leave, along with your companion, who says the Larb Gai was the greasiest, fattiest Larb Gai he'd ever tasted. He left most of it on the plate. He did say he liked the unsweetened iced tea.
I went here because of the reviews. Must have been a different chef that day. This was without a doubt the worst Thai food I've had in my life. 
Note to the restaurant. If you're going to take an order for "Thai hot" and allow someone to pay for it, have the decency to MAKE it Thai hot. Or refund the money.
Go to Thai Elephant. Or even International Market. But not here.

Filling healthy food try it

Oddly, the menu is odd, oddly delicious. Don't be fooled by the small plates any of the bowls are too much for me and more that is enough for my 6foot husband. The wait staff is very helpful. If you've never tried Thai or had Thai that was meh give this place a try. We took another couple who were hesitant they left saying it was the best food they had ever eaten. I've tried a few things on the menu the curry is wonderful it's not like the curry from other cultures like India or Jamaica it's lighter. I don't know what else well the pineapple fried rice is delicious and served in half a pineapple. Ok, one note though. I was brought up with spicy food I love hot peppers no way I would ever order a Thai dish hot. My husband did... Once lol. If it's your first time go for mild not even medium trust me on this. You don't use chopsticks with this food except for pad Thai and there is a story behind that you might want to look up. They have a full bar. The iced tea is good. Service with a smile and prompt. Excellent. I haven't had Greek food this good in years. The place is pretty and clean. Waitstaff (Brianna )was great. The manager, Danny, came over to see that we had everything we needed. Ok, it says buffet and I guess it is kinda. It's a hot pot restaurant. Lovely pastries. Real works of art . A bit pricey but no more than I expected them to be . I wish I had taken a picture but alas they were consumed very quickly . All 18 lol

It's good food but be prepared to wait it's all made fresh . I had the fried chicken which was very good my husband had the tacos not to be confused with Mexican tacos they are totally different . The other couple also had the chicken and the Carne asada . The meat was delicious. I'd never had Honduran food before but I will definitely have it again. Try it .
Get the wings . Really get the wings . Everything else is good but the wings are outstanding . Get the wings

og3jtLj21flZ2Xtlu82Oww.review_text: I went to The Victoria Freehouse for lunch the other day, and I really enjoyed it. I liked the layout of the place and loved the Harry Potter banners. What I'm assuming was the owner was really nice. We ordered the crab on toast, curry chips, pickled beetroot deviled eggs, and chicken and chips. It was all very good. Even my fiancé enjoyed it, and he's usually really picky.
This is my favorite pizza place. The staff is incredibly friendly. I love the house salad and the Chicago pie. The salads are always fresh and the pies are always hot.

This is my favorite place to order sushi. The food is always fresh and delicious. Most of staff is very nice. There are a couple of waitresses that seem annoyed but are never rude. Just not overly friendly, while others are very pleasant. My favorite rolls are the Jamie roll, crunchy salmon roll, and the eel roll. My fiancé really likes the mushroom soup. I've tried many of the rolls, and so far the only one I didn't like was the crazy tuna roll.

This place is really cool. It has fun treats and a fun design. The staff was really nice as well. I split the resses Belgian waffle with my fiancé and got his sister a strawberry and a nutella macaroon. She said they were amazing.
The pizza is good, but not amazing. They have a lot to choose from and the staff is really polite. It's nice to go to if you're in the neighborhood and want something quick.

My grandmother use to take my sister and I here when we were young. We always would get the "smiley face" cookies. Since then, I have loved this bakery! Nothing compares! My mom loves their doughnuts, my hhsband loves their brownies. The Washington cake, chocolate logs, blueberry cupcakes, apple cake are all amazing! I love the pretzels they sell for New Years as well. They made my wedding cake. It was chocolate chip with buttercream. It was beautiful and delicious!

I had the veggie burger which was really good but fell apart very easily. My husband had the turkey burger. He's very picky, but he did like it, so that's saying something. The fries were very good and the cole slaw was just okay. Overall this place was really good. I plan on going back again sometime.

I really enjoyed this place. I love the vintage vibe you get. The grilled cheeses are not your average grilled cheese. They're unique and delicious. The fries are homemade and very good. The tomato soup reminds me greatly of my husband's homemade soup, which is excellent. The service was also very good.

After seeing posts about Sweet Box all over social media, I decided to stop in. The lady behind the register was very nice and helpful. It's a small place, but they still had a nice selection. We got a bunch of stuff. I loved the strawberry and champagne cupcake and the chocolate chip cookies. Everything was fairly priced for the large sizes you are getting.

I have a favorite sushi place that unfortunately is not very close to me. I've tried finding one a bit closer that would compare with no luck. Until I tried Masami. I love this place, and the fact that they deliver makes it even better. It's not the closest place to me, yet they still deliver to my house and in a promptly manner. There's a lot of options, and I find most are really good. I highly recommend the spicy kani salad. That is both mine and my sister in law's favorite. The pork dumplings are really good. My mother in law is obsessed with the bbq squid. It's hard to pick a favorite roll. I like just about everyone I have tried.

Overall, I like Buffalo Wild Wings. I think some items are slightly overpriced for what you're getting, but other items are pretty fairly priced. I've never had a bad waitress or a negative experience. Last time I was there though, the hostess was no where to be found. It wasn't a busy day, and it took about 10 minutes before She headed back. Our waitress was great and so was the food we ordered.

My husband and nephew had the pepperoni pie. My sister and I split a personal clam pie. We went to pick our order up, and I was immediately impressed with how kind the staff was. The guy even walked us out. They give you small containers of garlic salt, oregano, pepper flakes, and cheese. I thought that was a cool touch. My nephew is the pickiest eater you can imagine. If anything is slightly different than what he's use to, he doesn't like it. To our surprise, he liked it a lot. He even went back for seconds! The clam pie was amazing, and I highly recommend it!

I have gone here about four times. Each time the food was delicious and the waitresses were very nice. The last time we went, our waiter's name was John. He was helpful, kind, and very funny. The stuff shells and pasta are very good. My brother really likes the chicken parm and the pizza is amazing.

I've been wanting to go here for about a year now. I've heard great things about Green Eggs Cafe, and it didn't disappoint. The Lox Egg Benedict was amazing as well as their signature potatoes. My husband had the Turkey Panini. It had avocado salsa and sprouts. He enjoyed it as well. The staff is nice and the service was very quick. The portions are huge, so you're definitely getting your money's worth. We will be going back. The menu looked too appetizing not to.

The pizza is absolutely amazing. They only come in personal size. Our waitress was really nice and the inside is nice, but we sat in one of those half table half booths. Normally I don't mind, but you are sat so close to the other customers, that getting up is incredibly uncomfortable. You feel like you're invading their space and it's almost impossible to prevent some part of your body from being in their face when you do get up. I've never tried the Gelato but would come back to try it being as it looks delicious! The prices are a bit steep, but it is excellent quality pizza. Based on the price and kind of strange seating, it's not a place I'd go all the time. They do have tables but it seems to be a busy place, so it depends on how long you're wanting to wait to be seated. It's a nice place to go once in a while though.

The food here is really good and the atmosphere is really nice. I've gone here many times and never had a bad experience. The service is always great and the staff is really friendly. My only complaint is that some things on the menu are slightly over priced. The menu has a nice selection though.

I ordered the Tuscany chicken wrap. It was the greasiest thing I have ever eaten. There was literally a puddle of grease on my plate. The tortilla was undercooked and gummy. The chicken was bland. Tasted as if it was cooked plain with zero seasoning. The Italian wedding soup was decent and the service was okay.
Good service and great food! My favorites are the crab fries, sweet potato fries, mussels (you get a ton!), wings, and shrimp. The sizes are great for the prices.

Nice restaurant with fast service. The food is flavorful and very filling. Chips and salsa are included with the meal. The serving is small compared to other places, but the salsa is very good. The staff is friendly. I thought it would be slightly more traditional Mexican food but it was still very good.

We were seated immediately and greeted by the nicest staff. Our waiter was very friendly and prompt. The menu had a nice selection. I wasn't a big fan of the salsa but my shrimp fajitas were excellent.
The restaurant has a quirky and fun aesthetic. The staff is nice and with such a large place, we were seated right away. The eggs benedict with smoked salmon was the best I've ever had.

As far as diners go, this one is superb. The place is a little small. It was packed when we went but the wait was only 10 minutes. The quality of the food was excellent. I had the fruity waffle with a side of cheese grits. There was a lot of fresh fruit on top of my waffle. It's always a plus when the fruit is fresh not frozen. Everyone else loved their food as well. The staff is all incredibly friendly and helpful. Our waiter was great. The staff was so sweet to my grandmother. One man even helped her out the door as we were leaving. When my mom went to the restroom, she heard what she believed was the manager encouraging and complimenting the staff on their good work, which I thought was nice as well. Overall, it was a nice atmosphere with very good food.

Unpopular opinion here, but I dislike The Dining Car. The food is average at best and way too greasy for my liking. The food also bothers my stomach and I prefer other restaurants or even my own cooking to that of The Dining Car's. I do feel like it was once better than it is now but has since gone down hill. Every time I have been there the establishment felt very hectic and was always very loud. You can hear the dishes clanking very loudly in the kitchen. I also witnessed one of the owners berate a waitress in front of their customers on one occasion. That in itself was enough to make me not want to go back. I do like the bakery and it being open 24 hours is convenient but I haven't been back since the incident with the owner.

The pizza is pretty good. It's not the best I've had but it is a solid place. The staff is very friendly as well and the service was pretty quick. The inside is small but cozy. We would definitely come here again. Our waitress was so nice to my two year old niece as well.

This may be an unpopular opinion but I prefer Qdoba to Chipotle. The service is always quick, no matter how many people are in line and the food is very good! Their burritos are my favorite. There are lots of options on the menu to choose from as well.

My husband and I have gone here two other times since my review because I really liked the food. The second time was great. I had the vegetarian shepherds pie, which, reminded me of something my mom would make. The third time we walked in and the lady told us to come in and take a seat. Every table in view was set with silverware and a placemat. We sat down and she asked us what name was it under. I told her we didn't have a reservation. She took us to the back and sat us. All this would have been fine but I think this made the woman who sat us mad because she bumped into me kind of forcefully twice when walking into the back and said nothing to me. I actually considered complaining but I hate to get people in trouble, so I said nothing. Our waitress, however,  was very nice and accommodating. On this day we had the Tikka Masala pizza. My husband asked to omit the onions but they didn't do that. I like onions so I thought the pizza was really good and my husband picked his off. He had the curried vegetables and liked it but they didn't remove the onions from that either. I got a small fish and chips which was still a big serving. The chips were delicious. Some of the best I've had. The fish was kind of bland but not too bad but not great either. It also took a very long time for our food to come out. I assume it was a little hectic since they were having an event. I had to remove a star due to the negatives we did experience in our last visit but overall, I still do like the food and would probably go back but I don't think I would order the fish again.

For being in the middle of the mall, the seating area is actually pretty nice. The staff was very friendly and the service was great. I've been to both locations and the service at this one was much better. The food, however, was not as good. It wasn't bad but since the other location cooked the pizza significantly better, I probably won't be back to this one unless I'm in the neighborhood.

I went here for the first time last night and it was probably the best ice cream I've ever had. There's a nice selection and it's homemade. I had a small hot fudge sundae and it was actually quite large. My husband had double chocolate fudge in a waffle cone, which was also very good. He had one scoop and even that was a pretty big size portion. There's a nice amount of seating for being at a stand and I love how it has kept its old school charm.

Not the best "Mexican" restaurant I've been to but it's definitely up there! It's pretty large inside and the staff is nice. Service is quick. The salsa is delicious! I had the carnitas, which were also really good. The diablo guac is pretty good and actually has a decent amount of crab in it.

I've only been here once but the inside was extremely loud. Luckily it was a beautiful night so we sat outside. The service was kind of slow but the food was really good! The truffle fries were amazing and the wings fell off the bone. The wing sauce was really good as well too.

I've eaten here a few times and I never disliked what I received but was not blown away either. I would have given them three stars, however, anytime I eat anything raw from here I get sick to my stomach. This only happens when I eat raw sushi from here. I've never gotten sick from seafood of any kind before.
I prefer this ice cream to Rita's, which seems to be most people's go to. The prices aren't bad and you get a lot of ice cream.

My brother and I went here and our coffee was just okay. I had better a different locations. It was almost empty inside but the guy making our coffees was taking a very long time. Then a lady he was friends with came in and he took even longer to make them. He forgot to put the vanilla syrup in one coffee but corrected this. He also almost spilt the second one. We probably won't be returning to this location.
Really enjoyed this restaurant. The ambience was nice and our waitress was great. The food was delicious! Some of the best pizza I ever had. The Forty Acres pizza was delicious and so was the nachos.

We ordered takeout off of a recommendation. For the price you get a lot of food and delivery was pretty quick. I liked the jerk salmon and beef patty but the macaroni and cheese was very sweet. It tasted like sugar was added and that's just not for me. The cabbage and carrots was just okay. There was barely any carrot and the cabbage was a bit undercooked. The rice and peas were decent but I had better.

We stopped here because Buffalo Wild Wings was overcrowded and we're glad we did. We loved it so much, we've gone back another time and plan to go again in the future. The burrito de carnitas was probably the best burrito I have had. The fried ice cream was much larger than I expected. The service both times was excellent and the food was great!
I had the Tony Soprano and it was good but I've had better. It could have been filled a little more. The rolls were great though and their baked goods are delicious.

I consider myself to be a  connoisseur when it comes to poutine!

I traveled to Montreal last year and went to the amazing La Banquise Resto, which serves over twenty different types of poutine.

So, when I went to La Poutine, I had high expectations. 

Overall, the poutine was fabulous. I went in and ordered the Granny poutine, with chicken and peas (my favorite from La Banquise happens to have peas and turkey). The service was friendly and the food was out very quickly. The fries tasted like fries in Quebec, which is quite a feat! The gravy was delicious and who doesn't love cheese curds? They had spiffy little "to go" containers that were perfect for keeping a poutine together. The price was right! I didn't mind spending about $10 for lunch for my boyfriend and I. 

Here are a few areas I think La Poutine was lacking:

We had stayed in the restaurant to eat, and I would have definitely preferred my poutine on a plate, instead of a "to go" container. I like to create as little waste as possible, but also if it is on a plate, all the toppings are more evenly spread out. 

The restaurant itself is very small, perhaps more intended for take out. I was hoping for a place with a little patio perhaps. In Montreal, La Banquise is open 24 h and people love to sit out on their patio and drink a beer with their poutine. La Poutine does not serve alcohol and it is quite squishy if you are there during lunch hours. Also, I did not see any bathrooms available to customers. Otherwise, the location is good and it is quite close to student housing for UofA. 

Overall, La Poutine had awesome food and good service. It was also nice to hear the cook in the back speaking French! They are brand new and I'm sure they're still working on fixing any minor issues. I would definitely go back again! 

-Ashley Marie

I went to the newest location of Good Earth Cafe with my sister, Michelle, for lunch.  She had told me only good things about this location and it was my first time trying a Good Earth Cafe so I thought why not?

I expected it to be like most coffee shops: lots of varieties of coffee with limited food. I was hungry, so I figured I would be stuck  having a muffin for lunch. However, I was so impressed the second I walked in. 

There was a huge variety of food items, that all sounded delicious! We ended up splitting their macaroni and cheese and a vegetarian breakfast panini. They both tasted awesome! The macaroni tasted like homemade macaroni and it was very tasty! The breakfast sandwich was interesting. It had a variety vegetables on it (what looked like eggplant and yellow peppers). I'm not such a fan of those types of vegetables so I just took them off. Still, there was a pesto sauce that made the sandwich so flavorful and scrumptious. 

The service was excellent! We weren't sure what type of drink to get. We just knew we wanted something slushy to enjoy in the sun. The girl behind the counter gave us a bunch of suggestions and we loved our drinks! I got the mocha frappe (yum!) and Michelle ordered the banana cafe frappe (double yum!). The drinks were frothy and not too sweet. 

The price was alright. It came to about $20 for two frappes, macaroni, and a breakfast panini. 

Walking into the restaurant, there was so much space! Lots of tables to sit at and huge counter space to look at the large variety of foods. The whole shop had a really nice, friendly atmosphere. Not like some coffee shops where everyone seems quite pretentious. 

We were hoping to enjoy some of the sun and were lucky enough to get a spot on their patio. With the sun shining and our delicious treats, it was a fabulous lunch experience!

I already want to go back again and enjoy another meal on their patio. Just need a little more sunshine!!

-Ashley Marie

My friends and I were looking for a place to grab some food and good drinks. We checked out a few restaurants, looking at their menus and finally deciding on Lazia.

Definitely a nice atmosphere. Sharp colors and interesting decorations made the restaurant look fun but still fancy. 

They had drink specials each night, and, lucky for me, Wednesday nights have bellinis for cheap! Woot woot! 

I ordered their Kobe meatballs with naan bread. It was $8 and the food was delicious. The meat was tender and melted in my mouth. However, it was only 2 meatballs. The portion was way too small! 

My friend had the same experience. She had the spinach and artichoke dip but there was barely any dip! She really enjoyed the naan bread. She also had a side caesar salad which she said was mushy and gross. 

My other friend ordered the Kobe beef burger. He said it was phenomenal. He said the beef was exceptional and really enjoyed his burger. However, his fries were soft and mushy and he had to add salt to them because they were flavorless. 

The service was fast and friendly. Although, there were very few customers in the restaurant. Our waitress was always available to refill drinks and ask how we were enjoying our meal. 

Overall, I enjoyed the night and would definitely give Lazia another try.

Devaney's Irish Pub is an awesome place to go for drinks, hang out with friends, and enjoy a night out!

My friends and I have been coming here for a little over a year. It's in a great location, on the Faculte St. Jean campus of the UofA (just off of whyte ave). 

It is a small pub but a great atmosphere. There are always really interesting decorations on the walls and a nice little patio out back. They have lots of t.v.'s to watch any sporting event on and every Wednesday is open mic! Fun! I don't have a voice that carries very well, so it's nice to be able to go and have drinks somewhere and not have to shout just to chat at your neighbor. 

There is a large variety of food. They have an amazing steak and mushroom pot pie and their Devaney's Burger is mouthwatering! They used to have a really great spinach salad but, sadly, it is no longer on their menu. They also have great pizzas and nachos. In fact, I don't think I've ever been disappointed by anything I've ordered on the menu. 

The staff is very friendly and have even gotten to know some of our names and favorites! And the prices are very reasonable. Portion sizes are large and everyone leaves satisfied. 

We have even gone for breakfast on a weekend and it was excellent!

Overall, this is a great place to hang out with friends and have a fun night! I try and make it out a few times a month!

-Ashley Marie

I went to Cafe Select with my boyfriend for our anniversary. I had been in Quebec at the time of our last anniversary so I thought I'd love to go to a nice French dinner.

After researching reviews on yelp, I found Cafe Select. I made an online reservation, which was super easy however, they were supposed to email me the day before as a reminder and I never received the email. I had to call and double check the time I had made the reservation for. 

We found the restaurant very easily. There was parking close by and it cost about $6 to park for the rest of the evening. 

When we walked into Cafe Select I knew that this would be the perfect place for a romantic date. It was dark and quaint and very charming. There seemed to be lots of seating but we were surprised how few people were there. 

We sat at a small table with no other customers near by. Our server was there almost immediately to help us with our wine selection. The service was awesome. Our waitress helped us with pronunciation of different entrees and was very friendly. 

We started with a swiss cheese fondue. I had never tried one before and it was delicious. It was fun to eat and made the night memorable. The cheese was rich with a nice hint of white wine. However, in the future I don't think I would order this again. It was neat because neither of us had ever had it before, but for $18 I'd rather get the chocolate fondue for desert. Which I will definitely do the next time I go!

I ordered the Coquille St, Jacques. I literally told my boyfriend that it was the most delicious thing I had ever eaten. It was amazing! It was mushrooms and scallops with a white wine and mushroom sauce and duchess potatoes. I wasn't exactly sure what that meant when I ordered it but I knew that I loved all those things. So when it came out I immediately recognized it as one of my favorite dishes from Quebec. It was a nice surprise and I ate it all!

My boyfriend ordered the Beef Tagliatelle. It was noodles and beef tenderloin in a brandy and blue cheese sauce. He really enjoyed this. I scooped up a bite and found it a little plain but otherwise good. The portion was huge and he ended up packing up about half of it to take home. 

I had planned on ordering desert. I always plan on ordering desert but am always too full. When I heard that their desert is baked daily and that it was not just frozen cakes taken out of a freezer to thaw I thought I would definitely order something! We checked out the deserts and they all looked great but after eating everything on my plate I knew I would never be able to fully appreciate their desert. Another time for sure!

Our bill came to about $90, with both our meals, a fondue, and a bottle of wine is not bad at all! 

This is a great place to go for a romantic dinner, a nice night out with friends, or even to just check out for desert (which I will be planning soon!). 

-Ashley Marie

It was really hot today and I escaped the heat for ten minutes by stopping in at West Edmonton Mall. I had been wanting to try the cream puffs for quite some time.

So I bought a regular cream puff and could not believe how big they were! I should have just got a mini for $0.99 instead! 

When I ordered my cream puff they filled it with cream right in front of me which, I thought, was pretty exciting! 

I don't have a lot of experience eating cream puffs, though I love the ones you can buy from the freezer aisle in the grocery stores. 

When I bit into it, I was surprised that the cream was so cold. It was so refreshing after boiling outside. 

I enjoyed it, however I think it was too pricey for what it was (about $3). It was kind of nice to try something different though. I will have to get a mini next time, with maybe a different flavor!

-Ashley Marie

After hearing only good things about this coffee place, I was incredibly disappointed. I very rarely give bad reviews, but I doubt I would come back to Transcend on Jasper Ave.

As a brand new customer, and not the most informed coffee drinker, I was not sure what to order off of their menu. But I decided a mocha was a safe bet. 

I had to sit and wait because it was busy, but I had planned on sitting and enjoying my coffee at this shop anyways. Looking around it is very open and has a very appealing atmosphere. However, I couldn't enjoy because of the loud, terrible music blasting through their stereo (man this makes me sound like such a nag but it was not the usual type of easy going music you'd hear in a shop but instead hard, aggressive instrumentals). I thought that was annoying until I couldn't hear it anymore due to the loud customers talking to each other 3 tables down. I could not picture myself enjoying a relaxing coffee here with a friend, let alone trying to get any work done. 

Then my coffee arrived. I decided to take it to go so I wouldn't have to endure the shop any longer. When I took my first cup I noticed my mocha was only luke warm and it was the most bitter tasting mocha I have ever tasted. I'm not used to a mocha made from what I'm guessing cocoa and coffee. It was awful. Maybe if I had known that I need to add sugar or cream to this it could have been better, but I've never had to add anything to a mocha before. 

As a new customer this was a pretty bad experience. I had checked in at the location after purchasing my mocha, and I was surprised to see that because I had checked in that I could get a free coffee. This is a great idea, however I'm not sure I'll be going back to redeem that coupon. 

Sorry Transcend, but you are my first review under 3 stars. 

-Ashley Marie

During the fringe this summer, my friends and I took advantage of a 2 hour gap between shows and decided to enjoy a nice supper at Chianti's. 

Now it must be said that it was not my first time going to Chianti's. I actually celebrate my birthday with a large group of friends every year at Chianti's and I've never been disappointed. 

Anywho, we lucked out and our timing was perfect. The line behind us grew quite long, but we were seated almost right away. 

This is quite possibly the most perfect restaurant to visit while enjoying the fringe. There are "vintage" posters all over the restaurant advertising past fringe festivals. 

The prices are so reasonable here. I love that they offer all their pastas in a half portion for only $7! I know!! Only $7!? And I usually still have to ask to have it packed up. 

They serve hot, fresh bread with butter minutes after you order. They are so delicious, I find myself asking for another basket.

You can order drinks by the pitcher. Yes I do want a pitcher of bellini! =)

Then you see their pasta. It is made in-house and the noodles are thick and taste nothing like the pasta you boil at home. The sauces are rich and flavorful, I have yet to try one I didn't enjoy. I had ordered the fettuccine supremo. It has salmon and scallops in a creamy curry sauce. The curry was outstanding. I was always nervous to order this dish because I was worried that the curry would be too strong and I wouldn't enjoy it but it was divine! I highly recommend it!

You may find yourself too full from your main course here at Chianti's, but I know better. I always save room for desert! The tiramisu is delicious and I ordered it every time until on my birthday they brought out cake for me. It was their baileys cheesecake. It is literally the reason I go to this restaurant now. It is melt in your mouth, rich, addictive cheesecake. Do not miss out on this!

Now if you are still looking for reasons to stop in and visit this restaurant, I will give you only one more: on mondays and tuesdays, all their pasta creations are $9. Full size servings of authentic italian pastas for $9!?

All I can say is, watch out Olive Garden!

-Ashley Marie

My boyfriend and I make a habit of going on a date once a week. With no good movies out at the moment, we decided to grab some food at south common. So many restaurants to choose from! We ended up in the Joeys parking lot and decided to give it a try. 

The atmosphere is interesting. I'm glad we chose the dining room instead of the lounge. The dining room is quiet and you get a sense of privacy. While the lounge, on the other hand, is loud and jam-packed with people. I guess it depends what you're looking for. 

All the waitresses wear the typical short black dresses with high heels. My boyfriend even asked me how they can wear those for a whole shift. Looking at their stressed feet, I wasn't sure. 

However we had a friendly waitress and had our drinks come out almost immediately. 

There is a larrge variety of items on the menu, but so much seems very overpriced. I ordered the chicken souvlaki  and he ordered the fettucine alfredo. 

Now we get to my biggest pet peeve of all time in restaurants. When something is in your food that is not written on the menu. That is really aggravating! I take a bite into my chicken souvlaki and it is stuffed with onions. I am not a fan of onions. If I had known they would be on my food I would have simply asked for my souvlaki sans onions, however I never even got the opportunity. Instead, I'm stuck with a mouthful of onions deciding what to do about it. 

In the end, I didn't eat my meal, instead I picked at my boyfriends, which I'm sure he was happy about. His was pretty tasty. The sauce was flavorful but quite greasy. Also, in order to get garlic bread with his pasta meal, it costs extra. 

The waitress didn't ask any questions about why I wasn't eating my meal and just took my plate. 

If you read my other reviews, you will know I rarely complain. I just wonder about people with allergies to specific food, who order something off a menu that doesn't actually represent what you are about to order. 

I am in no rush to go back. 

-Ashley Marie

The first time I tried Famoso, it was after the earthquake in Japan. They were having a whole day to support the efforts in Japan. They gave 100% of their proceeds to the funds. I was amazed and knew immediately that I would love this restaurant.

And I was right!

I've been a few times now and always have a great experience. However, if it is your first time it may seem a bit confusing. 

You sit down, take out the menu and decide on what you want, that's easy. But when you're ready to order you go up to the counter and tell them your table number and place your order. There are still waiters who serve you. It's a kind of strange set up, but it never bothered me.

Anyways, on to the important part, the food!

Everytime I go, I order a bowl of the fire-roasted tomato bisque. It's only $4 and it is fabulous! It's spicy and has a huge spoonful of feta cheese in the middle. You get flatbread on the side to dip in. IT. IS. AMAZING! 

I also will order their Mediterranean flatbread to share with a friend. It comes with hummus and tzatziki. I'm not sure if I spelt that right... It tastes fresh and delicious.  

I know I should eat pizza at a pizzeria, but I have yet to try it. It's hard because I fell so hard for their soup! All my friends order the pizza and I've never heard a complaint.. The pizzas have super thin crust and are covered in yummy toppings.

This, however, is not where the meal ends. Do not forget about desert at Famoso! Save room for it. Trust me! 

I was so full the last time I went, but really curious about trying the tiramisu. The waitress convinced me to give it a try, but I got it to go. When I got home and took a bite of this tiramisu, I was literally in heaven. Melt in your mouth, flavorful, delicious, eat every last crumb tiramisu. If you like tiramisu at all, make sure to give this a try. It was the best tiramisu I have ever had. EVER.

As you can tell from all the capital letters and exclamation marks in my review, I am obviously excited about this restaurant. I was just there and I already want to go straight back. 

And I might just do that...

-Ashley Marie

I'm a pretty big fan of sushi. Especially sushi that is very reasonably priced! 

On average I will go out to sushi probably once every two weeks, however it is often to Miyako's in Sherwood Park. But Tokyo Noodle Shop (TNS) is definitely my first choice! If I can convince my friends to do the extra drive there, I would go there every chance I've got. 

The restaurant is really quaint and comfortable. Be warned! The chairs look normal but, in fact, are super heavy and sometimes difficult to move!

The service is quick and friendly! And the menu has a really large selection. I always check out the different kinds of maki rolls at sushi restaurants and TNS has my favorite rolls! You must try their Chef's Spicy Uramaki and their Deep Fried Spicy Tuna! Om nom nom.

 If you're a vegetarian, they have a large selection of meat-free maki so you're not stuck eating boring cucumber maki all the time. 

They also have an amazing bean sprout salad that I really enjoy. 

The only food that I don't care for at this restaurant is their miso soup. They have chunks of seaweed in theirs, and I'm not a fan of that. 

If you're searching for creative, interesting sushi that's not too pricey, I definitely suggest this restaurant. In fact, I'm craving their food right now. Might have to swing over there!

-Ashley Marie

I had never heard of this little Vietnamese restaurant but friends from work took me here for lunch. 

It's going to sound silly, but I'm always scared and shy about ordering off of menus with food I'm not as familiar with. I just never know what to expect. But my friends had been here often and made suggestions and ordered for me. 

I ended up going with 22b. It was a soup with curry and chicken. 

When it came out I could not believe just how huuuuge it was! I am not sure how one person is supposed to actually finish one of these bowls of soup.

It was the most delicious soup I had ever eaten. The curry was delicious and added the perfect amount of kick. The noodles were amazing and the chicken nice and tender. It was so tasty, but sadly my chopstick skills with soup are incredibly limited. I wanted to eat as much and as quickly as possible because of how good it was, but found that to be a difficult and messy process. 

My suggestion: definitely make your way to this restaurant but be sure to go with friends and family who love you, no matter how much food gets on your face and lap. 

Om nom nom!!!

-Ashley Marie

Flirt Cupcakes is a rarity among cupcake shops in the Edmonton area. It's hard to find cupcake shops that bake their cupcakes from scratch, fresh everyday. And you can taste it! 

The buttercream icing on the cupcakes is something I could eat from a jar with a spoon. It is creamy, sweet, and tastes like home baking. The perfect topping on a fluffy, delicious cake. 

I am a repeat customer of Flirt and have yet to try a flavour that I did not enjoy. My favourite is definitely the "Heartbreaker". It's a red velvet cake with cream cheese icing. The red velvet cake makes it taste almost between a chocolate and a vanilla cake. It's like getting the best of both worlds. 

They have about a dozen different types of cupcakes they make on a regular basis, with an addition of a "Flavour of the Month". This, I think, is what brings me in regularly. I love to try the newest creation from the Flirt kitchen. 

Their prices are comparable, if not cheaper, than other local shops. I recommend Flirt to all my friends!

-Ashley Marie

A friend recommended Culina for a date night. So off I went, dragging along my sweet heart.

When we entered the restaurant we were surprised to have to walk through a curtain in order to get into the restaurant. It's a very small restaurant with interesting art and dark lighting. The restaurant was empty. Not another diner at 6:00 p.m. though it did get a bit busier when we left, around 8:00. 

Each table was decorated with white paper bags with a fake candle inside. It created a nice mood with the flickering glow. 

Water was poured into our glasses and left on the table in an old wine bottle (that was my date's favorite part). I started with their persian platter. It was spectacular! The portion was quite large so I suggest you order it to share. It has fresh flatbread with the most delicious hummus I've ever tasted. There were also olives, artichoke hearts, and yogurt cheese. I would come back to Culina just to have this dish again. Looking back, I wish I had ordered this as my main.

Instead, I ordered the duck breast for dinner. Recently, I tried duck in Montreal and it was so good I've decided to try it at different locations. Sadly, Culina could not compare to the culinary delight that was Holder of Montreal. Culina's duck is flavorful and the more I ate of it, the more I enjoyed it. The skin was slightly crispy and buttery, and the local fresh potatoes were a great addition. I think the texture of the duck is what threw me off. 

Overall, I thought the food was alright but the main courses overpriced and the restaurant a bit pretentious. If I happen to go back, it will only be for appetizers. 

-Ashley Marie

I, unfortunately, have to give this restaurant a 1 star. 

I came here for the first time with a group of 6 during peak hours. It was crazy busy but my friends had arrived 30 minutes early to secure a table. The items on the menu looked and sounded great!

We ordered and our appetizers came out quite quickly. Everything was delicious and I even recall saying "this place is amazing!". 

Things took a huuuge turn with our meals. Our rolls came out all at the same time. I had eaten a few from my plate when my friend across from me made a huge crunch noise. He spit out pieces of glass from his maki. 

We were shocked! It surprisingly didn't cut his mouth open, but he had bit into it pretty hard with his teeth. 

We told the waiter and he looked somewhat alarmed and said he'd be right back after he spoke with the manager. I stopped eating entirely. My sushi came out the same time with his and I didn't trust that my food was glass free. 

After about 15 minutes our waiter came back and apologized and said he would take that dish off of my friend's bill. My friend politely explained that he did not feel like he should be paying for any of his meal, after having such a health hazard come from their kitchen. The waiter went and got the manager. 

She apologized and offered his entire meal for free. We asked the waiter for our bills immediately, as no one was interested in finishing their meal. He said he was off to get it. 

At least 20 minutes went by without seeing our waiter again. I had to wave down a different waiter and let him know we were still waiting for our bill. He went and found our waiter who then asked if we wanted our bills separate. So that entire time, he had not gone to fetch our bill. 

I was astonished to have such a horrible thing happen at our dinner, and for the waiter and manager not to at least put some effort into getting us out of there quickly. I was actually really surprised that any of us had to pay our bills at all. We had all lost our appetites and no one finished their meal. 

Overall, I spent quite a bit of money on a meal I couldn't eat, with awful service. I can't imagine going back without fearing what is going to be in my food. 

-Ashley M.

I finally had the chance to make it out to Edmonton's newest cafe that not only offers delicious food and drinks, but a huge selection of board games. 

I went with a girlfriend on a Tuesday night to avoid some of the rush at the shop. We were greeted by friendly staff, as well as the owner, who was chatting up all the new customers. 

The space is bright and open with a variety of tables and couches to set up a board game. 

It was $5 to play any board game from the wall of games. We were to choose our table and then started a tab with food and drinks, including our gaming fee. 

The menu was large including coffee, tea, beer, coolers, paninis, and desserts. My friend ordered a tea latte and I had a hot chocolate. Both drinks came out quickly and were really delicious! The hot chocolate was made with a really delicious dark chocolate syrup and had a really light flavor, the only thing missing was whip cream. 

We shared the cold pasta salad. It was made fresh that day and had a tasty light vinaigrette sauce. The brownie I ordered was quite possibly the most scrumptious, gooey, chocolate brownie of all time. 

We browsed the game selection and had a hard time making a choice to play. All of the games are organized in categories and are easy to peruse. They also have a large wall of games for sale, in case you find a game you really enjoy.

Our tab ended up only being $25 for playing games, both drinks, and all of our food. It was a cheap, entertaining night out. 

I will definitely be making my way back to learn my hand at a few more strategic games!

Ashley Marie
