Tanias was a tale of two cities for me. When it was good, it was downright sublime. Some of the bad items though make me hesitate it to give it 4 stars. 

First, the bad since I'm a negative nancy like that. The fresa agua tasted like kool aid. Blech! The bathroom was nasty. My enchilada style burrito was cold, and I couldn't taste the guacamole or pico de gallo inside.

The soy machaca burrito was very tasty although it didn't seem that close to real macacha. I did enjoy having an alternative to refried beans as a burrito filling, and I'm curious to try their soya verde next time. The salsas are good, but I didn't need all that much because their food is pretty spicy. I am a hot sauce freak so that is saying something. The horchata we got to replace the nasty fresa agua was a cold, sweet foe against all that heat.

What truly blew me away was the spicy breaded cauliflower tacos from their "Ermagherd" specials board. I love when food can take you back to another time and place, and that's exactly what these did with me. They reminded me of eating fish burritos from Nico's when I was in college. It's one of the dishes that I dearly miss since becoming a vegetarian, so this was like a sweet reunion. Next time I will request that filling in one of their excellent tortillas.

It's places like Little Cafe Poca Cosa that make me realize how deficient Phoenix is in simple, homey Mexican food restaurants. I guess it's one thing the Old Pueblo has on us.

My sister and I stopped here for breakfast right when they opened up, and our waitress was so friendly and welcoming. As stated on the website, the music is on the loud side, but it certainly didn't inhibit our conversation. I liked what they were playing so I say bring it on!

I got poached eggs over a green chile tamale (I *think* it's huevos entamorados on the menu, but I hate to be wrong about these things). The eggs were cooked perfectly, the sweet tamale was delicious, and I couldn't stop snarfing down the pintos and rice. The coffee was particularly good, strong with a hint of cinnamon, and our sweetheart of a waitress gave us some to go cups of it for our trip back home.

Like the loud music, we received our promised "mandatory hugs" on the way out. I can't wait to come back here the next time I'm in Tucson.

I came here with my mom and sister during a stay at the El Conquistador. We're all big fans of Indian food, and this place was just what we needed on a very cold day. 

We went with the dinner for two (portioned for 3) so we could try as man dishes as possible. It was a ridiculous amount of food especially since my mom is such a dainty eater. I think my sister got two more meals from the leftovers.

All the dishes were very good other than the average saag paneer. We agreed the eggplant was our favorite dish which was surprising to me. Eggplant is difficult to work with and often is too greasy. The eggplant was so smokey and flavorful. That dish got scraped clean.

We still managed to fit in a couple bites of dessert. The rice pudding was a bit bland, but the warm gulab juman was delightful.

Bacchanal was everything that my fellow Yelpers promised! We were enjoying ourselves so much that we stayed a few hours and went through a couple bottles of wine. And that was without the live band.

For our first round, we grabbed some cheese to go our rose. I was really impressed with the cheese board they presented. Much nicer than what I expected with the additional jams, pickles and grilled bread.

It was an unusually cold day on our visit, so we enjoyed our second bottle upstairs after placing a food order at the downstairs window. I asked for some direction on our second bottle, and he pointed towards a nice cabernet franc. Our food came fairly quickly, and it was all delicious. My husband got a shrimp dish, and I had a big bowl of risotto that kept me warm and cozy. 

Bacchanal was well worth the drive out to the Bywater. I'm glad we ventured out beyond the French Quarter and CBD.

I had the best veggie burger of my life here! The homemade buns were heavenly, and I loved watching them being crafted while we ate. The patty was hearty and covered in tons of cheese and sauce. Most other veggie burgers I've had have been too soft, under flavored and overwhelmed by a huge bun. 

The food beyond the veggie burger is terrific too. My husband got three different sliders, and he loved them all. He was impressed that the pork belly wasn't overcooked; it was just right. We finished off with a yummy German chocolate donut. 

When we went, the line was very long, but our food came out surprisingly fast. Don't let the crowds deter you!

This was our favorite meal during our NOLA trip, and the best dish was also the most surprising: fried kale! I saw it on many tables so I knew it was a must-order. We were impressed with how well the batter stayed attached to the kale leaves and kept a great crunch.

We also got pizza, two pasta dishes and bottle of Sicilian wine that was a good value. We got the artichoke pizza because I can never get enough of those veggies, and it was delicious. The pasta dishes were also great, and it was obvious the pasta was homemade. 

The restaurant interior, like the rest of the hotel, is gorgeous. Despite the fancy surroundings, we didn't feel out of place in our casual clothes. Since it was during Mardi Gras, there were people wearing far less.

Funny that the highest rated restaurant in Tucson is a vegetarian Mexican joint. Also perfect since my husband and I both knew we wanted Mexican food when we were stopping Tucson during a road trip. 

Although it was lunch time, we were both in a brunch mood and got egg dishes. They just sounded so good! He got huevos rancheros and I got huevos enmolados which is very similar and includes mole. We both liked our dishes. Not falling out of chairs in love, but we thought both dishes were good. His ranchero sauce was just a bit too bland for my tastes. I thought the turmeric onions were a yummy accent on top of the surprisingly good beans and rice.  

I thought the restaurant did a good job with safety precautions and social distancing. Water was brought to the table instead of being self-serve, and hand sanitizer was able at each table.

I decided to make this place my one wine tasting spot in the Funk Zone based on the glowing Yelp reviews. I didn't have quite the great experience that others did. Perhaps it's a COVID issue that limits the ambience and service.

It's $20 for 4 wines which seems a little steep, but they are decent sized pours for the tasting. The server brought out all four at once and told me what they were, but I got no further descriptions than that.  She came back once to clear a couple of the glasses but made no effort to inquire about how I was enjoying the wine or to give me more information on the wine. All the wines were good. I decided to go with the rose since I don't have much of that at home, and I found their style to be pretty unique. 

I was kind of irked they automatically charge a 20% gratuity for the tasting. I'm happy to tip the person pouring my wine if they provide great service, but I got almost no service.

My veggie malta melt was delicious. Like really, really good, and that's the only reason why this isn't a one star review. In short, it took over 40 minutes for our two sandwiches to be prepared. I have no idea why it took so long, and I wouldn't have minded nearly as much if the cashier had simply told us to expect a long wait. Seriously. That's all it takes. MANAGE EXPECTATIONS. This is such a simple and vital part of customer service no matter what the industry. If we had known about the long wait, we would have munched on the pickle popcorn and happily browsed around the shopping area. Instead we just waited, waited, and waited some more.

I'm so happy our server at Jamie Slone wines told us about Rori's. We ended up going twice in our three nights in SB. On our first visit, we shared a premade ice cream sandwich with snickerdoodles, brown sugar banana ice cream and a nutella schmear. It was fantastic, and I was surprised how soft the cookies were despite coming straight from the freezer. On our second visit, we got a double scoop of chocolate malted milk ball and the milk & cookies. Of course the cookies ice cream was good, but the malted chocolate was the star of the show. It was so good, and it's an absolute must if you like malt flavor.

I had to try at least one winery while I was visiting Santa Barbara, and I chose Jamie Slone based on the great reviews and variety of wines. We were the only customers during our visit, and we had a wonderful server who really took his time educating us on the wine. I loved hearing about the area since I've never been to Santa Barbara before. I've done many wine trips to Napa and Sonoma so I liked hearing what made these AVAs unique.

I started off with a great chardonnay that reminded me of the lovely chards I had in Oregon wine country. More acid, less oaky than Napa. The remaining three wines were red blends. I liked the malbec blend quite a bit, but I can never turn away from a GSM. Jamie Slone's is wonderful so I knew I had to take it home. 

The tasting fee is waived with a 3 bottle purchase so I decided to get the GSM and chard. I asked about the albarino I saw online, and the server told me it was available for purchase, but there was none open to taste. I was fine with that, and he then suggested their grenache blanc would be a great wine to take home. I ended up getting the two white I didn't even try plus the GSM. I'm sure I'll love them both based on my tasting experience.

We had just arrived in SB after a long drive and wanted something close to our hotel. My husband was craving sushi, but we couldn't find a place with good veggie options for me so we decided on ramen instead. Since it was a chilly night, we decided we would be ok with dining on the patio rather than bringing it back to the hotel.

Our order came out lighting fast, and the ramen was piping hot. My veggie ramen was surprisingly good. The broth was rich and flavorful. I've had veggie ramens that were basically over salted boxed broth so this was a real treat. I'd even say Nikka edged out my local favorite veggie ramen back in AZ. I liked the treasure trove of veggies on top especially the charred eggplant. I could do without the raw red onion though. It's overpowering and doesn't feel like it belongs with the ramen at all.

My husband got his usual tonaktsu ramen and was amazed how big the pork belly slices were that came with it. Because the slices were so big, they were a bit overdone in some areas, but he was very happy with the ramen overall.

Service was above expectations too. Even though we were on a casual outdoor patio, our server was out often to check on us and kept our water refilled. I don't think we could have done much better for a quick dinner choice in town.

This place absolutely lives up to the hype! I'm especially happy with my visit because there was only person ahead of us in line when we went midday on a Thursday. The interior of this place is so cool. It's an old Safeway, and the exposed brick is beautiful. I love that we could watch them roast beans in the same large, open space.

I got an oat milk latte like others have recommended. It was my first time having oat milk with my coffee, and it turned out great! We needed a quick bite to eat so we got an almond croissant and a just-out-of-oven cowboy cookie. OMG. All so, so good. Nothing better than espresso with your dessert/lunch.  

I took home a bag of beans for my sister because I know she would appreciate Handlebar's goodness. I wouldn't have minded a longer line because it would have given me more time to peruse the unique wine selection too.

Sometimes there positives about Covid like avoiding an hour-long wait at La Super-Rica. We had just two people ahead of us.

We panicked when we saw it was cash only, but we at least had enough to order 4 items and leave a tip. Had they accepted credit, my husband would have ordered a few more things after tasting his frijol super rica and super rica especial. He was head over heels in love with his food! We live within a stone's throw of an authentic Mexican place in AZ, and he said Super Rica makes them seem like garbage. I got the rajas taco which was divine. How can you not love melty cheese and poblanos on two made to order tortillas? I also got a gordita which was good and definitely spicy, but the beans seemed dried out, perhaps because it was close to closing time.

All in all, it was a memorable meal. My husband just wishes he could have tried more on the menu.

I knew we had to eat at Bettina after seeing them listed in Eater. Just the phrase "sourdough crust" would have sold me.

We planned on taking our order back to our hotel room, but we ended up eating everything on the cute patio tables out front. The restaurant was nice enough to provide some cutlery and sturdy paper plates. Not always something you can count on these days! 

We started with the baby gem salad which is full of everything I love: cheddar, pickled onions and a herby homemade ranch. Yum! The pizza came out right as we finished, and I'm so glad we got to enjoy it hot. The crust, cheese, and meaty maitake mushrooms were great. My favorite part was the sauce. Nothing overdone or added. Just superb crushed tomatoes (Bianco di Napoli brand, a hometown hero). 

I must return when indoor dining is allowed again. It looks so cute inside! I'd also like to try something from their interesting wine list too.

This spot was recommended by our AirBnb host in Dunedin. What better way to end a day at the beach than with some pizza, right? We did take out and got the Bayshore speciality pizza. The toppings intrigued me, especially the peppadews. My husband has been on a huge pickled pepper kick lately, so I asked for double peppadews.

The pizza was just plain delicious. All the elements of the pizza were high quality, and the crust was great. 

We used their online ordering, and that worked out well. I'd certainly eat here again if we were in the area.

We came here on Father's Day while on a bike ride, and it was an absolute poop show. I put in our name for a table and was told 15-20 minutes. The manager, however, never wrote down my name which should have been an immediate red flag. At the half hour mark, I went back in to check on the status, and it was apparent they had forgotten about me. We waited 15 more minutes, and just before we were about to give up and eat at Starbucks, they called us in. BUT!! one of hostesses gave our seats at the bar to another walk-in, surely a couple that had been waiting far less than us. They were about to clear off a small table by the hostess stand where an employee was doing side work when a high top became available. Finally we got seated. Our server was smiling, friendly fabulous young woman who was just tremendous. I'd like to say that the manager made sure our order came out quickly, but we waited another half hour for our brunch to come out. By that time, we could have gotten something off the regular lunch/dinner menu which would have been more appealing to me. The food was ok. My husbands biscuits and gravy were fine, but we can get better back home, and that's sad because we don't live in the South. My beignets were good, but the dish was not substantial. It seemed crazy I was paying the same price for the beignets as I would a plate of pancakes that would have fed two people. Normally, I would have left hungry, but all the anger I felt in waiting and witnessing the floor manager's ineptitude quelled my appetite. 

Again, I can't say enough how good our server was, and this is the only reason I gave this restaurant two stars.

Whoops! This review has been in my drafts far too long. We stayed at the AirBnb above the coffee shop and being able to coffee and pastries so close by was a big highlight.

We visited a few times. The first time was in the afternoon when we needed a caffeine pick me up and a snack. My husband had his usual cold brew, and I went with an oat milk latte. Both top notch! We also devoured a cinnamon roll and cookie. When we came back for breakfast, I got a snickerdoodle latte which was a treat without being a sugar bomb. We got savory pastries (ham & cheese for him, spinach and feta for me) and enjoyed them both.

The staff was very friendly. Some indie coffee shops serve a little too much condescending 'tude with their brew, but not so here. We were always greeted with a smile. One of the baristas was very helpful in picking out some coffee to take home for a gift.

q2Xcpp_5oAASImqVomwiPg.review_text:
My wife and I went for lunch on a Monday afternoon. There were two tables when we first entered that had patrons. Both of them cleared before we were served. So it was fairly quiet, except for the radio tuned into a local station. Radio was slightly too loud.

I had a grilled chicken wrap. It was pretty good, nothing too spectacular. My wife had a turkey club, she enjoyed it. Both came with a side of Hot Potato chips, essentially home made potato chips which were very good. The cheese dipping sauce came on the side and we ask for no bacon in it.

All in all, good for lunch or family meal after work. I'm not quite sure if its a destination yet or just for locals. Hopefully it will get better.
They don't cover the counter goodies and flies like to walk all over them, but I sure do love the Iced Coffee and Raspberry bars.

Ever since Joe's Peking Duck House bit it, I've been coming here. The Spicy Clam Soup is the best simple seafood soup I've ever had, hands down.

The service is phenomenal, whoever is walking by is your server, none of that "Oh, let me get your server" crap. 

If you eat in frequently get a VIP card, it will gate you free food in the future. Kinda strange that they don't let you use it on take out.

Remember, NO CREDIT CARDS!

The seating downstairs is much better than upstairs.

OK, I'm very disappointed that I have to write a less than stellar review of a neighborhood venture. I just cant look past the fast that I paid over $12 dollars for a burger that I ended up throwing away.

I decided to check it out one night while my wife was at work and I had the house to myself. Seeing all the positive feedback Sketch has been receiving and the fact that I live one street away had already formed a good opinion in my mind with out actually eating anything yet.

I ordered the Kobe burger with pepperjack cheese and aioli sauce. I believe the total came to just below $13. 

First of all, that instantly takes it out of the family friendly category for me. I can't fathom spending $39.00 before drinks and tips for my wife and son, but then again, I'm middle class. Seems like there are many new to the hood, where this isn't an issue, I'm envious of you.

Now I took my burger to go. I'm sitting at home, unwrapping the large sandwich, looking forward to my first bite. That's when I encounter my first problem and probably a personal preference, but it was an issue for me. The cheese was sliced way too thick. I had two quarter inch thick for a total of one half inch thick slice of cheese. They didn't melt at all and I like my cheese to some what melt. Maybe others like it this way, if that were my only problem, I'd give Sketch better review and make sure I tell the food prep person to slice thinner.

My main issue and this is the deal sealer is that the burger was so salty it was gross. I could feel the salt crystals on my teeth when biting down. It was the nastiest taste. My best guess is that the slat shaker lid fell off when making this, I cant see how else this could happen. i was able to eat about a quarter or so before the taste was so bad I tossed it.

If any of the Sketch people see this, please ditch the salt, leave it up to the individual eater to put salt/pepper on their own burger. I'm sure this was just a aberration since I didn't see anything in other reviews saying this, but it was enough for me.
Great coffee and good selection of vinyl. They have the best sign for any shop in Philly. I can see the orange mural when coming back home on a plane from the sky during final approach to boot!

My wife and I love going here. We go to many BYOB's (very rarely eating in a liquor licensed place) and August is the most consistent of them all. The owners & servers make you feel at home and never rush you out. The menu changes and we have never eaten a bad meal. Parking is easy too.

I hit up Kraftwork on many a nights when the wifey is at work. I dig the  samplers, $10 gets you four eight ounce beers, take advantage and load up on the pricey ones. If your lucky, the guys from Milkcrate are spinning some nice background music, not too loud for you to talk, that deserves 5 stars right there. The food is pretty good, standard gastropub type. They have TV's and the bar is suitable for people watching.

I love places like this, no pretensions. You stand in a line that stretches out the front door on to the sidewalk, employees constantly trying to maintain orders and a mixed crowd of blue collar, white collar, locals and tourists. The line leads to two area's, the grill or sandwich counters. Most people who want a roast pork stand in line a heck of a lot longer than they should because of the cheesesteak people. So remember, if your not ordering a steak, yell to the second counter (middle) that you want a pork/sandwich and they will get you up there without all the dirty stares.

I enjoyed the cheesesteak more than any I've ever had, and I'm a born and bred Philly guy.
OK, been back too many times to count and the over salting problem is fixed. Still way to expensive to take the family, but good burgers.
Best darn $2.80 mozzarella sticks! Great pizza too

I've been there alone, with wife, with son and I've taken my young daughter a few times. One time, we all were there together! Every time was a good time.

I've pretty much given up on JB's, Kraftwork is good. Loco Pez is too expensive for street style tacos. Interstate hits the nail on the head!

The wings rock, good fries, good fish, nice tacos (they need to double up the corn tortillas though). Good beer list to boot although I usually just get a Penn Pale Ale.

Basically, if your looking for no pretensions, no I'm too cool for the normal people scene (I'm looking at you JB's), then this place should merit a visit. 

Trust me, you'll be back.

The pizza was good - the wait was not.

I was surprised by the 45 minute wait and when I asked why they don't have a phone number to order ahead, the counter girl replied, "Just go drink a beer somewhere". Well, what if I don't drink?

What normal brick and mortar take out business doesn't have a phone number??

As much as I like the pie, I won't wait that long to eat one. I would wait about 20 minutes on a busy night. Stop trying so hard to be different and let your patrons have some convenience, not all of us can stand around the shop waiting so long.

Please get a phone and you can count me as a repeat customer, until then, no more pizza for me.

First off, service...wow, they totally fail at this. Another customer was before me, they took his order, then ignored me for at least 5 mins afterwards.

After I ordered my pizza, I asked what fountain sodas that had, the guy just stared at me for a moment, the told me three out of at least 6 options and stopped. I told him which one I wanted, he put the cup on it and walked away for another few mins on his cell phone before another employee reminded him I need my soda.

As for food, we ordered a large plain pie. It was hands down the worst pizza I've ever paid $14 for. The dough was thick, the sauce was practically non-existent and cheese? I wondered if it were a contest to see how little they could use to cover the pie. 

Stay away, seriously

The chicken is very good. Why only 4 stars? The level 2 spicy sauce can be hotter. If they offer level 3, I would be hooked. 

If you're a kfc fan, try Cafe Soho in Cheltenham, they rock.

I've been eager to eat here since reading about the opening in the Daily News a few weeks ago. Now that I have, I'm really disappointed.

We ordered three items:

1. Nashville Hot Chicken - what the heck happened to the "Hot" aspect? I've eaten many a NHC and the best I can come up here was they made a mistake and just gave me a fried chicken sandwich. NHC pickles should have some spice, as with rest of sandwich no spice here, at all.  

2. Falafel Burger - If they make it like the one we were served, I can only beg them to remove it from the menu. The middle of the sandwich was not fully cooked, very mushy and not a good falafel way.

3. Cheese fries - they were good, I liked the cheese, noting over the top special.

All in all, probably a first and last visit, which annoys me as I lived in Fishtown and Queens Village for years before moving back to NE Philly and looked forward to finally getting a decent meal up this way. I guess I need to keep looking....

Just an update, I've come to love Andy's and now favor them over Cafe Soho. The staff are super friendly and accommodating. 

Hands down, my favorite KFC place. I drive from Rockledge to Fishtown at least once to twice a month for this.

Provecho is very good. There may be better Mexican restaurants in Philly, but around these parts of Montgomery County, Provecho is a standout.

I'm a person of habit and once I like something I stick with it. Case in point for the chicken tinga burrito, it's tasty and has actually gotten better with each order. I like getting the pico inside with jalapenos, then add a side of arbol salsa. Very good.

My wife is a fan of the carne asada burrito with pico inside and a side of the house salsa. We also enjoyed chips as long as they are salted, sometimes we get the corn salsa, most times we get pico with jalapenos.

I've only eaten in one time, all others have been take out, I may have ordered about 7 or so times at this point. When they have live music, the place has a nice ambiance, but otherwise its a little too bright for my liking due to the fluorescent lighting. I'm sure this would be addressed in the future and is no means a deal breaker to eat in.

If they cannot take the time to properly cook a staple like a cheesebuger even somewhat correctly then I don't have the time to leave much of a review. 

A medium burger should not be completely black and dry as sand.

Seriously, this was a waste of time and money. Service sucked too.

The beer is better than the food for most part. We live close to this location and there's not too many other close alternatives, so we go somewhat frequently. 

My last meal was pretty good, ordered a salad with salmon. The fish was over cooked for sure, but the salads vinaigrette helped overcome it. Probably the best thing I've eaten there in a long time.

I did have an odd thing occur though, the sever asked if we were regulars and if I want to join the King of The Hill club. I knew of it, but didn't frequent the place enough to pay for membership. 

When I ordered another beer, he brings it back in the KOTH  members mug and I quote "So I can have a taste of what's it like to be a member ". As these mugs hold more than the pints, I was like all good, thanks man, appreciate it! 

The the bill comes and he up charged me for the beer size a few dollars. I found this lame as he acted he was serving the mug size as a courtesy, not that I was paying the difference. He should have asked, not assumed I want to pay for a bigger beer.

The food was wonderful,  the margaritas are awesome. 

Why 3 stars?

We ordered the pricey guacamole and while dropping off the main entree, the server removed the unfinished bowl despite us repeatedly saying we are not done with it. He didn't give a you know what, ignored us and took it anyway.  We were shocked enough at the time and didn't want to hassle our main server that we let it go, but we're very annoyed to say the least.

q4Oz1c_OjGu_a8ZkP53Vnw.review_text:
I lived in Tokyo for four years, so I'm fussy about Japanese food. The sushi is consistently good - all right, it's not LA or New York, much less Japan, but it is good - the food is always well presented, fresh, and the restaurant itself is always spotlessly clean. This is also one of the few Japanese restaurants that also does simple stir-fried vegetables. They're good about accommodating allergies and have one of the old Shintomi chefs behind the sushi bar. The only disappointment I've ever found was the gyoza - I have to say, Shintomi's were lighter, and the accompanying sauce was the best I've had in the US. But otherwise, an excellent choice and a well kept secret. 
Also, they do "happy hour" sushi and rolls just before dinner time, at a dollar off!

Located on the site of the old Shintomi , I had high hopes for this chain restaurant. It's in my neighborhood, perfect for a quick lunch. I invited a friend and we met at 11.30 on a weekday. I entered, was a bit confused because I couldn't find any server to help me - located the cash register, cashier, and a server moments later.Having no idea whether to seat myself or ask for help, I said politely "How does this work?" The cashier barked "I'll take your order now!" Nonplussed, I stepped back and my friend said "No, how does it work? do we get our own table?" and the cashier again said "I'll take the order now!!" I finally took a deep breath and said "Forgive us, we have not been here before. Do we seat ourselves, is there waiter service, where are the menus?" At that point we were finally told to seat ourselves and given menus. 
My friend ordered a salad with chicken; I made the mistake of ordering the pork loin. We were quite specific - dressing on the side, blue cheese please, no dressing  or sauce on the pork.
 Although there were only two other tables seated, the waitress rushed away before we could tell her she'd brought the wrong dressing.  Portions were average, lettuce was what you'd expect from a chain restaurant. The chicken and pork, however, were so salty they were almost inedible. (And I love my salt!)
When the manager asked how our meal was, we told him the truth. He explained that their recipes came from the main office, and he wasn't allowed to change them. My friend had eaten at another Tzatiki's, though, and said this was much much saltier. When she suggested he tell the chef not to add additional salt, he just shrugged.
I really miss the days when a bad meal and polite complaint brought apologies instead of excuses! We won't be back.
OH. On another note, I think it's really astonishing that Yelp! would allow the five star review by "Chase G." to stand, since he's a partner or owner. That's really not okay.

I was planning to stay at this hotel for a few days anyway, but when I arrived last Saturday (Oct 28) they'd already begun accepting evacuees from Hurricane Sandy. I have to say, outside of my room being really clean, the beds being really comfortable, and everything working well, the staff have been incredible. I'm stuck here for another 3 days because of the airport closings, and I am so glad it's here and not somewhere else! Amethyst, especially, at the front desk, has been wonderful, and John in engineering/maintenance too. But the entire staff have remained upbeat and cheerful, even when everyone else was getting grouchy.
They even had a "greeter" in the lobby yesterday, directing people and making suggestions. And they hooked up a microwave there so people could heat food.
Yesterday about half the people they needn't didn't or wouldn't come in - you would never have known it, except that the restaurant attached closed early and was completely overwhelmed. (Short-staffed by almost two thirds.) Their solution was to only take to-go orders as we rolled toward evening, though they did seat families with lots of small children. The hostess there, whose name I didn't get, was trying so very hard to remain calm through the craziness, as was the bartender. They closed early so staff could get home, and good for them I say!
It's a great location, too, though you have to watch for those "No left turns" in Jersey areas. There's a huge Wegman's and a Home Depot within walking distance, though it's a little bit of a hike. Less than half a mile though. Loads of restaurants. (I have to say, Red Hot & Blue is not my idea of decent ribs - I've never had any that were falling off the bone at one. BUT this restaurant's burgers are terrific.)
Really, I commend everyone here and will recommend this place without hesitation in future. 
My only request would be - and I don't know where you'd put them! - the addition of another washer and dryer somewhere. Though the lobby floor machines are large and high efficiency, another set would be terrific.
Otherwise, thank you for seeing us through what could have been a remarkably unpleasant experience!

This is a nice addition to the neighborhood, but it needs a little work on continuity - and perhaps a slight overhaul? The staff are lovely, eager to please. Decor very pretty, but darn the place is noisy! I wish they'd put some acoustic tile in, at least around the bar area (sadly, a lot of the seating is there too.
Re the continuity, I had absolutely fabulous chicken tacos there one afternoon, so I took a friend there for brunch the next Saturday - and the tacos were dry, flavorless, and lacking a few things (like heat). The flautas were overdone, but the guacamole was great both times. And their homemade salsa? I can't say enough good things about the salsa - just the right amount of heat, made fresh every day. 
My main problem is with the beef dishes. They're all marinated in exactly the same slightly-sweet, over-caramelized sauce. That means if you order the barbacoa, or the beef steak, or the beef taco, or the beef appetizer, you will get exactly the same taste. Unfortunate for me, who is not a fan of sweetness coupled with beef. 
Black beans were good, though if you're looking for Tex-Mex or true Mexican frijoles, don't look here - they are pureed. Very flavorful, though. 
The rice was average, not very tasty, which is a real pity. 
My main "beef", outside of the sweet marinade issue, is that both the rice and the beans were lukewarm both times, which was really unfortunate. The kitchen could use a little improvement in that area. 
Still, it will be interesting to see what happens with this restaurant. The drinks were excellent, though one of my guests noted that for a Mexican restaurant, the bar listed very few tequila choices, The location and parking are terrific. And they have Saturday/Sunday brunch starting at 10 am! There are very few places in Nashville that offer a decent Sunday brunch before 11 or 11.30. 
I'm going to give it a few months, then try it again. Will report back...

This is a great restaurant. Okay, the ambiance is a little funky - but it's clean. The dishes aren't all that adventurous but they're also not the crappy American-style rolls fake "sushi restaurants" have been making up these past few years - cream cheese, really?! The Korean food is authentic, the side dishes alone are worth the price of the dinner entree (and you can get them as an entree too). The sushi is fresh - and again, maybe not quite as fresh as if you sit at the sushi bar at Peter's Sushi Thai, but half the price. My family and I love this place and have not sent a single person here who was disappointed. It beats Peter's if you're not at the sushi bar (because they tend not to take you seriously then). Beats the heck out of Ru-San and Hanabi. Just a wonderful little unpretentious restaurant in a strip mall. Like you'd find in Japan.

We read about this restaurant in The Scene last year, and decided to try it on a Wedneday night - luckily for us, it was Shrimp Taco Special night. Great deal - two tacos filled with large shrimp and lovely condiments, vegetables etc, with nice dressing, small side salad, soup. All for nine dollars. We've been back a few times; the food is always fresh, the place is spotless (you can watch them cooking your food in fact). Great for families and people on a budget.

My family and I love this restaurant - it's too big to be a hideaway, and it's at the end of a very busy huge mall complex (from O'Charley's to Publix to Starbucks, the complex is huge). Easy to overlook in the hubbub, which doesn't seem to affect their business. The sushi is fine - not as good as Midori at its best, but good. The ikura in particular is always fresh, the gyoza aren't overcooked - nice and moist without being too chewy or wet. Highly recommend the age tofu, and the interesting salads. The tuna sashimi salad in particular is lovely. Nice atmosphere, and once in a while you'll actually be able to do some star spotting -- we actually saw Bette Midler there one night, having dinner with Janis Ian and a couple of other people! And they don't have any problem handling a party of 6-10, which is not always the case.

Oh, sorry to disagree with the most recent reviews. This restaurant was formerly Ben Kay, where they made their own ginger dressing, served the best hamachi kama (yellowtail collar), and were the first Japanese restaurant to open an adjunct Japanese grocery in Nashville. It used to be the only place you could find fairly fresh udon and Poke sticks without trekking to K&S, which always smelled bad and had no personnel who spoke English. (Not that that's a criticism, because it is an Asian grocery, but it makes it difficult to find anything if you can't read Japanese, Chinese, or Korean signs.) 
AT any rate, Ben Kay went a bit downhill, and at some point was renamed Sonobana and I assume taken over by new owners. The staff are still friendly, the shop is still there, but the food is increasingly poor. The basics - tuna, salmon - are tired. The rice is below par; maybe its Nishiki or another good brand, but it's often dried out. The menu is enormous - it would be better if they'd concentrate on half the dishes and do them twice as well. The saddest is their salad and dressing, which tastes nothing like the previous.
Which brings me to my biggest beef about Japanese restaurants in Nashville. Why not spend the extra couple of cents a salad, and use something other than iceberg lettuce? Maybe drain the bowls so there's not a huge collection of water at the bottom? 
Oh well. There is a reason most of the reviews here date from a few years ago. This is no longer a good restaurant. More's the pity, because it's the only one in the neighborhood outside of a Sushi Train, which just opened.

I'm willing to go back once, and just once, to try this place again, but I can't believe the reviewer before me said Tenno Brentwood is better than Peter's Sushi Thai. Or even Hanabi, which varies widely depending on the day of the week and the chef (and how many people are in the restaurant - weirdly enough, the more people, the better quality.) 
My favorite sushi place in town, Midori, was too far, so I was meeting three friends at Miyako when we discovered Tenno had bought it out. Okay, the West End location is all right - no Koto, but all right. So I suggested we try it. Mistake. The salmon sushi was way below par, cuts of salmon that rightly belonged in a cheap salmon salad, or in a roll where they'd be hidden. The ikura was average. The eel sushi was dreadful; overcooked, dried out. The shrimp shumai, which should have come with mustard, came instead with a strange ponzu-like dipping sauce. The miso soup was watery, the seaweed salad was drowning in oil, and all in all there was absolutely nothing in anything the four of us ordered that I would recommend to a stranger, let alone a friend.
Adding insult to injury, they played opera - loudly - for the first half of our meal, and when we complained, they switched over to Christmas music.
Go figure.
Like I said, I'm willing to try it once more in a month or so, when hopefully things have settled, but for right now, I'd suggest Hanabi - which at its worst is a bit better than the meal we had at Tenno - or if you get there early and can sit at the sushi bar, Peter's. 

It's unfortunate that in a city Nashville's size, there is absolutely nothing to compare with Atlanta for sushi, Thai (Smiling Elephant excluded here!), or Chinese. We really do need a bunch of the hole-in-the-wall strip mall places other large cities wind up with - limited seating, great food, basic funky but friendly atmosphere.

Let me say first that I would go back here - good value for the money. I could see taking my extended family here as well, 10-12 people sharing dishes. And I'm curious what the chef would do if we ordered a "regular Thai feast" in advance. We did that once as a group at Smiling Elephant, and it was revelatory.
We wandered in on a very hot Saturday afternoon, and the atmosphere was cool and pleasant. Were immediately greeted warmly, told to seat ourselves - the seats, by the way, are comfortable even at my wife's petit height.
The chef himself came out when my wife ordered "Thai hot" to make sure she meant it - and for the very first time in Nashville, she was served something truly Thai hot. I asked about Yum Woon Sen, one of my absolute favorite bean thread salads that was not on the menu, and he assured me he could make it. What came really didn't bear much of a resemblance to any YWS I'd had before, anywhere in the world, and though the basic cold noodle salad with some veggies and chicken and shrimp was all right, it was a bit disappointing when I'd been expecting something else. My own personal test of Thai restaurants are the Larb Gai and the Tom Yum soup. His Larb Gai was fine, though nowhere near as delicate as Smiling Elephant's. And at a requested "seven hot", it was really really spicy. Almost too much, obscuring the taste of the food. I don't know how Smiling Elephant manages to do lethally hot dishes and retain their delicacy and taste, but this restaurant could use a bit of help in that direction.
Service was fine, the girl serving was pretty young but nice. She didn't check back with us at all, though; we had to find her to ask for the check, or motion from across the room to catch her eye when we needed something. But still, she was pleasant and professional otherwise. 
Unfortunately, Smiling Elephant has set a standard for Nashville Thai that's going to be difficult to beat. I would go back to Thai Star - it was remarkably clean (their 97 food rating hung proudly and visibly on the wall), not noisy, and the food was good. But I wouldn't bring anyone used to great Thai food here, personally.

* Note: we did not end up eating here. If you are looking for a food review please skip this!
My wife and I tried to go here on Labor Day weekend. It was incredibly crowded and noisy, but we expected that. 
What we didn't expect was the complete lack of management. No attempt was made to help anyone in the very long line as we waited - no separation into takeout or eat in, for instance. No one asking whether anyone had special needs or was disabled. No one passing out menus so people could make their decisions before reaching the counter, which meant when people did finally get to order at the counter, they had to look at the menu and discuss their choices with the staff there, adding to the wait time. The only menu we could find was the chalkboard with the day's special, and that was printed so lightly and tiny that it was impossible to read from the back of the line. 
No one was even walking around apologizing for the wait. They were under-staffed to say the least.
Because it was so busy, everyone in line was delegating a person to grab a table and stay at it, with the person still in line ordering for both. This is pretty customary, in my experience. My  wife sat down at a table right next to the long line, but when I told her to take a booth she said the booths should be saved for families. I was about 10 people from the ordering spot, and not 3 minutes later a gentleman came over and asked my wife to get up because the table (a four top) was too large for a party of one. She explained that it was a party of two, and they had no two-tops so she'd taken this. He didn't believe her at first, so she called to me to verify. He was very apologetic but told her she had to get up, that people were complaining they'd gotten their food and had nowhere to sit. There were at least five empty tables at this point, and we saw no one waiting around with food at the counter or in the restaurant, but my spouse got up and stood in line with me. We watched him go around to all the other people holding tables and insist they get up as well, even though no one seemed to be trying to get a table - and again, there were plenty of empty tables, almost the entire outside seating area, as well as several inside. 
After another few minutes of staring at empty tables no one was allowed to touch, we decided to leave and went to Burger Up, where at least they're nice. I would not go back.

Oh, I really wanted to love this restaurant. With Shalimar going downhill at the speed of light, I was thrilled when Zyka opened near my regular B&B. And they would deliver! My first meal was exquisite - shrimp biryani "Indian hot", raitha, papadum. My next, lamb korma, was just as good. Sadly, though, the restaurant appears to be pretty uneven. We have ordered from them - and eaten there - seven times now. Three times, the food was fabulous (although a few things were odd - but more on that later). Twice, it was all right. Twice, it was not good.
What's most annoying, outside of the inconsistency, is the kitchen's apparent deafness to requests. Last time, we ordered salad "with dressing on the side", and instead received salad with dressing, plus an extra side of dressing. Zyka offers "dal soup" rather than the customary dal, but we requested that they provide something more like "dal stew" (in the words of the gentleman on the phone and at the desk) and were told it could be done. When I arrived to pick it up, I reminded him again and was told it was done. But we got the soup.  liquid, not much solid. 
Two friends of mine who'd lived in India for years went there for dinner, and I asked their opinion. "The naan was strange", they said. I agreed. When we ordered garlic naan, which normally comes as a whole piece of naan stuffed with garlic, with garlic on top, w were served a soggy naan cut into five or six strips, nothing stuffed inside, just garlic on the outside. When I said I'd never seen naan like this and would have preferred a whole piece of bread I could tear pieces from, I was told if I'd ordered the "regular" naan, it would have been like that. But without garlic.
The dal is strange. I have never seen dal soup at an Indian restaurant in America, though as a disclaimer I've probably only visited a few dozen in my life. But every other Indian restaurant I've ever eaten at has offered a nice, thick dal, perfect for scooping up with a piece of naan.
The lamb is fabulous - I've had the rogan josh, the korma, and one other. If you can convince them you really mean "Indian hot", the heat is exquisite - still tasty, not sacrificing any flavor for the spiciness.
I would heartily recommend not getting the Tandoori Chicken. I've tried it twice, and both times the chicken (all white meat) tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp all day. Tough, stringy, essentially tasteless. And snd again strangely enough, it's not served with grilled onions, or lemon, as it is everywhere else I've eaten it.
The Raitha is good, not terribly flavorful but nice to cool the tongue. 
Service is nice. They share the space with a pizza parlor (curtained off) but it never smells of pizza, only Indian food. 
I really hope they're able to make a few changes, like consistency. I'd love to visit more frequently, but after the last Tandoori Chicken, I'm going to try Taj on Nolensville for my next visit to Nashville instead.

I began going to Shalimar when I started visiting Nashville. They had just opened, in a tiny place where Rajij's (sp?) smoke shop is now. The food was pricey, but fantastic - everything cooked to order, great attention to detail. And if they were the first Indian restaurant I'd seen that didn't provide any condiments free with the meal, that was okay, because all the chutneys were homemade, and delicious.
They moved to a larger location a few years back, and for a while they were still excellent. But I would not recommend them any longer. My wife and I tried them three times over the past year, each time hoping for the best, and each time it was terrible. AND when I presented a coupon at one of the visits, I was told it couldn't be honored on that date, even though the coupon said nothing about it. AND on another visit we were "accidentally" overcharged by almost 10%. Outside of the food, which is now about as bland as Applebee's, the consistent mistakes with coupons, checks, and orders (on one visit we suddenly had ordered more food than we had ordered - we thought they were being nice and giving us an extra side, until the bill came) is very disturbing.

I wish I'd known about this place when it first opened - I shudder to think of how many delicious meals I've missed! First, yes, spotlessly clean, with no annoying smells. All due respect to other local Asian groceries, it's one thing for the fish section to smell like fish and the ocean, and another for it to smell rank. Second, great selections - all the different types of fish sauce, for instance. AND the staff speak enough English to clearly explain what each item is used for, why not to use Vietnamese fish sauce with Thai cooking, for instance. Lots of noodle choices. The fresh vegetable and fruit section in back is fine, though I'd like to see something showing where items like the Yu Choy came from, and a bit of a crisper wouldn't hurt. The frozen shrimp are a concern - they're the typical cheap imports that have been dehydrated to save weight, shipped over, then pumped full of who-knows-what to plump them up, giving the shrimp that metallic aftertaste you find so often nowadays. But it was good to see the larger fish vacuum-packed and available at reasonable prices. I'd like to see a little more variety in the Japanese pickles available - very few other than the bottled, which are awful. If you want those, try the market next to Sonobana restaurant, across town. Still, for variety, consistency, and helpful English-speaking staff, Bangkok Market can stand up against anything in Los Angeles that I've seen.

I took my wife here last week for our anniversary . I was a little leery, given how crazily enthusiastic the reviews have been. My concern didn't end when they seated us at a booth above the bar area, and I nervously asked the host whether it wouldn't be noisy. He assured us the bar would be quiet, and considering it was early Tuesday evening, I believed him. (For those wanting real quiet, there are several rooms toward the back that looked like they could be used for private events. There's also the "Union" room, opposite the bar, with only 7 or 8 tables.)

I asked about champagne by the glass, and the server recommended the Malbec - excellent value for the money, dry as I'd requested, and very chilled. My wife had a martini, and said it was the best she'd had in years. (Especially compared to Watermark, which charged us seven dollars more for a warm martini a few months ago.)

I'd intended trying a steak, but was derailed when the server (Tarin) mentioned  Atlantic sea bass. We ended up with "13 mile" oysters and Wagyu carpaccio, followed by black olive Caeser and a scallop "Crudo", then spicy string beans and potatoes au gratin as vegetables, black grouper and sea bass for mains.

The amuse-bouche, on the house, was a revelation - some small red spicy pepper with something crunchy in it that knocked our socks off.
 
For myself, I would not get the oysters or scallops again, but that's just my taste. I prefer my oysters plain with just a squirt of lemon. There was a Tabasco "slushy" served with that was outstanding, but the honeydew sauce on top totally obscured the taste of the oysters. Then again, if you're not used to fresh oysters, these would make you very happy.

Same with the scallops - the pop rocks on top were fun, but there was entirely too much sweetening for my taste. I'm not sure why this menu has so many sugary items on the appetizers, because the quality of food and chefs could certainly make plain oysters or scallops astonishing without. But again, these foods were indeed delicious - just not to my personal taste.

Wagyu carpaccio was hands down the best beef carpaccio either of us has ever tasted. Based on that alone, we're going back.

Black olive Caeser was stunning - and for a change, this restaurant doesn't obscure the salad by loading on the dressing. A perfect amount. Highly recommend this dish. Ditto both fish dishes; in America, fish is usually overcooked and dried out. These were perfect. Could not have been better. I asked if my sea bass skin could be "crunchy" and was told that since they'd be roasting it, the skin would naturally be crisp. Tarin suggested I not ask for extra-crisp since that would overcook it, and she was absolutely correct.

String beans were the only disappointment - the sauce tasted vaguely of ketchup and sweetener and too much tomato. The dish wasn't at all spicy, just sweet. When our waitress noticed we weren't eating them, she immediately replaced them with a different vegetable of our choice. We picked the brussel sprouts, which were wonderful. 

Now, the potatoes... I am not thrilled at the thought of sliced potatoes with some cheese slopped on top. But the "potato aligot" was a revelation. The cheese (gruyere) actually tasted fresh, if there is such a thing with aged cheese. There was just enough crème fraiche to make the cheese melt nicely, with no lumps. The potatoes, unusual in this sort of dish, were not overcooked. We could have made a meal of this dish dish alone. 

We shared "donuts and coffee" dessert, a fabulous chocolate mousse with a thin layer of creamy something on top, also fantastic. 



All in all, I have not had a better meal since I dined at Spiaggia in Chicago. We are so very happy to have a place in Nashville that we can use for special occasions! I can't recommend this restaurant highly enough. I would sit in the Union room next time, or toward the back, in case the bar did get noisy, but our booth had nice high walls, and felt like a romantic little cocoon for much of the meal. That I wasn't fond of a couple of the appetizers says more about my own tastes than the restaurant's capabilities - my wife loved both. 

Our waitress was perfect. I hate it when waiters come up and interrupt you as you're in the middle of a sentence, or an intense discussion, but Tarin and the bussers hovered discreetly, sometimes even walking away for a moment to wait. I never felt rushed in any way.

A friend of ours had complained that the train goes by occasionally. We found it romantic, and were happy our seats looked out the window as it went past. The whistle was a sweet little piece of "icing on the cake" for us. But you could avoid it entirely by sitting toward the back of the restaurant. 

Including two martinis, Malbec, and coffee, the bill was just under $200. Considering that this could have been two meals entire meals for us, it was fine - we over-tipped (a pretty generous 25%) because we were so pleased with everything.

I took my wife and two friends here last night for Valentine's, making it our third "special occason" trip to Kayne Prime. The food, service, atmosphere were yet again superb, with a few reservations (below). Here is our evening:
The amuse-bouche was some sort of lobster in crispy wonton-type wrappers, and as our previous Kayne amuse-bouches, absolutely astonishing. Somehow, the combination of ingredients in the lobster mixture popped our taste buds wide open and started us salivating, literally. I'd love to know how the chef managed that without going into over-kill.
Instead of the Wagyu carpaccio, which we've had twice before, my wife and I decided to experiment. Sine so many reviews mentioned it, I ordered the homemade bacon with cotton candy. I have to admit that I'm not a huge fan of fat, and while the combination was interesting, I wouldn't order this again. I suppose every good restaurant needs one dish people will always talk about, that's unusual and not replicated elsewhere, but we found it too fatty to compensate. Our table mates had the carpaccio, and while they had their doubts about "eating raw beef", they didn't regret it for an instant. That dish is superlative!
We followed it with two black olive Caesers, dressing on the side, split amongst us. As before, the dish was gorgeous. My wife ordered the fish, some sort of sea bass, and I got the sous vide New Zealand ribeye. Our companions ordered the bone-in ribeye, and the filet mignon.
The sea bass was perfect, as their fish has been the past two trips - and I am not a fish lover! Our guest was kind enough to allow us each a taste of the bone-in ribeye, which was mouth-watering. His wife loved her filet. 
I will note that this was my first experience with sous vide, and while my steak was cooked absolutely perfectly - just past rare, a bit of crunch on the outside - I found it (as strange as this will sound) almost too tender for a ribeye. I'm not sure if this is a sous vide issue, but when I bit into my friend's bone-in ribeye, it exploded on my tongue, the act of chewing releasing a stupendous melange of flavors that permeated my mouth. (Forgive the pretentious-sounding language, but this really does describe what I felt.) There was enough "give" to the meat that it was beautifully tender, but enough firmness that my jaw, teeth, tongue felt satisfied. The sous vide steak, on the other hand, was tasty, tender, but missing what I associate with a good steak - everything the bone-in had. 
We all shared the potatoes au gratin, beautiful as always, and the charred broccoli, which I'd highly recommend. 
For desert, we tried the toasted banana bread with hot toffee sauce and mascarpone gelato, which was very good but not something I'd order again - how I wish this restaurant had the type of small sorbet plate combinations Spaggia has! Their coffee is delicious - I'm not sure how they brew it, but making strong coffee that isn't bitter was a welcome change from the local Starbucks.
For drinks, the designated driver (me) had their filtered water, our friends had a nice Syrah, and my wife had two dry Grey Goose martinis, with olives in each. Which brings me to the odd extra charge. For this area and this restaurant, the martinis were priced fairly reasonably - $12.50 or $12.75. What shocked us was the upcharge for the blue cheese stuffed olives - 50 cents apiece!! This was the first time in our lives we've been charged for olives in a martini, and given the restaurant's overall pricing, no warning from the bartender (where we started the evening) and no indication of this on the menu, we found it annoyingly petty, if not downright greedy. It was a disappointing realization at the end of an otherwise fabulous evening. 
Two other minor details, admittedly small and personal. It was Valentine's Day; I'd have liked music commensurate with a slightly more important occasion than the regular blend of hip hop and pseudo-modern music Kayne normally plays. Classical would have been lovely. And while it was pouring rain outside, and we'd arrived five minutes before opening so the lot wasn't busy, the valet parking attendant had no umbrella for any of us. Not in keeping with this restaurant's reputation or standard..
But yet again, this is a wonderful place for any sort of celebratory occasion, and I'd still recommend it without hesitation.

In my continuing search for decent Chinese food while visiting Nashville for business, 3 friends and I went to dinner here last night. As Michael M notes, there were quite a few people eating there, although I disagree with his "which means it must be good". It can also mean the people dining have no experience with good Chinese food.
First, though, let's look at what seems to satisfy everyone - quantity. Yes, there are a lot of different dishes available. Even sushi, and a hibachi-style grill.
Unfortunately, most of the sushi is filled with crabstick, a pet peeve of mine as my wife is violently allergic to it. I wish the FDA would demand it be labelled such instead of "crab"! There is no soy sauce available in the sushi are, though low-sodium soy sauce is available at each table. When I asked for regular soy sauce, I was told they had none.
There are also none of the small soy sauce dishes one associates with sushi. When I asked for one, I was given a plastic takeout container instead.
The salad buffet is forgettable - iceberg lettuce, still water-logged from washing. The cheapest salad dressings available, and no ginger dressing to be seen. The fruits look good to the eye until you taste them and realize they've been kept in the fridge for far too long.
The hibachi grill was my next stop. I loaded some shrimp, daikon, rice, mushrooms, water chestnuts, and pork onto my plate, carefully keeping meats seperate from vegetables and rice, assuming they'd also be cooked seperately. Not so. In what I can only call a "dumping technique", the chef put a pat of butter on the grill (which had not been wiped down from the previous customer, by the way), dumped my plate onto it, threw the food around for a few minutes, then dumped it back onto the plate. The result was one big mush, and some very undercooked shrimp. When I bit into one and asked him to re-cook the shrimp, he dumped the whole plate back onto the still-unwiped grill, pressed down with the spatula for a minute, then dumped it back onto a new plate. The new plate was the best part of the grill experience. The hot sauce I asked for wasn't spicy. The pork tasted like a meat substitute, only worse. And the fact that the grill didn't get wiped down and cleaned after each customer's dish was made means if you have any food allergies, this is not a good idea for you!
On to the "Chinese buffet". Spicy chicken, General Tso's, fried chicken all tasted exactly the same. When my wife pressed her chicken wing, oil oozed out and dripped all over the table. Disgusting. One of the waitrons came to replace the old (so old the edges were blackening) pork with vegetables with a new pan, then dumped the old remainders on top of it. 
The egg drop soup was full of glutinous liquidy "something" - we couldn't agree on what it was - it was inedible, though. The chicken with broccoli seemed to be coated with the same substance. The person at our table with an MSG allergy said it was more MSG than she'd tasted in years, and she stopped after a few bites. 
I could go on, but it's not worth it. For $14.95 I had one of the worst Chinese meals of my life, and that's saying something. Everyone at our table agreed, it was horrendous. If you must have buffet in the Nashville area, don't bother with this - go to Golden Coast, on West End, but only for the weekend buffet. The actual menu is not very good there either.
One good food at this restaurant - the frog's legs. Surprisingly tender and nicely spicy. But that's about it.

I was taking two business associates to dinner and realized my usual Vietnamese restaurant was closed on Mondays, so we wound up at Kien Giang. This had been one of my favorite Nashville restaurants, but since the original owner sold it, I'd only been once. At that point, the spring rolls were still the best in town, as was the nuoc cham, The vermicelli dishes had gone downhill, but still featured large shrimp and good quality pork.
Sadly, not so. I don't know what changed about the pork but it's no longer traditional Vietnamese barbecued pork, it's just pieces of soggy meat that could really be anything. The shrimp rolls featured the same pork, and while they tasted okay, it was obvious they'd been sitting for a while. The Vietnamese iced coffee, once a Kien Giang specialty, is using a much lower grade than the chicory New Orleans fresh brew the old restaurant owner used. The condensed milk was likewise a cheap knock-off brand, and you could taste it. Extremely unpleasant.
They were out of every single beer but Bud light, Michelob light, and Michelob. Not an Asian beer to be found, though they were all on the menu. 
I ordered the traditional pancake dish Banh Xeo, expecting it to be nice and crisp, with loads of shrimp and vegetables inside. The edges were crisp but the inside was a soggy mess, mostly bean sprouts and liquid. I counted two small shrimp in a cake the size of a dinner plate.
The lettuce, and mint, were old. Brown, not just at the edges. We even ordered and paid for an extra dish of it, to see if any of it was usable. 
Even the nuoc cham was a disappointment. The old Kien Giang made it with bits of chili and julienned vegetables. The new one has none of that.
Our waiter was willing, as was the waitress, and both spoke English. Unfortunately, between them and the busboy our orders were taken over and over again, with the result that one of our party didn't get fed until long after the other three had been. 
All in all, there was absolutely nothing on our table - appetizers, drinks, main courses - I would ever recommend. This is a real shame, because it used to be a terrific restaurant. I'm sorry to write this.

Once upon a time - oh, 30, 40 years ago - Loveless was a secret place I took people to when I wanted them to get a taste of the "real southern cuisine." Unfortunately, no longer. It used to be terrific, homey, everything from scratch.
It may be all from scratch now, but it's really become nothing more than a tourist joint. If you haven't ever had good fried chicken, you might think this was acceptable, but you'd do better at a gas stop Krispy Krunchy. 
If you want the real deal, ask around for old-fashioned meat & threes. Sorry to be so brief but there's not much more to say except that it's also quite expensive given what you get - poor service, low quality. If you want really great southern cooking, take the time to visit Lynchburg and go to Miss Mary Bobo's, former home of Jack Daniels. Just make sure to reserve in advance.

I've had breakfast here twice when in town on business, and dinner once, when my wife and I went to the theater. I found nothing to criticize whatsoever. The staff were attentive without being obsequious. The food was excellent, portions reasonable. The ambience was good, although I would avoid sitting next to a large, noisy party - it's old, there's not any noise cancellation in the dining room. Highly recommend listening to your waitron's opinions, as every one I've had was knowledgeable about the menu, the history of items on it, and the area. 
I haven't stayed in the hotel itself, but I understand that like most historic hotels, the rooms are mainly small and dark. It's quite expensive for Nashville, too. But I'd come here any time for breakfast.
One note. If you are used to East Coast style "iced coffee", be aware that the iced coffee here is more of a milk drink with a dollop of coffee, and some ice in it. I found that a little odd, but I'm sure it's just me, since everyone else in the dining room who was drinking it was enoying it.
The "sock sausage" is very smokey, so if you don't like smoked meats, this is not for you. The link sausage is fabulous. The grits are great and they'll add cheese on request - they even brought mine on the side. Fresh juices, too. I'd recommend any time.

I'm downgrading my review for a couple of reasons, below. Hopefully these will get sorted out soon, because this is normally a great restaurant, but...
On the plus side, valet parking has improved enormously. They actually open your door for you now, greet you, and wait for you to get out of your vehicle without looking impatient. 
The wait staff are still wonderful, as are the front door and behind-the-desk people. 
On the minus side:
Still an up charge of 50 cents apiece for blue cheese stuffed olives. Ridiculous. I don't know why this place isn't embarrassed to be so penny-pinching over something so minor. When a table orders four vodka martinis with stuffed olives, twice, amounting to $104.00 plus tax and tip,  throwing an additional $4.00 onto it for the olives is so petty that I can scarcely credit it.. 
The carpaccio appetizer, which is the main reason for my bringing three business associates there last week (all from New York, all dying to review Kayne locally), is off the menu! In its place? a steak tartare with a "smoked sous vide egg yolk". Not at all comparable, not at all unusual. And for my wife, who is allergic to eggs, a non-starter. Also, why "smoke" an egg yolk? I assume we could have chosen a fresh yolk had we wanted the tartare, but the carpaccio really made this restaurant stand out, with the yuzu and wasabi. A pity.
Last but of note - my bone-in ribeye was tough. Much gristle through and through. I'm not sure if this was because we dined much earlier than usual (first seating rather than 7 pm) and the chef on call didn't know to avoid this piece, but it was gristly. Really unexpected. I'm sure if I'd sent it back and complained, they would have replaced it - we had a lovely waitress and bus person - but after the carpaccio disappointment, and in front of my business guests, I really didn't want to call attention to the problem.
However. I really hope the management pay attention to this. M Street have just opened Moto across the street, which I'll be trying when I'm back in town later this summer - and I'll re-visit Kayne Prime at that time to see what, if anything, has changed.
My companions had the fish of the day, which was pronounced delicious, and the whole fish, ditto, and the steak tasting platter, also pronounced delicious. So perhaps I just got a bad piece of meat. Still, in a restaurant striving for this kind of quality, there should NEVER be a bad piece, so filled with gristle that it's difficult to cut with a good steak knife - either the purveyor or the chef needs to be aware of it.
Sad to report this, because it has been our go-to dining place of late. Perhaps, just an off night for the chef and steak, but the carpaccio was such a disappointment..

Update: We've been back numerous times since I first posted this review. I wish they'd decide what they want to be, and I wish they'd get consistent. After this morning, sad to say that I think we're done.
It's the day before Mother's Day. We went assuming there'd be a full menu, or there'd be a special menu for Mother's Day. Instead, we got 1/4 of the old menu (which is the "new menu') and the special Mother's Day menu (not available until Mother's Day, tomorrow.) 
My wife is allergic to eggs. Normally, she orders from the "sides", or (if the restaurant isn't busy) asks whether the chef would make her an "eggless omelet", using potatoes and extra vegetables instead of the eggs. But... there were no sides listed.
"Where are the sides?" we asked our waitress, who spoke so quietly that we had to ask her twice to speak up.
"Oh, we don't list them any more. But tell me what side you want, and we can do it."
Wait. How could we ask for the side we wanted if they weren't listed?
We went through the ingredients on the main courses. (There weren't many main courses. Be forewarned. The menu is sadly shortened.) Okay, they can probably do a side of bacon, or sausage, or grits, or something. 
We looked at the sadly smaller menu. We looked at the hostess(es) and the waitress(es) huddled around a digital machine next to the kitchen doors. We waited and waited and waited. And we finally decided to go elsewhere.
It's unfortunate that the waitrons in this establishment aren't better trained. It's unfortunate that the kitchen can't decide what it wants to be. It's unfortunate that the reduced menu has nothing that doesn't contain eggs - really, how hard would it be to say "We can substitute tofu for eggs in any scramble" or even just offer something eggless?
Oh, I realize everyone doesn't have egg allergies. I know it's not a big deal to other people. But what should be a big deal is a constantly changing menu that becomes smaller and smaller, with less and less choices.
With Mother's Day being the biggest restaurant day of the year, one would think they'd have amplified, rather than reduced, the choices. Not to mention the staff.
Unfortunate. A great idea gone bad.
PS they are definitely no longer as accomodating about eggless omelettes as I noted below.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
it's unfortunate that this restaurant's first few weeks seem to have gone so badly. My family and I went for brunch last Saturday. 
I had no problem with the ambiance. I was thrilled that even though they had a television on, the sound was off. And for once, the music was very low, real "background" music.
The service was excellent. The food was really, really fresh - one of our party is extremely fussy about her omelettes, and said it was lovely. One of us asked whether the chef could accomodate a "no-egg" omelette due to allergies, and he created a wonderful substitution with loads of spinach, vegetables, potatoes, and sausage. (The sausage by the way was wonderful.) The coffee was delicious, and they have Perrier, which is a big plus in my book.
The biscuits, home made, were delicious. Not gummy at all, and just sweet enough. I'd have preferred plain butter to butter with honey in it, or at least a warning, but I'm sure if I'd asked, they'd have brought some. 
My one criticism would be that the food was all cooked with a fair amount of oil, but I'm going to ask for minimal oil next time, and I'm betting it won't be a problem.
The fixings are fresh, still a real rarity in Nashville breakfast places. And there are so few of them here! Noshville Green Hills, with it's low health scores. Athens, which can be great or meh depending on day and staff mood. The Southern opens early weekdays but not until 10 weekends, so an early breakfast isn't possible. There are a few places in Belle Meade, over priced and under-quality.
I'm willing to go back to Wholly Chow a couple of times, based simply on the freshness of the food and the very accomodating staff. I hope they make it.

Loved Ian R's review and agree completely. Just to throw my own thoughts in:
Maybe we hit Martin's at a bad time, around 3 pm on a weekday. There were only about 25 people in the place, and perhaps the cooks were between rib rounds. However, based on our experience I wouldn't go back.
Ambiance was okay, music way too loud. Annoyingly loud. The kind of loud where you can't really talk, even in a pretty empty restaurant. There was no escaping it, either - no matter where you sat, loudspeakers were blaring.
Beer choices were terrific, loads of local tastes. Bartender was knowledgeable and friendly. 
The three of us ordered barbecue pork sandwich, brisket sandwich, wet ribs, cole slaw, potato salad. The pork sandwich was okay, but once you've had it somewhere like Saw's in Homestead, it's difficult to live up to that. I certainly wouldn't give it a five out of five, or anything close.
The sauce was just all right, but the coleslaw was really good - not overly mayonaissed, just right. 
It was the ribs that were a real disappointment. I ordered the baby back, figuring they'd be the tenderest. The outsides were overcooked, to the point that chewing on those sections was uncomfortable. You know when you bite into a rib, a piece pulls away, and you think "Wait. This is so overcooked and dry, I'm going to cut my mouth on it!" and you really don't want to finish that piece? 
The ribs themselves were dry, as though they'd been sitting in the cooker or under the lights for way too long. And that was the "wet" ribs! To my mind, a barbecue place advertising their ribs is supposed to have tender ribs every single minute they're open. Or don't serve them! 
Portions were small, and to my mind, over priced. I suspect most people calling this "great" barbecue have never had really great barbecue. I'd rather go to Swett's on a day when they're serving ribs and 'cue, or drive to Birmingham for Saw's, myself. 
All in all a really great disappointment.

Everything the other rave reviews said, and then some. Banh Minh banh minh banh minh! The baguette was so fresh, and so good, we wondered where they were sourcing it - a local Vietnamese bakery, perhaps? The cucumber, cilantro, carrot and other vegetables were as fresh as it gets. I loved that they put in whole vertical sliced jalapeno, as opposed to rings - and again, the jalapeno was super fresh. We drove twenty minutes out of our way to try this place, and will be going back often.
On the place itself. We were a little nervous because it's traditionally not been a great neighborhood - close to the train tracks, and the car race track. High crime. However, on a Saturday morning it all felt homey, despite the proliferation of used car lots and repair places. InterAsian has parking right in front, which helps. 
The market itself is super clean, comparable to Bangkok Thai but much, much bigger. None of that funky smell associated with both K&S Markets. Better still, everyone I spoke with had enough English at their command to help me.
The center aisles feature tons and tons of canned foods and food in jars - hard to find things like Pearl River soy sauce (though they were out of the light, they promised it would be in soon) and Chinese pickled vegetables with tofu, a student staple over rice there. Almost everything was labelled in English, and unlike the reviewer who complained about lack of Japanese ingredients, I saw quite a few. 
Frozen foods are to the right, a full long wall of them. On the left cold storage, just about every drink you could want, from water to hard-to-find Asian specialties. Lots and lots of Asian sweets, including a number of homemade items like Banh Tet. 
Head to the very back and take a left - you're in the "fresh grocery" section. I bought fantastic home made kimchee as well as pickled cabbage (ditto home made), and was severely tempted by half a dozen other items.
If I had one bone to pick, it's that the green vegetables (wrapped in saran wrap, and kept cold, very nice!) weren't labelled other than price. I suppose I could have gotten someone from the front to tell me what each was, but there were so many, and the market so busy, I didn't want to. And I'm just not knowledgeable enough to know whether I'm looking at choy sum, yu sum, or what!
Nashville jumped on the Vietnamese food wagon a lot earlier than most cities, and for a long time we had a few of the best in the country - Kien Giang leading the pack. Unfortunately, since it's been under new ownership the quality has steadily deteriorated. Miss Saigon is hit or miss, and really, the wait staff could care less most of the time. The Banh Minh everywhere else I've tried is usually day-old bread instead of crusty fresh, with too much greasy pork and not enough fresh vegetables.
Be aware - there is no seating (we ate in our parked car), and they take cash only. But it's a five star choice nevertheless.
Last word. The people who run it/own it are really, really nice. The older gentleman at the cash register asked where we'd heard about it, and when we said "Yelp", he rushed to show us their sandwich featured in Food & Wine Magazine. It was really quite marvelous how thrilled he was.
All in all, one of the best "Yelp-induced" experiences we've ever had.
