You know its going to be an epic trip when upon check-in the front desk person says "Mr. Danimal, we have good news for you. You have been upgraded to The Ritz Carlton."  Finally someone knows who I am!

We had booked several rooms at their adjoining sister hotel, The Iberville Suites, which is nearing the end of extensive renovations. I assume some rooms were still under construction and were not quite ready. Whatevs, paid off in spades for me and my nephew.

Once upon a time this was a department store, so the rooms may not be as big as other RC's, but the luxury that one would expect is still in abundance. 

*Décor reminiscent of typical New Orleans Garden District mansions. Check!
*Luxurious, 100% cotton, 400 thread-count sheets. Check!
*Feather beds and duvet covers. Check!
*Goose down and non-allergic foam pillows. And.....check!

The staff were all great, most in fine humor as well. My 8th floor corner room afforded sweeping views of the downtown business district on one side, and of The French Quarter and Mississippi River on the other. The double pane windows shut out pretty much all of the noise on Canal Street below. I was amazed how quiet the room was. All this for under $800 for 4 nights, including all of the taxes, fees etc. Nice! 

Great location too. 2 blocks from Bourbon, and just across Canal from the Central Business District, where you can dine and shop with the locals. There is also a classy lounge that has an awesome Frank Sinatra style band playing several nights a week. 

Yep, Mr. Danimal thoroughly enjoyed his upgrade.

For this latest NOLA trip I decided I was going to go out of my way to try an old institution that I have long had on my list. Additionally, I wanted to search out a couple of spots that two of my most trusted Yelp buds highly recommended as well. 

On our first full day, I insisted on coming here for an early lunch, as we never got around to it on my last two trips to the Crescent City.  This is as old school as it gets, in an old house a few miles up Canal from The Quarter. Very well kempt, and a very comforting homey interior as well. The staff is about as low key as can be, even for the South, but still very efficient and there when needed.

An uncle of a friend of mine has lived in NOLA for several decades and proclaims their turtle soup to be the best in town. Yep, possibly even better than Commander's Palace, although I would need to do a side by side comparison to be certain of that bold statement. A beautiful thick roux, with lots of turtle meat. Once the server places the bowl in front of you he asks if you want a spot of Sherry drizzled on top. Of course young man, drizzle away! Absolutely wonderful along with their homemade bread, so feel free to dunk. 

From another review we were both sold on the "Fresh Gulf Fish Meuniere with French Fried Potatoes." Although we opted for veggies instead of the fries. On this day the fish was buddy drum fish, and it was muy delicious. Cooked to moist flaky perfection. Options are grilled or fried, but when in NOLA fried is mandatory. Go back to grilled when you get home, as will I. 

For an Old New Orleans dining experience with a bunch of locals, this is not to be missed. It is forever on my must hit list.

When Marissa S. proclaimed the All That Jazz Sandwich was the best thing she ate in NOLA on her last trip, well I had to follow like a little puppy. No shame, as I know she is not normally prone to hyperbole.

Since this was a buddy trip, meeting a friend from Atlanta that recently got divorced, we actually chose this spot for our New Years Eve dinner. Yep, dudes without wimmin get to roll like that on NYE. Picture if you will: two old fellas standing under the roof overhang in the pouring rain moaning like a couple of hookers with each bite. OK, maybe not a pretty picture. 

That sandwich? WOW, indeed. My bud had earlier questioned having a lowly sandwich as our NYE dinner, but after one bite he was def on board, and the next day expressed his wish to return. Nah, move on brutha! This is 'Nawlins, there are more delights to be had elsewhere.

All That Jazz combines sautéed shrimp, with turkey, ham, mushrooms, Swiss & American cheese on grilled French bread. Added to all of that is their amazing "Wow Sauce." Another Yelper suggested that it is halfway between Russian dressing and chipotle mayo. That sounds about right, whatever it is, twas absolutely magical.  

Not to be missed when in The Quarter, buzzed or sober. BTW, opened 24/7 so you can pick what state of mind you prefer to enjoy this epic creation.

Another pre-planned stop for our most recent NOLA trip due to a glowing review by a trusted fellow Yelper, this time Dave G. As he stated - no trip to New Orleans is complete without ordering their crab cheesecake. It was pure serendipity that they happened to be located just around the corner from our hotel, so off we went.

We arrived around noon on New Years Day to a packed house, and most everyone was dressed to impress. We found a high-top in front of the open kitchen and were immediately greeted by a smiling pro of a waitress. 

Everyone I mentioned "crab cheesecake" to voiced basically the same response: "What? That doesn't sound like it would work." Well that is why we need Yelp, so others can lead us to food that we might normally pass on. It is a savory dish, and will please your taste buds from bite number one all the way to the last lip smacking forkful. A generous amount of crab within, and is topped with a complex meunière sauce tying all ingredients together nicely. A glass or two of  prosecco and this was one terrific start to our New Years Day 2017.

Thanks again Dave G!

This was our adoptive local dive bar over this past New Years Weekend, and the staff and regs were very accepting of us outta towners. IMO, not really a dive as it is a very clean well run establishment, with a professional caring and hilarious staff.

Over our 3 night stay, we prob stopped in 5 or 6 times. Quick drink on our way to hit The Quarter, and for our nightcap before stumbling back to the hotel. Later in the evenings they cranked up the jukebox and the whole bar loudly sang along. Reasonably priced drinks with several craft beers in the mix as well. Supposedly they make a mean po' boy, but I only tried a very late-night cheeseburger, and it was tasty, I think. It was after 1 in the morning for cri' sake. 

So if you are fortunate to have your hotel nearby as we were, this should be your ground zero watering hole. BTW - open 7 days a week from 11:30am - 8:00am. Gotta love those hours!

My second trip to NOLA this year, this time with a group of 6 with 3 of us celebrating birthdays, and my buddy chose Sbisa for the Friday night of mine. A very inviting ambiance awaited us immediately upon entering - two smiley hosts and live jazz will accomplish that every time.

Our table was ready for us at exactly our reservation time, and service was spot on throughout our entire 2 hour stay. I had a sizeable lunch earlier at Mandina's and thought to go a bit light for dinner. Well if you know New Orleans, you know that is not allowed. Even my prosciutto and melon salad was huge with a very generous portion of prosciutto parma, with goat cheese and very fresh greens alongside. YAY! Finally some veggies to be had in this town. The homemade vinaigrette was perfect as well. All of this wonderfulness for a lousy $14. It no longer surprises me how reasonable fine dining is in NOLA. Especially compared to SoCal and San Francisco prices. 

In another feeble attempt at "going light" I ordered their Louisiana Blue Crab Cakes. These 2 large cakes were pan seared and served with a citrus aioli sauce. They were definitely the most rich tasting crab cakes I have had in my long lifetime. Well, rich food is their specialty in this wacky town, so to be expected. I try not to eat too much bread, but their fresh baked hot buttered bread was too tempting to pass up. And pass up I did not. 

Working backwards here: our sweet as peach cobbler waitress highly recommended the fresh that day blue soft shell crab. As a starter we ordered one for 3 of us, and it was incredibly tasty. I have mostly had this at local OC sushi bars, and will probably never do so again going forward. The meat was so sweet and juicy, and even the outer skin was melt in your mouth edible, unlike most of the chewy versions of my past experiences. Not surprising that the seafood here is straight out of the gulf fresh, as per their website - they own their own seafood dock and distribution business in Hopedale, Louisiana. Yep, aint-a-gonna be this fresh most any place else. 

Two of my friends ordered the Courtbouillon, and it was stocked with a plethora of fresh fishes of various tribes. It looked fantabulous, and If I make a re-do here I will come hungry and def give this dish a go.

And I will make good on that statement, as I will surely be back to my favorite American culinary city sooner than later.

Alrighty, I guess I am one of many that now shun the venerable Acme across the street, and may be joining them at Felix's for my preferred oyster bar in The Quarter. I say may, because some of the staff on the night of my visit should not be front of the house ppl. Standing around showing each other pics on their phones, ignoring customers, forgetting requested beverages, you know the drill. Luckily the one gentleman that seemed to give a damn came to the rescue to help save the day. I was close to walking until he stepped up.

I have been a loyal Acme fan for nigh on 30 years, with countless visits. Went there on a birthday weekend a few years ago, and most of the food was just plain not good. The oysters had a dull grey color, didn't taste fresh, and the Chicken/Andouille Gumbo was not up to par per their glory days past. Take into account that Acme always has a line, and Felix rarely does, well the decision was easier than I previously thought possible. Sorry Acme.

The char-grilled oysters last week at Felix's were plump and the buttery-cheesy-garlicky sauce was as decadent as one would hope for. The seafood gumbo was lacking any discernable seafood, but the incredible roux made up for it to the extent I barely longed for any actual pieces of sea-creatures. The fresh bread delivered with was begging to be dipped in both the oyster sauce and the gumbo. This meal was shortly after I arrived for my 4 day weekend, and it was a mighty fine way to get into the NOLA Spirit. Well except for the slackers on staff. In case mgmt. cares, I was there around 7:30 the night of September 21st.

I will give old Felix one more shot, and depending on how that goes I might have to resume my search for another old school Oyster House.

After countless trips to my favorite American culinary city, I search out at least one new spot on each subsequent trip. I really hit pay dirt this last time. 

I perused the Eater NOLA e-newsletter, and Bacchanal immediately grabbed my attention. After looking over their entertaining website I was pretty much sold on fitting it into my itinerary. After exchanging messages with long time Yelp Bud Qui C, who had paid a visit back in 2015, I was further encouraged to make it a must visit.

On a hot September noonday visit I arrived to an almost empty front of the house store like space, with a variety of wine and charcuterie choices. You make your purchases at that time, and pick up your food from the window facing the backyard. It is an actual old house with a spacious backyard, with live music daily from noon until 10:30 or so by 2 or 3 different bands. Check their website calendar for details. On my visit it was a local duo, the Tangiers Combo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B8xODK4FFlE. Perfect music for a relaxing hot New Orleans afternoon away from the bustle of The Quarter. 

My charcuterie plate was assembled with high quality ingredients of my choosing out of the refrigerator by a friendly staff member. See pic. It did get busier towards the end of my 2 hour stay, and it is supposedly packed to the gills in the evenings.

Bacchanal has been added to my must do list for all future NOLA trips. Thanks Eater and Qui!

We were told by at least 3 people that this was one of Nashville's best restaurants, and since it was a block from our hotel we stopped in late on New Year's afternoon. After reading a few 4 and 5 star Yelps, I was sold. We had walked by on NYE, and it was packed to the gills, so we were pleased that when we strolled in it was barely half filled. 

We had spent the day bar hopping on the world famous Broadway enjoying several live bands, which is what makes B-way famous. So we were in full New Years celebratory gear, and the staff were more than happy to enable us and to help keep the party going. The friendly host turned us over to our very gregarious waiter, and the good times were on a continued roll.

I ordered up a bottle of California Chardonnay, and 1/2 dozen oysters to split. My old buddy of 30+ years tends to order whatever I do (i know, a general faux pas) so we both requested one of the evening specials: crab cake hash. Hard to believe, but that potato hash was so good, it almost outshone the crab cakes. It appeared to have bits of squash, red bell pepper, with sweet potato along with regular potato and seasoned perfectly. Dang, I can still taste it. 

We finished up with key lime pie that was almost pudding like in texture, and loved every bite.

Highly recommended when in Music City.

Having been to New Orleans many times I try and search out a new spot on each subsequent visit.

This past weekend we chose Boucherie. I had read once that this was one of Anthony Bourdain's favorite NOLA restaurants, and from there decided to research further. Chef Nathanial Zimet previously started out with a truck he called The Que Crawl. And just like some of our most ambitious and creative young chefs/restaurateurs here in Southern California, he worked his way to a unique brick and mortar place of his own where he could better assemble a team to help with his vision and passion.

Unlike SoCal, Boucherie, like many other great NOLA restos is housed, well, in an actual house and not some random strip mall. Not only was the ambiance warm and inviting, so was the host and our waitress, and every other staff member that we encountered. 

Boudin Balls were mentioned in several other reviews, so after the refreshing amuse-bouche we requested an order. Loved the contrast in textures, with the fried crispy outer and soft slightly spicy inner of the mixture of pork and rice. They came with a tasty homemade garlic aioli sauce on the side for dipping. 

My entrée of choice was what was called Jerk Chicken. I have been to Jamaica twice and have had it several times here in the Lower 50, and this did not taste as though it had any traditional jerk seasoning. Semantics schemantics! Once my brain got over the fact that what I was tasting was unlike what I had before, twas a non-issue. Whatever seasoning that was used resulted in possibly the best chicken recipe in memory. Not only tantalizing to my taste buds, but so juicy and mouth watering. Will remember this for a long long time. Included alongside was a 'cheesy arepa, plantains, & wilted greens.'

We shared some wonderful collard greens that had grit fries resting atop, that we agreed were the best greens also in memory. 

Definitely worth the drive, or Uber fare, if you are staying in The Quarter, can't recommend highly enough. Now added to my NOLA must hit list for future trips to this incredible culinary city.

qzkA4pdGVtQOxYUOdQtuKA.review_text: They had me at coal oven pizza. You ever just know that a place is excellent before you walk in the door?  That's the feeling I had today as I took the family into this small Italian restaurant with a nice patio area outside. Having been to lombardis in NYC many times my mouth actually watered at the thought of having a coal oven pizza in Clearwater Florida. The state that has a bad reputation of having horribly bad eateries has one place that can claim the top spot for best pizza in the entire state of Florida hands down. Lenny has nailed it here and the people of Clearwater should erect a monument to him.

Better than going to red lobster. Good local fresh fish. Upbeat atmosphere and good people.  Had the grouper blackened. Wifey had the mahi mahi and shrimp skewer combo. Wasn't like Gordon Ramsey was behind the grill but at least it didn't suck like I expected it would. The littlest princess wolfed down the gator bites like she grew up in the swamps of alligator alleyway.  Crabby Bills is exactly what you want so just go there.

Unlike the other guests that scored a room on priceline for pennies, I paid almost 4 bones for a one bedroom suite so I could take my beautiful wife and grand daughter to see Winter, the dolphin from the film dolphin tale. Have no regrets. They gave me a giant suite measuring 1400 square feet which includes big master bedroom with 2 queens, large living room, dining room, granite full kitchen, second living room and second bathroom. So big it was almost stupid. Top of the line mattresses, luxurious robes and a large jacuzzi that is practically private off the second living room. If I return to Clearwater beach this is where I'm staying even if I don't try to low ball priceline it like alot of the yelpers did.

Delicious. Went there for a light lunch between meals and was blown away. Went there based on the good reviews from fellow yelpers. Excellent chips made to order. Fajitas superb and they load you up bigtime. Got the combo steak and chicken and there were lots of red and green roasted peppers and onions. Salsa bar at your disposal too. Probably the best Mexican food in Reno. Don't even think about eating any other Mexican food near or in the casinos. This is a short block away from harrahs.
If you don't get the French toast I'm picturing here then get one of giant pancakes or a griddle scramble. Best bfast in Reno.

Classic Steakhouse. On par with Ballys in Vegas. Small cut of filet seemed big. Bread was to die for with the butter shaped like rose buds. More of everything please.  Godiva like chocolates served over smoking dry ice is a nice free treat they slip you just before they slip you the big black one. Big black leather check holder that is. Make sure you slide your total rewards card in along with your payment and they take 10% off the bill.

Nice casino hotel right on main drag in DT Reno. Older mattresses are still comfortable but need replacing. Also old style bulge TVs need to be disposed of and replaced. Never understand why a big corporate hotel with a money making casino doesn't keep the rooms up to date. Hallways and doors to rooms are nice and new. Just have to go the next logical step and this place would be full all the time. Too bad Reno couldn't afford to renovate the downtown area. Kinda reminds me of post apocalyptic downtown Fresno with casinos.

You have no idea how much I wanted to give this restaurant 5 stars. From the moment we sat down I could tell there was a good chance of not making it to 5. Perhaps they shouldn't mention that they are ranked in the top 10 in the USA. Having dined at many great Italian restaurants that kind of statement messes with you alittle. If I had to hear about the mushroom raviolis one more time I think I would have lost it. They were ok but would be better with red sauce. The veal piccata my wife ordered was very good but very small. The chicken parm I ordered was good but I've had better. The bread basket beforehand was good but not to die for. The staff could be heard in the open kitchen and were asking each other about a "pizza slide" for 10 minutes and they sounded pretty stupid. Would have preferred hearing them calling each other names in Italian kind of like an Italian version of Gordon Ramsay.

You can tell this Denny's has got it together. Went there on way out of town after weekend of street vibrations. All the food was good and the noise level is surprisingly low considering the place is filled with bikers. Or maybe it seems quiet because I'm usually nursing a world class hangover Sunday morning in Reno. Can I get a "yeah sisters"?  Good choice for breakfast grub. Everybody is nice and professional.

Ate an incredible breakfast here the first time we stayed at the Hyatt across the street in oct of '11.  Now we're back and we brought back up, our friends from Fresno, ca. Can't wait to save a ton of money in the morning at this small family owned breakfast joint. Will update in the morning when the 7 of us hit them with a Gordon Ramsey style "stress test". Lets see if they get to keep the 5 star rave.  Ok, our stress test shrank to only 3 of us and they came through with flying colors. Laura was out waitress and checked in with us regularly. My wife had the eggs Benedict and when she was done it looked like they could put the plate right back in a stack of clean ones. My little grand daughter scarfed down the French toast. We did send the bacon back in for extra scorching after she brought it back not looking well done enough.   But that's because we love bacon almost burnt like many do.  If I stayed at the Hyatt for a week I would eat here every morning. I wouldn't even think twice.

Really wanted to give frenchys 4 or 5 stars but our party of 7 imbeciles were not that impressed as many of the other reviewers. I had one of their most expensive entrees at $19. Shrimp and scallops grilled. Shrimp were cooked perfectly and the mini scallops were ok too but very small portions. Scallops were smaller than a dime. Shrimp were medium at best. Wifey had yellowfin tuna on my suggestion because she usually loves it but that's in California. Florida yellowfin not so much. I had a bite and choked it down. The bill for 4 adults and 2 kids came to $100. That was food only as we opted to not plow in the bar dept. food came out crazy fast. Almost like they brought the food to the wrong table fast. Since my plate was very tasty I'm gonna upgrade my review to 4stars now that I'm thinking about it. Good prices and good taste keeps this beach side joint full. Nice.
Great pizza. Came here for lunch and ordered the large cheese pie. Came out looking and tasting great. Will be back next time we're in Clearwater beach.
Went here during our short 2 night stay on our shell collecting trip. Delicious. Bruschetta excellent. Gnocchi excellent. Chicken Parm dinner excellent.
On point filet mignon. Ate her last night. Enjoyed every bite of our world class meal. Slept like a baby.

Great spot for great Italian. Had the chicken parm and the gnocchi and both were great.  Sauce was a little watery but delicious. Got to meet Stella's mom who is wonderful. Will be back every time we make the trip from  California.

Crazy Bernie and Tammy the Tornado ate their way thru NO and it started with the Red Fish. It was packed to the gills , lol, so we sat in the bar. She ordered the Mahi Mahi and a cocktail. The drinks are good here. The solid 4 stars on yelp and only $$ are what you're looking for when you duck into a place to eat to get away from the craziness on BS. Pleasantly surprised by the perfectly cooked fish. Delicious.  I took off one star because jalapeño corn bread sucked

Love this small joint. Wait on line awhile then in. EggsBenedict delicious. Americano breakfast good too. Bacon Bloody Mary. Excellent coffee. Wish this gem was a little bigger but an excellent choice forBreakfast. Desiree was our server and she was awesome. My review was 6 stars but after having coffee spilled on me I lowered it to only 5 stars. Lol. Great people make great businesses. This place is awesome.

Had to try what yelp ranks as the #1 restaurant in Nola. Stood in the short line that formed before they opened at 5pm on new year eve eve. Tammy The Tornado shopped with no money as I waited like a chooch. At 5:05 the flood gates opened and 25 people or so filed in. Reservations welcome and all others (us included) can wait 1 hr. Well like the seasoned diners we are we walked our way to the bar where you can ALWAYS SIT AND ORDER FOOD.  The Tornado ordered the Ahi and I ordered the Salmon from Jordan, our ultimate bar tender / waitress/ spiritual advisor. Just kidding on the last part. Anyway, we were probably first in as far as food orders go. Both entrees were nothing short of amazing.

Crazy Bernie and Tammy The Tornado ate one of our 3 breakfasts here with some regrets. She orders Eggs Benedict everytime we eat breakfast and had to get the special Bacon & Artichoke special Ben. Sadly you cannot get regular Eggs Ben when they have the special. Seems weird since you only have to slap on a slice of Canadian Bacon instead of the regular bacon but oh well. The special was just ok. I got the American which was just ok too. This little gem is streetside just inside the Hotel Conti and with only 9 tables they do a great business here. Solid choice for morning munch down after a nights of amateur hour drinking but if they want my opinion make the potatoes more awesome by getting them crunchy and fried with red bell peppers and onion. The way they are now reminds me of hospital breakfast. The two little baguette slivers you call toast is kind of a joke too. Get much bigger toast. You are competing with 100's of awesome breakfast places within walking distance. Also your eggs Benedict could compete with others if you always have Canadian bacon on hand and lose the bed of baguette instead of English muffin. English muffin is king when it comes to Benedict!

Stopped in to buy a 15 pack of macs for our spoiled rotten Grand daughter Sienna. She will love them by the looks of them. We got a slice of the bread pudding bar and OMG. This is Mecca for all who love sweetness.

When you say no to excellent Italian food you say no to life!  Crazy Bernie and Tammy The Tornado walked here from the French Qtr through torrential downpours with driving winds only to be told "there's no room at the inn" but you what I do. I say "hell no". We're gonna sit in the bar and we did. Worked out way to a prime bar table and started by lovin this moist bread with spicy olive oil. We ordered the meatballs and the lasagna and a pizza with caprese salami added to an ordinary Marg pie. All were outstanding as you'd expect from the #2 Italian restaurant in the city of New Orleans according to Yelp. Our waiter was Nick and he was awesome. I can't stress enough how impressed I was by this awesome dining experience.

We loved this steakhouse.  Came in not so hungry and walked out stuffed.  There is sooo much competition in NO it's hard to believe restaurants can make any money.  Our steaks were cooked to perfection and delicious.  This place does not disappoint with size of portion and taste.  Perfectly seasoned.
Awesome branch of America's best pizza chain. Had a large cheese and like always it was delish. Large Caesars salad hit the spot first. If you're into authentic NY pizza look no further.

r8oK5vfSE5E9St-0gCN9uw.review_text: This is the best bowl of Pho in Tucson/Phoenix. The portions are huge and the meal incomparable.

I was a weekly customer several years ago. The service was superb, the food was OK, and the beer choices were excellent. We returned last week to find a new staff, new menu and new barkeep. The food was most disappointing, the beer choices are still pretty good, but the barkeep couldn't mix a pre-mixed margarita. It looks like a change of management. How can you take one of the best bars in town and screw it up this badly? Well, they did.
Far too expensive for mediocre fare. Good drinks and excellent service, but it's not worth the money.
The food is exceptional. The service is excellent. Did I say that this is the best Italian in town? And the cost is reasonable. You obviously need a reservation. It is worth the wait.
Try the Jimmy McKenna. That is a sub. Good beers on tap. Classic photos on the walls. Great attitude. Good prices. How do you beat that?

We go once a week for Tortilla Soup. It is the best in town. Friendly staff and a nice place even in if it is in a strip mall. Try the shrimp with injected cheese and bacon wrap. Life will not be the same after this experience.

On another note, very few of these establishments are interested in good beer. Say "India Pale Ale" and they can only repeat the mantra of Modelo, Tecate and Corona.

This is the best breakfast joint in town. You can still get the $1.99 special, but if you have more, you are in for a treat. Try the sage turkey sausage, apple omelet or a dish with green chile and eggs on yellow and blue tortilla. It looks like a dive on the outside, but if you venture inside, it is well worth your time and money.

It's an excellent bar. Great selection of beer, wine and drinks. The bar staff is as good as you will find in Tucson. The ambiance is great. The service is usually very good, with a few exceptions. The cheeses and breads are excellent. BUT...the food is mediocre at best. Tucson has some great eating establishments. Go to this one for the ambiance and good drinks. Go somewhere else to eat. Overpriced, mediocre food. We've tried the breakfast and dinner. When Mother Hubbard's kicks your ass for breakfast and Club Congress makes you look amateur, time to change direction.
Exceptional food. Exceptional service. The vegan "meat" dishes are exquisite. Brown rice? No problem.

Last week they had an artichoke quiche that was as good as any we have ever tasted. Then today the cajun poached eggs with mushroom gravy and green fried tomatoes. Holy moly. This is absolutely the best breakfast in town.

One of the best downtown lunch venues. The clam chowder was exceptional. The lamb-pita roll was very good. The salad was as good as any I have had...anywhere. The tea was very good and the service is exceptional. Don't miss it. Good folks doing a great job...
Yes, it is loud. Few places in Tucson understand acoustics and these guys don't get it anymore than Club Congress, the Beeline or most any eating/entertainment venue. I just accept it as a given here.

When they opened, the food was not as good as the original location, but it was OK. I tried it again last night....When they opened, good blues music was playing. Last night it was some country crap at a level too high to hear a conversation. The ribs were fatty and poorly cooked. Even the sauce has changed. It is some watery slop without any substance. The beans were bland, at best. They used to be one of the best side dishes in town. The potato salad was no better than what you buy at Fry's. My friend's green beans were cold.  

Go to the original location on Park. Same guys. Same great BBQ. Their cole slaw is exceptional and the meat is heavenly. It is well worth the drive. Don't bother with this crap...

This was one of my worst experiences in Tucson. The guy behind the counter obviously had no interest in food or service. The soup was microwaved out of a can. The bread bowl was ok, but the soup ruined them. Why would anyone stop here? For coffee and a bagel? I won't go back to experience such amateur food service. There are so many places with folks who enjoy and take interest in their work.

Sabra and Heather. The only reason to go to the bar is to see Sabra Faulk and Heather Hardy. They do a great show here. Otherwise, go elsewhere. The bartenders can't handle anything other than beer and shots, the music is waaay too loud (forget having a conversation), the beer selection sucks and the stupid stage light is irritating. There are great dive bars in Tucson like the Buffet, the Golden Nugget and several in the 4th Ave./downtown area. The only reason to go here is to see those grrrls play and that is exceptional.
Great food, great drink and great service. The leg of lamb was superb.

Yes, the building is unique and for racing fans, it is an interesting experience, BUT the food is some of the worst in Tucson, the service sucks, the drinks are sugary, watery crap, and there is no real beer selection. Just walk around the place and go eat and drink somewhere else.

The owner came back in and turned the place around. It is back to one of the best bars and grills in the neighborhood. Great selection of beers. Good bar keep. Good food. Great service. Good happy hour prices. Damn. I better go tonight....

Great beer selection. Excellent IPA's. The food is mediocre bar food, at best. But there is plenty of room and the service is good. Go eat at one of the many fine establishments downtown and end the evening here with a good beer. Guaranteed to return here.

I am well versed in good cajun cooking, so....what the hell is this? Deep fried, overcooked, bland meats popular in the gulf area. The cole slaw was uneatable. Folks, go to the Parish. It is pretty damn good cajun cooking for this far west. Don's is not. 
Don's does have a great outside area and yes, he's a nice fellow. But for the money, I'll go elsewhere.

Tucson Sunday mornings' best kept secret. The Bloody Mary is excellent, the quiche is superb. The service is outstanding. 
For those special occasions, it is the best ice cream in town...
I returned for dinner with a few folks from work. Great drinks and an excellent beer selection. The steaks were excellent, the tuna was superb and the grits and shrimp...well....I'll be back...

Nice looking place. But, after we were seated, we had to ask for water. We had to flag down a waiter to order drinks. Then the bartender forgot the drinks. After finally flagging down someone else, we got a menu. There are some excellent Thai restaurants in town. This is not one. We flagged down a waiter for more water after the food appeared. They had no IPA or pale ales and the drinks were a watery mess. We left with food on the table. Go elsewhere.

I used to own a vegan cafe so....
I was most disappointed. They are so caught up in their veganness that they forget that they are competing with many places that also serve vegetarian and vegan. Vegans live and die with spices. This is very bland.. Where were the onions and garlic and...and...and....My wife can out cook these folks hands down. And service...well...I don't get it.

The only reason to go to Shooter's is the Sunday afternoon concerts. They have great musicians most every Sunday afternoon. The outside area is a great place to listen to music. Beyond that...forget this joint. Crappy fried food with a lousy beer and wine selection. Service? What service? We waited 30 minutes for drinks and an hour for the food. There's too many great places in town now. Go downtown, UNLESS there is a band. Then just kick back and enjoy the tunes and go somewhere after to eat...The only reason this joint gets two stars is the music.

It's still a good dog and a fair breakfast in a nice courtyard. But there are far too many places serving an exceptional breakfast. This is not it. But for a decent dog at lunch, it ain't bad. Not the best. But not bad.
Good food in a great little cafe. The owner is friendly, the food is good and the portions are generous. They need a better selection of beer but...I'll be back....

We tried again tonight. The bar is still good, the service is good, but the food is mediocre at best. Don't look at the online menu. It is much more expensive than listed. The soup was cold. The grilled cheese (which the cooks whined about making) was cheese and bread. Go to Zona or most anywhere for the food. Go here for the overpriced drinks...At least they are good.

OK. Things are much better now. We had a great experience with the mahi mahi tacos. Good beer. Great staff. Some of the best desserts in town. Back on the list for good food and good places...Still too damn noisy, but we go at off hours. And don't miss breakfast...

They need to figure out how to use acoustics to take the noise down a few notches. It is very small, very noisy, and the food is good, but not great. And it is expensive. They have a fair beer and wine selection, but I think they should wake up. There are a lot of very good places to eat in Tucson now...This is no longer on my list...

This used to be on my must-do list for out of towners. In years past, they had a motivated crew that made a good dog and fries and made it a good experience. Now it looks like a minimum wage joint where no one really gives a crap and that is the experience. There are too many great choices in town. Go somewhere else.

For all the hoo-rah about this place, I give a a big so-what. Empire makes better pizza and the atmosphere is better. The bar is very good here, but the pizza? Thin hard crust, a few fresh items that don't mix so well...and it is very pricey....
I hear they wait hours in Phoenix to eat here. That's Phoenix for you. Tucson has better to offer...I suggest Empire on Congress or Falora on Broadway...
Great tamales. Some of the best in town. I buy at Sprouts or the Farmer's Market.

Folks, this is not BBQ. 3 slices of brisket with some petite looking onion and apple, placed for decor is NOT bbq. Memphis style sauce my ass...I don't know what that stuff was, but it was not Memphis style sauce. Yeah. The meat was good, but that does not make it good BBQ.
Good beer selection and the drinks are very good. BUT if you want real BBQ, go to Mr. K's at Park and Valencia. This is overpriced, not worth the money or the time. Go to the bar at happy hour, then drive out to Mr. K's for the real deal.

This used to be the best bar in Tucson. Pat and crew knew their business and knew how to treat their customers. Pat was one of the most gracious hosts in the business. I had to listen to the new owner's spiel about his own self for 15 minutes too damn long. The new owners have no clue. Two of the bartenders have left. The jazz is still great. The staff are still wonderful people, but things have changed.
This little cafe is the best in Tucson. This is Mexican Soul Food. The owner is the most kick ass woman on the planet (outside of my wife). You can't find a better playlist of music. This is it.

Mediocre at best. Go across the street to Dante's for good food and great drinks. I posted this and the manager of this establishment had it removed. Too sad.
We ate here on a week night and had the chicken and the ribs with drinks. For the money, and considering the competition in Tucson, it is an expensive, mediocre restaurant/bar. My kids enjoy the gaming area and the atmosphere, but they are not there for food or drinks.
Oh lord, yes. Great joint for a taco and a beer. What else do you need? Nice tacos for the money. Sign me up.

We went for the dim sum on Saturday at 11. The dim sum is good. But...the first dish and tea came in 15 minutes. The second came 15 minutes later. The final two dishes came 40 minutes later after we chased the waiter around the room. The staff was yelling at each other which was free entertainment, but I think you are better off at Gee's or the place at Ina and Oracle.
By the time we paid the bill, it had been an hour and a half and that seemed to be the situation with most everyone.

This is one of the best experiences in Tucson. Get there before 6 on Wed-Sat for happy hour. You will be happy with the $7 appetizers. The shrimp and corn dish is so good that I may have to go back tonight. The ribs and salmon entrees are as good as you can find. There's no draft beer, but there are plenty of places to go after if that is important. The bartender and staff are great folks. I really don't want to share how good this is, as I might not get in tonight...but....

This is damn good BBQ. The pulled pork is the star, but the ribs are just fine. Yes, they are a Tucson joint and that means heat in the sauce. Coleslaw was just dandy. The chicken was damn near perfect. Nice folks. Great place. The best BBQ in town is Mr. K's. But that takes a drive to Valencia. I'll take this place for my neighborhood BBQ fix.
And for the whiners who don't understand BBQ joints...BBQ is and always has been a first come, first serve proposition. Get there early. It's worth it.

Excellent staff and a nice, big room, BUT we were there to eat breakfast. The potatoes were frozen cubes, the toast was mediocre at best and the eggs...meh...They have no interest in fresh food, local or much of anything having to do with a good breakfast. Give the cooks and the great employees something to work with....

The Campbell location is an excellent, well-managed cafe with exceptional food and staff. We tried the Broadway location today. The food was mediocre in comparison and the service...what service? There are better places. Go to the Campbell location or try Bisquits a few doors down. Much better elsewhere.

rDpysBqhldE0poFgF_DX8w.review_text: I read a lot of these reviews, and if you notice the people giving 1 and 2 stars all mention how great the food is but how expensive it is. Well, let me clarify a few things. It is not a cheap place because they are serving real food, not Sysco truck garbage. We were there on a Sat night, and it was packed , and the wait staff (and kitchen) are still a little confused on how to deal with big crowds, but they managed to deal with a smile which is all I can ask for. The wings are without a doubt some of the best I have ever had. This is the real deal people...they may not cook up the flavor that appeals to you, but it is real BBQ happening right there is west philly, and its not out of a truck or trailer. Highly recommend it, and hope to hear from you after your visit. I've been to more than a few famous BBQ joints, County Line in Austin, Pappy's Smokehouse in St Louis, Daddy D's in Atlanta....this place can stand right next to the most famous. For the record...Famous Dave's shouldn't be as  famous as it is in my book. Only complaint is beer could be a few degrees colder (it would help when you are eating such hot food) and the short haired girl who is the hostess needs to learn how to say YES, to a walk in, when they have 10 empty tables,. Go...eat....enjoy. The burp keeps on delivering hours later.
There are a lot better places in NOLA to feed yourself. This place is ok if you are drunk on Bourbon St desperate for some fried garbage, but other than that I would avoid it. Its a dirty fryer...

Do NOT, I repeat.... Do NOT eat here. The BBQ gave my son 24 hours of pure food poisoning hell. Just drive by and let the place go out of business. Staff is lifeless, service-less joke. I should have listened to my internal alarm .... When a restaurant is empty at prime time, in a prime location there is a very simple reason.... because the people know when to stay away from the poison. Go to Rons a mile away, heck... Get a Twinkie out of the trash at the Sunoco across the street and you'll still have better odds at having a pleasant night.

I have only been here a few times in 2012, so I can't tell you whether or not the previous posts are accurate. I have brought some serious world traveling pizza aficionados here, and all have left raving about what an awesome slice they have. The slice is light and crispy, unlike the giant grease bomb slabs of cheese that you normally get at a Pennsylvania pizza joint. I completely understand that a few clientele don't "get it," because they are used to the typical pizza joint slice. This is a world class slice. If you care about what you eat, try a slice. It's good food. The guys that designed or "borrowed" this slice should be absolutely proud of what they have accomplished. They could franchise this so easily. The marketing would be simple....Do you love pizza? Do you hate dominos, pizza hut, poppa johns, little Caesars and every other pizza chain you ever tried? Come to Saucys. Enjoy.

Vegetarians Run Away At Full Speed!!!

Obviously if you have read any of my other posts, you know I am NOT a vegetarian... But my wife is. She enjoys Mexican restaraunt a because they can normally serve up a pretty decent plate of rice and beans. She was excited to try this new spot... We ordered their Margarita's. Frozen. We were just going to get a couple of beers, but the site of the big baskets full of fresh limes signaled the possibility of a good Margarita. Not. Nastiness. My wife ordered the cheese and onion enchiladas. As she ordered, she made it quite clear that she was vegetarian, and the waitress quite clearly acknowledged her request and insisted that they could handle the order. A few bites in, and she was pretty disgusted to find her enchilada was slathered in ground beef sauce. When she pointed this out to the waitress, the waitress insisted that red pepper flakes. Not. So the manager/proprietor (Mark) visits the table and now is when things get really interesting. He acknowledges that the plate is... In fact, full of beef. With sort of an obnoxious cynical comment, he then informs my wife that the beans are cooked in lard. He said this in a way that suggested that no matter what he did, he still got some meat over on her, and he was quite amused by it. He graciously removed the cost of her dish from the bill. Big deal buddy. For someone who hasn't had any meat in her diet for years, the whole thing disgusted her. The fact that he was somewhat amused by her disgust.... Well, that's why you get to read this awesome post. If you like mediocre mall food wrapped in a Mexican package, this place is just fine. If you are a vegetarian or looking for something of half decent quality, run from this place and get a glass of water.


A few other places you might want to avoid:

Consolidated Restaurant Operations:


Cantina Laredo, III Forks Steakhouse, Cool River Cafe, Silver Fox Steakhouse,
El Chico, Good Eats and Luckys Café. We serve more than 14 millio

Florina was our waitress. I am normally an annoyance to wait staff, or they just ignore my requests. Florina (I called her Joy), really paid attention and with a smile. Everyone loved their food. I was a little worried that I wouldn't find anything on the menu.... But I had the rib eye with potatoes. The language on the menu might scare away a steak lover.... But it was awesome. Have no fear. If you haven't been.... Put it on the schedule. If you aren't familiar with Malvern.... Have a pre-dinner drink one block away at The Flying Pig. Solid.

If you have read any of my reviews, you know I don't hold back when I encounter garbage. The same holds true when I encounter QUALITY. Come on folks, real BBQ (not yesterday's BBQ) in an old garage, with a cobblestone courtyard, valet parking, open air with the garage doors opening to the outdoor area.... great little bar. Yes...5 Stars. The place is far from perfect, but at least they have a clue at what they are shooting for. They are a little disorganized, and maybe slightly understaffed... But who cares? No risk here.... Open up your schedule and go.
For Milkshake aficionados... This is Mecca. They also happen to have some seriously awesome hash brown/ home fries. I know that's a weird combo, but that's all I had.

I really hate to give out two stars, but I have given Uncle B's three tries to get it right. This is a real bummer, cause these guys are so close to being legit. They just don't know how to finish. First of all... The rubs on the ribs is great, real tasty...but you have to cook the ribs longer and slower. You've heard of "fall off the bone" good? The meat on these, unfortunately... sticks to the bone. Too chewy. I don't know if it's a low quality cut of meat, or a combination of not cooked long enough. There is no pink smoke color on these ribs at all, and like I said... this is three different visits over a period of a year. The wings... man, again... so close. They are delicious... until you discover that you are eating undercooked wings. They also lose points for putting absolutely zero effort into their take-out presentation. I mean, they always act like we're the only ones who pick stuff up, and they are just gonna improvise for us by putting the ribs in tin foil then throwing them in a wet old beer box. Thanks for caring guys. So, that's it. I guess the short review is... These guys know how to make pretty damn tasty BBQ, but they don't know how to cook. Does that make sense? I'm sure if you were a guest at THEIR dinner it would be killer. I have talked to many friends who have tried them, they have all had similar experiences.

This won't be a long winded, detailed review. Just a couple of comments.

1.) this place is cold cold cold. I kept my heavy parka on, and it was still cold.

2.) I may not know how to spell margarita, but they don't know how to make one. Bla. 

3.) I think the their waitstaff and food runners are trained very well, bartender...not so much. I know they just opened up, but it shouldn't take 15 minutes to get a margarita (that sucked) in the time it took for the rest of the table to get two rounds, especially in a restaurant that only has 10 or so tables.

4.) I had the wings. I just tasted Sysco. Sorry guys. The menu was a bit limiting. I would also add at least one race car beer.

This is a tough one to write, as I live nearby and have been a customer for a few decades now, but sometimes you just have to say it out loud. Chef Mike is a shortsighted (fill in the blank) !!! I heard they had lobster on special and got excited to drop in on a Tue for a little treat. The plate comes with a pound of shrimp (can't remember if it was fried, peeled or whatever) a side of cole slaw, and an ear of corn. I don't like shrimp, in any form, and my favorite way to eat lobster is with a side of roasted potatoes, or baked, or even with some decent French fries. So I asked the waiter if he could drop all of the sides and replace it with some fries or roasted potatoes... Whatever was easier. He stated, emphatically, that Chef Mike would not allow any substitutions on this particular special. He was happy to make substitutions on the regular menu, but not on this special. He would be happy to box up the shrimp, slaw and corn for me to throw away and waste, and then charge me extra for a side of potatoes or fries, but a straight substitution wasn't going to happen. I can absolutely understand a policy like this if the substitution worked to the establishments financial disadvantage, but... Something else is going on here. I was so bummed, and really annoyed, that I didn't order anything. I drop in here for a drink from time to time, but I rarely eat there because there always seems to be attitude coming out of the kitchen. It's a very odd vibe that I can't say I ever experience at other places. I mean, how often do you hear a waiter say "no, the chef won't allow it" to a very small, simple request? Not often. Not sure who this guy thinks he is, but I'm not a fan. My son thought he knew why the chef was so adamant about no substitutions..."because then he would have to split open the Costco bag before he throws it into the microwave." Sounds like a logical reason to me. Well done Chef Mike, thanks for a great Tue night.

Oh yeh, not sure what this is all about, but I ordered two beers, from the same tap, and when I got the second one it tasted distinctly different, it wasn't the tap, it was the glass... It was dirty. Nasty. I think they do the old dunk dunk rinse, and that's not a great tasting pint by anyone's measure. Moody bartender to.... Hey Barkeep, Hey Chef Mike, if you hate your jobs so much, you could do all of us locals a favor, and quit.

If you've read any of my past reviews, you know I don't hold back. When you suck... I say you suck. When you're average, I also say you suck, because I have no room for average during my precious time here on this planet. This plate of fried chicken is neither of those things... it's absolute premium. Done with love and care and passion, it's as though the Colonel himself invited me into his dining room to serve me his latest (very slight) tweak on his Original. Now I'm not talking KFC garbage here people. I'm talkin the premium. The stuff the Colonel put out at his house on Sunday nights. The biscuits matched the chicken in quality. Heavenly, buttery... crispy on the edges but fluffy where they needed to be. A true masterpiece. If I could deduct points (and I can't, because everything I just said is true), I would deduct for the simple misdemeanor of not having a "bailout" beer on your menu. It's rare that I find a craft beer that I like. I try... there's just so much bad beer. I understand the motivation of wanting to support the smaller breweries, that's a honorable position to take... but for Christ's sake, hold them to a minimum standard of drinkability... or better yet, hold a race car beer in reserve, out of the public's eye, for those of us who would rather not go through the painful process of trying another loser. 


On another note... my wife is a vegetarian, and she could not have been more pleased with her selection and her choice. It's rare we find one that we both love.... but here it is. 

World Class Fried Chicken.

It's over. It's sad, but there is nothing left of the original Gracie's. I think she is still there, but she has obviously lost her passion for restaurantuering. Don't second guess me on this one...you'll be sorry.

Let me start by saying.... I love that The Perky exists. This less than stellar review is simply to get a message to the owner. You've done the work. You've figured out how to put real bbq on the table... and it's pretty damn good. I think you have a heavy hand on your spice jar when it comes to the brisket, but that's just my personal taste. It's you're art, so do what ya do... BUT, you are doing your regular customers a disservice when you lie to them. I live VERY far away. I got some "old" brisket once, so before my next trip to the Perk, I thought it prudent to call and check when the next batch was coming off the smoker. I told the women on the phone that I would arrange my visit to coincide w a fresh brisket day, to which she took offense. "Our brisket is fresh every day!" She said. No it's not. It's not even close to every day. You think your customers don't know the difference? You so underestimate us. Three day old brisket, reheated... is winning you no new fans. You studied how the masters cook their meat, now study how they run their restaurants. It's ok to run out of something great, it's ok if on certain days it's not available. That makes it scarce... that makes your customers behave differently. Folks.... this stuff is pretty damn good if you hit it when it's fresh... if you don't... it's pretty damn below average. And Mr Owner... if it's all just too much of a pain in the ass to deliver "pretty damn good to great" every day, that's your prerogative to... just do us a solid, and train your staff to tell us the truth. We won't abandon you... we'll respect and support you. Cheers.

I'm going to keep this shirt and sweet. I had the $22 hamburger, and it's totally worth $23. Off the hook... prepared, assembled and presented with nothing but great taste. Fries match to perfection. Don't hesitate.

rlFUes82nBIyEnYp42yEqA.review_text: Horrible service walked in got seated quickly, then waited for over ten minutes to have someone come back to take our order. We tried to flag down the waitress twice and she literally looked at us and turned around and walked away the second time. At which time I decided we were not going to wait anymore, grabbed our stuff and left, they didn't seem to care at all we were leaving. I would not go back again or recommend it ever.

Really good food for cheap. You really can't go wrong with a place where the food is good and everything on the menu is less than $5. The chili relleno is yummy and so are the tortas but make sure to get a side of three fried jalapeños for $0.50. Only downside is the service can be a little rough, but overall it's a really good quality place.

Pretty middle of the road, not authentic, but pretty good flavor. They just moved to South Virginia next to their sushi restaurant so they are offering 10% off your bill until the 6/31/16. It's not a lot of savings but it is nice since you can expect that with a location change they might not be to their normal standard. We had a shoyu ramen, tonkatsu ramen and some tempura veggies, all just okay but we were stuffed when we left and only spent $25 with included a 25% tip, which is super cheap in my book for two people. 

All in all just okay, but I'd like to try it again to see if I can find something I love.

Really yummy! Went with a group of 5 so I got to sample a lot of the menu. The biscuits and gravy is great, pork chops and eggs were good, fish and chips were good, chicken fried steak not so much, but everything else was really delicious. I can't remember what it was called but the dish that had ham steak, sausages and bacon is cheap and has soooo much food. I recommend trying it if you are near.

Went there last night and everything was delish. We tried a spicy stir fry, two different drunken noodles and green curry. They flavors were very good really authentic, not as spicy as I'm used to for Thai food, but still really yummy. The service was great and I definitely want to go back and try more dishes.

Really yummy! Good selection of food. Had the chicken tiki masala, pork vindaloo and aloo gobi. Lots of food a attentive staff. The pork was my favorite, nice flavor and spicy. I am definitly going to come again.

Very good food for the price. My fiance and i tried the 3 taco plate with rice and beans. I got asada, pastor, and shredded chicken, he got asada, pastor, and carnitas. The mean was a little wet for all but the asada, but the flavor was very good. They bring you a little cup of salsa with your order that was delicious. We would definitely recommend it for the street tacos and we would like to go back and try more dishes. I kind of regretted not getting pozole after I saw the table next to us get soup, it looked amazing.

Very good food. Really in between on the 4-5 star, but since they only opened a couple days before we went they really are doing an awesome job, and deserve the 5. Most restaurants have a lot of growing pains when they just open, this restauraunt felt like a well established kitchen and staff. 

I highly recommend the fire naan if you like spicy food. I loved that the food that was represented as spicy in the menu actually had some kick. I feel like I'm always going to restaurants that list things as hot on the menu and then I get disappointed when it has zero heat. They did not have a beer menu when we went so that is a little odd to open and not have your menus ready but the server knew the choices and let us know. Overall the service was good and the restaurant very clean.

For an appetizer we has the vegitarian samosas, very good, they had a little kick. For dinner we had paneer tikka masala, aloo gobi, a large bowl of rice and fire naan. I also purchased garlic naan and chicken took a masala to go. The tikka masala with both the paneer and chicken was a little bland, just kind of under whelming. The samosa, fire naan and aloo gobi were really very delicious though. Lots of flavor and just really good all around.

Good sushi. Not my favorite sushi place in town, but very good. I liked the ambiance, I like that they have a sushi bowl and burrito bar. I don't know why more sushi restaurants don't do this, it is very smart. 

Huge plus is that they have a very spicy sauce for the rolls, very delicious. 

My partner and I decided to have dinner here, he arrived before I did and asked for 2 seats at the bar. He started our order before I got there as I was starving after work. When I arrived every one was friendly and yelling  'Aloha'. I was then bombarded with 4 people walking up to ask if I needed a table, it was a little much. When I got to my seat my partner had his setting with the wasabi and ginger, I asked him where min was, he said the guy was working on it. I sat for a couple minutes, then asked for it. He seemed shocked I was waiting on it, but he greeted me when I sat and said welcome, but never brought me one...?

Other than that is was really good sushi and good service, a little slower than I am used to, but people stater trickling in and they got busy toward the end of our dinner. It was pretty loud in the restaurant, but no big deal. 

Only real criticism I have is the owner who was very friendly and very welcoming was loudly giving advice to the staff right next to us a lot. He was kind of yelling at them to greet people, pick up plates and bring more napkins, stuff like that. I figure the longer they are open the more he will trust his staff and that will not happen. We just felt a little bad for the girls, because they were doing a really good job.

Went there before my flight out of town. Seemed like a quick and easy location. Service was great, the restaurant was clean. The tacos were incredibly dry and the condiment station with salsa and sides was practically empty. The papusa was good though, nothing special. We got 3 asada and 3 pastor tacos and I didn't even eat mine. I ate the papusa and that was it. I won't go back.

I don't want to rant on this place. It wasn't some place I would ever seek to eat again. 

The service was not good, very inattentive. Myself and one of the other 4 dinners I went with had empty drinks a large portion of the evening. The server came by with pepper for the salads or cheese an couple minutes after we had our plates, making it kind of a superficial offer. 

Myself and another person at my table went with the mushroom risotto after asking the server how it was and it showed up as a huge mound of brown mush. It was unappetizing to look at but after tasting it, it was just bland and more like a overcooked rice in gravy. It takes a lot for me to return food, I don't even remember the last time I have done that (and honestly it was probably because it was brought out wrong and I got the same dish) this dish I just could not eat and wanted something different. 

The other dinners enjoyed their meals, one said hers was delicious and loved it, she got the chicken piccata. The other two said it was good, but nothing special, they got a rigatoni with peas and prosciutto in a white sauce and chicken parmesan. The portions were massive. I think if you found something you loved on the menu and you became a regular with the service staff, it would be a great place for you, unfortunately it's just not for me.

I don't know what else to say but figure yourself out Del Taco. They were only taking orders for 1 car at a time and filling that order before they would take another order. Just super inefficient. I believe it was in an attempt to keep their window time down, but we waited in the drive thru with no way to get out for 30min. By the time we got to the ordering window we just decided to put in an order. Which took another 8- 9 min based on the clock at the window. Took at picture at 7 min 30 sec. 

So 40 min to get 2 bean and cheese burritos and 6 tacos....

I can't believe they made me into the monster that reviews fast food this critically.

My favorite sushi in town.

Always great service, and even more important great fish. I usually stick to a lot of nigiri, lots of sake(salmon), and the cut on the fish is always clean. I find it really important that the fish look as beautiful as it tastes. It always tastes fresh and has a good rice to salmon ratio. 

I can't say enough good things about Hiroba and it's staff. I love coming here and leaving full and happy.

Yum! I've had good food here before, but I never really thought of it as a go to place...until today. I had the western burrito and it was fantastic. I added serrano peppers, it was spicy, flavorful and I love that they have a salsa bar. The burrito ended up being about $9 and it was huge. It was enough for 2 meals, I ate it all, but I had half was full, then 2 hours later came back for round 2. The second time around it didn't look as good, but it tasted great. 

Good flavor, good prices, and the young man behind the counter was really helpful and polite. Definitely going to be going here more often. 

Sorry no pictures, I was too hungry... lol

Let me start with I've never been a huge fan of the food at Great Basin. I always like to try the different beers and they have a great happy hour. That being said today they wowed me. 

I'll start with the beer which is the main reason I usually come here. The Biggest Little Saison was so great....-basin (sorry pun intended). It was totally to style, a little funky, clear, and Belgian. I had 2 of the same beer because I liked it so much, normally I never get 2 of the same beer. 

Next the food. I had the Go Brown's Crispy Onion Burger. The chipotle mayo and pretzel bun made it. It was juicy, packed with flavor, and a little messy, all things a good burger should be. The flavors were on point and I will try and order it next time I come, even though it is a daily special. 

The service is normally pretty good and today was not exception. Service was fast and friendly. I hope GB meets this expectation next time I come.

Came in today and there was the usual weekend long wait for a table. We were a party of 2, so the wait was shorter than normal, 20 min. We sat and wait to be called and the time estimate was pretty spot on, little less than 20 min, but not much. 

Server was great. He was a young man, very muscular and dark hair. He was attentive filled my coffee and water at the proper times, this I find is usually lacking here. Servers are normally very busy and are good at filling one or the other, but not both. He promptly took out order and checked in on us when the food got to the table, another thing that is normally lacking and he was on top of, usually they come way after the food is brought to the table and do superficial I hope everything is good as they are walking by checks. 

The reason for the bad review however is the food. I don't go to Peg's for the service, usually it is just mediocre. I always get the Huevos Rancheros with the eggs over medium. Today my eggs were cooked over hard not once, but twice. I know they were busy, but that is expected and understandable. Eggs can be tricky even if you are used to cooking them, so I don't get too upset if they are close to the right temp. The first batch was browned they were cooked so over hard and the second batch was just lightly over hard, still no runny yolk but not an atrocity to eggs. 

I ended up just eating the beans, hash browns and cabbage slaw side and picking at the tortillas. I probably should have said something the second time, but I was pretty full and didn't want to waste their time and mine by sending the dish back again. 

I'll definitely be back because I love the breakfast 9 times out of 10, today just made me feel like I wasted my time and disappointed me .

Nothing really special. It was a pretty good burger. I had the Spanish and my boyfriend had an Angus Beef. We both though they were pretty basic. I liked mine more than he liked his because mine actually had some spice kick. I wasn't a huge fan of the potato circles in lieu of fries, but they weren't bad. 

They do serve beer, which could be a redeeming factor. I think next time we go we will try the wings and sweet potato fries and see if that changes out mind. 

Service was good though. A gentleman was walking around and helping people making sure everyone was happy. I was going to give a 3 rating, but the service kicked it up to a 4.

I was so excited to try this place, but was left pretty disappointed. The service was great, the young guy taking orders was very nice and helpful. The food just wasn't what I was expecting. We ordered two #2's which comes with 1 scoop mac salad, 1 scoop rice, and marinated steak strips served over more rice. The steak was super sweet and just drenched in marinate. The mac salad and rice were good, but I picked at the meat and didn't eat more that a couple bites.

Happy Hour is a great deal at Ruth's Chris. The Seared Ahi Tuna Appetizer is always delicious. The cocktails are hand crafted and well worth the $9 happy hour price. We always have great service at the bar and more than enough food. Lately we have gotten the spicy shrimp appetizer because the shrimp are crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, with great flavor. We always have really great service when we eat in the dinning room too. Only down side is the prices are a bit steep, but for a special occasion the food and service are hard to beat.

The food was under whelming and the service was not very good. The only reason I gave them a 3 was becaise the crazy man ramen was very spicy and the other dishes were pretty middle of the road. We were seated immediately, but it took a long time for the server to take our order. We received our gyoza appetizer very promptly, but it was very over cooked and too dark, almost burned. We sat for a very long while with empty water glasses, and when I received my crazy man ramen, I had to flag someone down for more water. The server never came to check on us and it felt like we were forgotten after our order was taken. The only redeeming factor is if you like spicy food, their ramen is SPICY, and will hit the spot if you like to sweat. I might go back just for the hot ramen, but definitely not the service or other foods.

The last time I came to Peg's Glorified Ham and Eggs the eggs were over cooked not once, but twice. It is a little disappointing when half of the restaurant's name stake can't be consistent. 

This experience was much better though. My meal looked and tasted delicious. As I have said in another review the service is never stellar, but the food usually does not disappoint. Peg's is one of my go to breakfast spots because of the Huevos Rancheros. Period.

Yum! Really good food, very authentic. Good service, very friendly people. The prices are very reasonable. It is an order at the front and rear yourself kind of place. I can imagine when they are busy there would be a problem getting a table. There was a steady flow of orders while we were there 50/50 to go. 

My family ordered 10 asada tacos, 10 pastor tacos, chilli verdi and an asada plate. They have a salsa bar which is really good for a larger party we could go and get what we each wanted and didn't have to bug them for more salsa or toppings. The pickled cabbage and carrots are good there, not too spicy.  

The food was all really good, the tacos were street tacos, so very small. For a meal a person would probably order 4 or 5 a la carte to get full. The asada plate and chilli verdi had very good flavor and was a lot of food. Probably the best thing about the place to me was HOMEMADE TORTILLAS! Yum. I love homemade tortillas and not many places do it. The chips were kind of lacking because they were just kind of stale bagged chips, but the tortillas made up for it. 

Definitely going back.

Delicious food even togo. This is one of my favorite Thai food restaurants in town and they keep the quality top notch on takeout. 

Drunken noodles are a must try they are moist and have great flavor. 

One really stand out thing right now is how clean they are. When paying they disinfect the pen and clip board as well and using lots of sanitizer to keep cross contamination to a minimum.

Dinner was fantastic! I dont know if the experience was heightened by all restaurants being closed for so long or if it really was that great, but there is only one way to find out and that is to go back a lot more... in all seriousness dinner was delicious, the service was great, and the atmosphere unbeatable. 

I've seen the restaurant on walks and always wanted to try it, and it did not disappoint. We showed up early, the hostess opened the door for us, and explained that as part of the restaurants precautions for preventing the spread of covid they would be taking all the guests temperatures and the menus would be shared at the table and not reused. We happily agreed and it made us feel good that they were so cautious.

Once seated we had bread and water delivered to the table. I ordered a dirty martini and my partner got a Manhattan, both were delicious. 

We ordered the octopus appetizer, it was tender and had great flavor. Maybe a bit too much avocado, but still delicious.

For dinner we had the duck confit with pork belly and pork crackling and lamb leg with ratatouille. The duck was good, very salty with the sauce and pork sides adding to the amount of salt. The real star though was the lamb and ratatouille. I would go to the restaurant and order that everyday. I love ratatouille and the flavor of this one was exceptional. The lamb was cooked perfectly, so tender, and delicious.

For dessert we had the coffee creme brulee. So original and such good flavor. The custard could have been set more, but that didn't stop us from devouring it all. 

Throughout dinner our server was very attentive, polite, and quick. We had a great time and WILL go back again.

Love this business! It is a great locally owned business that I am happy to support. They always have fun events and great beers. I am so excited they are open again. I dont know why I've never given a yelp review before, but they have always been great to us. 

Service and beers tonight were spot on. Thank you Imbib!

Went to SF Kitchen on my lunch break from work today, as they are only 6 min from my office. I was hoping to have a quick lunch and figured Chinese food would be a pretty good bet. Arrived at the restaurant around noon and was surprised to see only 2 tables occupied. We were promptly seated and our order take within the first 5 min of being in the restaurant. We ordered potstickers, vegetable chow mein, and a lunch special with mongolian beef and steamed rice. 

While the food and service was great the one big complaint I had was it took almost 30 min to get our potstickers. At lunchtime 30 min for any item is too much, we would have happily not ordered them had the server said that they have a long lead time. 

On to the food: 
I want to start with everything was hot and you could tell made to order. 

The hot and sour soup that came with the lunch special was bland and a little thicker than we are used to, we didn't like it but it was nice to have a couple bites before out appetizer. 

The potstickers were FANTASTIC they were very large and doughy, a little light of the filling, but great flavor and a awesome dipping sauce to go with them. 

The chow mein was good, not the best I have ever had, but a very solid dish. It was a good size portion, and it was fresh so the noodles weren't gummy at all, it have good flavor and I didn't have any complaints. 

The mongolian beef lunch special, was very good. The meat was tender, the sauce spicy and a perfect size to eat it all and not have to worry about leftovers. For $10 it was a very good price. 

All in all a good lunch place, I will be back. I won't order the potstickers for lunch unless I place the order ahead of time, but all the food was good and everything else came out very quickly. I'd recommend giving them a shot.

Love the food here. I thought it was time to update my review, since the last time I posted a review it was just opening. We went for lunch on the weekend as they were opening. The server quickly seated us and got us water. She had some opening duties to do, so we waited and looked over the menu until she was ready. 

We ordered the Chicken Samosas, Fire Naan, Aloo Golbi, and Pepper Masala with Lamb. The samosas seemed a little drier than when we usually order them, but the flavor is always delicious. The order only comes with 3, but don't let that stop you from ordering them, because they are very large. 

The Aloo Golbi and Pepper Masala with Lamb were amazing. My favorite dish on the menu is the Aloo Golbi, and being a big meat eater that is saying something. The depth of flavor is incredible. The pepper masala was really good as well, with a nice spice to it. I love when the menu items that say spicy are actually spicy, there is nothing more disappointing than ordering a dish that promises to be spicy and it falls flat on the heat. 

As the meal went on the service wasn't great, it was quite a long time for us to get helped after being seated. To go containers and the check were a long wait, but as long as the food is still this good, we are going to keep coming and we will be happy to wait.

There is always a line at Scooper no matter the time of day I have observed. They have the best milkshakes in town I think, but I have yet to find something to eat on their menu that I love. I have in the past had a burger and fries, which was so so, chili cheese fries which were okay, and a hot pastrami which tasted good, but was so oily I couldn't finish. 

This time I thought I would give a burrito a try. It was chili inside of a tortilla. It did not work well, and I immediately regretted straying from the normal drive-in menu. 

All this being said, I will go back for a milkshake any day of the week. In the summer I go every 2-3 weeks if not more often to get a black cherry milkshake, and I love it. I will just pick up food at another spot and continue to only get a milkshake. If anyone knows a great menu item, let me know, because if I could find something I like to eat at Scoopers it would be a deadly combo of delicious milkshakes and good food.

I hadn't been here in years and on a whim decided to go to dinner here. The menu is very diverse and looks like it has a lot to offer, so we thought we would give it a try. 

We made a reservation for 5pm, and were seated promptly on arrival. There was an odd fishy odor to the restaurant. We didn't say anything, but a table that was sat shortly after us with a seafood allergy, made a comment that he hoped the smell did not set anything off with his wife's allergy. A little rude, but the smell was quite strong. 

The server was nice and he was very attentive. Our only complaint with him was that were arrived at 5pm, and the website says Happy Hour is from 3-6pm daily, we did not receive Happy Hour prices on our drinks. 

After hearing the daily specials we decided to go with the daily appetizer of artichoke hearts to start, then decided to share the paella and sautéed scallops, and finish with the mixed berry crepes. Every dish we got was overly zested with lemon...every dish...

The artichoke hears were okay, nothing special. The scallops were cooked wonderfully, but were not cleaned properly as they were really gritty, I could only eat one before I was done. The paella was VERY over cooked, watery, and tasted so much of lemon I only had a couple bites. Finally the mixed berry dish was also okay, and nothing special.

The service was good, but I will not be coming back for dinner. I remember the breakfast dishes being good, so maybe I will come back and try that another time, but as of now I think we were disappointed enough to where even coming back at a different time to try breakfast will be a ways down the road.

Really good soup, great for the winter weather. 

Called ahead for a reservation for 2, table was ready when we got there, and we were promptly seated. The service was good very quick throughout the meal.

The soup was delicious, a very rich broth that didn't need any extra flavor. Dumplings were flavorful and the portion was a good size. 

It was a nice, quick, 30 minute, in and out lunch with good food. We will be back again.

SO yummy! My first time going here was at a Yelp Elite Event, it was so good, I bought gift certificated for 4 more ice creams to make sure I went back. 

The Thai Tea flavor is by far my favorite, I bought a pint to take home it was so good. I love how the flavors rotate, I've tried the vanilla, ube, thai tea, coffee, and mango flavors now and they are all delicious. I highly recommend giving them a try. A little pricey, but worth it.
