Really good and very fast, I didn't think I would like a savory crepe, but it was very good. This would be 5 stars, but I ordered a 5th crepe and the cashier must not have heard, I later looked at the receipt and wasn't charged for it. The crepes are very big, so we are able to share. Also, the coffee tasted a little burnt, not my favorite, but everything else was really good. It is a fun concept and also tasty. Perfect for before or after a Costco run.

I wanted to update my rating of Bawarchi. They have become our go to for Indian food in the Reno/Sparks area.The flavor is amazing and when the menu says spicy they aren't messing around. I still do not prefer the chicken tikka masala from Bawarchi, but we've loved every other dish we have tired from here. Our staple dishes that we seem to go back for over and over are the alu gobi, pepper masala (golbi, lamb, goat, and chicken are all fantastic), tandoori chicken, samosas, and tonight we found a new favorite mix veg pakora.

If you like Indian food please give this place a try, I promise you won't be disappointed.

Quick and easy meal. The food was good and pretty reasonably priced. They were out off the onion rings and sizl fries, but not a big deal. I had the Caliente burger it had good flavor, slightly spicy but not too bad and my husband got the classic and it was good too. Only thing that could have been better was a warm bun, both were cold, but favor was still there.

ry0kAvWu83fu-Ku8jcMLoQ.review_text: My turkey sandwich was not bad, the atmosphere was nice, but I was hoping the grilled peppers would be more flavorful.
Everything was incredibly greasy and my lamb shepherd's pie was a very small portion for dinner.  Nice atmosphere though and great staff.

The ambiance is great and perfect for group meals (but beware of the slow service!)  The menu has a variety of local options and classy items as well.  I didn't think my po boy was the best and the sweet potato beignets were more interesting in name rather than taste, but they had a nice pork sandwich appetizer and cocktail as part of their prix fixe dinner option.

I enjoyed the simple shrimp rolls for lunch although the salad dressing was a little sour for my taste.  It was a nice place to meet colleagues over a meal and in a convenient location so I'd probably come back again if I'm in the area.

I've never tried a muffaletta before and this seemed to be the best place to go.  It was a small grocery store that seemed to carry some authentic Italian goods with a hometown feel.  It was a really great place to get a quick, inexpensive, and hearty meal!  I bought half a sandwich but I might have gotten by with the quarter size.
Excellent fluffy donuts that weren't overly sweet!  I tried the chocolate-iced one with coconut and it was a delicious breakfast.  Hoping to try other flavors later on!

The tufoli was amazing!  It wasn't greasy at all and the ingredients tasted really fresh.  The atmosphere was perfect for a business lunch meeting especially since it's pretty close to the convention center and I hope I have a chance to try the other items on their menu!

I just tried a few drinks during happy hour which were okay but they tasted really dilute.  The space at the bar was really small and they don't take reservations during happy hour.  A few people from our group ordered food from the happy hour menu which was extremely tiny.  I didn't like smelling like food for hours after leaving.  I probably won't come back in the future.

I stopped by for a taro milk tea which was more intensely purple than I expected as I hadn't had one for awhile.  It was nice, refreshing, and smooth without being overly sweet and reasonably priced.  Although I got mine to go, the interior was nicely designed and would be a good place to chat with friends.

I had their huge portion of stir fried chicken noodles with hand drawn noodles and I really did like the noodles!  I would have enjoyed having more vegetables beyond cabbage and less oil but I liked that it also came with some chili sauce on the side and the taste overall.  I hope to try some of their noodle soups later on!

I really enjoyed my braised pork enchilada with tender meat and a combination of sauces with an unexpected hint of sweetness.  They served a healthy portion for dinner and it had a fun and casual vibe to enjoy with friends.  They had some great daily specials and tequila tasting in a balloon which sounded intriguing so hopefully I'll have a chance to return later on!

I had an amazing seafood benedict with a biscuit that surprisingly had more flavor than I expected, with sweet hints of corn, topped with delicious crab and crawfish cakes, perfectly cooked poached eggs, and creamy hollandaise sauce.  I arrived early and enjoyed the pleasant spring morning breeze on the second floor that opened out onto a balcony.  I hope to try more from their menu in the future!

I liked that they offered a sampler Taste of the Bayou on the menu and I tried the chicken and andouille gumbo, the crawfish etouffée and Cajun jambalaya.  It would have been nice to have more crawfish in the etouffée and less salt overall.  The rice was nice and fluffy and I enjoyed the gumbo the most with a combination of two types of meat.  It probably would have been more filling to order all four items, but it was a very convenient choice located close to the French Quarter.

This was a great BBQ place and I enjoyed the Carolina sandwich with tender and nicely seasoned pulled pork with coleslaw and mustard BBQ drizzle on top.  The cornbread was all right, although a little on the dry side but it came with softened honey butter.  The brisket and half rack were also great, especially since there was a great spread of sauces to try.  The line was organized efficiently so we could and see all the sides and fill our trays as we went through the line.  It was great that it was conveniently located next to public transportation and the convention center.  I'm glad we arrived early for lunch since it's a popular spot for a filling meal!

I was intrigued by the sign that highlighted their appearance on the Food Network.  I tried a square of the espresso gooey cake they're known for and it was very buttery but surprisingly not as sweet as I anticipated, especially with an iced coffee on the side.  The interior was cute with a Midwest vibe that was conveniently located near the convention center.

I had the turkey panini and I really liked the fresh goat cheese and fig spread, along with the nice side salad with mild vinaigrette dressing.  It was a cute cafe that's a great place for a casual and convenient lunch near the convention center.  I hope I have a chance to go back and try their smoothies!

I really enjoyed the basil pesto tomato egg brioche with so many flavors all in one which made for a flaky, buttery and delicious breakfast!  I didn't have time to try the coffee and juices that they're known for but I hope to visit again in the future!

s34ZmKzCaWE2z-FBlJiIxw.review_text:
The good: arancini, home made bread, bruschetta, cheese and flash fried mozzarella appetizer topped with shrimp and arugula.

The bad: the shrimp on the appetizer tasted like it had been in the freezer for a long, long time. I got the eggplant entree and it was incredibly oily and nondescript. 

I would definitely go back, but I am steering clear of the eggplant and seafood unless it's a fresh special.

Drink: the Sexican
Eat: Nachos and guacamole.
Dessert: Churros

I have ordered here many times. The food is always good, no frills, standard Chinese takeout. Living in the neighborhood, I always see the owners' children playing outside. Sure, it's aesthetically unappealing but the food meets the requirements and I like to support a little family owned business.

I am SO disappointed. Up until Saturday night, Monsu was my favorite Italian restaurant in the city. I had friends coming in so I made a reservation for all 6 of us and I told them how wonderful our dining experience was going to be. We had the antipasti to start, which was delicious, $10pp and a nice size. We ordered a la carte, several different pasta dishes. I have dined here many times before and the portions were a perfect size. On Saturday, they were MINUSCULE. If I am paying $16 for a pasta dinner, I want DINNER not 12 little noodles and 2 shrimp. Not one of us felt the serving size was anywhere near appropriate, and when we complained we were dismissed. 

I am so dismayed, not only was it very embarrassing to have lauded this restaurant to my guests and then have that disappointing experience, but I feel I cannot return to this place I once enjoyed so much. The food is delicious, but that experience was so bad I don't see myself willing to give it another chance. When you're paying for a meal, you expect to get a meal. For the record, shortly after we left we went and got pizza.

Living in Queen Village, my options for a local market are this and 7-11 which is directly across the street. I choose Palm Tree every time! They have healthy options for everything from canned goods to the sandwiches they make. The prices are very fair and I don't ever feel like I'm getting ripped off in order to have the quality things. It's clean and the service is quick, really all you could want from your local corner store!

This is my go to place for delivery, they're reasonably priced, quick and the food is really good. My orders are always here within a reasonable amount of time, I've tried a bunch of menu items and I like them all. If you're looking for more traditional Mexican,  go to Las Bugambilias. If you're looking for a good meal with a nice portion size,  come here! I should also note that the watermelon juice is FANTASTIC.

Their prices are good, theyir serving sizes are good, the turnaround time is quick. All in all, this is a great lunch spot. You can call ahead with your order so it's ready by the time you get there to just pick it up and go. When you become a regular, they know you by name! My staples are the egg sandwiches, club sandwiches, and salads. Hard to go wrong!

I had been wanting to come here for a really long time, and I was a bit disappointed. I saw wild mushroom risotto with pork belly on the menu and it was a no brainer, as I love both. The risotto portion was small, not enough to eat alongside many bites of the pork belly. The meat itself was overcooked and the dryness of the meat in conjunction with the softness of the thick fat strip down the center of the meat was weird on the palette. The cream sauce that came with it was just ok. If I'm going to splurge calories on a cream sauce I want it to knock my socks off. Maybe I got the wrong menu item. The zuppa de pesce looked good on someone else's table. . We also got the calamari which was delicious, it was well cooked and had a nice sauce. For dessert we had the tiramisu which was good, a solid homemade standard. The table at the top of the basement stairs had drafts coming up from the basement, I wore my coat almost the entire time! Would I go back again? Maybe for lunch. There are too many other places to explore to come back again anytime soon.

I have eaten here a few times and I will keep coming back! The fresh rolls appetizer is comparable to Vietnamese summer rolls, but they are larger and just as good. The crispy Tamarind duck is great,  the red curry is fantastic if you like a little kick. I have enjoyed everything I have gotten here, be it take out or dine in. The service is great and the atmosphere is nice.

Yikes. There's a beer list on the wall written in chalk that differs from the printed beer list. A good 40% of them are unavailable. My friend got a wrap that he said was really tasty, but I didn't try it so I can't speak to it personally.  If you want to come here and causally bro out & don't care what kind of beer you're drinking,  then great. Otherwise,  there's a ton of other great places in the area.

I love this coffee shop. I'd just moved to the neighborhood and I was looking for something to eat for breakfast while strolling through Liberties Walk, and I smelled something amazing. I followed my nose one block "off the beaten path" and found One Shot. The food is incredible,  I love The Ultimate Breakfast Sandwich in particular, The Abe is a close second. The ingredients are healthful and delicious. They often change their specialty drink list, the combinations are unique and fantastic. They sell a variety of fresh pastries that are always changing,  with vegan options if you're so inclined.  They also sell artisinal products such as chocolate and nut butters. You can sit outside and there are designated stations to tie up your dog, too. I really love this place!

Let me begin by stating the bad: There's always a wait, the place is small, it's cash only. That being said, I do not care about any of that because it's worth it. I have never had something here I didn't love! When I have people visit from out of town I bring them here because I am certain they'll have an incredible meal that they can't just get anywhere. I love the salmon benedict (those fried capers!!!) and the short rib benedict. Their short ribs are great, I love getting them over the grits. The mac & cheese is absolutely incredible. The specialty stuffed french toast options are always fantastic, they are decadent but worth the treat. The chicken cutlet sandwich is very good, their tomato soup is a great side. The short rib panini is delicious, as is the buffalo chicken mac & cheese. The specialty coffees are delightful as well as the lemonade. Long story short, you cannot go wrong when you come here.

This is a current James Beard nominated restaurant, & I can completely understand why. The cuisine was imaginative, flavorful, brave, and delicious. Our experience was only furthered by the knowledge and kindness of our server, Steven R. We started with the oysters, they were incredibly delicious. In fact, they were so good I had no time to stop and take a photo. The same could be said for the deliciously fresh bread and clearly homemade butter. We also got the escargot with Brussels sprouts, mushrooms, speck, & a cream sauce. It was delicious, the sauce was amazing. The second course was the lobster and shrimp mousse; I was concerned it was going to be too gastronomic, but it was absolutely perfect. For the third course, I got the lamb. I personally preferred the sliced rare lamb on my plate as opposed to the stewed lamb with the fruit that came along with it. However, my dining companion preferred that so it's entirely subjective. We finished our meal with the chocolate souffle, which was incredible. Definitely give it at least 5 minutes to cool off! I couldn't wait, so burning my tongue was completely my own fault. Best drink I had was the champagne, it is crisp and uniquely delicious. It's a pricey meal, but a dining experience you won't soon forget.

I want to love this place. I don't. My experiences here have been "meh". It's nothing special and two visits in a row now my burgers have not been medium as requested, but completely well done. It's hard to direct yourself here if you want a burger when Sketch is just down Girard Ave. The burgers are alright but nothing amazing, I really wouldn't say I recommend them. The adult milkshakes are unique and delicious, though. I am also a fan of their large, home made onion rings. I think this place is more of a novelty; if you want to come here and try whatever wacky special they are currently promoting, that could be a better experience but their uniqueness hasn't appealed to me just yet.

The breakfast pocket sandwich is tasty. I am not a fan of sweet and salty things together but I do enjoy their sausage, egg and waffle version. The coffee is standard. My problem with this place is that the smoothies are made with premixed purees that have a lot of added liquid cane sugar. I guess if you're not interested in the health benefits of a smoothie, then it's fine. As for me, I prefer real fruit with no added sugars. With One Shot just down the street, it's hard to want to come here.

I came here during my lunch break at work. I can't believe people would go to the chain restaurant around the corner when this is here. I got lunch special #9, guacamole salad, tamal, beef tip quesadilla.  It's inexpensive,  came very quickly and fresh.  The decor is really nice too, bright and cheerful and you can tell someone put a lot of love into it. I'll definitely be back for lunch and I'll bring coworkers to help spread the word.

I have to give this place a solid 3 although I really wanted to give more. The whole premise of a burger place is the burger, right? They should know how to time it so the burgers are cooked to the right temperature. My dining companion and I both ordered ours cooked medium and both came out well done. We were starving or else we would have sent them back. The brisket is absolutely delicious.  I love that there are lots of options and that the business is health conscious. I'll give it another try sometime, but I was definitely disappointed.

This is what fast food should strive to be. Extremely quick,  healthy, eco conscious, simple yet flavorful. I can't fathom why someone would choose mass produced chain food over something like this. Bonus points for local sourcing!

I was in the area and thought, "You know what, they're well known and popular, I should give them another chance." I ordered a "big ass" salad, as it's called on the menu; it's essentially a Cobb. I paid $3 extra to add chicken. Look at the photos, it's a tiny amount! It was ok but definitely not worth $15. PYT, I tried to make it work but that's it, we're over.

Unbelievable.  The best meal I have had in Philadelphia and I have lived here for half a decade. The ingredients are fresh, the chef is ingenuitive, the service is great, the price point is fantastic, it's BYO... I could go on and on.

I had a birthday celebration at the 9th St location after hours and it was AWESOME. Sam and Kyle were great to work with, they were so knowledgeable and accommodating. My friends and I all had a wonderful time and we thoroughly enjoyed everything we tasted. The fact that it's BYO probably contributed to some extra purchases being made, haha. I can't even tell you where to begin in this store, just try it all!

Very good hummus, and that pita is so FRESH and aromatic and delicious! The frozen lemon drink... blanking on what it's called but it's nice and refreshing and not overly sweet which I appreciate. I can see that being a summertime craving. It was busy but they were efficient. I'l be back!

There are so many coffee shops in the area, one really has to stand out in order to differentiate. They have a lovely variety of teas, and the standard coffee drinks which are very good. The ambience is nice, but perhaps the best thing is that they allow you to bring your dog inside. I do love La Colombe, but I do not feel comfortable leaving my pet tied up outside while I run in for a drink. You often hear about dogs being stolen and I'm not willing to risk it. This is now my go to coffee place, and I couldn't be happier.

I'm originally from northern NJ and we have the gift of delicious NY style pizza there. I moved to Philly and I love it here, but MAN do I hate the pizza here. The sauce tends to be sweet, the cheese lacks bite, the dough is reminiscent of the flavor of a soft pretzel... It's just not good, anywhere. Anywhere except Pete's, that is. 

If you are looking for ambiance, this is not your place. This is a little hole in the wall, but what's it's lacking in aesthetics it makes up for by flavor. This pizza is the real deal, FINALLY! The flavors are fantastic, and I guarantee if you gave me a blind taste test against other pizza places I could choose Pete's out of the line up because the taste is so truly authentic.

If you are looking to just grab a quick slice or get a pie to go, this is your spot.

Can we talk about the brunch here?! Pork shoulder Benedict with Rival Bros coffee, I mean... This was our first time going and we will definitely be back. My friend's steak and eggs were also good, but I preferred my dish.

It's hard to find quick, healthy meals when you're in the go. I popped in Talia's once when I felt like trying something new in the neighborhood and I was so pleasantly surprised! The owner made me a salad he concocted based off what I said I was in the mood for (vague, at best lol) and it was DELICIOUS! I don't even like white meat chicken and I ate every bite that was in my salad, so flavorful! We chatted for a while, he is relatively new to this business/location but had cooked for presidents and celebrities in the past.

He cares so much about the neighborhood that even the local pigeons get to sample the bagels at the end of the day! I came in for a second time, he remembered me and when I said I forgot my wallet he said I could simply pay him next time. This is a caring business owner who has made a repeat customer from his kindnesses and delicious food. Definitely try it if you like Mediterranean food and the bagels are great too!

I was looking forward to trying this place for a long time and I was kind of disappointed. I got the BBLT, and there were only 2 pieces of bacon! I was thinking there would be a significant piece of burrata also, but it's really just like a spread on one side of the bread. It's okay but not amazing as I'd hoped. I did also try the tomato basil soup which is quite tasty. I would try it again for something else because you can tell they use quality ingredients; I just wish it was a little more robust in this case.
Good food, good value. We got the breakfast quesadilla and monte cristo; perfectly filling for brunch on a rainy day.

This is the best ice cream in Philadelphia! As much as I want to try everything there, I cannot break away from the Hydrox and Rocky Road. The homemade hot fudge is perfect and they put it both below and on top of the ice cream - genius! The raspberry sorbet is amazing with the hot fudge, too.

It's cash only and the line often wraps around the block. Try coming back later or just sucking it up and waiting; the line is there for a reason! Yummmm

What can I say besides EVERYTHING IS GREAT?!

I only recently discovered this place in South Philly and now they are coming to Fishtown, too!  The pork bao is amazing and I don't even eat pork. This is the one exception I'll make for it. The caterpillar bread is incredible, the ribs are good, the vegetarian dumplings... MMMMM

I emailed Perla a few months ago with questions about having a private party there on a Saturday night. They were great & easy to work with and last night was the big day; my guests were so impressed with the ambiance, the experience and the food's quality and quantity. We did the Kamayan dinner, there were whole fish, halved chickens, delicious bok choy, eggplant, onions & carrots, lumpia, pork belly and delicious rice. There was more food than we could have possibly eaten in one sitting, but we sure tried! The staff was extremely gracious & accommodating, we couldn't have had a better experience. Thank you to Linda and the rest of the Perla team!

The good outweighed the bad, but....

I was here on a Saturday night around 8-10ish with some girlfriends. We had a good time bowling, the lanes were nice (but they need more balls, the 8 & 9 lb mediums especially!), the service was good and we enjoying reading the little trivia facts on the screens between turns. As it got later, a DJ came (he was great) and some flashing lights came on (a bit distracting, but still ok). We were in the downstairs area, there were a bunch of people there just bowling, hanging out and being pretty chill. Then these dancers came wearing underwear, fishnets and these weird ripped t-shirts and it felt so incredibly awkward so watch them climb up on these little tables and start gyrating like we were at a club. People are there dressed in flannel, sipping a beer, bowling and watching March Madness. This isn't some Vegas club, no one is coming to a bowling alley bar to dance the night away. I felt bad for the dancers who got down off their tables and walked off somewhere after about 15 minutes, and I felt bad for all of us who were wondering what the hell was happening and feeling uncomfortable. Know your audience, Revolutions.

Well, that didn't go very well. I came in with my parents for the first time, excited to take them to a new restaurant (to us) in the city. We weren't starving so we just ordered the bone marrow croquettes and the fettuccine carbonara. The bone marrow bites were fine, I don't know if I'd get them again but no real complaints there. 

I have real complaints about the fettuccine carbonara, though. We ordered the full sized portions and thought the server made a mistake and gave us the half size when they were brought out, the servings were TINY! For $26, I wanted to have a meal. The noodles were over cooked, and it lacked that creamy, cheesy goodness carbonara usually has. I swear there were about 7 noodles in the tiny portion of the gigantic plate where the food is meant to be. 

My parents said I've never failed before on choosing a restaurant for their visit, but this was the first time. We actually left looking to go somewhere else to have an actual meal, for far less $. We were really disappointed and won't be back.
We needed a place like this in the city. It's so nice to go and have somebody teach you how to play new games. The food and drinks are good, you can easily spend a good afternoon or evening here

It was my first time going and I didn't have extremely high expectations due to some reviews I had read but I wanted to go because of the current collaboration with Hop Sing. I will start with that, the pitcher from the Hop Sing collaboration was fantastic, 10/10. The food was the low point. We got the buffalo chicken sandwiches, and I paid a two dollar upcharge to have them come with "seafood boil spice" and cheese sauce. The server described them akin to Chickies and Pete's so I went for it. The buffalo chicken sandwiches were just chicken tenders in buffalo sauce on a bun & the small portion of fries barely had any seasoning and the cheese sauce was cheese wiz. I definitely wouldn't go back for the food but I would for the drinks. The atmosphere is nice, it's a cute little oasis, but the food game needs to be stepped up.

sPd0RchbmH68DiPwEacutQ.review_text:
Ambience: 5/5 (well-kept dining area with a relaxing, laid-back feel that is great for lunch with friends but is probably too casual for dinner--although it would be nice if it were open late for a late-night snack; lots of Philadelphia memorabilia is a plus)

Food: 5/5 (delicious, authentic Philly cheese steaks using fresh ingredients brought in from Philly; best Philly cheese steaks in the area)

Service: 4/5 (counter service; friendly staff; orders filled quickly; only complaint is the hours of operation: this place should be open later)

Value: 4/5 (the sandwiches are about 1 to 2 dollars more than they should be, but it's not a deal breaker)

Verdict: One of the 5 restaurants in Tucson that I absolutely must take my out-of-town friends to eat at.

Ambience: 4/5 (considering it's a hole-in-the-wall sushi shop in a strip mall, the inside decor is pretty decent; a little crowded but not too bad)

Food: 5/5 (best sushi in Tucson, prepared by authentic Japanese chefs; always fresh, reasonably priced)

Service: 5/5 (friendly, knowledgeable wait-staff on the dining floor; same to the sushi chefs at the counter)

Value: 5/5 (given how over-priced other sushi restaurants are in Tucson--especially considering the quality of some of their fish--you won't find better quality fish at cheaper prices anywhere else in the desert)

Verdict: best sushi in Tucson, no question about it.

Ambience: 4/5 (trendy, contemporary decor, ideal for a dinner date)

Food: 4/5 (fairly large menu; well-presented and good-tasting food)

Service: 4/5 (water glasses kept filled; server was decent; no complaints)

Value: 4/5 (dishes are about 2 - 3 dollars overpriced, but still very reasonable given the ambience and the food quality)

Verdict: If you're looking for good Indian food in Tucson and wan to eat it in a contemporary setting, I recommend Saffron.

Ambience: 4/5 (nice little pizza restaurant on trendy 4th Ave., powered by solar panels on the roof!)

Food: 4/5 (very good NY-style pizza by the slice; crust was a little too big; otherwise perfect)

Service: 4/5 (perfunctory but efficient counter service; late hours of operation is a plus)

Value: 5/5 (reasonably priced, especially given the quality of the pizza)

Verdict: highly recommended if you want pizza but don't have enough friends to order a whole pie somewhere; one of the better pizza restaurants in Tucson.

Ambience: 3/5 (It's a hole-in-the-wall, a little run down, but they try to compensate for that with festive colors and wall decorations. I wouldn't bring a first date here, but maybe a 3rd or 4th date) 

Food: 4/5 (the food is good, but I agree with another reviewer in that, while there seems to be a good variety on the menu, in reality they are almost all variations of the same thing: meat covered in too much sauce + rice + black beans) 

Service: 2/5 (we were the only customers there, but it took quite awhile for the server to address us, take our order, and deliver our food; this is probably due to the laid-back atmosphere, which was evident in the fact that the server was having a phone conversation during the entire meal--no joke, she spoke on the phone even as she delivered our food to us, which is simply unnacceptable.) 

Value: 4/5 (reasonable portions, reasonable prices, good food) 

Verdict: Other Yelpers have this place so highly rated that I came in with high expectations. I left satisfied, but under the impression that it is over-hyped. Bottom line is that it's a good restaurant with good food, but it's nothing spectacular.

Ambience: 2/5 (there are two dining rooms, both of which are a little run down and make me think of restaurant from the 1970s that hasn't been renovated yet)

Food: 4/5 (good food, diverse menu, and arguably the best complimentary chips and salsa served in Tucson)

Service: 2/5 (servers were inconsistent, but not terrible; owner berated us for asking for separate checks ["It's says on the menu that you can't!"] and also snuck the gratuity onto the check without making it clear, both of which soured the post-dinner mood)

Value: 4/5 (reasonably priced, portions were a little small, but the superb, complimentary chips and salsa compensated for that)

Verdict: despite flaws in service and ambience, I will probably come back again for the food and the chips, but La Indita won't be on my list of must-go places to take out-of-town visitors.

Ambience: 3/5 (on weekend nights, it's a zoo; tables are way too close together, resulting in a cramped feel even for someone without claustrophobia that really undermines what otherwise would've been a pleasant ambience)

Food: 4/5 (I love thin crust--especially the unique, crisp taste of coal-oven pizza--and this pizza is indeed really good; although, I was a little surprised by the lack of toppings available to choose from; I don't think it's the best pizza in Tucson, but I'm also not so sure that it isn't)

Service: 2/5 (I made the mistake of going on a Friday night when they were admittedly very busy, but even then the service was quite bad as it took almost an hour for our pizza to come out of the oven, which certainly doesn't create fond memories, especially since we didn't see our waitress at all during the time she took our order and finally delivered our pizza)

Value: 2/5 (the pizza is good, but it's not $25-for-a-regular-sized-pizza good; that's how much it will cost you for a pizza for two if you add 3 to 4 toppings; considering there is better pizza in Tucson for half the price, it's hard to justify cleaning out your wallet for Grimaldi's)

Verdict: I don't care much for chain restaurants, but I was still excited about Grimaldi's given its legacy and its coal-fired pizza; while the pizza was quite good, I left disappointed given that I had to wait an eternity for it and had to pay twice as much as I would've had I gone to a different pizzeria, and had to eat it in a very cramped restaurant; given the price tag, I doubt I'll return anytime soon, but then again that unique coal-fired taste just might beckon me sooner than I think.

Ambience: 4/5 (even on a weekend night this place is never too crowded, which is strange given that it's been named Tucson's best pizza for 20 consecutive years; it's a nice ambience, feels like a pizzeria with its checkered table clothes; I like it) 

Food: 4/5 (the pizza is quite good and quite satisfying, but I'm not convinced it's the best in Tucson; what I do love, though, are the options: wheat, regular, or sourdough crust, lots of different specialty pizzas concoctions (including a cheese-less pizza for the health conscious or lactose intolerant), plus the choice to go halves or even quarters on a pie for more variety) 

Service: 4/5 (friendly staff, always eager to help, prompt delivery of pizza; never have to wait too long; the service doesn't stand out as exceptional, but that doesn't mean there is anything to complain about) 

Value: 2/5 (Like Grimaldi's, the pizza is quite good, but they'll make you pay for it with higher than average prices) 

Verdict: in my quest to find the best pizza in Tucson I finally get to Tucson Weekly's perennial favorite, but my opinion is that while the pizza is very good, and the menu options are simply great, I can't definitively say it's the best pizza in Tucson, especially given the price; still, I like the ambience and will definitely be back for more.

Ambience: 5/5 (dimly lit, in a good way, with the stone pizza oven visible in the center; a good place for a date; was pleasantly surprised since I had thought that Zona was slang for the University of Arizona and had assumed it'd be some type of rowdy sports bar; apparently Zona is Italian for 'zone' / location and, with the 78, refers to the place's address) 

Food: 4/5 (the pizza is quite good, thin and crispy as it should be; my only complaint is that it was a little too salty; not the best in Tucson, but still quite worthy; also appreciative of the wheat crust option) 

Service: 4/5 (friendly staff, knowledgeable about the menu, always eager to help; food delivered in a timely manner; no major complaints) 

Value: 4/5 (A pizza for one will cost about $10-11, which isn't too bad considering that it's good pizza) 

Verdict: I was pleasantly surprised with Zona 78's ambience, while the pizza was quite good and left me satisfied, I don't think it's the best in Tucson; still, I will return in the future.

Ambience: 4/5 (Zachary's is a run-down hole in the wall, there is no question about that, but it pulls it off somehow and it actually adds to the charm; not a good place for a first date, but a great place to go out with a group of college friends for beer and pizza) 

Food: 3/5 (full disclosure: I am biased toward thin crust and there is no such thing as thin crust at Zachary's; you either get the regular (deep dish) pan style (which I recommend) or you get the "thin" pan-style (which is not thin at all and which I do not recommend since the former is much tastier; still, despite my bias, I will admit that Zachary's deep-dish pizza has a unique taste that I think is the best deep-dish in Tucson; but it's just got so much cheese on it that after one slice I've usually had enough; I recommend the Athenian specialty pizza; it's the best on the menu)

Service: 2/5 (friendly staff, but the service is very slow; I've been here 4 times and each time it took one hour for our pizza to come out, which is ridiculously long regardless of how thick the crust is) 

Value: 4/5 (given the mass of each slice, you can easily feel content with 1, feel full with 2, and learn what gluttony is on 3, so given that their prices are average, you're actually getting a pretty good deal) 

Verdict: despite my dislike for thick crust pizza, I admit that Zachary's has a good pie; I like the hole-in-the-wall ambience, which is ideal for groups; I don't like how much cheese they put on the pizza, which makes me feel sick and guilty afterward; but I'll be back in the future nonetheless

Ambience: 3/5 (a little more upscale than the other major deep-dish pizzeria in town, Zachary's, but that's not saying much; not bad, but not overly memorable either) 

Food: 3/5 (I am biased against deep-dish pizza, which is what Rocco's is known for, and biased in favor of thin crust; I ordered both types; I was not impressed with the thin crust as it was not thin enough, but it wasn't bad either; the thick crust was decent--I see why people like it as it was very thick, with stuffed cheese in the crust and a layer of extra sauce on the top, but like Zachary's and all deep-dish pizza, there is way too much cheese) 

Service: 4/5 (I was satisfied; the pizza came out in what felt like a reasonable time; water glasses were kept full; but nothing too special) 

Value: 3/5 (on par with Zachary's as far as getting what you pay for; not overpriced but also not a bargain) 

Verdict: again, as with Zachary's I see why people like this place and their pizza; and despite my dislike for deep-dish, if you like deep dish you can't go wrong with Rocco's

Ambience: 4/5 (It's a market, like a convenience store, but a little more classy, with a few tables inserted in and a large pizza oven behind a counter) 

Food: 4/5 (The pizza is pretty good, definitely some of the better you can get in Tucson from similar places; comparable to No Anchovies and Brooklyn Pizza) 

Service: 4/5 (Counter service; staff is usually friendly) 

Value: 4/5 (Prices are on par with similar restaurants [No Anchovies and Brooklyn Pizza] 

Verdict: 4/5 (I'd recommend as a good place to get some pizza, but it's not my favorite)

I discovered this place about two years ago, but have selfishly held off writing a review because I didn't want the word getting out that this is definitely the best pizza restaurant (and probably the best restaurant) in Tucson, which would mean longer wait times whenever I decided to go. (I know what you're thinking: "If you liked it that much, wouldn't you want others to patron it so it stayed in business?" My response: "I ate here often enough on my own to keep them afloat"). But the word's out now, so it's time to laud it publicly.

Ambience: 5/5 (It's in a strip mall, as are most restaurants in Tucson, but once you get inside, the atmosphere is great. It's a pizza-and-wine-type place; a nice place to take a date)

Food: 5/5 (If they can't make their ingredients there fresh, daily, they import them from Italy. The food is amazing, from the wood-oven cooked bread, the great salads, the phenomenally crispy thin crust Neopolitan-style pizzas, to their home-made chocolate chip cookie, you won't find better food anywhere else in Tucson)

Service: 5/5 (Friendly, extroverted, and informative staff; great service)

Value: 5/5 (Pizzas feed about one person each and range in price from $9 to $14 or so; for how good they taste, though, that is a great price)

Verdict: 5/5 (Hands down my favorite restaurant in Tucson, pizza or otherwise)

Don't mistake this for something it's not: it's a cheap, 24/7 fast-food Mexican restaurant. It's not Cafe Poca Cosa. If you're looking for inexpensive, greasy, delicious, and unhealthy fast-food Mexican food, you can't do better than Nico's. Similar to Losbetos and the Taco Shop, but in my opinion a little bit better (but really, if you've already made the decision to eat at one of these places, what's the difference anyway). 

I love the carne asada burrito. The breakfast burritos are also good.

Overall, I was pleasantly surprised. The food was decent, as was the service, and the price was reasonable. It was more reasonably priced than Sher-E-Punjab with better food, not as cheap as Gandhi of India but with better food. I'll return.

seCeEjqhAhGFJvzNnc75ow.review_text: I'm not much into leaving reviews but I just had to when I saw all the bad ones, I was honestly shocked! I have never ever had a bad experience, the delivery guy is always nice and friendly. The food is great especially there bbq chicken! The general tsos is amazing as well. My go to Chinese place for sure.. My boyfriend especially loves the crab rangoons. Try it out for yourself :) because I have alway been pleased!

I'm so sad... So ordered online. Went and picked it up, the guy at the reg was not very friendly. I get it. I work at Starbucks and sometimes I hate my life too. Maybe he had a bad day. I understand, I'm sure most of the time he is a joy.  I hoped the food would be a little better but to my disappointment it was not. I only took one bite and spit it out, it was just so greasy I couldn't even do it... My drink was good though!  I should have listened to the reviews.. I always do but I just was so excited and hungry.. I should have gone to subway. I've learned my lesson.

Kind of disappointed... It tasted very plain and just tasted like crappy Chinese food that makes you feel greasy and your stomach hurt after. The food I got looked like a microwave meal and had so much sauce poured on it. I was hoping for something healthy but got the opposite
It wasn't terrible but my panang curry was basically just steamed vegetables and rice..
We always have a great time when we come to this establishment! Their food is always great and everyone is always nice. The place is clean and service is fast. What more can you ask for!
Loved, my boyfriend and I stopped by wanting to try something new. Cute little place. Everyone was really friendly. Will be back
Got pickup and the gentleman on the phone was sooo nice. The food we got was amazing and we will be back!

If you like mediocre sushi for the price of actual good real sushi, then this is the place for you! If you enjoy seeing your miso soup coming out of a 7/11 lookalike soup dispenser then .. again.. this is the place for you! Has a suspicious fishy smell when you walk through the door.. but.. have I ever gotten sick from this place (the 2 times that I did go) no! Thank goodness. Try sushi inc :)

Consistently out of ingredients. Always. The staff is very unorganized. Where is the manager? The employees are very nice, they deserve to have a more set up and organized work environment. I come here because it's close. It does satisfy the craving but.. it needs to be allot better.

Alright, so.. first time here. Walked in, kinda overwhelmed because there was so much to take in. I ordered an ice coffee soy with hazelnut, boyfriend ordered a large flat white with toffee nut and he ordered a sandwich and a croissant. Cashier was very nice. My biggest concern was that they didn't have much of a system when it came to giving the barista the drink orders, the cashier would just go over to the girl on bar and tell her what it is we ordered. After we paid I saw two drinks sitting on the bar one large ice coffee black and a small little hot cup filled half way. Assuming it wasn't ours (because it didn't look like it) we sat down and waited. The barista looked super scatter brained and honestly, she wasn't very nice .. at all. She asked if the drinks on the bar was ours, I told her I didn't know what they were but told her I had an ice coffee with hazelnut and soy and he had a flat white. She handed him the small cup saying it was his and she said she needed to add the hazelnut to mine and she gave me the carton of soy (again.. why there needs to be a system..unless you get the ice coffee and then ask them again for the hazelnut.. but I assumed they did that already..) we got the sandwich and left. My boyfriend was still very lost about what coffee he got because there was no toffee nut and he asked for a large and got a small drink that looked pretty much like an espresso macchiato..  My ice coffee was good no complaints there.   He finished his weird drink that he didn't order (but still paid for ...) and we stopped at Starbucks. In the end, we spent 15$. The verdict: Over priced, not helpful at all, didn't feel very welcomed and felt like we were a burden. I'm not sure I'll be back ...

Wowza!! Fresh and amazing! I heard great things about this place from co workers and friends so I of course had to stop by. The staff there were all very friendly and super helpful. I created my own bowl and everything was great. They also had bowls you could pick from and I'll do that next time because they had some really yummy looking ones. They even had vegan options!  Welcome to St.Pete Pacific Counter!! I am so happy you are here and I will most definitely be back!

The service is sub par and if you come here for any sort of event (I came here for Valentine's Day) be prepared to be completely ignored by servers. I have also heard many things about the owner being quite the jackass from previous employees that have worked here. The food Is mediocre and in my opinion the only good thing about this place are the pastries and drinks. There are many other fantastic places downtown, may I suggest The Mill and Bacchus :).

If you aren't part of their weird "click" the service is lackluster. The drinks are subpar. The "bartenders" aren't the nicest and look at you as though you are bothering them, its very uncomfortable and not a welcoming environment. Coming here felt as though I've stepped back into those terrible high school times that I had tried to forget about lol... Overall I definitely prefer grassroots in downtown St. Petersburg. They are friendly, communicate well and are always willing to help you out when you have questions.

Basically, if you live in the Downtown St Pete area you know not to go here. The food is not great, the only upside is that they're 24/7 and the service I have had has been great as well but... besides that.. not very impressed. St Pete has so many more places to check out for breakfast food. They need to do better.

Absolutely love this place, I live in Downtown St. Pete and drive the 25 minutes to this place on the weekends with my boyfriend. Very creative and fun drinks that are always delicious! They also sell very cute bathing suits and beach gear! I have even bought some of the cute jewelry they have to offer and they are made very well! I really appreciate the covid precautions they take! It is full of tourists around that part so I feel safe knowing everyone is required to social distance and keep their masks on unless sitting at a table. The minute someone leaves an employee is quick to wipe the tables down.  The staff is absolutely lovely and the drinks are killer!

shxYntiDEE2_A_MwIt2yGA.review_text:
Eating here was such a pleasant experience for me. I had the classic, eggs, toast, and bacon, but the service and atmosphere put the meal over the top. My boyfriend had the Hoosier style and said it was delicious. Good food, fun atmosphere, and speedy staff made the wait time bearable. 

I would suggest carpooling on the weekends, it gets a little bit busy in the parking lot. If you don't mind walking park across the street in the neighborhoods and enjoy the walk!

I planned a surprise birthday party at Nada for my boyfriend. I called the staff ahead of time and they were great to work with! They accommodated our party of 8 (it's hard to get larger tables here day of) and they were willing to set half the party early and wait till the birthday boy showed up. The service alone was great, but the food was even better.

The guacamole was FRESH and the salsa platter was a good choice for our group. Everyone was full and loved their meals. I highly advise you to try something new at Nada, they have a very diverse menu and everything looked delicious. Fan favorites included the fish tacos with the hot salsa and splurging for the eggs on top.

This restaurant looks so darn cute and I was thrilled to try it. I decided to go with my roommates for margaritas around 9pm on Cinco De Mayo. When we walked in and the staff told us it would be about 45 minutes to an hour for food, understanding that it was a busy night we weren't too concerned about it and just decided to get drinks with chips and salsa. 

We ordered the cinco de mayo pitcher on special for the night. As the waitress hurriedly brought us our pitcher and glasses we tried to order chips and salsa, but she ran away too fast to hear us. The pitcher gave us about 7-8 drinks and they were the weakest drinks I've ever had. I would put money on it that there was only one shot of tequila in the whole thing. Unfortunately, we didn't even get to order our chips, our waitress didn't come back to our table for the rest of the night until we flagged her down for the bill. Disappointed in the entire experience and even with the fun umbrellas to sit under on the deck I will probably not being going back.

This was a fancy version of noodles and company. The options were better for a more mature pallet, but it was pricy. The food came out fast and it was fresh and filling. No need to get the full bowl unless you are very hungry, it is a lot of food! 

Tried the pasta and piada, the piada was delicious. Pasta was average. 

The Italian soda machine was broken when I visited and this was a big let down.

If you live in Indianapolis and need a cake this is the place to go. They have the small town bakery feel and quality with a good price. 

Great people to work with and they made me exactly what I needed. I will be going back the next time I need a birthday cake!

My boyfriend and I went here for our 1 year anniversary. They remembered that it was our anniversary and gave us each a complimentary glasses of champaign to help us celebrate! It was too cold to sit outside when we went, but the outside patio is a lovely place and will be great on a nice summer evening. The staff was amazing and continually brought us fresh bread and kept our glasses full all night. 

As for food we ordered the shrimp appetizer, it was delicious. Highly comparable to Bonefish Grill's "Bang Bang Shrimp". Shortly after finishing our appetizers both plates came out hot with our entries. I had the shrimp pasta and it was delicious. We both had leftovers to take home and they tasted just as good the next day. I will be going back to try more of their menu, everything looked so good. 

I highly recommend this place for a nice date night, evening with friends, or a place to celebrate any occasion. However, I would not bring kids here, it is too fancy to have little ones running around all the tables.

Burgerhaus is a cute little restaurant on the canal. It's a great location to walk to, especially on a nice summer night. We went to Burgerhaus during burger week. My mom ordered a regular burger and I ordered the burger week burger with a pretzel bun. We shared a side of fries. Both burgers were incredibly filling and splitting a side of fries was more than enough for the two of us. 

The burgers were sub-par on taste, but good on quality and quantity. My burger was in serious need of some form of seasoning, but was cooked well. The pretzel bun was also good, but would have been much better if it wasn't served so cold with the burger. The best part of the meal was the seasoned fries. They were delicious. Also, if you like sweet potatoes be sure to try those fries here, they are great! 

We were seated very quickly, but it took the staff a little while to recognize that we had been seated and even longer to take our orders. The entire staff seemed to be quite stressed out, waitresses were buzzing by left and right with many plates at a time. It was quite hectic, but our meals came out within a reasonable amount of time. 

Overall a decent meal. I wasn't blown away this week, and rarely am by Burgerhaus, but I continue to go back for the consistency, location, and fries.

Met up with old friends and this was the perfect place. The extensive beer menu made sure that everyone could find something they liked. We all tried something different. I got a pear cider, it was light and refreshing, great for the summer. 

My fiancé got the hermanaki wings and said "they were as good as advertised" and that he would 100% get them again. He also got a side of fries which were delicious. 

I had a chicken sandwich with Swiss cheese and teriyaki sauce. It was delicious as well! I had the chips with my sandwich and wish that I would have gotten a different side, they were too oily with minimal flavor. 

Slightly pricy, but the service was good and the food was filling. 

Overall great experience and we're looking forward to going back!

This is a really great place for a quick, tasty, and healthy bite downtown. With a very fresh and contemporary menu it's a great place to go!
I've enjoyed the sandwiches and the salads. Fan favorites are the chicken parm sandwich and the tuna salad. Both are fresh and filling. The locally sourced chips are a must with any meal. 

Eating outside is always lovely on a nice summer night and you can even take a gondola ride after finishing dinner!

I would highly recommend trying the frozen drinks or the s'mores stand for a little dessert. 

Great place for all ages. Must go when visiting the canal.

Great pizza, better people. This is the best pizza you can find in town. They make speciality pizza's and have great options from their menu. You can't go wrong here with anything you order. 

The breadsticks are always hot and fresh. I often times have trouble picking between the marinara sauce and the cheese sauce, but don't worry they'll give you both! 

The soda comes in cans, but you only pay for one and can drink as many as you need. 

Seating is limited but I've never had trouble getting a table when I wanted to eat in.

There is also no delivery fee! What a beautiful thing. 

Recommend this place 100 times over again.

Great place for a causal meal with friends or family. Dawson's has a great diverse menu that has a need for any tastes. 

They have dishes from seafood to steaks to chicken. We had the chicken parm, which was delicious! Also had the pot roast which was good. The pot roast didn't do well reheated, tasted much better fresh. 

The prices are a little on the medium to high end. However, we ALL went home with leftovers and had a second meal. Well worth the "extra" price. 

This was a great place to go to get away from the chain atmosphere that often times plagues the Brownsburg area. We plan to go back to place again and again. Everyone was quite pleased with the meal. 

They also have catering and a banquet hall available for bigger parties. Not a ton of character at this place, but the food makes up for it tenfold.

Owner gave me a giftcard to retry Paida after a disappointing visit. Was very excited to give this place a second chance. 

Went back to Piada for lunch one day. The gift card didn't work and the soda machine was still out of syrup. Very disappointed and won't be going back. 

On the upside the lobster bisque was still tasty!

Really fun place. Food was quite delicious! Went after lunch rush, at 2pm, and it was still packed. Got our food ordered quickly and found a table no problem. 

We ordered a lemonade, bonuts, and the East Nasty. Lemonade was delicious and refreshing! Bonuts were sweet and hit the spot. East Nasty wasn't very hot when brought to the table but taste was good regardless. 

Overall, loved this place and the fun selections of food. Will be going back to try more things on the menu!

Always love grabbing a burger at Bru. Went later at night on a Friday and had a short wait. Got seated fast. Thought it would be too cold to sit outside, but the patio heaters really helped. The music was way too loud, so I asked the waitress to turn it down. She did and I could finally hear my friends! It was lovely.

Everyone got a drink and we shared a platter of fries for a group of four. The portion was perfect and I would highly recommend for big groups, no sense in paying individually for the same amount of fries. I ordered the Melt Your Face Off Burger. Absolutely delicious. I wish I had a better drink to tone down the spicy, but the burger was amazing. I plan to get it again in the future!

On other visits I've also gotten the cheese and hummus tray as an appetizer. This is a must try. Good to share between 2-3 people as an appetizer. 

Great place for double dates, taking your parents, or just having a good burger downtown.

Mimi's is a great place to take your parents, for date night, or have a night out with the girls. Big surprise Mimi's specialize in meatballs, who woulda thought?!?

Anyways, last night was delicious. My mom lives out of town and I wanted to take her to a fun place on Mass Ave. We decided on Mimi's solely because it is fun to mark your menu to take an order. Hello easy decision making! Quick tip, if you order 3 meatballs you have to get all the same sauces and meats, if you get 4 you can mix and match. I love splitting 4 meatballs with a pair to try different combos. 

We ordered a glass of wine, brussels sprout, dirty mashed potatoes, and 4 meatballs to share. The brussels sprout and mashed potatoes were the perfect side dishes for the meatballs. 

In order from least favorite to most favorite here are the meatballs we ordered.
1. Garlic sauce with Turkey meatballs, the garlic wasn't my favorite but the turkey meat was delicious 
2. Sirachi sauce with a regular meatball. This is a classic with my group of friends, but all the other meatballs last night were just too good to compare. 
3. "The Special" this was a pizza themed meatball with all the pizza meats you love in a meatball with marinara. highly recommend. 
4. Buffalo Turkey with Cilantro. Throwing on the spicy buffalo meat with cilantro was such a great idea. I will 100% get this meatball again. 

Anyways, I highly recommend Mimi's and love to go here!

Went to Anderson Orchard with a group. Was very excited to get there and was sorely let down as the day went on. It was way overcrowded and the parking was confusing to me (take that with a grain of salt though, I'm not the best driver). 

I was really looking forward to warm apple cider, but it was too hot that day so they only gave me cold. It was a big let down as well. I also felt that the store was overcrowded and hard to navigate.

The plus sides of the trip, I enjoyed the craft fair and felt that there were many talented people present. I also really enjoyed the pumpkin patch and thought they had very friendly staff helping out in the common store. 

Overall I would go again, but I need to be better prepared for large crowds as well as availability based on the weather. 

Good family activity, but could get pricy quickly.

Flap Jacks is a favorite among co-workers at my company. We love to go here for a consistent, cheap meal during the workday. 

The staff at Flap Jacks is always super friendly and accommodating. The food comes out fast and is reasonably priced. I have never been disappointed when going. 

There's no glamour or glitz to Flap Jacks, but it still holds a very special place in my heart because of it's reliability. 

Highly recommend the Buffalo Chicken Wrap, the Salads, and any of the breakfast food. If you need a good hearty meal Flap Jacks will not let you down.

I want to start this review by saying that McAlister's chain is one of my favorites. I love the food, the prices, and the sweet tea. Although all those wonderful experiences, my visit to this specific McAlister's was terrible. 

I ordered a Ceasar salad, cup of soup, and sweet tea. I got my sweet tea right away, grabbed a pickle and sat down with my friend. We waited about 30 minutes and our food still had not come out. I went up to the front desk and asked why, they responded that they were out of the soup we ordered so they had simply not brought our food. I still cannot understand why the didn't come ask us to pick a different soup, but they didn't. We ordered a different soup and sat down, another 10 minutes go by and no food. Finally I went to the kitchen and asked 3 different people to get the meals out. A 1 hour lunch break was quickly turning into potentially 2 hours. After standing there and watching them prepare our soup and salads they finally brought it to the table and apologized profusely. 

I appreciate that they tried to fix up everything for us and apologize, but that doesn't give me back the 40 minutes that they waited to finally prepare our food. Highly disappointed and I was unhappy how  late I was making it back to the office. I will not be going back to this location.

Louie's Wine Dive. You have my heart. 
Every time I come to Louie's its a great experience. The staff is always upbeat and friendly. They know and understand how to make appropriate wine suggestions and they are always willing to entertain questions. I think the manager has done a great job staffing this restaurant.

Now on to the good stuff, the wine and food. Tonight we got 2 flights, the Pinot Noir and the Champaign plus a glass of white wine. We also share a chess tray...Ordered "the most popular cheeses" and we were brought out a Sharp cheddar, a bruschetta, and a marbled cheese of sorts. All cheeses were high class and flavorful in their own unique ways. The other sides including the Pida and onions were the perfect accompaniment. 

For our main meal each ordered something different. My mom had an Chicken Apple salad that was lick your plate clean good. I had the Diablo, one of my favorites and felt fiery and fully by the end of the dish. My friend also tried to spice noodles.

Louie's doesn't skip on their flight pours or on their spice. Can't wait to go back again.

Really good mall with lots of shops and different options. 

I am only giving 2 stars because the bathrooms and crowds were appalling. I couldn't go to the bathroom because there was not any toilet paper or clean toilets. The crowds were also hard to push through. Lots of people standing in the way as well as too many strollers and mechanized animal 4 wheelers that took up too much space in the walkways. 


Great deals and will go back, but I will 100% use the facilities somewhere else before I go.

Longs is the best bakery in town. There is always a line because the baked goods are just that delicious. Line moves fast and service is always friendly. Make sure you know what you're ordering when it's your turn. Helps the line move faster.

The cake donuts are the best. However all the donuts are good, so you really can't go wrong. 

Quick reminder they are cash only. 

A dozen donuts costs $7.20 

Make sure you leave a little time in your schedule to stop by!

Have been to Punch Bowl Social twice in the past month for work events. The staff did a really great job of working to coordinate the event and make things run smoothly. There were natural bumps along the road (like with any event), but the staff did a really great job alleviating any problems as soon as they could. 
Taco bar was fresh and continuously refilled when it got low. Highly recommend using this option, especially because it is one of their better priced buffet/taco truck items. 
The only problem with both events was the lack of bar service, it is quite difficult to get a drink when at larger events. The bar space isn't designed well and the staff has trouble keeping up with a large flux of people.

I'm a really big fan of quills. They are in a great location for people on the canal or drivers. There is a parking garage in the same building so you never have to worry about finding a spot.

They have really rich coffee, which is much appreciated by me. A good atmosphere, relaxing music and many forms of seating. They seem to bring in pastries from somewhere else,  but they are usually pretty tasty. 

Recommend if you're looking for something quick and simple, not a lot of fluff around here.

Giving it 4 stars because it's nothing over the top or amazing, but still love going here.

Joelle's is a gem. I will be back here sometime very soon. So excited that we found this place.

For our meal we split a half of a chicken and two sides. We also both got a beer. Our check was about $25. Very reasonable for how much food we received.

The chicken was fresh and had an AMAZING flavor. Slight kick but the taste was perfect. For our sides we got mac and cheese and garlic fries. I would get the mac and cheese again, but probably opt for regular fries. 


Incredibly friendly and hospitable staff. The manager brought out our food and he clearly took a lot of pride in the restaurant. 


If you're looking for Nashville hot chicken in Indianapolis this is the place to go. 


Enjoy!

Food was pretty good and came out quickly. We will be back! Chips and salsa were fresh and tasty and they had great margarita and taco specials throughout the week. 

Nothing out of the ordinary and nothing that made the visit poor. Main reasons for 3 stars include water not being filled up during our visit. And my husband ordering the "lunch special" because he pointed to the "lunch" section on the menu. However we were charged for the regular meal. Not a heal deal in the grand scheme of things but still bummed. 

Looking forward to more visits and spending time on the shaded patio.

So good for late night snacks. 

Love the cups (we save them and always use them at my house).

I'm not sure if I have ever had HotBox pizza earlier than 10pm, but every time I eat there it really hits the spot. Very quick service and the staff is quite friendly (especially after dealing with so many drunk people on Georgia street).

All in all, stopping here is always a great idea!

Recently went to Big Lug with a group of friends. We found Big Lug because of location and positive yelp reviews. 

I will 100% be back to Big Lug. They have a really great atmosphere, a great beer menu and even better cheese curds. The backyard outdoor patio is kid and pet friendly. There is a walk-up bar where you can order various drinks and snacks. There is also lots of parking and clean restrooms, what more can a girl ask for?! 

From our group the favorites were the cheese curds, the cider, and the walking taco. Can't wait to go back and try more.

Rick's has become a staple for my family. We save Rick's for special occasions (it is generally a little more expensive than most places I eat). It sits on the water and I am a big fan of sitting on the deck, only down side is getting the sun in your eyes during sunset if you're facing west. 

As a table we share a few appetizers, 2 was plenty for our party of 8. We had the bread with cheese and dips as well as some mushroom dish. It was liked by all! We also all enjoyed a few drinks. We were pleased with the wine selection, rum runners, and canned beer selection. I guess you could say we tried it all. 

For Indiana the seafood is always quite tasty and seems somewhat fresh. We almost all tried the fish of the day that came with veggies and a potato. I also shared the shrimp pasta with my friend. We were both pleased with both. The shrimp were quite large and the pasta cooked just right. The vegetables were seasoned well and didn't need any salt or pepper. 

On the weekends Rick's has live music on the deck which is a lot of fun. Parking can be a little tight or your might have to walk a little to your car, but later in the evening they do offer a small golf cart shuttle that lots of people take.

Big fan of Daredevil Brewing Co.
They have great brews, a fun atmosphere, and good snack options. 

Daredevil is right off of Main Street speedway so it's a great way to start or end a day at the track or even for a quick stop after dinner at one the many delicious restaurants on main street. 

As soon as you walk into Daredevil the yummy brewery smell hits you immediately. The drink lists are plastered throughout the place while listing how hoppy a beer is and alcohol level. They also have the snacks listed throughout. We didn't try any but I'm eager to go back. They were priced well!

After ordering at the counter you can choose to sit inside or outside. I think ordering inside gives you a better chance at having a waitress check up on you (when we visited it was quite hot, so we were the only people outside).


Regardless, really enjoyed this place. Highly recommend sitting outside. They have plenty of picnic tables plus a few games and umbrellas. Looking forward to becoming more of a regular here.

Visited this location for the first time this week. Very pleased with the experience. I have always liked Bru Burger as well as other restaurants owned by the same management group. Happy to see a restaurant in Plainfield that is a little bit different than the standard chains.

My husband and I both ordered a burger with a side of fries. My burger was the Melt Your Face Off burger well done. Thankfully I still have my face, but this burger is quite hot. It's one of my favorite burgers around. The fries are always delicious and the homemade ketchup tops off the meal. 

Our waiter was friendly and attentive. He kept our water glasses full and checked on us multiple times during our meal.

This location is a bit different than the downtown. The wait wasn't nearly as long, we got seated in the bar almost instantly. They also had much more space more to around within the restaurant, I appreciate the fact that all the tables aren't right on top of each other. The parking was also great with some many options around the mall. 


All in all great experience and I can guarantee I'll be back soon!

Went to El Meson for lunch with coworkers. 

Overall good experience. 

Fresh salsa and chips are always my favorite part of Mexican restaurants. They kept both full the entire time. We had 9 people and our dishes were brought out very quickly. 

I had the taco salad with jalapeños, this was on the lunch menu. Most meals were in the $6-$8 range and I felt they were a grey bargain. 


Main reason for 4 stars in inconsistency. Two coworkers order the same meal and got different plates. They were both happy with their meals but it was slightly confusing. 

Overall solid choice if you're on the north side and want a quick hearty bite to eat

I'm very happy with Barbecue and Bourbon!! Only reason for complaints is the small amount of seating. 

We went on a Friday with some friends. While waiting for our seats we all grabbed a drink from the bar. Our waitress was so friendly and helpful. 

I ordered the ribs, French Fries, and green beans. All meal platters come with corn bread. I will be getting the ribs again, they fell off the bone and both the regular and the hot BBQ sauce were a great pairing. The fries were some of the best I've ever had. Crinkle cut and fresh. Will be ordering the fries again as well. 

For drinks we had a frutti tuttie and it was DELICIOUS, and quite potent. The rest of the party ordered a bourbon and lemonade that was refreshing.

Went to The Sutler for drinks and a show. The Sutler was clean and the waitress we worked with was very friendly. The drink specials are the way to go. During happy hour most drinks are 50% off. Very happy with them music, Alyssa Brown was playing when I was there. 

I ordered one of the dessert mugs. I was pleased with the dessert, but not super impressed will probably not order again. My friends enjoyed the cucumber drinks and the whiskey drinks as well. 

The Bathrooms are downstairs and the elevator is not easily accessible. This was especially hard if you had bad knees!

I LOVED Party Fowl. Went here with a big group, they said the wait would be over an hour. So we went next door and had a beer, it was way under an hour wait and the beer made the time go by quickly! 

After sitting down our entire group got very excited about the menu. They had great chicken options, vegetarian options, and some good fish.

I split a half bird and two sided with my husband. Usually we have disagreements about the flavor to get on our chicken. Thank goodness he won the argument this time! I wanted to get the hot chicken flavor and he was nervous. Let me tell you, that Hot Chicken was HOT. We got the sauce on the side and that was a very good decision. Someone ordered the Hot on their wings and couldn't finish them in one sitting. That being said the sauce was amazing. So hot but so full of flavor. I was very happy with the flavors. 

For fun at the end of the meal we ordered the hottest flavor "just to try it". Holy smokes, I've never has my sinuses cleared so much before (p.s. We did get charged $2 for the sample). Again, it was so full of flavor, but even hotter than the hot. 


The sides were also good, but nothing much to highlight. My assumption is that you cannot go wrong with what you order here.


Excited to go back and try more dishes!

This Noodles & Company is great in terms of Noodles locations. They have a very friendly staff which always makes ordering and dining a pleasant experience. The business is clean and kept orderly.

Only down side is the location. The parking can be a nightmare here. It's best if you can get to this location right before the 12 o'clock lunch rush.


My go to order is the Penna Rosa. I've seriously been frequenting noodles since 2010 and have never gotten something different. It's a delicious blend of tomatoes, mushrooms, and spice on top of penne. The protein options are great for anyone, although I usually opt to go without. I also order a sir Caesar salad for a little extra flavor. The sides are priced very well!!

All in all big fan, but like I said the parking is a nightmare.

Hilligoss is the best bakery in town. We recently moved to town and were quite pleased to find this gem right on Main Street. 

The pastries are always made fresh in store. I can attest to this based on the delicious scents you smell the moment the door opens.

Pro tip - If you want fresh treats on the weekend plan to get here early because they sell out quick! They also have coffee and milk if you need something to dunk your donuts in. 

A few of our favorites are the glazed twists and the fruit filled parties. All in all you can't go wrong at Hilligos and they have great prices as well!

Love Metazoa, big fan. The beers are great and I appreciate being able to bring my own food into the bar. I also appreciate the puppies and animals running around. The beers are always rotating so sometimes its a crap shoot as to what they will have on any given day (this is pretty standard for most breweries I've been to though). 

The main reason for the 3 stars, is the overcharging that has happened. More than once I have ordered a beer at a certain price point and been charged over that price. Make sure to check the prices posted and compare that with your receipt! 

Real talk, lots of cute puppies, rabbits and even ponies!! I'm still not thrilled with the "extra charges", but I enjoy the atmosphere and business model. Overall will be back, but will always watch my check.

I am such a huge fan of Metro Diner! We went here for my husbands birthday dinner, truthfully I was skeptical at first. 

We got a table quickly and the waitress was very friendly. She gave the usual recommendations and our table ended up with 2 friend chicken plates, the special, and a tenderloin. 

I had the fried chicken with vegetables and potatoes. It was AMAZING. It was very warm and fresh with really great flavor. They also have a honey hot sauce that is great to dip your chicken in. I had to add a lot more hot sauce to get a good flavor, but that was easy to do. 

After we had our meal we ordered the chocolate cake. It was a good sized slice and the portions were perfect to split 1 piece amongst 2 people. 

Overall, great experience...  I plan to go back and will order everything exactly the same way.

I usually enjoy Hotel Tango, the drinks are generally tasty and creative and I love the popcorn machine. However, there are some distinct flaws that keep me from giving a better review. Before I get into any negatives I also want to mention that some profits go towards supporting veterans and I LOVE that about Hotel Tango. 

Now for "ok" pieces of Hotel Tango. Overall, I find it is difficult to find a place to sit and talk with friends here. There are not a ton of functional seating options and the building is usually quite loud. When there is a band performing it is impossible to talk, let alone hear anyone (or place an order with your waiter). Parking can also be tricky as the lot is small. I would highly encourage walking or ubering to Hotel Tango.

I am a huge fan of Rush on Main. This is a great bar to grab a quick bite to eat, hang out with friends, or go on a date. I usually order the chicken tenders and a seasonale beer when I go to Rush on Main and I'm never disappointed. The breading is very good and the food is always very hot.
I've also heard good things about their sandwhichs and wings, it's hard to go wrong here. 

Fair warning, parking can be difficult around main street Zionsville so there might be a little walking before you get here. Although, it's worth it.

This is also a Cubbies bar!

I am a big fan of Emmy's. We went here off of a friends recommendation and were blown away. I had the chicken fried steak with potatoes and I was quite happy. The portions were huge so I took at least half home and got two meals out of it. They are known for their pancake options and I have to say it was hard to pass up the different fruit and chocolate toppings.

The staff was incredibly friendly and accommodating. The menu had something for everyone. Our food came out quickly but we weren't rushed out the door after we were done. 

Looking forward to making Emmy's a regular spot!

I have been to Cabin Coffee a few different times now. I usually get a Mocha and have also tried their breakfast sandwiches and coffee beans. The mochas are delicious and a great pick me up. 

The last time I ordered a Mocha I asked for no whipped cream and the barista recommended getting a latte with Mocha flavor to save a bit on my order since I did not what the whipped topping. This was greatly appreciated. 

The breakfast sandwich was made fresh and was quite filling. 

Inside there are various different types of seating options from bar stool, table, to booth. They have soft music playing and the store is relatively quiet for a coffee shop. I personally appreciate when a store does not blast out its patrons with loud music. The facilities are also very clean. 

This is a great place to meet a friend, read a book, or get some work done. I will continue going back!

Love the icecream at Fundae's. Lots of good flavors and variety. My favorite is the mint chocolate chip as well as Zanzibar. Highly recommend one of their freshly made waffle cones as well. Fun to grab a cone and walk down Main Street Speedway. 

There are lots of games inside to play as well if you want to sit down and enjoy your time while visiting. 

We have visited during COVID and they had very good social distancing safe precautions to make getting ice-cream safe still.
