Also if you order here your stomach will wrap into a coil and you will feel sick for a day.  I warned you fools.

1.8/5 stars. My brother says try the cheesy bread.

Fascinating name for a restaurant. Somehow describes the feeling you have after eating there.

1.7/5 stars.  My brother says try a turkey wrap.

The spot is nothing special but will satisfy your craving for a burger and fries.  On the positive side the burger is alright and the benches behind the spot are a good place to relax and catch your breath.  I have often found myself back there with a coke looking at the mountains and contemplating my existence.  Am i doing all i can with my life? Should I be trying to help the environment or save victims of sex slave trafficking? 

Staff will usually get your order wrong and put a thousand island dressing on despite me requesting it be removed.  Seriously that crap does not belong on a burger.  Fries have an odd peanut flavored taste though I could see how folks might be into that.

3.1/5 stars.  My brother says try a banana milkshake and I hate bananas

Subway. Do i need to review subway? We have all eaten there.  The food is overprocessed.  I remember reading somewhere that the bread is more paper than wheat or something.  The chicken is this strange rubbery substance.  I have no idea what it is and I have eaten it more times than I would like to admit.

The only way subway is edible is by drowning the sandwich in italian dressing.  For some reason most places do not have this dressing and are therefore inedible.  The wrong chain has won the war for sandwiches and its time it was usurped.

0.2/5 stars. My brother says try the turkey sandwich.

Bit torn on this review.  Their food is a bit greasy. They use too much cheese.  Their burritos are not very good.  Taco tuesday I suppose is pretty great.  Their crunchy chicken or crunchy beef tacos are enormous and pretty tasty.  Salsas are average. Stop using so much cheese.

If they had a bit cleaner place and cut down on the grease this might be a higher score.  As is the crunchy tacos are the only thing worth getting.  Use less cheese.

2.8/5 my brother says try the crunchy beef taco and remove 3/4 of the cheese.

Ah dargans. I want to like you so much.  I love irish bars.  I love irish food.  I love irish music.

Unfortunately you just have an Irish name.  The beer selection is abysmal.  I mean its one of the worst beer selections in all of santa barbara and you are specifically a pub.  I don't get it.  Food is dry and bland.  Kind of like eating a bunch of paper towels, which I do regularly. You don't play any irish music.  Even on St Patricks day it was white girl trash music.

Being in your pub is like when you are anticipating the love of your life to call you.  Your phone rings and you excitedly pick it up, unfortunately it is just someone else that you did not want to speak to.  That is the soul crushing feeling everytime I have when I come back.

0.6/5 stars.  My brother says get an 805

Pricy but good place for small plates and drinks.  Quality food, service, and drinks.  Good atmosphere.  Really good place for a date.  I have had several dates here and when I was inevitably stood up, I still had a great meal. 

3.9/5 stars. My brother says try the octopus.

Wonderful food.  Great wings, steak, chicken, brussel sprouts, whatever you get you know its going to be great.  Its on the pricy side but I think its worth it.  Very good selection of liquor as well if you're into that sort of thing.  Atmosphere is nice.

Only downside is occasionally you get those waiters talking to you like they are making a lifelong friend.  I understand that some places may push this but if were not clicking dont force it.  I dont care how much you know about the wine list, if you grew up on a farm, or where the cauliflower is from.  One time I came here with my girlfriend and we both nearly fell asleep ordering.  

4.6/5 my brother says try the chicken

TUNA CEVICHE. YOU WANT A GOOD CEVICHE GO HERE. GREAT SALSA GREAT CHIP.  

This place seems to have better seafood than chicken or beef.  I highly recommend the crab tacos.  Pretty much everything is on point here and you can't go wrong.  Only thing I would say is get your food without the chipotle sauce or on the side. All of the ingredients stand on their own.  Classic mistake of a restaurant putting an overpowering sauce on something amazing.  

4.5/5 my brother says TRY THE TUNA CEVICHE.

This place has everything you can ask for.  Careless staff, horrendous custom brewed beer, and bad food.  Compounded by the fact that this is really the only true "sports bar" on state street its a real shame.  Id take a movie theater hot dog and a warm keystone over what they serve here.  Like the movie theater hot dog that hasnt been eaten in 3 months and is wrinkled.

0.7/5 stars my brother says try some water and playing shuffle board.

A world class burrito. You would be lucky to ever taste this. I have driven here at 2 am from nearly an hour away to eat here.  Beware the college students they have no sense of wellbeing.

4.6/5 stars. My brother says try the monster chicken burrito.

v0PgIFuRoit2iI4j9ZRyfQ.review_text: Not a single complaint. Quality of food is significantly better than similar restaurants and the service was literally unbelievable. I've never had an employee visit me at my table to thank me for coming and specifically invite me back with a complimentary dessert and free sandwich coupon. Dessert was phenomenal by the way. Only mild criticism would be the corn bread which was quite dry and average. Will go back for sure.

Food still very good for "bar food" but place feels run down now; not as I remember at all. Restaurant was surprisingly empty for a Thursday night with march madness games on. Place doesn't seem managed well. No soap in bathroom, food came out but no utensils, table next to us was dirty and nobody cleaned it during entire meal. Individually these things are no big deal but collectively, you start to notice.
Best sandwiches around. On same level as Primos (arguably better) but none of them nearby. They have made mistakes on orders but more than made up for it both times. Personally suggest the #23.

The bar itself is excellent and a welcome addition to the area. Outside seating and big open windows are great. Drinks are great too. The menu is limited and gets noticeably smaller with each visit. Wings are excellent as are the cheesesteak egg rolls. Have heard others say the place has an identity crisis and I agree. Came with a group of 15 or so to watch the march madness finals and saw they had live music and the game on two tvs while their menu was on the others. We left. Best for happy hours in my opinion.

Always love the food here. Have had just about everything on the menu which is huge. Only things I'd hesitate to order again are the BBQ burger and the cheese steak egg rolls which are too wet and messy for some reason. They put bacon under the burger instead of on top which is odd. Neither are bad- just not as good as other options. Live music on the patio on a nice night is about as good as it gets especially in this area. Worth mentioning that wait times for uber and lyft here are usually quite long.

Very good pizza and very good prices particularly for pizza. Staff is always very friendly. My only complaint is that you can't just stop in and pick up some slices, like you can at Joe's or Cicontes. Plain slices and sometimes pepperoni are all they usually have on demand even at peak times like lunch. But for ordering whole pizzas, definitely recommend.

First, completely agree with other reviewers that the service is terrible. The bartenders are specifically awful, which isn't a great reputation to have as a bar. It's an easy thing to fix for an otherwise great place. Food is good, not great but good and the place is very nice with a great outdoor area. Once came with a party of 8 and were told they were booked that night. Would have been happy to sit at bar for hour or two waiting for a table but the hostess refused to give us a wait time because she couldn't promise a table. Never heard of such a thing. Decent place with bad service, but two stars for potential!!

The new restaurant is beautiful, much improved over the previous location. Food was delicious as it always has been and the service was particular good. Each dining area has a unique design and the secluded booths are the best in the city if you are lucky enough to get one. Didn't care for the trio of sauces that came with the steak; but the rest of the meal was superb. Still the best steak in the city in my opinion.

We enjoyed our time here before a concert next door at the Fillmore. Prices were a bit high but not bad for the area. Beer was $4 and the cheeseburger was $15. The burger was a little disappointing considering the waiter mentioned that's what they were known for. Not bad by any means though. Curly fries were solid. Chicken sandwich and pretzel appetizer all quite good. Service was good and drinks were good and the building itself is great. Very cool place with good views. Was a little slow on a Sunday afternoon but looks like a great place to be at night. Bowling and bar were fun. Enjoyed the atmosphere thoroughly. Would definitely go back.

Easily the best sports bar in the area. Service and prices are very good. Food for the most part is good. However I have to say the "chicken" fingers are awful which is unfortunate because they used to have the best chicken fingers ever made. They used to be large pieces of actual chicken hand breaded. Now they are basically frozen chicken nuggets as you can see in the picture. Do not order the fingers! Fries and mozzarella sticks are solid. Fantasy football drafts of 10+ get free pitcher of beer and appetizer sampler which is great!

Prices for food and drinks are much less than I anticipated- probably due to proximity to college. Speaking of which, this area has come a long way. Great street and setting for the restaurant. The outdoor seating and fire pit is perfect at night. Chicken fingers are average. Fried shrimp are solid and the fries are great as always. Service was particularly good. Parking is easy in the garage across the street.

Thoroughly enjoyed the chicken and pork tacos. Very good value in comparison to other food trucks in the area. High quality meat and ingredients. The peppers and sauces and such on the tacos were delicious. If I have any complaint, it would be more sauce and poblano peppers. First time I liked the chicken better but yesterday I liked the pork better with the lesson being you can't go wrong with either. Finally, the guys working on the food truck were especially nice and happy and proud to be serving people their great food. I assume they were the owners considering the quality of the service. Nice job.

Four stars because I love their food. The grilled cheese is simple but delicious. It is large and delicious and fairly priced. The varieties of the sandwich are excellent too- especially the short rib grilled cheese. I am subtracting a star because their food truck always fails me. The first time they ran out of brioche rolls and put my chicken sandwich on bread which is gross. Then I ordered a grilled cheese and they ran out of bread and asked if putting it on a brioche was okay. Also gross. At least they told me in advance the second time. Lesson being to get in line for food truck early!

Like others said, this place is surprisingly expensive for lunch. I don't mind paying $9-$10 for a wrap if it's worth it but that's not the case here. Food is just okay. My biggest issue as other reviewers have said is the wait time. It takes forever to get your food here. Like mind bogglingly long. I keep giving this place more chances because their is a serious lack of lunch options in the area, but they keep disappointing.

Love the atmosphere. Lighting is cool and the open air feel is great. We sat by the front and enjoyed the breeze and people watching. Very industrial inside. Had a few very minor issues worth noting. They had ran out of silverware which was odd. Waitress told us they didn't serve a scotch which we later saw on the shelf behind the bar- she switched them out no problem. Napkins were not served with our meals. These are basic things that management needs to get in order. But good and drinks were great and reasonably priced. Pizza is very good- I suggest cooking longer for a crispier crust though. Burgers were very good but the meat was frozen. Although it was only $12 so no issue there. Toppings were excellent in spite of the average meat and the fried chicken sandwich was excellent.

Didn't eat here but giving 5 stars for the service. I called on a Saturday night to see if they did call ahead seating and to inquire about wait to eat as we had a show to go to. The manager informed me it quite busy that night as they were having an Oktoberfest event and that eating elsewhere would be a good idea- was more of a bar scene then restaurant scene especially that day. Really appreciated the honesty.

The Chophouse is the best steakhouse in South Jersey, by far. I'd put it head to head with any restaurant in Philly. Absolutely top notch. The Kona crusted sirloin is probably my favorite steak at any restaurant anywhere. With that said, it's very expensive to eat here. But you get what you pay for. Service is fantastic. They have valet and coat check. The Cosmos are and the Caesar salad are notably good too.

I never think to go here for some reason but am usually pretty happy when I do. The service is excellent and the restaurant has a homey feel. Kelly particularly is excellent. I always enjoy the cheeseburgers and chicken sandwiches. The fried shrimp are good here as well. The chicken fingers are just okay- good but not really my style. I prefer more crisp. I would go here for bar food but I don't order entrees.

We come every year for tradition more than anything else at this point. The quality and size of proportion seems to decrease a little bit each year. Even my go to fried shrimp and king crab legs is underwhelming now. They ran out of French fries during my last visit so each meal came with broccoli. I'm still a fan but less so each time I go.

Menu is improving. Mozzarella Lunas are delicious as always. The cheesesteak is better than I remember and the wings are also better than I remember. Service was especially good. Seat yourself in Bar area is nice too.  I find the actual dining rooms dated and unappealing.

Good news and bad news. I used to hate this place but they have come a long way. Menu is constantly improving. Cheesesteak is excellent and the fries are solid too. My beef is with the cheeseburger sliders. They used to be great with an excellent sauce. Now they are dry and gross (as you can see in the picture) Cheese is minimal and the bun to meat ratio is off.. like way off.

I love this restaurant. It's a nice alternative to the usual pizzeria type places in this area. The food is simple, yet delicious. The shrimp rolls and the grilled chicken dishes are excellent. The meals are a little pricey- $10-$11 for grilled chicken and vermicelli noodles, but i still buy anyway. Could do without the salads that come with the meals.

This place came through for us after the Eagles paraded. Was the perfect spot to go for some beers after the champs went down Broad. Atmosphere is excellent. The bar is cozy and the drinks are priced right. Service is friendly. Exactly what I think of when I picture a south philly bar. Oh and charging only $3.50 for a 16 oz Miller Lite that people would have paid double for on that day was a good look.

Big fan of this place. They have the best sugar cookies and butter cake. (Although the butter cake starts getting stale within hours so eat it fast) They are always so nice; gave a cookie to my daughter today while we waited in line. Most importantly, I just leaned they make breakfast sandwiches on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. They are excellent and come with western potatoes and a croissant. You can see one half of a breakfast sandwich in my picture. All of this for just $6.99. A very good value considering their normal bakery items are a bit expensive - but worth it.

General Tso chicken is pretty good. Not amazing by any means but pretty good. I was hoping it would be better for $12 so I probably won't get it again. Like most places, there were some solid bites and some questionable bites. I look forward to trying other dishes though. Broccoli and rice were very good and the place is very nice inside. Updating my review to mention the sweet and sour chicken was bad and the sesame chicken was excellent (imo). I have also had several sushi dishes and all have been solid.

I like this place. All of the food taste good and is reasonably priced. It's a step up in food quality from usual chains like Cheesecake Factory and such. The menu is very large with some creative items. I've never had anything bad there, but I've also never had anything great. Everything is consistently good, which is fine with me. The atmosphere is excellent as is the bread. I dislike that they don't have reservations and the service has been hit or miss in my experience.

Great place to go for lunch. Lots of options up front and their lunch specials are great and change frequently. Much nicer restaurant to eat inside than your typical pizza place. My only complaint in the frequent bait and switch. There will be a fresh pizza up front, but when you order, you see that you're actually getting a slice from a much older previously cooked pizza behind the counter. Sometimes you must toss stale food in this business. Cicontes however does not do this. Other than that, highly recommend!

The best restaurant in the area by far. The renovations are incredible and the outdoor seating is perfect. Happy hours are until 6:30 and are very good. Everything I get there is fantastic. Only exception are buffalo shrimp which are just okay. You get a lot of them but they are small; not my style. Wife loves the cheesesteak egg rolls. Shrimp vestito is my favorite. Bread and peppers are fantastic too. Pizzas during happy hour are a steal. $6 delicious and good size.

Chicken tenders were incredible; maybe best I've ever had. They were more like chicken cutlets, definitely hand made. I typically don't like those thin fries but they actually weren't bad here. Everyone else raved about their short rib and prime rib sandwiches. Look forward to going back. Prices very reasonable!

We were golfing nearby and stopped in here despite the average reviews. There just weren't many other options in the area. We thought the place was great, sat outside on the second floor, loved the service and loved the food. We ordered sandwiches and appetizers so can't speak on the entrees but the burgers, pork sandwich, and buffalo rolls were all quite good. The whiskey was even better!

Ate here while golfing and really enjoyed it. Drinks are extremely reasonably priced. We got beers to go while golfing and they were only $3 each which is unheard of. And they put them in a cooler bag with ice! We enjoyed the buffalo chicken bites and cheesesteak pot stickers. The atmosphere here inside is underwhelming but the patio outside is nice.

One of the best breakfast sandwiches I've ever had although I think it would have been even better with a different cheese, even American. Croissant was incredible. Minus one star because the guy behind the counter used his bare hands to fill my cup with Ice. Gross.

The percentage of simple orders they get wrong is staggering. It's laughable at this point. You order two plain bagels and don't bother checking the bag because it should be impossible to get wrong, but sure enough you get home and see two plain donuts and it's not worth the time or money to drive back. So frustrating. The convenience of the drive thru isn't worth it anymore. I just go across the street to Heritages now.

5 stars for having the best chicken around. Delicious chicken tenders and chicken sandwiches. Pretty much everything is good here although the burgers are very average and the lobster beignets are flat out bad. Folks who answer the phone are very nice every time too. Highly recommend!

v12_ycZ0eSjtkirSWuON5w.review_text:
For some reason, it took me a whole year of living at 39th and Locust to go to Troy. I am sad I missed out for that whole year!

The first time I went to Troy, I had the lahmacun (pronouced lahmajun). This is a common Turkish food, which many people call "Turkish Pizza." It is a flat bread covered with ground meat, spices, lettuce, and tomato. It is only $3 at Troy. I had a ton of lahmacun while I was in Turkey for four months, and they were always very large. So I was expecting this one to be large too and I was thinking that I would be getting a great deal. But it turned out to be incredibly small. It was very delicious though! While it is not large enough to be a whole meal, it makes a great appetizer or snack!

The next time I went to Troy, I had the chicken wrap. Oh man, it was amazing! The meat was SO flavorful. So, now I just always stick with the chicken wrap.

Definitely a great place to go for anyone in the area. The man who owns it is from Istanbul and is very friendly.

Okay so...I am obsessed with Underdogs. It is hard to explain really, but they are just great. 

I went for the first time about a year and a half ago. I have never been disappointed. There are SO many funky and unique hotdogs. My absolute favorite is "The Tryp," which is Turkey Sausage with stuffing, gravy, and cranberry sauce. YUMMM. I also really like "The Adonis," which is lamb sausage with lettuce, tomato, onions, and tzatziki. Even just these two examples should give you a picture of how fun the hotdogs at Underdogs are. 

I have tried about seven or eight of the hotdogs. If you try all of them (there are 23), you get your name on the wall! That is my dream :)

This place isn't for the pretentious eater. It is just for people who love trying fun, interesting, casual foods.

If you are in the University City area in the morning, you can't go wrong with Metropolitan for breakfast. 

All of the breakfast sandwiches are delicious. I especially like the South Philly Slammer sandwich. Most of the sandwiches are around $7. Metropolitan also has other breakfast items like oatmeal, pastries, etc. 

The main problem with Metropolitan is that the service is INCREDIBLY slow. The line to order moves slowly, and it takes them forever to prepare the food considering that the food is pretty simple. Also, the restaurant is pretty small. If you go on a weekend morning, it may be hard to find a table because the place is brimming with Penn students.

I seriously do not understand why my friends always rave about Tampopo. I grew up on Japanese food. And let me tell you, this is not Japanese food. I would give it 2.5 stars.

I have a had a number of dishes at Tampopo because I somehow get dragged there by others. They are all sub-par. The ramen is probably the worst ramen I have gotten at a restaurant. The curry bowl and chicken katsu bowl are also not that great (they are not terrible though). People seem to love the bibimbap, but I really didn't care for it.

The main appeal for me of Tampopo is that it is affordable and offers good value. Also, it is right next to Little Pop Shop, so you can pop in there for a nice little dessert.

I had a wonderful dinner at El Rey tonight! 

The atmosphere is very funky and casual. The outside is made to look like an old movie theater and the walls on the inside are covered in old Mexican movie posters. Service was prompt and friendly. 

The food is extremely affordable for the quality. I had the short rib enchilada, which was $9.75. My friend had the zucchini and corn Quesadilla, which was $7.50. Both of these dishes were delicious. We also split the chips and salsa for $4. This was good too, but I think they just gave you complementary chips and salsa. The margaritas were $8. I really want to come for happy hour because then the margaritas are only $4! Also, they have $1 tacos during happy hour. 

This is restaurant is great for both friends having a fun night and for couples going on dates.

To be honest, when HipCityVeg first opened, I thought I would never go there. As a meat-lover, I didn't think I would enjoy eating vegetarian food. And I especially thought that the idea of fake meat was strange. 

But I actually really like HipCityVeg. Generally, I go to HipCityVeg when I need a quick meal that won't put me in a food coma. The Udon Noodle Salad is my favorite menu item, though most of the food is pretty good. The desserts and drinks are also really good. The banana whip is delicious. And surprisingly, I found that I like the fake chicken here. 

The main problem I have with HipCityVeg is that it is pretty pricy. I can see how they get away with it because they serve a niche group of customers and make it seem like the ingredients are higher quality than at other places. But $9 for a tiny salad is a bit much.

Why did I only go to Dock Street for the first time last week!?!?! I have been missing out!

The food and beer here were amazing! I had the sausage pizza, and it was seriously the best pizza I have had in Philly. The beer was also amazing. There are about six or seven beers on the menu. I tried a few of them, and they were all great.

The atmosphere was very hip in a laid-back, off-the-beaten-path kind of way. Definitely a great place to just chill with a few friends in the evening. I will 100% be going back to Dock Street!

The ramen at Ramen Bar is only alright. It is the best ramen in the area, but that is not saying much.

I usually get the Miso Ramen. It tastes fine, but I think that is just because they put so much butter in the broth. When they give you your ramen, you can still see the slabs of butter in it that haven't completely melted yet. Kinda gross...

The restaurant design and atmosphere are nice. It is nice just for a quiet, laid-back dinner with friends. The happy hour specials sound pretty good, but I have never gone for happy hour. I am not sure that the atmosphere is really conducive to having a good happy hour.

A few of my friends and I go to Han Dynasty all the time. Every time we make plans with each other, we all pretend to think about other places to eat. But in the end we always go to Han Dynasty. 

I really love the food at Han Dynasty. But just as a warning, be prepared to go into a food coma after eating here because the food is really oily. My personal favorites are the Dan Dan Noodles and Eggplant with Garlic Sauce. The food is pretty spicy. Each dish comes with a spice rating from 1-10. But if you can't handle too much spice, you can ask them to tone the spice down to a lower number. 

If you have a big party, you can get a table in the back that has a Lazy Susan on it. The tables in the back are also semi-private. 

Waiters are always prompt and friendly. Ambiance is casual. Over, just a great place for lunch or dinner with friends.

Cuba Libre's brunch is one of the best things to exist ever. $26 for unlimited delicious food!? That just cannot be beaten. You are allowed to pick as many items from the brunch menu as you would like. The menus for brunch and dinner have many of the same dishes. All of the menu items are tapas that cost around $8. So it is pretty easy to get your money's worth at brunch. My favorite dish is the Guacamole Cubano. They say to do the unlimited options, everyone in your party must do it. But if you ask reeeeeally nicely, they will let you get away with only some people doing it.

I have also been to Cuba Libre for dinner during restaurant week. But the unlimited brunch in a much better deal. $26 for unlimited food compared to $35 for limited food. I think the better choice is pretty clear.

Came here with five friends after checking out the art galleries at First Friday. It was a good place to just chill with friends.

We each got a "small dish," such as the baked Brie or Mac n cheese. The Mac and cheese was good but was nothing special. My friends said the baked Brie was amazing. 

We all checked in on yelp to get a buy-one-get-one-free deal for beers. Most of the beers were $6. So $6 for two beers was great.

Overall, I had a good experience here. But it was nothing extraordinary.

Arabian Breeze is one of my go-to places for delivery. I think the food is delicious. I usually get the Chicken Tikka Masala or the Lamb Paratha Roll. The food is a bit heavy and oily, so I get kind of sleepy after eating it. 

A great thing about Arabian Breeze is that it is open until midnight. So it is great for late night food cravings. 

I have never actually been to the restaurant. But I would definitely recommend it for those nights when you just don't want to leave your home!

White Dog is a great place for brunch in University City. I would definitely recommend going to White Dog for brunch rather than dinner because the dinner items are a lot more pricey.

For brunch, I usually get the Eggs Benedict. But I have also tried the omelet, turkey sandwich, and more. Everything I have had for brunch has been good. The menu items change slightly sometimes because they source their food from local farms.

For Penn students, this is a great place to go with your parents when they are in town. It is also just good for brunch with some friends. If you are looking to day-drink, they offer bottomless drinks for $12 during brunch on the weekends.

There is no great ramen in Philly. But I did think Nom Nom was pretty good.

This new University City location is a bit hidden. It is inside the small food court next to the CVS at Walnut and 34th. 

The Pork Belly ramen is just under $10. It feels strange to pay $10 for food court ramen. But there is not any cheaper ramen around.

The broth of the ramen was only okay. But the pork was amazing. It was so tender and flavorful. It was especially great compared to the pork at Ramen Bar. At Ramen Bar, the "pork" is basically just fat. The pork at Nom Nom was actually meat and very delicious. 

I would recommend Nom Nom if you are in the area. But don't go out of your way to go there.

Bistro La Baia is my least favorite restaurant in the history of ever. Seriously. I have never been to a restaurant with such terrible service and such a rude staff.

When we entered Bistro La Baia, we were standing in the area between the door and the hostess stand, which is about 1 square foot wide. Because there wasn't much space some of the people in my party were standing in the doorway with the door open. The hostess (who I think is also the co-owner), aggressively demanded that we close the door. The entire staff spoke rudely to us the whole evening. 

Our party of 10 was seated in a space that should really have been for 4 people. I was so cramped and uncomfortable during my meal. When I tried to go to the bathroom, it took eons because the walkways are so skinny that only one person can pass through at a time. When I was walking back to my seat from the bathroom, a waiter was trying to get through from behind me and actually pushed me out of the way to barge through.

We raised our concerns to the owner, who proceeded to scream at us. TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE. 

I've read through a bunch of the Yelp reviews, and my experience is definitely not unique. Countless other people have reported the exact same rudeness and terrible customer service.

The food was fine. Wasn't bad, but was nothing too memorable.

I have ordered delivery from Sakura a few times. It is not horrible, but is not that good.

The most disappointing item I have ordered is the vegetable tempura. I don't think that their tempura could even be classified as tempura! Tempura batter is supposed to be light and flaky. But this tempura had a heavy, thick coat that was really gross. I did like the gyoza I ordered once though.

I don't think I will be ordering delivery from Sakura much in the future. I may occasionally order though because I sometimes need to break out of my usual places to order-in from.

Okay, so it is not like Greek Lady has amazing food. But it is pretty good and you get good value for your money. If you are in the University City area and need a casual, affordable breakfast, Greek Lady is great.

My favorite dish is at Greek Lady is the Greek Omelet. It is an omelet with feta cheese, spinach, and tomatoes. All of the omelets come with home fries or fruit. I usually get the home fries. The fruit they give you is mostly melon-type fruit, which I don't really like. I also really like getting a gyro if I need a quick dinner. The best value on the menu for sure is the salads. They are HUGE. And that means something coming from me. 

Overall, definitely don't go more than a few blocks out of your way to come here. But it is really convenient and great if you are in the area.

Going to Amada for Restaurant Week was one of the best decisions ever. When we arrived, the waitress asked if we had been there before. When we said "no," she seemed shocked. I now understand why. How could I have never gone there before?? I had been missing out.

My favorite item was the manchego cheese dish. It came with honey and and bread. But the honey wasn't normal honey, it had spices in it! The Escalivada was also wonderful. It was bread with eggplant and red pepper spreads. The only disappointment was that the chicken in the chicken and romaine salad was a bit dry. Other than that, everything was DELICIOUS!

I can't wait to go back to Amada. If you haven't been there yet, go!!

Yogorino is hands-down my favorite frozen yogurt place. 

The frozen yogurt is creamy, but not too creamy. And it is not grainy like a lot of frozen yogurt. There are a plethora of toppings, ranging from syrups to fruit to candy. I usually get the dark chocolate syrup. I took a few friends from Baltimore to Yogorino the other day, and they were seriously amazed at how delicious it is. 

I have never tried the ice cream here (the yogurt is too good to try anything else!), but I imagine it is good.

My only complaint is that you only get one topping with your yogurt. You can pay for additional toppings, but I feel like they could include at least two toppings with the base charge.

Hemo's is a classic on Penn's campus. Hemo's serves delicious, affordable sandwiches that make for a great breakfast or lunch.

For breakfast, I usually get the bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich. The quality of bacon at Hemo's is better than at other food carts. The cheese is always perfectly melted. For lunch, I usually get the grilled chicken sandwich with spinach and tomatoes, which is also good. 

I would definitely recommend getting food from Hemo's if you are in the area. The food is simple but good. Most sandwiches are about $3, which is awesome.

The amount of Federal Donuts that I have eaten recently is out of control. Not that I am complaining about this..Every time I organize a student event at Penn, I order Federal Donuts for it. A dozen "Hot & Fresh" donuts are only $11! Then when there are some left over, I take them home and eat them for the next few days.

My favorite donuts are the cinnamon Hot & Fresh donuts. When you bite into the warm dough coated in cinnamon, it is just wonderful. I thought I would like the chocolate peanut butter donuts the best, but strangely they weren't as great. The third type of Hot & Fresh donut is orange flavored, which I don't really care for. I have also tried a bunch of different "Fancy" donuts, which are good, but I prefer the cinnamon Hot & Fresh donuts. 

This new West Philly location is super clean and bright. (I have been to other Federal donuts that I cannot say the same about.) The staff is always friendly.

I definitely recommend Federal Donuts! I mean, how can you go wrong with donuts and friend chicken?? Well, besides in terms of cardiac health...

I have only been to Barbuzzo once, but I really enjoyed it.

I went in early October when it was still warm out. We were seated by the giant open windows, which was really nice. 

We had a smattering of different dishes since Barbuzzo is tapa-style. My favorite dish was the Pan Seared Brussels Sprouts. I usually don't eat brussels sprouts because, for some reason, they don't sound very appealing in my mind. But they were great! The flavor on them was delicate, but delicious. And they were cooked wonderfully. The Salted Caramel Budino, which Barbuzzo is known for, was great. The mix of sweet flavors in it was amazing and every bite just melted into my taste buds. 

My only problem with Barbuzzo is the fact that it is tapa-style. I think I have an inherent problem with tapas places because I pay so much money for such tiny dishes, and my total spend comes out to way more than it would at a normal restaurant.

Shane's is the oldest candy store in America, so they have really perfected the candy business. 

The store is totally old-school, with many of the original features of the store still there.  One of the employees told us that even the candy jars and cases are original. 

Because it is the fall, Shane's had many seasonal candies when I went. I can't remember exactly which ones I got, but they were all delicious. They were all chocolate coated candies of different flavors. 

I heard that in late 2014, Shane's will be opening up a chocolate cafe in the back of the store. I really want to go back once that opens to enjoy a nice hot chocolate :)

I went to Supper for the first time two nights ago, and really enjoyed myself. 

We started with a couple bottles of wine, which was nice. I then had the Supper Burger. It was $19, which is expensive for a burger, but it was HUGE (10 ounces)! It came with three types of sauces: chipotle aioli, mustard, and thousand island. I kept rotating between the three sauces because they were all good, but the thousand island was my favorite. The burger was really succulent, and all of the toppings on it (caramelized onions, ham, cooked tomato) were awesome. It was a bit of a challenge to eat because it was so big. The duck fat fries that came with it were also amazing. 

The restaurant itself was really nice. It was small, but we were not cramped at all. I was there with a bunch of friends for a birthday, but Supper would also be a great spot for a date.

I always hear people I know saying that they don't really care for Chattime. But I liked it! 

When I walked up to the restaurant, I was shocked. I was expecting a small, unassuming place. But the restaurant was very large and had funky purple lighting. 

I had the Japanese Roasted Pork Noodle Soup. I had the option of hand-drawn noodles or shaved noodles, and went with hand-drawn noodles. I really enjoyed this dish. The noodles were just the right softness, the broth was super flavorful, and the pork was tasty. I also had the "Jelly wow milk." I don't exactly know what that means (lol I just kind of picked it at random from the Special Drink List), but it was really good. It was a milk bubble tea, but with jelly and some other squishy thing instead of the boba/bubbles. 

Considering the less than enthusiastic reviews on Yelp and that I hear around campus, my guess is that the food items are really hit or miss. But the noodle soup I had was good, so I recommend that. I will definitely be back to Chattime in the future.

Zesto is a great new pizza place that just opened near Penn's campus.

I had the White Margherita Pizza, which was really good. It was $10 for the small pizza, which lasted me two meals (and I eat a lot). Zesto also has hoagies, wraps, paninis, calzones, pasta, and more. 

Zesto's pizza is wayyy tastier than the pizza at any other place around campus (I'm looking at you, Allegros). It is open until 3am on Fridays and Saturdays, so I think it will become a popular option for late night munchies amongst Penn students.

Jake's Sandwich Board just opened right off of Penn's campus.

Jake's has a wide variety of menu options. You can choose to get your meal as a sandwich or as a bowl. There is a menu, or you can design your own. They have turkey, beef, pork, and veggies options.

I went with the "Classic Pork" sandwich for $8.50, which was pork, broccoli rabe, and provolone cheese. It was very tasty; the cheese was especially flavorful. It was also very filling. It should be noted that this sandwich was one of the cheapest ones on the menu.

The restaurant itself is nice. It is very casual and clean. You order at the counter and then can take any seat you want or take your meal to go. Jake's is a good place for a casual lunch with friends between classes or on the weekend.

I have been to Aya's cafe twice and loved it both times.

The first time I went was with about 20 other people for a friend's birthday BYO. I think Aya's is normally a place for a more intimate meal and isn't used to such large groups, but all of the employees were very accommodating and kind to us. Everyone loved their food. I had the moussaka, which was so so tasty. 

The second time I went was with four others for a BYO. We went on a Thursday night. The place was very quiet, with just a few other groups there. The moussaka was so good the first time that I got it again. The four others I went with loved their kofta, kebab, and ravioli dishes. They kept complimenting me on my great restaurant selection :)

I 100% recommend having dinner at Aya's. It is a great place for dinner with a few friends or a date. Bring along a bottle of wine since it is BYO.

I think it's about time that I write a review for Sweetgreen seeing as I go there about twice a week. 

Obviously, I like Sweetgreen a lot since I go there so often. I've never had salads that are as good as Sweetgreen salads. The ingredients are just SO fresh and delicious. I also really like eating salads from Sweetgreen because I don't fall into a food coma after eating them. 

I always get the Kale Caesar (Kale, romaine, parmesan, tomatoes, chicken, parmesan crisps, lime squeeze...SO YUMMY), which is $9.45 with tax. So, you can see that Sweetgreen is a bit expensive, especially considering that the Kale Caesar is one of the cheapest salads on the menu. 

The main problem I have with Sweetgreen is the lack of consistency. Depending on who makes your salad, it can come out really differently. For example, they always ask you "Light, medium, or heavy?" for your dressing, but each employee defines those levels differently. 

But overall, I love Sweetgreen. Even if you think you don't like salad, Sweetgreen can probably make you a convert.

I order delivery from Pattaya all the time and sit-down to eat at the restaurant about once every month and a half. 

I love Thai food. I am pretty much always get the Chicken Drunken Noodles at Pattaya, which are extremely tasty and very filling. Pattaya's curries and pad thai are also really good. Pattaya has a good lunch special for $10 where you get an entree and appetizer.

Pattaya's service is great. A large reason that I order delivery from Pattaya so often is that the food comes super quickly. The staff is also friendly and nice.

Overall, I definitely recommend Pattaya. Don't come all the way to University City just for Pattaya, but if you are in the area, it is a great choice for lunch or dinner!

Erawan is a great Thai restaurant. I have been there twice now, and enjoyed myself both times!

The food is tasty and reliable. Every person I have gone with liked their food. I get the Chicken Drunken Noodles (as I usually get at Thai restaurants), and they were warm and flavorful. 

Both times I went to Erawan were for BYOs. The place can be a bit loud because of all the young people BYOing. But I would describe it as lively and not overwhelming. The staff is quick and courteous. 

I definitely recommend Erawan for an enjoyable dinner or BYO. Be sure to check in on Yelp to get a free appetizer!!

Thai Singha is back! I've been a long time fan of Thai Singha, and was so sad when it closed about a year and a half ago. But now it is back, and I couldn't be more excited. It moved to a location just down the street from the original location. The decor and ambiance are brighter and livelier, the food is still delicious, and it is now BYO! 

I prefer Thai Singha over Pattaya, which is just down the street. At Thai Singha, the specials are better and the food has more flavor. I highly recommend having dinner at Thai Singha if you are looking for a casual, enjoyable dinner with yummy Thai food.

Hai Street is a good new addition to the University City food scene. 

Hai Street is known for its "Sushirritos." If you ask me, there is nothing burrito-like about them except for their size and they are not very sushi like either. They are kinda like giant sushi, but with very non-traditional sushi ingredients.

I've have tried a few of the rolls from the menu, and my favorite was the Hai Street Chicken. The chicken katsu and green papaya salad in it were delicious. You can also make your own roll if none of the pre-determined ones on the menu sound good to you. You can also get your meal as a bowl instead of a roll if you wish. 

My real qualm with Hai Street is that I am never very full after eating there. The sushirritos look huge, but they are actually not that big or filling. I have overheard multiple people in the restaurant saying, "I am actually still kinda hungry..." after eating their sushirritos. 

Overall, the food is tasty and a modern take on sushi. Since it is not too filling, it is good to eat when you need a boost but do not want to be weighed down with food.
