UPON ARRIVAL:  As soon as my friends and I stepped in to this place, we began to think we were in the show "Hidden Camera."  There was water dripping from the ceiling onto the tables and down our legs.  When we asked to move, the waiter said "well that's how these buildings are."   The front door was stuck so I actually had to get up to push it open for people trying to enter.  
ORDERING AND FOOD:  We were not able to order tap water; the waiter actually told me they didn't have a tap.  I asked him "how do you wash your dishes?"  We politely told him that we were in a hurry and ordered only salads and appetizers.  The shrimp cocktail never came, half the drinks were never delivered, we were charged for drinks we never received and for drinks we didn't even order.   When orders arrived that were WRONG and my friends politely asked him for a different order, he told us that "the manager was going to go ape-sh*t" and that when other people complained "he came running out of the back and told them to 'get the f*ck out!'" 
TRYING TO LEAVE:  We repeatedly tried to ask the waiter for our bill so we could make it to our vampire tour on time.  He ignored us.  Even though we didn't want to, we decided to leave a tip just because we are nice people.  We repeatedly asked him to break up a large bill so we would have change to leave him, and he stood there and responded "well actually right now I'm trying to find a lighter so I can smoke with my friend."

There is still part of me that believes that this experience MUST have been on Hidden Camera, because this is the WORST experience I've EVER had at a restaurant.  It was so bad that it became a joke and one of our funniest experiences while on vacation in New Orleans.

I dream of Meltdown coming to Chicago!! 
This place delivers the best popsicles your mouth will ever encounter!
The owner is a very nice girl who I ended up chatting with for nearly 30 minutes.... she told us about starting her business, what restaurants to check out, and where to go in NOLA.  
The businesses around her also were fans- about 3 other shopkeepers had directed us to go there.  I wish I would have discovered this place the first day I was there- there would have been popsicles for breakfast, lunch, and dinner!

I recommend the Salted Caramel.  Yum yum YUM!

LOCATION: Convenient spot right across from Jax Brewery in the French Quarter.

SERVICE: Super nice waitstaff, very personable.  They made me genuinely smile.  Originally we went in for drinks.  We left to watch the 4th of July fireworks on the river and came back for a late night bite to eat because we were so impressed earlier.

CLEANLINESS: Very clean!

PRICE: Not too bad!  Pretty affordable and great bang for the buck.

FOOD: I thought the food was great!  

Corn and crab bisque: (Yum!) I love corn and crab bisque, and try to order it at every New Orleans restaurant when I see it!  I was very impressed by the consistency and by the fact that I never bit into a hard bit of crab shell (something I've experienced quite often!)

Margherita pizza: (Great for a light lunch or evening snack)  The pizzas are big enough for 2-3 people to share (6 decent sized pieces).  The crust was cooked perfectly and was crispy and light.  There was just the right amount of cheese, olive oil, tomatoes, and basil.

Jambalaya: (Favorite so far!)  Until now I didn't understand the big deal about jambalaya.  Now I be wrong because I'm not a true New Orleanian but I thought it was great! Thicker consistency, great flavor, no spice overkill.  Loved it!

FINAL VERDICT: Go there!

SERVICE: Friendly enough!  This is the ONLY reason I gave it 2 stars instead of 1.

ATMOSPHERE:  Cute- adds to false sense of goodness.

PRICE:  WAY overpriced for what you get.

FOOD:  Very disappointing.  From the looks of the cafe, you get excited and think "this is going to be good."  This was a big letdown.

*BLT- Definitely not what was expected.  The bacon is battered and deep-fried!  Ends up tasting like gobs of deep-fried salty fat.  The bread is of your typical white bread loaf variety.

*Grilled cheese- For $7, I expected a decent grilled cheese.  Instead, I got 2 white bread slices and what looked like melted processed cheese.  Don't forget the bag of chips.  What a letdown.

FINAL VERDICT:  Pass this place up.

This welcoming cafe, located in the convenient Bywyater neighborhood with easy street parking, is a welcoming escape from fried food and cajun spices (although I absolutely love it, sometimes we all just need a break!)

What I love: the funky, unforced bohemian vibe, the fact that they use local bakeries and farmer's markets to buy supplies, the paintings.

Love the turkey sandwich on ciabetta!  The bread is fresh and the crust isn't uncomfortably "rough" as some ciabetta rolls are.  It literally melts in your mouth: crispy crust and soft, porous flesh.  The avocado mash, spicy mustard, ailoli, and thanksgiving-style turkey chunks are refreshing and satisfying.  Compliment it with a watermelon lemonade- a true flavor explosion in your mouth.  

Come here to do schoolwork, visit with friends, or just watch the daily summer monsoon roll through.  You won't be disappointed!

Three words: Goat Cheese Croquettes.  Seriously life changing.

What is better than goat cheese croquettes drizzled with a warm honey sauce and carmelized onions?  Exactly.  Nothing.

Paired up with some wine and some good tunes in the upstairs bar and you've got yourself a great night out!

PARKING- A quick trip up to Mid-City; between the small parking lot and the street off of Iberville, there is always a place to drop your car- which is great, considering you are probably recovering from a night of festivities and you don't want to walk too far.

COST- Typical po-boy price points, averaging around $7.

WHAT I EAT: The roast beef is amazing.  The bread is always soft in the right spots (Leidenheimer), the beef is shredded, and it's always dressed in just enough clothes!    I love the sweet potato fries, but they have been a bit too overcooked at times (this explains the 4 instead of 5).  I also enjoy the mustard-y potato salad.

LEVEL OF MESSINESS: On a scale of 1-10, 10 being you should wear a baby bib and then hose off outside, I would give Yang's a proper 10.  After folding up the four sides of your paper, you will realize it won't matter after a puddle of juicy deliciousness pools on the table underneath the mess.  My advice is to keep on eating, let the mayo and gravy decorate your face, and worry about cleaning up after!

LENGTH OF TIME SPENT SUFFERING IN LINE: 5 minutes, tops!  If you are starving and don't want to deal with long lines at some other nearby hot spots, like Parkway, you probably won't regret coming to Yang's (especially if your po-boy of choice is a roast beef).

ATMOSPHERE: Great people work there; always friendly and smiling.  The TV's playing the news or some trashy talk show are sometimes a bit much (again explains the 4 instead of 5), but if you feel like spacing out and catching up with some headlines while you dig in, it's not so bad.

After you eat your fill of fantastic dogs down at Dat Dog, head over here for dessert! Or as hangover treatment...or a summer treat...

Best snoball place, hands down!

The ice melts in your mouth (no pun intended) and the juices are so fresh, they instantly make you feel refreshed and healthier!

The watermelon is the BEST.  So good, so refreshing, so satisfying!!

Parking is pretty easy along Freret St. most of the time.

So head over there.  NOW.

Buffa's is the perfect little neighborhood dive!  Great people watching and laid back atmosphere.  Type of place where you could easily go solo; someone would quickly strike up a conversation or be happy to leave you alone.

I like that it is never is too crowded or overtaken by tourists (not a bad thing for business, but sometimes you just want your "me" time).  I appreciate the fact that Bonnie will give you a kiss and a hug as she calls you Baby, remembering the conversation she had with you quite some time ago.  

Dog friendly! 

The Shrimp Creole was pretty good, served up with french bread (perfect blend of soft, crunchy, chewy) and packed quite a blast of heat.  At $13, I did think it was a bit too pricey.

The corn nuggets are AWESOME.  If you like corn, get the corn nuggets.

Thanks Buffa's, for being you!

Soft and fresh tasting! Just enough sweetness, just enough cinnamon.  Ooey-gooey goodness.  

It survived, and flourished, after many hours on neutral ground.

Well done, Manny!

Ice is shaved down into fine sandlike particles. The cream of chocolate is awesome! Kind of tastes like a Wendy's Frosty.

One of the best snoball shops in New Orleans! 

Easy street parking.

I REALLY want to give this place a 5 because my ice cream (southern praline) was AMAZING, and the staff was very nice, BUT...

Why aren't there more flavors of ice cream? Not even caramel? How about caramel with chocolate covered pretzels? Yum.....

While I enjoyed my meal, I thought it was overpriced for what you got.

Pros: pulled pork was very tender, fries were excellent, slaw was pretty tasty, waitstaff was friendly, fun decor, quick service once you ordered, but....

Cons: long time waiting in line to order, might be faster if there were simply servers during the dinner rush? Portions were small compared to the price; stingy on the sauce on the pulled pork (went to front counter to the waitress station and decided to fill up a cup of bbq sauce on my own); had to cut through order line to go to bathroom.

Final verdict? I would return if it was not a dinner time rush.

Fantastic prices and great food. I recommend a chocolate croissant and an iced hazelnut coffee.  I really enjoyed talking with Kathy while I was in town. She and Stephanie will bring you your croissants and coffee with a smile!  You really appreciate the FQ sense of community while in this wonderful little shop.

There is a $10 minimum for card purchases. 

Be aware of when the shop is open- they close fairly early.

I think everyone pretty much said what I would say!  The servings are huge, the food is great, and my friend visiting from Europe was almost ready to explode from over-eating. The joke of our trip became the phrase "Supersize me!"  This restaurant allowed him to live out our joke. Success!

The only thing I would point out is this: **Make sure you add your name to the list right away!!** it is kind of a chaotic waiting system, and if your name isn't "on the list," you are as good as being invisible. 

Happy overeating y'all!

PARKING: Paid street parking; it was easy to find a spot this time of year.

SERVICE:  Our server was great!  She was sociable, friendly, and attentive.

FOOD:  We really enjoyed the red potatoes as a free appetizer.  We were starving so we ate them right up.  This is a fun and unique touch. 

WAIT TIME:  There was no line waiting to get in, which was great because we were starving and impatient!

BALCONY SEATING: Deanie's on Magazine has a good-sized 2nd floor balcony for seating.  This would be nice to enjoy in warmer weather.

I had the crab au gratin years ago at the Deanie's in the Quarter and loved it.  I was happy to try this location and have it once again.  My boyfriend got the charbroiled barbecue oysters and loved them. They had a cheesy garlic breadcrumb crust.  My dad, who does not like oysters, tried them and liked them.  We also had the gumbo and jambalaya, which we enjoyed.  My dad liked his catfish poboy. 

For desert, we got the cheesecake. It was a MASSIVE generous slice.  Very creamy, not too sweet, and tasty! 

I know New Orleans is a big foodie town and this place might not be on the top of a foodie's list, but it it checked off all the boxes for our party: we wanted cheesy crabs, oysters, poboys...and we got them!  I would return to this place.

vBfiUxNlhlYImJziqJ1JSg.review_text: Awesome place for frozen yogurt. Some flavors repeat but they are still good. Workers are always friendly. Definitely a place to go if craving ice cream that's low calorie & low sugar.

Very busy and popular location.  One of the newest Chick-fil-A's in the area. The workers are very friendly and greet you when you enter.  Store is clean and food is consistent with the other Chick-fil-As.

This location also has a children's play zone where they can climb on stuff.

Good food and good location (across the street from International Mall). The restaurant has it's own parking lot and I've never had a problem getting a spot.

Inside there are many tv's so you can basically sit anywhere in the restaurant and be able to watch a tv. One side of the restaurant has the bar area and the other side is more of a sit-down family like restaurant. I mainly choose the sit-down side where you can still enjoy a great meal with your family but still be able to watch the game.

The food is delicious. I love the nachos. There is something for everyone - salads, burgers, and regular entrees to choose from. I also like that they bring hot/warm wet hand-towels so you can wipe/clean your hands.

It doesn't look like much from Gandy Blvd but once you walk past the Getaway sign, it's wonderful.

It's very casual. The food is very good. They have burgers, tacos, salads, and appetizers. They also have non-alcoholic and alcoholic drinks. The staff is very friendly and the parking is free. Side Note: they can get really busy and so you might have to park a bit down from the entrance and it might be difficult to get a table at that time.

There is a huge pavilion which has tables and chairs and a long bar. You can sit there and it feels like you are just on the outside deck of a restaurant that's on the water. There are smaller pavilions that are mainly focused for dancing or has a bar for drinking. Off to the side of the large pavilion, there are beach chairs for just relaxing and drinking. Pretty much every part of this place has a view of the waterway.

Overall, I definitely recommend giving this place a try (even if this isn't your typical kind of place). The relaxed atmosphere and the waterview are definitely the top reasons to try it out.

It's a small shop with little amount of seating inside. There isn't much selection on the different cupcake flavors that were available. They list a bunch of different cupcake flavors on the wall but only several of them will be available based on what was baked that day.  If you don't like cupcakes, they also offer ice cream.

I went on a Saturday evening when there were no events happening at Hyde Park. I was surprised that there was a line inside Sprinkles but I soon realized it was because the service was slow. There wasn't much of a selection to choose from since it was end of day but the cupcake I ordered was moist.  I wasn't impressed with my overall experience especially for the price paid and lack of seating inside.

First Watch is a good steady choice if looking for breakfast/lunch in Downtown Tampa. The quality of the food is consistent - I usually order the same thing time and again and it always tastes good. There are several First Watch locations and I have had the same great experience at all of them.

They have recently changed up their menu but they still have the breakfast basics: eggs, omelettes, skillet hashes, pancakes, waffles, juices.  For the non-breakfast items, they have sandwiches and salads to choose from. They also have a section on their menu for their healthiest entrees.

They do a good job at keeping the restaurant clean. If there's a large wait for a table in the morning there is hot coffee (with cream and sugar/sugar substitutes) available in the front area while you wait.

Definitely recommend giving First Watch a try especially if you're with a group that might be hard to please - there is something on the menu for everyone.

Good casual fast-food Greek place. They are part of a small shopping plaza that has Starbucks and several other stores so sometimes it's a bit difficult to get a parking spot. You  order at the counter, they give you a number and they bring your food to your table. They have booths and regular tables. It's never too full that you can't find a table inside but they also have some tables and chairs outside. The staff is very friendly and helpful.

They have daily specials - something different every day. There's a lot of selection on the menu. They have their Greek chopped salad which has the potato salad underneath. They have appetizers like hummus and pita, dips, soups. They have Flatbreads, Signature sandwiches (which are basically regular non-Greek sandwiches - but still really good), Pita sandwiches/platters and Greek entrees. The desserts that are available are located in the see-through case next to where you place your order. They also have beer and wine beside the usual soda machine and tea (sweet/unsweet). 

I mainly stick to the Greek salad since it's my favorite but my friends and I have tried several things from the menu and were very pleased. The hummus and their other spreads have always been good and I also like the pita gyro.

I would definitely recommend giving this place a try.

Great casual fast service sandwich place. Located at International Mall but on the outside where the other eateries are at (near Brio and The Pub). They usually greet you when you walk in. The menu is pretty basic and straightforward. You have sandwiches, wraps (which contain more or less the same ingredients as the sandwiches), flat breads and salads. You can combo your meal with potato chips (or cookie) and a drink. They also have cookies and muffins. When you order, you get a transponder which buzzes when it's time to go and pick up your order at the counter.

I usually stick to the combo meal of sandwich or wrap and drink with chips. My favorite is the Chipotle Chicken Avocado sandwich  or Chicken Bacon Avocado wrap - they are very similar. Another favorite is the Original 1762 sandwich which has roast beef, cheddar and horseradish sauce. The chips are their brand and you just select the one you want as you order. They have the typical soda machine and also tea. My favorite is the Earl Grey Lemonade Tea.

There is plenty of seating inside with table and chairs. They also have a counter that faces the mall walkway so you can people watch while you eat. There are also table and chairs outside as well. I have been there during some peak busy times and had to wait for a table after I ordered my meal. 

I would definitely recommend eating here if you are in the mood for some sandwiches or wraps.

Wonderful place! They don't have that many locations that I know of. Every time I go, there is a wait. Sometimes it's 30 minutes (which is reasonable) and other times it's well over an hour (closer to the hour and a half). It's definitely worth the wait in my book. They do have a nice indoor waiting area but there are benches outside where you can wait as well. They give you a transponder so you can go next door into Bed Bath & Beyond while you are waiting if you want to. It's located in the same shopping plaza as Bed Bath & Beyond so there are plenty of parking spaces.

They have a good selection of breakfast items on the menu - pancakes, waffles, eggs, omelettes, stuffed french toast, etc. The staff is very friendly and nice. They constantly walk around and will refill your coffee. I've had to wait a little to get a refill though - they are pretty busy running around. Everything that I have tried on the menu so far has been delicious. I've tried the stuffed french toast, the basic eggs, sausage and waffle. Everything is good and that's probably why there's always a wait to eat there. I always leave feeling super stuffed and usually with a doggy bag. 

Definitely recommend giving this place a try if you haven't already.

Met up with some friends here - had a little bit of a difficult time finding parking. They share the same parking lot with the neighboring business and it's not a large parking lot especially if there's an event going on. 

Very nice inside with lots of seating with tables/chairs and a bar. They are dog friendly since I did see several dogs there. The staff is very friendly. 

Good selection of beers to choose from. I had a dark one and it was delicious. During the time I was there, they had someone explain their beer making process and describe what each tank does. It was fascinating to learn more about how they make their beer.

This is a good place to meet up with friends and have a drink or two. The atmosphere is very casual and relaxing. Plus the beer is good.

Wasn't too thrilled with this place. I'd give it a high-five hand slap since it renovated the old Chinese restaurant that sadly sat at that spot. But a so-so on the other hand, the price for the portion/quality of the food received was just not a good value. I have hope that the owners of this place can improve (the food and the consistency of the quality of it) and so I will be coming back to give it another try.

My table ordered: Onion Rings, Cheddar Cheese Burger, Pastrami Burger,Belgian cut fries, and a side of Chipotle Mayo. I wasn't too thrilled with my Cheese Burger - it was a bit greasy and wasn't cooked as fully as I wanted it. The Pastrami Burger didn't have barely any pastrami. I did like that the Onion Rings and Fries came in matching blue/white bowl and mug, respectively. I thought that was cute, but not totally functional since some of the fries hit the table as I was taking some to eat. Fries and Onion Rings tasted good but I wasn't impressed with either. It was slow to get napkins/utensils and ketchup but the waitstaff was trying hard to serve everyone since the restaurant had gotten busy.

I do like the eclectic arrangement of tables, chairs and sofas. The different style of furniture made it very casual and relaxed. And I definitely liked all the plants hanging up. It's nice that they have so many large windows since it's makes it very bright and cheery inside.

Try it if you just want a new experience -- It's a different type of burger place that's a little pricey.

CineBistro is as good as it gets for going to the movies. It's pricey but for the expense you get a 21 and over crowd, comfortable leather seating, restaurant menu items including popcorn, alcoholic drinks, and great picture/sound quality. I also like the reserve seating so you can choose your seats.

The best thing to do to guarantee that you get the seats that you want, is to book online as soon as you know they are selling tickets for the movie that you want to see. You can purchase online with the usual payment methods (credit cards, etc) and also Fandango money.

I would recommend to get there 30 minutes before showtime because that 30 minutes is the window in which you can order your food (like your meal or just popcorn, if that's what you want). It's good to order as soon as you are seated since it takes time to get the food out to you (since they are like a regular restaurant). I like ordering quickly because I like my food to come before they dim the lights since I like seeing my food while I'm eating it. LOL!

If you show up earlier than the 30 minutes before showtime and they haven't started seating for the movie, CineBistro has a wonderful lounge area. There's a bar at one end of the lounge where you can order drinks and food. You can also sit in the lounge and someone will take your order for drinks or food (I think they have a lounge menu- which offers less selection of food than the theater menu). 

CineBistro is perfect for: "Dinner and a Movie" date night,  "Girls' Night Out" or if you just want to spoil yourself and relax in luxurious seats while watching a movie.

Great Starbucks! Good location and plus there is a shared parking lot behind it so you don't have to worry about parking. The parking lot does get full if you go during the prime going out hours like Friday and Saturday nights. But that's the same for all the parking lots on Howard during those hours.

This Starbucks has the typical selection of food and drinks. There's plenty of seating inside if you don't mind sitting at the long table or the bar-like counter that faces the outside. There are several comfy leather seats and also several smaller tables. As with any Starbucks, there's always people in there working on their laptops. 

They do have lots of seating outside. They have tables that face Howard ave and also a couple of tables tucked on the side that faces 717 South (which is more quiet than the street noise).

I've been to this Sweet Tomatoes several times and have been happy each time. The staff that works here keeps this place clean. Also they are very friendly and helpful.

When you enter this Sweet Tomatoes, the salad bar is the first thing you encounter. It is usually pretty well stocked and there's usually a worker prepping more salads right behind it. If an item is running low or out, you can just tell that person and they will immediately get you that item. They do very well at trying to make sure none of the salad bar items totally run out.

At the end of the salad bar is where the cashier is located for you to pay. The cashier is also the one to give you the cups or mugs if you are also wanting soda, tea or coffee.

Behind the cashier is the rest of the Sweet Tomatoes restaurant. They have baked potatoes, rice, muffins, flatbread-like items, soups, and a dessert / fruit section. Across from the food is the beverage area. This Sweet Tomatoes has coffee, brewed tea (sweet and unsweet) and the standard soda dispenser with ice and soda. The blue water cups are located in that area as well. There's a small spigot for dispensing water. 

The dessert area has soft serve ice cream and toppings like fudge, caramel, granola, and sprinkles. In that same area are jello, sugar free mousse, oranges for those that want a little bit healthier dessert.

There is plenty of seating in the dining room area. As you finish eating and put your plates to the side, there's busboys that come around and pick up your plates. There is not a place to put your tray or plates/bowls when you are finished since they expect you to leave them on the table because they have workers that take care of that for you.

Sweet Tomatoes is a good place when you are craving endless salad and soup (especially if you are wanting a meat-free meal). There's enough selection of items to satisfy you.

Great place for thin crust coal fired pizza.

This place has a parking lot outside and plenty of seating inside. There are some seating outside. Inside they have several TVs along one wall so you can definitely catch a game while you are eating. There is also a TV at the bar. 

This Anthony's is kept clean and organized. They have craft brews available along with coffee and soda / tea. The soda / tea are the individual single serve bottles like those you buy in a vending machine. The menu is a bit limited but they focus on keeping the quality up on the food that they do have. They offer salad, personal sized and regular sized pizzas, baked chicken wings, sandwiches and meatballs. There is dessert but I've never had it.

I mainly focus on the pizza, chicken wings, sandwiches and meatballs depending on what I'm craving. The servers know the menu very well and can help you make a decision on what to get. I definitely like the thin crust pizza and tuna sandwich. I've never had a soggy salad either. I order the chicken wings when I'm craving wings but want to be healthy about it. They are usually good sized, too. It's a good family atmosphere and they can accommodate large groups as well.

This Chipotle is a pretty good place. It's located in a shopping plaza of sorts so it shares the parking lot with several business. So needless to say, parking can get a bit hard to find. During the peak Howard Ave party hours (Friday & Saturday evenings/nights), there is someone staffed at the parking lot but it's still free parking if you are eating at Chipotle.

The restaurant is kept pretty clean and it's usually cold inside for me. They do have seating outside as well. They have the usual Chipotle offerings and their drink area (soda/ tea/ water) is in the center of the restaurant.

The food is pretty consistent. The only complaint would be sometimes the chips are a bit stale or too salty. Other than that, the food is good and definitely a good price (especially if you have a BOGO or deal).

Interesting place. It's a simple looking building from the outside but the inside is very chic. It has dark wood with white accents of decor. It looks very classy/trendy inside. The hostess and waitstaff are very friendly and nice. It has it's own parking lot and in the afternoon there's complementary valet.

They have 2 large conference rooms that can be closed off from the main dining area. It's a good place to have a meeting or get-together (for a party or celebration). The waitstaff is very attentive and make sure that everyone is taken care of.

The main dining room is nice. There are booths that are pretty private and then regular tables as well. The dishes are a bit gourmet and nice food presentation is standard. I've eaten here during lunch and dinner. I prefer lunch since it's the standard fair with burgers, salads, etc. For dinner the menu's are illuminated and the food menu is a little more creative and pricier. It's definitely a nice date night place. During the day, I do see business people in there have their business lunches/meetings. 

It's a nice trendy place where you can go to eat, experience the chic vibe, and get good service. Also I would recommend this restaurant, if you want to impress someone.

Pleasantly surprised! When you arrive at the location, it's very basic. A food truck in a parking lot with some tarp to create a shaded area for you to sit and eat. The food truck is located in the back of the parking lot away from the street, so it's easy to miss it when you are driving by.

There's a large menu board, with descriptions of everything included for each item, on the side of the window where you order. The lady that took the order was very nice and spoke English. They take cash and credit card. 

For drinks, they have a cooler located next to the order window that has bottled water, canned soda, etc. If you order and are going to eat there, there are a couple of benches and chairs to sit on. They bring out 3 different bottles of sauces. I liked the orange colored one the best because it was really spicy.  I ordered 2 U.S. tacos, one chicken and one steak. My friend ordered the chicken quesadilla - which was huge. The food was good.

It seems to get a lot of customers. I went on a Friday around 2-3pm there were people constantly coming to order food from the truck. The workers keep the area clean and constantly come out of the truck to bring you the sauces, your food order, and to clean up the tables.

Don't let the area and the basic set-up discourage you, it's definitely worth a try if you are craving Mexican.

Very happy with this Grill Smith in Carrollwood area. It's in a good location - at the end corner of a strip mall area that has other shops and restaurants. Finding a parking spot is pretty easy. 

They not only have seating inside but also 2 separate outside seating areas that have ceiling fans. One is more with large round tables and the other outside area has some couches for lounging.

The staff/hostess have usually been good and do a great job seating large parties. The menu is the standard American fare of salads, burgers, steaks, fish, soup, etc. Grillsmith gives you a    complementary little bread basket that has small little seasoned bread loaves and crunchy crackers. Both the bread and crackers are delicious.

I've had the salads, steak, and salmon entrees - I have been happy with everything that I've ordered. Grillsmith's selection of menu offerings is very diverse and would please pretty much anyone. It's easy to suggest to eat there for a group of people since there is something for everyone on the menu.

Definitely a place to go when you're hungry for good food but don't know what to eat or that you are entertaining /meeting a group of people that all have different tastes.

I love this place! It's fast food but a bit healthier. PDQ stands for People Delivering Quality - and you can definitely taste it.  It's a very popular location and the drive-thru usually has a long line.

They have outside seating that have fans that mist water into the air to cool you off. There is also corn hole you can play.

Once inside they have a digital menu board with the items and also shows some pictures of the specials. You order at the counter and when your food is ready, they call out the name that you gave them so you can pick it up. 

In the back of the dining room area, there is a sink where you can wash your hands (by stepping on the pedal) and also 2 Freestyle soda machines (which have a variety of soda flavorings). There is fresh tea, napkins and ketchup located in this area as well.

In the main dining room area, there's booths and some high-top tables. You can also sit at the counter to eat. There are several TVs so you can watch the game while you eat.

The food is delicious - they have thin fries and turkey & chicken sandwiches. They also have breaded and grilled chicken tenders.  My favorite is the Cali Chicken Club sandwich which has bacon and avocado. I also like the Crispy and the Grilled Chicken Salads. They have plenty of sauces to choose from for your chicken tenders. The hand-spun shakes are delicious and very thick and rich tasting.

Cute place and wonderful atmosphere. The Oxford Exchange is many different things all under one roof. There is the sit-down restaurant, the eclectic gift shop, book store/eye glasses store, and TeBella tea counter and Buddy Brew coffee counter.

The parking is good for the location. There are many different places to park and plenty of signs telling you if it's right lot to park in.

It's a great place to go if you want to chill, waste time, or hang out with friends.  If you have time to waste, it's great to spend it in the book store or the gift shop. The gift shop store has a lot of unusual items to look at and touch. They also have some standard items like candles, jewelry, and cards. It's a great place to walk around and look at stuff.

Having TeBella and Buddy Brew counters across from each other is great especially if you are with a group of friends and some only drink tea and some only drink coffee. So this lets everyone get whatever drink they are craving.  The counters also have some pastries and cookies.

In between the tea and coffee counters are several couches and comfy chairs to lounge in. There are other chairs and a large table also in that room. You can go upstairs for quiet conversation since there are several comfy chairs up there as well. Seating is very limited on the 2nd floor. 

I've heard good things about the sit-down restaurant but haven't tried it since I mainly take my  visiting friends here to hang out and chat while having a tea or coffee. It's definitely a nice place to take out-of-town visitors since there's plenty of stuff for them to wander around to look at and there is coffee and tea to drink.

Located a little bit away from the crowded hubbub of Howard Ave you would think Cask Social Kitchen wouldn't be that busy, but due to it's atmosphere and food it's pretty popular.  I went during a typical Thursday Ladies Night. I arrived around the start of Happy Hour (about 5:30pm) and had to wait on the complementary parking.  The parking was already pretty full and the valet was working as fast as he could.  By the time I got inside,  there was a huge line on Howard Ave of cars waiting to park. 

Once I was inside,  I was impressed.  It's very nicely decorated and had a comfy feel.  The hostess greeted me right away.  To the left is mainly the dining room and to the right has more tables and the bar.  In the back of the room on the right,  is a large table that's good for large gatherings.  There's also outside seating that faces Howard  Ave.

The service was great.  I was part of a large party  (10+) and the server was attentive and quick.  We ordered some Ladies Night Drink Specials and appetizers. Everyone liked the Truffle Deviled Eggs, Buffalo Cauliflower and Tuna Tartare. It was a nice atmosphere for a large group.  The only issue I noticed was the pricing listed on the Ladies Night Drink menu (lower) was different than on the bill (higher).  I would recommend that they update the Ladies Drink menu so that the bill matches.

vLhIQd0jIPaOosntvZEY8A.review_text: Nice breakfast. Had the shrimp and "krab meat" omlette. It was full of shrimp. Overall good breakfast for the price. The staff were great at keeping my coffee cup filled and quick service. The atmosphere is a little tacky but charming in a beachy way. Not the most flavorful breakfast, but good for those who may have stayed out too late the night before.

Vacationing in Indian Rocks Beach and we found this place. Excellent sushi! The Fujiyama or Fuji Mountain roll was amazing!!! It has baked tempura crumbs and crab on top. The atmosphere was very nice for a place in a strip mall. The server was really quick and very polite. I would definitely come back when I am the area again.

Fast service, great food. The crab cakes were fantastic. The fish dinners were great tasting, but portions of fish were a little small. My husband left hungry, even after wine, an appetizer and a fish dinner.  I would suggest drinks and two appetizers, then dinner for a couple. Wonderful atmosphere. This place is a little on the pricey side.
Atmosphere and strong drinks! Amazing!!! I love this place.

This place had amazing pho! It's hard to impress me with that as I have asian family that also cooks their own pho recipie. Wow, excellent atmosphere on the patio, beautiful lighting and very relaxing. The summer rolls were really good and meaty. The pho was the best broth that I have ever tasted. I like the scaled down decor inside the restaurant, it felt very urban. Finished dinner with a chocolate crossiant and it was an amazingly delicious experience! I will come back and also suggest this place to others in the area.

Great little place. The owner took extra time to brew me a nice fresh cup of decaf.  Had a nice ham and cheese croissant and left happy! Great seating area overlooking the street, great for people watching.
Cute little kid friendly coffee shop. The owner was so sweet and genuine. Nice place to chill out and drink some coffee with the family. The decaf latte I had was excellent and I am really picky!
Nice and moist, great flavors!

A really quirky place for fans of WWF or WWE. Hulk Hogan is an owner of this place and his championship belts are displayed in the hallway entrance. The food was pretty good! Had the Mongolian bbq ribs with hosin to start, they were incredible, totally and unexpectedly good! The main course of a black angus burger with "the works" was really juicy and delicious too. The ranch dressing is made in house and it really made the burger and fries! I used it as a fry dip and I am sure I ate an insane amount of calories, but it was worth it! The staff was really attentive and offered drink suggestions. Had a nice experience while vacationing at the adjacent hotel.

What a super cute little place, chock full of sweetness! Checked in on Yelp and claimed an offer for 3 free toppings so I was able to turn a couple of scoops into a nice little sundae that was super reasonable in price. I had chocolate peanut butter ice cream with hot fudge, nuts, and whipped cream. The ice cream had a nice soft, creamy texture. It seemed a little lighter than solid ice cream with a higher fat content, I liked the softness. The flavor was great! I asked the owner if she made her own ice cream and I found out the place uses locally sourced ice cream providers, so love that it's all local. The owner was really friendly and genuine. Also, it's close to Krispy Kreme, so there is a nice doughnut breeze outside. In the back of the store there is a little gazebo to hang out and enjoy your ice cream. Had a great visit and this place is so adorable.
Really bad service and terrible drive through. Sorry not sorry, this is a terrible place to go. If you want to waste 45 minutes of your time come to this location.

What a fun place for breakfast. Fray's is right across from Dunkin Donuts, but given the choice to go with a small, local place I was happy to try out Fray's. They had croissant breakfast sandwiches which were nice. Even more intriguing was the "baked donut" breakfast sandwich. It was essentially doughnut dough that was baked and unglazed, like a really tasty English muffin used to make breakfast sandwiches. It was really delicious and had a great texture. The basic glazed doughnuts were light and soft, very nice texture again, not overly heavy or doughy. The coffee was great, the staff was fast to assist, and I loved the atmosphere. The sign out front boasts "the worlds best coffee", and it was pretty darn good. There is even a drive thru.  If you're in the neighborhood be sure to stop in for breakfast.

Wow, love the beer at this place. We were in the area for an athletic event and a friend (she's a total beer expert) suggested Cigar City Brewpub for lunch. This is a fun place with some expertly crafted beer and so many wonderful varieties to try. I feel like I almost tried them all! I had the four beer flight and a brunch burger. The favorite beer of the group was Lilith with a smooth citrusy flavor and crazy 10% alcohol content. Woo that made for a fun afternoon. For lunch I had the all natural brunch burger with 1/2 lb of ground beef, a black bean cake, fried egg, cheese, and a soft egg bun. It came with a side salad and yucca hash. It was enormous and so satisfying. The place was not too crowded for a Sunday afternoon, which was nice. The servers we had were great, very friendly with the right amount of sass to make our late brunch extra entertaining. When I'm in the area again I'll drive out my my way to come here!

I try to hit this place for lunch almost every time I'm in the area. The outside of the restaurant has fun "bus" decor and a walk up "to-go" window. The tacos with beef or carne asada are a solid choice. Two tacos are great for a lunch portion. I usually skip the side of rice and beans. Also, I usually add cheese and jalapeño on my tacos, which I think is about .60 cents extra per taco. I'm all about upgrading for things like cheese and jalapenos, but wish at least that cheese was included. 

Taco Bus has some house made beverages, I've had them before and they are mostly good. The watermelon aqua fresca was a bit heavy and thick this time, so I would probably stick with a soft drink or horchata drink. The green and red sauces taco sauces they serve with the tacos really add to the flavor. Without the sauces I find the tacos a little bland., so be sure to sample some sauce. This is a nice place for lunch and the service is usually pretty quick. Just stick to basic tacos and you can't go wrong.

So dark in here, wow! I'm sure in other cities there would be regulations against this lack of illumination, but this is very, very old place. The beer and liquor here is served up old school, like "1761" old school. 

This is a historic bar in the French Quarter of New Orleans named for its pirate owner of the past, Jean Lafitte. It's a great place it go any night that you want to drink, chat, and pretty much sit around the old hearth (fireplace). It's supposed to be one of the most haunted places in New Orleans. After a few visits I have no evidence to support this claim, but it's very dark and hauntingly fun. It's feels like you're walking into a different time period coming here. 

The most recent time I visited there was a man playing the piano with people sitting around the piano and adjacent bar stools. There was only candlelight on the little bar tables and on the top of the piano. Super dark until your eyes adjust. It was rowdy and everyone was singing. Not the well organized dueling piano bar type of singing.  Just serious belting it out-drunk type singing and various people doing some wobbly impromptu dancing. It sounds like a mess, but the throwback vibe here is so old it just works. No one was terribly rowdy, just a fun, lively, and talkative crowd...just what you would expect at a bawdy haunted pirate bar. This place is all about atmosphere, so come get some drinks, laugh and relax. Do what a pirate would do here!

I see my first review for Pat O'Brien's was way too short. I have something to say, this place is awesome, a classic even. Could it be the hurricanes talking?  I don't even know. It's just wonderful to walk into the courtyard under the plants, to see the glowing fire fountain, then sit down and order a nice refreshing hurricane. In my experience you really should only have one (maybe two?) hurricanes. Anything beyond that and you are in dangerous territory.  If you choose to sit inside it's usually a little more crowded. There is a piano bar with singing, it's okay but outside is the place to be. My favorite experience here is to watch the gorgeous fire fountain outside while sipping a drink. The vibe is so fun and lively. The patio is beautiful. 

The service is usually very swift and you're greeted kindly by a server dressed in the formal Pat O'Brien's green and white uniform. Once they bring your order you'll have to pay on the spot. There are other beverages here besides the hurricane, but if you go you must try this classic drink at least once. 

You can take your empty hurricane glass to go (packaged up) as a souvenir or turn the glass in at the bar and get $3 back. If you are not done drinking your drink just ask for a plastic "to-go" cup and keep on sipping while you stroll away.

Some people don't like Pinkberry. They dislike that the toppings are served by people behind the counter and that you can't control how many toppings you get on your yogurt. Nay to this. Any time I've asked them to load me up with toppings they overload me with toppings and it's awesome! There is no extra charge for toppings you basically get what you want included in the price of your yogurt with the exception of the "Luxe toppings", those are extra. 

I haven't been to pinkberry in a while because the three locations near where I live have all recently closed. I was excited to find one in New Orleans. Upon ordering I found that they now offer a mini size yogurt which is a perfect snack. The original tart yogurt is a wonderful contrast with the sweet fruit and various toppings. The luxe topping including melted chocolate with crispy rice is so good. My favorite is to just the original tart yogurt with pomegranate, raspberry, pineapple, and mango. That is perfect mix and you just feel better after eating all that fruit.

I know there are a ton of Froyo places around these days, but pinkberry does it best. Love their store designs and their yogurt really tastes the best to me. It's a little more tart and yogurt like then other frozen yogurt places which just taste very sugary to me. I love that their toppings are always so organized and they look freshly chopped, no stale stuff. Stop by if you're in the area.

This place is really something. I don't really understand the atmosphere or know why it's called Port of Call,  but it's pretty cool. So the atmosphere-there are ropes going across the ceiling and it looks like you're in some sort of weird Key West style shipwreck when you walk in. There's some seating down a couple of stairs at small tables, or you can sit at the bar which is sort of wide and oval-shaped. At the bar you'll be crowding in with other bar patrons. My husband and I sat at the bar and it was fun talking to the people next to us. Waiting for a small table, the wait was 30 to 45 minutes on a busy Friday evening. Bar seating was immediate as soon as some stools opened up, so that seemed better for us. 

The house specialty drink is called "Neptune's Monsoon" and it is served in a large plastic to-go cup. It's pinkish in color and seriously full of rum and a bit of juice! It may knock you off your barstool. I had a few big sips of the monsoon (on a mostly empty stomach) and felt like I was going through a storm. 

The menu seems a little odd to me, it was very specific. It's mostly cuts of steak and baked potatoes and hamburgers with different toppings. The baked potato you can get loaded or stuffed with mushrooms which is kind of different. They also have hamburgers and cheeseburgers which are huge and you can get these with assorted toppings including mushrooms. Great burgers! They were very juicy and large, not chewy or overcooked. The staff at the bar was super attentive. My drink was filled frequently, they asked if we needed anything, and they were super prompt with getting our meal out. I understand why this quirky place as an institution in New Orleans and I would definitely come back here next time I'm in town.

It's touristy but it's just so mouthwatering good. There is probably going to be a line to order and they may even be out of their famous muffuletta sandwich if you get there too late in the day. Only so many are available daily as they are usually made in advance. I have been here too late on a Saturday and they were all gone. Sadly, it happens. Call ahead and ask what's available if you're stopping in later in the day.

This is a really no nonsense Italian deli in the French Quarter. It's famous for the muffuletta. If you've not tried one here, you absolutely must. The olive salad that is used as sandwich dressing is exceptional. The bread on the muffuletta is a bit chewy, maybe even tough to start, but it's softened by the rich and oily olive salad that soaks into the bread, making it moist and insanely delicious. The balance of the bread and the olive salad is just right. This is just a great sandwich that you need to try. I usually only order a half muffuletta and share this with my husband so we can each have a quarter. Otherwise, it's just too much sandwich. If you grab a soda and a bag of Zapp's crawtator chips you will have a perfect meal.   

The Central Grocery store also sells local products  and food to go. Browse the groceries for some regional specialities and Italian foods. Love this place and I stop in each time I'm in Nola. It's closed Mondays, so plan ahead.

Can't help it, but I love this place. It might not be a five star place for everyone, but for me this place just feels like I belong here. Love the imaginative decor and the seriously chilled out vibe.  It's hipster-ish, so I'll just throw that out there to get it out of the way first. Is it annoyingly hipster-ish? Nope. 

So about the place-it's dimly lit and the decor has a definite "under the sea"/nautical theme. It's not so overdone that it's weird, it's just a nice subtle nautical motif all around. The chairs I believe are from an old ship and the lights inside the bar look like hanging jellyfish. The wall hangings and photos are nautical themed as well, a very interesting collection. 

There are some local bands they play here and a ton of board games piled up in the corner shelf to play while you enjoy drinks and tapas. It's the kind of place where you can disengage or chat with others. 

The house sangria is phenomenal. I don't know what all the magic ingredients are, but it's nicely liquored up with an exquisite cinnamon aftertaste. This bar has some fabulous locally brewed beer. The tapas is wonderful too. Try the "All-A-Board" cheese and meat board. It's perfect to share. This is a super place to go when you want to getaway from it all.

The line of people waiting for brunch gave this place away...it's good, really good and worth waiting for. Tried out Wildflower Cafe on a Sunday morning and we were seated relatively quick, but it was a full house. This is one of those places that you have to go to if you're in the area! 

The restaurant is hidden away from the street. The interior is quaint and cheerful. The outside has a pet friendly small patio with a few tables. The outside is very cute with flower boxes lining the windows. 

We sat inside and the place is just plain charming in an afternoon tea house type of way. There is small counter area that showcases cookies, cakes, and other bakery items. It was very pretty and nicely laid out. I had the the malted Belgian waffles, they are like little delicious pillows. The size is small for each individual waffle, but it's a perfect portion since they are very filling. The waffle breakfast I had came with eggs and bacon, whipped cream, a bit of fruit, two waffles dusted in powdered sugar, and garnished with fragrant fresh mint leaves. Sheer perfection! I added cheese grits because I couldn't resist trying them. It might have been a bit too much food, but the best indulgence for brunch. We also tried the biscuits with honey butter and strawberry preserves and it was carb heaven! Like that this place serves iced coffee and some decaf flavored iced teas also. I had the wild berry tea, lovely flavor and so refreshing. 

The service was fast and we were well taken care of.  This place is all pros and no cons! Stop in if you're nearby.

Yep, this place nails it. Charming, creepy, pretty, a tad weird, and caffeinated. Located in uptown New Orleans on a quiet street, this little coffee shop keeps late hours for those in need of a coffee fix. There are lots of students here with laptops working late. Inside the decor is like "Goth Halloween" with lots of fun photos, wall paintings (seriously, the bathroom is home to a gorgeous wall to wall mural), hanging mystery objects, and some generally voodoo inspired decor. There is a bit out outside seating, lots of seating across from the kitchen area, and a back room area that looks like a secret passageway. 

Z'otz has a nice selection of dessert snacks like cookies and brownies, some items are gluten free. When I visited late in the evening they were well stocked on sweets and cold brew coffee. I'm picky about iced coffee (hate when it's weak or diluted), but their coffee was smooth, bold, and strong without being bitter. I love that they use chipped ice, it made the iced coffee just perfect. Also they have a squeeze bottle of simple syrup nearby to make your iced coffee sweet, so much more useful than granulated sweetener. Also had a brownie with nuts to accompany the coffee. The brownie was very chocolatey and not too sweet, it paired nicely with the iced coffee.  Found the prices super reasonable and was happy to buy from a locally owned (non-franchised) coffee shop. I liked everything about this little place. Lots of local charm and a mostly quiet atmosphere. The guy behind the counter was great and super fast.

You know when you find that place that you could call a second home? This is mine. It's dark, spacious, cool, and classy inside. The beer, so good! I am a beer enthusiast, not an expert-but this place rocked my world. There is not much inside except some open space, a brewery, a bar, a merchandise area, a confessional booth from a church, and some interesting art. That's all you need, and a little merchandise. I tried their brews and fell in love with a nice sour dragonfruit IPA. I hear a brewery tour is in order next time, but I was happy to bask in the dim lights of the bar and just relax. Very enjoyable brewery and worth the trip if you're in the area.

Kind of a hot mess. They made a s'mores frappucino without any coffee in it. Not sure why, we were only customers ordering so not like it was busy. They were friendly but didn't know how to Starbucks. Ordered coffee drink and got a lot of ice and milk but no coffee in it. Didn't satisfy my coffee urge. Attached to a Sheraton hotel and it's very stuffy, like they are trying to be high end but miss the mark. Dunno. Double "meh".

So, after a grueling day at the local Indianapolis speedway, this place really did the trick to refresh our weary souls! Great pizza and atmosphere. Their logo is so cute and the interior is woodsy and fresh. 

Our server Ellen was very personable and provided great service. Didn't care for the pulled pork nachos, good but just not my thing to order. My husband loved them. The pizza with the hand tossed crust was phenomenal, so order it!!! The roasted garlic made the pizza perfect. It was loaded with cheese and so luscious. The menus here seems a little small to me, but they do their food items right. Quality over quantity for sure. 

Like the pretty tall ceilings, light fixtures, and chill woodsy vibe here. Would definitely come back when I'm in the area.

This place way exceeded my expectations! The place was slammed with customers and we were on a 1 hour wait for a table for two. The servers on the patio, although not a bar area, took our order and payment for bar drinks. Received great service on a very busy day. We tried the house Bloody Mary and it was superb, jumbo mug with a nice shot of Guinness Stout on top of it. Around 35-40 minutes we received a text that our table was ready. 

We had a great server (a guy from Florida-wish I could recall his name), and he made some excellent suggestions. Tried the 1/2 fried chicken, collard greens, mac & cheese, a shrimp PO boy, and some local beer. The fried chicken is pressure cooked and then fried, it was out of this world!!! It rivaled some of the best southern fried chicken I've had in places like Louisiana, Alabama, and Florida. The chicken is served with cayenne   pepper spicy honey. It really complimented the crispy, salty chicken. Not sure why, but the honey really worked with the chicken. The Mac & cheese had bread crumbs and it was just perfect. The shrimp PO boy was great with soft bread, large shrimp, and avocado chunks-spicy and succulent. Not at all like New Orleans PO boys, but good nonetheless. Would definitely go out of my way to come here again and have more fried chicken and local beer.

Tried the Embassy Suites in downtown Tampa and was hoping it would be a peaceful experience, but not really. I was in a room that was up quite high and facing the bright lights of the adjacent parking garage. The light managed to come through the curtains. The front of the room, although inside an interior corridor, had two front windows with blinds  that faced the interior hallway. My blinds were a little wonky so I was concerned people passing by could see in. These two windows to view into the corridor are completely unnecessary. 

The positive-The room had a nice mini fridge and kitchen/bar sink. Otherwise...The room thermostat worked on sensors. When I arrived I was sure the air conditioner in my room was broken (the room was so hot) , so I called the front desk. They assured me that lights and motion would keep the air from turning off. So what happens when I'm sleeping in the dark and not moving around? Well, the room was pretty warm all night, and because of this I wasted more electricity by leaving all the lights on in the room all night hoping the air would stay on. I tried to keep the sensors from turning it off. 

The bed comforter however smelled like strong body odor. Florida is a humid place, and sometimes laundry if not dried properly can stink, but this smell was unmistakably human body odor, like armpit stink. The positive for this place is the location in downtown Tampa. The staff were nice and the location was great, but really didn't like the room being hot and the bad bed linen smells. Yuck!

Wonderful breakfast and brunch place in downtown St. Pete.  Not a lot of places were open at breakfast time, so we were happy to find this little gem. 

You order and pay at at the counter and the cashier will give you a number. They call out your number and bring over the crepes when ready. Drinks are picked up immediately when you order, so don't walk away from ordering until you grab your drinks. Like that coffee, tea, wine, and bloody Mary's are served here. That's a nice accompaniment to crepes. 

The Bloody Mary was unusual, very good and spicy! It tasted like they make their own fresh tomato, cilantro, and jalapeño mix, almost a smoothie consistency and then add vodka. It was a little chunkier than I am used to, but I really liked the spicy flavor. 

You can have savory or dessert crepes here. I had a few bites of the Nutella crepe, it was heavenly. Would have posted a photo of it, but we ate it too quickly! Definitely come here for a delicious Parisian meal if you're in the area.

Dined here in the past for lunch and felt like it was just okay. Tried the stinky buns that are bao buns with various meats. Pretty good bao, but didn't find it too exciting. Fast forward a year and I came to Anise for dinner while staying in downtown tampa. Yum, it really hit the spot! Tried the beet salad with arugula, pine nuts, and goat cheese for a starter. Fell in love with it, sweet beets, rich pine nuts, decadent goat cheese, and fresh arugula tossed in a citrusy vinegarette. Perfect meal starter. It was pretty ample, so would have even been good for two people if entrees were being ordered too. 

For my main entree I tried the beef tenderloin with mashed cauliflower. This came with brown mushroom gravy, it was perfect! Don't eat a lot of starchy things and the mashed cauliflower was a perfect alternative to carby potatoes. The tenderloin comes out sliced and it was cooked to medium perfection as requested. Had a great dinner here and would come back again anytime. Service was great at the bar.

Cute place that looks like a little night club in Ybor city. The lights are dim with neon light accents and they serve handcrafted ice cream in rolls. When visiting Tampa this place caught my eye at night and I stopped in shortly before closing. The staff was nice and helped me understand the menu. The ice cream is spread out and it freezes on metal platters with different sauces and mix in items. So fun to watch and lots of great combinations for dessert. The ice cream art process takes some time  to perform, especially if the store has a line. It took about 10-15 before my order was ready, so a little patience is needed for preparation. Really enjoyed this and my coconut-vanilla ice cream was delicious!

Hey girl, do you like Brussel sprouts and avocado toast? So do I, and this place has got it going on. Vale, if you're reading this, please bring this concept to downtown Orlando, we need it! 
This is one of those places that some may scoff at as a millennial/hipster food joint, but I'm here to tell you I'm probably neither of those things and I enjoyed the heck out of this place. Honestly, I felt like my stomach was smiling after eating here. 

I tried the regular size bowl today and I had it loaded with the following: fresh greens (aka lettuce), roasted sweet potato cubes, balsamic mushrooms (omg!!!), shredded Brussel sprouts, then topped with steak (+$1.50), southwestern chicken, spicy feta cheese, and a side of chipotle dressing. Truth be told, I could not get it in my mouth fast enough.  The mushrooms were perfect and the texture of the shredded Brussel sprouts were satisfyingly crunchy event after being cooked a bit. 

If you're in downtown Tampa and love the veg life, come here. My only veggie suggestion-add zucchini noodles to the menu. Appreciated that their food packaging was compostable. Loved the free minty detox water too! Will be back.

It's just so pretty! Came here on a whim since I heard it was close to downtown Tampa and I was in the area. Was excited they had their own ample parking lot, and around noon it was pretty full. 

The inside is just so damn cool, industrial space that is quaint, cool, modern, and rustic all at the same time. To be honest, I wish we had a food hall place of this capacity and caliber in Orlando. Enjoyed some tacos for lunch from Empanmama. It was hard to decide, all the food and drink places looked so tempting. There was ramen/sushi, Italian, deli sandwiches, a bar for beer/wine/coffee, Cuban, baked desserts, ice cream, a florist, and even a small retail shop. Love the water-tap near the entry area. Free sparkling water on tap to stay hydrated while you scope out where to eat. 

The tables are mostly communal, so when you find a seat you may be sitting with others that you don't know, but it was a fun experience. Definitely come here when you have some time to spare. Would be a perfect date or hangout spot. Looking forward to coming back for a leisurely day sometime and trying the ramen and the flash frozen ice cream.

Favorite in downtown Tampa when you need all the  delicious flavors of Vietnamese food. This cozy little cafe does freshly wrapped spring rolls with your choice of meats and vegetables. Great pho and banh mi sandwiches. Every time I am in downtown Tampa at lunch time I try to spot in and check out this place. Grab an iced Vietnamese coffee and you're good to go here!

Geez, I come in here as a full grumpy cat, all hungry and cranky. I was "that customer". I ordered a Bloody Mary and cheese curds. The server took our order and the cheese curds came out very quickly. The server reports back and said bloody marys are made in large batches on the weekends only, and that they were incorrect in telling me they had them on a weekday. I literally came for the Bloody Mary, but whatever, and I had already started eating the cheese curds. Well damn if the cheese curds were not phenomenal and the dipping sauces were simply delightful. What started out as a disappointing experience was turned around by amazing cheese curds, a super nice server that was dealing with my hangry attitude, and a few glasses of local beer. 

Follow up: I came back the next day and tried the Bloody Mary, and it was pretty damn good. The place was packed on a weekend! Overall I have to say the few things I tried here and the fun, pleasant staff made this a great stop for a snack and drinks.

Really, really like this place! I can't handle much caffeine but I need a little something with low caffeine. Kahwa has delicious iced decaf coffee. It's always ready when I need it, I never have to wait. 

The staff are quick to take your order, and this place is always efficient. They have a nice vibe and I stop in here every time I'm in the Tampa/St. Pete area.

Not sure if I was starving, but this place nailed it for me. So yummy. Had two tacos, one with beef and the other with shrimp. Had a side of green chili mac & cheese. 

The inside of the place is super humble, it was formerly a Pita Pit. But damn if the food isn't lovely! You can also order Poké bowls here, but I was really into the taco menu. I got my tacos spicy style, and got a side of their salsa. Their salsa, wow!!! The best homemade salsa I've ever had, and I'm a salsa snob. Was surprised at how delicious it was. Wish I had ordered double salsa, but there is always next time. Despite this looking like a small little mom & pop type place, the service was attentive and friendly and the food was super. Will definitely be back.

What can I say about Ulele that hasn't already been said in another yelp review? I have to jump on the bandwagon and give this place five stars for a tantalizing meal and great service. 

This was my first time trying this super popular place and even for a weeknight it was packed completely at 7:30 PM. I called ahead to check and see if I should make a reservation or just drop in and dine at the bar. The staff warned that they are there most packed between 7 and 8:30 PM on a nightly basis. I took a shuttle ride to this location so I didn't have to concern myself with parking. When I arrived it was raining outside.  The outside bar area does not serve food while it was raining. I went inside and took my chances with asking for a table and I expected to wait quite a while based on the amount of people I saw inside.  Surprisingly, the weather cleared up and I was able to sit at one of their outside tables almost immediately. I ordered the Scottish steak but I substituted the cranberry beans for their amazing mashed potatoes that have popcorn on the side. The Scottish steak with roasted garlic and mashed potatoes was absolutely spectacular. It hit all the flavor notes I was looking for: meaty, juicy, and roasted garlic ... need I say more!? I had really stellar service from a person named Jerri. She was an amazing server and anticipated all of my needs. I would suggest going there and definitely ask for Jerri.

Great Thai food in downtown Tampa. Have been here many times for lunch and the food is always warm, delicious, and consistently good. Could have sworn I had already written a review for this place?  The Thai curry and soups are perfect. The place gets super full daily around noon, so come a little before or after that time for the best service. Very consistent and great quality flavors.

Driving back from Tampa to Orlando, I always see that billboard with Parksdale Farm Market with that pic of strawberry shortcake, and it calls to me like I'm a stranded sailor beckoned by a siren song. 

Stopped in yesterday to try a great strawberry milkshake. There is a summer treat menu in effect, so pineapple and strawberry dole whip but no shortcake right now. It's fine, but the people ahead of me were disappointed. However, the dole whip and the milkshakes are both worth a stop in. 

Enjoyed the Cajun hot boiled peanuts, picked up some meyer lemon & blood Orange pepper jelly, rhubarb preserves, strawberry preserves, and a loaf of award winning strawberry bread (ahem, it's cake!). There is a cute picnic table area to sit and enjoy treats and take a pic in the strawberry chair. Was a fun stop between Tampa and Orlando perfect for some local product and cool treats. Would like to visit again during spring and the be there for the Plant city strawberry festival.

A great place of lunch! Love to come here for lunch and get the pizza & salad special. The salad is a nice, heaping plate of romaine with a lovely house balsamic or Cesar dressing. The pizza is a nice flatbread style with ample cheese, my favorite! Definitely check this place out if your in the area and hungry.

Loved it. Friendly people. Portion large like all typical Vietnamese Restaurants. Two people can eat lunch  for $7.50.
Best Indian food in Metro Philadelphia.  If it was in the city, you would not get reservation.  Moderately priced wonderful restaurant.

10 (or was it 20 ) years back it was one of my favorite restaurant,  I have not gone back for last five years as the experience was not pleasant.  Tried again  -  just feels dated, pricey and food is very ordinary.  Not going again
Yes modern with hip crowd and pricey but some of the food is terrific that I go there for special occasions.  Nice vegeterian options
Really nice north Indian food served with class in NJ suburb.  If this was in Philly center city,  it wold be difficult to get reservation.

Food is okay but I will never go again!

Lunch buffet  - half the items were not filled in time.  Bread is suppose to be served on table side. new to Indonesian so may not be best person to judge.  Tested like Thai - ordered only one entree for lunch.

The best new restaurant of 2015.  Absolutely fabulous.  Can't wait to go again.  BYOB.  Smallish so call to make reservation.

Went second time and lowered the rating for Summer Menu  - still very good but Spring Menu was amazing

Distrito was one of my favorite restaurant in Philadelphia.  Couple months back we could not get reservation in the Philadelphia city so we went to Moorestown, NJ and were extremely disappointed.  We did not care for menu or quality of food.  However,  we Assumed the standard it Moorestown New Jersey restaurant was not as good.  Yesterday we went to Philadelphia location and menu was simian to Mrestwon Menu,  All interesting items were gone replaced with Burrito and Enchilada etc.  Most vegeterain options were gone..  Those  that were available were poorly executed that includes Chilango Chop, Huarache De Hongos, Esquites , Churos .  Corn Bread and Soups have been gone for a long time.  Not going again !
Very ordinary. Will not be going again. South Indian Restaurant which did served ordinary South Indian food and terrible North Indian food
We ordered two different variety and both were semi dry ( although description says creamy).  No crusty cheese - just awful pre-made toppings.  I will not be going again ever!

I have been there few times already. Fast Indian food in nice environment and very reasonable price.  There is sometime inconsistency in food preparation especially Paneer  but these are delicious.  Loving the concept !
Fast food -  falafel and middle eastern food.  I probably will not be going again unless I am in rush and don't want something cheap

vqzWERrURYgK1-kmHheaxA.review_text: Love, love, love this place!  They have amazing sandwiches with some of the best meats and cheeses in town. Everything I've gotten here has been delicious!  Sooo good!

Eat your heart out Starbucks!  San Giorgi's  has amazing coffee, delectable pastries, and excellent customer service!  Probably my favorite coffee shop in all of Tucson.  Try one of their blended drinks- you won't be sorry ;)
Great lunch spot!  Food came out fast and it tasted wonderful!  Large portions too so had leftovers for later :)

Oh my goodness- this place is amazing!!  The food was EXCELLENT-- there were three of us who went and we all sampled each other's food... did not try one thing that wasn't scrumptious.  Best Arnold Palmer in town too btw- their lemonade is delicious!  I got the Gruyere stuffed burger... need I say more??  Also their grilled cheese sandwich and tomato soup was heavenly-- along with their waffles and berry compote.  Seriously go try this place out!  You won't be disappointed :)

Looks like a Taco stand- is NOT a Taco stand- but some of the best middle eastern food I've had in Tucson.  Service is attentive, friendly and fast!  The gyro was amazing, tzatziki phenomenal, rice flavorful and the salad outstanding.  Would come again just even for the salad!  Definitely try this place if you're even slightly in the area.

3.5 stars.  My husband's shredded beef burrito was very sweet and there wasn't much meat.  The salsa was a little bland too.  The saving grace was their chicken - very moist white meat that was way better than Chipotle's in my opinion.  Worth a try - some might be really into all the sweet/savory dishes they have.

Amazing drinks!  And a drive thru??  Yes please!  Have tried their mocha, power coffee, hazelnut latte and caramel macchiato - all are delectable.  Maybe the best coffee place in town?  And our son loves to get the kids mooka- iced chocolate milk with whipped cream, chocolate drizzle and animal crackers eep!
Very unorganized and slowwwwwwwwwwwww.  Save yourself the time and frustration and go somewhere else

LOVE this place!  Go here for my birthday every year and for any special occasion - great atmosphere and the food is amazing.  Have never had something I didn't like... some favorites are the spinach lasagna, chicken and broccoli crepes, eggs benedict, chai tea, arnold palmer (delicious lemonade makes it), soup of the days and their salads!  You can't go wrong here - and their desserts are awesome too!  A Tucson gem!

First of all - I LOVE this Tucson chain!  This is one of my favorite locations too.  The food is always wonderful and the service friendly and fast.  These sandwiches are more than say, Subway, but you get what you pay for... and that is a gourmet sandwich with high quality meat, bread, cheese and toppings. 

I've had soo many sandwiches off of their board and while all are wonderful my favorite still remains the Unforgettable Baggins (I always get provolone on it instead of cream cheese).  It is probably my favorite sandwich to get in all of Tucson... sooo good.  The bacon, every time, is crisp and crunchy.  I hate soggy bacon and so does Baggins because they never have it :)

Their salads are also amazing - love the Cobb salad with ranch.  Another favorite is their chicken bowtie pasta (tho I do wish they'd use less sauce and more pasta so it's not so salty).  They have great iced tea - always mix mine with their raspberry lemonade to make an Arnold Palmer.  Really you can't go wrong here!

To expound on their service... I took one of my friends here who was 3 months pregnant last fall.  She ordered their Sundown Baggins, but didn't realize it had stuffing on it (totally her fault since it says so on the board).  She was having an aversion to stuffing b/c of Thanksgiving just having passed... she took one bite of her sandwich and felt queasy.  We were going to just scrape off the stuffing but one of the workers caught wind of it and immediately made her a new sandwich at no extra cost.  Our two little kids ended up finishing the one with the stuffing so it wasn't wasted.  Was very impressed that they did that tho!  

Have seen some negative reviews on here for people disliking what they ordered... if you go and for some reason do NOT like what you got... tell the staff.  Am sure they can find a way to help remedy the issue.  Doubt you'll need to though b/c really, this place is a Tucson gem!
Food was awesome - their chicken tenders are amazing!  Our server was very attentive and manager Andrew came by to check on us and see if we needed anything - excellent service!
Soooo good.  Can't beat them hot off the line  Glad this chain made its way back to Tucson

My husband's favorite restaurant in all of Tucson - best deep dish you can find (dare I say better than you can find in Chicago?!)  Their house salad is also delicious and their ranch, amazing (better than Eegee's people!)  Can't go wrong with their hot sticks or wings either.  Just go, you'll see

Sooo glad we have a place like this over here now!  Have been to the Grant location and prefer this one.  Food is amazing and reasonable - and comes out fast and hot!  Fish tacos are some of the best I've ever had.  Have also had the quesadilla, burrito, pork and barbacoa tacos, rice and beans - all are delicious.  Try this place - you won't be disappointed!
Omgosh please have the servers cover up their cleavage!  Couldn't believe how low-cut their outfits were - takes the place down from classy to a Hooters vibe eep...!

It's open again!  Thank goodness bc this place is amazing- excellent sushi rolls.  The taste in great and they have a lot of variety for the All-You-Can-Eat option.  Try this place - you won't be disappointed!

I called ahead so I wouldn't have to wait in line... when I got there I STILL had to wait in line even tho my order was ready as waiting in the wings.  What's the point of calling ahead if I'm still waiting as the 10th person in line... SMH.  Do better Little Caesars.
What a difference a new building and drive thru make - much faster service now, well done CVS.

Horrible business practices.  Have been lied to about bottles they have gotten or rather "not gotten," my friends have been threatened and treated poorly by their staff - and the employees are rude.  Especially the woman who works there.  Why do I even bother?  Probably b/c it's a local business and I like supporting local - but Total Wine far surpasses them in every area so what's the point?  Very disappointed.
Delicious food, excellent service!  This was our first time here - we will definitely be back!  The salad and garlic knots are so good!  Pizza was amazing as well - 5 stars all around!
Everything we have had from here has been excellent!  The owner / head chef is from the Netherlands- his take on cuisine is a delight to the senses given his European upbringing... highly recommend!!
