It took them a while to get us water as well and my friend never got the lemons that she requested with her water. The dining area wasn't even that busy compared to happy hour so there was really no excuse. For all of us just ordering pretty much entrees we sat there for 2 hours with glasses of water and no bread. The service could be better. Otherwise the food was pretty good.

This place is amazing! We had the garlic shrimp, octopus, calamari, jamon serrano, flatbreads and the portions were plenty. We went during restaurant week and I thought maybe 4 tapas wouldn't be enough for each person. It was more than enough and there was plenty. The sangria is unique, I like the white more than the red. The white sangria had fresh pears/apples/rosemary while the red had fruit and cinnamon. I've been to tapas in Spain and to Jaleo in DC and this place is quite authentic. I can't wait to go back. Everyone loved the food in my party. The service was quick and our drinks were always filled.

We went during restaurant week since I heard such great things about it. The concept of latin-asian fusion was interesting. The empanadas, ceviche (shrimp and oyster), pork belly buns were awesome. The shrimp noodle is definitely better than the beef noodle. You know it's a good place if the earliest reservation is 5:45. The place itself is very trendy and it's nice to see new restaurants poppping up in the area. I thought Amada was better that's why Chifa only got 4 stars.

My mother in law loves italian food so she found this place on the internet. Amazingly, on a Tuesday night it was NOT crowded and we were of two tables taken in the restaurant. We were looking for a place that served ossobucco. Let me tell you, the portions here were HUGE. We each ordered the ossobucco which came with risotto. The lamb was HUGE. We couldn't even finish and had to take it to go. The atmosphere was romantic. We had the tomato soup which was sooo fresh and tasty and the tomato/mozzarella salad. All the portions were decently sized. I have been to Italy and had their ossobucco and have never been able to find anything like it in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia, but now my searching is done. When i want a huge chunk of meat with marrow this is my place. The prices were very reasonable.

Our waiter was strange and mumbled to himself a lot, that was the only problem I had with the place.

We went to this place 6 years ago and just recently. It has changed ownership and recently renovated. It is very trendy now and the decor is much nicer and open than before. The seafood was fresh. I really wanted the lobster bisque and they ran out for the night which was a disappointment. I had the clam chowder instead which was good, but I really wanted that lobster bisque. I would like to go back to try out their happy hour. It's nice to have a fresh seafood place in the vicinity. Plus they have a great lobster roll, just like from Boston.

I read the reviews before I went. I've been to quite a few Brazilian steakhouses and I thought there was quite a variety of meat on a Tuesday night. They don't list this online but they do have filet mignon wrapped in bacon. The salad bar was fresh and the place was actually quite crowded. I like how they bring this small sidedishes like fried polenta and these croquettes which were yummy. The service was actually quite decent unlike the other remarks I've seen. What is great is if you go to the website you get a $25 off coupon and you don't miss out on much if you use it. It's 39.50 per person and we ended up paying $55 for lots of meat and salad bar for 2 people! I would give it a try. I haven't been to Fogo de Chao but if you're a meat lover and want a nice deal, get the coupon and head over there. They also send these great emails for discounts.

I thought I would have a great steak. I tried the aged steak. It was okay. I think maybe I should have tried the filet mignon instead. The sides were great. The green beans were slightly salty but the creamed spinach and mashed potatoes were good. We had the calamari which was average and the cold seafood platter which was really good. The crabcakes were good. We did bump into Mayor Nutter on the way out which was coincidence.

The restaurant is in a cute area of Rittenhouse. We went for restaurant week. I think if I ordered these separately it might be somewhat costly and the portions were on the smaller side. I had the duck penne, which i thought was salty and a little too saucy. The other people in my group had the salmon, hanger steak and the tuna which looked good, but small in portions. The fried calamari on my salad was a little salty as well. My husband liked the vietnamese meatballs. I thought the ambience was modern and nice and the service was impeccable.

My friend and I went during Philadelphia Sips thinking we would get some of the specials, but you had to be at the bar to get the drink specials. They had a different food selection than at Amada. I can't explain how the two are different but both good in their own ways. The presentation of the food were great and the portions were sized for 3 people to sample. I would like to go back and try the chef's tasting. Another one for Jose Garces!

We went for Sunday Brunch. I noticed online there was a 3 course 14.95 Cuban Brunch Get-away which you should ask the waiter for the menu because I don't they reveal it otherwise. Boy was this a deal! First course I had the churros and guava jam...which the churros were FRESHLY made and had just enough cinnamon and sugar. The guava jam was unique which I also spread on the bread. Yes the mango butter was good. If you're in a salty mood the black bean soup was good too, you can taste the ham stock. At my table, my husband had the chorizo omelette which came with a side of salad and he picked the plantains which he enjoyed very much. My friend had the crab omelette with a side of home fries and yuca hashbrown. I had the ropa vieja. The portions were supple and more than enough I had to take mine home. I am definitely coming back for brunch to try the other omelettes. We each had the cuban cafe with coconut milk. VERY VERY YUMMY.

i'm in love. i've been to a lot of vietnamese restaurants in this city which most are the same pho, summer rolls, broken rice but this place has a wide variety of stuff and it's very affordable, plus free parking when you can find it!. It's hard to tell the difference between places but I think if you want to try new stuff and have authentic vietnamese food this is the place to go! I'm definitely going back and trying their other vietnamese items. The service is pretty decent for asian places (we're not known for our politeness).

Even better the second time around. Tried their new prix fixe menu with the vietnamese meatballs as an appetizer while my husband and friend had the kobe beef carpaccio. All very good. Then we did the beef short rib....very tender and melts in your mouth. Of course we ended with the choc souffle which was just as orgasmic as I remembered. I was tempted to try the pumpkin mousse but why miss out on the choc souffle. The great thing about the night was that it was my friend's first night in Philly and we were talking so much we didn't realize our entree took almost an hour to get to us. The waitress apologized and the manager came to our table and said he could take off a discount off our bill. I was like well we already got the prix frixe why don't we get some drinks instead?? He offered us 2 free drinks each = total 6 and boy were we happy campers. That made our night and the food was to die for :) Can't wait for next season's prix fixe menu.

Well...you might miss this place going past Washington Ave but I read the reviews looking for authentic Mexican food and decided it was worth a try. I got the 3 taco combo which is sooo affordable and had the pastor, steak and chorizo. My husband had this big mishmosh of a platter which was only 15 bucks of beef, chicken, shrimp with peppers with fresh tortillas. Very flavorful and the corn tortillas were great. The chips and salsa were plenty with their mole salsa and salsa verde. I would definitely go back because 1. it's affordable 2. it's good.

The service was impeccable. I had the steak trio. The seafood towers were amazing and fresh. The decor is amazing and I can't wait to see it in the movie they were shooting a couple months ago. The food is pricey but the quality shows through. Definitely try the bread pudding, it is like a warm chocolate cookie with walnuts. MMMM....

Tria had a beer tapping for Pliny the Younger. It was severely unorganized with two lines around the corner and they were allowing "friends" of people who were already inside going in. The managers, or people who pretended to be managers went outside to apologize. When 6 people left after they had their beer they didn't allow 6 people to enter. The hostess, though nice, had no idea what to do with the eager customers outside. Two snobs decided oh since we're already inside, let's get our friend inside, who didn't even wait in line after they were already done with their beer and decided to sit at the bar after standing and just take up space. After waiting in line after 50 minutes, the keg was out. It was completely unorganized and a fiasco. I think the food is overpriced and I would have never gone to this place unless it was for this stupid tapping. They should know approximately how many people they can serve and allot for that amount. Instead I as well as a bunch of other beer connoisseurs waited outside in the rain for almost an hour for nothing watching people push through the line without standing in it because they had a "friend" inside. 

Completely unorganized. The only good thing was that the Garces Trading Company was a block away and they have much better food. 

Would never come back. I've had their food before. It's small and way overpriced for some toast and tomatoes. There are much better places in the city with better service to go to.

The guacomole was pretty good and addicting. We had the chef's table and the first couple of plates were mostly nachos, quesadillas, flour like stuff, beans and cheese stuff. The good stuff was at the end and by that time I was very full. The shrimp skewers were good and reminded me of the garlic shrimp from amada. My husband said the steak was good. Too bad I filled up on chips. Had lots of drinks and their margaritas, especially the Jefe was good. I had the horchata alcoholic drink was strangely tangy and wasn't that good but must be my taste and my expectations. I had the grapefruit margarita and pineapple margaritas as well. They should start making other kinds like mango and strawberry :) Otherwise it was a good experience and would go back. Recommend the karaoke room if anyone wants to bring a group along with them. We had a blast in there.

This place is a hidden treasure in South Philly. It sits on 11th street hidden behind a Vietnamese shopping center. We have been there 2 times and enjoy their beer selection. They have a wide selection of Belgian beers and even have a sampler for like 5-8 bucks. Things to try are their spicy chorizo mussels, which I think is the best I've had. It's flavorful, and you just want to use the bread to sop up the sauce. For brunch you can get 1000 open table points which is halfway towards a $20 gift certificate from open table. It has a cozy atmosphere with a smokeless fireplace in the middle of the room. Parking is doable in that area. It's a really nice hidden gem in South Philly. Can't wait to try their happy hour.

So my husband walked by this place so many times we decided to try it for happy hour. They have a great happy hour for prices in Rittenhouse. For $6 you can get a pretty decently sized lobster roll, which was actually two including a small side of fries. We had fresh oysters for 75 cents each. Their drinks were like $6-$6.50 cocktails and they were yummy. My husband had the Caribbean lemonade and I had a strawberry mojito. All very yummy. Their fresh biscuits were great. I think everybody else had the same idea since it was hard but not impossible to find a seat at the bar. One lady next to me recommended going to their website to sign up for their mailing list. After I signed up I got a $15 coupon for my next dinner and supposedly they give you a coupon for your birthday. I really enjoyed their wide selection of appetizers during happy house, ranged from 6-8 dollars and it included a lot of seafood. This was great. Can't wait to try it for dinner.

Now this place is a random neighborhood joint away from Rt 1 in northeast Philly. You would never expect it. It's a peruvian restaurant tucked away a couple of blocks away from Rt 1. I went with some coworkers and the portions were very generous. You can tell when you are the only non-Hispanic person in the room and the waitresses can only speak Spanish that this is the real deal. When you order the ceviche the portion is HUMUNGOUS. I loved the tostones. I'm not a big plantain banana fan, but these were to die for. Lightly salted and crispy, they are yummy. Next time I want to try their tostones filled with chicken or meat. If you love seafood, their seafood platters are plentiful. My brother had the paella valenciana and it was filled with lots of chicken and seafood. For $18 it was huge and we brought it back home. The guy next to us had some HUGE platter of calamari and shrimp and I forgot what it was called but that's what I want next time. Sounds like jaleo or something like that. It is slightly out of the way but you know what...it's worth the trip. Tax is included with each entree and it even has a full serviced bar. I think el balconcito II may be closer off interstate 95, so maybe I'll try that next time. 

Again, pretty damn good for philadelphia and a neighborhood gem. You can easily find parking on the street.

This place shows you that this area is growing. True, some people loiter outside of the Chinese place across the street but not so much here. The family here is nice and hard working. I'm a fan of bubble tea and I really like how they make it with fresh fruit. It's a family run place and the kids help out which I think is great. I haven't tried the sandwiches but they look really affordable. I've had their salads and fruit salad and they are loaded. It's great to have a neighborhood deli just to stop by and have some Breyer's ice cream or a soda. They have other some other items for cleaning and lots of snacks. I really do try and support them as much as I can.
I used to go here once in a while to get some $2 dim sum to go but lately I haven't seen them there! Where are you guys!!!

I read the reviews and decided to give this place a try since I've been to taqueria veracruzana and la lupe. I thought it was average. There was no one else in the restaurant except for us and the service was average, nothing to complain about. The waitress never asked what we wanted to drink. I thought the el pastor tacos were ok. The complimentary salsa (red) was way too spicy and the salsa verde didn't have much flavor and chips cost extra there. Even though it wasn't that expensive $1, it's still the point that the other two places include unlimited chips and their salsas were much better tasting. I judge a mexican place on their salsa and chips. The chips were also sort of stale.

I think everyone agrees taco tuesdays are what drives the customers in. I like how you can try a variety of different tacos for a good price and the chips and salsa are good. I've tried their chicken burrito special and it's good too which I think included beans and rice, but I may have been mistaken. They also deliver! (not their special tacos though). It's worth trying and pretty authentic. The service is pretty good too. I highly recommend it. I have definitely gone back and it's where I would prefer to go for mexican in the city.

My friends and I decided to splurge and go and finally try vetri. It was quite an experience. We had the grand tasting menu. They made an attempt to give each of us something different. It wasn't a HUGE amount of food but it was satiating because of the small courses. I have to admit that I think most places undercook risotto and this place I think got it right, at least for my taste buds. My husband had the wine pairing with it which I thought every wine was very tasty. I am over 9 months pregnant and the sommelier gave me an extra two small glasses to try. The service was impeccable as well as the food. It is pricey which was expected but I think it was worth at least trying once. The food was fresh and appetizing, even though some of the stuff was exotic it was all good. I have nothing to complain about, each course was great!

I've been living in South Philly for the almost 2 years now and there are lots of great vietnamese places but until I found this I haven't been hooked on any of the Chinese places and I'm Taiwanese. I finally found a place that makes my favorite dish, mapo tofu! I'm hooked. I've gone back at least once a week since. Their chinese broccoli with chicken is very good. I have yet to eat in the restaurant since I'm just buying food for myself for the week but the portions are decent and ingredients are fresh and not overly sauced American-style. I need to bring my husband and family there sometime to try their stews and other dishes.

I finally went there for brunch. It's definitely a great place for a foodie. They have a really nice variety of different foods and it's nice to see something different. I've been to the Four Seasons which is just as pricey but not unique. They have a great seafood raw food section which my husband loves oysters. Their shrimp cocktail was huge. Everything was done very French style with portions on spoons. I love how the main entrees (hot) were in their kitchen. Since I can't have anything raw the person at the meat carving station cooked the meat well done for me. You just take your time there trying all the different foods and it's nice to see some different items. They had wagyu beef (very yummy) to gnocchi with escargot. It was nice not too see like all these cheap items like eggs, sausage, and breads. You can tell people were there to really just try the food itself and not stuff yourself with the muffins and breads since it looked like no one really went there.

The desserts were amazing. They had a chocolate fountain and gelato but the actual little cakes were worth every calorie! This place you really could stuff yourself but you really focus on the taste of everything. It's quite an experience that I think if you have the privilege to splurge go for it.

We got there at 11:30 to meet some friends there and the first thing the waitress said was "we are not serving food until noon because the kitchen staff isn't here yet." what restaurant does that? Then the waitress came at noon and said the kitchen staff had to prepare the food. So we waited an hour to get our food. I had to ask for something to snack on and she gave us house chips which had no flavor and I had to add salt to. Then when we ordered we asked for the Marguerite pizza and she came back and said they couldn't make that. What can they do? The food was okay but when you've been waiting an hour for the kitchen staff to arrive anything would be good. I just think it is lunch time and if you run a restaurant you would apologize and comp people something like a round of drinks. Ridiculous. I wouldn't go back. They have no idea how to run a business.

Went to their nye party and booked the VIP. First of all they mentioned a chefs selection of hors d oeuvres and tapas. What we got for $125 pp not including a 10% liquor tax and a 20% gratuity which totaled an extra 30% to our bill, was pitas and hummus, burnt crostini with this crappy ass apple and cheese dip, fries!!, and overcooked empanadas. disgusting. And disgusted. So i should have just booked the open bar. I could vomit thinking about how gross that was. For the money we paid I expected more. They probably though they would get away with crappy pod by getting people drunk. And the waitress wouldn't serve us water we asked for it. The is why we all got sick.

Very authentic and prices are reasonable. Naomi tofu is made with silken tofu and extra spicy. Soup dumplings are fresh and delicious. Don't be fooled by the location next to the Chinatown bus station, it's amazing food. We get it here every time we visits

y-BbYIT__p4e09CW6hws6Q.review_text: Great dining room and ambiance. Scallops were great. Soup was creative. I'll be back for sure. Major upgrade.
Awesome view but just average food. The side of pasta was far better than the steak or seabass. Worth one visit though if in Stl
This place is just terrible from top to bottom, start to finish. If you gave me a $100 gift certificate to eat here I'd donate it to someone I don't like.
Garlic chicken was literally one of the best things I've ever had at a Mexican restaurant. However, minus 1 star for average salsa.
The Last Holdout says it is actually much better...and I hate to admit it but the pizza tracker is entertaining.
Prime rib sandwich is incredible. A bit expensive for a lunch and wish more toppings were available.

I've eaten here over 25 times, and this is my routine: canneloni appetizer (best thing in St. Louis, seriously), house salad, 5 loaves of bread dipped in the best balsamic outside of Sicily, then go with the seabass, filet (yes, filet at an Italian restaurant), the veal trio (not on menu), or rack of lamb. Instead of pasta side dish, get another canneloni to accompany the entree.

Too full for dessert, so get an Irish coffee.

Thank me later.
accidentally ate lunch here once because it is across the street from my office. Oops.
Great dining experience from the cocktails to the tableside guac, but the red snapper entree I had was absolutely sensational. I keep forgetting to go back...

New to the neighborhood and had no idea about this gem. In seriousness we have eaten here 4 times this week. I've had three different things and all were delicious. Try the Neno's Special or the Dream sandwich or....anything!

Eat here once a week because we can walk home . The guys that run it- Fernando, Flacco and company act like every guest is family and the fiesta never stops. We've tried 20 different things and never once been disappointed. Their house margarita stands up to most Mexican restaurants premium. It's an event so be prepared...

This place is ridiculously good and I don't even like ice cream. It is a little on the slow side but it's all part of the process. I should give it one less star because now I don't really like other ice cream or frozen yogurt places...oh well.
Hidden gem. We tried a pizza, a pasta, and the scallops and all three were tremendous.

Can't believe it took me so long to try this place! It took me 10 minutes to order because I wanted 15 different things. 
Next time I'm getting the giant sampler because everything looked tremendous.

Craft did it again. Good luck getting in though. We ended up sitting at the bar bc the place was FULL at 530 on a Thursday. You rallly can't wrong here but I'd go with the pasta and meat/chicken. The chicken is similar to the chicken at Taste (best in the world) but modified enough that it's a must try. The ravioli is similar to the pistachio ravioli at Pastaria but same scenario I just stayed. Oh, and the bread

Nixta nailed it. It's so different from anything else in St Louis that there's nothing to compare it to. We tried 4 things which were all great and will try 4 new things next time without hesitation because it seems like they can do no wrong.

y6PIysm_WZpeqUl2PZRYsA.review_text:
Service was very friendly 
Handle issue with orders like a champ
Even though they are working out the issue of a new place....made are experience awesome....
I have been to a lot of new restaurants and it is usually a bad experience....
B Spot is great!!! And can only get better!!

Great Service from Scott....dirty silverware all silverware 
Pizza ok would not call it wood grilled...maybe gas grilled
Savanna and Madison both waited on me. What a great combo. Watched basketball had a great wrap suggested by Savanna..crisp chicken wrap and tattered tots
I have always wanted to try Poutine and Craft St had pulled pork poutine on menu. And that's what I had for lunch on Saturday. It was really good....
Fun place to meet friends and watch ball games or live music at night. Good bar food, better than most. Good Beer selection and drink specials

Went there every Thursday for the last year for lunch today was my last day.... they do not care about there customers...could care less attitude 
It's very unfortunate I always try to support local business owners...I will never set foot in there again
Found a new place for my Thursday lunch with my Dad...awesome waitress very friendly and cares about her customers...looking forward to lunch next Thursday there...and the food was very good
I ordered a large vegetable Pizza extra crisp & large Greek salad made by Neil and Stormy it was awesome.....
The buffet a lunch was very good. The Restaurant was clean and the people were friendly I will make it a regular lunch stop
What a great place...Always friendly...the Brats are awesome and the German Chocolate Cake is marvelous...try to go there 3times a month

Clam chowder was cold microwave made tougher 
Smoked tuna was good 
$17 is a lot for what I got
Ivy was the worst waitress...never around for my best friends birthday dinner This place is horrible for a Celebration.....ivy was the worst service l have had will never come back
Kitchen and wait staff was overwhelmed never around for my best friends birthday dinner This place need help for a Celebration
Dominic is the best always take great care of my father and I at lunch. The food is awesome no matter what I choose off the menu....tasty and fresh. Best Italian Food in the State

y6nCJj6kP4ynm1AvGlcmkg.review_text: The food and beer was absolutely incredible... The wait staff was attentive and on top of it in regards to services. The place was clean, including the bathroom. I highly recommend the baked macaroni and cheese as a starter... it was out of this world.

We went to Silver Peak Restaurant and Brewery for a late lunch/early dinner and it was truly outstanding. I have never been so impressed with the quality of the food, service and price before. I thoroughly enjoyed everything that we ordered from the appetizers through the dessert. We ordered the black bean nachos and clam chowder as an appetizer. My partner ordered a beer sampler and I ordered this incredible drink called a Citrus Solstice (it was strong and refreshing). We ordered the lamb burger and a curry dish, which he thoroughly enjoyed. The service was exceptional, the food was delicious and the bathroom was extremely modern and clean. We will hit this place up again next time we visit Reno...

We found this incredible place while on vacation in the area in May of 2016. While aroma labels itself Mediterranean, it is more specifically Lebanese fare. Located in the nondescript Valley Forge towers, it's a bit off the beaten path, The inside was comfortable and the service was truly exceptional. We had a lot of questions in regards to the menu and she took the time to explain things and offered her recommendations, which were excellent. The food was absolutely outstanding with flavors that seemed to come off the plate. I will certainly go there again if we ever find ourselves in this part of the proverbial woods again.

We had to try this place while in the area on vacation in May 2016. We had heard so much about this place and even saw it featured on travel channel. Located in the middle of Reading Terminal, this place was a lot of fun. We got the pulled pork sandwich, it came with broccoli rabe and provolone cheese, nothing fancy but the pulled pork was delicious. I highly recommend having it with the cheese. We actually visited this place twice while in the area, because my partner neglected to have cheese on his first sandwich (big mistake, get the cheese). The seating in this place is a little crazy, especially at lunch time. Also, if you do not like crowds or standing in line... you might avoid this place during the peak lunch time rush.

We visited this place while on vacation in May of 2016 and I fell head over hills in love with something called the "Whoopie Pie." It was probably the best thing that I have ever had. I want to travel back to Philly, just to visit this place again. Located in Reading Terminal Market, this shop is right in the center and there's a ton of dessert competition around the whole place. They also had a few other desserts such as pies, pumples, and cakes in addition to coffee and teas, but all you need to know is the whoopie pie, since that's what they're known for.

I had to try this place while in the area on vacation in May 2016. This was my first true Philly cheese steak and it was magical.  Located in the middle of Reading Terminal, this place was a lot of fun. I hit it during the peak lunch rush and so I had to stand in line for about 30-minutes (but it was so worth it). The seating in this place is a little crazy, especially at lunch time. Also, if you do not like crowds or standing in line... you might avoid this place during the peak lunch time rush. There are many places to get a cheese steak sandwich in Philly, but when you are at the Reading Market, stop by Carmen's.

We found this cute little place while in the area on vacation in May 2016. I am serious this place was just plain precious. Lots of seating.  A good place to go with friends for some sweets (a virtual diabetic coma just waiting to happen, but I took extra insulin and so I was up to the challenge). The service was so above and beyond sweet, just like what they were serving up. They were busy and there was a long line, but when we got to the register to order, we had questions and the young lady at the register was so friendly and willing and wanting to help us make a decision. I will certainly return.

We stopped for lunch in Reno at this interesting German inspired place. We enjoyed a beer sampler of different German beers, and we both ordered different sausage plates, which were delicious. The buns were a little lacking (like they were like cut in half), but then the sausage is what is important in the end, and they were delicious.  The place had German music playing and actually made you feel like you might be visiting some obscure German location. The beer cheese was good, but served cold which was different. The servers were polite, efficient, and friendly.

We went to all you can eat Sushi at the Oceano Seafood restaurant located inside the Peppermill Resort and Spa Casino. We sat at the sushi counter and the person making the sushi was extremely attentive and efficient. The rolls were all delicious, and freshly prepared to order.  I thought that the other wait staff could have been a bit more attentive, but it was very busy in there being that it was Saturday night. We enjoyed multiple rolls, and appetizers and it was an incredible deal.

We found this cute little place for dinner.  This place was really only English in name only, as it would seem that they really did not serve any U.K. beers. The food was delicious and the waitress was incredibly friendly, efficient, and made the experience even better. This would be a fun place to be a local at if we lived closer.

We found this awesome ice cream shop called, Black Rock Dessert. They made these most creative and coolest milkshakes that were like art pieces. The staff were attentive, efficient, and extremely friendly. They have an incredible ice cream flavor called, Reno911 which is a mixture of coffee and doughnuts, it was incredible.

The food at the brunch was super delicious, as was the mimosas. I finally had to stop drinking those as one of us had to drive. I like how they converted the buffet into the staff serving you the food, I kind of prefer that. There was such a wonderful and wide selection of food, it was all freshly prepared and extremely delicious. Our table staff person was so very attentive, polite and friendly.

We tried this place while visiting Reno and were very impressed by the food and beverages. The one thing that was awkward and this is probably a staffing or COVID thing, is that I would have liked more time to actually review the menu. You enter and immediately order at the counter, with no real time to look through the menu. We did like what we ordered, but I have to admit that I just picked the first biscuit and gravy option that I saw, there were probably other items that I would have liked to have had the option to ponder. Perhaps even posting a menu board would be helpful. The food was efficiently delivered to the table and it was delicious. You do have to bus your own table at the end of your meal, which is a little different.

We tried this place while we were waiting for a comedy show to start next door and it was delicious. We told the server that we were on a tight schedule and he got our food and check out to us efficiently. The food and beer was delicious, and the server was extremely polite and attentive. We will certainly return next time we are in the area.

We tried this place while visiting Reno, and were blown away by the food and beer. Our server was extremely efficient, polite, and attentive. I never had to ask for a refill of my cherry coke (which she made), she kept bringing them. The food was absolutely delicious, and freshly prepared to order. The place was clean, and the bathrooms well stocked (that says a lot about a business). We tried multiple beers all were not disappointed, they had several that were extremely unique. We will certainly be back again.

This absolutely one of our favorite places to go for dinner while in Reno. On this last visit, we both literally filled our selves to the point of almost being sick with sushi, but it is soooo extremely good. It is made on site, and like I said totally delicious. Our server was polite, efficient, and extremely attentive. I am just so sad that I was too full to try the lobster bisque (as it is included with the all you can eat sushi), I will certainly order that first during our next visit.

Went looking for Melagrano and stumbled across Audrey Claire. VERY LOUD inside as the outside tables had over an hour wait. Very pleasant menu and wait staff and service was very good. 

Ordered the brussell sprouts for an appetizer and were not cooked enough. had a hard time slicing them with a knife. The Trout with crab meat and spinach was good but a bit over salted. Would try again but wasn't overjoyed with first visit.

Lots of mediocre meat for a lot of cash. The coupon thru the end of august made the entire meal digestible.

If you ever been on cruise ship, this is it. From the decor to the gobs of mediocre food, this is a cruise on land. The only thing missing was the band and the rocking back and forth. 

Fago is better but Capital and Palm are hands down better than both. who needs all of the excess food anyway. If that is what you want, go to the Chinese Buffet on Columbus Blvd for a lot less.

We went for  walk and stumbled across this pleasant looking trattoria in Queen village. The service was spotty but the waiter was very pleasant when available. 

The sign posted outside said it was pizza night so we thought it would be a nice way to get a lite bite. We selected the Positano pizza which had carmelized onions, mushrooms and chicken in a light tomato sauce. What a mistake.

The pizza was dry, the chicken was bland, the onions weren't carmelized and the dough tasted like it came from Shoprite.

Although our taste for pizza revolves around Taccanellis, Mara's and Mam Palma's, which are the best of the best, this place is a far cry and ranks with the pizza at the Wachovia Center. Awful!

We have been to Chloe several times and have yet to be dissapointed. Although a bit cramped and noisy during busy times, the food, atmosphere and waitress service is well worth putting up with some minor invconveniences.

If you are a BBQ rib lover, this is the place. Although not your typical rib joint, these are meaty, messy, tasty and over the top in flavor, quality and quantity. coupled with the Mac and Cheese and you can;t go wrong. Also at the top of the hit parade are the Scallops which are large, browned to perfection and delicious.

The beet salad is a great way to start off the meal along with a few bottles of your favorite vino and you have a complete meal. Although not a dessert lover, the Mrs. loved the slection.

They don't take cards, reservations and sometimes close without notice to go "fishing" . You can;t go wrong with Chloe for a nice meal in Olde City.

Dined at Melograno for the second time and have yet to be dissapointed. Start with the antipasto for two. That and some bread and wine would make a great meal by itself. Assorted smoked Italian meats, fresh roasted veggies, assorted spereads and it is just heaven. 

For the main course, the Griglio Mista, assorted seafoood on a bed of mashed, creamed potatoes is delectable. The pasta witht he shredded Guinea Hen is also a great choice. The pasta is home made and the sauce a perfect complement. The chicken dish with mozzarella is a good choice.

A bit noisy, long waits on weekends make it a 4 star but well worth the inconvenience.

We have visited this establishment twice. The food is very flavorful but HOT and SPICY! My wife dislikes fires in er food and ordered #1 level. The cold sesame noodles are excellent. The level 6 spicy disk was good but hot. Have plenty of water available.

although the food is good, the place is dirty, disorganized and the wait staff is slow and not very attentive.

If you like spicy dishes, this is the place.

After reading the review in Philadelphia Scene, we decided to check it out for an early Saturday night dinner and drink. Having been a fan of David Ansil and his previous establishments, PIF and Ansil, we thought it would be terrific like the review stated. Boy, were we wrong.

The place is cavernous and must be a hangout for young professionals who wouldn't appreciate fine food but lots of alchohol as the seating for dinner is limited but there is  lots of room for drinking.

Even so, the food is what David is known for and this place was a huge disappointment. We tried the beat salad which tasted like it came out of a harvard beet jar from Super Fresh.

Next, we went for the grilled chirozo sandwich which was two shriveled pieces of overcoooked sausage on a slice of Italian bread with some pine nuts and wilted greens. Not very good. My spouse went with the Grilled Eggplant Parm sandwich which was awful, soggy, lacked cheese flavor and had enough peppers in it to burn your throat.

There are lots of great new neighborhhod pubs and bistros that offer terrific food (Adsum, Pub and Kitchen, 20 Manning, etc;) and I would go to any of these instead of returning to this gastro nightmare. David, try another PIF if you want to satisfy customers and make some legit income.

We have been to this place at least a dozen times. It was always excellent. However, the last two times, it appears that ownership has changed hands (everyone there are new faces) and so has the food.

We always get the salt baked shrimp and the dish has gotten smaller as have the shrimp. The hot and sour soup was the best and now is just OK and the General Tso's is not suited for even a private, let alone a general.
Even the spare ribs, which were the BEST are now greasy, boney and fatty. "Where's the meat?"

It is hard to find excellent Chinese food in a pleasing environment, which this place now doesn't offer either. I suggest Sang Kee or Lee How Fuk for a better experience.

They lost a loyal customer.

We visited JG this past Saturday expecting the same wonderful experience we get at all of Jose's establishments. Boy, was this a dissapointment. We have been to all of his places several times and this was unlike any of our other visits.

At first, we were seated at a table right at the entrance to the restauarant which is like sitting in an office building lobby. (actually, it is in the lobby)
Then we asked to be moved and we were located under the escalator on raised bar stools which were like sitting on a park bench. with other tables vacant, we asked to be seated in one of the empty booths but were told that they were reserved. We made this reservation 3 months ago! finally, after asking the manager, we were moved to a nice location.

The food was good but not on the same level as Tinto, Amada, Distrito or even our favorite Garces joint, GTC. The wine was overpriced (Archery Summit 2007 cuvee for $152. btl. is outrageous!) 
The dishes were skimpy as Tapas style plates go (2 scallops for $21.) and only afew dishes were outstanding. (try the chicken dish, the beignets, flatbread pizza and the chanterelles.)

After visitng all of Jose's places, this is the one place that we won't be returning.

Brought my wife and two adult kids here for daughter's birthday dinner. Have eaten here several times before and always good. This time was also very good. The special Veal Chop was superb as was the asparagus rolled in prosciutto and shrimp in balsmaic vinegar. Evryone else's meal was great too and very reasonable. The bread is hot and delicious with the olive oil tapenade accompanying it.

A few notes:
We wanted to order the special of grilled striped bass, shrimp and calamari that the waiter suggested. When ordered, the waiter came back after taking our order to the kitchen and told us that the fish wasn;t done yet. How can it be a special and at 7PM they say it wasn't doen yet?

At dessert time, we ordered the suggested fabulous Tirmisu and once agin, the waiter came back and told us the dessert was still frozen and couldn;t be served. Weird as the table next to us ordered it and received it about a half hour earlier.

Even with these two weird instances, I would still recommend this establishment.

Ish is the best! Don't waste your time standing in line across the street but head to  The Ish for a treat! Opening soon up the street to a larger sit down venue

Watch out Jims!

Went here for dinner on way to Flyers game. No one there the entire time we dined and left at 6:30.

The entire family of the proprietor sat in the small dining room watching us, playing on their phones, taking care of kids and walking around a screaming kid. Not very appetizing. The place is dirty and food was under our table when we sat down;the place gave us the creeps!

The food was ample and delicious but I guess you get what you pay for. The quality of the chicken was noticeably of low quality as was the seafood. The vegetables were good and the papaya salad was awesome.

I would do take out next time or stick with Nam Phong or LeViet for similar tasting food but more appetizing environments.

Never eaten there but get take out all the time!
Fresh and healthy Meditteranean food at reasonable prices and ample servings.

Definitely recommend for a good take out offering !

Wasn't sure what to expect at a Jewish Diaspora influenced restaurant. It was AMAZING!
The price fix dinner was ample to select everlasting dishes. All were fantastic the chopped liver to the pastrami hash knish to the veal schnitzel tacos and topped off with a bacon egg cream

A must try for the adventurous diner. $$$

Interesting food offerings. Loved the pork dumplings, fried green beans, fried cauliflower and mussels, especially the dipping bread.
The pastrami bao was too chewy and mushy and the sesame noodles were spicy but too me, lacked richness in flavor.

Still a worthwhile visit and will return for the wings and more dumplings!

Good local Italian restaurant with Mediterranean flair.
Byob makes it even better

Grilled portobello with smoked mozzarella was excellent starter. Wife had caprese salad which was perfect. Entrees were Bronzino with crab meet and the other dish of shrimp and beans were very good

Reasonable and CC accepted.

Fun place in a great location. Good beer selections with adequate dining fare.
Nice environment outdoors with easy access near independence hall.

Decided last minute to try the new neighborhood restaurant. Arrived without a reservation around 6:45 on Saturday and the maitre d said he will need to squeeze us in. When we left, the tables next to us was still empty.
Pleasant Redone interior from previous tenants Coquette and Adsum.
Started with charcuterie which was good but not the best. Wife had tri tips which she enjoyed and I had the vegan mushroom burger. Could have been a bit less mushy by crusting the top. Fries were good with Siracha ketchup.
Martinis were good but not memorable. Olives need blue cheese stuffing to be excellent.Waiter didn't seem knowledgeable of menu's details.
Will try again but won't rush.

Great noodle bar with creative good offerings.
Try the wings and dumplings that are well worth the wait. The bridle sprouts are fabulous but the highlight is the brisket soup with S matzah ball
Don't forget the additional egg in the soup.

Small place but well worth a visit

Went to neighborhood new Argentinian steakhouse. Showed up without reservation but was seated promptly. First thing waiter did was to apologize for a potential long delay in food delivery as they were busy. It went all downhill from there.
 Cocktails took forever to arrive but Mgmt did  comp them. People seated after us were served their main course and we still hadn't even gotten any bread which was fine as it was awful anyway. I think it was a Wawa shortie roll cut into pieces. 
Food was adequate but unmemorable. The best dish were the empanadas but could have used a bit more filling. Salad was plain and steaks were sized well but lacked any pizzazz. Passed on the overpriced desserts and decibel levels are extreme.

Won't be returning anytime soon until they are more seasoned in their food and delivery.

Went here for the third time but first visit since remodel. Pleasant surroundings and attentive wait staff.
Appetizer of spring veggies with ricotta tartine was bland and underwhelming. The other diners ordered mussels and beet apps which were much more appetizing and tasteful.Chicken entree was very good but wife's lamb dish was just so so.

Decent BYO and won't kill the budget.

Had a dinner party for 20 people on a Sat night. Joe, Lydia and staff were very accommodating and flexible; from bringing our own selection of spirits, to our own birthday cake and table flowers. They are the best!
The food was delicious and feeding 20 people off the menu seemed like a difficult task but they pulled it off with everyone served at once. Awesome performance by the entire staff! Everyone loved the ample servings of tasteful, delicious Italian food. Pasta, veal or seafood ( great crab cakes!) are all well prepared and good value.
Highly recommend going for an intimate dinner or a large party. They won't disappoint you!

Very tasty drawn hand or shaved noodles. Had them in stir fry and in soup.
Bol Choy and garlic is wonderful as are the steamed coconut and chicken dumplings.
Nice surroundings and CASH only but byob.

Go for it!
Went here with friends. Great food, pleasant environment and the complimentary chocolate lemoncello was the best way to finish off a terrific meal. Pork chop special was awesome!
Best sushi in CC. Great fish, excellent value and pleasant surroundings. Difficult to get in without a reservation no matter on time.

Went here to celebrate a family birthday. Fantastic environment whichever room you are seated in. High end decor and hopping on a Friday evening.
Great cocktails and the food.....awesome!
Cauliflower plate was terrific as was the crudo, pork ribs and mixto seafood starters.
Pizza was delicious and ample size to share. Large plates were the best with the brick chicken, veal cheeks and hanger steak all tasty and ample too to share.

The secret will be out on this non-fish town like establishment. You will love it!

We went for dinner Sunday night and it was delicious!
Had the cowboy steak for two with Cole slaw and beans. Awesome!
Brussels sprouts and tuna tartar was perfect starter.

Wish they had more dessert choices (2?) and a few more specials from standard menu but worth a return trip

First time trying this new establishment.
Ordered Butterfly bowl and dragon bowl. Both were excellent, fresh, tangy and ample in size. A bit more fish would have made this a 5 but still very enjoyable.
Delivery was great even during a torrential downpour. On time and even early!

Tried this small but quaint BYOB on a friends recommendation and yelp reviews. Not disappointed! Great food, varied menu, quaint space and friendly host/waiter.
The octopus, Brussels sprouts and mushroom tarting were well prepared and enjoyed by all.

The salmon entree was the finest prepared piece of fish that was perfectly done. The sea bass also was a winner.

Not dessert eaters but the pot de creme was the perfect ending to a great meal. Will be back again.....and again........and again!

Lovely new place just south of Washington near VSEC. Assorted cuisines from Sushi to Tempura to Ramen and Udon. Everything was delicious especially the Rainbow roll and Deluxe seafood Udon soup. 
Also try the Tuna Tataki salad for a starter along with the tastiest miso soup!

Interior is attractive and staff super friendly (Linda) and attentive. BYOB on top makes it s great choice!

I haven't been to this restaurant for awhile and decided to give it a try. Turned out to be a bad decision.
Ambiance is very nice and well kept over the years.
Came on a Monday eve and place was half full. 
Our waitress greeted us and took beverage order and delivered them efficiently. She asked if we decided on our dinner selections and we asked for a moment. Another bad decision by us as she disappeared for a long time! She had a large group across the restaurant and forgot about us. 
Once I tracked her down to order, she informed us that one item wasn't available. It's Monday, not busy, limited plates are offered and they didn't have pork chops. Oh well.

One guest ordered another selection of Mahi, Mahi. After about 20 minutes, the mgr. Came over to inform us that they forgot to defrost the fish and that wasn't available either. Defrost fish??

Finally, the salad arrived (comped) which was good. When dinner arrived, it was all presentable but nothing stood out as anything memorable.

In today's Philly restaurant scene, they need to step up the service and product offerings or they will be extinct, which would be a shame for a place that has survived many years. Good luck!

Good brew pub with very tasty food menu. Tried the sampler beer selection and was very good. Had the buffalo cauliflower and pork belly fries as apps and were excellent. Had the brown sugar pizza and cheesesteak pizza as entree.  Wasn't s fan of the steak pizza but overall, great beer and good grub.
Sat on side patio with our pup which was an added bonus. The flies were annoying and would suggest a catcher or something to address. Still go to the Vault! Will be back!

Avoid this place at all costs. Ordered online and sounded good. Big mistake.
I had three chicken tacos and sat in bathroom that night and morning. My wife had shrimp tacos and broke out in hives the next day. Never had them before. We shared nachos so something wasn't right.

Drs office visit, food and lost time in bathroom not worth it. Never again!

Had a very unpleasant experience with this restaurant. Made a birthday dinner reservation a month in advance on Open Table. A week before the dinner, I get a call that they booked out the restaurant for an event and couldn't accommodate us. A week before on a Saturday night is not an easy reservation to get at a good place in Philly.
The person blamed it on Open Table and I requested a call from one of the owners which never happened.

So unprofessional and rude. Will never go back to this neighborhood establishment. What a shame how the treat repeat customers!
