Haven't been to POD for years. Had tickets to Annenberg and thought to give it a try.

Very pleasant experience especially the food. A cross between Morimoto (maybe a minor league) and Continental from Stephen Starr. 

The sushi was fresh, the entrees we're delicious, good cocktails and great attentive service. Tried the Ramen, cheesesteak bao, hamachi toro, eggplant skewer and some rolls.

A bit spendy for meal but thoroughly enjoyed.
Nice , space age interior and will be back next time in area.

The best pound cake you can buy! Give for Xmas gifts every year!

Also have great doughnuts and sticky buns along with cookies. The lines at Xmas time exemplifies how good this 5 generation bakery is!

Awesome place for a very special meal. Beautiful environment with excellent wait staff. 

The food is ample in quantity, superb preparation and presentation and of course, delicious! 

Good cocktails, complimentary sweets to top off dinner and a must go when in the area. The cheese selections are top notch and we'll presented with accouterments.

Been before when outside seating is available and is relaxing and refined.

Stopped there for a bite and cocktails.
Beautiful redo after fire gutted it.

Went back for Sunday brunch. Sat under heat lamps on rainy day and very comfortable. Food was good as were the bloody Mary's.

Got to support local establishments!

Went here for birthday celebration. Been here several times before with glowing results. However, whatever the reasons, it isn't the same.
The food was good but not like pre Covid.
The staff is unprofessional, not knowledgeable of procedures or menu offerings and had to be reminded three times about our birthday celebration. It was even noted on the reservation and confirmed with hostess. The waitress took the cake off the table and then brought it back with a candle in it and not everyone was even at the table when she delivered the lit candle.
Also, we picked a wine and then was informed they were out of it. Why put a bottle on a paper menu or QR code if you don't have it? The waitress substituted another bottle on the bar tenders recommendation and charged us $15. More without even telling us.

Very disappointed and unprofessional for a $235 dinner/per couple. Lots of other great places where that money can be spent!

First time here and will be back soon! 
Great inventive Thai food not found elsewhere. 
Attention to details and great attentive service. Owner even checks in on you during mealtime.

Tried the mushroom assortment which was superb along with pork dumplings (nothing like it anywhere in Philly). The whole fish was filleted table side (not one bone) and the lobster fried rice was awesome! Finished it off with pineapple laced pana cotta Thai style. Yummy!

Not on the low end price wise but well worth it for quality, quantity and taste. Want cheap Thai, go to Chinatown!

Sat outside which was clean, ample space and under cover too! Must try again!

yG71EKJXRO6Y-LPrsmFpNQ.review_text:
Had a 6-hr layover in Philly yesterday so we decided to have a quick trip to downtown. We both ordered small diy bowl. Brown rice was warm and chewy. Sashimi was fresh. I love the selections of dressings and crunchy toppings. Price and portion were perfect. We left with a satisfied belly.

Drop two stars because of the cashier. My mom does not read English so I had to translate everything on the menu. The cashier was staring at us indifferently all the time until another staff gave us a menu in Chinese! What's funnier was we overheard she spoke Chinese later! I was like if you do not want to speak Chinese with us, at least give us a Chinese menu, right?! Maybe I am wrong but I think she treats people differently. Not cool.
We had passion fruit green tea + boba + lychee jelly and hot taro milk tea + boba. They both tasted fine, nothing special. Service was fast. Interior was kinda dark.

I do not really eat at airports but we got stuck at the airport for too long and had to eat something. Our server was very nice and attentive. We ordered philly cheesesteak and buffalo shrimp. They came out quick. My mom liked her sandwich with onion, mushroom and green pepper, with a side of fries. I was too exhausted to realize that actually I do not like buffalo sauce... (-_-) So no comment on the shrimp dish.
Portion and price were fine. Not bad for a meal at an airport.

We got seated right away during weekday lunch time. Their menu is huge. It took me a while to decide what to order. Neither of us like fry food so we ordered blackened redfish and chargrilled catfish. Both came with salad and canjun potatoes. Salad was fresh and juicy. Potatoes were cooked well. I prefer the blackened redfish because it's crunchy and crispy on the outside. Catfish tasted too soft to me.
All the waitresses were super nice. Price was very reasonable. A rum bread pudding filled with pear, pineapple, grape and peach is just for $3.5!

Our hotel front desk recommended this place to us. We were surprised by how packed it was on a weekday late morning.

Our server greeted us with "welcome to America". I'm like...WHAT??! I wonder if he says that to all non-white customers?? That's so political incorrect‍

Mocha - very smooth and tasty
Blueberry hibiscus - subtle sweetness 
Brisket hash - I highly recommend this one. Very flavorful and cooked perfectly
Vegan quesadilla - another customer recommended it to us while we were waiting for seats. I'm not a fan for vegan though. I prefer something meaty lol
Chia seed pudding - if you like coconut and granola, you'd love it

Portions are huge. Prices are right. Service is mediocre. I feel like they are understaffed which makes everyone rushed and overwhelmed.

My friend wanted to try alligator meat and turtle soup so we came here. It was not busy during dinner time.

Blackened alligator meat - tender that I expected, tasted like chicken, too salty
Turtle soup - meat was a little hard to chew, too salty 
Chargrilled oyster - pretty good
Sweet potato fries - freshly cut, highlight of the dinner

We don't see many Asians around the city so we are surprised to find a KFT here! Good job franchising!

Strawberry lemonade green tea - one of the top 10. You can't control sugar level for this one. It turned out to be too sweet for me. Also there's not enough green tea taste.

Yogurt grapefruit - yummy! Sour and refreshing, helps with digestion

The very first, the most expensive and the only disappointing meal we had in LA.  It was super loud inside. We got seated outside on a dark and cold patio. 
Frog legs were dry. Crab soup was weak and boring. Shrimp came with a sour-taste weird sauce. Home potatoes were bad.
Service was okay but slow. I was starved waiting for food coming. We didn't take advantage of the happy hour which everyone raves about so probably that's why we had a bad experience :/

Our front desk recommended Frenchmen St for great music so here we are! Our top choice was too packed and loud so we came to Three Muses.
The lady at the front door asked us how many people then closed the door and went back to kitchen, leaving us outside...Ugh bizarre... Our waitress was nice.
It's tapa style so most dishes are small.
Lamb sliders were pretty yummy. Meatballs were okay.
I enjoyed their drinks the most. The Muse and Champagne Supernova were strong and flavorful. 
What disappointed me was the music. I'm not an expert but it's pretty clear that the music was mediocre...

I picked this place for crab cakes, which were quite delicious. Asparagus were very hard to chew though. Sweet potato fries were not freshly cut. My friend had the trilogy and really enjoyed it. Oysters were very fresh but varied much in size. 
Service was very friendly. I'd like to go back for their happy hour.

Our last meal in LA was the local coffee shop PJ's on a Thanksgiving morning. Iced mocha and biscotti were good. My friend's egg cheese muffin was yummy. 
I enjoyed people watching while listening to the acoustic version of pop songs played in the shop.

Rib was kinda dry, not juicy and tender enough. Potato salad and bbq beans were okay.

The guy who took my order was nice. But the young lady who served the food next to him was not very friendly. She also gave me a wrong side.

The lunch special seemed to be the most popular item. I wonder if that tasted better.

Cuban coffee: very different from what I had in Miami. I don't know which one is authentic but I like CREMA's better. It tasted like a sweetened latte to me.

Kouign Amann: not the best but pretty decent. I was surprised to find it here since not many bakeries have it, not even in nyc.

Good service. Spacious interior with a patio seating area.

Food were surprisingly good as an AYCE place.

Shrimp Tempura: very yummy, even better than what I had in Japan.

Sashimi: unlimited, not like some places where you can only have 2 pieces:/ Also tasted good

Almost everything we ordered here were delicious, except for custard bun and sushi rice pizza, which I don't recommend at all.

Service: very friendly and generous. New menu was put on our table without asking for it. 
I just wanna mention that the restaurant smelled weird, almost unpleasant to me...

I ordered online ahead of time to avoid long line. Website told me 25min but it was actually less than 10min which was quite misleading.
There was barely a line when I got there on a weekday afternoon so I decided to eat there.

Mild fried chicken 3/5: okay, the skin was crispy but the meat was flavorless. I've had many chickens that are better than this. 
Fries 5/5: The seasoning was amazing! I usually need to put lots of salt, pepper and ketchup on my fries but no need this time!
Beans were good. 
Mac&cheese was okay.
Peach cobbler was bad.

Lobster bisque: very creamy and tasty
Lamb: okay, everything on this plate-lamb, mashed potatoes and squash were just okay. I didn't like the sauce and had to ask for salt n pepper
Pork chop: my friend said it's the best he's ever had
Rainbow room cocktail: not a fan at all

Prices are on the high end. Very very dark as you can tell from the pics.

Came here 7:15am when there was already a line. I ordered everything recommended: east nasty, bonuts and oj.

East nasty: The fried chicken was better than Hattie's but still tasteless in the middle

Bonuts: not sure why people rave about it. To me those are just fried biscuit dough balls

Orange juice: I like my vitamix oj much better

I had sweet potato French toast, which, according to a yelper, is "mind blowing". Well, to me, I kinda knew how it would taste like if you made French toast with mashed sweet potatoes, so not a surprise to me. I did enjoy it, especially the chopped walnuts on the top.
Latte was also good.

I did a self-guided tour which was informative and fun. First you get to see a 10min film which was great. Then you walk around the theatre to see displays and videos filmed with famous people talking about history of Ryman. Price is a bit high given how small the place is but I enjoyed learning all the histories about Tom Ryman and Sam Jones, Lula(I admire her intelligence and toughness), and the renovation.

Went for a weekday brunch and found the place surprisingly empty. We ordered the signature dishes: Huevos Rancheros and Stuffed Challah French toast. Both were okay, really nothing impressive. I've had better ones. I would recommend leaving potatoes on side because they got quite soggy with the sauce. Service was okay.

Huge portion, low price and fast service. Perfect for a quick bite at night. I ordered a lamb sandwich with tzatikki sauce. Bread could be cooked crunchier. They should also put more sauce because it was quite bland. I end up putting lots of ketchup on it. Lamb itself was great.

yJqqBsh__fl_SGle-Qzi-g.review_text: The Larb-chicken was great! As well as the egg rolls & soft rolls were very good. They also have great food in the carmel location.
The food was excellent! Drunken Noodles and Calamari appetizer. I will definitely return and frequent this restaurant.
The best corn beef hash in central Indiana ! Service is great and they are very accommodating for larger tables.
The food was very good and service was great. Loved the taco menu for lunch. It was perfect!
They are always great! Love this place and they absolutely have the best hummus in the city! I'm never disappointed with their service and quality food.
Love Maggiano's! Maggiano's salad and lighter fare Chicken Marsala. I had chicken to take home.

I ordered in the drive-thru asking for a double cheese with pickle, mustard, and onion, fries. She repeated back with back Ketchup. I spoke up so she could hear my voice Mustard, not ketchup. Went to the widow and kicked up my food. The young woman said, "You should show more respect to people that are handling your food." I tried to question her but she closed the window and turned away. So I went home and ate my food but I began to think about what she did do to my food. This employee needs customer service skills and the prima donna attitude is a bit much. She wouldn't address what bothered her or discuss how I offended her delicate ego. With all the hateful things being done to people, I will never return to this location. Called the manager Chris but I don't feel comfortable. Sent a complaint to Corporate HQ but I don't expect any action.
Their food and service is excellent. If you want a great breakfast go to A2Z. They have a nice variety of brunch and lunch items. I love A2Z!

I purchased the small Chicken Thai pie at farmers market and it was decadent! All fresh ingredients plenty of chicken. Very good! I could only eat  1/2. Very filling. I will make it a point to use them for family and friend gatherings in the future.
Binkleys is the best! I love their Mushroom appetizers and wings. Their food is very good and the staff is friendly and accommodating.
All the food is great! You can't beat their good customer service and good food. Zucchini fries are excellent!
Sitting on the patio is lovely looking at the lake. The food is good and variety of foods to choose from when your with a group.
This is the true essence of the southwest in Mexican food! Very eclectic and authentic in your choice of foods.

Nobody at the counter and when they did come forward they had no interest in taking my order. One man stirring something on the stove and the other individual was talking on the phone. Finally I left. There are too many restaurants that have good customer service. They had no intention of waiting on me. Maybe it was because I was a woman.
We had barbecue from 317 and it was excellent. Moist and the seasoning on the pork was perfect. I would recommend this to anyone

Great News! This location has new ownership and they will be adding Indian food to their menu. I happened to drive by and the open sign was on. I stopped to see what was going on. I ordered some food and it looked great. I was excited that they still had Mediterranean food plus Indian food. They haven't started the Indian food yet but in the next couple of days, they will have a new menu. I'm looking forward to ordering the new menu.
The food and service was excellent. I would recommend that you try Catello's. Very good experience

If you like pancakes this is the place to go but if you like breakfast food not so good. Potatoes weren't cooked enough and sausage links seemed under cooked. The pancakes had a large amount of fruit and seemed good. I was with a friend and she lived the pancakes.

yOkG-b14sdWbZrNvoCj4XQ.review_text: Loved my aerial yoga class today.  Yes, Susan is energetic, knowledgeable and very personable.  She caters to every level.  The studio is very clean and welcoming.  Highly recommend!!

Casual dining at its best!  We have eaten at the bar several times since we moved here in January.  Stella in Stella glasses, Peroni in Peroni glasses, a good start!   
Favorites are pasta fagioli, mista salad, rigatoni bolognese, chicken parm.  Salad and entrees big enough to split. 
Outdoor dining available on the quiet side of the parking lot.
Great value.  Delicious food.  Friendly service.  Glad to have this option close by.

Fresh food in a clean cheerful environment.  We liked the beef tacos and the pork.  Maybe they could post the prices on the blackboard?  This is a great alternative to the pricey places on N Wayne Ave and Chipotle's dark tunnel.  Family friendly but also great to BYOB.  Definitely a welcome addition to the restaurant scene in Wayne.

VF flowers called to deliver this lovely arrangement but we were away on vacation. They offered to deliver a new arrangement upon our return a week later. Thank you!  I love the colors and the low profile of this arrangement for the dining table.   It is now day 4 and the blooms are just beginning to fade.
This is a hidden gem on the east side of 202 in KoP. We had an $8 spider roll (soft shell crab!), a tuna roll and egg foo young. The food is very fresh and inexpensive. The restaurant is spotless.

We ate dinner on the gorgeous patio, lush with flowers. Already can't wait to go back. We had steak frites and Bronzino. We both enjoyed our meals. Our waiter, Ben was extremely professional. 

Inside feels a bit dark, clubby, masculine but I like the idea of a big square bar so you're not staring at a wall. Lots of rooms with different layouts. 

Need more Pinot Grigio for the summer menu. How about more fresh juice cocktails?  Maybe some fresh sangrias?

Flatbread pizza is what they serve and I am a fan.  There's a lot of selection as far as toppings on premade pizza slices.  I had one slice of the artichoke pizza which felt healthy and satisfying at the same time.  The vegetables were very flavorful.  I thought the prices for veggie pizza were fair but you pay almost as much for a slice of plain or tomato pie which seemed pricey. 

I am a local and there is a lot of pizza competition here.  I'm glad I finally tried Jules.  This will be my pizza go to in Wayne.

The Conshy dining/drinking scene got a big boost up with Jasper's!  I heard the space was amazing and it did not disappoint.  Whether you eat in the bar, in the dining room, the patio or the garage, you'll be happy with your table.  The patio has heaters that will keep it open late into the season.  It's open to the dining room and garage so that everyone gets a bit of fresh air.  We sat at the beautiful bar in the loft so we could keep an eye on the World Series.

I loved my spicy margarita, perfectly balanced between hot and sweet.  The crab fries are topped with lump crabmeat, a creamy mornay sauce and a dusting of bay seasoning.  It was more than enough appetizer for 2 people and so good we could not stop eating them even after they cooled.  I had the pork sandwich with a side salad that was perfectly dressed and actually tasted great IN the sandwich.  The short ribs and mashed potatoes were generous and delicious.

Jasper's is great for date night, girls' night, watching a game, any night!

This is exactly what I was craving! Perfectly dressed lobster salad, large pieces of meat on a delicate butter grilled roll. The side of Cape Cod chips and old bay hummus says "we care."  Staff is friendly and made sure to thank me on my way out. Why did I wait so long to try this???

Hands down THE BEST BAR STAFF in the Philadelphia area. Craft cocktails are outstanding. This is the most attentive, courteous, accommodating, pleasant bar service you will find anywhere, no matter how crowded. FRIENDLY service with a smile, but you never have to ask for anything because they anticipate your needs.
Always a nice crowd here. We love the small plates, the kale Caesar salad, meatballs, cheese and charcuterie. 
The decor is hip, interesting, cozy despite the large capacity, warm and inviting.
So sad I wasted calories on a hot dog with a very hard dried out bun at 1 PM. Whyyyy? Parking lot is insane.

Cool decor, generous margarita with fresh juices, homemade chips. Why would you go to a chain Mexican restaurant when you can go to this cool place with authentic food and drinks and beautiful array of Tequilas. Order the blood orange añejo margarita. Yum! The owner is such a nice guy, too!

Husband and I had a great brunch today. Perfect Bloody Mary, 
delicious Cobb salad
mouth watering chicken sandwich on a light pillowy bun, bursts with flavor

My husband said "that tomato relish is really good, where did I just have that?" Umm, Louie Louie last weekend?!

Great tasting, healthy, fresh options. We are fans!

Nice bartender to top it off

Well done, @fearlessrestaurants !

We stayed at the Radnor Hotel for my son's wedding this weekend. It was VERY busy but the rooms felt new and clean. Complimentary water, plenty of ice and the Glenmorgan kindly accommodated several wedding after parties. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel. Congratulations to owners on the remodel. (When staffing is back to normal, maybe vacuum the elevators. :) And hopefully breakfast will be back soon too)

We held a wedding rehearsal dinner on the porch last July. Casey was a phenomenal, pleasant planner who seemed to say yes to everything. I thought they couldn't possibly deliver on so many promises. But this event staff is very seasoned and intuitive. They even helped me get flowers and photos on the tables. It was a perfect evening. Staff was very attentive and congenial.  I kind of wish I had asked to bring home some of the untouched appetizers and desserts for entertaining over the weekend. Bravo, Casey! Sorry for my late review.

yUxv-ZpaGqEUJ3Iaaw9X5w.review_text: We had an excellent meal here but the service was lacking. We arrived about an hour before closing and were sat at the communal table inside as we intended only to get a few apps and drinks rather than entrees. The hostess let us seat ourselves and then didn't come back to bring us menus for over 5 minutes. It was a Tuesday night, there were many servers bustling but it was not busy/full at all and we were mostly ignored and this continued throughout the meal. From the time we finished eating until they came to clear our plates and offer dessert menus was roughly 20 minutes. We had the lamb tartare, duck confit, and some kind of chocolate-y dessert with passion fruit ice cream, which was an odd combination to us but still very tasty. I came back a couple of weeks later with a 6pm reservation on a Friday night to celebrate Mother's Day and the service was much better and the food was incredible, maybe the first time I was there was just an off night.

Excellent happy hour food and drink prices. Came at 4pm on a Friday and service was great but food mediocre. We had the Cajun popcorn shrimp, Hawaiian poke, beef sliders, and crab cakes. It gets very busy toward the end of happy hour/beginning of dinner time, so go early to get a table!

I love corks. The wine-tenders are all lovely and give great recommendations. They are friendly and always on top of it, even when they get crazy busy on the weekends. I have been a member here for about 7 months and love the perks - I can bring three friends in for a free flight anytime! I enjoy coming early on weekday afternoons and sitting by the wood burning stove inside, or outside on the deck in the sunshine depending on the weather. Highly recommend!

We love edomasa and frequent at least once/week, usually on the late night. I have been eating here for close to 15 years. We always get great service and the fish is consistently fresh and well prepared. We order mostly rolls and sashimi/sushi, but have had their chicken Katsu and a few other cooked/non sushi dishes that were also tasty. We love that they are open late and even towards the end of the night the servers are friendly and upbeat. We rarely go anywhere else for sushi! It is super casual and I love that we can go in sweatpants and no one looks at us sideways  favorite roll is the buffalo volcano, it always hits the spot!

My favorite sandwich in sb. I crave it weekly. Same owners since I was a toddler; they are so kind and I still have fond memories of eating turkey sandwiches here with my mom when I was 3 or 4 years old. They use fresh ingredients and though it's nothing fancy, I haven't found a more satisfying sandwich in Santa Barbara.

I came here for my normal Sams to go sandwich that I get all the time on the mesa, but the one I got here left something to be desired. It wasn't terrible, but something was definitely lacking. I will just go to the one on the mesa from now on.

I've eaten here since I was a kid, and i always remember it being good. However, my last meal here left something to be desired and wasn't at all what I remembered from past experiences. I had a mediocre steak and my boyfriends fish was not great. The best part of the meal was the muffins they serve in lieu of bread. It's expensive for mediocre food, probably won't be back.

I've eaten here for over 20 years. I love the club sandwich, also the tuna salad is suuuuper tasty, and they have great daily specials. They have an incredible selection of desserts. The owners are great and they have many longtime staff who have worked there for 10+ years. Fresco is my go to! I only wish they were open later!!

Our food was fine but the service was terrible. We were here around 5pm on a weekday so it was pretty much empty, but we were totally ignored. The bartender was technically our server but he hardly came by at all and was mostly preoccupied having inappropriate conversations with a couple of people over at the bar. The hostess was sweet and came by to refill our water a couple of times when the bartender couldn't be bothered. I've eaten at pascucci downtown since I was a little kid and it's always been solid, even recently, but this experience left a bad taste in my mouth. :(

We don't eat out a lot as my boyfriend is a chef... we've found most of the restaurants around here to be mediocre so we usually prefer to make something at home. However, we wanted to take some friends to dinner last night and decided on boathouse due both to its proximity to our house and the fact that we get free corkage there with my wine club. I'm SO glad we came here. Our server, Tony, was gracious and attentive from start to finish, and the food was better than I was expecting. Tony gladly opened our two bottles of wine, brought us all new glasses when we switched from white to red, and brought us multiple baskets of bread throughout the course of our meal (yowza, their bread and butter is bomb!) We got the grand seafood platter to share (totally worth it, though next time we'd probably skip the raw clams and ask them to double up on shrimp). I had the salmon entree with truffled potatoes and veg, which I loved. Boyfriend has the cioppino which he seemed to enjoy, my friend sent back her Manhattan clam chowder because it wasn't good and tasted like minestrone, but she totally devoured her mahi salad, and her fiancé was raving about his ahi. 

The only reasons I give 4 and not 5 stars is that I've found the hostesses to be snooty/rude on multiple occasions, last night they weren't so bad but you still get the feeling they hate their jobs, which isn't the most welcoming vibe when you're about to drop 200+ bucks on dinner. Im also bummed that their patio is not dog friendly, and lastly, though dinner seems reasonable for seafood, when we came for brunch was super overpriced (it ended up being about $60 for two entrees and one drink). 

All in all a good meal, the interior and patio are beautiful and the ambiance is way nicer than when it was the brown pelican many years ago!

They generally have good prices but are often out of the produce we come for and sometimes the check out lines get soooooooo long (like more than halfway down the aisle, long). On the upside, employees are helpful and friendly and someone is always kind enough to check in the back for produce items when they look to be sold out of something.

Brought my aunt and cousin here for a quick lunch on their way through town. Everything was incredible! I usually go the de la vina location because it is closer to home, but I forgot to specify which location for my family to meet me at and they went to milpas on accident. It did not disappoint! We had the chilaquiles, enchiladas de los altos (breakfast enchiladas) and mole enchiladas. Everything is bomb and the servers were so friendly even though it was crazy busy and brought me my to go order as we finished eating. Will be back!

I will start by saying that my significant other is a professional chef and I have the privilege of eating extremely well at home on a daily basis, so my standards when eating out are VERY high. I have eaten here countless times (30+) while sipping on my favorite beer (Chief peak) next door at topa topa. This is one of the only places I eat out at regularly in SB and recommend to other people. Ive ordered most things on the menu, and never been disappointed or had something I didn't like. The service is friendly, they use high quality ingredients, and everything is fresh and tastes delicious. The pork belly quesadilla is my go to (someone else said it was greasy but that's the nature of the ingredients - pork belly and cheese, hello!) I also LOVE their fried chicken sandwich. It ties for 1st place with the best chicken sandwich I've ever had. The pimento cheese gives just the right amount of spice and the chicken is perfectly crunchy on the outside and so succulent on the inside, yum!

Other stand outs are the crab cakes, lobster Mac n cheese, fish tacos, and any burger. I love the TOPA TOPA Burger but the lama dog burger is also great, as is the short rib and the foie burger. I also enjoy the steak sandwich and the salmon salad. The jalapeño poppers were too spicy for me (May have just been that particular batch of peppers, and I'm a wimp), but even though they made me cry spicy tears, they were cooked to perfection and the filling was delicious. They also make some fabulous desserts in house that tend to sell out - Oreo cheesecake anyone?! BOMB! 

I recently had to go gluten free so last night I ordered the topa burger and they were happy to make it for me over greens instead of on a bun. It was delicious and so satisfying. I'm not even drinking alcohol at this point in time, but I still come to Lama dog just to eat at the Nook. Thanks for being fabulous, Nook fam!

We got to check this place out yesterday and it was great. Thoughtfully curated beer selection, relaxed atmosphere, and super friendly folks working behind the bar. Easy parking, too. Centennial is the perfect addition to old town Goleta, and a welcome alternative for those  who want to avoid the crowds and LA vibes of the funk zone. Looking forward to enjoying many a Sunday afternoon on their back patio!

We are so happy that Teru opened his own place after many years of enjoying omakase by him at the Sakana bar. After getting takeout a couple of times before they opened for dine in, then being out of town most of the summer, we FINALLY had the opportunity to dine in last night and it was such a beautiful and impressive meal. If you're somewhat adventurous, I'd recommend doing omakase so you can get the chef's most inspired and creative food. we got to try new things that we wouldn't have necessarily chosen if we'd ordered off the menu, and everything was spectacular and just to die for. The fish is fresh and super high quality, presented beautifully, snd tastes delicious. The service was super on point, too - efficient, attentive, and friendly. Ashley was our main server but the other gals came by to fill our water as well and they were all great. We can't wait to come again - thank you, Teru + Team! :)

Alessia's croissants blow Renauds out of the water, and their signature candy bar is to die for. We can't wait to come back for breakfast!  So stoked to have another fabulous, locally-owned spot in town.

I'll preface this by saying I hate writing bad reviews. I rarely write them. We work in food service so we are extra understanding of staffing shortages and covid challenges, but tonight was just really awful - they weren't even trying. We had a little time to kill before a show at the Lobero but there weren't many restaurants open and Kai was mostly empty, so I figured it would be quick and I remembered it being pretty good the last times I ate here 15ish years ago. I have never felt so unwelcome sitting at a sushi bar. We were the only ones sitting up there and ordered 2 rolls from the chef within 2-3 min of sitting down, figuring that's all we'd have time to eat before heading back to the theater. The server came and took our drink order but never came back to ask if we wanted anything else off the menu or to refill drinks. It took over 30 minutes for the first roll to come out and another 10 minutes for the second one.  The server never brought us napkins, chopsticks, soy sauce bowls, etc, so once we finally had our first roll we had to ask her to bring stuff so we could eat. Immediately after, I flagged her down to ask if she could go ahead and run my card so we could make a quick exit since I knew we were now on track to be late getting back to our show. I left a 20% gratuity hoping the experience would get better and finish off well. The rainbow roll tasted fine, but the fish was cut really poorly and the whole roll was falling apart so it was really hard to eat. The king cobra roll was just not good and super overpriced. We realized well after ordering that it was 20.95, the most expensive roll on the menu, which would have been fine since it said it had "crab meat"  but it turned out to just be imitation crab, super disappointing and again rolled and cut so poorly that it was impossible to eat without making a mess. The two sushi chefs were totally apathetic and had zero sense of urgency about getting food out, and they weren't even wearing masks (I wish I'd noticed this before we ordered as I would have left). The total before tip was 44.00 for two rolls and a Diet Coke. I felt totally ripped off and bummed about the experience overall both while sitting there and after we left. I will never spend my money here again. Our sushi go-tos are Edomasa and Teru (newly opened on State and Victoria by a longtime chef of Sakana), both of which take pride in the quality of food they serve and the service they provide. There are a ton of sushi places in Santa Barbara and within walking distance from this place that you'd probably be better off eating at.

yd-PRvnG9tXxJDFo9Ohpvg.review_text: Went to Mixto with my parents on a Thursday night. The restaurant was crowded and overly loud. Bar service was the slowest I've experienced in awhile. Service throughout the night was slow, although our server was at least nice. Overall the food left a lot to be desired. I expected a lot more given the price. I wont rush back again.

I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. I placed an order for delivery this afternoon. When the order arrived, they had forgotten my two sodas. I called back and they returned 20 minutes later, but only brought one. I didn't have the energy to try to get the other one. But that paled in comparison to the food. It was disgusting. Lukewarm when it arrived. Strange slimy consistency, with weird grittiness at times. Bland tasting. I  had to throw it away because I was worried it would make me sick. Honestly when you've got great places that deliver, like Circles and Pad Thai, I'm not sure why anyone would ever order from this restaurant.

For the record, this is the first review I've ever written on Yelp. Never before has a food experience been so bad that I've been compelled to let people know.
If you like slow service, Garces Trading Co. is for you. Tasty food, though.

Delicious crepes, but bloody marys were fairly bland. Don't go unless you've got time to spare; when we went the meal for three took nearly two hours. Servers are very nice but seem slow. Also in my opinion the food is overpriced for what you get. If you love crepes, give it a try; otherwise, you can find better value for your money elsewhere.

Most amazing experience I've ever had at a beer distributor. HUGE selection of beers from all over the country, including imports as well as hard-to-find craft beers. We were able to stock up on both the standards and some unique beers from Tampa and Seattle for our Philadelphia-based wedding. Also, staff was tremendous: we walked in, told the guys what we wanted, they brought it to the front, we paid, and they helped us get the cases in the car. Whole thing took 8 minutes. Phenomenal! I'll definitely be back here in the near future!

A great local business that has been in operation for 50 years, 39 under current ownership. Great staff, amazing and varied beer selection, and solid pub-style food. The pub easily and graciously handled our party of 9 in their back dining area. All-in-all, a great place to take the family for a low-key meal, or to grab a unique drink. Highly recommended. We will back as soon as possible.

I have been getting my hair cut in this unassuming salon for several years. Although I don't live in Philadelphia any longer, I still make a point to come back for a hair cut whenever I'm in town. Juju is the main stylist/hair cutter, and somehow she remembers the names of all of her customers. Remarkably, she remembered my name after it had been more than a year since my last visit! Hair cuts are quick, good, and provided with a smile. You'd be foolish to get your hair cut anywhere else.
Friendly service. Rice bowl was dry and flavorless. Meager portions for sides. Too many good options nearby to make this place worthwhile.

Cheesy faux-Italian restaurant in Horsham. Servers don't know anything about the beer or wine they serve. Even when there's only 15-20 people at the bar the bartenders run around like there's 100. They don't pay attention and often bring the wrong drinks. Decent for large groups because they have the space, but otherwise nothing special. Food is ok but nothing to write home about.

There was a letter to the editor of Philadelphia Magazine recently where the writer lamented that many of the restaurants in the city were "just okay and not remarkable;" I imagine SuGa could have been one of the establishments he had in mind when he wrote it. It is a place struggling to define its vibe: is it a sports bar with a giant TV? A hip cocktail bar? Asian fusion restaurant? At the end it does none of those things well. The tiny space is cramped, with hurried bar goers knocking into those seated too close. The service feels harried for no reason, with a waitstaff that is inexperienced and mostly unapologetic for mistakes. We waited 15 minutes after being seated just for someone to take a drink order; we were never asked for a second round. No one checked to see how the food was. Everything was slow. Multiple tables in our section seemed to be having the same experience, with apologies being handed out sporadically. The food could have made up for it, but it was simple at best; a young chef's version of plates made much better by more accomplished peers. Don't rush out to SuGa; the food simply can't make up for the terrible experience. The lobster fried rice came close, and the Kung Pao Chicken was nice, but not nearly enough to make up for the awful service. There are too many other restaurants to try in Philadelphia to make SuGa worth going to.

Slowest service in the city. Nothing special. Not easily accessible from the street. Go somewhere else unless you're staying at the Westin. Oh, and service not friendly at all.

Update: this bar is where fun and drinking go to die.

Not the best haircut, and certainly not a friendly place. Not sure the barber gave two craps if I was there or not. He took barely 5 minutes for the entire thing, and didn't even use scissors. I probably should have demanded more, but I was just so shocked I paid and left. Definitely wouldn't recommend going here ever; I certainly won't go back. If you want a decent cut, honesty Supercuts does a fine job. I still think Citrus Salon is the best haircut in the city; you can't go wrong with Juju!

Good food for a reasonable price. The chicken teriyaki is a strong choice, and the jalapeño Brussels sprouts are fantastic. Staff is exceptionally nice and always very attentive and helpful. A great place for a quick good meal at a reasonable price. I will definitely be back in the future!

Super friendly staff and incredible breakfast sandwiches. Big portions and fresh ingredients. Loved the atmosphere as well. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying out some of their lunch sandwiches. Oh also the college-aged cashier called me "hon." Fun!

Very laid-back atmosphere. Good layout of location, with variety of table sizes and a good-sized tasting bar. They are very pet-friendly, which is cool. People are incredibly nice and fun to chat with. Unfortunately, the beer is average at best. Only really decent one on tap was the Raisin' Kane Winter Spiced Ale. If the only OK beer you have is a spiced ale, that doesn't bode well for ability to craft more subtle options.

Ordered food and it took 2 hours to arrive. Called and staff was surly and rude. Said rain was cause for delay, which is ridiculous. Delivery person couldn't be bothered to apologize. Food was decent, but certainly not worth the wait. Very clear why this place has only two stars. Definitely recommend ordering from any other place.

Fantastic restaurant. Our server Jonas was everything we wanted. Friendly, fast, cordial, knowledgeable. Food was delicious. I highly recommend the Penicillin cocktail. Also, SCS roll was perfection, as were all of the deserts. Can't go wrong here; all the food and deserts are delicious. Great for many occasions!

This is the best brewery in Philadelphia, hands down. The quality of the beer is outstanding. If you like Pacific Northwest-style beers, loaded with Simcoe and Mosaic hops, this is the place for you. Check them out on Facebook or Twitter to see what delicious food truck will be there that night. We had Babalouie BBQ there last night; the brisket was to die for. ARS also often has pizza trucks too. Owners are super friendly, and from Upstate NY to boot! Totally unassuming, relaxed, casual atmosphere that makes it super fun. My wife and I try to get here as much as we can!

Trendy restaurant on 13th. Loud and boisterous atmosphere, with a clientele that skews younger (millennial). Service on a Friday night wasn't paced very well; we waited a long time for a server to first see us, and our first drinks took a long time to come. We ordered 5 small plates with the thought that they would come out one at a time; however, all the plates essentially came out at once, making the eating portion feel rushed. Still, overall drink service was slow, making it difficult to balance timing with food. I decided against my normal drinks due to the slow service. Server was nice. Food was fantastic: highly recommend the cacio e pepe and the swordfish meatballs. Sweetbreads probably not worth getting again. Overall a decent experience, but probably wouldn't come again just due to the sheer number of other fantastic restaurants in Philadelphia.

Fantastic hidden gem in up-and-coming Brewerytown. Staff is always friendly, and they serve a mix of well-made cocktails and a great beer selection. Food is a few steps up from your normal bar food; try the flatbread, the wings, and the Brussels sprouts! Good place to watch a game or listen to live music at one of their weekday sessions. Couldn't recommend this place more!

Enjoyed a fantastic lunch with a friend here today. Service was extraordinary: friendly and prompt. This was my first time eating here, so the server offered and delivered a very thorough and helpful review of the extensive menu. So many options to choose from! The gelato-food pairings are a must: I enjoyed the Carbonara with bacon-infused gelato. Delicious! Of course, we also enjoyed gelato for desert; the hazelnut and pistachio flavors were incredible. Finished everything off with a great cappuccino. Nice and quiet, too; good for a business lunch or a visit with family. I will definitely come back here with my wife and perhaps my parents as well!

Personally I think RTM is overrated. Yes, you can theoretically buy some of Philly's best food here; if you can actually get it, that is. Most of the vendors here are textbook examples of how not to set up businesses: inefficient food preparation, messy serving, slow check-out, etc. Combine this with the fact that there's so many people that you can't move 5 feet without being jostled by someone. So, so, so many tourists all the time. You couldn't feasibly shop here with any frequency; RTM is a place to go for a one-time novelty and then go get your actual food someplace else.

Friendly service. Pastries look delicious although I didn't have one. Breakfast sandwich was tasty but VERY greasy which was not ideal when trying to eat while working. Also seems to get loud even when just a handful of people here. Worst part is the WiFi is VERY slow. Overall a nice place to grab a coffee but there are better places if you're looking to get some work done.

Hip vibe in a reconfigured warehouse space. Lots of variety in seating options for both small and large groups. Loved the exposed brick walls and industrial elements, as well as the food truck that they pull right into the building. Don't get put off by the weird location; it may feel like you're in a bad part of town but Spring Garden is just a block north. Beer is great: be sure to try the Lager (I recommend  making it a Citywide), or even try a cocktail in a can. Good NE style IPA and the stout is good as well. Also, bottomless popcorn, pretzels, and mixed nuts for just $5 is a great deal!

I would have given this place 5 stars, but I had to take one off because the service was atrocious. For some reason the bartenders serve both those seated at the bar as well as people who walk up to the bar and then sit elsewhere. Be prepared to wait a significant amount of time in between drinks at the bar. Because of the service, I probably wouldn't make another special trip here, but wouldn't be against stopping in if I was in the area. Probably best to go on an off-time and not on a Friday or Saturday night.

Interesting little bar tucked away on Cypress Street in Center City. Not sure exactly what vibe they are going for: there's a bit of a clash between the neon sign and modern exterior out front, the tiny bar with crossword puzzle wallpaper on the first floor, and a library decor upstairs. Found the place overall to be rather uninviting: the downstairs bar is tiny and set away from the front door, which kind of makes you feel like you're interrupting a private club when you enter. Bartenders were nice enough but took a while for us to even be acknowledged when we came in. Also not sure what the scene is like on the weekends, but on a cold Wednesday night the upstairs was dead, and the third floor was closed, which made it feel like they didn't really want us there. Cocktails were decent enough but nothing special; you can do better at places like Tipling Place. Overall an OK experience but probably won't go back, instead opting to go to a place that's a bit more welcoming.

I would really love to give Spice Finch a 5-star review: it is one of the few bars in the city we find ourselves coming back to time and again. The cocktails are outstanding (try one of the "redemption" series, each of which features a delicious take on a forgotten or maligned mixer like Jaeger), as is the food (spiced nuts!). Also a chill vibe, where you can almost always find a seat at the bar. Yet every time we've been there (4 times in the past 3-4 months), the bartenders have seemed like they couldn't care less if we were there or not. They have been standoffish, inattentive, rude, even condescending at times. Eventually it will become too much; in fact, if the cocktail menu doesn't change soon we may take our business elsewhere.

Nic's is hit or miss. First time I came I walked right in and got a great haircut right away. Today I waited over an hour before they got to me, which is WAY too long to wait. Problem seemed to be that the stylists just take too long even for basic haircuts, so they're not efficient. The staff is very nice, and I liked my haircut both times; however, I'm not sure I'm going to come back here if there's a risk it will take that long. Maybe the wait and cost is worth it for people who have more complicated needs for their hair. For me just needing a basic men's haircut honestly Supercuts is half the price, you can reserve your place in line, and the cut looks the same.

We weren't sure how well the BBQ would manage through delivery, but we absolutely weren't disappointed. We ordered the Fat Cow, which is the all beef plate with 1/2 pound of brisket, 1/2 pound of  short rib, as well as a bunch of delicious sides. Meat was incredibly tender and juicy, just like when we've been there live. We also ordered hot Italian sausage on the side, which was amazing. If you order sides a la carte, make sure to grab the Mac & cheese! We couldn't recommend ordering delivery here enough, and will absolutely be ordering again soon. Probably top 5 food deliveries we've had in the past four months.

Really difficult ordering system. The website says to call to order ahead for pickup but they don't list the phone number and once you find it, no one answers. Menu items on Caviar don't match items on the website. Signs at the door say order on GrubHub but GrubHub says they don't have a relationship with the restaurant. JFK store employees aren't super friendly. Good part was food prep is pretty quick. Food is OK. Recommend trying other places.

yr2bXeRoijzcg6RYM26HyQ.review_text: We were told by others that Shepherds Tiki Beach Bar and Grill was a fun place to meet other like minded adults.  Granted we went on a Monday evening, but the food was terrible, the bartender had the personality of a dead Opossum, and folks didn't seem particularly interested in engaging with others outside their little groups.  The location is stunning, however.  And we will probably give it another try on a weekend afternoon/evening.
Awesome sushi and very friendly waitstaff.  Fun location - downtown Dunedin is a great little place.
Sadly Honu fell far short of our hopeful expectations.  Totally cool atmosphere out back, but our food was less than good and the bartender was not very welcoming/friendly.
Phenomenal meal and friendly staff... It is located in a kind of plain mini-mall, but they have done a nice job making the inside classy/fun.  Would be a 5 star if it was on the water somewhere.
Awesome pizza and incredible stromboli!! I'm sure other dishes are wonderful as well - just haven't gotten there yet.  My wife is reminding me the cannolis are perfect!

Just GO!  They provide a wonderful atmosphere and a top-notch menu!  The waitstaff are friendly, but sometimes a little slow on refills and checking in on our table, but overall this place is a winner!
Waitstaff is on the ball.  Very casual place.  Come as you are and enjoy some pulled pork nachos, chicken wings, smoked gouda mac n cheese, and the warm butterfinger brownie a la mode.

Would give it 0 stars if allowed.  Who manages this location?  They have messed up so many of my orders i refuse to go there anymore.  And the wait time between ordering and receiving your messed up order is unreal.
We love it here!  Always meet wonderful people and the waitstaff are super friendly.  The food is top notch, but the outside seating at the bar can sometimes be hard to procure.

Wonderful food and a great atmosphere!  We love the pita and assorted spreads appetizer, the Greek salad, the calamari, and the huge assortment of deserts to choose from.  Right in the heart of Tarpon, if you grab a seat overlooking the street - great people watching!

Wish i could give Frenchy's a higher rating... We love the outside bar and the bartenders are really nice people.  But the food isn't spectacular and the beer is served in 12oz plastic cups.  Would hugely benefit them to do 20oz glasses of beer.  Always meet nice people there, fun place to watch a game, and again - bartenders are A-1!
Awesome location!  Lots of history to this little place!  Right on the water and you enter the restaurant through a tackle shop.  Awesome drunken shrimp!

Ok.  So... Local favorite.  And yes, the ice cream is unbelievable!  But damn.  Almost $9 for my wife and I to get 1 scoop each in a cup!  Trying not to sound like a cheapskate, but that is a lot of Ben and Jerry's for the same coin.  Just saying.
Yessir!  Awesome pizza... And I would know! Nice outdoor seating, fun bars, cool waitstaff.  If you are craving consistently good pizza, check them out.

Great outside seating right on the marina.  Small but nice bar.  Great people watching and fun to see the charter boats come in and lay their catch on the dock.  The Salt Cracker will fry, blacken, or cajun season fish you catch and fillet! That is super cool!  And they serve it with fries and coleslaw.

A few years ago we really enjoyed this place but damn the food and service have gone downhill.  Really sad.  The outside tiki bar used to be a fav... But it is always filthy and people sit there chain smoking.  Kinda ruins dinner for those of us non-smokers.  Seems like it is a locals hangout and though we are only a few miles from there, I guess we aren't local enough.  Not a friendly vibe.  Lastly, the bartenders and waitstaff pretty much suck.  You wait a long time for refills, orders are screwed up, and it seems like most don't give a s#@t.
Islandy feel.  Food is great! Staff is on the ball.  Stop by for some island vibes!  Beef empanadas, Jerk chicken pasta, salmon... Are all excellent!  Hannah S. Is awesome!! Be a decent patron!

So, i am sorry if i come across as a "Richard", but this place flat out annoys me.  We just drove past - 7:45 PM - and they were blaring music.  Lots of people milling about, trying to listen to the kid with the electric violin across the street... And this place is blaring rock louder than the woofer clown in the noisy Honda.  Then there is the sign out front that reads, "Eat my taco, baby".  Ok.  I am no prude but is it just me that finds that a wee bit inappropriate for downtown Dunedin? Anyway they get 2 stars, despite my never having eaten there because it IS downtown Dunedin and I applaud small businesses AND at least they were blaring good classic rock.

Amazing lunch!!! Cedar plank seafood special - sea bass, salmon, mahi mahi.  Great zucchini - italian style.  And greek salad with grilled chicken.  Also started out with the firecracker shrimp appetizer.  DELICIOUS!!  Craziest location - in the middle of a couple working boatyards/marinas.  They have a beautiful patio with chaises, a pool, and hot tub.  Water views, shaded tables, and a constant breeze.  Truly a hidden gem!  It is a Monday at 2pm and a very decent dining crowd - kinda speaks for itself

We absolutely LOVE our visits to the Don!  Right on St Pete Beach - voted best beach in America.   Staff, save for the grumpy short old man at the reception desk, are VERY accommodating.  Excellent food and drinks both poolside and inside.  The Don has history almost as colorful as its exterior.  If you have the opportunity to stay in the seaside suite - do!!  Sun setting over the gulf... Amazing!

Wow!  This place is rocking it!  Expect a lengthy wait for outdoor seating or a seat at the outdoor bar.  Worth the wait.  Food is excellent!  Waitstaff are friendly and cool under pressure.  Prices are completely reasonable.  Live music is fun and talented.  And fellow customers are fun!

Well... Sadly the last 2 times we have ordered pickup from Franks, they have COMPLETELY messed our orders up.  They seem to have a bunch of young women working there that just can't seem to get it together.  While there we overheard someone calling in to complain their delivery order was a mess too.  What is happening, Franks???

Ok... Just wanted to add that we are here on a Sunday afternoon to enjoy cold beers while poolside and in the pool.  For a couple with no kids and who are used to "adult' poolside settings... This is NOT it.  Kids running and screaming everywhere.  More pool water in my cup than beer from the little turds doing cannonballs.  Once we accepted this is not a sexy atmosphere, we have been enjoying the kid-insanity.
We loved the food, Sam (waitress), the music, the drinks, atmosphere... Just an overall great experience.

Folks... You have to come down to this little corner of Palm Harbor and support this little corner place.  They have a great beer selection, wine  coffee, gelato... And the owner is a true stand up guy.  Perfect spot to relax and take in all the surrounding activities.  There are several nearby food/drink establishments - which is cool.  But don't forget the "Little guy".

z89zvVnsyKqXLXVfAnRVWw.review_text:
My husband and I went here this past weekend for my birthday on our quest to dine at every Garces restaurant before we move in three weeks (6 down, 1 to go!). I had a feeling I would enjoy this one, and it actually exceeded my expectations.

I actually quite liked the decor and feeling of the restaurant. Where else can you dine so well in a train station under an escalator? It felt warm and comfortable, probably because of the wood and plants. And I couldn't get over how much bigger our table was than at most other Garces restaurants. We had plenty of room to spread out our food (Even though we were at one of the long tables and not our own).

We came in thinking we would order the Chef's Tasting, which is what we usually do at Garces restaurants because the menus are so vast and you don't know what to choose. Once we really looked at the menu though, there were clear things that we wanted to try, and when we added up the cost it was far less than if we had both ordered the tasting.

Cocktails: My husband ordered the Empire Builder and seemed to enjoy it. I'm not a bourbon-drinker but I had a sip and it tasted good. I ordered the Keystone, which was sweet but not too much, and lasted me throughout dinner.

First course (All of these things came out at once, when we expected them to come out in two courses. It was almost overwhelming, but we handled it.): 
Housemade Rolls: Simple, hot, and delicious. The apple jelly was extra great.
Slim JG: 4 sticks of housemade sausage, 4 crackers, mustard. It was a nice snack, can't complain.
Maine Lobster Cappuccino: I heard many good things about this, but just couldn't imagine how it could taste good. Wow, it was so good. One of the highlights of the night.
Keswick Creamery Fondue: Cast iron crock filled with creamy fondue, served with breadsticks, apples, and a fantastic onion jam. This was my husband's favorite first course. There's more cheese than dippers, but you can get creative with things to dip (rolls, spoons, etc.)
Hawaiian Opah Ceviche with Spiced Passion Fruit Sorbet: This was one of the specials of the night. It might have been the best ceviche I've ever had. Perfect acidity and sweetness, and I love the texture of opah. I'm a sucker for Jose's sorbets.

After a small break, we got our second course plates:
Kabocha squash: There seems to be a lot of hate for this dish, and really we weren't thinking about ordering it. But when we realized how few vegetables we were ordering, and we saw the people next to us get it, we decided to go for it. It was cooked perfectly (still with some bite, not mushy at all) and had a really nice vinaigrette. Its also two of my favorite veggies (kabocha and black kale), so I'm glad we listened to ourselves instead of the reviews on this one.
California Organic Maitakes: Two maitakes in polenta. The plate for this one was so big we each just grabbed a mushroom and put it on our plate to get the big bowl out of the way. These were very good, but kind of forgettable since we rushed through them.
Green Village Suckling Pig: This was the whole animal of the night. It was a last-minute decision to order this and I'm so glad we did. Every bite of the pork was moist and extremely flavorful. Every cut was better than the last. And the portion on this one was much bigger than we expected from the sound of the reviews. Definitely enough for us.

Dessert course: I always expect dessert to be my favorite, but I don't think I could ever have expected this. My hubs ordered the Bourbon, which gives you three hot beignets covered in powdered sugar with a bourbon butterscotch sauce. These were excellent (recommended by our waiter, even though we would have ordered them anyway) and my husband's favorite dish of the night. Then, my dessert came. I ordered the Maple, which is a Maple souffle that comes out hot from the oven. The server pokes a hole in the middle of the souffle, scoops in some ice cream, then pours a hot maple creme anglaise to melt the ice cream into a delicious creamy maple-y soup. I took my first bite and I almost died right there. It.was.so.good. Seriously, if you like maple or souffle or dessert at all, order this. It was the perfect dessert to end the meal.

The dinner ended with 2 petit fours each, one a blood orange and one a chocolate/marshmallow combo. Both were good, but I scraped one last taste of my souffle because I wanted to end with that taste in my mouth.

Our waiter was very nice and helpful, as we've come to expect from any GRG establishment.

Yes, the portion sizes can be small on some dishes, but some of that perception is because we're all used to giant portion sizes. For people who love to have many tastes of different things, this is perfect. The amount of plates we ordered was perfect for us, and we left feeling extremely satisfied but not overly stuffed. It may not Jose's best value for the volume of food, but for quality, its worth every penny.

I grew up on this place and crave it as soon as the weather gets warm. While Ted Drewes may be superior in quality, the variety at Spanky's wins any day. Get a slustard. Might sound disgusting (half slush/half custard) but it's the best thing on the menu. If you're not in a custard mood, get a fresh fruit slush - the most refreshing drink! The pumpkin pie concrete is also incredible, but only a seasonal item.

The topping bar is top notch. They even have mochi, which is my all-time fave FroYo bar topping and pretty hard to find. The fruit was fresh and the housemade sea salt caramel almost had me licking my bowl to get the last bit. One star off for yogurt selection... I've seen stores with more and there were no really inspiring flavors, though all I tried were excellent. Great place!

I planned my sister's bachelorette party for this past weekend and made dinner reservations at Eclipse. We met at the rooftop bar of the Moonrise, then went down to Eclipse for dinner. I was somewhat worried after reading some reviews of the place, but I couldn't have been happier with the level of service we received, and the quality of drinks and food. 

There were about 18 girls in our party, and we were given 2 large tables in a somewhat separate room (there were other people in there, but it felt pretty private). We had a server for each table, and I was very impressed by their attentiveness and accuracy, given we had such a large (and somewhat rowdy) party. They even let us get individual checks, which made everything so easy. I'm so happy with the service, I can't say it enough.

The drinks: I stuck with wine, but I had sips of other's drinks to try, and all of the cocktails I tried were outstanding. The Plantation had a mix of gin, grapefruit juice, and basil that I would order again and again and will try to recreate at home. The Italian Greyhound was also a gin and grapefruit juice concoction, that was very refreshing and easy-drinking. Next time I'll take the hubs to try out the great-sounding bourbon cocktails.

The food: Half the people at my table ordered the veggie ravioli, which was stuffed with Boursin cheese and was smothered in a fresh tomato sauce with big slices of roasted tomatoes and vegetables. It far exceeded my and everyone's expectations. Most of the other people at my table got the chicken, which looked great and everyone seemed to enjoy. I know one other person ordered the steak, and said it was fantastic.

I think Eclipse has stepped up it's game, and people giving it negative reviews should give it another chance, even if just for the drinks. I'm very happy that I planned the party here, and I'd love to come back next time I'm in town.

I loved First Watch when I lived in St. Louis. I usually went to the Kirkwood location and never had a bad meal. On a trip back this weekend, the hubs and I went to the Clayton location and were just underwhelmed with the whole experience. The wait wasn't bad (25 min), but we watched the busser clear off our table, then we were seated when there were still giant crumbs left on the table. Everything seemed to be a little dirty and sticky, like a greasy diner. The memories of First Watch I had were that everything was clean and fresh, but I didn't have that experience here. The hubs and I left satisfied with our food, but not blown away by anything, and not having a strong desire to return next time we're in town.

I was pleasantly surprised on our trip to Max Brenner's after reading some of the negative reviews here. We had always kind of avoided the place when we lived near Philly, but I'm not so sure why now. The hubs and I went with his parents and sister. 

The place was smaller than I expected, and I was happy that we got in a reservation for 5 people that afternoon. The only negative on the atmosphere was that we were sitting at a high top table, and the ceiling fan on above us was blocking a light, causing a strobe light effect on our menus that almost made us a little carsick. Otherwise, the stools were comfy and the restaurant well-decorated. 

The service was the thing most people complained about, but our waitress (I wish I remembered her name) was as sweet and helpful as could be. 

The portions of food were much larger than I expected. I had the Asian chicken and vegetable salad (which I definitely recommend, especially if you like herby salads), 3 others got burgers (Brenner, Chicken, and Turkey), and 1 ordered the steak and mushroom quesadilla. Everyone raved about their dish, but also commented that it was so large and we wanted to save room for dessert (it's that why you come here?)

For dessert we ordered a few hot chocolates, the Works chocolate pizza, and SIL ordered the Max-wich cookie/ice cream sandwich for herself. I was expecting a small sandwich that she could eat on her own, but this was giant, (I'd guess 6 inches in diameter?) and definitely for sharing. I'm glad she was able to share too, because it was rich and delicious, perfect for a dark chocolate lover. We probably could have gotten by with a half pizza too, which was very good, but if we went again, I'd try something else.

Overall, I was very pleased and very full of good food and chocolate when I was finished. And I left with 2 hug mugs from the gift shop, thanks to the 10% off with your dinner receipt that our waitress made sure to tell us about.

I had my first introduction to the self serve froyo concept here soon after it opened, and I have been obsessed ever since. Abundant yogurt flavors and toppings, all great quality. It's a must-stop whenever we're on South Street, or whenever we're in Philly, really.

This opened just as we were leaving the area, but luckily I got a chance to try it before we moved. Pretty standard yogurt and toppings, which isn't a bad thing. Toppings were fresh, yogurt flavors were good, which is really all you can ask for. Solid addition to the up-and-coming plaza.

I didn't know how good we had it living so close to this place when we did. It is the place that made us love and crave Indian food. Their chicken tikka masala is the dish by which I judge all CTM, and I haven't found one that even comes close to being that good. And their garlic naan is just amazing. I can't describe it with any other words. 

I miss Sultan, and hope to find something closer to our new home that will be able to stand up to it, but I don't have high hopes.

We're usually not ones to repeat restaurants, but we went here every Friday when we were living in Blue Bell. It was that good. Always the same order - two meats (always pulled chicken, the other varied by our mood) + ribs (St. Louis style) + two sides (mac & cheese + baked beans).

I never liked baked beans until I tasted Smoke Daddy's baked beans. And the pulled chicken is the best BBQ I've had to date. It is just so good. Try it out, you'll be very happy.

Lion's Choice is like no other fast food I've ever encountered. We generally never go to fast food restaurants, but Lion's Choice is a must-go every time I go home to StL, and my husband had grown to love it as well. 

The quality of ingredients they use is what sets them apart from other fast food - medium rare roast beef and the best fast food fries by a long shot. 

If you're in the area and need a quick meal, try the roast beef and you will not be disappointed, I promise.

And finish your meal off with a 14 cent ice cream cone. Seriously. It's the best.

Delicious ice cream you can feel good about eating.

We were surprised to happen upon this store in Nashville, and to find it's the only location outside of Ohio. 

Friendly scoopers let you try as many samples as you'd like. While it makes the line (and boy, is there a line!) move a little slower, you appreciate it when its your turn at the counter and you couldn't make up your mind during your wait. My favorite was the goat cheese and cherries, and I loved the hubs' black coffee.

I love that you get half scoops to maximize the number of flavors you can put on a cone!

Hubs found this little place through Yelp on our trip to Nashville over Labor Day.

Arrived around 8:00 and waited about 10 minutes for a table. The space is pretty small, but very relaxed and cute. Everyone we encountered was very nice and helpful.

Hubs got the basil lemonade (yum!) and the pork tenderloin special. He liked it but didn't love it. I tried a bite and it was good. No complaints, just nothing memorable. I got the red tea (a little too sweet, but I'm an unsweet tea kinda girl), Zipper sandwich with both herb couscous and a salad. All very good, but again, not really memorable. I want to note though that all of the food was presented really beautifully, which does add to enjoyment. 

We decided to pass on dessert to venture to Jenis next door (even though they did have a selection of Jenis ice cream at the restaurant, we wanted the full experience). 

Overall, I would come back, but I wouldn't become a regular.

Good hot dogs, super friendly staff. Hubs and I tried the Chicago, Boston, and New York on our trip and very much enjoyed the quick, casual lunch.

Tip - Skip the french fries and get the fried pickle spears! They were my favorite thing.

Happened to be in Nashville on a Friday afternoon, and decided to take advantage and check out Arnold's while it was open. We walked the mile from our downtown hotel in the 100+ degree heat and I am very happy to say it was worth it.

While waiting in line, I was convinced by a man eating that I needed to get the fried shrimp. I also got the fried green tomatoes, asparagus, and candied yams. For dessert, peach pie. Hubs got the lunch special BBQ beef on a jalapeno grit cake, + his 3 sides, and pecan pie for dessert. Mmmmm. Everything was excellent. 

Believe the hype. You don't earn 2 James beard awards for being mediocre. I hope to make it back someday, the sooner the better.

This was one of my favorite restaurants in the area when we lived here, and I still miss it when going to other brewery/restaurants other places. Nothing quite compares to Iron Hill.

We went here many times, both dining in and taking advantage of their great take-out deal (2 pizzas + a growler for $25!) and were never disappointed. The food is fresh, and they really stand behind it. Some favorites were the carrot soup, halibut with crispy Brussels sprouts, and the rock shrimp pizza. 

Of course the beer was great, too. The sampler is a good tool to get you familiar with the different brews, and the seasonal beers are always interesting to try. Raspberry wheat was always my go-to, but there's always something to satisfy any craving I was having.

I look forward to going back when I'm in town!

Love this chain and hope as it gets a little bigger it still stands by its morals (grass-fed beef, organic ingredients). My only complaint is that they use Blue Bunny ice cream for their shakes. Seriously? They could do so much better.

This place is kind of crazy.

I grew up as the mini golf course was being built. Driving by it every day, it seemed like it was never going to be finished. In my mind (and I'm pretty sure in reality also), it took years to open. When it was finally finished, it was worth the wait. It's the strangest, most unique mini golf course I've ever played on. Definitely worth a visit.

I'm also very familiar with the bowling alley. During about a month or two in high school, I took bowling for gym class and we would pile into the bus and drive over here 3 times/week. On a recent trip back home and a random decision to go bowling, I even found the old balls I used during that time. It was kind of surreal.

A fine complex with almost anything you'd want to do.

Good food, decent beer selection, and great atmosphere. It has a neighborhood feel that makes me feel nostalgic for St. Louis. 

The outdoor patio is great when the weather is, which makes this a summertime must. I'm sure I'll be back when I'm in town!
